stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned Monday of a "bloodbath" if the United States attacks the island, as Washington imposed new sanctions on Cuba's intelligence agency and senior officials. The escalation follows reports of Cuban drone acquisitions from Russia and Iran amid heightened military tensions.

stories.title: Israel bombs Tyre in Lebanon following displacement threat
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck a building in the al-Mushaqqa area of the Tyre district in southern Lebanon. The air strike came less than an hour after Israeli military spokesman Avichay Adraee issued a forced displacement warning ordering residents to evacuate the area.

stories.title: Official says Iran will force US to 'retreat and surrender'
stories.summary: Mohsen Rezaei, a member of Iran's Expediency Council, mocked U.S. President Trump for postponing a planned military strike on Iran. Rezaei said Iran's armed forces would force the United States to retreat and surrender.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Emergency Service shares wartime experience with Swedish colleagues
stories.summary: A delegation from Sweden's Rescue Services Agency visited Ukraine to learn about the operations of Ukraine's State Emergency Service under wartime conditions caused by Russia's ongoing military aggression.

stories.title: Russian hiker becomes Japan’s latest bear attack victim as another grim record looms
stories.summary: A Russian hiker was seriously injured by a bear attack near Mount Sanukido in the town of Okutama, west of Tokyo, on Sunday. The man sustained severe facial and arm injuries and was airlifted to a hospital. The incident raises concerns about another record year of bear encounters in Japan.

stories.title: ‘Game over’ graffiti appears outside Russian residential building struck by drone. Two days later, it was painted over.
stories.summary: A "Game over" graffiti mural appeared near a residential building in Yekaterinburg, Russia, that was recently struck by a Ukrainian drone. Municipal workers painted over the artwork two days after it appeared on May 16.

stories.title: Croatia blocks Israeli ambassador nomination amid diplomatic dispute
stories.summary: Croatian President Zoran Milanovic rejected approval for Israel's proposed ambassador to Zagreb, citing objections to policies pursued by the current Israeli government. The presidential office said the nominee would not receive consent and broke with its usual practice of not publicly commenting on ambassadorial nominations.

stories.title: Tributes paid as ‘outstanding’ soldier who died in fall at Royal Windsor Horse Show is named
stories.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence identified the soldier who died after a fall at the Royal Windsor Horse Show as Lance Bombardier Ciara Sullivan, 24, of the King's Troop, Royal Horse Artillery. Sullivan fell from her horse at around 7 p.m. on Friday after exiting the arena.

stories.title: Lebanese ministry says death toll from Israeli attacks crosses 3,000
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported on Monday that the death toll from Israeli attacks on the country since March 2 has surpassed 3,000. Hezbollah said it carried out a retaliatory drone attack targeting Israeli soldiers in the southern Lebanese town of Rachaf.

stories.title: Officials say 39 pupils abducted in Nigeria's Oyo state, one teacher killed
stories.summary: Gunmen abducted at least 39 schoolchildren and seven teachers in Nigeria's southwestern Oyo state, killing one teacher in captivity. Security operatives were wounded by explosive devices during a rescue attempt.

stories.title: Cuba warns US military action would cause ‘bloodbath’ after drone report
stories.summary: Cuba warned that U.S. military action against the island would result in a "bloodbath," following reports related to U.S. drone activity near Cuban territory.

stories.title: China’s firms have a glaring weakness as they face a barrage of EU probes
stories.summary: Chinese firms expanding overseas face challenges from a growing number of European Union investigations and probes. The article examines how companies seeking new markets amid narrowing domestic profits are encountering a complex regulatory environment in Europe.

stories.title: Can PLA training catch up with China’s rapid weapon development?
stories.summary: China's official military newspaper, PLA Daily, warned that personnel may lack sufficient training to operate new weapons systems, including unmanned platforms, despite rapid hardware advances. The article highlighted weak coordination between human operators and technology in some military units.

stories.title: Ancient China laws punished men for crying; people with messy handwriting forced to drink ink
stories.summary: An article examines unusual and sometimes bizarre laws from ancient China's legal history, including punishments for public crying by men and penalties for messy handwriting. The legal system served as a mechanism of imperial control across dynasties, producing codes like the Tang Code.

stories.title: Organisers say Israeli forces seize more Gaza-bound flotilla ships
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted additional Gaza-bound flotilla vessels in international waters, according to the Freedom Flotilla Coalition. The group said the ship Perseverance, carrying volunteers from Australia, Belgium, Canada, and France, was seized and its crew detained. Organizers said at least 47 ships had been seized while around 30 vessels continued sailing toward Gaza.

stories.title: Israeli forces raid villages near Ramallah, clashes erupt
stories.summary: Israeli forces raided the villages of al-Mughayyir and Abu Falah in the Ramallah and el-Bireh governorate of the occupied West Bank on Monday. Clashes erupted with residents in al-Mughayyir, where troops reportedly fired toxic gas canisters. No immediate information on injuries or arrests was available.

stories.title: How Hamas’s internal cracks are becoming impossible for Gazans to ignore - opinion
stories.summary: Questions are growing inside Gaza about whether Hamas retains the popular support that once underpinned its legitimacy after seizing control of the Strip in 2007. Internal divisions within the group are becoming increasingly visible to the local population.

stories.title: Former Russian lawmaker Magomed Gadzhiyev is sentenced in absentia to life in prison for murder and corporate raiding
stories.summary: Dagestan's Supreme Court sentenced former Russian State Duma deputy Magomed Gadzhiyev in absentia to life in a maximum-security prison. He was convicted of organizing a double murder and extortion, and fined 900,000 rubles.

stories.title: Hong Kong finance chief woos French wealth managers as European tour kicks off
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po began a five-day European tour in Paris, meeting French financial management representatives and think tank officials. The visit is part of Hong Kong's push to attract global capital and reinforce its standing as an international financial hub.

stories.title: Trump’s shifting remarks on Taiwan are perfect for China to exploit
stories.summary: President Trump's remarks characterizing Taiwan arms deals as a "negotiating chip" with Beijing have unsettled Taipei and been amplified by Chinese state media. During Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing, Xi issued a stark statement reaffirming China's claims over Taiwan. The comments raise concerns about the stability of longstanding U.S. support for the island.

stories.title: Liberal senator breaks ranks to take aim at Angus Taylor’s ‘negative’ rhetoric on immigration
stories.summary: Australian Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan publicly criticized opposition leader Angus Taylor's plan to bar non-citizens from accessing welfare. McLachlan warned the policy would create "two types of members of the community" and said migrants should not be blamed for economic problems including the housing crisis.

stories.title: Cash-strapped UN refugee agency to cut more jobs, even as crises mount
stories.summary: UNHCR, the UN refugee agency, will need to cut additional jobs and implement urgent reforms due to declining funding, according to a letter from the agency's head. The cuts come even as global displacement crises continue to mount.

stories.title: Spanish king to attend a World Cup match in Mexico
stories.summary: Spanish King Felipe VI will travel to Mexico to attend a FIFA World Cup match, signaling warming relations between the two countries. Ties had been strained over disputes related to colonial-era abuses.

stories.title: Israel, Hezbollah war persists despite truce extension; Lebanon's death toll passes 3,000
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes in southern Lebanon on Monday while Hezbollah announced new attacks on Israeli forces, continuing hostilities despite the extension of a U.S.-backed ceasefire. Lebanon's death toll from the conflict has surpassed 3,000.

stories.title: Jury rules against Musk in blockbuster OpenAI trial
stories.summary: A US federal jury in Oakland, California, ruled unanimously against Elon Musk in his lawsuit against OpenAI, finding his claims were brought too late. The jury deliberated for less than two hours in the closely watched case.

stories.title: Teen gunmen kill 3 in apparent hate crime at California Islamic Center
stories.summary: Two teenage gunmen opened fire at the Islamic Center of San Diego, California, killing a security guard and two other men before being found dead from self-inflicted gunshot wounds. The San Diego police and FBI are investigating the attack as a hate crime. All children at a school housed in the mosque compound were confirmed safe.

stories.title: Texans accuse Japan of doing ‘deal with the devil’ by funding US fossil fuel projects
stories.summary: Residents from Texas Gulf coast communities traveled to Tokyo to urge Japanese financial institutions to halt funding of fossil fuel projects linked to U.S.-Japan tariff negotiations. They met officials from the Japan Bank for International Cooperation and government ministries, citing health and safety concerns.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says Iran attack postponed at request of Gulf allies
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a postponement of a planned military strike on Iran, citing requests from Gulf allies. Iranian leaders in Tehran have responded with defiance, rejecting what they describe as American pressure.

stories.title: Hydrometeorological Center forecasts thunderstorms across Ukraine on Tuesday
stories.summary: Ukraine's Hydrometeorological Center forecast partly cloudy weather with brief rain showers and thunderstorms across the country on Tuesday, May 19.

stories.title: Hydrometeorological Center forecasts thunderstorms across Ukraine on Tuesday
stories.summary: Ukraine's Hydrometeorological Center forecast partly cloudy weather with short-term rain and thunderstorms across the country on Tuesday, May 19.

stories.title: Mark Fuhrman, LA detective convicted of lying at OJ Simpson trial, dies
stories.summary: Former Los Angeles police detective Mark Fuhrman, who found a bloody glove at O.J. Simpson's home during the 1994 murder investigation, has died. Fuhrman was convicted of perjury after audio recordings revealed his use of racial slurs, undermining his credibility during the high-profile trial.

stories.title: Gunman kills six, wounds eight in southern Turkey
stories.summary: A 37-year-old gunman killed six people and wounded eight others in a shooting spree in southern Turkey. The suspect reportedly first shot his ex-wife before targeting others in the area.

stories.title: 4 dead, 8 hurt as gunman opens fire in southern Turkey: Reports
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire in southern Turkey, killing at least four people and injuring eight others. At least two of the victims were killed inside a restaurant.

stories.title: Analyst says Trump’s Iran demand blocks path to deal
stories.summary: U.S. foreign policy analyst Matt Duss of the Center for International Policy argued that Washington's demand for zero uranium enrichment from Iran is blocking prospects for a diplomatic deal. He attributed the condition to pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and hawkish figures in Washington.

stories.title: US tightens Ebola precautions as outbreak declared international emergency
stories.summary: The United States announced enhanced Ebola precautions including airport screening of travelers from outbreak-affected areas and suspension of visa services, after the WHO declared the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak an international health emergency.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns drone strike on Saudi Arabia, expresses solidarity with Riyadh
stories.summary: Pakistan strongly condemned drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressing solidarity with Riyadh. Saudi Arabia's defense ministry reported intercepting three drones originating from Iraqi airspace, while Iraq said it is investigating the incident.

stories.title: Turkey has potential to influence Ukraine, Iran wars, German minister says
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Turkey has the potential to exert influence over the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. He called for strengthened strategic ties between the European Union and Ankara.

stories.title: Minnesota officials charge ICE agent in shooting of Venezuelan immigrant
stories.summary: Prosecutors in Hennepin County, Minnesota, charged ICE agent Christian Castro with four felony counts of second-degree assault for shooting a Venezuelan immigrant in Minneapolis in January. He was also charged with a misdemeanor count of falsely reporting a crime.

stories.title: Opposition lawmakers stage protest in National Assembly, demand medical care for Imran
stories.summary: Opposition lawmakers from PTI staged a protest in Pakistan's National Assembly demanding proper medical care for incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan, with opposition leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai stating the government had missed its deadline to act.

stories.title: US suspends joint defence effort with Canada dating back to World War II
stories.summary: The Trump administration suspended a joint defense arrangement with Canada that dates back to World War II. The move follows repeated U.S. accusations that allied nations have not met their mutual defense commitments.

stories.title: Trump says US may accept Iran deal if Gulf allies back terms
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump indicated Washington could accept a diplomatic deal with Iran if key Gulf allies endorse the terms. He reiterated that any agreement must include a total ban on Iranian nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Iran commander warns US against ‘strategic mistake’ amid tensions
stories.summary: Major General Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, warned the United States against making a "strategic mistake or miscalculation" amid rising tensions. He said Iran's armed forces are on high alert and prepared to respond to any aggression.

stories.title: War update: 203 combat clashes on front line, heaviest fighting continues in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 203 combat clashes along the front line, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector. Russian forces reportedly suffered 70 casualties in that direction.

stories.title: 4 dead, 8 hurt as gunman opens fire in southern Turkiye: reports
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at a restaurant in southern Türkiye, killing at least four people and injuring eight others before fleeing the scene in a car.

stories.title: China joins global sell-off of US Treasuries in March as Iran war prompts panic
stories.summary: Mainland Chinese investors reduced their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills in March, joining a global sell-off driven by uncertainties surrounding the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. Analysts said the reductions reflected concerns over inflation, energy prices, and fiscal pressures pushing Treasury yields higher.

stories.title: Mexico freezes bank accounts of ex-officials investigated by US
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that Mexico has frozen the bank accounts of former officials accused by the United States of ties to the Sinaloa Cartel. She described the action as a preventive measure rather than part of a domestic investigation.

stories.title: Flawed tests and funerals allowed Ebola to spread undetected, sources say
stories.summary: Reports indicate that flawed diagnostic tests and funeral practices allowed Ebola to spread undetected. The crisis has been compounded by years of underinvestment and funding cuts to public health infrastructure.

stories.title: Ex-British soldier imprisoned by Russia says he feels abandoned in occupied Ukraine
stories.summary: Hayden Davies, a former British soldier imprisoned by Russia in occupied Ukraine, said in letters to the BBC that he has had no contact with British authorities and feels abandoned by his government.

stories.title: Three killed in attack at San Diego Islamic centre in suspected hate crime
stories.summary: Two teenage gunmen opened fire at the Islamic Center of San Diego on Monday, killing three men before dying by apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds nearby. Authorities are investigating the attack as a suspected hate crime, and officials credited a mosque security guard with preventing further casualties.

stories.title: What really holds China and Russia together
stories.summary: An analysis examined the durability of the China-Russia relationship, noting that despite a significant power imbalance, both Moscow and Beijing view the partnership as too strategically important to allow it to fail.

stories.title: U.S. extends sanctions waiver on Russian seaborne oil by 30 days
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury extended a 30-day sanctions waiver on Russian seaborne oil to allow vulnerable nations continued access to stranded Russian crude. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described the temporary general license as a measure to support energy-dependent countries.

stories.title: ISIS leader killed in Africa as US commander raises force reduction concerns
stories.summary: A senior ISIS leader was killed during U.S. operations in Africa. However, U.S. force reduction plans on the continent have raised concerns among military commanders about America's ability to counter terror plots emanating from the region.

stories.title: Despite tense podium incident, Israeli fighter Yoav Manor wins bronze in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Israeli fighter Yoav Manor won a bronze medal in the under-77 kilogram division at a competition in Abu Dhabi, securing three victories in four matches. The podium ceremony reportedly involved a tense incident.

stories.title: Racist abuse of NHS nurses rising amid ‘normalisation’ of extreme views, RCN warns
stories.summary: The Royal College of Nursing reported an 86% increase in racist abuse directed at NHS nurses in recent years. Incidents include a nurse being called a monkey by a colleague and a patient throwing a hot drink followed by racial slurs. The union's leader attributed the rise to the normalization of extreme views in politics and media.

stories.title: Free up fertiliser supplies to avert global food crisis, Yvette Cooper urges
stories.summary: UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper urged the urgent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to restore fertiliser and fuel shipments disrupted by the war in Iran. The supply crunch has already damaged harvests in the UK, Europe, and the U.S., with the worst impacts felt in developing countries where farmers face soaring prices.

stories.title: Third of university students in Great Britain think AI job losses will cause social unrest, poll finds
stories.summary: A King's College London survey found that one in three university students in Great Britain believe AI-driven job losses will trigger civil unrest. The poll also showed 77% of students use AI at least a few times a month, compared with 46% of workers, and nearly half the general public would prefer to avoid AI.

stories.title: Hong Kong property upswing poised to hold despite interest rates risk: Moody’s
stories.summary: Moody's Ratings said Hong Kong's residential property recovery is unlikely to be derailed by potential interest rate increases linked to the Middle East conflict. Demand is supported by relocating professionals and rising rents, while the office and retail property sectors are also showing improvement.

stories.title: Romanians stabbed journalist in London at behest of Iran, UK court told
stories.summary: A UK court heard that Romanian nationals stabbed journalist Pouria Zeraati in London on behalf of Iran. Zeraati, who works for a Saudi-funded television outlet, was described by prosecutors as an obvious and identifiable target.

stories.title: India will be ‘relegated to history’ if it attempts misadventure against Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif warned that India would be "relegated to history" if it attempted military aggression against Pakistan, referencing last year's confrontation that began after the April 2024 Pahalgam attack.

stories.title: US to screen for Ebola at airports, one American in DR Congo infected
stories.summary: The United States announced enhanced Ebola screening at airports for travelers from outbreak-affected areas and temporarily suspended visa services. The measures follow the WHO's declaration of the DRC Ebola outbreak as an international health emergency, with one American infected.

stories.title: Angela Merkel criticizes Europe for 'not making sufficient use of diplomacy' in Russian-Ukrainian war
stories.summary: Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel criticized Europe for not making sufficient use of diplomacy in the Russia-Ukraine war. She urged greater diplomatic efforts alongside increased support for Ukraine.

stories.title: Three killed in shooting at San Diego mosque, two teenage gunmen found dead
stories.summary: Three men were fatally shot outside San Diego's largest mosque, and two teenage suspects, aged 17 and 19, were subsequently found dead from apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds. Police are investigating the incident as a potential hate crime.

stories.title: Australia news live: Liberal senator says ‘we cannot continue to blame migrants’ for economic issues in direct attack on Angus Taylor’s rhetoric
stories.summary: Australian Liberal senator publicly challenged opposition leader Angus Taylor's rhetoric linking migration to the housing shortage. Separately, eleven Australians aboard a humanitarian aid flotilla bound for Gaza were intercepted off the coast of Cyprus.

stories.title: Five people, including two suspects, killed in shooting at San Diego’s largest mosque
stories.summary: Three people were killed in a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, California, and two teenage suspects, aged 17 and 19, died of self-inflicted gunshot wounds. The FBI is investigating the attack as a hate crime and has set up a public tip line.

stories.title: Iranian transactions flow through Tron, BNB Chain amid Trump-family crypto ventures
stories.summary: Iranian institutions reportedly processed over $2.3 billion in transactions through the Tron and BNB Chain blockchains. The activity has drawn scrutiny over potential links to Trump-family-backed cryptocurrency ventures and possible conflicts of interest.

stories.title: India will be ‘relegated to history’ if it attempts future misadventure against Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif warned that India would be "relegated to history" if it attempted any future military action against Pakistan. He referenced last year's confrontation that began with the April 2025 Pahalgam attack and the subsequent military conflict, which ended with a ceasefire on May 10.

stories.title: Indian firm to pay $275m to settle US Iran sanctions probe
stories.summary: Adani Enterprises Limited, owned by Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, agreed to pay $275 million to settle a US Treasury Department investigation into 32 alleged violations of Iran sanctions. The violations involved purchases of liquefied petroleum gas.

stories.title: Trump says he called off new Iran attack at request of Gulf states
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced he called off a planned military strike against Iran on Tuesday, stating that Gulf Arab allies urged restraint as diplomatic negotiations continue.

stories.title: Brazil call up Neymar to World Cup 2026 squad
stories.summary: Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has called up forward Neymar, the country's all-time leading scorer, to the national squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. It marks Ancelotti's first selection of the veteran player.

stories.title: Ukraine declares its first homegrown guided aerial bomb combat-ready
stories.summary: Ukraine announced that its first domestically developed guided aerial bomb has reached combat-ready status. The 250-kilogram munition is intended to counter Russia's daily glide-bomb strikes and reduce Kyiv's reliance on Western precision weapons for mid-range targets.

stories.title: Analyst says Trump giving false impression of control in Iran talks
stories.summary: Foreign policy analyst Trita Parsi of the Quincy Institute challenged President Trump's portrayal of control over the Iran crisis. Parsi argued that Trump's messaging aims to shape public perceptions rather than reflect the actual state of negotiations.

stories.title: Russian attack damages Ukrposhta branch in Dnipro
stories.summary: A Russian military attack during the night of May 18 struck a Ukrposhta postal branch at 28 Budivelnykiv Street in Dnipro, Ukraine, causing significant damage to the building.

stories.title: Trump claims Gulf leaders requested he hold off on striking Iran, originally 'planned' for Tuesday
stories.summary: President Trump claimed that the leaders of the UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia called him to request he delay strikes on Iran that he said were originally planned for Tuesday.

stories.title: A redistricting re-do? What to know about Alabama’s primary elections
stories.summary: Alabama voters may face a return to the polls in August as the state attempts to implement a redistricting plan that was previously blocked. The primary elections hinge on the outcome of that effort.

stories.title: Pakistan deployed 8,000 troops, a Chinese air defence system and warplanes to Saudi Arabia: Report
stories.summary: Pakistan reportedly deployed 8,000 troops, Chinese-made air defense systems, and warplanes to Saudi Arabia, according to a media report. The deployment highlights Saudi Arabia's defense pact with Pakistan amid the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: 'FedEx says your parcel has drugs': The scam that trapped an Indian comedian
stories.summary: Indian comedian Ankita Shrivastav fell victim to a cybercrime scam involving fake FedEx parcel notifications claiming drugs were found. She is among millions of Indians targeted by such scams annually.

stories.title: Zelensky approves new special operations against Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced he had approved new special operations targeting Russia, without disclosing specific details about the operations.

stories.title: Is the US trying to force regime change in Cuba?
stories.summary: The United States is maintaining its economic blockade of Cuba, which has triggered a fuel crisis on the island. Washington has offered aid but reportedly conditioned it on influencing Cuba's political future.

stories.title: Cuba warns of 'bloodbath' if US attacks; Washington adds sanctions
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned Monday of a "bloodbath" if the U.S. attacks the island, while the U.S. Treasury sanctioned Cuba's main intelligence agency and top leaders. Reports indicate Havana has obtained over 300 military drones from Russia and Iran amid escalating tensions between the two countries.

stories.title: Five dead, including two suspects, after shooting at San Diego mosque
stories.summary: Two teenage gunmen killed three men outside the Islamic Center of San Diego on Monday, including a security guard, before being found dead from apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds. Police in California are investigating the shooting.

stories.title: US senator blames Trump’s Iran war for surge in fuel prices
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Chris Murphy, a Democrat from Connecticut, blamed the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran for surging fuel prices domestically. He said petrol in his state is approaching $5 per gallon and diesel nearly $6, calling the conflict a 'war of choice.'

stories.title: Lebanon president says he will do the ‘impossible’ to stop war with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese President stated he would do the "impossible" to prevent further war with Israel. A ceasefire and direct negotiations between the two countries had previously failed to end the fighting.

stories.title: US: At least one dead in attack at San Diego mosque
stories.summary: At least one person was killed in a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, California, on 18 May 2026. The attack occurred amid a reported spike in Islamophobic incidents in the United States following the war on Iran.

stories.title: Milei guts China currency lifeline after Trump ultimatum on financial ties: reports
stories.summary: Argentina is moving to repay and wind down its currency swap arrangement with China's central bank by mid-2026, reportedly under pressure from the Trump administration. The swap had served as a financial lifeline for Argentina during years of economic turmoil.

stories.title: Jewish man gang-beaten in antisemitic hate crime in Golders Green
stories.summary: A Jewish man in his 20s was gang-beaten in an antisemitic hate crime in Golders Green, London, sustaining injuries to his face and back that required hospital treatment.

stories.title: Iran submits new proposal, says U.S. open to sanctions relief
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new proposal in nuclear negotiations and stated the U.S. is open to sanctions relief. On May 17, Tehran unveiled the Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a new body requiring all ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz to obtain confirmation messages regarding rules and regulations.

stories.title: War and sanctions have cut Russia’s nonstop flight network to about 30 countries this summer — fewer than during the Iron Curtain era
stories.summary: Russia's nonstop flight network has shrunk to roughly 31–32 countries this summer due to war and sanctions, about 25% fewer than winter schedules and a third of what the Soviet Union offered during the Iron Curtain era, according to ATOR.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia loses 10% of its oil refining capacity, Putin leads his country toward bankruptcy
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Russia lost 10% of its oil refining capacity in the first five months of the year, with the country's budget deficit far exceeding planned levels and multiple regions approaching bankruptcy.

stories.title: Iran announces new body to manage Strait of Hormuz as peace talks stall
stories.summary: Iran announced the creation of a new authority to oversee maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz amid stalled peace talks with the United States and Israel. Tehran said the body will manage tolls and restrictions that are reshaping global shipping routes.

stories.title: US extends Russian-oil waiver for second time — one Bessent had told allies he wouldn’t make
stories.summary: The United States extended its waiver allowing vulnerable countries to purchase Russian oil for an additional 30 days. The extension contradicts earlier indications from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that the waiver would not be renewed.

stories.title: ‘Dodgy’ shops handling criminal cash targeted by new specialist unit
stories.summary: The UK government announced a new £20 million National Crime Agency unit targeting retail shops suspected of laundering an estimated £1 billion annually in criminal cash. Outlets such as vape stores, barbers, mini-marts, and sweet shops are the primary targets.

stories.title: How China is becoming the gravitational centre of global diplomacy
stories.summary: As Russian President Vladimir Putin prepares to visit Beijing shortly after US President Trump's departure, analysts suggest China is positioning itself as a central hub of global diplomacy rather than merely balancing between Washington and Moscow.

stories.title: DRC Ebola outbreak 'way bigger that what we see now', virologist says
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo a public health emergency of international concern. Virologist Muhammad Munir of Lancaster University warned the outbreak's true scale is far larger than currently reported, with cases also confirmed in Uganda.

stories.title: Russian Orthodox priests hold procession to ward off Ukrainian drones, calling the attacks an ‘affliction’
stories.summary: Russian Orthodox priests in Perm held a prayer procession through the city carrying the "Permskaya" icon of the Mother of God, seeking divine protection against Ukrainian drone attacks, which they called an "affliction."

stories.title: US refueling aircraft to stay at Ben-Gurion Airport until the end of 2027 - report
stories.summary: US aerial refueling aircraft and military personnel will remain stationed at and around Israel's Ben-Gurion Airport until the end of 2027, reportedly creating significant logistical challenges for the airport.

stories.title: Trump says Gulf leaders urged delay to planned US strike on Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed urged Washington to delay a planned military strike on Iran. Trump said the Gulf leaders cited active diplomatic negotiations as the reason for their request.

stories.title: Budanov on clearing operation in Stepnohirsk: Russians have no chance of threatening Zaporizhzhia
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine's presidential office, said special forces from military intelligence and other defense units have prevented Russian forces from making any gains in Stepnohirsk for over a year, eliminating threats to Zaporizhzhia.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1546: For first time, Russians fear Ukrainian strikes more than front
stories.summary: On day 1,546 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine's intelligence agency claimed to possess Russia's secret internal war-damage assessment, reportedly hidden from the Russian public. Reports indicate that for the first time, Russians fear Ukrainian strikes more than frontline combat.

stories.title: Clashes as Morales-allied protesters march on Bolivian capital
stories.summary: Protesters allied with former Bolivian President Evo Morales clashed with security forces while marching toward the capital. The demonstrations are fueled by a deepening economic crisis and growing discontent with President Paz's government.

stories.title: Nationwide protests erupt in Kenya over soaring fuel prices
stories.summary: Deadly protests erupted across Kenya over soaring fuel prices, leaving at least four people dead and hundreds arrested. Demonstrators blamed the government's handling of economic fallout linked to Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Protest in Greece after Israeli forces storm Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Demonstrators gathered outside Greece's foreign ministry in Athens to protest after Israeli forces stormed a humanitarian aid flotilla bound for Gaza.

stories.title: Trump pauses possible Iran strike after Gulf intervention
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced he is delaying a planned military strike on Iran following intervention related to the Gulf region.

stories.title: Flawed tests and funerals allowed Ebola to spread undetected in Congo
stories.summary: Delayed detection allowed a major Ebola outbreak to spread undetected in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, including into rebel-held territory and across the border into Uganda. Congolese officials cited flawed diagnostic tests at a local laboratory and local funeral practices as key factors that helped the virus spread before alarms were raised.

stories.title: Iraq launches desert sweep after reports of secret Israeli bases
stories.summary: Iraqi security forces launched large-scale sweep operations in the country's western desert after reports emerged of secret Israeli bases operating in the area.

stories.title: Selling children to survive: Afghan fathers forced to make impossible choices
stories.summary: In Afghanistan, where three out of four people cannot meet basic needs, some fathers have been forced to sell their children as a desperate measure for survival amid the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Middle East war threatens millions of jobs, says UN labour agency
stories.summary: A United Nations labour agency report warned that the ongoing Middle East war threatens millions of jobs globally. The Middle East and the Asia-Pacific region are expected to be the hardest hit by the economic fallout.

stories.title: Watch: Clock is ticking for Iran, says Trump | Above the Fold | 18.05.2026
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a new warning to Iran, raising fears of potential additional U.S. strikes and escalating tensions in West Asia. The developments come amid an ongoing standoff between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Indian court declares another historical mosque a temple
stories.summary: An Indian High Court ruled that the medieval Kamal Maula mosque is originally a Hindu temple dedicated to a goddess. The decision adds to a series of similar court rulings reclassifying historical mosques as temples in India.

stories.title: Croatian president rejects new Israeli ambassador
stories.summary: Croatian President Zoran Milanovic rejected Israel's new ambassador, stating that Israel violated an unwritten diplomatic rule by publicly announcing the appointment before receiving Croatia's approval.

stories.title: Elon Musk loses lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman
stories.summary: A nine-member federal jury in California ruled unanimously against Elon Musk in his $160 billion lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman. The jury deliberated for less than two hours and found that Musk had filed the case beyond the statute of limitations.

stories.title: US drops fraud charges after billionaire Adani pledges $10bn investment
stories.summary: The United States dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani after he pledged a $10 billion investment. Adani had been accused of bribing Indian officials and misleading US investors in connection with a solar power project.

stories.title: Will Cuba be forced to accept the US president’s demands?
stories.summary: Cuba is struggling to maintain its electricity supply as Washington intensifies economic pressure and military threats against the island nation.

stories.title: Ukrainian soldier says supplier swapped ordered drone batteries for cheaper cells that risk thermal runaway at front
stories.summary: A Ukrainian soldier reported that a supplier replaced ordered drone batteries with cheaper cells prone to thermal runaway, a dangerous overheating condition. He discovered the substitution only after cutting open the battery casing himself at the front line.

stories.title: Trump says Gulf leaders asked him to 'hold off' on resuming Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump announced the U.S. would not resume a 'full, large scale assault' on Iran that had been scheduled for Tuesday. He said the decision followed direct appeals from Gulf state leaders who expressed confidence a deal could be reached.

stories.title: Belarus will face preemptive strikes if it prepares attack on Ukraine – military expert
stories.summary: Ukrainian military expert Ivan Tymochko warned that if Belarus shows signs of preparing military aggression against Ukraine, it would face preemptive strikes without delay.

stories.title: Cuba warns of ‘bloodbath’ if US attacks; Washington adds sanctions
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned of a 'bloodbath' if the United States attacks Cuba, asserting the country's right to self-defense. Simultaneously, the U.S. Treasury imposed new sanctions on Cuba's main intelligence agency and top leaders amid reports Havana acquired over 300 military drones from Russia and Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine hit Moscow with its biggest drone attack since the start of the war. Russian national TV networks all but ignored it.
stories.summary: Ukraine launched its largest drone attack on the Moscow area since the start of the war overnight on May 17, killing three people and wounding 16. Russia's national television networks largely ignored the strike, days after Moscow authorities banned publishing photos and videos of drone strike aftermath.

stories.title: EU’s Ursula von der Leyen wants to seal investment agreement with India, calls it ‘missing puzzle’
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen expressed her desire to finalize an investment agreement with India, calling it a "missing puzzle" in EU-India relations. Negotiations had stalled due to differences over dispute resolution mechanisms.

stories.title: G-7 Finance Ministers Discuss Economic Fallout of Iran War
stories.summary: G-7 finance ministers convened to discuss the economic consequences of the Iran war. Rising oil prices and increasing bond market volatility have intensified concerns about a potential global recession.

stories.title: Iranian vice president says 70 percent oppose internet curbs amid blackout
stories.summary: Iranian Vice President Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah acknowledged that 70 percent of Iranians oppose internet restrictions, citing a survey by the Presidential Center. The remarks came amid a prolonged internet blackout across Iran.

stories.title: Russian drone strike hits enterprise in Chernihiv
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike hit an enterprise in the city of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine. Details on casualties and the extent of damage to the facility were not immediately available.

stories.title: Hundreds join interfaith ‘human rights and peace’ march in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Hundreds of people participated in an interfaith march in Jerusalem promoting human rights and peace. Marchers carried signs reading 'Justice,' 'Peace,' and 'Soul' in Hebrew, Arabic, and English, offering a counter-narrative to nationalist Flag Marches held on Jerusalem Day.

stories.title: Nearly of 80% of Gazans open to emigrating from Strip, COGAT survey finds
stories.summary: A survey conducted by Israel's COGAT found that nearly 80% of Gazan respondents sought information about emigrating from the Strip. The findings, which referenced relocation through the Rafah and Kerem Shalom crossings, were presented to senior Israeli officials.

stories.title: Massie race breaks spending record as pro-Israel groups target Trump critic
stories.summary: Pro-Israel groups and donors have poured record-breaking spending into Kentucky's Republican primary, aiming to unseat U.S. Congressman Thomas Massie, a vocal critic of former President Trump. The race has become the most expensive in its history.

stories.title: Federal court rejects Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI, saying he filed his lawsuit too late
stories.summary: A federal jury in Los Angeles ruled Monday that Elon Musk waited too long to sue OpenAI and its co-founders, ending a three-week trial. Musk had alleged that OpenAI's shift toward a for-profit model violated its original nonprofit mission. The verdict was a decisive win for the ChatGPT maker.

stories.title: Hormuz tanker traffic edges higher after wartime low
stories.summary: Shipping data showed 55 commodities vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz between May 11 and 17, marking a sharp increase from the previous week's wartime low in tanker traffic.

stories.title: Iran arrests over 4,000 on charges related to war: rights group
stories.summary: Iranian authorities arrested over 4,000 people on charges related to the US-Israeli war against Iran, according to the Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA), describing the detentions as a mass crackdown.

stories.title: EU extends sanctions on former Assad regime for one year
stories.summary: The European Union renewed sanctions on entities and individuals linked to Syria's former Assad regime for one year, while removing seven government agencies from its blacklist.

stories.title: Iran court to hear case against director Panahi after return
stories.summary: An Iranian court is set to hear a case this week against award-winning film director Jafar Panahi, who returned to Iran during the war in March.

stories.title: Lebanon president will 'do the impossible' to end Israel war
stories.summary: Lebanon's president pledged to do everything possible to end the war with Israel. Lebanese health authorities reported over 3,000 people killed in Israeli strikes since March 2, when Hezbollah entered the Iran conflict.

stories.title: New York Times sues Pentagon again over ‘utterly unreasonable’ press restrictions
stories.summary: The New York Times filed a second lawsuit against the Pentagon, challenging a policy requiring journalists to have official escorts on Pentagon grounds as unconstitutional. The Trump administration introduced sweeping press access restrictions at the Department of Defense in September.

stories.title: Somaliland marks independence day with renewed push for international recognition
stories.summary: Somaliland marked its independence day while renewing its push for international recognition. Despite Israel's earlier recognition, no other country has followed, leaving Somaliland's broader diplomatic quest unresolved.

stories.title: Irish president says sister 'kidnapped' by Israel on Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Irish President Catherine Connolly condemned Israel's seizure of the Gaza-bound Global Sumud aid flotilla, stating her sister, Dr. Margaret Connolly, was among six Irish citizens taken. The president expressed concern for all those detained aboard the vessel.

stories.title: Irish president says sister abducted by Israel on Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Irish President Catherine Connolly condemned Israel's seizure of the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla, stating that her sister, Dr. Margaret Connolly, was among six Irish citizens taken by Israeli forces.

stories.title: Hamas said to appoint Mohammed Odeh to replace group’s slain leader in Gaza
stories.summary: Hamas reportedly appointed Mohammed Odeh to replace the group's slain leader in Gaza. Odeh previously served as head of military intelligence in the al-Qassam Brigades and was reportedly involved in identifying vulnerabilities in border defenses ahead of the October 7, 2023, attack.

stories.title: Hamas names former intelligence head Mohammed Ouda as new leader of military wing - report
stories.summary: Hamas has reportedly named Mohammed Ouda, a former intelligence head, as the new leader of its military wing. Ouda had previously been offered the role after the assassination of Mohammed Sinwar in May 2025 but initially turned it down.

stories.title: Iran Is Winning the Vibe War
stories.summary: Analysts argue that Iran is effectively leveraging information operations in what some call a "vibe war," exploiting AI-generated content and disinformation. Experts suggest that traditional frameworks for countering disinformation may be insufficient in the era of AI-generated media.

stories.title: Russian soldiers who want out of the war are deserting and turning themselves in, hoping for prison time. Some are hiring lawyers to make it happen.
stories.summary: Growing numbers of Russian soldiers unwilling to fight in Ukraine are deserting and turning themselves in to face prosecution and imprisonment rather than return to the front lines. According to independent outlet Mediazona, some soldiers are hiring lawyers to persuade investigators to open criminal cases against them.

stories.title: British volunteers rescue 30 animals from front-line Kramatorsk
stories.summary: A team led by ex-Royal Marine Pen Farthing's charity Nowzad drove approximately 13,000 kilometers to rescue 30 cats and dogs from front-line Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine. The Donbas city faces daily Russian strikes.

stories.title: Ukraine seizing battlefield initiative – Bratchuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesman Bratchuk stated that Ukrainian forces are gradually seizing the battlefield initiative through flexible defense tactics and strikes on Russian rear positions. He said Russia has failed to achieve its spring offensive objectives and is suffering heavy losses.

stories.title: Trump delays ‘scheduled attack’ on Iran, crediting ‘serious negotiations’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced he has delayed a planned military strike on Iran, citing ongoing serious negotiations. Gulf states reportedly pressed Trump to avoid escalation in the broader U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran, which had already prompted regional attacks.

stories.title: Four reported killed, 30 injured, in Kenyan fuel price protests
stories.summary: At least four people were reported killed and 30 injured during nationwide protests in Kenya triggered by fuel price hikes. The demonstrations disrupted multiple cities across the country.

stories.title: 2 suspects in a shooting at a San Diego Islamic centre are dead, police say
stories.summary: Both suspects in a shooting at the Islamic Centre of San Diego are dead, according to police sources. Authorities believe multiple people were shot at the mosque, located about 14 kilometers north of downtown San Diego, which is the largest in San Diego County.

stories.title: Heavy sandstorm hits Iraq as hospitals battle respiratory issues
stories.summary: A severe sandstorm swept across Iraq, affecting cities including Baghdad and Najaf. Hospitals reported a surge in patients with respiratory problems linked to the dust storm.

stories.title: Jewish man in hospital after attack by group of men in Golders Green
stories.summary: A Jewish man in his 20s was hospitalized with injuries to his face and body after being attacked by a group of men in Golders Green, north London. Police were called early Monday after the victim was assaulted outside a property on the Grove.

stories.title: Activists raise alarm over 'flood' of military supplies from India to Israel
stories.summary: Activists reported that six shipments of suspected military-grade steel from India were being transported to Israel aboard the Swiss vessel MSC Valeria, raising concerns about a flow of military supplies via India's Mundra port.

stories.title: Noam Bettan meets with President Isaac Herzog after winning second place at Eurovision
stories.summary: Israeli Eurovision contestant Noam Bettan met with President Isaac Herzog after securing second place at the competition. Bettan's result came despite demonstrations, boos, and pro-Palestinian protests directed at Israel's participation.

stories.title: Damage control over prevention: International health system 'closing gaps instead pushing forward'
stories.summary: Professor Anne Moore of University College Cork warned that existing Ebola vaccines and tests may not be effective against the current Bundibugyo strain outbreak. She said shrinking international health funding is undermining the global response, leaving systems focused on plugging gaps rather than deploying full countermeasures.

stories.title: One man injured in shelling of Nikopol district as injury toll in Dnipro rises
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted 40 drone and artillery strikes across four districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring one man in the Nikopol district. The attacks targeted civilian areas in the region.

stories.title: Israeli forces reportedly detain Saad Edhi, others after intercepting Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted at least 10 boats from the Global Sumud Flotilla in the eastern Mediterranean and reportedly detained Saad Edhi, son of Pakistani social worker Faisal Edhi, along with other flotilla members. Contact was lost with a total of 23 vessels. Israel's foreign ministry stated it would not allow any breach of its naval blockade on Gaza.

stories.title: Jewish communities worldwide mark Liberation and Rescue Day amid rising antisemitism
stories.summary: Jewish communities around the world marked Liberation and Rescue Day under the theme "From generation to generation in the face of antisemitism." Holocaust survivors, community leaders, and diplomats attended ceremonies amid concerns over rising global antisemitism.

stories.title: ‘Going to change everything’: Special Forces joins Army’s next-gen C2 prototype experiments
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's 10th Special Forces Group has joined next-generation command-and-control prototype experiments alongside the 4th Infantry Division. The collaboration included participation in the recent Ivy Mass exercise, where units tested emerging C2 technologies designed to modernize battlefield decision-making.

stories.title: Lapid warns Likud MKs backing haredi draft bill from Netanyahu pressure will ‘not fall under radar'
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid warned Likud coalition members against supporting a Haredi draft exemption bill under pressure from Prime Minister Netanyahu. Lapid said Netanyahu's office has been conducting a massive campaign to secure coalition support for the legislation.

stories.title: Belgian diplomat linked to Lumumba case dies before landmark trial
stories.summary: A Belgian diplomat linked to the 1961 assassination case of Congolese independence leader Patrice Lumumba died before a landmark trial could take place. The pursuit of accountability continues to resonate in both Belgium and the Democratic Republic of Congo more than six decades later.

stories.title: U.S. has shown flexibility on Iran maintaining limited nuclear activities, source says
stories.summary: A source indicated the United States has shown flexibility regarding Iran maintaining limited nuclear activities during ongoing negotiations. However, on the issue of Iran's frozen assets, Washington has only agreed to release one quarter under a phased timetable.

stories.title: Ukraine Has a New War Strategy—and It’s Working
stories.summary: Over the past year, Ukraine has shifted its war strategy to strike targets directly inside Russian territory. Kyiv's forces have sustained cross-border operations and long-range attacks on Russian soil, marking a significant escalation in its approach to the conflict.

stories.title: Trump says he has called off Tuesday’s planned Iran strike at request of Gulf allies
stories.summary: President Trump announced he called off a military strike on Iran that had been planned for Tuesday, citing 'serious negotiations' underway. He said the decision came at the request of Gulf allies but instructed the U.S. military to remain ready for a large-scale assault if no deal is reached.

stories.title: Gunmen kill 3 people at San Diego Islamic centre in suspected hate crime
stories.summary: Two gunmen opened fire at an Islamic center in San Diego, killing three people in what police are investigating as a hate crime. San Diego's police chief confirmed both shooters are dead.

stories.title: Protests erupt over Kenya fuel price hikes, strike strands commuters
stories.summary: Protests erupted in several Kenyan towns over fuel price hikes linked to the Iran war, accompanied by a nationwide public transport strike. The strike stranded commuters in Nairobi and other cities, forcing many people to walk to work.

stories.title: Israel built two secret military bases in Iraq to aid Iran war, New York Times reports
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Israel constructed two secret military bases in Iraq's western desert to support its strikes on Iran, with U.S. knowledge. An Iraqi official and lawmaker cited by the report suggested the bases' presence may be linked to the death of a Bedouin shepherd who first revealed their existence.

stories.title: Gofman likely to helm Mossad after affidavit appears to undercut claims against him
stories.summary: Israeli official Gofman is now considered likely to lead the Mossad after an affidavit from an intelligence officer appeared to undermine allegations against him. The statement indicated the prime minister's military secretary was never asked about a controversial influence operation involving a teenager.

stories.title: Ukraine, Poland should create export corridor from Europe to Middle East – expert
stories.summary: An expert has proposed that Ukraine and Poland jointly develop a major export corridor linking Europe to the Middle East. The initiative would leverage the two countries' geographic positions to boost trade connectivity.

stories.title: Even in Exile, Russia’s Political Opposition Struggles to Rise Above Its Divisions
stories.summary: Russia's exiled political opposition continues to struggle with internal divisions and perceptions of ineffectiveness. However, some activists still operating inside Russia say the opposition abroad continues to play an important role.

stories.title: PM Modi receives Norway’s highest civilian honour
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi received the Grand Cross of the Royal Norwegian Order of Merit, Norway's highest civilian honor. The award recognizes exceptional service in advancing Norway's interests and international relations.

stories.title: First Somaliland ambassador to Israel presents his credentials
stories.summary: Somaliland's first ambassador to any foreign country presented his credentials to Israeli President Isaac Herzog. The appointment marks a diplomatic milestone for the self-declared republic, which lacks broad international recognition.

stories.title: English Premier League clubs accused of sportswashing Israel's atrocities
stories.summary: Campaign group War on Want accused four English Premier League clubs—Arsenal, Brighton, Burnley, and Everton—of mistreating pro-Palestinian staff and supporters in ways that may breach freedom of expression or constitute discrimination.

stories.title: Health workers race to respond to Congo's fast-spreading Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Medical personnel rushed to respond to a new Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, centered near Bunia. Health experts expressed alarm over its late detection and rapid spread.

stories.title: Protests over fuel price hikes turn deadly in Kenya
stories.summary: Several people were killed in Kenya as transport workers protesting fuel price hikes blocked roads, leading to violent clashes across the country.

stories.title: Gunmen kill 10 in attack on farming settlements in Nigeria's northwest, residents say
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a rural community in Katsina State in northwestern Nigeria on Sunday, killing at least 10 people including women and children. The attackers also burned homes and looted livestock.

stories.title: Aaron Rai’s US PGA win inspires golf’s next generation in Wolverhampton
stories.summary: Aaron Rai, a 31-year-old from Wolverhampton, became the first Englishman since 1919 to win the US PGA Championship on Sunday. His victory was celebrated at the 3 Hammers golf complex, where he trained as a youth, inspiring young players in the area.

stories.title: DRC faces a severe Ebola outbreak caused by a highly lethal variant [Africanews Today]
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is facing a severe Ebola outbreak caused by a highly lethal variant for which no specific cure or vaccine currently exists. Health authorities are working to contain the spread.

stories.title: Mushfiqur ton leaves Pakistan needing record run chase to beat Bangladesh
stories.summary: Bangladesh set Pakistan a target of 427 runs to win the second Test after posting 390 all out in their second innings. Veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahim scored 137, his 14th Test century, setting a new Bangladesh record.

stories.title: Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi returns home after hospital release
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi has been released from hospital and returned home, where she will remain under close medical observation, according to her foundation.

stories.title: PSX plunges by nearly 3,800 points as investors remain cautious amid geopolitical tensions
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index fell 3,791 points, or 2.29 percent, to close at 161,805, marking a seventh consecutive session of losses. Investor sentiment remained depressed amid a lack of progress in U.S.-Iran negotiations and broader geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Ukraine to test new version of Ruta missile with range of up to 2,000 kilometers
stories.summary: Dutch defense company Destinus and Germany's Rheinmetall are jointly developing the RUTA Block 3 long-range missile, capable of striking targets up to 2,000 kilometers away. The missile is scheduled for testing in Ukraine in 2027.

stories.title: Musk loses landmark lawsuit against OpenAI after jury finds he filed his claim too late
stories.summary: A federal jury ruled against Elon Musk in his lawsuit against OpenAI, finding that he had filed his claim too late. The trial featured prominent Silicon Valley figures and centered on competing visions for artificial intelligence development.

stories.title: ‘Are you Jewish?’ Israeli attacked by group of men in London after speaking Hebrew
stories.summary: An Israeli man named Shalev Ben Yakar was attacked by a group of Arabic-speaking men in London after being heard speaking Hebrew. He was beaten until near unconsciousness, and police are searching for the assailants.

stories.title: PM Modi calls for peaceful resolution of conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Modi called for peaceful resolution of conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine during a joint statement with Norwegian officials. He emphasized that India and Norway share a belief in rules-based order, dialogue, and diplomacy over military conflict.

stories.title: US issues 30-day sanction waiver for Russian oil
stories.summary: The US Treasury Department issued a 30-day general licence allowing the release of Russian oil cargoes blocked during recent disruptions, aiming to ease global energy supply pressures linked to the US conflict with Iran and the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: Kremlin spokesman complains of ‘unrelenting drone strikes by Ukraine’s forces against civilian targets,’ makes no mention of the attack on Moscow
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged reporters to focus on what he called unrelenting Ukrainian drone strikes against Russian civilian targets but made no mention of the May 17 attack on Moscow. That strike was the largest Ukrainian drone attack on the Moscow region since the war began.

stories.title: Netanyahu’s leaks undermined Israel’s ties with Arab leaders - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Prime Minister Netanyahu's repeated publicizing of private diplomatic meetings has undermined Israel's relationships with Arab leaders. The leaks are reportedly making secret diplomacy increasingly difficult to conduct.

stories.title: Congo announces three Ebola treatment centres in Ituri region amid outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo announced the establishment of three Ebola treatment centres in the Ituri region to address an outbreak first confirmed on May 15, 2026. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare Ebola variant for which no approved therapeutics or vaccines exist.

stories.title: Ex-Everton director loses Russian sanctions challenge
stories.summary: Sarvar Ismailov, a former Everton football club director, lost a legal challenge against Russian-related sanctions imposed on him in 2022. The sanctions were linked to his billionaire uncle's ties to President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Iranian Nobel laureate discharged from hospital and sent home, family say
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was discharged from a cardiac care unit and sent home after being transferred from prison to hospital following a suspected heart attack weeks earlier, her family's foundation reported.

stories.title: Iran Nobel winner Mohammadi discharged from hospital
stories.summary: Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi was discharged from hospital following her release on bail from Iranian custody.

stories.title: Poland ready for joint defense industry ventures with Ukraine
stories.summary: Poland has signaled its readiness to establish joint defense industry ventures with Ukraine, including production of dual-use goods. The announcement underscores deepening military-industrial cooperation between Warsaw and Kyiv.

stories.title: ICE officer charged over shooting of Venezuelan man in Minnesota
stories.summary: A Minnesota prosecutor charged ICE officer Christian Castro with four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime in the January 14 shooting of Venezuelan man Julio César Sosa-Celis. The shooting occurred during the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, and a warrant was issued for Castro's arrest in Hennepin County.

stories.title: US says American contracted Ebola in Congo as CDC announces new travel screening measures
stories.summary: U.S. health officials confirmed that an American contracted Ebola while working in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The CDC announced proactive measures, including new travel screening, in response to the ongoing Ebola epidemic in the DRC and Uganda.

stories.title: Bessent grants a 30-day extension for Russian oil in tankers as Iran war squeezes supply
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a 30-day extension allowing countries to import Russian oil already in tankers at sea, continuing a policy reversal aimed at alleviating supply shortages caused by the Iran war.

stories.title: UAE standardises deadline for payments of private-sector salaries
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is standardizing private-sector salary payment deadlines under its Wage Protection System. Starting June 1, salaries must be paid on the first day of each month, with any later payments classified as delayed.

stories.title: No ‘tailor-made’ deal for UK if it wants to rejoin bloc, say former EU Brexit officials
stories.summary: Former EU Brexit negotiation officials said the United Kingdom would not be able to rejoin the bloc on the special terms it previously enjoyed. While Britain could expect a welcoming stance, any re-entry negotiations would involve hard-headed conditions with no tailor-made deal.

stories.title: UAE and Israel established fund for joint defence acquisition, sources say
stories.summary: The UAE and Israel have reportedly established a joint fund for defense acquisition, according to unnamed sources. The emerging defense partnership between the two countries puts the Gulf state at odds with some of its regional neighbors.

stories.title: Lebanon’s death toll tops 3,000 in fighting between Israel and Hezbollah
stories.summary: Lebanon's cumulative death toll from fighting between Israel and Hezbollah surpassed 3,000, with casualties including 292 women and 211 children. Israel also killed a senior Islamic Jihad commander during the operations.

stories.title: Trump rejects concessions, says 'I’m not open to anything'
stories.summary: US President Trump struck a harder line on Iran, telling The New York Post he is not open to concessions and warning that developments are imminent. The remarks followed earlier indications that Washington might consider addressing Iran's nuclear program through negotiations.

stories.title: US soldiers learn to identify drones by sound
stories.summary: U.S. Army personnel are being trained to identify different types of drones by their sound signatures. While audio drone identification has not yet been formally added to the Army's training curriculum, field experience listening for drone sounds is being used as an introduction to differentiating among various drone types.

stories.title: ‘Propaganda uses me now in both directions,’ says Russian archaeologist freed in prisoner exchange
stories.summary: Alexander Butyagin, a St. Petersburg archaeologist and Hermitage Museum researcher, was arrested in Warsaw in late 2025 at Ukraine's request over alleged illegal excavations in Crimea. He was returned to Russia in an April prisoner exchange and has said he plans to return to Crimea.

stories.title: Modena car-ramming suspect not linked to terror groups, Italian minister says
stories.summary: Italian Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi said a man who drove a car into a crowd in Modena on Saturday, injuring eight people including four seriously, appears to have no links to any terrorist groups.

stories.title: Pakistan deploys jet squadron, thousands of troops to Saudi Arabia amid escalating Iran war tensions
stories.summary: Pakistan reportedly deployed a fighter jet squadron and thousands of troops to Saudi Arabia under an existing defense agreement. The deployment comes as regional tensions involving Iran continue to escalate.

stories.title: Andy Burnham vows to ‘change Labour’ in direct challenge to Keir Starmer
stories.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham announced he would seek to "change Labour" as the expected candidate in the upcoming Makerfield byelection. Burnham directly challenged Prime Minister Keir Starmer, saying the party needed to regain public trust and that he would campaign on national issues where Labour was failing.

stories.title: ‘It is heartbreaking’: panic in eastern DRC over return of Ebola
stories.summary: Residents of Ituri province in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo are experiencing widespread panic over a resurgence of Ebola, particularly in the mining town of Mongbwalu. The outbreak involves the Bundibudyo strain, for which no vaccine is currently available. The WHO has confirmed the return of the disease six years after the last outbreak in the region.

stories.title: Bolivia: Ten thousand Evo Morales supporters descend on La Paz as government warns of armed groups
stories.summary: Approximately ten thousand supporters of former Bolivian president Evo Morales marched into La Paz after a six-day trek from the highlands, demanding President Rodrigo Paz's resignation. The Bolivian government accused the march of harboring armed groups and characterized the mobilization as an attempt by Morales to destabilize the country.

stories.title: Kremlin dismisses Zelenskiy warning on Russian threat to NATO from Belarus
stories.summary: The Kremlin dismissed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's warning that Russia was considering an attack on a NATO country from Belarus, saying the assertion did not deserve a response.

stories.title: Croatian president not approving Israel’s proposed ambassador due to ‘policies of Israeli gov’t’
stories.summary: Croatian President Zoran Milanovic has refused for seven months to approve Israel's proposed ambassador to Croatia. An official statement cited disagreement with the policies of the Israeli government as the reason for blocking the appointment.

stories.title: A 14-year-old girl vanished in Russia after a drone strike burned her family’s home to the ground. Her body was never found.
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the city of Tuapse on April 16 in the first of a series of large-scale attacks targeting the Tuapse oil refinery and Rosneft marine terminal. The strikes reportedly caused an environmental disaster in the city. A 14-year-old girl went missing after a strike destroyed her family's home, and her body was never recovered.

stories.title: Somaliland marks first Independence Day following Israeli recognition
stories.summary: Somaliland celebrated its first Independence Day following recognition by Israel, with leaders emphasizing the territory's stability and strategic importance, though broader international recognition remains elusive.

stories.title: Israeli troops intercept vessels from a flotilla trying to breach the blockade of Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli troops intercepted vessels from the Global Sumud Flotilla that departed from the Turkish port of Marmaris attempting to breach the naval blockade of Gaza. The flotilla's stated aim was to break through to the besieged territory.

stories.title: State Border Guard Service denies reports of increased Russian sabotage activity in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Border Guard Service denied reports that Russian sabotage and reconnaissance groups have increased their activity in the Chernihiv region near the border. The agency pushed back against claims of heightened infiltration threats in the area.

stories.title: Iran officially announces new body to manage Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced the creation of the Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a new body to manage the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran has effectively closed the strategic waterway and seeks to charge ships for passage. The authority said it would provide real-time updates on Hormuz Strait operations.

stories.title: Russian drones hit two ships including Chinese cargo vessel off Ukraine’s Black Sea coast
stories.summary: Russian drones struck two ships off Ukraine's Black Sea coast, including a Chinese cargo vessel. A source reported the Chinese vessel did not sustain significant damage and there were no casualties.

stories.title: Russian attacks Odesa and Dnipro; Ukraine strikes Belgorod region
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Odesa and Dnipro in Ukraine, with drones hitting residential buildings, a school, and a kindergarten in Odesa. Ukraine conducted retaliatory strikes on Russia's Belgorod region.

stories.title: Revised Iranian proposal to end war shared with U.S., Pakistani source says
stories.summary: A revised Iranian proposal to end the war has been shared with the United States through Pakistani intermediaries. Tehran's demands include compensation for war damage, an end to the U.S. naval blockade, guarantees against further attacks, and resumption of Iranian oil sales.

stories.title: IHC seeks CDA response on appeals of One Constitution Avenue apartment sub-lessees
stories.summary: The Islamabad High Court issued notices to the Capital Development Authority regarding appeals filed by 20 apartment sub-lessees of the One Constitution Avenue project. The sub-lessees seek protection of their possession rights after the project's lease was cancelled.

stories.title: Cuba instead? Trump ups pressure on Havana as Iran campaign stalls
stories.summary: The United States is increasing pressure on Cuba, with CIA Director recently dispatched to Havana to offer aid, amid a stalling campaign against Iran. The move comes as Cuba faces severe hardships under the longstanding U.S. economic blockade.

stories.title: Civil rights veterans see history repeating after high court guts Voting Rights Act
stories.summary: Civil rights veterans in Selma, Alabama, including Bloody Sunday participant Betty Strong Boynton, expressed concern about history repeating after the U.S. Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act.

stories.title: Belarus dismisses concerns as it launches joint nuclear drills with Russia
stories.summary: Belarus and Russia launched joint nuclear drills, drawing strong condemnation from Ukraine and NATO allies as the two countries' forces trained in the use of nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Iran says it has conveyed its concerns over latest US peace proposal
stories.summary: Iran said it has communicated its concerns regarding the latest U.S. peace proposal, with Tehran seeking the release of frozen Iranian assets held abroad and the lifting of sanctions.

stories.title: Trump’s China trip highlights bipartisan shift in Washington’s approach to Beijing
stories.summary: President Trump's visit to China drew bipartisan concern from US lawmakers, with Democrats criticizing him for appearing too accommodating toward Beijing and Republicans warning that economic engagement should not weaken support for Taiwan.

stories.title: Iran’s top security council announces new body to manage Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced the creation of a new body to manage the Strait of Hormuz, reinforcing Tehran's control over the strategically vital waterway that has unsettled global markets.

stories.title: Russia must understand it cannot dictate terms to end war – Mathernova
stories.summary: EU Ambassador to Ukraine Katarina Mathernova stated that Russia must recognize it cannot dictate the terms for ending the war, which she described as increasingly reaching a deadlock for the Kremlin. She called for a negotiated conclusion acceptable to both sides.

stories.title: Political tensions escalate as Philippines Senate begins vice-presidential impeachment proceedings
stories.summary: The Philippine Senate formally opened impeachment proceedings against Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio amid intensifying political tensions. The House of Representatives impeached her the previous week on allegations including corruption and betrayal of public trust.

stories.title: As Burnham emerges as PM contender, where does he stand on Gaza?
stories.summary: The New Arab examined the political record of Andy Burnham, who has emerged as a UK prime ministerial contender, on the Gaza conflict. His past comments have been characterized as both pro-Palestine and pro-Israel at various points in his career.

stories.title: Kremlin says it has ‘serious expectations’ for Putin’s trip to China
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to visit China on May 19-20, with the Kremlin stating it has "serious expectations" for the trip.

stories.title: Five companies win DoD’s Drone Dominance small drone ‘Lethality Prize Challenge’
stories.summary: Five companies won the U.S. Department of Defense's Drone Dominance "Lethality Prize Challenge" for small drones. Bravo, one of the winning drone makers, said the selection provides a pathway to orders of thousands or tens of thousands of units and has elevated discussions with investors and partners.

stories.title: Belarus begins drills on combat use of nuclear weapons
stories.summary: Belarus's Defense Ministry announced military exercises for units responsible for the combat use and logistical support of nuclear weapons. The drills involve Russian tactical nuclear weapons deployed to Belarus.

stories.title: Ukraine has found key through Moscow’s air-defense rings, military analyst says
stories.summary: A military analyst reported that Ukraine has found a way to penetrate Moscow's multi-layered air defenses, which consist of three to four rings of roughly 100 positions, including Pantsir systems atop government buildings in the city center.

stories.title: Smotrich attacks AG, rule of law in dramatic Knesset committee hearing
