stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich clashed with the Attorney General during a Knesset committee hearing over a bill to split the AG's role, with the opposition accusing the coalition of dismantling checks on governmental power.

stories.title: UN calls on Israel to prevent Gaza ‘genocide’
stories.summary: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called on Israel to end what he described as its unlawful presence in Palestinian territory and to prevent genocide in Gaza.

stories.title: London stabbing of journalist ordered by third party acting for Iran, court told
stories.summary: A London court heard that the 2024 stabbing of journalist Pouria Zeraati was a planned attack ordered by a third party acting on behalf of the Iranian state. Zeraati, a British-Iranian journalist working for the Farsi-language dissident broadcaster Iran International, was stabbed in the leg outside his west London home.

stories.title: Makerfield byelection is about more than Andy Burnham
stories.summary: The upcoming Makerfield byelection is being described as an existential moment for the Labour party, extending beyond Andy Burnham's candidacy. Labour MPs canvassing in areas like Hindley Green and Winstanley said the contest could effectively function as a presidential-style vote determining the party's future direction.

stories.title: Taiwan would ‘welcome’ its President speaking to Trump, Taiwanese Minister says
stories.summary: Taiwan's Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi stated that Taipei would welcome a phone call between President Lai Ching-te and U.S. President Donald Trump. The government said it was seeking confirmation from Washington on whether Trump intended to speak with the Taiwanese leader.

stories.title: Kremlin creates dangerous nuclear precedent with Belarus deployments – Ukraine’s MFA
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the deployment of Russian tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus and joint nuclear drills between Moscow and Minsk. The ministry called the moves an unprecedented challenge to global security architecture requiring a firm international response.

stories.title: Halifax could disappear from UK high streets as Lloyds assesses branding strategy
stories.summary: Lloyds Banking Group is reviewing whether to discontinue Halifax as a standalone brand, potentially removing the 174-year-old lender from Britain's high streets. The review examines whether Lloyds should continue operating everyday banking under three separate brands—Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland—consolidated after the 2008 financial crisis.

stories.title: Sorry, Europe, Russia Isn’t Satanistic Enough for Eurovision
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov criticized the Eurovision Song Contest, claiming its current contestant criteria amount to "outright Satanism." The remarks reflect Moscow's continued cultural estrangement from European institutions.

stories.title: Sorry, Europe, Russia Isn’t Satanic Enough for Eurovision
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov criticized the Eurovision Song Contest, claiming its current selection criteria amount to "outright Satanism." The remarks reflect Moscow's ongoing cultural confrontation with Europe.

stories.title: Iran’s World Cup team arrives in Turkiye amid US visa uncertainty
stories.summary: Iran's national football team arrived in Türkiye for a pre-World Cup training camp amid uncertainty over whether the squad will obtain US visas for the tournament.

stories.title: London Stock Exchange rises 1.26% driven by oil and defense sectors
stories.summary: The London Stock Exchange's FTSE 100 index closed up 1.26% on Monday, gaining 128.38 points to reach 10,323.75, led by oil and defense sector stocks. The rally was linked to rising crude oil prices amid stalled U.S.-Iran negotiations. The secondary FTSE 250 index rose 0.07% to 22,611.70.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills child in southern Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike in eastern Khan Younis in southern Gaza killed a child who had been wounded in an earlier attack. Doctors at Nasser Hospital confirmed the child died from injuries sustained in the strike.

stories.title: Kurds hand over Kobani administration to Syrian government
stories.summary: Kurdish-led authorities have handed over administration of Kobani to the Syrian government in Damascus. The transfer is part of ongoing integration agreements between the Syrian Democratic Forces and the central government.

stories.title: Greens split over how hard to challenge Burnham in Makerfield byelection
stories.summary: The UK Green Party is internally divided over how aggressively to challenge Andy Burnham in the Makerfield byelection. Some members worry that a full campaign could split votes and help Reform UK win, while others, including newer left-wing activists, argue for an all-out effort.

stories.title: Iran officially announces new body to manage Strait of Hormuz: top security council
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced the formation of the Persian Gulf Strait Authority to manage the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has effectively closed and seeks to charge ships to transit. The new body's account was also promoted by the Revolutionary Guards' navy on social media.

stories.title: Russians stormed empty houses for the cameras 26 km from the town they claimed to take—and Russia’s top general announced its “liberation”
stories.summary: Russian forces claimed to have liberated a settlement approximately 26 kilometers from their stated objective, but Ukrainian officials say the area remains under Ukrainian control behind the front line. Russia's top general announced the supposed liberation after troops were filmed storming empty houses.

stories.title: Escaped tiger shot dead by German police
stories.summary: German police shot and killed a tiger that had escaped from a privately run enclosure after the animal attacked one of its keepers.

stories.title: 2,000-km strike missile, designed in Netherlands, tested in Ukraine, built in Germany: Rheinmetall and Destinus accelerate RUTA Block 3
stories.summary: Rheinmetall and Destinus are accelerating development of the RUTA Block 3, a 2,000-kilometer strike missile designed in the Netherlands, tested in Ukraine, and built in Germany. The weapon is intended for mass production to address Europe's shortage of indigenous deep-strike missile capability.

stories.title: ‘Disposable’ operatives for hire are a new menace for western countries
stories.summary: A 32-year-old Iraqi man, Mohammed Saad Baqer al-Saadi, was charged in a New York court with planning attacks on Jewish community sites in the United States. Al-Saadi was detained in Turkey and his case revealed details of Iran's use of technology to recruit operatives for attacks in Europe, the UK, and the U.S.

stories.title: Ukraine protects over 1,170 km of frontline logistics routes from drone attacks – Defense Minister
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Minister reported that over 1,170 kilometers of frontline logistics routes have been protected from drone attacks. The pace of constructing anti-drone road defenses has doubled compared to 2025.

stories.title: The Muhajirin: Inside Syria's uneasy pact with foreign fighters
stories.summary: The arrest of an Uzbek fighter in Syria has exposed tensions between the Syrian government and foreign fighters who helped bring it to power. The incident highlights the uneasy relationship Damascus maintains with international militants who fought alongside Syrian forces.

stories.title: Europe breathes a sigh of relief after Israel loses Eurovision
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest, defeating Israel's entry amid months of backlash, boycotts, and protests over Israel's participation. The result was met with relief in parts of Europe where opposition to Israel's inclusion had been vocal.

stories.title: Nigeria, U.S. carry out new strikes on Islamic State in Nigeria: AFRICOM
stories.summary: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) reported that Nigerian and American forces conducted new air strikes against Islamic State targets in northern Nigeria. The region faces a dual threat from IS-allied jihadist groups and criminal gangs that carry out mass kidnappings against villages.

stories.title: Islamic regime launches Persian Gulf Strait Authority, ships reportedly start paying tolls
stories.summary: Iran has launched the Persian Gulf Strait Authority to oversee shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, imposing tolls on transiting vessels. JPMorgan forecasts the tolls could generate annual revenue in the tens of billions of dollars for Tehran.

stories.title: IED blast kills three, including tribal chief, in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: An improvised explosive device detonated in a busy plaza in Wana town, South Waziristan district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in northwest Pakistan. The blast killed three people, including a tribal chief.

stories.title: Iran makes new proposal for deal to end war, regional officials say
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new proposal aimed at ending the broader Middle East conflict, according to regional officials, though a source in mediator Pakistan expressed pessimism about prospects. A ceasefire has paused most fighting after weeks of U.S.-Israeli airstrikes and Iranian retaliation, but negotiations remain stalled.

stories.title: In war‑scarred Gaza, brides turn to refurbished wedding dresses
stories.summary: In war-devastated Gaza, brides have turned to refurbished wedding dresses as mass weddings provide rare moments of celebration amid ongoing destruction.

stories.title: Nuclear exercises in Belarus part of Russia’s strategy ahead of major summer offensive, diplomat says
stories.summary: A diplomat stated that demonstrative nuclear exercises in Belarus are part of Russia's strategy to create an additional threat on Ukraine's northern border. The aim is reportedly to force Ukraine to redeploy forces ahead of a planned Russian summer offensive on the main front.

stories.title: The new Indo-Pacific security architecture: From hub-and-spoke to allied security web
stories.summary: The article analyzes the evolving Indo-Pacific security architecture, describing a shift from the traditional U.S.-centered hub-and-spoke alliance model to an interconnected web of allied security partnerships among regional and extra-regional partners.

stories.title: Pressure on Mexico after two ex-officials surrender to US over alleged cartel ties
stories.summary: Two former Sinaloa state officials and members of Mexico's ruling Morena party surrendered to U.S. authorities over alleged ties to the Sinaloa cartel. Former security minister Gerardo Mérida Sánchez was taken into custody in Arizona, and former finance minister Enrique Díaz Vega was detained in New York. President Claudia Sheinbaum denied any party links to organized crime.

stories.title: Two policemen deployed with polio teams martyred in KP's Bajaur
stories.summary: Two policemen deployed to protect polio vaccination teams were shot and killed by unidentified assailants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Bajaur district. The attacks occurred on the first day of a four-day anti-polio campaign across the province.

stories.title: Iran warns unauthorised Strait of Hormuz passage will be 'illegal'
stories.summary: Iran has escalated its control over the Strait of Hormuz, warning that any vessel passing through without authorization will face consequences. A newly formed Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced that all navigation must comply with directives from Iran's armed forces.

stories.title: US prosecutors drop fraud charges against billionaire Indian businessman Gautaum Adani
stories.summary: U.S. prosecutors asked a judge to dismiss criminal fraud and conspiracy charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani. Adani had been accused in 2024 of paying bribes and defrauding investors in connection with a major solar energy project in India.

stories.title: 46 children, adults kidnapped in southern Nigeria school attack: Christian group
stories.summary: A Christian group reported that 46 people, mostly children aged two to 16, were kidnapped in a school attack in southwestern Nigeria's Oyo state on May 15.

stories.title: Iran officially announces new body to manage Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran officially announced a new body to manage the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has largely blocked shipping through the vital waterway since the outbreak of war with the United States and Israel on February 28.

stories.title: Romanians stabbed Iranian journalist in London at behest of Tehran, UK court told
stories.summary: A UK court heard that three Romanian nationals stabbed Iranian journalist Pouria Zeraati in London in March 2024 at the behest of Tehran. Zeraati, who works for opposition outlet Iran International, suffered serious injuries. Iran denies involvement.

stories.title: Syria to join G7 finance talks in Paris in sign of growing status
stories.summary: Syria will participate in a closed-door session with G7 finance ministers and central bank governors in Paris, reflecting its growing international status less than two years after the ousting of former president Bashar al-Assad.

stories.title: English Premier League clubs accused of sportswashing Israel's atrocities
stories.summary: A new report by War on Want accuses four English Premier League clubs of sportswashing Israel's actions against Palestinians. The report highlights alleged discrimination against pro-Palestinian staff and corporate complicity by major sponsors.

stories.title: Starbucks Korea CEO resigns over ad evoking massacre of pro-democracy protesters
stories.summary: The CEO of Starbucks South Korea was fired after the company ran a "Tank Day" promotional campaign on May 18, a date commemorating the 1980 Gwangju pro-democracy uprising in which soldiers killed civilians. The promotion sparked public outrage and boycott calls for what critics called a mockery of the massacre.

stories.title: Zelensky honors memory of victims of deportation of Crimean Tatar people
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and First Lady Olena Zelenska commemorated the victims of the deportation of the Crimean Tatar people. Zelenskyy emphasized that Russia's current war began with the seizure of Crimea and that Moscow continues to threaten the Crimean Tatar homeland.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill more than 3,020 in Lebanon since March
stories.summary: Lebanon's Ministry of Health reports that Israeli attacks have killed at least 3,020 people and wounded 9,273 others across the country since 2 March. The figures represent the latest official toll from the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla says Israeli forces intercepted 10 boats, contact lost with 23 vessels
stories.summary: The Gaza-bound aid flotilla reported that Israeli forces intercepted 10 of its boats on May 18, with contact lost with 23 additional vessels. Live video showed military vessels approaching the fleet.

stories.title: Counsel for Imran, Bushra challenges IHC order setting deadline for arguments in £190m case
stories.summary: Counsel for imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi challenged an Islamabad High Court order setting a deadline for concluding arguments in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case. Imran is serving a 14-year sentence at Adiala jail in Rawalpindi.

stories.title: Russia’s harbor-guard boat struck in the Caspian — Ukraine’s fifth reported vessel hit there this month
stories.summary: Ukraine reportedly struck a Russian harbor-guard boat in the Caspian Sea, marking the fifth reported vessel hit there this month. Ukraine's General Staff noted the vessel's purpose was specifically to prevent the type of attack that struck it.

stories.title: Hungarian President rejects resignation pressure from PM Magyar
stories.summary: Hungary's President reportedly refused to resign despite pressure from opposition leader Péter Magyar, according to local media reports.

stories.title: Geopolitics has changed since last India-Nordic Summit, conflicts on agenda for talks: Norwegian envoy
stories.summary: Norway's ambassador indicated that geopolitics has shifted significantly since the last India-Nordic Summit, with conflicts now a key agenda item. As U.S. sanction waivers on Russian oil lapse, Norway may seek to increase energy supplies to India.

stories.title: Kenya transport protests turn deadly as four killed in fuel price unrest
stories.summary: At least four people were killed in Kenya during protests triggered by government-announced fuel price hikes, including a 23.5-percent increase in diesel prices. The unrest followed a strike called by transport workers in response to rising costs linked to global oil prices.

stories.title: Gaza-bound flotilla says Israeli forces intercept fleet near Cyprus
stories.summary: A flotilla of fifty ships that departed southwestern Turkey on May 14 was intercepted by Israeli forces near Cyprus while en route to Gaza.

stories.title: IDF kills Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander in targeted strike in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military carried out a targeted strike in Lebanon that killed a commander of Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ). The IDF stated that the commander, identified as Halim, had led the integration of PIJ operatives into Hezbollah's combat operations.

stories.title: Israel joins MENA execution states after enforcing death penalty
stories.summary: Israel has enforced the death penalty, joining other Middle East and North Africa states that carry out executions. Human rights experts have raised concerns that the military will exploit the law and that it does not apply to Jewish Israeli citizens.

stories.title: Belarus holds drills with Russian nuclear weapons, drawing criticism from Ukraine
stories.summary: Belarus began military training exercises involving Russian tactical nuclear weapons deployed on its territory, drawing strong condemnation from Ukraine. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko agreed in 2023 to host Russian tactical nuclear missiles, though Moscow retains control over their use.

stories.title: Freedom of speech 'not an absolute right', Hong Kong trial of Tiananmen activists hears
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court heard arguments that freedom of speech is not an absolute right during the trial of activists linked to Tiananmen Square commemoration events, which were once publicly held only in Hong Kong and Macau.

stories.title: Philippines launches VP Duterte impeachment trial amid political division
stories.summary: The Philippine Senate has established an impeachment court to try Vice President Sara Duterte, following House leadership changes and a shootout incident that underscored deep political divisions in the country.

stories.title: 'Like madmen': Palestinian family attacked in their sleep by Israeli settlers
stories.summary: Dozens of Israeli settlers stormed a Palestinian home in the occupied West Bank overnight and attacked members of the Shalalda family while they slept. The incident occurred amid ongoing settler violence in the territory.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Oschadbank says Hungary revokes unlawful measures against its employees
stories.summary: Hungarian authorities revoked March 6 decisions that had targeted employees of Ukraine's state-owned Oschadbank involved in cash collection operations. The revoked measures included a ban on the employees' entry into the Schengen Area.

stories.title: What we know about Israel’s interception of Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted multiple vessels from the Global Sumud Flotilla, a Gaza-bound aid convoy, in international waters. The flotilla was attempting to deliver humanitarian supplies to the blockaded Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Norway joins EU's Baltic Sea Region cooperation amid greater security focus
stories.summary: Norway announced it has joined the European Union's Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region, which coordinates work on shared challenges including security, reflecting increased Nordic focus on regional defense.

stories.title: Belarus is now drilling nuclear-weapon use with Russian forces from “unprepared” deployment areas next to EU and Ukraine
stories.summary: Belarus has begun conducting nuclear-weapon-use drills with Russian forces from unprepared deployment areas near the EU and Ukrainian borders. Minsk publicly announced the exercises while stating they pose no threat to neighboring countries.

stories.title: Jewish, Arab Israeli activists launch 'Hasbara' flotilla opposing Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla
stories.summary: Jewish and Arab Israeli activists launched a counter-flotilla opposing the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla. Arab-Israeli activist Yoseph Haddad described it as sending a message that the aid flotilla's activists were not welcome.

stories.title: At least 100 deaths reported in Ebola outbreak in DR Congo as six Americans exposed
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused at least 100 deaths, with one province reporting 390 cases. Six Americans have been exposed to the virus, with one reportedly experiencing symptoms.

stories.title: Russia and Belarus stage joint nuclear weapons drills
stories.summary: Russia and Belarus conducted joint military drills practicing the use of Russian nuclear weapons, the Belarusian defense ministry announced Monday. Russia deployed nuclear-capable hypersonic missiles to Belarus last year and revised its nuclear doctrine in 2024 to place Belarus under its nuclear umbrella.

stories.title: Death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon passes 3,000, officials say
stories.summary: Lebanese officials report that Israeli strikes on Lebanon have killed more than 3,000 people since March, marking a significant milestone in the Israel-Hezbollah conflict despite a nominal ceasefire being in place.

stories.title: After setting out from Libya, Gaza land convoy stalls in Sirte, where last effort failed
stories.summary: A Gaza-bound land convoy organized by the Global Sumud Flotilla, which departed from Libya, has stalled in the city of Sirte. The convoy was paused while organizers evaluated security risks, citing indications that Libyan forces were preparing to confront them.

stories.title: Government Auction Fails to Sell Majority Stake in Gold Miner After No Bids Submitted
stories.summary: A Russian government auction failed to sell a majority stake in Yuzhuralzoloto Group of Companies after no bids were submitted. The stake had been seized from billionaire regional lawmaker Konstantin Strukov in July on allegations he illegally took control of the gold mining company using his government position.

stories.title: China committed to not providing material support to Iran: U.S. trade representative Jamieson Greer
stories.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that China has committed to not providing material support to Iran, adding that the U.S. has achieved strategic stability with Beijing and that President Trump is not pursuing joint military operations with China.

stories.title: Pakistan’s mediation faces limits as Iran-US tensions deepen
stories.summary: Pakistan is mediating between Iran and the United States, with Tehran and Washington exchanging proposals through Islamabad. However, growing military escalation between the two sides is increasingly undermining diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Putin faces 'very difficult choices' in Ukraine as sanctions bite, Estonia's spy chief says
stories.summary: Estonia's foreign intelligence chief said Russian President Vladimir Putin faces difficult choices in Ukraine, with his forces unable to make significant battlefield advances while Western sanctions erode Russian resources.

stories.title: Zionism was built as a bulwark against socialism
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Zionist leaders historically positioned their movement as a defense against socialism and communism. The article draws connections to contemporary attacks on leftist politicians and Palestine solidarity movements in Europe.

stories.title: Israeli Navy seizes Gaza-bound flotilla as commandos board boats at sea
stories.summary: Israeli Navy commandos boarded the Gaza-bound flotilla at sea, seizing vessels and detaining activists on board. Israel's Foreign Ministry linked the convoy to Hamas and referenced the Trump peace plan in its justification.

stories.title: Russia cutting active oil wells as war losses mount – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service reported that Russia is reducing the number of active oil wells, with oil refining declining by 10% in 2026. President Zelenskyy cited the data as evidence of mounting economic pressure from war-related losses.

stories.title: Regulator demands fairness from Israeli banks as they cash in on hefty fees
stories.summary: Israel's banking supervisor has warned financial institutions to treat customers fairly or face consequences. The regulator noted that the entry of new players into the market could increase competition against established Israeli banks benefiting from high fees.

stories.title: A TikTok feature that Pakistan’s dirty money loves
stories.summary: An analysis highlights how TikTok and other social media platforms are being used in Pakistan to move money outside formal financial regulations. Virtual gifts and livestream donations are converted into digital credits that can be withdrawn or transferred.

stories.title: Report: US shows flexibility on limited Iranian nuclear activity
stories.summary: The United States has reportedly signaled flexibility on allowing Iran to maintain limited peaceful nuclear activity under IAEA supervision. However, Washington's position on releasing Iran's frozen assets remains more restrictive, with only a quarter of funds offered under a phased timetable.

stories.title: Exclusive: ICC prosecutor's office seeks arrest warrant for Israel's Smotrich
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court prosecutor's office is seeking an arrest warrant for Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. The charges relate to the West Bank occupation and reportedly include the crime of apartheid against Palestinians.

stories.title: CIC revamps Sustainable Construction Award to accelerate decarbonisation
stories.summary: The article concerns a sponsored promotion by Hong Kong's Construction Industry Council for its 2026 Sustainable Construction Award, which aims to accelerate decarbonization. New features include a Low Carbon Citation and mandatory joint submissions by project teams, with applications closing June 18.

stories.title: US conducts follow-up strikes against militants in Nigeria's northeast
stories.summary: U.S. Africa Command carried out additional air strikes against Islamic State targets in northeastern Nigeria on Sunday in coordination with the Nigerian government, as joint operations against militant groups continue to intensify.

stories.title: Nigeria: Joint US strikes hit militants as 46 kidnapped in school raids
stories.summary: Nigeria is combating both jihadist insurgents in its northeast and criminal gangs known as bandits who target rural communities and schools. Joint U.S.-Nigerian strikes have hit militants, while 46 people were kidnapped in recent school raids.

stories.title: Ukrainian Agriculture as Strategy, Diplomacy, and Legacy
stories.summary: The article is a curated digest from Ukrainian media analyzing the strategic, diplomatic, and economic role of Ukraine's agricultural sector during wartime. It highlights how Ukrainian commentators view agriculture as a key element of national resilience and international engagement beyond the battlefield.

stories.title: Ukraine, Hungary to hold consultations on Hungarian minority
stories.summary: Ukraine and Hungary announced plans to hold consultations this week on the rights of Ukraine's ethnic Hungarian minority. The talks aim to rebuild bilateral ties following a change of government in Hungary.

stories.title: Belarus holds nuclear weapons drills, defence ministry says
stories.summary: Belarus announced on Monday that it is conducting training exercises in the use of nuclear weapons. Belarus hosts Russian nuclear weapons on its territory.

stories.title: Rwanda closes Goma border crossing following Ebola emergency
stories.summary: Rwanda closed its border crossing with the Democratic Republic of Congo near Goma and Gisenyi in response to the ongoing Ebola emergency. Eyewitness accounts confirm the closure has been in effect since Sunday morning.

stories.title: Iran’s revolution was not destined to end in clerical rule
stories.summary: An analysis revisits Iran's 1979 revolution through the social forces that drove it, arguing that the establishment of clerical rule was not a historically inevitable outcome. The piece examines how various political actors shaped the revolution's trajectory.

stories.title: Somaliland divisions remain as it marks independence day after Israel recognition
stories.summary: Somaliland marked its independence day amid continued internal divisions. Hopes that Israel's recognition of Somaliland would prompt other countries to follow suit have not materialized.

stories.title: G7 finance ministers to discuss Ukraine war, Hormuz Strait crisis at Paris meeting
stories.summary: G7 finance ministers are set to meet in Paris to discuss the war in Ukraine, the conflict involving Iran, and the crisis surrounding the Strait of Hormuz. The agenda reflects multiple simultaneous geopolitical flashpoints facing the group.

stories.title: Ukraine’s steel capacity fell fourfold after Russia destroyed Azovstal. Now EU’s new quota could cost it €1 billion more
stories.summary: Ukraine's steel production capacity fell fourfold after Russia destroyed the Azovstal plant in Mariupol. A new EU quota offering 713,000 tonnes of duty-free access could cost Ukraine an estimated €1 billion, as the country shipped 2.65 million tonnes to the EU last year.

stories.title: Cop martyred in firing by attackers while returning from polio duty in KP's Bajaur
stories.summary: A police officer providing security for a polio vaccination team was shot and killed by unidentified attackers in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The officer, Sayed Aziz, 35, sustained multiple bullet wounds and died en route to the hospital.

stories.title: Could the Iran war trigger the next debt shock?
stories.summary: Rising tensions over a potential Iran conflict are putting pressure on government bond markets. Analysts warn that households could soon feel the economic impact of increased geopolitical instability.

stories.title: US Air Force looks to convert offshore oil rigs into rocket recovery platforms
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force has proposed converting decommissioned offshore oil platforms into sea-based recovery stations for the U.S. Space Force and private spaceflight companies. The plan aims to repurpose existing maritime infrastructure for rocket recovery operations.

stories.title: Federal Shariat Court strikes down 2022 legislation decriminalising suicide attempts
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Shariat Court struck down 2022 legislation that had decriminalized suicide attempts, declaring the law un-Islamic. A three-member bench led by Chief Justice Iqbal Hameedur Rehman ruled on two petitions challenging amendments to the Pakistan Penal Code.

stories.title: Rebuked by court and military, police say they will detain draft evaders
stories.summary: Israeli police announced they will detain ultra-Orthodox draft evaders after being rebuked by the court and military. The Shas party condemned arrests of Torah scholars, while Finance Minister Smotrich called on Haredi leaders to endorse military service for those not in full-time study.

stories.title: Former US negotiator with Iran: Trump falling into Vietnam trap
stories.summary: Former US negotiator Rob Malley has criticized the Trump administration's approach to Iran talks, comparing it to a Vietnam-era trap. Malley assessed that the current negotiations have a very small chance of success.

stories.title: A Russian airliner revival sold as breakthrough now survives on extended flight-cycle limits, Ukrainian spy agency says
stories.summary: Ukraine's intelligence agency reports that roughly 159 Russian Sukhoi Superjet aircraft remain dependent on turbofan engines co-developed with a French firm that withdrew after Russia's 2022 invasion. Russia has extended flight-cycle limits to keep the fleet operational.

stories.title: Ebola: DR Congo outbreak a global health emergency, says WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo's eastern Ituri province a public health emergency of international concern. The outbreak involves a rare strain and has caused at least 91 deaths, with approximately 350 suspected cases reported.

stories.title: Magyar announces talks with Ukraine on Hungarian minority rights in Transcarpathia
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar informed European Council President António Costa on May 18 about the start of negotiations with Ukraine. The talks concern legal guarantees for the rights of the ethnic Hungarian community in Ukraine's Transcarpathia region.

stories.title: Iraq probes drone attack targeting Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Iraq announced it has opened an investigation into Saudi Arabia's claims that a drone attack was launched from Iraqi territory. Iraq's Foreign Ministry stated that its air defense systems did not detect any drones taking off from or passing through Iraqi airspace.

stories.title: Tata-ASML deal: How significant is it for India’s semiconductor push?
stories.summary: Tata Group and Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASML have signed a deal reflecting India's ambition to build domestic chipmaking capacity. The agreement is part of India's broader push to enter a sector dominated by a small number of global powers.

stories.title: Why is US General David Petraeus visiting Baghdad?
stories.summary: Retired US General David Petraeus is visiting Baghdad and holding meetings with senior Iraqi officials. The nature of the visit and the capacity in which Petraeus is conducting his mission have not been publicly disclosed.

stories.title: Lone rabbi speaking at mass DC prayer rally calls antisemitism ‘utterly un-American’
stories.summary: Rabbi Meir Soloveichik spoke at a large prayer rally in Washington, D.C., calling antisemitism "utterly un-American." The prominent Jewish conservative referenced Irving Berlin's "God Bless America" at the largely Christian event.

stories.title: Unmarried partners of deceased Russian soldiers sue over denial of benefits and payments
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court received its first lawsuit challenging a law that denies benefits to unmarried partners of fallen Russian soldiers. The case, reported by the business daily Kommersant, seeks to extend survivor payments beyond legally married spouses.

stories.title: No need for 28th Constitutional Amendment, says Raza Rabbani
stories.summary: Former Pakistani Senate chairman Raza Rabbani of the PPP opposed a proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment, stating the Constitution cannot bear further changes. He argued that the 26th and 27th Amendments had already defaced original provisions, particularly those concerning the judiciary.

stories.title: Online grocery sales growth in Russia slowed sharply in early 2026. Mobile internet outages are partly to blame.
stories.summary: Growth in Russia's online grocery sales slowed sharply in the first quarter of 2026, according to data from the consulting agency Infoline cited by Kommersant. Mobile internet outages were identified as a contributing factor to the deceleration.

stories.title: Ukraine says it has Russia’s hidden war-damage assessment — one Moscow won’t show its own population
stories.summary: Ukraine claims to have obtained Russia's internal war-damage assessment that Moscow has kept hidden from its own population. The intelligence reportedly shows that a single mid-sized Russian oil company was forced to shut down approximately 400 wells.

stories.title: Houthi court sentences 19 to death for aiding Saudi coalition
stories.summary: A Houthi court in Yemen sentenced 19 individuals to death for allegedly aiding the Saudi-led coalition. The verdict, which can be appealed, came shortly after the Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognized government agreed on the largest prisoner exchange to date.

stories.title: Israeli settlers rampage through West Bank under army protection
stories.summary: Israeli settlers carried out coordinated attacks on several Palestinian communities across the occupied West Bank. Reports indicate the settlers operated under the protection of Israeli military forces during the rampage.

stories.title: What to know about Ebola outbreak after WHO sounds global alarm
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a global health emergency. Ebola is one of the deadliest diseases on earth, with fatality rates reaching as high as 90 percent.

stories.title: Renewed Israeli attacks kill 7 in Lebanon as death toll exceeds 3,000
stories.summary: Renewed Israeli strikes on Lebanon have killed at least seven people, pushing the total death toll past 3,000. The attacks came just days after Lebanese and Israeli officials agreed to extend a ceasefire by 45 days.

stories.title: Unbeatable China? Beijing a global focal point as Russia pins hopes on Putin-Xi summit
stories.summary: Chinese political scientist Zheng Yongnian, a government adviser, suggested U.S. President Trump now understands Washington cannot defeat China and must engage Beijing. Russian President Vladimir Putin confirmed plans to visit China for a summit with President Xi Jinping, as Beijing positions itself centrally in U.S.-China-Russia relations.

stories.title: NT laws to allow police to hold young people for 48 hours will be ‘funnelling Aboriginal children into prisons’, advocates warn
stories.summary: The Northern Territory government in Australia introduced draft youth justice laws allowing police to detain and question young people for up to 48 hours without a legal guardian present. Advocates warned the legislation would disproportionately funnel Aboriginal children into the prison system. The amendments were introduced by corrections minister Gerard Maley.

stories.title: Australia’s social media ban preventing teens from accessing the news, research finds
stories.summary: A new study found that Australia's social media ban, in effect since December, is reducing news access among teens. Half of the young people blocked from platforms reported seeing less news, though two-thirds of under-16s have remained on social media despite the ban.

stories.title: ‘Settler violence’: A buzzword used to single out Israel - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the term "settler violence" is used as a political label to single out Israel and imply direct state responsibility for actions by individual settlers in the occupied territories.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes in Dnipro damage two hospitals, two medical centers relocated from Luhansk region
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes overnight hit four medical institutions in the city of Dnipro, including two hospitals and two medical centers that had been relocated from Luhansk region. Among the facilities damaged was the regional clinical hospital evacuated from Luhansk.

stories.title: Belgian ex-diplomat dies before standing trial over 1961 murder of Congolese leader
stories.summary: Étienne Davignon, a 93-year-old former Belgian diplomat and European commissioner, died before standing trial for his alleged role in the 1961 assassination of Congolese Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba. Davignon was the first and last living person charged in the investigation into Lumumba's murder in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike Grachonok anti-sabotage boat in Republic of Dagestan
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck a Project 21980 Grachonok anti-sabotage boat near Kaspiysk in Russia's Republic of Dagestan. Additional strikes targeted Russian military assets in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories.

stories.title: Israel raid of Gaza-bound flotilla near Cyprus sparks outrage
stories.summary: The Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla reported that Israeli naval forces raided several of its vessels in international waters approximately 250 nautical miles from Gaza's coast, near Cyprus. The flotilla said it was surrounded and under active interception by Israeli warships.

stories.title: Iran Could Be Trump’s Greatest Failure
stories.summary: The article examines U.S. policy setbacks regarding Iran, suggesting that developments in the conflict have gone significantly wrong for the Trump administration. No specific new events or policy actions are detailed beyond a broad critical assessment.

stories.title: Bail posted for Andriy Yermak, former Ukrainian presidential chief of staff. He has been released from pretrial detention.
stories.summary: Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court approved bail of 140 million hryvnia for Andriy Yermak, the former chief of staff to the Ukrainian president. Yermak was subsequently released from pretrial detention, as reported by the Ukrainian news agency UNIAN.

stories.title: French Minister visits Algeria amid diplomatic thaw
stories.summary: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin visited Algeria to discuss improved judicial cooperation and the case of a detained French journalist. The visit signals a diplomatic thaw between Paris and Algiers following tensions triggered in part by France's support for Moroccan sovereignty over the disputed Western Sahara.

stories.title: Gaza-bound flotilla says Israeli forces intercepting fleet near Cyprus
stories.summary: Israeli military forces intercepted a Gaza-bound humanitarian aid flotilla west of Cyprus on Monday. The Global Sumud Flotilla, which departed from Turkey, reported that IDF forces boarded the first vessel and demanded safe passage for the mission.

stories.title: Iran police chief claims regime arrested more than 6,500 suspected ‘elements linked to the enemy’
stories.summary: Iran's police chief announced that security forces arrested more than 6,500 suspected individuals linked to enemy elements during wartime conditions. He also claimed that 166 armed individuals described as professional thieves who resisted arrest were killed by security forces.

stories.title: Donald Trump’s approval rating sinks to lowest point of second term
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to 37%, the lowest point of his second term, amid frustration over the cost of living and the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. Polling showed most American voters believe Trump's decision to go to war with Iran was the wrong choice, with midterm elections approaching in November.

stories.title: Rural Britain is becoming ‘food desert’ for lower-income families, study finds
stories.summary: A new study found that rural Britain is becoming a "food desert" for lower-income families due to the closure of local shops and poor public transport. Over half of countryside households earning under £40,000 annually struggle to access affordable and healthy food, including fresh fruit and vegetables.

stories.title: What is Ebola and why is stopping this outbreak so difficult?
stories.summary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo involves a rare strain of the virus. The affected area is also experiencing active armed conflict, complicating containment and response efforts.

stories.title: IDF's Central Command chief signs amendment to enact death penalty for terrorists in West Bank
stories.summary: IDF Central Command chief Major General Avi Bluth signed an amendment enabling the death penalty for terrorists in the West Bank. The signing marks a significant policy shift within Israel's defense establishment following the October 7 attack.

stories.title: Cuba warns US of ‘bloodbath’ if military action follows drone claims
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned that any U.S. military action against Cuba would lead to a "bloodbath" with severe consequences for regional stability. His statement came after U.S. media reports based on classified intelligence alleged Havana had acquired over 300 drones that could potentially target the Guantanamo Bay naval base.

stories.title: Rwanda: Singer Yampano Arrested Over Alleged Assault, Threats
stories.summary: Rwandan artist Florien Uworizagwira, known as Yampano, was arrested by the Rwanda Investigation Bureau. He faces allegations including assault, issuing threats, and drug abuse.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kirehe - Rice Farmers Seek Govt Help to Recover Rwf64m Owed By Buyer
stories.summary: A rice farming cooperative in Rwanda's Kirehe District is seeking government assistance to recover more than 64 million Rwandan francs owed by a now-defunct processing company. The debt has been outstanding since 2019.

stories.title: Rwanda: Genocide Survivor Recounts Father's Last Days At Ndera Seminary
stories.summary: Elvis Nkundanyirazo, a survivor of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda, recounted the final days of his father at Petit Séminaire St Vincent Ndera. Thousands had sought refuge at the seminary during the genocide.

stories.title: JI emir challenges petroleum levy in FCC, terms it 'unconstitutional'
stories.summary: Jamaat-i-Islami emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman filed a challenge in Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court against the petroleum levy, arguing it grants the government unrestricted taxing power through executive notifications without parliamentary oversight. The levy was linked to commitments with the IMF.

stories.title: Syrskyi visits Khartia unit in Southern Slobozhanshchyna region
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi visited the Khartia brigade, the 2nd Corps of Ukraine's National Guard, operating in the Southern Slobozhanshchyna region. Russian forces carried out more than 150 attacks in the area during the first half of May, while Khartia continues active defensive operations.

stories.title: Ukraine’s anti-corruption agencies deny the Russian propaganda story about Olena Zelenska’s “arrest”
stories.summary: Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies denied Russian propaganda claims about the arrest of First Lady Olena Zelenska. Russian state media had spread the false story citing unnamed "security structures," and Ukrainian authorities confirmed none of the claims were true.

stories.title: Iran sets up new Strait of Hormuz managing body amid stalled talks with US
stories.summary: Iran established a new body to manage the Strait of Hormuz as peace talks with the United States remained stalled. Iranian media previously reported that vessels seeking transit through the strait would need to apply for permits, disclosing ownership, insurance, crew, and cargo information.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Vows Justice for Rachel Wandetto After Fatal Petrol Attack Over Tattoo
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto vowed justice for Rachel Wandetto, a woman who died after being doused with petrol and set on fire over a tattoo bearing the president's image. The fatal attack occurred in circumstances that drew national attention in Nairobi.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s dog-friendly restaurant scheme receives 700 applications on first day
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department received approximately 700 applications on the first day of a new licensing scheme allowing dogs into restaurants. The scheme has a cap of 1,000 places, with applications closing on June 8 and a planned launch in July.

stories.title: What we know about the deadly new Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
stories.summary: A fresh Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 90 people. Health authorities are working to contain the spread of the virus in the affected regions.

stories.title: Kenya: Two Killed in Kiambu and Nakuru As Fuel Hike Protests Turn Deadly
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in Kenya's Kiambu and Nakuru counties during protests sparked by recent fuel price hikes. Police arrested several demonstrators amid reports of widespread destruction and looting.

stories.title: ‘High time to push peace agenda’: Ebola outbreak in DRC spreads in conflict-hit, hard-to-reach areas
stories.summary: The latest Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has been linked to the rare Bundibugyo strain, which was first identified in Uganda in 2007. Dr. Hypolite Muhindo Mavoko of the University of Kinshasa warned that deceased bodies can continue transmitting the disease, highlighting risks from traditional burial practices. The outbreak is spreading in conflict-affected, hard-to-reach areas.

stories.title: Lebanon’s president says he will do ‘impossible’ to end war with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun pledged to do the "impossible" to end Israel's war on Lebanon as Israeli strikes continued despite a ceasefire. Aoun outlined a negotiating framework including Israeli withdrawal, army deployment along the border, return of displaced residents, and economic assistance.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland Marks 35th Anniversary With Recognition Push
stories.summary: Somaliland celebrated the 35th anniversary of its restored statehood with military parades and ceremonies in the capital Hargeisa. More than 25 international delegations attended as Somaliland renewed its diplomatic push for wider international recognition.

stories.title: Nigeria: APC Now Running Akwa Ibom PDP, Exco Member of Wike-Backed PDP Faction Laments
stories.summary: An executive committee member of a faction of Nigeria's People's Democratic Party in Akwa Ibom state alleged that the ruling All Progressives Congress is effectively controlling the local PDP. The official claimed aspirants, including himself, were denied PDP nomination forms.

stories.title: Uganda: Allies of Former Speaker Among Quiet As Corruption Probe Deepens
stories.summary: Joint security teams conducted extensive searches at the Kampala residence of former Ugandan Speaker Anita Annet Among on Mackinnon Road in the Nakasero suburb. The operations reportedly expanded to properties linked to her associates as a corruption probe deepens, while her former allies have been retreating from public association with her online.

stories.title: Belarus holds nuclear weapons drills, Defence Ministry says
stories.summary: Belarus conducted nuclear weapons drills, with its Defence Ministry stating the training was not directed against any other state and posed no regional security threats.

stories.title: The Gulf’s African Aftershocks
stories.summary: The article discusses how the Iran war is intensifying proxy conflicts in the Red Sea region and the Horn of Africa, with Gulf states playing a significant role. It examines the ripple effects of Middle Eastern hostilities on African security dynamics.

stories.title: More than 30 wounded in Russian attacks on Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russian overnight attacks on Ukrainian cities wounded more than 30 people. The strikes came after both sides exchanged some of their bloodiest attacks in months during the conflict, which has lasted over four years.

stories.title: Putin faces 'very difficult choice' because of war in Ukraine – head of Estonia's foreign intelligence service
stories.summary: The head of Estonia's foreign intelligence service said President Putin faces a very difficult strategic choice regarding the war in Ukraine. He noted that the Russian army cannot achieve significant battlefield progress while Western sanctions continue to drain Russia's resources.

stories.title: Infectious diseases such as hantavirus and Ebola becoming more frequent and damaging, say experts
stories.summary: Experts warned that infectious disease outbreaks are becoming more frequent and damaging globally. Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda are scrambling to contain an Ebola outbreak, while a hantavirus outbreak has also raised international concern. The Global Preparedness Monitoring Board said pandemic risk is outpacing investments in preparedness.

stories.title: Cuba dreads possible US invasion amid energy blockade
stories.summary: Cuba accused the Trump administration of fabricating a pretext for invasion, citing U.S. media reports based on classified intelligence claiming Havana acquired hundreds of drones. Cuban officials say the economic sanctions imposed by Washington are strangling the nation and allege the U.S. is seeking justification for military action.

stories.title: 'Long live Al Aqsa Flood:' US Nakba Day protests rife with terrorism support
stories.summary: Protests took place across the United States on Nakba Day, May 15, with demonstrators expressing support for Palestinians. Some participants made statements referencing the October 7 attack and called for the liberation of Palestine.

stories.title: Dogs allowed on glitzy Cannes beach newly renamed after French film star Brigitte Bardot
stories.summary: A beach in Cannes, France, was renamed in honor of French film star Brigitte Bardot and will allow dogs in tribute to her animal rights activism. Bardot, who retired from acting, has become a controversial figure for her animal welfare work and vocal support of far-right politics.

stories.title: Some items in Luigi Mangione’s backpack won’t be used as evidence in trial, judge rules
stories.summary: A Manhattan judge ruled that several items found in Luigi Mangione's backpack during his arrest—including a magazine, cellphone, passport, wallet, and computer chip—will be suppressed as evidence. The defense argued that police who arrested Mangione in connection with the murder of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson did not properly inform him of his rights.

stories.title: Ex-assistant principal faces trial after six-year-old shot Virginia teacher
stories.summary: Former assistant principal Ebony Parker went to trial in Newport News, Virginia, on charges of ignoring warnings that a six-year-old student brought a loaded gun to Richneck Elementary School. The weapon was later used by the child to shoot his first-grade teacher in January 2023.

stories.title: Trump moves to dismiss $10bn lawsuit against IRS amid reports he’s considering settlement
stories.summary: President Donald Trump moved to dismiss his $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS amid reports he is considering a settlement with the federal government. The reported settlement would create a $1.7 billion fund to compensate allies for alleged government persecution. The filing came ahead of a court deadline requesting briefing on whether a legitimate controversy existed.

stories.title: Uganda's president signs contentious law meant to curb foreign influence
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni signed a controversial law aimed at curbing foreign influence in the country. The measure has drawn heavy criticism, including from Uganda's central bank, which warned it could trigger economic disaster.

stories.title: China agrees to boost trade for U.S. agricultural products following Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: China agreed to increase purchases of U.S. agricultural products following a summit between President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping in Beijing, aimed at easing the impact of the ongoing trade war on American farmers.

stories.title: What is the UAE’s Barakah nuclear plant, nearly hit by a drone?
stories.summary: The Barakah nuclear power plant, located in Abu Dhabi, UAE, reportedly came close to being struck by a drone. The facility has the capacity to supply approximately one-quarter of the UAE's total electricity demand.

stories.title: WHO kicks off annual assembly amid Ebola, hantavirus, US withdrawal, funding cuts
stories.summary: The World Health Organization opened its annual assembly of global health ministers amid concerns over a hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship and an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The meeting also faced uncertainty surrounding announced withdrawals by the United States and Argentina, along with funding cuts.

stories.title: Russia offers continued military cooperation to Equatorial Guinea
stories.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Foreign Minister Simeon Oyono Esono Angue met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow on Monday. The two officials discussed defense cooperation and Russia's broader military engagement in Africa.

stories.title: Spared Wang Fuk Court block owners given mid-October to finalise buyback offer
stories.summary: Owners of Wang Chi House, the only block spared in the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court complex in Hong Kong, have been given until October 15 to finalize sales under a government buyback scheme. At least 75 percent of owners must indicate their intention to sell by the end of next month. Residents have expressed frustration over the tight timeline and lack of details on insurance and maintenance.

stories.title: Russia and Belarus Launch Joint Nuclear Drills
stories.summary: Russia and Belarus launched joint nuclear military exercises. The Belarusian army stated the drills are not directed against third countries and do not threaten regional security.

stories.title: Biggest French cinema producer's blacklist threat could recall Hollywood 'McCarthyism'
stories.summary: Canal+ head Maxime Saada threatened to blacklist approximately 600 French cinema professionals who signed a petition opposing right-wing billionaire owner Vincent Bolloré's influence on the industry. The petition called for mobilization against what signatories described as the growing grip of the far right on French cinema. Critics have compared the move to Hollywood-era McCarthyism.

stories.title: PM Modi lands in Norway; to hold talks on trade, technology
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Norway for talks on trade and technology, marking the first visit by an Indian prime minister to the country in 43 years.

stories.title: The world cannot afford to fail women, children and adolescents
stories.summary: International aid cuts, rising debt burdens, and ongoing armed conflicts are severely undermining maternal and child health services worldwide, pushing healthcare systems for women, children, and adolescents toward a critical breaking point.

stories.title: China's moment? Putin heads to Beijing after Trump courts Xi
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to host Russian President Vladimir Putin in Beijing just days after receiving U.S. President Donald Trump. The back-to-back summits highlight Beijing's growing centrality in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical landscape.

stories.title: Ukrainian troops carry out counterattacks on certain sections of front in southern regions – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Vladyslav Voloshyn, spokesperson for Ukraine's Southern Defense Forces, reported that Ukrainian troops are conducting counterattacks on certain sections of the southern front. He noted that Russian forces continue active assault operations using aviation and kamikaze drones in the region.

stories.title: Can women's football help reconnect North and South Korea?
stories.summary: North Korean athletes are set to compete in South Korea for the first time in over seven years through a women's football event. Analysts are divided on whether Pyongyang's participation represents a propaganda effort or a genuine step toward détente.

stories.title: Can a women's football team reconnect North and South Korea?
stories.summary: For the first time in over seven years, North Korean athletes will compete in South Korea through a women's football event. Analysts are divided on whether Pyongyang's participation represents a propaganda move or a genuine step toward easing inter-Korean tensions.

stories.title: Nigeria: Who was the targeted Islamic State group leader and why was he targeted by the US?
stories.summary: A senior Islamic State figure identified as Abu-Bilal al-Minuki was killed on May 16 in a joint Nigerian-U.S. strike in northeastern Nigeria. Despite U.S. President Trump's claims, analysts say al-Minuki was not the second-in-command of IS worldwide, though he was a prominent figure within the group's West African operations.

stories.title: Experts locate bodies of four missing Italian divers inside Maldives cave
stories.summary: Rescue teams located the bodies of four Italian divers deep inside an underwater cave in a Maldives atoll, four days after they were reported missing. A local military diver had previously died during a perilous search mission to reach them. Authorities said they would attempt to recover the bodies within the next couple of days.

stories.title: International Gymnastics Federation lifts all sanctions on Russia and Belarus without explanation
stories.summary: The International Gymnastics Federation lifted all sanctions on Russia and Belarus, allowing both countries to return to full international competition under their own flags and anthems. The decision was made without public explanation while Russia's invasion of Ukraine continues.

stories.title: Iran submits updated 14-point proposal to US through Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran submitted an updated version of its 14-point proposal to the United States through Pakistani mediation. The revised draft reportedly focuses on ending the ongoing war between the two countries.

stories.title: Israel raid of Gaza-bound flotilla near Cyprus sparks outrage
stories.summary: Israeli forces seized the Global Sumud Flotilla, a Gaza-bound aid convoy, in international waters near Cyprus. The raid is the latest in a series of Israeli interceptions of vessels attempting to break the naval blockade on Gaza.

stories.title: The only Iran deal Trump can get is no better than Obama’s ‘horrible’ JCPOA
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that any nuclear deal the US can negotiate with Iran would not significantly differ from the 2015 JCPOA, which was previously abandoned. Weeks of bombing and threats have reportedly not changed Iran's position on ballistic missiles or regional proxies.

stories.title: Russian drone attack in Odesa leaves damaged residential buildings, kindergarten and lyceum
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack overnight on May 18 damaged residential buildings in two districts of Odesa, along with a kindergarten, a lyceum, and a police station. No casualty figures were immediately provided.

stories.title: Iran's nuclear project is 'unchanged', says senior ex-Israeli intelligence officer
stories.summary: Former senior Israeli military intelligence officer Tamir Hayman, executive director of Israel's Institute for National Security Studies, stated that Iran's nuclear project remains "essentially unchanged" despite Israeli and US attacks during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Iran says it responded to ‘excessive’ US proposal, after Trump warns ‘clock ticking’
stories.summary: Iran announced it responded to what it called an "excessive" US proposal while President Trump warned the "clock is ticking." Tehran also said it created a new body to manage the Strait of Hormuz and warned Gulf countries against cooperating with Israel.

stories.title: PA partially coordinating with Israel for security while glorifying terror, US State Dept. says
stories.summary: The US State Department reported that the Palestinian Authority is partially coordinating with Israel on security matters while simultaneously glorifying acts of violence. The department noted that recent statements by senior PLO members are incompatible with recognizing Israel's right to exist free from threats.

stories.title: Lebanon braces for Pentagon talks over Hezbollah disarmament
stories.summary: Lebanon is preparing for Pentagon-led talks concerning the disarmament of Hezbollah. There are concerns that US-backed discussions with Israel could pressure the Lebanese army into a direct military confrontation with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Former University of Michigan researcher accused of hiding Chinese military drone ties
stories.summary: Former University of Michigan researcher Chuan Wang was accused of concealing his ties to the Chinese military's drone program. Investigators allege Wang claimed modest roles on U.S. visa applications while being publicly known in China for his involvement in military drone development.

stories.title: Italy's Andrea Maldera named new Ukraine football manager
stories.summary: Italy's Andrea Maldera has been officially appointed as the new head coach of Ukraine's national football team. The appointment marks a new chapter for Ukrainian football management.

stories.title: Kristen Stewart on the red carpet in Cannes, while Javier Bardem slams toxic masculinity
stories.summary: The 79th Cannes Film Festival reached its midpoint with premieres including "Paper Tiger," directed by James Gray and starring Adam Driver and Miles Teller. The film explores corruption and moral decline in 1980s America. Actor Javier Bardem also spoke out against toxic masculinity during the festival.

stories.title: Israel to build military 'museum' on ruins of Unrwa HQ in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to build a military museum and recruitment center on the site of the demolished UNRWA headquarters in the Sheikh Jarrah neighborhood of East Jerusalem. Israeli forces had demolished the UN agency's building in January 2026.

stories.title: CM Afridi seeks PM's intervention on CNG crisis in KP, warns of possible 'widespread agitation'
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urging intervention in an ongoing CNG crisis that has shut filling stations across the province since April. Afridi warned the shortage could trigger widespread public unrest.

stories.title: London tube strikes called off at last minute
stories.summary: The RMT union called off planned strikes by London Underground drivers at the last minute. Two 24-hour stoppages that were set to begin midday Tuesday and disrupt travel over four days were suspended.

stories.title: Defense Intelligence shows how soldiers clear Russian forces out of Stepnohirsk in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Soldiers from the Artan special unit of Ukraine's military intelligence, alongside other defense forces, drove Russian troops from fortified positions in Stepnohirsk in the Zaporizhzhia region. The Defense Intelligence directorate released footage of the clearing operation.

stories.title: The 15 May deadline for Ukrainian elections has passed. Only one in ten Ukrainians wanted to meet it
stories.summary: The May 15 deadline for holding Ukrainian elections has passed, with polling showing only about one in ten Ukrainians supported meeting that timeline. Sociologist Tymofii Brik presented the data at the Lviv Media Forum, noting deeper unresolved questions about post-war governance.

stories.title: Israeli attacks across Lebanon kill seven
stories.summary: At least seven people were killed in Israeli attacks across Lebanon since dawn on Monday, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The Israeli army also issued forced evacuation orders for residents of three southern Lebanese villages, including Harouf, Borj El Chmali, and Debaal.

stories.title: Somaliland’s first ambassador to Israel welcomed by Herzog in historic ceremony
stories.summary: Somaliland's first ambassador to Israel was welcomed by President Isaac Herzog in a ceremony marking the establishment of formal diplomatic ties. Herzog said the partnership would promote cooperation benefiting both peoples and the wider region.

stories.title: Iran's foreign ministry: US talks ongoing through Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry confirmed that negotiations with the United States are continuing through Pakistani mediation. Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the US rejected Iran's initial 14-point proposal but later submitted amendments via Pakistan. Iranian and Omani technical teams also met in Oman for separate discussions.

stories.title: Lebanon-Israel UAVs: Uncounted Acts of Violence
stories.summary: An editorial cartoon by Palestinian-Jordanian cartoonist Emad Hajjaj addresses the issue of Israeli UAV operations over Lebanon. The cartoon highlights what the artist characterizes as uncounted acts of violence resulting from drone use.

stories.title: Ukraine lets companies build their own air defense, and 24 have already signed up
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry launched a program allowing private companies to build their own air defense capabilities to protect their facilities from drone attacks. Twenty-four companies have already enrolled, using trained staff or licensed security firms.

stories.title: Iran eyes challenging stock market reopening after lengthy war closure
stories.summary: Iran is preparing to reopen its stock market after an extended closure caused by the war. While the capital market is not the primary financing mechanism for Iran's economy, its reopening carries significant political and psychological weight.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills 2 in Belgorod Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack killed two people in the village of Borisovka in Russia's Belgorod region, located north of the border with Ukraine's Kharkiv region.

stories.title: Rare strike forces busiest US commuter line to a halt
stories.summary: A strike by five unions shut down the Long Island Rail Road, the busiest commuter rail line in the United States, beginning May 16. Negotiations between union leaders and New York government representatives continued into Sunday night as workers sought higher wages from the Metropolitan Transportation Authority after years of failed talks.

stories.title: Trump’s Taiwan independence comments: a blow to William Lai and ruling DPP?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated he is "not looking to have somebody go independent" regarding Taiwan, sparking debate over the implications for President Lai Ching-te and the ruling Democratic Progressive Party's pro-independence stance. The remark came after Trump's summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing, where Taiwan was a key topic.

stories.title: Russian forces concentrate artillery in Pokrovsk agglomeration to support offensive operations – Ukrainian military
stories.summary: In the Pokrovsk area of eastern Ukraine, Russian forces are concentrating artillery and building an extensive network of drone launch sites to support offensive operations. Ukrainian military officials said the buildup is aimed at bolstering Russian assault actions in the region.

stories.title: PM Modi woos Swedish companies to invest in India, says 'reform express' going at full speed
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi encouraged Swedish companies to invest in India, promoting what he described as a fast-moving reform agenda during his visit to Sweden.

stories.title: Take food for three days. Then you’ll come back. The Crimean Tatars never did
stories.summary: An article examines the 1944 Soviet deportation of Crimean Tatars, who were told to take food for three days but were never allowed to return home. Those who returned to Crimea in the 1990s and their descendants now face political persecution under Russian rule.

stories.title: PSX loses 2,000 points during intraday trade as bearish momentum persists
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index fell over 2,000 points during Monday intraday trading, declining 1.31% to 163,424.91 points amid rising oil prices driven by Middle East tensions and stalled US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: The Afghan problem
stories.summary: A wave of terrorist attacks in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province between May 9 and 14 struck targets in Bannu, Lakki Marwat, and Bajaur, raising concerns about cross-border militancy from Afghanistan. Pakistan's Foreign Office issued a strong demarche to the Afghan chargé d'affaires following the Bannu attack.

stories.title: Shakira acquitted by Spanish court of tax fraud, over US$64 million to be returned
stories.summary: A Spanish court acquitted Colombian singer Shakira of tax fraud for the 2011 tax year, finding that authorities failed to prove she was a resident of Spain. The court ordered the government to return more than 55 million euros (over US$64 million) in wrongly imposed fines.

stories.title: Pakistan deploys thousands of troops to Saudi during Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan has deployed approximately 8,000 troops to Saudi Arabia during the Iran war, with a pledge to send additional forces if needed. The deployment also includes a Chinese-made HQ-9 air defense system, according to five sources who spoke to Reuters.

stories.title: How fight for Philippine Senate presidency will shape Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial
stories.summary: The Philippine Senate convened as an impeachment court for Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio, who was impeached by the House of Representatives on allegations of corruption and constitutional violations. A parallel battle for control of the Senate presidency could shape the trial's direction, alongside the International Criminal Court case against her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, in The Hague.

stories.title: The Gulf does not have to choose Iran or Israel
stories.summary: Gulf states face strategic decisions regarding their relationships with both Iran and Israel amid the ongoing regional conflict. The central choice is framed as one between pursuing regional stability or risking prolonged warfare.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: 'Staggering' Iran toll drives up global executions: Amnesty
stories.summary: Amnesty International highlighted Iran's high execution toll. Separately, the UAE reported a drone strike near the Barakah nuclear power plant, and Saudi Arabia intercepted three drones originating from Iraqi airspace.

stories.title: Four crew members eject safely after two Navy jets crash during air show in Idaho
stories.summary: Two U.S. Navy EA-18G Growler jets from Electronic Attack Squadron 129, based at Whidbey Island, Washington, collided during an air show near Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho. All four crew members ejected safely.

stories.title: G7 finance ministers meet amid Middle East war economic fallout
stories.summary: G7 finance ministers convened in Paris to discuss economic fallout from the ongoing Middle East war. France, holding the G7 presidency, faces the challenge of maintaining dialogue amid rising tensions with Washington over tariff threats from President Donald Trump.

stories.title: PM Modi in Norway: PM Modi emplanes for Oslo
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for Oslo, Norway, as part of a Nordic visit. Trade, energy, and discussions on global conflicts are expected to top the agenda. India and Sweden agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership.

stories.title: Iran sends response to US proposal to end war via mediator Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran has sent a response to a US proposal to end the war, using Pakistan as a mediator. Tehran's demands include the release of frozen assets held abroad, the lifting of international sanctions, and control over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Uganda enacts new law to protect sovereignty despite opposition
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni signed into law legislation prohibiting foreign interference in the country's affairs. The law was enacted despite warnings from opposition groups and other concerned parties.

stories.title: Russian attack in Dnipro leaves tax administration building damaged
stories.summary: A Russian overnight attack on May 18 damaged a tax administration building in one district of Dnipro, Ukraine.

stories.title: World Gymnastics Lifts Ban on Russian and Belarusian Flags and Anthems
stories.summary: The World Gymnastics governing body lifted its ban on Russian and Belarusian flags and anthems at competitions. Russia's Gymnastics Federation welcomed the decision, calling it a step toward strengthening unity in the global gymnastics community.

stories.title: Hantavirus cruise ship arrives in the Netherlands to be disinfected
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius arrived in Rotterdam, Netherlands, for crew disembarkation and disinfection following a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people. The World Health Organization maintained its assessment that the outbreak poses a low global risk, and disease specialists said a pandemic of the virus is very unlikely.

stories.title: The secret Israeli bases scandal roiling Iraqi politics
stories.summary: The discovery of two secret Israeli military bases in Iraq has triggered a major political controversy in Baghdad. The revelation complicates Iraq's efforts to balance its relationships with both Iran and the United States.

stories.title: Israeli attacks in Gaza have stepped up since halt in bombing in Iran
stories.summary: Israel stepped up military strikes on the Gaza Strip after halting its joint bombing campaign with the United States in Iran. At least five Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes on May 17. The Gaza Strip has experienced near-daily Israeli fire since an October ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns drone attack on UAE nuclear power plant
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office condemned a drone attack on the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Abu Dhabi, calling it reckless. The UAE defence ministry reported a fire near the facility but no injuries or radiation impact, and said two additional drones were intercepted.

stories.title: Israeli forces storm Gaza aid flotilla in international waters
stories.summary: Israeli naval forces boarded and seized Gaza-bound aid boats in international waters. Activists aboard the vessels accused Israel of piracy and of enforcing what they described as a siege on Gaza.

stories.title: China and Russia hold trade expo as Putin and Trump visits draw global attention
stories.summary: China is hosting the 10th edition of a major bilateral trade expo with Russia ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin's expected visit to Beijing. The event follows U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to the Chinese capital the previous week, highlighting intensified diplomatic activity as Beijing balances relations with Washington and Moscow.

stories.title: France & Africa partnering on jobs, education, investment: 'Not just about money, also the diaspora'
stories.summary: France's Minister Delegate for Francophonie Éléonore Caroit highlighted a renewed partnership between France and African nations focused on private investment, education, and digital innovation. The remarks came against the backdrop of 23 billion euros in investment commitments tied to the Africa Forward summit in Kenya, split between French and African companies.

stories.title: Islamic regime’s extremism being imported to Europe, Kosar Eftekhari warns ‘Post’
stories.summary: Iranian activist Kosar Eftekhari, who lost an eye after being shot by security forces during the Women, Life, Freedom protests, warned of the Islamic regime's extremism spreading to Europe. She was attacked in Germany by supporters of Supreme Leader Khamenei.

stories.title: Iran Nobel winner Narges Mohammadi discharged from hospital
