stories.summary: Czech security analyst and diplomat Tomas Pojar said Europe must recognize that the United States views the war in Ukraine differently from European nations. He urged European countries to increase their own support for Kyiv rather than relying on Washington.

stories.title: Yvette Cooper wrote Palestine Action article despite CPS warning it could affect trial
stories.summary: Former UK Home Secretary Yvette Cooper wrote a newspaper column justifying the proscription of Palestine Action despite Crown Prosecution Service warnings that it could prejudice the criminal trial of six activists. The activists were charged in connection with a 2024 break-in at an Israeli arms manufacturer's factory.

stories.title: AI agents face trust issues in ‘high-risk’ industrial sectors: experts
stories.summary: Experts at an International Data Corporation event warned that deploying autonomous AI agents in high-risk Chinese industrial sectors such as healthcare and aerospace poses significant trust and safety challenges. Despite strong state support for AI integration, critical vertical markets may not be suited for fully autonomous systems.

stories.title: US, Iran stall on Hormuz reopening as oil supplies tighten
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz have stalled, with neither side closer to resolving their differences. The impasse has contributed to tightening global oil supplies.

stories.title: Hezbollah reports rocket attack on Israeli troops near Hadatha
stories.summary: Hezbollah said its fighters detonated explosive devices targeting Israeli military bulldozers advancing between the southern Lebanese towns of Rashaf and Hadatha. The group also reported launching rockets at Israeli soldiers and military vehicles on the outskirts of Hadatha.

stories.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, Uganda a global health emergency
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern. The DR Congo accounts for nearly all suspected cases, with two reported in neighboring Uganda.

stories.title: ‘Fiercely loyal, endlessly generous’ father named as victim of Rottnest Island shark attack
stories.summary: Steven Mattaboni, 38, a surveyor from Perth, has been identified as the victim of a fatal shark attack at Horseshoe Reef near Rottnest Island in Western Australia. The incident occurred around 9:55 a.m. on Saturday. He is survived by his wife and two young daughters.

stories.title: FIFA holds ‘positive’ talks with Iranian football officials on World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA held talks described as "positive" with Iranian football officials regarding Iran's participation in the 2026 World Cup. Iran's football chief said FIFA offered solutions addressing each of Iran's concerns about playing games in the United States.

stories.title: Russian envoy warns US and Israel against renewed strikes on Iran
stories.summary: Russian envoy Mikhail Ulyanov criticized reports that the United States and Israel are preparing for a possible resumption of strikes on Iran. He said such action would suggest Washington and Israel have not learned from past strategic mistakes. The New York Times reported that President Trump has not made a final decision.

stories.title: Bulgaria wins Eurovision 2026, Ukraine finishes ninth
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest 2026, while Ukraine finished in ninth place in the competition.

stories.title: Discover Jerusalem. Discover Hebrew U. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Hebrew University of Jerusalem is promoting its English-taught academic programs, including BA, MA, and PhD degrees. Applications are closing soon, and a digital open day is scheduled for May 31.

stories.title: Hong Kong draws over 310 firms and HK$26 billion in capital, InvestHK head says
stories.summary: Hong Kong's InvestHK agency reported that over 310 enterprises from mainland China and abroad established or expanded operations in the city by early May, bringing in more than HK$26 billion (US$3.3 billion) in capital. Director General Alpha Lau cited stabilizing Sino-US relations following the Xi-Trump summit as a positive factor for investment.

stories.title: Next stop, Sri Lanka: how scammers fleeing Cambodia, Myanmar found a new hub
stories.summary: Sri Lankan authorities are concerned that the island is becoming a new hub for online scam operations after networks were displaced by crackdowns in Cambodia and Myanmar. Officials cite Sri Lanka's relaxed visa regime and reliable high-speed internet as factors attracting foreign scam syndicates, with a surge in arrests of suspected foreign scammers since the start of the year.

stories.title: Trump narrows space for Taiwan independence, mainland scholar says
stories.summary: Mainland Chinese scholar Wu Yongping, dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for Taiwan Studies, argues that President Trump has narrowed the space for Taiwan independence. He discussed signals from the Xi-Trump Beijing summit regarding the Taiwan question and prospects for peaceful reunification between mainland China and Taiwan.

stories.title: Russian drone attack sparks fires in Dnipro, one injured
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes caused several fires in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro overnight, seriously injuring a 70-year-old woman, according to regional officials.

stories.title: US exemption on Russian oil expires amid rising energy prices
stories.summary: A US Treasury exemption permitting the delivery and sale of Russian-origin crude oil and petroleum products expired on Saturday. Washington had issued the waiver in April to ease pressure on global energy markets. The expiration comes amid rising energy prices linked to the regional conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine launches more than 500 drones at Russia in deadly overnight attack, authorities say
stories.summary: Ukraine launched over 500 drones at Russia in a massive overnight attack, killing three people in the Moscow region. Russian air defenses intercepted drones across 14 regions and the annexed Crimean peninsula in what authorities described as one of the largest aerial assaults of the conflict.

stories.title: ‘They lost a historic opportunity’: Ken Loach laments Your Party infighting
stories.summary: British filmmaker Ken Loach criticized Your Party, the socialist movement co-founded by Jeremy Corbyn and Zarah Sultana, for squandering a chance to unite the left against the far right. Loach noted that 800,000 people initially expressed interest in the party, but internal infighting and poor behavior undermined its potential.

stories.title: ‘You could dig up a lot of asphalt’: Tim Smit’s Chelsea garden prioritises growing food
stories.summary: Eden Project co-founder Tim Smit has designed an "edimental" garden for the Chelsea Flower Show combining edible plants like cabbages and strawberries with traditional bedding plants. Smit is calling on local councils to convert asphalt areas into community gardens where young people can grow vegetables.

stories.title: JLR and General Motors eye £900m contract to build new range of military trucks
stories.summary: Jaguar Land Rover and General Motors are among automotive firms competing for a £900 million UK military contract to build thousands of 4x4 trucks for the British armed forces. The vehicles would replace an ageing fleet of Land Rovers discontinued since 2016, as NATO countries increase defense spending.

stories.title: China turns coal power plant exhaust into cheap, effective fertiliser
stories.summary: A Chinese company has begun converting coal-fired power plant flue gas emissions into fertiliser, expanding a carbon-capture technology that could reduce both emissions and food production costs. The project was reported by China Electric Power News, a publication under China's National Development and Reform Commission.

stories.title: Haredi extremists brag openly of campaign to obstruct cops, but evade consequences
stories.summary: Jerusalem Faction organizers in Israel have been using carefully worded communications to boast of mobilizing protests to block law enforcement against ultra-Orthodox draft dodgers. The organizers have reportedly evaded legal consequences by hiding behind free speech protections.

stories.title: Regardless of election results, voters must let the government govern - editorial
stories.summary: A May poll by the Jewish People Policy Institute found that 65% of Israelis said they would accept upcoming election results. However, the survey revealed a notable ideological divide among respondents regarding acceptance of outcomes.

stories.title: Video: 250,000 protestors march in London to commemorate Nakba Day
stories.summary: Approximately 250,000 protesters marched in London on Saturday to mark the 78th anniversary of the Nakba, according to organizers. The march was organized by a coalition including the Palestine Solidarity Campaign and Stop the War.

stories.title: ‘Timmy’ the rescued humpback whale confirmed dead
stories.summary: A humpback whale nicknamed 'Timmy,' previously rescued, has been confirmed dead after its body was found off the coast of Denmark.

stories.title: Is a Chinese invasion of Taiwan imminent?
stories.summary: The article examines rising tensions over Taiwan amid the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, the first US presidential visit to China in nearly a decade. China claims Taiwan as its territory while the US maintains military support and diplomatic ties with the island, which has developed into a thriving democracy despite lacking formal recognition from most countries.

stories.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in Congo, Uganda a global health emergency
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a global health emergency. The UN health agency reported 80 suspected deaths and warned the outbreak could spread to neighboring countries, noting no approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for this strain.

stories.title: A Port Kembla nuclear submarine base would ‘place a massive target on our backs’, NSW labour union warns
stories.summary: The South Coast Labour Council in Australia has warned that establishing a nuclear submarine base at Port Kembla, a Wollongong suburb in New South Wales, would make the area a military target. The concern follows the release of previously secret documents identifying Port Kembla as the preferred east coast base for AUKUS nuclear-powered submarines.

stories.title: Bloomberg reports tanker resumes voyage after US detention
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported that a large tanker carrying two million barrels of Iraqi crude oil resumed its voyage toward Vietnam after being detained for several days by US forces in the Gulf of Oman. The Financial Times separately reported that daily shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped dramatically amid ongoing regional conflict.

stories.title: Middle East live: USS Ford returns from Iran war after longest deployment since Vietnam
stories.summary: The USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, returned to Virginia after a 326-day deployment to the Middle East, its longest since the Vietnam War era. The carrier was dispatched ahead of the Iran war and also conducted operations in the Caribbean, including involvement in the capture of Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro.

stories.title: India, Netherlands elevating ties to strategic partnership, says PM Modi
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that India and the Netherlands are elevating their bilateral relationship to a strategic partnership. The two countries signed multiple agreements to enhance cooperation across various sectors.

stories.title: Flag with portraits of thousands prisoners of war and missing soldiers unfurled in Kropyvnytskyi
stories.summary: In the Ukrainian city of Kropyvnytskyi, participants unfurled a large flag bearing portraits of thousands of Ukrainian prisoners of war and soldiers missing in action currently held in Russian captivity.

stories.title: Move over K-beauty, Thailand is the next big thing in aesthetics
stories.summary: Thai dermatologist Dr. Dissapong Panithaporn notes a shift in Asian beauty trends away from plastic surgery and fillers toward natural skin preservation. Younger consumers in their mid-twenties are increasingly prioritizing longevity, prevention, and preservation of skin health rather than correction, positioning Thailand as a rising force in aesthetics.

stories.title: Russian envoy supports Beijing’s stance on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Russian envoy Mikhail Ulyanov expressed support for China's position that a permanent ceasefire is needed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi stated that resolving tensions in the strait requires a comprehensive ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Ronda Rousey vs Gina Carano fight: Rousey wins with a 17-second submission
stories.summary: Ronda Rousey defeated Gina Carano with her signature armbar submission hold just 17 seconds into their bout.

stories.title: Late-night blast, fireball near Beit Shemesh rattles jittery residents
stories.summary: A large explosion and fireball near the Israeli city of Beit Shemesh alarmed local residents. A defense firm later stated the blast was a pre-planned experiment that had been coordinated with authorities.

stories.title: The Palestinian Authority is reinforcing and institutionalizing notorious 'pay-for-slay' policy
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority is reportedly reinforcing its "pay-for-slay" policy, which provides payments to imprisoned militants and their families. A Palestinian Authority court ruling allegedly favored a terrorist prisoner whose salary under the program had been suspended.

stories.title: Hong Kong police to prosecute 7th suspect in 1999 murder, seeking 8th
stories.summary: Hong Kong police announced they will prosecute a 57-year-old man surnamed Lin for murder in connection with the 1999 killing of newspaper vendor Ho Wai-ha in Sham Shui Po. Lin, the seventh suspect in the case, was handed over by Shenzhen authorities and is accused of recruiting attackers and arranging a vehicle. Police are seeking an eighth suspect.

stories.title: Venezuela hands over to the United States former minister and Maduro frontman Alex Saab
stories.summary: Venezuela deported Colombian businessman Alex Saab to the United States on Saturday, where he arrived at Opa-locka airport in Miami-Dade County escorted by DEA agents. Saab, considered former President Nicolás Maduro's main financial operator, served as minister of Industry and National Production until January 2026 and was among the most wanted figures by US justice.

stories.title: ‘Feels like an illusion’: inside post-Maduro Venezuela’s bewildering new era
stories.summary: Four months after a U.S. military raid ordered by President Trump, Venezuela is experiencing a political transition following the departure of Nicolás Maduro's government. Residents describe a mix of hope and trepidation amid the upheaval, with some neighborhoods still bearing physical damage from the operation.

stories.title: Will Gulf states find new oil pipelines fast enough to reduce Hormuz reliance?
stories.summary: An analysis examines whether Gulf states can develop alternative oil pipeline routes quickly enough to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz. The report notes that Iran's ability to pressure its neighbors through the strategic waterway remains high for the foreseeable future.

stories.title: Tehran asserts sovereignty over Strait of Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: Iranian Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref declared that Iran would no longer permit the passage of military equipment intended for its adversaries through the Strait of Hormuz. Aref said Tehran had previously allowed such shipments but would assert its sovereignty over the waterway going forward.

stories.title: Republican Senator Bill Cassidy pays the price for voting to convict Trump
stories.summary: US Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana lost his Republican primary re-election bid after President Trump and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. campaigned against him. Cassidy was targeted for being one of seven Republican senators who voted to convict Trump on charges of inciting the January 6, 2021 insurrection.

stories.title: US Centcom says 78 vessels redirected under Iran blockade
stories.summary: US Central Command reported that 78 commercial vessels had been redirected and four disabled as part of enforcement of President Trump's blockade on ships traveling to and from Iran through the Strait of Hormuz. Regional tensions have remained elevated since US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Israel says military at highest readiness level for possible Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli media outlet Yedioth Ahronoth reported that Israeli officials believe the military is at its highest readiness level for a possible resumption of fighting with Iran. Israeli and US officials are reportedly continuing senior-level coordination as assessments suggest Iran has restored part of its missile capabilities.

stories.title: Melbourne-US Qantas flight diverted after man bites crew member
stories.summary: A Melbourne-to-Dallas Qantas flight was diverted to Papeete, French Polynesia, after a disruptive male passenger reportedly bit a flight attendant. Fellow passengers restrained the man before the aircraft landed. No serious injuries were reported among the crew.

stories.title: ‘A place for everybody’: Stockholm to open its first publicly run sauna
stories.summary: Stockholm is set to open its first publicly run sauna, addressing long waiting lists at the Swedish capital's private member clubs. The city aims to create an accessible bathing facility for residents and visitors alike, unlike other Nordic countries where public saunas are more widely available.

stories.title: China launches new war on deserts with technology tested on far side of the moon
stories.summary: China has launched desertification-prevention projects in Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region using technology previously tested on the far side of the moon. The Chinese Academy of Sciences' Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography initiated projects for sand control, wind erosion management, and salinity reduction to build ecological barriers and safeguard food security.

stories.title: China offers Southeast Asia clear nuclear power advantages
stories.summary: Several Southeast Asian nations are pursuing nuclear power development, with Vietnam signing an agreement with Russia for the Ninh Thuan 1 plant and the Philippines and Indonesia targeting operational reactors by the early 2030s. Malaysia, Thailand, and Singapore are studying small modular reactors. The article argues China offers clear advantages as a nuclear technology provider for the region.

stories.title: Iran warns it is ready for renewed war if talks fail
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran remains prepared to resume direct military confrontation with the United States if negotiations fail to produce outcomes acceptable to Tehran. He also argued that the conflict involving the US and Israel is causing growing economic consequences inside the United States.

stories.title: Hong Kong man, 38, killed after motorcycle crashes into fallen tree
stories.summary: A 38-year-old motorcyclist died in Hong Kong's New Territories after crashing into a fallen tree on Yuen Shin Road in Tai Po while heading toward Sha Tin. Police received the accident report at 10:32 p.m. on Saturday. The rider reportedly failed to brake in time before the collision.

stories.title: Every window a solar panel: Australia-China joint venture to set up in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Australian solar technology firm ClearVue Technologies will establish a joint venture with Chinese vacuum-glass maker LandVac in Hong Kong to produce power-generating glass for building facades. The partnership aims to leverage mainland China's manufacturing capabilities to provide affordable solar glass for commercial buildings amid rising energy prices.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s iconic Bank of China Tower opens in 1990 – SCMP archive
stories.summary: The article revisits the May 1990 opening of the Bank of China Tower at No. 1 Garden Road in Hong Kong, which became the territory's tallest building at the time. Political, financial, and commercial leaders from Hong Kong and China attended the ceremony, setting aside recent diplomatic tensions for the occasion.

stories.title: US Treasury allows sanctions waiver on Russia’s seaborne oil to lapse
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury allowed a sanctions waiver on Russia's seaborne oil exports to lapse. The waiver had been intended to ease oil supply shortages and price spikes linked to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Pakistan PM says second round of Washington-Tehran talks could bring peace
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed optimism that a second round of direct talks between Washington and Tehran could lead to a peace agreement. Sharif said Pakistan continues to play a mediation role and maintains the trust of all parties involved, including Iran, the U.S., and Gulf states.

stories.title: Iran allegedly behind Canada attacks on US consulate, synagogue
stories.summary: Canadian and U.S. law enforcement allege that a suspect named al-Saadi, working on behalf of an Iranian proxy, claimed responsibility for attacks on a U.S. consulate and a synagogue in Canada. Al-Saadi reportedly told an undercover officer that his associates carried out the attacks.

stories.title: Israeli settlers force Palestinians to abandon village in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Residents of the village of Yanoun in the occupied West Bank say repeated attacks and harassment by Israeli settlers have forced Palestinians to abandon the area. The village, once home to more than 200 residents, is now largely deserted, with settlers reportedly taking control of over 16 square kilometres of surrounding land.

stories.title: With an Iranian proxy commander arrested for attacks in the UK, will Starmer respond? - analysis
stories.summary: A suspect identified as al-Saad was arrested in connection with orchestrating attacks in the United Kingdom on behalf of an Iranian proxy. He allegedly posted propaganda videos claiming responsibility for 18 attacks across Europe, most of which occurred in London over a two-month period.

stories.title: CNN says Trump faces growing dilemma over Iran strategy
stories.summary: CNN reported that U.S. President Donald Trump faces a policy dilemma on Iran after both military pressure and diplomatic efforts failed to yield clear results. Trump's administration is reportedly divided between officials advocating renewed military action and those favouring continued negotiations with Tehran.

stories.title: Venezuela deports Maduro ally Alex Saab to US
stories.summary: Venezuela deported Maduro ally Alex Saab to the United States. Saab had fallen out of favor with the new Venezuelan administration that took power following Maduro's ouster and capture by US forces in January.

stories.title: Israeli strikes intensify across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: More than 30 Israeli strikes, including air strikes near Tyre and artillery shelling in border towns such as Qlailah, Hanine, and Majdal Zoun, were reported across southern Lebanon. Additional attacks hit Yohmor and Arnoun in the Nabatieh region, despite an extended ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: 30,000 people evacuated in Germany due to World War II bomb
stories.summary: Approximately 30,000 residents were evacuated from the southwestern German city of Pforzheim after a World War II-era bomb was discovered. Authorities ordered the evacuation as a precautionary measure while the device was handled.

stories.title: Comoros suspends fuel price hikes after deadly protests
stories.summary: The Comoros government suspended planned fuel price increases following deadly protests and unrest. The demonstrations were triggered by rising costs linked to broader economic pressures from the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Lights, camera, Bangaranga: Highlights from Eurovision
stories.summary: Bulgarian singer Dara won the Eurovision Song Contest 2026, while Ukraine set a record for the longest note ever sung at the competition. Israeli performer Noam Bettan finished in second place.

stories.title: Indonesia pushes back after Chinese business group complains tougher rules hurt investors
stories.summary: Chinese businesses in Indonesia issued a public warning to President Prabowo Subianto that tightened regulations are undermining investor confidence, particularly in the nickel sector. Indonesian ministers pushed back, emphasizing national sovereignty over natural resources while expressing openness to dialogue.

stories.title: What do China’s plans for ‘comprehensive’ new AI law mean for future of technology?
stories.summary: China confirmed it is drafting a comprehensive law on artificial intelligence, as outlined in the State Council's annual legislative work plan. Industry observers said the move reflects China's accumulated practical experience with AI governance and its effort to accelerate regulatory frameworks.

stories.title: Fresh concepts lift Hong Kong retail property as tourists and consumers return
stories.summary: Hong Kong's retail property market is showing gradual recovery as consumer spending and tourist confidence return. Analysts noted a shift toward more diversified tenant mixes focused on experiential retail, rather than a return to previous peak rental levels.

stories.title: Rwandan genocide suspect Kabuga, 93, dies in custody
stories.summary: Lucien Kabuga, a 93-year-old suspect in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, died in custody at a UN court facility in The Hague on Saturday. His death was confirmed by the international tribunal.

stories.title: Palestinians, including children, arrested in Jerusalem’s Old City
stories.summary: Israeli police detained several Palestinians, including children, in Jerusalem's Old City following confrontations involving Israeli settlers and residents. Officials said a 16-year-old with medical conditions was detained after being attacked by settlers, and a 64-year-old shopkeeper was also arrested.

stories.title: Former mayor shot dead in central Colombia during election campaign
stories.summary: Former mayor Rogers Devia was shot dead by gunmen in the rural area of Cubarral in central Colombia during an election campaign. Cubarral is located roughly 170 kilometers south of Bogotá, and Devia had governed the city from 2020 to 2023.

stories.title: UK deploys anti-drone system on RAF jets in Middle East
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced the deployment of the Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS), a low-cost anti-drone system, on RAF Eurofighter Typhoon jets operating in the Middle East. The system is designed to destroy drone targets at a fraction of the cost of conventional missiles.

stories.title: Ukraine tracks every Shahed drone that flies through Belarusian airspace, says Brovdi
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces stated they are tracking every Shahed-type drone that enters or transits through Belarusian airspace. The monitoring effort is led by commander Brovdi as part of Ukraine's broader drone defense operations.

stories.title: Amid reports Iran war could resume, Trump posts image warning of ‘calm before the storm’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted an image referencing the "calm before the storm" amid reports that hostilities with Iran could resume. The IDF said it intercepted Hezbollah rockets aimed at troops in southern Lebanon, while Hezbollah claimed a drone swarm attack on an IDF base in northern Israel.

stories.title: In a world of chaos, China signals that stability is possible
stories.summary: Three recent international polls suggest a growing global narrative around economic stability and direction. A CNN poll found 76% of Americans view high prices as their most serious economic problem, with broader data pointing to shifting public sentiment about national trajectories.

stories.title: Lilian Gandelman: How the ‘girl from Ipanema’ became the woman from Tel Aviv
stories.summary: The article profiles Lilian Gandelman, a Brazilian-born lawyer living in Tel Aviv who also navigates life as an amputee. She is engaged in a personal mission to educate Israelis and change attitudes about disability.

stories.title: IDF reservist dismissed after allegedly vandalizing, damaging Palestinians' property while off duty
stories.summary: An Israeli Defense Forces reservist was dismissed from reserve duty after allegedly vandalizing and damaging Palestinian property while off duty. The reservist's weapon was confiscated following the incident.

stories.title: Eurovision final begins amid protests over Israel’s participation
stories.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest final took place under tight security amid ongoing criticism of Israel's participation due to its military actions in Gaza. Spain, the Netherlands, Ireland, Iceland, and Slovenia boycotted the event, and pro-Palestinian demonstrations were held outside the venue.

stories.title: Prosecutors seek death penalty for shooter in 2025 Capital Jewish Museum attack
stories.summary: Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty for Elias Rodriguez, the suspect in the 2025 Capital Jewish Museum shooting. The attorney's office filed a notice of intent stating that the suspect committed the act with substantial planning and premeditation.

stories.title: Tunisians protest against Saied over arrests and economic strain
stories.summary: Hundreds of Tunisians protested in the capital Tunis on Saturday against President Kais Saied, accusing him of undermining freedoms and worsening economic and social conditions in the country.

stories.title: Tunisians rally amid economic crisis and political arrests
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters marched through Tunis to denounce worsening economic conditions and a government crackdown on political dissent, including recent arrests of opposition figures.

stories.title: 'Double standards': Iran criticises US over Francesca Albanese sanctions case
stories.summary: Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi criticized the United States after a federal court temporarily suspended sanctions against UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese. Gharibabadi accused Washington of double standards, saying U.S. human rights commitments end when accountability over Gaza is raised.

stories.title: Brazil's Lula tied with Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in second-round in Datafolha poll
stories.summary: A Datafolha poll released Saturday indicated that a hypothetical second-round presidential runoff in Brazil between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro would result in a statistical tie ahead of October elections.

stories.title: Report: Just 3% of Israeli ninth graders met science requirements in latest tests
stories.summary: A report found that only 3% of Israeli ninth graders met science proficiency requirements on the latest standardized tests. Israel's education minister alleged the results were leaked for political reasons without addressing why the science scores had been withheld from previously published exam data.

stories.title: Romania finds unexploded projectile in village near Ukraine border
stories.summary: Romania's defence ministry reported that an unexploded projectile was discovered on a property in southeastern Romania near the country's border with Ukraine on Saturday. Romania is a member of both the European Union and NATO.

stories.title: Spanish star Javier Bardem says 'narrative changing' on Gaza
stories.summary: Spanish actor Javier Bardem stated at the Cannes Film Festival that the narrative around the Gaza conflict is changing. Speaking while promoting his film "The Beloved," Bardem said his support for Palestine has not negatively affected his career.

stories.title: Hezbollah launches drone swarm at Israeli military target
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it launched a swarm of attack drones targeting an Israeli military site in northern Israel and carried out over a dozen additional attacks on Israeli forces. The Israeli military reported that one officer was killed in southern Lebanon when a Hezbollah drone detonated near troops.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s MPF authority flags fraudulent certificates in early pension payouts
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority is intensifying efforts to detect fraudulent medical certificates used to make early withdrawals from pension accounts. The crackdown follows reports by two medical groups to police about suspected fake certificates. The authority's online platform has recently flagged several suspected fraud cases.

stories.title: Woman, 76, became China’s oldest mum giving birth to twins at 60 after enduring family tragedies
stories.summary: Sheng Hailin, a 76-year-old woman from Anhui province in central China, has gained renewed attention after a photographic series about her life won an international award. She gave birth to twins at age 60 after her only daughter and son-in-law died of carbon monoxide poisoning in 2009. She now has nearly one million social media followers.

stories.title: Iran condemns Israeli killing of Hamas commander and his family in Gaza
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry condemned Israel's killing of Hamas commander Izz al-Din al-Haddad in a strike on Gaza City's Remal neighbourhood, calling it a "terrorist act." Hamas said the strike also killed civilians, including al-Haddad's wife and daughter.

stories.title: Land convoy sets out from Libya as part of Gaza flotilla effort
stories.summary: A land convoy of approximately 200 participants from 25 countries departed from Libya as part of a broader Gaza flotilla effort. The convoy includes 20 mobile homes, seven ambulances or medical transport vehicles, and other vehicles.

stories.title: FIFA says held positive talks with Iran's FA ahead of World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA reported holding positive talks with Iran's Football Association regarding Iran's participation in the 2026 World Cup. The discussions addressed visa concerns related to U.S. and Canadian entry restrictions for the tournament.

stories.title: Five arsonists working for Russians detained in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service and National Police detained five individuals in the Cherkasy region accused of carrying out arson attacks on behalf of Russian intelligence services. The suspects were identified as agents of Russian special services.

stories.title: Bulgaria wins Eurovision Song Contest, amid protests over Gaza
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest held in Vienna. The event was overshadowed by protests and boycotts by several countries objecting to Israel's participation amid the ongoing Gaza war.

stories.title: Bulgaria wins 2026 Eurovision, Israel lands a nail-biting second
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the 2025 Eurovision Song Contest with singer Dara's anthem "Bangaranga," securing the country's first-ever title. Israel's Noam Bettan finished a close second with "Michelle" after strong televoting. The contest was marked by protests and boycotts over Israel's participation.

stories.title: Iraq’s new PM Ali al-Zaidi formally takes over
stories.summary: Ali al-Zaidi formally assumed office as Iraq's new prime minister in Baghdad, pledging to pursue reforms during his tenure.

stories.title: Israel’s Noam Bettan finishes second at Eurovision as Bulgaria takes the win
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest held in Vienna. Israel's Noam Bettan finished second with his song "Michelle," placing third in the televote and marking Israel's second consecutive runner-up finish.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran plans tolls in Hormuz; Trump warns of ‘very bad time’
stories.summary: Iran announced plans to reveal measures related to the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating regional tensions. U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran of a "very bad time," while Israeli strikes continued in Lebanon and Gaza, causing dozens of casualties.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1543: 37 countries back a tribunal for Russia’s war leadership — the “point of no return” arrives
stories.summary: Thirty-seven countries have formally agreed to advance the creation of a special tribunal to prosecute Russian leadership for the decision to wage war against Ukraine. Officials described the agreement as a "point of no return" in accountability efforts on day 1,543 of the conflict.

stories.title: Tens of thousands march in London in separate immigration, pro‑Palestinian protests
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people participated in separate immigration and pro-Palestinian protests in London on Saturday. Some demonstrators chanted "Death to the IDF," language that police have previously cited as grounds for arrests when directed at Jewish individuals.

stories.title: FIA to probe agency raid on jewellery shop in Karachi’s Sarafa Bazaar
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency Director General Dr. Usman Anwar ordered a probe into a raid on a jewellery shop in Karachi's Sarafa Bazaar on May 15, 2026, targeting alleged silver smuggling. The FIA alleged that 163 kilograms of silver were unaccounted for during the operation.

stories.title: Bulgaria’s Dara wins Eurovision contest, beating out Israel for top spot
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest for the first time, with performer Dara claiming victory at the 70th edition of the competition. Israel finished in second place after receiving a large public vote. The final was overshadowed by a boycott from five countries over Israel's military offensive in Gaza.

stories.title: Boycott over Israel takes some glitz off Eurovision final
stories.summary: Five countries, including Spain, boycotted the Eurovision final in protest over Israel's war in Gaza, diminishing some of the event's usual spectacle.

stories.title: Eurovision abandoned its values over Gaza, and lost me as a lifelong fan
stories.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest final proceeded amid protests and boycotts by several countries over Israel's participation, linked to the ongoing war in Gaza. The article reflects a personal perspective from a longtime viewer who chose not to watch this year.

stories.title: Defense products in Europe have become more than 50% more expensive in two years — Estonian Defense Minister
stories.summary: Estonian Defense Minister reported that defense product prices in Europe have risen by more than 50% over the past two years. The increases are attributed to heightened NATO defense spending across European countries.

stories.title: Defense products in Europe have become more than 50% more expensive in two years — Estonian Defense Minister
stories.summary: Estonian Defense Minister reported that defense product prices in Europe have risen by more than 50% over the past two years. The increase is attributed to heightened NATO defense spending across European member states.

stories.title: ‘They may draw racist maps, but we are the south’: thousands rally in Alabama for Black voting rights
stories.summary: Thousands of people gathered in Montgomery, Alabama, for the All Roads Lead to the South rally in support of Black voting rights. The demonstration was organized by a coalition of civic engagement groups in response to the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision, which significantly weakened protections under the Voting Rights Act.

stories.title: Bolivia launches early-morning crackdown on roadblocks outside La Paz
stories.summary: Bolivia's government under President Rodrigo Paz deployed approximately 3,500 soldiers and police in an early-morning operation to clear roadblocks set up by protesters outside La Paz who are demanding his resignation.

stories.title: Iran conflict reshapes energy markets as US gas demand surges
stories.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration reported that U.S. industrial natural gas consumption hit a record 23.6 billion cubic feet per day in 2025, with demand expected to remain elevated through 2027. The Iran conflict has intensified disruptions across global oil markets and tightened energy supplies worldwide.

stories.title: War update: 195 clashes on front line, Ukrainian forces neutralize 60 occupiers in Pokrovsk direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 195 combat clashes with Russian troops along the front line on May 16. The Pokrovsk direction in eastern Ukraine was the most active sector, with 23 Russian attacks and 60 Russian soldiers reported neutralized.

stories.title: USS Gerald R Ford returns after longest deployment since Vietnam
stories.summary: The USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, returned to Naval Station Norfolk in Virginia after an 11-month deployment — the longest for a U.S. carrier since the Vietnam War era. Approximately 5,000 sailors came home after operations spanning the Mediterranean and Caribbean linked to Iran and Venezuela.

stories.title: Gofman accuses AG acting in bad faith in case against his appointment as Mossad head
stories.summary: David Gofman accused Israel's Attorney General Baharav-Miara of acting in bad faith in legal proceedings challenging his appointment as head of the Mossad. The attorney general raised concerns about meetings between Gofman and a senior Mossad official that may have been intended to influence the case's outcome.

stories.title: Hezbollah drone strike videos show evolving tactics against Israel
stories.summary: BBC Verify analyzed dozens of videos showing Hezbollah using fibre-optic guided drones in attacks against Israeli targets, revealing evolving tactical methods by the Lebanese armed group.

stories.title: Seven injured as driver in Italian city runs over pedestrians
stories.summary: A driver in his 30s ran over pedestrians on a sidewalk in the northern Italian city of Modena on Saturday, injuring seven people, four of them seriously. Mayor Massimo Mezzetti said the driver appeared to aim for the sidewalk and was seen holding a knife afterward, though he did not stab anyone.

stories.title: German police assault protesters at Nakba anniversary rally
stories.summary: German police used force and pepper spray against demonstrators in Berlin as thousands gathered to mark the 78th anniversary of the Nakba, the displacement of Palestinians in 1948.

stories.title: Whale that was rescued after stranded in Germany found dead in Denmark
stories.summary: A whale nicknamed "Timmy" by German media, which had been rescued after becoming stranded on a sandbank in Germany on March 23, was later found dead in Denmark.

stories.title: Zelensky instructs MFA to engage Moldova over simplified Russian citizenship for Transnistria residents
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky directed Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to coordinate with Moldova after Russia simplified citizenship procedures for residents of the unrecognized Transnistria region in Moldova.

stories.title: Pakistan, Iran push trade ties during Tehran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi made an unannounced visit to Tehran, meeting Iranian counterpart Eskandar Momeni. The two sides agreed to ease border trade procedures, boost cross-border transit and goods exchange, and discussed opening new crossing points.

stories.title: Zelensky: If Russia's war machine survives, its next strikes may be against Europe
stories.summary: President Zelensky warned that if Russia's war machine survives the current conflict, its next strikes could target Europe. He emphasized Ukraine's efforts to pursue sanctions cutting Russia's global connections that sustain the war.

stories.title: Pakistani minister arrives in Tehran to ‘facilitate’ US-Iran peace talks: media
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran reportedly to help facilitate ongoing US-Iran peace talks. Islamabad has been actively mediating between Washington and Tehran in nuclear negotiations.

stories.title: What raising my children in Israel is teaching me - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on raising children in Israel, tying personal experience to national pride around Independence Day and Jerusalem Day. The author expresses optimism about the next generation's role in shaping the country.

stories.title: Dog owned by Palestinian family beaten by Israeli settler now stable after severe bleeding
stories.summary: An Israeli settler was filmed violently beating a dog named Lucy belonging to a Palestinian family in the occupied West Bank village of Atara. The dog suffered serious head injuries but has since stabilized after receiving treatment, according to Haaretz.

stories.title: Eurovision Director: No plans for Russia to return to contest
stories.summary: Eurovision Director Martin Green stated at a press conference ahead of the 2026 final in Vienna that there are no plans for Russia to return to the song contest.

stories.title: Shell-shocked: California man arrested for attempting to traffic wild turtles
stories.summary: A California man named Donald Do was arrested on federal wildlife-trafficking charges for allegedly attempting to export 292 loggerhead musk turtles to Taiwan. Authorities say Do falsely claimed the turtles were captive-bred when they had been poached from the wild in Florida.

stories.title: Minister chalks up CSS failure rate to lack of preparation, competitive nature of exam
stories.summary: Pakistan's Minister-in-Charge of the Establishment Division, Senator Ahad Khan Cheema, attributed the high failure rate in Central Superior Services examinations to inadequate academic preparation and the competitive nature of the test. PPP legislator Sehar Kamran had raised questions about the examination system's alignment with international standards.

stories.title: World on the cusp of new global order, Iran speaker Ghalibaf says
stories.summary: Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf declared that the world is on the verge of a new global order, citing shifting international dynamics. He credited what he called Iran's "70-day resistance" with accelerating the transformation and asserted that the future belongs to the Global South.

stories.title: UN chief welcomes Lebanon ceasefire extension amid ongoing attacks
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres welcomed a 45-day extension of the ceasefire in Lebanon, reached through US-mediated talks in Washington between Israel and Lebanon. Guterres reaffirmed UN support for efforts to end hostilities and alleviate civilian suffering.

stories.title: Forty-two pupils missing after Nigeria school attack, lawmaker says
stories.summary: At least 42 Nigerian schoolchildren remained missing on Saturday after suspected Islamist militants attacked a school in Borno state in northeastern Nigeria. A senator representing the area confirmed the figure.

stories.title: Is China becoming Europe’s top science partner amid an American brain drain?
stories.summary: As the United States experiences an outflow of researchers, China and Europe are deepening scientific collaboration and absorbing American talent. Max Planck Society president Patrick Cramer noted massive shifts in the global flow of scientists driven by geopolitical changes.

stories.title: Israel's Noam Bettan prepares for the Eurovision final
stories.summary: Israeli singer Noam Bettan advanced to the Eurovision Song Contest final after performing in the first semifinal on Tuesday night, finishing among the top 10 qualifiers.

stories.title: Tens of thousands march in London in separate immigration, pro‑Palestinian protests
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people marched in London in separate protests focused on immigration and Palestinian solidarity. London's Metropolitan Police deployed approximately 4,000 officers in what they described as their largest public order operation in years.

stories.title: Two presidential campaign staffers killed in Colombia as elections near
stories.summary: Two staffers working on presidential campaigns in Colombia were killed as the country approaches its May elections to choose a successor to President Gustavo Petro. Colombia's rights office warned that the violence could impede citizens' exercise of political rights.

stories.title: Europe must strengthen its offensive capabilities – Czech security analyst
stories.summary: A Czech security analyst argued that European countries must strengthen both their defensive and offensive military capabilities. The analyst said enhanced offensive capacity could serve as a deterrent against potential acts of aggression.

stories.title: The innovation bridge: A new paradigm for the US-Israel alliance - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel should reposition itself as a vital innovation partner for the United States across sectors including AI, cybersecurity, defense technology, energy, and life sciences.

stories.title: Capt. Maoz Israel Recanati killed during combat in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Captain Maoz Israel Recanati, a platoon commander in the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion, was killed during combat operations in southern Lebanon. He was posthumously promoted from lieutenant to captain.

stories.title: Tens of thousands turn out for UK far-right rally, counter protest
stories.summary: Tens of thousands gathered in London for a far-right march organized by Tommy Robinson and a counter-demonstration coinciding with a pro-Palestinian Nakba Day protest. London's Metropolitan Police deployed approximately 4,000 officers to manage both events.

stories.title: Bannu police kill five militants after launching operation in district
stories.summary: Police in Bannu district, Pakistan, killed five militants within 24 hours during "Operation Intiqam-e-Shuhada," including a commander linked to a recent suicide attack on the Fateh Khel police post that killed 15 officers.

stories.title: IN-SPACe leads Indian space-tech delegation at Space Meetings Veneto 2026
stories.summary: India's space agency IN-SPACe led a delegation of nine Indian space-technology companies to Space Meetings Veneto 2026 in Venice, Italy, where three companies signed collaboration agreements with the Italian Space Industry Study Group.

stories.title: Spanish actor Javier Bardem says ‘narrative changing’ on Gaza and Palestine
stories.summary: Spanish actor Javier Bardem stated that his public criticism of Israel's military campaign in Gaza has not hurt his career, saying he is receiving more work than ever. At the February Academy Awards, Bardem called for a free Palestine from the stage.

stories.title: Israel names IAI CEO Boaz Levy Chairman in first for state-owned defense company
stories.summary: Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz and Government Companies Authority Minister Dudi Amsalem appointed Israel Aerospace Industries CEO Boaz Levy as the company's chairman, marking the first time a sitting CEO has held that role at a state-owned defense firm.

stories.title: The time has come for US-Israel partnership 2.0 - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece calls for a reimagined U.S.-Israel partnership focused on generating direct strategic value rather than relying primarily on historical commitment and security interests.

stories.title: Israel probes several settler attacks, troop misconduct, as West Bank assaults continue
stories.summary: Israeli authorities launched investigations into several settler attacks in the occupied West Bank, including the torching of Palestinian vehicles and a reservist filmed dragging a bound detainee. Separately, the IDF confirmed a Palestinian man was killed near Jenin during an ongoing military operation.

stories.title: European countries in talks with Tehran for Hormuz transit: Report
stories.summary: European countries are reportedly in talks with Tehran regarding transit through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has largely blocked since the outbreak of war with the US and Israel on February 28. A fragile ceasefire has been in place since April 8.

stories.title: Iran state TV says European countries in talks with Tehran for Hormuz transit
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported that European countries are engaged in negotiations with Tehran over transit rights through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has largely blocked shipping through the strategically vital waterway since the outbreak of war with the United States and Israel on February 28.

stories.title: Ukraine and partners prepares important foreign policy decisions – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine, together with France, the United Kingdom, and Germany, is preparing important foreign policy decisions. No specific details about the nature of the decisions were disclosed.

stories.title: Bangladesh arrests ex-soldier after attack plot threat
stories.summary: Bangladeshi police arrested 23-year-old former soldier Mohammad Rahed Hossain Mahed near the Indian border in the northeastern district of Moulvibazar in connection with an attack plot threat.

stories.title: Taiwan says it is an independent nation after Trump arms sale remarks
stories.summary: Taiwan publicly reaffirmed its status as a "sovereign and independent" nation following remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump related to arms sales to the island. The statement underscored Taipei's position on its self-governance amid ongoing cross-strait tensions.

stories.title: Palestinian Ministry says Israeli forces kill man in West Bank camp
stories.summary: The Palestinian Health Ministry in Ramallah identified a man killed by Israeli forces in Jenin Camp in the occupied West Bank as 34-year-old Nour al-Din Kamal Hassan Fayyad.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 11, wound more than 60
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on Gaza City and northern parts of the Gaza Strip killed at least 11 Palestinians and wounded more than 60 others over a 24-hour period, according to hospital sources in Gaza.

stories.title: FIFA says held positive talks with Iran ahead of World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom held what he described as a constructive meeting with Iranian Football Association president Mehdi Taj regarding Iran's participation in the upcoming World Cup. The tournament is scheduled to take place this summer across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

stories.title: Bolivian army attempts to clear roads after 11 days of protests
stories.summary: Bolivian military police moved to clear road blockades that had persisted for 11 days of protests, arresting demonstrators and deploying tear gas. The army's intervention aimed to restore transit on key routes disrupted by the unrest.

stories.title: Short-term rain forecast for Ukraine on Sunday, temperatures up to +23°C
stories.summary: Ukrainian weather forecasters predicted short-term rain and occasional thunderstorms across most regions of Ukraine on Sunday, May 17. Daytime temperatures were expected to reach up to 23°C.

stories.title: One dead in Comoros as clashes erupt over rising fuel prices
stories.summary: One person was killed and five others injured on the Comorian island of Anjouan during clashes between protesters and security forces on May 16. The unrest was triggered by rising fuel prices and has spread across the Comoros archipelago.

stories.title: At least eight injured in car ramming in Italian city of Modena
stories.summary: At least eight people were injured in the Italian city of Modena after a driver allegedly rammed a car into pedestrians and stabbed a bystander who attempted to intervene. The driver was arrested, and authorities are investigating the motive, including a possible terrorism link.

stories.title: Thousands protest at Eurovision final as five countries boycott over Israel
stories.summary: Spain, Ireland, Iceland, Slovenia, and the Netherlands boycotted the Eurovision Song Contest final in protest against Israel's participation amid the ongoing war in Gaza. Thousands of demonstrators gathered outside the venue to voice opposition.

stories.title: Maldivian military diver dead while searching for bodies of four Italian divers
stories.summary: A Maldivian military diver died during search operations to recover the bodies of four Italian divers who went missing in underwater caves in the Maldives.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF strikes nearly 100 Hezbollah targets, kills two terrorists near rocket launch site
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces struck nearly 100 Hezbollah targets and reported killing two operatives near a rocket launch site. Hezbollah fired several projectiles toward Israeli territory over the preceding 24 hours, including explosive drones and mortar shells.

stories.title: Over UAH 30B in additional grants allocated to support frontline communities – Kuleba
stories.summary: Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister Kuleba announced that more than 30 billion hryvnias in additional grants are planned for 2026 to support communities in frontline territories. Over 6.6 million people currently live in the affected areas.

stories.title: Fifa expects Iran at World Cup despite visa concerns
stories.summary: FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafstrom expressed confidence that Iran will participate in the 2026 World Cup after meeting with Iran FA president Mehdi Taj. Uncertainty remains over U.S. visa arrangements after Taj was denied entry to Canada over alleged IRGC links.

stories.title: Litton's rearguard ton propels Bangladesh to 278 in Pakistan Test
stories.summary: In the second Test between Bangladesh and Pakistan in Sylhet, Litton Das scored 126 to help Bangladesh reach 278 in their first innings after a top-order collapse. Pakistan reached 21-0 at stumps, trailing 1-0 in the series.

stories.title: Rwandan genocide suspect Kabuga dies in custody in The Hague at age 91
stories.summary: Félicien Kabuga, a 91-year-old Rwandan genocide suspect accused of financing the 1994 mass killing of Tutsis, died in custody at a hospital in The Hague. A UN court had declared him unfit to stand trial in 2023, three decades after the genocide that killed 800,000 people.

stories.title: France's justice minister to visit Algeria amid diplomatic thaw
stories.summary: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin is set to visit Algeria as part of a diplomatic thaw between Paris and Algiers. Discussions are expected to cover bilateral cooperation and the case of jailed French journalist Christophe Gleizes.

stories.title: IDF infantry platoon commander killed by Hezbollah drone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces identified Captain Maoz Israel Recanati, 24, as the platoon commander killed by a Hezbollah drone strike in southern Lebanon. The IDF said it struck over 100 Hezbollah targets over the weekend in response.

stories.title: “Gaza Sunbirds”: Film crew arrives by sea at Cannes Film Festival
stories.summary: The crew of "Gaza Sunbirds," a documentary about a Palestinian paracycling team of amputee athletes from Gaza, arrived symbolically by sea at the Cannes Film Festival for the film's screening.

stories.title: France arrests 6 over Palestinian flag on Eiffel Tower
stories.summary: French authorities arrested six people in connection with a large Palestinian flag being draped on the Eiffel Tower in Paris. The climate activist group Extinction Rebellion France claimed responsibility for the action.

stories.title: Can new Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions lead to another border clash?
stories.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan have resumed targeting each other along their shared border despite a March-mediated ceasefire pause, raising concerns about a potential escalation into another border clash.

stories.title: The little shop on Jaffa Street that captured old Jerusalem - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on the significance of a shop on Jaffa Street in Jerusalem as Jerusalem Day approaches, connecting the city's history to the aftermath of October 7 and the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed in south Lebanon, military says
stories.summary: Israel's military reported that a soldier was killed during combat operations in southern Lebanon on Saturday. The death brings the total Israeli military losses to 21 personnel since its war on Lebanon began in early March.

stories.title: Moldova reacts to Putin's decree simplifying Russian citizenship for Transnistria residents
stories.summary: Moldovan Prime Minister Alexandru Munteanu responded to a decree by President Putin simplifying Russian citizenship for residents of the unrecognized Transnistria region. Munteanu suggested the Kremlin's decision may be linked to efforts to recruit soldiers for the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Law Minister Tarar sees ‘no indication’ of 28th Amendment for now
stories.summary: Pakistani Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said he sees no current indication of a 28th Constitutional Amendment being introduced. He stated that any future amendment would require consensus-building and consultation with coalition partners.

stories.title: London police arrest 31 amid massive anti-migrant protest, smaller anti-Israel march
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police arrested 31 people during a large anti-migrant protest and a smaller anti-Israel march, deploying approximately 4,000 officers in one of its biggest operations in years. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer accused far-right figure Tommy Robinson of peddling hatred.

stories.title: In response to Trump, Taiwan says it is ‘sovereign and independent’
stories.summary: Taiwan reaffirmed its sovereignty and independence in response to remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump, stating it will maintain the status quo while seeking to deepen ties with Washington following a Trump–Xi Jinping meeting.

stories.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon day after ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Israel launched heavy airstrikes on southern Lebanon just one day after both sides agreed to extend the ceasefire by 45 days. The strikes fuelled further displacement and raised doubts about the durability of the truce.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Lebanon kill 18, wound 124 in 24 hours
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli strikes across the country killed 18 people and wounded 124 others over a 24-hour period. The bombardment continued despite ongoing hostilities across multiple areas of Lebanon.

stories.title: General Staff clarifies results of strike on Ryazan oil refinery
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff clarified the results of strikes carried out on the night of May 15 against the Ryazan oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region. The update provided additional details on damage to the refinery's infrastructure.

stories.title: Timmy, the stranded whale that captivated Germany, found dead in Denmark
stories.summary: A humpback whale nicknamed Timmy, which had been the subject of a rescue operation in Germany after beaching itself, was found dead near the Danish island of Anholt. Danish authorities confirmed the stranded whale was the same animal rescued two weeks earlier.

stories.title: Trump returns from China with stability and a stalemate
stories.summary: President Donald Trump returned from a two-day summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing with limited concrete results. The talks underscored that despite last year's trade war and subsequent detente, the US and China remain locked in their longstanding economic and strategic rivalry.

stories.title: Israeli settlers attack shops in Jerusalem’s Old City
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked shops along al-Wad Street in the Old City of occupied East Jerusalem on Saturday evening. The Jerusalem Governorate reported that settlers stormed commercial properties and vandalised their contents in the busy area.

stories.title: Germany stakes claim in new space race
stories.summary: German companies across the country are developing satellites and space applications as part of a growing commercial space sector. The industry is seen as increasingly important for both civilian and military purposes.

stories.title: Germany gets ahead in the new space race
stories.summary: German companies across the country are expanding into the satellite and space-applications industry. The sector is growing in strategic importance for both civilian and military purposes.

stories.title: Congolese report constant burials as deaths in new Ebola outbreak reach 80
stories.summary: An Ebola outbreak in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of Congo, has killed at least 80 people. Health officials have intensified emergency response measures amid fears of further spread. Residents report constant burials in affected communities.

stories.title: Occupiers attack Dnipropetrovsk region over 70 times, one killed, nine injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Dnipropetrovsk region in Ukraine more than 70 times on May 16, killing one person and injuring nine others, including two children, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Alleged drug queenpin Anmol remanded into police custody till May 22 in narcotics case
stories.summary: A judicial magistrate in Karachi remanded alleged drug queenpin Anmol, also known as Pinky, into police custody until May 22 in a narcotics case. She was arrested earlier in the week from her Karachi apartment and faces charges in at least 15 cases involving narcotics and weapons.

stories.title: At least eight dead, 25 injured in train collision that sparks bus fire in Thailand
stories.summary: A collision between a freight train and a bus in central Bangkok on Saturday killed at least eight people and injured more than 30. The crash occurred at a busy downtown intersection, and the bus caught fire following the impact.

stories.title: Police Peace Committee in Bannu launches operation against militants
stories.summary: The Police Peace Committee in Bannu, Pakistan, launched "Operation Revenge of the Martyrs" in response to rising militant violence in the district. Committee President Hazrat Ullah vowed operations against militants would continue with full force.

stories.title: Rising diesel costs from Iran war strain US school budgets
stories.summary: Rising diesel costs linked to the ongoing Iran war are straining school budgets across the United States. Higher fuel prices are increasing the cost of busing students and running generators. School officials warn the financial burden is unsustainable.

stories.title: Trump returns from China with stability and a stalemate
stories.summary: President Donald Trump returned from a visit to Beijing that yielded modest results but underscored a return to the familiar US-China economic and strategic standoff. The summit followed the extremes of last year's trade war, with both sides settling into a posture of stability without major breakthroughs.

stories.title: Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages on Sunday
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that no electricity consumption restrictions are planned for Sunday, May 17.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war is worth the economic pain. These rural voters agree
stories.summary: Rising fuel prices across the United States, now exceeding $4.50 per gallon, have followed the Trump administration's military conflict with Iran. Rural voters interviewed expressed support for the war despite the economic impact.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war is worth the economic pain. These rural voters agree
stories.summary: President Trump defended the Iran war as worth the economic costs it has imposed. Rural voters in communities like Wiggins, Colorado, expressed agreement despite rising gasoline prices.

stories.title: Francesca Albanese on Israeli sexual violence suffered by Palestinians
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese discussed allegations of sexual violence committed by Israeli forces against Palestinians in an interview with journalist Redi Tlhabi.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defence Forces strike Russian command posts, warehouses in occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defence Forces conducted overnight strikes on Russian command posts, warehouses, and other military facilities in occupied areas of the Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions on the night of May 16.

stories.title: UK police brace for far-right rally and counter-demonstration
stories.summary: Thousands gathered in London on Saturday for a far-right march organized by Tommy Robinson and a counter-demonstration linked to pro-Palestinian Nakba Day protests. The Metropolitan Police deployed approximately 4,000 officers along with horses, dogs, drones, and helicopters in one of its largest operations in recent years.

stories.title: DRC health minister warns ‘very high’ Ebola lethality rate as toll hits 80
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's health minister has warned of a very high lethality rate as the Ebola death toll reached 80. The Africa CDC expressed concern that the Bundibugyo strain outbreak could spread rapidly due to intense population movement in the region.

stories.title: Israeli strike in Gaza City kills two, wounds three
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck a vehicle near al-Wahda Tower in western Gaza City on Saturday evening, killing two people and wounding three others. The overall death toll in Gaza has reached at least 72,757 killed and 172,645 wounded since October 7, 2023.

stories.title: North America’s largest commuter rail system shuts down as workers strike
stories.summary: North America's largest commuter rail system shut down operations after unionized workers went on strike, disrupting service for passengers.

stories.title: Ending war along front line can be major victory for Ukraine – Czech analyst
stories.summary: A Czech analyst assessed that ending the Russia-Ukraine war roughly along the current front line would constitute a major victory for Ukraine.

stories.title: Tommy Robinson tells tens of thousands at London rally to prepare for ‘battle of Britain’
stories.summary: Far-right activist Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, held a rally in central London on Saturday drawing tens of thousands of supporters. Islamophobic and ethnonationalist hate speech and flyers were distributed at the event, which Robinson called preparation for the "battle of Britain."

stories.title: Republican Senator Cassidy loses re-election to Trump retribution campaign
stories.summary: Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana became the first elected US senator to lose re-nomination since 2012, falling in the Republican primary as part of a Trump-backed retribution campaign against those who voted to convict the former president.

stories.title: Republican Cassidy faces Trump retribution effort in Louisiana Senate primary
stories.summary: Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana faced a primary election on Saturday against two rivals, including a Trump-backed challenger, after being targeted for retribution by President Donald Trump. A loss would make him the first sitting Senate incumbent to lose renomination in over a decade.

stories.title: Rising diesel costs from Iran war strain U.S. school budgets
stories.summary: Rising diesel fuel costs linked to the conflict with Iran are straining U.S. school district budgets, forcing administrators to use emergency funds, reduce spending, and restructure transportation plans.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in south Lebanon kill couple, hit multiple towns
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit the town of Haboush in southern Lebanon, destroying a home and killing Muhammad Hassan Jammoul and his wife Sakina Muhammad Abbas Makki. The strikes occurred despite Israel and Lebanon agreeing to extend their ceasefire by 45 days on Friday. Lebanon's Health Ministry reported 2,969 killed and 9,112 wounded since March 2.

stories.title: 8 injured as man rams car into crowd in Italy’s Modena
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man drove a car into a crowd in Modena, northern Italy, injuring at least eight people, four seriously. The driver, of North African origin, attempted to flee and attacked a bystander with a knife before being subdued by pedestrians.

stories.title: Ukrainian border guards capture three Russian soldiers near Vovchansk
stories.summary: Ukrainian border guards from the "Forpost" brigade captured three Russian soldiers near the city of Vovchansk in the Kharkiv region along the southern Slobozhanshchyna front.

stories.title: Karachi courts reserve decision on police pleas for alleged drug queenpin Anmol’s physical remand
stories.summary: Multiple courts in Karachi, Pakistan, reserved decisions on police requests for the physical remand of alleged drug queenpin Anmol, also known as Pinky, in over 15 cases including murder. She was arrested earlier in the week in a joint police and intelligence raid.

stories.title: Over 250,000 join Nakba Day march against Gaza war, far-right
stories.summary: Approximately 250,000 pro-Palestine demonstrators marched in London on Nakba Day to protest the war in Gaza and far-right movements. The march reportedly far outnumbered a separate rally organized by far-right activist Tommy Robinson.

stories.title: Hamas official says military chief has died after Israel says it targeted him
stories.summary: A Hamas official confirmed the death of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the group's military chief, after Israel said it targeted him in Gaza City. Witnesses reported that mosques in Gaza City announced his death.

stories.title: Canada deepens Arctic defense ties with Nordics after Trump threats
stories.summary: Canada is strengthening Arctic defense cooperation with Nordic countries amid heightened concerns over Arctic security and pressure from statements by U.S. President Trump.

stories.title: 'There is little which is Jewish about Israel': Haim Bresheeth on antisemitism and Gaza
stories.summary: A planned Nakba commemoration march in London is expected to draw thousands of participants. British-Israeli author Haim Bresheeth-Zabner, a son of Holocaust survivors, plans to join. A separate far-right march led by Tommy Robinson is also scheduled nearby, raising concerns about potential clashes.

stories.title: China, US agree to reduce tariffs on certain goods
stories.summary: China and the United States agreed to reduce tariffs on certain goods to promote bilateral trade, according to a statement from China's Ministry of Commerce.

stories.title: At least 8 killed, 25 injured in train collision that sparks bus fire in Thailand
stories.summary: At least eight people were killed and 25 injured when a train collided with a bus in Thailand, sparking a fire that engulfed the bus and nearby vehicles. Firefighters and rescue crews responded to the multi-vehicle incident.

stories.title: US sanctions relief for Russian oil shipments appears to end with no renewal issued
stories.summary: U.S. sanctions relief allowing Russian oil shipments appears to have expired with no renewal issued. The waiver had been introduced during global energy disruptions linked to the Iran conflict as a temporary measure to stabilize supply.

stories.title: The existential choice: Next Israeli election must be about policy, not poison - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel's 2026 elections should focus on substantive policy rather than divisive politics, warning that growing internal divisions may pose a greater threat than external enemies.

stories.title: Former MK Yousef Jabareen elected leader of Arab-majority party Hadash
stories.summary: Former Knesset member Yousef Jabareen was elected leader of the Arab-majority party Hadash following a leadership shakeup in which two sitting MKs stepped down. Jabareen has signaled plans to revive the Joint List alliance of Arab-majority parties.

stories.title: Timmy the whale confirmed dead by Danish authorities
stories.summary: Danish authorities confirmed that Timmy, a beached humpback whale transported to the North Sea in a rescue attempt, was found dead near the island of Anholt in the Kattegat strait. The rescue operation had been criticized by wildlife experts as "pure animal cruelty."

stories.title: War update: 61 clashes on front line since morning
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported 61 clashes with Russian troops since the morning. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk, Northern Slobozhanshchyna, and Kursk sectors of the front line.

stories.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon day after ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on at least five villages in southern Lebanon one day after a ceasefire extension was announced. The strikes occurred despite the renewed truce agreement between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: UK’s ex-health minister Streeting says will run to replace PM Keir Starmer
stories.summary: Former UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting announced he will run to replace Prime Minister Keir Starmer as Labour leader. Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham also launched a bid and is considered the frontrunner in the anticipated leadership contest.

stories.title: Taiwan insists it is independent after Trump warning
stories.summary: Taiwan reasserted its independence following a warning from U.S. President Trump, who cautioned against a formal declaration of independence after his summit in Beijing. The statement highlighted ongoing tensions over Taiwan's status.

stories.title: Whale found dead near Danish island after German rescue operation
stories.summary: A whale that had been the subject of a rescue operation off the German coast was found dead near the Danish island of Anholt. Wildlife experts had previously criticized the rescue effort, warning it would cause the animal additional distress.

stories.title: French judge to probe Jamal Khashoggi killing after complaint against Saudi crown prince
stories.summary: A French investigative magistrate will probe a complaint filed by rights groups against Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman over the 2018 killing of journalist Jamal Khashoggi. Khashoggi was strangled and dismembered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey.

stories.title: Trump officials urged UAE to seize Iranian island, report says
stories.summary: Senior Trump administration officials reportedly urged the United Arab Emirates to seize Iran's Lavan Island in the Persian Gulf, according to The Telegraph. The report indicated that the island had already been targeted in covert Emirati strikes in early April.

stories.title: IDF kills two Hamas terrorists who infiltrated Israel during October 7 massacre
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces killed two Hamas militants who had infiltrated Israel during the October 7 massacre. An additional Hamas fighter from the Bureij Battalion was also killed in a separate strike on Wednesday.

stories.title: Another Naftogaz employee Injured in Russian attack on Poltava region on May 5 dies
