stories.summary: The FBI confirmed the arrest of Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, who the US has charged with ties to the Iraqi armed group Kataib Hezbollah and involvement in a series of attacks. Al-Saadi was detained in Turkey before being transferred to the United States.

stories.title: Fear as health officials raise alarm over new Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
stories.summary: Health officials raised alarm over a new Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province. At least 80 people have died and 246 suspected cases have been identified in the latest wave of the virus.

stories.title: Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu: The art of self-confidence
stories.summary: French actress Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu attended the Cannes Film Festival as an ambassador for L'Oréal Paris. She spoke about self-confidence as a personal journey shaped by overcoming hardships.

stories.title: Tech features at Hong Kong’s Terminal 2 to enable efficient departures: transport chief
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Transport Secretary Mable Chan announced that the reconfigured Terminal 2 at Hong Kong International Airport will launch on May 27. The terminal will feature technology-led services designed to reduce departure bottlenecks and improve passenger efficiency.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes Kharkiv center
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a road in the central part of Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city.

stories.title: General Staff shows how Ukrainian helicopter pilots train in UK
stories.summary: Ukrainian helicopter pilots are undergoing training in the United Kingdom as part of the multinational Interstorm Operation, according to footage released by Ukraine's General Staff.

stories.title: Nepal students protest government ban on unions in universities
stories.summary: Students in Nepal protested a government ban on student unions in universities. Student leaders warned they would resist any measures they view as undermining democratic practices in the country.

stories.title: Pakistan announces repatriation of sailors detained after US seizure
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar announced the successful repatriation of 20 Iranian and 11 Pakistani sailors whose vessel had been detained by the United States near Singapore. The sailors were flown from Singapore to Islamabad via Bangkok.

stories.title: Tennessee Rep. Steve Cohen won’t seek reelection after GOP carved up his district
stories.summary: U.S. Representative Steve Cohen, a Democrat representing the majority-Black Memphis area in Tennessee since 2006, announced he will not seek reelection after Republicans redrew his congressional district.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon extending ceasefire, US says, despite new Israeli strikes
stories.summary: The United States announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire and hold expanded talks on a political settlement. However, Israel carried out new strikes in southern Lebanon, insisting those operations are not covered by the truce.

stories.title: US charges alleged Iran-backed ⁠Kataib Hezbollah suspect – What we know
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department arrested and charged an Iraqi national identified as a senior commander of Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed armed group operating in Iraq.

stories.title: Trump says ISIL second-in-command Abu-Bilal al-Minuki killed
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Islamic State second-in-command Abu-Bilal al-Minuki was killed in a joint operation carried out by U.S. and Nigerian forces. Al-Minuki had been designated a global terrorist in 2023.

stories.title: Hundreds march in New York to commemorate 78th anniversary of Nakba
stories.summary: Hundreds of people marched through Manhattan in New York on Friday to mark the 78th anniversary of the Nakba, commemorating the displacement of Palestinians in 1948.

stories.title: US officials suspect Iran behind cyberattack targeted fuel systems
stories.summary: US officials suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting fuel-level monitoring systems at petrol stations in several states. Hackers exploited unprotected online systems, altering display readings but causing no physical damage, according to CNN.

stories.title: Israel on alert as Trump weighs Iran military action
stories.summary: Israeli officials are on heightened alert as US President Donald Trump weighs possible military action against Iran while also signaling willingness to continue diplomatic negotiations with Tehran, according to Yedioth Ahronoth.

stories.title: UK drivers struggle to get insurance for Chinese EVs such as Jaecoo
stories.summary: Research indicates UK insurers are more reluctant to cover some Chinese-made hybrid and electric vehicles or charge higher premiums compared to equivalent petrol cars. Drivers purchasing models from brands such as Jaecoo may face more limited insurance options than those buying EVs from European, American, or South Korean manufacturers.

stories.title: Record numbers of UK renters crowdfunding to cover bills
stories.summary: GoFundMe reported that April saw more rent-related fundraisers created in the UK than in any month on record, with donations toward rent support rising 60% since 2022. More than 100,000 people per month are contributing to help others meet housing costs on the platform.

stories.title: Trump says Xi agrees Iran must not obtain nuclear weapon
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed that Iran must not obtain a nuclear weapon and affirmed the Strait of Hormuz would remain open. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran was open to any role China could play in a future settlement.

stories.title: LHC upholds widows’ right to interest on delayed insurance payments
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court upheld the right of widows and legal heirs of deceased policyholders to receive statutory interest on delayed group insurance payments. Justice Raheel Kamran dismissed four appeals filed by the State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan in disputes dating back to the late 1990s.

stories.title: NYT accuses Israel of trying to 'stifle journalism' by taking legal action over op-ed
stories.summary: The New York Times accused Israel of attempting to "stifle journalism" after Israel's government threatened legal action over an article. A Times spokesperson said the threat was part of a political strategy to undermine independent reporting.

stories.title: Taiwan says it is a ‘sovereign’ nation with US ‘security commitment’ after Trump’s warning
stories.summary: Taiwan's foreign ministry affirmed the island is a "sovereign and independent" nation and that U.S. arms sales represent Washington's security commitment. The statement followed President Trump's warning to Taiwan against declaring formal independence during his state visit to Beijing and meeting with President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: 2 Hong Kong tourists killed, 2 injured in New Zealand car crash
stories.summary: Two Hong Kong tourists were killed and two others injured in a car crash near the intersection of North Rakaia Road and State Highway 1 in New Zealand's Selwyn District on May 15. The Chinese consulate in Christchurch confirmed the incident based on a New Zealand police report.

stories.title: Lubinets: Authorities hold negotiations on humanitarian evacuation from occupied parts of Kherson region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Lubinets reported that authorities held negotiations on Friday regarding a humanitarian evacuation from settlements in Russian-occupied areas of the Kherson region.

stories.title: ‘The New York Times’ and the grotesque NGO ‘halo effect’ - opinion
stories.summary: Debate continues over a New York Times report on allegations against Israel, with critics arguing that politicized NGOs and sympathetic media outlets amplify unverified claims as established fact.

stories.title: Tens of thousands expected at major Nakba Day demonstrations in London
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people are expected to gather in London on Saturday for demonstrations marking the Nakba, alongside a separate march led by far-right campaigner Tommy Robinson. Around 4,000 police officers, including 660 from outside London, are being deployed.

stories.title: Congregation returns to Los Angeles synagogue that was damaged in 2025 wildfire
stories.summary: Roughly 250 members of the Kehillat Israel congregation in Los Angeles, including all three clergy, lost their homes in the Pacific Palisades wildfire. The synagogue, which was damaged in the 2025 fire, has reopened for its congregation.

stories.title: Bangladesh tests its India ties by seeking China’s aid for Teesta River
stories.summary: Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman formally asked China to assist with the approximately $1 billion Teesta River restoration project, after years of unsuccessful requests to India for cooperation on the waterway. The move tests Dhaka's relationship with New Delhi as millions of Bangladeshis depend on the Teesta for their livelihoods.

stories.title: Trump says he is losing patience with Iran, did not ask China for favours
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he is losing patience with Iran during his visit to China and denied asking Beijing for any favors in relation to the situation.

stories.title: Hong Kong parents warned of choking, injury risks from catapult and tangram toys
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Customs and Excise Department warned that a catapult toy and a tangram set pose choking and injury risks to children. Authorities seized 700 units of the products during an operation and issued a prohibition notice banning their sale, following safety tests on toys purchased at a Chinese New Year fair.

stories.title: UAE pushed GCC to join coordinated war against Iran, bloomberg reports
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported that the United Arab Emirates unsuccessfully sought to persuade other Gulf Cooperation Council members to join a coordinated military campaign against Iran during the early stages of the US-Israeli conflict. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman declined the proposal.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Israel, Lebanon extend shaky ceasefire
stories.summary: The United States announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire, originally declared April 17, for an additional 45 days and to hold expanded political settlement talks. The ceasefire had not fully stopped fighting between Israel and Hezbollah, and hundreds have died in Lebanon from Israeli strikes since it began.

stories.title: British Palestinians feel ‘gaslit’ and unable to speak out, says leading activist
stories.summary: The director of the British Palestinian Committee, Sara Husseini, said British Palestinians feel unable to speak openly about Israel's war on Gaza due to a growing climate of hostility. Some reportedly fear wearing Palestinian symbols or displaying Arabic jewelry at work amid what campaigners describe as treatment as suspects rather than victims.

stories.title: Down and then out in Paris and London? Why Starmer isn’t the only one with a popularity problem
stories.summary: An analysis examines declining approval ratings for political leaders across Europe and the UK amid economic headwinds. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's popularity is notably low, with only 11% of Britons rating him a good or great prime minister according to YouGov polling, following poor local election results.

stories.title: Outbreak of rare strain of Ebola claims at least 65 lives in DR Congo
stories.summary: A new Ebola outbreak in the Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 65 people, with 246 suspected cases reported.

stories.title: Trump says Islamic State ‘second in command’ killed by US and Nigerian forces
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, described as the global second-in-command of ISIS, was killed in a joint U.S.-Nigerian military operation. Trump called it a meticulously planned and complex mission to eliminate what he termed the most active terrorist in the world.

stories.title: Video: Araghchi says US-Iran talks ‘suffering from lack of trust’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said US-Iran negotiations are "suffering from the lack of trust," speaking at a BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi. He stated Tehran seeks clearly defined terms before agreeing to any deal and said US military pressure had failed to achieve its objectives.

stories.title: Iran giving mixed signals on deals, US open to 20 year halt to enrichment deal, Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump said a 20-year halt to Iran's uranium enrichment could form the basis of a deal, but noted Tehran has sent mixed signals. Trump stated that agreements reached in talks were sometimes walked back by Iranian negotiators.

stories.title: UN expert condemns Israeli response to sexual abuse allegations
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese criticized Israel's foreign ministry for dismissing a New York Times article on alleged sexual abuse of Palestinians in Israeli prisons as lies and for announcing plans to sue the newspaper. Albanese described the article as accurate.

stories.title: How ancient seeds are rewriting the history of biblical-era trade with Arabia
stories.summary: New radiocarbon dating of seeds found at the Ein Hatzeva fortress along an ancient trade route in Israel's Arava region suggests the site was built approximately 2,800 years ago by the Kingdom of Israel, supporting biblical accounts of trade with Arabia.

stories.title: Trump says Isis second in command Abu-Bilal ‘eliminated from battlefield’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, whom he called ISIS's global second-in-command, was killed in a joint operation by American and Nigerian forces. Trump described the mission as meticulously planned and called al-Minuki the most active terrorist in the world.

stories.title: Who is Raul Castro, the Cuban leader facing a US indictment
stories.summary: Former Cuban President Raul Castro, 94, faces a potential U.S. indictment in connection with Cuba's 1996 shootdown of planes operated by the humanitarian group Brothers to the Rescue, which killed four people.

stories.title: The 1996 incident at the root of expected Raul Castro indictment
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department is reportedly preparing to seek an indictment against former Cuban President Raúl Castro. The case is linked to a 1996 incident in which Cuban military jets shot down two small civilian planes, killing four people.

stories.title: The 1996 incident at the root of expected Raul Castro indictment
stories.summary: The Trump administration plans to file criminal charges against former Cuban President Raul Castro over the 1996 incident in which Cuban military jets shot down civilian planes, killing four people, according to a U.S. Justice Department official.

stories.title: Trump sets timeframe for moratorium on Iran's nuclear program
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that a 20-year moratorium on Iran's nuclear program would be sufficient for reaching an agreement and ending the conflict. The statement signals a potential diplomatic framework for resolving the standoff with Tehran.

stories.title: Mamdani posts Nakba Day video, saying the ‘catastrophe’ continues until today
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Mamdani posted a video on Nakba Day supporting the Palestinian right of return and presenting a narrative of the 1948 war, drawing strong criticism from Jewish organizations shortly before Shabbat.

stories.title: Paz thanks Milei for sending Hercules aircraft to bring food to blockaded Bolivian cities
stories.summary: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz thanked Argentine President Javier Milei for sending two C-130 Hercules military aircraft to airlift food and basic goods to La Paz and El Alto. The cities have been affected by ten consecutive days of road blockades by highland peasant unions, creating shortages amid political tensions with factions aligned with former president Evo Morales.

stories.title: Sri Lanka civil war: 17 years later, the imprints remain
stories.summary: Seventeen years after the end of Sri Lanka's civil war, the Tamil population in the northern and eastern regions continues to face poverty, high unemployment, and land seizures. Tamils say successive governments have failed to implement a comprehensive recovery plan for war-affected areas.

stories.title: Stafford byelection tipped to swing towards LNP as danger looms for Steven Miles’ leadership of Queensland Labor
stories.summary: A byelection in the Brisbane seat of Stafford, triggered by the death of independent MP Jimmy Sullivan in April, is expected to swing toward Queensland's governing LNP. Experts say a strong LNP result could threaten former premier Steven Miles' leadership of the Queensland Labor party.

stories.title: US plans to indict Raul Castro raise Cubans' fears of force
stories.summary: U.S. plans to indict former Cuban leader Raul Castro over a 1996 plane shootdown have heightened tensions in Cuba, which is already facing severe fuel shortages and its worst crisis in decades.

stories.title: Have Chinese defence firms broken the sniper rifle range record – again?
stories.summary: Two Chinese defense companies—Chongqing Changjiang Electric Appliances Industries Group and Hunan Huanan OptoElectronic Group—issued cryptic statements in late April suggesting a long-distance sniper rifle shooting record may have been broken. The ammunition manufacturer said a product "refreshed the world record" during a specialized test.

stories.title: Stateside with Kai and Carter: Stacey Abrams on why gutting of the US Voting Rights Act is ‘evil’ – podcast
stories.summary: A Guardian podcast discusses the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, which barred the consideration of race in redistricting, effectively weakening the 1965 Voting Rights Act. Several southern states have moved to eliminate majority-Black congressional districts, causing upheaval ahead of midterm elections. Voting rights activist Stacey Abrams discusses the ruling's consequences.

stories.title: Man in his 70s dies after falling on board bus in Hong Kong
stories.summary: A man in his 70s died after falling on a KMB route 5 bus near 125 Chatham Road South in Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, on Saturday. He was taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Police classified the incident as a fatal traffic accident.

stories.title: UAE foreign minister meets Reform UK leader Nigel Farage
stories.summary: UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Reform UK leader Nigel Farage during a visit to the United Kingdom. The two discussed regional developments, including what the UAE described as Iranian attacks targeting the Emirates, as well as bilateral strategic relations.

stories.title: Iranian diplomat says solidarity with Palestinians is not enough
stories.summary: Iran's UN Ambassador Amir Saeid Iravani said support for Palestinians must go beyond solidarity and address the root causes of suffering under Israeli occupation. Speaking at a UN event marking the 78th anniversary of the Nakba, he called for international mobilization and an action-oriented approach.

stories.title: Oscar-winning Iranian director Farhadi calls crackdown, war deaths 'deeply painful'
stories.summary: Oscar-winning Iranian director Asghar Farhadi, speaking at the Cannes Film Festival, described as deeply painful the deaths from a January crackdown on protesters and the ongoing war affecting Iran.

stories.title: Israeli forces and settlers carry out raids across West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces and settlers carried out raids across multiple governorates in the occupied West Bank on Friday night, including Salfit, Hebron, Ramallah, Bethlehem, and Jenin. In Adh Dhahiriya near Hebron, a Palestinian man was reportedly shot, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society.

stories.title: Trump claims he will engineer a "turnaround" in Cuba and pull it away from China and Russia
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said his administration aims to realign Cuba with Washington and pull it away from Chinese and Russian influence, following CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Havana. The remarks came during a week of mixed U.S. signals toward Cuba, including a $100 million humanitarian offer and judicial pressure on former president Raúl Castro.

stories.title: China criticises US-backed Hormuz resolution at UN
stories.summary: China's Ambassador Fu Cong criticized a US- and Bahrain-backed UN Security Council draft resolution on the Strait of Hormuz, calling both its content and timing inappropriate. The resolution calls on Iran to halt attacks and mining operations in the waterway and is expected to face vetoes from China and Russia.

stories.title: Israel launches deadly air strikes on Gaza City apartment building
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes struck a residential building and a vehicle in Gaza City, killing at least seven Palestinians.

stories.title: Israel says over 220 Hezbollah fighters killed in past week
stories.summary: Israel reported that over 220 Hezbollah fighters were killed in the past week. Fighting has continued between Israeli forces and Hezbollah despite a truce agreed on April 17.

stories.title: Czech police recover medieval saint’s 800-year-old skull encased in concrete
stories.summary: Czech police arrested a man suspected of stealing the nearly 800-year-old skull of Saint Zdislava of Lemberk from the Church of St. Lawrence in Jablonné v Podještědí and encasing it in concrete. Investigators used special equipment to confirm the relic was hidden inside a concrete block, and the suspect admitted to the theft.

stories.title: National Guardsman who protected Chornobyl NPP returns from captivity
stories.summary: A Ukrainian National Guardsman who helped protect the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant has returned from Russian captivity. Ukraine has recovered nearly all National Guard members captured after Russia occupied the Chornobyl facility.

stories.title: Venezuela and World Bank agree to define technical cooperation areas after seven-year pause
stories.summary: Venezuela and the World Bank agreed in Caracas to identify areas of technical cooperation in their first high-level meeting after a seven-year pause in institutional contacts. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez received the World Bank's Vice President for Latin America and the Caribbean, Susana Cordeiro Guerra, at Miraflores Palace.

stories.title: Iraqi militia commander charged in US for plotting attacks on Jewish targets for Iran
stories.summary: US prosecutors charged Mohammad al-Saadi, described as a Kataib Hezbollah member and IRGC operative, with coordinating attacks on Jewish targets in Western countries on behalf of Iran. The attacks were claimed by a group called Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya.

stories.title: Trump closes China visit without substantial agreements but with Xi's offer on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump concluded his state visit to China without substantial agreements on key bilateral issues, though he described the trip as successful. Chinese President Xi Jinping offered to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been closed by Iran since the start of the current regional conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky says Russia considering plan to attack NATO country from Belarus
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia is considering a plan to attack a NATO member country from Belarusian territory. Belarus borders NATO members Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia to its north and west.

stories.title: AI helps South Korea stop 99% of suicide attempts on Han River bridges in Seoul
stories.summary: Seoul's Hangang Bridge CCTV Integrated Control Centre, established in 2021, uses AI to monitor 900 cameras across 17 pedestrian-accessible Han River bridges to prevent suicide attempts. The system has helped stop 99% of such attempts. The center provides comprehensive emergency response for the river area.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF conducts 'Sulfur and Fire' readiness exercise along eastern border, Dead Sea area
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces conducted a readiness exercise dubbed "Sulfur and Fire" along Israel's eastern border and the Dead Sea area. The exercise included simulated scenarios of community infiltrations, drone threats, and complex security incidents.

stories.title: Hackers breach US gas monitoring systems, officials suspect Iranian involvement - report
stories.summary: Hackers breached US gas monitoring systems, and officials suspect Iranian involvement based on Iran's history of targeting automated tank gauges. However, sources told CNN that the hackers left little evidence to allow definitive attribution.

stories.title: Drone strikes residential building in Russia’s Belgorod, injuring nine
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Armed Forces drone struck a multi-story residential building on Vokzalnaya Street in Russia's Belgorod region, injuring nine people. The local emergency operations center confirmed the strike on Friday.

stories.title: Trump ‘not optimistic’ on Jimmy Lai’s release after raising case with Xi
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he raised the case of imprisoned Hong Kong media figure Jimmy Lai with Chinese President Xi Jinping during his Beijing visit but expressed pessimism about Lai's release. Lai was sentenced to 20 years for violating Hong Kong's national security law. Xi reportedly told Trump the case was difficult.

stories.title: On synagogues, playgrounds: In NY, swastika graffiti is increasingly common and rarely prosecuted
stories.summary: Swastika graffiti incidents have become increasingly common across New York, frequently targeting synagogues and Jewish sites. At least three graffiti sprees occurred in recent months, following a rise documented last year by the Anti-Defamation League, and prosecutions remain rare.

stories.title: A mother in Russia’s Irkutsk region filmed herself sexually abusing her six-year-old son. Child welfare authorities removed all five children from her home.
stories.summary: Child welfare authorities in Russia's Irkutsk region removed five children from their mother's care after she filmed herself sexually abusing her six-year-old son. An adult boyfriend also participated in the abuse, according to journalist Ksenia Sobchak and the outlet People of Baikal.

stories.title: Even as drones usher in an era of ‘cheap kill,’ Army leaders look to what’s next
stories.summary: At the LANPAC conference, U.S. Army leaders discussed the evolving role of drones in modern warfare and the era of low-cost unmanned strike capabilities. Military officials are examining what comes next as uncrewed vehicles become increasingly prevalent on the battlefield.

stories.title: London police charge MAGA influencer over alleged assault
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police charged Melissa Rein Lively, a U.S. MAGA-aligned influencer, over an alleged assault. Lively had previously sought the role of White House spokesperson during President Donald Trump's second term.

stories.title: Nearly 200 ex-diplomats call on Canada to act against Israel
stories.summary: Nearly 200 former Canadian diplomats signed a letter urging Prime Minister Mark Carney's government to impose robust sanctions on Israel over its actions in the occupied Palestinian territories and Lebanon. The signatories argued that without international sanctions, Israel would continue disregarding international law and expanding settlements.

stories.title: Trump says Iran will not use Hormuz ‘as a weapon’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared that the Strait of Hormuz would remain open and vowed to prevent Iran from using the strategic waterway as leverage. Speaking to Fox News, Trump noted that China relies on the strait for roughly 40 percent of its oil supplies and accused Tehran of previously restricting passage.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to extend ceasefire by 45 days, US State Dept says
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 45-day extension of the ceasefire that U.S. President Donald Trump declared on April 16, according to the U.S. State Department. The announcement was made on Friday from Washington.

stories.title: US congresswoman says ‘Nakba did not end in 1948’
stories.summary: US Representative Rashida Tlaib, a Palestinian American, addressed Congress to commemorate the Nakba, the displacement of an estimated 750,000 Palestinians during Israel's founding in 1948. Tlaib stated that the Nakba did not end in 1948 and continues today.

stories.title: Russia’s Supreme Court proposes reducing prison sentences for large-scale drug possession without intent to distribute
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court submitted a bill to the State Duma proposing reduced prison sentences for acquiring and storing drugs in large quantities without intent to distribute. The legislation has been published on the lower house's website.

stories.title: Israel targets Hamas militant chief in Gaza, medics say three killed
stories.summary: Israel said it carried out an airstrike in Gaza targeting the head of Hamas's armed wing, whom it described as an architect of the October 7, 2023, attacks. Palestinian medics reported that at least three people were killed in the strike.

stories.title: The West was never the whole world. It’s time to move on
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Western social science erred in assuming its frameworks were universally applicable to all societies. The piece contends that global convergence toward Western models, once taken for granted, no longer reflects reality.

stories.title: Can AI-assisted unmanned vessels be Beijing’s answer to South China Sea patrols?
stories.summary: Chinese researchers proposed using wave-powered unmanned surface vessels for maritime patrols and law enforcement in contested waters, including the South China Sea. The AI-assisted vessels could convert wave motion into forward thrust for sustained, long-range operations.

stories.title: Hong Kong market regulator takes on ‘collection agent’ role for wronged investors
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission facilitated a record HK$1.5 billion settlement for wronged independent shareholders of Giordano International. Hundreds of Hongkongers queued at Edinburgh Tower in Central to claim their share of the payout.

stories.title: Gaza aid convoy in Libya prepares to head to Gaza
stories.summary: A land convoy named "Soumoud 2" is preparing to depart from Libya to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza.

stories.title: Putin eases path to Russian citizenship for residents of Moldovan breakaway republic Transnistria
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree creating a simplified pathway to Russian citizenship for residents of Transnistria, a breakaway republic within Moldova's internationally recognized borders.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to 45-day extension of ceasefire, says U.S.
stories.summary: The United States announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 45-day ceasefire extension following two days of talks described as productive. Further negotiations are scheduled for June 2-3, according to State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott.

stories.title: Google’s YouTube, Snap settle first-of-its-kind school social media suit ahead of trial
stories.summary: Google's YouTube and Snap settled with a rural Kentucky school district in the first lawsuit to go to trial over claims that social media addiction disrupted learning and caused a student mental health crisis. TikTok and Meta Platforms, also named in the suit, still face a trial set for June 12 in Oakland, California.

stories.title: Zelenskiy says Russia considering plan to attack NATO country from Belarus
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy stated on May 15 that Russia is seeking to draw Belarus further into the war and is considering plans to launch attacks on Ukraine's north or a NATO member state from Belarusian territory.

stories.title: Amid Eurovision tensions, Israelis find allies in Austria’s youth Green party, cafe
stories.summary: During Eurovision tensions, Israel's representative Bettan found support from Austria's Young Greens party, which posted an Instagram video welcoming the performer and condemning boycott calls against Israel.

stories.title: US senators criticise Trump over economic impact of Iran war
stories.summary: Democratic US senators criticized President Donald Trump over the economic consequences of the conflict with Iran. Senator Tammy Baldwin cited rising fertilizer and gas costs for farmers, while Senator Mark Warner pointed to increasing home and fuel costs affecting American households.

stories.title: Lebanon and Israel agree to extend ceasefire for 45 days
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel agreed to a 45-day extension of their ceasefire following two days of negotiations in Washington. Despite the truce agreement, Israeli attacks continued across Lebanon, killing at least 11 people on Wednesday. Beirut called for an independent monitoring mechanism and firm US guarantees.

stories.title: IDF declares closed military zone in Rosh HaNikra, Achziv areas after situational assessment
stories.summary: The IDF declared a closed military zone in the Rosh HaNikra and Achziv areas in northern Israel following a situational assessment. The closure was ordered Thursday night by Northern Command commander Major General Rafi Milo.

stories.title: UK Labour Party says it will let Burnham run for parliamentary seat
stories.summary: Britain's Labour Party announced on May 15 it would allow Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham to seek a parliamentary seat. The move is seen as a potential step toward a future challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership of the party.

stories.title: Author tracing family’s Holocaust survival finds partner’s ancestors took same path
stories.summary: Author Daniela Gerson, while researching her family's Holocaust survival, discovered that her partner's ancestors followed the same path. She notes that most of the roughly 300,000 Polish Jews who survived the war were not in camps, ghettos, or forests but in the mountains of Siberia.

stories.title: Two St. Petersburg men sentenced to 15 and 16 years for plot to poison food supplies bound for fighters in ‘Espanyola’ Russian paramilitary brigade
stories.summary: A Russian court sentenced two men from St. Petersburg—Nikita Krasilnikov, 22, to 16 years and Rinat Ilyin, 20, to 15 years—for plotting to poison food supplies destined for fighters in the "Espanyola" Russian paramilitary brigade.

stories.title: Iranian UN mission says US seeking cover for ‘aggression’
stories.summary: Iran's mission to the United Nations accused the United States of attempting to manufacture a false image of broad international support for a Bahrain-backed draft resolution on the Strait of Hormuz. The mission described the resolution as politically motivated and one-sided.

stories.title: China couple make wedding memorable by hosting wrestling match, with loser facing housework
stories.summary: A couple in Zunyi, Guizhou province, China, held a professional wrestling match at their wedding, with the loser agreeing to do housework for life. The groom, He Yinsheng, is a professional wrestler who installed a wrestling ring in place of a traditional wedding stage.

stories.title: Iran war fallout triggers massive biofuel shift across Asia
stories.summary: Shipping disruptions caused by the Iran war have driven sharp increases in fuel and cooking gas prices across Asia, prompting a shift toward biofuels. In New Delhi, taxi driver Ravi Ranjan reported paying three times as much for LPG as India's government urged residents to reduce driving.

stories.title: Araghchi warns Americans will pay economic price for Iran war
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that Americans would face growing economic costs from what he called a US-Israeli war of choice against Iran. He cited rising gas prices, stock market instability, climbing debt and mortgage rates, and auto loan delinquencies at 30-plus-year highs.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi says Iran launched 3,000 missiles and drones at UAE
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates' Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused Iran of launching approximately 3,000 ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones toward the UAE. Abu Dhabi condemned the attacks and reaffirmed its commitment to regional security and stability.

stories.title: Superpower summit: On the Trump visit to China
stories.summary: An editorial notes that as the United States and China renegotiate their bilateral relationship during Trump's visit to Beijing, India should work to reinforce its own strategic autonomy.

stories.title: Russian online marketplaces lost up to 10% of users after blocking VPN access
stories.summary: Russian online marketplaces experienced up to a 10% decline in users after they began blocking VPN access in April, according to a study by Digital Budget cited by the Russian business daily Kommersant.

stories.title: Ukraine ready to share air defense experience with Azerbaijan – Hnatov
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Hnatov stated that Ukraine is prepared to share its air defense experience, gained during the ongoing war against Russia, with Azerbaijan to help strengthen Baku's air defense capabilities.

stories.title: Former Mexican governor's ally in US custody on charges of cartel ties
stories.summary: A political ally of former Sinaloa state governor Ruben Rocha is now in U.S. custody, according to federal court records filed in New York. Rocha was charged last month in the United States over alleged involvement with the Sinaloa Cartel.

stories.title: Cornell trustees back Jewish president after anti-Israel students mob his car
stories.summary: Cornell University's board of trustees expressed support for President Michael Kotlikoff after anti-Israel protesters mobbed his car on April 30. Kotlikoff decided not to pursue complaints against the student and non-student protesters, who were also cleared in an investigation.

stories.title: Suspected militants abduct students in Nigeria's Borno state, residents say
stories.summary: Suspected militants abducted an unspecified number of students from a primary and junior secondary school in Nigeria's northeastern Borno state on May 15, according to local residents in the insurgency-affected region.

stories.title: US may ask Israel to put Palestinian tax money towards Trump’s Gaza plan, sources say
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering asking Israel to direct approximately $5 billion in Palestinian tax revenues toward President Trump's plan for Gaza, according to sources familiar with the discussions.

stories.title: US charges Iraqi with plots to target Jews in cities from London to LA
stories.summary: The US has charged Iraqi national Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi with allegedly directing plots to attack US and Israeli interests in cities including London and Los Angeles, reportedly in retaliation related to the Iran war.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon agree on 45-day ceasefire extension, negotiation to continue on two tracks
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed on a 45-day extension of their ceasefire, with negotiations set to continue on two separate tracks. The framework includes full mutual recognition of sovereignty and territorial integrity.

stories.title: Iraqi accused of terrorism attacks and plots in US and Europe arrested and charged
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department arrested and charged Iraqi national Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi on six terrorism-related counts, accusing him of involvement in nearly 20 alleged attacks and plots across the United States and Europe. The UK has been particularly affected, with Jewish community centres, synagogues, and charities among recent targets.

stories.title: ‘A watchdog without resources is not a watchdog’: Labor accused of letting key accountability body languish
stories.summary: Australia's Labor government faces criticism for underfunding the Australian National Audit Office, a key accountability body responsible for independent reviews of public administration. Independent Senator David Pocock and transparency advocates have raised concerns that the ANAO's budget allocation will prevent it from meeting its audit targets.

stories.title: Beyond bamboo: Vietnam’s To Lam mounts a diplomacy offensive
stories.summary: Vietnamese leader To Lam has undertaken an extensive diplomatic offensive since assuming the country's top position, visiting Beijing, Washington, Pyongyang, Moscow, and numerous other capitals. Analysts describe his accelerated travel schedule as a deliberate departure from Vietnam's traditionally restrained diplomatic approach.

stories.title: Iran war live: Lebanon, Israel extend truce; Tehran ready for more US talks
stories.summary: Lebanon's Ministry of Health reported that Israeli attacks have killed 2,951 people and wounded at least 8,988 since March 2. Meanwhile, Lebanon and Israel extended their truce, and Tehran signaled willingness to continue negotiations with the United States.

stories.title: US arrests Iraqi Kataib Hezbollah commander wanted for plots against Jews, US interests
stories.summary: The US Justice Department announced the arrest of Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, an Iraqi national and senior commander of Kataib Hezbollah, on May 15. He was wanted for alleged plots against Jewish targets and US interests.

stories.title: ‘World’s oldest dog’ contender dies in France aged 30
stories.summary: Lazare, a Papillon dwarf spaniel born in 1995, has died in France at the age of 30. The dog was considered a contender for the title of world's oldest dog.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it launched 33 attacks on Israeli forces in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced that its fighters carried out 33 attacks against Israeli forces operating in southern Lebanon on Friday, employing rockets, drones, roadside bombs, and artillery fire targeting troop concentrations and armoured vehicles across several border villages.

stories.title: Israel says carried out Gaza strike targeting head of Hamas armed wing
stories.summary: Israel announced it carried out a strike in Gaza targeting Izz al-Din al-Haddad, described as the head of Hamas's armed wing. The Israeli Defence Minister's office said al-Haddad was responsible for harm inflicted on thousands of Israeli civilians and soldiers.

stories.title: From misfit to rap sensation: A 'Reble' storms into Indian hip-hop
stories.summary: Indian hip-hop artist Reble, from India's northeast, has risen as a distinctive new voice in the genre. His music channels personal defiance and regional identity into a unique sound.

stories.title: Mamdani posts Nakba Day video, claims ‘the catastrophe continues to this day’
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Mamdani posted a Nakba Day video produced by his office, stating that the catastrophe continues to this day. Separately, six people were reportedly killed in an Israeli strike on a civil defense center in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump’s lack of focus on human rights in China is big departure for US diplomacy
stories.summary: During his visit to Beijing, President Donald Trump was asked whether he would raise the case of jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Jimmy Lai with China's president. Trump acknowledged he would mention Lai but drew a comparison to a domestic political adversary, signaling a departure from traditional U.S. diplomatic emphasis on human rights in China.

stories.title: Greek probe finds suspected Ukrainian sea drone lost course after malfunction, sources say
stories.summary: Greek investigators concluded that a military sea drone found on a Greek island likely went off course due to a technical malfunction. Sources indicated the suspected Ukrainian drone may not have travelled far from its intended path before landing on the island.

stories.title: BRICS members agree on ‘independent’ State of Palestine with East Jerusalem as capital
stories.summary: BRICS members issued a statement agreeing on an independent State of Palestine with East Jerusalem as its capital. Members disagreed, however, on the future of the Gaza Strip and the status of the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran claims falls within Iranian and Omani territorial waters.

stories.title: Death toll rises after Israeli strike on Lebanon ambulance centre
stories.summary: The death toll from an Israeli strike on an ambulance centre in the southern Lebanese town of Harouf rose to six, including three paramedics. An additional 22 people were wounded in the attack on the health facility in the Nabatieh district.

stories.title: Number of injured in Zaporizhzhia attack rises to three
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian drone attack on the city of Zaporizhzhia in southeastern Ukraine rose to three, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Iran FM says U.S. willing to continue talks, open to China’s help
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister said the United States is willing to continue diplomatic talks and is open to China playing a mediating role. His remarks followed President Trump's statement that Chinese leader Xi Jinping had offered help to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israeli strikes wound dozens in Lebanon as talks in U.S. enter second day
stories.summary: Israeli strikes wounded dozens of people in Lebanon as US-mediated negotiations between Israel and Lebanon entered a second day. A truce between Israel and Hezbollah has been in place since 17 April, but hundreds have been killed in strikes since then.

stories.title: Switzerland to open secret files on Auschwitz 'Angel of Death' Mengele
stories.summary: Switzerland announced plans to open secret files related to Josef Mengele, the Nazi doctor known as the "Angel of Death" at Auschwitz. Rumors have long circulated that Mengele spent time in Switzerland after fleeing Europe following World War II.

stories.title: Death toll in attack on Kyiv apartment building rises to 24
stories.summary: A Russian cruise missile struck a nine-story apartment building in Kyiv, killing at least 24 people. The Ukrainian air force described the attack as part of the largest Russian aerial barrage against the country since the full-scale invasion began.

stories.title: Settler filmed brutally clubbing dog in Palestinian village
stories.summary: A settler was filmed violently attacking a dog in a Palestinian village in the West Bank. No arrests were reported following a series of settler attacks on Friday, which also included the overnight burning of a mosque.

stories.title: Where is Dela Rosa? Philippine senator outmanoeuvres president in evading arrest
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity linked to the country's 'war on drugs,' evaded arrest and escaped from the heavily guarded senate building in Manila amid gunfire. His whereabouts remain unknown, and the episode has drawn criticism of the Philippine government's competence in enforcing the warrant.

stories.title: US scraps deployment of 4,000 troops to Poland
stories.summary: The United States canceled the planned deployment of 4,000 troops to Poland as part of a reorganization of US forces in Europe. The decision followed Washington's announcement that it would withdraw thousands of troops from Germany.

stories.title: Russians shell Komyshany in Kherson region with artillery, two injured
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the settlement of Komyshany in Ukraine's Kherson Oblast with artillery, injuring two people.

stories.title: Palestinian Authority says Israeli forces kill teen in West Bank
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority reported that Israeli forces killed a Palestinian teenager in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Trump leaves China after much pomp and pageantry, but little to show for it
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump concluded a two-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, returning to Washington with what analysts described as impressive optics but disappointing concrete achievements. Industry trade groups and former officials said economic deliverables fell well below expectations.

stories.title: Israel threatens to sue media over report on sexual abuse of inmates
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Gideon Saar ordered a defamation lawsuit against The New York Times over its reporting on alleged sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees by Israeli personnel.

stories.title: Pussy Riot added to Russia’s list of ‘terrorists and extremists’
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Financial Monitoring Service added the protest group Pussy Riot to its official list of "terrorists and extremists." The independent Russian news outlet Vot Tak was among the first to report the designation.

stories.title: Russians attack Kharkiv with drones, woman injured
stories.summary: Russian drones struck two districts of the city of Kharkiv in northeastern Ukraine. A woman was injured in the Osnovianskyi district of the city.

stories.title: Backers of Abbas rival excluded from Fatah confab, despite Egypt’s push for inclusivity
stories.summary: Supporters of Mohammed Dahlan, a rival of Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, were excluded from a major Fatah party conference despite Egypt's push for inclusivity. Abbas reportedly gave a non-committal response to a visiting Egyptian official, and elections were held for the party's top panels without the Dahlan faction.

stories.title: Showdowns and spycraft on Trump-Xi summit sidelines
stories.summary: During the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, tensions between US and Chinese security services surfaced in multiple incidents. A standoff occurred over a US Secret Service agent's weapon, and a US staffer was trampled in a melee. US officials also confiscated badges and pins given to staffers by the Chinese side.

stories.title: ‘The Wanderers’ tells the story of Poland’s Holocaust survivors who fled to the Soviet Union
stories.summary: Daniela Gerson's new book "The Wanderers" chronicles the story of Polish Holocaust survivors, including her own family, who fled to the Soviet Union. The work blends memoir, history, and journalism.

stories.title: Israeli strikes west of Gaza City kill at least seven people
stories.summary: At least seven people were killed and dozens wounded after Israeli forces struck a residential building and a civilian vehicle west of Gaza City. The dead included three Palestinian women and a child, according to local ambulance services.

stories.title: Activists hang Palestinian flag on the Eiffel Tower for Nakba Day
stories.summary: Members of Extinction Rebellion climbed the Eiffel Tower in Paris and hung a Palestinian flag to mark Nakba Day, the annual commemoration of Palestinian displacement.

stories.title: US Army’s 7th Infantry Division, 1st MDTF to merge as Multi-Domain Command-Pacific
stories.summary: The US Army announced it will merge the 7th Infantry Division and the 1st Multi-Domain Task Force into a new two-star Multi-Domain Command-Pacific, combining Stryker infantry brigades, a combat aviation brigade, and multidomain capabilities.

stories.title: Drone attack on Odesa region: Injury toll rises to eleven
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian drone strike on Ukraine's Odesa region rose to eleven, according to local officials.

stories.title: Ukraine’s sling against Russia: How 'geniuses in garages' transformed robotic warfare
stories.summary: Ukraine has rapidly developed robotic warfare capabilities driven by battlefield necessity. Despite initial skepticism, Ukrainian innovators have transformed the country into a leader in military robotics as part of its defense against Russia.

stories.title: UK man appears in court over stabbing of two Jewish men in London
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man appeared in a London court charged with attempted murder over the stabbing of two Jewish men in the city. The trial has been scheduled for March of next year.

stories.title: Trump suggests deadly Russian strike on Kyiv could set back peace efforts
stories.summary: A Russian strike on an apartment building in Kyiv killed 24 people, including three children. President Donald Trump suggested the deadly attack could set back ongoing peace efforts between Russia and Ukraine.

stories.title: Israeli strike on civil defence centre kills three paramedics in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli strike hit a civil defence centre in the town of Harouf in Lebanon's Nabatieh district, killing three paramedics and critically injuring a fourth. Lebanon's health ministry said the attack destroyed the facility.

stories.title: Trump and his CEOs want China’s business – but has Asia moved on?
stories.summary: President Trump's visit to China coincides with the US-Iran war's disruption of global energy supplies. The report examines how rising capital expenditure across Asia is driving a broader shift in economic power away from traditional Western dominance.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Kharkiv with drones, injuring woman
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes hit two districts of Kharkiv, Ukraine. A woman was injured in the city's Osnovianskyi District.

stories.title: US considering asking Israel to redirect PA tax funds to Gaza plan - sources
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly weighing a proposal to ask Israel to redirect some withheld Palestinian Authority tax revenues toward President Donald Trump's postwar Gaza plan, according to sources familiar with the discussions.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack kills four in Ryazan, igniting refinery fire and showering city in ‘oil rain’
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the city of Ryazan overnight on 15 May, killing four people including a child and injuring twelve. The attack damaged residential buildings and ignited a fire at the Ryazan oil refinery, causing an "oil rain" of black residue across the city.

stories.title: Zelensky: Important that world does not remain silent about Russian strikes
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy urged the international community not to remain silent about continued Russian strikes on Ukraine. He emphasized the need for stable international support to protect human lives.

stories.title: Travolta gets surprise Cannes prize: ‘beyond the Oscar’
stories.summary: Actor John Travolta received a surprise honorary Palme d'Or lifetime achievement award at the Cannes Film Festival during the premiere of his directorial debut, Propeller One-Way Night Coach.

stories.title: Israeli strikes hit coastal areas near Tyre in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck the town of Mansouri in Lebanon's Tyre district, targeting coastal areas. Separate strikes on the city of Tyre also caused casualties, though exact figures were not immediately available.

stories.title: Thirty-six countries approve creation of special tribunal for Ukraine
stories.summary: Thirty-six countries approved the creation of a special tribunal to prosecute Russia over its invasion of Ukraine. The tribunal could in theory try senior Russian figures, potentially including President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Pentagon quietly shut legally required program to prevent civilian deaths by military, watchdog finds
stories.summary: The Pentagon's inspector general found that the Trump administration quietly dismantled a legally mandated program to prevent civilian casualties in US military operations. The report concluded the military lacks the personnel and infrastructure to comply with federal statutes, amid scrutiny over a US strike on a girls' school in Iran.

stories.title: Barbs fly in Senate over PTI founder’s health, access to political prisoners
stories.summary: Pakistan's Senate saw heated exchanges over the health of imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan and conditions facing political prisoners. PTI Senator Azam Swati claimed Khan had lost sight in one eye and called for an independent committee to inspect prison conditions.

stories.title: How to deal with this ‘very Chinese time’ in Western lives
stories.summary: An opinion piece explores Western perceptions and cultural associations with China, Japan, and South Korea, examining how stereotypes and familiarity shape attitudes toward East Asian countries.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel controls 60 per cent of Gaza Strip
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel now controls 60 percent of the Gaza Strip. His comments came as efforts to advance a truce and permanently end the conflict appear to have stalled.

stories.title: UAE rejects ‘attempts to justify Iranian terror’ after Tehran alleges role in war
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates rejected accusations by Iran's foreign minister that it was an active partner in aggression against Tehran. The UAE affirmed its right to respond to Iranian missile and drone attacks targeting its territory.

stories.title: Canada takes key step towards new oil pipeline to serve Asia markets
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith took a major step toward building a new oil pipeline to increase crude exports to Asian markets, part of a strategy to reduce Canada's economic dependence on the United States. The project faces environmental opposition.

stories.title: Russia’s biggest nationalist group is funded by a pro-Kremlin analyst and a billionaire linked to the son of a former FSB chief, BBC investigation finds
stories.summary: A BBC investigation found that Russkaya Obshchina, described as Russia's largest nationalist organization, is funded by foundations linked to pro-Kremlin analyst Sergei Mikheyev and billionaire Igor Khudokormov. The group, whose members target migrants and LGBTQ+ people, had claimed it operated solely on member donations.

stories.title: Ryazan declares state of emergency after strike on oil refinery and 'oil rain'
stories.summary: Authorities in Ryazan, Russia, declared a state of emergency on 15 May after a nighttime drone attack damaged one of the country's largest oil refineries. The strike caused a fire and an "oil rain" that coated the city.

stories.title: 'Farcical proceeding': Mahmoud Khalil's lawyers want deportation case terminated
stories.summary: Lawyers for Mahmoud Khalil, a former Columbia University student facing deportation, have asked for the case to be terminated, citing what they called a "farcical proceeding." The New York Times reported unusual events in the immigration court proceedings.

stories.title: Trump says 20-year nuclear programme suspension by Iran would be enough
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that a 20-year suspension of Iran's nuclear programme would be sufficient, insisting Tehran must demonstrate genuine commitment to removing nuclear fuel and halting uranium enrichment.

stories.title: IDF struck, likely killed Hamas military chief, sources confirm
stories.summary: Israeli sources confirmed that the IDF struck and likely killed Izz ad-Din al-Haddad, described as Hamas's highest-ranking military commander and the last leader of the 7 October attack still in the Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims drone and rocket attacks on Israeli forces in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced a series of coordinated drone, rocket, and artillery attacks against Israeli forces across southern Lebanon. Targets included an Israeli force near the town of Houla and the headquarters of the Israeli army's 300th Brigade.

stories.title: What are World Cup 2026 national team base camps and their locations?
stories.summary: FIFA has announced training base camps and accommodation locations for national teams competing in the 2026 World Cup, including Argentina, Portugal, Spain, Brazil, England, and Iran.

stories.title: Seven killed in Gaza on Nakba Day as Israel says it targets Hamas member
stories.summary: At least seven people, including three women and a child, were killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza City on Nakba Day. Israel stated the operation targeted a Hamas member.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel agree 45-day ceasefire extension in Washington
stories.summary: Lebanon, Israel, and the United States agreed to extend the current ceasefire for 45 days following two days of negotiations in Washington.

stories.title: Watch: Opposition slams fuel price hike, BJP says ‘unavoidable’ | Above the Fold | 15.05.2026
stories.summary: India's opposition criticized a ₹3-per-litre hike in petrol and diesel prices, while the ruling BJP called it unavoidable. Separately, Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the UAE, over 100 people died in storms and lightning across Uttar Pradesh, and new developments emerged in the U.S. bribery case involving Gautam and Sagar Adani.

stories.title: 200,000 small and medium-sized businesses closed in Russia in the first quarter of 2026. Experts cite falling demand and higher taxes.
stories.summary: Approximately 209,000 small and medium-sized businesses closed in Russia during the first quarter of 2026, nearly 9 percent more than in the same period of 2025. Experts cited falling demand and higher taxes as primary causes, according to Forbes Russia.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi, UK Chief of Defence Staff discuss frontline situation
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi held discussions with UK Chief of the Defence Staff Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton. The two officials reviewed the current frontline situation in Ukraine.

stories.title: Your Taxes: How Israel’s new war compensation system works
stories.summary: Israel implemented a new war compensation system governed by complex legislation. In practice, accountants typically enter data into the Israel Tax Authority system, which calculates compensation amounts.

stories.title: New Ebola outbreak hits DR Congo
stories.summary: A new Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 65 people, raising concerns about potential regional spread. Separately, Cape Verde is preparing for legislative elections scheduled for Sunday, and Ethiopia's coffee sector faces pressure from falling global prices even as domestic coffee costs have tripled in six months.

stories.title: Kommersant reports General Lapin may chair State Duma’s defense committee. In 2024, he failed to defend Russia’s Kursk region against Ukrainian incursion.
stories.summary: Colonel General Alexander Lapin is being considered to chair the defense committee in Russia's incoming State Duma, according to Kommersant. Lapin previously commanded the Central and Leningrad military districts and was in charge during the failed defense of Russia's Kursk region against a 2024 Ukrainian incursion.

stories.title: WHO warns loosely regulated nicotine pouches risk youth addiction
stories.summary: The World Health Organization urged governments to strengthen regulation of nicotine pouches, warning that the highly addictive products are being aggressively marketed in ways that particularly appeal to younger people.

stories.title: India raises fuel export duties amid US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: India increased export duties on petrol, diesel, and aviation fuel one day after raising domestic fuel prices for the first time since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28. The new levies range from three to 16.5 rupees per litre.

stories.title: What did Trump and Xi discuss during the China summit?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump concluded a two-day summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing, though specific details of the discussions were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Trump says China to buy 200 Boeing jets, order could go up to 750
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said China has agreed to purchase 200 Boeing jets, with the order potentially increasing to 750 aircraft. He added that the planes would be equipped with General Electric engines.

stories.title: Porous ceasefire extended for 45-days after third round of Israel-Lebanon talks
stories.summary: The United States announced a 45-day extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon following two days of talks in Washington described as "highly productive." Fighting between Israeli forces and Hezbollah has continued despite the existing truce.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones keep straying into Baltic and Finnish airspace after being diverted by Russian electronic warfare
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones targeting Russian oil refineries in the St. Petersburg region have repeatedly strayed into Baltic and Finnish airspace, reportedly due to Russian electronic warfare diversion. Latvia officially rejected Russian claims that these countries allow Ukraine to use their airspace for drone operations.

stories.title: Taiwan casts long shadow over Trump’s summit with Xi
stories.summary: Taiwan emerged as a key issue following the summit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Analysts noted subtle differences in how Washington and Beijing characterized Taiwan in their respective post-summit statements.

stories.title: UAE to ‘accelerate’ new oil pipeline bypassing Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced plans to accelerate construction of a new West-East oil pipeline that would bypass the Strait of Hormuz. The pipeline is expected to become operational in 2027.

stories.title: Ex-Sinaloa security chief in Mexico arrested in US over alleged cartel ties
stories.summary: Gerardo Merida Sanchez, a former security chief in Mexico's Sinaloa state, was arrested in Arizona on May 11 on allegations of cartel ties and subsequently transferred to New York.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine to strengthen Kyiv–Chernihiv direction amid threat of Belarus involvement
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine will reinforce defenses along the Kyiv–Chernihiv direction in response to Russia's efforts to involve Belarus more actively in the war.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1542: Day of Mourning for 24 in Kyiv. Odradne raises the flag again. 205 Mariupol defenders come home.
stories.summary: On day 1,542 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, 205 Ukrainian defenders were freed from Russian captivity, most captured at Mariupol in 2022. Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Caspian Fleet base at Kaspiysk and a Rosneft refinery in Ryazan. Kyiv held a Day of Mourning for 24 people killed in a Russian missile strike on May 14.

stories.title: Trump says China to buy 200 Boeing planes in major deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced that China agreed to purchase 200 Boeing aircraft, with the potential to expand the order to 750 planes. The deal would be Boeing's first major sale to China in nearly a decade.

stories.title: 11 Pakistanis, 20 Iranians aboard US-seized vessels repatriated, says DPM Dar
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar announced that 11 Pakistani and 20 Iranian crew members aboard vessels seized by the United States on the high seas have been repatriated. Pakistan coordinated with Singaporean authorities to facilitate the process, as the vessels were near Singaporean waters. Dar said all individuals are in good health.

stories.title: We won't stop protesting Britain's role in the ongoing Nakba
stories.summary: Ryvka Barnard wrote about continued pro-Palestine protests in Britain, arguing that British government repression of demonstrations reflects decades of complicity in Israeli actions since the Nakba.

stories.title: Ukraine wants the playbook of the German newsroom Russia banned
stories.summary: A report examined how a German newsroom model banned by Russia could serve as a template for Ukrainian media. The piece noted that reader-funded journalism has become an alternative following the end of USAID support.

stories.title: UAE building pipeline to double oil exports that can bypass Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is constructing a pipeline that would double its oil export capacity while bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The project would enable the UAE to export nearly all of its pre-war oil volumes through an alternative route via Fujairah.

stories.title: Prosecutors seek death penalty for man charged with killing Israeli DC embassy staffers
stories.summary: U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced prosecutors are seeking the death penalty for the man charged with killing Israeli embassy staffers Yaron Lischinsky and Sarah Milgrim in Washington, D.C., citing political, ideological, and religious bias as motivations.

stories.title: US says Israel-Lebanon talks extended after ‘highly-productive’ meetings
stories.summary: US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott announced that US-mediated negotiations between Israel and Lebanon have been extended after two days of talks. Political track discussions are set to resume on 2–3 June, while a separate security track involving military delegations will begin at the Pentagon on 29 May.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in the central Russian city of Ryazan, according to the commander of Ukraine's drone forces. The attack is part of Ukraine's ongoing campaign targeting Russian energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attacks paralyze oil refining in Russia – Reuters
stories.summary: Since the start of the year, Ukrainian drone strikes have hit at least 16 Russian oil refineries, according to Reuters. The attacks have reduced Russia's refining capacity, lowered petroleum product exports, and put additional pressure on Moscow's oil revenues.

stories.title: Trump calls journalist’s Iran reporting ‘treasonous’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump labeled a New York Times journalist's reporting on the Iran conflict as "treasonous" while claiming a victory in the situation.

stories.title: AI supremacy, ‘secret police station’, Taiwan propaganda: 7 US-China relations reads
stories.summary: A roundup of seven significant U.S.-China relations stories covered topics including the Xi-Trump summit outcomes, AI competition, allegations of a Chinese secret police station, and Taiwan-related tensions.

stories.title: Judge bars Kars4Kids from advertising in California, saying it misled donors about Jewish mission
stories.summary: A California judge barred the charity Kars4Kids from advertising in the state, ruling it misled donors about its Jewish mission. The charity, which funds Orthodox Jewish programs in New York, said it would appeal the ruling.

stories.title: Moscow court orders Belgian depositary Euroclear to pay massive damages to Russia’s Central Bank
stories.summary: A Moscow arbitration court ordered Belgian depositary Euroclear to pay 18.17 trillion rubles, equivalent to approximately 200 billion euros, in damages to Russia's central bank. The ruling fully granted the Russian central bank's claim against the Brussels-based financial institution.

stories.title: Judge declares mistrial in Harvey Weinstein rape retrial amid deadlocked jury
stories.summary: A judge declared a mistrial in Harvey Weinstein's rape retrial after the jury became deadlocked. Accuser Jessica Mann, a hairstylist and actress, alleged Weinstein raped her in 2013 despite her repeated refusals.

stories.title: A Russian tank division rolls toward Pokrovsk, adding major manpower to Russia’s eastern push
stories.summary: A Russian tank division is advancing toward Pokrovsk in eastern Ukraine, adding significant manpower to Russia's offensive push. Ukrainian forces from the 7th Rapid Reaction Corps face the challenge of halting the reinforced Russian advance toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk.

stories.title: Hantavirus outbreak tests post-Covid health communications playbook
stories.summary: An outbreak of the Andes strain of hantavirus aboard a luxury cruise ship in the Atlantic has killed several passengers and sickened others, prompting quarantine measures. Health officials, including those in Illinois, are working to communicate clearly about the virus while avoiding pandemic-era panic, noting hantavirus is not new and unlikely to cause a pandemic.

stories.title: Israel says it assassinated Hamas military commander Izz al-Din al-Haddad
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Israeli forces killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, described as Hamas's top military commander in Gaza. They said al-Haddad was one of the architects of the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Fatima Sana breaks world record for fastest 50 in women’s T20
stories.summary: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana set a new world record for the fastest 50 in women's T20 cricket, scoring 50 off 15 balls during a match-winning innings against Zimbabwe in Karachi.

stories.title: International law will eventually hold Putin accountable, expert says
stories.summary: An international law expert stated that legal mechanisms could eventually hold Russian President Vladimir Putin accountable for actions related to the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: DRC: Health officials scramble to respond to latest ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo are responding to a deadly Ebola outbreak in the country's eastern region. Health workers in Kinshasa met with National Institute of Public Health Director General Dieudonne Mwamba to coordinate the response.

stories.title: Russian human rights activist Nina Litvinova dies by suicide, leaving a note condemning Putin’s war in Ukraine and crackdown on dissent
stories.summary: Russian human rights activist Nina Litvinova died by suicide in Moscow. Her cousin, journalist Masha Slonim, published an excerpt from Litvinova's suicide note in which she condemned President Putin's war in Ukraine and the crackdown on dissent in Russia.

stories.title: Israel says it has killed Hamas commander in Gaza air strike
stories.summary: Israel announced that an air strike in Gaza City killed Izz ad-Din al-Haddad, a Hamas commander it described as one of the architects of the October 7 attack.

stories.title: Israeli strike targets Hamas military leader Izz al-Din al-Haddad, ‘last architect of Oct.7’
stories.summary: Israel reported that an air strike targeted Hamas military leader Izz al-Din al-Haddad, described as the last architect of the October 7 attack. Military officials indicated he is believed killed, though there was no official confirmation.

stories.title: Is the US dialling down its support for Taiwan?
stories.summary: During a visit to China, President Donald Trump reportedly did not commit to an arms sale to Taiwan, raising questions about the future of U.S. support for the island.

stories.title: Palestinians in Gaza mark anniversary of 1948 mass expulsion ‘Nakba’, say today's catastrophe is worse
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza commemorated the anniversary of the 1948 Nakba, the mass displacement that accompanied Israel's founding. Residents said the ongoing war in Gaza has caused suffering and devastation surpassing the original catastrophe.

stories.title: US Army to receive thousands of Barracuda-500M cruise missiles in Anduril deal
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has entered a deal with defense technology company Anduril to procure Barracuda-500M cruise missiles. The contract falls under the Pentagon's Low-Cost Containerized Missiles program, which seeks to acquire more than 10,000 low-cost cruise missiles over three years.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange 205 prisoners each
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine conducted a prisoner exchange, with each side returning 205 prisoners of war, according to Russia's Defense Ministry.

stories.title: US mulling asking Israel to provide PA tax funds for Trump’s Gaza plan — sources
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering asking Israel to redirect a portion of approximately $5 billion in withheld Palestinian Authority tax funds to support President Trump's postwar Gaza plan. A parallel amount would be released to the PA in Ramallah.

stories.title: Georgia town sues over ICE plan for vast immigration detention center
stories.summary: Officials in Social Circle, Georgia, a town of about 5,000 residents, filed a federal lawsuit against ICE and DHS over plans to convert a warehouse into a 10,000-capacity immigration detention facility. The lawsuit alleges the project would overburden local services and harm the environment.

stories.title: UN says Israeli military obstructed peacekeepers in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that the Israeli military obstructed UN peacekeepers in southern Lebanon on two occasions on Thursday. In one incident, an Israeli tank stopped a convoy escorting the Lebanese Red Cross near al-Bayada and pointed its main gun at the group before ordering it to leave.

stories.title: BBC asks Trump if China will help open the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: BBC journalist Tom Bateman asked U.S. President Donald Trump whether China would be willing to pressure Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The question came amid ongoing tensions over maritime security in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Firefighters battling forest fire in Chornobyl zone after drone strike
stories.summary: Firefighters have been battling a forest fire in the Chornobyl exclusion zone for more than a day after a Russian drone strike ignited the blaze in the radioactively contaminated area of northern Ukraine.

stories.title: Pollution from coal is hurting global solar output, study finds
stories.summary: A study found that pollution from coal-burning facilities is reducing global solar energy output. The effect is most pronounced when solar installations are located in close proximity to coal plants.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A news quiz covers major events from the week of May 9, including U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to China, summits hosted by India and Kenya, and political difficulties faced by several prime ministers around the world.

stories.title: Ukraine doubles strikes on Russian oil refineries this year
stories.summary: Ukraine has doubled the number of drone strikes targeting Russian oil refineries since the start of the year, according to information posted by Russian officials. The campaign is part of Kyiv's broader effort to disrupt Russia's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit: all you need to know from the final day of the meeting in Beijing
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a second day of talks in Beijing, with Trump floating the idea of a "G2" partnership. A state banquet was attended by prominent tech executives including Apple's Tim Cook and Tesla's Elon Musk.

stories.title: Lebanon and Israel extend ceasefire for 45 days
