stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel agreed to extend their ceasefire by 45 days following U.S.-mediated talks in Washington. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott announced further negotiations aimed at a permanent political agreement would be held on June 2–3.

stories.title: Army leaders in hot seat over Poland deployment cancellation
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers questioned Army leaders about the cancellation of a military deployment to Poland. Representative Don Bacon (R-Neb.) criticized the decision, saying it sent a "terrible message to Russia and our allies."

stories.title: Trump says China may release the detained pastor but media tycoon Lai ‘is a tough one’
stories.summary: During his visit to Beijing, President Trump suggested China may release a detained American pastor but called the case of imprisoned Hong Kong media tycoon Jimmy Lai "a tough one." Lai's detention has drawn global concern over Hong Kong's national security crackdown.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon agree ceasefire extension, US says
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 45-day extension of the ceasefire between Israel and the Hezbollah militant group, following two days of talks in Washington. U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said additional negotiations are scheduled for June 2–3.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to extend ceasefire, US state department says
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon have agreed to extend their ceasefire, according to the US State Department. President Trump announced the original truce last month, but Israel and Hezbollah have continued to exchange fire since then.

stories.title: Russia launches new strike on Zaporizhzhia industrial facility, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an industrial facility in the city of Zaporizhzhia on Friday, May 15, injuring two people. The attack was part of ongoing Russian strikes targeting Ukrainian infrastructure.

stories.title: Iran has ‘no trust’ in the US, will negotiate only if it is serious, foreign minister says
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister said Iran has "no trust" in the United States and will only negotiate if Washington is serious. Talks on ending the conflict remained on hold.

stories.title: Hungary's visa halt plan for non-EU workers alarms businesses
stories.summary: Hungary's new government faces pressure from companies and business groups to reconsider a planned halt to non-EU worker visas. Businesses warn that an abrupt ban could reduce output in an already tight labor market.

stories.title: ICC fines Pakistan, docks eight WTC points for slow over rate in Dhaka Test
stories.summary: The International Cricket Council fined Pakistan 40 percent of their match fee and docked eight World Test Championship points for maintaining a slow over rate during the first Test against Bangladesh in Dhaka. Pakistan was ruled eight overs short of the required target.

stories.title: Israel says it targeted senior Hamas military leader in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel said it carried out a strike in Gaza targeting Izz al-Din al-Haddad, described as the most senior Hamas military leader remaining in the territory. There was no immediate confirmation of al-Haddad's condition, and Hamas did not comment on the claim.

stories.title: Russia planning strikes on Ukraine’s Presidential Office and state residence, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence obtained documents showing Russia is planning strikes on Ukraine's Presidential Office, state residence, military command posts, and other protected government facilities.

stories.title: How team Burnham finally cleared the first of many hurdles on route to Westminster
stories.summary: Andy Burnham, the mayor of Greater Manchester, cleared a key hurdle in his effort to secure a seat in the UK Parliament. His path has been marked by multiple setbacks, including two prior Labour leadership contest losses and a blocked return to a constituency.

stories.title: Jerusalem Day: Israelis cannot afford to take a united Jerusalem for granted - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece published ahead of Jerusalem Day argues that Israelis should not take a united Jerusalem for granted, calling the city's status a historic achievement, political challenge, and spiritual opportunity.

stories.title: At least nine militants, four security personnel killed in gunfire in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: Nine militants and four security personnel were killed in separate exchanges of gunfire in northwest Pakistan during ongoing security operations in the region.

stories.title: The 156,000 and the 1.4 Billion
stories.summary: The article compares the soccer development approaches of Curaçao, a small Caribbean island with about 156,000 people, and India, which has a population of 1.4 billion. It examines how Curaçao has achieved greater World Cup success despite its far smaller population.

stories.title: Foreign diplomats shown aftermath of Russian strike on residential building in Kyiv
stories.summary: More than 60 foreign diplomatic representatives accredited in Ukraine visited the site in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district where a Russian missile struck a nine-story residential building, witnessing the aftermath firsthand.

stories.title: No sound of silence: US soldiers train eyes — and ears — for drone swarms
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is developing tactics to counter large-scale drone swarm threats, moving beyond defenses designed for individual unmanned aircraft. Soldiers are training to use both visual and auditory detection methods in environments with saturated drone activity.

stories.title: Probe shows foreigners' involvement in network run by alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky: Karachi AIG
stories.summary: Karachi police, in collaboration with a civilian intelligence agency, arrested alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky from her apartment in Karachi. The investigation revealed possible involvement of foreign nationals in operating the drug network. A court granted police a three-day physical remand.

stories.title: 36 countries sign agreement establishing ‘tribunal for Putin’
stories.summary: Thirty-six countries signed an agreement during the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers meeting in Chisinau, Moldova, to establish a steering committee for a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Amidst West Asia pressures, India’s goods exports grew 14% in April 2026
stories.summary: India's goods exports rose 14% in April 2026, while the overall trade deficit—covering both merchandise and services—fell 30% to $7.8 billion, amid ongoing pressures in West Asia.

stories.title: Trump-Xi, the alpha power summit: a debrief
stories.summary: Dr. Bates Gill, an American international relations scholar and China specialist, provided analysis on the recent summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping, examining the dynamics between the two leaders.

stories.title: European markets fall as Iran war fuel inflation fears
stories.summary: European stock markets fell sharply on Wednesday amid inflation fears tied to the conflict involving Iran. Paris dropped 1.60 percent, Frankfurt fell 2.07 percent, London declined 1.71 percent, and Milan lost 1.87 percent following inconclusive Trump-Xi talks that failed to ease tensions.

stories.title: AIRO’s ‘slowed rotor’ hybrid-electric VTOL drone aims to solve resupply issues
stories.summary: AIRO is developing a hybrid-electric VTOL drone using a "slowed rotor" design intended for both military and civilian logistics. Company executives said the aircraft targets a supply gap between rear-operational hubs and forward-deployed units.

stories.title: UAE made failed attempt to get Saudi Arabia, Qatar to jointly attack Iran: Report
stories.summary: The UAE reportedly made an unsuccessful attempt to persuade Saudi Arabia and Qatar to jointly launch an attack on Iran. UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed allegedly lobbied Gulf leaders to coordinate the military action, according to a media report.

stories.title: Trump & Xi, Carry on Westminster, the french pivot
stories.summary: President Trump traveled to Beijing for the first U.S. presidential state visit to China in nearly a decade. Discussions covered trade, technology, and Taiwan, while broader questions about whether the United States and China can coexist as dominant global powers remained a central underlying theme.

stories.title: Dozens of Countries Pledge Support for Special Tribunal to Prosecute Russian Leaders for Ukraine Invasion
stories.summary: Dozens of countries pledged support for a special tribunal tasked with prosecuting Russian leaders for the crime of aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: War Is an International Crime. Why Does It Go Unpunished?
stories.summary: The article reviews a legal history examining how the international community has largely failed to prosecute the crime of waging aggressive war. It traces the gap between the promises made at the Nuremberg trials and subsequent enforcement of international law.

stories.title: Ukraine seeking to keep international focus on return of children – Betsa
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Betsa emphasized the importance of using international platforms to maintain global attention on Russia's abduction of Ukrainian children and to ensure accountability for those responsible.

stories.title: Harvey Weinstein’s New York retrial ends in mistrial with jury deadlocked
stories.summary: Harvey Weinstein's retrial in New York on a rape charge ended in a mistrial after the jury deadlocked, the second consecutive jury unable to reach a verdict. The former Hollywood producer remains imprisoned on other sex-crime convictions but the New York rape charge is now in limbo.

stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 6.4 strikes near east coast of Honshu in Japan, GFZ says
stories.summary: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near the east coast of Honshu, Japan, at a depth of 10 kilometres, according to Germany's GFZ Research Centre for Geosciences.

stories.title: Trump says China to buy 200 Boeing planes, much lower than expected
stories.summary: President Trump announced that China would purchase 200 Boeing aircraft, a figure lower than anticipated. Neither the Chinese government nor Boeing issued statements confirming the reported purchase agreement.

stories.title: How a Jim Caviezel film got mixed up in a Brazilian political scandal
stories.summary: An upcoming biopic called "Dark Horse," starring American actor Jim Caviezel as former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, has become entangled in a Brazilian political scandal. The film has been described as a thriller about Bolsonaro's fight against a corrupt establishment.

stories.title: Trump concludes China visit hailing ‘fantastic deals’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump concluded a state visit to Beijing, where Chinese President Xi Jinping said both sides reached important understandings on maintaining stable economic and trade ties and expanding practical cooperation.

stories.title: Zelenskyy vows response after Russian strike kills 24 in Kyiv
stories.summary: A Russian aerial strike on Kyiv killed 24 people on Thursday, prompting President Zelenskyy to vow a response. Ukraine's air force described the attack as part of the largest aerial assault since the full-scale war began.

stories.title: Israeli strikes hit ambulance centre in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes carried out two air strikes on the town of Harouf in southern Lebanon, destroying an ambulance centre linked to the Islamic Health Authority and wounding at least two people, including paramedics. The United Nations reports that at least 103 Lebanese medical workers have been killed in over 130 Israeli attacks.

stories.title: Trump says hasn’t determined whether to move forward on major arms package for Taiwan
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he has not made a final decision on whether to proceed with a major arms package for Taiwan, a move that China opposes.

stories.title: USS Gerald R. Ford to return from 11-month deployment on Saturday
stories.summary: The USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, is scheduled to return home on Saturday after an 11-month deployment. The ship's extended tour is being noted as a milestone in U.S. Navy history.

stories.title: Trump warns Taiwan against declaring independence from China after meeting Xi
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned Taiwan against formally declaring independence from China in a Fox News interview at the end of his visit to Beijing. Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping had pressed him during their meetings not to support the self-ruling island.

stories.title: Gaza sisters awarded Earth Prize for turning rubble into bricks
stories.summary: Palestinian sisters Farah and Tala Mousa from Gaza won the Middle East regional Earth Prize for developing a method to turn rubble into bricks. The Earth Prize is described as the world's largest environmental competition for young people.

stories.title: I Was the Russian Commander in a War Game. This Is How I Defeated NATO.
stories.summary: The article recounts a war game in which the author played the role of a Russian military commander and defeated NATO forces. The exercise highlighted how decision paralysis and internal divisions among alliance members created exploitable vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Russia could use Belarus for operation against Ukraine or NATO country – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia has intensified contacts with Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko in an effort to draw Belarus into new aggressive operations against Ukraine or potentially a NATO country.

stories.title: Judge declares mistrial in Harvey Weinstein sexual assault case
stories.summary: A New York jury was unable to reach a verdict in the new rape trial against former Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein. The judge declared a mistrial on Friday after deliberations concluded without consensus.

stories.title: Putin’s peace rhetoric clashes with Russia’s battlefield actions in Ukraine - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examined the contradiction between Russian President Vladimir Putin's stated willingness to negotiate over Ukraine and Russia's continued military operations on the battlefield. One expert characterized Russia's diplomatic posture as "surrender language packaged as diplomacy."

stories.title: Aleem Khan blames Punjab, KP govts for delays in highway projects
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Communications Minister Abdul Aleem Khan blamed the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial governments for delays in highway projects during a National Highway Authority review meeting. He signaled federal intervention to accelerate completion of critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Putin Hails ‘Positive’ Economic Growth in March Despite Sharp Downgrade in Annual Forecast
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin highlighted what he called positive economic growth in March, despite the government having recently issued a significant downward revision to its 2026 economic forecast.

stories.title: Harvey Weinstein’s third New York rape trial ends in mistrial
stories.summary: Harvey Weinstein's third trial in New York ended in a mistrial after the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict on the charge that he raped aspiring actress Jessica Mann. The 74-year-old former film producer remains incarcerated on other sex-crime convictions from prior cases.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli tank and bulldozers in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced that its fighters struck an Israeli tank near the southern Lebanese town of Biyyada and targeted three Israeli military bulldozers operating in Khiam. The group also said it launched rocket and artillery attacks on Israeli soldiers stationed in the town of Rashaf.

stories.title: Trump departs China touting deals, but little clarity on Iran or Taiwan
stories.summary: President Trump departed China promoting trade deals but left unresolved questions on Iran and Taiwan. He told reporters he was still deciding on a new Taiwan weapons package and said he was not seeking favors from Beijing regarding Iran.

stories.title: Russians published footage of a drone striking a UN convoy in Kherson. UN says they “don’t know” who did it.
stories.summary: Footage emerged showing a drone striking a UN convoy in the Kherson region of Ukraine. The UN said it could not confirm who carried out the attack, though Kherson has faced sustained drone strikes from Russian-held territory across the Dnipro River.

stories.title: US justice department to seek death penalty for man charged with killing two Israeli embassy staffers
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department announced it will seek the death penalty for Elias Rodriguez, who is charged with fatally shooting two Israeli embassy staffers, Yaron Lischinsky and Sarah Milgrim, outside the Capital Jewish Museum in Washington, D.C. Rodriguez faces federal hate crime and murder charges.

stories.title: Anti-Israel US Senate candidate with covered up Nazi tattoo splits Jewish Democrats summit
stories.summary: A US Senate candidate named Graham Platner, who has a covered-up Nazi tattoo and supports ending US military assistance to Israel, divided attendees at a Jewish Democrats summit. The party is weighing whether to back Platner as a potential candidate to help retake the Senate.

stories.title: Russia pounds Kyiv as its advance in eastern Ukraine slows to a crawl
stories.summary: Russia launched heavy strikes on Kyiv while its ground advance in eastern Ukraine slowed significantly. Ukraine has conducted a successful campaign to disrupt Russian arms and fuel supplies reaching the front lines.

stories.title: Threatened indictment of Raúl Castro ratchets up US pressure on Cuba
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering a federal indictment of former Cuban President Raúl Castro, 94, echoing the earlier indictment of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. The move is seen as an effort to intensify pressure on Cuba's communist leadership amid an ongoing fuel crisis on the island.

stories.title: India-U.K. trade deal hits late-stage ‘sticking points’ just before implementation date
stories.summary: India and the United Kingdom face late-stage sticking points in their trade deal ahead of its implementation date, with Indian Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal citing unresolved issues related to steel that both sides are working to address.

stories.title: Ukraine vows more strikes on Russia after attack on Kyiv kills 24
stories.summary: Ukraine vowed to carry out additional retaliatory strikes against Russia following a Russian attack on Kyiv that killed 24 people, including children. The strike on the Ukrainian capital prompted international condemnation.

stories.title: Pentagon informed Army ‘just a couple of days ago’ on decision to halt Poland deployment
stories.summary: Acting Army Chief of Staff Gen. Christopher LaNeve said the Pentagon informed the Army only days before the decision to halt a planned deployment to Poland. LaNeve described the process as recent, with recommendations exchanged before the final order was issued.

stories.title: Tennessee Democrat ends re-election bid after map redrawing carves up his district
stories.summary: Democratic Representative Steve Cohen of Tennessee announced he will not seek re-election after Republicans enacted a new congressional map that carved up his majority-Black Memphis district. The redistricting followed a recent Supreme Court decision and is part of a broader GOP strategy to protect its House majority.

stories.title: A test for Ukraine, a dilemma for Zelensky: What's at stake in the Andriy Yermak corruption probe
stories.summary: Former top Ukrainian presidential aide Andriy Yermak was arrested on corruption charges, accused of laundering roughly 460 million hryvnia (over $10 million) through an elite real estate project near Kyiv. The case poses a significant test for Ukraine's anti-corruption institutions and President Volodymyr Zelensky's government.

stories.title: India can play ‘greater role’ for peace in West Asia, says Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said India can play a greater role in promoting peace in West Asia. He added that Iran is ready to help ensure passage of all vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, describing the current situation there as very complicated.

stories.title: Palestinian family accuses Booking.com of illegal land use
stories.summary: A Palestinian family has accused the online travel platform Booking.com of profiting from land that was confiscated from them and allocated to Israeli settlers in the occupied territories.

stories.title: Palestinian family accuses Booking.com over illegal land use
stories.summary: A Palestinian family has accused Booking.com of profiting from land that was confiscated from them and allocated to Israeli settlers. The family alleges the platform facilitates listings on illegally occupied territory.

stories.title: Authorities search waters in the Maldives after five Italians killed in a cave dive accident
stories.summary: Authorities in the Maldives are searching waters after five Italian divers were killed in a cave diving accident. An Italian expert has joined police divers and rescue vessels in the search effort.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia preparing new strikes on “decision-making centers” in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense intelligence obtained documents indicating Russia is preparing new missile and drone strikes targeting nearly two dozen political decision-making centers and military facilities across Ukraine.

stories.title: Drake hits out at DJ Khaled for Gaza war silence
stories.summary: Canadian rapper Drake released a track titled "Make Them Pay" in which he criticised DJ Khaled for not speaking out about Israel's war on Gaza.

stories.title: Israeli army chief stresses 'readiness' during surprise military drill
stories.summary: Israeli army chief of staff Eyal Zamir conducted a surprise military exercise called "Broil and Fire" on Israel's eastern border. Zamir emphasized the need for constant readiness against surprise attacks, citing lessons from the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.

stories.title: BRICS ministers fail to issue a joint statement over differences on West Asia conflict
stories.summary: A two-day meeting of BRICS foreign ministers in New Delhi ended without a joint statement due to differing views among member states on the conflict in West Asia.

stories.title: Spain 'on right side of history' with Eurovision boycott: PM
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Spain's boycott of the Eurovision song contest over Israel's war in Gaza places the country "on the right side of history."

stories.title: Met police preparing for large scale far-right and pro-Palestine protests in London
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are preparing a large-scale operation as more than 100,000 demonstrators from far-right and pro-Palestine marches are expected on the same day as the FA Cup final at Wembley. Officers across central London will receive extra powers to manage the events, including a march organized by Stephen Yaxley-Lennon.

stories.title: Congo, Rwanda head for showdown over Francophonie top job
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda are competing over the leadership of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), with both countries fielding rival candidates. The diplomatic contest comes as fighting continues in eastern Congo.

stories.title: UAE to 'accelerate' new oil pipeline bypassing Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will fast-track construction of a new oil pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. The decision follows disruptions to oil exports through the waterway caused by the regional war.

stories.title: Latest Ukraine–Russia prisoner swap completed with UAE mediation
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates mediated the latest Ukraine-Russia prisoner swap, resulting in the release of 205 prisoners on each side. It marks the 23rd successful exchange facilitated by the UAE.

stories.title: India, UAE agree on framework for strategic defence partnership during Modi visit
stories.summary: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to the UAE, India and the United Arab Emirates agreed on a framework for a strategic defence partnership, including deepened defence industrial collaboration. The two nations also signed agreements on strategic petroleum reserves and liquefied petroleum gas supply.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine swap 205 prisoners of war each
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged 205 prisoners of war each on Friday, fulfilling an agreement linked to a ceasefire brokered by U.S. President Donald Trump earlier in May.

stories.title: Trump dismisses reports Iran retains missile launchers as ‘fake news’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump dismissed reports that Iran still possesses a large number of missile launchers, calling the claims "fake news." Speaking aboard Air Force One, he said most launchers had been destroyed and warned remaining ones could be quickly eliminated.

stories.title: Canada-led brigade in Latvia moves beyond tripwire role, commander says
stories.summary: The Canada-led NATO brigade deployed in Latvia has expanded beyond its initial tripwire deterrence role, according to its commander. The unit leader told Defense News that no force currently positioned across the border could defeat the brigade.

stories.title: Zelensky condemns Russia after strike on Kyiv apartment block kills 24
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike on an apartment block in Kyiv killed 24 people, including three children. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned Russia for the attack.

stories.title: Israel army chief 'secretly visited UAE during Iran war'
stories.summary: Israeli army chief Eyal Zamir reportedly made a secret visit to the United Arab Emirates during the Iran war. He is the latest Israeli leader said to have visited the UAE, following reports of Prime Minister Netanyahu's secret talks with Mohammed bin Zayed.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine swop 205 prisoners of war each
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine carried out a prisoner-of-war swap of 205 detainees each. The exchange came a week after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a large swap agreement between the two sides.

stories.title: Eurovision boycotts: "The biggest crisis in the contest's 70-year history"
stories.summary: Multiple countries have boycotted the Eurovision Song Contest over the inclusion of Israel in the 2026 edition, prompting what commentators call the biggest crisis in the competition's 70-year history. France 24 reported that politics have increasingly shaped the contest over the past three years.

stories.title: Zaha omitted from Ivory Coast World Cup squad
stories.summary: Former Crystal Palace forward Wilfried Zaha has been omitted from Ivory Coast's squad for the World Cup. Four current Premier League players were included in the selection.

stories.title: Lack of trust impeding talks to end war with the US: Iran FM
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that a lack of trust is the primary obstacle in negotiations to end the war with the United States. He indicated Tehran would be open to receiving diplomatic assistance from other parties.

stories.title: BRICS talks end without joint statement as divisions over Iran war deepen
stories.summary: A BRICS meeting concluded without a joint statement as member states disagreed over the Iran conflict. Iran's foreign minister had pushed members to condemn what he called violations of international law by the United States and Israel.

stories.title: ‘Extremely cruel and tragic’: Iranian director Asghar Farhadi speaks out against state violence and the war
stories.summary: Oscar-winning Iranian director Asghar Farhadi condemned both the killing of protesters in Iran and civilian deaths from bombing campaigns during a press conference at the Cannes Film Festival. His new Paris-set drama, Parallel Tales, premiered at the festival.

stories.title: Ukraine develops frontline power modules designed for extreme conditions – manufacturer
stories.summary: Ukrainian engineers have developed ruggedized power modules for frontline use that are dust- and water-resistant, produce no thermal signature, and can withstand drops and being run over by vehicles. The systems provide autonomous power for equipment and command posts.

stories.title: German leader Merz says he ‘would not advise my children to go’ to US
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told a conference of young Catholics in Würzburg that he would not advise his children to study or work in the United States given the current social climate, which he described as deeply polarizing. The remarks came amid an ongoing dispute with President Donald Trump over the Iran war.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Shabbat 250’ call divides US Jews ahead of National Mall prayer rally
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump called on Americans to observe "Shabbat 250," marking the first time a sitting president has urged the public celebration of the Jewish Sabbath. The initiative has drawn support from some Orthodox rabbis but criticism from left-leaning Jewish groups concerned about blurring the line between religion and state.

stories.title: 24 people killed in Russian strike on Kyiv. Rescuers clear the rubble of a destroyed nine-story building. The city is in mourning.
stories.summary: Two days after a May 9–11 truce ended, Russia struck Ukraine with 670 attack drones and 56 missiles. A nine-story residential building in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district collapsed, killing 24 people including three children. The search-and-rescue operation lasted over 24 hours.

stories.title: UK picks 4 companies for Apache drone wingman demonstrator project
stories.summary: The United Kingdom selected four companies for Project NYX, an Apache drone wingman concept demonstrator effort. The chosen firms are BAE Systems, the UK divisions of US-based Anduril, Portugal's Tekever, and French manufacturer Thales.

stories.title: Pakistan repatriates nationals from vessels seized by US
stories.summary: Pakistan Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced the repatriation of 11 Pakistani nationals and 20 Iranian citizens who had been aboard vessels seized by the US in international waters. The individuals traveled through Singapore and Bangkok before arriving in Islamabad, with Iranian nationals continuing onward to Tehran.

stories.title: Poland Arrests Alleged Russian Criminal Authority Near Warsaw
stories.summary: Polish authorities arrested an alleged senior Russian-speaking organized crime figure near Warsaw. The suspect was described as a "thief-in-law," a high-ranking status within the Russian-speaking criminal hierarchy.

stories.title: Israel kills seven in Lebanon as direct talks continue in US for second day
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed seven people in Lebanon while Lebanese and Israeli delegations held direct talks in Washington for a second day. Lebanon's delegation demanded an end to Israeli military attacks and the withdrawal of Israeli forces from its territory.

stories.title: Iran says lack of trust is the main obstacle in US negotiations
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that deep mistrust toward the United States remains the primary obstacle in ongoing negotiations between Tehran and Washington.

stories.title: US Marines practice seizing remote islands in Philippine exercise
stories.summary: U.S. Marines conducted exercises simulating the seizure of remote islands as part of a military drill in the Philippines. Personnel operating the Marine Air Defense Integrated System used the opportunity to conduct live-fire training with rounds and missiles.

stories.title: New York Times defends journalist after Israel threatens to sue
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered legal action against The New York Times over an article alleging that Israeli security officials raped Palestinian detainees. The newspaper has defended its journalist and the reporting.

stories.title: First Palestinian ICC filing against Hamas alleges war crimes, seeks arrests - exclusive
stories.summary: A Palestinian has filed what is described as the first complaint by a Palestinian against Hamas at the International Criminal Court, alleging war crimes committed against Palestinian civilians and seeking arrest warrants. To date, the ICC has not charged Hamas with crimes against its own population.

stories.title: US energy secretary says China likely to buy more American oil
stories.summary: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said he expects China to increase purchases of American crude oil amid the ongoing US-Israeli conflict with Iran. He called for reopening the Persian Gulf and placed responsibility on Iran for the timeline of normalization.

stories.title: Arrest warrants for Putin and Lvova-Belova must be enforced – Betsa
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Betsa called for the enforcement of International Criminal Court arrest warrants issued for Russian President Vladimir Putin and Commissioner Maria Lvova-Belova. Betsa urged intensified sanctions and continued international pressure to secure the return of deported Ukrainian children.

stories.title: The Xi-Trump summit is over. What comes next in the US-China rivalry?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump concluded a state visit to Beijing with private discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping in the Zhongnanhai compound. The two leaders walked the compound's gardens and agreed to continue meeting throughout the year, though no formal deal-signing ceremony took place.

stories.title: Russia’s state pollster changed its methodology and also started going door-to-door to ask people whether they support Putin. The president’s rating immediately went up.
stories.summary: Russia's state pollster VTsIOM reported President Putin's approval rating rose to 66.8% for May 4–10, up 1.2 points from the prior survey. The increase followed a change in methodology that included door-to-door polling.

stories.title: The Trump-Xi Summit Was Remarkably Banal
stories.summary: A summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping took place with relatively low-key outcomes. Observers noted that a more confident China appeared content to downplay the significance of the presidential meeting.

stories.title: 5 suspects, including teen, indicted in deadly shooting in north caught on camera
stories.summary: Five suspects, including a teenager, were indicted in Israel for the fatal shooting of 21-year-old Wael Saeida outside a bakery in the country's north. Police said the attack was part of a series targeting businesses owned by a relative of a student involved in a high school brawl.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian Caspian Fleet base deep inside Russia, home to missile-capable ships used in Kalibr strikes – General Staff
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported strikes on the Russian Caspian Fleet base at Kaspiysk, damaging naval vessels capable of launching Kalibr cruise missiles, as well as a major oil refinery. Additional Ukrainian strikes targeted Russian logistics and weapons storage sites.

stories.title: Cannes: Iranian director Farhadi condemns both US-Israeli attacks, crackdown on protesters
stories.summary: Iranian director Asghar Farhadi condemned civilian deaths caused by US and Israeli air strikes in Iran as well as the Iranian government's crackdown on domestic protesters during a press conference at the Cannes Film Festival, where his latest film Parallel Tales premiered.

stories.title: Oman caught between US and Iran after Tehran claims joint strait of Hormuz plan
stories.summary: Oman faces diplomatic pressure after Iran claimed it is coordinating with Muscat on managing the Strait of Hormuz, including plans to impose fees on transiting commercial ships. The United States opposes the plan. The waterway, which normally carries a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, has been blockaded for 10 weeks since the US-Israeli attack on Iran.

stories.title: Haiti: At least 78 dead in violent Port-au-Prince gang clashes
stories.summary: At least 78 people have been killed since May 9 in violent clashes between gangs in the suburbs of Port-au-Prince, Haiti's capital. The Caribbean nation has experienced a severe deterioration in security over the past two years due to escalating gang violence.

stories.title: Full list of Israel's ceasefire violations in Gaza, seven months on
stories.summary: More than seven months after a US-mediated ceasefire was announced in Gaza, Israel has continued near-daily strikes and violations of the agreement. A humanitarian crisis persists as Israel maintains a blockade on the Palestinian enclave.

stories.title: Russia must return Ukrainian children unconditionally, not through exchanges – Betsa
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Betsa stated that including deported Ukrainian children on any exchange lists is unacceptable, insisting Russia must return them unconditionally rather than as part of prisoner or hostage swaps.

stories.title: UAE chooses to deepen ties with Israel amid war with Iran, risking rift with Saudis
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is deepening its ties with Israel amid the ongoing war with Iran, a move experts say reflects a pragmatic security partnership. The decision risks straining relations with Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states that view Israel more critically.

stories.title: Health authorities order halt to use of medical devices tied to patient’s death
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Department of Health ordered hospitals to stop using a batch of blood pressure monitoring sets after an improperly sealed device was linked to the death of a 75-year-old man during heart surgery at Tuen Mun Hospital. The local supplier was also ordered to halt sales of the affected batch pending investigation.

stories.title: Philippines will ‘definitely’ comply with ICC request to arrest senator, Minister says
stories.summary: A Philippines government minister said the country would "definitely" comply with any International Criminal Court request to arrest a senator wanted by the court.

stories.title: Eight Pakistani troops killed in nighttime storming of border outpost
stories.summary: Militants attacked a security outpost in northwestern Pakistan, ramming an explosives-laden vehicle into the camp before engaging in a gun battle. Eight Pakistani troops were killed in the nighttime assault.

stories.title: EU facing 'second big wake-up call' on energy, Irish Minister Darragh O'Brien says
stories.summary: Irish Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment Darragh O'Brien warned that the EU is facing a "second big wake-up call" on energy security. O'Brien has been directly involved in managing rising energy costs stemming from the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: 36 countries approve creation of special Ukraine tribunal to prosecute Russia
stories.summary: Thirty-six countries, including 34 European states plus Australia and Costa Rica, approved the creation of a special tribunal for Ukraine. The proposed legal body would enable Kyiv to prosecute Russia for the crime of aggression related to its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister reiterates Iranian control over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi affirmed Iran's role as protector of security in the Strait of Hormuz during a meeting with Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. Araghchi also called on BRICS nations in New Delhi to condemn US and Israeli actions against Iran.

stories.title: India and UAE sign defence pacts, as Iran war tensions simmer
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and UAE leaders signed defence agreements during Modi's visit to the UAE. The pacts focus on maritime security, cyberdefence, and military collaboration amid regional tensions linked to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on oil refinery in Ryazan, Russian warships in Kaspiysk
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region and Russian warships stationed in Kaspiysk, Dagestan, carried out on May 14–15 as part of broader operations against key enemy targets.

stories.title: Palestinians in Gaza mark anniversary of 1948 mass expulsion
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza commemorated the anniversary of the 1948 Nakba, when hundreds of thousands were expelled from their homes. Yusuf Abu Hamam's village of al-Joura was demolished by the Israeli military and is now covered by neighborhoods of the city of Ashqelon and a national park. The area where his family resettled also lies largely in ruins.

stories.title: ‘Some hide their crosses’: Jerusalem nun attack highlights Israel’s growing anti-Christian problem
stories.summary: A foreign nun was physically assaulted in Jerusalem last month, highlighting what local activists and clergy describe as a surge in anti-Christian incidents in Israel. They attribute the rise to a small minority of ultra-religious nationalist and ultra-Orthodox Jews becoming increasingly emboldened in their hostility.

stories.title: Israeli-born Dutch politician calls for violence worse than Gaza against Palestinians
stories.summary: Israeli-born Dutch lawmaker Gidi Markuszower called for blocking Palestinian refugees from entering the Netherlands "with more force than where they came from." The remarks, made in a video interview with Left Laser, prompted a formal complaint over incitement to violence.

stories.title: Ukraine: Dozens of European countries sign up to special tribunal plan to prosecute Russia
stories.summary: More than 30 countries agreed at talks in Moldova to join a planned special tribunal to prosecute Russia over its invasion of Ukraine. Questions remain about how the tribunal would compel Russian officials to stand trial.

stories.title: UK: 'Andy Burnham is by far and away the favourite of all Labour Party members across all stripes'
stories.summary: Political commentator Matthew Torbitt assessed UK Labour leader Keir Starmer can likely survive a leadership challenge in the short term because Labour's internal rules require 81 MPs to back a single challenger. Torbitt identified Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham as the clear favourite among Labour members across all factions.

stories.title: Last chance: join the Hartman Institute in Jerusalem this summer! - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Hartman Institute in Jerusalem is promoting its remaining spots in summer programs for community leaders, rabbis, and educators. This is sponsored promotional content.

stories.title: Parts of Somalia face famine risk for first time since 2022
stories.summary: Parts of southern Somalia face the risk of famine, with one district reaching a level of hunger not recorded in the country since 2022.

stories.title: US has redirected 75 commercial ships in Strait of Hormuz as of today
stories.summary: US Central Command reported that the United States has redirected 75 commercial vessels and disabled four others as part of its ongoing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Over 20 US warships are currently enforcing the blockade.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine swap 205 prisoners of war each
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine each exchanged 205 prisoners of war on Friday under an agreement tied to a three-day ceasefire brokered by U.S. President Donald Trump. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy described the swap as the first step in a larger exchange of 1,000 POWs per side.

stories.title: Hamas urges unity talks as Fatah conference begins
stories.summary: Hamas called for direct unity talks with Fatah on a unified Palestinian strategy as Fatah held its eighth conference. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas was re-elected during the gathering.

stories.title: Army’s autonomy office looks beyond drone, robot platforms to ‘packages of capability’
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's Campaign of Prime Experimentation Mission Autonomy office is shifting focus beyond individual drone and robot platforms toward integrated "packages of capability." The office will initially prioritize combat engineering, fires, and logistics applications.

stories.title: Return of deported Ukrainian children gains Global South support
stories.summary: Panama joined the International Coalition for the Return of Ukrainian Children, marking growing Global South support for the effort to repatriate Ukrainian minors deported to Russia.

stories.title: Full list of Israel's ceasefire violations in Gaza, seven months on
stories.summary: A report compiled alleged Israeli ceasefire violations in Gaza over a seven-month period since a US-backed truce took effect. The documented violations include deadly air strikes, expansion of no-go zones, restrictions on humanitarian aid, and border closures, deepening the humanitarian crisis in the enclave.

stories.title: Trump says he’s OK with Iran suspending nuke program for 20 years if there’s a ‘real’ commitment
stories.summary: President Trump indicated he would accept Iran suspending its nuclear program for 20 years given a "real" commitment, stepping back from his earlier demand for a total end to Iranian enrichment. Iranian FM Araghchi responded that Tehran has "no trust" in the US.

stories.title: Russia wants Belarus to join new “aggressive operations” against Ukraine or NATO, Kyiv says
stories.summary: Ukraine's government reported it has documented contacts between Russia and Belarus tied to potential planning for aggressive operations that could be launched from Belarusian territory against Ukraine or NATO countries.

stories.title: Hegseth memo calls for sweeping, open-ended review of Pentagon's legal system
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a memo directing a broad, open-ended review of the Pentagon's legal system. The directive targets both military and civilian lawyers within the Department of Defense and represents his latest unconventional action regarding DOD legal operations.

stories.title: Two more Russian air defense systems gone, along with a naval plane and helicopter
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone forces destroyed a Russian Tor-M2 air defense system in Luhansk Oblast and a Pantsir-S1 in Crimea. They also struck a ship in Berdyansk and destroyed a Be-200 aircraft and Ka-27 helicopter at Russia's Yeysk base.

stories.title: Hong Kong police call to criminalise bid-rigging in wake of Tai Po estate blaze
stories.summary: Hong Kong police have proposed legislation to criminalise bid-rigging, enforced by a designated agency, following the deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po last November. The proposal, submitted to an independent inquiry, also recommends enhanced leniency agreements for whistle-blowers, citing shortcomings in the current civil competition regime.

stories.title: Erling Haaland to make film acting debut – as a Viking called Haaland
stories.summary: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland will make his feature acting debut voicing a Viking character named Haaland in the animated film Viqueens. The film is directed by Dutch-Norwegian filmmaker Harald Zwart, known for The Karate Kid.

stories.title: ‘May do it. May not do it’: Trump keeps up suspense over arms to Taiwan, says no to war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump declared the United States will not go to war over Taiwan, while revealing he and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed Taiwan extensively during his state visit to Beijing. Trump declined to confirm future arms sales to Taiwan, leaving the status of major pending arms packages uncertain.

stories.title: Palestinian Prisoners Club: over 23,000 arrested in occupied West Bank since start of Israel's genocide
stories.summary: The Palestinian Prisoners Club reported that Israel has arrested over 23,000 Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since the start of the war in Gaza, according to Wafa news agency. The figure excludes thousands more arrested in Gaza during the same period.

stories.title: Angus Taylor says migrants are a ‘net drain’ on Australia. The numbers say the opposite is true
stories.summary: Australian opposition leader Angus Taylor characterized migrants as a "net drain" on Australia. Analysis of available data indicates the opposite, showing migrants are generally younger, more skilled, and more educated than the average Australian, typically paying more in taxes than they receive in government services.

stories.title: Secret documents reveal preferred Australian nuclear submarine base – and warn it could be a military target
stories.summary: Previously secret New South Wales government documents identify Port Kembla, 75 kilometers south of Sydney, as the preferred east coast base for Australia's proposed nuclear submarine fleet under the AUKUS agreement. The documents warn the base could become a target for military adversaries and anticipate local resistance over nuclear accident risks.

stories.title: Russian troops refuse to cross Dnipro River in Prydniprovske sector, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian troops resumed operations near the Antonivskyi Bridge in the Prydniprovske sector after regrouping, but assault units are refusing orders to cross the Dnipro River channels and land on the islands.

stories.title: Trump says he discussed Taiwan arms sale with China’s Xi Jinping
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump confirmed he discussed American arms sales to Taiwan during talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, though specifics of the exchange were not disclosed.

stories.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power
stories.summary: Mali's armed forces, supported by Russian mercenaries, launched airstrikes against a rebel alliance comprising Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists. The strikes targeted the northern town of Kidal, which rebels seized during a surprise offensive across much of Mali in late April, as the ruling military junta fights to maintain control.

stories.title: Civilians caught in war of drones in eastern DR Congo
stories.summary: In eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, ongoing fighting has taken a new turn as civilians are being struck by drone attacks far from front lines, even as peace talks continue.

stories.title: Israeli and Lebanese diplomats arrived at US Department of State for ceasefire negotiations
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese delegations arrived at the US Department of State for a second day of ceasefire negotiations ahead of the expected expiration of the Lebanon ceasefire agreement. Lebanon's Health Ministry reports Israeli attacks have killed over 657 people in Lebanon since the truce began.

stories.title: From destroyers to drones, how a Europe-led coalition aims to open the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A European coalition led by the United Kingdom and France is planning an operation to secure the Strait of Hormuz, potentially involving up to 40 nations. The initiative, combining destroyers and drones, would only begin after a ceasefire is declared in the region.

stories.title: Russia already fights with significant shortage of manpower, says Hnatov
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Hnatov stated that the Russian army is conducting combat operations in Ukraine while facing a significant shortage of manpower on the battlefield.

stories.title: Far-right activists barred from UK before Tommy Robinson rally
stories.summary: Eleven foreign far-right activists were blocked from entering the UK ahead of a rally organized by Tommy Robinson supporters. Prime Minister Keir Starmer accused Robinson of "peddling hatred and division," while the Archbishop of Canterbury urged people to "choose hope" before the Saturday demonstration.

stories.title: India ready to extend all possible support for peace in West Asia: PM Modi in UAE
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, speaking during a visit to the UAE, condemned recent attacks on the Emirates and offered India's support for peace in West Asia. Modi made the remarks during a meeting with the UAE's leader.

stories.title: 9 terrorists killed, 4 security personnel martyred as attack on army camp in Bajaur repulsed: sources
stories.summary: Security forces in Pakistan's Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, repulsed an attack on an army camp by Fitna-al-Khawarij militants linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. Nine attackers were killed, while four Pakistani security personnel died in the engagement.

stories.title: UAE accelerates pipeline project to bypass Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will accelerate construction of a West-East oil pipeline to double the export capacity of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC). The pipeline, expected to be operational by 2027, is designed to allow the UAE to bypass the Strait of Hormuz for oil exports.

stories.title: Araghchi: Iran doubts US ‘seriousness’ about talks amid nuclear deadlock
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi expressed distrust toward the United States regarding war negotiations during a BRICS meeting in India, citing doubts about Washington's seriousness in pursuing diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Putin Expected to Visit China Next Week, Reports Say
stories.summary: The Kremlin confirmed preparations are underway for President Vladimir Putin to visit China, with reports indicating the trip could take place as soon as next week. A specific date has not yet been announced.

stories.title: Egypt's farmers hit by Iran war price surge
stories.summary: Egyptian smallholder farmers have been severely affected by the Iran war, as soaring fertilizer prices have forced many to lay off workers and reduce the amount of land under cultivation.

stories.title: UAE tried to coordinate with Saudi Arabia, Qatar to strike Iran during recent war - report
stories.summary: The UAE attempted to persuade Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and other Gulf states to coordinate a military response to Iranian missile and drone attacks during the recent war, according to Bloomberg sources. The neighboring countries refused to participate in the proposed joint action.

stories.title: Nakba: Jewish voices are challenging the stories Israel tells about itself
stories.summary: A film director, historian, and Holocaust survivor spoke to Al Jazeera about shifting perspectives among Jewish voices regarding the narratives Israel tells about its own history, tied to the anniversary of the Nakba.

stories.title: India and UAE sign defence and energy deals during Modi's state visit
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi signed defense and energy agreements with the UAE during a state visit to Abu Dhabi. The deals were concluded amid rising economic pressures on India linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Hungary’s Power Shift Opens Door for EU Sanctions on Israel
stories.summary: With a recent shift in Hungary's political stance removing Viktor Orbán's previous veto power, the European Union may now have an opening to expand sanctions against Israel over its activities in the West Bank.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teen, settlers set mosque ablaze
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a Palestinian teenager in the occupied West Bank, while settlers set a mosque ablaze in a separate incident. The arson was part of a series of settler attacks reportedly carried out under Israeli police protection.

stories.title: Peugeot, Jeep take on Chinese rivals with new models using local EV technologies
stories.summary: Stellantis, the parent company of Peugeot and Jeep, announced new investments to produce four electric vehicles with Chinese partner Dongfeng Motor, with production set to begin in 2027. The move leverages Chinese EV technologies to compete with domestic Chinese automakers in the world's largest car market.

stories.title: Russians intensify artillery fire in south and increase ammunition use, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian forces on the southern front have significantly intensified artillery fire and increased ammunition expenditure to support ongoing assault operations.

stories.title: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan faces growing pressure over its role as a mediator in the Iran conflict, balancing relationships with the United States, Iran, China, and Gulf allies. A recent US media report has placed Islamabad under additional scrutiny.

stories.title: Antisemitic comments flood posts celebrating Jewish American Heritage Month
stories.summary: The Blue Square Alliance reported that antisemitic comments have flooded social media posts celebrating Jewish American Heritage Month, including apolitical tributes from organizations like Sesame Street and the Grammys. The group warned the backlash is deterring organizations from recognizing Jewish contributions.

stories.title: Trump says he 'made no commitment either way' to Xi on Taiwan
stories.summary: President Trump stated he made "no commitment either way" to Chinese leader Xi Jinping regarding whether the US would defend Taiwan. Trump said Xi had asked directly, and he responded that he does not discuss that topic.

stories.title: 'The settlers are in control': How the West Bank is being ethnically cleansed
stories.summary: Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, backed by Israel's far-right government, have intensified actions against Palestinian communities. Travel between cities like Ramallah and Nablus, normally an hour-long journey, now takes much longer due to increased Israeli checkpoints.

stories.title: Israeli-born Dutch politician calls for violence worse than Gaza against Palestinians
stories.summary: Dutch far-right lawmaker Gidi Markuszower, who is Israeli-born, called for the use of force against Palestinians seeking asylum in the Netherlands. He suggested they should face harsher treatment than what they experienced in Gaza.

stories.title: North Korea slams U.K. over sanctions on children's camp
stories.summary: North Korea criticized the United Kingdom over sanctions related to a children's camp. The issue is connected to broader concerns about Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied territories being subjected to political indoctrination since Russia's 2022 invasion.

stories.title: Hantavirus outbreak tests post-COVID health communications playbook
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak has raised public health concerns after a cruise ship was placed in quarantine at sea. Several people have died and additional cases have been reported. The incident is testing health communication strategies developed in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic.

stories.title: Rapid-fire to restrained: China state visit reveals a changed Trump on social media
stories.summary: During his state visit to China, President Donald Trump adopted an unusually restrained social media presence, posting only about 10 updates since arriving in Beijing. His posts mostly featured arrival footage and official greetings, along with praise for Chinese President Xi Jinping as "one of the World's Great Leaders."

stories.title: Pressure mounts on embattled UK PM Keir Starmer as rivals circle
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting, seen as a rival to Prime Minister Keir Starmer, publicly backed Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham as a strong potential challenger to Starmer's leadership.

stories.title: War worsens Lebanon's economic crisis with job losses, slow business, soaring prices
stories.summary: Lebanon's economic crisis has worsened due to the 2024 war between Israel and Hezbollah, which caused an estimated $11 billion in damage. The World Bank reported that the country had already suffered approximately $70 billion in financial sector losses prior to the conflict.

stories.title: Pro-Israel protests at NYT over Palestinian detainees report
stories.summary: Pro-Israel demonstrators gathered outside the New York Times headquarters in New York City to protest a published report detailing allegations of abuse against Palestinian detainees held by Israeli forces.

stories.title: Israel strikes towns near Tyre, Southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces launched air strikes near Hiram Hospital and residential areas on the outskirts of Tyre in southern Lebanon. An Israeli military spokesperson also announced new displacement orders for four additional villages in southern Lebanon, despite an ongoing ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Is Europe getting its act together on defence? Multiple threats prompt EU rearmament
stories.summary: The European Union is advancing its Readiness 2030 defense plan, originally called ReArmEU, to significantly boost military capacities. European intelligence agencies have warned the bloc could face a major conflict by 2030, prompting accelerated rearmament efforts.

stories.title: Drones to fight school shooters? One US company says yes
stories.summary: A U.S. company is developing drones designed to respond to school shootings. The drones do not fire bullets or any other projectiles.

stories.title: Two killed as heavy rains batter Sri Lanka; thousands affected
stories.summary: Heavy rains in Sri Lanka killed at least two people and affected more than 4,000 others. Authorities placed over 100 people from 29 families in two temporary relief centers.

stories.title: Russia deploys 320 soldiers to assault units of 5th Army following losses near Huliaipole, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Russia deployed 320 soldiers from rear areas in the Russian Federation to the Rostov region to reinforce assault units of the 5th Army, which suffered losses in fighting near Huliaipole, according to Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn.

stories.title: Lebanese deeply divided over chances of peace talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese public opinion is deeply divided over the prospects of peace talks with Israel. A third round of direct negotiations is taking place in the United States while fighting continues in southern Lebanon despite an existing truce.

stories.title: Russian Dissident Nina Litvinova Dies by Suicide at 80
stories.summary: Russian dissident Nina Litvinova died by suicide at the age of 80. In a note shared by her cousin, Litvinova wrote that life had become unbearable since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump, Xi weigh AI ‘guardrails’ as Nvidia chip exports hang in the balance
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese officials discussed artificial intelligence "guardrails" and the status of Nvidia H200 chip exports during Trump's state visit to Beijing. Trump said both sides talked about possibly working together on AI safeguards.

stories.title: Ukraine war: 36 nations approve tribunal creation to prosecute Russia over invasion
stories.summary: Thirty-six parties—including 34 European states, Australia, Costa Rica, and the EU—approved joining a future special tribunal to prosecute Russia for its invasion of Ukraine. The tribunal is based on an accord signed between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and the Council of Europe.

stories.title: 78 years later: Palestinians are still denied their right to return.
stories.summary: The article marks 78 years since approximately 800,000 Palestinians were displaced during the events of 1948. Their descendants remain refugees, and their right to return has not been fulfilled.

stories.title: Spain's Sanchez slams Israeli minister for attack on Yamal over Palestinian flag
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez defended FC Barcelona star Lamine Yamal after Israel's defense minister accused the 18-year-old of inciting hatred for waving a Palestinian flag during a victory parade. Sanchez said he was proud of the player.

stories.title: Ukrainian flag flies again over Odradne, six months after Russia overran the village
stories.summary: Ukraine's 129th Brigade recaptured the village of Odradne in Kharkiv Oblast's Kupiansk sector, pushing Russian forces from fortified positions, treelines, and strongpoints roughly six months after Russia had overrun the settlement.

stories.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Invade Oyo School, Abduct Principal, Students
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a school in the Ahoro-Esinele community in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State, Nigeria, abducting the school's principal and an unspecified number of students during a morning raid.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia pushes for regional non-aggression pact with Iran
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is promoting a regional non-aggression pact with Iran, modeled on the 1970s détente between the West and the Soviet Union. European countries are backing Riyadh's proposal for a broad understanding with Tehran.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 - Daniel Challenges Abiodun to Live Debate Over Ogun East Ticket
stories.summary: Former Ogun State governor and current senator Gbenga Daniel challenged Governor Dapo Abiodun to a live television debate over the Ogun East senatorial ticket ahead of Nigeria's 2027 elections.

stories.title: Nigeria: Alleged N36m Fraud - EFCC Arraigns Blessing CEO in Lagos
stories.summary: Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission arraigned social media figure Blessing CEO in Lagos over alleged fraud amounting to 36 million naira.

stories.title: Kenya: Matatu Operators Announce 50 Percent Fare Hike, Threaten Nationwide Strike Over Fuel Price Shock
stories.summary: Matatu operators in Kenya announced plans to raise fares by up to 50 percent following a sudden rise in fuel prices and threatened a nationwide strike starting Monday unless the government intervenes to address rising operating costs.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit: China, US disagree on what they agreed on
stories.summary: Following the Trump-Xi summit, the US highlighted trade deals while China said it warned Washington over Taiwan. Neither side confirmed the other's version of what was agreed upon.

stories.title: What was actually achieved at Trump and Xi’s ‘stalemate summit’ in Beijing?
stories.summary: President Trump's state visit to Beijing—the first U.S. presidential visit to China in nearly a decade—concluded with Trump claiming he and President Xi Jinping "settled a lot of different problems." However, Trump provided little detail on specific outcomes or agreements reached during the talks.

stories.title: Iran has 'no trust' in the US, will negotiate only if it is serious, Araghchi says
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated in New Delhi that Iran has no trust in the United States but is willing to negotiate if Washington demonstrates seriousness. He said Iran is maintaining the ceasefire to give diplomacy an opportunity, while attending the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting.

stories.title: From Nakba to genocide: A Gaza grandmother’s lifetime of loss and resilience
stories.summary: Fatema Obaid, a 95-year-old Palestinian grandmother who survived the 1948 Nakba, has endured Israeli bombardment in Gaza and the loss of 70 family members. She refused to leave Gaza City when ordered to do so by the Israeli military during the conflict that began in 2023.

stories.title: China’s Xi Jinping to pay first state visit to US in more than a decade
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to pay a state visit to the United States in September, the first such visit in over a decade. U.S. President Donald Trump said after departing Beijing that he and Xi plan to meet three more times this year, including at the APEC summit.

stories.title: Weaponizing the Westerlies: Ukrainian balloons sow havoc over Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine is increasingly deploying aerostats carried by westerly winds to conduct strikes and gather intelligence over Russian territory. The balloon operations also force Russia to expend air-defense resources intercepting them.

stories.title: Defense Forces regain control over Odradne in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces regained control of the village of Odradne and its surrounding areas in Kharkiv Oblast, reclaiming territory previously held by Russian forces.

stories.title: UK government faces weeks of uncertainty over the prime minister's future
stories.summary: The UK government faces prolonged uncertainty after internal Labour Party maneuvering failed to oust Prime Minister Keir Starmer but triggered a leadership contest that could extend into the summer. One Cabinet member resigned and dozens of lawmakers called for Starmer to step down.

stories.title: Here’s how the Army plans to spend nearly $1 billion in procuring small counter drone tech
stories.summary: The US Army's fiscal year 2027 budget request allocates approximately $994 million in discretionary funding for the procurement of small counter-drone technology, reflecting growing Pentagon investment in counter-UAS capabilities.

stories.title: Trump's silence on Taiwan during summit with Xi comes as relief for island nation
stories.summary: During his state visit to China, U.S. President Donald Trump remained silent on Taiwan while Chinese President Xi Jinping warned that mishandling the issue could lead to conflict. Analysts in Taiwan interpreted Trump's silence as a sign the U.S. would maintain its longstanding policy.

stories.title: IDF chief Zamir is latest top Israeli official said to have visited UAE amid Iran war
stories.summary: IDF Chief Zamir reportedly visited the UAE during the Iran war, adding to a series of disclosed high-level Israeli visits to the Gulf state. US officials previously confirmed that Israel provided the UAE with Iron Dome defense systems during the conflict, though the UAE has denied the reported visits.

stories.title: Indian magnate Adani agrees to multi-million-dollar penalty in US court case
stories.summary: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani agreed to pay a multi-million-dollar civil settlement in a U.S. court case linked to an alleged $250 million bribery scheme involving Indian solar energy contracts. Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani did not admit guilt as part of the agreement.

stories.title: Dakar Eilat: Inside prisons for Hamas terrorists
stories.summary: A former Israeli prison commander responded to New York Times allegations of sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees, offering his perspective on prisoner treatment and oversight mechanisms within the prison system.

stories.title: The Rubble Doctrine: Inside Israel's new security policy in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military has adopted what has been described as a "Rubble Doctrine" in southern Lebanon, exemplified by the destruction of El-Khiam. The approach reflects a shift in Israeli security thinking after October 7, aimed at denying adversaries the physical capability to launch attacks.

stories.title: Funeral in Jabalia after Israeli strike hits Gaza wake despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Residents of Jabalia in northern Gaza buried two Palestinians killed in an Israeli strike that hit a wake, despite the ceasefire. Gaza authorities report nearly 73,000 total deaths, with ongoing truce violations.

stories.title: US-China summit exposes Trump's limits on Iran war, Taiwan
stories.summary: During a two-day US-China summit in Beijing, President Trump sought Chinese cooperation to help end the war in Iran, but no guarantees were secured. President Xi Jinping used the meeting to warn the United States over Taiwan.

stories.title: Israeli activists protest at New York Times building after article exposes rape of Palestinians
stories.summary: Pro-Israel activists protested outside the New York Times headquarters after the newspaper published an article by journalist Nicholas Kristof detailing allegations of Israeli soldiers raping Palestinian prisoners. Israel's government vowed to sue the paper and the journalist.

stories.title: Philippines vows to hand fugitive senator to ICC following shootout
stories.summary: The Philippine government announced it would surrender Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa to the International Criminal Court. Dela Rosa is wanted for his alleged role as a key enforcer of former President Rodrigo Duterte's deadly anti-drug campaign. The decision followed a recent shootout incident.

stories.title: SSU releases exclusive footage of today’s prisoner exchange
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service released footage of the May 15 prisoner exchange in which Ukrainian captives returned home after being freed from Russian custody.

stories.title: Palestine Action prisoner with muscular dystrophy says he is forced to 'crawl like a wounded dog'
stories.summary: Muhammad Umer Khalid, a Palestine Action member with muscular dystrophy, was denied bail despite medical evidence that his condition deteriorated during detention. He is held on remand in connection with charges related to a break-in at RAF Brize Norton in the UK.

stories.title: Tories suspend leader at Worcestershire council after he made deal to oust Reform
stories.summary: The Conservative Party suspended its leader at Worcestershire county council, Adam Kent, after he struck a deal with the Greens and Liberal Democrats to oust Reform UK from minority control of the council.

stories.title: A billionaire, a taco, reality TV: the top 4 attack lines in California’s elections
stories.summary: California's gubernatorial and mayoral primary races are intensifying less than three weeks before the primary election, with candidates engaging in sharp debates and social media exchanges.

stories.title: Iran allowing more ships through Strait of Hormuz, report says
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have begun allowing more ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state television. Tehran had largely blocked shipping through the strategic waterway following US-Israeli strikes since the outbreak of war on February 28.

stories.title: Is the Met favouring Tommy Robinson over the peaceful Nakba marchers?
stories.summary: Questions arose about London's Metropolitan Police treatment of pro-Palestinian Nakba marchers compared to far-right activist Tommy Robinson. Critics alleged that Palestinian voices were being marginalized while xenophobic figures received more favorable treatment from authorities.

stories.title: Russia presses college students to fill ranks of drone pilots
stories.summary: Russia's military is recruiting college students to serve as drone pilots, targeting a demographic that had previously been largely shielded from frontline combat roles in the war effort.

stories.title: Russia presses college students to fill ranks of drone pilots
stories.summary: Russia's military is recruiting college students to serve as drone pilots, targeting a demographic that had previously been largely shielded from frontline conscription. The effort reflects the military's growing need to fill specialized roles amid ongoing combat operations.

stories.title: How the fall of Starmer will reshape British policy on Israel
stories.summary: The leadership contest to succeed outgoing British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is expected to bring Israel's actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank into focus. Starmer's handling of the Gaza conflict is anticipated to become a major issue once the contest formally begins.

stories.title: Deadly attack on Pakistan outpost puts Afghanistan ceasefire at risk
stories.summary: Two attacks on Pakistani military outposts in the country's northwest region killed more than 20 people in recent days. The violence threatens to undermine a ceasefire arrangement between Pakistan and Afghanistan along their shared border.

stories.title: Prisoner swap goes ahead as Kyiv mourns 24 killed in Russian strike on flats
stories.summary: A prisoner swap between Ukraine and Russia proceeded on May 15 while Kyiv mourned 24 people killed in a Russian missile strike on a residential building. Among the victims was 12-year-old Lyubava Yakovleva, whose father had also been killed during the war.

stories.title: Rapprochement, debates, dissidents: US presidential visits to China
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing was the latest in a decades-long history of high-level diplomatic encounters between the two countries. Past presidential visits to China include Richard Nixon's groundbreaking 1972 trip to meet Chairman Mao Zedong.

stories.title: Finland says Helsinki drone threat has ended, reopens airport
stories.summary: Finland reopened Helsinki Airport after its defense forces declared that a drone threat in the area had ended. Fighter jets and emergency services had been scrambled in response to the earlier threat. Authorities did not immediately identify the source of the drone activity.

stories.title: Israeli settler attacks activist during tour on settler violence
stories.summary: A group of Israeli settlers physically attacked Israeli human rights activists during a tour focused on settler violence in the occupied West Bank. The incident occurred while the activists were documenting conditions in the territory.

stories.title: Trump leaves China without breakthroughs on Iran, Taiwan or AI
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump left China after a two-day summit with President Xi Jinping that featured extensive pageantry but produced few concrete breakthroughs on Iran, Taiwan, or AI. Details of announced trade deals remained scarce.

stories.title: IMF lauds resilient Hong Kong economy but warns of risks linked to Middle East war
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund praised Hong Kong's economic resilience and sustained recovery but warned of downside risks from escalating geopolitical tensions, including the Middle East conflict. The IMF also urged Hong Kong to pursue medium-term fiscal reforms, including introducing a goods and services tax.

stories.title: Bangalore: India's Silicon Valley, a city straining under pressure
stories.summary: Bengaluru, known as India's Silicon Valley, has grown into a major global tech hub hosting companies such as Apple, Microsoft, and Boeing, along with thousands of startups. The city of nearly 15 million people faces significant environmental pressures from its rapid development.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post published Shabbat candle lighting times for communities in Israel and the United States.

stories.title: In Zaporizhzhia, Russians strike industrial infrastructure facility; one person killed, and others injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an industrial infrastructure facility in the city of Zaporizhzhia, damaging a fuel tanker. One person was killed and three others were injured in the attack.

stories.title: UK artist defends pro-Palestine drawings after show cancellation
stories.summary: A UK art exhibition titled "Drawing Against Genocide" featuring pro-Palestine artwork was cancelled after UK Lawyers for Israel accused the show of being antisemitic. The artist defended the drawings and their intended message.

stories.title: What did American allies make of Trump’s trip to China to meet Xi?
