stories.summary: Pakistan's passport has been ranked 100th globally by the Henley Passport Index, offering visa-free access to 30 destinations. The ranking has gradually improved since 2021, though it remains near the bottom among 199 passports surveyed.

stories.title: Philippine politician wanted by ICC flees Senate
stories.summary: Philippine Senate President confirmed that Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court, fled the Senate building where he had been taking refuge.

stories.title: What is at stake as Fatah holds its 8th general congress?
stories.summary: The Palestinian Fatah movement is holding its 8th general congress after years of delays, with the event described as a contest over loyalty, succession, and the future direction of the movement.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 973 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region over past day, one person killed
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 973 strikes on 49 settlements across Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over the past day, killing one person. The attacks targeted a wide swath of communities in the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: 'Miraculous': 11 plane crash survivors rescued at sea off Florida
stories.summary: All 11 people aboard a private airplane that crashed into the sea off central Florida on May 13 survived and were rescued from a lifeboat. A U.S. Air Force Reserve team and the U.S. Coast Guard carried out the rescue operation hours after the crash.

stories.title: Eric and Lara Trump – the new US first family faces making the trip to China
stories.summary: Eric Trump, executive vice-president of the Trump family business empire, accompanied President Donald Trump on the state visit to Beijing. Eric and his wife Lara arrived on Air Force One on Wednesday night. Eric oversees investments in real estate, golf, and more recently cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.

stories.title: The New Era of Air and Missile Defense
stories.summary: A retired US Air Force brigadier general, now leading international business development at Northrop Grumman, argues that modern air and missile defense is approaching a structural limit. The article advocates for a new approach built on fire-control-level integration, disaggregated architectures, affordable magazine depth, and integrating offensive action as a central element of defense.

stories.title: Inside the rise of the Haftar family’s Dubai-based 'money man'
stories.summary: Ahmed Gadalla, described as the Haftar family's Dubai-based financial operative, controls companies across Libya, the UAE, Malta, and the UK. He is accused of being central to the Haftar family's illicit financial operations, allegations he denies.

stories.title: IMF funds arrive as govt opens pre-budget talks
stories.summary: Pakistan received $1.3 billion from the International Monetary Fund, boosting the State Bank of Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves above $17 billion. Simultaneously, an IMF mission began pre-budget discussions with Pakistani officials on revenue targets, tax measures, and fiscal reform.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Iran working on Hormuz ‘protocol’ to cover ‘costs’, says Dy FM Gharibabadi
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes struck seven vehicles in Lebanon, killing 12 people including a woman and her two children, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry. Separately, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi said Tehran is developing a Hormuz Strait protocol to cover associated costs.

stories.title: Trump in Beijing
stories.summary: An editorial discusses Donald Trump's arrival in Beijing for the first U.S. presidential visit to China in nearly a decade. The summit agenda includes trade, tariffs, and the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, amid broader debate about shifting global power dynamics.

stories.title: Israel issues threats to eight towns and villages in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation threats to residents of eight towns and villages in Lebanon's Bekaa region and the south ahead of potential strikes. Ongoing Israeli attacks have killed and wounded over a dozen people since the previous day.

stories.title: Israel's Prison Service expanded solitary confinement of Palestinians, report says
stories.summary: Israel's Prison Service has significantly increased its use of solitary confinement against Palestinian prisoners, including minors and women, since 2023. The data was obtained through a freedom of information request and reported by Physicians for Human Rights Israel, as cited by Haaretz.

stories.title: One killed, 16 injured in massive overnight attack on Kyiv
stories.summary: One person was killed and 16 others were injured during a massive overnight Russian attack on Kyiv. The strike was part of a large-scale combined missile and drone assault on the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Liaqat posthumously awarded for foiling suicide attack
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari posthumously awarded the Sitara-i-Shuja'at to Muhammad Liaqat, a railway employee who foiled a suicide attack in Attock. The honor was received by Liaqat's mother at an investiture ceremony at Aiwan-i-Sadr in Islamabad.

stories.title: Cathay Pacific moves forward Hong Kong boarding gate closure times by 5 minutes
stories.summary: Cathay Pacific Airways announced that starting June 1, boarding gates at Hong Kong International Airport will close 15 minutes before departure, five minutes earlier than the current policy. The airline will also begin boarding passengers five minutes earlier to improve on-time departures, citing late-arriving passengers as a key cause of delays.

stories.title: Iran ‘frighteningly close’ to developing nuclear weapons, US energy secretary says - report
stories.summary: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that Iran is "frighteningly close" to developing nuclear weapons. Wright said he considers even 20%-enriched uranium "very concerning" given the size of Iran's existing stockpile.

stories.title: China’s expanding industrial strategy
stories.summary: A report by the US Chamber of Commerce and Rhodium Group found that China's industrial policy is becoming more systematic, expanding beyond specific sectors to cover all layers of production. The latest five-year plan now encompasses frontier technologies including biomanufacturing, embodied intelligence, and intelligent driving.

stories.title: Cyber Operations Aren’t Slow — Our Thinking Is
stories.summary: A former cyber operations practitioner recounts a time-critical mission in which an al-Qaeda-affiliated group captured an American aid worker. Special operations forces required cyber-enabled geolocation within 30 minutes to launch a rescue, highlighting the speed at which cyber capabilities can be employed in real-world scenarios.

stories.title: Meet the New Host of Cogs of War
stories.summary: Ryan, the outgoing host of the defense-technology podcast Cogs of War, introduces Jonathan Panter as the new host and executive editor. Panter, a former naval officer turned scholar, discusses major defense technology issues and his goals for the show, published by War on the Rocks.

stories.title: Kenya: Voting Underway in Emurua Dikirr, Porro and Endo By-Elections Amid Ruto-Gachagua Rivalry
stories.summary: By-elections are underway in Kenya's Emurua Dikirr, Porro, and Endo constituencies. The contests are seen as an early test of political strength between President William Ruto and former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua ahead of the 2027 general election.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed US President Donald Trump in Beijing on Thursday for high-stakes discussions expected to cover trade, Iran, and Taiwan. Separately, Lebanon and Israel were set to hold new peace talks in Washington, even as Israel carried out overnight strikes killing and wounding more than a dozen people.

stories.title: DR Congo: HRW accuses M23 and Rwandan forces of killings, rape in Uvira
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch accused M23 rebels and Rwandan forces of committing summary executions, rape, and enforced disappearances during a month-long occupation of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Body of second missing US soldier recovered in Morocco
stories.summary: A search and rescue team recovered the body of a second U.S. service member near Cap Draa, Morocco, on May 14. The soldier had gone missing during a training exercise near a cliff. The recovery was announced jointly by the U.S. Army and Morocco's Royal Armed Forces.

stories.title: Law enforcement identifies Russian soldier involved in torturing judge in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement identified a Russian serviceman suspected of torturing a judge from a local court in the temporarily occupied territory of the Kharkiv region in 2022. The suspect has been formally notified of the charges against him.

stories.title: NY school district pays $125K to settle suit over erased pro-Palestinian student art
stories.summary: A Long Island, New York school district agreed to pay $125,000 to settle a lawsuit after a student's pro-Palestinian watermelon-themed parking spot artwork was painted over by the high school in 2024.

stories.title: While the War Continues in Ukraine, the Kremlin’s Real Battlefield is at Home
stories.summary: Russian officials announced the liberation of the Luhansk People's Republic for a third time on April 1, 2026, following earlier claims in July 2022 under then-Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu and again in July 2025. The article examines a pattern of repeated, contradictory success claims by the Kremlin as its war in Ukraine enters a fifth year.

stories.title: China’s Silk Road Express, best things to do in Nanjing: 7 Lifestyle highlights
stories.summary: The article highlights seven lifestyle stories, including a feature on China's luxury Silk Road Express train and its new route departing from Chengdu West Railway Station. The curated selection also covers things to do in Nanjing and other travel and culture topics from the past week.

stories.title: Supreme Court settles controversy over drug test reports
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court ruled by a 4-1 majority that mentioning full forensic protocols in government analysts' drug test reports is directory rather than mandatory, settling a long-running legal controversy over narcotics case evidence standards.

stories.title: Trump, Xi meet in Beijing for high-stakes summit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping at Beijing's Great Hall of the People for a high-stakes summit. The U.S. delegation included Secretary of State Marco Rubio, War Secretary Pete Hegseth, and business leaders such as Elon Musk.

stories.title: Nigeria: Leah Sharibu At 23 - Women's Group Seeks to Keep Her Story Alive
stories.summary: Nigerian women's groups are seeking to keep alive the story of Leah Sharibu, who turned 23 while still in captivity after being abducted and held for refusing to renounce her Christian faith.

stories.title: Kyiv region hit by massive overnight attack, five people injured, homes, vehicles damaged
stories.summary: The Kyiv region was struck by a Russian missile and drone attack overnight, injuring five people and damaging residential buildings and vehicles. Fires broke out in the area as a result of the assault.

stories.title: Russia to fulfil all agreements on energy supply to India: FM Lavrov
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov affirmed that Moscow will fulfill all energy supply agreements with India, invoking the "Hindi-Rusi bhai bhai" slogan to underscore the bilateral relationship's cultural depth.

stories.title: Hong Kong formally issues buy-back offer letters to Wang Fuk Court homeowners
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities formally issued buy-back offer letters to homeowners at the fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, giving them until August 31 to accept. The government earmarked HK$6.8 billion (US$870 million) for the acquisition of flats as part of a long-term resettlement plan.

stories.title: Ukraine: Russian drone and missile barrage slams Kyiv, killing at least one
stories.summary: A large-scale Russian drone and missile attack struck Kyiv early Thursday, killing at least one person and injuring 31, according to local officials.

stories.title: Iran war day 76: Vance says progress made in talks; Israel pounds Lebanon
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance reported progress in negotiations with Iran on day 76 of the conflict, while Israeli forces continued strikes on Lebanon and President Trump began his visit to China.

stories.title: Musk, Rubio, Hegseth: Who are in Trump’s entourage to China?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's delegation to China includes top administration officials such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, along with Elon Musk and other prominent American executives.

stories.title: Trump in China for talks with Xi Jinping
stories.summary: President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for a high-stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, with Iran, trade, and Taiwan among the key issues straining US-China relations.

stories.title: US federal judge blocks US sanctions against UN's Francesca Albanese
stories.summary: A US federal judge blocked sanctions imposed on Francesca Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories. Albanese had been sanctioned after recommending that the International Criminal Court pursue war-crimes prosecutions against Israeli and American nationals.

stories.title: Nawrocki not planning to visit Ukraine this year
stories.summary: Polish President Karol Nawrocki stated he does not plan to visit Ukraine in 2025, though a trip could take place in 2027. The announcement signals a delay in high-level diplomatic engagement between Warsaw and Kyiv.

stories.title: South Africa: Can South Africa's President Ramaphosa Avoid Impeachment?
stories.summary: South Africa's highest court has revived an impeachment inquiry against President Cyril Ramaphosa, which his ANC-dominated parliament had blocked in 2022. The political landscape has shifted with former adversaries now part of the governing coalition.

stories.title: Chinese firms plot secret arms sales to Iran, US officials say
stories.summary: US officials disclosed that Chinese firms are plotting secret arms sales to Iran. The revelation is expected to intensify pressure on President Trump to raise the issue during his visit to Beijing.

stories.title: Iran’s US-bound World Cup squad given public sendoff in Tehran
stories.summary: Thousands of Iranians gathered in Tehran for a public sendoff of the national football team heading to the World Cup, where Team Melli's new kit was unveiled before the squad departed for a training camp in Turkey.

stories.title: Federal judge blocks US sanctions against UN expert on Palestinian territories
stories.summary: A federal judge temporarily blocked US sanctions against Francesca Albanese, a UN expert on the Palestinian territories. The judge found the Trump administration likely violated her free-speech rights by imposing sanctions after she criticized Israel's war in Gaza.

stories.title: Combined attack on Kyiv: Residential buildings, infrastructure damaged, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russia launched a combined missile and drone attack on Kyiv, damaging residential buildings and civilian infrastructure in several districts. Casualties were reported across the Ukrainian capital as a result of the strikes.

stories.title: Plans to lower age bar for cabby health checks delayed to second half of year
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities have postponed plans to lower the age threshold for mandatory medical checks for taxi and commercial vehicle drivers. Legislative proposals requiring annual health certifications are now expected in the second half of the year.

stories.title: UK economy records surprise 0.3% growth in first month of the Iran war
stories.summary: The UK economy grew by 0.3% in March, according to Office for National Statistics data, despite the ongoing Iran war. The reading exceeded expectations, suggesting the Middle East conflict had not yet significantly dampened British economic momentum, though rising fuel costs remained a concern.

stories.title: Russia pounds Kyiv and cities across Ukraine in massive air attack
stories.summary: Russia launched a large-scale aerial attack on Kyiv and several other Ukrainian regions using drones and ballistic missiles. Local officials reported at least one person killed and dozens wounded in the strikes.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: M23 Rebels Commit Atrocities in Eastern City
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that M23 rebels, backed by Rwanda, committed atrocities including killings, rape, and abductions in the eastern Congolese city of Uvira. The armed group seized the city and targeted civilians in the aftermath.

stories.title: Netanyahu, Kisch, Smotrich allocate over NIS 1b., outline AI education plan for summer schools
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, along with ministers Kisch and Smotrich, announced the allocation of over one billion shekels for summer school programs. The initiative includes an AI education plan designed to address academic and emotional setbacks caused by extended school closures during Operation Roaring Lion.

stories.title: Israel must confront Jewish extremism while rejecting Europe’s double standards - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial discussed the challenge Israel faces in confronting Jewish extremism while also pushing back against what it characterizes as European double standards. The piece questioned whether Jewish power in the region would be governed by law and restraint or co-opted by extremist ideology.

stories.title: Farage criticised for backing preacher who says homosexuality is ‘abomination’
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage faced criticism after recording a video supporting Essex pastor Stephen Clayden, who has preached that homosexuality is an "abomination." Clayden is fighting a banning order sought by Colchester council to restrict his street preaching activities.

stories.title: Falling backwards and plunging through clouds: British paratroopers’ landing on Tristan da Cunha
stories.summary: A squad of British paratroopers and two medics parachuted from an RAF transport aircraft onto Tristan da Cunha in the south Atlantic to assist a patient with a suspected hantavirus infection. Captain George Lacey described the challenging 2,500-metre descent, including flying backwards into the wind.

stories.title: ‘There’s a risk of another Liz Truss moment’: City raises spectre of bond market meltdown again
stories.summary: A sell-off in UK government bond markets has intensified amid speculation over a potential Labour leadership challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Investors warned that a leadership contest ignoring fiscal discipline could trigger a crisis reminiscent of the 2022 market turmoil under former PM Liz Truss.

stories.title: China’s first female expert tree climber transforms fear of heights into thriving career
stories.summary: Yu Yanling, China's first internationally certified female professional tree climber, has turned a former fear of heights into a career pruning urban trees. Based in Xiamen, Fujian province, the former track athlete has climbed trees as tall as 60 meters.

stories.title: Malaysian minister rejects claims Chinese nationals ‘freely’ given citizenship
stories.summary: Malaysian Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail rejected allegations that citizenship was freely granted to Chinese nationals, calling the claims "malicious slander" and fake news. He stated the matter had been repeatedly clarified in parliament.

stories.title: China-US summit ‘remarkable’ but is it enough to change relations?
stories.summary: Analysts described the U.S.-China summit in Beijing as "extremely important" for arresting the downward spiral in bilateral relations. Leading Chinese academic Li Cheng noted that while the summit was significant, it alone would not fundamentally change the overall structure of fraught ties.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1539: Russia strikes previously untouched Zakarpattia amid B9 summit in Romania
stories.summary: On day 1,539 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia struck the Zakarpattia region of western Ukraine for the first time, coinciding with a Bucharest Nine summit in Romania. Separately, Russian forces abandoned their assault on Stepnohirsk.

stories.title: Gunfire chaos as Philippine senator resists ICC arrest: What we know so far
stories.summary: Gunshots erupted inside the Philippine Senate building in Manila, where Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa had taken refuge to evade an International Criminal Court arrest warrant related to the country's deadly anti-drug campaign.

stories.title: From Rutgers speaker to Kristof column, disputed dog rape claim against Israel goes mainstream
stories.summary: A disputed claim alleging Israeli forces used dogs to commit sexual assault has spread into mainstream discourse, including a Rutgers University speaking event and a Nicholas Kristof column. A canine training expert told JTA that it was "highly unlikely" a dog could be trained to carry out such an act.

stories.title: Israeli air attacks injure nine in multiple Lebanese towns
stories.summary: Israeli air attacks targeting multiple towns in southern Lebanon injured at least nine people in the Zibqin area, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Four women were among the wounded and were evacuated to hospitals in Tyre. Additional Israeli strikes were reported in the town of Aitit and al-Mansouri.

stories.title: Philippines authorities investigating reports lawmaker wanted by ICC has fled after taking refuge in senate
stories.summary: Philippine authorities are investigating reports that Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for his alleged role in the deadly anti-drug crackdown, may have secretly fled the Senate building in Manila where he had been evading arrest for days.

stories.title: Nigeria ex-power minister Saleh Mamman jailed 75 years for graft
stories.summary: A Nigerian court sentenced former power minister Saleh Mamman to 75 years in prison for corruption. Mamman was convicted of siphoning millions of dollars from hydro-electricity projects during his tenure.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Blames Somalia Instability for Failed Border Reopening
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto blamed renewed conflict and political instability in Somalia for the failure to reopen the Kenya-Somalia border. Ruto said the security situation in Somalia disrupted the planned reopening process.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Rejects 'Babysitting' Sudan Generals, Defends Neutral Role in Conflict
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto rejected the continued "babysitting" of Sudan's warring military factions and defended Kenya's neutral mediating role in the conflict. Ruto intensified criticism as the war pushes Sudan deeper into humanitarian catastrophe.

stories.title: Tanzania: Zanzibar Begins Using Drones to Identify and Eliminate Mosquito Breeding Sites
stories.summary: Zanzibar has launched a project using drones to identify and eliminate mosquito breeding sites as part of its campaign to eradicate malaria on the islands. The initiative represents a technological advancement in the region's public health efforts.

stories.title: Trump, Xi begin Beijing talks with trade truce, Iran war at stake
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping began talks in Beijing focused on a trade truce and the Iran war. Trump's delegation included Elon Musk and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as U.S. companies sought greater access to Chinese markets.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims three separate attacks on Israeli forces
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed three separate attacks targeting Israeli army vehicles and soldiers stationed in southern Lebanon. Concurrently, Lebanon's National News Agency reported ongoing Israeli shelling and strikes in towns near Tyre. The Litani River area was also subjected to Israeli shelling overnight.

stories.title: Iran’s ‘anti-American’ rhetoric tests India’s balancing act at Brics meeting
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to seek support for Tehran's position in its conflict with the U.S. during the BRICS Foreign Ministers' meeting in New Delhi. India, holding the BRICS chair, is hosting the gathering that includes both Iran and the UAE, which are on opposing sides of the conflict.

stories.title: Israel ruling coalition proposes dissolving Parliament for early elections: PM’s party
stories.summary: Israel's ruling coalition proposed a bill to dissolve Parliament and hold early elections. According to Israeli media reports, the dissolution bill could be put to a vote on May 20.

stories.title: Sudan: French President Emmanuel Macron - 'War in Sudan Fuelled By External Forces'
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron described the war in Sudan as involving "mass crimes, war crimes, and a catastrophic humanitarian situation" fueled by external forces. Speaking in Nairobi, Macron called the warring parties "warlords dividing the country" but stopped short of using the term genocide.

stories.title: 'They shot my neighbour in the head' - the lakeside city traumatised by war
stories.summary: Rebel fighters and Rwandan troops are accused of committing atrocities after capturing the city of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in December. Residents described killings of civilians, including a neighbor who was shot in the head.

stories.title: Lebanon and Israel set to hold new peace talks in Washington
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel are expected to begin new peace talks in Washington on Thursday as their ceasefire, in effect since April 17, nears expiration. Despite the truce, Israel has carried out near-daily attacks that have killed over 380 people, including 23 children, with the Norwegian Refugee Council reporting nearly 600 deaths.

stories.title: France to host conference on financing AU peace efforts, says Macron
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that France will host a conference on financing the African Union's peace efforts in Paris by the end of 2026. Macron made the announcement during a visit to Ethiopia.

stories.title: WA’s Yindjibarndi traditional owners consider appeal against Fortescue’s $150m record native title payout
stories.summary: Yindjibarndi traditional owners in Western Australia are considering an appeal against a federal court ruling ordering mining company Fortescue to pay a record $150 million in native title compensation for its Solomon Hub iron ore operations. The Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation called the payout "unsatisfactory."

stories.title: Kyiv building collapses after Russian strike, reportedly trapping residents
stories.summary: Russia launched a combined drone and missile attack on Kyiv, damaging several buildings. Reports indicate that at least one building collapsed, reportedly trapping residents inside.

stories.title: Africa: 'I'm Incredibly Proud of My Record' On Africa, Macron Tells RFI
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron told RFI he is proud of the evolution of France's relationships with African countries under his leadership. Speaking at the close of the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, Kenya, he described progress toward a "partnership of equals."

stories.title: Trump, Xi speak ahead of talks to make relations ‘better than ever’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping spoke ahead of formal talks in Beijing. Both leaders expressed optimism about improving bilateral relations between the United States and China.

stories.title: UK police plan operation to prevent trouble at anti-Israel, anti-immigration protests
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced an unprecedented operation deploying some 4,000 officers with helicopter support to manage concurrent anti-Israel and anti-immigration protests, aiming to prevent unrest.

stories.title: NYT doubles down in support of controversial op-ed claiming abuse of Palestinians in Israel
stories.summary: The New York Times defended a controversial opinion piece by columnist Nicholas Kristof alleging abuse of Palestinians in Israel, stating the article was extensively fact-checked and based on corroborated accounts.

stories.title: Israel's Eurovision Song Contest entrant heard booing as he went onstage
stories.summary: Israel's Eurovision Song Contest entrant Noam Bettan faced audible booing from pro-Palestinian protesters as he took the stage during the semi-final in Vienna. Bettan advanced despite the disruptions.

stories.title: NATO concludes Steadfast Deterrence 2026 exercise in Europe
stories.summary: NATO concluded the Steadfast Deterrence 2026 military exercise in Europe on May 13, a large-scale drill aimed at reinforcing the alliance's deterrence posture.

stories.title: Iran war looms over Trump’s China visit, shifts alliances
stories.summary: President Trump's visit to China is dominated by the ongoing Iran war, with Trump expected to seek Chinese assistance in resolving the conflict. The war is reshaping regional alliances and diplomatic dynamics.

stories.title: China gains edge over US amid war on Iran: Report
stories.summary: A US intelligence assessment produced for Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Dan Caine indicates that China is gaining strategic advantages over the United States amid the war on Iran. According to The Washington Post, the report details Beijing expanding its edge militarily, economically, and diplomatically, including by assisting countries facing energy shortages.

stories.title: South Korean official says 'unlikely' anyone but Iran behind attack on vessel
stories.summary: A senior South Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs official said it is unlikely that any entity other than Iran was responsible for an attack on a South Korean cargo vessel near the Strait of Hormuz earlier this week. Seoul has been cooperating with the United States on the investigation, according to Yonhap news agency.

stories.title: Calls grow to hire locals as graduate jobs decline amid AI, economic pressures
stories.summary: Hong Kong industry leaders called for prioritizing local graduate hiring after full-time graduate vacancies dropped 61 percent, from about 80,000 in 2022 to around 31,000 in 2025. The decline has been attributed to AI adoption and broader economic pressures.

stories.title: ‘Miraculous’ rescue off US coast as 11 survive crash and 5-hour sea ordeal
stories.summary: All 11 people aboard a twin-engined turboprop that crashed into the sea off central Florida survived and were rescued from a lifeboat after a five-hour ordeal. U.S. Air Force Reserve crews, the Coast Guard, and Air Force personnel carried out the rescue operation.

stories.title: The secret mission to rescue the UN’s vital Palestinian refugee archive
stories.summary: UNRWA conducted a 10-month operation to rescue millions of archival documents chronicling Palestinian refugee history from Gaza and East Jerusalem. Workers transported the materials to Amman, Jordan, facing significant logistical challenges during the summer of 2024 due to conflict conditions.

stories.title: Wife of Briton pleads for Saudi Arabia to release him from ‘arbitrary detention’
stories.summary: The wife of British national Ahmed al-Doush has called on Saudi Arabia to release him, citing his declining health since his arrest in 2024 over social media posts. In November, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention ruled his imprisonment unlawful and recommended his immediate release and compensation.

stories.title: Lead Microsoft AI scientist Li Hongzhi joins China’s Tongji University
stories.summary: Li Hongzhi, a former lead AI scientist and head of GenAI at Microsoft Research Asia, has joined China's Tongji University. Li previously obtained his PhD from Columbia University and spent over a decade at Microsoft Research.

stories.title: Thucydides Trap, personal touches – all you need to know from Xi-Trump summit so far
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump began closed-door talks in Beijing following an elaborate welcome ceremony featuring a 21-gun salute and military honors at the Great Hall of the People.

stories.title: In pictures: China welcomes Trump ahead of high-stakes talks in Beijing
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed US President Donald Trump with a handshake at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Thursday. The summit is expected to address trade, Iran, and Taiwan.

stories.title: Neo-Nazi who plotted to poison Jewish children gets 15-year sentence in NYC
stories.summary: Michail Chkhikvishvili, a Georgian national and leader of the neo-Nazi group Maniac Murder Cult, was sentenced to 15 years in prison in New York City. He pleaded guilty to soliciting hate crimes, including plotting to poison Jewish children, and distributing bomb-making instructions.

stories.title: Assam ships first legal agarwood chips to West Asia
stories.summary: India's Assam state shipped its first legal consignment of agarwood chips to Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. The shipment is expected to unlock an industrial potential valued at approximately ₹50,000 crore.

stories.title: Students in Caracas to demand release of political prisoners
stories.summary: University students in Caracas, Venezuela, blocked the city's main highway to demand the immediate release of political prisoners. The protest was organized by students from several of the country's leading universities.

stories.title: Who is Tammy Tyrrell, the former Jacqui Lambie senator who just defected to Labor?
stories.summary: Tasmanian Senator Tammy Tyrrell, formerly aligned with Jacqui Lambie's party, has defected to the Australian Labor Party. The move gives Labor an additional Senate seat but still does not provide the party with a majority in the upper house.

stories.title: Ukrainian capital Kyiv under attack from Russian drones, missiles, officials say
stories.summary: Russian drones and missiles targeted the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, with debris from intercepted drones striking the roof of an apartment building and falling in a street, according to the head of Kyiv's military administration, Tymur Tkachenko.

stories.title: Lebanon and Israel to hold new talks in Washington as ceasefire nears end
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli delegations are set to begin a third round of ceasefire talks in Washington on Thursday, days before their current truce expires. Since the ceasefire took effect on April 17, continued Israeli strikes have killed more than 400 people in Lebanon, according to an AFP tally based on Lebanese authorities' figures.

stories.title: House catches fire in Vyshhorod district of Kyiv region following Russian drone attack
stories.summary: A private house in the Vyshhorod district of the Kyiv region caught fire following a Russian drone attack, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: US thought Iran war would hasten Gaza’s demilitarization. Instead, Hamas is emboldened
stories.summary: The US had anticipated that its war against Iran would weaken Tehran's ability to support proxy groups and accelerate the demilitarization of Gaza. Instead, Hamas has been emboldened, refusing to disarm and seeking to prolong negotiations, mirroring Iran's own approach to the talks.

stories.title: ‘A flying White House’: Trump’s Air Force One fuels fascination in China
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's Air Force One generated widespread fascination in China, with hundreds of photographers and residents gathering near Beijing Capital International Airport to capture its arrival. Images of the aircraft quickly flooded Chinese social media.

stories.title: Iran war: Why the BRICS foreign ministers meeting in India matters
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from BRICS member nations convened in India ahead of the 2026 BRICS summit scheduled for September. The meeting's agenda included discussions related to the ongoing conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: US embargo on Hormuz Strait hits Cuba's energy stock
stories.summary: Cuba's Energy Minister Vicente de la O Levy announced that the country has completely exhausted its fuel and diesel reserves due to the U.S. blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. He said the national power grid is in a critical state and called for any willing seller to provide fuel.

stories.title: Chinese companies planning clandestine arms sales to Iran, US intelligence finds - report
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence reportedly found that Chinese companies are planning clandestine arms sales to Iran. China has already significantly aided Iran during the war by providing intelligence on U.S. forces and supplying dual-use materials for drone and missile production.

stories.title: At Jewish Dems event, Minneapolis mayor says anti-Zionism can blur into antisemitism
stories.summary: Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey, speaking at a Jewish Democrats event, said anti-Zionism can blur into antisemitism. Frey expressed concern that political leaders lack the courage to challenge rising anti-Israel sentiment within their own party.

stories.title: US Senate blocks latest bid to rein in Trump Iran war powers, support grows
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate blocked a measure seeking to limit President Trump's war powers regarding the conflict with Iran. However, the bill edged closer to passage after a third Republican senator voted to advance it, signaling growing bipartisan support for congressional oversight of the military campaign.

stories.title: Deserter detained in Kyiv for registering Starlink terminals for Russians
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a military deserter in Kyiv who had been acting as a Russian agent by illegally registering Starlink satellite internet terminals for Russian operatives.

stories.title: Pentagon considering renaming Iran war 'Operation Sledgehammer' if ceasefire fails - report
stories.summary: The Pentagon is reportedly considering renaming the Iran war operation to "Operation Sledgehammer" if ceasefire efforts fail, which would distinguish renewed military strikes from the current Operation Epic Fury, according to NBC.

stories.title: Poland says it intercepts Russian aircraft over Baltic Sea
stories.summary: Poland's air force intercepted a Russian reconnaissance aircraft over international waters in the Baltic Sea. Polish authorities described the Russian flight as a provocation and a potential security threat.

stories.title: Remains of second missing US servicewoman found in Morocco, military says
stories.summary: The U.S. Africa Command confirmed that remains found in Morocco were identified as Spc. Mariyah Collington, an air and missile defense crewmember and the second missing U.S. servicewoman located in the country.

stories.title: Iran conflict casts shadow over Trump-Xi talks in Beijing
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are meeting Thursday in Beijing for a summit where few breakthroughs are expected. Divisive issues including the Iran war, trade, technology restrictions, and Taiwan are on the agenda.

stories.title: Holocaust survivor Albrecht Weinberg, who moved back to Germany in his 80's, dies aged 101
stories.summary: Holocaust survivor Albrecht Weinberg died at age 101 in the town of Leer in northwest Germany. Born in Rhauderfehn in 1925, Weinberg had returned to Germany in his 80s after surviving the Holocaust.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit live: welcome ceremony underway as US president meets China’s leader ahead of key summit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People. The talks come amid the ongoing Iran conflict, with heightened security across the Chinese capital. Key issues include trade, technology, and Taiwan.

stories.title: Settlers kill Palestinian teen in Ramallah
stories.summary: Israeli settlers shot and killed 16-year-old Youssef Ali Youssef Kaabneh in the town of Sinjil, north of Ramallah, injuring several others. The Palestinian Health Ministry confirmed the teen was struck in the chest with live ammunition and died at a hospital in Salfit.

stories.title: Trump’s trillion-dollar business delegation arrives in China, eager for deals
stories.summary: A U.S. business delegation accompanying President Trump to Beijing includes 17 executives from the technology, finance, aerospace, and semiconductor sectors, with a combined net worth exceeding $1 trillion. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined the delegation at the last minute.

stories.title: Families demand release of Pakistani crew captured by Somali pirates
stories.summary: Families of 10 Pakistani crew members held hostage by Somali pirates rallied in Karachi demanding the government secure their release.

stories.title: UK cops plan ‘unprecedented’ operation for concurrent Nakba Day, ‘Unite the Kingdom’ rallies
stories.summary: British police announced an unprecedented security operation involving approximately 4,000 officers and helicopters for concurrent Nakba Day and "Unite the Kingdom" rallies expected to draw at least 80,000 participants on Saturday.

stories.title: Rand Paul’s son apologizes for antisemitic and anti-gay rant after accosting lawmaker
stories.summary: William Paul, son of Republican Senator Rand Paul, apologized for a drunken tirade at a Washington, D.C., bar in which he reportedly told a Republican congressman he "hates Jews and hates gays." Paul said he had too much to drink and announced he is seeking help for a drinking problem.

stories.title: Board of Peace High Representative for Gaza says ceasefire 'far from perfect'
stories.summary: Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Trump's Peace Council in Gaza, acknowledged that the ceasefire in effect since October 2025 is functioning but "far from perfect," citing daily violations. More than 850 people have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire began.

stories.title: Middle East live: Lebanon, Israel to hold new talks in US before ceasefire expires
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel are scheduled to begin new peace talks in Washington on Thursday as their latest ceasefire nears expiration. The ceasefire is considered nominally in place despite hundreds of deaths from Israeli strikes in Lebanon.

stories.title: ‘Stunned and shocked’: Ingrid Horrocks wins top prize at New Zealand’s Ockham awards for her fiction debut
stories.summary: New Zealand writer Ingrid Horrocks won the NZ$65,000 Jann Medlicott Acorn prize for fiction at the 2026 Ockham New Zealand Book Awards for her debut short story collection, All Her Lives. It is only the fifth short story collection to win the prize in 58 years.

stories.title: Federal judge blocks US sanctions against UN's Francesca Albanese
stories.summary: A US federal judge in Washington blocked Trump administration sanctions against Francesca Albanese, a UN expert on the Palestinian territories. Judge Richard Leon found the administration likely violated her free-speech rights by imposing sanctions after she criticized Israel's war in Gaza.

stories.title: Netanyahu held secret meeting with Emirati president in the UAE during Iran war, PM's office says
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secretly visited the United Arab Emirates and met with the Emirati president during the ongoing war with Iran, according to a statement from Netanyahu's office on Wednesday.

stories.title: US House members defy leadership, to force vote on Ukraine aid
stories.summary: A U.S. House of Representatives petition to force a floor vote on security aid for Ukraine and new sanctions on Russia reached the required 218 signatures on Wednesday. The bipartisan effort defied Republican House leadership.

stories.title: Xi and Trump: diplomatic and military communication, business cooperation encouraged
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a summit in Beijing focused on strengthening diplomatic and military communication channels and encouraging business cooperation between the two nations.

stories.title: A year after USAID cuts, Philippine development groups struggle as anger lingers
stories.summary: A year after the U.S. froze and slashed USAID funding, development organizations in the Philippines continue to suffer job losses and abandoned projects, affecting some of Asia's most vulnerable populations.

stories.title: Centuries ahead of Wall Street: how China’s Song dynasty pioneered global fiat currency
stories.summary: An analysis examines how China's Song dynasty pioneered the world's first paper currency in the 1020s, when merchants in Sichuan province began issuing paper promissory notes called jiaozi to address bronze coin shortages amid economic expansion.

stories.title: Jimmy Lai case shows press freedom is not a get-out-of-jail-free ticket
stories.summary: The trial of media owner Jimmy Lai in Hong Kong has raised questions about the boundaries of press freedom, amid broader reflections on the evolving media landscape since CNN founder Ted Turner's era of 24-hour news coverage.

stories.title: Who is Ronald dela Rosa, the ICC-wanted lawmaker holed up in the Philippine Senate?
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity related to the Duterte-era drug war, called on the public to prevent his handover to the ICC as gunfire was heard at the Senate building in Manila.

stories.title: UK police plan 'unprecedented' operation to prevent trouble at weekend protests
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced an "unprecedented" policing operation for the coming weekend to prevent violence at two large protests — an anti-immigration rally and a pro-Palestinian demonstration — in the British capital.

stories.title: Nigerian court sentences ex-power minister Mamman to 75 years in prison for fraud
stories.summary: A Nigerian court sentenced former power minister Saleh Mamman to 75 years in prison for laundering 33.8 billion naira (approximately $24.71 million). The conviction, announced by Nigeria's anti-graft agency, is a rare outcome for corruption cases in the country.

stories.title: Hungary summons Russian ambassador over drone strikes on western Ukraine
stories.summary: Hungary summoned Russia's ambassador over drone strikes on western Ukraine, Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced on Wednesday.

stories.title: Netanyahu's office says he visited UAE, Gulf state denies claim
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's office announced he secretly visited the UAE during Operation "Lion's Roar" and met with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The UAE's Ministry of Foreign Affairs promptly denied the visit took place.

stories.title: ‘Basically a Chinese racket’: how China streaked ahead at a global AI conference
stories.summary: An analysis of papers accepted at the International Conference on Learning Representations found that Chinese universities accounted for about 44 percent of contributions from the top 50 institutions, significantly surpassing American rivals in AI research output.

stories.title: China parent brings son, 12, to work, where he plays with fire, destroying entire office
stories.summary: A 12-year-old boy in Ningbo, Zhejiang province, China, accidentally started a fire that destroyed an entire office after being brought to work by a parent on April 30. The child was left unsupervised and began playing with fire out of boredom.

stories.title: Moscow authorities restrict publication of photos and videos of aftermath of drone strikes
stories.summary: Moscow authorities imposed restrictions on publishing photos and videos showing the aftermath of drone strikes and other attacks described as "terrorist attacks," according to the office of Mayor Sergei Sobyanin.

stories.title: US’ Rubio calls on China to play an ‘active’ role in ending Iran war, despite Trump rhetoric
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on China to play a more active role in resolving the Iran crisis ahead of the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing. Rubio described the Iran war as a major source of instability threatening Asia due to the region's reliance on the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill, wound nearly 60 children over the past week, despite truce deal
stories.summary: UNICEF reported that Israeli attacks across Lebanon killed and wounded at least 59 children over the past week despite a ceasefire that took effect on April 17. Over 23 children have been killed and 93 injured since the truce began.

stories.title: Saudi warplanes struck militias in Iraq during war, sources say
stories.summary: Saudi fighter jets struck targets linked to Iranian-backed Shiite militias in Iraq during the Iran war, according to multiple sources. Retaliatory strikes were also launched from Kuwait into Iraq.

stories.title: US Army recovers remains of second soldier reported missing during Moroccan exercise
stories.summary: The U.S. Army recovered the remains of Spc. Mariyah Symone Collington, 19, one of two soldiers reported missing on May 2 during a military exercise in Morocco. The recovery concluded a multinational search effort.

stories.title: Saudi warplanes struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq during war, sources say
stories.summary: Sources report that Saudi warplanes struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq during the Iran war, targeting sites near Saudi Arabia's northern border used to launch drones and missiles at Gulf states. Kuwait also reportedly fired on positions in Iraq.

stories.title: Russia damages 1,783 cultural heritage sites in Ukraine
stories.summary: As of early May 2026, Russia has destroyed or damaged 1,783 cultural heritage sites and 2,540 cultural infrastructure facilities in Ukraine since the start of its full-scale invasion. The figures underscore the extensive toll of the conflict on Ukraine's cultural patrimony.

stories.title: Soldier sentenced to 30 days in prison after IDF Chief of Staff catches him with 'Messiah' patch
stories.summary: An IDF soldier was sentenced to 30 days in prison after Chief of Staff Zamir discovered him wearing a 'Messiah' patch during a West Bank tour. Zamir encountered several soldiers behaving inappropriately and failing to follow military discipline.

stories.title: Netanyahu’s office says he visited UAE secretly during the Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's office confirmed he secretly visited the UAE during the war with Iran. The disclosure followed US Ambassador Mike Huckabee's revelation that Israel sent Iron Dome air-defence systems and personnel to the UAE.

stories.title: ​Elusive peace: On the Russia-Ukraine war
stories.summary: An editorial argues that Europe must actively push for a negotiated settlement to end the Russia-Ukraine war, emphasizing the difficulty of achieving lasting peace through military means alone.

stories.title: PTI defends MNA Iqbal Afridi’s son over asylum move, assails govt’s ‘oppression’
stories.summary: Pakistan's PTI party defended the son of MNA Iqbal Afridi after he surrendered his passport and sought asylum in a European country, saying government oppression left him no alternative. The issue surfaced during a National Assembly Standing Committee meeting where a state minister alleged the son used a diplomatic passport.

stories.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians and burn land in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Armed Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian homes in the Masafer Yatta area of Hebron, injuring a Palestinian resident and a foreign activist. Settlers also set fire to agricultural land in the village of Al-Mughayyir near Ramallah.

stories.title: Japan-South Korea ‘comfort women’ row stoked by statues abroad
stories.summary: Disputes over "comfort women" statues erected abroad by South Korean civic groups have reignited tensions between Japan and South Korea. Local governments in Berlin and Auckland have moved to rescind or decline permits for the memorials, drawing support from Japanese conservatives.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit live: US, China leaders to hold talks on trade, tech, Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a summit in Beijing addressing trade tensions, technology disputes, and the ongoing war on Iran, which continues to disrupt global commerce.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran slams ‘collusion’ as Netanyahu ‘secretly’ visits UAE
stories.summary: Iran's first vice president asserted that Tehran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz is established and non-negotiable, condemning what it called collusion following reports of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's secret visit to the UAE.

stories.title: Major among five soldiers martyred during operation in Balochistan’s Barkhan: ISPR
stories.summary: Five Pakistani soldiers, including a major, were killed during a security operation in Barkhan district, Balochistan, targeting militants the state designates as Fitna al Hindustan. Seven militants were also killed in the joint Pakistan Army and Frontier Corps operation in the Nosham area.

stories.title: New York man found guilty of acting as an unregistered agent of China
stories.summary: A federal jury in Brooklyn found Lu Jianwang, 64, of New York, guilty of acting as an unregistered agent of the Chinese government. Prosecutors accused him of operating a covert police station in Manhattan's Chinatown on behalf of Beijing starting in 2022 and helping locate a pro-democracy activist.

stories.title: How has the Iran war affected Middle East states?
stories.summary: The war that began on February 28 with a large-scale Israeli-U.S. bombing campaign against Iran has destabilized the broader Middle East, damaging infrastructure and economies and upending long-standing regional security assumptions.

stories.title: Iran frees prominent rights lawyer Sotoudeh on bail, reports say
stories.summary: Iran released prominent human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh on bail on Wednesday. She had been arrested in early April during a crackdown amid the conflict with the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Zelensky thanks Hungarian PM Magyar for condemning Russian attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar for condemning Russia's latest attack on Ukraine. The exchange highlights diplomatic engagement between Kyiv and Budapest on the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Board of Peace envoy: Hamas tightening its grip on Gaza, taxing those with nothing left
stories.summary: Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov said Hamas is tightening its grip on Gaza and taxing impoverished residents. He stated that a disarmament plan would not eliminate Hamas as a political movement, with weapons to be handed to a technocratic government rather than Israel.

stories.title: 'Beginning of end of worst gov't in history': Opposition heads react to Knesset dissolution bill
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leaders reacted to a Knesset dissolution bill, with Benny Gantz calling it the beginning of the end of what he described as the worst government in Israeli history. The bill signals a potential move toward new elections in Israel.

stories.title: UAE denies Netanyahu held secret meeting with Emirati president during Iran war
stories.summary: The UAE's foreign ministry denied claims from Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's office that he secretly visited the UAE and met President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed during the war with Iran. The Emirati statement emphasized that its relations with Israel are conducted publicly and transparently.

stories.title: 'No indication' Andes strain of hantavirus has mutated: EU agency
stories.summary: The EU's European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control said there is no indication that the Andes strain of hantavirus has mutated following a deadly outbreak on a cruise ship traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde. Three passengers died and at least seven others were confirmed infected, with all evacuated and quarantined.

stories.title: UN rights chief calls on Israel to abolish Oct 7 military tribunal
stories.summary: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called on Israel to abolish a military tribunal established to handle cases related to the October 7 attacks. Israel's parliament had passed legislation creating the tribunal.

stories.title: Nearly 9,000 war crime cases launched in Dnipropetrovsk region – Prosecutor’s Office
stories.summary: Authorities in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region have opened 8,958 criminal proceedings related to alleged war crimes committed by Russian military forces. The Prosecutor's Office reported the cases as part of ongoing efforts to document and prosecute violations in the region.

stories.title: Chinese memory module makers ramp up production as CXMT DDR5 breakthrough hits market
stories.summary: Chinese memory module manufacturer Powev has begun mass production of 64GB DDR5-5600 RDIMM server memory under its Sinker brand, using chips from ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). The development reflects CXMT's breakthrough in domestic DDR5 chip production, which is now filtering through China's memory supply chain to both consumer and enterprise markets.

stories.title: Hezbollah support endures in south Lebanon as ceasefire fails to stop war with Israel
stories.summary: In southern Lebanon, many residents continue to support Hezbollah despite ongoing Israeli military operations and occupation, viewing the armed group as the only force capable of defending them even as a ceasefire remains ineffective.

stories.title: Sarah Lawrence student senate rejects J Street U chapter after fierce backlash
stories.summary: The student senate at Sarah Lawrence College rejected a petition to recognize a J Street U chapter on campus. Some student senators reportedly compared the group to a white supremacist organization during the debate.

stories.title: War update: 187 clashes on front line, Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors see fiercest fighting
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 187 combat engagements along the front line in the past day. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors, where Russian forces launched nearly 50 attacks.

stories.title: No Indo-Pacific peace without industry surge and burden sharing, US general says
stories.summary: U.S. Army Gen. Xavier Brunson stated that expanding industrial capacity to far-reaching frontlines and increasing burden sharing among allies are essential for Indo-Pacific security. He emphasized the need for an industry surge to support operations across the region.

stories.title: Russia places former UK defence minister Ben Wallace on wanted list
stories.summary: Russia placed former UK Defence Minister Ben Wallace on its wanted list. Wallace has been a vocal critic of Russian aggression in Ukraine.

stories.title: State Duma passes bill on president’s right to use armed forces to protect Russians abroad
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma passed a bill authorizing the president to deploy armed forces abroad to protect Russian citizens. The legislation cleared both its second and third readings.

stories.title: Iran working on Hormuz ‘protocol’ to cover ‘costs’, says Minister Gharibabadi
stories.summary: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran is developing a protocol for the Strait of Hormuz to cover associated costs. He suggested a BRICS-member neighbouring country, reportedly the UAE, is attempting to undermine a joint statement by pushing for condemnation of Iran.

stories.title: Trump administration offers $100m in aid to Cuba in exchange for reform
stories.summary: The Trump administration offered Cuba $100 million in aid contingent on political reforms, while an oil blockade continues to affect the island. Washington blamed Cuba's communist leadership for obstructing the delivery of assistance.

stories.title: Remains of second US soldier who went missing during military exercises in Morocco have been recovered
stories.summary: The U.S. Army confirmed the recovery of remains of Spc. Mariyah Symone Collington, 19, of Tavares, Florida, who went missing during military exercises in Morocco. Collington and Spc. Kendrick Lamont Key Jr. died after falling off a cliff during an off-duty hike near Cap Draa. A multinational search operation using air, naval, and AI assets was deployed.

stories.title: Housing market in England and Wales weakening due to Iran war, say estate agents
stories.summary: Estate agents in England and Wales report weakening housing demand linked to fears of mortgage rate rises and higher inflation stemming from the Iran war. A Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors survey found a noticeable softening in buyer interest as sellers hold back properties.

stories.title: Hong Kong tech crimes are dropping. So why is hacking becoming more lucrative?
stories.summary: Hong Kong police reported that overall technology-related crimes declined over the past year, but financial losses from hacking more than doubled to HK$62.6 million (approximately US$8 million). Senior Superintendent Carmen Leung of the cybersecurity and technology crime bureau attributed the increased losses to several high-value cyberattacks targeting financial institutions.

stories.title: Warm words, thin relief: Macron's Africa financial push under scrutiny
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced $27 billion in new investments at a Franco-African summit in Nairobi, Kenya. The pledges face scrutiny over whether they will deliver meaningful economic relief to African nations.

stories.title: France probes whether Israeli firm BlackCore interfered in local elections, sources say
stories.summary: French authorities are investigating whether Israeli firm BlackCore carried out a foreign interference campaign targeting a hard-left party ahead of France's March municipal elections, according to three sources familiar with the matter.

stories.title: Zelensky proposes cooperation in Drone Deal format to Romania
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky proposed a cooperation framework with Romania under a special Drone Deal format aimed at bolstering drone-related collaboration between the two countries.

stories.title: Israel’s ruling coalition proposes early elections amid ultra-Orthodox anger at Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israel's ruling Likud party submitted a proposal to dissolve parliament and hold early elections amid mounting pressure from ultra-Orthodox coalition partners. The ultra-Orthodox parties are angry at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over his failure to secure military service exemptions, putting the multi-party coalition at risk of collapse.

stories.title: Ukraine attacks Russian energy sites - what has been hit?
stories.summary: Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian energy infrastructure in recent months as peace negotiations have stalled. Multiple energy sites across Russia have been targeted.

stories.title: Latvian government loses majority in parliament over handling of Ukraine drone incidents
stories.summary: Latvia's Prime Minister Evika Silina lost her ruling majority in parliament on Wednesday after the left-wing Progressives party withdrew support over the government's handling of Ukraine-related drone incidents on Latvian territory.

stories.title: Turkey’s Kurdish peace process falters as Iran war complicates negotiations - analysis
stories.summary: Turkey's peace process with Kurdish militants has stalled as the ongoing Iran war deepens regional instability. Both sides have reportedly been reluctant to take decisive steps toward a resolution.

stories.title: Coalition submits bill to dissolve Knesset, vote expected next week
stories.summary: Israel's governing coalition submitted a bill to dissolve the Knesset, with a vote expected next week. The move comes as opposition figures Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid launched a joint campaign under their merged Together party.

stories.title: Howard Lutnick said he had three ‘meaningless and inconsequential’ meetings with Epstein
stories.summary: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told a House committee in a closed-door interview that he had only three "meaningless and inconsequential" meetings with Jeffrey Epstein. Lutnick denied any personal or professional relationship with the disgraced financier, according to a newly released transcript.

stories.title: US wants China to press Iran to change course in Gulf: Secretary of State
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington hopes to convince China to take a more active role in pressuring Iran to change its behavior in the Gulf. Rubio made the comments in an interview aired on Fox News on Wednesday.

stories.title: Herzog warns Israel’s greatest internal threat is growing division at ‘Time to Talk’ conference
stories.summary: Former Israeli President Isaac Herzog spoke at a 'Time to Talk' conference, warning that growing internal division poses the greatest domestic threat to Israel.

stories.title: Lebanon says 10 more killed in Israeli strikes on south
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that 10 more people were killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon on Wednesday, raising the day's death toll to at least 22. Victims included children and women in the towns of Arab Salim, Harouf, and Roumin.

stories.title: Netanyahu says he 'secretly visited' UAE during war with Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office claimed he made a secret visit to the UAE during the war with Iran. The UAE denied the report, stating that relations between the two countries were not based on unofficial arrangements.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Defense Forces wipe out Russian Merlin-VR reconnaissance drone
stories.summary: Operators of Ukraine's Phoenix Border Guard Unit destroyed a Russian Merlin-VR reconnaissance drone on the eastern front.

stories.title: Australia politics live: Taylor unveils policy to block noncitizens from access to 17 benefits including paid parental leave
stories.summary: Australian opposition leader Taylor announced a policy to block noncitizens from accessing 17 government benefits, including paid parental leave. Housing minister Clare O'Neil separately discussed budget measures aimed at helping first home buyers compete against investors at property auctions.

stories.title: Influencer detained in Tennessee over alleged confrontation involving gunfire
stories.summary: Dalton Eatherly, 28, an online influencer known as Chud the Builder, was detained in Clarksville, Tennessee, after an alleged shooting outside the Montgomery County courthouse. The district attorney's office said shots were fired during a confrontation with another man on Wednesday afternoon.

stories.title: US renews $100M aid offer to crisis-hit Cuba while tightening sanctions
stories.summary: The United States renewed a $100 million aid offer to Cuba as the island faces worsening blackouts and a deepening economic crisis. Washington is simultaneously tightening sanctions, increasing pressure on Havana over fuel shortages and political reform.

stories.title: Third round of Israel-Lebanon talks to take place with military officials, sources tell 'Post'
stories.summary: A third round of Israel-Lebanon negotiations is set to take place involving military officials from both sides. Lebanon's military attaché in Washington and IDF Head of Strategy Brig.-Gen. Amichai Levin will be among the delegations' representatives.

stories.title: Iranian FM threatens UAE, claims Tehran knew of Netanyahu’s visit to Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister threatened the UAE and claimed Tehran had prior knowledge of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's reported visit to Abu Dhabi. The UAE has denied the visit took place, while Netanyahu's former spokesman maintained that the wartime trip occurred.

stories.title: The Shottas
stories.summary: The Shottas are a leading criminal group in Colombia's port city of Buenaventura, known for their violent rivalry with the Espartanos. In 2022, both groups agreed to participate in President Gustavo Petro's "Total Peace" plan, which aims to establish an urban peace laboratory in the city.

stories.title: Israeli firm BlackCore investigated for role in alleged French election smear campaign
stories.summary: French authorities are investigating Israeli firm BlackCore for allegedly conducting a smear campaign against left-wing candidates ahead of France's March municipal elections.

stories.title: Iran military says control over Hormuz to bring significant economic revenues
stories.summary: An Iranian military spokesperson stated that Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz could generate significant economic revenues, potentially doubling the country's oil income.

stories.title: U.S. House gathers votes to force consideration of USD1.3B aid package for Ukraine – NYT
stories.summary: The US House of Representatives gathered enough signatures to force a vote on a $1.3 billion military aid package for Ukraine, according to The New York Times.

stories.title: 'Rogue state behaviour': Israel carrying out covert influence operations in Canada, report says
stories.summary: A report alleges that Israel has been conducting covert influence operations in Canada. The advocacy group Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East is calling for Israeli agents to face scrutiny comparable to that applied to Chinese or Indian operatives.

stories.title: Chinese-American found guilty in New York ‘secret police station’ case
stories.summary: A federal jury in New York's Eastern District Court found Chinese-American Lu "Harry" Jianwang, 64, guilty on three charges of acting as a Chinese agent. The case centered on an undeclared Chinese police station established in New York's Chinatown, which prosecutors said was used to intimidate Chinese diaspora communities.

stories.title: ‘Transactional’ but pivotal: how Xi-Trump talks could redefine US-China fault lines
stories.summary: President Trump arrived in Beijing on Wednesday for the first US presidential visit to China in years, amid the US-Iran war's disruption of global energy supplies. The visit comes as Washington and Beijing navigate tensions compounded by geopolitical crises and economic interdependence.

stories.title: Iran war brings Turkey-PKK peace process to near standstill
stories.summary: Turkey's peace process with the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) has nearly stalled after the Iran war erupted, introducing fresh instability to the Middle East. The setback came just two weeks after Turkey's parliament made recommendations on advancing the peace process.

stories.title: Explainer-What's at stake in Turkey's bid to end conflict with PKK militants?
stories.summary: Turkey's decades-old effort to resolve its conflict with the PKK militant group has stalled, with both sides waiting for the other to act. The ongoing Iran war has further complicated the peace bid.

stories.title: Russian airspace breaches show need to boost NATO eastern flank air defence, say leaders
stories.summary: Leaders of 14 NATO allied nations meeting in Bucharest called for strengthened air defences along the alliance's eastern flank. The statement followed repeated Russian airspace violations of NATO member countries, highlighting the need for improved missile and drone defense capabilities.

stories.title: Mass protests in Argentina decry Milei's funding cuts to prized public universities
stories.summary: Mass protests erupted across Argentina against President Javier Milei's funding cuts to public universities. Milei, echoing ally U.S. President Donald Trump, has characterized university campuses as centers of ideological indoctrination.

stories.title: Price shocks from the Iran war power solar sales in energy-hungry Asia
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs driven by the Iran war are accelerating adoption of rooftop solar power across energy-dependent Asian nations. China, as the world's largest provider of solar technology, stands to benefit significantly from the shift in demand.

stories.title: Injury toll rises to eight following Russian drone attack on Ivano-Frankivsk
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential high-rise building in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine, injuring at least eight people, including a minor.

stories.title: Palestinians say West Bank teen killed by Israeli fire
stories.summary: Palestinian sources reported that a teenager was killed by Israeli fire in the occupied West Bank. Four other people were injured in the incident.

stories.title: Both Trump and Xi Overestimate Themselves
stories.summary: The article examines the US-China summit, arguing that elites in both countries are prone to overestimating their own strengths. The analysis suggests both President Trump and President Xi bring inflated self-assessments to their diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: Israeli drone strikes on vehicles in Lebanon kill 12, including 2 children
stories.summary: Israeli drone strikes on vehicles in Lebanon killed 12 people, including two children. Lebanon and Israel are scheduled to hold another round of direct talks in Washington on Thursday.

stories.title: IDF officers said to tell PM Jewish terror accounts for up to 80% of West Bank incidents
stories.summary: IDF officers reportedly informed the Israeli prime minister that Jewish settler violence accounts for up to 80% of security incidents in the West Bank. Officers warned the issue is diverting resources from offensive operations. A Palestinian teenager was reportedly killed by the IDF following a settler raid.

stories.title: Cartel corruption claims push US-Mexico relations to breaking point
stories.summary: US-Mexico relations are under severe strain amid Washington's accusations that Mexican officials have colluded with drug trafficking organizations. President Claudia Sheinbaum pushed back against the allegations, while analysts compared the tensions to the most fraught period since the 1980s. Reports of CIA agents operating in Mexico have added further friction.

stories.title: Why stability must come before denuclearisation on the Korean peninsula
stories.summary: Following US strikes on Iran, North Korea has doubled down on deterrence rather than showing interest in denuclearization. Pyongyang has tightened security around its leadership and continued missile launches, signaling sensitivity to Washington's military posture in the region.

stories.title: UN food agency halves Syria food aid, halts bread subsidy over funding shortages
stories.summary: The World Food Programme announced it has halved emergency food assistance in Syria due to funding shortages and halted bread subsidies. The agency warned that millions of Syrians remain vulnerable despite some signs of stabilisation in parts of the country.

stories.title: Two drone strikes hit Iranian opposition camp north of Iraq’s Erbil, security sources say
stories.summary: Two drone strikes targeted an Iranian opposition camp north of Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region, according to security sources. The strikes reportedly hit an arms and ammunition depot inside the camp.

stories.title: Trade, tech, and rare earths to dominate Trump's China trip
stories.summary: President Trump's visit to China is expected to focus on trade, technology, and rare earth minerals, with more than a dozen executives from major companies joining the delegation. Separately, the US Senate approved Kevin Warsh as the next Chairman of the Federal Reserve.

stories.title: Ukrinform journalist Olha Zvonariova wins prestigious military journalism award in Italy
stories.summary: Ukrinform journalist Olha Zvonariova received the Premio Montecatini di Giornalismo 2026 award in Italy, recognizing outstanding editorial work on defense, security, and armed forces coverage.

stories.title: Pakistan, WHO launch Prime Minister's Hepatitis C Elimination Programme
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ministry of Health and the World Health Organisation launched the Prime Minister's Hepatitis C Elimination Programme in Islamabad, aiming to reach 1.6 million people within six months and eliminate the disease as a public health threat by 2030.

stories.title: Funeral held for two Lebanese paramedics killed in Israeli attack
stories.summary: Hundreds of mourners attended the funeral of two Lebanese paramedics who were killed in an Israeli strike. The ceremony drew significant public attendance as communities mourned the loss of emergency responders.

stories.title: World Food Programme slashes Syria aid, affecting 7.2 million as funding crisis deepens
stories.summary: The World Food Programme has cut emergency food aid in Syria by half due to funding shortages, affecting approximately 7.2 million people despite signs of stabilization in the country.

stories.title: US Senate warns of China’s nuclear capabilities hours before Xi-Trump summit
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee held a hearing on nuclear capabilities, with Chairman Roger Wicker warning of China's "unprecedented nuclear expansion," including construction of hundreds of new missile silos. The hearing took place hours before President Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: As Trump readies to meet Xi, experts say he is ‘desperate for a win’
stories.summary: As President Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping, analysts suggest he is eager to secure a diplomatic achievement. Bilateral trade has declined since Trump took office, even as China's overall exports have reached record levels.

stories.title: Watch: Gold and silver import duties doubled following Modi’s appeal | Above the Fold | 13.05.2026
stories.summary: India's central government doubled import duties on gold and silver as part of austerity measures amid a deepening West Asia crisis. The episode also covers U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to China and BJP leaders reducing convoy sizes.

stories.title: S. African non-Jewish activists protest at Holocaust center with ‘Jews for Free Palestine' shirts
stories.summary: Non-Jewish South African activists staged a protest at a Holocaust center wearing "Jews for Free Palestine" shirts, claiming solidarity with Jewish voices who reject Zionism and call for Palestinian freedom.

stories.title: Philip Davis and Progressive Liberal Party win general election in Bahamas
stories.summary: Philip Davis and his Progressive Liberal Party won the general election in the Bahamas. The victory marks the first time in three decades that a Bahamian political party has secured back-to-back election wins.

stories.title: Chinese-linked ships cross Strait of Hormuz on eve of Trump-Xi meeting
stories.summary: A Chinese-linked supertanker carrying two million barrels of Iraqi crude oil crossed the Strait of Hormuz and then turned off its transponder. The transit occurred on the eve of a meeting between U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: ‘The threat is manageable’: IDF downplays Hezbollah drone campaign
