stories.summary: The United Nations reported that Palestinian children in the occupied West Bank have been shot and stabbed by Israeli forces and settlers. Approximately 2,500 Palestinians were displaced in the first four months of the year by Israeli operations.

stories.title: Zelensky's ex-chief of staff in court as Ukraine corruption probe escalates
stories.summary: Former Ukrainian presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak appeared in court after being named a suspect in a money-laundering investigation. Ukraine's two anti-corruption agencies are leading the probe as part of an escalating corruption crackdown.

stories.title: SAPO seeking pre-trial detention for Yermak with UAH180M bail
stories.summary: Ukraine's Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO) announced it will seek pre-trial detention for former presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak, with bail set at 180 million hryvnias.

stories.title: Pentagon seeks additional funding as cost of Iran war tops $29 billion
stories.summary: The Pentagon is seeking additional funding as the estimated cost of the US war with Iran has risen to $29 billion, up from $25 billion two weeks earlier. The increase reflects updated equipment repair, replacement, and general operational costs.

stories.title: Russia strikes Ukraine with drones as ceasefire ends, Ukrainian officials say
stories.summary: Russia launched more than 200 drones at Ukraine overnight on Tuesday, hours after a U.S.-mediated ceasefire expired. Ukrainian officials reported the strikes, which dimmed hopes that the truce would be extended.

stories.title: Pentagon gives new $29bn Iran war price tag, downplays munitions concerns
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth told a congressional panel that a potential war with Iran could cost $29 billion. He stated the U.S. is prepared to either escalate or de-escalate the conflict.

stories.title: Israel kills, injures average of 4 children daily amid Lebanon ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Save the Children reported that an average of four children per day have been killed or injured in Lebanon during the first 25 days of the ceasefire that took effect on April 16.

stories.title: Macron and Ruto pledge mutal respect and co-investment at Africa Forward summit in Nairobi
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and Kenyan President William Ruto pledged mutual respect and co-investment at the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi. The two-day event was described as a milestone in France-Africa relations, framed around a shared agenda.

stories.title: Kuwait captured four IRGC-linked operatives who infiltrated their territory, Foreign Ministry says
stories.summary: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry confirmed the capture of four operatives linked to Iran's IRGC who infiltrated Kuwaiti territory. Kuwait condemned the incursion as a hostile violation of sovereignty and demanded Iran cease such actions.

stories.title: 'Cultural genocide': Palestinian musicians urge Eurovision boycott over Israel's inclusion
stories.summary: Palestinian musicians called for a boycott of Eurovision over Israel's inclusion, urging attention to the plight of musicians in Gaza as the competition's semi-finals began.

stories.title: Palantir CEO visits Kyiv; Ukraine’s defense minister says company’s technology helps plan deep strikes inside Russia
stories.summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp visited Kyiv and met with President Volodymyr Zelensky and Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Ukraine's defense ministry said Palantir's technology is being used to help plan deep strikes inside Russia.

stories.title: Barcelona soccer star Lamine Yamal raises Palestinian flag during title parade
stories.summary: Barcelona's 18-year-old winger Lamine Yamal raised a Palestinian flag during the club's title parade. Coach Hansi Flick said he doesn't normally favor such gestures but respected the player's decision.

stories.title: Trump heads to China in bid to boost trade, reduce Iran and Taiwan tensions
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is expected to arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Discussions are set to focus on expanding bilateral trade, the ongoing conflict involving Iran, and US arms sales to Taiwan.

stories.title: Ukraine and US prepare landmark “Drone Deal” to expand weapons production and exports
stories.summary: Ukraine and the United States are preparing a landmark "Drone Deal" that would formalize cooperation on drone manufacturing, technology exchange, and expanded weapons production and exports.

stories.title: Israel entered Hamas war with weakened domestic weapons-production capacity, probe finds
stories.summary: An Israeli government probe found that Israel entered the Hamas war with weakened domestic weapons-production capacity. The investigation examined the country's ability to maintain production of weapons, raw materials, components, and defense infrastructure.

stories.title: Weaponised antisemitism joins Israel's genocide denial tactics
stories.summary: Analyst Emad Moussa argued that pro-Israel media campaigns weaponize antisemitism accusations to deflect from allegations of genocide and deny Palestinian suffering.

stories.title: 'Children paying intolerable price': UN condemns child death toll from Israel's West Bank operations
stories.summary: The United Nations condemned the toll of Israeli military operations and settler attacks on children in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem. UNICEF spokesman James Elder reported that 70 Palestinian children have been killed since the start of 2025, averaging roughly one child per week.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers are hiding behind 'dummy troops' in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces in southern Lebanon are reportedly deploying lifelike mannequins dressed as soldiers to serve as decoys against Hezbollah first-person-view drones.

stories.title: French media tycoon Vincent Bolloré casts shadow over Cannes opening
stories.summary: As the 79th Cannes Film Festival opened, hundreds of French film industry figures signed a letter warning about far-right influence in cinema and media. The controversy centers on billionaire Vincent Bolloré, owner of Canal+, which plays a major role in financing French films.

stories.title: Kremlin comments on Putin’s remarks about “conflict nearing its end”
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov responded to President Vladimir Putin's weekend remarks suggesting the war in Ukraine is nearing its end, stating there are currently no concrete details to support that claim.

stories.title: Online scams: How our personal data is being used against us
stories.summary: Frequent data breaches in France, affecting public bodies including La Poste, France Travail, and the ANTS identity documents portal, have exposed personal information that cybercriminals purchase to conduct scams involving bogus bank managers and brokers.

stories.title: Israelis report receive recruitment, threatening text messages from Iran
stories.summary: Israeli police reported that citizens in Israel and abroad received threatening text messages identified as recruitment attempts by Iranian intelligence elements seeking to enlist Israeli nationals.

stories.title: Allies surpassed the US in military budget purchasing power last year, new report shows
stories.summary: A new report indicates that the combined military spending of U.S. allies surpassed American military budget purchasing power last year. However, in absolute dollar terms, Washington remains by far the single largest military spender globally.

stories.title: Inside Israel's covert Litani raid and Hezbollah's counterstrike
stories.summary: Israeli troops crossed the Litani River during a covert operation in southern Lebanon, leading to close-range clashes with Hezbollah fighters. Hezbollah subsequently launched a counterstrike.

stories.title: Ukraine designates 6 more suspects in $10.5 million money-laundering case tied to Zelensky’s former chief of staff
stories.summary: Ukraine's NABU and SAPO identified six additional suspects in a $10.5 million money-laundering case linked to elite residential construction outside Kyiv. The case is connected to former presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak.

stories.title: AI engine: China’s booming tech exports give Beijing ‘wind in its sails’ for Trump summit
stories.summary: China's integrated circuit exports doubled year on year in April to US$31.09 billion, driven by global demand for artificial intelligence hardware. Analysts say the booming tech exports give Beijing strategic leverage ahead of President Trump's visit to the Chinese capital.

stories.title: Kenya: Appeal Court Temporarily Lifts High Court Orders Blocking Kenya-U.S. Health Deal
stories.summary: Kenya's Court of Appeal temporarily suspended High Court orders that had blocked a Kenya-US health cooperation framework, allowing the government to proceed with the programme while an appeal is determined.

stories.title: Gambia: Barrow Vows to Recover 'Every Dalasi' Lost
stories.summary: Gambian President Adama Barrow pledged to pursue legal procedures to recover public funds from Local Government Councils after receiving the Local Government Commission of Inquiry report, which followed three years of hearings.

stories.title: Israeli startup Frame Security raises $50m
stories.summary: Israeli startup Frame Security raised $50 million in funding for its AI-driven cybersecurity platform. The tool is designed to help organizations defend against AI-powered social engineering attacks and deepfake threats.

stories.title: Barca striker Yamal waves Palestinian flag during La Liga celebrations
stories.summary: FC Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal held a Palestinian flag during the club's La Liga title parade after Barcelona secured their 29th league title with a 2-0 victory over Real Madrid.

stories.title: In Russian military parade meant to project power, analysts see ‘real vulnerability’
stories.summary: Analysts reviewing Russia's latest military parade on Red Square identified signs of vulnerability rather than strength. Timothy Ash of Chatham House told Breaking Defense the display reflected growing nervousness in Moscow about the sustainability of Russia's military posture.

stories.title: Israel killing at least one child a week in occupied West Bank, UN says
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that Israeli military forces and settlers have killed at least one Palestinian child per week on average in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Ukrainian company Phantom Defense developing comprehensive counter-drone ecosystem
stories.summary: Ukrainian company Phantom Defense, specializing in counter-drone systems and electronic warfare, is developing a comprehensive ecosystem for detecting and neutralizing unmanned aerial vehicles on the battlefield.

stories.title: French film industry at risk from the far right, say actors and directors
stories.summary: More than 600 French cinema figures, including actress Juliette Binoche, signed an open letter warning that billionaire Vincent Bolloré's dominance in French film production and distribution risks enabling far-right influence over the industry. The letter was published to coincide with the Cannes film festival.

stories.title: Will Donald Trump relaunch attacks on Iran?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, raising questions about the future of the fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Two Lebanese civil defence workers killed in Israeli strike on Nabatieh
stories.summary: Two Lebanese civil defence workers were killed in an Israeli airstrike on the southern town of Nabatieh while conducting a rescue mission following an earlier attack, according to Lebanon's state news agency NNA.

stories.title: Ukraine’s anti-corruption agencies uncover major laundering scheme involving former top officials and elite real estate near Kyiv
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau and Special Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office uncovered a 460 million hryvnia money laundering scheme involving elite real estate construction near Kyiv and tied to former senior officials.

stories.title: UAE's main gas complex to resume full capacity next year after attacks
stories.summary: ADNOC Gas reported that its Habshan gas complex in Abu Dhabi is operating at 60 percent capacity following attacks. The company aims to reach 80 percent by the end of 2026 and full restoration by 2027.

stories.title: Wang Fuk Court administrator outlines HK$127 million refund for displaced owners
stories.summary: The administrator of Hong Kong's Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po disclosed that HK$180 million has been paid to parties involved in renovation after one of the city's deadliest fires. The remaining HK$127 million is to be refunded to displaced owners.

stories.title: Hamas committed 'systematic' sexual violence during October 7 attacks, says report
stories.summary: An independent Israeli investigative commission reported on May 12 that Hamas and allied Palestinian militant groups committed systematic, widespread sexual violence during the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel and against hostages held in Gaza.

stories.title: Starmer stands his ground despite growing pressure to resign
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer sought to shore up Cabinet support amid growing pressure to resign following significant Labour losses in local elections. Speculation has intensified about potential successors, including Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham.

stories.title: Naim Qassem says Hezbollah's arms not part of talks with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem stated that the group's weapons are not subject to ongoing negotiations with Israel. Israel has continued strikes in south Lebanon, killing 380 people since the ceasefire began.

stories.title: How one Palestinian teen’s life changed forever after Israeli gunfire
stories.summary: Amir Othman, a 16-year-old Palestinian, was shot by Israeli soldiers on a hill near Nablus in the occupied West Bank, resulting in life-altering injuries.

stories.title: Budget earmarks more than $600m for Bondi attack response, with half going to Australia’s Jewish community
stories.summary: Australia's federal budget allocated more than $604 million in response to the December Bondi beach terror attack, with approximately $300 million directed to the Jewish community for security and support. The Executive Council of Australian Jewry will receive $124 million for additional security measures.

stories.title: Rugby league, bird flu and drones: things you may have missed in the 2026 budget
stories.summary: Australia's 2026 federal budget included lesser-noticed allocations for fuel resilience, bird flu preparedness, rugby league facility upgrades, and electronic screens at sporting grounds, alongside headline measures on negative gearing, capital gains tax, and family trust reforms.

stories.title: ‘Frogs in a well’: Chinese diplomat slams Europe’s ‘outdated’ approach to China
stories.summary: A senior Chinese diplomat, Li Jian, accused Europe of taking an outdated approach to China at a forum hosted by the EU delegation in Beijing. He signalled that Beijing remains open to addressing Brussels' concerns about economic dependencies.

stories.title: Israeli report accuses Hamas of ‘systematic, widespread’ sexual violence on Oct 7
stories.summary: An Israeli report accused Hamas of committing "systematic, widespread" sexual violence during the October 7 attack. Hamas has repeatedly denied the accusations since 2023.

stories.title: Israel and UAE: A ‘brothers-in-arms’ alliance against Iran's growing threat - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlights deepening military and defense-industrial cooperation between Israel and the United Arab Emirates, framing the partnership as a joint effort to counter Iran's growing regional threat.

stories.title: Ukraine pitches EU on an “airport ceasefire” with Russia—Moscow’s two main airports are now in Ukrainian striking range
stories.summary: Ukraine's foreign minister proposed a mutual "airport ceasefire" with Russia, noting that two main Russian airports are now within Ukrainian striking range. The proposal is framed as a complementary diplomatic track to U.S.-led negotiations.

stories.title: Israel passes law establishing military tribunal for October 7 perpetrators
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed legislation establishing a special military tribunal to try hundreds of Palestinians accused of participating in the October 7, 2023, attack, with the death penalty as a possible sentence. Rights groups criticized the measure over fair-trial concerns.

stories.title: Blast in KP's Lakki Marwat claims 9 lives, injures 33
stories.summary: A blast in the Serai Naurang tehsil of Lakki Marwat district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killed at least nine people, including two traffic police officers, and injured 33 others.

stories.title: These images do not prove that Iran has unveiled kamikaze dolphin drones
stories.summary: Social media posts claiming Iran unveiled kamikaze dolphin-shaped underwater drones were debunked. The images circulating as evidence were determined to be AI-generated.

stories.title: Top Swedish universities eager to forge ties with city, Hong Kong minister says
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry Sun Dong said top Swedish universities expressed strong interest in collaborating with Hong Kong, particularly in life sciences, during an official visit to Sweden.

stories.title: India declines Russian LNG under sanctions, talks continue on permitted cargoes, sources say
stories.summary: India has declined to accept an LNG cargo from Russia's U.S.-sanctioned Portovaya plant in the Baltic Sea, leaving the shipment unable to discharge. Talks continue regarding permitted Russian LNG cargoes.

stories.title: Student opens fire at school in Russia, wounding 2
stories.summary: A ninth-grade student opened fire at a school in Gulkevichi, Krasnodar Krai, Russia, wounding two people, according to local media reports.

stories.title: Israel deports Gaza flotilla activists Avila, Abu Keshek
stories.summary: Israel deported two Gaza flotilla activists, identified as Avila and Abu Keshek, following their detention. Spain, Brazil, and the United Nations had all called for the men's swift release amid widespread international criticism.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Shevchenkove in Kharkiv region, injuring two people
stories.summary: Two people were injured in a Russian strike on the settlement of Shevchenkove in the Kupiansk district of Kharkiv region.

stories.title: 'King of North' Andy Burnham: 'Widely thought' most capable of rebuilding Labour's loose coalition
stories.summary: As UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a leadership crisis following Labour's poor local election results, analysts point to Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham as a potential challenger capable of rebuilding Labour's coalition. Experts described Starmer's situation as existential rather than merely electoral.

stories.title: Inside the Pentagon’s latest ‘alien’ files, plus driving a CV90 in northern Sweden
stories.summary: The Pentagon released a new tranche of declassified files on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena, explored in the latest episode of The Break Out. The program also visited a CV90 tank training facility in northern Sweden.

stories.title: ‘Genuine urgency’: China’s underlying concerns at the Xi-Trump talks
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that the Iran conflict's shadow over the upcoming Xi Jinping–Donald Trump summit in Beijing may give China a strategic advantage in negotiations with the United States.

stories.title: Congress waits on Iran-war costs while mulling $1.5T defense request
stories.summary: The US Department of Defense's latest estimate for the cost of the Iran war stands at $29 billion, but Congress is still awaiting detailed breakdowns requested from the Pentagon. Lawmakers are considering the figures as part of deliberations over a $1.5 trillion defense budget request.

stories.title: Lamine Yamal’s Palestine flag wave hailed by fans, activists and athletes
stories.summary: FC Barcelona and Spain footballer Lamine Yamal waved a Palestinian flag, drawing praise from Palestinians in Gaza, global football fans, and activists.

stories.title: Russian forces strike previously destroyed Skovoroda Museum in Kharkiv region with drone
stories.summary: The Hryhorii Skovoroda National Literary and Memorial Museum in the Zolochiv community of Kharkiv region was struck by a Russian drone. The museum had already been destroyed in a previous attack.

stories.title: Russia seeks to seize large assets from former deputy defense minister accused of corruption, Kommersant reports
stories.summary: Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has asked a Moscow court to seize assets worth 5.5 billion rubles from former Deputy Defense Minister Ruslan Tsalikov and his close relatives, according to the newspaper Kommersant. The case involves corruption allegations.

stories.title: WHO chief says 'work not over' after hantavirus evacuation
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated that containment work continues after a hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius killed three passengers. Health officials stressed the global public health risk remains low.

stories.title: Citing Israel’s ‘international crimes,’ NYC student government trying to defund Hillel
stories.summary: The student senate at The New School in New York City voted to block funding for the campus Hillel chapter, citing Israel's alleged international crimes. The university president pushed back against the move, described as the first of its kind in the U.S.

stories.title: Human hair protects French forests from hungry deer
stories.summary: French recycling company Capillum collects human hair clippings across several European countries and transforms them into biodegradable materials. Among other uses, the hair is deployed in French forests to deter deer from damaging trees, diverting thousands of tonnes of waste from landfills and incinerators each year.

stories.title: Denver airport: Surveillance footage shows moment aircraft fatally struck runway intruder
stories.summary: Surveillance footage from Denver International Airport captured the moment an intruder on a runway was fatally struck by an Airbus A321 that was preparing to depart for Los Angeles on Friday. Authorities confirmed the individual died in the incident.

stories.title: The Love Truck: Easing Lebanon's displacement amid Israel's war
stories.summary: A red truck delivering toys, blankets, and food has become a vital resource for thousands of displaced Lebanese families. The mobile aid effort, known as the Love Truck, operates amid ongoing Israeli airstrikes and mass displacement in Lebanon.

stories.title: Judge bars Jewish DA from trying Stanford anti-Israel protesters, alleging conflict
stories.summary: A judge removed a Jewish district attorney from prosecuting anti-Israel protesters at Stanford University, citing a potential conflict of interest. Critics argued the ruling risks reinforcing antisemitic tropes.

stories.title: Why Trump’s visit to Beijing has Taiwan on edge about US arms sales
stories.summary: Taiwan is closely watching the upcoming summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing, concerned that arms sales to the island could be used as leverage in broader Sino-American negotiations. Trump's three-day state visit includes bilateral meetings and a state banquet.

stories.title: The Flotilla Diaries: Inside the 2025 mission to break the Gaza siege
stories.summary: Two filmmakers aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla documented their firsthand experiences during the 2025 mission attempting to break the naval siege on Gaza.

stories.title: Ukraine officials name Zelenskyy's ex-Chief of Staff as suspect in money-laundering probe
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau and Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office identified Andriy Yermak, President Zelensky's former Chief of Staff, as a suspect in an alleged 460-million-hryvnia money-laundering scheme.

stories.title: Pentagon says US war on Iran has cost $29bn so far
stories.summary: A senior Pentagon official told US lawmakers that the war on Iran has cost the United States $29 billion so far, an increase of $4 billion from estimates provided the previous month. The figure includes equipment repair, replacement, and operational expenses.

stories.title: Iranian press review: Unexploded US Tomahawks used to develop missile technology
stories.summary: Iranian media reported that unexploded US Tomahawk cruise missiles recovered during the conflict are being studied to develop Iranian missile technology. Separately, displaced Iranians face uncertainty over housing, and the UAE's role in the US-Israeli war is drawing scrutiny.

stories.title: Israel slams NYT opinion article on Palestinian abuse, ignoring Oct. 7 sexual violence
stories.summary: Israel condemned a lengthy New York Times opinion piece alleging sexual abuse of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli detention. Israeli officials accused the article of ignoring sexual violence committed during the 7 October attacks.

stories.title: Rana stars as Bangladesh win first home Test against Pakistan
stories.summary: Fast bowler Nahid Rana took five second-innings wickets as Bangladesh claimed their first-ever home Test cricket victory against Pakistan.

stories.title: 'Insane following': African fans' unbreakable bond with Arsenal FC
stories.summary: The article explores the deep popularity of Arsenal FC among African fans, highlighting Kenyan influencer Nana Owiti's two-decade devotion to the club, rooted in the era when the London team's largely Black squad resonated across the continent.

stories.title: More than 2,134 children abducted by Russia return to Ukraine — Lubinets
stories.summary: Ukraine's human rights commissioner Lubinets announced that 2,134 children abducted by Russia have been returned to Ukraine through the Bring Kids Back UA initiative.

stories.title: NATO to cultivate vetted counter-drone vendor pool for nations to pick and choose
stories.summary: NATO is establishing a vetted pool of counter-drone system vendors from which member nations can select equipment. The alliance has also set up common funding to allow countries to test counter-UAS systems before committing to procurement decisions.

stories.title: Trump-Xi meeting: Could China, US form a ‘G2’?
stories.summary: An upcoming meeting between President Trump and President Xi Jinping in Beijing has revived discussion of a so-called 'Group of Two' arrangement between the United States and China.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz closure, FAO warns of fertilizer scarcity and calendar for new planting season
stories.summary: FAO Director-General QU Dongyu warned that global fertilizer scarcity caused by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz will lead to lower agricultural yields and tightening food supplies in late 2026 and into 2027.

stories.title: BBC: 184 sanctioned Russian tankers made 238 journeys through UK waters since the PM’s March intercept threat
stories.summary: A BBC investigation found that 184 sanctioned Russian tankers made 238 journeys through UK waters since the British prime minister's March threat to intercept such vessels. Ninety-four instances involved entry into UK territorial waters, with zero confirmed boardings.

stories.title: Namibia: Oshikoto Seeks N$22m to Tackle Water Crisis ... Oshigambo Canal Revival Underway
stories.summary: Oshikoto Governor Sacky Kathindi stated that the Namibian region requires approximately N$22 million to address persistent water shortages affecting communities. Efforts to revive the Oshigambo Canal are also underway.

stories.title: Iran war creates new must-have for summer holidays: the plan B
stories.summary: Greg Abbott, a traveler in Europe, is adjusting his summer holiday plans due to the Iran war. Concerns over rising airfares and flight cancellations are prompting him to stay closer to home and prepare backup travel options.

stories.title: South Africa: Unemployment Rate Rises 1.3 Percentage Points to 32.7 Percent
stories.summary: South Africa's unemployment rate rose by 1.3 percentage points to 32.7 percent. Analysts warn the economic outlook may worsen amid fallout from the Middle East conflict triggered by US and Israeli attacks on Iran.

stories.title: Mozambique: Violence and Attacks Continue in Cabo Delgado Province - Bishop of Quelimane Calls for Prayer
stories.summary: Islamist insurgents continued attacks across multiple districts in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province, including Nangade, Mocímboa da Praia, Ancuabe, and Macomia. A raid in Namacuili killed at least four people. The Bishop of Quelimane called for prayer as violence displaces hundreds of civilians.

stories.title: Mossad chief says Netanyahu pick to replace him 'unfit' for role
stories.summary: Mossad Director David Barnea submitted a letter to Israel's Supreme Court warning that Prime Minister Netanyahu's nominee to replace him, Roman Gofman, is "unfit" for the role. Barnea cited what he described as a "serious moral problem" with Gofman, Netanyahu's current military secretary.

stories.title: Kenya: Police Link Nakuru Cleric's Killing to Notorious Armed Gang
stories.summary: Kenyan detectives investigating the murder of Reverend Julius Ndumia Ngari in Nakuru County have linked the killing to a criminal gang believed responsible for a series of violent robberies in the area.

stories.title: Kenya: What to Do If You Encounter a Hyena in a Residential Area
stories.summary: The Kenya Wildlife Service responded to reports of a hyena sighting near Mwananchi Road off Eastport Drive in Syokimau, Nairobi. Residents in surrounding areas were urged to remain vigilant.

stories.title: ‘Insatiable appetite’ for AI: Maven usage surged for strikes on Iran, Pentagon AI chief says
stories.summary: Pentagon AI chief disclosed that use of Palantir's Maven Smart System surged during Operation Epic Fury, the U.S. military campaign involving approximately 13,000 airstrikes on Iran. Department of Defense users consumed roughly 20 billion AI tokens per day as the system assisted in planning and coordinating strikes.

stories.title: Maker of Canvas learning platform strikes deal for hackers to return data
stories.summary: Instructure's Canvas learning management platform was shut down for several hours following a cyberattack on May 7. The company has since reached an agreement with the hackers to secure the return of stolen data.

stories.title: US-China summit could reshape global power
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is preparing for an upcoming summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. The Iran war, trade agreements, and Taiwan are expected to dominate the agenda as Trump seeks a major foreign policy achievement.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit: High stakes for the US, China and the world
stories.summary: President Trump is set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping at an upcoming summit in Beijing. The Iran war, trade deals, and Taiwan are expected to dominate the agenda as Trump seeks a foreign policy achievement.

stories.title: Cyprus to join agreement on Special Tribunal
stories.summary: Cyprus has notified the Council of Europe of its intention to join the agreement on establishing a Special Tribunal for the crime of aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Suspect in UK ex-synagogue arson was in touch with person with Iraqi number, prosecutors say
stories.summary: Moses Edwards, 45, appeared in a UK court charged in connection with the firebombing of the former East London Central Synagogue. Prosecutors said he had been in contact with a person linked to an Iraqi phone number. A 52-year-old woman was also arrested and released on bail.

stories.title: Farmer-owned supermarket sets example for better remuneration model
stories.summary: In southern France, farmers have launched their own supermarket to deliver fresh produce and secure better prices for growers. The initiative comes as annual wholesale price negotiations between agricultural producers and supermarket chains coincide with rising fuel and fertilizer costs linked to the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz amid conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Mossad chief opposes Netanyahu’s successor pick: Israeli press review
stories.summary: Mossad chief David Barnea publicly opposed Prime Minister Netanyahu's choice of Roman Gofman as his successor. Separately, Israel's civil aviation chief warned that Ben Gurion Airport has effectively become a US military base during the Iran conflict.

stories.title: “Future of war” meets Ukraine’s black soil: ground drone commander on why combat robots often don’t survive the first battle
stories.summary: A Ukrainian ground-drone commander described how battlefield conditions—including mud, electronics failures, and unreliable first missions—quickly expose the limitations of combat robots despite their perceived role in the future of warfare.

stories.title: 'Our democracy has passed all the tests now,' says Botswana's president
stories.summary: Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko spoke with FRANCE 24 at the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, Kenya. Boko, a Harvard-educated human rights lawyer elected in October 2024, ended the former ruling party's six-decade hold on power. He credited growing opposition momentum and declared that Botswana's democracy has now passed every test.

stories.title: US consumer inflation jumps as Iran war sends energy prices higher
stories.summary: U.S. consumer prices rose 3.8 percent year-over-year in April 2025, according to Labor Department data, the highest jump since 2023. The increase was driven largely by rising energy costs linked to the ongoing U.S. war with Iran, with gasoline prices climbing 5.4 percent month-over-month.

stories.title: Supermajority of Israeli Arab students support non-security-linked national service, study finds
stories.summary: A new study found that 75% of Israeli Arab 12th-grade students support volunteering for non-security-related national service. The survey also showed strong support among respondents for Arab political parties joining a future coalition government.

stories.title: Trump to head to China for high-stakes talks with Xi – US politics live
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is heading to China for a three-day state visit including talks with President Xi Jinping, amid a tentative trade truce. The Pentagon updated the cost of the U.S. war with Iran to approximately $29 billion, up from $25 billion disclosed in late April.

stories.title: Ukraine drafted a ‘right to forget.’ Then NABU named Yermak a suspect.
stories.summary: Ukraine drafted legislation described as a 'right to forget,' but the National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) subsequently named former presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak as a suspect. A related case is already pending in court.

stories.title: Navy pushes Congress to back constructing auxiliary ships overseas
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy's latest shipbuilding plan urges Congress to authorize construction of auxiliary vessels at overseas shipyards. The plan also confirmed that the Trump-class battleship will be nuclear-powered and that the Navy aims to field an inventory of 15 battleships by 2056.

stories.title: Kuwait says it stopped armed Iranian team from attacking one of its islands
stories.summary: Kuwait said six armed individuals linked to Iran's IRGC attempted to infiltrate Bubiyan Island on May 1 to carry out hostile acts. Four were captured and two escaped. Kuwait condemned the incursion as an infringement on its sovereignty.

stories.title: Germany invests more than EUR 10M in development of military training centers in Ukraine
stories.summary: Germany announced an investment of more than 10 million euros in infrastructure for military training centers in Ukraine, part of an EU initiative aimed at sustaining long-term combat readiness of Ukrainian forces.

stories.title: Israel approves law on death penalty for October 7 detainees
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed legislation allowing the death penalty for detainees linked to the 7 October attacks. The law enables special public trials and possible execution of Palestinians accused of involvement in the assault.

stories.title: Trump’s cadre of CEOs hunts for wins in China, from soybeans to semiconductors
stories.summary: A delegation of 17 American CEOs is accompanying U.S. President Donald Trump on a state visit to China, including Apple's Tim Cook. Analysts said the executives represent industries affected by trade tensions and are expected to push for deeper commercial engagement with Beijing.

stories.title: US official urges South Sudan authorities to uphold 2018 peace agreement
stories.summary: Nick Checker, head of the U.S. State Department's Bureau of African Affairs, visited Juba and urged South Sudanese authorities to take urgent action to restore peace and uphold the 2018 peace agreement.

stories.title: UK govenrment divided around Starmer as three junior ministers resign
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting internal pressure after three junior ministers resigned and dozens of Labour MPs called for him to step down. Several senior figures, including the Interior Minister, have advised him to consider his position following Labour's poor results in last week's local elections. Starmer says he has no intention of resigning.

stories.title: Trump says Cuba is seeking help, will hold talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced on social media that Cuba is seeking help and that talks would take place, without providing further details. He described Cuba as a "failed country" heading in a negative direction. The White House and State Department did not immediately comment.

stories.title: 'Amman's Epstein': Fake doctor allegedly assaults three minors
stories.summary: Jordanian authorities arrested a man accused of posing as a cosmetic doctor who allegedly sexually assaulted three minors. The suspect has been dubbed "Amman's Epstein" in media coverage of the case.

stories.title: Irish TV to air Father Ted instead of Eurovision final in protest against Israel’s inclusion
stories.summary: Ireland's national broadcaster RTÉ announced it will air the 1996 Father Ted Eurovision episode instead of the Eurovision Song Contest final, in protest against Israel's inclusion in the competition. RTÉ has been accused of antisemitism over the decision.

stories.title: WHO cautiously optimistic over hantavirus as more cases still possible
stories.summary: The World Health Organization said its response to the hantavirus outbreak is ongoing, noting that the virus's long incubation period means additional cases may emerge. Many countries are coordinating efforts based on WHO guidelines, drawing on cooperation frameworks built during the Covid pandemic. The United States has not followed the WHO's recommendations.

stories.title: Yulia Navalnaya Rejects Claims of ‘Fictitious Employees’ as FBK Infighting Goes Public
stories.summary: Yulia Navalnaya rejected claims of fictitious employees at the Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK) after former CEO Ivan Zhdanov called for an internal audit, alleging that ex-chairman Leonid Volkov had hired non-existent staff. The dispute has made internal FBK tensions public.

stories.title: Elon Musk joins Trump’s Beijing delegation as a ‘natural bridge’ for trade
stories.summary: Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is part of U.S. President Donald Trump's delegation for a three-day state visit to Beijing beginning Wednesday. Musk is expected to join meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping, adding a commercial dimension to the diplomatically sensitive trip.

stories.title: UK Defense minister “sick and tired of journalists and armchair generals” talking our military are ‘unprepared’
stories.summary: UK Defense Readiness and Industry Minister Luke Pollard said he was "sick and tired" of journalists and commentators suggesting the British military is unprepared. He later retracted the remark, which came in response to a BFBS Forces News audience poll.

stories.title: Qatar says Iran should not use Hormuz to 'blackmail' Gulf
stories.summary: Qatar called on Iran not to use the Strait of Hormuz as a tool of pressure against Gulf states. Qatari officials said the key waterway should not be weaponized amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: How a British prime minister is replaced: the keys to a possible Starmer succession
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces his most serious political crisis since taking office in July 2024 but has ruled out resigning. A potential leadership change is complicated by Labour Party rules, the absence of a consensus successor, and internal political dynamics.

stories.title: Nauseda hopes for rapid launch of joint military production with Ukraine
stories.summary: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda expressed hope for the rapid launch of joint military production projects with Ukraine. The initiative aims to strengthen defense cooperation between the two countries amid the ongoing Russian threat.

stories.title: Hezbollah tries to shoot down Air Force fighter jet with surface-to-air missile
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired a surface-to-air missile at an Israeli Air Force fighter jet, marking a new challenge to the air force's previously unchallenged air supremacy over the conflict zone.

stories.title: Africa’s richest man plans new Mombasa oil refinery: Why this matters
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote, Africa's richest man, announced plans to build a new oil refinery in Mombasa, Kenya. The East African facility would be modeled on his recently completed mega refinery in Lagos, Nigeria.

stories.title: Argentina sees new university protest as government pledges post-march dialogue
stories.summary: Argentine public universities staged a fourth Federal University March on Tuesday against budget cuts imposed by President Javier Milei's government, with the main rally in Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires. The government announced it would meet with university rectors after the protest to discuss funding for university hospitals.

stories.title: A secret Israeli base in Iraq? What we know
stories.summary: Reports indicate that Israel operated a covert military base inside Iraq, which was allegedly used to launch attacks against Iran during the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Bpifrance’s Arnaud Floris: ‘Our scope is high-impact commerce’
stories.summary: Arnaud Floris, Bpifrance's Africa director, said a wave of specialized small and medium-sized enterprises and local partnerships is reshaping French commercial engagement on the African continent as larger corporations scale back their presence.

stories.title: The two 'Spartas': How the UAE doubled down on ties with Israel
stories.summary: UAE-Israel defense and intelligence cooperation has deepened significantly during the Iran war. Analysts are examining how this strengthened partnership between Abu Dhabi and Jerusalem will affect regional dynamics going forward.

stories.title: France invites Kenya to attend G7 summit amid Africa Forward Summit
stories.summary: France invited Kenya to attend the G7 summit during the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi, promoting what it calls a new partnership model with African nations. The move comes as France completes a military withdrawal from West African countries, widely seen as a sign of its declining influence on the continent.

stories.title: UK, EU, and Canada sanction Russian networks linked to deportation of Ukrainian children
stories.summary: The United Kingdom, European Union, and Canada imposed sanctions on Russian networks linked to the deportation of Ukrainian children. More than 20,000 Ukrainian children are estimated to have been taken to Russia or occupied territories since the full-scale invasion began.

stories.title: China backs Hong Kong courts, ignores calls to free Jimmy Lai ahead of Trump visit
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs rejected calls to release jailed Hong Kong media figure Jimmy Lai ahead of U.S. President Donald Trump's state visit. Spokesman Guo Jiakun described Lai as a "principal mastermind" behind unrest in Hong Kong and reaffirmed Beijing's support for Hong Kong's judicial authorities.

stories.title: At least nine killed in explosion at Pakistan market
stories.summary: At least nine people were killed and around 30 injured in an explosion at a market in the town of Sarai Naurang, located in Lakki Marwat district in northwestern Pakistan.

stories.title: Don’t Fall for Rumors of Putin’s Weakness
stories.summary: An analysis argues that reports suggesting cracks in Russian President Vladimir Putin's regime are overstated, contending that Putin retains firm control through his mastery of authoritarian governance. The piece cautions against interpreting signs of internal dissent as evidence of meaningful weakness in the Kremlin.

stories.title: Independent Israeli report accuses Hamas of 'systematic' sexual violence during October 7 attacks
stories.summary: An independent Israeli commission found that Hamas and allied groups committed systematic, widespread sexual violence during the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel and against hostages taken to Gaza. Separately, Israel's Knesset passed legislation creating a special military tribunal to try Palestinian militants accused of participating in the attack, with provisions allowing the death penalty.

stories.title: Report alleges Israel operated covert outpost in Iraq during war on Iran
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Israel operated a military base in Iraq during the US-Israeli war on Iran. The outpost was reportedly used to support military operations against Iranian targets.

stories.title: Report: Ukrainian drone strikes residential building in Russia, governor confirms damage
stories.summary: Ukrainian Telegram channels reported an explosion in the Russian city of Orenburg, with unconfirmed reports indicating a Ukrainian drone struck a residential building. The regional governor confirmed damage.

stories.title: US inflation jumped to 3.8% in April as war with Iran continues to drive up prices
stories.summary: U.S. inflation rose to 3.8 percent year-over-year in April 2025, the highest since 2023, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data. The increase was driven largely by rising energy prices linked to the ongoing U.S. war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Anduril wins Army contract for prototype C2 missile defense system
stories.summary: Anduril Industries has been awarded a U.S. Army contract to develop a prototype command-and-control missile defense system. The system will use Anduril's Lattice software platform to integrate data from multiple existing missile defense systems into a unified operational picture.

stories.title: Starmer replacement remains to be found as pressure for PM to resign grows
stories.summary: A second junior minister resigned from UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's government on May 12 as more Labour lawmakers called on him to step down. Despite growing pressure, no clear replacement candidate has emerged within the party, though some potential contenders have been identified.

stories.title: Zelensky, Fedorov meet CEO of American company Palantir to discuss defense cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Digital Transformation Minister Mykhailo Fedorov met with Palantir Technologies CEO Alex Karp to discuss defense cooperation. Discussions covered technological development for both military operations and civilian applications.

stories.title: Oil prices rise for third day in a row as Iran ceasefire talks stall
stories.summary: Oil prices rose for a third consecutive day as US-Iran ceasefire negotiations stalled. Brent crude futures climbed nearly four percent to approximately $108 per barrel after President Trump said the ceasefire was "on life support."

stories.title: Naomi Shloush's 'Academic bimbo' confronts Mizrahi identity in modern Israel
stories.summary: Naomi Shloush's book "Academic Bimbo" explores Mizrahi identity in modern Israel, confronting themes of stigma, belonging, and exclusion.

stories.title: Russia cuts 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.4% from 1.3%
stories.summary: Russia's government cut its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.4 percent, down from a previous projection of 1.3 percent. Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak announced the revised figure.

stories.title: Noam Bettan shines in Eurovision rehearsal as Israel faces antisemitism campaign
stories.summary: Israeli Eurovision contestant Noam Bettan rehearsed in Basel ahead of the competition, performing inside a rotating structure with dancer Lihi Freud. Israel's participation in the 2026 contest has drawn protests and boycott campaigns.

stories.title: Los Angeles's housing crisis: Essential workers priced out of the city
stories.summary: In Los Angeles, soaring property prices and rents are pushing essential workers—including nurses, teachers, and firefighters—out of the city and far from their workplaces. Many face long commutes as home ownership becomes increasingly unaffordable, highlighting a deepening housing crisis in one of America's largest cities.

stories.title: Namibia: Diesel Costs Bite Mining Operations
stories.summary: Rising diesel costs and global supply disruptions are pressuring mining operations in Namibia, as highlighted during a media visit to Swakop Uranium in Arandis.

stories.title: When food becomes memory: Alon Shaya's culinary tribute to Holocaust survivors
stories.summary: Israeli-American chef Alon Shaya created a culinary project transforming Holocaust survivors' stories into dishes, aiming to preserve identity, resilience, and remembrance through food.

stories.title: 'Upside-Down Love': An Israeli-Palestinian memoir of marriage across borders
stories.summary: Israeli-American lawyer Sari Bashi published a memoir titled "Upside-Down Love" about her marriage to a Palestinian. The book recounts a relationship shaped by legal restrictions and physical distance imposed by border controls.

stories.title: 'Digital Warrior': How a lone soldier shaped Israel's global narrative after October 7
stories.summary: An account details how a lone Israeli soldier contributed to shaping Israel's international media narrative after the October 7 attack, describing involvement in real-time information operations.

stories.title: Kenya: At Least 11 Arrested As Police Disperse Protesters Near Africa Forward Summit Venues
stories.summary: At least 11 people were arrested in Nairobi after Kenyan police dispersed groups of protesters attempting to reach venues hosting the Africa Forward Summit.

stories.title: Nearly 50 countries join Ukraine’s coalition to return children abducted by Russia
stories.summary: Nearly 50 countries have joined Ukraine's International Coalition for the Return of Ukrainian Children, with Switzerland and Cyprus among the latest members. The coalition works to locate and repatriate minors taken during Russia's war.

stories.title: Winners for life 2026: “Hasidut Be-Class” takes the stage in Jerusalem
stories.summary: A tribute concert called "Hasidut Be-Class" was held at Sultan's Pool in Jerusalem in support of Israel's emergency response system. The event is part of the Winners for Life 2026 initiative.

stories.title: South Africa: Granny Flees Flooded Shack As Storms Kill Three in Western Cape
stories.summary: Severe storms in South Africa's Western Cape killed three people and displaced more than 41,000 across 26 informal settlements. In Khayelitsha, Cape Town, residents including 50-year-old Nomabhaso Veli fled flooded shacks as the province declared a disaster.

stories.title: Suparco says Eidul Azha likely to fall on May 27
stories.summary: Pakistan's Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) forecast that the Zilhajj crescent moon could be sighted on May 17, projecting Eidul Azha to fall on May 27.

stories.title: How Israel's 7 October law differs from Ben-Gvir's death penalty
stories.summary: Israel's new 7 October law allows special trials and possible death sentences for Palestinians accused of involvement in the attack. The legislation differs from earlier death penalty proposals pushed by National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

stories.title: Why the Iran war is threatening whales near South Africa
stories.summary: Increased shipping traffic linked to the Iran conflict is raising the risk of ship strikes on whales in waters near South Africa. The rerouting of vessels has heightened exposure of whale populations to maritime hazards.

stories.title: Damage after Russia's overnight attack in Kyiv region reported in three districts
stories.summary: Russian drones struck nine facilities overnight on May 12 across the Fastiv, Vyshhorod, and Bila Tserkva districts of the Kyiv region, causing damage to infrastructure.

stories.title: 'Too Israel-focused, too Jewy': How publishing closes its doors to Jewish writers - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses how political pressures, fear, and quiet boycotts in the publishing industry are reportedly narrowing opportunities for Jewish writers and Israel-related voices in the literary world.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict likely to dominate strategic calculations during Trump’s China visit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrives in China on May 13 for a three-day state visit focused on trade and economic ties. The ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict is expected to influence strategic discussions between Washington and Beijing.

stories.title: IDF says it carried out weeklong raid on Hezbollah sites beyond Lebanon’s Litani River
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces said they conducted a weeklong operation targeting Hezbollah sites north of the Litani River in Lebanon. Separately, Hezbollah's leader stated that the group's weapons are not a subject of Israel-Lebanon negotiations.

stories.title: Hezbollah leader vows to never surrender, calls for Lebanon to withdraw from negotiations
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem vowed that the group would never surrender and called on Lebanon to withdraw from negotiations. Qassem stated that Lebanon would not return to conditions that existed before March 2.

stories.title: Chad's 'At the Heart of Art' festival empowers a new generation of talents
stories.summary: The third edition of the "At the Heart of Art" festival concluded in N'Djamena's Bakara district in Chad, showcasing music and performance by young Chadian artists as a vehicle for youth empowerment.

stories.title: Uganda: Museveni Calls for End to Raw Exports, Pushes Africa Toward Value Addition
stories.summary: Ugandan President Museveni outlined a post-election economic plan focused on industrialization, value addition, and skills development, arguing that exporting raw materials while importing finished goods prevents prosperity for Uganda and Africa.

stories.title: Turkey supporting efforts to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said in Doha that Turkey supports efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and opposes its use as a weapon in the Iran conflict. He added that Ankara is contributing to Pakistan-led negotiations seeking a diplomatic end to the US-Iran war.

stories.title: In a bind over rare earths, Europe watches US-China tussle from the sidelines
stories.summary: European officials are watching U.S.-China tensions over rare earth minerals with concern, as China has expanded export controls with an extraterritorial element that could restrict products made in third countries containing Chinese-origin rare earth content. Europe remains largely on the sidelines of the dispute.

stories.title: Opposing Taiwan independence is in America’s own interest
stories.summary: As U.S. President Donald Trump prepares to visit China, the article discusses Taiwan's role as one of the most sensitive issues in U.S.-China relations. It argues that a clear U.S. stance on Taiwan independence could help avoid a broader conflict with Beijing and stabilize trade and geopolitical cooperation.

stories.title: Huckabee: Israel sent Iron Dome, personnel to UAE amid Iran war
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee revealed that Israel deployed Iron Dome missile defense systems and military personnel to the UAE during the Iran war. This represents the first publicly acknowledged Israeli military deployment to the Emirates since the conflict began.

stories.title: 'It started on October 7': How war reshaped Israel's defense-tech boom
stories.summary: Israel's defense-technology sector has experienced rapid growth since October 7, with battlefield demands accelerating innovation. The country has emerged as a central player in a rapidly evolving global defense-tech landscape.

stories.title: Dela Rosa’s flight turns Philippine Senate into battleground for ICC accountability
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, a former national police chief and close ally of ex-President Rodrigo Duterte, evaded an International Criminal Court arrest warrant by taking refuge in the Philippine Senate. The standoff has turned the chamber into the center of a legal and political dispute over ICC accountability.

stories.title: President, PM pay tribute to shepherd who sacrificed his life while averting suicide attack in Attock
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif honored a shepherd named Liaqat who died confronting a suicide bomber near a security post in Attock's Jand tehsil, on the Punjab–Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border.

stories.title: 'Am I a murderer?' Yad Vashem restores a Jewish ghetto policeman's Holocaust confession
stories.summary: Yad Vashem has restored and published a Holocaust-era diary written by a Jewish ghetto policeman. The document, which had been buried and later distorted, contains the author's personal confession about his wartime role.

stories.title: One radar sees 250 km out. The other measures altitude at 300 km range. Ukraine’s drones just took both out in Donetsk Oblast
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone forces and special operations units struck two Russian radar systems in Donetsk Oblast—one with a 250-km detection range and another capable of measuring altitude at 300 km. Additional targets included fuel depots and military bases.

stories.title: Defense Intelligence publishes data on companies involved in production of Russian Pantsir-S1 air defense system
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Intelligence (HUR) published details on companies involved in manufacturing the 72V6 combat vehicle, a component of Russia's Pantsir-S1 anti-aircraft missile and gun system.

stories.title: Pakistan scrambles to salvage US-Iran diplomacy as ceasefire faces collapse
stories.summary: Pakistan rejected allegations that it provided military aid to Iran, amid efforts to mediate between the US and Iran. US President Donald Trump described the existing ceasefire as being on "life support" due to stalled negotiations.

stories.title: Israeli army chief warns reserve forces could 'collapse' amid manpower crisis
stories.summary: Israeli military chief of staff Eyal Zamir warned Knesset lawmakers that the army's reserve forces could collapse within months. He urged the government to pass legislation expanding conscription and extending mandatory military service to 36 months.

stories.title: CYBERCOM requests 2,660 percent increase in AI for cyber operations
stories.summary: U.S. Cyber Command has requested a 2,660 percent funding increase for artificial intelligence capabilities in cyber operations, totaling $138 million. The funds are intended to deliver measurable improvements across ISR, offensive cyber, defensive cyber, and integrated foundational activities.

stories.title: Israel sent Iron Dome to UAE during Iran war, Huckabee confirms
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee confirmed that Israel deployed Iron Dome air defense batteries to the United Arab Emirates during the Iran war. The move represents a significant step in military cooperation between Israel and the UAE.

stories.title: Kenya: Gachagua Moves to Supreme Court to Strike Out Appeal On Impeachment Bench
stories.summary: Former Kenyan Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua filed a motion at the Supreme Court seeking to strike out an appeal challenging the composition of the High Court bench handling petitions related to his impeachment.

stories.title: If Starmer gets his way, Reform - not the Greens - will be his legacy
stories.summary: The article discusses the political implications for UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, arguing his approach could strengthen the Reform party rather than the Greens. It examines parallels with Jeremy Corbyn's earlier insurgent politics within the Labour movement.

stories.title: Elon Musk, Apple's Tim Cook to head to China with Trump, per White House
stories.summary: The White House announced that Elon Musk and Apple CEO Tim Cook will accompany President Trump on his visit to China. Beijing said it is prepared to work with the U.S. toward greater stability.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike two Russian radars, fuel, ammunition depots in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Operators from the Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces' 1st Separate Center struck PRV-16 and P-18 radar systems, a fuel depot, an ammunition storage site, and Russian temporary deployment points in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Malawi: Kamuzu Stadium Turned Into a Place of Tears As Malawi Received 15 Bodies From Zimbabwe Bus Tragedy
stories.summary: Kamuzu Stadium in Malawi served as a receiving site for 15 coffins carrying Malawians killed in a bus crash in Zimbabwe, drawing large crowds of mourners.

stories.title: IDF to establish haredi-manned suicide drone factory, aiming to counter Hezbollah threat - report
stories.summary: The IDF plans to establish a factory staffed by ultra-Orthodox (haredi) personnel to produce suicide drones, according to Army Radio. The initiative aims to counter the growing threat from FPV drones operated by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Kuwait says it has arrested four IRGC affiliates
stories.summary: Kuwait's interior ministry announced the arrest of four individuals it said were affiliated with Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps after they attempted to enter the country by sea. A member of Kuwait's armed forces was injured during clashes with the infiltrators.

stories.title: New Israeli law sets military tribunal for Hamas October 7 militants
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed legislation on Monday establishing a military tribunal to prosecute hundreds of Palestinian militants involved in the October 7, 2023 attack. Lawmakers said the measure would help address national trauma from the assault.

stories.title: Video: Philippine senator flees ICC arrest over role in drug war
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald Dela Rosa took refuge in the country's parliament to avoid arrest by police acting on an International Criminal Court warrant. The ICC sought his detention over his alleged role in the Philippines' drug war.

stories.title: Iran war creates new must-have for summer holidays — the plan B
stories.summary: The Iran conflict is affecting summer holiday planning, with travelers opting for short-haul European destinations and train travel to avoid potential flight disruptions and rising air fares.

stories.title: Iran expands operational definition of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has expanded its operational definition of the Strait of Hormuz from an estimated 20-30 miles to between 200 and 300 miles, according to Iranian media reports. The move broadens the area Iran considers within the strait's operational scope.

stories.title: Malaysia, Tamil Nadu share deep ties, says PM Anwar Ibrahim; congratulates new Tamil Nadu CM Joseph Vijay
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Joseph Vijay on becoming Tamil Nadu's new Chief Minister, highlighting the deep cultural and historical ties between Malaysia and Tamil Nadu.

stories.title: IDF uses robots to advance beyond Lebanon’s Litani River, FPV drones continue challenging military
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported using ground robots to advance beyond Lebanon's Litani River and said it killed approximately 15 Hezbollah fighters over three days of operations. FPV drones continue to pose significant challenges to IDF forces in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Can China counter US sanctions with its trade power?
stories.summary: Economic tensions between the United States and China are escalating, spanning sanctions and rare earth mineral exports. Analysts are examining whether China can leverage its trade power to counter US sanctions pressure.

stories.title: 173 Indians among foreigners arrested in latest cyber crime crackdown in Sri Lanka
stories.summary: Sri Lankan authorities arrested 198 foreigners, including 173 Indians and 25 Nepalese nationals, in the southern resort areas of Galle, Hikkaduwa, and Midigama on May 11, 2026. The arrests were part of a crackdown on cyber crime operations.

stories.title: Estonia appoints Tiina Intelmann as new ambassador to Ukraine
stories.summary: Estonian President Alar Karis appointed Tiina Intelmann as Estonia's new ambassador to Ukraine.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine resume strikes as truce expires, one dead: authorities
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine resumed strikes against each other after a truce expired, with at least one person killed. Ukrainian military officials in Kyiv warned residents of enemy UAVs over the capital and urged them to seek shelter.

stories.title: Peace deal hopes fade after Trump rejects ‘garbage’ Iran proposal
stories.summary: Iran called for an end to hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon, as hopes for a peace deal faded after U.S. President Trump rejected Tehran's counterproposal to a peace plan.

stories.title: Peace deal hopes fade after Trump rejects 'garbage' Iran proposal
stories.summary: Prospects for a U.S.-Iran peace deal dimmed on Tuesday after President Donald Trump described Tehran's counterproposal as "garbage" and said a ceasefire was "on life support." Iran rejected Washington's proposal and maintained its own list of demands.

stories.title: US top diplomat Rubio discusses Iran, Strait of Hormuz with Britain and Australia
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio held discussions with British and Australian counterparts on the Iran conflict and efforts to restore freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel passes law to publicly try and execute Palestinians linked to 7 October attacks
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a law enabling public trials and potential execution of Palestinians linked to the 7 October attacks. The legislation gained broad political support, with Israel's justice minister calling it one of the Knesset's most important moments.

stories.title: Spain reports new hantavirus case as outbreak grows to 11
stories.summary: Spain confirmed a new hantavirus case involving a passenger evacuated from a cruise ship at the center of an outbreak. The World Health Organization has confirmed 11 cases total, including three deaths. The patient is quarantined in a military hospital in Madrid.

stories.title: Burnham allies warn against quick ‘coronation’ of Streeting if Starmer quits
stories.summary: Allies of Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham warned against a quick "coronation" of Health Secretary Wes Streeting as Labour leader if Prime Minister Keir Starmer resigns. They called on Labour's ruling body to ensure Burnham could stand for a parliamentary byelection to enter the leadership race.

stories.title: Key events in ties among United States, China and Taiwan
stories.summary: The Trump administration approved $11 billion in arms sales to Taiwan, prompting China to launch its most extensive military exercises around the island. The developments mark an escalation in US-China tensions over Taiwan.

stories.title: Melania, Rush Hour director returns to China with Trump’s delegation
stories.summary: Film director Brett Ratner, known for the Rush Hour franchise and the documentary Melania, is traveling to China as part of U.S. President Donald Trump's delegation. Ratner plans to advance preparations for Rush Hour 4, including meetings with potential Chinese film distribution partners.

stories.title: How a fake Iraqi officer infiltrated Lebanon's security agencies
stories.summary: An Iraqi man was uncovered after allegedly posing as a senior security official and infiltrating Lebanon's political and security circles. The suspect reportedly gained access to high-level contacts before his deception was discovered by Lebanese agencies.

stories.title: After the Raj, the most powerful weapon in Pakistan's arsenal is a name
stories.summary: A report examines how Pakistan named its May 2024 retaliatory military operation against India "Operation Bunyan um Marsoos," and the editorial challenges newsrooms faced in correctly transliterating the Arabic-origin name across various media outlets.

stories.title: We were there. The Supreme Court did not tie the IDF’s hands on the Gaza border
stories.summary: Two former senior IDF officers disputed claims that Israel's Supreme Court restricted open-fire rules before the 7 October attacks. They argued such assertions are a pretext to avoid establishing a state commission of inquiry into the security failures.

stories.title: Hegseth faces new round of questioning from Congress on the Iran war and more
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Hegseth and military chief Caine face congressional questioning on the Iran war and the proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget. The budget emphasizes increased spending on drones, warships, and missile defense systems.

stories.title: TV Rain Editor-in-Chief Jailed 8 Years in Absentia Over War ‘Fakes’
stories.summary: Tikhon Dzyadko, editor-in-chief of the independent Russian outlet TV Rain, was sentenced to eight years in prison in absentia on charges of disseminating false information about Russia's armed forces.

stories.title: Palestine Action trial lawyer wins appeal against contempt of court charge
stories.summary: Human rights barrister Rajiv Menon KC won an appeal against a contempt of court referral stemming from his closing speech during the trial of six Palestine Action activists. The activists were tried for a 2024 protest at Elbit Systems UK's arms factory in Filton, near Bristol.

stories.title: Eyeing migrant returns, EU moves to bolster Syria ties
stories.summary: The European Union announced steps to strengthen ties with Syria, partly aimed at facilitating the return of migrants. New EU funding will support the rehabilitation of a hospital near Homs, and officials said they would explore ways to improve Syrian access to financing.

stories.title: Was Abe Foxman the last ‘Jewish pope’?
stories.summary: Abe Foxman, the longtime director of the Anti-Defamation League, died at age 86. He was widely regarded as a leading voice against antisemitism in the post-Holocaust era and a prominent figure in American Jewish communal life.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Israeli strikes kill six in south Lebanon, says state media
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed six people in southern Lebanon, according to state media. U.S. President Donald Trump warned that the ceasefire in the broader West Asia war was on "life support" after rejecting Iran's latest counteroffer.

stories.title: Israeli MPs back special tribunal with death penalty powers for alleged 7 October attackers
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset voted 93-0 to establish a livestreamed special military tribunal with death penalty powers for Palestinians convicted of involvement in the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. The remaining 27 lawmakers were absent or abstained. The measure has drawn comparisons to the 1962 Adolf Eichmann trial.

stories.title: Pakistan extends countrywide austerity drive after U.S., Iran fail to strike deal
stories.summary: Pakistan extended its countrywide austerity drive after the United States and Iran failed to reach a deal. Key measures include a 50 percent reduction in fuel allowances for official vehicles, exempting operational vehicles such as ambulances and public buses.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 24 attacks on Chernihiv region over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 24 strikes on settlements in Ukraine's Chernihiv region over the past day, primarily using first-person-view (FPV) drones.

stories.title: Ukraine’s IMF lifeline depends on tax reforms parliament keeps stalling
stories.summary: Ukraine faces a funding bottleneck as parliament has stalled a $614 million parcel tax reform now six weeks past its deadline. The tax measure is required to unlock $8.1 billion in IMF financing.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 12: Extremist settlers dealt a blow with EU sanctions
stories.summary: The European Union imposed sanctions on extremist Israeli settlers, in a move seen as a significant blow to settlement activity. Separately, developments include Trump's comments on Iran, a new Gaza police force, and diplomatic tensions involving Israel's US envoy.

stories.title: Rwanda: Exports to China Surge 92 Percent As Demand Rises
stories.summary: Rwanda's exports to China surged 92% in 2025, reaching $160.8 million compared to $83.7 million the previous year, according to the Rwanda Development Board.

stories.title: Brics foreign ministers to meet in New Delhi this week
stories.summary: The annual BRICS foreign ministers' meeting will take place in New Delhi on May 14–15, India's foreign ministry confirmed. The bloc now includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, and the UAE, with India chairing for 2026.

stories.title: EU agrees to sanctions on Israeli settlers after Hungary’s new government lifts veto
stories.summary: The European Union agreed to impose sanctions on Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank after Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar lifted the veto previously maintained by his predecessor Viktor Orbán. The move ends a prolonged deadlock over the long-awaited measures.

stories.title: Liberia: Tweah's Verdict Reflects Judicial Independence, Says Cso Group
stories.summary: A civil society group in Liberia, the Independent Societal Watch Advocates, defended Justice Minister Oswald Tweh amid criticism over the government's handling of a $6.2 million corruption case involving former Finance Minister Samuel Tweah.

stories.title: US negotiating establishment of new bases in Greenland in high level talks with Denmark - report
stories.summary: The United States is negotiating with Denmark to establish new military bases in Greenland, according to reports. Sources indicate the US has proposed that three new bases be formally designated as US sovereign territory.

stories.title: Israel will prosecute Oct 7 suspects in Eichmann-style tribunal
stories.summary: Israel's new law will allow the prosecution of October 7 suspects before a military tribunal. The proceedings will be broadcast publicly and archived, drawing comparisons to the trial of Adolf Eichmann.

stories.title: Historian Achille Mbembe: Africa’s ‘rule of gerontocracy’ is coming to an end
stories.summary: Historian and political theorist Achille Mbembe, speaking at the Africa Forward Summit at Strathmore University, argued that Africa is undergoing a profound transformation. He stated that the era of gerontocratic rule has ended in the minds of the people, even as institutional change remains slow.

stories.title: New Israeli law sets military tribunal for Hamas fighters linked to October 7 attack
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law establishing a military tribunal to try hundreds of Palestinian fighters linked to the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack. The attack killed at least 1,200 people, and Israel's subsequent assault on Gaza killed more than 72,000 Palestinians.

stories.title: Turkey’s Aselsan eyes growth in networked, mass-producible weapons, CEO says
stories.summary: Turkish defense firm Aselsan is pursuing growth in networked and mass-producible weapons systems, according to CEO Ahmet Akyol. In an interview, Akyol stated that the technologies discussed could realistically enter inventory by 2027.

stories.title: European Union adopts new sanctions Israeli settlers over violence in West Bank
stories.summary: European Union foreign ministers agreed on May 12 to impose new sanctions on Israeli settlers over violence against Palestinians in the West Bank, after Hungary's change of government ended months of blockage. The EU also moved to sanction Hamas leaders; Israel condemned the settler sanctions as baseless.

stories.title: An Israeli ‘Excursion’ in Babylon
stories.summary: Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj published a cartoon in The New Arab/Al-Araby Al-Jadeed commenting on Israeli military operations in Iraq-related contexts. The cartoon is part of the publication's daily editorial cartoon series.

stories.title: Aukus costs balloon with more cash and staff for submarine agency amid ongoing search for nuclear waste dump
stories.summary: Australia's budget for the AUKUS submarine program has increased by more than A$430 million over four years, with the Australian Submarine Agency's funding jumping to A$512 million in the next financial year. Concerns persist about whether the sovereign nuclear-powered submarine fleet will ultimately be delivered.

stories.title: Starmer criticised by Holocaust survivors for smearing Palestine marches
stories.summary: More than 40 British Holocaust survivors and their descendants sent an open letter to Prime Minister Keir Starmer criticizing him for linking attacks on Jewish people to pro-Palestine marches. The letter was also addressed to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood and Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley.

stories.title: New power outages reported in five regions following Russian attacks – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: As of the morning of May 12, power outages caused by Russian attacks affected consumers in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, Sumy, Chernihiv, and Mykolaiv regions. Separately, bad weather knocked out electricity in six settlements in the Zakarpattia region.

stories.title: German firms in China more upbeat about economy despite Iran war, trade headwinds: survey
stories.summary: German companies operating in China have grown more optimistic about the country's economic outlook, according to a German Chamber of Commerce survey. Thirty-seven percent of respondents expected improvement over the next six months, up 22 percentage points from the prior year, despite the Iran war and trade tensions.

stories.title: US-China summit tests ties as tensions grow over Taiwan, trade, AI technology
stories.summary: A US-China summit is testing bilateral relations as tensions escalate over Taiwan, trade, and AI technology. Despite President Trump claiming a good relationship with President Xi Jinping, divisions between Washington and Beijing continue to deepen.

stories.title: A Kyiv Oblast kindergarten was hit hours after Russia’s “ceasefire” ended
