He said the attacks, carried out with military support, aim to forcibly displace Palestinians from their land, targeting civilians including schoolchildren.

stories.title: Kuwait's army says it has intercepted hostile drones over airspace
stories.summary: Kuwait's military announced it detected and intercepted several hostile drones in its airspace at dawn on Sunday, May 10. The incident follows a series of cross-border drone incursions linked to the broader Iran conflict in the region.

stories.title: ‘Iconic Jewish leader’: Former Anti-Defamation League director Abe Foxman dies at 86
stories.summary: Abe Foxman, who led the Anti-Defamation League from 1987 to 2015, has died at the age of 86. His successor, Jonathan Greenblatt, called him an 'iconic Jewish leader,' while Israeli President Isaac Herzog described him as a 'passionate Zionist, humanist, and friend.'

stories.title: Iran's enriched uranium under US surveillance, will be extracted 'at some point', Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump stated that Iran's enriched uranium is under U.S. surveillance and warned that anyone approaching the sites would be destroyed, adding that the material would be extracted "at some point."

stories.title: PM Shehbaz recalls Pakistan's 'historic response' to India on Marka-i-Haq's first anniversary
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif addressed a ceremony at the Pakistan Monument in Islamabad marking the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, the state's name for the April–May conflict with India. President Asif Ali Zardari and Field Marshal Asim Munir also attended. The conflict spanned from the April 22 Pahalgam attack to a ceasefire on May 10.

stories.title: Iran sends response to U.S. proposals to end war
stories.summary: Iran transmitted its response to U.S. proposals aimed at ending the war through mediators based in Pakistan, though specific details of the response were not publicly disclosed.

stories.title: Hezbollah airs drone footage showing strike on Iron Dome in northern Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah released drone footage purporting to show a strike on an Iron Dome battery in northern Israel. The group continued firing rockets and drones at IDF troops in southern Lebanon, while Israel struck Hezbollah infrastructure. Beirut reported two Hezbollah-affiliated medics were killed.

stories.title: India, Trinidad and Tobago sign eight MoUs during Jaishankar visit
stories.summary: India and Trinidad and Tobago signed eight memorandums of understanding during External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's two-day visit. The agreements cover tourism, healthcare, infrastructure, and Ayurveda. Both sides also reviewed progress on initiatives announced during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's earlier visit.

stories.title: A campaign by Eurovision fans calls out the EBU for unfairly targeting Israel
stories.summary: Eurovision fans launched a campaign accusing the European Broadcasting Union of unfairly targeting Israel. EBU managing director Martin Green confirmed he issued a formal warning to KAN, Israel's public broadcaster, over an advertising campaign.

stories.title: Tehran sends response to US peace proposal via Pakistan: Iranian state media
stories.summary: Iran transmitted its response to a US peace proposal through Pakistani mediators, according to Iranian state news agencies IRNA and ISNA. Tehran's reply reportedly focuses on ending the ongoing war and ensuring maritime security in the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Knesset panel demands state share losses to passengers and airlines during Iran war
stories.summary: A Knesset panel called on the Israeli government to compensate passengers and airlines for losses incurred during the war with Iran. Major European and U.S. carriers continue to avoid Israeli airspace even after the ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: Nikopol district attacked by Russian drones throughout day, damage reported
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Nikopol district in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region with drones throughout the day, causing damage to civilian infrastructure. No casualty figures were immediately reported.

stories.title: Germany sceptical on Putin's suggestion of Schroeder role in Ukraine peace talks
stories.summary: Germany rejected a proposal by Russian President Vladimir Putin that former Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder serve as a coordinator for EU-Russia peace talks on Ukraine. Berlin dismissed the suggestion on Sunday, May 10.

stories.title: 15 security officials killed in militant attack in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: At least 15 security officials were killed in a militant attack in northwest Pakistan. An explosion destroyed a police post and collapsed the roofs of nearby houses, burying several security personnel under the rubble.

stories.title: How hotels are stopping the 'dawn dash' for sunbeds after man wins payout
stories.summary: Some hotel resorts have introduced sunbed allocation rules enforced from check-in to prevent guests from reserving loungers with towels. The policy changes follow a case in which a guest received a payout over the practice.

stories.title: Gaza volunteers plant olive trees at devastated al-Shifa Hospital
stories.summary: Volunteers at al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza cleared rubble and planted olive trees in the facility's courtyard as a symbol of hope. The hospital had sustained severe devastation during the conflict.

stories.title: Medics among 51 killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon in past 24 hours
stories.summary: Israeli attacks on Lebanon over the past 24 hours killed at least 51 people, including medics. Since a ceasefire began on April 16, a total of 552 people have been killed in southern Lebanon amid intensifying Israeli military operations.

stories.title: Berlin renames state parliament plaza after German Holocaust survivor Margot Friedlander
stories.summary: Berlin renamed the plaza in front of its state parliament after Margot Friedlander, a German Holocaust survivor. Mayor Wegner said the square represents human dignity, Jewish life, and democratic values.

stories.title: Lebanon says two paramedics killed by Israeli strikes in south
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed two paramedics in southern Lebanon on Sunday, according to Lebanese authorities, despite a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah that has been in place since April.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims multiple attacks on Israeli forces in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced multiple attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, including strikes using aerial-dropped explosives on equipment in al-Bayyada and targeting Israeli soldiers near Deir Seryan and the Jal al-Alam site.

stories.title: Current repairs on all public roads in Ukraine to be completed by June 1 – PM Svyrydenko
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko announced that current repairs on all public roads across Ukraine are to be completed by June 1.

stories.title: UK's Starmer says his government is a ten-year project despite calls to quit
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue in office, describing his government as a 'ten-year project' despite calls for his resignation following his Labour Party's significant losses in local elections earlier in the week.

stories.title: Culture Minister Miki Zohar claims Hamas plotted Oct. 7 attacks during Bennett-Lapid gov't
stories.summary: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar claimed Hamas planned the October 7, 2023, attacks during the Bennett-Lapid government, though Netanyahu's coalition was already in power when the attacks took place.

stories.title: Iran sends response to latest US peace proposal as Netanyahu insists war ‘not over’
stories.summary: Iran submitted its response to the latest U.S. peace proposal, with state media emphasizing ending the war and maritime security without mentioning nuclear talks. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told "60 Minutes" the conflict will continue until uranium is removed from Iran.

stories.title: Russian attacks leave four civilians injured in Kherson region
stories.summary: Four civilians were injured during Russian attacks on the Kherson region in southern Ukraine over the course of one day.

stories.title: Hungary’s new PM apologises to those wronged under Orbán in first speech
stories.summary: Péter Magyar was sworn in as Hungary's new prime minister on Saturday, succeeding Viktor Orbán. In his first speech, Magyar apologised to citizens who had been targeted or maligned by the state during Orbán's tenure and the rule of his Fidesz party.

stories.title: Explosion at coal mine in Colombia, at least four trapped
stories.summary: An explosion occurred at the Las Quintas coal mine in Cucunuba municipality, Cundinamarca department, Colombia, on Saturday afternoon. At least four miners were trapped, according to Governor Jorge Emilio Rey.

stories.title: Iraqi media shocked by reports of secret Israeli base as Baghdad hits critical juncture - analysis
stories.summary: Reports of a secret Israeli military base operating in Iraq's desert have generated shock in Iraqi media and political circles. The alleged outpost reportedly supported Israeli operations against Iran, raising serious questions about Iraqi sovereignty.

stories.title: Macron says France 'never considered' Hormuz deployment, backs Iran coordination
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron, speaking in Nairobi, stated that France has "never considered" deploying warships to the Strait of Hormuz and instead supports a maritime security effort coordinated with Iran amid rising tensions in the waterway.

stories.title: Ukraine reports multiple casualties despite Trump-backed truce with Russia
stories.summary: Russian attacks wounded at least nine people in eastern Ukraine on Sunday, the second day of a Trump-backed three-day truce. President Zelensky said Russia continued front-line assault operations and was not complying with the ceasefire.

stories.title: Ministers back bills giving government ‘sole discretion’ over senior appointments
stories.summary: Israel's Ministerial Committee for Legislation backed bills granting the government "sole discretion" over senior appointments. The committee postponed decisions on proposals to cancel the Oslo Accords and bar immigration and citizenship for non-Orthodox converts.

stories.title: Iran army says countries siding with US to ‘face difficulties’ in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's army warned that countries siding with the United States would face difficulties in the Strait of Hormuz, where Tehran has permitted only a trickle of ships to pass through the vital waterway.

stories.title: Trump-Netanyahu bond fraying as Iran conflict continues without resolution - report
stories.summary: Relations between US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are reportedly fraying over the unresolved Iran conflict. Former Israeli diplomat Alon Pinkas was cited calling Netanyahu a "conman" who invoked Venezuela as a model for action in Iran.

stories.title: US transportation safety agency mulling investigation into fatal Frontier incident
stories.summary: The US National Transportation Safety Board is gathering information about a fatal incident at Denver International Airport in which a Frontier Airlines aircraft struck and killed a person on the runway during takeoff on Friday night. The flight had been bound for Los Angeles.

stories.title: Israel orders evacuation of villages in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military ordered residents of several southern Lebanese villages, including Deir al-Zahrani, Jarjouh, and Sajd, to evacuate and move at least 1,000 metres from their homes.

stories.title: Iran’s two navies and the fate of its “Midget Submarines”
stories.summary: Bryan Clark of the Hudson Institute's Centre for Defence Concepts and Technology examines the structure of Iran's two naval forces and the operational status of its fleet of midget submarines.

stories.title: One killed as Somali forces break up protest: opposition
stories.summary: One person was killed in Mogadishu after Somali security forces opened fire to disperse an anti-government protest, according to opposition figures and witnesses.

stories.title: Russia says Ukraine violates ceasefire by launching drones and artillery attacks, Ifax reports
stories.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry accused Ukraine of violating the ceasefire by launching drone and artillery strikes against Russian troops, according to Interfax news agency on Sunday.

stories.title: Facing ‘epidemic of hate,’ UK Jews hold Downing Street rally decrying antisemitism
stories.summary: An estimated 20,000 Jewish community members rallied near Downing Street in London on Sunday to protest rising antisemitism in the United Kingdom. Speakers warned that attacks on Jews threaten the country's democratic values.

stories.title: There are 'vast opportunities for investment' in Pakistan, Naqvi tells Bangladeshi state minister
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Bangladeshi Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam in Dhaka, highlighting investment opportunities and agreeing to increase bilateral trade cooperation. The two officials discussed regional dynamics and Pakistan's conciliatory role.

stories.title: Ukraine Reports Multiple Casualties on Second Day of Russia Truce
stories.summary: Ukraine reported multiple casualties on the second day of a Russian-declared truce. Ukrainian air force data indicated a decrease in long-range Russian drone strikes compared to pre-truce levels, but officials confirmed continued attacks causing injuries and deaths.

stories.title: The Tories are still on life support – so why is Badenoch in celebratory mood?
stories.summary: UK Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch claimed positive momentum despite the party losing roughly 500 council seats in England's local elections and ceding control of three councils to Nigel Farage's Reform UK across England, Wales, and Scotland.

stories.title: Israel reportedly operates covert base in Iraq during Iran campaign
stories.summary: A covert Israeli outpost allegedly operated in the Iraqi desert to support airstrikes against Iran. The base reportedly remained hidden until an Iraqi military patrol came close to discovering it.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers say orders were to kill any man encountered in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers disclosed that they received orders to kill any male encountered in Gaza during operations beginning in 2023. One soldier described instructions to shoot men of any age immediately and to use personal judgment regarding women and children.

stories.title: Qatar condemns drone attack on cargo ship in Gulf
stories.summary: Qatar condemned a drone attack on a cargo ship in the Gulf. Iran allowed a Qatari gas tanker to pass through the Strait of Hormuz for the first time since the US and Israel launched their war against Iran in February.

stories.title: Iran may ‘give assurances on the use of nuclear facilities’
stories.summary: Iran has signaled willingness to negotiate over its nuclear facilities but insists it will not destroy its enriched uranium stockpile or permit it to be transferred out of the country.

stories.title: British paratroopers land on Tristan da Cunha for suspected hantavirus case
stories.summary: British Army paratroopers landed on Tristan da Cunha's rocky terrain to deliver oxygen and medical personnel after the UK Health Security Agency confirmed a British national from the cruise ship MV Hondius was suspected of having hantavirus on the remote South Atlantic island.

stories.title: Central Elections Committee taps acting director-general following shock resignation
stories.summary: Israel's Central Elections Committee appointed Dean Livne, a recently retired legal adviser, as acting director-general following the unexpected resignation of Orly Adas. CEC chairman Noam Sohlberg said Livne will serve through the upcoming election.

stories.title: Trump says US will not allow Iran to reach enriched uranium
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Washington has Iran's nuclear material under surveillance and threatened to "blow up" anyone who approaches the sites, underscoring the U.S. refusal to allow Iran to retain enriched uranium.

stories.title: Lebanese Red Cross retrieves bodies after days of blocked access by Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese Red Cross teams recovered several bodies in southern Lebanon after being denied access to affected areas for more than nine days. Among the recovered remains were those of a Syrian family killed in an Israeli strike on the Mefdoun–Zawtar–Wadi Kfardjal road in Nabatieh.

stories.title: Over 1,200 remote inspections of destroyed housing conducted in Kherson region
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Kherson region, over 1,200 remote inspections of destroyed housing have been carried out using drones and satellite imagery in areas where physical access is impossible due to ongoing hostilities.

stories.title: British paratroopers drop onto Tristan da Cunha to treat suspected hantavirus case
stories.summary: British paratroopers parachuted onto Tristan da Cunha, the UK's most remote overseas territory in the South Atlantic, on Saturday to deliver medical aid and oxygen for a British national suspected of contracting hantavirus. The island has 221 residents and no airstrip.

stories.title: Spanish passengers start disembarkation from ship hit by hantavirus
stories.summary: Spain began disembarking Spanish passengers from a hantavirus-affected cruise ship anchored near Tenerife on Sunday. Passengers showing no symptoms were transported in small groups to shore and flown to Madrid on a military plane for quarantine at a hospital.

stories.title: Syria: Court charges Bashar Assad's cousin Atef Najib with war crimes amid 2011 uprising
stories.summary: A Syrian court charged Atef Najib, a cousin of former President Bashar Assad, with acts amounting to war crimes for allegedly orchestrating the violent crackdown on 2011 protests that escalated into a decade-long civil war.

stories.title: Levin-backed appointments bill advances despite warning from A-G it would politicize civil service
stories.summary: An Israeli bill backed by Justice Minister Levin that would give ministers and the government broader control over senior civil service appointments advanced in the Knesset. The Attorney General warned the legislation would politicize the civil service. The bill covers a wide range of posts requiring government approval.

stories.title: Fearing return to war, Iran conservationists shore up damaged heritage sites
stories.summary: Conservationists in Iran are working to repair historic sites damaged during the war with the United States and Israel, though experts warn some restorations could take years. Golestan Palace in central Tehran, a UNESCO-listed former royal residence, sustained significant damage from strike shockwaves.

stories.title: Non-binary Indian migrant elected member of Scottish Parliament
stories.summary: Manivannan, a non-binary Tamil immigrant running for the Scottish Greens, has been elected as a member of the Scottish Parliament. They campaigned on a platform of advocacy for working-class and marginalised communities at Holyrood.

stories.title: French evacuee from hantavirus-hit ship shows ‘symptoms’, PM says
stories.summary: One of five French nationals repatriated from a hantavirus-stricken cruise ship developed symptoms during the flight to France, Prime Minister Lecornu announced. All five passengers were placed in strict isolation and are receiving medical treatment.

stories.title: War update: 60 clashes on front lines since midnight, Pokrovsk axis hottest
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 60 combat engagements along the front line since midnight, with the Pokrovsk axis in the Donetsk region experiencing the heaviest fighting.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 3, testing fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed at least three people, including the head of the criminal police force in Khan Younis. The attacks tested the fragile ceasefire in the territory.

stories.title: Iran warns of response to French and British warships in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi warned that Tehran would confront French and British warships deployed in the Strait of Hormuz. He condemned the Western naval presence as an escalation of the crisis rather than a stabilizing measure.

stories.title: Iran war ‘not over’, uranium must be removed, Israel’s Netanyahu says
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated in a CBS 60 Minutes interview on Sunday that the US-Israeli war against Iran is not over, insisting that Iran's enriched uranium stockpile must be removed and its enrichment sites dismantled before the conflict can be considered concluded.

stories.title: Inside Israel’s AI targeting system: How data from a phone becomes a death sentence
stories.summary: A report detailed how Israel's AI-powered targeting system uses phone data to identify and strike individuals in Gaza. In one described incident, Ahmad Turmus was killed by two missiles that struck his car less than 30 seconds after he drove away.

stories.title: Iraqi parliament ‘to summon defence minister’ over alleged secret Israeli base
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament is reportedly set to summon the defense minister over allegations that a covert Israeli base operated in the Iraqi desert. The base allegedly supported Israeli military operations against Iran, sparking anger among Iraqi lawmakers.

stories.title: Plaid Cymru leader plans minority Welsh government built on cooperation
stories.summary: Plaid Cymru leader Rhun ap Iorwerth announced plans to form a minority government in the Welsh Senedd, pledging cooperation with opposition parties. He said his administration would seek additional powers from the UK government over areas including policing and justice.

stories.title: Israeli politics have shifted from institutional decline to perpetual negation - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that Israeli politics have shifted from institutional decline to a state of perpetual negation, with information overload weakening institutions and elevating political figures who thrive in disorder.

stories.title: Israeli drone and airstrikes near kill at least 13 in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli drone and airstrikes in Lebanon killed at least 13 people, including four killed in three drone strikes on vehicles south of Beirut on Saturday and additional casualties in southern Lebanon, among them a man and his 12-year-old daughter.

stories.title: Food inflation hammers households in war-hit Iran
stories.summary: Iranian households are experiencing surging food prices driven by high inflation and a plummeting currency, exacerbated by a U.S.-enforced naval blockade affecting the country's economy.

stories.title: Renewables accounted for 11% of Ukraine's electricity generation in 2025 – regulator
stories.summary: Ukraine's energy regulator reported that renewable energy sources accounted for 11% of the country's total electricity generation in 2025.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Iran war 'not over' amid fragile US ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated in a CBS 60 Minutes interview that the war with Iran is "not over" despite a fragile US-brokered ceasefire. He called for the removal of Iran's highly enriched uranium and the dismantling of its enrichment facilities.

stories.title: British paratroopers lead airdrop onto Tristan da Cunha for suspected hantavirus case
stories.summary: British paratroopers conducted an airdrop onto the remote South Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha to respond to a suspected hantavirus case. The UK Ministry of Defence said it was the first time the military deployed medical personnel via parachute jump for humanitarian support.

stories.title: Abbas seen positioning son for Palestinian leadership, dismaying those seeking new blood
stories.summary: Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas is seen as positioning his son Yasser Abbas for a leadership role, following meetings between the businessman and senior PA officials. The moves have drawn criticism from those seeking new leadership within Fatah.

stories.title: Iranian businesses said resorting to mass layoffs amid wartime economic struggles
stories.summary: Iranian businesses are reportedly conducting mass layoffs amid wartime economic pressures. Business leaders warned that 3.5 million industrial jobs are at risk, while several tech firms have shut down due to internet blackouts imposed during the conflict.

stories.title: State asks High Court for more time in Arab-Israeli bodies retention petition, families oppose
stories.summary: Israel's state asked the High Court for additional time to respond to a petition demanding the release of Arab-Israeli bodies retained by authorities. The petitioning families opposed the delay, arguing the original justification for retention no longer applies.

stories.title: IDF reservists created 150 new startups during last year, innovation program reveals
stories.summary: The 18x Elite Impact innovation program revealed that IDF reservists and veterans who participated in the program created 150 startups and raised $15 million in investment over the past year.

stories.title: Liut Brigade's UAV operators destroy Russian flag installed by drone in Kostiantynivka
stories.summary: UAV operators from the Liut Assault Brigade of Ukraine's National Police destroyed a Russian flag that had been placed by drone in Kostiantynivka, Donetsk region.

stories.title: Starmer says his govt is a 10-year project despite calls to quit
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue leading the government despite mounting calls for his resignation after the Labour Party suffered significant losses in local elections. He described his government as a long-term, ten-year project.

stories.title: Large-scale security operation continues for 3rd day in North Waziristan's Shewa tehsil
stories.summary: A large-scale security operation in North Waziristan's Shewa tehsil continued for a third day, with reports of seven militants killed, including two key commanders. Multiple hideouts were destroyed, and the Alam Khel Market in Dorwazanda was reportedly almost completely demolished during the operation.

stories.title: WhatsApp co-founder gives Shaare Zedek $200m in record Israeli hospital donation
stories.summary: WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum donated $200 million to Shaare Zedek Medical Center in Jerusalem, the largest donation in Israeli hospital history. The funds will finance a new medical tower, and the hospital will be renamed Koum Shaare Zedek Medical Center.

stories.title: Israeli settlers launch 20 attacks on Palestinians in WB
stories.summary: Israeli settlers carried out at least 20 attacks against Palestinians in the West Bank over Friday and Saturday. Among the victims was a 35-year-old pregnant woman.

stories.title: Rayner warns Starmer to change direction as Streeting preparing leadership bid
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a leadership crisis after roughly 40 Labour MPs called for his resignation following poor local election results. Allies of Health Secretary Wes Streeting indicated he is prepared to launch a leadership bid, while Deputy Leader Angela Rayner warned Starmer to change direction.

stories.title: Iran ceasefire tested as cargo ship catches fire after being hit off Qatar's coast
stories.summary: A cargo ship was struck and caught fire off Qatar's coast, testing the Iran ceasefire as Washington awaits Tehran's response to a proposal aimed at ending the war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and rolling back Iran's nuclear program.

stories.title: Ukraine reports battlefield clashes, drone strikes despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials reported Russian drone strikes and nearly 150 battlefield clashes over a 24-hour period on Sunday despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire between Kyiv and Moscow.

stories.title: Russia kills three Ukrainians in 24 hours, accuses Kyiv of violating truce
stories.summary: Russia reported killing three Ukrainian civilians within 24 hours while accusing Kyiv of committing more than 1,000 violations since a three-day truce took effect on Saturday.

stories.title: Putin hints at ending Russia’s war in Ukraine, but why now?
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signaled openness to peace talks on the war in Ukraine amid a US-backed ceasefire, though broader negotiations between the parties remain stalled.

stories.title: China, US confirm Seoul trade talks days before Trump-Xi summit in Beijing
stories.summary: Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng will meet US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in Seoul on May 12–13 for trade talks ahead of a Trump-Xi summit in Beijing on May 14–15. Both sides confirmed the negotiations as a final round before the presidential meeting.

stories.title: UAE intercepts two drones from Iran, Qatari PM warns Iran against using Hormuz as 'pressure tool'
stories.summary: The UAE intercepted two Iranian drones after four weeks of relative calm following a US-announced ceasefire in the Iran war. Qatari Prime Minister Al Thani warned Iran against using the Strait of Hormuz as a pressure tool.

stories.title: Russian drone attack in Kherson injures city council employee
stories.summary: Russian forces targeted a city council employee's vehicle with a drone strike in the Korabelnyi district of Kherson. The employee was injured in the attack.

stories.title: Iran responds to US peace proposal as drones hit Gulf
stories.summary: Iran sent its response to the latest US peace proposal, emphasizing the need to end wars "on all fronts." Separately, drones threatened several targets in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill three, medics say, testing fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip killed three people, including one person in the Maghazi refugee camp and the head of the criminal police force in Khan Younis, Wessam Abdel-Hadi, along with his aide, according to medics and Hamas's Interior Ministry. The strikes tested a fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Iran submitted response to US ceasefire proposal to Pakistani mediators, state media says
stories.summary: Iranian state media confirmed that Tehran submitted its response to a U.S. ceasefire proposal via Pakistani mediators. The negotiations are reportedly focused on ending the war in the region.

stories.title: Iran sends response to US ceasefire proposal via Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran transmitted its response to a US ceasefire proposal through Pakistan, with Tehran emphasizing that negotiations should prioritize ending hostilities and securing guarantees against future attacks.

stories.title: IDF chief pushes Knesset to help draft ultra-Orthodox as manpower concerns grow
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir urged the Knesset to help draft ultra-Orthodox men into the military amid growing manpower concerns. In March, Zamir warned at a cabinet meeting that the IDF faced a severe manpower shortage and risked collapse without action.

stories.title: Zamir warns Knesset that military urgently needs more soldiers amid multifront war
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir urged the Knesset to pass legislation enabling the enlistment of military-age ultra-Orthodox men and extending mandatory service from 30 to 36 months. He cited urgent personnel shortages as Israel conducts operations on multiple fronts.

stories.title: Europe weighs Putin’s ceasefire signals and security proposals
stories.summary: European officials are responding with deep skepticism to Russian President Vladimir Putin's latest signals about potential ceasefire talks regarding Ukraine. Discussions continue over NATO expansion and European security architecture, but repeated promises of imminent peace are fueling doubt about the substance of Russia's proposals.

stories.title: RSF urges Niger to ditch 'abusive' French media ban
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders urged Niger's military government to lift its suspension of nine French media outlets, calling the ban "abusive." The media crackdown comes amid broader instability in the Sahel region, including neighboring Mali.

stories.title: Russian forces attempt to amass troops in ruins on Oleksandrivka front
stories.summary: On the Oleksandrivka front, Russian forces are attempting to concentrate troops in the ruins of destroyed buildings and shelters. Ukrainian forces are monitoring the enemy's efforts to amass manpower in the area.

stories.title: Mother of hostage killed by IDF gunfire says troops were told to open fire on sight
stories.summary: Iris Haim, the mother of an Israeli hostage killed by IDF gunfire in Gaza in December 2023, said soldiers involved told her they were operating under broad "shoot to kill" orders. Three Israeli hostages died in the incident.

stories.title: PTCL users may face internet disruption during evening hours from May 11-18
stories.summary: Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) announced that internet users may experience service disruptions during evening hours between May 11 and 18 due to planned maintenance on one of its submarine cables by an international cable consortium.

stories.title: Thousands attend rally against antisemitism outside Downing Street
stories.summary: Thousands gathered outside Downing Street in London on Sunday for the "Standing Strong: Extinguish Antisemitism" rally, organized by over 30 Jewish groups. Conservative and Reform UK leaders addressed the crowd, while Labour's Pat McFadden was met with boos. The protest was prompted by a rise in antisemitic hate crimes.

stories.title: Doctors warned Andrea could die without safe housing, then discharged her to sleep on the streets
stories.summary: Andrea Woodley, a First Nations woman in Perth, Western Australia, has been hospitalized repeatedly with septicemia caused by infected blisters from sleeping rough. Despite being on the priority public housing list since 2023 and doctors warning she could die without safe housing, she faces an estimated two-year wait.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine trade blame over ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine accused each other of violating a three-day ceasefire announced by U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday. Ukrainian officials reported that Russian attacks wounded at least nine people on Sunday, the truce's second day. The ceasefire was meant to halt all kinetic warfare and include a mutual exchange of 1,000 prisoners each.

stories.title: If Europe wants to help with Iran, it can target its proxies - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Europe has an opportunity to assist in countering Iran by targeting its proxy network, rather than engaging Tehran directly.

stories.title: ‘Unidentified aircraft’ hit Korean cargo ship in Hormuz on Monday: Seoul
stories.summary: South Korea's foreign ministry said a Korean cargo ship, the HMM Namu, was struck by "unidentified aircraft" in the Strait of Hormuz six days ago. US President Trump claimed Iran was responsible and urged South Korea to join US operations to restore shipping through the waterway.

stories.title: Pakistan, Qatar reaffirm shared commitment to support 'constructive dialogue across region'
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Qatari counterpart Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani spoke by phone on Sunday, reaffirming their shared commitment to promoting peace, stability, and constructive dialogue in the Middle East amid the evolving regional situation.

stories.title: Bill seeking to overturn Oslo Accords to be reviewed in Knesset
stories.summary: A bill seeking to overturn the Oslo Accords is set for review in the Israeli Knesset. The Oslo Accords serve as the foundation for the two-state solution and have been central to peace efforts aimed at ending Israel's occupation of the West Bank.

stories.title: Iran says it has replied to US proposal as reported drone strikes strain ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran announced it has responded to a U.S. peace proposal, with the reply passed to Pakistani mediators. The development came as a month-old ceasefire showed signs of unraveling, with drone strikes or incursions reported in the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, and Iraq.

stories.title: Sudan army retakes area on Ethiopia border after RSF clashes
stories.summary: The Sudanese army recaptured an area near the Ethiopian border following clashes with the Rapid Support Forces. An RSF-led opposition coalition reported that more than a dozen people were killed in an army drone strike in South Kordofan.

stories.title: Estonia tells Ukraine to control its own drones
stories.summary: Estonian ministers Pevkur and Tsahkna told ERR that Estonia expects Ukraine to improve control of its drones after months of breaches into Baltic airspace.

stories.title: Dress made from 500 loaves stuns African film awards
stories.summary: A dress made from approximately 500 loaves of bread drew attention at a major African film awards ceremony. The event showcased work by filmmakers, celebrities, and creators from across the continent.

stories.title: Iran sends response to US proposals to end war
stories.summary: Iran has transmitted its response to U.S. proposals aimed at ending the ongoing war, though neither the content of the response nor the details of the American proposals have been publicly disclosed.

stories.title: High Court judges challenge comptroller’s authority, competence to probe Oct. 7
stories.summary: Israel's High Court judges questioned the state comptroller's authority and competence to investigate the October 7 invasion. Bereaved parents at the hearing accused the judges of bearing responsibility for the attack. The comptroller argued the probe is essential for institutional independence.

stories.title: CDF Munir warns Pakistan's response to any future ‘misadventure’ will be ‘extremely widespread, painful’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, speaking at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, warned that any future military action against Pakistan would provoke an "extremely far-reaching and painful" response. The remarks came at a ceremony marking one year since Pakistan's conflict with India in 2025.

stories.title: Small grocers’ neighbourhood links can help them beat price war, experts say
stories.summary: Hong Kong's small grocery stores face intensified price competition as major chains ParknShop and Wellcome launched aggressive discounts ahead of Mother's Day. Economists suggest smaller grocers can leverage their neighbourhood connections to remain competitive, while a lawmaker noted online shopping platforms also limit large chains' ability to monopolize the market.

stories.title: UAE, Kuwait and Qatar all report drone attacks as Iran ramps up its threats
stories.summary: The UAE, Kuwait, and Qatar each reported drone attacks amid escalating Iranian threats. Abu Dhabi directly blamed Tehran, while Doha and Kuwait City did not name the attackers. South Korea also reported that one of its ships was struck by an unidentified aircraft in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: All passengers on hantavirus-hit ship considered high-risk contacts, EU health agency says
stories.summary: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control classified all passengers aboard a cruise ship affected by a hantavirus outbreak as high-risk contacts. The ship was expected to anchor off Tenerife, Spain. Asymptomatic passengers were to be repatriated via specially arranged transport for self-quarantine in their home countries.

stories.title: Russia becomes market of forced substitutes for foreign companies, FISU says
stories.summary: Due to international sanctions and geopolitical isolation, Russia has become a market dominated by forced substitutes, parallel imports, and rising prices, according to a report by FISU.

stories.title: 321 foreigners arrested in Indonesia online gambling crackdown
stories.summary: Indonesian police arrested 321 foreign nationals, mostly Vietnamese, in a raid on an alleged online gambling operation in a commercial building near Jakarta's Chinatown. Investigators described the site as a hub for more than 70 online gambling websites targeting players outside Indonesia.

stories.title: Berlin sceptical as Putin proposes Germany's ex-chancellor Schroeder as Ukraine mediator
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder as a mediator in the Ukraine war, citing their longstanding relationship. Berlin reacted with scepticism, noting Schroeder's continued closeness to the Kremlin since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Could military AI use be on the agenda when Chinese and US leaders meet?
stories.summary: A potential discussion on military AI use is being examined ahead of US President Donald Trump's planned visit to China. The visit comes amid the US-Iran war, which is disrupting global energy supplies and adding strain to Washington-Beijing relations. Both countries face growing calls to address the safe military application of artificial intelligence.

stories.title: 15 police personnel martyred in Bannu suicide attack
stories.summary: At least 15 police officers were killed when militants detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at the Fateh Khel police post in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Of the 18 officers stationed at the post, three survived with injuries. Attackers followed the blast with heavy gunfire from multiple directions.

stories.title: Eisenkot says Bennett-Lapid uniting without him is ‘not how you build partnerships’
stories.summary: Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot criticized the merger between Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid for excluding him, saying it is not how partnerships are built. Eisenkot told Yashar party activists he had wanted to join, consolidating Zionist opposition into three slates representing left, right, and center.

stories.title: Support Israel’s families and businesses in crisis now - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored campaign is soliciting donations to provide emergency loans and financial guidance to Israeli families and small businesses affected by the ongoing crisis.

stories.title: Football on ruins: Gaza’s orphans find refuge on the pitch
stories.summary: In Gaza, a teenager orphaned by an Israeli attack has found solace playing football, even as the conflict has devastated Palestinian sports infrastructure across the territory.

stories.title: Stories of those killed in a single day of Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least 39 people in a single day of attacks across Lebanon, despite an existing ceasefire agreement being in place.

stories.title: NYT: Lost Starlink, throttled Telegram, missed recruits — Russia’s worst battlefield year since 2023
stories.summary: According to the New York Times, Russia's military advance in Ukraine has slowed significantly, marking its worst battlefield performance since 2023. Factors include lost Starlink access, throttled Telegram communications, and recruitment shortfalls.

stories.title: Iran at the World Cup a 'major diplomatic asset': football chief
stories.summary: The head of Iran's football federation said the country's participation in the World Cup is a major diplomatic asset and that withdrawing would be a loss. He reiterated that Iran's participation remains conditional.

stories.title: Two arrested over arson attack at former synagogue in east London
stories.summary: Counter-terrorism officers in London arrested a 45-year-old man and a 52-year-old woman on suspicion of conspiracy to commit arson following an attack at a former synagogue in Whitechapel, east London. Both suspects were taken into police custody on Sunday.

stories.title: LNG tanker from Qatar passes through Strait of Hormuz for first time since war started — Bloomberg
stories.summary: An LNG tanker from Qatar passed through the Strait of Hormuz for the first time since the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: This is the sentence that protects every abuser in Pakistan
stories.summary: The article examines how deeply ingrained social stigma in Pakistan discourages women from reporting domestic violence to police. It highlights the cultural phrase "good girls don't go to police stations" as a barrier that enables abusers to avoid accountability.

stories.title: Israel deports two foreign activists seized from Gaza flotilla
stories.summary: Israel deported Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila, two activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla intercepted by the Israeli navy in international waters off Greece on April 30. The remaining activists aboard the flotilla were taken to Crete and released.

stories.title: Iran sends response to US proposal via Pakistan, states agency says
stories.summary: Iran transmitted its response to the latest US proposal through Pakistan, according to the official Islamic Republic News Agency. The agency reported that negotiations at this stage would focus on ending the war.

stories.title: Ex-Knesset speaker: Israel failed in Gaza, Lebanon, Iran wars
stories.summary: Former Knesset speaker Abraham Burg stated that Israel failed in its wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and against Iran. He warned that continued military campaigns risk broader disaster for the region.

stories.title: Israeli envoy takes rare swipe at US Jewish groups for cosponsoring Spanish exhibit
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter criticized U.S. Jewish organizations for cosponsoring a Spanish embassy exhibit on Jewish life in Moorish Spain, arguing it risks legitimizing a government that vilifies Israel. The World Jewish Congress responded that disengagement is not the answer.

stories.title: Pistorius is flying to Washington for Tomahawks, despite worsening relations between Merz and Trump — Financial Times
stories.summary: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius is traveling to Washington to pursue the purchase of U.S. Tomahawk cruise missiles and Typhon launchers, despite strained relations between Chancellor Merz and President Trump over the Iran war, according to the Financial Times.

stories.title: 'Historic, unprecedented': IDF, US ran covert rescue operations from Iraq during Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli and US forces conducted covert rescue operations from Iraq during the war with Iran. IDF special forces rescue units had been clandestinely positioned in Iraq to recover any Israeli pilots who might be shot down and crash-land in the country.

stories.title: A Quieter Victory Day in St. Petersburg Hints at the Strains of Russia’s Long War
stories.summary: Victory Day celebrations in St. Petersburg were scaled down compared to previous years, with a smaller military parade, though thousands of residents still participated in the Immortal Regiment march, reflecting the strains of Russia's prolonged war.

stories.title: New government speaks less about supporting Ukraine, but support continues, says Czech ambassador
stories.summary: The Czech ambassador stated that while the new Czech government speaks less publicly about supporting Ukraine, practical support for Kyiv continues.

stories.title: ‘Ukraine has momentum in war with Russia’
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials and analysts assert that Ukraine currently holds momentum in its ongoing war against Russia, though specific details on recent battlefield developments were not provided.

stories.title: UKMTO says bulk carrier hit by unknown projectile near Qatar
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a bulk carrier was struck by an unknown projectile while sailing 23 nautical miles northeast of Doha, Qatar. The incident was reported on May 10.

stories.title: Hong Kong man dies after chasing thief and falling off industrial building
stories.summary: A man died in Hong Kong after chasing a suspected cable thief and falling from the Kimball Industrial Building in Kwun Tong. Police received the report around 5:15 p.m. on Sunday. The victim, who worked in the building, landed on air-conditioning pipes on the third-floor facade and was later certified dead.

stories.title: Qatari ship struck, ISIS claims responsibility for Shi'ite cleric assasination
stories.summary: A Qatari-flagged ship was struck in an attack, and ISIS claimed responsibility for the assassination of a Shi'ite cleric. Details were provided in a Jerusalem Post news roundup.

stories.title: Qatar’s foreign ministry urges freedom of navigation in call with Iranian counterpart
stories.summary: Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani spoke by phone with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi about mediation efforts to end the war. Al Thani warned that using the Strait of Hormuz as a pressure tool would deepen the crisis and increase regional risks.

stories.title: France turns to Africa for strategic partnerships
stories.summary: France is seeking to rebuild its strategic partnerships in Africa following its withdrawal from the Sahel region. The first Africa Forward Summit in Kenya is intended to mark a fresh start for French engagement on the continent.

stories.title: Africa summit in Kenya: France seeks new partners
stories.summary: France is hosting its first Africa Summit on May 11–12 in Kenya, seeking to establish new strategic partnerships on the continent following its withdrawal from the Sahel region.

stories.title: Gas supply suspended after pipeline damaged in Karachi Red Line construction
stories.summary: A high-pressure gas pipeline in Karachi was damaged during construction of the Red Line bus rapid transit project near Jail Chowrangi. The Sui Southern Gas Company reported that the 12-inch pipeline breach forced an immediate suspension of gas supply to several neighborhoods including Saddar, Garden, Lyari, and Lines Area.

stories.title: AI app to detect drunk drivers through Cantonese speech analysis in the works
stories.summary: Researchers at Hong Kong Metropolitan University are developing what they describe as the world's first AI app to detect intoxication through real-time Cantonese voice analysis. The project, funded by a HK$3.4 million grant, aims to help users assess whether they are fit to drive after drinking. It may also monitor speech abnormalities linked to medication or fatigue.

stories.title: Can Asian economies cope with the fallout from the Iran war?
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs, inflation, and growing debt pressures linked to the Iran conflict are straining economies across Asia, raising questions about the region's ability to manage the economic fallout.

stories.title: Iranian regime relying on foreign militias to bolster security efforts, suppress protests - report
stories.summary: According to reports, Iran's government has been relying on foreign militias to bolster internal security and suppress protests, though Tehran has not officially acknowledged their role.

stories.title: New opposition coalition rallies in Togo
stories.summary: A new coalition of major Togolese opposition parties and civil society groups held their first meeting to organize protests against constitutional changes they say allow President Faure Gnassingbe to further consolidate power.

stories.title: Google Finance, an AI investment tool, comes to Israel
stories.summary: Google Finance launched an AI-powered investment tool in Israel featuring customized portfolio displays and advanced market analysis capabilities.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill three in Gaza, testing fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza on Sunday, including two police force members, according to health officials. The attacks tested a fragile ceasefire in the territory.

stories.title: Slovak Prime Minister: Zelenskyy should call Putin if he wants a meeting
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico stated that Ukrainian President Zelenskyy told him during a meeting in Armenia that he is ready to meet Russian President Putin in any format. Fico suggested Zelenskyy should call the Kremlin directly. Moscow denied any message was relayed.

stories.title: AG says High Court should strike down Gofman’s appointment as next Mossad director
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General Baharav-Miara has recommended that the High Court strike down the appointment of Gofman as the next Mossad director. She argued the appointments panel process was flawed, as members did not review a dissenting opinion or documents regarding Gofman's use of a minor in a military operation.

stories.title: Syria president shuffles government officials and ministers, boots brother from key post
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa reshuffled his government, replacing the foreign, information, and agriculture ministers. He also removed his brother Maher from the key post of secretary-general of the Syrian presidency, replacing him with the former governor of Homs. No reason was given for the changes.

stories.title: Health advocates warn government’s claims of baby formula safety contradict data
stories.summary: Health advocates are challenging the Trump administration's claim that hundreds of baby formula samples meet a high safety standard. Independent scientists who reviewed the testing data said most samples were contaminated with PFAS or phthalates, raising concerns about data gaps and contradictions in the government's public statements.

stories.title: 'Nothing like COVID': Expert urges calm over hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship
stories.summary: Medical experts say a hantavirus outbreak linked to a cruise ship remains contained and should not spark fears of a COVID-style pandemic. Former Institut Pasteur chief Christian Bréchot told FRANCE 24 that human-to-human transmission of the virus is rare but emphasized the need for faster testing and stronger global outbreak response systems.

stories.title: Buoyed by rare earths, China approaches Trump summit with fresh confidence
stories.summary: Chinese officials have privately signaled growing confidence in their economic leverage ahead of US President Donald Trump's planned visit to Beijing. Sources told the South China Morning Post that Beijing has grown bolder since deploying rare-earth export restrictions in October and is now less concerned about US tariffs.

stories.title: Zelensky and Stubb coordinated their positions ahead of weekly meetings
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Finnish President Alexander Stubb coordinated their positions ahead of a series of meetings and negotiations scheduled for the week.

stories.title: Hong Kong police arrest 2 drivers over alleged truck racing viral video
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested two drivers on suspicion of dangerous driving after dashcam footage showing two trucks allegedly racing and cutting lanes inside a tunnel went viral on social media. The footage was recorded on a Friday evening at around 5:20 p.m.

stories.title: Germany revives effort to buy US Tomahawks, FT reports
stories.summary: Germany is reviving efforts to purchase Tomahawk cruise missiles from the United States, according to a Financial Times report citing sources familiar with Berlin's defense strategy.

stories.title: Macron heads to Kenya to push new France-Africa partnership
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is visiting Kenya to host the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi on Monday and Tuesday. The event will convene heads of state, business executives, and cultural figures as France seeks to promote a partnership-based approach to strengthening ties with the African continent.

stories.title: Israel kills two paramedics in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military killed two paramedics and wounded five others in strikes targeting Islamic Health Committee positions in southern Lebanon on Sunday. The attacks hit locations in Qlaouiyeh and Majdal Selem, both in the Bint Jbeil district.

stories.title: Army parachutes onto remote island to help Briton with suspected hantavirus
stories.summary: A British Army specialist team parachuted onto Tristan da Cunha, a remote British overseas territory in the South Atlantic, to treat a resident with a suspected hantavirus infection.

stories.title: Atef Najib faces at least 10 charges in landmark Syria trial
stories.summary: Atef Najib, a cousin of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, faces at least 10 charges in a landmark trial in Syria. The charges include murder, torture, and responsibility for massacres.

stories.title: Iran sends response to US proposal to end war via mediator Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran has sent its response to a U.S. proposal to end the war through Pakistani mediators. The initial negotiations are reportedly focused on ending hostilities in the region.

stories.title: Spanish health officials board hantavirus-hit ship near Tenerife to evacuate passengers
stories.summary: Spanish health officials boarded the hantavirus-affected cruise ship MV Hondius near Tenerife to begin evacuating passengers. Spanish nationals were designated as the first group to disembark and were to be transported by bus to the local airport.

stories.title: Don’t let Farage and Reform divide us, Labour’s Sarwar urges Holyrood leaders
stories.summary: Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar urged Holyrood party leaders not to focus on Nigel Farage and Reform UK after Labour tied for second place with Reform in the Scottish Parliament elections. The SNP won a fifth consecutive Holyrood victory with 58 MSPs, while Labour recorded its worst result since devolution in 1999.

stories.title: China shouldn’t view a tired US as signifying a Europe ready to pivot
stories.summary: A U.S. decision to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany has prompted analysis of how Beijing might interpret the move. China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi has been pursuing a "partners not rivals" approach with European nations throughout 2026, but analysts caution that a fatigued U.S. posture does not necessarily mean Europe is ready to pivot toward China.

stories.title: Germany resumes efforts to purchase Tomahawk missiles from U.S. — FT
stories.summary: Germany is renewing efforts to purchase American Tomahawk long-range cruise missiles after the Pentagon abandoned plans to station a U.S. battalion equipped with those weapons on German soil, according to the Financial Times. The move aims to address a gap in European deterrence against Russia.

stories.title: Russia’s strikes across six Ukrainian oblasts on the day of the ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia launched 27 drones, fired 780 strikes on Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and attacked rescuers in Nikopol district during the declared ceasefire of May 9–10. At least one person was killed and 25 wounded across six Ukrainian oblasts.

stories.title: Israel deports two activists detained over Gaza-bound flotilla
stories.summary: Israel deported two activists who had been detained in connection with a Gaza-bound flotilla. The activists were part of the second Global Sumud Flotilla, which launched from Spain on April 12.

stories.title: The Manhattan bookstore that wouldn't host her: Lihi Lapid on what October 7 did to Israeli authors
stories.summary: Israeli author Lihi Lapid, who secured a publishing deal with HarperCollins and a planned Manhattan book launch, was unable to find a single bookstore in New York willing to host her event after May 2024, in the wake of October 7.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers say orders were to kill any man encountered in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers reportedly stated that their orders in Gaza were to shoot any male encountered, regardless of age or whether the person was armed or holding a white flag, according to testimony published by the report's authors.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire under strain as Gulf states report drone attacks
stories.summary: A drone struck a cargo ship off Qatar's coast, while Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates reported intercepting or repelling separate drone attacks, straining the US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: UAE says it intercepted two Iranian drones
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates said its air defence systems intercepted two Iranian drones on Sunday morning, with no casualties reported. Kuwait's defence ministry also reported detecting hostile drones in its airspace the same day. The UAE military stated it has engaged over 2,265 UAVs, 29 cruise missiles, and 551 ballistic missiles since the start of the war with Iran.

stories.title: Africa: Beyond Xenophobia - Africa Needs a Sustainable Migration Strategy
stories.summary: An editorial argues that Africa needs a comprehensive and sustainable migration strategy rather than reactive measures. It cites recent xenophobic attacks in South Africa as evidence that violence against foreign nationals driven by migration tensions is worsening across the continent.

stories.title: Lebanon arrests man posing as high-level Iraqi security official
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities arrested a man who had been impersonating a high-level Iraqi security official. Commentators compared the case to the infamous Abu Omar, who posed as a Saudi prince to gain access to Lebanon's political and business elite.

stories.title: Fifa World Cup matches face heightened terror risk in US amid Iran conflict
stories.summary: Security experts warn that the 2026 FIFA World Cup matches across 11 U.S. cities face heightened terrorism risks due to the ongoing U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran and a reduction in federal counter-terrorism expertise. Homegrown violent extremists and lone actors radicalised online are identified as the primary threat to the 78 scheduled matches.

stories.title: Underwater anti-mine technology and robot dogs take centre stage at Chinese defence show
stories.summary: China showcased advanced military technology at the 2026 Chengdu Defence Technology Industry Expo in mid-April, including AI-enabled autonomous underwater vehicles designed to neutralise mines and robot dogs. The underwater vehicles can be launched from submarine torpedo tubes and are intended for deep-ocean surveys and seabed operations.

stories.title: Remembering Shulamit Newman, a true Jerusalem icon of warmth and faith
stories.summary: Shulamit Newman, described as a fixture of Jerusalem community life, has been remembered for her contributions through Torah teaching, acts of kindness, and dedication to faith.

stories.title: How the smear campaign targeting the Green Party and Muslim voters failed
stories.summary: The UK's Green Party faced a sustained smear campaign accusing it of engaging in 'Muslim sectarianism' ahead of local elections. Despite the attacks from rival parties and sections of the media, the Greens made significant gains in the local elections under leader Zack Polanski.

stories.title: Israel deports two activists detained on board Gaza flotilla
stories.summary: Israel detained and deported two aid flotilla activists—Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Ávila—after intercepting a Gaza-bound flotilla. Both were held in Israeli custody before being sent back to their home countries.

stories.title: The genocide is still taking Gaza’s mothers
stories.summary: The article describes the ongoing toll of the conflict in Gaza on Palestinian mothers and civilians, with the author expressing fear for their own mother's safety.

stories.title: Iran's chief of armed forces 'briefs Khamenei on readiness'
stories.summary: Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Sunday to brief him on military readiness and new measures to confront what he described as American and Israeli adversaries, according to Fars news agency.

stories.title: Alabuga Special Economic Zone, where Russia manufactures Shaheds, expands by 340 hectares
stories.summary: The Alabuga Special Economic Zone in Russia's Tatarstan region, where Shahed-type kamikaze drones are manufactured, has expanded by 340 hectares over the past year. The facility is a key production site for drones used in the conflict in Ukraine.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 36 in Lebanon in last day, despite truce
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed 36 people in Lebanon over the preceding day despite a ceasefire that has been in effect since mid-April. Clashes between Hezbollah and Israeli forces also continued.

stories.title: Passengers on hantavirus-hit cruise ship begin to disembark on Spain’s Canary Islands
stories.summary: Passengers from approximately 20 countries began disembarking a hantavirus-affected cruise ship at Spain's Canary Islands, with authorities aiming to send all passengers home by Monday. Separately, British Army medics parachuted onto a remote island to treat a resident with a suspected hantavirus case.

stories.title: Saudi Aramco says quarterly profits up as crude prices surge
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reported Sunday that its first-quarter net profit rose 25.5 percent compared to the same period last year, driven by surging crude oil prices linked to the ongoing war.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 10: Political parties form new constellations ahead of elections
stories.summary: Israeli political correspondents reported that opposition parties in Israel are undergoing mergers and defections ahead of upcoming elections. A wave of new legislation is also being introduced as the Knesset resumes its sessions.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: British military says ship caught fire after being hit off coast of Qatar
stories.summary: Iran said on May 9 it was still reviewing a U.S. proposal related to ongoing negotiations over the broader West Asia conflict. Separately, a British military report indicated a ship caught fire after being struck off the coast of Qatar.

stories.title: Iraqi ministers summoned by parliament over secret Israeli base
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament announced it would summon government ministers over allegations that Israel operated a secret military base on Iraqi territory during the war against Iran.

stories.title: How did Gaza’s sea become a wall?
stories.summary: Israel has enforced a naval blockade around the Gaza Strip for 18 years, effectively restricting maritime access and turning the sea into a barrier for Gaza's residents.

stories.title: Russian forces attack rescue car with drone in Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked a rescue vehicle with a drone in the Myrove community of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. The crew was en route to assist local residents at the time of the strike.

stories.title: EAM Jaishankar hands over India-assisted agro-processing facility in South Trinidad
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, from Paramaribo on May 8. He handed over an India-assisted agro-processing facility in South Trinidad as part of the concluding leg of a three-nation Caribbean tour including Jamaica and Suriname.

stories.title: Qatar says cargo ship hit by drone off its coast
stories.summary: Qatar's Ministry of Defence reported that a cargo vessel traveling from Abu Dhabi to Mesaieed Port was struck by a drone off Qatari waters on Sunday morning, causing a limited fire. No injuries were reported, and the fire was brought under control.

stories.title: Hong Kong Mother’s Day dining shifts from traditional banquets to casual meals
stories.summary: Mother's Day dining in Hong Kong shifted away from traditional Chinese banquet restaurants this year, with families in areas like Causeway Bay increasingly choosing casual options such as lunch, afternoon tea, and hotpot. Industry representatives reported weaker business compared to the previous year at conventional banquet venues.

stories.title: 'No comment' after Schröder named by Putin for Ukraine talks
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder as a potential mediator in Russia-Ukraine peace talks. Schröder's representatives offered no comment on the suggestion.

stories.title: El Clasico: Kylian Mbappe not in Real Madrid squad to face Barcelona
stories.summary: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé was left out of the squad for the El Clásico match against Barcelona despite having trained with teammates on Friday following his recovery from injury.

stories.title: Russians shelled settlements in Donetsk region 18 times, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian troops carried out 18 attacks on settlements in Ukraine's Donetsk region over a 24-hour period, resulting in casualties. The strikes targeted multiple locations across the region.

stories.title: Petroleum dealers, lawyers slam fuel hike
stories.summary: The Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association and the Supreme Court Bar Association criticized the government over fuel price increases. An official notification effective May 9 imposed a petroleum levy of Rs117.41 per litre on petrol and Rs42.60 per litre on high-speed diesel at retail outlets.

stories.title: Car bomb at checkpoint kills at least 15 in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: Militants detonated a car bomb at a checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan and opened fire on police, killing at least 15 people and wounding three others.

stories.title: China's free ride: How Beijing turned the Middle East war into a military laboratory - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that China is using the Iran war as a live testing ground to study Western military capabilities and architecture. The analysis suggests Beijing benefits from the conflict's exposure of Western systems without bearing direct costs.

stories.title: Saudi Aramco profits jump despite conflict in Middle East
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reported a 26% increase in first-quarter profits, reaching $33.6 billion, while revenue rose nearly 7% to $115.5 billion. The company's east-west pipeline enabled it to continue shipping millions of barrels of oil despite ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the Gulf region.

stories.title: Israeli authorities indict 16 teens over Independence Day murder of pizzeria worker
stories.summary: Israeli authorities indicted 16 teenagers in connection with the murder of a pizzeria worker on Independence Day. Additional charges filed against the suspects include obstruction of justice and witness tampering.

stories.title: How TMZ is finding its footing on the political scene, even after some misfires
stories.summary: TMZ has expanded its coverage to Washington, D.C., where it has begun tracking politicians' activities, including monitoring members of Congress during a two-week recess. The outlet has reported on lawmakers' travel and vacations, including a senator's trip to Disney World.

stories.title: Pakistani Taliban splinter group claims suicide attack, 14 police dead
stories.summary: A suicide attack on a security post in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, killed 14 police officers. A suicide bomber and gunmen detonated an explosives-laden vehicle near the post late Saturday, triggering an intense firefight. A splinter group claiming affiliation with the Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility.

stories.title: Why is Iran taking time to respond to the US proposal to end the war?
stories.summary: Iran is still reviewing a US proposal to end the war, with Tehran's nuclear programme and control of the Strait of Hormuz remaining the principal sticking points in negotiations.

stories.title: At least 15 police personnel martyred in Bannu suicide attack
stories.summary: At least 15 police officers were killed in a suicide attack on the Fateh Khel police post in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Militants rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the post and then opened fire from multiple directions. Three of the 18 officers present survived with injuries.

stories.title: Teen indicted for negligent murder in Yemanu Zelka’s killing; 15 minors charged for assault
stories.summary: A teenager was indicted for negligent murder in the killing of Yemanu Zelka, a pizzeria worker killed on Israel's Independence Day, while 15 minors were charged with assault. The victim's family criticized prosecutors for not filing murder charges against all those involved.

stories.title: Twelve Pakistani police officers killed in car bombing and shootout
stories.summary: A militant alliance called Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen claimed responsibility for an attack in Pakistan that killed twelve police officers. The assault involved a car bombing followed by a shootout at a police facility.

stories.title: Iran war
stories.summary: A brief report dated May 10, 2026, references an ongoing Iran war but provides no further details on specific operations, actors, or developments.

stories.title: Firefighting efforts continue in Chornobyl Exclusion Zone in Kyiv region
stories.summary: Firefighters are working to contain a large-scale forest fire covering 1,200 hectares in the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone in Ukraine's Kyiv region. Efforts to extinguish the blaze are ongoing.

stories.title: CDF Munir says India’s ambitions exceeded its capabilities, armed forces cannot be intimidated
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir stated at a ceremony at GHQ Rawalpindi that India's ambitions exceeded its capabilities during the 2025 conflict. He spoke on the one-year anniversary of what Pakistan calls its victory, covering the period from the April 22 Pahalgam attack through the May 10 ceasefire.

stories.title: Kuwait says 'hostile drones' detected in airspace
stories.summary: Kuwait's armed forces announced on Sunday that several hostile drones were detected in Kuwaiti airspace and were intercepted in accordance with established military procedures.

stories.title: Anxiety, anticipation as World Cup one-month countdown begins
stories.summary: Concerns about affordability, politics, and ongoing conflict are dampening the mood as a one-month countdown begins to an upcoming World Cup tournament.

stories.title: Alibaba brings chat-style shopping to Taobao and Qwen amid AI gateway push: source
stories.summary: Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba is preparing to integrate AI chatbot shopping into its Taobao and Tmall platforms, allowing users of its Qwen AI assistant to find and purchase items through natural language conversations rather than keyword searches.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes hit southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes targeted multiple locations in southern Lebanon on Sunday, including a poultry feed factory in the Tyre district, a site in Marjayoun, and a building belonging to the Islamic Health Committee in Bint Jbeil. Multiple people were reportedly wounded.

stories.title: Russian forces attack two districts in Dnipropetrovsk region with drones; child injured
stories.summary: Russian forces used drones to attack two districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring a child. The strikes targeted civilian areas in the region.

stories.title: How could Labour remove Keir Starmer? Four possible routes
stories.summary: Several Labour MPs believe leader Keir Starmer may not survive to contest the next general election, but party rules make formal removal extremely difficult. No Labour leader has been formally ejected in the postwar era, though some like Tony Blair resigned under internal pressure. MPs are debating possible routes to force a change.

stories.title: Fearing return to war, Iran conservationists shore up damaged heritage sites
stories.summary: Iranian conservationists are working to shore up heritage sites damaged during the recent conflict, fearing a possible return to hostilities. Initial estimates suggest repairs at the UNESCO-listed Golestan Palace could cost around $2.1 million.

stories.title: Three killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials reported that three people were killed by Russian strikes across Ukraine, and frontline fighting continued despite a declared two-day ceasefire between the two countries.

stories.title: Ukraine reports battlefield clashes, drone strikes despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials reported Russian drone strikes and nearly 150 battlefield clashes over a 24-hour period despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire being in effect. The incidents underscore the fragility of the truce.

stories.title: Iran military warns of ‘surprising’ methods of warfare if attacked again
stories.summary: Iran's army spokesman warned that any future attack by adversaries would be met with new and 'surprising' methods of warfare, without specifying the nature of those methods.

stories.title: Global food supply under threat by continuing Iran War
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war has disrupted global food supply chains, particularly affecting farmers entering key sowing periods who depend on urea fertilizer and imported fuel.

stories.title: Spanish, Brazilian flotilla activists released after detention in Israel
stories.summary: Israel deported Spanish-Swedish citizen Saif Abukeshek and Brazilian citizen Thiago Ávila on Sunday after detaining them near Greece for over a week. Both were members of the Global Sumud Flotilla steering committee, intercepted by the Israeli navy while attempting to break the naval blockade of Gaza.

stories.title: Benin opposition joins ruling coalition
stories.summary: Benin's opposition party, the Cowry Forces for an Emerging Benin (FCBE), joined the ruling coalition. FCBE had been the only opposition group contesting the most recent election against the outgoing majority.

stories.title: Aramco CEO says world lost 1 billion barrels of oil in two months
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said the world lost approximately one billion barrels of oil supply over the past two months. Aramco reported a 25 percent rise in first-quarter net profits. Nasser noted that energy markets would need time to stabilize even if the Strait of Hormuz reopened.

stories.title: Qatar PM meets Rubio, Witkoff amid push for Iran deal
stories.summary: Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met U.S. officials Marco Rubio and Steve Witkoff as part of ongoing mediation efforts to broker a deal between Iran and the United States. Qatar has been working to help resolve the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Likud minister claims Hamas ‘hatched’ Oct. 7 attack during Bennett-Lapid government
stories.summary: Israeli Likud minister Ofir Zohar claimed Hamas planned the October 7 attack during the Bennett-Lapid government, saying Hamas leader Sinwar acted upon perceiving weakness. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett accused the current government of evading responsibility, while opposition leader Yair Lapid said the government should be ashamed.

stories.title: Russian forces damage high-rise building and private houses in Kherson region; casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck critical and social infrastructure in Ukraine's Kherson region over a 24-hour period, damaging a high-rise building and eight private homes. Seven people were injured, including a child.

stories.title: All passengers on hantavirus-hit ship considered high-risk contacts, EU health agency says
