stories.summary: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control classified all passengers aboard a cruise ship affected by a deadly hantavirus outbreak as high-risk contacts. The ship was expected to anchor off Tenerife, Spain, on Sunday, May 11, as a precautionary measure.

stories.title: Why Trump’s war on Iran may be ‘accelerating end of US hegemony’ and damaging Stargate
stories.summary: Chinese analysts argue that President Trump's war with Iran is undermining the $500 billion Stargate AI project involving OpenAI, SoftBank, and Oracle, and accelerating the decline of U.S. global hegemony.

stories.title: Nobel laureate’s smuggled memoir details beatings and neglect in Iranian prisons
stories.summary: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi, arrested 14 times in Iran for activism, has detailed beatings, solitary confinement, constant interrogations, and systematic denial of medical care in a memoir smuggled out of prison. The writings, spanning the past decade, will be published soon. Mohammadi is reportedly in critical condition.

stories.title: Israel strikes kill several in Lebanon despite truce
stories.summary: Israel conducted multiple airstrikes across Lebanon on Saturday, killing at least nine people in the south and targeting a highway near Beirut outside Hezbollah's traditional strongholds. The strikes were among the most intense since a three-week-old ceasefire between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah began, which has failed to halt daily exchanges of fire.

stories.title: Libya’s Zawiya refinery resumes full operations
stories.summary: Libya's Zawiya refinery, located approximately 40 kilometers west of Tripoli, resumed full operations after being shut down for about two days due to fighting near the facility.

stories.title: Shenzhen nuclear power plant glitch posed no safety risk, Hong Kong authorities say
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Security Bureau confirmed that an operational event at the Ling Ao Nuclear Power Station in Shenzhen, involving the closure of a cooling water isolation valve, posed no risk to public health or the environment. The plant is located about 50 kilometers north of urban Hong Kong.

stories.title: Eight people, including two children, injured in Kharkiv region due to Russian shelling
stories.summary: Eight people, including two children, were injured in Ukraine's Kharkiv region as a result of Russian shelling over recent hours.

stories.title: Hantavirus live: French evacuee from hantavirus-hit ship showing 'symptoms'
stories.summary: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced that one of five French nationals evacuated Sunday from the cruise ship affected by a hantavirus outbreak is displaying symptoms of the illness. Lecornu said he would issue a decree authorising isolation measures to protect the public.

stories.title: Battle of Truth
stories.summary: An analysis examines the May 2025 military confrontation between India and Pakistan, which began after India launched strikes on non-military sites in Pakistan on May 7, killing 31 civilians. India attributed the strikes to retaliation for the April 22 Pahalgam tourist attack in Indian-occupied Kashmir, which it blamed on Pakistan without evidence.

stories.title: Smotrich orders uprooting of Palestinian trees in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich ordered the uprooting of 3,000 Palestinian trees in the northern West Bank. He said the removal would facilitate the construction of a new Israeli settlement.

stories.title: Smotrich unveils plan to uproot Palestinian trees in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced a plan to remove approximately 3,000 Palestinian-owned trees in the northern West Bank. Smotrich said the removal would facilitate the construction of a new Israeli settlement.

stories.title: US Secretary of State Rubio and Qatari PM discuss Iran mediation in Miami
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani in Miami to discuss mediation efforts related to the Iran conflict. The talks also addressed Pakistani-led de-escalation efforts. The U.S. State Department thanked Qatar for its role as an intermediary.

stories.title: Mer Group signs deal with West African country
stories.summary: Israel-based Mer Group signed a deal with an undisclosed West African country to provide operational technologies, professional support, and long-term guidance. The company declined to reveal further details about the agreement.

stories.title: Phillipson: challenge to Starmer would be wrong despite election ‘kicking’
stories.summary: UK Education Secretary Bridget Phillipson said Labour MPs would be wrong to challenge Keir Starmer's leadership despite the party losing around 40 councils and 1,500 seats in Thursday's local elections. She acknowledged voters felt "bitterly let down" and admitted the party erred in attempting to withdraw the winter fuel allowance.

stories.title: Momentary relief
stories.summary: The IMF approved the latest review of Pakistan's ongoing Fund programme amid growing global economic volatility and Middle East-driven energy market disruptions. The new tranche provides some balance-of-payments relief for Pakistan, whose external position remains vulnerable to imported energy shocks.

stories.title: In Sumy region, drone hits private car, injuring one person
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a private car in the Znob-Novhorod community of Ukraine's Sumy region, injuring one man.

stories.title: Iran strikes tanker off coast of Doha after Qatari ship breaks Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Iran struck a tanker off the coast of Doha after a Qatari vessel reportedly broke through Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian lawmakers said they are drafting legislation to formalize Iran's management of the strait, including banning passage by vessels of "hostile states."

stories.title: Iran sends response to US proposal via Pakistan, amid strikes
stories.summary: Iran transmitted its response to a U.S. peace proposal through Pakistani intermediaries as several Gulf states reported attempted strikes and attacks in their territorial waters.

stories.title: Iran warns of 'new weapons, methods, fronts' if attacked again
stories.summary: Iran issued a warning that it would deploy new weapons, warfare methods, and open new regional fronts if it comes under attack again. The statement followed recent military flare-ups in the region.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes kill two Palestinians in Khan Younis
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit a police vehicle in the al-Amal neighbourhood of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, killing two Palestinians and wounding several others. Those killed were identified as a local police investigations chief and his aide.

stories.title: AFC Asian Cup 2027: Japan to face defending champions Qatar in tough draw
stories.summary: The 2027 AFC Asian Cup draw placed Japan against defending champions Qatar. Saudi Arabia, which will host the tournament from January 7 to February 5, was drawn alongside Palestine, Kuwait, and Oman.

stories.title: Prospects for peace?
stories.summary: One year after the May 2025 India-Pakistan ceasefire, the two countries have failed to begin meaningful dialogue. Despite U.S. President Trump and Secretary of State Rubio announcing that both sides had agreed to talks at a neutral site, no such discussions have materialized.

stories.title: Spain starts evacuating passengers from hantavirus-hit cruise ship in Tenerife – Europe live
stories.summary: Spain began evacuating passengers from the MV Hondius cruise ship after it arrived in Tenerife, ending a voyage that departed southern Argentina on April 1. All 146 passengers remained asymptomatic. Norway dispatched an air ambulance to Tenerife at Spain's request, coordinated by the European commissioner for crisis management.

stories.title: Labour MP challenges ministers to trigger leadership contest as PM vows to fight on – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Labour MP Catherine West publicly challenged cabinet ministers to trigger a leadership contest against Prime Minister Keir Starmer, saying she would stand herself if no cabinet minister came forward by Monday. Starmer vowed to continue as leader despite mounting internal pressure.

stories.title: Two Tehrans: The parallel lives of a city
stories.summary: A report from Tehran describes the contrasting realities experienced by residents across the Iranian capital in the aftermath of the war. The piece highlights uneven hardship and divergent perceptions of life in post-war Iran.

stories.title: 2026 ‘most violent year in recent memory’ for Canada’s Jews, B’nai Brith warns
stories.summary: B'nai Brith Canada warned that 2026 is the most violent year in recent memory for Canadian Jews, with 11 violent attacks recorded so far, surpassing the total for all of 2025. The organization described the situation as a spiraling antisemitism crisis.

stories.title: Starmer vows to stay on after local elections deliver losses for Labour
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to remain in office after Labour suffered significant losses in local elections across the country. Voters shifted toward hard-right and nationalist parties, with Labour experiencing particularly severe defeats in its traditional Welsh strongholds.

stories.title: Could Spain’s ‘compliment sandwich’ approach to China work for the EU?
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez visited China and pursued closer bilateral ties while raising concerns about the trade deficit and the Ukraine war. Analysts suggested his balanced diplomatic approach could serve as a template for the European Union in managing relations with Beijing amid tensions with Washington.

stories.title: War update: 147 clashes on front lines, Russia intensifies attacks in three sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 147 combat engagements with Russian troops on May 9, with the heaviest fighting concentrated on the Pokrovsk, Huliaipole, and Kostiantynivka axes. Russia intensified offensive operations across three sectors of the front line.

stories.title: At least 15 killed in car bomb attack on northwest Pakistan checkpoint
stories.summary: Militants detonated a car bomb at a police checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan's Bannu district, killing at least 15 officers and wounding three. Gunmen then stormed the post with gunfire and small drones.

stories.title: Week in pictures: Met Gala, Russia's Victory Day parade and the far right makes gains in the UK
stories.summary: A weekly photo roundup covered several global events, including the Met Gala in New York, Russia's Victory Day military parade in Moscow that excluded heavy weapons for the first time in nearly two decades, and gains by the anti-immigration Reform UK party in local and regional elections across England.

stories.title: Two Singaporeans confirmed dead in Indonesia volcano eruption, bodies found
stories.summary: Two Singaporean nationals were confirmed dead after a volcano eruption in Indonesia, with their bodies recovered from the site. Seventeen survivors, including seven Singaporeans and ten Indonesians, were rescued.

stories.title: Russian President Putin accuses West of arming Ukraine on Victory Day
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin presided over a Victory Day military parade on Moscow's Red Square that notably excluded heavy weapons for the first time in nearly 20 years. Putin accused Western "globalist elites" of arming Ukraine to defeat Russia and declared he believes the conflict is nearing its end.

stories.title: Petrol pain doubles ride fares
stories.summary: Ride-hailing fares in Pakistan have surged dramatically as petrol prices rose to Rs415 per litre from Rs253 in February, following the U.S. and Israeli military action against Iran. Yango costs increased 64 percent and Islamabad fares rose 35 percent, pushing commuters toward carpooling and WhatsApp-organized ride-sharing groups.

stories.title: Syria sees first government reshuffle since al-Assad’s ouster: State media
stories.summary: Syria's interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa carried out the first government reshuffle since the ouster of former President Bashar al-Assad. The changes were announced by state media amid public protests over the government's performance.

stories.title: Gwadar Port gains strategic weight amid Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: Gwadar Port Authority Chairman Noorul Haq Baloch stated that rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have increased the strategic importance of Gwadar Port due to its shorter access routes to Iran and Central Asia. Speaking to the All Pakistan Shipping Association in Karachi, he highlighted tax exemptions, free storage, and modern infrastructure as investor incentives.

stories.title: Rebel fighters kill at least 69 people in northeastern DR Congo
stories.summary: Militia fighters from the CODECO armed group killed at least 69 people in Ituri province in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Security officials confirmed the attack.

stories.title: Condemnation and support after Niger bans French broadcasters
stories.summary: Niger's media regulatory authority, the National Observatory of Communication, suspended multiple French media outlets including France 24, RFI, AFP, TV5 Monde, TF1 Info, Jeune Afrique, and Mediapart, citing the need to 'preserve peace.' The move drew both condemnation and support.

stories.title: Air defense destroys all 27 Russian drones launched overnight against Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted and destroyed all 27 Russian drones launched in an overnight attack on May 10. No drones reached their intended targets.

stories.title: JNIM and Tuareg fighters join forces
stories.summary: Fighters from the al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and Tuareg armed groups have reportedly joined forces in Mali, posing a new threat to the Malian government. Russian forces operating in the country have reportedly retreated rapidly in the face of the alliance.

stories.title: Can China engineer a price recovery that doesn’t make people feel poorer?
stories.summary: China's producer price index rose 0.5 percent year on year in March, ending 41 months of decline. The development has renewed debate over whether Beijing can reverse deflationary pressures without further squeezing household purchasing power and consumer sentiment.

stories.title: 2 convicted for going to London Jewish area to film themselves verbally abusing locals
stories.summary: Adam Bedoui, 20, and Abdelkader Bousloub, 21, were convicted in London for traveling to the predominantly Jewish neighborhood of Stamford Hill to film themselves verbally abusing residents for a TikTok video. Separately, a British MP received death threats linked to his Jewish wife.

stories.title: Hiker killed by bear in ‘surprise encounter’ at Glacier National Park in US, officials say
stories.summary: A hiker was killed by a bear in a surprise encounter at Glacier National Park in the United States. Officials noted that, excluding this fatality, ten people have died in bear attacks since the park was established in 1910.

stories.title: A year ago today: Normality returns as nuclear-armed neighbours step back from the brink
stories.summary: The week of May 6–10 marks the first anniversary of the five-day military conflict between Pakistan and India, triggered by the April 22 Pahalgam attack. India launched air strikes in Punjab and Azad Kashmir on May 7; Pakistan retaliated by downing multiple Indian aircraft. A ceasefire was reached on May 10 after tit-for-tat strikes on airbases.

stories.title: Cruise ship hit by hantavirus arrives in Tenerife to evacuate passengers
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius, at the center of a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people and sickened eight others, anchored offshore in Tenerife in the early hours of Sunday. Authorities were arranging aircraft to repatriate the 146 people still aboard.

stories.title: Deadly car bomb attack hits checkpoint in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: A suspected car bombing followed by a firefight at a police checkpoint in Bannu, northwestern Pakistan, killed more than a dozen people. The attack targeted a police position in the restive region.

stories.title: Rain to hit upper Pakistan after intense heat
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast rain, dust storms, and thunderstorms across the country's upper regions from May 10 to May 12, following a three-day heat wave in northern areas. A fresh westerly weather system was expected to approach the northwestern parts of the country.

stories.title: Iran war day 72: Tehran yet to reply to US plan; Israel bombs Lebanon
stories.summary: On day 72 of the Iran war, Israel carried out strikes in Lebanon that killed at least 24 people in a single day. Tehran has not yet responded to a U.S. proposal aimed at ending the conflict.

stories.title: Russian army loses 840 troops, two air defense systems over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces lost approximately 840 troops over the past day in the war against Ukraine. Cumulative Russian combat losses from February 24, 2022, to May 10, 2026, are estimated at approximately 1,341,110 personnel, with two air defense systems also destroyed.

stories.title: IRGC navy threatens ‘heavy attack’ on US assets if its oil tankers come under fire
stories.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy threatened a "heavy attack" on U.S. assets if Iranian oil tankers are fired upon. Iran's army warned that ships from countries complying with U.S. sanctions would face difficulties in the Strait of Hormuz. A bulk carrier was reportedly struck by a projectile near Doha without injuries.

stories.title: Israel warned by EBU over ad campaign calling to support Noam Bettan at Eurovision
stories.summary: The European Broadcasting Union warned Israel's Kan broadcaster over an advertising campaign encouraging viewers to vote for Israeli contestant Noam Bettan at Eurovision. EBU director Martin Green said Kan was asked to immediately stop distributing the videos and complied.

stories.title: China’s Comac looking to upgrade C919 flying experience with more cabin luggage capacity
stories.summary: China's Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (Comac) is planning design upgrades to its C919 narrowbody jet, including larger overhead luggage compartments and improved air conditioning outlets. The changes aim to enhance passenger experience and strengthen the aircraft's competitiveness against Boeing and Airbus.

stories.title: What was Qing dynasty’s imperial yellow jacket, what it symbolised, why it mattered
stories.summary: The article discusses the historical significance of the huang magua, or imperial yellow jacket, during China's Qing dynasty (1644–1912). Yellow clothing was restricted to emperors, empresses, and empress dowagers, making the jacket a potent symbol of imperial authority.

stories.title: Twelve Pakistani police officers killed in car bombing, ambush in Bannu
stories.summary: Twelve Pakistani police officers were killed in a car bombing and subsequent ambush in Bannu, a city in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Three surviving personnel were recovered alive and transported to a hospital for treatment.

stories.title: US, Iran no closer to ending war as Qatari tanker sails towards Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran remain stalled, with no sign of Tehran responding to Washington's latest proposal. Meanwhile, a Qatari-flagged tanker was reported sailing toward the Strait of Hormuz amid continuing tensions in the region.

stories.title: Report: Iranian speedboat network poses challenge to US Navy operations
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported on Iran's "mosquito fleet," a network of fast attack boats operated by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in and around the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels are designed to pressure commercial shipping and U.S. naval forces in the vital energy corridor.

stories.title: Flotilla activists arrive in Turkiye before setting sail to Gaza
stories.summary: More than 30 vessels belonging to the Global Sumud Flotilla arrived at the port of Marmaris on Turkey's coast. The activists aboard are preparing to set sail toward Gaza as part of an aid mission.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists deported from Israel after week-long detention
stories.summary: Two activists from the Gaza-bound flotilla were deported from Israel after approximately one week in detention. The activists had reportedly been on hunger strike since being detained following the interception of their vessel.

stories.title: Analysis: No war, but no peace either
stories.summary: One year after the 90-hour Pakistan-India military confrontation of 2025, bilateral ties remain stalled. Pakistan's institutional coherence during the crisis reportedly undermined India's assumptions about dealing with a weaker neighbor. The dispute over the Indus Waters Treaty, which India has unilaterally held in abeyance, has become a central flashpoint.

stories.title: Fifteen civilians evacuated from Beryslav in Kherson region
stories.summary: Fifteen civilians were evacuated under shelling from the frontline town of Beryslav in Ukraine's Kherson region. The evacuation was conducted amid continued Russian attacks on the area.

stories.title: 'A full-time job': How a self-proclaimed Swiss king's 'empire' is riling local authorities
stories.summary: Jonas Lauwiner, who crowned himself king of Switzerland in a self-styled 2019 coronation, has exploited a loophole in Swiss law to acquire a 117,000-square-metre tract of land. Local authorities are now working to halt his expanding self-proclaimed empire.

stories.title: Flotilla activist gives defiant message after Israel deports him to Greece
stories.summary: Flotilla activist Saif Abu Keshek was deported by Israel to Greece after spending a week in Israeli custody. Abu Keshek delivered a defiant message following his release.

stories.title: The geopolitical weaponization of shipping channels
stories.summary: The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz has drawn renewed attention to the vulnerability of key global shipping routes. Experts warn that waterways such as the Taiwan Strait and the Strait of Malacca are increasingly being used as geopolitical leverage points.

stories.title: The weaponization of shipping channels
stories.summary: The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz has drawn attention to the vulnerability of other global maritime chokepoints. Experts warn that waterways such as the Taiwan Strait and the Strait of Malacca are increasingly being used as geopolitical leverage.

stories.title: Electric bike demand surges amid costly oil
stories.summary: Rising petrol prices linked to the Middle East conflict since February 28 have spurred growing demand for electric bikes in Pakistan. Millat Tractors Ltd disclosed that a group company is evaluating the feasibility of EV bike production, while Chery Master Pakistan and Pak Suzuki plan new vehicle models.

stories.title: Saudi Aramco reports soaring profits amid global energy turmoil
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reported first-quarter 2026 net profits of approximately $32.5 billion, a 25.5 percent increase year-on-year. Sales rose to $114.9 billion, aided by full utilization of its East-West Crude Oil Pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukraine presents Maul evacuation system at defense exhibition in Istanbul
stories.summary: Ukrainian company AIDronesUA presented its ground-based robotic evacuation system called Maul at a defense exhibition in Istanbul. The system, developed with the First Separate Medical Battalion, is designed to transport wounded soldiers from dangerous frontline areas without risking additional personnel.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A regional briefing noted that the fragile ceasefire between Iran and the United States continues to hold, though tensions remain elevated. Iran's Revolutionary Guard warned Washington against interfering with Iranian commercial shipping, while Israeli strikes in Lebanon continue. Diplomatic mediation efforts are intensifying.

stories.title: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa announces first cabinet reshuffle since Assad ouster - report
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa announced the first cabinet reshuffle since the ouster of former President Bashar al-Assad. No official explanation was provided for the ministerial changes.

stories.title: Mali: Hundreds rally to show support for beleaguered army leader
stories.summary: Hundreds of supporters of Mali's military junta gathered at a stadium in Bamako on Saturday to show support for the country's transitional authorities. The rally comes as the army faces growing security threats from armed groups.

stories.title: Iran keeps US waiting for a response
stories.summary: Iran questioned the seriousness of U.S. diplomatic efforts following renewed naval clashes in the Gulf while delaying a response to Washington's latest negotiating position. A CIA report reportedly claims Tehran can withstand a blockade for months. Separately, Bahrain arrested over 40 individuals alleged to be pro-IRGC, and the UK deployed a warship to the region.

stories.title: Iran’s Guards threaten US sites as Trump waits for Tehran response
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued threats against U.S. sites following American strikes on two Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman. The warning came as President Trump awaited a formal response from Tehran on ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Israel deports two Gaza aid flotilla activists
stories.summary: Israel deported two Gaza aid flotilla activists who had been seized by Israeli forces from the flotilla in late April. The pair were held in Israel before being released.

stories.title: Historian: Support for Ukraine is a matter of security for Germany, not charity
stories.summary: A historian argued that Germany's support for Ukraine is a matter of national security and European order rather than charity. While support for Ukraine remains a majority position in Germany, parts of society and the governing coalition reportedly lack full understanding of the security implications.

stories.title: Nuclear disaster can unfold any moment, experts fear
stories.summary: At a conference organized by the Pakistan Institute of International Affairs in Karachi, Sindh Governor Syed Nehal Hashmi and other experts discussed the risk of nuclear disaster. Hashmi questioned the effectiveness of international institutions and the United Nations in addressing global crises, referencing the situation in Gaza.

stories.title: Shadow APIs: how Chinese developers bypass restrictions to access Claude and Gemini
stories.summary: A grey market of API relay platforms has emerged in China, allowing developers to access restricted overseas AI models including Anthropic's Claude and Google's Gemini through proxy servers. These relay services route requests through servers outside mainland China, circumventing official access restrictions despite crackdowns by foreign AI providers.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire tested near Qatar as Trump awaits ceasefire response
stories.summary: A cargo ship was struck by an unknown projectile and caught fire off the coast of Qatar, according to the British military. The incident further tests the month-old ceasefire between the United States and Iran, which has already been strained by Iranian restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz and a U.S. blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Pakistan army chief says mediation efforts aimed at lasting peace
stories.summary: Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir said Islamabad is conducting neutral mediation efforts in the Middle East aimed at achieving lasting peace amid regional tensions involving Iran, the United States, and Israel. He pledged continued diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Prague derby abandoned after fans storm pitch with Slavia seconds from title
stories.summary: The Czech league match between Slavia Prague and Sparta Prague was abandoned after hundreds of Sparta home fans stormed the pitch during stoppage time. Slavia were leading 3-2 and seconds from clinching the league title. Fans breached security barriers carrying lit flares, and Sparta goalkeeper Surovcik announced plans for legal action.

stories.title: Live: Iran's Guards threaten US sites in the region if its tankers come under fire
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to strike U.S. military sites across the Middle East if Iranian tankers are attacked, according to Iranian media. The threat came as Washington awaited Tehran's response to its latest proposal for a peace deal.

stories.title: Dozens killed in fresh attacks in central Mali: local, security sources
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM claimed attacks in central Mali on May 8, following earlier strikes on villages on May 6 that killed at least 30 people. The combined death toll from fresh attacks left dozens dead.

stories.title: Bulk carrier struck by 'unknown projectile' near Qatari waters
stories.summary: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported that a bulk carrier was struck by an unknown projectile in the Gulf, approximately 23 nautical miles northeast of Doha, Qatar. A small fire was extinguished, and no casualties or environmental damage were reported.

stories.title: German historian: Occupation of Ukraine means genocide, not peace
stories.summary: A German historian argued that many Germans struggle to understand that a Russian occupation of Ukraine would constitute genocide rather than peace. The historian attributed this to a lack of comparable historical experience in German collective memory.

stories.title: Israel says two Gaza flotilla activists deported after weeklong detention
stories.summary: Israel deported Gaza flotilla activists Thiago Avila and Saif Abu Keshek after holding them for approximately one week. Both were released without charge. Israel had accused them of being part of a group it alleged was clandestinely controlled by Hamas.

stories.title: Downing Street rally asks ‘silent majority’ to fight antisemitism
stories.summary: A rally titled "Standing Strong: Extinguish Antisemitism" was held in central London, backed by more than 30 Jewish groups calling on the "silent majority" to oppose antisemitism. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch was expected to speak, while Prime Minister Keir Starmer was considering attending. An open letter criticized the invitation extended to Nigel Farage.

stories.title: Israeli settlers dig up Palestinian grave and force family to rebury father
stories.summary: Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank exhumed the grave of 80-year-old Palestinian Hussein Asasa near Jenin, forcing his family to rebury his body elsewhere. The settlers, reportedly accompanied by Israeli forces, claimed the cemetery land belonged to the recently re-established Sa-Nur settlement.

stories.title: Death toll from Russia's May 4 strike on Merefa rises to nine
stories.summary: The death toll from Russia's May 4 missile strike on Merefa in Ukraine's Kharkiv region has risen to nine. The strike targeted the town, causing significant casualties.

stories.title: Poll shows majority dissatisfied with Trump over Iran war
stories.summary: A Financial Times poll found that 58 percent of American voters disapprove of President Donald Trump's handling of the war involving Iran. Approximately 20 percent of Republican voters also expressed dissatisfaction with Trump's management of the conflict.

stories.title: Syria’s president changes govt officials and ministers, replaces brother
stories.summary: Syria's president carried out a government reshuffle, replacing several officials and ministers including his brother. The reasons behind the changes have not been publicly explained.

stories.title: Dozens killed in jihadist attacks in central Mali
stories.summary: Jihadist fighters launched a series of deadly attacks on villages in central Mali, killing dozens of people. A local official said the overall death toll exceeded 70 in recent days as Islamist armed groups intensified assaults across the region.

stories.title: Report outlines phased US Iran framework to end conflict
stories.summary: According to Reuters, the United States and Iran are pursuing a memorandum of understanding to end hostilities. The proposed framework involves three phases: formally ending the conflict, resolving the Strait of Hormuz crisis, and opening a 30-day period for broader negotiations.

stories.title: Bafta doubles down on preparations for Sunday TV awards after N-word fallout
stories.summary: BAFTA organizers are reinforcing preparations for their Sunday TV awards ceremony following controversy over the broadcast of a racial slur during the February ceremony. Officials said they are taking event procedures "extremely seriously."

stories.title: Pension scams: Britons warned over criminals offering inheritance tax loopholes
stories.summary: British authorities have warned the public about pension scams in which fraudsters exploit confusion over upcoming inheritance tax changes. Criminals are targeting savers by offering schemes to move pension funds overseas, claiming to provide a way to avoid new IHT rules that will apply to defined contribution pensions from April next year.

stories.title: Israel's national security should not be sold out by its citizens - editorial
stories.summary: A Jerusalem Post editorial argued that Israel's national security should not be compromised by its citizens regardless of domestic grievances. The piece stated that economic hardship and political frustration do not justify actions that endanger the country.

stories.title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards threaten US sites in Middle East if tankers come under fire
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned they would target U.S. sites in the Middle East and enemy ships if Iranian tankers or commercial vessels come under fire. The threat followed U.S. strikes on two Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman, while Washington awaited Tehran's response to its latest peace deal proposal.

stories.title: IRGC warns against interference with Iranian commercial vessels
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy warned it would target US military bases and warships in the region if Iranian oil tankers or commercial vessels are attacked. The threat came as Washington awaited Tehran's response to a proposed agreement to end the conflict.

stories.title: Dubois stops Wardley in 11th round to take WBO heavyweight boxing title
stories.summary: Daniel Dubois recovered from two knockdowns to defeat Fabio Wardley with an 11th-round stoppage, claiming the WBO World Heavyweight title as his second world heavyweight belt.

stories.title: Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla arrives off Turkish coast
stories.summary: More than 30 vessels from the Global Sumud Flotilla gathered off the Turkish coast near Marmaris as activists prepared for a maritime journey toward Gaza. Turkish coast guard and local supporters greeted the flotilla at its anchoring point.

stories.title: Cruise ship hit by hantavirus outbreak arrives in Spain's Canary Islands
stories.summary: A cruise ship experiencing a hantavirus outbreak arrived in Spain's Canary Islands, where authorities prepared a controlled evacuation of hundreds of passengers. Three people died and several others fell ill during the voyage; all passengers were classified as high-risk contacts.

stories.title: Vietnam joins rush for India’s battle-tested BrahMos missiles
stories.summary: Vietnam is in advanced negotiations with India over a potential $700 million deal to purchase BrahMos supersonic missiles. Talks progressed during Vietnamese President To Lam's visit to India, where he met Prime Minister Modi and Defence Minister Singh. At least 15 other countries have reportedly expressed interest in the system.

stories.title: Ukrainian armwrestling master of sport killed in action in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian officer Ihor Hladkyi, a Master of Sport in armwrestling, was killed while carrying out a combat mission in the Donetsk region. His death was confirmed by Ukrainian authorities.

stories.title: Israel built and defended a secret base in Iraq for Iran war, WSJ reports
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Israel established a clandestine military outpost in the Iraqi desert to support air operations against Iran. Israeli forces allegedly struck Iraqi troops who came close to discovering the base, according to U.S. officials familiar with the matter.

stories.title: Two wins, two losses: What India, Pakistan have learned a year after war
stories.summary: One year after a four-day military conflict between India and Pakistan, both nations claim strategic successes. Tensions between the two nuclear-armed neighbors continue to persist.

stories.title: Israel says it deported activists detained from Gaza-bound flotilla mission
stories.summary: Israel announced it deported two activists, Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila, who were detained following the interception of a Gaza-bound flotilla. The Israeli Foreign Ministry said the deportations followed the completion of an investigation.

stories.title: Soldiers who shot hostages had orders to shoot all men on-sight - report
stories.summary: A report revealed that Israeli soldiers who fatally shot three Israeli hostages—Yotam Haim, Samer Talalka, and Alon Shamriz—in Gaza had been given orders to shoot all men on sight. The three had been captured during Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack.

stories.title: Israelis protest against Netanyahu government and Lebanon war
stories.summary: Dozens of Israelis protested overnight in Tel Aviv against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government and continuing Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon. The demonstrations reflected growing domestic tensions over wars involving Iran and Lebanon and disputes over ultra-Orthodox military exemptions.

stories.title: UK warns against ‘foreign intimidation’ over Hong Kong-linked spying convictions
stories.summary: The UK summoned Chinese Ambassador Zheng Zeguang after two men linked to Hong Kong's London trade office were convicted of spying on activists in a British court. The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office warned it would not tolerate foreign states intimidating or harassing individuals on British soil.

stories.title: China’s criticism of Israel is no longer just perfunctory
stories.summary: An analysis notes that China's criticism of Israel has become more substantive and pointed in recent months. The report suggests that relations between Beijing and the Jewish state are unlikely to improve in the near term.

stories.title: Home Front Command chief meets with emergency service representatives in wake of Iran war
stories.summary: Israel's Home Front Command chief met with emergency service representatives to coordinate responses amid the war with Iran. He emphasized the importance of unified, real-time cooperation among emergency organizations.

stories.title: Iran conservationists shore up heritage sites damaged during war
stories.summary: Iranian authorities reported that at least 140 culturally and historically significant locations sustained damage from airstrikes and shockwaves during the war, including five UNESCO-listed World Heritage sites. Conservation efforts are underway to shore up the affected heritage sites.

stories.title: “Putin – war criminal” banner displayed on Narva Castle in Estonia
stories.summary: A banner reading "Putin – war criminal" was displayed on Narva Castle in the Estonian city of Narva on May 9, facing across the border toward Russia. The demonstration took place on a date commemorating the end of World War II in Europe.

stories.title: Pressure mounts on Angus Taylor as Pauline Hanson declares One Nation ‘here for the long haul’
stories.summary: One Nation won its first federal lower house seat in Australia's Farrer byelection, with candidate David Farley defeating independent Michelle Milthorpe. The historic result has intensified internal pressure on Coalition leader Angus Taylor just three months into his tenure. Party leader Pauline Hanson declared One Nation is "here for the long haul."

stories.title: Person dies after being hit by plane at Denver airport
stories.summary: A person was struck and killed by a Frontier Airlines plane at Denver International Airport. Details surrounding the circumstances of the incident have not been fully disclosed.

stories.title: Nationals MP Colin Boyce says he’s considering move to One Nation after ‘wake-up call’ in Farrer byelection
stories.summary: Australian Nationals MP Colin Boyce, who represents the Queensland seat of Flynn, said he is considering switching to One Nation following the Coalition's poor performance in the Farrer byelection, where its primary vote fell to about 20 percent. He described the result as a "wake-up call."

stories.title: Putin suggests Russia’s war on Ukraine ‘coming to an end’
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin suggested that Russia's war in Ukraine may be nearing its end. He also stated his willingness to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a third country if a long-term peace agreement is reached.

stories.title: Russia has lost more than 350,000 soldiers, new estimate finds
stories.summary: A new estimate indicates Russia has lost more than 350,000 soldiers since the start of the Ukraine war. The figure underscores the significant human cost President Putin has been willing to accept in pursuit of his military objectives.

stories.title: Hong Kong to seek more elderly care places in Guangdong, Chris Sun says
stories.summary: Hong Kong Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun said authorities will negotiate with care home operators in Guangdong province to secure more places for elderly Hong Kong residents. The move responds to a ninefold surge in city residents moving into such cross-border facilities in recent years.

stories.title: Tehran, Taiwan, trade … what are the hazards facing Trump on Xi summit tightrope?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is preparing to visit Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the first such presidential visit to China in nearly a decade. Key agenda items include tensions over Iran, Taiwan, and trade, with Trump seeking economic concessions amid a turbulent global backdrop.

stories.title: China’s ‘super catalyst’ turns waste water into fertiliser building block, tripling output
stories.summary: Chinese researchers have developed a catalyst that converts nitrate pollution from agricultural and industrial wastewater into ammonia with nearly three times the efficiency of conventional catalysts. The study was published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society and featured on its cover.

stories.title: Britain deploys warship amid multinational mission to secure Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced the deployment of the warship HMS Dragon to the Middle East as part of preparations for a multinational mission to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative is led by the UK and France, which recently deployed the Charles de Gaulle carrier strike group to the Red Sea.

stories.title: Residents say Israeli strikes targetted families seeking refuge in Lebanon
stories.summary: Residents and rescue workers in southern Lebanon reported civilian casualties from Israeli bombardment of residential areas, including the town of Saksakiyeh near Sidon. At least seven people were reportedly killed and 17 injured in the strikes, which hit families displaced by earlier fighting.

stories.title: Israeli lawmaker pushes bill to scrap Oslo Accords entirely
stories.summary: Far-right Israeli lawmaker Limor Son Har-Melech announced that her bill to annul the Oslo Accords would be reviewed by Israel's Ministerial Committee for Legislation. She described the proposal as a step toward preventing the establishment of a Palestinian state.

stories.title: Twelve Pakistani police officers killed in car bombing, shoot-out
stories.summary: A militant alliance called Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen claimed responsibility for a car bombing and shootout that killed twelve Pakistani police officers. The attack targeted a police post in Pakistan.

stories.title: Minister Klymenko: 15 rescuers injured in Russian strike on Poltava region still hospitalized
stories.summary: Fifteen Ukrainian rescuers injured in a repeated Russian strike on the Poltava region on May 5 remain hospitalized, with two in serious condition. Interior Minister Klymenko provided the update on their status.

stories.title: Minister Klymenko: 15 rescuers injured in Russian strike on Poltava region still hospitalized
stories.summary: Fifteen Ukrainian rescuers injured in a repeated Russian strike on the Poltava region on May 5 remain hospitalized, with two in serious condition, according to Minister Klymenko.

stories.title: Iran seeks World Cup visas for players linked to Guards
stories.summary: Iran confirmed its participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup and is seeking US visa guarantees for players and officials. Some players reportedly have links to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, adding political complexity to the request.

stories.title: British PM Starmer, weakened by local elections, is challenged by former minister
stories.summary: Former UK minister Catherine West announced she would challenge Prime Minister Keir Starmer for the Labour leadership on May 11 if no alternative plan to replace him materializes. The move follows Labour's worst governing-party performance in local elections since 1995.

stories.title: Dozens charged in global insider trading scheme after making millions in illicit profits
stories.summary: Authorities have charged dozens of individuals in an international insider trading scheme that generated millions in illicit profits. Two defendants, located in Russia and Israel, are considered fugitives according to the Massachusetts District Attorney.

stories.title: China scrambles to close AI security gap as Anthropic, OpenAI pull ahead with new models
stories.summary: U.S. AI firms Anthropic and OpenAI are advancing models with enhanced cybersecurity capabilities, with Anthropic's Mythos model launched in April demonstrating the ability to discover and exploit vulnerabilities rapidly. China is aggressively scaling up its own AI-driven cyber defense market but currently lags behind in developing comparable systems.

stories.title: Russia’s Putin says he thinks the Ukraine conflict is coming to an end
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin told reporters he believes the conflict in Ukraine is approaching its end. He expressed willingness to engage in talks with European leaders as Russia and Ukraine observed a three-day ceasefire.

stories.title: Indonesia finds bodies of 2 Singaporeans killed in Mount Dukono eruption
stories.summary: Two Singaporean nationals were confirmed dead following the eruption of Mount Dukono on Indonesia's Halmahera Island. Rescuers found the bodies near the crater rim, but evacuation efforts were hampered by continuing eruptions and bad weather. Around 150 personnel and two thermal drones were deployed in the search.

stories.title: Spain’s Canary Islands brace for arrival of hantavirus-stricken cruise ship
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius, carrying passengers affected by a hantavirus outbreak, is expected to arrive at Spain's Canary Islands. The WHO director stated the outbreak is not comparable to COVID-19, while health officials prepared for screening and disembarkation procedures.

stories.title: Putin says Moscow prepared to store Iranian enriched uranium
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced that Moscow is prepared to transport and store Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium, reviving an arrangement used under the 2015 nuclear agreement. Putin noted Russia had previously removed enriched uranium from Iran and expressed readiness to repeat the process.

stories.title: Young Palestinian killed in stabbing attack near Jerusalem checkpoint
stories.summary: A 22-year-old Palestinian man from East Jerusalem, identified as Ahmad Almashny, was fatally stabbed in the occupied West Bank. Palestine Red Crescent paramedics transported him to the al-Za'im checkpoint near Jerusalem, where Israeli medics attempted resuscitation, but he was later pronounced dead.

stories.title: Syria sets first cabinet reshuffle since Assad ouster
stories.summary: Syrian leader Ahmed al-Sharaa carried out the first cabinet reshuffle since the ouster of former President Bashar al-Assad, replacing key ministers and governors. The changes come amid growing public criticism over economic hardship and government performance.

stories.title: Number of Ukrainian refugees in EU slightly decreases – Eurostat
stories.summary: Eurostat data shows that as of March 31, 2026, approximately 4.33 million Ukrainian citizens held temporary protection status in the European Union, a slight decrease from previous figures.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine trade accusations of ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged accusations of ceasefire violations on May 9, though no major strikes were reported by either side on that date.

stories.title: Syria supports Bahrain security measures after IRGC arrests announced
stories.summary: Syria expressed "full solidarity" with Bahrain after Bahraini authorities arrested 41 individuals accused of ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Egypt and Kuwait also voiced support for Bahrain's security measures amid rising regional tensions.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills seven in south Lebanon, Lebanese health ministry says
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on the southern Lebanese town of Saksakiyeh killed at least seven people, including a child, and wounded 15, according to Lebanon's health ministry.

stories.title: IRGC navy threatens ‘heavy attack’ on US assets if oil tankers come under fire
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy threatened a heavy attack on US military assets if Iranian oil tankers come under fire. The warning followed US strikes against two Iranian tankers, while Israel reported deporting Gaza flotilla activists.

stories.title: Thousands of fans arrive in Vienna as 70th edition of Eurovision kicks off
stories.summary: The 70th edition of the Eurovision Song Contest opened in Vienna, Austria, with thousands of fans arriving in the capital on Sunday. A turquoise-carpet ceremony welcomed 35 participating delegations as part of the event's colourful opening festivities.

stories.title: Police investigate alleged antisemitic abuse at children’s netball game in Sydney
stories.summary: New South Wales police are investigating an alleged antisemitic incident at an under-12s netball game between Maccabi and Saints clubs at Heffron Park in Maroubra, Sydney. Officers were called after reports that a woman made offensive comments toward a group at the Saturday morning match.

stories.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship nears Canary Islands for WHO-led evacuation
stories.summary: The Dutch-flagged cruise ship MV Hondius, carrying nearly 150 people affected by a hantavirus outbreak, is expected to reach Tenerife at dawn on Sunday. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus will help coordinate the evacuation. Three passengers — two Dutch and one German — have died.

stories.title: Putin says Ukraine war winding down, blasts West for backing Kyiv
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he is ready to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a third country, but only after all conditions for a peace agreement are settled. Putin also criticized Western nations for their continued support of Kyiv.

stories.title: Australia news live: triumphant Hanson blasts ‘arrogant’ major parties; Ley says ‘voters never get it wrong’
stories.summary: In Australia, Pauline Hanson celebrated a strong byelection result, criticizing major parties as 'arrogant,' while former Liberal leader Sussan Ley resigned as member for Farrer after losing the opposition leadership. Coalition figure Tim Wilson signaled the party would clarify its stance on migration and net-zero policies in the coming weeks.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer challenged by former Labour minister after tough local election results
stories.summary: Former UK Labour minister Catherine West publicly challenged Prime Minister Keir Starmer following poor local election results, saying the cabinet must develop a plan to replace him or she would launch a leadership bid. She warned other Labour figures might do the same.

stories.title: Peru opens investigation into former IDF soldier after Hind Rajab Foundation files complaint
stories.summary: Peru has opened an investigation into a former IDF soldier following a complaint filed by the Hind Rajab Foundation. The allegations include war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide committed in the Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Is Hong Kong’s cultural hub of West Kowloon emerging as ‘Central 2.0’?
stories.summary: Hong Kong's West Kowloon district is positioning itself as the city's second-most important office sub-market after Central, driven by new commercial buildings attracting banks and insurance companies. Industry officials note that leasing activity is dominated by relocations rather than new entrants, with higher vacancy rates expected in other business districts.

stories.title: Rise of China complicates ‘authoritarian’ vs ‘democratic’ binary
stories.summary: Analysts argue that China's political and economic rise is challenging the conventional binary framework of 'authoritarian' versus 'democratic' systems. The discussion highlights how terms such as 'free,' 'liberal,' and 'democratic' have become increasingly blurred, reflecting a mismatch between established political language and evolving global realities.

stories.title: Amnesty praises expected release of Global Sumud Flotilla activists
stories.summary: Amnesty International's Erika Guevara Rosas welcomed reports that Israel intends to release activists Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila, who were detained after Israeli forces intercepted the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla on 29 April. The activists alleged abuse during their custody in Israel.

stories.title: Russian president warns world will suffer if Iran war continues
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed hope that the conflict involving Iran would end soon, warning that a prolonged war would have severe consequences globally. He said all parties would lose if fighting continues, as Middle East tensions disrupt energy markets and regional stability.

stories.title: Ivano-Frankivsk court finds minor guilty of assaulting Ukrinform photojournalist Yurii Rylchuk
stories.summary: A court in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine, convicted a minor for assaulting Ukrinform photojournalist Yurii Rylchuk and imposed a fine of 8,500 UAH.

stories.title: Satellite images show likely oil slick off Iran’s Kharg Island
stories.summary: Satellite imagery has revealed a suspected oil slick covering dozens of square kilometres near Iran's Kharg Island, a major oil export terminal in the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Qatar Saudi ministers discuss Iran ceasefire and regional stability
stories.summary: Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani spoke by phone with Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud to discuss regional stability and ceasefire efforts between the United States and Iran. The call also covered bilateral relations between Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Blonde, fervent and fake: Can AI-generated Trump fans boost him in the midterms?
stories.summary: AI-generated images of women, often depicted in swimsuits or military attire, are flooding tech platforms with fabricated pro-Trump political messaging ahead of the November US midterm elections. The fake accounts lavish praise on President Donald Trump and attack his political rivals.

stories.title: Israel built and defended a secret base in Iraq for Iran war
stories.summary: Israel reportedly constructed a secret military base in the Iraqi desert to support strikes against Iran and allegedly targeted Iraqi troops who approached the site.

stories.title: Iranian commander warns missiles locked onto American military targets
stories.summary: IRGC Aerospace Force General Sardar Mousavi stated that Iranian missiles and drones are locked onto American military targets and vessels in the region, awaiting orders to strike. The remarks were carried by Iran's state-run media.

stories.title: Tenerife medics poised for arrival of virus-hit cruise ship
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius, struck by a deadly hantavirus outbreak, is approaching Tenerife in Spain's Canary Islands. Medical teams on the island are preparing for the ship's arrival to treat passengers and crew.

stories.title: Qatari LNG tanker sailing towards Hormuz Strait, shipping data shows
stories.summary: A Qatari LNG tanker, Al Kharaitiyat, departed Qatar's Ras Laffan port and was sailing toward the Strait of Hormuz en route to Port Qasim in Pakistan, according to shipping data from LSEG.

stories.title: ISIS disrupts Damascus calm, says it assassinated Shi'ite figure
stories.summary: ISIS claimed responsibility for the assassination of a Shiite figure in Damascus on May 1, 2026. The attack revived concerns about the group's capacity for targeted hit-and-run operations against religious and military figures in Syria.

stories.title: Hezbollah reports attacks on Israeli troops across southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah reported carrying out 22 strikes against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon and northern Israel on Saturday. Targets included Israeli troop gatherings and vehicles in Biyyada, Rachaf, Deir Siryan, Chama, Khiam, Naqoura, and Tayr Harfa, using rockets, artillery, and attack drones.

stories.title: China TV variety show exposes scam linking ‘peace’ sign selfies to privacy risks
stories.summary: A Chinese television variety show aired in April highlighted privacy risks associated with making peace-sign gestures in selfies. Financial expert Li Chang demonstrated that fingerprints could potentially be extracted from photos taken within 1.5 metres if fingers face the camera directly, raising concerns about biometric data exposure.

stories.title: Report says Israel operated secret Iraq base during Iran war
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Israel established a covert military base in the Iraqi desert to support its air campaign against Iran. The installation reportedly housed Israeli special forces, served as a logistics hub for air operations, and included search-and-rescue teams for downed pilots.

stories.title: Iran Guards threaten US Mideast sites as Trump awaits response
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to strike US targets in the Middle East as President Trump awaited Tehran's response to a proposed peace deal. Tensions remain high amid the ongoing standoff between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Are there any winners in unfinished Iran war? - analysis
stories.summary: Ongoing explosions, US self-defense strikes, and clashes near the Strait of Hormuz highlight unresolved tensions over maritime leverage and Gulf vulnerability in the Iran conflict. Political deadlock risks further escalation.

stories.title: Vladimir Putin suggests Ukraine war is ‘coming to an end’
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin suggested the war in Ukraine is 'coming to an end' during remarks to reporters following a scaled-back Victory Day parade in Moscow on May 9. Putin criticized Western support for Ukraine and expressed willingness to negotiate new European security arrangements.

stories.title: Pro-Russian separatist held in France over Ukraine torture claims
stories.summary: French authorities detained Yevhen Brazhnikov, a pro-Russian separatist suspected of torturing detainees at a prison in Russian-occupied Donetsk city, Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump’s religious liberty commission hopes to do away with separation of church and state
stories.summary: A 17-member US religious liberty commission appointed by President Trump is broadly aligned on reducing the separation of church and state. One former member was removed after defending Candace Owens during a contentious hearing on antisemitism.

stories.title: Turkish minister meets Hamas delegation for Gaza peace discussions
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met a Hamas delegation led by Muhammad Darwish to discuss peace efforts in Gaza and humanitarian aid access. Fidan stressed that regional conflicts should not overshadow the Palestinian cause and pledged Turkey would continue raising international awareness about conditions in Gaza.

stories.title: Putin says he thinks Ukraine conflict 'coming to an end'
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated he believes the conflict in Ukraine is nearing its end, making the remarks as Moscow and Kyiv observe a three-day ceasefire in the four-year war. He also criticized Western support for Ukrainian President Zelensky.

stories.title: Russian saboteur sentenced to 15 years for arson attack on Ukrzaliznytsia equipment in Dnipro
stories.summary: A Ukrainian court sentenced a Russian saboteur to 15 years in prison with property confiscation for setting fire to a railway relay cabinet near a Ukrzaliznytsia station in Dnipro. The arson was intended to disrupt transport logistics in the frontline region.

stories.title: Bar Association proposes ‘double-track’ approach to criminalising bid-rigging
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Bar Association has proposed a 'double-track' amendment to the Competition Ordinance that would criminalize bid-rigging, currently punishable only by civil fines under the 2015 regime. The proposal aims to increase deterrence and encourage whistleblowers following the city's deadliest fire in decades.

stories.title: Police foil suicide attack on Bannu post; at least 2 personnel martyred
stories.summary: Terrorists rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into the Fateh Khel police post in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, in a foiled suicide attack. At least two police personnel were killed and two others injured along with two civilians. The blast caused the police post's roof to collapse.

stories.title: UK man charged for threatening messages to Israeli embassy, Muslim orgs, MP office
stories.summary: British authorities charged 30-year-old Nick Daly with nine counts of sending offensive messages. He allegedly sent eight anti-Muslim messages to a Muslim organization and one antisemitic message to the Israeli embassy in the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Finmin says economic recovery remains intact amid regional conflict, assures uninterrupted fuel supply
stories.summary: Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb stated that the country's economic recovery remains on track despite regional tensions. He cited 11 percent year-on-year growth in large-scale manufacturing for April and assured uninterrupted fuel supply alongside Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik.

stories.title: Mystery sea drone in Greece is from ‘foreign state’: Minister
stories.summary: Greek authorities identified an unmanned sea drone found in Greek waters as originating from a foreign state. Ukraine has previously acknowledged targeting Russian tankers in the Mediterranean Sea, though no direct attribution was made in this case.

stories.title: Border Police fatally shoot unarmed Bedouin man in Rahat, say it was in self defense
stories.summary: Israeli Border Police fatally shot an unarmed Bedouin man, an IDF veteran, in the southern city of Rahat. Police claimed the reservist officers acted in self-defense, saying the man forcefully resisted arrest. The suspected officer has been barred from police facilities for two weeks.

stories.title: UK man charged for threatening to cut Jews throats while they were going to synagogue
stories.summary: Wayne Kelly, a UK man, pleaded guilty to threatening to cut Jewish people's throats as they walked to a synagogue. He faced charges of racially aggravated assault, intentional harassment, and racially aggravated harassment.

stories.title: K-pop moved on from Goo Hara, Sulli and Jonghyun’s suicides. Fans never did
stories.summary: Fans of late K-pop stars Goo Hara, Sulli, and Jonghyun continue to mourn years after their deaths by suicide. Vancouver-based fan Edward Sugiana has traveled annually to a memorial hall on the outskirts of Seoul dedicated to former Kara member Goo Hara, who died nearly seven years ago.

stories.title: China’s AI drive seen widening wealth gap, testing ‘common prosperity’ push
stories.summary: Recent studies suggest China's push to adopt artificial intelligence as an economic growth engine may widen regional wealth disparities. Major cities with concentrations of talent and capital are better positioned to benefit, while smaller cities and rural areas risk falling behind, complicating Beijing's 'common prosperity' agenda.

stories.title: Iran war live: IRGC warns US against attacks on ships; Israel bombs Lebanon
stories.summary: The ceasefire between the United States and Iran remains in place, while Tehran's IRGC has warned Washington against targeting Iranian tankers. Separately, Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed at least 24 people.

stories.title: Cabinet approves winter readiness, economic support measures for Kherson, Mykolaiv regions
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers held an off-site meeting in Mykolaiv and approved measures for winter readiness and economic support for the Kherson and Mykolaiv regions. The decisions addressed key infrastructure and humanitarian challenges in the two southern regions.

stories.title: Pakistan expands US lobbying push with focus on defence, critical minerals and policy influence
stories.summary: Pakistan signed a new $1.2 million, two-year contract with Washington-based Ervin Graves Strategy Group LLC, registered under FARA as a foreign agent of Pakistan's embassy. The lobbying effort focuses on defense cooperation, critical minerals, and broader economic diplomacy in the US.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills one in Bedias as Lebanon death toll rises to 24
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the southern Lebanese town of Bedias killed one person and wounded 13 others. The attack occurred despite the ceasefire, bringing the day's death toll from Israeli strikes across Lebanon to at least 24.

stories.title: Greek minister says mystery drone from a 'foreign state'
stories.summary: A mystery drone discovered off the Greek island of Lefkada is believed by military sources to have originated from a foreign state, possibly Ukraine. Kyiv has acknowledged using drones to target Russian oil tankers in the Mediterranean.

stories.title: Katz said to sign certificate of confidentiality, paving way to indict firebrand MK Gotliv
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz reportedly signed a certificate of confidentiality, clearing the way for the indictment of Likud MK May Golan Gotliv. Katz had allegedly delayed signing for nine months until the Shin Bet warned that further delay could harm state security.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes apartment building in Kharkiv
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential apartment building in Kharkiv, Ukraine. An eight-year-old boy suffered an acute stress reaction as a result of the attack.

stories.title: Suicide attack targets police post in KP's Bannu, casualties feared
stories.summary: A suspected suicide attack targeted the Fateh Khel police post in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. An explosives-laden vehicle was rammed into the post, followed by at least four explosions and heavy gunfire from multiple directions. Casualties are feared.

stories.title: Moscow’s Victory Day parade draws muted response from Russians
stories.summary: Russia held its annual Victory Day military parade on Red Square in Moscow, but the event drew a muted public response. Some Russians expressed frustration over internet outages and fatigue with the war in Ukraine, now in its fourth year.

stories.title: Indian model's understated Met Gala debut revives debate on cultural representation
stories.summary: Indian model Bhavitha Mandava's understated appearance at the Met Gala has reignited debate about cultural representation and aesthetic diversity on the global fashion stage.

stories.title: Another year, another controversy for Eurovision - but fans are sticking by it
stories.summary: Several countries, including Spain and Ireland, withdrew from the Eurovision Song Contest over Israel's participation, renewing controversy around the event. Despite the withdrawals, fans continue to support the competition.

stories.title: Gazan public opinion turning against Hamas as support for disarmament grows - report
stories.summary: A report by Israel's KAN news indicates that a majority of Gazan residents now support Hamas disarming and relinquishing its weapons. Many Gazans reportedly view disarmament as a potential path out of prolonged turmoil and violence.

stories.title: Rubio defends new U.S. sanctions on Cuba, targeting military-run conglomerate GAESA
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended new sanctions targeting Cuba's military-run conglomerate GAESA. Established in the 1990s under military control, GAESA was created as a strategic response to economic collapse following the Soviet Union's fall.

stories.title: Ben Gvir branded 'hangman of the century' over push for Palestinian executions
stories.summary: The Red Ribbons Campaign, a human rights group, condemned Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir for advancing death penalty legislation targeting Palestinians. The group called him the "hangman of the century" and highlighted concerns for over 9,100 Palestinians held in Israeli detention.

stories.title: UK deploys warship to Middle East with eye on potential Hormuz mission
stories.summary: Britain announced the deployment of warship HMS Dragon to the Middle East on Saturday. The vessel is being positioned in preparation for a potential multinational mission to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Three arrested for serious assault near Bloomfield Stadium
stories.summary: Three suspects were arrested for a serious assault near Bloomfield Stadium. Earlier the same Saturday, police detained five other suspects near the venue on suspicion of planning to bring weapons to a soccer match.

stories.title: Marka-i-Haq a 'defining landmark in the nation’s journey': ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan marked the first anniversary of its brief 2024 war with India, with ISPR calling the event "Marka-i-Haq" a defining landmark. The military said the conflict demonstrated Pakistan's measured response and exposed what it described as adversarial disinformation campaigns.

stories.title: Israel built secret base in Iraqi desert during war with Iran - report
stories.summary: According to reports, Israel established a secret military base in the Iraqi desert during its conflict with Iran. The base was intended to support Israeli Air Force operations, with IDF troops stationed there in case pilots were shot down over enemy territory.

stories.title: Lack of reckoning with Soviet crimes contributed to Russia's war against Ukraine – German historian
stories.summary: German historian argues that Russia's failure to critically confront the mass crimes of the Stalin era is a key precondition for Moscow's war against Ukraine. The historian also contends the West shares responsibility for never firmly demanding such a historical reckoning from Russia.

stories.title: UN mission in Democratic Republic of Congo warns of wave of attacks in east
stories.summary: The United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo warned of a surge in attacks across the mineral-rich eastern provinces. The region has experienced three decades of conflict involving armed groups, militias, and government forces.

stories.title: PTI demands judicial commission to identify, punish culprits behind May 9 riots
stories.summary: Pakistan's PTI party demanded the formation of an independent judicial commission to investigate the May 9, 2023 events, when PTI founder Imran Khan was arrested at the Islamabad High Court. Khan remains imprisoned in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail, with restricted access to family and party leaders.

stories.title: Israeli drone strikes near Beirut kill four; southern airstrikes claim at least 13 lives
stories.summary: Israeli drone strikes near Beirut killed four people, while separate airstrikes in southern Lebanon claimed at least 13 lives. The Israeli military stated that Hezbollah had fired explosive drones into northern Israel near the Lebanese border, wounding three soldiers.

stories.title: Settlers force re-burial of Palestinian man in West Bank, family says
stories.summary: In the occupied West Bank village of Asasa, Israeli settlers forced a Palestinian family to exhume and relocate the body of their father from a freshly dug grave, according to the family. The incident occurred near a settlement that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government recently re-established.

stories.title: Putin Says Ukraine War Winding Down, Blasts West for Backing Kyiv
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin stated that the war in Ukraine is winding down while criticizing Western nations for supporting Kyiv. He made the remarks during Russia's commemoration of the 81st anniversary of the Soviet victory in World War II.

stories.title: Iran threatens to target 'American centres' if tankers are attacked
stories.summary: Iran warned it could strike "American centres" across the region if its oil tankers are attacked, according to Iranian media reports cited by Agence France-Presse. The threat comes amid rising tensions between Tehran and Washington.

stories.title: Britain sending warship to Middle East ahead of Hormuz mission
stories.summary: Britain is deploying a warship to the Middle East ahead of a mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz. Britain and France have stated that joint military plans to protect the strategic waterway are progressing.

stories.title: German politicians differ on escalation risks if Taurus missiles are delivered to Ukraine – Bundeswehr general
stories.summary: German politicians are divided on the escalation risks of supplying Taurus cruise missiles to Ukraine. A Bundeswehr general stated the missiles would have real military impact for Ukraine but emphasized the delivery decision rests with Germany's governing political parties.

stories.title: Iran says ties with China will deepen after war, praises support
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to China, Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli, said Tehran expects ties with Beijing to deepen significantly after the current conflict, including a US-led naval blockade. Fazli praised China as a key ally that supported Iran during difficult times.

stories.title: Magyar sworn in as Hungary’s prime minister on promises of change
stories.summary: Péter Magyar was sworn in as Hungary's new prime minister, pledging political change. He faces immediate pressure to secure billions of euros in European Union funding that had been suspended, needed to stabilize Hungary's economy and public finances.

stories.title: Ben Gvir branded 'hangman of the century' over push for Palestinian executions
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir faces growing international condemnation over proposals to execute Palestinian prisoners. Critics have labeled him the "hangman of the century" in response to the initiative.

stories.title: Israel said to have built secret base in Iraqi desert to support Iran air campaign
stories.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, Israel constructed a secret military base in the Iraqi desert to support its air campaign against Iran. Israeli forces reportedly launched airstrikes against Iraqi troops who nearly discovered the facility in early March; Iraq blamed the United States for those strikes.

stories.title: U.K. PM Starmer turns to Labour Party grandees after tough local election verdict
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer responded to poor Labour results in local elections by appointing senior party figures to key roles. Former Prime Minister Gordon Brown was brought in to work with international allies on boosting the United Kingdom's security and resilience.

stories.title: 'Etched in history': PM Shehbaz says Pakistan cannot be 'intimidated or subdued' as nation marks Marka-i-Haq anniversary
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif marked the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, commemorating the 2024 military confrontation with India that followed the Pahalgam attack. Sharif declared that Pakistan cannot be intimidated, framing the episode as a demonstration of national resilience.

stories.title: With the US, China must choose constructive power over destruction
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that China must pursue a constructive foreign policy approach in its relations with the United States. It draws on historical lessons from conflicts in Ukraine, the Middle East, Libya, and Afghanistan.

stories.title: Efforts ongoing to extinguish forest fire in Polissia Nature Reserve in Zhytomyr region
stories.summary: Rescuers in Ukraine's Zhytomyr region are working to extinguish a forest fire in the Polissia Nature Reserve. Drones are being used to monitor smoldering hotspots as containment efforts continue.

stories.title: One killed in Gaza as Turkish FM talks peace efforts with Hamas official
stories.summary: At least one person was killed in Gaza amid ongoing Israeli military operations, despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October. Turkey's foreign minister held discussions with a Hamas official regarding peace efforts for the territory.

stories.title: Russia and Iran use Caspian Sea trade route to aid Tehran’s drone program - NYT
stories.summary: According to a New York Times report, Russia and Iran are using a Caspian Sea trade route to support Tehran's drone program. The report noted that maritime trade across the Caspian is difficult to monitor remotely.

stories.title: Iran to play World Cup but demands guarantees from Fifa and hosts
stories.summary: Iran confirmed it will participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup but is seeking guarantees from FIFA and the host nations — the United States, Mexico, and Canada. The Iranian Football Federation's demands follow Canada's refusal to grant entry to federation president Mehdi Taj ahead of a recent match.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists to be released from Israel detention and deported
stories.summary: Activists detained in Israel after participating in the second Global Sumud Flotilla are set to be released and deported. The flotilla launched from Spain on April 12 as part of a campaign to reach Gaza.

stories.title: France arrests Russia’s war criminal who ran torture at “Donetsk Dachau” and has been living under refugee status for years
