stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Rome, said Washington expected a response from Iran regarding negotiations. Rubio described US military actions in the Strait of Hormuz as defensive and stated the US would not negotiate with Iran over Hezbollah, insisting Lebanon should be governed by its own government.

stories.title: Cannes Film Festival 2026 MENA lineup: Films of war and exile
stories.summary: The 2026 Cannes Film Festival features a lineup of films from the Middle East and North Africa, including works from Iran, Palestine, and Sudan. The selected films explore themes of war, exile, and memory across the region.

stories.title: IS claims responsibility for killing of Shia cleric in Syria
stories.summary: The Islamic State claimed responsibility for the killing of a prominent Shia cleric in Damascus, Syria. The attack has raised concerns about renewed militant activity in the country.

stories.title: Netherlands pushes renewed talks on using frozen Russian assets to support Ukraine – Politico
stories.summary: The Netherlands is pushing to restart negotiations on using up to €210 billion in frozen Russian sovereign assets to support Ukraine's defence, according to Politico. The initiative aims to secure continued funding for Ukraine.

stories.title: 3 convicted in Hong Kong’s largest football match-fixing scandal in years
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court convicted two footballers, Brian Fok and Luciano Silva da Silva, and betting agent Waheed Mohammad in the city's largest match-fixing case in recent years. Fok, a former Hong Kong Under-23 player, was found guilty of five charges including bribery offences under the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance.

stories.title: Hiker dead of apparent bear attack in Glacier national park in Montana
stories.summary: A hiker was found dead in Glacier National Park, Montana, with wounds indicating a bear attack, likely the park's first such fatality since 1998. The man had been reported missing on Sunday, and search and rescue teams discovered his body on Wednesday.

stories.title: In UK local elections, anti-Israel Greens win 1st mayoralty and anti-immigrant Reform soars
stories.summary: In UK local elections, the Green Party won its first mayoralty in the London borough of Hackney, while Nigel Farage's Reform party made significant gains. Prime Minister Keir Starmer stated he would not resign despite Labour's losses.

stories.title: Italy-US ties strained as pope and Iran war dominate talks
stories.summary: Relations between Italy and the United States have come under strain as Rome navigates domestic pressure related to the conflict involving Iran. The alliance faces challenges from economic fallout linked to the regional hostilities.

stories.title: Chinese EV maker Leapmotor taps Stellantis’ Spanish plant for EU production
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle maker Leapmotor, based in Hangzhou, has agreed with shareholder Stellantis to produce vehicles at the Figueruelas plant in Zaragoza, Spain. The Spanish facility, previously earmarked for Opel, will build Opel's new electric SUV and B10 models for the European market.

stories.title: UAE charts its own course across the Middle East and Africa
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is pursuing a more independent foreign policy across the Middle East and Africa than many Gulf neighbors, including Saudi Arabia. Its close relations with Israel and the United States have made it a target for Iran.

stories.title: Keir Starmer vows to fight on despite Labour’s heavy losses in local elections
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged to continue leading Labour despite significant losses in local elections. The defeats have intensified doubts among party members and observers about his leadership.

stories.title: Head of Jewish National Fund UK loses council seat in UK local elections
stories.summary: Alan Mendoza, head of the Jewish National Fund UK and executive director of the Henry Jackson Society, lost his council seat in UK local elections. Mendoza had stood as a Reform UK councillor. His charity reportedly donated £1 million to what has been described as Israel's largest militia.

stories.title: China’s shipping firms brace for a new ‘era of chaos’ as Iran war drags on
stories.summary: Chinese shipping companies are preparing for prolonged global disruption as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz shifts from causing transit delays to reducing cargo volumes. The blockage stems from the ongoing U.S.-Israel war on Iran, prompting firms like Cosco Shipping Holdings to pursue long-term contracts and new multimodal routes.

stories.title: Drone attack disrupts operations at 13 airports in southern Russia
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on Friday disrupted operations at 13 airports across southern Russia and Moscow's Vnukovo Airport. Drones struck the Air Navigation of Southern Russia traffic control center in Rostov-on-Don.

stories.title: Iran war hangs over Trump's Beijing visit
stories.summary: The ongoing war in Iran is expected to overshadow President Trump's upcoming visit to Beijing, where both sides aim to reset bilateral ties. The trip comes as U.S.-China relations face pressure from the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Chornobyl forest fire spreads through mined areas amid wildfire crisis in Ukraine
stories.summary: A forest fire in the Chornobyl exclusion zone has spread through mine-contaminated areas, burning over 2,000 hectares across four Ukrainian regions. Mine contamination from the ongoing war and Russian damage to infrastructure are complicating firefighting efforts.

stories.title: Latvia Summons Russian Diplomat Over Drone Incident
stories.summary: Latvia summoned a Russian diplomat following an incident in which two drones crashed on Latvian territory. Latvia's defense minister said the drones were likely Ukrainian and were traveling toward Russian targets.

stories.title: Three IDF soldiers moderately, severly wounded in two separate incidents in Lebanon
stories.summary: Three Israeli Defense Forces soldiers were wounded—some moderately, some severely—in two separate incidents in Lebanon. All soldiers were evacuated for medical treatment, and their families were notified.

stories.title: Kehillat Israel Synagogue to reopen after damage from Palisades fire
stories.summary: Kehillat Israel Synagogue in the Pacific Palisades area of Los Angeles will reopen after 16 months of repairs following damage from the Palisades fire. A rededication ceremony will mark the congregation's return.

stories.title: Boko Haram jihadists kill 18 loggers in Nigeria's Borno state
stories.summary: Boko Haram fighters killed 18 loggers in Nigeria's northeastern Borno state, according to local sources. The attack comes amid a surge in violence in the region, where displaced communities already struggle with food insecurity.

stories.title: Global perceptions of US fall below Russia under Trump, survey finds
stories.summary: An annual global democracy survey released on May 8 found that international perceptions of the United States have declined for a second straight year under President Donald Trump, now ranking below views of Russia, amid growing strains on the NATO alliance.

stories.title: DeepSeek to soon close first external fundraising in US$50b valuation: sources
stories.summary: Chinese AI company DeepSeek is expected to close its first external fundraising round soon at a valuation of up to US$50 billion. The round is backed by state-linked investors, including affiliates of China's national semiconductor investment fund.

stories.title: Russia urgently deploying more forces to counter Ukrainian drones – CinC Syrskyi
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Russia is urgently deploying four additional regiments, 24 battalions, and 162 batteries specifically to counter Ukrainian strike drones. The redeployment reflects the growing effectiveness of Ukraine's drone operations.

stories.title: Mossad hunted Iran’s terror operatives abroad - so why are British Jews still under attack?
stories.summary: The article examines why terrorist incidents targeting Jewish communities in Britain and elsewhere persist despite Israel's Mossad historically pursuing Iranian-linked operatives abroad. Iran is identified as a key driver behind threats to Diaspora Jewish communities.

stories.title: Giving chilling testimony, Australian Jews unsure antisemitism inquiry can bring change
stories.summary: A royal commission in Australia, launched after the Bondi massacre, heard testimony from Jewish community members describing harassment, threats, and fear. Witnesses expressed doubt that the antisemitism inquiry would lead to meaningful change amid a post-October 7 surge in hate incidents.

stories.title: Why Iran’s ambassador to China thinks the US can’t turn Beijing against it
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to China, Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli, said Tehran does not believe Washington can leverage Beijing against Iran. His remarks came ahead of U.S. President Donald Trump's planned visit to China, amid speculation of possible trade concessions in exchange for pressure on Tehran.

stories.title: How Nvidia’s Corning pact shines light on China’s dominant role in global fibre supply
stories.summary: Nvidia's deepening partnership with U.S. fibre optics maker Corning to replace copper links in next-generation AI systems is highlighting China's dominant role in the global optical fibre supply chain. Chinese manufacturers are positioning themselves as key suppliers of high-capacity components for AI infrastructure.

stories.title: Report: Russia revokes all foreign press credentials for Victory Day parade
stories.summary: Russia revoked press credentials for journalists from all foreign news outlets ahead of the Victory Day military parade, according to German publication Der Spiegel. The decision was reported on the evening of May 7.

stories.title: Kenya: Title Race On a Knife's Edge! Police Bullets and Ulinzi Starlets in Final Sprint for FKF Wpl Glory
stories.summary: The FKF Women's Premier League title race in Kenya is heading to a close finish, with Police Bullets and Ulinzi Starlets among the teams competing in the final stretch of the season following a weekend of high-scoring matches.

stories.title: UAE's ruling al-Nayhan family receives tens of millions in EU farming subsidies
stories.summary: An investigation by DeSmog revealed that the UAE's ruling Al Nahyan family, considered the world's second-richest family, has acquired large tracts of European farmland and received tens of millions of euros in EU agricultural subsidies.

stories.title: Anger mounts after Tennessee Republicans redraw maps to split only Black-majority district – live
stories.summary: Tennessee Republicans redrew congressional maps to split Shelby County, which includes Memphis and the state's only Black-majority district, into three Republican-leaning districts. The redistricting has drawn widespread anger.

stories.title: Uganda: Health Fears Rise As Heaps of Garbage Seal Off Soroti Main Market Street
stories.summary: In Soroti, Uganda, a growing garbage crisis at the main market has raised health concerns as waste collection services have stalled. Uncollected refuse is disrupting business and exposing vendors and residents to potential disease outbreaks.

stories.title: Energy security vs climate crisis: Norway reopens three old gas fields
stories.summary: Norway announced plans to reopen three old gas fields in the North Sea and proposed 70 new offshore locations for oil and gas exploration to boost European energy supply. Environmental activists accuse Oslo of using geopolitical conflicts as justification for continued fossil fuel extraction.

stories.title: Chinese health authority says no need to worry about latest hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: China's Centre for Disease Control and Prevention said the country has recorded no human infections from the Andes hantavirus strain linked to the current international outbreak. The CDC noted there are no natural hosts for that variant in China.

stories.title: UK's Labour Party punished in local elections, populist Reform gains
stories.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party suffered significant losses in UK local elections on May 8, reflecting widespread voter discontent less than two years after Labour's landslide national victory. The populist Reform party made notable gains.

stories.title: Project Get Zack: How the media used antisemitism against the Greens’ Jewish leader
stories.summary: UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, has faced what supporters describe as a media campaign using personalised and antisemitic attacks against him. The allegations come as Polanski has made pro-Palestinian politics a centerpiece of the Greens' platform ahead of local elections.

stories.title: Here’s what’s at risk if the Pentagon’s $350B reconciliation gambit fails
stories.summary: The US Pentagon has proposed approximately $350 billion in defense funding through a congressional reconciliation bill. Congress has already advanced a second reconciliation measure covering immigration enforcement, but the prospects for dedicated defense reconciliation funds remain uncertain.

stories.title: Russia forced to scale down its victory parade for the first time in almost 20 years
stories.summary: Russia scaled down its annual Victory Day parade for the first time in nearly 20 years after mutual attacks between Russia and Ukraine undermined a unilateral ceasefire Moscow had declared ahead of World War II commemorations.

stories.title: Ukraine sentences Medinsky, head of Russian institute in absentia to ten years in prison
stories.summary: A Kyiv district court sentenced Vladimir Medinsky, an aide to Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Anatoly Torkunov, rector of Moscow's MGIMO university, to ten years in prison in absentia with property confiscation. The charges related to an anti-Ukrainian textbook.

stories.title: ADF fighters kill at least 36 people in northeastern DR Congo
stories.summary: Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters killed at least 36 people in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The attacks reportedly occurred over two days beginning on a Tuesday in the country's northeast.

stories.title: Soft armour, pert nipples: how London design team made Kim Kardashian’s Met Gala breastplate
stories.summary: The article profiles how a London-based design team, Whitaker Malem, created Kim Kardashian's fibreglass breastplate for the Met Gala in collaboration with sculptor Allen Jones and a Kent car bodyshop.

stories.title: Indonesia volcanic eruption kills 3 hikers: officials
stories.summary: Mount Dukono on Indonesia's Halmahera island erupted on Friday, killing three hikers—including two foreigners—and leaving ten others missing. The volcano sent an ash cloud approximately 10 kilometres into the air. Authorities had declared the area off-limits the previous month due to increased volcanic activity.

stories.title: Hungary: new govt intent on initiating swift systemic change
stories.summary: Hungary's new government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar is moving quickly to implement systemic reforms, though a resignation occurred even before the cabinet was formally sworn in. Questions remain about Magyar's policy toward Ukraine and the ongoing war.

stories.title: UAE says air defences intercepted two missiles and three drones from Iran
stories.summary: The UAE Ministry of Defence reported that its air defence systems intercepted two ballistic missiles and three drones launched from Iran, with three people wounded. The ministry said it has engaged a cumulative total of 551 ballistic missiles, 29 cruise missiles, and 2,263 drones since Iranian attacks on the UAE began.

stories.title: Janice Tse is the ‘property queen’ of Hong Kong ministers. Here’s what she owns
stories.summary: Hong Kong Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Janice Tse declared ownership of 25 properties across Hong Kong, mainland China, and the UK, making her the largest property holder among the city's ministers. She also disclosed shareholdings in eight private companies.

stories.title: UK Greens engulfed in antisemitism scandals as Jewish leader Polanski targets historic local election gains
stories.summary: UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who has made anti-Israel and pro-Palestinian politics central to the party's platform, faces allegations of antisemitism along with several Green candidates. The controversy comes as the party targets historic gains in local elections.

stories.title: To negotiate with China, Europe must first figure out what it wants
stories.summary: The article discusses the European Union's two-year window to finalize key legislation, including its Industrial Accelerator and Cyber Security acts, while navigating negotiations with China. Beijing is already working to influence EU policy outcomes.

stories.title: The disaster unfolding on Russia’s Black Sea coast is of its own making
stories.summary: An environmental disaster is spreading along Russia's Black Sea coast, with reports indicating that pollution linked to systemic failures under the current Russian government has caused significant ecological damage in the southern coastal region.

stories.title: Palestine Action activist says he ‘did the right thing’ over protest at arms firm site
stories.summary: Palestine Action activist Jordan Devlin, acquitted in a trial related to a protest at an Elbit Systems UK site near Bristol in August 2024, said he and his co-defendants acted to save Palestinian lives. Four co-defendants were convicted of criminal damage.

stories.title: Fertilizer shortages: What are Africa's options during the Hormuz crisis?
stories.summary: The ongoing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is severely affecting African nations' access to fertilizer supplies. Analysts are exploring short-, medium-, and long-term solutions to mitigate the impact on the continent's agricultural sector.

stories.title: Fertilizer shortages: What Africa's options during the Hormuz crisis?
stories.summary: The ongoing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is causing severe fertilizer shortages affecting African nations. Analysts are exploring short-, medium-, and long-term alternatives to mitigate the crisis's impact on the continent's agricultural sector.

stories.title: Philippines shifts defence strategy with Japan, eyes wider security focus
stories.summary: The Philippines is shifting its defence strategy through deeper cooperation with Japan following the Balikatan joint drills. Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro voiced concern over the disputed Diaoyu/Senkaku Islands, while Tokyo offered warship transfers to Manila.

stories.title: Uganda: Abandoned Health Centre Turned Into Busy Tomato Market
stories.summary: Residents of Jalamba village in Uganda are calling on the government to restore healthcare services after a government health facility was abandoned and converted into a tomato market by local traders.

stories.title: Iran claims to have seized ‘offending’ oil tanker in Gulf of Oman
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps boarded and seized the Barbados-flagged oil tanker Ocean Koi in the Gulf of Oman. Iranian state television broadcast footage of IRGC forces detaining the vessel, which Tehran described as an "offending" ship.

stories.title: Firefighting efforts continue in Chornobyl Exclusion Zone, radiation levels normal across Ukraine – State Emergency Service
stories.summary: Firefighting operations continued in Ukraine's Chornobyl Exclusion Zone as of May 8, with the State Emergency Service reporting that radiation levels across Ukraine, including northern Kyiv region, remained stable and within normal parameters.

stories.title: Bahrain expels three MPs after they voted against royal decree on citizenship oversight
stories.summary: Bahrain's Council of Representatives unanimously expelled three lawmakers—Abdulnabi Salman, Mamdooh al-Saleh, and Mahdi al-Shuwaik—after they voted against a royal decree that removed judicial oversight of citizenship matters. The expulsions came days after dozens of Bahrainis had their nationalities revoked in connection with the Iran war.

stories.title: India pushes for inclusive migration, stronger anti-trafficking laws at United Nations General Assembly
stories.summary: India's representative Kirti Singh addressed the UN General Assembly, advocating for inclusive migration policies and stronger anti-trafficking laws. Singh highlighted India's use of digital technologies and other initiatives to support its nationals abroad.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Govt Says BIPPA Farm Returns Do Not Reverse Land Reform
stories.summary: The Zimbabwean government stated that returning farms protected under Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (BIPPA) does not reverse the country's land reform programme. Officials described the process as a legal and constitutional exercise to resolve outstanding obligations.

stories.title: Holders Flamengo see Copa Libertadores match abandoned amid crowd trouble
stories.summary: A Copa Libertadores match between Independiente Medellín and defending champions Flamengo in Colombia was abandoned after crowd violence twice interrupted play. The match was ultimately called off due to the disturbances.

stories.title: Labour’s better than expected thrashing may allow Starmer to cling on in No 10
stories.summary: The Labour Party suffered significant local election losses across England, with Reform making sweeping gains in pro-Brexit areas. Despite calls from some MPs and allies for Keir Starmer to resign, potential challengers have remained quiet.

stories.title: Russia Readies for Dialed-Down Victory Day Spectacle as Drones Fly and Millions Go Offline
stories.summary: Russia scaled back Victory Day celebrations across the country, with 11 regions canceling events entirely while 12 held full military parades. The reduced festivities came amid ongoing drone threats and internet outages affecting millions.

stories.title: South Africa: South Africa Constitutional Court Rules Parliament Unlawfully Blocked Ramaphosa Impeachment Bid
stories.summary: South Africa's Constitutional Court ruled that Parliament acted unconstitutionally in 2022 when it blocked efforts to initiate impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa.

stories.title: Israeli settlers establish new outpost in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers established a new illegal outpost northwest of Bruqin, near Salfit in the occupied West Bank. Local researcher Raed Mauqadi reported that groundwork began south of bypass Road 60, approximately 100 metres from schools and 50 metres from nearby Palestinian homes.

stories.title: Netanyahu, defending Mossad pick, tells Court security responsibility his alone
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended his choice of Gofman to lead the Mossad in response to a court petition challenging the appointment. A bereaved families group argued that Netanyahu's legal response effectively accepted personal responsibility for security failures surrounding the October 7 attacks.

stories.title: Nigeria: Two Soldiers, Terrorists Killed in Borno Attack
stories.summary: Two Nigerian soldiers were killed when Boko Haram/ISWAP militants attacked a Forward Operating Base in Magumeri Local Government Area, Borno State. Militants were also reported killed during the assault.

stories.title: Iran war costs Toyota £3bn as prices of materials soar and sales fall
stories.summary: Toyota reported a £3 billion financial hit from the war in Iran as costs for parts and materials surged and sales declined. The world's largest carmaker said it was likely unable to absorb the added impact from the Middle East conflict, compounded by U.S. tariffs.

stories.title: Spain to repatriate guests as hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads for Canaries
stories.summary: Spain announced it will begin repatriating passengers from the hantavirus-affected cruise ship MV Hondius after it arrives at Granadilla port on Tenerife in the Canary Islands on Sunday. Cabinet minister Angel Victor Torres said planes would be available that same day.

stories.title: Why the UK is unlikely to shut Hong Kong’s London trade office despite spying verdict
stories.summary: Observers say the UK is unlikely to close Hong Kong's Economic and Trade Office in London despite a British court convicting two men of spying on Hong Kong activists for Chinese authorities. Maintaining relations with Beijing is seen as a priority for the British government.

stories.title: Kenya: Rescue Operations Intensify After 15 People Killed in West Pokot Gold Mine Collapse
stories.summary: At least 15 people were killed in a rockfall at an informal gold mining site in Rumos Hills, West Pokot County, Kenya. Rescue teams are racing to find additional miners feared trapped underground.

stories.title: China Is Transforming Brazil’s Car Market
stories.summary: Chinese automaker BYD has achieved landmark sales in Brazil, transforming the country's car market. The expansion has sparked debate over working conditions at BYD's Brazilian operations and broader questions about Brazil's deepening economic relationship with China.

stories.title: Wall Street giants lead China-profit surge despite market polarisation, uneven recovery
stories.summary: Overseas-invested securities firms saw combined net profits from their China businesses surge more than fourfold to 2.65 billion yuan (US$390 million) in 2025. The growth was driven by China's relaxation of capital restrictions and a market rebound, though performance varied widely among individual firms.

stories.title: Why China-Russia ties are ‘better than alliance’ and immune to US containment efforts
stories.summary: A senior Chinese policy adviser at Tsinghua University described China-Russia relations as 'better than an alliance' and resistant to U.S. efforts to drive a wedge between the two countries. He cited deep structural contradictions between Washington and Moscow as a stabilizing factor.

stories.title: V+Short makes its debut with a bold new vision for mobile storytelling at exclusive Hong Kong launch event
stories.summary: PT MNC Digital Entertainment launched V+Short, a premium micro drama platform, at an event at The Peninsula Hong Kong. The mobile-first platform aims to deliver bite-sized immersive content blending global appeal with local resonance.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda Explores Partnership With Leading U.S. Clinic
stories.summary: Rwanda is exploring a potential healthcare partnership with Cleveland Clinic, a leading U.S. medical institution. The initiative is part of Rwanda's broader efforts to advance its healthcare system.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill 17,400 civilians since beginning of full-scale war – Prosecutor General's Office
stories.summary: Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office reported that more than 17,400 civilians have been killed by Russian strikes since the start of the full-scale invasion in February 2022.

stories.title: Tai Po fire: building authorities slammed at inquiry for ‘mechanical mindset’
stories.summary: A former Hong Kong Housing Bureau inspection director admitted at an inquiry into the deadly Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court that his team had 'blindly' followed outdated guidelines when deciding not to audit renovation works. Building authorities were criticized for a 'mechanical mindset.'

stories.title: What we know about Iran’s response to the latest US ceasefire proposal
stories.summary: Iran has not yet issued a formal response to the latest US ceasefire proposal. Officials familiar with the discussions indicate that a significant gap remains between the positions of both sides.

stories.title: AFU engineering units clear 157 hectares of farmland in April
stories.summary: In April, engineering units of Ukraine's Armed Forces Support Forces cleared 157 hectares of agricultural land and approximately 35 hectares of forest of explosive devices, enabling safer civilian use of the terrain.

stories.title: Sexual violence against Palestinians in Israeli prisons is ‘systematic’
stories.summary: An analyst has described sexual violence against Palestinian detainees held in Israeli prisons as systematic. The claims point to a pattern of abuse within the Israeli detention system affecting Palestinian prisoners.

stories.title: Israeli strike in Lebanon kills emergency worker
stories.summary: An Israeli strike in southern Lebanon killed a medical emergency worker. The Israeli military also issued displacement orders for seven villages in the south Lebanon area.

stories.title: Bahrain expels three MPs after they voted against royal decree on citizenship oversight
stories.summary: Bahrain's parliament expelled three lawmakers after they voted against a royal decree on citizenship oversight. The expulsions came days after dozens of people had their nationalities revoked in connection with the Iran war.

stories.title: Trump says ceasefire still holds after fighting between the US and Iran flares
stories.summary: US and Iranian forces clashed in the Persian Gulf on May 8, and the UAE came under renewed attack, endangering a month-old ceasefire. The fighting shook hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the broader crisis between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: British MPs to visit China for first time in 7 years: Sources
stories.summary: British Members of Parliament are set to visit China for the first time in seven years, according to sources. Details about participating MPs and the itinerary have not been disclosed.

stories.title: EU tells airlines passenger rules maintained despite Iran crisis
stories.summary: The European Commission told airlines that passenger protection rules remain unchanged despite the Iran war's impact on the jet fuel market. Airlines are not permitted to impose fuel surcharges or avoid compensation for cancelled flights, unless local fuel shortages cause cancellations.

stories.title: Electrical substation on fire in Krasnoperekopsk after drone attack, strike reported on military unit in Simferopol
stories.summary: In Russian-occupied Crimea, a large electrical substation in Krasnoperekopsk caught fire following an overnight drone attack on May 8. A fire was also reported at the Brom chemical plant, and a Russian military unit in Simferopol was reportedly struck.

stories.title: Airports in Southern Russia Paralyzed After Ukrainian Drone Hits Air Traffic Control Center
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck an air traffic control center in southern Russia in the early morning hours after Russia's self-declared May 8–10 ceasefire took effect, paralyzing airport operations across the region.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Opposition MP Condemns Evictions in Mogadishu, Calls for Protest
stories.summary: Somali opposition lawmaker Caano Nuug condemned the eviction and displacement of residents in Mogadishu, accusing the government of demolishing homes belonging to poor families. The lawmaker called for protests in support of those displaced.

stories.title: Spanish authorities prepare for arrival of hantavirus-stricken cruise ship
stories.summary: Spanish authorities are preparing for the arrival of the hantavirus-affected MV Hondius off Tenerife in the Canary Islands on Sunday. An 'unprecedented operation' is under way to receive, assess, and repatriate the 149 passengers and crew aboard the Dutch-flagged vessel.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: The article provides weekly Shabbat candle lighting times for communities across Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill three in Gaza despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Three Palestinians were killed by Israeli strikes in Gaza on Thursday despite an ongoing ceasefire. Hamas condemned the attacks and called on mediators to intervene to halt the violence.

stories.title: Iran army says seized oil tanker in Sea of Oman
stories.summary: Iran's military announced it seized the oil tanker Ocean Koi in the Sea of Oman. Iranian state media said the vessel was intercepted over an alleged attempt to disrupt Iran's oil exports.

stories.title: South Africa: Weather Service Warns of Cold Front in the Western Cape, Northern Cape
stories.summary: The South African Weather Service warned that a cold front is expected to reach the western parts of the Western Cape and south-western Namakwa in the Northern Cape on Sunday morning.

stories.title: South Africa: Mop-Up Operations Continue At Garden Route National Park Following Flooding
stories.summary: South African National Parks teams are conducting mop-up operations to restore access to the Garden Route National Park after persistent rainfall caused widespread infrastructure damage.

stories.title: Michigan man receives 20-year sentence for providing material support to ISIS
stories.summary: Aws Mohammed Naser, a Michigan man convicted of attempting to provide material support to ISIS and creating bomb-making materials, has been sentenced to 20 years in federal prison.

stories.title: First Thing: US-Iran ceasefire at risk after exchange of fire in strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran exchanged fire in the Strait of Hormuz, posing the most serious test to their month-long ceasefire. President Trump insisted the ceasefire remains intact, while Tehran accused Washington of breaching the truce by targeting ships and civilian areas.

stories.title: Civilian, three IDF soldiers indicted for spying for Iran prior to enlistment
stories.summary: Israeli security authorities have indicted a civilian and three IDF soldiers on espionage charges for allegedly spying for Iran before their military enlistment. The suspects reportedly photographed public and security-related sites across Israel and were asked to acquire weapons.

stories.title: Drones of NGU Azov take control of skies over Mariupol
stories.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicles operated by the National Guard of Ukraine's Azov 1st Corps are conducting surveillance over Russian-occupied Mariupol in the Donetsk region, patrolling roads up to 160 kilometers from the front line.

stories.title: Can India’s rice farmers reap from US$30 million Amazon carbon credit deal?
stories.summary: Amazon signed a US$30 million carbon credit deal with India's Good Rice Alliance, backed by Bayer, GenZero, and Shell, to help thousands of Indian smallholder rice farmers adopt climate-smart growing practices. Experts say the deal could boost global carbon markets.

stories.title: After 18 months of mourning, a Gaza son is found alive in an Israeli prison
stories.summary: A family in Gaza discovered their son, whom they had believed dead and mourned for 18 months, is alive and being held in an Israeli prison. The family had considered him martyred before learning of his detention.

stories.title: Turkey touts propellant breakthrough for Yıldırımhan long-range ballistic missile
stories.summary: Turkey announced a propellant breakthrough for its Yıldırımhan long-range ballistic missile program. The Turkish government has been developing hypersonic technologies and liquid-propellant propulsion systems for nearly a decade as part of its expanding domestic defense industry.

stories.title: Child deaths mount from Bangladesh measles outbreak
stories.summary: Bangladesh is experiencing its deadliest measles outbreak in decades, with more than 300 children killed and hospital wards overwhelmed. Vaccination coverage gaps during and after the 2024 political upheaval that ousted the previous government left many children unprotected.

stories.title: U.K. local elections: Partial results show losses for Starmer’s Labour and wins for Reform U.K.
stories.summary: Partial results from the UK local elections showed significant losses for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party, while Nigel Farage's Reform UK made notable gains. The vote is widely seen as an unofficial referendum on Starmer's leadership, less than two years after Labour came to power.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanese town kills two
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on the southern Lebanese town of Toura killed two people and wounded five others, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The wounded were transported to hospitals in Tyre. Israeli warplanes also struck the nearby town of Tayr Falsayh in a separate raid.

stories.title: Cathay Pacific to lower fuel surcharges for passenger flights by up to 14%
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific Airways will reduce fuel surcharges for passenger flights by up to approximately 14 percent starting May 16. Long-haul surcharges will drop from HK$1,560 to HK$1,362 per leg.

stories.title: Reports that Islamic State-linked rebels kill 36 people in DR Congo
stories.summary: Fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces, an Islamic State-linked armed group, reportedly killed 36 people in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The attacks occurred over two days beginning Tuesday.

stories.title: 2 Indian nationals part of crew of luxury cruise ship that reported hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: A luxury cruise ship operated by Oceanwide Expeditions reported a hantavirus outbreak, with two Indian nationals among its crew. The vessel departed from Ushuaia, Argentina on April 1 and is expected to arrive at Spain's Canary Islands on May 10.

stories.title: Surviving two wars: The struggle of Sudanese migrants in Lebanon
stories.summary: Sudanese migrants in Lebanon face compounded displacement, having fled conflict in Sudan only to encounter another war in their host country. The report highlights their ongoing struggle to find safety across borders.

stories.title: Ships in Strait of Hormuz remain stranded amid hopes of US-Iran deal
stories.summary: Ships remain stranded in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran maintains effective control of the critical waterway following US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. Diplomatic hopes rest on a potential US-Iran deal to reopen the passage.

stories.title: Are China and Russia flexing their maritime muscle near Japan?
stories.summary: Japan's Ministry of Defence reported that three Chinese Navy warships—two Type 055 and one Type 052D guided-missile destroyers—transited the Tsushima Strait toward the East China Sea last week. Japan's JS Ootaka conducted surveillance and intelligence gathering on the vessels amid heightened regional tensions.

stories.title: U.S. slaps sanctions on Iraqi deputy oil minister over Iran
stories.summary: The US State Department imposed sanctions on Iraqi Deputy Oil Minister Ali Maarij al-Bahadli, accusing him of abusing his government position to divert Iraqi oil revenues in support of Iran and its proxies. Spokesman Tommy Pigott confirmed the action was related to illicit oil diversion benefiting the Iranian regime.

stories.title: Updated version of nazism labeled 'made in Russia' - Zelensky
stories.summary: On May 8, the Day of Remembrance and Victory over Nazism, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukrainians are once again forced to confront evil, describing Russia's actions as an updated form of Nazism.

stories.title: Inside TikTok's prostitution recruitment networks
stories.summary: An investigation reveals that criminals are using TikTok to recruit women and girls into prostitution networks. Separately, Myanmar's military government has expanded a ban on menstrual products, claiming resistance groups use them as first aid for wounded fighters, raising health concerns for women and girls.

stories.title: Death toll rises to 37 in China fireworks factory blast
stories.summary: An explosion at a fireworks factory in Liuyang, Hunan province, China, on May 4, 2026, killed at least 37 people. The blast occurred at approximately 4:40 p.m. local time. Liuyang is known as China's fireworks capital, producing about 60 percent of domestic output and 70 percent of exports.

stories.title: Ahead of Nairobi summit, France highlights youth, innovation and 'huge diaspora' investing in Africa
stories.summary: France is preparing for the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, its first summit held in English-speaking Africa. Deputy Minister Éléonore Caroit said France aims to expand partnerships across the entire African continent, focusing on youth, innovation, and diaspora investment rather than limiting engagement to former colonies.

stories.title: South Africa: SA Loses 6,000 Educators Annually, but a Targeted Mentorship Is Fighting the Mass Exodus
stories.summary: South Africa is losing approximately 6,000 educators per year, with more than 32,000 teachers departing in the past five years. A targeted mentorship fellowship program is providing support and community to combat the exodus.

stories.title: Ukraine may have turned tide of Russian territorial gains, says think tank
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reports that Russia's territorial advance in Ukraine is slowing. Ukraine claims Russian forces suffered more than 35,000 casualties in April, suggesting a possible shift in battlefield momentum.

stories.title: Why Russia has scaled back May 9 Victory Parade
stories.summary: Russia scaled back its traditional May 9 Victory Day military parades in Moscow and cancelled them in other cities. The Kremlin attributed the reduced celebrations to threats from Ukraine.

stories.title: Russian attacks in Kharkiv region over past day leave ten injured
stories.summary: Russian attacks struck the city of Kharkiv and 17 other settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region over the past day, injuring ten people including three children.

stories.title: 'Peacemaker' Rubio tries to appease pope over spat with Trump
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican to ease tensions following a public dispute between the pontiff and President Donald Trump. Italian newspapers marked the pope's first year in office. Separately, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer suffered significant losses in local elections.

stories.title: Rubio meets Pope Leo: Can they heal White House-Vatican rift?
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican. The State Department characterized the meeting as reflecting strong bilateral ties, despite recent tensions between the White House and the Vatican under President Trump.

stories.title: British broadcaster David Attenborough turns 100, notable for not joining anti-Israel boycotts
stories.summary: British broadcaster and naturalist Sir David Attenborough has turned 100. He is noted for never joining cultural boycotts of Israel, and his family helped rescue Jewish sisters before the Holocaust.

stories.title: Why is a Chinese research ship the latest flashpoint with Philippines in South China Sea?
stories.summary: China and the Philippines exchanged accusations over the presence of the Chinese research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 near a disputed South China Sea reef. China's Coast Guard alleged a Philippine Coast Guard aircraft harassed the ship, while both sides warned of potential countermeasures, reflecting ongoing territorial tensions.

stories.title: South Africa president faces call to resign after court ruling
stories.summary: South Africa's Constitutional Court ruled that members of parliament were wrong to block impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa. The ruling has prompted calls for Ramaphosa's resignation.

stories.title: How China’s sharper tech edge forces South Korea to rethink decades of industrial ties
stories.summary: Experts say China's rapid technological advances and aggressive pricing are undermining South Korean firms' ability to maintain profitable industrial partnerships with Chinese counterparts. At a recent forum in Beijing, speakers urged companies from both nations to develop interdependent ecosystems in sectors like batteries and artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Trump says Iran talks advancing despite rising tensions at Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that negotiations with Iran are advancing despite a fresh exchange of fire, maintaining that a ceasefire remains in place. Trump suggested a deal could be reached soon, even as tensions persist in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks Singapore's support in repatriating nationals, Iranians aboard vessels seized by US
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar spoke with Singapore's foreign minister seeking assistance in repatriating 11 Pakistanis and 20 Iranians aboard vessels seized by the United States near Singaporean waters. Dar also coordinated with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the matter.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of breaching Victory Day ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine each accused the other of violating a ceasefire declared for Victory Day, marking the Soviet Union's World War II victory over Nazi Germany. Both sides reported responding to hundreds of drone attacks within hours of the truce taking effect.

stories.title: Ukraine sends mass drone attack on Moscow as Russia’s unilateral ceasefire takes effect
stories.summary: Ukraine launched a mass drone attack on Moscow just after midnight on May 8, coinciding with the start of Russia's unilaterally declared ceasefire for May 8–10, according to Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin.

stories.title: Russia carries out 596 strikes on energy infrastructure since start of full-scale war – SSU
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service reported that Russian forces have carried out 596 strikes targeting Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the start of the full-scale invasion in February 2022.

stories.title: Baghdad's 'Agatha Christie House' and Iraq's vanishing past
stories.summary: A crumbling house in Baghdad, linked to disputed claims about author Agatha Christie, has become a focal point in debates over Iraq's cultural heritage. The building's deterioration reflects broader concerns about war damage, historical myth, and cultural erasure in the country.

stories.title: More than half of Lebanon's population depends on aid, EU official says
stories.summary: An EU official said more than three million people—over half of Lebanon's population—now depend on humanitarian aid. EU crisis management chief Hadja Lahbib made the statement after meeting Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in Beirut, as Israeli attacks on Lebanon continue despite a ceasefire.

stories.title: US and Iran exchange fire, but Trump says ceasefire still in effect
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran exchanged fire on Thursday in the most serious test of their month-long ceasefire. Iran said Washington targeted two ships entering the Strait of Hormuz and struck Iranian territory, while the U.S. described its actions as responsive and said it did not seek escalation. Tehran reported the situation returned to normal.

stories.title: 'Too much at stake to accept ignorance': Lawmakers challenge US ambiguity over Israel’s nuclear capability
stories.summary: Nearly 30 Democratic U.S. lawmakers sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging Washington to end its longstanding ambiguity over Israel's alleged nuclear weapons program. They argued that such secrecy is untenable during the ongoing war against Iran, which they described as a conflict with nuclear dimensions.

stories.title: Iraq denies US claims deputy oil minister helped Iran evade sanctions
stories.summary: Iraq's oil ministry denied U.S. accusations that its deputy oil minister assisted Iran in evading American sanctions. Washington has been increasing pressure on Baghdad over alleged sanctions violations.

stories.title: UAE sends Trump's Board of Peace '$100m' for training of new Gaza police force
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has transferred $100 million to the US-backed Board of Peace to fund the training of a Palestinian police force intended for the Gaza Strip. The donation is the largest the board has received since its creation at a February donor conference.

stories.title: China ‘full-time children’ re-enter job market, believe experience will ease future challenges
stories.summary: Some young Chinese adults who adopted the "full-time children" trend—living at home and receiving parental salaries in exchange for companionship and household help—are now re-entering the job market. The phenomenon went viral in 2023 amid a difficult employment landscape, but participants say it was not a lasting solution.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV marks first anniversary as leader of global Catholic Church
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV marked his first anniversary as head of the global Catholic Church. Initially maintaining a low profile, the pontiff has grown increasingly outspoken on issues of armed conflict and human rights.

stories.title: UDF strikes Russian oil facility in Yaroslavl, 700 kilometers from border – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine's Defense Forces struck an oil industry facility in Yaroslavl, Russia, located approximately 700 kilometers from the Ukrainian border.

stories.title: Ghana: Attacks On Firefighters Threaten Public Safety - Northern Regional Minister
stories.summary: Ghana's Northern Regional Minister Ali Adolf John Mburidiba urged residents of Tamale and surrounding communities to stop attacking firefighters. He warned that violence against emergency responders threatens public safety in the region.

stories.title: Defiant Starmer digs in after UK Labour’s local election drubbing
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue governing after Labour suffered heavy losses in local elections, including in traditional strongholds across central and northern England. The results, coming less than two years after Labour's national landslide victory, saw populist parties make significant gains.

stories.title: Where are the flash points in next week's Trump-Xi talks?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to visit China next week for talks with President Xi Jinping, the first such presidential visit in nearly a decade. The agenda is expected to cover trade, including Chinese purchases of US aircraft, agriculture, and energy. Tensions over Iran, Taiwan, and an uneasy trade truce remain key flash points.

stories.title: Police seek aggravated murder charge for main teen suspect in Yemanu Zelka killing
stories.summary: Israeli police are seeking an aggravated murder charge against the main teenage suspect in the stabbing death of Yemanu Zelka, a 21-year-old Pizza Hut employee. Authorities also plan to recommend joint enterprise murder and aggravated assault charges against several other suspects.

stories.title: Rwandan President Paul Kagame tours Botswana diamond hub
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame visited the Diamond Trading Company Botswana in Gaborone on the final day of his state visit. The tour focused on Botswana's diamond industry, a key driver of the country's economy.

stories.title: Inside Gaza's race to save ancient manuscripts from Israel's war
stories.summary: Volunteers in Gaza City's Old Quarter are working to recover ancient manuscripts from the damaged Al-Omari Mosque library, which has sustained destruction during repeated Israeli military operations since 2023.

stories.title: Trump's White House considers implementing AI regulation after cybersecurity warnings
stories.summary: The Trump administration is considering implementing regulatory oversight of artificial intelligence systems following cybersecurity warnings. The shift marks a departure from the administration's previously noninterventionist approach to AI technology.

stories.title: Iran and the US trade fire over Hormuz, Trump says ceasefire still in effect
stories.summary: A new exchange of fire between Iran and the United States occurred late Thursday night in the Strait of Hormuz, with each side accusing the other of firing first. President Trump stated that a ceasefire remains in effect despite the incident.

stories.title: EU moving toward implementing sanctions on Israeli West Bank settlements, ambassador confirms
stories.summary: The European Union is moving toward implementing sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The EU Foreign Ministers' Council is scheduled to meet on May 11, where such measures could potentially be approved.

stories.title: Keir Starmer's Labour braces for heavy losses in UK local elections
stories.summary: UK local election results showed Labour losing control of several councils, with Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, on course for major gains. The far right made advances across England as pressure mounted on Prime Minister Keir Starmer, with most results still to be declared later Friday.

stories.title: Israel and Hezbollah continue to trade blows despite the ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel acknowledged responsibility for a Wednesday night airstrike on Beirut's southern suburbs, with Prime Minister Netanyahu saying he authorized the attack to kill Hezbollah commander Malek Balou. The strikes continue despite an existing ceasefire, further straining U.S.-backed negotiations between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: UAE sends Trump's Board of Peace '$100m' for training of new Gaza police force
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates reportedly sent $100 million to the Trump administration's Board of Peace to fund a new Gaza police force. An Emirati security firm is expected to train approximately 27,000 Jordanian and Egyptian police officers for deployment in Gaza.

stories.title: Three dead after volcano erupts on Indonesian island
stories.summary: A volcanic eruption on an Indonesian island killed at least three people. Officials had previously issued warnings against climbing the active volcano due to safety concerns.

stories.title: No Russian military units present on territory of Belarus – Demchenko
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence spokesperson Demchenko stated that no Russian military units are currently detected on the territory of Belarus.

stories.title: US military struck empty tankers 'trying to break Iran blockade'
stories.summary: The U.S. military carried out fresh strikes against several tankers allegedly attempting to break the blockade on Iran. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington expected a response from Tehran regarding its negotiation proposal on Friday.

stories.title: US-Iran truce shaken after fire, UAE intercepts Iranian strikes
stories.summary: US President Trump stated that the ceasefire with Iran remained in effect despite an exchange of fire. The UAE reported intercepting Iranian strikes, indicating continued hostilities despite the declared truce.

stories.title: Trump reversed Hormuz plan after Saudis denied airspace access
stories.summary: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman denied the United States access to Saudi airspace, forcing President Trump to abandon a military plan involving the Strait of Hormuz. The decision reportedly stunned U.S. officials and led to a reversal of the operation.

stories.title: Toyota sees 20 percent drop in annual profit as Iran war weighs
stories.summary: Toyota has forecast a 20 percent decline in operating profit for the financial year ending March 2027, projecting 3.0 trillion yen compared with 3.77 trillion yen the previous year. The automaker cited cost and supply-chain uncertainties linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Pink hair and red herrings: viral quiz invites you to guess politicians’ stripes from their photos
stories.summary: A viral online game called Guess the Party challenges players to identify UK local election candidates' political affiliations based solely on their photographs. Created by Sam Hamill-Stewart, the quiz reveals that guessing political alignment from appearance is far less reliable than stereotypes suggest.

stories.title: FBI’s lack of progress on Israeli killing of journalist ‘troubling’: CPJ
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) criticized the FBI's lack of progress in investigating the Israeli killing of a journalist. The CPJ described the stalled investigation as a failure by the U.S. government to pursue accountability.

stories.title: Early England election results make it clear: we are in an era of five-party politics
stories.summary: Early results from England's local elections indicate the emergence of five-party politics, with Labour losing more than 250 council seats while Reform UK made notable gains. Analysts caution that the voting patterns are more nuanced than the headline losses suggest, with results still being counted across England, Scotland, and Wales.

stories.title: Why has the war on Iran not sparked a mass protest movement?
stories.summary: An analysis explores why the US-led war on Iran has not generated a large-scale protest movement in the United States, suggesting that everyday normalized violence has desensitized Americans to military action and the targeting of marginalized communities.

stories.title: UAE reports drone, missile attack as Iran war ceasefire is challenged
stories.summary: The UAE reported a drone and missile attack amid challenges to the Iran war ceasefire. The UAE Ministry advised residents not to approach, photograph, or touch any debris or fragments resulting from air interceptions.

stories.title: US, Iran clash in Hormuz as war escalates: What happened, why it matters
stories.summary: A ceasefire between the United States and Iran has been in effect since April 8 amid their conflict in the Strait of Hormuz region. The two sides have not yet reached a broader peace agreement.

stories.title: Veteran politician Jeffrey Lam to lead Hung Shui Kiu industrial park operator
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government appointed veteran politician Jeffrey Lam Kin-fung to chair the board of the Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park Company, the first entity created to accelerate the Northern Metropolis development project. The board includes five bureau chiefs and five non-official members overseeing the 23-hectare industrial park.

stories.title: War update: 208 combat clashes on front line
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces recorded 208 combat engagements with Russian forces along the front line on May 7.

stories.title: Hamas is rebuilding, and Israel faces the same dilemma again - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis examines how Hamas is reconstituting its organizational capacity in Gaza, highlighting Israel's recurring strategic dilemma of lacking a clear political plan for post-conflict governance in the territory.

stories.title: My Word: Nice words are not enough - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses the framing of Holocaust remembrance and criticisms directed at those who center Jewish experiences in Holocaust discourse, arguing that such critiques mischaracterize Jewish advocacy.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine trade major attacks despite Victory Day ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine accused each other of violating a two-day ceasefire Moscow declared to mark Victory Day. Ukraine's air force reported downing 56 Russian drones near the frontline, while Russia's Defence Ministry claimed it intercepted 264 Ukrainian drones in Friday's early hours.

stories.title: Man pleads guilty to assaulting US lawmaker Ilhan Omar in January town hall
stories.summary: A man pleaded guilty to assaulting U.S. Representative Ilhan Omar during a town hall event in January. He used a syringe to spray apple cider vinegar, which landed on her clothing and skin.

stories.title: Drones strike Russian military HQ in Chechnya — second blast lands 120 meters from the FSB
stories.summary: Drones struck the headquarters of Russia's 42nd Motor Rifle Division at the Khankala military base in Grozny, Chechnya, at dawn. A second blast landed approximately 120 meters from the Chechen FSB headquarters, according to the Astra news outlet.

stories.title: Malaysia’s EV import curbs to protect local car sector criticised for inconsistency
stories.summary: Malaysia announced that from July 1 it will impose price curbs on imported electric vehicles to protect domestic automakers. Business experts warn the restrictions could sharply reduce EV demand and delay the country's renewable energy transition before its nascent EV market fully develops.

stories.title: Exclusive: ICC prosecutor Karim Khan details 'dangerous' attempt by states to remove him
stories.summary: ICC Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan has accused members of the court's governing body of conducting a biased campaign to remove him from office. Khan told Middle East Eye the effort is linked to unfounded sexual misconduct allegations and his investigation into alleged Israeli war crimes.

stories.title: Iran on the verge of economic asphyxiation -- rare footage from Tehran
stories.summary: Two months into the U.S.-Israeli military offensive against Iran, France 2 obtained rare footage from Tehran showing the country on the verge of economic collapse. Runaway inflation has triggered a severe cost-of-living crisis, while the Iranian regime remains in power and continues political repression.

stories.title: South Africa: South African Xenophobic Violence - When the State Retreats, Something Else Governs
stories.summary: The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights warned that xenophobic violence against African migrants in South Africa reflects a longstanding pattern of serious rights violations. Critics say political leaders have responded with silence or escalation rather than accountability.

stories.title: China reports attack on oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry reported that an oil products tanker carrying Chinese crew was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Beijing expressed deep concern over the incident amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. No crew casualties have been reported so far.

stories.title: Zelensky says Russian war commemoration ceasefire shows ‘strange logic’
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Russia's ceasefire tied to its war commemoration as reflecting "strange logic." Following the ceasefire deadline, no Russian strikes or other military activity were reported.

stories.title: Exclusive: ICC prosecutor Karim Khan details 'dangerous' attempt by states to remove him
stories.summary: ICC Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan accused member states of orchestrating an effort to remove him from his position. Khan described the campaign as a dangerous threat to the rule of law and characterized it as a politically motivated process.

stories.title: Iraq denies US claims deputy oil minister helped Iran evade sanctions
stories.summary: Iraq's oil ministry has denied US accusations that Deputy Oil Minister Ali Maarij al-Bahadli helped Iran evade sanctions. The US State Department announced sanctions against al-Bahadli, alleging he diverted Iraqi oil to benefit Iran and its proxy groups.

stories.title: Bulgaria approves new cabinet led by Rumen Radev — the ex-president who called Crimea Russian
stories.summary: Bulgaria's parliament approved a new cabinet led by former President Rumen Radev by a vote of 124 to 70. Radev has drawn controversy for previously describing occupied Crimea as Russian.

stories.title: LTC Nadav Shoshani: Is Israel telling the right story to the world?
stories.summary: Outgoing IDF spokesman Lt. Col. Nadav Shoshani acknowledged that Israel's international reputation is poor. He maintained that his communications unit has performed well despite what he described as an inherently biased media environment.

stories.title: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law on China spies in UK: ‘We’re not surprised’
stories.summary: Exiled Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Nathan Law said he was not surprised by revelations that a Chinese spy ring had photographed him entering the Oxford Union in November 2023. Chi Leung Wai and Chung Biu Yuen were convicted at the Old Bailey, marking the first criminal conviction of Chinese spies in British history.

stories.title: Why are China’s coastal fish farms disappearing while India’s are expanding?
stories.summary: A new satellite-based dataset reveals that China's coastal aquaculture ponds have been shrinking since 2017 due to environmental regulations, while India's fish farming area has expanded at the fastest rate globally. The global trend of rapid pond expansion reversed after 2017, with significant variation between countries.

stories.title: Trump’s Beijing trip, Iran war diplomacy, tech earnings
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump plans to bring a smaller delegation of CEOs to Beijing for a May 14–15 summit, scaled back from his 2017 visit. The trip's agenda may be overshadowed by the ongoing war on Iran. Companies such as Nvidia, Apple, and Boeing are among those considered for the delegation.

stories.title: Mexico: A mother exhumes her son’s bones, seven years after his disappearance
stories.summary: Ceci Flores, leader of a Mexican collective of mothers searching for disappeared relatives, discovered the remains of her son in northern Mexico in late March 2025. Her son had vanished in 2019. Such civilian-led collectives have emerged across Mexico to compensate for authorities' inaction on cartel-related disappearances.

stories.title: Australian remanded on fresh eat-and-run charges in Hong Kong a day after being fined
stories.summary: Australian national Samuel Anthony Monkivitch, 50, was remanded in custody in Hong Kong after being charged with fleeing restaurants without paying more than HK$2,000 in bills. The new charges came just one day after he was fined at Eastern Court for similar eat-and-run offences and a common assault charge.

stories.title: Ukraine’s air defenses down 56 out of 67 Russian drones overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Force reported that air defense systems shot down or suppressed 56 out of 67 Russian drones launched against Ukraine starting the evening of May 7.

stories.title: CPJ demands update on US probe of journalist Abu Akleh’s killing in West Bank
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists demanded a public progress update from the U.S. Department of Justice on its investigation into the 2022 killing of Palestinian American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh. Abu Akleh was shot dead by Israeli military forces while reporting for Al Jazeera in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Starmer vows to fight on as PM despite heavy local election losses for Labour
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue leading despite Labour suffering heavy losses in local elections across England, Scotland, and Wales. Many seats were lost to Nigel Farage's Reform UK party. Some Labour MPs called for Starmer to resign, but he insisted he remained committed to delivering on his election promises.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump insists ceasefire is intact after Iran and US exchange fire in Hormuz
stories.summary: The U.S. military struck Iranian targets after Iran attacked three American destroyers in the Strait of Hormuz, while President Trump maintained that a ceasefire remained intact. In Lebanon, an Israeli strike killed a civil defence rescue worker in the south, further eroding the April 17 ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Lobito Corridor faces delivery test as global powers compete for Africa's minerals
stories.summary: The Lobito Corridor, a transport route from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Angola's Atlantic port of Lobito, is becoming operational with trains now carrying copper and cobalt. The project has drawn competition among global powers seeking access to Africa's critical minerals.

stories.title: Russia reportedly rushes four regiments and 162 batteries to defend Moscow from Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Russia is deploying four air defense regiments and 162 batteries to protect Moscow and Krasnodar from Ukrainian drone attacks, citing military intelligence.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia accuse each other of breaking proposed ceasefires ahead of Victory Day parade in Moscow – Europe live
stories.summary: Ukraine proposed an indefinite ceasefire this week, but Kyiv accused Russia of repeatedly violating it ahead of Moscow's Victory Day parade on May 9. Russia threatened a major strike on central Kyiv if Ukraine disrupted the celebrations and urged foreign diplomats to evacuate the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Yemen fuel price hikes deepen hardship as transport costs rise
stories.summary: Rising fuel prices across Yemen are forcing transport drivers to increase fares, deepening financial hardship for passengers already struggling with the country's economic crisis.

stories.title: Does the US Navy have trained kamikaze dolphins operating in the Strait of Hormuz? - explainer
stories.summary: An explainer examines whether the U.S. Navy has deployed trained dolphins in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military has used dolphins for decades to detect underwater obstacles, though they are not typically deployed in active war zones.

stories.title: Bennett, Eisenkot, Liberman merger could secure 61-seat opposition bloc without Arab parties - poll
stories.summary: A new Israeli poll suggests that a merger between Naftali Bennett, Gadi Eisenkot, and Avigdor Liberman's parties could form a 61-seat opposition bloc in the Knesset. Under this scenario, Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition would hold 49 seats, with Arab parties at 10.

stories.title: Russia closes 13 airports as Ukrainian drones strike air traffic control center in Rostov-on-Don
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck an air traffic control center in Rostov-on-Don, Russia, forcing the closure of 13 airports and stranding at least 14,000 passengers. Rostov authorities declared a local state of emergency.

stories.title: The invisible battlefield: Why spectrum dominance is the ultimate weapon - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that dominance of the electromagnetic spectrum has become a decisive factor in modern warfare. As battlefields become saturated with overlapping signals, the ability to achieve spectrum clarity is framed as a critical military capability.

stories.title: Zelensky says Russia violated ceasefire with over 140 strikes and 10 assaults
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Russia violated the ceasefire with over 140 strikes on frontline positions, 10 assault operations, and more than 850 drone strikes as of the morning of Friday, May 8.

stories.title: Trump invites Boeing, Mastercard CEOs to join China trip next week: sources
stories.summary: The Trump administration has invited CEOs from Boeing, Mastercard, Citigroup, and other major U.S. corporations to join a presidential delegation visiting China on May 14–15. The trip was originally scheduled for March 31 but was postponed following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran.

stories.title: Putin's 'paranoia': 'He's fearful of Ukrainians & afraid the elite around him is starting to break'
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Russian President Vladimir Putin's increasingly defensive posture ahead of Russia's May 9 Victory Day celebrations reflects a psychological and military shift in the war. Atlantic Council fellow Melinda Haring contends that Putin is showing signs of fear regarding both Ukrainian resistance and potential fractures within Russia's elite.

stories.title: Prepare for ‘China shock 3.0’ to the global food economy
stories.summary: A consultation paper warns that China is poised to trigger a "China shock 3.0" affecting global food markets as Beijing intensifies efforts to secure its food supply. The report suggests China may reshape global agricultural commodity supply chains, following earlier disruptions to Western manufacturing.

stories.title: The case for peace
stories.summary: The article advocates for peace between India and Pakistan, noting that hawkish voices have dominated since the brief military exchange of May 2025. Progressive voices calling for shared interests of ordinary citizens on both sides have been largely drowned out in the post-conflict environment.

stories.title: China: Calls for death penalty after teen gets life sentence
stories.summary: A 14-year-old in China's Yunnan province has been convicted of intentional homicide and rape and sentenced to life in prison. The victim's family is calling for the death penalty, sparking public debate across China.

stories.title: UK’s Labour set for heavy losses in elections as Reform makes early gains
stories.summary: Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, has secured early victories in local elections across traditional Labour strongholds, signaling significant losses for the ruling Labour party.

stories.title: WHO warns of more hantavirus cases in ‘limited’ outbreak
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned that additional hantavirus cases may emerge in what it described as a "limited" outbreak. Hantavirus is a rare respiratory disease typically transmitted to humans from infected rodents.

stories.title: Eisenkot-Liberman merger would be biggest faction, could boost opposition – survey
stories.summary: Israeli polls suggest a potential merger between the factions of Gadi Eisenkot and Avigdor Liberman could create the largest opposition bloc. Surveys show the Zionist opposition with a narrow majority, and Reservists' party leader Ofer Hendel is reportedly in talks with Benny Gantz about a joint run.

stories.title: Karachi mass transit: a pipe dream
stories.summary: The Frontier Works Organisation has taken over construction of Karachi's University Road, part of the delayed Red Line Bus Rapid Transit project, on an emergency basis with a 90-day deadline. The concept of BRT in Karachi dates back to the 1987-1990 Karachi Mass Transit Study, roughly 25 years before Lahore implemented Pakistan's first BRT in 2013.

stories.title: Lobito Corridor moves into operation as global powers compete for Africa’s minerals
stories.summary: The Lobito Corridor connecting the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Angola's Atlantic port of Lobito has become operational, with trains now transporting copper and cobalt. The infrastructure project reflects growing competition among global powers for access to Africa's critical minerals.

stories.title: U.S. isn’t looking at imminent military action in Cuba despite Trump threats, say sources
stories.summary: US officials indicated that imminent military action against Cuba is not under consideration despite threats from President Trump. The Treasury and State departments announced sanctions after Trump signed an executive order expanding authority to impose penalties on Cuba.

stories.title: Shifting climate tone
stories.summary: Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb acknowledged at the Breathe Pakistan Climate Conference that the country can no longer rely on external aid after climate disasters and must demonstrate domestic seriousness first. The remarks signal a shift in Pakistan's official climate tone, moving beyond post-disaster calls for international donor support.

stories.title: UK elections – early results and takeaways; will Starmer have to resign?
stories.summary: In the United Kingdom's local council elections, the ruling Labour party has suffered early losses while Reform UK and the Green Party have made notable gains, raising questions about Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership.

stories.title: A year ago today: Indian 'kamikaze drones' intercepted
stories.summary: On the first anniversary of the May 2025 India-Pakistan military conflict, reports recall that the crisis was triggered by the April 22 Pahalgam attack in Indian-occupied Kashmir. India launched air strikes on targets in Punjab and Azad Kashmir on May 7, and Pakistan claimed to have downed multiple Indian aircraft in retaliation before both sides eventually stood down.

stories.title: Ukraine marks Day of Remembrance and Victory over Nazism in World War II
stories.summary: Ukraine observed the Day of Remembrance and Victory over Nazism in World War II on May 8.

stories.title: Fate of China’s ex-defence heads shows party won’t allow disloyalty: state media
stories.summary: China's PLA Daily stated that the harsh sentences given to former defence ministers Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu demonstrated Beijing's zero tolerance for disloyalty within the military. The editorial marks the first time an official outlet has publicly accused Li Shangfu of being disloyal to the Chinese Communist Party.

stories.title: British Airways owner issues profit warning over soaring jet fuel costs
stories.summary: International Airlines Group, parent company of British Airways, Aer Lingus, and Iberia, issued a profit warning citing soaring jet fuel costs linked to the Iran war. IAG expects to spend approximately €2 billion more on fuel than originally forecast this year, with total fuel costs rising to around €9 billion.

stories.title: Senate lauds courage, sacrifices of armed forces
stories.summary: Pakistan's Senate passed a resolution on Thursday honoring the armed forces and national unity on the first anniversary of the May 2025 military conflict, referred to as Marka-i-Haq. Information Minister Naqvi claimed India had sought a ceasefire through the US, while Pakistan agreed to a truce after what officials described as teaching a lesson.

stories.title: Hong Kong-based mediation body resolves international maritime dispute
stories.summary: The International Organisation for Mediation, headquartered in Hong Kong, has successfully resolved a maritime dispute between parties from mainland China and Singapore. Secretary General Teresa Cheng Yeuk-wah announced the achievement at a summit, as the organization continues to attract new member states since its launch last year.

stories.title: Indonesia volcano eruption kills 3 hikers, several missing
stories.summary: A volcanic eruption in eastern Indonesia has killed at least three hikers, with rescuers searching for several others still missing on the mountain.

stories.title: Judge releases note purportedly written  by Epstein
stories.summary: A federal judge in New York released a document described as a suicide note purportedly written by Jeffrey Epstein, which was reportedly found by his former cellmate Nicholas Tartaglione. Epstein was found dead in his Manhattan jail cell in August 2019 in a ruling of suicide. US District Judge Kenneth Karas oversaw the release of the handwritten note.

stories.title: Benazir programme cuts child stunting rates: study
stories.summary: An Aga Khan University evaluation found that Pakistan's Benazir Nashonuma Programme significantly reduced child stunting, with rates 22 percent lower at six months and 18 percent lower at one year among beneficiaries. The study also reported a 6 percent reduction in low birth weight, an 11 percent decline in premature births, and a 7 percent decrease in vulnerable newborns.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,130 over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia's total combat losses since February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,339,190 personnel as of May 8, 2026, including 1,130 troops lost in the previous 24 hours.

stories.title: Twin jihadist-claimed attacks kill more than 30 in central Mali
stories.summary: Two attacks in central Mali claimed by Al-Qaeda-linked jihadists have killed more than 30 people, according to local, security, and administrative sources.
