stories.title: Fury in France as national toy revealed to be secretly made in China
stories.summary: French toy company Vulli has been revealed to have secretly moved production of Sophie la Girafe, an iconic French rubber giraffe toy, to China approximately a decade ago. The revelation has sparked a scandal in France, as the toy had long been marketed as a symbol of French craftsmanship.

stories.title: Reports of an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon amid army threats
stories.summary: Several news outlets reported an Israeli airstrike targeting a road between Kfarshouba and Kfarhamam in southern Lebanon. The Israeli army had earlier ordered residents of nearby villages to stay at least 1,000 meters from certain sites. The strikes continue despite a ceasefire that took effect in April.

stories.title: ASEAN leaders meet to discuss plans to ease Iran war impacts
stories.summary: ASEAN leaders are meeting in the Philippines to discuss strategies for mitigating the economic impact of the Iran war. The summit agenda also includes South China Sea territorial disputes and border clashes between Thailand and Cambodia.

stories.title: Every Moment Is a Life: A Gaza anthology curated by Susan Abulhawa is a tour de force
stories.summary: A new anthology titled "Every Moment Is a Life," curated by Susan Abulhawa, compiles writings from Gaza. The collection documents daily life during the conflict, with descriptions of routine existence under wartime conditions.

stories.title: PTI walks out of Senate to protest Bushra’s ‘secret’ hospital visit
stories.summary: PTI senators walked out of Pakistan's Senate after parliamentary leader Syed Ali Zafar raised concerns over the alleged secret nighttime transfer of Bushra Bibi, former PM Imran Khan's spouse, from Adiala jail to a hospital and back without disclosure. Rana Sanaullah advised PTI to pursue the matter through legal channels.

stories.title: No ceasefire. Now Russia’s victory parade is a target for drones.
stories.summary: As Ukraine's ceasefire proposal went unreciprocated by Russia, Ukrainian forces prepared potential drone operations targeting Moscow's May 9 Victory Day parade, prompting Russian air defenses to brace for possible raids.

stories.title: More than 50 Moscow-bound drones intercepted by Russia, mayor says
stories.summary: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that Russian air defense units intercepted more than 50 drones heading toward Moscow over approximately 15 hours on May 8.

stories.title: ‘Saudi pressure’ led US to pause Hormuz project: NBC
stories.summary: NBC News reported that Saudi Arabia pressured U.S. President Trump to pause a naval escort operation called Project Freedom in the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia reportedly suspended U.S. military access to its bases and airspace after being surprised by Trump's unilateral announcement of the operation.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine trade fire, blame despite Victory Day ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine have exchanged fire and mutual accusations of violations despite a declared Victory Day ceasefire, with attacks continuing along the front lines.

stories.title: Nigeria: Reps Approve N2.3trn 2026 FCT Budget
stories.summary: Nigeria's House of Representatives has approved a 2.285 trillion naira budget for the Federal Capital Territory for 2026, with significant allocations to personnel costs, overhead, and capital development projects.

stories.title: Amid Ukraine’s daring assaults, Russia scales back Victory Day celebrations
stories.summary: Russia has scaled back its annual May 9 Victory Day celebrations amid ongoing Ukrainian strikes, reducing military displays that traditionally feature prominently in the national commemorations.

stories.title: Three hikers dead and 10 missing after Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcano erupts
stories.summary: Mount Dukono on Indonesia's Halmahera island erupted, killing three hikers—two foreigners and one resident of nearby Ternate island—and leaving ten others missing. Police said the volcano ejected an ash cloud roughly 10 kilometres high. Seven people descended safely, but the area had been declared off-limits the previous month.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone operators destroy Russian Grad launcher near Huliaipole
stories.summary: FPV drone operators from Ukraine's Asgard Battalion of the 412th Nemesis Brigade destroyed a Russian BM-21 Grad multiple launch rocket system near Huliaipole in the Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: Pakistan remains ‘positive’ as Iran mulls peace offer
stories.summary: Pakistan expressed optimism that the United States and Iran could soon reach a peace agreement after weeks of conflict and a fragile ceasefire in the Persian Gulf. The Foreign Office spokesperson said an agreement was expected "sooner rather than later." Iran's foreign minister spoke with Deputy PM Ishaq Dar about continuing diplomacy and briefed him on a China visit.

stories.title: How South Asian military calculus has changed after May 2025
stories.summary: Analysts assess that the four-day India-Pakistan conflict of May 2025 marked a new phase in South Asian military dynamics, with air power, drones, satellites, and electronic warfare becoming central to battlefield planning. Both sides recognized that conventional escalation remained possible without crossing the nuclear threshold. China now features more prominently in India's military calculations regarding Pakistan.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: U.S. and Iran trade fire, threatening fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: US and Iranian forces exchanged fire near the Strait of Hormuz, threatening a fragile ceasefire. President Trump downplayed the incident and confirmed the United States is negotiating with Iran.

stories.title: As Adversaries Integrate, U.S. Partners Bypass Washington
stories.summary: An analysis describes how Gulf Arab states are being targeted by Iranian drones whose designs were improved through Russian battlefield testing in Ukraine. In response, multiple countries—including the United States—have sought Ukrainian counter-drone expertise, highlighting how U.S. partners are increasingly bypassing Washington to cooperate directly with each other.

stories.title: Chad declares state of emergency in Lake Chad region after Boko Haram attacks
stories.summary: Chad has declared a 20-day state of emergency in the Lake Chad region following a series of deadly attacks attributed to the jihadist group Boko Haram.

stories.title: Shekel hits 33-year-peak, hammering exports, yet policymakers are insistently inactive
stories.summary: The Israeli shekel has reached a 33-year peak, putting pressure on Israeli exporters and tech startups. Companies are reportedly considering hiring abroad and relocating R&D centers out of Israel, raising concerns about long-term economic growth.

stories.title: Hackers block access to platform used by thousands of US schools
stories.summary: Hackers disrupted access to a platform used by thousands of U.S. schools. The group threatened to release all stolen data unless affected schools made contact by May 12.

stories.title: US trade court once again rules Trump tariffs illegal, but issues narrow block
stories.summary: The U.S. Court of International Trade ruled on Friday that President Trump's 10% temporary global tariffs are not justified under the 1970s trade law invoked by the administration. However, the court blocked the duties only for two private importers and the State of Washington, leaving them in effect for all others pending appeal.

stories.title: China confirms it helped Pakistan’s air force during last year’s war with India
stories.summary: China has officially confirmed for the first time that it provided on-site technical support to Pakistan's air force during last year's war with India. State broadcaster CCTV aired an interview with a Chinese engineer from AVIC's Chengdu Aircraft Design and Research Institute who assisted Pakistan during the conflict, during which a Chinese-made fighter downed at least one Indian French-made jet.

stories.title: Iran defends measures in Hormuz Strait at UN
stories.summary: Iran defended its actions in the Strait of Hormuz during a session at the United Nations, asserting that its measures comply with international law. Iranian representatives accused the United States of destabilizing the region.

stories.title: US hosts Ukrainian military medics for battlefield medicine training
stories.summary: Representatives of Ukraine's Medical Forces Command are training in the United States alongside the U.S. Army's 44th Medical Brigade. The program includes field exercises, the international SOMA conference, and a course on prolonged field care.

stories.title: Uganda: Women Leaders Warn of Persistent Political Intimidation After January Elections
stories.summary: Women politicians and activists in Uganda have raised concerns about continued political intimidation, financial barriers, and shrinking civic space following the January 2026 general elections. They warned that these conditions could deter women from seeking leadership roles.

stories.title: Dozens killed in jihadist attacks on villages in central Mali
stories.summary: Jihadist fighters attacked multiple villages in central Mali on Wednesday, killing an estimated 30 to 50 people. The exact death toll remains unclear as sources provide varying figures.

stories.title: Nigeria: Ignore AI-Generated Image Showing Nigerian Activist Omoyele Sowore Shaking Hands With President
stories.summary: Africa Check flagged an AI-generated image circulating online that falsely depicted Nigerian activist Omoyele Sowore shaking hands with the country's president. The organization urged the public to disregard the fabricated image.

stories.title: Could Russia Follow the “Hormuz Playbook” in the Baltic and Black Seas?
stories.summary: An analysis examines how U.S.-Israeli strikes near the Strait of Hormuz effectively shut down tanker traffic — from 56 tankers to just seven within two days — not through a naval blockade but through drone strikes and soaring insurance costs. The article explores whether Russia could replicate this approach in the Baltic and Black Seas.

stories.title: Africa: South Africa Ready to Defend Itself Against Xenophobia Charges At AU
stories.summary: Ghana has asked the African Union to address what it calls xenophobic attacks in South Africa. South African Minister Ronald Lamola has welcomed the opportunity to discuss broader migration issues at the AU forum.

stories.title: World Cup 2026 squad deadlines: Key dates, team lists, final announcements
stories.summary: Al Jazeera has outlined the key dates for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including squad submission deadlines, final team announcements, and rules governing player replacements ahead of the tournament.

stories.title: Southeast Asia’s leaders confront fallout from Iran war at ASEAN summit
stories.summary: Leaders at the ASEAN summit in Southeast Asia are addressing the economic and energy fallout from the ongoing Iran war. The bloc is expected to call for deeper energy cooperation and demand the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Former SriLankan Airlines chief in US$16 million Airbus corruption case found dead
stories.summary: Kapila Chandrasena, former CEO of SriLankan Airlines, was found dead at a relative's home in Colombo. Chandrasena had been charged with conspiring to accept a US$16 million bribe from Airbus in connection with an aircraft purchase and was remanded in March.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland, Israeli Businesses Hold Historic Talks in Addis Ababa
stories.summary: Business leaders and officials from Somaliland and Israel held a historic meeting in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, aimed at strengthening trade and investment cooperation between the two sides.

stories.title: Ukraine marks Day of Remembrance and Victory over Nazism on 8 May
stories.summary: Ukraine observed 8 May as its Day of Remembrance and Victory over Nazism in World War II. The commemoration replaced the Soviet-era 9 May Victory Day following a 2023 law signed by President Zelenskyy.

stories.title: Rwanda: Govt Critic Dies in Prison On Release Day
stories.summary: A Rwandan government critic died in prison on what was supposed to be his release day. Human Rights Watch, based in Nairobi, has called for an investigation into authorities' claims that the death was caused by an overdose.

stories.title: Ukraine warns UN of massive migration crisis triggered by Russian war
stories.summary: Ukraine's delegation participated in the International Migration Review Forum at the United Nations, highlighting the massive migration crisis caused by Russia's ongoing war against the country.

stories.title: South Africa: The Israel/US-Iran War Is Hitting South Africa Hard - Our Oil Dependency Is Why
stories.summary: South Africa is facing economic pressure from the Israel-U.S.-Iran war due to its heavy dependence on imported oil. GroundUp reported that while the government continues investing in oil and gas, renewable energy could reduce vulnerability to foreign price shocks.

stories.title: Kenya: Caution Urged As MET Agency Projects Intensified Rains Amid Deadly Murang'a Landslides
stories.summary: Kenya's meteorological agency has projected intensified rainfall across several regions, prompting the government to urge vigilance in landslide-prone areas. Deadly mudslides in Murang'a County have already displaced hundreds of families.

stories.title: France keeps Kyiv embassy open after Russia’s pre-9 May threat to strike “decision-making centers”
stories.summary: France announced it would keep its embassy in Kyiv open after Russia threatened to strike "decision-making centers" ahead of 9 May. Germany and the European Union also condemned the Russian threats and maintained their diplomatic presence.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran exchanged attacks on Wednesday, raising concerns about the collapse of ceasefire talks. Washington described its strikes as defensive, while Tehran said it fired on U.S. forces in the Strait of Hormuz after an American attack on an Iranian oil tanker.

stories.title: Ethiopian woman's joy at rare quintuplets after 12 years trying for a baby
stories.summary: A 35-year-old Ethiopian woman gave birth to quintuplets after 12 years of trying to conceive. She described being overjoyed at being blessed with five babies at once.

stories.title: NATO-Ukraine Council: War lessons must shape Alliance’s future defenses
stories.summary: A NATO-Ukraine Council session emphasized that Ukraine's security is inseparable from NATO's and that lessons from the war must inform the Alliance's future defense planning. The NATO-Ukraine Joint Analysis, Training and Education Center was cited as an example of mutually beneficial cooperation.

stories.title: US-proposed Iran resolution at UN faces likely vetoes from China, Russia
stories.summary: A US-proposed UN Security Council resolution condemning Iran over its actions in the Strait of Hormuz faces likely vetoes from China and Russia. A Chinese veto would be diplomatically awkward ahead of President Trump's planned visit to Beijing next week.

stories.title: Tesla China posts 36% sales rise, as local rivals’ new models nip at heels
stories.summary: Tesla's Shanghai factory delivered 74,478 vehicles in April, a 36% year-on-year increase driven by local government subsidies and rising EV interest amid the global energy shock. The figures include both mainland China sales and exports to overseas markets.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson accused of 'complete revision of history' as defamation case closes
stories.summary: Actress Rebel Wilson faces accusations of a "complete revision of history" as her defamation case nears its close. The case involves claims that an actress retracted a complaint about sexual harassment by a producer.

stories.title: Iran war day 70: US, Iran trade fire in Hormuz amid ceasefire tensions
stories.summary: On day 70 of the Iran war, U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged fire near the Strait of Hormuz amid ceasefire tensions. Iran accused the United States of breaching the ceasefire, while U.S. Central Command stated its forces were responding to Iranian attacks.

stories.title: Ukraine hits one of Russia’s largest oil refineries — days after Moscow refused Zelenskyy’s ceasefire and struck kindergarten
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck one of Russia's largest oil refineries, a facility that processes around 15 million tons of oil annually. The attack came days after Moscow rejected President Zelenskyy's ceasefire proposal and struck a kindergarten in Ukraine.

stories.title: Japanese bus driver admits he ‘misjudged speed’ before crash that killed teenaged student
stories.summary: Japanese police arrested 68-year-old bus driver Tetsuo Wakayama on suspicion of negligent driving after a crash on a Fukushima expressway killed a high school student. The driver admitted he misjudged his speed, and investigators are examining whether he lacked the proper license for passenger transport.

stories.title: 264 drones, three Russian cities, one burning oil refinery — Russia’s pre-Victory Day night
stories.summary: Overnight on 7–8 May, Ukrainian drones struck targets in Moscow, Yaroslavl, and Rostov-on-Don, igniting a fire at the Yaroslavnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Yaroslavl. Russia claimed it shot down 264 drones during the attacks.

stories.title: Some 1,500 ships trapped in Gulf due to Iran war
stories.summary: Approximately 1,500 ships and 20,000 crew members are trapped in the Persian Gulf due to Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, according to the head of the UN's International Maritime Organisation. The blockade followed the war launched against Iran by Israel and the United States in late February.

stories.title: Ukraine running critically low on air defense missiles after relentless Russian strikes – Air Force spox
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson warned that Ukraine is critically low on missiles for its Patriot, NASAMS, and IRIS-T air defense systems. Intense Russian strikes and difficulties with weapons resupply have depleted stockpiles, leaving some air defense units partially without ammunition.

stories.title: U.S. and Iran trade fire, threatening fragile truce
stories.summary: Iran's military accused the United States of violating the ceasefire by attacking an Iranian oil tanker and another vessel. Tehran said its forces immediately retaliated by firing on American military ships in the area.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson is a ‘fantastical liar’ who ‘made up terrible allegations against multiple people’, court told
stories.summary: In an Australian defamation trial, actor Charlotte MacInnes's legal team accused Rebel Wilson of fabricating allegations against colleagues and revising past events. Wilson, the Pitch Perfect star, has denied the defamation claims brought against her.

stories.title: US military says it carries out retaliatory strikes against Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. military carried out retaliatory strikes against Iranian targets. Iran accused the United States of violating a ceasefire by targeting an Iranian oil tanker and another vessel.

stories.title: US military says it carries out retaliatory strikes against Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced on May 7 that it conducted retaliatory strikes against sites in Iran it said were responsible for attacks on American forces. Washington characterized Tehran's actions as unprovoked hostilities.

stories.title: China scenic spot entertainer sparks debate for giving ‘lollipop kiss’ to female visitors
stories.summary: A performer known as "Little Yellow Fish" at Ge's Fairy Village scenic resort in Jiangxi province, China, sparked controversy for offering visitors "lollipop kisses." The viral videos raised debate about the boundaries of interactive entertainment at tourist attractions.

stories.title: Israel's self-defense cannot be infringed upon, even if US, Iran reach a deal - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that Israel's right to self-defense must be preserved regardless of any U.S.-Iran deal. It raises concern that Jerusalem appears to have no say in the ongoing negotiation process between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Report: US hosting third round of Israel-Lebanon talks on 14 May
stories.summary: The United States will host the third round of Israel-Lebanon negotiations on May 14–15, according to a State Department official and an Israeli official. For the first time, military representatives from both sides are expected to join the delegations.

stories.title: Oil tanker reaches South Korea after passing Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: A Malta-flagged oil tanker carrying one million barrels of crude passed through Iran's Strait of Hormuz blockade and arrived in South Korea. It is the first vessel to reach the country via that route since Tehran effectively closed the waterway following U.S.-Israeli attacks in late February.

stories.title: What we know about the latest exchange of fire between the US and Iran
stories.summary: Despite an exchange of fire between U.S. and Iranian forces in the Strait of Hormuz, President Donald Trump maintained on Thursday that the ceasefire with Iran remained intact. Both sides gave conflicting accounts, each claiming the other fired first.

stories.title: Moldovan parliament restricts use of Russian, prompts opposition walkout
stories.summary: Moldova's pro-European parliamentary majority voted on May 7 to restrict the use of Russian in legislative proceedings. Pro-Russian and right-wing opposition parties walked out in protest against the measure passed in Chisinau.

stories.title: UK Labour dealt blow as far-right Reform surges, Greens gain in local elections
stories.summary: The UK Labour Party under Prime Minister Keir Starmer lost control of at least five councils and more than 100 seats in local elections. The far-right Reform party, led by Nigel Farage, made significant gains, as did the Green Party. Farage described the results as a historic shift in British politics.

stories.title: ‘A calamity’: Why is a record heatwave sweeping South Asia?
stories.summary: A record heatwave is sweeping across South Asia, with India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh experiencing temperatures well above seasonal averages. The extreme heat has raised concerns about public health and infrastructure across the region.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims 13 attacks on Israeli military
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it carried out 13 attacks on Israeli forces and military positions in southern Lebanon using drones, artillery shells, and guided weapons. The group said the strikes targeted troop gatherings, military vehicles, and positions in response to escalating Israeli attacks in Lebanon.

stories.title: UN experts warn US fuel blockade in Cuba puts human rights at risk
stories.summary: United Nations experts warned on May 7 that a U.S. fuel blockade on Cuba, imposed by executive order in January, amounts to energy starvation. They said the policy poses grave consequences for development and human rights on the Caribbean island.

stories.title: 9 Singaporeans among hikers trapped by Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcanic eruption
stories.summary: Indonesian authorities were working to rescue 20 hikers, including nine Singaporeans, after Mount Dukono erupted on Halmahera Island in North Maluku province on Friday. The eruption sent volcanic ash as high as 10 kilometers into the sky. Indonesia's Geology Agency maintained the alert status at the third-highest level.

stories.title: Azerbaijanis collecting signatures in support of Crimean political prisoners
stories.summary: Journalists, public figures, and members of Azerbaijan's intelligentsia have launched a signature campaign supporting Crimean political prisoners illegally detained by Russia. The appeal is expected to be submitted to Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev.

stories.title: Latmiya: Inside the Ashura rituals shaping Iran’s wartime narrative
stories.summary: In Iran, traditional Ashura mourning rituals incorporating Karbala symbolism are being reinterpreted with nationalist themes as part of the country's wartime messaging. Performances in darkened halls across the country have become a prominent feature of Iran's wartime atmosphere.

stories.title: Eurovision hopes 70th anniversary celebration outshines Israel controversy
stories.summary: The 70th anniversary Eurovision Song Contest faces its largest-ever boycott over the continued inclusion of Israel amid the ongoing conflict. Organizers hope the milestone celebration will outshine the controversy surrounding Israel's participation.

stories.title: Ex-prisoners recount abuse in Israeli detention centres
stories.summary: Former Palestinian detainees have publicly recounted experiences of torture and sexual violence during their time held in Israeli detention centres.

stories.title: US trade court rules Trump tariffs illegal, but issues narrow block
stories.summary: A U.S. trade court ruled that tariffs imposed by President Trump were illegal but issued only a narrow block on their enforcement. One judge said it was premature to grant victory to the small business plaintiffs who brought the case.

stories.title: Energy crisis dominates Asean summit, forcing long-standing issues to back burner
stories.summary: The global energy crisis, driven by surging fuel costs from the Iran war, dominated the three-day ASEAN summit in Cebu, Philippines, pushing longstanding regional issues to the background. A Thailand-Cambodia joint statement of solidarity was noted as a bright spot. Analysts described fuel costs as the "defining issue" for Southeast Asian leaders.

stories.title: The WW2 spy killed in mystery crash days after the war ended
stories.summary: Jacques Vaillant de Guélis, a World War II spy born in Cardiff, served as a French operative behind enemy lines. He died in a mysterious crash just days after the war ended.

stories.title: Explosion hits Netherlands' largest political party's headquarters, police say
stories.summary: An explosion damaged the headquarters of D66, the largest party in the Dutch parliament, in Amsterdam on the evening of May 7. Local police reported no injuries from the blast. An investigation is under way.

stories.title: Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon kill at least 12, including children
stories.summary: Israeli attacks on Thursday killed at least 12 people in southern Lebanon, including two children and a paramedic, according to Lebanon's Ministry of Health. The overall death toll since early March has risen to 2,727, with 8,438 others wounded.

stories.title: Northern Irish police charge man in connection with March police station attack
stories.summary: Northern Irish police announced on May 7 that they charged a 48-year-old man in connection with an attack on a police station that occurred in March. Further details about the specific station and the nature of the charges were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Iran can survive the US blockade on Hormuz for months: Report
stories.summary: A confidential CIA analysis reported by the Washington Post indicates Iran could withstand the U.S. naval blockade on the Strait of Hormuz for at least three to four months. The assessment also found that Tehran retains significant ballistic missile capabilities despite intense bombardment of its sites.

stories.title: Iran's state broadcaster says US military naval units came under missile fire after US attack on Iranian oil tanker
stories.summary: Iran's state broadcaster reported that US naval units near the Strait of Hormuz came under Iranian missile fire after US forces attacked an Iranian oil tanker. The report cited an unnamed Iranian military official.

stories.title: Global Sumud Flotilla activists report sexual abuse while in Israeli custody
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla reported that activists detained by Israeli forces during a Gaza-bound aid mission were subjected to sexual violence and physical abuse. The group said testimonies from at least four individuals described anal penetration, physical assault, and systematic degradation while in Israeli custody.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran ceasefire still in place after exchange of fire in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States and Iran exchanged fire in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran accusing Washington of violating the ceasefire by targeting an oil tanker and striking coastal areas. U.S. President Donald Trump stated the ceasefire remains in place despite the incident.

stories.title: Trump says ceasefire still in effect, but Iran ‘better sign agreement fast’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump declared the ceasefire with Iran still in effect following clashes in the Strait of Hormuz, while urging Tehran to quickly finalize a deal.

stories.title: US response to hantavirus outbreak could be hindered by withdrawal from WHO - NBC
stories.summary: Health experts warned that the US withdrawal from the World Health Organization could hinder the country's response to a hantavirus outbreak. Both the CDC and the WHO may face disadvantages from the lack of cooperation between the two organizations.

stories.title: Shanghai’s changing expats, Hong Kong trail sign fallout: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: Two former Chinese defense ministers, Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu, were handed suspended death sentences after being convicted of corruption. This was among several major stories highlighted in the South China Morning Post's weekly roundup covering Hong Kong, mainland China, and the wider Asia region.

stories.title: Labour losses pile up in England local elections as Reform UK makes gains
stories.summary: Reform UK emerged as the dominant winner in northeast England local elections, likely pushing Labour into opposition in Hartlepool. Labour lost councillors across multiple councils including Chorley, Wigan, Redditch, and Tamworth, underscoring the electoral challenge facing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's party.

stories.title: U.S. trade court rules against Trump's global 10% tariff
stories.summary: The US Court of International Trade ruled 2-1 against President Trump's global 10 percent tariff policy. The ruling currently blocks the tariffs for two companies and Washington state but could set a precedent for broader challenges.

stories.title: ‘Being human helps’: despite rise of AI is there still hope for Europe’s translators?
stories.summary: The article examines the impact of AI translation tools on European literary translators, noting that while neural-network-powered services like DeepL have disrupted the profession, human translators remain valued. French translator Yoann Gentric tested AI on a passage from Dana Spiotta's novel and found limitations in machine output.

stories.title: Why today’s ‘unravelled’ international order echoes the lead-up to WWI
stories.summary: Former US National Security Council senior director Thomas Wright warned that the unraveling of the post-Cold War international order has created conditions resembling a pre-war environment, echoing the lead-up to World War I. Wright, who served in the Biden administration, said a "familiar pattern" of great-power tension is taking shape.

stories.title: UAE says its engaging with missile and drone threats from Iran
stories.summary: The UAE Ministry of Defense stated that Emirati defense systems are intercepting missile and drone attacks originating from Iran. The ministry said sounds heard across the country resulted from ongoing interception efforts.

stories.title: Jewish real estate mogul equates Mamdani’s ‘tax the rich’ with ‘from the river to the sea’
stories.summary: Jewish real estate developer Steven Roth compared New York City Council Member Zohran Mamdani's "tax the rich" proposal to the anti-Israel slogan "from the river to the sea." His remarks came in response to a video by the NYC mayor announcing a proposed pied-à-terre tax that referenced Roth's $238 million penthouse.

stories.title: Health officials race to find dozens who left hantavirus-stricken ship after 1st fatality
stories.summary: Health officials are searching for up to 40 people who disembarked from a cruise ship affected by a hantavirus outbreak without undergoing contact tracing in late April, following the first reported fatality. Israel's Health Ministry stated there are no cases of hantavirus in the country.

stories.title: US and Iran trade fire, threatening fragile truce
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran exchanged fire, threatening their fragile ceasefire. President Trump warned he would "knock out" Tehran if Iran does not agree to a deal.

stories.title: Office of Military Ombudsman launches contact center in test mode
stories.summary: Ukraine's Office of the Military Ombudsman launched a contact center in test mode following a selection and training process for operators. The center is designed to handle inquiries and complaints related to military service.

stories.title: US official claims attacks on Iran a 'defensive' move: Report
stories.summary: U.S. military strikes on Thursday hit Iranian drone launch sites, coastal defense cruise missile installations, and radars at locations including Qeshm, Bandar Abbas, and Garuk, according to the Wall Street Journal. A U.S. official described the attacks as defensive, claiming Iran had planned to target American warships from those sites.

stories.title: North Korea to move artillery capable of striking Seoul to border with South
stories.summary: North Korea announced it would deploy new long-range artillery systems capable of striking South Korea's capital region this year and would commission its first naval destroyer in coming weeks. The announcement followed South Korea's revelation that North Korea's revised constitution has dropped all references to Korean unification, consistent with Kim Jong-un's two-state policy.

stories.title: Tai Po probe: housing checking unit admits ‘blind spots’ amid ‘robotic’ workflow criticism
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Home Affairs Department and the Housing Bureau's Independent Checking Unit testified at a public hearing into the city's deadliest blaze in decades, related to the Tai Po district. Officials acknowledged "blind spots" in their workflow and faced criticism over "robotic" procedures during the fourth round of evidential hearings.

stories.title: Oil prices jump as US, Iran trade fire in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged after U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil transit.

stories.title: GW University investigates possible chemical attack on student-led Israel festival
stories.summary: George Washington University launched an investigation into a possible chemical attack targeting attendees of a student-led Israel festival on campus. The university said it will examine whether individuals were targeted based on their Jewish faith.

stories.title: China marks milestone with first home-certified airship pilots
stories.summary: China's Civil Aviation Administration issued domestic commercial airship pilot licenses to four pilots for the first time, marking a milestone for the country's growing low-altitude economy. The Aviation Industry Corporation of China said the achievement addresses a critical talent shortage in the sector.

stories.title: Chinese J-35 stealth jets set to give Pakistan edge over India in fifth-generation tech
stories.summary: The Pakistan Air Force announced plans to acquire Chinese Chengdu J-10C fighters and upgrade its JF-17 fleet, one year after the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict. The PAF also confirmed signing an initial agreement for the acquisition of fifth-generation Shenyang J-35 stealth fighters from China, without disclosing further details.

stories.title: Iran opens fire on US after Iranian oil tanker struck, state media reports
stories.summary: Iran's state broadcaster, citing an unnamed military official, reported that Tehran opened fire on US forces near the Strait of Hormuz after the US military struck an Iranian oil tanker.

stories.title: Shakira teases official 2026 FIFA World Cup song
stories.summary: Colombian singer Shakira released a preview of "Dai Dai," the official 2026 FIFA World Cup song featuring Nigerian Afrobeats artist Burna Boy.

stories.title: US-proposed Iran resolution at UN faces likely vetoes from China, Russia
stories.summary: The United States urged UN member states to support a resolution demanding Iran stop attacks and mining of the Strait of Hormuz. Diplomats indicated that China and Russia are likely to veto the measure.

stories.title: Hamas operatives are being trained in Turkey to launch attacks against Israel - KAN
stories.summary: According to a report by Israel's KAN broadcaster, Hamas operatives are being trained in Turkey to carry out attacks against Israel. The operatives reportedly train at public shooting clubs in civilian clothing, practicing small arms, tactics, and drone operations.

stories.title: The Palestinian shot dead hours before his son was born
stories.summary: Nayef Samaro, a 26-year-old Palestinian man, was shot and killed just hours before his son was born.

stories.title: Ukraine and Finland sign agreement on equipment for gas engine power plants
stories.summary: Ukraine and Finland signed a framework agreement for the supply of equipment for gas engine power plants, aimed at bolstering Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Asean members warm towards Myanmar, raising hopes it could come in from the cold
stories.summary: Some ASEAN members are signaling a willingness to ease Myanmar's isolation five years after the military coup. ASEAN Secretary General Kao Kim Hourn said Southeast Asian foreign ministers agreed to hold a virtual meeting with Myanmar's counterpart during the association's summit in the Philippines.

stories.title: United States imposes new sanctions on Cuban military conglomerate GAESA amid escalating pressure
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced new sanctions against GAESA, the Cuban Armed Forces-linked conglomerate controlling roughly 40 percent of Cuba's economy. The sanctions were issued under Executive Order 14404, signed by President Trump on May 1, targeting those responsible for political repression and threats to US national security.

stories.title: FBI: Austin bar shooter was motivated by support for Iran, but acted alone
stories.summary: The FBI determined that Ndiaga Diagne, 53, who carried out a deadly shooting at an Austin, Texas bar, was motivated by support for Iran but acted alone. Diagne wore an Iranian flag T-shirt and a sweatshirt reading "Property of Allah" during the attack, which occurred hours after U.S.-Israeli strikes killed Ali Khamenei.

stories.title: Lula and Trump declare bilateral relationship reset after three-hour meeting at the White House
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and U.S. President Donald Trump met for nearly three hours at the White House on Thursday. Both leaders declared a reset of bilateral relations after one of the most severe diplomatic crises between the two countries in two centuries, agreeing to establish channels for trade, security, and regional cooperation.

stories.title: Openness, not isolation, is the bedrock of the West
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the West's strength lies in institutional resilience and the ability to attract and integrate global talent, rather than solely in military alliances or economic power.

stories.title: Star-crossed bromance? Bennett and Lapid aim to unify Israel, but electoral heavens may not align
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and former Prime Minister Yair Lapid are reportedly seeking to present a unified front ahead of elections. However, analysts note Bennett faces trust deficits while Lapid is perceived as left-wing, potentially limiting their ability to unseat Benjamin Netanyahu.

stories.title: Trump says US is negotiating with Iran, despite fire exchange
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters that Washington is continuing negotiations with Iran despite a fresh exchange of fire between US and Iranian forces.

stories.title: Report: Rubio OKed $25.8 billion sale of interceptors and other arms to Israel, Mideast nations
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio approved a $25.8 billion arms sale including interceptors to Israel and other Middle Eastern nations, according to Bloomberg. The amount is roughly three times larger than the originally reported $8.6 billion figure.

stories.title: First counts confirm Reform UK's advance in Labour heartlands and open the door to a leadership crisis
stories.summary: Early results from local elections held across the United Kingdom confirmed significant gains for Nigel Farage's Reform UK party in traditional Labour strongholds in northern England. The outcome triggered public expressions of discontent within Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party, with analysts describing it as one of the ruling party's worst electoral nights since taking office in July 2024.

stories.title: 'They kept shooting at us while I kept driving': Female soldiers recall near-death Gaza incident
stories.summary: Three female Israeli soldiers, including Maj. Nurit Rokach, recounted an April 2025 ambush in Gaza that left two of them severely wounded. The incident exposed failures in deploying the soldiers without a convoy escort.

stories.title: As US and Iran weigh peace deal, stranded seafarers wait in limbo
stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Gulf region due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, as the United States and Iran continue to weigh a potential peace deal.

stories.title: IS-linked mother and daughter charged with crimes against humanity including slavery face Melbourne court
stories.summary: Kawsar Ahmad, 53, and her daughter Zeinab Ahmad, 31, were arrested at Melbourne airport and charged with crimes against humanity, including slavery offences, allegedly committed during Islamic State's rule in Syria. Separately, Janai Safar, 32, faced charges in Sydney that included joining a terrorist organisation.

stories.title: Russian court sentences Ukrainian citizen to 22 years in prison
stories.summary: A court in Rostov-on-Don, Russia, sentenced captured Ukrainian citizen Roman Kliukin to 22 years in prison. Russia's Southern District Military Court convicted him on charges of espionage and participation in a terrorist organization.

stories.title: Hong Kong needs the people’s wisdom for its 5-year plan to succeed
stories.summary: Hong Kong is preparing its first five-year economic plan to align with China's national 15th five-year plan. Officials aim to combine the city's market dynamism with strategic planning to drive future development.

stories.title: Al-Qaeda-linked attacks in central Mali kill more than 30 people
stories.summary: More than 30 people were killed in two attacks in central Mali on Thursday attributed to JNIM, an al-Qaeda-linked militant group. The strikes come amid renewed violence in the West African nation following recent coordinated assaults on military positions.

stories.title: Trump: Hormuz clash a ‘trifle,’ deal with Iran ‘might not happen, but could happen any day’
stories.summary: President Trump characterized the US-Iran clash in the Strait of Hormuz as a "trifle" and said a deal with Iran "might not happen, but could happen any day." Separately, a man pleaded guilty to assaulting US Representative Ilhan Omar.

stories.title: Falklands brace for Middle East fallout with fuel, shipping and supply contingencies
stories.summary: The Falkland Islands are preparing fuel, shipping, and supply contingencies in response to the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and its impact on global oil distribution. A local lawmaker noted the islands sit "at the tail end of global distribution," making them particularly vulnerable to supply chain disruptions.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky warns against attending Russia’s parade as Moscow repeats threats
stories.summary: Moscow unilaterally declared a ceasefire from May 8 to 10 in its war against Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned world leaders against attending Russia's upcoming military parade, as Moscow continued to issue threats.

stories.title: Humanoids, robots to drive next chapter of China’s manufacturing dominance: Morgan Stanley
stories.summary: A Morgan Stanley report predicts China will leverage the humanoid and robotics market to strengthen its global manufacturing dominance over the next five to ten years. Analysts drew parallels to China's rise in the electric vehicle sector.

stories.title: US military says it intercepted Iranian attacks in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States and Iran exchanged fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. Washington said it intercepted Iranian attacks and struck back at military targets, while Tehran reported retaliatory action. The exchange strained a fragile ceasefire and heightened regional tensions.

stories.title: Insurgents kill dozens, including civilians, in central Mali attacks, sources say
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked insurgents attacked two villages in central Mali on Wednesday night, killing approximately 50 people. The dead included members of pro-government self-defense forces and civilians, according to three sources who spoke to Reuters.

stories.title: Was China’s ‘fireworks capital’ rushing its July 4 orders when deadly blast hit?
stories.summary: An explosion at a fireworks factory in Liuyang, Hunan province — known as China's "fireworks capital" — killed 26 people and injured 61. Industry insiders said factories in the area were in peak production to fill overseas orders, including for US July 4th celebrations.

stories.title: China tourist dies after cliff swing fall as safety rope was loose despite her warnings to staff
stories.summary: A young woman died after falling from a cliff swing ride in Huaying, Sichuan province, China, after staff reportedly ignored her warnings that the safety rope was loose. The incident drew over 200 million views on Chinese social media and prompted calls for stronger safety oversight of adventure activities.

stories.title: Israeli settler to face trial over attack on nun in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Yona Simcha Schreiber, an Israeli settler residing in the West Bank, will stand trial for an assault on a nun in Jerusalem. The attack was reportedly motivated by hostility toward a religious group.

stories.title: Trump-ally Roger Stone condemned for providing lobbying services to Myanmar’s military junta
stories.summary: U.S. lobbyist Roger Stone, a longtime ally of President Donald Trump, has drawn condemnation for accepting $50,000 per month to lobby on behalf of Myanmar's military junta. Myanmar's military government has been internationally isolated since its 2021 coup and faces accusations of atrocities potentially amounting to war crimes.

stories.title: UK to summon Chinese ambassador after spying convictions
stories.summary: Two men were convicted in a British court on May 7 of spying on behalf of Hong Kong and ultimately China. In response, the UK government announced plans to summon the Chinese ambassador over the espionage case.

stories.title: Trump says ceasefire is still in place despite attacks from Iran
stories.summary: President Trump stated that a ceasefire with Iran remains in place despite recent exchanges of fire. No additional details were provided.

stories.title: Police officers said to beat, break nose and arrest Arab prosecutor over noise complaint
stories.summary: Israeli police officers allegedly beat and broke the nose of an Arab prosecutor from the State Attorney's Office during a noise complaint incident, then arrested him. Police claimed the lawyer attacked officers, which he and coworkers denied. The Department of Internal Police Investigations has opened a probe.

stories.title: Suspect in deadly Colorado firebombing pleads guilty to all state charges
stories.summary: The suspect accused of throwing gasoline bombs at a pro-Israel rally in Boulder, Colorado, last year pleaded guilty on Thursday to all state charges. The firebombing killed one person and injured more than a dozen others.

stories.title: Authorities detain curator of Russian disinformation network in Argentina
stories.summary: Argentine authorities detained Russian citizen Dmitry Novikov, identified as a leader of the Russian influence network known as La Compañía. He was arrested for activities targeting Argentine state institutions and the government of President Javier Milei.

stories.title: Russia’s internet regulator declines to block ‘YaPlakal’ site, says court ruling failed to identify prohibited content
stories.summary: Russia's internet regulator Roskomnadzor declined to block the popular Russian website YaPlakal, stating that a court ruling had failed to identify specific prohibited content on the site.

stories.title: Russia’s unilateral ceasefire takes effect as Moscow threatens missile strike on Kyiv if Ukraine disrupts May 9 celebrations
stories.summary: Russia's self-declared unilateral ceasefire in its war against Ukraine took effect at midnight on May 8 and is set to last until May 10. Moscow threatened a missile strike on Kyiv if Ukraine disrupts Russia's May 9 Victory Day celebrations.

stories.title: Some 1,500 ships trapped in Gulf due to Iran conflict, says UN maritime organisation
stories.summary: The United Nations' maritime organization reported that approximately 1,500 ships are trapped in the Gulf due to the ongoing Iran conflict. Around 20,000 crew members remain stranded aboard their vessels.

stories.title: US strikes Iran following clash in Strait of Hormuz; Trump says ceasefire still in effect
stories.summary: The US carried out strikes against Iran following a clash in the Strait of Hormuz, with President Trump calling them a "love tap" while asserting the ceasefire remains in effect. Iran accused the US of violating the truce but said the situation had returned to normal.

stories.title: As the US Army adds drones to formations, here’s how one base trains its operators
stories.summary: Fort Stewart in Georgia established the Marne Unmanned Center of Excellence to train soldiers on drone operations. The effort comes as the U.S. Army integrates unmanned aerial systems into its formations.

stories.title: Can Vietnam’s bureaucracy reform boost investment amid growth threats?
stories.summary: Vietnam's leadership under General-Secretary and President To Lam has set an annual growth target of 10 percent until 2030 and is pursuing bureaucratic reforms to boost investment. Analysts say the reforms may not fully offset damage from US tariffs and a fuel crisis threatening the country's growth.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says ceasefire still ‘in effect’ as Iran, US clash
stories.summary: Iran accused the United States of violating an existing ceasefire by targeting Iranian vessels and conducting strikes on coastal areas. President Trump maintained that the ceasefire remains in effect despite the clashes.

stories.title: Fedorov holds series of meetings in Sweden to increase assistance to Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov held meetings in Sweden focused on increasing the quantity and quality of military assistance to Ukraine. Discussions included preparatory work for signing contracts related to Saab JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets.

stories.title: Trump says US destroyers passed Hormuz under fire, no damage
stories.summary: President Trump stated that three US Navy destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz under fire and reported no damage to American vessels. Trump claimed significant damage was inflicted on Iranian attackers during the passage.

stories.title: Lebanon: Israel attacks kill 12 in Nabatieh, Marjayoun districts
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out attacks in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh and Marjayoun districts, killing at least 12 people. The strikes followed an earlier Israeli assault on Beirut that killed a Hezbollah commander.

stories.title: US congressman says pro-Israel groups behind 95 percent of funding against him
stories.summary: Kentucky Congressman Thomas Massie said that at least 95 percent of the funding backing his main Republican primary opponent comes from pro-Israel lobbying groups. Massie has been a vocal critic of foreign aid and US involvement in overseas conflicts.

stories.title: 'I'd rather live in hiding in the US than return to Somalia'
stories.summary: Somali migrants in Minnesota continue to face fear and uncertainty despite receiving a legal reprieve from deportation. Some say they would rather live in hiding in the United States than return to Somalia.

stories.title: AI Holocaust content is booming. Is it all ‘slop’ - or a solution for fading firsthand memory?
stories.summary: The growth of AI-generated Holocaust-related content is raising concerns among researchers and educators. While AI technology offers new possibilities for preserving memory, experts warn it also serves as a tool for Holocaust distortion.

stories.title: Are global alliances fracturing?
stories.summary: Global alliances including NATO and OPEC are reportedly experiencing heightened strain, raising questions about the durability of long-standing international partnerships.

stories.title: Solomon Islands to get new leader after PM ousted in no-confidence vote
stories.summary: Solomon Islands Prime Minister Jeremiah Manele was removed from power after losing a no-confidence vote in parliament. The ousting followed months of political upheaval in the Pacific nation, which is regarded as one of China's closest regional partners. Parliament was adjourned to arrange the election of a new prime minister.

stories.title: US and Iran exchange fire as Trump says war will ‘be over quickly’
stories.summary: U.S. forces launched retaliatory strikes against Iranian military facilities on Thursday after Iran fired missiles and drones at three U.S. Navy vessels. President Trump stated the war would "be over quickly."

stories.title: Islamic State-linked Australian women charged with keeping slave in Syria
stories.summary: Two Australian women were charged in Melbourne with keeping a female slave after traveling to Syria in 2014 to support Islamic State. The women returned to Australia from a Syrian detention camp and were arrested upon landing at Melbourne International Airport.

stories.title: Finance ministry, SBP show optimism over economic growth amid expected $1.2bn tranche from IMF
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ministry of Finance and the State Bank of Pakistan expressed optimism about economic growth and meeting fiscal targets despite regional instability. The IMF is expected to approve disbursement of over $1.2 billion, with another mission scheduled to visit on May 15 for next year's budget formulation.

stories.title: Polish diplomats do not plan to leave Kyiv on May 9 – Polish embassy
stories.summary: The Polish embassy in Kyiv stated that its diplomats do not plan to leave the Ukrainian capital on May 9. The embassy said it has operated under established security procedures since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion and will not change its operations.

stories.title: Mali: Double Al-Qaeda-linked attacks kill more than 30
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM carried out twin attacks on the villages of Korikori and Gomossogou in Mali's Mopti region, killing more than 30 people and marking an escalation of the ongoing insurgency.

stories.title: Can Trump’s push for a deal with Iran turn a tactical pause into lasting peace?
stories.summary: The Trump administration appears to be exploring diplomatic options to resolve its confrontation with Iran after weeks of military escalation and economic pressure. President Trump's decision to pause a planned naval escort operation in the Strait of Hormuz has sparked debate over whether Washington is shifting toward negotiation or recalibrating its pressure campaign.

stories.title: Huge fire at Mexican fair kills five people
stories.summary: At least five people were killed when a massive fire broke out at a fairground in Villahermosa, in southeastern Mexico.

stories.title: War update: 156 combat clashes on front line
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 156 combat clashes along the front line. On the Pokrovsk sector, Russian forces launched more than 20 attacks on Ukrainian positions and lost 95 troops during assaults on defensive lines.

stories.title: Explainer-Can Trump pull thousands of US troops out of Germany?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany as disagreements over the Iran war deepen between his administration and NATO allies in Europe.

stories.title: Trump gives EU ultimatum deadline to approve trade deal with US
stories.summary: President Trump issued an ultimatum to the European Union, setting a deadline for it to approve a trade deal with the United States. The move came as a US trade court ruled that his global tariff policy violated US law.

stories.title: Jewish leaders decry ‘inadequate’ plea deal for California man guilty of pro-Israel protester’s death
stories.summary: Loay Alnaji pleaded guilty to all charges, including involuntary manslaughter, in connection with the death of a pro-Israel protester in California. Under the plea deal, he will serve no more than one year in county jail. Jewish community leaders criticized the agreement as inadequate.

stories.title: Two men found guilty of spying on Hong Kong dissidents in UK for China
stories.summary: Two men were found guilty in the United Kingdom of spying on prominent Hong Kong pro-democracy dissidents based in Britain on behalf of China.

stories.title: Lula won’t sideline China or anyone in rare earths, tells Trump refining stays in Brazil
stories.summary: Brazilian President Lula told President Trump that Brazil's rare earth reserves are open to investment from China and all nations, provided mineral refining takes place on Brazilian soil. Lula resisted US pressure to exclude Beijing from critical mineral supply chains.

stories.title: US says it intercepted Iranian attacks, launched strikes in Hormuz
stories.summary: US Central Command said American naval forces intercepted a coordinated Iranian assault involving missiles, drones, and small boats as the destroyers USS Truxtun, USS Rafael Peralta, and USS Mason transited the Strait of Hormuz toward the Gulf of Oman. CENTCOM reported no US assets were struck and said retaliatory strikes were launched.

stories.title: China’s move to cut EV payment cycles may push weaker carmakers out: S&P
stories.summary: Beijing's new regulations shortening payment cycles in the automotive sector are expected to increase borrowing pressure on China's carmakers. S&P Global Ratings warns the move could accelerate the exit of weaker, debt-laden manufacturers. The change comes as more than 100 mainland assemblers face softening consumer demand and intense price competition.

stories.title: Two men found guilty of spying on Hong Kong dissidents in Britain for China
stories.summary: Two men were convicted in Britain of spying on prominent Hong Kong pro-democracy dissidents for China. The individuals targeted activists now based in the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Ukrainian Air Force explains low effectiveness of some interceptor drone crews by their lack of combat experience
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Air Force acknowledged that some interceptor drone crews have yet to shoot down a Russian Shahed drone. Officials attributed the low effectiveness to the units being newly created and still gaining operational experience.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on Iraq's deputy oil minister, militias over Iran support
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department on May 7 imposed sanctions on Iraq's deputy oil minister and Iraqi militias for their support of Iran. The measures target individuals and groups Washington accuses of facilitating Iranian interests in Iraq.

stories.title: US carries out strikes on Iran, Strait of Hormuz, in retaliation for Tehran targeting US destroyers
stories.summary: The US military carried out strikes on the Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas and Qeshm island in retaliation for Tehran targeting US destroyers. Iranian media characterized the US actions as hostile, while a Fox News reporter cited a senior US official confirming the strikes.

stories.title: Pakistan turns down two lowest evaluated LNG bids
stories.summary: Pakistan's state-run PLL rejected the two lowest LNG bids from BP Singapore at $17.28 per mmBtu and TotalEnergies at $16.98 per mmBtu for deliveries scheduled in mid and late May. Seven total bids were received against urgent tenders for two cargo windows.

stories.title: US military says it carried out retaliatory strikes over ‘unprovoked hostilities’ by Iran
stories.summary: The US military carried out retaliatory strikes on Iranian military facilities after what it called unprovoked hostilities by Tehran. Iran's joint military command accused the US of violating a ceasefire by targeting an Iranian oil tanker and striking civilian areas near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Hundreds of Iranian nationals detained by ICE amid June 2025 attack on Iran
stories.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained hundreds of Iranian nationals during the June 2025 US attack on Iran, according to government data obtained by the National Iranian American Council via a FOIA request. ICE arrested 220 Iranians in June and 80 in July 2025.

stories.title: Ukraine’s EU membership: when, not if—but 2027 is unrealistic, says veteran MEP
stories.summary: A veteran Lithuanian MEP who negotiated his own country's EU accession said Ukraine's EU membership remains a matter of when, not if, but called the proposed 2027 timeline unrealistic. He noted that the procedural machinery for accession has not yet begun moving.

stories.title: Russian forces drop aerial bombs on residential district of Kramatorsk, killing one person, injuring another
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped three FAB-250 high-explosive aerial bombs on a residential neighborhood in Kramatorsk, in Ukraine's Donetsk region. The strikes killed one person and injured another.

stories.title: Elections 2026 live: counting under way after votes in England, Scotland and Wales
stories.summary: Votes were cast across England, Scotland, and Wales on May 7 in local, mayoral, and parliamentary elections. Counting began with the first English results expected overnight. Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy acknowledged the election cycle had been tough for Labour.

stories.title: Radev sets out plans for new Bulgarian government after election win
stories.summary: Pro-Russian eurosceptic Rumen Radev announced plans for a new Bulgarian government after receiving a mandate from the president in Sofia. He pledged to lower prices and restore stability following mass protests that toppled the previous cabinet.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of violating ceasefire by targeting civilian areas and ships on strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran accused the United States of violating a ceasefire by targeting two ships near the Strait of Hormuz and striking civilian areas. The U.S. military maintained its strikes were retaliatory, directed at sites responsible for what it called unprovoked attacks on American forces by Tehran.

stories.title: US, Gulf allies press UN to condemn Iran over Hormuz attacks
stories.summary: The United States and Gulf allies are pushing for a United Nations resolution condemning Iran over its activities in the Strait of Hormuz. China and Russia are widely expected to veto the measure.

stories.title: Russia is now dropping FPV drones with explosives from bigger “Gerbera” carriers
stories.summary: Russia is deploying larger carrier drones called "Gerbera" to drop first-person-view explosive drones on Ukrainian targets. One such FPV drone with an explosive payload was found on the roof of a high-rise apartment building more than 30 kilometers from the Russian border.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference concludes with calls for climate resilience, coordinated action
stories.summary: The second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference, organized by Dawn Media, concluded in Islamabad after two days of discussions. Participants including policymakers, international organizations, and climate experts addressed climate resilience, adaptation, energy transition, water security, and equitable policymaking for Pakistan.

stories.title: Smotrich announces uprooting of 3,000 trees planted by Palestinians in northern West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced the uprooting of 3,000 trees planted by Palestinians in the northern West Bank. Israel's Civil Administration said the removal would enable the creation of a new settlement. Three Palestinians were reportedly injured in a related settler attack.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz discusses regional situation with Qatari counterpart: PMO
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke by phone with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani about the regional situation. Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to supporting peace efforts in the region, following Sharif's recent visit to Doha.

stories.title: Thousands of North Koreans fought for Russia. A memorial hints at the death toll
stories.summary: An estimated 11,000 North Korean soldiers were sent to fight alongside Russian forces in the war against Ukraine. A newly identified memorial site offers evidence of the significant casualties North Korean troops have sustained.

stories.title: Videos show interceptions over the skies of Tehran
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that air defense systems were activated in western Tehran after multiple explosions were heard over the city.

stories.title: Hungry to sell, UAE slips hidden oil tankers through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The UAE's Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) has been covertly moving oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz to maintain exports. The shipments carry the risk of Iranian attacks amid ongoing tensions in the waterway.

stories.title: Hundreds of Iranian nationals detained by ICE amid June 2025 attack on Iran
stories.summary: More than 500 Iranian nationals were held in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention as late as December 2025, amid a wartime crackdown linked to the June 2025 US attack on Iran.

stories.title: Anti-Kremlin Pussy Riot demonstrate in Venice against Russia's Biennale return
stories.summary: Dozens of Pussy Riot activists staged a protest in Venice on May 7, waving Ukrainian flags and chanting against President Vladimir Putin. The demonstration opposed Russia's return to the Venice Biennale art exhibition.

stories.title: Anti-war protests rock Japan as PM pushes for stronger defence
stories.summary: Japan is experiencing its largest anti-war protests in decades as the public remains divided over Prime Minister's push for stronger defense capabilities and proposed changes to the country's pacifist constitution.

stories.title: 2026 election results: latest from local, Scottish and Welsh votes
stories.summary: Local council elections in England and devolved parliament elections in Scotland and Wales took place on May 7, 2026. The first results were expected around midnight, with Scottish and Welsh parliament outcomes due from midday the following day.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1534: 2,000 civilians are starving in occupied Oleshky as Russia blocks aid corridor
stories.summary: On day 1,534 of Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine, approximately 2,000 civilians in Russian-occupied Oleshky are reportedly starving as Russia blocks an aid corridor. Ukraine's air defenses destroyed nearly 6,000 targets during the month of April.

stories.title: Trump gives EU until 4 July to ratify trade deal or face ‘much higher’ tariffs
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump set a July 4 deadline for the European Union to ratify a trade deal with the United States. Trump warned that failure to meet the deadline would result in significantly higher tariffs, posting the ultimatum on Truth Social after speaking with EU chief Ursula von der Leyen.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz: What role for France?
stories.summary: France is moving its aircraft carrier group toward the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran. France and the United Kingdom are jointly developing a proposal to establish conditions for safe transit through the strategic waterway once hostilities end.

stories.title: Wrapped in a Boeing: will Trump’s China visit include another aircraft deal?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump's upcoming visit to China is being examined for the possibility of a major Boeing aircraft deal, as the US-Iran war disrupts global energy supplies and adds strain to Washington-Beijing relations. Chinese airlines have not placed a significant Boeing order in nearly a decade.

stories.title: Russian troops attack Zaporizhzhia, injuring four people
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Zaporizhzhia with a drone strike in the evening. Four people were injured in the attack, including a teenager.

stories.title: Zelensky warns Russia’s allies against attending WWII parade as Moscow repeats threats
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Russia's allies against attending Moscow's May 9 World War II victory parade. Russia declared a unilateral ceasefire from May 8 to 10 but urged Kyiv residents to evacuate, citing a potential retaliatory strike.

stories.title: UAE sends Board of Peace $100 million for training of new Gaza police force — officials
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates transferred $100 million to the US-led Board of Peace for training a new Gaza police force. The payment is the largest single sum the oversight body has received, out of $17 billion in total pledges from various countries.

stories.title: US congressman says pro-Israel groups behind 95 percent of funding against him
stories.summary: US Republican Congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky stated that pro-Israel groups account for 95 percent of campaign funding directed against him. His upcoming Republican primary is expected to be one of the most expensive congressional races in history.

stories.title: 75-hectare forest fire in Ukrainian region bordering four European countries is being investigated as possible Russian arson
stories.summary: A 75-hectare forest fire in a Ukrainian region bordering four European countries is being investigated as possible Russian arson. Authorities report no open flames remain, but smoldering hotspots persist in the forest floor and dry vegetation.

stories.title: White House inviting Nvidia, Apple, Boeing CEOs on Trump’s China trip, report says
stories.summary: The Trump administration is inviting CEOs from Nvidia, Apple, Boeing, Exxon, Qualcomm, Blackstone, Citigroup, and Visa to accompany the president on his trip to China next week, according to a Semafor report. Citigroup confirmed CEO Jane Fraser received an invitation.

stories.title: US-proposed Iran resolution at UN faces likely vetoes from China, Russia
stories.summary: A US-proposed UN Security Council resolution on Iran faces likely vetoes from both China and Russia. A Chinese veto could complicate diplomacy ahead of President Trump's upcoming visit to Beijing, where the Iran war is expected to be a major agenda item.

stories.title: US trade court rules against Trump’s 10% global tariffs
stories.summary: The U.S. Court of International Trade ruled 2-1 against President Trump's 10% global tariffs on May 7, finding they were not justified under a 1970s trade law. The case was brought by small businesses that challenged the tariffs, which had taken effect on February 24.

stories.title: Myanmar junta claims recapture of trade artery towards China
stories.summary: Myanmar's military junta claimed to have recaptured a key trade route connecting Mandalay to the northern city of Myitkyina, approximately 50 kilometers from the Chinese border. The junta said it defeated what it termed "terrorist insurgent groups" along the route.

stories.title: Israel Police stops wedding between 40-year-old man, teenage bride in northern Israel - report
stories.summary: Israeli police intervened to stop a wedding ceremony between a 40-year-old man and a teenage bride in northern Israel. Law enforcement officials noted that community members have claimed such events are "engagement parties" rather than weddings, creating legal complications.

stories.title: Talks with Ukraine on Gripen fighter jet deal are going well, Swedish defence minister says
stories.summary: Swedish Defence Minister Pal Jonson said on Thursday that talks between Sweden and Ukraine on a deal for Saab-made Gripen fighter jets are progressing well. The discussions are part of broader Western efforts to bolster Ukraine's military capabilities.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike three air defense systems, Russian fuel depots
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck Russian Buk-M3 and Strela-10 air defense systems as well as fuel depots. The drone operations targeted key Russian military assets in the Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions.

stories.title: Iran can last for months under US Strait of Hormuz blockade, US officials say - report
stories.summary: US officials reportedly assessed that Iran can sustain itself for months under a US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. One official noted that Iran's leadership has grown more radical and confident in its ability to outlast American political will while maintaining domestic control.

stories.title: CIA says Iran has 70 percent of pre-war missiles, can ride out blockade for months: Report
stories.summary: A reported CIA assessment concludes that Iran retains roughly 70 percent of its pre-war missile stockpile and can withstand the current blockade for months. The analysis contradicts public claims by President Donald Trump and senior officials about Iran's diminished capacity.

stories.title: Why China’s warning over military blocs is finding listeners in Asia
stories.summary: The US-Philippines Balikatan military exercises involved over 17,000 troops and included Japan's first live-fire participation, along with forces from Australia, Canada, France, and New Zealand. China issued warnings about the formation of military blocs in the region, a message gaining traction among some Asian nations.

stories.title: Watch: DMK authorises Stalin to take decisions for a ‘stable’ T.N. govt. | Above the Fold | 07.05.2026
stories.summary: India's DMK party authorized leader M.K. Stalin to make decisions aimed at forming a stable government in Tamil Nadu following recent elections. Other major stories include Bihar's cabinet expansion, the anniversary of Operation Sindoor, and a virus outbreak at sea.

stories.title: Tenerife resort town awaits hantavirus-hit cruise ship
stories.summary: A cruise ship affected by a hantavirus outbreak is scheduled to dock in southern Tenerife, prompting reactions from local residents in the resort town.

stories.title: Iran’s President Pezeshkian says he met Supreme Leader Khamenei
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he met with Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, praising the leader's vision and approach during their meeting.

stories.title: Kremlin suspends trilateral peace talks until AFU withdraws from Donbas
stories.summary: Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov declared that trilateral peace talks in the U.S.-Ukraine-Russia format are pointless until Kyiv withdraws its forces from areas of Donbas under Ukrainian control. The statement effectively suspends the negotiation process.

stories.title: Iranian media says air defences down drones as military reports strikes
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported explosions at the southern port of Bandar Abbas and on Qeshm Island. Mizan News Agency and Tasnim News Agency said air defenses intercepted several small drones over both locations. IRIB cited a military official saying Iran launched retaliatory missiles at what it described as US forces following an attack on Iranian territory.

stories.title: Philippines warns Chinese research ship in disputed waters
stories.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard warned a Chinese research vessel, the Xiang Yang Hong 33, operating near a reef in the contested Spratly Islands chain. The ship is capable of supporting submersible craft.

stories.title: How the Abraham Accords Fueled a New Era of Conflict
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the Abraham Accords, which normalized Israeli-Gulf state relations, inadvertently contributed to escalating conflict with Iran despite their stated goal of promoting regional peace.

stories.title: Iran says it attacked US Navy ships after they targeted Iranian tanker
stories.summary: Iran claimed it attacked US Navy ships after they targeted an Iranian tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. The US military described the Iranian attack as unprovoked and said it intercepted and responded to the assault, emphasizing it does not seek escalation.

stories.title: Explainer: What’s included in talks to end the Iran war and reopen Hormuz?
stories.summary: Washington and Tehran have narrowed their negotiating objectives amid the ongoing Iran conflict, which threatens global economic stability. Rather than pursuing a comprehensive peace deal, both sides are now seeking a limited agreement that defers more contentious issues.

stories.title: Five killed in huge fire at packed Mexico fairground
stories.summary: A large fire broke out at a fairground in Villahermosa, southeastern Mexico, killing at least five people. The blaze erupted during a concert reportedly attended by approximately 135,000 people.

stories.title: Facing a mixed reception at Eurovision, Noam Bettan is ready ‘to enjoy the journey’
stories.summary: Israeli singer Noam Bettan, 28, born in Israel to French parents, is preparing to represent Israel at Eurovision. He acknowledged the mixed reception he may face and expressed readiness to embrace the experience.

stories.title: Polls close in elections across England, Scotland and Wales
stories.summary: Polls closed across England, Scotland, and Wales for local, mayoral, and parliamentary elections on May 7. Over 30 million people were eligible to vote in what is considered the biggest electoral test for Prime Minister Keir Starmer since the 2024 general election.

stories.title: Crowds cheer China's new snooker star on return from championship win
stories.summary: Chinese snooker player Wu Yize, 22, received a hero's welcome upon returning home after winning a world championship title, becoming the second-youngest player to achieve the feat.

stories.title: Trump sets July 4 deadline for EU tariff hike decision
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump set a July 4 deadline for a decision on raising tariffs on the European Union. Trump said he had a positive phone call with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen regarding the looming tariffs.

stories.title: Ukraine should first integrate with EU in defense – MEP Juknevičienė
