stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced a dedicated team of 100 officers, including counter-terrorism specialists, to protect Jewish communities following a series of anti-Semitic attacks, including a stabbing of two men. Commissioner Mark Rowley cited sustained threats from hostile state actors and extremists. A 35-year-old man was arrested after rocks were thrown at a Jewish community ambulance.

stories.title: Party boss of China’s emerging tech hub under  investigation for corruption
stories.summary: Fei Gaoyun, the Communist Party chief of Hefei, capital of China's Anhui province, has been placed under corruption investigation. China's top anti-corruption watchdog announced the probe, making the 54-year-old the latest senior official caught in President Xi Jinping's long-running campaign.

stories.title: US must be transparent about Israel's nuclear programme, Democrat lawmakers say
stories.summary: Thirty Democratic members of the U.S. House of Representatives sent a letter to Secretary of State Rubio urging Washington to end decades of ambiguity over Israel's nuclear weapons program and hold Israel to the same nonproliferation standards as other nations.

stories.title: Sudan recalls ambassador to Ethiopia amid rising tensions
stories.summary: Sudan recalled its ambassador to Ethiopia amid rising tensions between the two neighboring countries. No specific details on the immediate cause of the diplomatic escalation were provided.

stories.title: Reform-led Lancashire county council to quit refugee resettlement scheme
stories.summary: The Reform UK-led Lancashire county council announced plans to withdraw from the UK government's refugee resettlement scheme. Councillor Joshua Roberts made the announcement, which would make Lancashire the first local authority to leave the program.

stories.title: Israel kills several in Gaza, death toll rises to 72,619
stories.summary: The Palestinian Ministry of Health in Gaza reported that Israeli forces killed three more people over the past 24 hours, raising the official death toll to 72,619, with thousands more missing and presumed dead.

stories.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz passage to be ensured after US pauses operation
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy stated it would ensure safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz, announcing that new procedures would be implemented following the U.S. pause of its escort operation.

stories.title: More charges filed against WH correspondents' dinner attacker
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, accused of targeting President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, faces additional charges for allegedly firing at a Secret Service officer during the incident.

stories.title: What is the FDD, the pro-Israel think tank shaping Trump’s Iran policy?
stories.summary: The Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), a Washington-based pro-Israel think tank, has reportedly influenced the Trump administration's Iran policy, with its talking points on the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran being adopted by senior officials.

stories.title: Hong Kong pledges deeper ties with Uzbekistan as China signs bilateral agreements
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee met with Uzbek Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov to strengthen trade ties. China and Uzbekistan signed 15 bilateral agreements covering infrastructure, healthcare, and metal production during the visit.

stories.title: Pakistan again turns to spot LNG market, seeks bids for 2 cargoes
stories.summary: Pakistan LNG Limited issued urgent tenders for two spot LNG cargoes for mid-to-late May delivery as rising temperatures increase power demand. The purchase follows unmet expectations that the Middle East crisis would ease and the Strait of Hormuz would reopen.

stories.title: How India uses remote island to show strength against China
stories.summary: India is developing Great Nicobar Island, located at the edge of the Indian Ocean, into a strategic military and trade hub. New Delhi intends the facility to strengthen its position along key shipping routes and counter China's expanding regional influence.

stories.title: European Commission warns Italy that Russia’s Venice Biennale pavilion violates sanctions, Financial Times reports
stories.summary: The European Commission warned Italy's government and Venice Biennale organizers that opening Russia's national pavilion would violate EU sanctions by providing services to the Kremlin, the Financial Times reported.

stories.title: IRGC announces 'safe and stable' transit through Hormuz with the end of US threats
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC Navy announced that "safe and stable" transit through the Strait of Hormuz would be ensured now that U.S. threats are ending, stating new procedures would be implemented without specifying details.

stories.title: Russian oil revenue jumped 52%—Moral Rating Agency lays out how to make Russia poor
stories.summary: A report from the Moral Rating Agency indicated that Russian oil revenue increased by 52%. The agency argued that while some sanctions measures have been implemented, significant gaps remain in efforts to curtail Moscow's energy income.

stories.title: Airlines among companies using fuel surcharges to cover surge in costs, UK survey shows
stories.summary: A UK survey found that airlines and other service-sector companies are increasingly using fuel surcharges to cover soaring energy and wage costs. Businesses raised prices at the fastest rate in over three years in April, driven partly by Iran war-linked inflation.

stories.title: Protests erupt over Israeli settlement sales in New York
stories.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside an Israeli real estate event in New York City to protest the sale of properties linked to settlements in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Amputee football empowers Rwandan women on and off the pitch
stories.summary: Amputee football is growing in Rwanda, providing women with opportunities for physical rehabilitation, social inclusion, and self-acceptance through organized competitive play.

stories.title: China’s chipmakers rush to embrace DeepSeek’s V4. Which names stand out?
stories.summary: Multiple Chinese semiconductor manufacturers are racing to adopt DeepSeek's latest large language model, V4, on domestic hardware platforms. Huawei was among the first to adapt the model, as geopolitical tensions over advanced chips drive efforts to localize AI capabilities.

stories.title: Gulf banks tightens digital oversight to curb Iran crypto flows
stories.summary: Gulf banks are tightening digital oversight to curb cryptocurrency flows linked to Iran. A Chainalysis report found illicit crypto flows grew 694 percent over the past year, reaching $154 billion in total value.

stories.title: Turkish exercise sees Libya’s rival forces train together for second time within weeks
stories.summary: Turkey hosted a military exercise bringing together forces from Libya's rival factions, marking the second such joint training event in recent weeks. The initiative falls under Ankara's "One Army, One Libya" policy aimed at unifying Libyan military structures.

stories.title: US and Iran nearing one-page war-ending agreement
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are reportedly nearing a one-page agreement to end the war. Key terms include mutual lifting of Strait of Hormuz blockades, US sanctions removal, and Iran committing to a 15-year moratorium on uranium enrichment.

stories.title: Varus distribution center damaged in Dnipro due to Russian attack; fatalities reported
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Dnipro on May 5 damaged the distribution center of the Varus grocery store chain, resulting in fatalities among staff members.

stories.title: Iran struck over 228 US structures, equipment across region: Report
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported, using satellite imagery, that Iranian air strikes have damaged or destroyed at least 228 U.S. structures and pieces of equipment across the region since the war began in late February.

stories.title: Climate shocks and Hormuz crisis deepen MENA food insecurity
stories.summary: The Middle East and North Africa region faces a deepening food security crisis as climate shocks and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz strain import-dependent supply chains across the area.

stories.title: US offers $10m reward for Iraq armed group leader Akram al-Kaabi
stories.summary: The U.S. government designated Iraqi militia leader Akram al-Kaabi as a terrorist and offered a $10 million reward for information leading to his capture or identification.

stories.title: China condemns Japan’s first overseas ‘offensive missile’ test since WWII
stories.summary: China condemned Japan's firing of a Type 88 surface-to-ship missile in the Philippines during the U.S.-led Balikatan 2026 joint drill. Beijing called it Japan's first overseas "offensive missile" test since World War II, warning it threatened regional stability.

stories.title: Cuba says US Secretary of State Rubio lying about oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuba's foreign minister accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of lying about an oil blockade, saying Rubio is fully aware of the harm his policies are causing to the Cuban people.

stories.title: Lessons from the war: A call for strategic reckoning in West Asia
stories.summary: The Israeli-U.S. war on Iran has disrupted longstanding assumptions about security, deterrence, and regional stability in West Asia, prompting analysts to call for a strategic reassessment of the conflict's broader implications.

stories.title: Trump pauses 'Project Freedom' amid potential deal with Iran
stories.summary: President Trump paused 'Project Freedom,' the U.S. military operation escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz, amid progress toward a potential deal with Iran. The U.S. said its blockade on Iran would remain in place.

stories.title: Coyote swam 2 miles to Alcatraz Island, going farther than scientists expected
stories.summary: A coyote that swam to Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay earlier this year actually traveled approximately 2 miles from Angel Island, farther than biologists initially estimated. Scientists had originally guessed it swam the shorter distance from San Francisco.

stories.title: Alaska’s 2025 mega tsunami highlights risk to cruise lines as glaciers retreat
stories.summary: A 481-metre mega tsunami struck Tracy Arm fjord in southeast Alaska in August last year, triggered by a massive rockslide near a glacier. Researchers warn the event highlights growing risks from coastal rockslides and glacier retreat linked to climate change.

stories.title: Reform and Plaid Cymru likely to benefit from polarisation of Welsh politics
stories.summary: Polls suggest Reform UK could win the most seats in the Welsh Senedd election under a new proportional voting system, though it is unlikely to form a government. The polarization of Welsh politics is also expected to benefit Plaid Cymru.

stories.title: Has the US accepted Iran’s demand to settle Hormuz first, nuclear later?
stories.summary: The United States paused its Strait of Hormuz escort operations after Pakistan-led mediation between Washington and Tehran gained traction, suggesting a possible shift toward addressing Hormuz transit issues before nuclear negotiations.

stories.title: Two Russian drones strike kindergarten in Sumy
stories.summary: Two Russian drones struck a kindergarten building in the central part of the city of Sumy, Ukraine. No immediate details on casualties were provided.

stories.title: Looking ahead to the UK's local elections with British politics expert Colm Murphy
stories.summary: UK local elections are being held on Thursday, with polls predicting significant losses for the ruling Labour Party. Reform UK and the Green Party are expected to make gains in English council races and devolved parliament elections in Scotland and Wales.

stories.title: Israel to supply Germany with jet fuel amid shortages caused by Iran war
stories.summary: Israel will supply Germany with jet fuel to help address shortages caused by the Iran war. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar communicated the decision to Germany's Economic Affairs and Energy Minister during a visit to Berlin.

stories.title: Thailand vows strict tourist oversight after public sex incidents
stories.summary: Thailand announced it would tighten oversight of tourist behavior following multiple incidents of foreigners caught having sex in public. The prime minister's office warned that inappropriate conduct, including illicit drug use, would face prosecution.

stories.title: Israel kills four in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on the town of Zellaya in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley killed four people, including two women and an elderly man. Several others, including a child, were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Was former synagogue targeted in London arson attack a mosque?
stories.summary: A former synagogue in east London was targeted in an arson attack. The building has been disused since 2020, and a Muslim community group had been making plans to purchase the property.

stories.title: Russia ignores Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire and attacks kindergarten
stories.summary: Russia continued attacks on Ukrainian targets despite Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire declaration, including a strike on a kindergarten. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated Russia had "spurned the ceasefire" and said Kyiv was considering its response.

stories.title: Cruise passengers tell of life on board ship stranded off Cape Verde after hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: Passengers aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship remain stranded off Cape Verde following a hantavirus outbreak on board. While passengers report calm conditions, officials warn the disease may have spread, and the ship faces additional days at sea.

stories.title: Russia strikes Ukraine with over 100 drones as Zelensky’s ceasefire takes effect
stories.summary: Russia launched three missiles and 108 drones at Ukraine in the early hours of May 6, coinciding with the start of a ceasefire declared by President Zelensky, according to Ukraine's Air Force.

stories.title: Indonesian captain among crew held as Somali pirates strike again in Horn of Africa
stories.summary: Somali pirates seized the Palau-flagged tanker MT Honour 25 near the Horn of Africa, taking hostage its crew including Indonesian captain Ashari Samadikun. The captain sent a voice note to his wife warning of the impending attack on April 21.

stories.title: Met sets up specialist unit as antisemitic hate crimes in London hit two-year high
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced a specialist community protection team of 100 extra officers after antisemitic hate crimes in April reached a two-year high. The unit will combine neighbourhood policing with counter-terrorism capabilities to protect Jewish communities.

stories.title: Hantavirus: Latest updates on the ongoing outbreak aboard the MV Hondius
stories.summary: South Africa confirmed that the hantavirus strain identified from the MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak can spread among humans. The ship, marooned off Cape Verde with nearly 150 people aboard, was heading to Spain as investigations continued.

stories.title: Ukrainian Attack Kills 5 in Annexed Crimea as Kyiv Accuses Russia of Violating Its Ceasefire
stories.summary: Kremlin-installed officials reported that a Ukrainian attack on the town of Dzhankoi in northern Crimea killed five people on Tuesday night. Dzhankoi is home to a military airbase. Kyiv accused Russia of violating its declared ceasefire.

stories.title: China calls for a ‘complete’ end to war on Iran
stories.summary: China has called for a complete end to the war on Iran, signaling its diplomatic position on the ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.title: United Russia coaches deputies to justify internet restrictions by citing an ‘information-psychological war’
stories.summary: Russia's ruling United Russia party prepared a pamphlet coaching deputies and campaign workers on how to justify internet restrictions by framing them as responses to an "information-psychological war," according to Russian newspaper Kommersant.

stories.title: Can Hezbollah dominate the lower air battlefield against Israel?
stories.summary: An analysis examines Hezbollah's use of fibre-optic-guided drones against Israel, noting that while not a decisive weapon, the technology exposes vulnerabilities in Israel's low-altitude air defenses.

stories.title: New weapons charges filed against suspect in deadly shooting at Bondi Beach Hanukkah festival
stories.summary: Naveed Akram faces new weapons charges in addition to 59 existing counts, including murder, attempted murder, and committing a terrorist act, after two gunmen opened fire at a Hanukkah festival at Bondi Beach in Sydney in December 2025.

stories.title: United States: Los Angeles fire suspect had grudge against wealthy
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors said the man accused of deliberately setting the deadly Los Angeles fire last year harbored a grudge against the wealthy and admired Luigi Mangione, who is accused of fatally shooting a health insurance CEO.

stories.title: Enemy shelling causes new power outages in three regions, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Russian shelling on the morning of May 6 caused power outages affecting consumers in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kharkiv regions, according to the national grid operator Ukrenergo.

stories.title: German police raid neo-Nazi criminal youth groups
stories.summary: German police conducted coordinated raids against neo-Nazi criminal youth groups, searching locations across 12 of the country's states. Prosecutors said the operations were concentrated mainly in eastern and southern Germany.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi meets Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in Beijing
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in Beijing during a one-day visit. The meeting took place a week before U.S. President Donald Trump's scheduled summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14–15.

stories.title: Iran Nobel winner Narges Mohammadi at risk of dying in custody
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi is reportedly at risk of dying while in custody in Iran. Concerns about her health and treatment in prison have been raised by international observers.

stories.title: Local elections could hasten the exit of Britain’s embattled Prime Minister
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces political pressure ahead of local elections, with his popularity declining due to a weak economy and repeated questions about his judgment.

stories.title: Sick crew members evacuated from hantavirus cruise ship | First Thing
stories.summary: Three passengers have died and crew members have been medically evacuated from the cruise ship MV Hondius following a suspected hantavirus outbreak. Spain has granted permission for the vessel, carrying close to 150 people, to dock at the Canary Islands.

stories.title: US announces phased closure of Peshawar consulate, says operations will shift to Islamabad
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department announced the phased closure of its consulate in Peshawar, Pakistan, with operations transferring to the embassy in Islamabad. The decision was attributed to personnel safety and resource management. Diplomatic engagement with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province will continue from Islamabad.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: Ministry official says govt ‘very actively engaged’ with all provinces on climate change
stories.summary: The second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference, organized by DawnMedia, is being held in Islamabad. A ministry official stated the government is actively engaging all provinces on climate change policy. Pakistan remains among the most climate-vulnerable nations despite contributing minimally to global emissions.

stories.title: Cuba says Rubio lying about oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuba accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of lying about an oil blockade on the island. Rubio had previously stated there was no oil blockade on Cuba "per se."

stories.title: ‘Operation Epic Fury’ has ended: Is the Iran war over?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that President Trump's pause of 'Project Freedom' and the end of 'Operation Epic Fury' could mark the beginning of the end of the U.S.-Iran war, though uncertainty remains about a final resolution.

stories.title: Arms deliveries and Africa Corps training: How Russia is bolstering its presence in Madagascar
stories.summary: Security cooperation between Madagascar and Russia has intensified since the October 2025 coup, with Russia delivering drones and armoured vehicles and deploying Africa Corps instructors for training. Russia's growing influence is expanding into other sectors on the island nation.

stories.title: Australian nationals 'linked' to IS members returning from Syria
stories.summary: Australia's home affairs minister confirmed that a group of women and children linked to Islamic State members are returning from the Roj camp in northeastern Syria, and the government will provide them with assistance.

stories.title: 27 held, HK$3.3m fuel seized as Hong Kong cracks down on illegal sales by triads
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities arrested 27 people and seized over 21,000 litres of illicit fuel worth approximately HK$3.3 million in a crackdown on triad-linked illegal fuel sales. The joint operation, code-named "Knockout," also resulted in the seizure of 15 vehicles and a speedboat.

stories.title: Sudan blames Ethiopia, UAE for recent drone attacks: What we know
stories.summary: Sudan recalled its ambassador to Addis Ababa, blaming Ethiopia and the UAE for recent drone attacks that disrupted a period of relative calm following years of civil war in the country.

stories.title: Explosions heard in Crimea; FSB building damaged
stories.summary: Explosions and gunfire were reported across Russian-occupied Crimea on the evening of May 5. An FSB border guard building in Armiansk was damaged, and the Kacha Airfield was also struck. Russian air defense systems were activated during the incidents.

stories.title: Pakistan Army cadet gets top honours at Australian military college
stories.summary: Pakistan Army Cadet Sardar Arsam Abbas was named the overall best foreign military cadet at Australia's Royal Military College Duntroon in Canberra. The award, announced by Pakistan's ISPR, was given at the passing-out parade on May 5 and recognizes the highest-performing foreign cadet across all training areas.

stories.title: By downplaying Islamophobic attacks over antisemitism, the BBC is reinforcing racism
stories.summary: New research alleges the BBC systematically downplays Islamophobic incidents compared to antisemitic attacks in its coverage, raising concerns about unequal treatment of different faith communities in British media.

stories.title: Does Syria’s rise in the Press Freedom Index reflect reality? - analysis
stories.summary: Syria rose 36 places in the 2026 Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index, but analysts note that significant constraints on independent journalism persist in the country.

stories.title: Trump-backed candidates win majority of Republican primary races for Indiana Senate
stories.summary: A majority of Republican Indiana state senators whose opponents were endorsed by President Donald Trump lost their primary races. Trump-backed candidates won most of the contested Republican primary elections for the Indiana state Senate.

stories.title: Romania's government falls, far-right firewall crumbles
stories.summary: Romania's Social Democrats allied with far-right opposition parties to topple Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan's pro-reform government in a no-confidence vote. The move raises concerns about the far right's growing political influence and potential economic consequences for the country.

stories.title: 5 dead in US strikes on alleged drug boats off Latin America: Pentagon
stories.summary: The Pentagon reported that five people were killed in U.S. strikes on alleged drug trafficking boats off Latin America. The deaths bring the total toll from the U.S. bombing campaign targeting suspected narco-trafficking operations to 190.

stories.title: US and Iran 'closing in' on one-page memo to end war: Axios
stories.summary: Axios reported that the U.S. and Iran are close to finalizing a one-page memorandum to end the war, with provisions covering nuclear enrichment limits, the lifting of U.S. sanctions, and Hormuz-related restrictions.

stories.title: What the BJP’s historic West Bengal victory means for Modi’s India
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party won 207 of 294 assembly seats in West Bengal, ending three consecutive terms of rival rule. The victory gives Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling coalition control of roughly 70 percent of India's state legislatures.

stories.title: Hundreds of European doctors hoping to make aliyah attend MedEx conference
stories.summary: Hundreds of European doctors attended the MedEx conference exploring immigration to Israel. The country faces a physician shortage driven by a high birth rate and an aging medical workforce.

stories.title: Members of Russia’s Espanyola Brigade arrested on weapons and explosives trafficking charges, Kommersant reports
stories.summary: Several former and active members of the Espanyola Brigade's naval unit were arrested in occupied Sevastopol on charges of illegal weapons and explosives trafficking. The case came to light through a ruling by the Southern District Military Court, Kommersant reported.

stories.title: Hong Kong police launch investigation after man and woman found dead in flat
stories.summary: Hong Kong police launched an investigation after a man and a woman were found dead inside a flat at Tat Yan House, Po Tat Estate, in Sau Mau Ping. Officers responded after a report from a man who suspected his brother had taken his own life.

stories.title: Who flew Israel’s first F-35 mission? Meet the man taking the stage in New York
stories.summary: The pilot who flew Israel's first F-35 combat mission, identified as Eshel, will speak at The Jerusalem Post Annual Conference in New York on June 1 alongside Israeli and American defense figures.

stories.title: Venice Biennale: Boycotts and threats over participation of Russia & Israel
stories.summary: The Venice Biennale's 61st edition opened amid unprecedented turmoil after the jury resigned over the participation of Israel and Russia. Boycotts and threats have disrupted the world's oldest contemporary art exhibition.

stories.title: US suspends Hormuz operation: Washington believes close to deal with Iran
stories.summary: The United States suspended its naval operations in the Strait of Hormuz as Washington reportedly believes it is close to reaching a deal with Iran. The suspension signals a potential de-escalation in tensions between the two nations.

stories.title: Ex-MNA Abidi’s killing in 2018 was not terrorism: Sindh High Court
stories.summary: The Sindh High Court ruled that the 2018 targeted killing of former MQM-P MNA Ali Raza Abidi in Karachi did not constitute terrorism. The court acquitted four appellants of terrorism charges and commuted their life sentences to time already served. The bench also questioned police over the weak investigation in the high-profile case.

stories.title: Two people injured, and fire breaks out in Kharkiv following Russian drone strike
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike hit the Novobavarskyi district of Kharkiv on the morning of May 6, injuring two people and starting a fire.

stories.title: Algeria: 'Economic Diplomacy' Key in Algeria, French Employers' Union Chief Tells Rfi
stories.summary: Following a visit to Algeria, the head of France's main employers' union Medef, Patrick Martin, discussed economic diplomacy between Paris and Algiers amid strained bilateral relations, Chinese competition in Africa, and the impact of the global tariff dispute.

stories.title: Hongkongers to pay only HK$240 a year for leukaemia drug after system shake-up
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Hospital Authority began subsidizing the leukemia drug Dasatinib in April, reducing annual patient costs from up to HK$500,000 to HK$240. Over 400 cancer patients are expected to benefit, with the government allocating an additional HK$49 million annually.

stories.title: What does an improved Hong Kong property outlook mean for land sales?
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings expects competition to intensify at tenders for Hong Kong residential land plots as developers replenish land banks amid a recovering property market. The agency forecast a relatively modest residential market recovery, though some analysts say returning confidence is supported by robust housing demand.

stories.title: Africa: Xenophobia - African Nations Threaten Retaliatory Action Against South Africa
stories.summary: Multiple African nations are threatening retaliatory measures against South Africa in response to renewed xenophobic attacks targeting foreign nationals, particularly Nigerians. Diplomatic pressure on Pretoria is mounting over the violence.

stories.title: Iranian and Chinese FMS meet as Beijing urges countries to maintain ceasefire
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of Iran and China met as Beijing urged all parties to maintain a ceasefire. The meeting highlights China's diplomatic engagement amid ongoing tensions in the region.

stories.title: SSU detains head of Zhytomyr Regional Territorial Recruitment Center
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SSU) detained the head of the Zhytomyr Regional Territorial Recruitment Center on charges of extorting money from a local businessman in exchange for exempting his employees from conscription.

stories.title: Injured Mbappe faces backlash over Sardinia trip before Clasico
stories.summary: Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappé faced backlash from supporters after taking a holiday in Sardinia while sidelined with a hamstring injury. The trip triggered a media storm ahead of Sunday's Clásico match against Barcelona.

stories.title: Pakistan’s first Chinese submarine set to boost naval capability
stories.summary: Pakistan is set to receive its first Chinese-built submarine, enhancing its naval capabilities as part of broader military modernization efforts. China's defense supplies remain central to Pakistan's buildup, with both nations deepening their partnership amid strategic considerations involving India.

stories.title: Supreme Court overturns rape conviction after review
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court, sitting as an expanded panel, overturned the rape conviction of Adel Heib, who had been acquitted in 2023 of raping an 82-year-old woman but was later convicted on appeal.

stories.title: Donald Trump renews pressure and plans to hike tariffs on EU cars
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump announced an increase in tariffs on cars and trucks from the European Union to 25 percent from the previously agreed 15 percent. Trump said the EU had not complied with its trade deal with Washington, putting pressure on European car parts makers.

stories.title: Thai Foreign Minister seeks ASEAN talks with Myanmar counterpart
stories.summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said he is pushing to restore ASEAN engagement with Myanmar's leadership, including at the foreign minister level. He sought talks with his Myanmar counterpart.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia posts $33.5bn budget deficit amid drop in oil sales
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reported a $33.5 billion budget deficit driven by declining oil revenues linked to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, marking a sharp rise in the kingdom's fiscal shortfall.

stories.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads to Spain to dock in Canary Islands
stories.summary: A luxury cruise ship affected by a hantavirus outbreak is traveling from Cape Verde toward Europe after Spain authorized it to dock in the Canary Islands. The vessel was preparing to make the journey on Wednesday.

stories.title: China erects monument in Egypt to commemorate 1943 Cairo Declaration
stories.summary: China erected a monument at the historic Mena House hotel in Egypt to commemorate the 1943 Cairo Declaration, a World War II agreement signed at that location.

stories.title: Israeli attacks on southern, eastern Lebanon kill at least six people
stories.summary: Israeli forces issued forced displacement orders for 12 villages in southern Lebanon and carried out attacks in the country's south and east, killing at least six people.

stories.title: Kyiv says Russia broke unilateral ceasefire with drone and missile attacks
stories.summary: Ukraine accused Russia of violating a unilateral ceasefire declared by Kyiv, reporting that Russian forces launched 108 combat drones and three missiles against Ukrainian cities overnight on Wednesday.

stories.title: Iran Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi 'between life and death'
stories.summary: Jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been hospitalized under guard for five days with a heart condition and is reportedly fighting for her life. Her family described her situation as being "between life and death."

stories.title: Hong Kong to ban new EVs with only electronic door handles
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities plan to ban new electric vehicles equipped only with electronic door handles, aligning with mainland China's mandate requiring physical manual door releases on all new cars from 2027. Transport Secretary Mable Chan said the government is monitoring technical and regulatory developments to ensure road-user safety.

stories.title: ADL: Antisemitic assaults in US hit record high in 2025 as overall incidents declined
stories.summary: The Anti-Defamation League reported that antisemitic assaults in the United States reached a record high in 2025, with 203 violent incidents including three murders, even as the overall number of antisemitic incidents declined 33 percent from 2024.

stories.title: Russians attack car with drone in Sumy region this morning; woman killed
stories.summary: A woman was killed in Ukraine's Sumy region on Wednesday morning when Russian forces struck a car with a drone.

stories.title: Live: Hantavirus-infected patient hospitalised in Zurich as three more 'evacuated' from cruise ship
stories.summary: A former passenger on the MV Hondius cruise ship tested positive for hantavirus and was hospitalized in Zurich, according to the Swiss health ministry. The World Health Organization said three other infected passengers were evacuated from the ship, which remains anchored off Cape Verde.

stories.title: China’s new marine buoy says goodbye to classic Western design used since WWII
stories.summary: Chinese researchers deployed what they describe as the world's first intelligent ocean-observation buoy off Rongcheng in Shandong province. The six-metre-wide platform has joined the Yellow Sea observation network for real-time monitoring. Its design abandons a mooring architecture that has dominated Western marine engineering since World War II.

stories.title: Sculpture in middle of ‘Mirror of the Sky’ China lake criticised for disrupting serene beauty
stories.summary: China's Chaka Salt Lake in Qinghai province, renowned for its mirror-like reflective surface and nicknamed the "mirror of the sky," has drawn criticism over a sculpture installation that visitors say disrupts its serene natural beauty. The lake attracts around 40,000 visitors daily and is ranked among China's top must-visit sites.

stories.title: Burkina Faso junta secretly held and abused journalist Atiana Serge Oulon: RSF
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) reported that Burkina Faso's military authorities secretly detained and abused investigative journalist Atiana Serge Oulon along with dozens of others in a makeshift facility in the capital, Ouagadougou.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict reasches painful stalemate: US will respond if fired on
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict has reached a tense stalemate, with the United States warning it will respond if fired upon. A France24 correspondent in Washington reported on the ongoing standoff.

stories.title: French vessel attacked in Strait of Hormuz, several crewmembers wounded
stories.summary: A French vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, leaving several crew members wounded. The injured were evacuated and are receiving medical care.

stories.title: Oil prices retreat and global stocks hit record highs after Trump hails ‘great progress’ on Iran deal – business live
stories.summary: Oil prices retreated and global stock markets hit record highs after President Trump announced "great progress" toward a final agreement with Iran and paused the U.S. "Project Freedom" escort operation in the Strait of Hormuz. Markets were also buoyed by AI-related stock gains.

stories.title: Eritrea: U.S. Seeks to Lift Sanctions On Eritrea
stories.summary: The United States is pursuing the lifting of sanctions on Eritrea. Human Rights Watch urged concerned governments not to overlook the country's severe human rights record.

stories.title: Putin said to be 'hiding in bunkers' as his popularity erodes
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin's domestic popularity is reportedly declining amid economic difficulties and internet restrictions, with reports suggesting he has been confined to bunkers. Meanwhile, Russia's participation in the Venice Biennale art exhibition has drawn controversy.

stories.title: U.S. military operation against Iran commenced, says Rubio
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that the United States has concluded Operation Epic Fury, a military operation against Iran, and has transitioned to a new phase of operations in the Middle East.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 6 – Pay-to-slay is here to stay?
stories.summary: The Times of Israel's daily briefing covered US-Iran negotiations, efforts by the Board of Peace to influence Hamas, and the implementation of the Taylor Force Act targeting Palestinian Authority payments to attackers' families.

stories.title: Claiming ‘great progress’ in Iran talks, Trump pauses US naval escorts in Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump paused US naval escorts in the Strait of Hormuz, citing progress in Iran talks. Tehran expressed interest in a comprehensive agreement, while Israeli PM Netanyahu reportedly spoke with the UAE president about recent Iranian attacks.

stories.title: Zack Polanski says he was wrong to call himself a Red Cross spokesperson
stories.summary: UK Green party leader Zack Polanski admitted he was wrong to describe himself as a British Red Cross spokesperson during his leadership campaign and on his personal website. He accused right-wing media of politically motivated attacks amid the party's growing popularity.

stories.title: Will Trump pausing effort to open Strait bring an Iran deal? - analysis
stories.summary: President Trump's pause of the US effort to open the Strait of Hormuz highlights the complexity of military and diplomatic operations in the waterway amid the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: China erects monument to 1943 Cairo Declaration at historic hotel where it was signed
stories.summary: China erected a monument commemorating the 1943 Cairo Declaration at the Mena House hotel in Egypt, where the original World War II document was signed.

stories.title: Former SNP council leader jailed for sexual offences against young men and boys
stories.summary: Former SNP council leader Jordan Linden was sentenced to 18 months in prison at Falkirk sheriff court after being convicted of five sexual assaults against young men and teenagers, some as young as 14. The offences were committed over a decade between 2011 and 2021.

stories.title: Russia launches deadly attack in Ukraine: At least 28 killed
stories.summary: Russia launched a deadly attack on Ukraine, killing at least 28 people, according to France24's international affairs editor. The strikes occurred amid ongoing hostilities despite ceasefire discussions.

stories.title: China calls for Strait to be reopened 'as soon as possible' in Iran talks
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Beijing, with China calling for the Strait of Hormuz to be reopened as soon as possible. The visit marked Araghchi's first trip to China since the war began.

stories.title: Israelis' wealth grows 80% in six years
stories.summary: According to Bank of Israel data, the Israeli public's financial asset portfolio reached a record NIS 7.4 trillion, growing NIS 1.1 trillion in one year and representing an 80 percent increase over six years.

stories.title: Venice Biennale faces outcry over Israel and Russia's participation
stories.summary: The Venice Biennale contemporary art exhibition faced criticism over the participation of Israel and Russia, both involved in active conflicts. Iran cancelled its planned attendance. Ukraine and the United States are also represented at the biennial event held in Venice, Italy.

stories.title: Cruise ship hantavirus strain can spread among humans, says South Africa
stories.summary: South Africa's National Institute for Communicable Diseases confirmed that the Andes strain of hantavirus, which can in rare cases spread between humans, was identified in two cases linked to the MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak off Cape Verde. A Swiss passenger was also hospitalized in Zurich with the virus. The ship was due to head to Spain.

stories.title: ‘Putin only cares about parades’: fury as Russia rains missiles on Ukraine during 24-hour truce
stories.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced a unilateral 24-hour ceasefire, but Russia launched attacks on multiple Ukrainian cities with over 100 combat drones and three missiles, killing dozens. Moscow had previously requested a Saturday truce to hold its annual military parade on Red Square.

stories.title: Polanski accuses Times of ‘scraping the barrel’ over his claim to be charity spokesperson – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Green party leader Zack Polanski told the BBC he hosted fundraisers for the British Red Cross but acknowledged he should not have called himself a spokesperson for the charity. He rejected comparisons to former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn while praising some of Corbyn's policy proposals.

stories.title: Trump threatens 'high level of bombing' if Iran deal not agreed
stories.summary: President Trump threatened a "high level of bombing" against Iran if a deal to end the war is not reached, following reports that Washington and Tehran are close to agreeing on a memorandum.

stories.title: Trump pauses 'Project Freedom' amid 'progress' in US-Iran talks
stories.summary: The United States halted its Project Freedom naval operation in the Strait of Hormuz amid reported progress in diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Colombia tourist jewel plagued by violence
stories.summary: Armed groups operating in Colombia's Sierra Nevada region are conducting extortion and turf wars that threaten Indigenous communities and the area's growing tourism industry.

stories.title: Russian strike on Dnipro: Death toll climbs to four, 19 wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces struck four districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region more than 30 times. In the city of Dnipro, the attacks killed four people and wounded 19 others.

stories.title: Strike delays release of election results in Central African Republic
stories.summary: A strike by IT specialists at the Central African Republic's National Elections Authority data processing center has delayed the release of results from the second round of municipal, regional, and parliamentary elections held on April 26.

stories.title: Starmer warns Iran against encouraging hatred towards British Jews
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer warned Iran against encouraging hatred toward British Jews. The UK's approximately 300,000 Jewish residents have experienced a rise in antisemitic violence since the October 7, 2023, attacks.

stories.title: Rwanda: French Court to Rule On Rwanda Genocide Case Against Agathe Habyarimana
stories.summary: A French court is set to rule on a long-running investigation linked to the 1994 Rwandan genocide against the Tutsi. Prosecutors and civil parties are seeking the indictment of former Rwandan first lady Agathe Habyarimana.

stories.title: US pauses Hormuz escorts, Donald Trump says progress on Iran deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the U.S. would pause its escort operations for commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz barely a day after they began, citing a desire to reach a peace deal with Iran. Trump said progress was being made toward an agreement with Tehran.

stories.title: Bird flu may spread through air on California dairy farms, study finds
stories.summary: A new study suggests that bird flu may be capable of airborne transmission on dairy farms in California. Scientists are concerned that the virus's ongoing spread among mammals could increase the risk of more efficient human-to-human transmission.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF kills Hezbollah terrorists, strikes 25 targets over past day in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported killing Hezbollah fighters and striking 25 targets in southern Lebanon over the past day. The Israeli Air Force also intercepted a drone over southern Lebanon near an area where IDF soldiers were operating.

stories.title: Three infected people taken off hantavirus-hit cruise ship for treatment
stories.summary: Three hantavirus-infected individuals were evacuated from the cruise ship MV Hondius while it was anchored off Cape Verde, according to the World Health Organization. Health officials confirmed the presence of the rare Andes strain, the only known form of hantavirus capable of human-to-human transmission.

stories.title: The 2025 Pakistan-India conflict — as it happened
stories.summary: The article provides a timeline of the 2025 India-Pakistan military conflict, from the April 22 Pahalgam attack through Operation Bunyanum Marsoos and the May 10 ceasefire. Pakistan has termed the conflict 'Marka-i-Haq.' The nuclear-armed rivals exchanged missiles from May 6 to 10, raising global alarm.

stories.title: Local elections in UK could hasten end of embattled PM Keir Starmer’s tenure
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a growing party crisis ahead of local elections, compounded by the Epstein-Mandelson scandal and economic difficulties worsened by the Iran war. Analysts suggest his removal may be inevitable.

stories.title: From Beijing, Iran FM says Tehran seeks 'fair' deal with US
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, speaking during a visit to Beijing, stated that Tehran is seeking a fair and comprehensive agreement with Washington to resolve the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Two Australian states prepare to resettle children from Syrian detention camp with most bound for Melbourne
stories.summary: Authorities in Victoria and at least one other Australian state are preparing to resettle four women and nine children returning from Syrian detention camps linked to Islamic State. Most are expected to settle in Melbourne, and some mothers may face criminal charges upon arrival.

stories.title: War update: 186 frontline clashes over past day, intense fighting in Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukraine's military recorded 186 combat clashes with Russian forces along the frontline on May 5. The most intense fighting occurred in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: South Africa: Deadly Storms Trap Thousands and Force Schools to Shut Doors
stories.summary: Deadly storms in South Africa have trapped nearly two thousand families in the Northern Cape and destroyed homes in the Free State. Authorities closed over one hundred schools in the Western Cape to protect children from rising floodwaters.

stories.title: Europe readies trade war weapon amid China export deluge
stories.summary: The European Commission is developing a new trade instrument to counter a surge of low-cost Chinese imports, potentially to be presented at a May 29 meeting. Plans for a China-focused session were previously delayed after the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran shifted the agenda toward energy prices. The specific form of the tool has not been disclosed.

stories.title: Florida baby ‘born twice’ after elaborate surgery involving partial delivery
stories.summary: A Florida infant named Cassian Joubert underwent a rare prenatal surgery at 25 weeks in which he was partially delivered for a procedure and then placed back in his mother's womb before being born later. Orlando Health Women's Institute publicized the case, describing it as an innovative, likely life-saving operation.

stories.title: EU cyber plan barring Chinese suppliers will cost US$430 billion: report
stories.summary: A new study warns that the European Union's proposed Cybersecurity Act, which would bar Chinese suppliers from critical infrastructure, could cost the bloc approximately €367.8 billion over five years. The bulk of costs stem from removing and replacing Chinese hardware, estimated at €146.2 billion, with additional losses from service disruptions, resource reallocation, and legal expenses.

stories.title: US military says it struck vessel in Eastern Pacific, killing 3
stories.summary: The U.S. military struck a vessel in the Eastern Pacific on Tuesday, killing three people. U.S. Southern Command described those killed as "narco-terrorists," while human rights groups have labeled such operations as extrajudicial killings.

stories.title: US petrol prices 50 percent higher than before war on Iran
stories.summary: Average US petrol prices have reached $4.48 per gallon, according to AAA, representing a roughly 50 percent increase since the start of the war on Iran.

stories.title: Iran’s Survival Is Not Victory
stories.summary: Tehran is employing rhetoric that reframes its strategic concessions as acts of sovereignty and self-respect, according to analysis of Iran's latest public messaging amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine’s air defenses down 89 out of 108 Russian drones overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 89 of 108 Russian drones launched in an overnight attack on May 6, 2026.

stories.title: Cape Verde prepares to help virus-hit cruise ship, Canary Islands oppose docking
stories.summary: Cape Verde is preparing additional medical assistance for a Dutch cruise ship anchored off its coast amid a suspected hantavirus outbreak. The Canary Islands rejected a Spanish proposal to allow the ship to dock, citing public health risks.

stories.title: Airport Authority reports ‘less than’ 5% cancellations despite Middle East war
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Airport Authority reported that fewer than 5 percent of flights were cancelled for May and June combined, and about 1 percent during the peak July travel period, despite a global fuel crisis triggered by the Middle East war. Transport Secretary Mable Chan said authorities would review charges to ease the industry's burden.

stories.title: ‘A stress test’: US-Germany rift widens as Iran war drags on
stories.summary: Tensions between the United States and Germany are growing as the Iran war continues. A German official described the relationship as being tested, while an opposition MP said Berlin is not neutral in the conflict.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Donetsk region leave six killed, 14 injured over past day
stories.summary: Russian strikes on Ukraine's Donetsk region on May 5 killed six residents and injured 14 others.

stories.title: Boko Haram attack on Chad army base kills at least 24 people
stories.summary: Boko Haram fighters attacked the Barka Tolorom military base on Lake Chad late on Monday, killing at least 24 people and wounding 46 soldiers, according to Chadian army sources.

stories.title: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas’s son, long in the shadows, seeks political role
stories.summary: Yasser Abbas, the businessman son of 90-year-old Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, is expected to run for a leadership role in his father's political party. The move comes amid a succession struggle for control of the Palestinian Authority. Critics have accused Yasser and his brother Tarek of using public funds for their businesses, which both deny.

stories.title: Hungary's new government pushes for euro by 2030
stories.summary: Hungary's new government has announced its goal of adopting the euro by 2030 while seeking to repair relations with Brussels. Experts caution that a weak economy and tight timelines make the transition challenging.

stories.title: Asia must unite to avert an Iran war food crisis
stories.summary: Following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz collapsed, disrupting energy, fertiliser, and food supply chains across Asia. Rising fuel, freight, and insurance costs are feeding into fertiliser and food prices. The strait carries around one-third of globally traded oil, amplifying the crisis's impact on the region.

stories.title: Next India-Pakistan conflict may be ‘more dangerous’, analysts warn
stories.summary: On the first anniversary of the May 2025 India-Pakistan military conflict, U.S. and international analysts warn that a future crisis between the two nuclear-armed states could be more dangerous and harder for outside powers to contain. The Washington Post noted the risks may be underestimated globally.

stories.title: Shopping centre fire kills at least eight people in Iran
stories.summary: A fire at a shopping centre in Iran killed at least eight people. Details on the cause and exact location were not immediately specified.

stories.title: Australian women with alleged ISIL ties returning from Syria, minister says
stories.summary: Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett confirmed that some Australian women with alleged Islamic State ties returning from Syria will be arrested and charged upon arrival.

stories.title: From “defending Crimea” to defendants: Russia jails its own Española naval unit fighters in occupied Sevastopol
stories.summary: A Russian court in occupied Sevastopol has jailed members of the Española naval unit, originally established by Stanislav Orlov in late 2024 to combat Ukrainian sea drones. The prosecutions came six months after Orlov's death.

stories.title: Injury toll in Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia rises to 43
stories.summary: The number of people injured by a Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia on May 5 rose to 43, with 18 hospitalized.

stories.title: 'Unconscionable to keep them on cruise ship’: WHOs Gostin warns against repeating COVID-era mistakes
stories.summary: WHO Center on Global Health Law director Lawrence Gostin warned against repeating COVID-era mistakes by keeping suspected hantavirus cases confined aboard a cruise ship off Cape Verde. He argued that the international community had already learned the dangers of denying passengers adequate medical care and disembarkation at enormous human cost.

stories.title: Spain opens port to hantavirus-hit cruise ship as rare Andes strain confirmed
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius, hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak while off Cabo Verde with nearly 150 people aboard, was set to head to Spain for port access. South Africa's health authorities confirmed that the Andes strain of hantavirus, which can in rare cases spread between humans, was identified among the victims. A returning Swiss passenger was hospitalized in Zurich with the virus.

stories.title: US pauses Hormuz escorts in bid for deal, as threats continue
stories.summary: President Donald Trump paused a U.S. military operation to escort vessels through the Strait of Hormuz after just one day, following a request from mediator Pakistan and other countries. The halt came as negotiations with Iran continued amid ongoing threats in the region.

stories.title: North Korea drops reunification goal from constitution
stories.summary: North Korea has amended its constitution to remove any reference to reunification with South Korea. The revision formalizes leader Kim Jong Un's policy of treating Seoul as a permanent adversary.

stories.title: Middle East War: US-Iran ceasefire appears to hold
stories.summary: A ceasefire between the United States and Iran appeared to be holding on Tuesday despite missile and drone attacks on vessels and an Emirati port the previous day.

stories.title: Democrats win big in US special elections, but Trump reinforces hold on GOP
stories.summary: Democrats won key special elections in Indiana, Ohio, and Michigan, signaling growing momentum ahead of November's midterm elections. Meanwhile, President Trump continued to demonstrate strong influence within the Republican Party.

stories.title: Israel orders evacuations for 12 villages in Lebanon before planned strikes
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings for 12 villages in southern Lebanon, mostly north of the Litani River, instructing residents to move at least one kilometre away ahead of planned air strikes targeting Hezbollah.

stories.title: Victory in Marka-i-Haq ‘elevated Pakistan’s global standing’
stories.summary: Pakistani leaders, including Deputy PM Ishaq Dar and others, marked diplomatic gains following the 2025 conflict with India, which Pakistan calls 'Marka-i-Haq.' Officials credited U.S., Saudi, and Turkish efforts toward the ceasefire and said Pakistan's international standing was elevated after repelling Indian aggression.

stories.title: Middle East War: Analyst says Strait of Hormuz situation 'highly uncertain'
stories.summary: Analysts describe the situation around the Strait of Hormuz as highly uncertain, with Iran continuing to signal its intent to target vessels that do not use its preferred transit route through the vital oil chokepoint.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,050 over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia's total combat personnel losses since February 24, 2022 have reached approximately 1,337,170, with 1,050 casualties recorded in the past day.

stories.title: U.S. Military strike on alleged drug boat kills three in the eastern Pacific
stories.summary: A U.S. military strike on an alleged drug trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific killed three people. President Trump has characterized the operations as part of an armed conflict with cartels in Latin America, framing the strikes as necessary to stop drug flows into the United States.

stories.title: UK Green Party said to probe dozens of council candidates over antisemitism
stories.summary: The UK Green Party is reportedly investigating more than 30 council candidates over antisemitism allegations and is introducing a fast-track system to handle cases. The party noted the number represents a small fraction of its 4,500 candidates.

stories.title: Syria says it dismantled Hezbollah-linked cell plotting assassinations
stories.summary: Syrian authorities announced they dismantled a cell linked to Hezbollah that was allegedly planning targeted assassinations against high-level government officials.

stories.title: Accelerating the climate transition
stories.summary: As monsoon season approaches, the article urges Pakistan to accelerate its transition to a climate-resilient, low-carbon economy. It notes the country remains highly vulnerable to climate impacts, as demonstrated by devastating floods in 2022 and again in 2025.

stories.title: Hard choices
stories.summary: One year after India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty, Pakistan's National Security Council warned that diverting water flows would be considered an act of war. India has accelerated controversial hydropower projects and revised completion deadlines. No progress toward restoring the treaty has been visible.

stories.title: US must not insult IRGC during the World Cup: Iran’s football chief
stories.summary: Iran's football federation chief Mehdi Taj demanded that co-host the United States ensure the Iranian military and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps are not insulted during the FIFA World Cup.

stories.title: Israel says strikes targeted Hezbollah sites across southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported striking approximately 25 Hezbollah-linked targets across southern Lebanon over the past day, claiming several fighters were killed. Targets included buildings allegedly used by fighters and a weapons depot.

stories.title: IRGC targets Komala headquarters in Kurdistan Region with drone strike - report
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reportedly carried out a drone strike targeting the headquarters of the Komala party in Iraq's Kurdistan Region. Separately, residents in Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, and Sirik reported hearing explosions in the early morning hours.

stories.title: China’s Wang Yi and Iranian FM back new regional security framework in Gulf
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi voiced support for a new Gulf security framework led by regional countries during talks in Beijing. Wang urged a swift reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, stating that Gulf and Middle Eastern nations should determine their own future.

stories.title: An asymmetrical war
stories.summary: The article discusses Henry Kissinger's 2012 remarks at the Woodrow Wilson Centre about the U.S. entering wars without clear exit strategies, using the Afghan conflict as an example. It draws parallels to broader patterns of asymmetric warfare involving major military powers.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says pausing Hormuz operation in push for Iran deal
stories.summary: President Trump announced a pause of U.S. operations in the Strait of Hormuz to advance an Iran deal. Secretary of State Rubio separately confirmed that the U.S. completed offensive operations against Iran, dubbed "Operation Epic Fury."

stories.title: The Cop on the Corner Is Our First Line of Defense: Local Police and the Surveillance Detection Gap
stories.summary: On November 24, 2025, New Castle County police officers in Wilmington, Delaware's Canby Park discovered a University of Delaware student in a parked Toyota Tacoma possessing a converted machine gun, over 100 rounds of ammunition, body armor, and a notebook detailing a planned attack on the campus police department.

stories.title: Trump pauses effort to escort ships in Strait of Hormuz, citing deal progress
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a temporary pause in a U.S. military operation to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz, citing progress toward a deal with Iran. The strait had been virtually shut during the conflict, blocking roughly 20 percent of global oil supplies. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had outlined the escort effort just hours earlier.

stories.title: Iran war day 68: Trump talks about progress in talks; Rubio says war ‘over’
stories.summary: On day 68 of the Iran war, President Trump paused the US 'Project Freedom' operation in the Strait of Hormuz, citing progress toward an agreement with Iran. Secretary of State Rubio declared the war effectively over.

stories.title: Mexico marks 164 years since Battle of Puebla with historic reenactment
stories.summary: Mexico commemorated the 164th anniversary of the Battle of Puebla on May 5, 2026, with hundreds of participants reenacting the 1862 clash against French forces in Mexico City.

stories.title: Russian drone hits private house in Kharkiv, fire breaks out
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a private house in Kharkiv, Ukraine, setting it on fire.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: The United States paused "Project Freedom," its naval escort mission in the Strait of Hormuz, as diplomatic talks with Iran appeared to gain momentum. President Trump said the operation would halt while negotiations move toward what he described as a "final agreement." Military activity continues in Lebanon and economic pressures linked to the broader conflict persist.

stories.title: Manipur’s ‘unknown’ killers: Three years of India’s bloody ethnic conflict
stories.summary: Ethnic conflict in India's northeastern state of Manipur has persisted for three years, with violence mutating and deepening. The identities of assailants remain officially unnamed despite ongoing killings.

stories.title: Syria’s Suwayda: A new hub for the multibillion-dollar Captagon trade?
stories.summary: Syria's Suwayda province has emerged as a major hub for the multibillion-dollar Captagon drug trade, prompting Jordanian military strikes and triggering a broader regional security crisis.

stories.title: Between Intent and Capability: Assessing the Lack of Iranian Attacks on the U.S. Homeland
stories.summary: Shortly after the start of the Iran war, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Qods Force publicly threatened to carry out attacks on the U.S. homeland. The Qods Force issued a televised statement warning that Americans would no longer be safe anywhere in the world.

stories.title: China builds world’s first ‘coal battery’, war on Alzheimer’s: 7 science highlights
stories.summary: Chinese scientists developed a "coal battery" that generates electricity from coal with zero carbon dioxide emissions and higher energy efficiency than conventional burning methods. The breakthrough was among several recent Chinese science highlights reported over the past two weeks.

stories.title: How India is cashing in on cows to beat cooking gas crunch
stories.summary: Amid an energy crunch caused by the Iran war, many Indians face long queues for cooking gas cylinders. In the village of Nekpur in Uttar Pradesh, residents like 25-year-old Gauri Devi are using biogas produced from cow dung as an alternative cooking fuel, easing pressure on conventional gas supplies.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi arrives in China for talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese counterpart Wang Yi, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts related to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: US military releases video of strike on alleged drug boat
stories.summary: The US military released video footage of a strike on a vessel it described as an alleged drug boat. No further details on the location or casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: ‘Gunpowder, sparks’: volunteer hurt at China fireworks blast scene tells of clean-up risk
stories.summary: An explosion at the Huasheng Fireworks Manufacturing and Display Company in Liuyang city, Hunan province, killed 26 people and injured 61. A volunteer excavator operator described dangerous clean-up conditions amid gunpowder and sparks, with secondary blasts on Tuesday morning wounding him and other rescuers.

stories.title: Iran seeks Fifa guarantees before attending World Cup in US
stories.summary: Iran's football federation chief Mehdi Taj demanded guarantees from FIFA that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and other state symbols would not be insulted when Iran's national team attends the World Cup in the United States in June.

stories.title: Russian guided bomb attacks kill at least 26 civilians across Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that Russian guided bomb strikes on May 5, 2026, killed at least 26 civilians across the country, with the heaviest casualties in the Zaporizhzhia and Kramatorsk areas.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'I Was Misled,' Alleged Coup Defendant Says in Video Recording Played in Court
stories.summary: In a Nigerian court, a defendant in an alleged coup plot case said in a video recording that he was misled, describing his encounter with the alleged mastermind of the failed plot.

stories.title: Illegal foreigner legalization scheme busted in Kyiv
stories.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement arrested a 45-year-old Kyiv resident and a 36-year-old lawyer's assistant for running a scheme to illegally legalize foreign nationals in Ukraine through fictitious companies and charitable organizations.

stories.title: Airlines hike fares, cut millions of seats as Iran war drives up fuel costs
stories.summary: Rising jet fuel prices driven by the Iran war are forcing airlines to cut millions of seats and raise fares, disrupting summer travel plans for passengers worldwide.

stories.title: How unbreakable is Iran's regime? Tehran defiant despite deepening hardship for citizens
stories.summary: Iran faces severe economic strain amid ongoing tensions with the United States, but the regime shows no sign of capitulating. A recent flare-up near the Strait of Hormuz has further disrupted oil flows. Both Tehran and Washington signal willingness to endure the financial consequences of continued brinkmanship.

stories.title: Nigeria: Only 28.5m of 61.9m Crude Oil Barrels Reached Local Refineries in Q1 - - NUPRC
stories.summary: Nigeria's upstream petroleum regulator reported that only 28.5 million of 61.9 million barrels of crude oil reached local refineries in the first quarter of 2026. Supply shortfalls were largely attributed to pricing disputes despite adequate allocation.

stories.title: Nigeria: INEC Begins Final Phase of Voter Registration Ahead of 2027 Election
stories.summary: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has launched the final phase of voter registration ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging all eligible citizens aged 18 and above to register.

stories.title: Tuareg separatists and al-Qaeda-linked fighters combine to cause havoc in Mali
stories.summary: An informal alliance between Tuareg separatist groups and al-Qaeda-linked fighters in Mali has intensified security challenges for President Assimi Goita's government. The partnership emerged amid ongoing instability, including a suicide attack that killed Defence Minister Sadio Camara in Bamako.

stories.title: Oil prices ease and markets rally as Trump works towards deal with Iran
stories.summary: Oil prices eased and stock markets rallied as President Trump cited "great progress" toward a final agreement with Iran and briefly paused the U.S. "Project Freedom" operation escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz. The strait, carrying about a fifth of global oil supplies, has been blockaded by Iran since late February.

stories.title: Man sets Ramat Gan cafe on fire after threatening owner over Saturday opening
stories.summary: A man set fire to a cafe in Ramat Gan, Israel, after threatening its owner over the establishment being open on Saturday. Ramat Gan Mayor Carmel Shama-Hacohen condemned the arson as an attack on the city's character as a place of liberty.

stories.title: US adds officer assault charge against suspect in Trump assassination attempt
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors added an officer assault charge against Cole Allen, a suspect in an assassination attempt on former President Donald Trump. The new charge accuses Allen of firing at a U.S. Secret Service agent at a security checkpoint.

stories.title: Two killed, three injured in shootings at shopping centre in Texas
stories.summary: A shooting at a shopping center in Texas killed two people and injured three others. The suspect, 69-year-old Seung Han Ho, was arrested approximately six kilometers away at a grocery store after a brief foot chase.

stories.title: Child protection workers stood down after alleged murder of Australian girl
stories.summary: Australian child protection workers have been stood down following the alleged murder of a five-year-old girl who was found dead five days after going missing from an Aboriginal town camp in Alice Springs.

stories.title: Albanese announces fuel stockpile plan amid Hormuz blockade concerns
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a 10 billion Australian dollar ($7.22 billion) fuel security package to boost national stockpiles amid concerns over a potential Strait of Hormuz blockade. The plan includes a reserve of approximately 1 billion litres to ensure at least 50 days of onshore fuel supply.

stories.title: Ukraine needs scenario planning and unconventional solutions, expert says
stories.summary: An expert called for Ukraine to pursue scenario planning and unconventional policy solutions as the post-World War II international order faces growing challenges. Ukraine's resilience against Russian aggression was highlighted as unprecedented.

stories.title: Africa: Uhuru Kenyatta Warns Trust Deficit Is Africa's Biggest Threat to Peace
stories.summary: Former Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta warned that a deepening trust deficit among African nations poses one of the continent's greatest threats to peace, stability, and effective conflict resolution.

stories.title: Malawi: Malawi Fuel Crisis Deepens As Oil Shortages Spread
stories.summary: Malawi is experiencing a severe fuel crisis as oil shortages spread across the country. The government has resorted to selling gold reserves to purchase fuel, a measure that carries significant economic costs.

stories.title: Jury convicts four from Palestine Action over UK break-in
stories.summary: A UK jury convicted four Palestine Action activists of criminal damage at Israeli defence firm Elbit Systems' premises in Bristol, England. The group was accused of breaking into the site in August 2024 and causing over $1.35 million in damage. The conviction came during a retrial after a previous jury failed to reach verdicts on the charges.

stories.title: U.S. State Department approves $374M bomb kit package for Ukraine
stories.summary: The US State Department approved a $373.6 million sale to Ukraine of Joint Direct Attack Munition – Extended Range (JDAM-ER) kits to convert conventional aerial bombs into precision-guided munitions.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump changes strait of Hormuz plan again as Rubio says US offensive is ‘over’
stories.summary: President Trump paused the U.S. "Project Freedom" naval escort operation in the Strait of Hormuz after just one day, saying he hoped to finalize a deal with Iran. Secretary of State Rubio said the U.S. had achieved its objectives. South Korean shipper HMM arranged to tow a damaged bulk carrier to Dubai after an explosion in the strait.

stories.title: China calls US Israel war against Iran illegitimate
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi declared the war waged by the United States and Israel against Iran "illegitimate" during a meeting with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Beijing. Wang said China would continue efforts to ease tensions and called for a complete ceasefire, describing the region as being at a "critical juncture."

stories.title: Trump says pausing Hormuz operation in push for Iran deal
stories.summary: President Trump announced on Truth Social that he is pausing "Project Freedom" in the Strait of Hormuz at the request of mediator Pakistan and other countries, citing "great progress" toward a final agreement with Tehran.

stories.title: Watch: How a huge wave of Israeli strikes brought chaos to Lebanon
stories.summary: On 8 April 2026, Israel carried out a large wave of airstrikes across Lebanon in one of the deadliest episodes in the country's recent history. The BBC's Nawal Al-Maghafi investigated the sequence of events and the resulting chaos.

stories.title: Australia: Suspect in Bondi massacre to face more charges
stories.summary: Nineteen additional charges have been filed against a 24-year-old man accused of a mass shooting at Bondi Beach in Sydney during a Jewish festival in 2025. The attack resulted in multiple deaths.

stories.title: Hong Kong school to seek feedback, review phone ban after student outcry
stories.summary: A Hong Kong secondary school, Kwun Tong Maryknoll College, said it would review its tightened mobile phone ban after student backlash. The school had launched a pilot restriction for Form Three and Four students and planned to extend it to all students. Principal Caroline Sin wrote to parents acknowledging the concerns.

stories.title: Venice Biennale previews in chaos, overshadowed by Israeli and Russian participation
stories.summary: The Venice Biennale preview events were disrupted by tensions over Israeli and Russian participation, leading to the resignation of the entire jury. The Israeli artist involved described the move as "fair" but expressed a desire to be judged on artistic merit rather than nationality.

stories.title: China woman loses 21kg after friend’s idea that being thinner makes her resemble famous actress
stories.summary: A woman in Zhejiang province, eastern China, lost 21.5 kilograms in four months after her friend told her she would resemble actress Yang Mi if she became thinner. She went from 64 kilograms to 42.5 kilograms and shared her experience on social media.

stories.title: Apps, activists and an ‘air war’: Essex campaign is test of Reform UK’s professionalisation
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage toured towns in Essex ahead of local council elections, with more than one million county council votes at stake. The party is using the elections to showcase a more professional campaign approach, incorporating digital tools and structured canvassing.

stories.title: Air defences engaged drones over Qeshm island, Iran says
stories.summary: Iranian authorities said air defense systems on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz engaged drones, attributing loud sounds heard on the strategic island to the interceptions. Officials in Hormozgan province denied reports of explosions or damage on the island.

stories.title: Israel ready to deploy ‘entire air force’ against Iran if needed: New chief
stories.summary: Israel's newly appointed air force chief, Major General Omer Tischler, stated that Israel is prepared to deploy its entire air force against Iran if necessary, pledging continued action "with determination" and power.

stories.title: In Gaza, the simplest of weddings are barely affordable
stories.summary: Couples in Gaza are holding weddings in tents as ongoing war, mass displacement, and soaring prices make even the simplest ceremonies barely affordable.

stories.title: Iran Has All the Hallmarks of a Forever War
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the ongoing conflict with Iran exhibits characteristics of a prolonged, open-ended military engagement. The article suggests a potential resolution exists but cautions it will not come quickly.

stories.title: Rubio says ‘Operation Epic Fury’ is over, insists US now acting defensively in Hormuz
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared that "Operation Epic Fury" has concluded and said American forces near the Strait of Hormuz are now operating in a purely defensive role. Rubio stated US forces would only fire if attacked first but warned Iran of potential "generational destruction."

stories.title: Wednesday briefing: How Trump’s attempt to reopen to strait of Hormuz brought war closer again
stories.summary: The U.S. effort dubbed "Project Freedom" to escort stranded vessels through the Strait of Hormuz threatened to collapse the fragile ceasefire with Iran. Fighting briefly restarted as Iran sought to maintain control of the critical waterway. Trump subsequently paused the operation.
