stories.title: What to know about Israeli President Herzog’s trip to Central America?
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog embarked on a four-day visit to Panama and Costa Rica. Israel's Foreign Ministry stated the trip aims to deepen diplomatic and partnership ties with Central American nations.

stories.title: Backlash grows over Israeli character in R.F. Kuang’s upcoming novel 'Taipei Story'
stories.summary: Author R.F. Kuang faced criticism and boycott calls after a leaked excerpt from her upcoming novel "Taipei Story" featured an Israeli character. The backlash grew on social media ahead of the book's release.

stories.title: CS Anthem chemical tanker was second US-flagged vessel to exit Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The US-flagged chemical tanker CS Anthem exited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday under US military protection, becoming the second known commercial American vessel to transit the waterway during the current tensions.

stories.title: Wadephul calls on Russia to accept Ukraine's ceasefire proposal
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul called on Russia to accept Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's ceasefire proposal and begin a ceasefire immediately.

stories.title: Ukraine reports Russian strike after Kyiv-declared ceasefire begins
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that Russia struck an industrial facility in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Wednesday morning, just hours after a unilateral ceasefire declared by Kyiv took effect. Both Ukraine and Russia announced competing ceasefires on different dates during the week, timed around Russia's celebrations of the Soviet Union's World War II victory anniversary.

stories.title: US president Trump restarts Pope feud ahead of Rubio visit to Vatican
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly attacked Pope Leo ahead of Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to the Vatican, accusing the Pope of supporting Iran's pursuit of nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Where do Bayern's prolific trio rank in greatest front threes ever?
stories.summary: Bayern Munich's front three of Harry Kane, Luis Diaz, and Michael Olise have scored 100 goals this season ahead of the Champions League semi-final second leg against Paris Saint-Germain.

stories.title: Sudan: Drone Strike On Khartoum Airport 'First in 7 Months' - Aid Ops Not Affected
stories.summary: A drone strike, believed to have been launched by the Rapid Support Forces, targeted Khartoum Airport and surrounding areas for the first time in seven months. The main terminal was reportedly not hit. Additional strikes targeted Obeid Khatim Street, areas south of Khartoum, and El Murkhiyat military base in Omdurman.

stories.title: New Hebrew press in Berlin seeks to build literary home outside of Israel
stories.summary: A new Hebrew-language publishing house called Altneuland has been established in Berlin, the first such venture since Israel's founding. Its founders aim to serve Israeli writers and readers abroad while declining Israeli government funding.

stories.title: Australia says Islamic State-linked citizens in Syria camp plan to return home
stories.summary: Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Australian citizens linked to Islamic State held in a Syrian camp are planning to return to Australia. Burke warned that any returnee suspected of criminal activity would face the full force of the law.

stories.title: US officials seek to maintain ceasefire with Iran, UAE says it was attacked
stories.summary: US officials are working to maintain a ceasefire with Iran while the UAE reported being attacked. The Strait of Hormuz has been virtually shut since the US and Israel began military operations against Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Horrified Wagga residents call for proper sanitation at homeless camp where baby was found dead
stories.summary: A newborn baby was found dead in a tent at a homeless encampment at Wagga beach in Wagga Wagga, Australia. The camp lacked basic sanitation, with the nearest public toilets and running water up to 15 minutes away. Residents called on authorities to provide proper facilities.

stories.title: Mother of detained flotilla activist Avila dies in Brazil
stories.summary: Teresa Regina de Avila e Silva, mother of detained Global Sumud Flotilla activist Thiago Avila, died in Brazil at the age of 63. Thiago Avila remains detained in Israel after being seized when a flotilla vessel was intercepted.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1532: Russia is losing troops faster than it can replace them, for fifth month in row
stories.summary: On day 1,532 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russian guided bomb strikes killed 12 people in Zaporizhzhia. Reports indicate Russia is losing troops faster than it can replace them for the fifth consecutive month.

stories.title: Palestinian ambassador protests to Foreign Office over ’erasure’ by British Museum
stories.summary: The Palestinian ambassador to the UK lodged a complaint with the Foreign Office after the British Museum removed references to Palestine from exhibits, replacing the name with "Gaza" and "the West Bank." The UK had officially recognized the state of Palestine in September 2025.

stories.title: Rare pregnancy complication has put UK women into ‘emergency surgery’
stories.summary: Scores of women across the United Kingdom have reported undergoing emergency surgery, including hysterectomies, after NHS medical staff failed to detect placenta accreta spectrum, a rare but potentially fatal pregnancy complication. A campaign launched in February aims to raise awareness of the condition among healthcare workers and expectant mothers.

stories.title: Attempts to stop prison drone drug deliveries hampered by crumbling Victorian walls
stories.summary: Prison governors in the United Kingdom say that crumbling walls in Victorian-era prisons are preventing the installation of stronger netting and window grilles designed to block drone deliveries of drugs and weapons to inmates. The aging infrastructure cannot support the additional weight of the proposed anti-drone measures.

stories.title: Iran’s Araghchi holds talks with China’s Wang Yi in Beijing
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing for diplomatic talks. The meeting took place one week before President Trump's scheduled visit to the Chinese capital.

stories.title: Australia warns of arrests as 13 people linked to Isis set to return from Syria
stories.summary: Australia's Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke confirmed that 13 Australians — four women and nine children — linked to Islamic State are returning from the Roj camp in Syria. Authorities warned some may face arrest upon arrival at Sydney and Melbourne airports.

stories.title: Mali: UN Warns of Worsening Human Rights Crisis in Mali After Deadly Attacks
stories.summary: The UN human rights office (OHCHR) warned that Mali's human rights situation is rapidly deteriorating following coordinated attacks by armed groups. Civilians have been killed, displaced, and cut off from food and humanitarian aid across the country.

stories.title: Sudan: Education or Food? Funding Shortfalls Force Sudanese Refugees in Egypt to 'Make Very Difficult Decisions'
stories.summary: UNHCR has warned that Sudanese refugees who fled the war to Egypt face potential loss of critical survival services due to funding shortfalls. Refugee families are being forced to choose between education and food for their children.

stories.title: Democrats urge US to acknowledge Israel’s nuclear program
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers urged the Trump administration to publicly acknowledge Israel's nuclear arsenal, arguing that continued secrecy on the matter undermines US credibility on global nuclear nonproliferation policy.

stories.title: Iran, China weigh ceasefire and Hormuz reopening efforts
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited China for the first time since the start of the conflict for talks with counterpart Wang Yi. Discussions focused on maintaining a ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, both priorities for Beijing's trade route stability.

stories.title: More than 600 attacks hit US sites in Iraq, official says
stories.summary: A senior US State Department official said more than 600 attacks have targeted American facilities in Iraq during the war with Iran. The official called on Iraqi leaders to take concrete action, including expelling militia groups from state institutions and cutting their access to government funding.

stories.title: Oil refinery in Leningrad region halts refining after drone attack – Reuters
stories.summary: The Kirishi Oil Refinery in Russia's Leningrad region halted oil processing following a Ukrainian drone attack on the night of May 4-5, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Protesters bearing Hezbollah flag scuffle with NYPD while marching on synagogue
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters marched toward a synagogue in New York during a demonstration against an Israel-linked real estate event. Some demonstrators carried Hezbollah flags and clashed with NYPD officers, chanting slogans against the IDF and Israel.

stories.title: Survey shows most Israelis oppose ending Iran war
stories.summary: A survey by the Israel Democracy Institute found that 59 percent of Israelis oppose ending the war with Iran under current conditions. Two-thirds of Jewish respondents said doing so would be only slightly or not at all compatible with Israel's national security interests, while Arab citizens of Israel were more divided.

stories.title: Anxious Australia and jittery Japan deepen ‘quasi-alliance’ for an uneasy age
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi visited Australia, where she and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signed an economic security pact and unlocked nearly US$1 billion in critical minerals funding. The deepened partnership reflects shared concerns about the U.S. under Trump, China, and supply chain vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Rubio says Israel-Lebanon peace deal is achievable but Hezbollah is a problem
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a peace deal between Israel and Lebanon is achievable but identified the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah as a major obstacle to progress.

stories.title: Romania’s pro-EU government ousted after no-confidence vote
stories.summary: Romania's pro-European Union coalition government led by Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan was removed from power following a parliamentary vote of no confidence.

stories.title: Draft UN resolution urges Iran halt actions in Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States and several Gulf allies, including Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, and Qatar, drafted a UN Security Council resolution calling on Iran to stop attacking vessels, laying mines, and imposing fees in the Strait of Hormuz. A vote is expected in the coming days.

stories.title: AI ecosystems in China and US grow apart amid tech war
stories.summary: China and the United States are developing increasingly divergent AI ecosystems amid the ongoing tech war. Chinese startup DeepSeek launched V4 AI models optimized for Huawei's Ascend chips, reflecting Beijing's push for technological self-reliance.

stories.title: Hong Kong Legco issues warning to lawmaker Judy Chan over traffic offence
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Legislative Council issued a written warning to lawmaker Judy Chan Kapui of the New People's Party after she was filmed driving against the flow of traffic in Wan Chai in January. The Supervisory Committee urged her to be mindful of her conduct.

stories.title: Four in five Britons worried Iran war will make food more expensive, poll finds
stories.summary: An Opinium poll found that 80% of Britons are concerned the Iran conflict will drive up grocery prices, while 73% expect costs of other products to rise as well. UK retailers warned the government that the window to reduce energy costs for businesses is closing, as the Middle East conflict threatens supply chains.

stories.title: Man accused of anti-Semitic Bondi Beach mass shooting faces 19 extra charges
stories.summary: Naveed Akram, 24, accused of killing 15 people in a mass shooting targeting Hanukkah celebrations at Bondi Beach, Australia, in December 2025, now faces 19 additional charges. His father and alleged accomplice, Sajid Akram, was killed by police during the attack.

stories.title: New gallery at Paris museum reckons with French role in Nazi art looting
stories.summary: The Musée d'Orsay in Paris opened a new gallery displaying artworks that remain unclaimed since being seized by Nazis during World War II. The exhibition addresses the French art market's role in profiting from property looted from Jewish victims of the Holocaust.

stories.title: South Korean judge who handed Kim Keon-hee 4-year term found dead days after verdict
stories.summary: South Korean appellate court judge Shin Jong-oh was found dead near the Seoul High Court in Seocho district with severe injuries. Shin had recently presided over the case of former first lady Kim Keon-hee, overturning her acquittal and imposing a four-year sentence. Police suspect he died from a fall.

stories.title: US pauses plan to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a pause of the US military operation escorting commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route.

stories.title: State must ensure mass centralized procurement of robots for AFU
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense is being urged to centralize procurement of ground robotic systems to supply the Armed Forces of Ukraine with reliable solutions in large quantities for frontline use.

stories.title: 'No one else can make us surrender': Iran defies US threats
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian declared that no one can force Iran to surrender, responding to US demands for concessions in war-ending negotiations. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps also announced a new security plan for the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Eight killed, dozens injured in Iran shopping centre fire
stories.summary: At least eight people were killed and 36 injured in a fire at the Arghavan shopping centre in Andisheh, west of Tehran. Iranian media reported the blaze was caused by flammable exterior cladding, raising concerns about building safety standards.

stories.title: Czechs pack Prague's Old Town Square to protest government media plans
stories.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Prague's Old Town Square to protest Czech government plans to change the funding model for state broadcasters. Critics warn the proposed changes could undermine the independence of public media.

stories.title: ‘May can give a false sense of safety,’ expert warns after Hong Kong hiker dies in Japan
stories.summary: A Hong Kong hiker died after becoming stranded with another man in Japan's Northern Alps. A mountaineering expert warned that May's warmer lowland temperatures can create a false sense of safety, while mountain conditions remain volatile with risks of snowstorms and freezing temperatures.

stories.title: US lawmaker says Trump falsely declared Iran war ended
stories.summary: US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi accused President Trump of falsely telling Congress that the war with Iran has ended. Krishnamoorthi cited the ongoing US naval blockade on Iranian ports and continued exchanges of fire between US and Iranian forces.

stories.title: US doubles down on urging Lebanese president to meet Netanyahu, unfazed by his refusal
stories.summary: The United States urged Lebanese President Joseph Aoun to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to advance peace and security agreements. Secretary of State Rubio described peace as "imminently achievable" but identified Hezbollah as the main obstacle, despite Aoun's refusal to hold the meeting.

stories.title: US pauses Hormuz escorts in bid for deal, as threats continue
stories.summary: The US military paused "Project Freedom," its escort operation for commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, in pursuit of a diplomatic deal with Iran. The escorts had drawn Iranian attacks, threatening an already fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: ICC fugitive? Duterte ally’s paid Philippine Senate vanishing act draws fire
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald "Bato" Dela Rosa, a former national police chief and key figure in ex-President Duterte's war on drugs, has been absent from work for six months. Reports suggest he is avoiding potential arrest linked to the International Criminal Court's investigation into crimes against humanity.

stories.title: UAE air defences engage missiles, drones; Tehran denies attacking UAE
stories.summary: The UAE's defense ministry reported that its air defenses engaged missiles and drones it attributed to Iran on May 5. Iran's joint military command denied carrying out any missile or drone operations against the UAE in recent days.

stories.title: Brazil's Lula to raise organized crime in talks with Trump this week
stories.summary: Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin announced that President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva plans to propose an agreement on combating organized crime during his meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump this week.

stories.title: Warhead of Russian Geran-2 drone found in Kyiv forest belt
stories.summary: Police in Kyiv's Desnianskyi District seized the warhead of a Russian Geran-2 drone found in a local forest belt.

stories.title: Russian attacks kill 27 in Ukraine before proposed rival ceasefires
stories.summary: Russian attacks across eastern Ukraine killed at least 27 people on Tuesday, including 12 in one of the deadliest strikes of the year. The attacks came hours before rival ceasefire proposals: Russia announced a pause for May 8–9 to mark Victory Day, while Ukraine proposed an open-ended ceasefire.

stories.title: China’s chipmakers pour revenue into R&D, outpacing US ratios
stories.summary: Chinese chipmakers are spending a higher proportion of revenue on research and development than their U.S. counterparts, according to first-quarter 2026 earnings. Beijing-based Moore Threads spent 50 percent of revenue on R&D, while Shanghai-based MetaX spent 45 percent, compared to lower ratios at AMD and Intel.

stories.title: Israeli hiker found dead in Japan after going missing on Mount Asahi
stories.summary: Israeli hiker Tevel Shabtai, 23, was found dead on Mount Asahi in Japan after going missing during a solo hike in severe weather conditions.

stories.title: Germany says Israeli troops needed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johannes Wadephul stated during a joint press conference in Berlin with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar that Israeli forces in southern Lebanon are necessary to protect communities along Israel's northern border from Hezbollah threats.

stories.title: Trump says US to pause operation to guide vessels through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: "Project Freedom", which began on Monday, will be halted because progress has been made toward a deal with Iran, the US president says.

stories.title: North Korea’s new own-brand phone is sleek, colourful – and possibly watching you
stories.summary: North Korea showcased its latest Jindallae smartphone at a trade fair, presenting it as a home-grown product for citizens. Analysts doubt North Korea's manufacturing base can produce high-quality consumer technology, and the device may include surveillance capabilities.

stories.title: Hezbollah reports drone attack on Israeli forces in Qantara
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it struck Israeli soldiers in the southern Lebanese town of Qantara using an attack drone, saying the operation was in response to Israeli ceasefire violations and strikes on Lebanese villages. The Israeli military has not commented on the claim.

stories.title: Teen shooter at Brazilian school kills two staff, injures children
stories.summary: A 13-year-old student was arrested after carrying out a shooting at the Sao Jose Institute school in Acre state, Brazil, on Tuesday. The attack killed two staff members and injured two others, including an 11-year-old girl. Brazil has experienced a rise in school violence in recent years.

stories.title: Trump says ‘great progress’ made on US-Iran deal, pauses Project Freedom in Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump announced the pause of "Project Freedom," the U.S. operation escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz, citing "great progress" toward a deal with Iran. Requests from Pakistan and other countries also influenced the decision.

stories.title: Rubio speaks with Lavrov on Iran, US State Department says
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov about Iran, bilateral relations, and the war in Ukraine. The call, initiated by Lavrov, followed recent communications between Presidents Trump and Putin regarding a Ukraine ceasefire proposal.

stories.title: An Asian alternative to Nato? How Cica is rethinking Middle East security
stories.summary: The Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) is being examined as a potential alternative security framework for the Middle East as ceasefire efforts fail and the Strait of Hormuz remains under blockade amid the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: US lawmakers challenge ambiguity over Israel's nuclear capabilities
stories.summary: Thirty Democratic members of the U.S. House of Representatives urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio to clarify longstanding ambiguity surrounding Israel's nuclear capabilities, arguing that Congress has a constitutional role in overseeing nonproliferation policy.

stories.title: IS families in Syria have booked tickets home to Australia, minister says
stories.summary: Australia's government said four women and nine children with links to Islamic State, who spent years in a Syrian detention camp, have booked tickets to return to Australia.

stories.title: CS Anthem chemical tanker was second US-flagged vessel to exit Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The CS Anthem chemical tanker became the second U.S.-flagged vessel to exit the Strait of Hormuz with escort from U.S. Navy guided-missile destroyers operating under the "Project Freedom" directive to restore commercial shipping through the waterway.

stories.title: For tiny Circassian community, food and language sustain ancient heritage amid conflict
stories.summary: Israel's estimated 5,000 Circassians, Sunni Muslims living in two northern villages who serve in the IDF, are working to preserve their cultural heritage through food and language while contending with Hezbollah attacks on their communities.

stories.title: US military kills three in another strike in eastern Pacific that rights groups label as ‘extrajudicial killings’
stories.summary: U.S. Southern Command reported striking a vessel in the Eastern Pacific on Tuesday, killing three people it described as "narco-terrorists" without providing detailed evidence. Human rights groups have labeled these recurring military strikes as extrajudicial killings.

stories.title: Just one day after its launch, Trump halts Hormuz reopening operation and turns to negotiations with Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump suspended "Project Freedom," a military operation launched just 24 hours earlier to escort stranded vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, citing progress toward a deal with Iran. The abrupt reversal contradicted messaging from Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and Joint Chiefs chairman General Dan Caine, who had framed the operation as a humanitarian rescue mission.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign minister arrives in Beijing for strategic talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Beijing leading a diplomatic delegation for talks with Chinese counterpart Wang Yi. Discussions are expected to cover bilateral relations and regional developments amid heightened U.S.-Iran tensions.

stories.title: Israeli hiker found dead in Japan after 5-day search
stories.summary: Israeli hiker Tevel Shabtai, 23, was found dead on Mount Asahi in Japan after a five-day search. Freezing temperatures and high winds had complicated rescue efforts after she went missing during a solo hike.

stories.title: Syria says arrests Hezbollah-linked cell plotting assassinations
stories.summary: Syrian authorities announced the arrest of a cell linked to Hezbollah that was allegedly plotting targeted assassinations against high-level government officials, according to preliminary investigations.

stories.title: Charges flagged as women and children from IS-linked families set to fly from Syria to Australia
stories.summary: Four Australian women and nine children linked to Islamic State fighters are expected to fly home from Syria this week after more than a decade abroad. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said some of the women face arrest and possible charges upon arrival, with federal police and ASIO preparing a hardline response.

stories.title: Israeli forces block Bethleham road, deploy gas and sound bombs
stories.summary: Israeli forces closed the main road in al-Khader, south of Bethlehem, using dirt mounds to block access, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. The closure reportedly cut off residents' access to schools, the Old Town, and surrounding areas.

stories.title: Why Japanese politician’s goal to reset ties with Russia is ‘a long shot’
stories.summary: Pro-Kremlin Japanese politician Muneo Suzuki met senior Russian officials in Moscow and said Russia is trying to arrange a foreign ministers' meeting in July. Analysts consider his efforts to reset Japan-Russia ties unlikely to succeed.

stories.title: The domestic dynamics driving Japan’s remilitarisation
stories.summary: An analysis examines the domestic factors driving Japan's remilitarization under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, including constitutional reinterpretation, expanded weapons exports, and deployment of counterstrike capabilities, arguing that internal dynamics are more decisive than external strategic shifts.

stories.title: Aung San Suu Kyi’s son asks France to help him locate mother in Myanmar
stories.summary: Kim Aris, the son of Myanmar's deposed leader Aung San Suu Kyi, asked France to help verify his mother's well-being after junta leader Min Aung Hlaing ordered her transfer to house arrest. Aris says he has not heard from the 80-year-old Nobel laureate since the move.

stories.title: Trump: Project Freedom paused as talks with Iran near final agreement
stories.summary: President Trump announced a temporary pause of "Project Freedom," the U.S. military escort operation in the Strait of Hormuz, citing a request from Pakistan and progress toward a final agreement with Iran. The U.S. naval blockade on Iranian ports remains in effect.

stories.title: US pauses naval escorts in Strait of Hormuz amid renewed Iran dialogue
stories.summary: The United States paused its naval escort operation for commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz following weeks of indirect talks with Iran mediated by Pakistan. While direct talks in Islamabad did not produce an agreement, officials noted signs of progress.

stories.title: US and Bahrain push UN-backed action for Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States and Bahrain are pushing for UN-backed action regarding the Strait of Hormuz amid fresh exchanges of fire between U.S. and Iranian forces and an ongoing struggle for control of the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Italy’s Meloni warns over AI deepfakes after false photos circulate
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said AI-generated fake photos of her were being circulated online and passed off as authentic by political opponents. She warned of the broader dangers posed by deepfake imagery.

stories.title: US Army fires Typhon for first time in Philippines during Balikatan drills
stories.summary: The U.S. Army fired a Tomahawk missile from its Typhon Mid-Range Capability launcher in the Philippines during the Balikatan military exercises, marking the system's first live firing since its deployment to Luzon two years ago. China rebuked the action.

stories.title: Germany's struggling coalition government strives to bridge differences
stories.summary: In Berlin, leaders of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's coalition government pledged on May 5 to resolve internal disputes over tax, welfare, and health reforms. Weeks of disagreement had raised concerns about the coalition's viability.

stories.title: Joyous reunion of Iranian boy with China classmates after family visit to Iran moves many
stories.summary: An eight-year-old Iranian boy named Radin returned to his primary school in Shaoxing, China, after losing contact with teachers for 42 days during a family visit to Iran, reuniting joyfully with classmates.

stories.title: Search called off for Australian hiker missing in rugged Canadian national park
stories.summary: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police suspended a six-day air and ground search for missing Australian hiker Denise Ann Williams in a rugged national park in Nova Scotia. The operation involved dogs, approximately 100 personnel, aircraft, and ground crews but yielded no new information on her whereabouts.

stories.title: Ten hurt in fire at shopping centre west of Tehran, Iranian media says
stories.summary: At least 10 people were injured in a fire that broke out at a shopping centre located west of Tehran, according to Iranian media reports on May 5.

stories.title: 30 Democratic lawmakers ask Rubio to reveal details of Israel’s nuclear program
stories.summary: Thirty Democratic U.S. lawmakers sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio requesting disclosure of details about Israel's alleged nuclear arsenal, arguing that a coherent nonproliferation policy for the Middle East requires transparency.

stories.title: The Hidden Risks Behind Free Content Platforms in the Digital Age
stories.summary: An analysis examines the security and privacy risks associated with free digital content platforms. While these services provide access to entertainment, software, and information for millions worldwide, especially in lower-income regions, they raise concerns about data exploitation and user safety.

stories.title: Will Hong Kong’s lending clampdown wean helpers off debt – and save their dreams?
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities are implementing a lending clampdown aimed at curbing excessive debt among foreign domestic helpers. Many helpers, like Philippine worker Anna, have taken on loans far exceeding their salaries, often on behalf of others.

stories.title: Ukraine expects UAH 13B from privatization in 2026 – Svyrydenko
stories.summary: Ukraine's First Deputy Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko announced that the government expects to raise approximately 13 billion hryvnias from privatization in 2026, with about 10 billion from large-scale sales and 3 billion from smaller assets.

stories.title: At least five killed in Russian strike on Ukraine’s Kramatorsk: Zelensky
stories.summary: Russia struck the center of Kramatorsk, an eastern Ukrainian city, with several aerial bombs, killing at least five people. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the casualties.

stories.title: Sherrod Brown and Jon Husted set for Senate showdown after Ohio primary victories
stories.summary: Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown and Republican Senator Jon Husted won their respective party nominations in Ohio's primary elections on Tuesday. The two will face off in a high-profile Senate race in the November midterm elections, with Democrats prioritizing the seat in their bid to retake chamber control.

stories.title: Crypto Casinos in 2026: Safety, Speed and Player Trust
stories.summary: A review of the cryptocurrency casino sector in 2026 examines how platforms using Bitcoin and USDT are balancing fast transactions and blockchain transparency with consumer protection. The industry is testing whether speed and trust can coexist in online gambling.

stories.title: London cops announce new unit to protect Jews amid surging antisemitic violence
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced a new community protection team of initially 100 officers to protect Jewish communities amid rising antisemitic violence. The unit will combine neighborhood patrols with specialist protection and counterterrorism capabilities.

stories.title: EU invites firms to join new Ukraine drone alliance
stories.summary: The European Union has invited defense firms to participate in a newly formed drone alliance focused on Ukraine. The initiative aims to strengthen Europe's military drone capabilities.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump pauses US Strait of Hormuz escort operation
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a pause in the U.S. military operation escorting vessels through the Strait of Hormuz as negotiations with Iran continue. U.S. forces maintain a blockade of Iranian ports, and tensions persist in the Gulf despite a fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Trump says Iran ‘should wave the white flag of surrender’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump called on Iran to surrender, dismissing Tehran's military strength. He characterized Iran as too proud to concede despite what he described as its limited capabilities.

stories.title: A year since Singapore election, how has Lawrence Wong’s team fared?
stories.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and the People's Action Party have governed for one year since winning the general election. The country now faces a global energy crisis linked to the Middle East conflict, intensifying the economic challenges Wong warned about during his campaign.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says Hormuz operation paused amid US, Tehran talks
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed that a ceasefire with Iran remains in place despite rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement came as the U.S. and Tehran continue diplomatic engagement over the waterway.

stories.title: War update: 155 clashes on front line, Ukrainian forces eliminate about 50 occupiers in Pokrovsk direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces engaged in 155 combat clashes with Russian forces on May 5, including 34 enemy attacks in the Pokrovsk direction. Ukrainian forces reported eliminating approximately 50 Russian soldiers in the Pokrovsk sector.

stories.title: What do a teenager's clothes tell us about North Korea's future?
stories.summary: Analysts say the clothing choices of Kim Jong Un's daughter Kim Ju Ae suggest she is being systematically prepared for succession in North Korea's leadership.

stories.title: Israel court extends Gaza flotilla activists' detention by six days
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of two Gaza-bound flotilla activists by six days. Their lawyer said the extension was granted to give police additional time for interrogation.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it struck Israeli vehicles as raids hit south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it targeted Israeli military vehicles with artillery fire in the Wadi al-Jamal area between Meiss el-Jabal and Hula in southern Lebanon. Separately, Israeli strikes on Deir Kifa killed at least two people and wounded others.

stories.title: Boy, 13, shoots 2 dead at Brazil school
stories.summary: A 13-year-old boy shot and killed two staff members and injured two others, including a student, at Sao Jose Institute in Rio Branco, the capital of Acre state in northeast Brazil. The suspect was arrested at the scene, and panicked students attempted to flee by climbing over a wall.

stories.title: Rubio says Israel-Lebanon peace deal is achievable but Hezbollah is a problem
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said an Israel-Lebanon peace deal is achievable but identified Hezbollah as a key obstacle, stating that the Lebanese government needs the capability to dismantle the group.

stories.title: Tigray party restores pre-war government in threat to northern Ethiopia peace
stories.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front reasserted control over Tigray's regional administration on May 5, violating a key provision of the 2022 peace agreement that ended the civil war with Ethiopia's federal government. The move threatens the fragile peace process in northern Ethiopia.

stories.title: Buses block off roads in Bolivia as transport workers strike over fuel
stories.summary: Transport workers in El Alto, Bolivia, launched a strike over fuel shortages, blocking streets with buses, cars, and trucks. The action disrupted public movement across the city.

stories.title: Israeli settler attack in Masafer Yatta injures three Palestinians
stories.summary: Three Palestinians, including a child, were injured during an Israeli settler attack on the community of Rujum I'li in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron in the occupied West Bank. All victims were members of the al-Adra family. Israeli forces at the scene detained three individuals, including two residents and a foreign activist.

stories.title: Trump pauses US operation in Strait of Hormuz in push for deal with Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the suspension of "Project Freedom," the U.S. military operation in the Strait of Hormuz, to allow time for finalizing a potential agreement with Iran.

stories.title: Russian strikes in Sumy region leave six injured
stories.summary: Six people were injured in the Sumy region of Ukraine as a result of Russian strikes targeting civilian infrastructure over the course of the day.

stories.title: India’s energy security amid conflicts
stories.summary: An analysis examines India's energy security vulnerabilities amid Middle East conflicts, noting that India imports over 85% of its crude oil needs and that geopolitical shocks in West Asia directly affect its domestic economy.

stories.title: Finding soldier Tom: Solving family mystery of WW2 Soviet prisoner of war
stories.summary: A BBC investigation traced the story of a World War II Soviet prisoner of war named Tom who escaped a Nazi labour camp in Jersey with help from a local family, only to disappear after returning to the Soviet Union.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian attack on Kramatorsk rises to 13, five killed
stories.summary: A Russian strike on Kramatorsk in Ukraine's Donetsk region killed five people and injured 13, with the casualty toll rising as rescue operations continued.

stories.title: Rubio says US military campaign in Iran ‘done’
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared that Washington's military campaign in Iran, dubbed "Operation Epic Fury," is now complete following a ceasefire. Rubio also criticized the War Powers Act as unconstitutional and noted the US had modified a draft UN resolution on the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian peace laureate at risk of dying after heart attack, husband says
stories.summary: Narges Mohammadi, Iran's jailed Nobel Peace Prize laureate, has been hospitalized with severe heart problems. Her husband expressed fears for her life after Iranian authorities refused to transfer her to a hospital in Tehran for proper treatment.

stories.title: ‘It kicks ass’: Rolling Stones launch new album at star-studded New York event
stories.summary: The Rolling Stones held a star-studded event in New York on Tuesday to preview their forthcoming 25th studio album, "Foreign Tongues." Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, and Ronnie Wood appeared on stage with host Conan O'Brien before an audience that included Leonardo DiCaprio and director Baz Luhrmann.

stories.title: Vienna police brace for protests at Eurovision Song Contest final
stories.summary: Vienna police announced preparations for protests against Israel's participation in the Eurovision Song Contest final, warning of potential blockades and disruption attempts. Austrian authorities described the event as one of the largest security operations the capital has faced.

stories.title: Consider Teesta water sharing deal under ‘current circumstances’: Bangladesh FM post BJP’s Bengal win
stories.summary: Bangladesh's foreign minister urged consideration of a Teesta River water-sharing deal with India amid what Dhaka sees as a political opening after the BJP's victory in West Bengal. The minister also confirmed the Teesta issue would be raised with China ahead of an upcoming visit to Beijing.

stories.title: Russian attack kills two in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia, governor says
stories.summary: A Russian attack on the city of Zaporizhzhia in Ukraine killed two people, according to the regional governor. The strikes damaged residential buildings, a car repair service, and a car wash.

stories.title: Reinstate windfall tax on banks after surge in profits, TUC urges
stories.summary: The Trades Union Congress urged the UK government to reinstate the bank surcharge from 3% to 8% after the four largest UK lenders reported nearly £14 billion in combined first-quarter profits. The TUC said banks have benefited from high interest rates and market turbulence linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Residents passed from pillar to post as warnings before fatal Hong Kong fire went unheeded
stories.summary: Residents affected by a fatal fire in Hong Kong reportedly raised safety warnings beforehand that went unheeded by authorities. The victims were reportedly directed between multiple agencies without resolution before the deadly blaze occurred.

stories.title: Trump to sign memo bringing back Presidential Fitness Test Award for students
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump plans to sign a memo reinstating the Presidential Fitness Test Award for students. The program, originally introduced decades ago, was phased out during the Obama administration.

stories.title: Claiming ‘great progress’ in Iran talks, Trump says US pausing naval escorts in Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump announced a pause of U.S. naval escort operations in the Strait of Hormuz, citing "great progress" in Iran talks and a request from mediator Pakistan. Separately, the UAE reported that Israeli PM Netanyahu was among leaders who called to condemn Iranian attacks.

stories.title: Zelensky calls Russia's attack on Zaporizhzhia cynical, senseless terrorist strike
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned a Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia that killed 12 people and injured 37, calling it a senseless terrorist attack. He also referenced strikes on the city of Dnipro, where four people were killed.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills one in southern Lebanon town of Adshit
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike killed one person in the southern Lebanese town of Adshit, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strike followed an earlier deadly Israeli raid in Deir Kifa, also in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran oil tanker likely beat US blockade, satellite tracker says
stories.summary: An Iran-flagged very large crude carrier named Huge signaled its position off the coast of Bali on May 3, suggesting it may have evaded a U.S. blockade aimed at restricting Iranian oil exports.

stories.title: US to lift Eritrea sanctions as Red Sea tensions reshape alliances, document says
stories.summary: The United States is preparing to lift sanctions on Eritrea, according to an internal government document obtained by Reuters. Analysts linked the decision to Eritrea's strategic position along the Red Sea shipping route amid ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: Tunisia temporarily bans prominent rights group
stories.summary: Tunisia temporarily banned a prominent rights organization, coming just 10 days after the Tunisian League for Human Rights also had its operations suspended for one month.

stories.title: China says wider U.S. sanctions on Cuba are 'illegal'
stories.summary: China condemned as "illegal" the broader U.S. sanctions imposed on Cuba after President Donald Trump signed an executive order on May 1 expanding restrictions against the Cuban government.

stories.title: Iran threatens Hormuz shipping, as Trump said to shelve strikes amid diplomacy
stories.summary: Iran has threatened shipping in the Strait of Hormuz while President Trump reportedly shelved further strikes amid diplomatic efforts. The UAE reported Iranian attacks for a second consecutive day, and Israel's IDF chief said forces were closely monitoring the situation and prepared to respond with force.

stories.title: China urges US to drop trade probe as key Trump-Xi summit approaches
stories.summary: China's state-backed trade body urged the United States to drop Section 301 investigations into alleged excess capacity, calling the probe legally flawed, days before a planned summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping in Washington.

stories.title: Woman, three children murdered in Multan; scene staged as suicide: officials
stories.summary: Police in Multan, Pakistan, confirmed that a woman and her three children were murdered in their home. City Police Officer Sadiq Ali Dogar stated the crime scene had been staged to appear as a suicide, and an investigation is underway.

stories.title: Dressed for succession: What Kim Ju Ae's outfits tell us about North Korea
stories.summary: Analysts note that Kim Ju Ae, the daughter of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, appears to be groomed as a potential successor, with her evolving fashion choices interpreted as deliberate signals of her rising political role.

stories.title: Australia news live: national cabinet meets to discuss fuel crisis; police treating fire at Melbourne car dealership as suspicious
stories.summary: Australia's national cabinet met to discuss the country's fuel crisis, while police in Melbourne are investigating a fire at a car dealership as suspicious. Federal shadow treasurer Tim Wilson warned that potential cash handouts in the upcoming budget could fuel inflation.

stories.title: Iran Nobel winner Mohammadi ‘between life and death’: Supporters
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi is described by supporters as being "between life and death." She reportedly suffered suspected heart attacks on March 24 and May 1 while already dealing with a pre-existing heart condition.

stories.title: Correspondents’ dinner suspect faces new charge of assaulting federal officer
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, the suspected gunman at the White House correspondents' dinner, now faces an additional charge of assaulting a federal officer with a deadly weapon. A federal grand jury in Washington returned a four-count indictment alleging he fired at a US Secret Service agent at a security checkpoint.

stories.title: Rubio says US military has completed offensive operations in Iran
stories.summary: The United States announced it has ended offensive military operations against Iran but warned of a potentially "devastating" response to new threats in the Strait of Hormuz. Ongoing clashes and rival warnings from Tehran raised fears that the fragile ceasefire could collapse.

stories.title: Russian strike on Dnipro: Three killed, nine injured
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on Tuesday evening killed three people and injured nine others.

stories.title: Iran denies UAE attack claims, says actions targeted US only
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry rejected UAE accusations that Tehran launched missile and drone attacks against it, calling the claims unfounded. The spokesperson stated that Iran's military actions were directed exclusively at the United States amid the escalating US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: 'A big pact': How the US plans to unite Libya through two ruling families
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly pursuing a plan to unify Libya by brokering an agreement between two ruling families. The effort has been energized by Russia's retreat from the region and rising global energy prices, though critics note the approach bypasses popular consent.

stories.title: 9 miles of archives: NYC Jewish history documents come to life in CUNY trove
stories.summary: The City University of New York system has made available a vast archival collection spanning nine miles of documents related to New York City's Jewish history. The trove includes Yiddish jokes, boxing posters, and student newspapers.

stories.title: France convenes G-7 on critical minerals to curb China’s grip
stories.summary: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure announced plans to convene G-7 partners on critical minerals to reduce dependence on China's supply dominance. France intends to rebuild its own critical materials industry as part of the effort.

stories.title: The rabbi defending Charlie Kirk's memory when most Jewish leaders won't - interview
stories.summary: Yeshiva University President Rabbi Ari Berman discussed his friendship with the late Charlie Kirk in an interview with The Jerusalem Post. Berman addressed Kirk's legacy and the broader alliance between Jewish leaders and conservative figures that he said many are reluctant to pursue.

stories.title: Beirut school converted to wartime shelter becomes flashpoint for societal tensions
stories.summary: A school in Beirut converted into a wartime shelter has become a flashpoint for social tensions in Lebanon. Many Lebanese see parallels to the internal divisions that fueled the country's 1975–1990 civil war.

stories.title: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia: 12 killed, injury toll rises to 37
stories.summary: A Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed 12 people, with the number of injured rising to 37.

stories.title: Four UK pro-Palestinian activists guilty of criminal damage over raid at Israeli firm Elbit
stories.summary: Four British pro-Palestinian activists affiliated with Palestine Action were convicted of criminal damage for a 2024 raid on a factory operated by Israeli defense firm Elbit in the UK. One defendant was also found guilty of striking a police officer with a sledgehammer.

stories.title: NYC anti-Israel activists set to protest outside Park East Synagogue
stories.summary: Anti-Israel activists in New York City planned a protest outside Park East Synagogue, claiming the venue was hosting an event selling properties on what organizers described as "stolen Palestinian land" through the Great Israeli Real Estate Event.

stories.title: Russia strikes at distances of up to 25 kilometers: Gas station owners near border advised to cover gas tanks with nets
stories.summary: Gas station owners located 20–25 kilometers from Russia's border with Ukraine are being advised to cover fuel storage tanks and vulnerable areas with protective nets. The guidance comes as Russian forces conduct strikes at distances of up to 25 kilometers.

stories.title: Spain agrees to receive hantavirus-hit cruise ship in Canary Islands following WHO request
stories.summary: Spain authorized the polar cruise ship MV Hondius, hit by a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people, to dock in the Canary Islands following a WHO request. Cape Verde had previously denied the vessel entry. The ship carries 147 passengers and crew, including 14 Spanish citizens.

stories.title: Rubio insists US is ‘very fortunate’ as Iran war pushes gas price near $4.50
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio argued the US is in a "very fortunate" position despite average gas prices approaching $4.50 per gallon, their highest in four years. The price increase is driven by oil supply disruptions linked to the US-Israel military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship to arrive in Canary Islands in 'three to four days'
stories.summary: Two critically ill crew members from the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship MV Hondius will be evacuated via Cape Verde to the Netherlands. The quarantined vessel, anchored off Praia, is expected to resume its journey to Spain's Canary Islands once evacuations are complete. Three people have died in the outbreak.

stories.title: Anti-Israel novelist’s new book includes minor Israeli character, prompts online backlash
stories.summary: Novelist Rebecca "R.F." Kuang faced online backlash after a leaked excerpt from her forthcoming book "Taipei Story" revealed a minor Israeli character. Some readers accused her of normalizing Israel, and a number canceled their preorders.

stories.title: FDA blocked studies finding Covid and shingles vaccines safe, HHS official says
stories.summary: The FDA blocked publication of several taxpayer-funded studies that found Covid-19 and shingles vaccines to be safe, according to an HHS spokesperson. The studies, costing several million dollars, analyzed millions of patient records and found serious side effects from the vaccines were rare.

stories.title: Russian army attacks three Ukrposhta branches in two days
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked three Ukrposhta postal service branches over two days in Ukraine's Kherson, Sumy, and Chernihiv regions. The strikes targeted civilian postal infrastructure.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky pitches drone deal during Bahrain visit
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Bahrain to pitch a drone technology deal. Ukraine has been marketing its drone expertise to Middle Eastern countries that face threats from Iranian-made Shahed drones.

stories.title: Israel military chief says forces ready to respond to Gulf developments
stories.summary: Israeli Army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir stated that the Israel Defense Forces are closely monitoring developments in the Gulf region and are prepared to respond to any threat. His remarks, reported by Ynet, signaled Israel's readiness to act amid rising regional tensions.

stories.title: Hamas disarmament 'almost impossible to bridge' as gaps with BoP grow, source tells ‘Post’
stories.summary: An Israeli source said gaps between Israel and the Board of Peace over Hamas disarmament are "almost impossible to bridge" following Hamas's refusal. Israel is coordinating with the Board of Peace and the US administration on next steps.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian Be-12 aircraft, three boats, support vessel in Crimea in April
stories.summary: Ukraine's Prymary (Ghosts) intelligence unit struck Russian military assets in occupied Crimea during April. The attacks damaged a Be-12 Chayka aircraft, three boats, and a support vessel.

stories.title: How China-Gulf ties can turn energy vulnerability into sustainability
stories.summary: An analysis examines how deepening China-Gulf economic ties, particularly in energy cooperation, could help transform Asia's vulnerability to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz into opportunities for long-term energy sustainability.

stories.title: Nigeria opposition alliance falters as two leading figures quit, clouding 2027 unity push
stories.summary: Nigeria's opposition coalition suffered a major setback as Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso both quit the newly formed alliance, citing legal disputes and internal divisions. The departures cloud opposition efforts to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 elections.

stories.title: BBC traces how 10 minutes of Israeli bombing brought devastation to Lebanon
stories.summary: A BBC investigation traced how a 10-minute Israeli bombing campaign beginning at 14:15 caused widespread chaos and destruction across Lebanon.

stories.title: Russians strike Dnipro, fire breaks out at enterprise
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Dnipro, causing a fire at an industrial enterprise. Details on casualties were not immediately reported.

stories.title: Most Israelis believe current ceasefire terms will not guarantee national security - poll
stories.summary: A poll found that 64% of Jewish Israelis believe the current security situation regarding Iran is incompatible with Israel's interests. Meanwhile, 48.5% of Arab Israelis consider the situation compatible. Most Israelis doubt current ceasefire terms will guarantee national security.

stories.title: Norway to reopen gas fields to bolster European supply
stories.summary: Norway announced plans to reopen gas fields to strengthen European energy supply. The energy ministry said operations will resume in 2028 and continue through 2048.

stories.title: California ‘failing victims’ of violent crime as financial support plummets
stories.summary: An analysis found that California's victims' compensation program is awarding less money to fewer people despite budget increases, making it harder for victims of violent crime to access funds for cleanup, relocation, funerals, and therapy.

stories.title: Pakistan court declares PM Shehbaz's daughter and her husband 'innocent' in corruption case
stories.summary: A Pakistani court declared Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's daughter and her husband innocent in a corruption case. No further details were provided in the source text.

stories.title: CENTCOM: ‘Safe path’ through Hormuz is US priority in ‘Project Freedom’
stories.summary: US CENTCOM spokesman Tim Hawkins stated that the main priorities of "Project Freedom" in the Strait of Hormuz are securing safe passage for shipping and maintaining a blockade on Iran.

stories.title: Japanese PM Takaichi in push to revise pacifist constitution as regional tensions rise
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is pushing for revision of Japan's pacifist constitution, calling for advanced discussions and establishing a panel to review the country's security and defense policies as regional tensions escalate.

stories.title: Zelensky announces new sanctions against Russia over recruitment of migrants for war in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced new sanctions against Russia over the fraudulent recruitment of foreign nationals from North Africa and the Middle East to fight in Ukraine.

stories.title: Germany urges more Gaza aid, warns against West Bank annexation
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul called for an urgent increase in humanitarian aid access to Gaza and reiterated Berlin's opposition to any further de facto annexation of parts of the occupied West Bank. He made the remarks at a joint press conference in Berlin with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar.

stories.title: Watch: Mamata Banerjee refuses to resign, rejects poll defeat | Above the Fold | 05.05.2026
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee refused to resign and rejected her party's election defeat. The broader news roundup also covered West Asia tensions affecting Indians and a virus outbreak at sea.

stories.title: Ukraine needs single coordination center for recruiting foreigners into military service – Budanov
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine's Office of the President, called for establishing a single coordination center to recruit foreign nationals into Ukraine's military service. The proposal aims to streamline the process of integrating foreign volunteers.

stories.title: European conservative network meet in Paris ahead of London rally
stories.summary: European conservative network members met in Paris ahead of a planned May 16 rally in London led by Tommy Robinson. Participants expressed support for Israel and President Trump's Iran policy.

stories.title: Before Vatican trip, Rubio defends Trump remarks on Pope Leo over Iran
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended President Trump's remarks about Pope Leo XIV ahead of Rubio's scheduled meeting with the new pope at the Vatican on Thursday.

stories.title: Russia’s State Duma considers bill barring students from master’s programs outside their undergraduate field
stories.summary: A group of Russian State Duma deputies, mostly from United Russia, introduced a bill to bar students from enrolling in master's programs unrelated to their undergraduate major or prior work experience. The legislation was published on April 29.

stories.title: Israel kills one boy, injures officers in strike on Gaza police station
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on a police station in Gaza killed 15-year-old Mahmoud Sahweil. Additional details on casualties among officers were reported but not fully specified.

stories.title: US and Bahrain push UN-backed action for Hormuz as Washington seeks maritime coalition
stories.summary: The United States and Bahrain are pushing for a UN-backed resolution on the Strait of Hormuz that could lead to sanctions against Iran and potentially authorize the use of force. Washington is seeking to build a broader maritime coalition in the region.

stories.title: US Army says ‘Project Freedom’ in blockaded Hormuz has ‘just begun’
stories.summary: A U.S. Central Command spokesperson announced the launch of "Project Freedom," a military operation aimed at securing safe passage for commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been subject to a blockade.

stories.title: Bennett responds to Smotrich comments that coalition with Arab party 'worse than Oct. 7'
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett responded to Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich's claim that forming a coalition government with Arab party Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas was worse than the October 7 attack.

stories.title: Palestinian photographer who captured ‘devastation and starvation in Gaza’ wins Pulitzer
stories.summary: Palestinian photographer Saher Alghorra was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for his documentation of conditions in Gaza. The prize committee praised his work as "haunting" and "sensitive." A front-page New York Times photo of an emaciated child had previously drawn scrutiny over famine claims.

stories.title: Twelve killed, dozens injured as Russia attacks Zaporizhzhia with bombs, drones
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Zaporizhzhia using four guided aerial bombs and drones, killing 12 people and injuring dozens more.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists until May 10
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of two Gaza flotilla activists — a Spanish and a Brazilian national — until May 10. The pair were detained by Israeli authorities on April 29 after their flotilla was intercepted and brought to Israel.

stories.title: Mission is to preach peace, says Pope in response to Trump attacks
stories.summary: Pope Francis responded to attacks from President Trump by stating his mission is to preach peace, after Trump criticized the pope for condemning the Middle East conflict. US Secretary of State was heading to the Vatican for discussions.

stories.title: JUI-F to hold nationwide protests on Wednesday, Friday over killing of cleric Maulana Idrees
stories.summary: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman announced nationwide protests on Wednesday and Friday following the killing of prominent cleric and former JUI-F provincial lawmaker Maulana Idrees, who was shot dead by unidentified assailants in Pakistan.

stories.title: Moscow court transfers majority stake in Russian agribusiness giant to the state
stories.summary: A Moscow court transferred a majority stake in Russian agribusiness giant Rusagro to the state, placing the company under government control. The ruling came as part of a lawsuit against founder and former senator Vadim Moshkovich.

stories.title: Board of Peace won’t hold Israel to truce terms if Hamas doesn’t okay disarmament offer
stories.summary: A U.S.-led body known as the Board of Peace indicated in a letter that it will not hold Israel to ceasefire terms from the first phase of the Gaza truce if Hamas does not accept a proposed disarmament framework. The letter implicitly acknowledged that Israel has not fully adhered to key provisions of the agreement.

stories.title: Middle East tensions: analysts react to Strait of Hormuz unrest
stories.summary: Analysts say the situation around the Strait of Hormuz remains uncertain, with Iran continuing to signal its intent to target ships that do not use its preferred transit route through the vital oil chokepoint.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill two Palestinians in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed two Palestinians in Gaza, according to medics. Violence in the territory has persisted despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025.

stories.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth: ceasefire with Iran is not over
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated on Tuesday that the ceasefire with Iran was not over, even as US and Iranian forces exchanged fire in the Persian Gulf. The clashes centered on control of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Palestinian leader’s son, long in the shadows, seeks political role
stories.summary: A succession struggle is emerging within the Palestinian Authority, with the son of the Palestinian leader seeking a political role after remaining largely out of public view.

stories.title: Ukraine flipped the drone math—and Russia’s assault tempo just stopped buying ground
stories.summary: Despite maintaining a high assault tempo across the Donbas region in April, Russian forces failed to make significant territorial gains. Ukrainian intelligence data indicates the cost per kilometer of territory captured in Donetsk has nearly tripled over the past year, partly due to Ukraine's effective use of drones.

stories.title: Lebanon open to European troops after Unifil withdrawal, president says
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun expressed openness to France and other European countries maintaining a military presence in southern Lebanon after the planned withdrawal of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) later this year. The goal would be to support the Lebanese army in the south.

stories.title: Nigeria to evacuate citizens from South Africa after attacks
stories.summary: Nigeria announced plans to evacuate its citizens from South Africa following a wave of anti-immigration protests. Separately, Sudan accused Ethiopia and the UAE of involvement in drone strikes, including an attack on Khartoum airport.

stories.title: India-UAE, India-U.S. among top 10 migration corridors in 2024: UN
stories.summary: A United Nations report identified the India-UAE and India-U.S. migration corridors as among the world's top ten in 2024. Approximately 3.2 million Indian-born migrants were living in the United States, making them the second-largest foreign-born group after Mexicans.

stories.title: Deadly hantavirus may have spread between humans on luxury cruise, but risk is low: WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization said it suspects rare human-to-human transmission of hantavirus occurred among close contacts aboard a luxury cruise ship with seven confirmed or suspected cases. Three passengers—a Dutch couple and a German national—have died. The WHO said the overall public risk remains low.

stories.title: Russian army drops high-explosive bombs on Kramatorsk: Five dead, five injured
stories.summary: The Russian military dropped three high-explosive aerial bombs on the center of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine, killing at least five people and injuring five others.

stories.title: Middle East tensions: US-Iran ceasefire appears to hold
stories.summary: A ceasefire between the United States and Iran appeared to hold on Tuesday despite missile and drone attacks the previous day targeting vessels and a port in the United Arab Emirates. Tensions remain elevated in the region.

stories.title: Regional peace, stability linked to collective restraint, respect for sovereignty: army's top brass
stories.summary: Pakistan's military leadership, led by Field Marshal Asim Munir, asserted at the 275th Corps Commanders' Conference in Rawalpindi that regional peace and stability depend on collective restraint, responsibility, and respect for sovereignty. The statement came amid heightened tensions between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Report: Russian border guards begin recording passport data of travelers crossing into and out of Russia via Belarus
stories.summary: Russian border guards began recording passport data of travelers crossing the Russia-Belarus border, according to the Belarusian human rights project Mayday Team. The move marks a change from previous open-border practices.

stories.title: ‘Defending from the goal line isn’t enough’: IDF entrenches grip in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces have expanded their military presence in southern Lebanon, razing structures deep inside Lebanese territory. Israeli flags have been placed along the southern coastal road. During a visit by journalists, Hezbollah launched a drone in the area.

stories.title: Ukraine steps up medium-range strikes on Russian forces
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Ukraine is rapidly increasing medium-range drone strikes against Russian forces. The growing capability is significant for Kyiv's outmanned military as the war with Russia enters its fifth year.

stories.title: Join the thousands coming home to Israel this year - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Nefesh B'Nefesh is promoting its Aliyah program, encouraging Jewish immigration to Israel. This is sponsored content.

stories.title: A great gift for Mom – or anyone: A year of entertainment for just $48! - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored advertisement promotes a streaming subscription for Jewish entertainment content at $48 per year, including a short film called "How to Make Challah."

stories.title: IRGC warns vessels against unauthorised routes in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy warned all vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to use only Iran-approved corridors. The IRGC said any deviation to unauthorized routes would be met with a "decisive response."

stories.title: ‘Grotesque’: parties criticise Reform UK plan to set up migrant detention centres in Green-voting areas
stories.summary: Reform UK's shadow home secretary Zia Yusuf announced plans to prioritize locating migrant detention centres in areas represented by Green Party MPs or councils, including Brighton. Other UK parties condemned the proposal ahead of local elections as inflammatory and unserious.

stories.title: Russia to expand ‘cyber squads’ in schools and universities to monitor online content
stories.summary: Russia announced plans to expand "cyber squads" and media patrols in schools and universities to monitor online content. The initiative is part of a 2026–2030 government program to counter what authorities call negative social phenomena among youth.

stories.title: EU, Armenia sign new partnership deals at first bilateral summit
stories.summary: The European Union and Armenia held their first bilateral summit, signing a connectivity partnership covering transport, energy, and digital infrastructure. The agreements signal Armenia's cautious shift toward the West, though the country remains economically dependent on Russia and is a member of the Eurasian Economic Union.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Kasta radar, multiple Russian military assets
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, coordinating with the Deep Strike Center, carried out a series of attacks between May 3 and 5 targeting Russian military assets including a Kasta radar system.

stories.title: Senate Republicans propose package including $1bn that could go to Trump ballroom
stories.summary: U.S. Senate Republicans released an immigration enforcement funding package that includes a proposed $1 billion that could be directed toward security measures related to a $400 million "East Wing modernization project" at the White House, which includes a ballroom for President Trump.

stories.title: Navy’s Cahill nominated for SWO boss, Air Force’s Tulley for AMC
stories.summary: Rear Adm. Joseph Cahill, currently commander of Naval Surface Forces Atlantic, has been nominated to lead the Navy's Surface Warfare Officer community. Separately, the Air Force's Gen. Tulley has been nominated to head Air Mobility Command.

stories.title: Pentagon assures safe passage through Strait of Hormuz despite presence of mines
stories.summary: The Pentagon assured commercial vessels of safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz after U.S. Naval Forces Central Command issued a security warning on Monday about the presence of mines in the waterway.

stories.title: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills 12; aerial bomb hits Kramatorsk, killing 5
stories.summary: A Russian military strike on Zaporizhzhia on May 5 killed at least 12 people. A separate aerial bomb attack on Kramatorsk killed five additional people.

stories.title: Trump dismisses China friction over Iran war, touts Xi ties before Beijing summit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed suggestions of friction with China over the war in Iran, citing his relationship with President Xi Jinping ahead of a planned summit. Trump stated that China has not challenged the U.S. on its Iran policy.

stories.title: Miscalculation over Strait of Hormuz could ‘bring an all-out war’
stories.summary: Tensions between the United States and Iran over control of the Strait of Hormuz continue to escalate, with neither side willing to compromise. Analysts warn that the standoff increases the risk of a miscalculation that could trigger a broader military conflict.

stories.title: Georgia county poll workers targeted by subpoena seeking their contact details
stories.summary: Fulton County, Georgia, is resisting a federal subpoena from the interim U.S. attorney in North Carolina's middle district seeking contact information for thousands of poll workers who served during the November 2020 election. The subpoena requests names, addresses, and phone numbers of the workers.

stories.title: US says Hormuz ‘Project Freedom’ is temporary operation
stories.summary: A US Central Command spokesperson described "Project Freedom" in the Strait of Hormuz as a temporary operation to secure maritime transit. The initiative aims to establish a safe corridor and security umbrella for commercial vessels. Officials said shipowners and insurers have responded positively so far.

stories.title: UAE restricts airspace after Iranian missile, drone attack
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates restricted its airspace to a handful of approved flight routes until at least May 11 following an Iranian missile and drone attack. The UAE's General Civil Aviation Authority activated emergency security protocols.

stories.title: EU hails 'leap forward' in ties with Russia's ally Armenia
stories.summary: The European Union praised a "leap forward" in relations with Armenia, a traditional Russian ally. Under Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, Armenia has pursued a diversification strategy that analysts describe as a tilt toward Brussels.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian Be-12 aircraft, three boats, support vessel in Crimea in April
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence operatives from the Prymary unit struck Russian military assets in occupied Crimea during April, damaging a Be-12 Chayka aircraft, three boats, and a support vessel.

stories.title: Despite mayor’s cancellation, ‘Globalize the intifada’ event proceeds in Sydney
stories.summary: A "Globalize the intifada" event in Sydney proceeded in a public park despite being cancelled by the city's mayor over concerns it could incite violence. The gathering attracted a small crowd of attendees.

stories.title: Trump hard-pressed to get better Iran nuclear deal than Obama's
stories.summary: Negotiations to end the U.S.-Iran war have stalled over President Trump's insistence that any deal include the dismantlement of Iran's nuclear program. Experts say Tehran is unlikely to agree to such terms, making a comprehensive agreement difficult to achieve.

stories.title: US threatens 'devastating' response to any Iran attack on shipping
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that any Iranian attack on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz would be met with a "devastating" response. The warning accompanied the launch of "Project Freedom," a U.S. operation to facilitate commercial transit through the strait, which Iran had closed in response to U.S.-Israeli strikes.

stories.title: Insurers assess shipping risks amid uncertainty in Iran war
stories.summary: Marcus Baker of Marsh Risk said the insurance market needs several days to assess shipping risks amid the US-Iran conflict. He noted uncertainty from both sides' rhetoric and said increased certainty would be key for markets to stabilize.

stories.title: Trump-Pope clash rehashes old gripes, casts cloud over Rubio's Vatican visit
stories.summary: President Trump escalated his criticism of Pope Leo XIV, who reaffirmed his commitment to peace while accepting public scrutiny. The dispute raised concerns about the impact on U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's upcoming Vatican visit and broader diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: US-Iran truce teeters on meltdown as stalemate takes toll on each side
stories.summary: The month-old ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran appeared increasingly fragile on Tuesday after fresh Iranian missile strikes targeted the United Arab Emirates for the second time in 48 hours. U.S. naval forces continued operations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth insisted the truce remained intact.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of flotilla activists Thiago Ávila and Saif Abu Keshek, who were seized by Israeli forces after their boats were intercepted near Greece the previous week.

stories.title: Zelensky condemns Iran's strikes on UAE, announces new security initiatives for Middle East
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned Iran's strikes on the UAE as reckless and ordered diplomats to strengthen security partnerships with Middle Eastern countries through new security initiatives.

stories.title: At handover ceremony, outgoing Air Force chief calls for ‘external’ Oct. 7 inquiry
stories.summary: Outgoing Israeli Air Force chief Maj. Gen. Tomer Bar called for an external, independent inquiry into the October 7 failures during his handover ceremony. Incoming chief Maj. Gen. Omer Tischler signaled readiness for a potential new round of conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Draft UN resolution threatens sanctions on Iran unless it opens Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A draft UN Security Council resolution co-sponsored by the US and Gulf nations threatens sanctions on Iran unless it reopens the Strait of Hormuz. If passed, the resolution could be enforced militarily as part of broader American efforts to escort ships through the blocked waterway.

stories.title: Problem with Ukraine’s 25,000 combat robots isn’t hardware — it’s keeping them connected on battlefield
stories.summary: Ukraine is deploying approximately 25,000 combat robots on the battlefield, but maintaining reliable connectivity remains the primary challenge. A brief loss of connection can cause unpredictable robot behavior rather than a graceful pause.

stories.title: Pakistan misses $8bn SEZ investment, 500,000-job targets: minister
stories.summary: Pakistan's Investment Minister Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh disclosed that the country fell well short of its targets to attract over $8 billion in foreign direct investment and generate 500,000 jobs in Special Economic Zones between 2018 and 2024.
