Only four SEZs, including those in Rashakai and Allama Iqbal Industrial City, have advanced beyond the planning stage.

stories.title: Reporter's Notebook: A look at developing Israel-Hezbollah conflict after a half-capsized ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire established on April 17 began to collapse in late April. IDF operations in southern Lebanon have continued amid the deteriorating truce.

stories.title: Sudan recalls Ethiopia ambassador after strikes on Khartoum
stories.summary: Sudan recalled its ambassador from Addis Ababa, accusing Ethiopia of involvement in strikes targeting Khartoum's airport. The move marks a sharp escalation in diplomatic tensions between the two neighboring countries.

stories.title: Andrew Tate sought CPS assurance he would not be arrested if he returned to UK, court hears
stories.summary: Andrew Tate's lawyers sought written assurances from UK prosecutors that he would not be arrested if he returned to Britain. The disclosure emerged at a preliminary hearing in a civil case in which four women accuse Tate and his brother of rape.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists until Sunday
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila until Sunday. Both were aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla, which attempted to break Israel's naval blockade of Gaza.

stories.title: Britain Leaves Two-Party Politics Behind
stories.summary: Local elections in the United Kingdom this week are expected to reveal deepening political fragmentation, with the traditional dominance of the two major parties continuing to erode across the country.

stories.title: Trump renews attacks on Pope Leo just days before Rubio’s Vatican trip
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump publicly criticized Pope Leo in an interview, accusing the first American-born pontiff of aiding Iran and undermining security with his pro-immigrant remarks. The comments came days before Secretary of State Marco Rubio's planned visit to the Vatican.

stories.title: Pakistan says there's ‘significant progress’ in efforts to end war on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said there has been "significant progress" in negotiations to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. Dar added that steps have been taken to protect Gulf states and expressed hope for a resolution benefiting both sides.

stories.title: Russia cuts mobile internet in Moscow and St. Petersburg ahead of Victory Day
stories.summary: Russian authorities cut mobile internet service in Moscow and St. Petersburg ahead of Victory Day celebrations on May 9.

stories.title: Outgoing air force chief Tomer Bar calls for independent inquiry of October 7
stories.summary: Outgoing Israeli Air Force chief Tomer Bar called for an independent inquiry into the October 7 attack. Bar said it is unacceptable that Israel's political leadership has not been investigated for over two and a half years.

stories.title: Video: Trump says Iran should ‘wave the white flag’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump called on Iran to "wave the white flag of surrender" amid the ongoing conflict. The remarks signal Washington's continued hardline stance toward Tehran.

stories.title: MoD has no system to detect civilian harm caused by military, study shows
stories.summary: A study commissioned by the UK Ministry of Defence revealed that the department has no system for detecting civilian harm caused by British military operations. The MoD also does not maintain a central register of civilian harm incidents or allegations.

stories.title: U.S. ‘not looking for a fight’ over Strait of Hormuz, Pete Hegseth says
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth described "Project Freedom" as a defensive, temporary operation to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz from Iranian interference. He stated that American forces would not enter Iranian waters or airspace and emphasized the U.S. is not seeking a confrontation.

stories.title: How the War with Iran Is Shaping U.S.-Chinese Competition
stories.summary: The U.S. war with Iran has intensified questions about Washington's ability to balance its military commitments with strategic competition against China in East Asia. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has created new challenges and potential opportunities for both the U.S. and China.

stories.title: US announces deals with tech firms for national security review of AI models before release
stories.summary: The U.S. government announced agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI to review new AI models before public release. The reviews, conducted by the Commerce Department's Center for AI Standards and Innovation, will focus on cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons risks.

stories.title: Nearly 20,000 patients ‘missing’ after initiating treatment at HIV centres, NA committee told
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Assembly Standing Committee on Health was told that nearly 20,000 patients who began HIV/AIDS treatment at antiretroviral therapy centers are now unaccounted for. The committee rejected a request to hold an in-camera briefing on the issue, as Pakistan faces one of the fastest-growing HIV epidemics.

stories.title: Pulitzer Prize awarded to Palestinian photographer who captured ‘starvation in Gaza'
stories.summary: Palestinian photographer Alghorra was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for images documenting starvation in Gaza. One photograph depicting an emaciated boy cradled by his mother drew widespread attention and controversy.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill two Palestinians near Gaza City
stories.summary: Israeli strikes near Gaza City killed at least two Palestinians and wounded several others, according to Wafa news agency. One attack near Bahloul Station killed a child, while another strike near Kuwait Roundabout left one dead and three injured.

stories.title: Russia recruited 994 Armenians for its war. Yerevan is pivoting west anyway.
stories.summary: Russia recruited 994 Armenian nationals through military contracts for its war in Ukraine, with 204 reported dead or missing. Despite this, Armenia under Prime Minister Pashinyan continues its strategic pivot toward Western institutions.

stories.title: US push for Lebanon and Israel leaders to meet could inflame tensions
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun is facing US pressure to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an upcoming visit to Washington. Analysts warn the proposed meeting could inflame tensions in the region.

stories.title: Two killed, eight injured in Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the city of Zaporizhzhia killed two people and injured eight others. No further details on the type of munitions used or specific targets were immediately provided.

stories.title: Iran war: Will tensions escalate in the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Analysts are debating whether the US "Project Freedom" naval operation will ease congestion in the Strait of Hormuz or escalate hostilities with Iran. The waterway remains a flashpoint amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Reuters reports Ukraine strikes Kinef oil refinery in Russia’s Leningrad Region, forcing shutdown
stories.summary: Ukraine's military struck the Kirishi oil refinery, known as Kinef, in Russia's Leningrad Region, forcing the facility to shut down. Reuters reported the development citing unnamed sources.

stories.title: Tired of oversimplified narratives surrounding Israel? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Jewish Federations' Rabbi Mike Uram is offering a free, self-paced course on Israel and Zionism covering facts and complexities of the topics. The course aims to address oversimplified narratives.

stories.title: Romania’s pro-EU coalition collapse 'does not alter the country's foreign policy', analyst says
stories.summary: Romania's parliament voted to oust liberal Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan through a no-confidence motion backed by the Social Democrats and the far right. Analysts say the political upheaval is unlikely to change Romania's foreign policy or security commitments as an EU and NATO member bordering Ukraine.

stories.title: State comptroller says government bloated, inefficient, with widespread dysfunction
stories.summary: Israel's state comptroller released an audit finding the government has too many ministries and that constant reshuffles have disrupted governance. The report cited weakened public services and contributed failures in rehabilitating northern Israel.

stories.title: Four Palestine Action members convicted over 2024 raid of Israeli arms firm’s UK site
stories.summary: Four Palestine Action members were convicted in a UK retrial for a 2024 raid on Elbit Systems' factory in Bristol. One defendant was also found guilty of striking a police officer with a sledgehammer, fracturing her spine during the break-in.

stories.title: Sick Iran Nobel winner Narges Mohammadi at risk of dying in custody, supporters warn
stories.summary: Supporters of jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi warned she could die in custody without urgent medical care after suffering two suspected heart attacks in recent weeks. Mohammadi won the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize for her human rights activism in Iran.

stories.title: Captain of stranded ship in Strait of Hormuz tells BBC of 'pressure'
stories.summary: Captain Raman Kapoor told the BBC about the pressure facing his ship, one of several vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing power struggle between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Bullrich vows that Argentina's government will capture former guerrilla Apablaza for extradition to Chile
stories.summary: Argentine Senator Patricia Bullrich stated in Santiago that President Javier Milei's government is committed to capturing Chilean former guerrilla Galvarino Sergio Apablaza, who has been a fugitive in Argentina since April 1. Bullrich made the remarks during a visit to meet Chilean President José Antonio Kast, pledging his eventual extradition to Chile.

stories.title: Italy PM Meloni warns over AI deepfakes after false photos of her circulate
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni warned that AI-generated deepfake photos of her were circulating online, alleging political opponents were passing off the fabricated images as real. She cautioned that such technology could deceive the public and harm individuals unable to defend themselves.

stories.title: Budanov: Ukraine ready to extend ceasefire if it is mutual
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine's Presidential Office, stated that Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire demonstrates a genuine desire for peace. He said Kyiv is prepared to extend the ceasefire on the condition that Russia reciprocates.

stories.title: Prosecutors to ‘fast-track’ hate crime cases in England and Wales after spate of attacks
stories.summary: The UK's Director of Public Prosecutions, Stephen Parkinson, instructed staff in England and Wales to fast-track hate crime prosecutions following a wave of antisemitic attacks. Prosecutors were told to bring cases forward quickly rather than waiting to gather all possible evidence.

stories.title: Russian man who served 5 years for social media comment is detained in Belarus while trying to emigrate
stories.summary: Ivan Lyubshin, a Russian citizen from Kaluga who served five years on a charge of "justifying terrorism" for a social media comment, was detained at Minsk airport in Belarus while attempting to emigrate to France, where he had been approved for a humanitarian visa. He had planned to transit through Armenia.

stories.title: Ex-US spy for Israel calls for Gaza ethnic cleansing as he seeks Knesset seat
stories.summary: Jonathan Pollard, a former U.S. Navy intelligence analyst who served 30 years in prison for spying for Israel, announced he will run for a seat in the Israeli Knesset. In a Channel 13 interview, Pollard advocated for the forced removal of all Gaza residents and the territory's annexation by Israel.

stories.title: Policies needed to share AI-generated intel across NATO countries, official says
stories.summary: A NATO official said the 32-member alliance needs formal policies to share AI-generated intelligence across member countries. Currently, NATO nations rely on exceptions and workarounds to share commercial data.

stories.title: ‘Iran wants to make a deal’, Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump claimed the US has "total control" over the situation with Iran, praising the naval blockade as effective. He stated that Iran "wants to make a deal" and is "trying to survive" under current pressure.

stories.title: Falkland House in London hosts an exhibition of ceramic work by Graham Bound
stories.summary: Falkland House in London is hosting an exhibition of ceramic art by Graham Bound, a Falkland Islands-born journalist and author known for his books on the 1982 war and contemporary island life. Bound also founded the weekly newspaper Penguin News.

stories.title: Israel court extends Gaza flotilla activists' detention by six days
stories.summary: An Israeli court in Ashkelon extended the detention of Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila, two activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla, by six days. The extension allows police additional time for interrogation; the pair were intercepted by Israeli forces in international waters.

stories.title: Can Pakistan play brother-in-arms role as Gulf states eye security shifts?
stories.summary: Pakistan is positioning itself as a potential security partner for Gulf states reassessing their reliance on U.S. protection. Its strategic geographic location, Chinese-made military hardware, and active diplomatic engagement by its army chief are seen as assets, though interest varies among Gulf nations.

stories.title: US to take steps to curb antidepressant prescribing, RFK Jr says
stories.summary: U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced plans to curb antidepressant prescribing, promoting a "deprescribing" initiative. Psychiatrists have pushed back, arguing the real crisis stems from lack of access to mental health care rather than overuse of medication.

stories.title: Vienna police bracing for protests and ‘disruption attempts’ at Eurovision next week
stories.summary: Vienna police are preparing heightened security measures ahead of the Eurovision Song Contest beginning May 12. Authorities plan to ban drones, collaborate with the FBI, and implement airport-style screening to counter anticipated protests and disruption attempts.

stories.title: Erdogan ally calls for official status for jailed Kurdish militant leader
stories.summary: Turkish nationalist party leader Devlet Bahceli called on Tuesday for jailed Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) leader Abdullah Öcalan to be given an official role in advancing a peace process. The proposal aims to help end the decades-long conflict between the PKK and the Turkish state.

stories.title: Stop plotting to oust Keir Starmer, ex-deputy Labour leader urges MPs
stories.summary: Former UK deputy Labour leader Tom Watson urged Labour MPs to stop plotting against party leader Keir Starmer. Housing Secretary Steve Reed warned that a leadership change could risk the party's "annihilation" with voters.

stories.title: Dark clouds, protests and resignations dampen start of 61st Venice Biennale
stories.summary: The 61st Venice Biennale opened amid political tensions, with the Russian pavilion remaining closed and growing protests over Israel's inclusion. British artist Lubaina Himid presented large-scale paintings addressing colonial history in the UK pavilion.

stories.title: Panama minister blasts China’s ship crackdown, tells deputies to demand answers in Beijing
stories.summary: Panama's Foreign Minister Javier Martinez-Acha Vasquez urged opposition lawmakers visiting China to defend Panama's sovereignty amid rising tensions over China's detention of Panamanian-flagged vessels. He called on the delegation to deliver a firm message to Chinese counterparts.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Zaporizhzhia with guided bombs, six injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out an airstrike on Zaporizhzhia using guided aerial bombs, striking industrial facilities. At least six people were reported injured in the attack.

stories.title: Strategic neutrality: How Syria is winning in the Iran war
stories.summary: Syria's new government has maintained deliberate neutrality in the Iran war, avoiding direct involvement. Damascus is positioning itself as a potential mediator and offering an alternative route to bypass the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: UK Jewish groups call for more action as Starmer convenes antisemitism summit
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer convened an antisemitism summit following a terror stabbing attack in Golders Green, London, and a series of arson and IED attacks on Jewish institutions in the capital in recent months. Jewish groups called for stronger government action.

stories.title: India, Japan hold key meeting on healthcare in Delhi
stories.summary: India and Japan held a meeting in Delhi on healthcare cooperation. Indian official J.P. Nadda noted that bilateral collaboration is guided by a Memorandum of Cooperation in healthcare and wellness, with shared goals of strengthening health systems and promoting innovation.

stories.title: Trump says US has ‘completely destroyed Iran’s army’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed Washington had "completely destroyed Iran's army" during remarks at the White House. He stated that every Iranian naval vessel was sunk and described Iran's remaining forces as reduced to small armed boats.

stories.title: Russia announces Victory Day ceasefire, threatens missile strike on Kyiv if Ukraine disrupts celebrations
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry announced on May 4 that President Vladimir Putin ordered a ceasefire for May 8–9 to mark Victory Day celebrations. The ministry warned that if Ukraine disrupted the celebrations, Russia would deliver a "massive missile strike on the center of Kyiv."

stories.title: Alberta separatists submit 300,000 signatures to push independence referendum
stories.summary: Alberta separatists submitted more than 300,000 signatures to Canadian elections officials to push for an independence referendum in the oil-rich province. The effort was immediately overshadowed by a data breach linked to a separatist-affiliated group that leaked personal details of nearly 3 million residents online.

stories.title: US, Bahrain push UN-backed action for Strait of Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: The United States and Bahrain introduced a UN-backed resolution addressing the Strait of Hormuz crisis. Diplomats described the measure as part of a broader strategy to pressure Iran diplomatically and prepare for a post-conflict situation.

stories.title: Israel prepares to return to war on Iran, Lebanon 'within days'
stories.summary: Israel is preparing for a possible resumption of military operations against Iran within days. Prime Minister Netanyahu signaled readiness while cities across Israel opened public shelters amid escalating tensions.

stories.title: Google AI workers unionising over US, Israeli military tech
stories.summary: Workers at Google DeepMind launched a unionisation effort over concerns about the company's artificial intelligence technology being used by US and Israeli military forces.

stories.title: Israeli children's mental health plummets as a result of ongoing war experiences
stories.summary: Data from Israel shows a significant decline in children's mental health linked to ongoing war, with increases of tens of percent in diagnoses of anxiety, depression, and suicide attempts among children aged 6 and 9.

stories.title: Moscow Court Orders Pre-Trial Detention of Veteran Activist Lev Ponomaryov in Absentia
stories.summary: A Moscow court ordered the pre-trial detention in absentia of veteran Russian human rights activist Lev Ponomaryov. Ponomaryov fled to France in 2022 after being detained for protesting Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: US intel says war on Iran has not set back Iran's nuclear programme: Report
stories.summary: A US intelligence assessment reportedly concludes that two months of war against Iran have not set back Tehran's nuclear programme. The estimated timeline for Iran to produce a nuclear weapon remains approximately one year.

stories.title: Why Israel's next move in Gaza may be a return to war
stories.summary: Israel is intensifying military operations in Gaza and hardening its demands for Palestinian disarmament. Analysts warn a return to full-scale war appears imminent as Israeli elections approach.

stories.title: Asio Technologies: Shaping the future of tactical defense innovation
stories.summary: Israeli defense company Asio Technologies highlighted its Orion platform and other systems designed to enhance IDF battlefield coordination and autonomous operations.

stories.title: Mapping Out US Alleged Drug Boat Strikes
stories.summary: Since September 2025, U.S. Southern Command has conducted strikes against alleged drug-trafficking boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. The campaign has drawn scrutiny for its lack of transparency, with Southcom providing minimal details on strike locations beyond references to known trafficking routes.

stories.title: UAV operators from 1st Mechanized Brigade repel Russian assault in Sumy region
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone operators from the 1st Heavy Mechanized Brigade repelled a Russian ground assault in the Sumy region. The defense relied on rapid response, precise reconnaissance, and close coordination between units.

stories.title: UK convicts four Palestine Action activists over break-in at Israeli firm
stories.summary: A UK court convicted four members of the now-banned Palestine Action group for breaking into an Elbit Systems facility in Bristol. The raid took place during Israel's military campaign in Gaza. One defendant was also found guilty of striking a police officer with a sledgehammer, fracturing her spine.

stories.title: Police officer tells of operation to retrieve human remains from crocodile
stories.summary: Police in Australia conducted an operation to retrieve human remains from a crocodile suspected of killing a missing man. DNA tests are underway to confirm whether the remains match the missing individual.

stories.title: Somali terror groups could tighten Hormuz chokehold through Bab-el-Mandeb piracy, experts say
stories.summary: Security experts warned that Somali terror groups could exploit instability near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait through piracy, compounding existing threats from Yemen's Houthi forces. The strait connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.

stories.title: Proposed UN Security Council resolution warns Iran could face sanctions over Hormuz
stories.summary: A draft UN Security Council resolution backed by the United States and Gulf states warns Iran it could face sanctions if it does not restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and disclose the locations of sea mines in the waterway.

stories.title: A veneer of normality has returned to Tehran but fears for the future are rife
stories.summary: A fragile ceasefire between Iran and the U.S. and Israel has allowed a surface-level return to normalcy in Tehran, with checkpoints removed and public spaces bustling again. However, residents express deep anxiety about economic hardship and the possibility of renewed hostilities.

stories.title: Iran launches fresh wave of drones, missiles at UAE, Defense Ministry says
stories.summary: Iran launched a new wave of drones and missiles targeting the UAE, according to the UAE Defence Ministry. Iranian opposition media separately reported a large explosion and plume of smoke in western Tehran.

stories.title: Romania's pro-EU minority government on the ropes as parliament debates no-confidence motion
stories.summary: Romania's parliament debated a no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan's minority government on Tuesday in Bucharest. The motion was brought by the country's two largest parties and was widely expected to pass, raising concerns about potential impacts on sovereign debt ratings, EU fund access, and the national currency.

stories.title: Golan: Zionist opposition must partner with Arab party Ra’am to topple government
stories.summary: Democrats party chief Yair Golan called on Israel's Zionist opposition to partner with the Arab party Ra'am, led by MK Mansour Abbas, to topple the current government. His comments followed Finance Minister Smotrich's claim that including Arabs in a previous coalition was worse than the October 7 debacle.

stories.title: With wood scarce, Gaza carpenters make simple beds from pallets
stories.summary: In Gaza, local carpenters are using scrap wood and shipping pallets to build basic beds and tables as Israeli restrictions continue to limit the entry of goods into the territory. The resourceful measures come after nearly two years of war between Hamas and Israel have devastated infrastructure.

stories.title: Israel Prison Service chief’s lawyers threaten High Court petition as indictment looms
stories.summary: Lawyers for the head of Israel's Prison Service threatened to file a High Court petition as an indictment looms. The case is connected to a broader investigation involving senior officials linked to National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.

stories.title: Hundreds of animals rescued from ‘appalling’ conditions at California sanctuary
stories.summary: Authorities in San Diego County, California, rescued more than 400 animals from Villa Chardonnay, a shuttered sanctuary in Julian. The San Diego Humane Society found horses, cats, dogs, and goats suffering from malnutrition and injuries amid an ongoing bankruptcy dispute.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Kharkiv suburb, fires break out
stories.summary: On the afternoon of May 5, Russian forces struck the Malodanylivka community on the outskirts of Kharkiv. The attack caused fires to break out in the area.

stories.title: Democrats urge Rubio to acknowledge Israel possesses nuclear weapons amid Iran war
stories.summary: Thirty House Democrats sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the U.S. to publicly acknowledge Israel's possession of nuclear weapons. They argued that maintaining ambiguity is unsustainable while the Trump administration collaborates with Israel on military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Iran strikes UAE for second day in a row, says Emirati defence ministry
stories.summary: Iran struck the UAE for a second consecutive day with missile and drone attacks, according to Abu Dhabi's defence ministry. The previous day's strikes hit an oil refinery in the emirate of Fujairah.

stories.title: BSEK chairman resigns following allegations of mismanagement of matric exams in Karachi
stories.summary: Ghulam Hussain Soho resigned as chairman of the Board of Secondary Education Karachi following a committee report revealing mismanagement of matric examinations. The report found that BSEK's administrator made unauthorized changes to 170 examination centres. The committee was formed on the directives of Sindh's Universities and Boards Minister.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of Gaza aid flotilla activists
stories.summary: An Israeli court in Ashkelon extended the detention of two Gaza aid flotilla activists — Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila — until May 10. The pair were seized by Israeli forces near Greece while participating in the Global Sumud Flotilla.

stories.title: Israeli army chief says West Bank troops ‘killing like we haven’t killed since 1967’
stories.summary: Israeli Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, head of the army's central command in the West Bank, was quoted by Haaretz as saying his troops were "killing like we haven't killed since 1967," including fatally shooting Palestinian stone-throwers. Bluth has not denied the leaked remarks, and the IDF did not respond to requests for comment.

stories.title: Iran war unresolved 'because of Trump’s mistake': Expert warns US, Israel must return to fighting
stories.summary: INSS Iran researcher Beni Sabti warned that Iran's unresolved conflict stems from what he called Trump's strategic mistake, arguing that renewed military strikes by the US and Israel are the only way to push Tehran to accept negotiations.

stories.title: Rescue of Timmy the whale ‘an all-round catastrophe’ after tracker failure
stories.summary: Marine biologists have criticized a privately funded €1.5 million operation to release a humpback whale stranded off Germany's Baltic coast after the tracking device fitted to the whale failed. The whale, nicknamed Timmy, was transported by barge to open waters, but its location and condition remain unknown.

stories.title: Russia limits mobile internet ahead of scaled-back WWII victory parade
stories.summary: A monitoring site reported mobile internet disruptions across multiple regions of European Russia ahead of scaled-back World War II victory parade preparations. The Kremlin cited security concerns related to potential Ukrainian drone attacks as the reason for the restrictions.

stories.title: I’ve asked power in Pakistan one question for ten years on my podcast. This is the answer
stories.summary: A Pakistani commentator reflects on the country's rare moments of national unity, such as last year's military confrontation with India, and questions why such collective will quickly dissipates. The piece draws on a decade of conversations with political, military, and business leaders.

stories.title: Sudan's military accuses Ethiopia, UAE of drone attacks, recalls its ambassador
stories.summary: Sudan's military accused Ethiopia and the UAE of conducting drone strikes, citing evidence that four attacks since March 1 originated from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport. Sudan recalled its ambassador in response to the alleged attacks.

stories.title: Ukraine slams Russian ‘cynicism’ ahead of separate truces
stories.summary: Several people were killed in overnight strikes after both Russia and Ukraine announced separate unilateral ceasefires. Ukraine condemned what it called Russian "cynicism," as hostilities continued despite the truce declarations from both Moscow and Kyiv.

stories.title: Egypt allows ship with stolen Ukrainian grain to unload despite prosecutor's request – Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha reported that Egypt allowed the vessel ASOMATOS to unload 26,900 tonnes of Ukrainian wheat at Abu Qir port, despite a formal request from Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko to block the shipment, which Kyiv says was stolen.

stories.title: Israel eyes dozens of new jets in airpower upgrade
stories.summary: Israel has signaled plans to significantly expand its air force by acquiring dozens of new fighter jets. The announcement points to a broad airpower upgrade initiative.

stories.title: US Secret Service agent placed on leave for allegedly fondling himself in public
stories.summary: U.S. Secret Service officer John Andrew Spillman, 33, was placed on administrative leave after being arrested at a Miami hotel for allegedly exposing and fondling himself while off duty. He was part of a security detail for the PGA Championship, which President Trump was attending.

stories.title: Two more Russian hypersonic scientists are convicted of treason
stories.summary: Two Russian physicists involved in hypersonic missile research were convicted of treason and each sentenced to 12 and a half years in a penal colony, according to Russian state media. The scientists had conducted research underpinning the development of Russia's hypersonic weapons program.

stories.title: Matti Friedman on Hannah Senesh, Israeli Resilience and Jewish Pride - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Author Matti Friedman discussed his new book about Hannah Senesh and a World War II mission to rescue Jews in Nazi-occupied Europe. The interview focused on themes of heroism and Jewish resilience.

stories.title: UAE comes under Iranian attacks for second consecutive day
stories.summary: Iran launched missile and drone strikes against the United Arab Emirates for a second consecutive day, one day after 15 missiles hit the Gulf nation. The attacks occurred amid a fragile US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia exchange drone strikes ahead of V-Day ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged drone strikes ahead of a planned Victory Day ceasefire. Ukrainian forces hit multiple targets in Moscow, while Russian strikes damaged a Ukrainian gas production facility.

stories.title: Zelenskyy condemns Russian ‘cynicism’ over parade truce as 23 killed in attacks
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned Russia's request for a truce to hold a Moscow military parade as "utter cynicism," noting continued strikes on Ukraine. At least 23 people were killed, including 12 in Zaporizhzhia and five in Kramatorsk.

stories.title: ‘Close to zero impact’: US study casts doubt on effect of phone ban in schools
stories.summary: A study by researchers at Stanford, Duke, and other U.S. universities found that strict mobile phone bans in nearly 1,800 schools had "close to zero" measurable impact on student learning, attendance, or online bullying. The findings come as UK lawmakers consider similar restrictions in England.

stories.title: While Russia talks about 9 May ceasefire, its guided bombs just killed 12 people in Zaporizhzhia
stories.summary: Russian guided bomb strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed 12 people, hitting businesses and residential areas with no military infrastructure. The attacks came as Russia discussed a potential ceasefire around the May 9 Victory Day.

stories.title: India: West Bengal election win boosts Modi's BJP
stories.summary: India's Bharatiya Janata Party won the West Bengal state election, further expanding Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political dominance across the country.

stories.title: Three Israeli strikes hit southern Lebanon towns
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out three air strikes on the towns of al-Sayyad and al-Mansouri in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Additional strikes and artillery fire targeted Qounine and Beit Yahoun in the Bint Jbeil district, with reports of phosphorus shell use.

stories.title: UK announces sanctions targeting Russia fighter recruitment, drone production
stories.summary: Britain announced sanctions on Tuesday against 35 individuals and entities accused of recruiting vulnerable migrants to fight for Russia in its war in Ukraine and producing drones for use in the conflict.

stories.title: Political row as report calls for sweeping cuts to French public broadcasting
stories.summary: A French parliamentary inquiry led by a right-wing politician has recommended merging major public broadcasting channels and cutting TV entertainment budgets by 75%. Left-wing and centrist politicians criticized the proposals amid growing culture-war tensions ahead of France's 2026 presidential election.

stories.title: Syria lets banks use Visa, Mastercard in major payment shift
stories.summary: Syria's Central Bank announced that Syrian banks and firms can now work with global payment systems including Visa and Mastercard, marking a major shift in the country's financial infrastructure.

stories.title: Russian political prisoner says he was was beaten, electrocuted, and threatened with rape at prison in Yamalo-Nenets
stories.summary: Azat Miftakhov, an anarchist and mathematician held as a political prisoner in Russia, reported being beaten, electrocuted, and threatened with rape after his transfer to Prison Colony No. 18 "Polyarnaya Sova" in Kharp, Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous District. The account was published by The Insider.

stories.title: Netanyahu trial: PM expected back on stand after another schedule battle
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial continued with scheduling disputes at the Jerusalem District Court. The defence submitted sealed material regarding Netanyahu's schedule in an attempt to reschedule Tuesday's hearing before the PM was expected to return to the stand.

stories.title: Europe spent two years waiting for US Tomahawks. Ukraine spent them building its own.
stories.summary: After the US withdrew Tomahawk missile commitments to Europe, Ukraine developed its own long-range strike capabilities over two years. Kyiv has now opened the door to exporting domestically produced missiles.

stories.title: Estonian general turned MEP: Europe’s long-range answer is already in Ukraine
stories.summary: An Estonian general serving as a member of the European Parliament discussed long-range strike capabilities already deployed in Ukraine. His remarks came after the US withdrew Tomahawk missiles from consideration for Ukrainian use.

stories.title: Iran vs Trump: Is war about to break out?
stories.summary: Iran broke a fragile ceasefire with the United States that had been in effect since April 8 by launching strikes on the United Arab Emirates. The escalation has raised concerns about a potential wider conflict between Iran and the U.S.

stories.title: CM Afridi announces pen-down strike on May 6 over Centre’s ‘discrimination’ against KP
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi announced a province-wide pen-down strike on May 6, accusing Pakistan's federal government of discrimination against the province. Afridi alleged the Centre is deliberately shortchanging KP in the National Finance Commission Award, electricity, and gas allocations because the province is governed by Imran Khan's PTI.

stories.title: One-way attack drones under the spotlight at SAHA 2026
stories.summary: At the SAHA 2026 defense exposition in Turkey, Turkish firms publicly displayed two naval vessels and three aerial one-way attack drone systems on the event's opening day, highlighting the country's growing unmanned combat technology sector.

stories.title: Zelensky proposes drone deal to Bahrain
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky proposed a drone cooperation deal during a meeting with Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Details of the proposed agreement were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Iran’s judiciary vows action against ‘enemy’s mercenaries’ amid executions
stories.summary: Iran's judiciary announced intensified action against individuals it described as foreign agents, citing national security threats. Authorities have escalated executions and asset confiscations targeting accused operatives.

stories.title: Carney appoints former war crimes prosecutor as Canada governor general
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney appointed Louise Arbour as the country's new governor general. Arbour, a former Supreme Court justice, previously served as a United Nations commissioner and prosecuted war crimes in the former Yugoslavia and Rwanda.

stories.title: Farage deploys the rottweiler to distract from awkward £5m gift story | John Crace
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage faced scrutiny after the Guardian revealed he received a £5 million undeclared donation from Thai-based crypto dealer Christopher Harborne. Party chair Zia Yusuf proposed building migrant detention centres in Green-voting areas, widely seen as an attempt to divert attention.

stories.title: FIFA invites Iran to HQ for World Cup talks as tournament nears
stories.summary: FIFA has reportedly invited the Iranian football federation to its headquarters in Zurich by May 20 to discuss preparations for the upcoming World Cup.

stories.title: What brings 28-year-old North Carolina construction worker in Ukraine’s 47th brigade? He explains in his own words
stories.summary: A 28-year-old construction worker from North Carolina joined Ukraine's 47th Mechanized Brigade. He explained his motivations for volunteering with the Ukrainian Armed Forces in an interview with ArmyInform.

stories.title: Four Palestine Action activists convicted over 2024 damage to Israeli weapons factory
stories.summary: A UK court convicted four activists affiliated with the now-banned group Palestine Action on criminal damage charges for a 2024 raid on an Elbit Systems facility in Bristol, England. Two other defendants tried in the same case were acquitted.

stories.title: As US eyes smaller military footprint in Europe, new unit trains for drone warfare
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is establishing a new unit in Germany dedicated to training personnel in drone warfare. The move comes as the Pentagon simultaneously considers reducing its overall military footprint in Europe.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Assembly Plans Visit to South African Parliament Over Xenophobic Attacks
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Assembly announced plans to send a joint Senate and House committee to South Africa's parliament to investigate rising xenophobic attacks against Nigerian nationals.

stories.title: Trump’s Gaza Impasse
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Hamas over Gaza remain stalled, with experts noting that Hamas has limited incentives to agree to disarmament as a precondition for a deal.

stories.title: Football: Finalists announced for the Marc-Vivien Foé award for best African player in Ligue 1
stories.summary: The finalists for the Marc-Vivien Foé award, recognizing the best African player competing in France's Ligue 1, have been announced. No further details on the nominees were provided.

stories.title: Seven cases of deadly hantavirus confirmed or suspected on stranded cruise ship
stories.summary: The World Health Organization confirmed two cases of hantavirus and identified five more suspected cases among people who fell ill aboard a cruise ship now stranded off the Cape Verde islands. The vessel has been unable to put passengers ashore.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Accuses Sudanese Military of Backing TPLF, Territorial Violations
stories.summary: Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the Sudanese Armed Forces of supporting "TPLF mercenaries" and violating Ethiopian territorial integrity. The statement followed Sudan's accusations that Ethiopia and the UAE orchestrated drone attacks on Khartoum.

stories.title: Putin ‘doesn’t care' about Russians or Ukrainians: ‘Pageantry and symbolism’ over civilian lives
stories.summary: Peter Zalmayev, director of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative, discussed Russia's war on Ukraine, emphasizing the growing effectiveness of drone warfare in asymmetric combat. He characterized Russia's proposed ceasefire for a Victory Day parade as political theater, suggesting Putin prioritizes symbolism over civilian lives.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces inflict over $300M in damage on port infrastructure, oil refinery in Tuapse – General Staff
stories.summary: Port infrastructure and an oil refinery in the city of Tuapse, Russia's Krasnodar region, have sustained more than $300 million in damage as a result of recent strikes by Ukraine's Defense Forces.

stories.title: What's stopping Pakistan from making the transition to renewable energy?
stories.summary: Pakistan lags behind South Asian neighbors India and Bangladesh in renewable energy adoption despite significant potential for solar, wind, and hydropower. Experts cite insufficient grid adaptation, weak financial frameworks, and a lack of supportive policies as key barriers to the country's energy transition.

stories.title: Ex-spy Jonathan Pollard says he’s entering politics, slams Netanyahu and Bennett
stories.summary: Former convicted spy Jonathan Pollard announced his entry into Israeli politics, citing the October 7 attack as motivation. He criticized Prime Minister Netanyahu and former PM Bennett, calling the current government ineffective in prosecuting the war.

stories.title: Sudan's Burhan confronts UAE and Ethiopia over Khartoum airport drone strikes
stories.summary: Sudanese army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan accused the UAE and Ethiopia of responsibility for drone strikes on Khartoum airport. Burhan pledged his forces would keep the nation protected following the attacks attributed to the Rapid Support Forces.

stories.title: Tanzania: Ruto Calls for Stronger Kenya-Tanzania Unity, Warns Against Regional Rivalry in Dodoma Address
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto addressed the Tanzanian Parliament in Dodoma, calling for deeper investment ties between Kenya and Tanzania. He warned against narratives that fuel division among East African nations.

stories.title: At least 24 soldiers killed in suspected Boko Haram attack in Chad
stories.summary: A suspected Boko Haram attack on the Barka Tolorom military base in Chad's Lake Chad region killed at least 24 soldiers and wounded 46 others, according to army sources.

stories.title: Russian forces kill 4, injure over 30 in strike on Ukraine’s Poltava region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Poltava region with drones and missiles, killing four people and knocking out gas service for nearly 3,500 subscribers, regional military administration head Vitaliy Dyakivny

stories.title: Romania’s pro-Europe government collapses unleashing fresh turmoil
stories.summary: Romania's pro-European government led by Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan of the PNL party collapsed after losing a parliamentary confidence vote. The fall comes amid an austerity drive and a surge in far-right support, less than a year after the coalition took office.

stories.title: Israel’s 'bloated, unstable' gov't harms public service, wastes millions each year, report finds
stories.summary: State Comptroller Englman recommends limiting ministries, ending duplication, and requiring full staffing and budget groundwork before government powers are reshuffled.

stories.title: Make Mother’s Day meaningful by feeding a child in Israel - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The charity Yad Ezra V'Shulamit promoted a Mother's Day campaign to fund daily hot meals for thousands of children across Israel.

stories.title: Ukraine hit VNIIR-Progress in Cheboksary — plant behind GPS components in Russia’s Shaheds and glide bombs
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the VNIIR-Progress plant in Cheboksary, Russia, which manufactures Kometa adaptive antenna arrays used in GPS components for Shahed drones and Russian glide bombs.

stories.title: NATO nations size up an interceptor-drone bazaar where low price is everything
stories.summary: NATO member states are evaluating counter-drone interceptor systems at competitive showcases where cost has become the decisive factor. Price differences between competing systems are now measured in thousands of dollars rather than millions.

stories.title: Morocco's left-wing parties near deal over electoral alliance
stories.summary: Several left-wing political parties in Morocco are moving toward forming an electoral alliance ahead of parliamentary elections, ending years of division among the country's leftist factions.

stories.title: Iraqi tankers bypass Hormuz, stream into Syria via Rabia gate
stories.summary: Dozens of Iraqi tanker trucks carrying oil crossed into Syria through the recently reopened Rabia–Yarubiyah border gate. The overland route was revived as tensions in the Strait of Hormuz continued to disrupt maritime shipping.

stories.title: Report: Ukrainian drone strikes apartment building in Russia, sparking a fire and injuring multiple people; possible fatalities
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a residential building in Cheboksary on the morning of May 5, according to the Telegram channels Shot and Ostorozhno Novosti, citing eyewitnesses. The strike set the building

stories.title: North Korea’s Strongwoman-in-Waiting
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is reportedly orchestrating the political rise of his daughter through a carefully managed campaign of public appearances and state imagery, positioning her as a potential successor.

stories.title: Boko Haram attack kills 23 soldiers in Chad’s Lake Chad region
stories.summary: Boko Haram fighters attacked a Chadian military base on the island of Barka Tolorom in the Lake Chad region, killing at least 23 soldiers and wounding 46 others, according to Chad's army.

stories.title: Multiple People Reported Dead in Ukrainian Strike on Republic of Chuvashia
stories.summary: A Ukrainian strike on the Republic of Chuvashia reportedly killed multiple people. Authorities in the city of Cheboksary suspended public transit and ordered schools to switch to online classes in the aftermath of the attack.

stories.title: 2 Killed in Ukrainian Drone Attack on Chuvashia
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on the Chuvash Republic killed two people. Authorities in the city of Cheboksary suspended public transit and ordered schools to switch to online classes following the strike.

stories.title: Gulf migrant workers face tough choices amid Mideast war
stories.summary: Migrant workers in Gulf states face difficult choices as the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran escalates. They must decide whether to remain in an active conflict zone or return to home countries grappling with rising costs and energy shortages caused by the same war.

stories.title: US tech giant Cisco buys Israeli AI cyber startup to protect digital workforce
stories.summary: US technology company Cisco acquired Israeli AI cybersecurity startup Astrix. The startup developed a platform to address security vulnerabilities created by AI agents and digital employees accessing enterprise systems.

stories.title: Iran ceasefire ‘not over,’ US ‘not looking for a fight,’ Hegseth says after Tehran fires on Gulf
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Iran ceasefire was "not over" and that Washington was "not looking for a fight" after Tehran fired on Gulf targets. Reports indicated Israel and the US were planning fresh strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure and senior officials.

stories.title: Iran's attacks 'below the threshold' of restaring war, US Gen. Dan Caine says
stories.summary: US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth added that the US established a "red, white, and blue dome" over the Strait of Hormuz as a "gift from the US to the world."

stories.title: Moscow mobile internet restored after Russia’s Digital Development Ministry says temporary restrictions lifted
stories.summary: Mobile internet went dark across neighborhoods in Moscow and St. Petersburg on Tuesday morning, May 5. Readers of the independent Telegram channel Astra reported outages in Moscow, as did journalists

stories.title: Armenia balances on the tightrope between Russia and the EU
stories.summary: Armenia is pursuing closer political and strategic ties with the European Union while maintaining its relationship with Russia. The balancing act reflects Yerevan's effort to navigate between Western integration and its traditional alliance with Moscow.

stories.title: Mobilization gap: Russia now losing more troops than it can replace, for fifth month running
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov highlighted that Russia has been losing more troops than it can recruit for five consecutive months. He described the shifting attrition rate as the 'mathematics of war' turning against Moscow.

stories.title: Middle East truce in doubt as US and Iran fight for control of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are engaged in a confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil, fertiliser, and commodity shipments. The struggle for control of the strait has put a Middle East truce in doubt.

stories.title: Will Trump's Freedom Project to reopen Hormuz reignite Iran war?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced 'Project Freedom' aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, raising questions about whether the initiative could reignite military conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Israel appoints settler who backs annexation to head powerful land authority
stories.summary: Israel appointed Yehuda Eliyahu, a settler and ally of Finance Minister Smotrich who supports annexation, to head the country's powerful land authority. The appointment raises concerns about expanded settlement activity in the occupied West Bank and impacts on Palestinian citizens of Israel.

stories.title: UAE air defences 'actively engaging' with Iran missiles, drones: ministry
stories.summary: The UAE's Ministry of Defence announced its air defences were actively engaging missiles and drones originating from Iran for a second consecutive day. The attacks come weeks into a fragile US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Palestine Action defendants found guilty of criminal damage charges in arms factory raid
stories.summary: A UK court found four Palestine Action defendants guilty of criminal damage for an August 2024 raid on an Elbit Systems weapons factory in Filton, England. Two other individuals tried alongside them were acquitted of the charges.

stories.title: Three killed after small plane crashes in southeastern Brazil
stories.summary: A small airplane carrying five people crashed into a building in Belo Horizonte, southeastern Brazil, on Monday, killing three people. Local officials and firefighters responded to the incident.

stories.title: South Korea to review joining US Hormuz operation
stories.summary: South Korea announced a review of potentially joining a U.S.-led operation in the Strait of Hormuz after a South Korean cargo vessel experienced an explosion and fire on May 4 in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: European Commission seeks founding members for new EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance
stories.summary: The European Commission has announced a call for applications to participate in the creation of a new EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance, aimed at bringing together manufacturers, innovators, startups, and end

stories.title: What’s the significance of UAE’s Fujairah, hit on Monday?
stories.summary: The UAE's port of Fujairah was reportedly struck on Monday. If confirmed, this would mark Iran's first attack on the UAE since the US-Iran ceasefire began on April 8.

stories.title: What’s happening in Mali one week after attack by armed groups? All we know
stories.summary: Mali's military government leader, Assimi Goita, has assumed the role of defence minister one week after armed groups launched attacks in the country.

stories.title: As a British-Palestinian, the Green Party gives me hope
stories.summary: British-Palestinian writer Kamel Hawwash described his political shift from Labour to the Green Party and explained why, as a Palestinian, he is standing as a candidate in UK local elections.

stories.title: Sudan accuses Ethiopia, UAE of being behind recent drone attacks
stories.summary: Sudan has accused Ethiopia and the UAE of involvement in recent drone strikes, claiming evidence that four attacks were launched from Ethiopian territory using UAE-supplied drones.

stories.title: NI police handling of Katie Simpson case ‘reflected institutional misogyny’
stories.summary: An independent review found that the Police Service of Northern Ireland's handling of Katie Simpson's 2020 death reflected institutional misogyny. Investigators concluded that officers missed clear warning signs that the 21-year-old's death resulted from grooming and abuse by a violent predator.

stories.title: Hegseth says US ‘hasn’t capitulated on anything’ regarding Iran
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that the United States has not capitulated on any of its demands in ongoing negotiations with Iran.

stories.title: UAE restricts airspace following suspected Iranian attacks
stories.summary: The UAE imposed temporary airspace restrictions through May 11 following missile and drone attacks it blamed on Iran. The UAE's General Civil Aviation Authority limited arrivals, departures, and overflights to specific routes and warned pilots of navigation disruptions.

stories.title: Russian attack kills five at Ukraine's Naftogaz gas production facilities, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian overnight missile and drone attack struck Ukrainian gas company Naftogaz's production facilities, killing five people including two rescue workers. The attack came as Kyiv and Moscow exchanged rival ceasefire proposals.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists amid abuse claims
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of two foreign activists by six days after they were seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla. The pair, held in Ashkelon, deny wrongdoing while supporters allege mistreatment in custody.

stories.title: Here's why some cities are banning fossil fuel and meat ads
stories.summary: Several cities worldwide, from Amsterdam to Sydney, are banning advertisements for fossil fuels and, in some cases, meat. The bans draw on strategies previously used in anti-smoking campaigns to discourage carbon-intensive consumption.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine announce rival ceasefires as deadly strikes continue
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine announced competing ceasefires as deadly strikes continued. Russia called for a pause on May 8-9, while Ukraine proposed an earlier start, positioning Moscow to bear responsibility for any violations.

stories.title: Ukraine’s E-300 drone bombers come home full of bullet holes—and fly out again tomorrow
stories.summary: Ukraine has increased its middle- and deep-strike drone sorties sixfold over the past ten months using E-300 drone bombers, which frequently return damaged but are rapidly repaired and redeployed. During the same period, Russia's spring territorial advance reportedly shrank by 60%.

stories.title: Google DeepMind staff unionise over Israel and US military ties
stories.summary: Staff at Google DeepMind, the company's AI division, launched a union drive opposing the use of their technology in Israeli military operations and Pentagon-linked projects. The effort represents a historic unionisation push within the division.

stories.title: Russia plans monument to soldier killed in Ukraine war at site of demolished memorial to exiled Poles
stories.summary: Yakutsk’s chief architect, Semyon Sergeyev, told the Yakutsk-based news outlet YSIA that a monument to Dmitry Yegorov — a participant in the war in Ukraine killed in 2023 — will be erected at the inte

stories.title: Gaza: Israeli strikes kill 2 Palestinians in latest truce breach
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on Tuesday hit an area near the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood in Gaza City and the enclave's centre, killing two Palestinians in what marks the latest breach of the truce.

stories.title: Lamuka opposition coalition warns against ‘two‑tier democracy’ in DR Congo
stories.summary: The Lamuka opposition coalition in the Democratic Republic of Congo has criticized what it calls a "two-tier democracy" after a pro-UDPS march in Kinshasa reignited debate over U.S. sanctions and a possible constitutional reform that could allow President Félix Tshisekedi a third term.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy aids crew of Indian vessel stranded in Arabian Sea
stories.summary: The Pakistan Navy, assisted by the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency, rescued and supported the crew of an Indian vessel stranded in the Arabian Sea, as reported on May 4, 2026.

stories.title: Fire services to be ‘gatekeepers’ for safety, Hong Kong security chief vows
stories.summary: Hong Kong Security Secretary Chris Tang Ping-keung reaffirmed that the Fire Services Department will serve as the primary gatekeeper for building safety. The pledge followed an inquiry into the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, which exposed a legal gap in safety oversight.

stories.title: ‘Not a good look’: witnesses refuse to appear before NSW parliamentary hearings after court ruling
stories.summary: Witnesses in New South Wales, Australia, are refusing to appear before parliamentary inquiries following a court ruling that invalidated arrest warrant provisions under the Parliamentary Evidence Act. The trend began after NSW Premier Chris Minns' chief of staff successfully challenged a summons.

stories.title: Philip Morris uses secret Senate hearing to warn illegal tobacco in Australia could wipe out legal trade by 2030
stories.summary: Philip Morris told a closed-door Australian Senate hearing that illegal tobacco trade could eliminate the legal market by 2030. The company advocated for lower excise taxes, while critics accused it of prioritizing commercial interests over public health.

stories.title: UK homebuyers face worst mortgage affordability since 2008, data shows
stories.summary: UK homebuyers face the worst mortgage affordability since 2008, with initial repayments consuming over 21% of gross income on average, according to UK Finance. The least affordable areas are concentrated in the London commuter belt.

stories.title: Russian strike on Chernihiv center: Injury toll climbs to five
stories.summary: The number of casualties resulting from the Russian strike on central Chernihiv has increased to five.

stories.title: Rubble from Trump ballroom dumped at DC golf course has toxic metals, data shows
stories.summary: A federal judge warned the Trump administration to proceed carefully with plans to revamp a historic Washington, D.C., golf course. Data showed that rubble from a demolished White House ballroom dumped at the course contained toxic metals.

stories.title: Several killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine ahead of rival ceasefires
stories.summary: Russian drone and missile strikes targeting Ukraine's power grid killed at least five people and wounded 39 others overnight. The attacks came less than a day before Kyiv's announced ceasefire and three days before Moscow's own planned pause in hostilities.

stories.title: Hegseth 'seeking to reassure people US is still in control' in Middle East
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that the ceasefire with Iran remains in effect despite ongoing exchanges of fire in the Gulf over control of the Strait of Hormuz. His remarks are seen as an effort to reassure allies that Washington maintains control of the situation.

stories.title: In Zaporizhzhia, injury toll after morning attack climbs to four
stories.summary: In Zaporizhzhia, the number of casualties from this morning’s Russian attack has increased to four.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire holds despite Hormuz standoff: Pentagon chief Hegseth
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the US-Iran ceasefire remains in effect despite a standoff near the Strait of Hormuz. He described a security 'dome' established to protect ships, though maritime traffic through the strait remains stalled.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelensky slams Russian 'cynicism' ahead of separate truces
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of "utter cynicism" for launching deadly attacks while simultaneously seeking a truce ahead of its May 9 Victory Day celebrations. Both Moscow and Kyiv have announced separate unilateral ceasefires on different dates this week.

stories.title: Iran strike on UAE pushes Abu Dhabi closer to Israel alliance - analysis
stories.summary: Iran’s attacks on the UAE will likely lead to Abu Dhabi viewing Israel as a stronger and necessary partner.

stories.title: Mali violence brings uncertainty to key Ivory Coast trade route
stories.summary: Violence in Mali is disrupting the Abidjan–Bamako trade corridor, a vital route for commerce between Ivory Coast and Mali. The Malian diaspora in Ivory Coast, estimated at 3 to 4 million people, plays a significant economic role and faces growing uncertainty from the instability.

stories.title: South African police find human remains inside crocodile airlifted out of river
stories.summary: South African police recovered human remains from inside a crocodile during a high-risk operation involving an airlift from a river. A police captain was praised for extraordinary bravery after being lowered into the crocodile-infested waters.

stories.title: Former Shin Bet chief Yoram Cohen joins Eisenkot’s Yashar party
stories.summary: Former Shin Bet chief Yoram Cohen, who led the Israeli security agency from 2011 to 2016 under Prime Minister Netanyahu, joined the Yashar party led by former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot. Cohen is described as a fierce critic of Netanyahu.

stories.title: Four Palestine Action activists convicted of criminal damage
stories.summary: Four Palestine Action activists — Charlotte Head, Samuel Corner, Leona Kamio, and Fatema Rajwani — were convicted of criminal damage for breaking into an Elbit Systems factory in Filton, near Bristol, on August 6, 2024. They destroyed property including drones and computers at the Israeli defense firm's UK site.

stories.title: Air Force wants AI in its air-ops command-and-control system
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force is pursuing the integration of artificial intelligence into its air operations command-and-control system. The effort is being managed by Kessel Run and aims to improve the Air Operations Center Weapon System used by combatant commands.

stories.title: Former IDF commander Wajdi Sarhan launches first Druze political party in decades
stories.summary: Former IDF commander Wajdi Sarhan launched the Brotherhood Alliance, the first Druze political party in Israel in decades. The party aims to win Knesset seats and serve as a kingmaker amid growing Druze frustration with major parties.

stories.title: Spain court seeks probe over Israeli detention of UN peacekeeper
stories.summary: A Spanish court is pursuing a potential criminal investigation after Israel briefly detained a Spanish UN peacekeeper in Lebanon. Spain has requested information from the United Nations about the incident.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi 'between life and death' in hospital
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was hospitalized and is reportedly in critical condition. Supporters said she suffered two episodes of complete loss of consciousness and a severe cardiac crisis after being arrested in December for speaking out against the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: 'Chicken wars': France's highly political fast-food fight
stories.summary: A French cultural segment explored the political controversy surrounding a roasted chicken restaurant chain in France, reflecting broader debates about fast food in the country. The discussion also touched on France's cultural relationship with chicken and related French-language expressions.

stories.title: Unwell British crew member to be ‘urgently’ evacuated from cruise ship after hantavirus cases
stories.summary: A British crew member aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius in the Atlantic Ocean is being urgently evacuated along with a Dutch colleague after both developed respiratory symptoms linked to a suspected hantavirus outbreak. Dutch authorities are overseeing the medical evacuation.

stories.title: Venice Biennale in crisis: The controversies explained
stories.summary: The Venice Biennale will not award its traditional Golden Lion this year after the jury resigned over the disputed participation of Russia and Israel in the event.

stories.title: Why Europe’s car industry is at the centre of a new US trade war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened to raise tariffs on European Union cars and trucks exported to the United States from 15 percent to 25 percent, intensifying a trade dispute centered on Europe's automotive industry.

stories.title: New Syria protest conditions raise concern over freedoms
stories.summary: Syrian authorities introduced new conditions for street protests that have raised concerns among civil society groups. Critics say the requirements bear similarities to restrictions imposed under the former Assad regime.

stories.title: Map of dominance: Why Iran can’t afford to give up Hormuz control
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical strategic asset for Iran as it seeks leverage in negotiations with Washington. The waterway is a vital passageway for global energy shipments.

stories.title: U.K. Targets Russian Army Recruitment Network and Drone Suppliers in Latest Sanctions Package
stories.summary: The United Kingdom imposed new sanctions targeting Russia's army recruitment network and drone suppliers. British officials described a scheme that lures foreign nationals to Russia with promises of employment, then forces them into frontline combat in Ukraine or military production roles.

stories.title: Smotrich says he promised his son ‘more destruction’ in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich stated publicly that he promised his son there would be 'more destruction' in Lebanon.

stories.title: Britain’s ruling Labour party faces bruising losses in local polls
stories.summary: Britain's ruling Labour Party is expected to face significant losses in local elections scheduled for May 7. The polls will serve as a gauge of public sentiment toward the party's governance.

stories.title: Romanian PM ousted in no-confidence vote
stories.summary: Romanian Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan was removed from office after losing a parliamentary no-confidence vote. The largest party in his governing coalition joined with the far-right opposition to oust him.

stories.title: Will Hong Kong’s claw machine regulations curb gaming habits and gambling risks?
stories.summary: Hong Kong has proposed stricter regulations on claw and pinball machines amid rising concerns about teenage addiction and the blurring of lines between gaming and gambling. Authorities plan to amend relevant laws to curb these risks.

stories.title: Will Pakistan’s new defence pact with Saudi Arabia give Chinese arms risk-free exposure?
stories.summary: A new Pakistan-Saudi Arabia defense pact could potentially give Chinese-manufactured weapons exposure to real combat conditions via the Iran conflict, without direct Chinese military involvement. The arrangement may allow Beijing to demonstrate its defense technology's effectiveness.
