stories.title: Iran’s top diplomat Abbas Araghchi to visit China days ahead of Donald Trump
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is scheduled to visit China this week for talks with Chinese counterpart Wang Yi, less than ten days before U.S. President Donald Trump's planned visit to Beijing. The two diplomats have held multiple rounds of calls since U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the current conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky shows footage of Flamingo missiles striking military-industrial complex facilities in Cheboksary
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky released footage of Flamingo missiles striking military-industrial complex facilities in Cheboksary, Russia. He noted the missiles traveled over 1,500 kilometers to reach their targets.

stories.title: Ukraine did math on Tuapse — and Russian reaction tells rest
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Tuapse oil refinery on Russia's Black Sea coast four times in a single month. The facility is Russia's only Black Sea oil refinery, and each successive attack reportedly compounded the damage to its operations.

stories.title: East Africa: IGAD Unveils Regional Youth Coalition to Shape Climate Policy, Drive Climate-Resilient Agriculture
stories.summary: The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) launched a regional youth coalition in Nairobi focused on shaping climate policy and promoting climate-resilient agriculture across Eastern Africa. The platform aims to place young people at the center of regional climate action.

stories.title: NATO needs policies, standards for sharing AI-enhanced geospatial intel: Official
stories.summary: A NATO official, UK Royal Marine Maj. Gen. Paul Lynch, stated that the alliance needs governance policies and standards for sharing AI-enhanced geospatial intelligence. He emphasized that achieving an allied intelligence advantage depends primarily on governance frameworks rather than additional capabilities.

stories.title: Ukraine could lift arms-exports ban this year as would-be buyers line up
stories.summary: Ukraine may lift its ban on arms exports this year as demand grows from foreign buyers. Gulf countries threatened by Iran are expected to be among the first customers for Ukrainian air-defense technology.

stories.title: Irish Cabinet defends alumina exports to Russia by citing refugees—then evicts 16,000 of them
stories.summary: The Irish Cabinet defended continued alumina exports to Russia by citing its acceptance of Ukrainian refugees. However, within 27 days of that justification, the government moved to evict approximately 16,000 refugees from their accommodations.

stories.title: Almost half of operational decisions will be done by AI in 2030, IBM reveals - poll
stories.summary: A global IBM poll of CEOs projects that artificial intelligence will handle 48% of operational decisions autonomously by 2030. The adoption is expected primarily in areas governed by clear, established rules and procedures.

stories.title: Japan pivots Indo-Pacific strategy toward Southeast Asia
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi used a visit to Vietnam to update Japan's Indo-Pacific strategy, refocusing it on energy security, critical minerals, and ASEAN resilience. The shift represents a strategic pivot toward deeper engagement with Southeast Asia.

stories.title: UK lawyer says police wrongly listed him as 'Hamas member'
stories.summary: A UK lawyer has accused police of wrongly labelling him a Hamas member after detaining him under terrorism powers and accessing his phone data.

stories.title: Sudan accuses UAE, Ethiopia of Khartoum airport drone strikes
stories.summary: Sudan accused Ethiopia of involvement in a drone strike on Khartoum's airport launched by the country's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. Airport officials said the drone was shot down before hitting its target. Sudan also accused the UAE of playing a role.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at former London synagogue in latest attack against UK Jews
stories.summary: A fire broke out at a former synagogue in London, and police are investigating possible links to a series of recent attacks targeting Jewish and Israeli communities across the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Amnesty accuses ADF fighters of war crimes in eastern DR Congo
stories.summary: Amnesty International accused Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters linked to the Islamic State of committing widespread war crimes and crimes against humanity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: India may discuss BrahMos missile sale to Vietnam during presidential visit, sources say
stories.summary: Vietnamese President To Lam is expected to discuss the potential purchase of BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles during a visit to New Delhi, in a deal potentially worth about $629 million. India has already sold BrahMos missiles to the Philippines and signed a contract with Indonesia.

stories.title: Ukraine tried to attack Russia's Kirishi oil refinery, governor says
stories.summary: Ukraine attempted to attack the Kirishi oil refinery, one of Russia's largest, in the Leningrad region on Tuesday, according to Governor Alexander Drozdenko. The attack sparked a fire in an industrial area of the town of Kirishi.

stories.title: REPLAY: Pentagon chief Hegseth says ceasefire with Iran not over
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated at a press conference that the ceasefire with Iran is still in effect. He described the U.S. operation to protect commercial ships from Iran in the Strait of Hormuz as temporary and said Washington is not seeking conflict.

stories.title: Japan, Philippines to fast-track transfer of navy destroyers
stories.summary: Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi pledged during a visit to Manila to expedite the transfer of Abukuma-class destroyers to the Philippines. The two countries have deepened military ties over shared concerns about Chinese territorial claims, including signing a reciprocal troop access agreement.

stories.title: Mapping Mali’s gold and natural resource wealth
stories.summary: Mali holds Africa's third-largest gold reserves along with significant lithium and uranium deposits, making it one of the continent's most resource-rich nations in West Africa.

stories.title: In Gaza, World Press Day is literally about life or death
stories.summary: The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate described journalism in Palestine as "a daily battle," citing killings, arrests, and restrictions on reporting.

stories.title: Ahmed Fouad Alkhatib: Israel has re-embraced Hamas rule in Gaza
stories.summary: Ahmed Fouad Alkhatib, head of Realign for Palestine, argued that Israel has effectively re-embraced Hamas governance in Gaza. He described deteriorating conditions in the territory and further entrenchment of Hamas amid stalled progress on peace plans.

stories.title: Russians attack rescue workers in Poltava region with rockets containing cluster munitions
stories.summary: Two Ukrainian State Emergency Service rescuers were killed in Russia's Poltava region after a follow-up Russian strike with cluster munitions targeted them as they responded to an earlier attack on energy infrastructure on the night of May 5.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz condemns drone, missile attacks in UAE
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned drone and missile attacks on civilian infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates, expressing solidarity with UAE President Sheikh Mohammad bin Zayed Al Nahyan. He called for the ceasefire to be upheld to allow diplomatic dialogue.

stories.title: 'For you, for them': Avila writes to daughter from Israeli jail
stories.summary: Detained Gaza flotilla activist Thiago Ávila wrote an emotional letter to his daughter as Israel extended his custody without charges.

stories.title: Two dead as car rams crowd in Germany's Leipzig
stories.summary: Two people were killed and three seriously injured when a car drove into a pedestrian zone in Leipzig, eastern Germany, on Monday. Police arrested the driver, identified as a 33-year-old German citizen.

stories.title: Rebel groups in Mali capture a drone control station
stories.summary: Two rebel groups captured the city of Kidal in northern Mali on April 26. Among the sites seized was a ground control station for drones previously operated by the Malian Army.

stories.title: Iran Nobel winner Mohammadi 'between life and death' after hospitalisation
stories.summary: Jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been hospitalized under guard for five days with a heart condition. Her supporters said on Tuesday that she is fighting for her life.

stories.title: Iran feeling confident in attacking after month of shaky ceasefire - analysis
stories.summary: The UAE intercepted multiple missiles and drones amid renewed Iranian attacks, including a strike on a key UAE oil port. CNN reported the UAE employed an Israeli air defense system during the engagements. The attacks followed a month of fragile ceasefire between Iran and its adversaries.

stories.title: Human-to-human hantavirus transmission suspected on cruise ship
stories.summary: The World Health Organization said it suspects human-to-human transmission of hantavirus occurred on a cruise ship where three people have died among seven confirmed and suspected cases. WHO official Maria Van Kerkhove indicated transmission may have occurred among close contacts aboard the vessel.

stories.title: Is Iran’s regime losing control? Khamenei rumors fuel command crisis, expert says
stories.summary: Amid unconfirmed rumors about the health of Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran expert Dr. Thamar Eilam Gindin suggested a potential command crisis within Iran's leadership. She urged opposition groups to cooperate with Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi to mobilize the Iranian public.

stories.title: DRC protest in support of US sanctions against former president
stories.summary: Protests took place in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in support of US sanctions imposed against the country's former president.

stories.title: Court remands 2 flotilla activists until Sunday; lawyer claims one was on fishing trip
stories.summary: An Israeli court in Ashkelon remanded two flotilla activists — Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila — until Sunday. A lawyer for Avila claimed his client had been on a fishing trip and never planned to break the Gaza blockade.

stories.title: UK Counter Terrorism police probe arson attack at former London synagogue
stories.summary: UK Counter Terrorism police are investigating an arson attack at a former synagogue in east London. The incident caused minor damage to the building's gates with no injuries, and officers are examining possible links to other attacks targeting the Jewish community.

stories.title: Palestinian photographer Saher Alghorra wins 2026 Pulitzer Prize
stories.summary: Palestinian photographer Saher Alghorra has won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for his "haunting" images documenting Israel's genocide in Gaza.

stories.title: Nine workers die in Colombia coal mine explosion
stories.summary: A coal mine explosion in Colombia's Cundinamarca province killed nine workers and injured six others. The national mining agency noted it had issued risk control recommendations for the site several weeks prior to the incident.

stories.title: Hegseth says US blockade on Iran ‘gift to the world’
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth described the American blockade on Iran as a 'gift to the world,' referring to a 'powerful red, white, and blue dome' the US has established.

stories.title: Released Flotilla activists describe‘torture’ in Israeli prison
stories.summary: Flotilla activists who returned to Argentina after being detained by Israeli forces described being subjected to torture while held in Israeli prison.

stories.summary: Crude and oil prices have surged once again following the latest trade of fire in the Middle East, impacting the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.summary: Videos from tournament kit reveal photo shoot and images from training sessions highlighting Team Melli's preparations.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia suffers major casualties in war every month; over 35,000 killed and severely wounded in April
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia suffered over 35,000 personnel killed and severely wounded in April alone. He characterized the losses as significant and recurring on a monthly basis throughout the war.

stories.title: Hot weather to persist in Karachi but temperature to stay below 40°C
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast hot and humid weather in Karachi through Thursday, with temperatures expected to remain between 35–39°C. Hot and dry conditions are also expected across most of Sindh province.

stories.title: US prepared for visa sanctions on China over migrants issue, official says
stories.summary: A U.S. official said Washington is prepared to impose visa sanctions on China over Beijing's longstanding refusal to accept the return of Chinese citizens residing illegally in the United States. China has for years resisted such repatriation requests.

stories.summary: The energy crisis triggered by the Iran war is severely impacting Asian economies, with oil imports to the region dropping 30% in April. The Asian Development Bank cut its growth forecast for developing Asia to 4.7% for this year and raised its inflation outlook to 5.2%.

stories.title: Kim Jong Un urges North Korean youth aged 14 to 30 to fight for Russia after losing 6,000 troops in Kursk
stories.summary: At a Pyongyang youth congress, Kim Jong Un cast 14- to 30-year-olds as the "vanguard" of state goals while the ruling party praised dead soldiers in Russia's war as "bombs and flames."

stories.title: Indian pilots demand further probe of last year's Air India crash
stories.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots has written to India's aviation ministry suggesting that electrical failure, rather than pilot error, may have caused the June 2025 Air India Boeing 787-8 crash that killed 260 people. The submission comes ahead of the expected final report from India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau.

stories.title: Mobile Internet Outages Reported in Moscow and St. Petersburg Amid ‘Security Concerns’
stories.summary: Mobile internet outages were reported across Moscow and St. Petersburg on Tuesday. Russia's Digital Ministry confirmed the restrictions were intentionally introduced as a temporary measure, citing security concerns.

stories.title: US, Iran, UAE trade Hormuz attack claims: What we know
stories.summary: Experts say claims and counterclaims threaten the diplomatic route to end the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Former NASA head Jim Bridenstine takes helm at Quantum Space
stories.summary: Former NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine has been named head of Quantum Space. The company focuses on potential Space Force operations in cislunar space, the region between Earth and the moon.

stories.title: Met police chief condemned for claiming pro-Palestine protests intended to go past synagogues
stories.summary: A coalition of campaign groups condemned London Metropolitan Police chief Mark Rowley for claiming that organisers of pro-Palestine protests repeatedly intended to route demonstrations past synagogues. The groups called on Rowley to retract the comments.

stories.summary: The lawyers representing the two activists will appeal the extension decision, calling it 'the state's lawlessness'.

stories.title: Moscow shuts down airports and mobile signals as Victory Day parade looms
stories.summary: Moscow shut down airports and cut mobile internet access for many users on Tuesday as Russia tightened security ahead of the May 9 Victory Day parade. The annual celebration has been scaled back, proceeding without heavy military hardware for the first time in nearly two decades amid fears of Ukrainian drone strikes.

stories.title: CSIS: 2025 saw Canadian intelligence intervene in seven violent threats motivated by Gaza war
stories.summary: Canada's intelligence service CSIS reported intervening in seven violent threats in 2025 motivated by the Gaza war. The agency described religiously motivated violent extremism as particularly concerning, citing ISIS operations, the October 7 conflict, and online radicalization as contributing factors.

stories.title: Macron backs Armenia’s pro-Europe PM as re-election campaign draws to close
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron publicly endorsed Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan ahead of upcoming elections in which Pashinyan faces a challenge from pro-Russia parties. Macron said Armenia's destiny lay with Europe and accused Russia of abandoning Armenia after the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war.

stories.title: Army turns to ‘hackathons’ to better connect dozens of weapons, systems
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is hosting its first "hackathon" event at Fort Carson, Colorado, bringing together nine major defense vendors to develop better integration among dozens of weapons systems and platforms.

stories.summary: Pilgrims have cautiously returned to Tunisia's Ghriba synagogue following a 2023 attack on the site. Visitors reported a welcoming atmosphere and a strong security presence on the ground.

stories.title: Approximately 2,000 people evacuated from frontline areas in south
stories.summary: Since the beginning of 2026, approximately 2,000 people have been evacuated from frontline areas in southern Ukraine, including nearly 500 children and 32 individuals with reduced mobility.

His defense attorneys argue he is being used as a scapegoat for the LA fire department's failure to fully extinguish an earlier fire.

stories.title: Russia’s oil exports drop by 1.8 mln tonnes in April amid port strikes and sanctions – Vlasiuk
stories.summary: Russia's oil exports fell by approximately 1.8 million tonnes in April due to sanctions pressure and strikes on key Baltic ports, according to Ukrainian official Vlasiuk. Russia is reportedly seeking alternative export routes to offset the losses.

stories.title: Russian drones, missiles kill five at Ukraine's Naftogaz gas production plants, CEO says
stories.summary: Russian drone and missile strikes hit Naftogaz gas production facilities in Ukraine, killing five people and wounding 37, according to the company's CEO.

stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran may push Tehran toward developing nuclear weapons in self-defense. It draws parallels with Israel's own clandestine nuclear program, which dates back to the 1950s.

stories.title: Mali junta chief to take over killed defence minister's role
stories.summary: Goita, the leader of Mali's junta since 2021 following a coup, will be assisted by General Oumar Diarra in his new role as defence minister.

stories.title: Trump accuses pope of ‘endangering a lot of Catholics’ with Iran stance
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump accused Pope Leo XIV of "endangering a lot of Catholics" over the pontiff's stance on Iran, claiming the pope supports Iran's right to nuclear weapons. The remarks came two days before Secretary of State Marco Rubio's planned visit to the Vatican to ease tensions.

stories.title: Russians attack port in Odesa region this morning; ship damaged
stories.summary: On the morning of May 5, Russian forces shelled a port in the greater Odesa region, damaging a ship flying the Cook Islands flag.

stories.title: Thailand's monkey business: Pharmaceutical labs rely on primate testing
stories.summary: An investigation reveals that pharmaceutical laboratories rely heavily on primate testing for drugs and vaccines. Since China banned primate exports in 2020, prices have surged, fueling an international black market centered on Cambodia, Thailand, and Laos.

stories.title: US, Iran launch new attacks as they wrestle for control of Gulf waters
stories.summary: The United States and Iran launched new military attacks against each other as both sides contest control of Gulf waters. The exchange marked the first apparent use of military force since a ceasefire was announced the previous month.

stories.title: Israeli officers 'threaten Gaza flotilla activists with death' during interrogations
stories.summary: Israeli lawyers report that activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla, seized in international waters, face threats and psychological pressure during interrogations. Activist Thiago Avila appeared at a magistrate's court in Ashkelon, Israel, as authorities extended detention for another week.

stories.title: Kenya: Former Kenya Women's 7s and 15s Coach Oloo Is Dead
stories.summary: Kenyan rugby coach Felix "Ade" Oloo Otieno has died, prompting mourning across the country's rugby community. Oloo was widely credited with reshaping the landscape of women's rugby in Kenya through his work with the national women's sevens and fifteens teams.

stories.title: Police investigate suspected arson attack at former synagogue in east London
stories.summary: Counter-terrorism police in London are investigating a suspected arson attack at a former synagogue on Nelson Street in Tower Hamlets, east London. CCTV footage shows the fire was started deliberately, and investigators are examining whether it is linked to an arson campaign connected to Iran.

stories.title: London Marathon sets record after 1.8% of UK adult population applies for 2027 race
stories.summary: The London Marathon received over one million applications from UK runners for its 2027 race, representing 1.8 percent of the UK adult population. A world-record 1,338,544 global entries were submitted, more than double the number received in 2024.

stories.title: China targets top spot in supercomputing with fully domestic, CPU-only machine
stories.summary: China unveiled a domestically built supercomputer called Lingsheng (LineShine) that aims to reach 2 exaflops, surpassing the current record holder, the 1.8-exaflop El Capitan at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. The machine uses entirely home-grown CPUs, bypassing US export controls on GPUs.

stories.title: South Africa: Public Urged to Exercise Caution Amid Severe Weather Warnings
stories.summary: South Africa's Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa urged citizens to exercise heightened caution following severe weather warnings issued by the South African Weather Service.

stories.title: Iraqi factions mull disarming in bid for government role
stories.summary: Several Iraqi armed factions have signaled willingness to disarm in exchange for political inclusion in the government. The move comes amid increasing pressure from the United States on these groups to lay down their weapons.

stories.title: East Africa: Kenya, Tanzania Set May 2026 Deadline to Eliminate Trade Barriers
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto and Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan agreed to eliminate all non-tariff trade barriers between their countries by the end of May 2026. The commitment was made in Dar es Salaam as part of broader efforts to strengthen regional integration in East Africa.

stories.title: UK counterterrorism police investigate arson attack at former synagogue
stories.summary: The incident in London comes after the UK's national threat level was raised to severe last week.

stories.title: Operational Command South names main requests for assistance received from communities
stories.summary: The Civil-Military Cooperation Department of Ukraine's Operational Command South receives roughly 200 requests per month from local communities, covering needs such as building inspections and mine safety assistance.

stories.title: German defense minister laments long-range strike ‘gap’ caused by planned US drawdown
stories.summary: German Defense Minister highlighted a long-range strike capability gap resulting from a planned US military drawdown. Both options under consideration — maintaining US Army Typhon launchers or purchasing them for the Bundeswehr — are reportedly not materializing.

stories.title: Romania's government collapses after Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan loses confidence vote
stories.summary: Romanian Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan was removed from office after losing a parliamentary no-confidence vote. The collapse of the coalition government was driven by disagreements over unpopular austerity measures, with the Social Democrats departing the coalition and moving to oust the prime minister.

stories.title: Sudan accuses Ethiopia and UAE of orchestrating drone attacks on airport
stories.summary: Sudan's foreign ministry accused Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates of orchestrating drone attacks on a Sudanese airport. Sudan's foreign minister warned that both countries had chosen the "wrong path" and would face consequences.

stories.title: Romania's pro-EU coalition government collapses after prime minister loses no-confidence vote
stories.summary: Romania's pro-European coalition government collapsed on Tuesday after parliament passed a no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan. The vote triggers political turmoil in the EU and NATO member state bordering Ukraine, less than a year after the coalition was formed.

stories.title: Lebanon Melkite bishops 'concerned' over Israeli demolitions
stories.summary: The Council of Melkite Greek Catholic Bishops expressed concern over Israeli demolitions in Lebanon. The bishops accused Israeli soldiers of destroying a Melkite convent in the southern Lebanese town of Yaroun during ongoing military operations.

stories.title: NollywoodWeek Film Festival co-founder Serge Noukoué on its 13th edition
stories.summary: The 13th edition of the NollywoodWeek Film Festival opened in Paris with the theme "Voyage." Co-founder Serge Noukoué discussed the Nigerian film industry's growth — now valued at over $6 billion — and the challenges it faces from streaming and global expansion.

stories.title: Blast at fireworks factory in China's Hunan kills 21, state media says
stories.summary: An explosion at a fireworks factory in Liuyang, Hunan province, China, killed 21 people and injured 61 on Monday. President Xi Jinping called for a thorough investigation into the blast.

stories.title: Russian forces attacked the center of Chernihiv: Administrative building damaged, casualties reported
stories.summary: On May 5, Russian forces launched a Shahed drone attack on the center of Chernihiv, damaging an administrative building and causing casualties.

stories.title: Gaza's no-cash transport crisis sparks new paper transit card
stories.summary: Amid Israel's ongoing war, Gaza's transport, cash, and internet infrastructure have been severely disrupted. Palestinians have introduced a paper-based transit card system to maintain mobility despite the collapse of digital and cash-based payment networks.

stories.title: Bowen: Strait of Hormuz standoff raises risk of sliding back into all out war
stories.summary: The US and Iran's determination to keep the pressure on each other has put the fragile Gulf ceasefire in serious jeopardy.

stories.title: Africa: More Nations Plan to Call Out South Africa Govt Over Xenophobic Violence
stories.summary: Multiple African nations are raising concerns with South Africa's government over a rise in xenophobic attacks against foreign nationals. Mozambique is expected to join Nigeria and Ghana in formally complaining to Pretoria about the alleged mistreatment of their citizens.

stories.title: IDF kills two fleeing terrorists with drone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military killed two armed suspects in southern Lebanon using a drone strike. According to the IDF, the individuals were operating near Israeli troops and attempted to flee on a motorcycle before being targeted.

stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces scrutiny over invoking his conservative Christian faith in connection with military operations against Iran. Questions are growing about whether his religious rhetoric could jeopardize his position in the administration.

stories.summary: An Israeli court has prolonged the detention of activists Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila until Sunday, amid reports of their ill-treatment in prison.

stories.title: Israel seeks to extend detention of Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: An Israeli court is set to hear a request to extend the detention of foreign activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla in international waters. The activists were captured during an interception operation the previous week.

stories.summary: Israeli company Smart Shooter is developing precision technology to help soldiers intercept Hezbollah's fiber-optic-guided drones, which are maneuverable and resistant to electronic jamming.

stories.title: Why Fujairah matters: UAE oil hub beyond Iran's reach in Hormuz
stories.summary: Fujairah, a UAE emirate located outside the Strait of Hormuz, has become a strategically vital hub for oil exports and global energy flows. Its geographic position shields it from potential Iranian disruption of traffic through the strait amid rising regional tensions.

stories.title: Tuareg rebels hold dozens of soldiers in Mali as prisoners
stories.summary: Exclusive video obtained by Al Jazeera shows dozens of soldiers held prisoner by Tuareg separatists in northern Mali.

stories.title: Hong Kong ‘block trade king’ exploited bank lapse to make HK$1.7 million, court told
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court heard allegations that hedge fund manager Simon Sadler exploited confidential information to earn HK$1.7 million in a single day by selling shares in a Hong Kong fashion company. Sadler, alongside the defunct Segantii Capital Management and former employee Daniel La Rocca Jnr, is on trial for insider dealing.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: India condemns attack on Indians in Fujairah Petroleum Zone
stories.summary: India condemned an attack on Indian nationals in the Fujairah Petroleum Zone in the UAE amid the ongoing Iran-Israel conflict. U.S. President Donald Trump launched "Project Freedom" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, prompting a sharp response from Iran.

stories.title: South Korea to probe ship fire in Strait of Hormuz, Trump blames Iranian attack
stories.summary: South Korea's Foreign Ministry said it would investigate a ship fire involving a South Korean vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. President Trump attributed the incident to an Iranian attack. South Korean officials said the exact cause would be determined after the vessel is towed and its damage assessed.

stories.title: Colorado firebomb suspect to plead guilty to all state charges, defence says
stories.summary: The suspect in a firebombing case in Colorado is expected to plead guilty to all 184 state charges he faces, according to his defence team.

stories.title: U.S. Military strike on alleged drug boat kills two in the Caribbean
stories.summary: A U.S. military strike on an alleged drug-trafficking vessel in the Caribbean killed two people. The Trump administration's campaign of targeting suspected drug boats in Latin American waters has persisted since early September and killed at least 188 people in total.

stories.title: Sudan military accuses Ethiopia and UAE of drone attacks
stories.summary: Sudan's military accused the United Arab Emirates and Ethiopia of involvement in a drone strike on Khartoum airport. Military officials said evidence and flight data indicated the drone originated from the UAE and was launched from Ethiopian territory.

stories.title: FP: Patriot supplies to Ukraine hinge on the war in Iran, which has already drained nearly half of the US stockpile
stories.summary: Foreign Policy reports that US Patriot missile supplies to Ukraine are being constrained by the ongoing war with Iran, which has consumed nearly half of America's Patriot stockpile. stories.title: China unveils new naval defence systems as drones change nature of war at sea

The post UK’s Starmer to meet with c

stories.title: Malawi: 'We Are Not Refusing Tax--We Are Fighting for Survival' - Traders Shut Shops Nationwide Over MRA's New System
stories.summary: Traders across Malawi's major cities shut their shops in a nationwide protest against the Malawi Revenue Authority's new electronic invoicing system. Business owners said the system threatens to penalize and overwhelm already struggling enterprises.

stories.title: Modi’s party wins control of India's West Bengal for first time
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP won control of West Bengal for the first time, taking the opposition stronghold in state elections. Opposition parties criticized the polls after the Election Commission removed millions of voters from electoral rolls.

stories.title: Russia’s African Recruitment Web Is Expanding
stories.summary: An investigation reveals that deceptive job recruitment schemes linked to Russia are expanding across Africa, with transnational networks pulling Kenyan nationals into Moscow's war effort in Ukraine.

stories.title: German minesweeper sets sail for possible Hormuz mission
stories.summary: A German Navy minesweeper departed for the Mediterranean on Monday in preparation for a possible deployment to the Strait of Hormuz. Berlin said it is prepared to help ensure freedom of navigation in the waterway, which Iran blocked in retaliation for US airstrikes, but will act only if certain conditions are met.

stories.title: Israel honors children killed in Iranian unrest, Druze children killed by Hezbollah, with new mural
stories.summary: Israel unveiled a mural honoring children killed in Iranian unrest and 12 Druze children killed by a Hezbollah rocket strike in Majdal Shams on July 27, 2024. The installation depicts the Druze children in green facing Iranian children in red.

stories.title: Stamps celebrate 100 years of America's famed Route 66
stories.summary: The US Postal Service issued a special series of eight stamps to celebrate the 100th anniversary of Route 66. Photographer David J. Schwartz, who spent two decades documenting the 2,448-mile highway, captured images representing each state the iconic road passes through.

stories.title: Canada adds 12.4 mn euros to Ukraine Energy Support Fund, total passes 57 mn
stories.summary: Canada contributed an additional €12.4 million to Ukraine's Energy Support Fund, bringing the total to over €57 million. Approximately €260 million worth of energy equipment is already in transit to Ukraine, with delivery expected before winter.

stories.title: 'This is how we prevail in the Pacific': US, allies train to repel amphibious assault
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's 25th Infantry Division deployed new weapons during the annual Balikatan military exercise with allies in the Pacific. The joint training focused on repelling amphibious assaults as part of broader regional defense preparations.

stories.title: Taiwan player victim of ‘inappropriate contact’ at UK table tennis event
stories.summary: Officials say a female player was subjected to inappropriate physical contact during a security check.

stories.title: Lawyer who represented Hamas in court says UK police falsely listed him as member of group
stories.summary: British lawyer Fahad Ansari, who represented Hamas in a legal challenge to its proscription in the UK, says police falsely recorded him as a member of the group. A detective inspector listed "Hamas" under group membership on a risk assessment form when Ansari was detained under the Terrorism Act upon returning from a family holiday in Ireland.

stories.title: IAEA discovers equipment malfunction at ZNPP following drone attack
stories.summary: During a visit to the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, the International Atomic Energy Agency discovered damage to meteorological monitoring equipment at the External Radiation Control Laboratory following a drone attack.

stories.title: Iran warns 'not even started' in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's chief negotiator warned the United States against further escalation in the Strait of Hormuz after a series of clashes. The US military said its helicopters struck six Iranian boats threatening commercial shipping, while the UAE reported fresh Iranian attacks on its territory.

stories.title: Education Bureau steps in after Hong Kong school’s phone ban sparks backlash
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Education Bureau intervened after Kwun Tong Maryknoll College announced stricter mobile phone rules for Form Three and Four students, sparking backlash. The new policy would ban on-campus phone use, requiring devices to be stored in lockers with limited access.

stories.title: US intel indicates limited new damage to Iran nuclear programme
stories.summary: US intelligence assessments indicate that recent strikes on Iran caused limited new damage to its nuclear program. Washington's focus on military rather than nuclear targets means Iran's estimated timeline to rebuild a nuclear weapon remains unchanged.

stories.title: Hong Kong home sales surge to 2-year high, boosting overall transactions
stories.summary: Hong Kong property transactions rose to a four-month high in April, with home sales reaching their highest level in 24 months. A total of 8,692 transactions were completed, up 12.3% from March, showing real estate resilience amid regional uncertainties.

stories.title: Ohio heads to polls as Ramaswamy hopes to lock in as Republican candidate for governor – US politics live
stories.summary: Ohio held primary elections on Tuesday, with Trump-endorsed Vivek Ramaswamy seeking to secure the Republican gubernatorial nomination against challenger Casey Putsch. Separately, Donald Trump threatened to blow Iran "off the face of the earth" if it attacks US vessels working to reopen a route through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Criminal complaint filed against Norwegian politicians over complicity in Gaza genocide
stories.summary: A criminal complaint was filed in Norway against Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and cabinet members alleging complicity in the Gaza genocide. Prosecutors have recommended a police investigation into the allegations.

stories.title: Hospitalised former NYC Mayor Rudy Giuliani breathing unaided; remains critical
stories.summary: Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani remains hospitalized in critical condition but is now breathing without assistance. A spokesperson said his condition was worsened by restrictive airway disease linked to dust and toxin exposure from the September 11, 2001 World Trade Center attack.

stories.title: US, Iran claim dominance in Hormuz amid fresh drone strikes
stories.summary: The United States and Iran continued to clash over control of the Strait of Hormuz as Tehran launched fresh drone attacks on the United Arab Emirates. Both sides claimed dominance in the strategically vital waterway.

stories.title: UK electric car sales leap ‘could be hit by Iran war inflation and energy price rises’
stories.summary: UK new car sales rose 24% year on year in April 2025, with battery electric vehicle registrations jumping nearly 60%, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders. The SMMT warned the sales momentum could be tempered by rising inflation and energy prices linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Smotrich: Including Arab party in government ‘a thousand times’ worse than Oct. 7 failures
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich drew criticism for stating that including an Arab party in government would be worse than the failures of October 7. Former PM Naftali Bennett accused Smotrich and Prime Minister Netanyahu of deflecting from past atrocities. Smotrich claimed media outlets distorted his remarks.

stories.title: Taiwan leader defies China after Eswatini trip and reasserts island's global role
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te returned from a three-day visit to Eswatini, declaring state-to-state travel a "basic right" and pushing back against Chinese efforts to block the trip. He reaffirmed Taiwan's commitment to maintaining international engagement.

stories.title: Will be ‘very happy’ to see woman elected as next U.N. chief: China
stories.summary: China expressed support for electing a woman as the next United Nations Secretary-General. The UN has never had a female leader in its 80-year history.

stories.title: Russians shell Naftogaz facilities in Poltava and Kharkiv regions: Five dead, 37 wounded
stories.summary: On the night of May 5, Russian forces launched a large-scale shelling campaign against Naftogaz Group facilities in the Poltava and Kharkiv regions, killing five people and wounding 37.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lagos Hits N807bn Revenue in Early 2026, Surpasses Nigeria's Subnational Peers
stories.summary: Lagos State, Nigeria, collected ₦807 billion in revenue in early 2026, driven largely by personal income taxes. The figure approached nearly one-fifth of the state's ambitious 2026 budget within three months, outpacing other Nigerian subnational governments.

stories.title: Trump torn on Iran war plan after attacks on US ships in Strait of Hormuz - WSJ
stories.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, President Trump is torn between negotiating with Iran to end its nuclear ambitions and authorizing a new round of military strikes following attacks on US ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Arab states condemn Iran attack on UAE as Hormuz tensions rise
stories.summary: Arab states condemned Iranian attacks on the UAE, the first since a truce was signed, calling them a threat to regional security. Gulf partners urged de-escalation and a return to meaningful diplomatic negotiations.

stories.title: First Thing: Tensions rise over Hormuz as Trump threatens to blow Iran ‘off the face of the earth’
stories.summary: The United States launched "Project Freedom" to reopen a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, where more than 800 vessels and roughly 20,000 crew members remain stranded. US Central Command said two US-flagged merchant ships successfully transited the strait, though Iran denied the claim, escalating tensions in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Liberia: PUL Sounds Alarm On Press Freedom Violations As Liberia Marks World Press Freedom Day in Kakata
stories.summary: The Press Union of Liberia's president, Julius Kanubah, raised concerns about press freedom violations during World Press Freedom Day events in Kakata. He warned that democratic progress and national development are at risk without full protection of journalists' rights and free expression.

stories.title: Ugandans slam bill as mimicking Russian 'foreign agents' law
stories.summary: Ugandan civil society organisations denounced a proposed bill that would criminalise promoting "interests of a foreigner" and label anyone receiving foreign funds a "foreign agent." At a Monday press conference, critics said the legislation replicates Russia's foreign agents law and is designed to suppress dissent.

stories.title: HSBC profits fall amid $400m fraud-related charge and Iran war
stories.summary: HSBC reported a 4% decline in first-quarter profits, falling to $9.4 billion, after absorbing a $1.3 billion hit tied to the US-Israel war on Iran and fraud in the private credit sector. The London-headquartered bank set aside an additional $300 million to cover Middle East conflict effects, while revenue rose 6% to $18.6 billion.

stories.title: UAE says oil facility hit by Iranian drone strike as attacks resume
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates said Iran struck a key oil facility with a drone on Monday, marking the first attack since a fragile ceasefire began in early April. The UAE Defense Ministry reported that Iran also launched four cruise missiles, three of which were intercepted and one of which fell into the sea.

stories.title: Indonesia caps ride-hailing commission fees at 8% in ‘radical correction’ of sector
stories.summary: Indonesia announced it has acquired stakes in ride-hailing companies and capped commission fees at 8% under President Prabowo Subianto's reforms. The measures aim to increase driver earnings on platforms like Gojek and Grab in one of Southeast Asia's largest gig economies.

stories.title: Liberia: Communities Elated Over Reported Oil Discovery
stories.summary: Residents of Beon and nearby towns in Grand Bassa County, Liberia, reported discovering a thick, black substance floating on a local river in November, which many believe to be crude oil. The reported find has generated significant excitement in the communities.

stories.title: 'The highest tensions have been' as US, Iran trade fire in Hormuz
stories.summary: The US military fired on Iranian forces and sank six small boats targeting civilian ships as it moved to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. The UAE simultaneously reported its first Iranian attack since the early April ceasefire. A France 24 correspondent in Tehran described tensions as the highest since the ceasefire began.

stories.title: Australia begins hearings into Bondi Beach attack and rising antisemitism
stories.summary: Australia launched Royal Commission hearings examining the Bondi Beach attack and rising antisemitism in the country. One witness testified that their family no longer feels safe or welcome in Australia.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia Denies Expulsion of UAE Ambassador, Warns Against Misinformation
stories.summary: Somalia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs denied reports that the UAE ambassador to Somalia had been expelled. The ministry warned against the spread of misinformation on media and social platforms regarding the diplomatic relationship.

stories.title: Australians are poorer because of war on the other side of the world – Michele Bullock’s logic is hard to fault
stories.summary: Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock warned that a global fuel shock linked to distant conflict is driving higher prices, lower growth, and stagnant real wages in Australia. The RBA announced a third interest rate hike amid forecasts of prolonged economic pressure rather than outright recession.

stories.title: Israel to extend detention of Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: Israel is seeking a six-day extension of detention for Gaza flotilla activists, including Spanish activist Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila, held in Ashkelon. A hearing is scheduled at Ashkelon court after an initial two-day extension was approved.

stories.title: Russia sentences 2 hypersonic researchers to 12.5 years in prison on treason charges, Kommersant reports
stories.summary: A court in Novosibirsk sentenced Russian hypersonic technology researchers Valery Zvegintsev and Vladislav Galkin to 12.5 years in prison each on treason charges, according to the newspaper Kommersant. The closed-door trial had been ongoing since 2024.

stories.title: Invaders attack railway infrastructure in three regions; damage reported
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked railway infrastructure in Ukraine's Kharkiv, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk regions using drones, damaging a train and railcars.

stories.title: Nine coal miners die in gas explosion in Colombia
stories.summary: Nine coal miners were killed in a gas explosion in Sutatausa, Colombia. The locality was also the site of another deadly mining disaster in 2023.

stories.title: Flotilla members recount harrowing details of Israeli detention
stories.summary: Participants in a Gaza-bound humanitarian flotilla described harrowing conditions during Israeli detention after their interception in international waters. Detainees reported injuries and said they were held without passports or phones.

stories.title: France’s Macron sings 'La Bohème' with the Armenian President
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron joined Armenian President Vahagn Khachaturyan in an impromptu performance of Charles Aznavour's "La Bohème" during a state dinner in Yerevan on Monday. Macron was concluding a state visit to Armenia.

stories.title: 'Super El Nino' raises fears for Asia reeling from Middle East conflict
stories.summary: The United Nations' World Meteorological Organization warned that strong El Niño conditions could develop between May and July, potentially reaching "Super El Niño" intensity. Analysts said the phenomenon could spike energy demand, reduce hydropower capacity, and damage crops across Asia, compounding existing economic stress from the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Vijay: From Tamil Nadu's biggest film star to Indian political leader
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP celebrated a state election victory in West Bengal, while Tamil film star Vijay won the Tamil Nadu state election with his newly formed political party. Indian media widely covered both results as significant shifts in regional politics.

stories.title: Can Indiana lawmakers win after defying the president’s vote?
stories.summary: Seven Republican state senators in Indiana face re-election challenges from Donald Trump-backed candidates after defying the president's push to redraw congressional districts. The primary vote is being viewed as a statewide referendum on political retribution within the Republican Party.

stories.title: Can South Korea’s most advanced fighter, the KF-21, compete with China, the US and Europe?
stories.summary: South Korea's Korea Aerospace Industries officially rolled out the first production unit of the KF-21 Boramae supersonic fighter jet, making South Korea the eighth country to indigenously develop advanced combat aircraft. Analysts say the KF-21 still faces significant challenges competing globally against US, European, and Chinese alternatives.

stories.title: 4 years after lockdown, Shanghai’s expat community is recovering – and changing
stories.summary: Four years after Shanghai's strict COVID-19 lockdown, the city's expatriate community is gradually recovering but with a notably different demographic profile. International presence is returning to neighborhoods like the former French Concession, though the composition of foreign residents has shifted.

stories.title: ‘Female Knights’: China mums reshape food delivery services by juggling freedom and family
stories.summary: On Qushan Island in Zhejiang province, China, a group of mothers known as the "Female Knights" has turned food delivery work into a source of financial independence. The women balance family responsibilities with delivery jobs on the small island, where most men work at sea or in urban areas.

stories.title: Golders Green attacks: A Muslim was also stabbed - not that you'd know
stories.summary: A stabbing attack in Golders Green, London, also injured a Muslim victim named Ishmail Hussein. Reports highlighted concerns that British media coverage largely omitted details about the Muslim victim.

stories.title: Romania: Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan faces confidence vote in parliament after largest party, PSD, quit his coalition
stories.summary: Romanian Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan faces a parliamentary confidence vote after the Social Democrats, the largest party, quit his coalition government. The coalition fractured over unpopular austerity measures championed by Bolojan's administration.

stories.title: Nine killed in Colombia mine explosion: government
stories.summary: Nine workers were killed and six injured in a coal mine explosion in Colombia's Cundinamarca province. The national mining agency said the blast was caused by a buildup of gases, weeks after it had issued risk control recommendations for the site.

stories.title: Finding yourself in the quiet: A stay at Cyprus's Anassa resort - review
stories.summary: A travel review highlighted the Anassa resort in Cyprus, located 50 minutes from Paphos airport, as a retreat offering tranquility following months of regional conflict and instability.

stories.title: Sweden to form new spy agency in Ukraine war reset
stories.summary: Sweden announced plans to establish a new foreign intelligence agency called UND, set to begin operations in January 2027. Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard said the move was prompted by security concerns arising from Russia's war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Starmer calls antisemitism ‘crisis for all of us’ ahead of Downing Street summit – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer hosted an antisemitism summit at Downing Street, calling rising antisemitism a "crisis for all of us" following an attack in Golders Green, London. He announced that universities will be required to publish data on antisemitism on their campuses and outlined £7 million in funding to tackle the issue.

stories.title: Two men injured in Chernihiv region due to Russian shelling
stories.summary: Two men were injured in Ukraine's Chernihiv region as a result of Russian shelling.

stories.title: Russia launches attacks on Ukraine energy infrastructure amid truce talks – Europe live
stories.summary: Russia launched missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure amid ongoing truce discussions. Mobile internet services were cut in parts of Russia, including Moscow, ahead of the May 9 Victory Parade due to security concerns about Ukrainian drone attacks. President Zelenskyy said Russia could stop the war by ceasing fire.

stories.title: ‘You just can’t get the air in’: How hantavirus turns deadly
stories.summary: Health experts warn that hantavirus infections can become fatal rapidly, with patients in the severe phase potentially dying within 24 to 48 hours. The virus currently has no specific cure or targeted treatment available.

stories.title: Crooning diplomacy: France, Armenia leaders unite over shared icon Charles Aznavour
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron performed a song by the late Charles Aznavour during a state dinner with Armenian leaders in Paris. Aznavour, born in France to Armenian immigrants, is a revered cultural figure in both countries.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down one ballistic missile and 149 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces shot down one ballistic missile and 149 drones launched by Russian forces since the evening of May 4.

stories.title: Macron sings as Armenia’s leader drums in unusual moment at state dinner
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron sang 'La Bohème' while Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan played drums during a state dinner, creating an unusual diplomatic moment between the two leaders.

stories.title: 'No pilgrims': Regional war hushes Iraq's worship tourism
stories.summary: In Najaf, Iraq, the shrine of Imam Ali has seen a sharp decline in pilgrims due to the wider Middle East conflict. Shopkeepers and hotel owners near the holy site report significantly reduced business as worship tourism has largely ceased.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: ‘We have not even begun’, Iran warns US amid escalation in strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran warned the United States that it had "not even begun" amid escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, where President Trump dispatched warships to break an Iranian blockade. Iran blamed U.S. military actions for a drone strike on a UAE energy installation in Fujairah, denying any pre-planned attack on oil facilities.

stories.title: 21 killed, 61 injured in massive explosion at fireworks factory in China
stories.summary: An explosion at a fireworks factory in China's Hunan province killed at least 21 people and injured 61 others. Nearly 500 rescuers were deployed to the scene and evacuations were conducted in surrounding danger zones.

stories.title: High Court allows Bazan to build new power plant after old one damaged by Iran
stories.summary: Israel's High Court approved Bazan oil refinery's construction of a new power plant after its previous facility was damaged by Iranian attacks. However, judges noted the refinery must eventually close in accordance with a government decision.

stories.title: Russian air attacks kill five at Ukraine’s Naftogaz gas facilities
stories.summary: Russian air strikes targeted Naftogaz gas facilities in Ukraine, killing three workers and two emergency service rescuers. Naftogaz CEO Serhiy Koretskyi reported that 37 others were wounded in the attacks.

stories.title: First Russian oil arrives in Japan since Iran war: media
stories.summary: Japan received its first shipment of Russian oil since the outbreak of the Iran war, which saw Tehran effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz. Japan, which depends on West Asia for approximately 95% of its oil imports, has been seeking to diversify its energy procurement sources.

stories.title: Controversial report calls for cuts, mergers for French public broadcasters
stories.summary: A French government-commissioned report proposed a major overhaul of public broadcasting, including merging channels and cutting costs. Critics warned the plan could weaken public service media, making the proposals highly controversial.

stories.title: Thousands march in DR Congo capital in support of US sanctions against Kabila
stories.summary: Thousands of people marched in Kinshasa, DR Congo, in support of U.S. sanctions imposed on former President Joseph Kabila. Washington blacklisted Kabila for allegedly supporting the Rwanda-backed M23/AFC rebels fighting in eastern Congo.

stories.title: Pakistanis 'should not have children': Racism row rocks Norway
stories.summary: A Norwegian right-wing party faced backlash after an adviser stated that Pakistanis "should not have children." The remarks exposed underlying tensions over race and immigration policy in Norway.

stories.title: Evacuations planned as suspected hantavirus outbreak traps 150 on cruise ship
stories.summary: Medical teams worked to evacuate two people with suspected hantavirus symptoms from the luxury cruise ship held off Cape Verde, where approximately 150 passengers and crew remain stranded. The vessel has been refused permission to dock due to the suspected outbreak.

stories.title: UAE air defences 'actively engaging' Iran missiles, drones
stories.summary: The UAE reported that Iranian missile and drone attacks targeted the country for a second consecutive day as tensions over the Strait of Hormuz continue to escalate.

stories.title: Hormuz tensions threaten US-Iran truce as UAE reports attacks
stories.summary: A series of attacks involving the US, Iran, and Gulf states in and around the Strait of Hormuz have threatened the fragile ceasefire between Tehran and Washington. The latest incidents raised concerns about a broader regional escalation.

stories.title: Armenia hosts historic EU summit as it charts path away from Russia
stories.summary: Armenia hosted its first bilateral summit with the European Union on Tuesday in Yerevan, formally declaring its ambition to join the bloc. The landmark diplomatic event reflects Armenia's cautious shift away from longtime ally Russia.

stories.title: Nigeria: How Opposition Party Realignment Could Shape 2027
stories.summary: Nigerian opposition parties held a summit in Ibadan and pledged to field a single candidate against President Tinubu in the 2027 elections. However, deep divisions quickly emerged over presidential zoning and ticket preferences, including debates between an Obi/Kwankwaso ticket and an Atiku-led option.

stories.title: War with Iran threatens to reignite as Trump launches 'Project Freedom'
stories.summary: The ceasefire between the United States and Iran was on the verge of collapse on Monday as the two countries exchanged fire over the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump announced "Project Freedom," a naval operation to escort trapped vessels through the strait.

stories.title: “Anyone who tries to break through, we will shoot” — a Ukrainian sailor describes two months at anchor in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A Ukrainian chief mate reports being stranded for two months near the Strait of Hormuz, facing a $2 million passage toll, $13,000 water deliveries, and warnings from Iranian authorities over VHF radio.

stories.title: ‘Group is a lifesaver’: strangers buy Wetherspoon’s meals for homeless people through app
stories.summary: A WhatsApp group in the UK has facilitated the purchase of tens of thousands of Wetherspoon's meals for homeless people through the pub chain's ordering app. The initiative connects donors with people in need via a Facebook page.

stories.title: Truce under threat as Iran, US trade fire in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The U.S. military destroyed six Iranian small boats, cruise missiles, and drones in the Strait of Hormuz after President Trump ordered the navy to escort stranded tankers through the waterway in an operation called "Project Freedom." The exchange of attacks between the U.S. and Iran has put the fragile Middle East truce in jeopardy.

stories.title: Remains of US airman missing since second world war laid to rest in Florida
stories.summary: The remains of U.S. Navy airman Robert Cyr Jr., who went missing on January 22, 1944, after his seaplane crashed in the Segond Channel in what is now Vanuatu, were recovered and identified through DNA analysis. His family recently laid him to rest in Clearwater, Florida.

stories.title: Hong Kong posts strongest quarterly economic growth in almost 5 years at 5.9%
stories.summary: Hong Kong's economy grew 5.9 percent in the first quarter, its strongest quarterly performance in nearly five years. The growth was driven by private consumption and government spending, outpacing the 4 percent rise recorded in the previous quarter.

stories.title: Takaichi signs Australia deals to boost Japan’s energy security
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi signed agreements with Australia to strengthen cooperation on critical minerals, defence, and energy security during a meeting in Canberra. The deals aim to counter China's dominance in rare earths and address fuel-supply disruptions caused by the Iran war.

stories.title: Russian missiles and drones attack Poltava region, leaving four killed, 31 injured
stories.summary: Russian missiles and drones struck the Poltava region of Ukraine on the night of May 5, damaging an industrial facility and railway infrastructure. Four people were killed and 31 others were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Drones target Khartoum airport, Sudan alleges Ethiopian involvement
stories.summary: A drone launched by Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces targeted Khartoum's airport but was shot down before impact. Sudanese officials accused Ethiopia of involvement in the attack.

stories.title: Kenya: Senate Debates Withdrawal of Former President Kenyatta's Benefits
stories.summary: Kenya's Senate is debating a motion by Nandi Senator Samson Cherargei to strip former President Uhuru Kenyatta of his retirement benefits. The controversial plan is expected to generate intensified exchanges among legislators in Nairobi.

stories.title: When drones dominate the battlefield, distance no longer matters - opinion
stories.summary: Recent weeks of conflict have underscored that the Israeli military was not fully prepared for the rapid evolution of drone warfare. The threat has appeared across multiple arenas, but its scale and aggressiveness have intensified significantly.

stories.title: Taiwan has ‘right to engage with the world’ after Eswatini visit
stories.summary: Following a visit to Eswatini, one of its few remaining diplomatic allies, Taiwan asserted its right to engage with the international community. The visit underscored Taipei's efforts to maintain its diplomatic presence globally.

stories.title: Russia will be combat-ready again by 2027 — Estonia’s military chief sets a two-year clock for NATO
stories.summary: Estonia's defense forces commander Andrus Merilo has warned that Russia will regain full combat readiness by 2027, outlining five areas where Estonia and NATO must prepare for potential conflict.

stories.title: US Army fires Tomahawk missile from new Typhon launcher during Philippines drill
stories.summary: The U.S. Army fired a Tomahawk cruise missile from its new Typhon ground-based launcher during a military exercise in the Philippines. A military official described the missile as highly precise, capable of hitting a specific window from a great distance.

stories.title: IAEA says drone damaged equipment at Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant in Ukraine
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency reported on Monday that a drone damaged meteorological monitoring equipment at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine. The facility is currently under Russian control. The IAEA has maintained a monitoring presence at the site.

stories.title: NBA semifinal series: Timberwolves stun Spurs in Game 1; Knicks beat 76ers
stories.summary: Anthony Edwards returned from injury and scored 18 points as the Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the San Antonio Spurs 104-102 in Game 1 of their NBA semifinal series. In another semifinal, the New York Knicks beat the Philadelphia 76ers.

stories.title: Requiem for Stalin’s spirit
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on the enduring ideological influence of Joseph Stalin, referencing recent events including King Charles's White House visit, political developments in India and Iran, and the Mujahideen-i-Khalq's alignment with Israel against Tehran.

stories.title: War update: 149 combat clashes over past day, with heaviest fighting in Huliaipole and Pokrovsk directions
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense forces recorded 149 combat clashes with Russian troops along the front line on May 4, with the heaviest fighting occurring in the Huliaipole and Pokrovsk directions.

stories.title: Japan army unit’s gun-toting AI-generated elephant logo gets trampled by critics
stories.summary: Japan's 1st Infantry Regiment withdrew an AI-designed unit patch featuring a helmeted, gun-wielding elephant after public criticism that the image was aggressive and inconsistent with the Self-Defence Forces' public image. The patch, unveiled on April 29, also depicted chains and a human skull.

stories.title: Explosion at fireworks factory in China kills at least 26
stories.summary: An explosion at a fireworks factory operated by Huasheng Fireworks Manufacturing and Display Co. in Liuyang, Hunan province, killed at least 26 people and injured 61 on Monday. Authorities ordered all other fireworks manufacturers in Liuyang, which produces about 60 percent of China's fireworks, to halt production.

stories.title: 12 trapped after central Colombia mine explosion
stories.summary: An explosion at a mine in central Colombia trapped 12 workers underground. Of the 15 miners present at the time of the blast, three managed to escape. Rescue operations are underway.

stories.title: Ukraine jails European ex-instructor for 8.5 years after FSB recruited him through pro-Kremlin forums
stories.summary: Ukraine has sentenced a European former military instructor to 8.5 years in prison after Russia's FSB recruited him through pro-Kremlin online forums to spy on training centers and plan terror attacks.

stories.title: Thailand scraps 25-year-old agreement with Cambodia on joint energy exploration
stories.summary: Thai Prime Minister announced on Tuesday that the cabinet cancelled a 2001 agreement with Cambodia on joint offshore energy exploration in disputed areas of the Gulf of Thailand. The 25-year-old pact aimed to develop a framework for jointly exploring hydrocarbons in overlapping claim zones. Cambodia had urged Thailand to maintain the agreement.

stories.title: America builds AI, China uses it. That gap may decide the future
stories.summary: A report from the Stanford Institute for Human-Centred AI indicates that U.S. private investment in artificial intelligence reached over $109 billion in 2024, nearly 12 times China's total. Despite America's lead in research and funding, training and deployment costs are falling rapidly, and China is accelerating its adoption and application of AI technologies.

stories.title: What Iran is saying about attack on UAE
stories.summary: Iran responded to reports of an attack on the United Arab Emirates. The UAE said it intercepted Iranian missiles following a suspected drone strike, though Iran has not officially confirmed involvement.

stories.title: Cabinet minister warns Labour against ‘doomscrolling’ through leaders like the Tories
stories.summary: UK Communities Secretary Steve Reed urged Labour MPs not to move against Prime Minister Keir Starmer following poor May election results, warning the party against "doomscrolling" through leaders as the Conservatives had done. Some MPs have reportedly discussed laying out a timetable for Starmer's departure.

stories.title: Dozens killed, scores injured in explosion at Chinese fireworks factory
stories.summary: An explosion at a fireworks factory in Liuyang, Hunan province, central China, killed 26 people and injured 61. Liuyang is a major global fireworks hub, producing roughly 60 percent of China's domestic supply and 70 percent of its fireworks exports. Authorities ordered nearby manufacturers to halt production.

stories.title: National Guard’s Omega unit downs $100,000 Russian Knyaz Veshchiy Oleg recon drone
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Guard Omega unit destroyed a Russian Knyaz Veshchiy Oleg reconnaissance drone valued at approximately $100,000. It is the fourth such UAV downed in 2026.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks in Kyiv region leave three injured
stories.summary: Three people were injured in the Kyiv region of Ukraine as a result of Russian drone attacks.

stories.title: Malawi fuel crisis deepens as oil shortages spread
stories.summary: Malawi is experiencing a deepening fuel crisis as oil shortages spread across the country. The government has resorted to selling gold reserves to purchase fuel, incurring significant economic costs.

stories.title: Afghanistan accuses Pakistan of killing three civilians in ‘war crime’
stories.summary: Afghanistan accused Pakistan of killing three civilians, calling the incident a war crime. The accusation comes as a fragile ceasefire agreed between the two countries last month faces renewed strain.

stories.title: Energy shock
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz has driven global energy market uncertainty, with the International Energy Agency warning of supply disruptions and weakening demand. Rising oil prices and volatility are constraining economic activity, particularly in energy-dependent nations.

stories.title: Alan Jones claims invalid warrants, police impropriety and ‘willy-nilly’ search in sex abuse investigation
stories.summary: Lawyers for former Australian broadcaster Alan Jones, 85, alleged that New South Wales police used invalid warrants and engaged in impropriety during a raid on his Sydney home in November 2024. The search was part of an eight-month investigation into reports of historical sexual abuse.

stories.title: As summer approaches, skin diseases spread through Gaza’s refugee camps
stories.summary: Healthcare workers in Gaza's refugee camps are contending with a surge of skin diseases as summer temperatures rise. Overcrowded conditions in the camps have exacerbated the spread of skin conditions among displaced populations.

stories.title: Acquisition Reform Needs Its Own Wargame
stories.summary: The Pentagon's FY2027 budget requests 785 Tomahawk cruise missiles, a dramatic increase from the 55 funded by Congress in 2025. The article argues this surge reflects acquisition decisions not stress-tested against a scenario involving sustained operations against Iran while maintaining deterrence against China.

stories.title: Chasing L5: WeRide CEO sees ‘ChatGPT moment’ in driverless cars within 10 years
stories.summary: WeRide CEO Tony Han Xu predicted that fully autonomous Level 5 vehicles could arrive on streets by 2035. Chinese regulators recently scaled back new autonomous driving licence approvals after a March 31 system failure involving Baidu's Apollo Go fleet in Wuhan left passengers stranded and disrupted traffic.

stories.title: Ni hao, new hire: Africa’s growing Mandarin job boom
stories.summary: Growing Chinese commercial investment across Africa is driving demand for Mandarin-speaking local workers. Smaller Chinese companies increasingly prefer hiring locally rather than bringing staff from China, while African firms involved in bilateral trade also seek Mandarin speakers. Few Chinese executives working in Africa are proficient in local languages.

stories.title: 'We need people to come back': Dubai's tourism industry reels as foreigners flee
stories.summary: Dubai's tourism industry has suffered significant losses as foreigners flee amid the war on Iran. Hotels and local businesses along Dubai's coast have been severely impacted by the decline in visitors.

stories.title: Russia loses 970 troops, four air defense systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces lost approximately 970 troops in a single day of fighting in Ukraine, bringing total estimated Russian personnel losses since February 24, 2022, to approximately 1,336,120. Four Russian air defense systems were also destroyed.

stories.title: Russia struck a Poltava gas site overnight — then hit the DSNS rescuers responding to the fire
stories.summary: Russia struck a gas facility in the Poltava region overnight on May 5 using Iskander missiles, then targeted State Emergency Service rescuers responding to the fire. Five people were killed and 37 injured.

stories.title: Divers find wreck of Coast Guard ship torpedoed by Germans, US’ largest naval loss of World War I
stories.summary: Divers discovered the wreck of the USS Tampa, a US Coast Guard cutter torpedoed by a German submarine during World War I. The Tampa's sinking represented the largest US naval loss of personnel in the war.

stories.title: High ambition: Rising star eyes Olympic ascent for Israeli climbing
stories.summary: Israeli sport climber Ayala Kerem, 24, is aiming to represent Israel at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. She believes an Olympic campaign could help raise the profile of competitive climbing in Israel.

stories.title: Armed man shot by US Secret Service near White House; teen bystander wounded
stories.summary: U.S. Secret Service agents shot an armed man near the White House on Monday after he opened fire, also wounding a teenage bystander. The incident occurred shortly after a motorcade carrying Vice President JD Vance passed through the area. Officials said Vance was not believed to be a target.

stories.title: Jefferson Lewis excused from appearing in court over alleged murder of Kumanjayi Little Baby
stories.summary: Jefferson Lewis, 47, was excused from appearing at his first hearing in Alice Springs local court after being charged with the murder of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, who was allegedly abducted from an Alice Springs town camp in the Northern Territory. Lewis also faces two additional charges.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Tensions are escalating across the Middle East, with clashes in the Strait of Hormuz and renewed pressure along the Israel-Lebanon border. The US is advancing a maritime mission with military support while Iran warns of a crushing response to further actions.

stories.title: One suspect in Zelka murder tells cops: ‘Everyone was hitting him, what, should I stop?’
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested 19 suspects in the murder of a 21-year-old pizzeria worker named Zelka. During interrogation, one suspect was confronted with video showing the victim being attacked as he lay on the ground.

stories.title: Cornell’s Jewish president clashes with students following on-campus debate about Israel
stories.summary: Cornell University president Michael Kotlikoff, who is Jewish, was surrounded by student protesters on campus following a debate about Israel. Kotlikoff stated he waited for his backup camera to show a clear path before reversing his vehicle.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Israeli security agencies sound alarm on settlers
stories.summary: Israeli security agencies warned that settler violence in the occupied West Bank threatens state stability. Despite the warnings, attacks on Palestinians, land seizures, and blockades have continued in the territory.

stories.title: Nigerians seek return from South Africa amid xenophobia concerns
stories.summary: Amid rising xenophobia-related violence in South Africa, Nigerians are seeking voluntary return to their home country. South African officials have condemned the violence and pledged action, but anxiety among migrant communities continues to grow.

stories.title: Russians carry out 843 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region in one day, leaving three killed, 11 injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 843 attacks on 49 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over 24 hours, killing three people and injuring 11 in Zaporizhzhia, Vilniansk, and the Zaporizhzhia district.

stories.title: Supreme Court upholds death sentences of Chotu gang members
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court upheld the death sentences of members of the Chotu gang, which operated in the riverine area of Rajanpur, Punjab. A three-judge bench rejected appeals by gang leader Ghulam Rasool alias Chotu and associates Ishaq and Khalid, who were convicted of kidnapping, extortion, robbery, and murder.

stories.title: 10 found dead as Karachi endures ‘hottest day in eight years’
stories.summary: At least 10 people died in Karachi on Monday as temperatures reached 44.1°C, the city's highest recorded temperature since 2018. The Edhi Foundation and Chhipa Welfare Association attributed the deaths to extreme heatwave conditions, compounded by prolonged power outages and water shortages.

stories.title: Israeli military orders evacuations in two Lebanon towns
stories.summary: The Israeli military ordered residents of Jabsheet and Sarafand in southern Lebanon to evacuate immediately, warning them to move at least 1,000 meters from the towns. The displacement orders cited proximity to what Israel described as Hezbollah elements and facilities.

stories.title: Practice Makes Deterrence: India’s Next Nuclear Challenge at Sea
stories.summary: India commissioned its third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, INS Aridhaman, on April 3, 2026, enabling it to maintain continuous at-sea nuclear deterrent patrols. India has also tested the capability to deploy multiple independently targetable warheads from a single missile, potentially enhancing its sea-based nuclear deterrent.

stories.title: Extreme heat prompts nationwide emergency protocols
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority issued sweeping emergency protocols and placed hospitals on alert as extreme above-normal temperatures are expected from May through June. Provincial administrations, health departments, rescue agencies, and armed forces across Pakistan were advised to implement protective guidelines.

stories.title: Deadly hantavirus outbreak traps 150 on cruise ship as WHO identifies more cases
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reported seven hantavirus cases, including two confirmed infections and three deaths, linked to the Dutch-flagged cruise ship MV Hondius off Cabo Verde. The vessel carries 147 passengers and crew from 23 countries. One British passenger is in intensive care in Johannesburg.

stories.title: Report: 15,000 Pakistanis arrested and deported from UAE, savings seized
