stories.title: UDF strikes Russian drone warehouses, air defense systems in occupied territories
stories.summary: On May 3–4, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck Russian drone storage facilities and air defense systems in occupied territories, hitting multiple military targets.

stories.title: Israeli TV Academy Awards present their 2025 prizes, and honor the late Alon Aboutboul
stories.summary: The Israeli TV Academy presented its 2025 awards and honored the late actor Alon Aboutboul. For the first time in two years, the ceremony did not include special categories for crisis and wartime broadcasting.

stories.title: Video: Modi’s BJP poised to take control in India’s West Bengal
stories.summary: India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is positioned to gain control of the West Bengal state government, marking a significant political shift in the region.

stories.title: Opaque nature of US-Iran shadow war: Are they 'dancing their way out of a minefield' toward a deal?
stories.summary: Global defence commentator Peter Apps described U.S.-Iran tensions as a fluid situation where ceasefire negotiations and military escalation are occurring simultaneously. The Strait of Hormuz has emerged as both a critical global shipping chokepoint and a central battleground in the conflict.

stories.title: In world first, Israeli scientists map digital atlas of healthy human liver
stories.summary: Researchers from Israel's Weizmann Institute, Sheba Medical Center, and the Mayo Clinic have created the first digital atlas of a healthy human liver. The study revealed differences between human and mouse livers and may improve treatments for fatty liver disease.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine declare competing ceasefires
stories.summary: Russia declared a unilateral ceasefire on May 9 to coincide with Victory Day, while Ukraine announced its own separate truce for May 5–6. Kyiv dismissed Moscow's gesture, citing the threat posed by Ukrainian drones as a factor behind Russia's move.

stories.title: Australia news live: four Australians among passengers on luxury cruise ship hit by deadly suspected hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius remains off the coast of Cape Verde after a suspected hantavirus outbreak killed three passengers and left three others seriously ill. Four Australians are among nearly 150 people isolating onboard the vessel.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least two in Gaza, Wafa reports
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza on Monday, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. A drone attack hit the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza, while a separate air strike struck southeast of Gaza City. At least 834 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 10 ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: German defence ministry says no 'definitive cancellation' of US weapons deployment
stories.summary: Germany's defence ministry stated on May 4 that the United States had not definitively cancelled a plan, originally devised under former President Joe Biden, to deploy a battalion equipped with long-range Tomahawk missiles to German territory.

stories.title: Russia intensifies drone attacks on ports, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that Russia has dramatically intensified drone attacks on its port infrastructure in 2026, launching more than 800 drones in the first four months of the year. That figure is more than ten times the number used in the same period a year earlier.

stories.title: Assimi Goita appoints himself defence minister
stories.summary: Mali's junta leader Assimi Goïta appointed himself defence minister following the killing of his predecessor amid a wave of attacks in the country. The move consolidates further military and political authority under Goïta's control.

stories.title: US decision not to deploy Tomahawks to Germany was even worse than withdrawal of 5,000 US troops. But Ukraine can help
stories.summary: A commentary argues that the US decision not to deploy Tomahawk missiles to Germany was more damaging than the withdrawal of 5,000 US troops from Europe. It also highlights that three years of full-scale war have made Ukraine's defense industry among the most combat-experienced globally.

stories.title: ADF neutralized 70 of 88 Russian drones since morning
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces neutralized 70 out of 88 Russian drones launched between 08:30 and 18:30 on Monday, May 4. A ballistic missile strike and 14 additional enemy strike UAVs were also recorded.

stories.title: Qatar emir condemns Iran attacks in call with UAE president
stories.summary: Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani condemned Iranian missile and drone attacks on the UAE during a phone call with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed al-Nahyan. The emir said the strikes targeted civilian sites and infrastructure, and Doha expressed solidarity with the Emirates.

stories.title: Moscow rehearses V-Day parade marking WWII victory
stories.summary: Russia rehearsed its annual Victory Day military parade in Moscow commemorating the World War II anniversary and declared a ceasefire with Ukraine to cover the May 9 celebrations.

stories.title: Mysterious world beyond Pluto may have an atmosphere: astronomers
stories.summary: Japanese astronomers have found evidence that a roughly 500-kilometer-wide object beyond Pluto in the Kuiper Belt may possess an atmosphere, which would make it only the second trans-Neptunian object known to have one after Pluto.

stories.title: Ukrainian Ambassador to Israel warns 'Post' about country's 'growing frustration' - interview
stories.summary: Ukrainian Ambassador to Israel Yevgen Korniychuk expressed his country's growing frustration in an interview, stating that Ukraine aims to open criminal proceedings against traders, exporters, and offshore entities that may have enabled sanctions breaches.

stories.title: Feminism play Liberation and first world war novel Angel Down among Pulitzer winners
stories.summary: The Pulitzer Prize for fiction was awarded to Daniel Kraus for "Angel Down," a World War I novel written as a single sentence, while Bess Wohl's "Liberation," about 1970s feminist consciousness-raising groups, won the drama prize. Other winners included works by Jill Lepore on the US Constitution and Brian Goldstone on housing insecurity.

stories.title: India's Modi celebrates 'record' win in opposition-held West Bengal
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party won a decisive victory in West Bengal state elections, wresting the opposition stronghold with at least 124 seats won and leading in 83 others in the 294-member assembly.

stories.title: Senior IDF official: No change in home front rules despite Iran attack on UAE, Oman
stories.summary: A senior IDF official stated that Israel's home front guidelines remain unchanged despite Iranian attacks on the UAE and Oman. The official said Israeli air defense systems and offensive capabilities are maintained at a high level of readiness.

stories.title: 'It's an elite matter': UAE confirms it's in talks for swap line loan with US
stories.summary: The UAE confirmed it is in talks with the United States over a swap line loan arrangement. The announcement came shortly before Iran launched fresh strikes on the UAE, reportedly in retaliation for US military operations in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israeli fintech startup partners with Elon Musk’s X to gauge market sentiment
stories.summary: Israeli fintech company BridgeWise has partnered with Elon Musk's social media platform X to integrate financial conversation data into its AI-powered investment analysis tool. The system will provide sentiment-based analysis across approximately 70,000 securities.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes sports facility in Kharkiv
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv with a drone, hitting a sports facility. No further details on casualties were immediately available.

stories.title: UAE says it intercepted 15 missiles and four drones launched from Iran
stories.summary: The UAE Ministry of Defence announced that its air defense systems intercepted 12 ballistic missiles, three cruise missiles, and four drones launched from Iran on Monday.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian Nobel laureate Mohammadi needs urgent heart treatment in Tehran, says brother
stories.summary: The brother of jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi said she urgently needs heart treatment at a hospital in Tehran. He reported she is suffering from severe headaches, nausea, and chest pain.

stories.title: First Druze party launches ahead of elections, aims for independent representation
stories.summary: A new political party called Alliance of Brothers has launched in Israel ahead of upcoming elections, aiming to unite Druze citizens and provide them with independent political representation. The party seeks to empower the Druze community to influence Israel's public agenda.

stories.title: After Russia unilaterally announced 9 May ceasefire to hold parade, Zelenskyy set Ukraine’s silence regime to start three days earlier
stories.summary: After Russia unilaterally announced a May 9 ceasefire to hold its Victory Day parade, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy set Ukraine's own silence regime to begin three days earlier. Reports indicate Russia's announcement appeared on social media rather than through formal diplomatic channels.

stories.title: Trump threatens to 'blow Iran off face of the Earth' if US vessels attacked
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to "blow Iran off the face of the Earth" if US vessels are attacked, citing upgraded military equipment and ammunition. The remarks came amid escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: EU, PA announce program to support Palestinians facing settler violence in West Bank
stories.summary: The European Union and the Palestinian Authority announced a six-million-euro program to support Palestinians facing settler violence in the West Bank. The initiative focuses on documenting attacks and providing protective presence and equipment to threatened villages.

stories.title: Israel's greatest generations: Gen Zers, millennials who answered the call after Oct. 7 - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlighted the contributions of Israeli Gen Z and millennial generations who mobilized after the October 7 attacks. The article called on Israelis, Jews, and others to help these generations rebuild.

stories.title: UNFPA committed to supporting midwifery education, workforce development in Pakistan
stories.summary: UNFPA reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Pakistan in strengthening midwifery education, workforce development, and health systems, with Representative Dr. Luay Shabaneh issuing the statement in Islamabad to mark International Day of the Midwife on May 5.

stories.title: SA President Rhamaposa becomes first head of state to sign ‘Free Barghouti’ pledge
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa became the first head of state to sign a pledge calling for the release of Marwan Barghouti. Barghouti is a former leader of the Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades, linked to attacks during the Second Intifada.

stories.title: Mali junta chief to take over killed defence minister's role
stories.summary: Mali's junta leader Assimi Goita assumed the additional role of defence minister by decree on Monday, following the killing of the previous minister in large-scale attacks. The move further consolidates military authority under Goita's leadership.

stories.title: Russian forces launch over 50 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region in one day, leaving five injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched over 50 attacks on the Nikopol and Synelnykove districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region in a single day, injuring five people. The strikes targeted civilian areas across the region.

stories.title: Gaza, Hamas, and the pre-Oct. 7 concept sources say Israel is still stuck in - analysis
stories.summary: Sources within Israel's defense establishment are questioning the foundational assumptions of Israel's current strategy toward Hamas for the first time since the October 7 attack, suggesting the country remains trapped in pre-attack strategic thinking.

stories.title: Belarus is building training grounds, transport hubs, and logistical routes — Ukraine says Russia could use them for offensive at any time
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials say Belarus is constructing training grounds, transport hubs, and logistical routes near the Ukrainian border that Russia could use for offensive operations. Kyiv warned the infrastructure could be activated at any moment.

stories.title: Austria expels three Russian diplomats over signals spying
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian diplomats, declaring them personae non gratae, over suspected signals intelligence operations involving satellite dishes installed on Russian diplomatic buildings in Vienna. The Austrian government said the antenna installations could be used for spying.

stories.title: War of words: Trump, Iran trade claims of missile strikes in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The US and Iran traded conflicting claims about military confrontations in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. President Trump announced "Project Freedom" to guide stranded ships through the waterway, while Iran claimed it struck a US frigate with two missiles — a claim Washington denied outright.

stories.title: Russia orders two-day ceasefire in Ukraine war to coincide with Victory Day
stories.summary: Russia ordered a two-day ceasefire on May 8–9 to coincide with Victory Day, marking the 81st anniversary of Nazi Germany's defeat. The Russian Defense Ministry said it expected Ukraine to observe the truce, following an order from President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Mali leader Goita takes defence post after minister killed
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita has appointed himself defence minister after the previous minister was killed in attacks linked to al-Qaeda and Tuareg separatist groups. The move consolidates Goita's control over the country's security apparatus.

stories.title: China consul in Mexico calls protectionism a ‘dead end’ as trade tensions with US escalate
stories.summary: China's Consul General Fu Xinrong in Tijuana, Mexico, denounced protectionism as a dead end, calling for trade relations based on sovereignty and mutual respect. The remarks came weeks before the US, Mexico, and Canada are set to review the USMCA trade agreement amid escalating US-China trade tensions.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia and its allies must curb the growing Israeli-Emirati axis
stories.summary: The article argues that Saudi Arabia and its allies should counter the growing strategic alignment between Israel and the UAE, amid escalating US-Iran tensions and the risk of a wider regional conflict involving the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Lebanon’s most senior Shi’ite politician says no to negotiations with Israel until war stops
stories.summary: Lebanon's parliamentary speaker Nabih Berri, the country's most senior Shi'ite politician, rejected negotiations with Israel until hostilities cease. His comments highlight challenges facing US-led efforts to broker peace between Lebanon and Israel.

stories.title: Missile strike on Merefa: Death toll rises to seven, 14 injured remain in hospitals
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian missile strike on Merefa, Ukraine, rose to seven after a severely wounded man died in hospital. Fourteen other injured individuals remain hospitalized.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF destroys 30-meter-long Hezbollah tunnel in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces destroyed a 30-meter-long Hezbollah tunnel in southern Lebanon. Dozens of explosive devices and anti-tank missiles were found inside the tunnel, along with several weapons storage facilities in the surrounding area.

stories.title: At least 130 Nigerians seek repatriation from South Africa after protests, Abuja says
stories.summary: At least 130 Nigerian citizens in South Africa have requested repatriation from their government following anti-foreigner protests in South Africa. Nigeria's Foreign Minister Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu confirmed the requests from Abuja.

stories.title: Russia offers Ukraine May 8-9 ceasefire amid WWII anniversary, but threatens major reprisals in same breath
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin unilaterally declared a two-day ceasefire on May 8–9 to mark the 81st anniversary of the World War II victory, while Ukrainian President Zelenskyy proposed his own truce starting a couple of days earlier. Both sides issued the proposals independently without coordination.

stories.title: 'America has confirmed everything that Iran has been telling its population', analyst says
stories.summary: Analyst Emma Salisbury of the Foreign Policy Institute told FRANCE 24 that US actions toward Iran have reinforced the Iranian regime's longstanding narrative that America seeks to destroy the country. She argued President Trump has done nothing to counter Tehran's characterization of the US as a hostile power.

stories.title: Russia Lost Ground in Ukraine in April, a First Since Mid-2023 – AFP Analysis
stories.summary: An AFP analysis found that Russia lost ground in Ukraine in April, marking the Ukrainian army's first net territorial gains since mid-2023. The gains were marginal, representing only 0.02 percent of Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Gangland wars killing dozens of bystanders, report Swedish police
stories.summary: Swedish police report that gang-related violence has killed dozens of bystanders, including people struck by stray bullets, victims of mistaken identity, and relatives of gang members targeted in ongoing turf wars across Sweden.

stories.title: UAE moves schools to remote learning as US-Israeli war on Iran threatens to restart
stories.summary: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates ordered all schools to transition to remote learning amid rising regional tensions linked to the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. Officials said the situation would be reassessed on May 8.

stories.title: PSL 11’s highest scorer Babar Azam named captain of the edition’s Team of the Year
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board named Peshawar Zalmi captain Babar Azam to lead the PSL 11 Team of the Year after he finished as the season's highest run-scorer. Peshawar Zalmi won their second PSL title by defeating Hyderabad Kingsmen by five wickets in Lahore.

stories.title: Austria expels three Russian embassy staff on suspicion of spying
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian embassy staff members on suspicion of espionage. The Russian embassy warned there would be a "harsh" response to the expulsions.

stories.title: Pakistani delegation attends US investment summit to expand global footprint
stories.summary: A delegation of 16 Pakistani entrepreneurs and business leaders is attending the SelectUSA Investment Summit in National Harbour, Maryland, seeking opportunities to invest in the United States and expand their global business presence.

stories.title: Iran-US clash over alleged warship attack in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran claims its navy forced a US warship to turn back from the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington denies any clash occurred. The competing accounts highlight escalating tensions over control of the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Effective cross-border payment solutions for IT and software businesses
stories.summary: The article discusses strategies for IT and software businesses to improve cross-border payment processes, emphasizing efficiency and globalization through appropriate solution selection.

stories.title: True Iranian regime change won't occur if the IRGC holds power - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that true regime change in Iran is unlikely as long as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retains power. The author contends that current developments represent a new form of IRGC control rather than genuine transformation.

stories.title: Cabinet ministers warn mutinous MPs over ousting Keir Starmer
stories.summary: Senior UK Labour cabinet ministers have warned backbench MPs against attempting to remove Prime Minister Keir Starmer following poor local election results. Several ministers told the Guardian that while Starmer intends to remain in office, the mood among Labour MPs is volatile and the situation could escalate.

stories.title: Rutte, Zelensky discuss PURL, Ukraine to continue to receive anti-ballistic missiles
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on the sidelines of the 8th European Political Community Summit in Yerevan, Armenia. Rutte confirmed that the PURL program is operational and that anti-ballistic missiles will continue to be supplied to Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukrainian soldier stumbled into a Russian dugout. Two weeks later he walked out with a POW
stories.summary: A wounded Ukrainian corporal spent 14 days unarmed in a Russian dugout alongside an armed Russian soldier. After two weeks, the Russian soldier surrendered and was taken as a prisoner of war.

stories.title: Fujairah oil zone hit by fire after drone attack as UAE says it intercepted Iran missiles
stories.summary: A fire erupted at a major oil industry zone in Fujairah, UAE, after a drone attack originating from Iran. The UAE military separately intercepted three Iranian missiles over its waters, while a fourth missile crashed into the sea.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll rises to 2,696 as Israeli attacks continue
stories.summary: Lebanon's National News Agency reported that the death toll from Israeli attacks since March 2 has reached 2,696, with 8,264 wounded. Israeli air strikes on Monday killed several civilians during intensive raids across towns in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran prevents entry of U.S. warships into Strait of Hormuz, Navy says
stories.summary: Iran's navy announced on May 4 that it had prevented enemy warships from entering the Strait of Hormuz by issuing what it described as a swift and decisive warning, according to Iranian state television. The statement did not name the warships involved.

stories.title: 56% of Russians want Western brands to return after war-driven exodus, survey finds
stories.summary: A survey by Russian research association Gruppa 7/89, conducted in February and March 2026, found that 56% of Russians want Western brands to return after their departure following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, as reported by Vedomosti.

stories.title: Two arrested over Golders Green Iranian memorial wall arson
stories.summary: Two individuals were arrested in connection with an arson attack on an Iranian memorial wall in Golders Green, London. The memorial, which was not damaged by the fire, is dedicated to protesters killed by the Islamic Republic of Iran.

stories.title: Putin threatens 'massive missile strike' on Kyiv if Ukraine breaks two-day truce
stories.summary: Russia's defence ministry threatened a massive missile strike on Kyiv if Ukraine breached a two-day ceasefire declared by President Vladimir Putin. The truce was timed to coincide with World War II commemorations on May 8–9.

stories.title: Fire causes ‘substantial damage’ to Book of Mormon theater in New York
stories.summary: A fire broke out in an electrical room at the Eugene O'Neill Theatre on Broadway in New York, causing substantial damage and forcing the temporary closure of the long-running musical The Book of Mormon. The New York fire department described it as a deep-seated blaze, and the cause remains under investigation.

stories.title: Chloe Zhao, Stellan Skarsgard and Demi Moore among Cannes Film Festival jurors
stories.summary: Filmmaker Chloé Zhao, actress Demi Moore, and actor Stellan Skarsgård have been named among the jurors for the upcoming Cannes Film Festival on the French Riviera. The nine-person jury will award prizes including the Palme d'Or for best film. Organisers announced the selections on Monday.

stories.title: Russian forces strike market, church in Vilniansk, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a market and a church in Vilniansk using drones, killing two people and injuring four others.

stories.title: Trump pleads with South Korea to join US mission to protect Gulf shipping
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump called on South Korea to participate in an international mission to protect shipping routes near Iran. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and General Dan Caine were set to provide further operational details at a Tuesday press conference.

stories.title: Tackling methane emissions key for climate change and energy security: IEA
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency published a report stating that reducing methane emissions is critical for both climate change mitigation and energy security, noting it could help offset the impact of the Iran crisis on global energy supply.

stories.title: Two dead as car ploughs into crowd in Germany's Leipzig
stories.summary: A car drove into a crowd on a street in Leipzig, eastern Germany, on Monday, killing at least two people and injuring several others. The driver was arrested. Germany has experienced multiple car-ramming attacks in recent years, including incidents in Magdeburg, Berlin, and Munich.

stories.title: Oil surges past $115 after reported drone strike on UAE port
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged past $115 per barrel, rising more than five percent, after reports of a drone strike on the port of Fujairah on the UAE's eastern coast. Fujairah serves as a critical oil export point located outside the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Sberbank and T-Bank disable in-app chats between users
stories.summary: Russian banks Sberbank and T-Bank have disabled in-app messaging between users and comments on money transfers, according to the independent Russian outlet Verstka.

stories.title: Mali junta leader names himself defence minister after predecessor killed
stories.summary: Mali's military junta leader appointed himself as defense minister after former Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed during a major offensive by combined jihadist and separatist forces.

stories.title: Support for Iran war among ‘connected’ US Jews falls again, poll finds
stories.summary: A poll found that support for the Iran war among politically connected American Jews has declined further, dropping to 60 percent after President Trump unilaterally announced a ceasefire on April 8. Support had already been falling in the weeks since the conflict began.

stories.title: Europe, Canada pull together in Yerevan in Trump's shadow
stories.summary: European leaders gathered in Yerevan, Armenia, for a European Political Community summit focused on defense independence amid US threats to cut military support. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney attended for the first time as a non-European leader, signaling closer transatlantic cooperation outside US frameworks.

stories.title: Russia names general sanctioned over Bucha killings as new Aerospace Forces commander
stories.summary: Colonel General Alexander Chaiko, who is under EU sanctions over the Bucha killings, has been appointed commander-in-chief of Russia's Aerospace Forces, replacing General Viktor Afzalov, according to RBC.

stories.title: Three Indian citizens wounded in Iranian drone attack on UAE oil facility
stories.summary: Three Indian citizens were wounded in an Iranian drone attack on an oil facility in the UAE. The UAE Defense Ministry said it intercepted three missiles, while a fourth fell into the sea.

stories.title: Career submariner selected to perform duties of under secretary of the Navy
stories.summary: Retired Navy Captain William Toti, a career submariner, has been selected to perform the duties of under secretary of the Navy. He is serving as the Navy's second-highest-ranking civilian.

stories.title: Iran says managing Strait of Hormuz is its ‘legitimate right’
stories.summary: Iranian First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref declared that managing the Strait of Hormuz is Tehran's legitimate right, according to ISNA. He stated Iran is not seeking conflict but would respond forcefully if provoked, as tensions over the vital energy corridor continue.

stories.title: Rapper Kid Cudi fires MIA from tour after ‘offensive’ Republican rant
stories.summary: Rapper Kid Cudi removed British artist MIA from his tour after she was booed during a Dallas concert on May 2 for declaring herself a Republican voter. MIA's on-stage remarks went viral, prompting Cudi to end her participation in the tour.

stories.title: Iran fires 'warning shots' as US Navy says its ships entered Gulf via Hormuz
stories.summary: Tensions flared as the U.S. Navy moved ships through the Strait of Hormuz to guide hundreds of stranded commercial vessels, prompting Iran to fire warning shots and call the action a ceasefire violation. The UAE reported coming under attack for the first time since the early April ceasefire, and a British military monitor said two cargo vessels were ablaze off the UAE coast.

stories.title: Zelensky after meeting with Pashinyan: We restore active dialogue between our countries
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Yerevan on the sidelines of the 8th European Political Community Summit, marking the first visit by a Ukrainian president to Armenia in 24 years.

stories.title: Poking the bear? Armenia welcomes European leaders in Russia's backyard
stories.summary: Armenia hosted two back-to-back summits featuring European leaders and regional players, including a first-ever EU leaders' gathering in Yerevan. The European Political Community meeting also included Ukraine, NATO members such as the UK and Norway, and Canada. The events took place against a backdrop of U.S. troop drawdown plans for Germany and fresh tariff disputes.

stories.title: Firewalls won’t protect GEOINT companies. Cyber resilience will, if we act now.
stories.summary: Norman Laudermilch argues that geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) companies need to adopt cyber-resilience models that allow continued operations during attacks, rather than relying solely on traditional firewalls. He warns that cyberattacks are increasingly designed to disrupt operations, not just steal data.

stories.title: NYC Jews targeted in 60% of hate crimes last month; swastika sprayed on synagogue
stories.summary: The NYPD reported 30 confirmed anti-Jewish hate crime incidents in New York City during April, comprising roughly 60 percent of all hate crimes that month. A swastika was sprayed on a synagogue, and Nazi graffiti was found on a Kristallnacht memorial and Jewish homes in Queens.

stories.title: Germany positions navy for possible Strait of Hormuz deployment: Report
stories.summary: Germany is repositioning naval assets toward the Middle East in preparation for a possible Strait of Hormuz deployment. The minesweeper Fulda has departed Kiel, and the support vessel Mosel in the Aegean Sea is being readied. Berlin said any mission would require a ceasefire, legal mandate, and parliamentary approval.

stories.title: US destroys six Iranian small boats, shoots down missiles, drones, admiral says
stories.summary: US Admiral Brad Cooper announced that American forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and shot down Iranian missiles and drones in the Strait of Hormuz. Cooper said Iran was attempting to interfere with a US military operation to reopen the waterway to commercial shipping.

stories.title: Israel ramps up raids and incursions across southern Syria
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out the second-highest number of military violations in southern Syria in April, including raids, incursions, and the establishment of checkpoints. The operations represent a continued pattern of Israeli military activity across Syria's southern border region.

stories.title: Russian missile attack kills five in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian missile attack on the town of Merefa in Ukraine's northeastern Kharkiv region killed five people and wounded several others on May 4, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: UAE condemns Iran attacks, warns it reserves right to respond
stories.summary: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned Iranian missile and drone strikes, calling them a dangerous escalation and describing the attacks as treacherous. Officials warned that the UAE reserves its full and legitimate right to respond, citing a direct threat to national security.

stories.title: Shin Bet quietly reverses ban on Urich accessing Prime Minister’s Office – report
stories.summary: Israel's Shin Bet security agency reportedly reversed its ban on Eli Urich, a key aide to Prime Minister Netanyahu and suspect in several police investigations, granting him renewed access to the Prime Minister's Office after discussions with a senior PMO official.

stories.title: Zelensky, Costa discuss swift opening of all negotiation clusters
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky met European Council President António Costa and said Ukraine expects all six EU accession negotiation clusters to be opened within the current and following month.

stories.title: US says it destroyed Iranian boats, Iran denies naval losses
stories.summary: The United States said its forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and intercepted cruise missiles and drones during operations to secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran denied any naval losses, with state television quoting a military official directly contradicting the US account.

stories.title: Iran foreign ministry says US must ‘abandon its excessive demands’
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry called on the United States to abandon what it described as excessive demands. The statement came as President Donald Trump said Washington would begin escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Finnish parliament strikes down initiative aimed at restricting weapons purchases from Israel
stories.summary: Finland's parliament rejected a citizens' initiative that sought to restrict weapons purchases from Israel. Finland has placed orders exceeding 800 million euros for Israeli weapons, including the David's Sling air defense system purchased in 2023 for 316 million euros.

stories.title: HRCP highlights severe contraction of civic space, erosion of judicial independence in 2025
stories.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan launched its 2025 annual report in Islamabad, documenting severe contraction of civic space and erosion of judicial independence. HRCP Chairperson Asad Iqbal Butt said human rights in Pakistan were in their worst state.

stories.title: Outgoing Indian envoy meets Bangladesh FM, discusses bilateral ties
stories.summary: India's outgoing envoy Verma met with Bangladesh's foreign minister to discuss bilateral ties. Verma reaffirmed India's commitment to strengthening people-centric cooperation with Bangladesh across all sectors.

stories.title: Senate Republicans prepare Iran authorisation bill: Report
stories.summary: A group of Senate Republicans is drafting an authorization for the use of military force against Iran, according to Semafor. The effort is proceeding behind closed doors as lawmakers anticipate possible renewed hostilities following President Trump's comments that the initial phase of conflict has ended.

stories.title: Former Qatari aircraft on track for summer Air Force One delivery
stories.summary: A former Qatari aircraft being modified under the Boeing VC-25B Bridge program is on track for delivery as Air Force One by summer. The plane has completed modifications and flight testing and is currently being painted in red, white, and blue livery.

stories.title: Iran drone hits UAE oil hub as Trump deploys navy to Hormuz
stories.summary: An Iranian drone struck a UAE oil facility, causing oil prices to surge. The attack came hours after President Trump deployed US warships to the Strait of Hormuz in an effort to weaken Iran's control over the strategic waterway.

stories.title: UAE quits OPEC: What next for oil, the Gulf, and geopolitics?
stories.summary: The UAE announced its departure from OPEC, a move with significant implications for global oil markets. The exit reflects a broader geopolitical shift and an intensifying rivalry between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over energy policy and regional influence.

stories.title: US’ Bessent urges China to help open Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged China to use its diplomatic leverage to pressure Iran into reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking on Fox News, Bessent noted that China purchases roughly 90 percent of Iran's energy exports. He also asserted that the United States maintains absolute control over the strategic waterway.

stories.title: War update: 59 combat clashes since morning
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces reported 59 combat engagements with Russian troops since the start of the day, with the heaviest Russian activity concentrated on the Huliaipole, Pokrovsk, and Kostiantynivka sectors.

stories.title: Attacks on Belgorod Region Leave At Least 1 Dead, Multiple Wounded
stories.summary: Attacks on Russia's Belgorod region killed at least one person and wounded others. Meanwhile, Russian strikes against Ukraine on the same day killed at least seven people and injured dozens.

stories.title: Flights to Dubai and Sharjah diverted amid Iranian drone and missile attacks
stories.summary: Flights bound for Dubai and Sharjah in the UAE were held or diverted due to Iranian drone and missile attacks disrupting regional airspace, according to Flightradar24. Multiple aircraft experienced delays as the escalation affected flight paths across the area.

stories.title: Sweden arrests Chinese captain of suspected Russia-linked vessel
stories.summary: Swedish authorities arrested the Chinese captain of a seized oil tanker suspected of having Russian links. The captain faces allegations of carrying false documents and violating seaworthiness laws, according to a Swedish prosecutor.

stories.title: Italy probes detention by Israel of Gaza flotilla activists aboard Italian-flagged vessel
stories.summary: Italian prosecutors opened an unlawful detention investigation after Israeli forces raided a Gaza-bound aid flotilla involving an Italian-flagged vessel. Spanish citizen Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila were detained and taken to Israel for questioning.

stories.title: Russia and “those sympathetic to it” will try to force Ukraine into capitulation this summer – source in Ukraine’s presidential circle
stories.summary: A source in Ukraine's presidential circle warned that Russia and its sympathizers will attempt to force Ukraine into capitulation during the summer. Russia is demanding control over the Donbas region, where approximately 200,000 civilians still reside.

stories.title: Fatal 2022 China Eastern Airlines plane crash points to deliberate fuel cut-off
stories.summary: Newly released findings from the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board indicate that fuel supply levers on the China Eastern Airlines jet that crashed in 2022 were switched off mid-flight. All 132 people on board were killed when the plane struck a hillside. The evidence supports the theory that the crash was deliberate; China has not yet issued a final report.

stories.title: Iraqi court sentences 4 to prison for promoting Baath Party
stories.summary: An Iraqi court sentenced four individuals to prison for promoting the Baath Party, which was outlawed after the fall of Saddam Hussein. Iraq's de-Baathification policy continues, and while convictions remain rare, investigations still lead to the disqualification of political candidates.

stories.title: Clashes erupt in Suweida between Syrian forces and Druze militia
stories.summary: Armed clashes erupted in Suweida, southern Syria, between Syrian government security forces and a local Druze militia. The fighting marks a renewed escalation in the area's fragile security situation.

stories.title: Death toll from strike on Merefa rises to six, 31 injured
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on Merefa in the Kharkiv region has risen to six, with 31 people injured.

stories.title: Iran executes three men over involvement in anti-govt protests
stories.summary: Iran executed three men convicted of involvement in anti-government protests that erupted across the country in December and January.

stories.title: Israeli doctors use 3D printer to lengthen woman’s leg for vanishing bone disease
stories.summary: Surgeons at Hadassah Medical Center in Israel used a 3D printer to lengthen a woman's leg by eight centimeters in the country's first such procedure. The patient suffered from Gorham-Stout disease, a rare condition that causes bone tissue to disintegrate.

stories.title: Narendra Modi’s BJP win election in West Bengal for first time
stories.summary: Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won assembly elections in West Bengal for the first time, defeating opposition forces in a state that had been a rare stronghold against Modi's party. The result further consolidates BJP's dominance across India's political landscape.

stories.title: Navy F/A-18Gs over Iran, Venezuela show rise in aerial electronic attack
stories.summary: US Navy F/A-18G Growler electronic warfare aircraft have been deployed over Iran and Venezuela, signaling an increase in aerial electronic attack operations. The missions highlight the expanding role of the Navy's jamming capabilities.

stories.title: Page of Theodore Roosevelt speech hit by bullet in 1912 assassination attempt uncovered
stories.summary: A presidential historian in Pennsylvania has uncovered the first page of a manuscript that helped save Theodore Roosevelt's life during a 1912 assassination attempt. The thick document, carried in Roosevelt's breast pocket, slowed a bullet that struck him while he was campaigning for another presidential term. The signed page had not been seen publicly in over a century.

stories.title: Atmosphere spotted on celestial body in far reaches of solar system
stories.summary: Astronomers detected an atmosphere on a trans-Neptunian object designated (612533) 2002 XV93, an icy body approximately 500 kilometers across in the far reaches of the solar system. The atmosphere is over five million times thinner than Earth's.

stories.title: Oil surges as Strait of Hormuz tensions escalate after UAE drone strike
stories.summary: Oil prices surged sharply following a reported drone strike on a UAE energy facility amid rising Strait of Hormuz tensions. Brent crude rose over 5 percent to $113.78 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate climbed 3.1 percent to $105.11.

stories.title: UAE says missile and drone strikes launched from Iran
stories.summary: The UAE defense ministry reported that four cruise missiles were launched from Iran, and a drone attack caused a fire at an energy facility in Fujairah. The strikes targeted infrastructure near the Strait of Hormuz, a critical corridor for global oil shipments.

stories.title: Missiles fired at U.S. frigate in Strait of Hormuz, claims Iranian media
stories.summary: Iranian media claimed missiles were fired at a U.S. frigate in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran asserted it had forced a U.S. warship to turn back. U.S. Central Command stated on May 4 that no U.S. Navy ships had been struck.

stories.title: All mainstream Norwegian Jewish organizations condemn Holocaust Center for Holocaust revitalization
stories.summary: An open letter to the HL Center stresses that the Holocaust represents "an industrial, ideologically driven genocide whose aim was the total extermination of the Jewish people."

stories.title: Putin Replaces Aerospace Commander With EU-Sanctioned General Amid Drone Surge, Reports Say
stories.summary: Russia replaced Aerospace Forces commander General Viktor Afzalov with Colonel General Alexander Chaiko, who is under EU sanctions, according to RBC and the pro-war Telegram channel Fighterbomber.

stories.title: Opinion: 'How Pakistan became the ultimate peacemaker between the US and Iran'
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses Pakistan's role as a mediator between the United States and Iran following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. The strikes, conducted without UN Security Council authorization, raised concerns about international law violations and global economic harm.

stories.title: India's Modi eyes important win in opposition-held West Bengal
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP appeared poised for victory in West Bengal state elections as votes were counted under tight security. The state of 100 million people is one of several opposition-held territories where the BJP sought to expand its presence.

stories.title: This Mysterious Occult Healer Is Behind Some of Russia’s Biggest Wartime Protests
stories.summary: Svetlana Lada-Rus, described as a mysterious occult healer in Russia, has emerged as a figure behind some of the country's largest wartime protests against President Putin's government.

stories.title: Three Russian diplomats expelled from Austria over spying accusations
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian diplomats over accusations of espionage. The foreign minister said the diplomats gathered intelligence using a network of antennas installed atop Russian diplomatic buildings in Austria.

stories.title: Nepal lodges protest against India over long-running border dispute
stories.summary: Nepal formally protested to India after India and China reached an agreement to resume a religious pilgrimage through a disputed Himalayan mountain pass, reigniting a long-standing border dispute between Nepal and India.

stories.title: Italy probes ‘abduction’ after Israel intercepts Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Italian prosecutors in Rome opened an abduction investigation after Israeli forces intercepted 22 boats from the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters near Crete. Israel detained 175 activists; most were released, but Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila were taken into custody in Ashkelon.

stories.title: Here is how you can protect yourself from extreme heat
stories.summary: Karachi, Pakistan, experienced temperatures reaching 44°C on Monday, with the Pakistan Meteorological Department warning that very hot and dry conditions will persist across southern Pakistan. The May outlook indicates above-normal temperatures nationwide with potential for heat spikes.

stories.title: UAE to get 10 C-390 aircraft, up to 10 more in the future
stories.summary: The UAE announced a deal to acquire 10 Embraer C-390 military transport aircraft, with options for up to 10 additional units. Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan noted it marks the C-390's first entry into the Middle East market and supports the UAE's defense industry localization goals.

stories.title: Russian forces increase combat activity in southern regions – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian forces intensified combat activity in southern sectors during April, particularly near Prydniprovske and Oleksandrivka, with the heaviest assaults recorded near Huliaipole.

stories.title: ‘Project Freedom’ marks a classic Trump flip from warmonger to humanitarian
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump shifted from escalatory rhetoric toward Iran to announcing "Project Freedom," a humanitarian initiative promising to free marooned ships. The pivot has been characterized as a move from wartime posturing to pursuing a Nobel Peace Prize narrative.

stories.title: Israeli-Turkish tensions continue to grow as Ankara prepares to launch new flotilla
stories.summary: Diplomatic officials are working behind the scenes to defuse tensions, and Israel is currently utilizing diplomatic channels with Turkey to try to prevent the flotilla from setting sail.

stories.title: Oil jumps, stocks mixed amid Iran, US claims of attack in Strait
stories.summary: US crude was last up 0.1 percent to $102.03 a barrel and Brent rose to $110.36 per barrel, up 2 percent on the day

stories.title: South Korean ship attacked near Strait of Hormuz, South Korea's government confirms
stories.summary: Earlier on Monday, an official from the South Korean Foreign Affairs Ministry told a Korean media outlet that there had been no Korean casualties in the attack.

stories.title: Trump's Gaza envoy to press Israel to uphold ceasefire
stories.summary: Nickolay Mladenov's visit to Israel comes as Hamas refuses to enter further talks until Israel stops violating the ceasefire.

stories.title: Canada allocates additional $200M to PURL — Zelensky
stories.summary: During a meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, President Zelensky announced that Canada has allocated an additional $200 million to the PURL program, bringing Canada's total contribution to over $830 million.

stories.title: Report: Putin fears assassination attempt by Russia’s political elite, tightens security
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Protective Service has significantly increased security measures around President Vladimir Putin amid his reported fears of a possible assassination attempt by the political elite, according to a European intelligence report reviewed by iStories, CNN, and the Financial Times.

stories.title: Bulls help PSX rebound by 900 points
stories.summary: Pakistan's benchmark KSE-100 index rebounded by 954.77 points, closing at 163,948.94 on the Pakistan Stock Exchange. The rally was driven by investor optimism following developments related to Iran-US tensions and market stabilization efforts.

stories.title: 2 dead, 2 injured after car ramming in German city of Leipzig
stories.summary: Two people were killed and two others severely injured when a car drove into a crowd on Grimmaische Street in central Leipzig, Germany. Police arrested the driver at the scene. Leipzig mayor Burkhard Jung confirmed the fatalities but said the motive remained unknown.

stories.title: UK government does all but admit Iran is behind attacks on British soil - analysis
stories.summary: Throughout the UK government and institutions, naming Iran, the IRGC, or even HAYI at times, has been avoided in favor of the more nebulous and anonymous "hostile states" and "state-linked actors."

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists 'threatened with death' in Israeli jail
stories.summary: Abu Keshek and Avila have been subject to ill-treatment in Israel, where they have been held following their abduction from international waters last week.

stories.title: Captain warns ‘no ship will be a hero’ by risking Hormuz transit
stories.summary: Captain Raman Kapoor stated that no vessel will attempt to transit the Strait of Hormuz without safety assurances, reflecting growing concerns among commercial shipping operators about the risks of navigating the critical waterway amid rising tensions.

stories.title: Pakistan Foreign Minister discusses regional situation with Iranian counterpart
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar spoke with his Iranian counterpart about the regional situation. Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to constructive engagement, emphasizing that dialogue and diplomacy are the only viable path toward peaceful resolution and lasting peace.

stories.title: Dubai's image as a financial hub faces its biggest test yet
stories.summary: Amid the ongoing Iran conflict, wealthy individuals and businesses are reportedly moving capital out of Dubai to destinations including Singapore and Switzerland. The trend is testing Dubai's reputation as a safe financial hub.

stories.title: UAE says it intercepted three missiles from Iran
stories.summary:

stories.title: Ecuador Says Extortion Is Down. The Reality Is More Complicated.
stories.summary: Ecuadorian police claim their offensive against criminal gangs has reduced extortion rates, citing official crime statistics. However, experts and victims dispute these claims, saying there is a significant gap between government statements and the extortion that Ecuadorians continue to experience on the ground.

stories.title: Pushback in Nigeria over ex-Boko Haram fighter reintegration
stories.summary: Nigeria plans to reintegrate more than 700 former Boko Haram fighters into society through a government deradicalization program. Authorities say the initiative is essential to ending the insurgency, but local communities have expressed skepticism and opposition.

stories.title: UAE issues new missile alert
stories.summary:
UAE issues new missile alert 

    
    

        
    
                The United Arab Emirates National Emergency and Crisis and Disaster Management Authority has sent out a warning that its air def

stories.title: Iran hangs three men over January protests in execution 'wave'
stories.summary: Mehdi Rassouli, Mohammad Reza Miri and Ebrahim Dolatabadi were executed after being convicted over unrest in the eastern city of Mashhad

stories.title: Peace talks, reconstruction, European integration: Zelensky meets with Tusk
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to discuss peace talks, reconstruction, and European integration. Ukraine signaled readiness for the next round of trilateral meetings aimed at achieving a long-term ceasefire and lasting peace.

stories.title: Austria Expels 3 Russian Embassy Staff on Suspicion of Spying
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian embassy staff members on suspicion of espionage. The Russian Embassy condemned the expulsions as "outrageous" and "politically motivated," vowing a harsh retaliatory response against Austria.

stories.title: Austria Expels 3 Russian Diplomats on Suspicion of Spying
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian diplomats on suspicion of espionage. The Russian Embassy condemned the expulsions as "outrageous" and "politically motivated" and vowed a retaliatory response.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia links three areas of eastern Yemen to power grid
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia links eastern Yemen to its power grid, raising questions over sovereignty, energy control and long-term strategic influence.

stories.title: Israel not equipped to put out electric vehicle fires, Fire and Rescue Commissioner says
stories.summary: When lithium-ion batteries enter thermal runaway, the fire can only be contained, not stopped, explained Israeli Fire and Rescue Commissioner Rabbi Eyal Caspi.

stories.title: Report: Moscow to restrict mobile internet and SMS from May 5 to 9 ahead of Victory Day parade
stories.summary: Russian Telegram news channel Ostorozhno Novosti reported that mobile internet and SMS services in Moscow will be restricted from May 5 to 9, ahead of the annual Victory Day parade on May 9.

stories.title: Lebanon Latest

stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders reported that approximately 90 percent of Gaza's health infrastructure has been destroyed or damaged during the war, severely hampering hospitals' ability to conduct diagnostic laboratory work.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strikes residential tower in Moscow less than 10 kilometers from Kremlin
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck one of the towers of the House on Mosfilmovskaya residential complex in Moscow, less than 10 kilometers from the Kremlin. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said air defense forces repelled an attack by two drones, and no casualties were reported.

stories.title: Iranian British man who chased Golders Green terrorist: ‘Maybe I can save someone’s life’
stories.summary: Ashkan Asadian, an Iranian-British man in London's Golders Green, recounted chasing and confronting a knife attacker, kicking him and grabbing for his weapon, which allowed a badly wounded Jewish victim to escape.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Project Freedom’: Can US navy ‘guide’ stuck ships out of Hormuz?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced "Project Freedom," a plan for the US Navy to escort ships stranded in the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, though details on implementation remain unclear.

stories.title: How child soldiers in Sudan become influencers on TikTok
stories.summary: Some child soldiers in Sudan have gained large followings on TikTok, with millions of users celebrating their social media accounts. Psychologists and experts have warned that this trend is dangerous.

stories.title: Most shipping blocked at Hormuz despite US assurances
stories.summary: Despite US assurances under "Project Freedom," vessel tracking data showed most commercial shipping remained blocked at the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with only a few ships permitted passage into the Gulf of Oman.

stories.title: NATO chief says Europeans have 'gotten message' from Trump on defence
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said European leaders have "gotten the message" from President Trump regarding frustration over the Iran war and are increasing defence contributions. His comments came after Washington announced the withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany, ahead of a European Political Community summit in Armenia.

stories.title: UAE says OPEC exit 'not directed against anyone'
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates said its recent exit from OPEC was "not directed against anyone," following months of tensions with Saudi Arabia, the cartel's de facto leader and the world's largest oil exporter.

stories.title: Decoding China: Beijing courts Europe amid US dysfunction
stories.summary: China is working to strengthen ties with European nations as the transatlantic partnership between the United States and European powers faces growing strain, seeking allies for a future multipolar world order.

stories.title: Shares of eBay take off on a $56 billion buyout bid from GameStop's Ryan Cohen
stories.summary: GameStop, led by Ryan Cohen, is pursuing an approximately $56 billion takeover bid for eBay, aiming to compete with Amazon in online retail. The proposal includes using GameStop's roughly 1,600 US stores as drop-off and shipping locations, as well as hosting live sales broadcasts featuring eBay products. eBay shares surged on the news.

stories.title: The loyal, lonely keepers of Sudan's pyramids
stories.summary: At the ancient site of Bajrawiya on Sudan's Island of Meroe, a guard continues to protect 140 pyramids built during the Kingdom of Kush's Meroitic period roughly 2,400 years ago. Three years into Sudan's war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces, the hereditary groundskeeper remains committed to safeguarding the site.

stories.title: Over 100 explosions heard in Chernihiv region; casualties and damage reported
stories.summary: The Chernihiv region of Ukraine recorded 108 explosions over 24 hours from Russian shelling, with enemy forces firing on border areas 56 times. Casualties and damage were reported across the region.

stories.title: Does Shaibani's Cairo visit signal a thaw in Egypt-Syria ties?
stories.summary: Syrian Foreign Minister Ahmad al-Shaibani visited Cairo for talks with Egyptian officials, potentially signalling a cautious thaw in Egypt-Syria relations after a rupture in 2024, amid broader regional tensions.

stories.title: Netanyahu testimony canceled overnight after defense cites security schedule
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's scheduled court testimony was cancelled overnight after his defence team cited security-related scheduling conflicts. The cancellation is the latest in a series of interruptions linked to wartime developments.

stories.title: North Korea ramps up executions over foreign media, says NGO
stories.summary: An NGO reports that North Korea has increased executions of people caught consuming foreign media. Children of North Korean elites are reportedly consuming smuggled South Korean and American entertainment despite the risk of severe punishment under Kim Jong Un.

stories.title: Kirsty, 11, seeks more Kirstys to help raise money for brain tumour research
stories.summary: An 11-year-old girl named Kirsty Waugh from Tunbridge Wells, Kent, who is being treated for a paediatric brain tumour, has tracked down over 10,000 people who share her name worldwide to help raise money for brain tumour research. The namesakes span locations from Colombia to Malaysia to Antarctica.

stories.title: Reform government could cause Truss-style chaos, says renewables industry
stories.summary: Britain's renewable energy industry chief lobbyist Tara Singh warned that a Reform UK government stripping renewable projects of subsidy contracts could trigger economic chaos comparable to the Liz Truss era. RenewableUK said such policies proposed by Nigel Farage's party would severely undermine investor confidence across the UK economy.

stories.title: US tech can use China as ‘listening post’ for global edge, Washington think tank explains
stories.summary: The Information Technology and Innovation Foundation, a Washington-based think tank, argued that US technology companies should maintain their presence in China rather than exit. The ITIF said firms can capitalize on Chinese market revenue, monitor consumer trends, and reinvest profits into US-based research and development to sustain American innovation leadership.

stories.title: First Thing: Trump says US navy will ‘guide’ trapped ships through strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced "Project Freedom," a plan to guide commercial ships trapped in the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran war. Trump claimed US representatives were having "very positive" discussions with Iran, while Iranian military officials insisted foreign armed forces would not be permitted in the waterway.

stories.title: Congo’s forests under strain from overlapping land use
stories.summary: The Congo Basin's forests, among the world's most important carbon sinks, face growing threats from overlapping land-use pressures. The concerns persist despite renewed global attention on ecosystem protection around Earth Day.

stories.title: Extreme heat could pose threat to players and fans at 2026 FIFA World Cup
stories.summary: Researchers are warning that extreme heat could threaten players, fans, and staff at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Games will take place across the United States, Canada, and Mexico during June and July, among North America's hottest months.

stories.title: ‘Far beyond’ EU and NATO: Armenia hosts EPC summit cast as ‘gateway’ in shifting diplomatic order
stories.summary: Armenia hosted the European Political Community summit, gathering approximately 50 leaders from Europe and Canada in the country's first-ever such event. Analysts described the summit as symbolically significant but structurally limited, serving as an informal platform to address transatlantic tensions, shifting US engagement, and shared security concerns.

stories.title: Europe must face up to ‘tensions’ with Trump, Keir Starmer says
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer acknowledged high "tensions" between Donald Trump and Europe at the European Political Community summit in Armenia. Starmer said Britain would use the summit to begin negotiations on joining the EU's loan scheme for Ukraine, as European leaders grapple with concerns over waning US interest in the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran.

stories.title: Welcome to Breaking Defense Europe. Here’s what you need to know.
stories.summary: Breaking Defense launched a European edition focused on delivering defense news for European audiences, produced by European journalists and analysts.

stories.title: Missile strike on Ukraine's Kharkiv region kills five, destroys infrastructure
stories.summary: A Russian Iskander-type ballistic missile struck the town of Merefa in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, killing five people and wounding at least 18. The strike damaged homes, businesses, and public buildings in an area far from the front lines. There was no immediate comment from Moscow.

stories.title: How the US-Israel war has cemented the IRGC's grip on Iran
stories.summary: Analysts argue that the US-Israeli war against Iran has strengthened the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' grip on power rather than weakening it, pushing Iran further toward a military-dominated state with clerical oversight.

stories.title: ‘Golden week’: Hong Kong draws more mainland Chinese visitors but spending uneven
stories.summary: Hong Kong recorded 714,765 mainland Chinese visitor entries between May 1 and 3 during the Labour Day Golden Week holiday, a 4.8 percent increase over the same period last year. However, industry figures cautioned that uneven spending patterns and more flexible travel habits could limit business gains despite hotel occupancy rates nearing 90 percent.

stories.title: Passenger traffic at Dubai International Airport drops 66% in March amid Iran war
stories.summary: Passenger traffic at Dubai International Airport fell 66 percent in March amid the ongoing Iran war. The airport was forced to shut down multiple times due to drone incidents in its vicinity.

stories.title: Iran's navy warns seafarers amid US effort to 'guide' stranded ships
stories.summary: Iran's navy warned that ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz must coordinate with Iranian authorities. The statement came after the United States announced efforts to guide stranded ships and open the strategic waterway.

stories.title: High Court freezes Second Authority council after state misses response deadline
stories.summary: Israel's High Court Justice Alex Stein froze the Second Authority council after the state missed a response deadline. Stein rejected new extension requests submitted on Sunday, calling them unacceptable regardless of the petitioners' positions.

stories.title: 5.2-magnitude earthquake jolts Islamabad, Pindi
stories.summary: A 5.2-magnitude earthquake struck near the Tajikistan-Xinjiang border region at a depth of 128 kilometers, with tremors felt in Islamabad and Rawalpindi on Monday morning.

stories.title: Wall Street dips, oil prices rise on reports of strike on US Navy vessel near Iran
stories.summary: Wall Street futures declined and oil prices surged on Monday amid conflicting reports of a strike on a US Navy vessel near the Strait of Hormuz. S&P 500 futures fell 0.2 percent and Dow futures dropped 0.5 percent. Oil initially jumped 5 percent before moderating after the US military denied the reports.

stories.title: Israel to buy more F-35 and F-15 warplanes
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to purchase additional F-35 and F-15 warplanes as part of a decade-long military modernization plan valued at $118 billion. The government confirmed the acquisitions as part of its broader defense investment strategy.

stories.title: Iran executes three men in relation to January anti-regime protests
stories.summary: Iran executed three men charged in connection with political protests that took place in January, as part of a wave of near-daily executions. Activists have denounced the killings as an attempt to instil fear amid the ongoing war with the US and Israel and domestic tensions.

stories.title: Hong Kong police launch investigation after elderly couple found dead in flat
stories.summary: Hong Kong police launched an investigation after an elderly couple—an 89-year-old man and his 87-year-old wife—were found dead in their flat at Lok Seen Lau in the Lok Man Sun Chuen estate in To Kwa Wan. A security guard reported a strange smell, and firefighters forced entry to discover both unresponsive on a bed.

stories.title: New alliances shakes up Nigerian political landscape
stories.summary: Nigerian opposition figures Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, who finished third and fourth respectively in the last presidential elections, have switched parties. The realignment is reshaping Nigeria's political landscape ahead of future contests.

stories.title: Nigeria to evacuate 130 citizens from South Africa amid xenophobia fears
stories.summary: Nigeria announced plans to evacuate 130 citizens from South Africa amid rising xenophobia fears. Previous outbreaks of anti-foreigner violence in South Africa in 2008, 2015, and 2019 have strained relations between the two countries.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief rejects direct talks with Israel, says move would 'serve Netanyahu and Trump'
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected direct negotiations with Israel, saying such talks would benefit Netanyahu and Trump. He accused Israel of violating the ceasefire agreement more than ten thousand times.

stories.title: Lebanon: Israel deploys new system to intercept Hezbollah drones
stories.summary: The Israeli military has deployed a new interception system in Lebanon designed to counter Hezbollah's explosive-laden drones, as tensions between the two sides continue to escalate despite the ceasefire.

stories.title: Michigan University professor praises anti-Israel student activists in commencement speech
stories.summary: A University of Michigan professor reportedly praised anti-Israel student activists during a commencement speech, deviating from prepared remarks. University President Domenico Grasso said the comments did not reflect the institution's position of neutrality.

stories.title: Labor extends EV tax break to encourage cheaper vehicles amid soaring fuel prices
stories.summary: Australia's Labor government announced it will extend its electric vehicle tax discount in full for another year, after which the benefit will apply only to EVs costing under A$75,000. The move comes amid surging fuel prices linked to the Iran war and rising EV demand, though the government plans to scale back support over the following three years.

stories.title: ‘Made in Europe’ law sets stage for an economic showdown with China
stories.summary: The European Union is moving toward introducing 'Made in Europe' protectionist measures that could trigger an economic confrontation with China, one of its largest trading partners. The push comes as EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has accused Beijing of undermining the rules-based international system, making a stand-off appear increasingly likely amid the ongoing US-China trade war.

stories.title: Army awards AV LASSO award, joining Textron, Uvision in prototyping competition
stories.summary: The US Army awarded an AV LASSO contract, adding a new competitor to a prototyping competition that includes Textron and Uvision. The awarded company will provide its Switchblade 400, a portable anti-armor loitering munition with medium range.

stories.title: Reuters: Senior Iranian official says Iran fired warning shot at US warship
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran fired a "warning shot" toward a US Navy vessel to prevent its entry into the Strait of Hormuz, though it remains unclear whether the ship sustained any damage. US Central Command denied reports of an attack.

stories.title: UAE condemns Iranian attack on Adnoc tanker transiting Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates condemned an Iranian drone attack on an Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) tanker attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Two drones targeted the vessel, but no injuries were reported. The UAE called the action "piracy" by Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps.

stories.title: Africa’s telecom towers turn to solar as diesel costs surge
stories.summary: Rising diesel prices, linked in part to the Iran conflict, are accelerating a shift across Africa's telecom industry from fuel-powered generators to solar energy systems. Operators are adopting solar to keep mobile networks running while controlling costs.

stories.title: France’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon announces 2027 presidential bid
stories.summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the 74-year-old leader of France's radical left party La France Insoumise, announced he will run for the French presidency for a fourth time in the 2027 election. He cited the urgency of opposing wars waged by the US and Israel in the Middle East as motivation for his candidacy.

stories.title: Trump says US will 'guide' ships in Hormuz despite Iran warnings
stories.summary: President Trump reiterated that the US Navy would guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iranian warnings. A tanker near the UAE reported being struck by a projectile shortly after Trump's announcement.

stories.title: Shropshire council staff met with rising ‘abuse and intimidation’ over removal of flags
stories.summary: Shropshire council in England reported rising abuse, harassment, and intimidation of staff and councillors linked to the removal of unauthorised Union Jack and St George's flags. The authority said workers have been threatened while carrying out routine duties including street lighting repairs.

stories.title: ‘Hegemonic power’: How Modi’s BJP won India’s Bengal for the first time
stories.summary: India's ruling BJP, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, won seats in West Bengal for the first time, leveraging religious polarisation and anti-incumbency sentiment against the state's ruling party.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Komyshuvakha with guided bombs; one person killed
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted a guided bomb airstrike on Komyshuvakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing one man. The strike is part of continued Russian aerial attacks on communities in the region.

stories.title: Israel seizes nearly 60 percent of Gaza as it plans to resume war, report says
stories.summary: Israeli Army Radio reported that Israel has expanded control over nearly 60 percent of the Gaza Strip despite the ceasefire. Senior military officials are pushing to resume fighting, with operational plans completed and awaiting political approval.

stories.title: No US Navy ships struck by Iran, says US Central Command
stories.summary: US Central Command denied Iranian state media claims that two missiles struck a US warship in the Strait of Hormuz, stating no US Navy ships were hit. Centcom said US forces are supporting "Project Freedom" and enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports.

stories.title: Russia hit a record oil revenue month—yet the federal budget still came up short
stories.summary: Russia recorded a record month for oil revenue, but its federal budget still ran a deficit. Sberbank's CFO forecasts the ruble will fall to 90 per dollar, and three Russian ports have seen cargo drops of 13–43%.

stories.title: Russia’s oil revenue nearly doubled in March. Its own bankers still expect a crash
stories.summary: Russia's oil revenue nearly doubled in March, but Sberbank's chief financial officer forecasts the ruble will weaken to 90 per dollar. Three Russian ports have already recorded cargo volume drops ranging from 13 to 43 percent.

stories.title: A diary of America's wars with photographer Peter van Agtmael
stories.summary: Photographer Peter van Agtmael has spent over two decades documenting US wars in Iraq and Afghanistan and their domestic repercussions. His photo book "Look at the U.S.A.: A Diary of War and Home" pairs battlefield images with snapshots of post-9/11 American life to illustrate the connection between distant conflicts and their impact at home.

stories.title: Japan, Australia agree to deepen cooperation on energy, defence and critical minerals
stories.summary: Japan and Australia agreed to deepen cooperation on energy, defense, and critical minerals. Australia supplies nearly half of Japan's liquefied natural gas, while Japan is among Australia's top five suppliers of refined gasoline and diesel.

stories.title: All 8 Miners Confirmed Dead After Coal Mine Collapse in Russia’s Far East
stories.summary: All eight miners were confirmed dead after a coal mine collapse in Russia's Far East. The mining company's CEO attributed the collapse to melting permafrost.

stories.title: Likud activist, a convicted felon, tells Knesset panel that teens ‘didn’t mean to kill’ pizza worker
stories.summary: Likud activist and convicted felon Rafi Kedoshim sparked outrage at a Knesset committee hearing on teen violence by claiming that teenagers involved in the killing of a pizza worker "didn't mean to kill."

stories.title: Cruise ship at centre of suspected hantavirus outbreak blocked from docking in Cape Verde
stories.summary: Cape Verde authorities refused to allow a cruise ship suspected of harboring a hantavirus outbreak to dock in its ports, citing public health concerns. Three passengers aboard the Atlantic cruise ship have died, and the outbreak is under investigation by global health officials. Hantavirus is a rare respiratory infection primarily transmitted by rodents.

stories.title: Green group warns of disturbance to uninhabited island known for breeding seabirds
stories.summary: A Hong Kong environmental group reported that people were landing on an uninhabited island in southern Hong Kong waters during mainland China's Labour Day Golden Week holiday. The island is a known breeding site for terns, and the disturbance coincides with the seabirds' breeding season.

stories.title: South Africa: South Africa's Road Rage Problem Goes Deeper Than Bad Drivers
stories.summary: A report by South Africa's Institute for Security Studies highlights a growing road rage problem linked to accumulated stress, inequality, and normalized violence. The presence of firearms can escalate road incidents to fatal outcomes.

stories.title: Lebanon warned against direct meeting with Netanyahu amid war
stories.summary: Reports that Lebanese President Joseph Aoun may meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House triggered sharp criticism in Lebanon and across the Arab world, amid Israel's ongoing military operations.

stories.title: New power outages reported in four regions due to enemy shelling, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Russian attacks caused new power outages affecting consumers in Ukraine's Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, and Kherson regions, according to state grid operator Ukrenergo. The outages were reported as of the morning of May 4.

stories.title: NATO is dead. Meet CALM.
stories.summary: A commentary piece discusses alternatives to NATO, proposing a new alliance concept referred to as CALM. The article notes that open debate about replacing the Alliance, long considered taboo, shifted after 2026.

stories.title: Lift technician dies after 10-metre fall down shaft at Hong Kong luxury estate
stories.summary: A 26-year-old lift technician died after falling 10 metres down a lift shaft he was repairing at Pacific View, a luxury residential estate on Tai Tam Road in Stanley, Hong Kong. The worker suffered fatal head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. Police are investigating the cause of the accident.

stories.title: Austria expels 3 Russian diplomats over signals spying
stories.summary: Austria declared three Russian diplomats personae non gratae over an array of satellite dishes—described as an "antenna forest"—on rooftops of Russian diplomatic buildings in Vienna. Austrian domestic intelligence had long warned the installations could be used to intercept other states' satellite communications.

stories.title: FO says 22 crew members on Iranian ship seized by US have been evacuated to Pakistan
