stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office confirmed that 22 crew members of the Iranian vessel M/V Touska, seized by U.S. forces, were evacuated to Pakistan for repatriation as a confidence-building measure by the United States.

stories.title: Hezbollah deploys hard-to-jam fibre optic drones, shifting battlefield tactics
stories.summary: Hezbollah has shifted battlefield tactics in its conflict with Israel by deploying fibre optic drones that can evade Israeli electronic jamming systems. The escalation followed exchanges of rockets and airstrikes linked to broader regional tensions involving Iran. A US-brokered ceasefire took effect in mid-April but remains fragile amid ongoing clashes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Republicans split with Trump and back Haitians – to save their seats
stories.summary: Several Republicans in Ohio are breaking with President Trump's stance on Haitian immigrants, recognizing the community's role in reviving local economies. In Springfield, Ohio, where an estimated 10,000 Haitians reside, vulnerable Republican lawmakers are reluctant to follow Trump's hardline immigration rhetoric ahead of elections.

stories.title: What’s behind the KMT’s internal splits over Taiwanese defence spending?
stories.summary: Taiwan's main opposition party, the Kuomintang, faces widening internal divisions over a proposed NT$1.25 trillion (US$40 billion) special defence budget put forward by the ruling Democratic Progressive Party. The US de facto ambassador in Taipei, Raymond Greene, has pressured the KMT on the issue ahead of upcoming local elections.

stories.title: Modi's BJP conquers Bengal, one of India's toughest political frontiers
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party made significant electoral gains in West Bengal, traditionally an opposition stronghold. The result in the state of 100 million people could reshape regional politics and the BJP's national trajectory.

stories.title: Boeing faces civil trial over 737 MAX crash
stories.summary: Boeing is facing a civil trial related to a 737 MAX crash. The company has acknowledged that its anti-stall software, known as MCAS, was implicated in the accident that led to the litigation.

stories.title: More than 300 families evacuate in Philippines due to ashfall from volcano
stories.summary: More than 300 families in the Philippines evacuated after massive ashfall from a volcano scattered over 87 villages in three towns. No deaths or injuries were reported, but poor visibility affected motorists.

stories.title: Italian prosecutors open investigation into kidnapping of Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: Prosecutors in Rome opened a kidnapping investigation after two activists aboard a Gaza-bound aid flotilla flying an Italian flag were seized by Israeli forces in international waters. The activists are currently imprisoned in Israel.

stories.title: Africa: Turkey Raises Residence Permit Fee By 930 Percent for Nigerians, 36 Other African Countries
stories.summary: Turkey's Directorate General of Migration Management announced residence permit fee increases of up to 930 percent for nationals of Nigeria and approximately 36 other African countries.

stories.title: Sudan: Cabinet Underscores Combating Corruption, Smuggling, and Narcotics
stories.summary: Sudan's cabinet met in Khartoum under the chairmanship of Dr. Kamil Idris to review anti-corruption, anti-smuggling, and anti-narcotics efforts. The meeting emphasized the role of the Ministry of Interior and General Intelligence Service in combating these issues.

stories.title: Coordination Headquarters hopes to resolve “Chechen issue” regarding POWs soon
stories.summary: Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War expressed hope for the near-term repatriation of all Ukrainian prisoners currently held in Chechnya. The statement addressed what officials termed the "Chechen issue" regarding POW treatment and return.

stories.title: Europe will not submit to an ‘insular and brutal world’, says Carney
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, the first non-European leader to attend a European Political Community meeting, said Europe will not submit to a more "brutal world" and can serve as the foundation for rebuilding a new international order. He spoke in Armenia amid tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and doubts about US commitment to NATO.

stories.title: Car show turns to tragedy as monster truck drives into crowd in Colombia
stories.summary: A monster truck lost control during a car show in Colombia and drove into a crowd of spectators, turning the event into a tragedy as onlookers captured the incident.

stories.title: ‘Israel is not implementing the ceasefire agreement in Gaza’
stories.summary: Accusations have emerged that Israel is failing to implement the terms of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza, raising concerns about compliance with the deal's provisions.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Slams Into Skyscraper Near Central Moscow
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a skyscraper near central Moscow. The attack occurred days before Russia's annual Victory Day military parade on Red Square.

stories.title: US denies ship hit by Iranian missiles, Axios reporter says
stories.summary: A senior US official denied that any American vessel was struck by Iranian missiles near the Strait of Hormuz, responding to reports from Iran's Fars news agency that two missiles hit a US warship near Jask.

stories.title: Bulls in control as PSX gains 4,000 points during intraday trade
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 stock index surged approximately 4,000 points during intraday trading on Monday, driven by investor reaction to developments surrounding Iran-U.S. tensions and efforts to stabilize global energy routes.

stories.title: Interview: Gen. Ronald Clark, US Army Pacific commander
stories.summary: US Army Pacific commander Gen. Ronald Clark discussed the 41st iteration of the Balikatan military exercises, describing them as a "full-circle event." Clark has led USARPAC since November 8, 2024.

stories.title: US to 'guide' stranded ships from Hormuz: What we know about 'Project Freedom'
stories.summary: The United States launched "Project Freedom" on Monday to guide commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing blockade caused by the Iran war. The US-led Joint Maritime Information Center advised vessels to transit through Omani waters via an enhanced security area, potentially involving guided-missile destroyers, over 100 aircraft, and 15,000 service members.

stories.title: Dubai airport passenger traffic drops 66 percent over Iran war
stories.summary: Dubai's airport reported a 66 percent decline in passenger traffic linked to the Iran conflict, with first-quarter 2026 figures falling 21 percent to 18.6 million passengers as Iranian retaliatory strikes disrupted regional air travel.

stories.title: Hong Kong puts its own spin on DeepSeek with China-chip AI push abroad
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Centre, a government-backed lab, is preparing to launch HKGAI-V3, a new AI model built on DeepSeek V4 architecture and optimized to run entirely on Chinese-made chips. The centre plans to unveil the model in the first half of this year and export its capabilities to overseas markets.

stories.title: Russian strike on Merefa in Kharkiv region: Death toll climbs to four, 16 injured
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the town of Merefa in Ukraine's Kharkiv region killed four people and injured at least 16 others, according to reports as of the morning of the attack.

stories.title: What is the Ukrainian anti-drone system Sky Map being used in the Gulf?
stories.summary: Ukraine's "Sky Map" anti-drone system, which uses thousands of acoustic sensors and interceptors to detect and destroy incoming drones, is reportedly being deployed in the Gulf region.

stories.title: US close to delivering Israeli 'Gideon' KC-46 refueling aircraft for future Iran attacks
stories.summary: The US is close to delivering the first KC-46 aerial refueling aircraft, designated "Gideon," to Israel. The tanker completed its maiden test flight in the US and is expected to arrive in Israel within approximately one month, potentially supporting future operations against Iran.

stories.title: ‘Scarlet Swan’ chat member says Russia’s FSB forced her to read prepared script in staged terrorism video
stories.summary: Sofia Chepik, a member of the "Scarlet Swan" Telegram chat group, was released from a Moscow detention facility on May 3 after serving 15 days on a hooliganism charge. She alleged that Russia's FSB compelled her to read a prepared script for a staged terrorism video.

stories.title: Sea of Galilee trail plan that keeps parts of shore off-limits to public sparks outcry
stories.summary: A proposed 32-kilometre hiking trail around Israel's Sea of Galilee has drawn criticism from environmental groups, who oppose plans to include fences, locked gates, and bypass routes that would restrict public access to parts of the shoreline.

stories.title: Survey finds fewer than 25% of Gaza border residents feel safe, 40% don’t trust state
stories.summary: A survey by the Tekuma Directorate found that fewer than 25 percent of residents near the Gaza border feel safe and 40 percent distrust the state, though life satisfaction and optimism about the future have increased.

stories.title: Winning peace in Lebanon is harder than winning war
stories.summary: Analysts note that achieving a lasting peace in Lebanon remains more difficult than military operations, requiring consideration of the country's complex history and shifting geopolitical dynamics in the region.

stories.title: Iran warns of ceasefire violation as U.S. plans to escort Hormuz ships
stories.summary: Iran's parliamentary national security commission warned that any US interference in the new maritime regime of the Strait of Hormuz would be considered a violation of the ceasefire between the two countries.

stories.title: Iranian media: Two missiles hit US warship which ignored Iran’s warnings
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported that two missiles struck a US warship near Jask in the Strait of Hormuz after it ignored Iranian warnings, and that the vessel subsequently turned back from the area.

stories.title: Iran says ships being ‘guided’ by US through Hormuz must work with its armed forces
stories.summary: Iran declared that any commercial ships being "guided" by the US through the Strait of Hormuz must coordinate their transit with Iranian armed forces. Tehran warned it would attack any foreign military forces entering the waterway under the US plan, as hundreds of ships remain trapped in the Gulf due to the Iran war.

stories.title: Iranian military commander warns ‘supporters’ of US over Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian Major-General Ali Abdollahi warned that nations supporting the United States should exercise caution before entering the Strait of Hormuz to escort commercial vessels. He accused the US military of jeopardizing vessel security and threatening global trade stability through aggressive actions in the waterway.

stories.title: Over thousand Ukrainians held captive by Russia since 2022 – Coordination Headquarters
stories.summary: Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters reported that over one thousand Ukrainian military personnel and civilians have been held captive by Russia since 2022.

stories.title: Money, power, exile: Inside an Iranian exile’s war on regime-linked wealth in Canada
stories.summary: An investigation profiled an Iranian exile in Canada working to expose regime-linked wealth. The activist began blogging under a pseudonym at age 15 and has since focused on tracking financial assets tied to the Iranian government.

stories.title: In the PR battle for AI data centres, tech giants have a blue-collar ally
stories.summary: Building trades unions in the United States have emerged as allies for tech companies in the public relations effort surrounding the construction of AI data centres.

stories.title: Village braces itself for closure of Spain's largest nuclear plant
stories.summary: A village in Spain is preparing for the closure of the country's largest nuclear plant. No additional details were provided in the source material about the timeline or specific community impacts.

stories.title: Hantavirus: Three cruise ship passengers die in suspected outbreak
stories.summary: Three passengers on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean have died in a suspected hantavirus outbreak, with three more passengers ill. Hantavirus, which is primarily spread to humans through contact with rodent urine, droppings, and saliva, has a fatality rate of approximately 40 percent.

stories.title: Trump administration claims food aid fraud but critics say ‘there’s no evidence’
stories.summary: US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins claimed without evidence that 14,000 SNAP food aid recipients included owners of luxury vehicles such as Ferraris and Bentleys. Critics called the assertion part of a disinformation campaign aimed at undermining the 87-year-old nutritional assistance program that supports tens of millions of low-income Americans.

stories.title: Nigeria: Dangote Denies Rift With Tony Elumelu, Rejects Refinery Funding Claims
stories.summary: Dangote Group denied allegations of a rift between its president, Aliko Dangote, and businessman Tony Elumelu. The company also rejected claims that the Dangote Petroleum Refinery was financed through personal borrowing from friends.

stories.title: Trump’s War Exposes the Weakness of Middle Powers
stories.summary: An analysis argues that collective action by middle powers will not be sufficient to shape the global order amid the challenges posed by the Trump administration's war policies. The assessment suggests that lesser powers lack the leverage needed to influence major geopolitical outcomes.

stories.title: Iran says it fired missiles at US warship to prevent it entering Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that Iran's forces fired two missiles at a US Navy destroyer near the Strait of Hormuz to prevent it from entering the waterway, though accounts of the incident are disputed.

stories.title: Shooting at lake near Oklahoma City in U.S. injures at least 10
stories.summary: A shooting at a gathering of young people near Arcadia Lake in Edmond, Oklahoma, injured at least 10 people. Authorities received multiple reports of gunfire at approximately 9 p.m.

stories.title: Shooting at US party sends at least 13 to hospital
stories.summary: A shooting at a gathering of young people near Arcadia Lake outside Oklahoma City on Sunday night sent at least 13 people to hospitals. Edmond police said they received reports of gunfire around 9 pm. No arrests had been made as of late Sunday.

stories.title: Russian forces carry out airstrike on Shostka, city council building and houses damaged
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out an airstrike on the city of Shostka in Ukraine, damaging the city council building and private homes. Three women were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Israeli commander boasts of West Bank killings unseen since 1967
stories.summary: The head of Israel's Central Command said Israeli troops are killing Palestinians in the West Bank at levels not seen since 1967. The statement referenced ongoing military operations across the occupied territory.

stories.title: India's Modi faces key test as vote count underway
stories.summary: Vote counting began in key Indian state elections, with particular focus on West Bengal, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP sought to unseat Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress. Elections took place across five states and territories in April and May.

stories.title: 18 Peruvians deceived into fighting for Russia return home, with more repatriations expected
stories.summary: Eighteen Peruvian citizens who were deceived into traveling to Russia and forced to fight against Ukraine have been repatriated over the past two weeks, according to Peru's Foreign Ministry. Additional repatriations are expected.

stories.title: Europe, Canada leaders hold Yerevan talks in Trump’s shadow
stories.summary: European and Canadian leaders held talks in Yerevan, Armenia, under the shadow of U.S. President Donald Trump's foreign policy. The ongoing Iran war has deepened divisions in transatlantic relations, adding urgency to the discussions.

stories.title: Death toll from Turkey school shooting rises to 10
stories.summary: The death toll from a school shooting in Turkey rose to 10, sparking public outrage. President Erdogan responded by dismissing a deputy education minister and pledging to introduce new gun restrictions.

stories.title: Two killed in Israeli attack on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in Israeli air strikes on the town of Shhour in southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes followed Israeli military evacuation warnings issued to residents in several towns in the Tyre and Bint Jbeil districts.

stories.title: Russian officials bar women from helping clean oil-fouled beaches, citing concern for reproductive health
stories.summary: Officials in Tuapse, Russia, and Emergency Situations Ministry representatives barred female volunteers from participating in cleanup of oil-fouled beaches, citing concerns about reproductive health, according to a Kommersant correspondent.

stories.title: No ceasefire in Lebanon while Israeli attacks ongoing, says Hezbollah
stories.summary: Hezbollah Secretary General Naim Qassem stated there is no ceasefire in Lebanon while Israeli attacks continue. He criticized direct talks between Lebanese and Israeli authorities and called for security guarantees before negotiations. Qassem reaffirmed Hezbollah's commitment to armed resistance to prevent Israeli gains in Lebanon.

stories.title: Dar and Iran's Araghchi discuss regional situation, Pakistan's ongoing diplomatic efforts
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar spoke with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi about the regional situation and Pakistan's diplomatic efforts for peace. Araghchi praised Pakistan's constructive mediation role between involved parties.

stories.title: Massive search continues for two missing US soldiers in Morocco
stories.summary: US, Moroccan, and allied forces launched a large-scale land, air, and sea search operation in the Cap Draa Training Area of Morocco after two US service members went missing during activities in the region.

stories.title: 30 students celebrating end of high school hospitalized with eye injuries from foam spray
stories.summary: Thirty Israeli high school students were hospitalised with eye injuries, including cornea damage, after using foam spray during end-of-school celebrations. Doctors warned against using foam spray without eye protection.

stories.title: Iran threatens to attack US warships that enter Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran warned that any US military vessels entering the Strait of Hormuz will be attacked, according to Ali Abdollahi, head of the unified command of the Iranian military. The threat came after President Trump announced the US Navy would accompany trapped ships out of the strait.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 4 – ‘One big failure’: An IDF official on the Iran war so far
stories.summary: An IDF official described Israel's war with Iran as "one big failure," while military correspondent Emanuel Fabian reported on the fragile ceasefire in southern Lebanon, preparations for further Gaza operations, and internal IDF tensions.

stories.title: Oil spill from refinery struck by Ukraine has contaminated 60 kilometers of Russian coastline, ecologist says
stories.summary: An oil spill following Ukrainian drone strikes on a refinery has contaminated approximately 60 kilometers of Russian coastline near Tuapse. Municipal district head Sergei Boyko said the city beach would be cleaned by June 1 in time for resort season.

stories.title: Pitch perfect diplomacy? North Korean footballers head to South Korea
stories.summary: North Korea's Naegohyang Women's FC confirmed participation in the 2025–2026 AFC Women's Champions League, which will require travel to South Korea. The visit would mark the first time North Korean athletes have set foot on South Korean soil in eight years, raising hopes that sports diplomacy could help ease bilateral tensions.

stories.title: Any vessel violating Iran’s rules will be stopped by force, says IRGC
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that any vessel passing through the Strait of Hormuz in violation of Iran's blockade will be met with military force. The IRGC Navy also issued a new map delineating the areas of the strait under Iranian armed forces' control.

stories.title: Russia adds nearly 100 professions to list eligible for alternative civilian service
stories.summary: Russia's Labor Ministry expanded the list of professions eligible for alternative civilian service by nearly 100 positions, raising the total from 271 to 363.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Kharkiv-Chuhuiv road with drone, leaving two people injured
stories.summary: On the morning of May 4, Russian forces struck the Kyiv-Kharkiv-Dovzhanskyi highway in Chuhuiv district with a drone, targeting vehicles on the road and injuring two people.

stories.title: Reform UK plan to set up migrant detention centres in Green-voting areas condemned by other parties – UK politics live
stories.summary: Reform UK proposed placing migrant detention centres in areas that elected Green Party council leaders or MPs. Other parties and commentators condemned the plan, with the British Future thinktank calling it potentially illegal and logically contradictory.

stories.title: ‘No pilgrims’: Regional war hushes Iraq’s holy cities
stories.summary: Iraq's holy cities have seen pilgrim visits virtually disappear due to the regional war. The cities previously drew pilgrims from Iran, Lebanon, Gulf states, India, Afghanistan, and other countries.

stories.title: Transgender student sues Hong Kong school over ‘discriminatory’ hair policy
stories.summary: A transgender student named Oscar Fung King-ho filed a lawsuit against a Hong Kong secondary school, alleging discrimination over a policy requiring short hair conforming to her sex assigned at birth. Her lawyers sought damages, citing public humiliation by teachers.

stories.title: Two worlds collide: the regulatory battlefield hanging over the EU’s ties with China
stories.summary: Cybersecurity tests conducted in a decommissioned Norwegian mine on Chinese-made Yutong electric buses revealed vulnerabilities including potential remote access, contributing to new EU regulations affecting EU-China relations.

stories.title: China ‘Madman of Science’ believes budget space travel is viable after low-cost rocket launch
stories.summary: Chinese self-taught innovator Lu Yulong and his five-person team built and launched the Shenzhen Pioneer rocket in Qinghai province in February. The 12-meter liquid rocket reached 3,700 meters altitude, setting a regional record and demonstrating low-cost space launch feasibility.

stories.title: Punjab cops in a bind over transfer to ‘hard areas’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Establishment Division transferred 10 Punjab police officers to postings in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, designated as "hard areas." Concerns were raised because many of the transferred officers are near retirement age, contrary to a rotation policy meant for younger officers.

stories.title: Iran threatens to attack US warships that enter Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran warned it would attack US warships attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz, as President Trump announced plans for the US Navy to guide ships trapped in the strait to safety.

stories.title: Africa: African Groups Push for Stronger Disease Surveillance Systems
stories.summary: More than 20 civil society and community organizations across Africa urged governments to prioritize epidemic preparedness and strengthen disease surveillance systems, warning that weak infrastructure could undermine responses to future outbreaks.

stories.title: Southern Africa: Misa Launches Sixth Edition of the Southern Africa Press Freedom Report
stories.summary: The Media Institute of Southern Africa launched the sixth edition of its Southern Africa Press Freedom Report, which highlights a widespread crisis of technology-facilitated gender-based violence.

stories.title: NATO chief says Europeans have ‘gotten the message’ from Trump on defence
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General stated that European allies have received President Trump's message on increasing defence spending, amid US criticism that some NATO members are not contributing enough to support the US-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: South Africa: Fuel and Fertiliser Costs Drive Up the Price of a Basic Food Basket
stories.summary: Rising fuel and fertiliser costs, partly linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict, are driving up the price of a basic food basket in South Africa. Analysts noted potential opportunistic pricing by processors and retailers even when producer prices stabilized.

stories.title: NATO's Rutte: Europeans are ensuring agreements with US on military bases are implemented
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said European nations are ensuring agreements with the US on military bases are being implemented. He added that an increasing number of European countries are pre-positioning naval assets, including minehunters and minesweepers, near the Gulf for potential future operations.

stories.title: Kenya: Duale Backs Kenya-Somalia Border Reopening to Boost Trade
stories.summary: Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale expressed support for reopening the Kenya-Somalia border, stating the move would enhance trade and ease the movement of people and goods between the two nations.

stories.title: Israeli minister's 'disgusting noose cake' draws widespread criticism
stories.summary: Israeli Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir drew widespread condemnation over a birthday cake featuring a noose design. Separately, Amsterdam became the first capital city to ban advertising for meat and fossil fuels, and The Washington Post reported on a Ukrainian soldier trapped in a combat kill zone.

stories.title: Drone gun-running ring from Jordan to West Bank busted, five suspects indicted
stories.summary: Israel's Shin Bet, IDF, and police dismantled a cross-border weapons smuggling network that used drones to transport arms from Jordan into the West Bank. Five suspects were indicted after dozens of weapons were trafficked into Israeli-controlled territory.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone hits upmarket Moscow high-rise ahead of Victory Day celebrations
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a high-rise residential building in an upscale Moscow neighborhood ahead of Russia's Victory Day celebrations. The attack came as the Kremlin prepared for a scaled-back military parade on May 9.

stories.title: UAE says it left Opec on good terms, Iran criticises exit
stories.summary: UAE Energy Minister Suhail Al Mazrouei said the UAE departed Opec and Opec+ on good terms and would continue cooperating with member states. Iran criticized the UAE's exit, with Iranian officials calling negative reactions toward fellow members unconstructive.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 135 of 155 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 135 of 155 Russian drones launched against Ukraine since the evening of May 3, leaving 20 drones unaccounted for.

stories.title: ‘I can’t feel my leg’: Israeli gunfire disables teenagers in West Bank
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported from a refugee camp in the occupied West Bank where Israeli soldiers have shot and injured multiple teenagers, leaving some with permanent disabilities. The report documents cases of young people killed or maimed by Israeli gunfire in the territory.

stories.title: Iranian ship, crew seized by US transferred to Pakistan: report
stories.summary: The United States transferred the Iranian vessel M/V Touska and its 22 crew members to Pakistan for repatriation after seizing the ship for failing to comply with a US-imposed blockade on Iranian ports. Six other passengers had been transferred to another country earlier.

stories.title: Iran foreign ministry: US must abandon ‘excessive demands’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei blamed the United States for the slow pace of diplomacy to end the war, describing US negotiating demands as "excessive." He called on Washington to adopt a more reasonable approach and said all countries involved directly or indirectly bear responsibility.

stories.title: Iran threatens American ships if they enter Hormuz, as US kicks off ‘Project Freedom’
stories.summary: Iran threatened to attack American ships entering the Strait of Hormuz as the US launched "Project Freedom" to move stranded commercial vessels. US officials indicated the initiative may not necessarily involve direct Navy escorts, while France said it would not participate in the "unclear" operation.

stories.title: In Moscow, drone strikes high-rise building 6 kilometers from Kremlin
stories.summary: Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin reported that a drone struck a high-rise building in Moscow on the night of May 4, approximately six kilometers from the Kremlin. No further details on casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: Iran's navy attacks US ship with missiles, CENTCOM denies strike
stories.summary: Iran's navy reportedly fired missiles at a US ship near the Strait of Hormuz, while US Central Command denied any American vessel was struck. The incident occurred as President Trump announced plans for the Navy to escort ships through the waterway.

stories.title: Iran warns US entry into Strait of Hormuz 'will be attacked'
stories.summary: Iran warned that any US forces entering the Strait of Hormuz would be attacked, after President Trump announced the US Navy would guide commercial ships through the waterway. The threat was issued by Iran's unified military command.

stories.title: Russian missile turns Monday morning in Kharkiv Oblast into a mass-casualty scene — 5 dead, 19 injured in Kharkiv Oblast
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike in Kharkiv Oblast on Monday morning killed five people and injured 19 others. The attack damaged an auto service station, four shops, and residential buildings in the region.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 66 as Trump announces Hormuz mission?
stories.summary: On day 66 of the Iran conflict, US President Donald Trump announced a new naval mission in the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement came after Iran said it had received a US response to its peace proposal, though diplomatic progress remains uncertain.

stories.title: This Energy Crisis Is Undoing the Last Ones
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the Western-led global order established after the 20th century's major energy crises is weakening. The current energy crisis is described as undermining the institutional and geopolitical frameworks that emerged from previous shocks.

stories.title: Iran warns US Navy to keep out of Hormuz after Trump says US will help stranded ships
stories.summary: Iran warned the U.S. Navy to stay out of the Strait of Hormuz after President Trump announced plans to assist stranded ships. Vessels have reportedly been trapped in the strait for over two months and are running low on food and supplies.

stories.title: Trump says US operation will aid ships stranded in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the U.S. would begin efforts on Monday to free ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz as a humanitarian gesture. He said hundreds of vessels and around 20,000 seafarers have been trapped with dwindling food and supplies as Iran blocks passage through the waterway.

stories.title: Europe, Canada leaders hold Yerevan talks in Trump's shadow
stories.summary: European leaders and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney gathered in Yerevan, Armenia, for a European Political Community meeting. The summit agenda focused on the war in Ukraine and the Middle East, with U.S. President Trump's unpredictable foreign policy looming over the discussions.

stories.title: Oil tanker hijacking stokes fears of new disruption in Gulf region
stories.summary: An oil tanker hijacking in the Gulf region has heightened concerns about potential collaboration between Somali pirates and Yemen's Houthi forces. The attack stoked fears of new disruptions to maritime shipping in the area.

stories.title: Australian inquiry opens public hearings into Bondi Beach shooting
stories.summary: A federal royal commission opened public hearings in Australia into the December shooting at a Hanukkah festival near Bondi Beach in Sydney that killed 15 people. The inquiry heard that Sydney's Jewish community had feared a catastrophic attack as antisemitic incidents rose. Two gunmen carried out the attack.

stories.title: Asia View: Taiwan’s President reaches Eswatini after China-linked travel hurdles
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te arrived in Eswatini, one of Taiwan's few diplomatic allies in Africa. The trip was delayed after several countries reportedly withdrew overflight permission under pressure from China.

stories.title: China says to ignore US sanctions even as Trump visit nears
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce ordered Chinese companies to ignore U.S. sanctions imposed on five oil refiners accused of purchasing Iranian crude, calling the measures a violation of international law. The directive came less than two weeks before a scheduled presidential summit.

stories.title: Can Malaysia’s Umno reclaim role as pillar of Malay political power with solo election bid?
stories.summary: Malaysia's UMNO, led by President Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, announced that its Barisan Nasional coalition is "almost certain" to contest the next general election independently, ending its junior partnership role after more than three years as it seeks to rally Malay-Muslim support.

stories.title: China, Indonesia launch cross-border QR payments – a boost for the global yuan?
stories.summary: China and Indonesia launched a cross-border QR payment system allowing users of apps like Alipay and Indonesia's QRIS to make retail payments in either country using home currencies. The initiative advances Beijing's efforts to internationalize the yuan and reduce U.S. dollar dependence.

stories.title: ‘Point of no return’: New Orleans relocation must start now due to sea level, study finds
stories.summary: A new study warns that New Orleans has reached a "point of no return" due to sea-level rise and wetland erosion in southern Louisiana. The authors say the city could be surrounded by the Gulf of Mexico before the end of the century and urge immediate relocation planning.

stories.title: Jailed for Palestine, Amu Gib is running for local UK elections
stories.summary: Amu Gib, a UK-based activist jailed for pro-Palestine activism, is running as a candidate in local UK elections. The candidacy follows a tradition of imprisoned individuals contesting elections to challenge state authority.

stories.title: German chancellor downplays row with Trump after troop drawdown announced
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz downplayed tensions with President Trump after the U.S. announced a withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany, its largest European base. Merz denied any link between his criticism of U.S. war planning in Iran and the drawdown, reaffirming Germany's commitment to the transatlantic alliance.

stories.title: 'Project freedom': Trump says the US will 'guide' stranded ships from the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump announced "Project Freedom," a U.S. effort to guide stranded ships out of the Iran-controlled Strait of Hormuz, involving hundreds of vessels and some 20,000 seafarers. Iran denounced the operation as a ceasefire violation. Few operational details were provided.

stories.title: Defence in focus at European Political Community Summit in Yerevan
stories.summary: Leaders from nearly 50 countries, including the EU's 27 member states and partners, convened in Yerevan, Armenia, for the eighth European Political Community summit. Discussions focused on economic and energy security, with the Ukraine war and the Middle East situation topping the agenda.

stories.title: War update: 148 clashes on front lines, fiercest fighting near Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, Huliaipole
stories.summary: Ukraine's military recorded 148 combat engagements with Russian forces along the front lines on May 3. The fiercest fighting was concentrated near Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, and Huliaipole.

stories.title: Three cruise ship passengers die in suspected hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: Three passengers died and three others fell ill on a Netherlands-based cruise ship due to a suspected hantavirus outbreak. The ship departed from Argentina roughly three weeks earlier with around 150 passengers and had stopped in Antarctica and other locations en route to Cape Verde.

stories.title: Lebanon's food security crisis and displacement 'going to have a lasting effect'
stories.summary: The World Food Programme's Lebanon Deputy Country Director Anne Valand described a deepening crisis driven by conflict displacement, agricultural disruption, and funding shortfalls. She reported that 1.24 million people in Lebanon face acute hunger, the highest level ever recorded in the country.

stories.title: May 9 in Moscow without weapons — and maybe with Ukrainian drones, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: At the European Political Community summit in Yerevan, President Zelensky said Russia's May 9 Victory Day parade in Moscow would proceed without military hardware. He suggested Ukrainian drones could fly over Moscow during the event.

stories.title: Pakistan’s AI reckoning
stories.summary: Pakistan has announced a nationwide AI training programme and committed $1 billion in AI investment by 2030 as part of the Islamabad AI Declaration unveiled during Indus AI Week 2026, signaling efforts to prepare its workforce for the AI transition.

stories.title: Coalition accused of secretly giving big tobacco lobbyists private platform in parliament
stories.summary: A Senate committee in Australia heard closed-session testimony from representatives of tobacco company Philip Morris regarding the illegal tobacco trade. Anti-smoking campaigners accused the Coalition of secretly giving big tobacco lobbyists a private platform in parliament, saying it undermines over 15 years of public health precedent.

stories.title: War on Iran has triggered a fundamental crisis of trust in the nuclear non-proliferation treaty
stories.summary: An opinion piece by Seyed Hossein Mousavian argues that the war on Iran has undermined trust in the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. Iran accused Israel and the US of attacking its nuclear facilities, highlighting what the author describes as flaws in the treaty's protections.

stories.title: NYT: Growing number of African men sign up for civilian jobs in Russia and end up on the Ukrainian front line
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that a growing number of African men are being recruited through fake civilian job postings on WhatsApp and Telegram, then forced to fight on the front lines in Russia's war against Ukraine. The employment contracts are written in Russian.

stories.title: A long war?
stories.summary: An analysis discusses the uncertainty surrounding the duration of the Iran war, now in its third month. Peace talks between the US and Iran, mediated by Pakistan in Islamabad, have stalled after a single face-to-face meeting.

stories.title: Driver arrested after wife killed in crash at Hong Kong border checkpoint
stories.summary: A 67-year-old driver was arrested after his vehicle lost control at the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge border checkpoint, striking traffic cones and a kiosk before overturning. His 62-year-old wife, a passenger, was killed in the early-morning accident near 80 Shun Wan Road.

stories.title: One killed, 12 injured in Russian attacks on Kherson region over past 24 hours
stories.summary: One person was killed and 12 others, including a child, were injured in the Kherson region over the past 24 hours due to Russian attacks. The strikes targeted areas across the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Are European automakers driving into the defense market? Analysts say to tap the brakes.
stories.summary: Analysts caution against expectations that European automakers will significantly pivot to defense production. One expert suggests car companies may participate in defense manufacturing as long as substantial EU or private funding remains available, but a major shift is unlikely.

stories.title: Interlinked crises
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines three interlinked Middle Eastern crises—the stalled Iran war, the Lebanese conflict, and Gaza's humanitarian situation—all involving either direct US military action or Washington-backed Israeli operations.

stories.title: Morocco king names son to senior defence post
stories.summary: Morocco's King Mohammed VI appointed his son to a senior defense post. The move mirrors the king's own experience in 1985, when his father King Hassan II gave him a similar military role as crown prince.

stories.title: Iran warns US to stay out of Hormuz after Trump says US will ‘guide’ ships
stories.summary: President Trump announced that the US will launch "Project Freedom" on Monday to guide stranded commercial ships out of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran warned the US to stay out of the waterway, saying any American military presence would violate ceasefire terms.

stories.title: Europe seeks to ‘take charge’ of its own defense as US to cut presence of troops
stories.summary: The EU foreign policy chief said the timing of Washington's announcement to reduce US troop presence in Europe was a surprise. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte acknowledged US disappointment with European responses to the Iran war, as European leaders discussed taking greater charge of their own defense.

stories.title: Iran: US Hormuz escort plan would breach ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian officials stated that the U.S. plan to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz under Project Freedom would constitute a breach of the ceasefire. Tehran reiterated it would not concede its position on control of the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Hong Kong media outlet cleared of tax evasion faces ‘unfair’ HK$40,000 costs
stories.summary: A Hong Kong online media outlet was cleared of tax evasion after a year-long review by the Inland Revenue Department, but incurred HK$40,000 in accounting fees. The Hong Kong Journalists Association called the process an unfair burden on faultless media and noted it had been required to prepay HK$730,000 in taxes.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,120 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost approximately 1,120 troops killed or wounded over the past 24 hours. Total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,335,150 personnel as of May 4, 2026.

stories.title: 167 flights, one country — how Russia turned Algeria into its African air bridge – investigation
stories.summary: An investigation by Defense News tracked 167 flights by Russian shadow airlines to Algeria over 14 months, linking aircraft manufacturing plants associated with Su-57 and Su-35 jets to Algerian military bases. Some flights continued onward to Niger and Guinea.

stories.title: United Airlines plane hits light pole on landing at Newark airport
stories.summary: A United Airlines plane struck a light pole while landing at Newark Liberty International Airport. No passenger injuries were reported in the incident.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest 21 over sacrifice attempt near Al-Aqsa Mosque
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested 21 people suspected of attempting to bring a sacrificial goat to the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem's Old City. The incident, linked to the observance of Pesach Sheni, was the second such attempt in two months; ritual sacrifice at the site is prohibited.

stories.title: Cheap Missiles, Not Drones, Will Win the Next Air War
stories.summary: An analysis argues that NATO's increasing investment in drones may be misplaced, as Russia is converting slow Shahed-type drones into faster, turbojet-powered missile-like systems in Ukraine. The shift is complicating Ukrainian air defenses and suggests cheap missiles may prove more decisive than conventional drones in future air warfare.

stories.title: London schools trialling VR to relieve pupils’ stress
stories.summary: All 15 secondary schools in the London borough of Sutton are trialling virtual reality headsets made by Phase Space in partnership with the local NHS mental health trust. The pilot program aims to help pupils manage stress related to exams, ADHD, and difficult home situations.

stories.title: How ‘lost’ Yiddish songs from a wartime ghetto in Ukraine revive links to Shanghai’s past
stories.summary: Yiddish Glory, a project by University of Toronto academic Anna Shternshis and musician Psoy Korolenko, will perform recovered anti-fascist Yiddish songs from a World War II Ukrainian ghetto in Shanghai, Hong Kong, and South Korea. Shanghai was chosen partly because some 18,000 Jewish refugees sheltered there during the Nazi era.

stories.title: Doubling down on lithium
stories.summary: An analysis discusses Pakistan's growing lithium-ion battery demand driven by electric vehicles, solar storage, and grid applications. The country's current lithium-ion ecosystem remains structurally shallow despite significant future potential.

stories.title: Minister vows to remove hurdles faced by investors
stories.summary: Federal Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal convened a meeting in Islamabad to review the situation after Chinese company Han Geng Group announced it would close all operations in Pakistan and China, including a factory in Gwadar, citing administrative and policy hurdles.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A morning briefing highlighted the Strait of Hormuz as the main flashpoint, with the US planning a naval escort mission dubbed "Project Freedom" and Iran issuing sharp warnings against any American entry. Fighting continued in southern Lebanon while diplomatic efforts remained uncertain.

stories.title: Kenya: Finance Bill 2026 Ends KQ Tax Relief, Widens Digital Tax Net
stories.summary: Kenya's proposed Finance Bill 2026 would end tax relief for Kenya Airways and significantly expand the country's tax reach into digital payments, software, and card transaction ecosystems.

stories.title: Queensland government in ‘integrity crisis’ over alleged undisclosed affair between two ministers, opposition says
stories.summary: Queensland's opposition accused the state's LNP government of an integrity crisis over an allegedly undisclosed personal relationship between Olympic Games Minister Tim Mander and Child Safety Minister Amanda Camm. Both ministers said they were not in a relationship when they were sworn in.

stories.title: Former New York City mayor Giuliani hospitalised in critical condition
stories.summary: Former New York City mayor Rudy Giuliani, 81, has been hospitalized in critical condition. Giuliani gained widespread recognition for his leadership following the September 11, 2001, Al-Qaeda attacks on New York City.

stories.title: Govt urged to reduce tax on milk
stories.summary: At a pre-budget consultation in Islamabad, Pakistan's government was urged to reduce the general sales tax on milk to support child development. The dairy association noted that an 18% GST had led to a 27% decline in the sector.

stories.title: Drone slams into Moscow high-rise 6 km from Kremlin — Sobyanin says no casualties, airports halt operations
stories.summary: A drone struck a high-rise building on Mosfilmovskaya Street in Moscow, approximately 6 kilometers from the Kremlin. Moscow Mayor Sobyanin reported no casualties, but airport operations were temporarily halted. Russia claimed 117 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight.

stories.title: Israeli military orders evacuations in four south Lebanon towns
stories.summary: The Israeli military ordered residents of Qana, Debaal, Qaaqaait al-Jisr, and Srifa in southern Lebanon to evacuate, warning of possible attacks. Spokesperson Avichay Adraee posted the announcement, instructing residents to move at least 1,000 meters to open areas.

stories.title: Three dead after monster truck crashes into crowd
stories.summary: At least three people were killed and 38 injured when a monster truck crashed into a crowd at a show in Colombia.

stories.title: Russia launches 868 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region over past day, 11 injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 868 strikes targeting 51 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over the past 24 hours. The attacks injured 11 people, including two children.

stories.title: AI cost-cutting not a legal excuse to fire workers, Chinese court says
stories.summary: A court in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, China, ruled that a company cannot legally fire an employee solely because AI could perform the role more cheaply. The case involved a 35-year-old fintech worker surnamed Zhou who was dismissed after refusing a demotion and pay cut tied to AI replacement.

stories.title: Still in stabilisation mode
stories.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan raised its policy rate by 100 basis points to 11.5%, signaling a preference for stability over growth as April inflation reached 10.9%, hitting double digits for the first time in 21 months.

stories.title: Three dead from suspected outbreak of hantavirus on Atlantic cruise ship
stories.summary: Three people have died from a suspected hantavirus outbreak linked to an Atlantic cruise ship. South Africa's health ministry confirmed that one patient in intensive care in Johannesburg tested positive for hantavirus, a rare disease typically spread through contact with infected rodents.

stories.title: Crew of Iranian ship seized by US forces evacuated to Pakistan, gov’t says
stories.summary: Twenty-two crew members from the Iranian vessel MV Touska, which was seized by US forces, have been evacuated to Pakistan for repatriation, according to government officials.

stories.title: Drone hits upscale Moscow tower as Russian capital readies for Victory Day parade
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a residential tower on Mosfilmovskaya Street in an upscale Moscow district, roughly 6–8 kilometers from the Kremlin. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said air defenses repelled two drones, and emergency services responded. No casualties were reported. The strike came ahead of Russia's annual Victory Day parade.

stories.title: Tanker hit by 'unknown projectiles' off UAE coast: U.K. maritime agency
stories.summary: A tanker was struck by unknown projectiles off the coast of the UAE, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency. The incident occurred amid a deadlock in US-Iran peace negotiations since a ceasefire took effect on April 8.

stories.title: Jerusalem Christians worried after attack on nun by Jewish extremist
stories.summary: A Jewish extremist attacked a Catholic nun in Jerusalem, shoving her to the ground in an incident captured on CCTV and widely shared. Christian worshippers at Saint Stephen's Basilica described it as the latest example of mounting religious hostility in the city.

stories.title: Iran threatens action against US presence in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's armed forces warned that all ships must coordinate with Iranian military forces when transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran declared that security of the strait remains under the control of the Islamic Republic's armed forces and urged commercial vessels not to transit without coordination.

stories.title: The Illusion of Sovereignty: How International Law and Big Tech are Eroding the State
stories.summary: An essay argues that modern state sovereignty is being eroded by two forces: international law constraints and dependence on private-sector digital infrastructure. The authors, drawing on firsthand experience from Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contend that states face catastrophic consequences in wartime when access to critical technology platforms is lost.

stories.title: UAE’s bumpy divorce from Opec
stories.summary: The UAE left OPEC after nearly six decades of membership, weakening the organization's capacity to influence global oil markets. The UAE held OPEC's second-largest spare capacity behind Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Ministries told to surrender unspent funds
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ministry of Finance directed all ministries, departments, and autonomous bodies to surrender unspent allocations within 10 days. The move aims to finalize revised estimates for FY2025-26 and prepare budget estimates for FY2026-27.

stories.title: Top diplomats from Iran and Pakistan stress on regional stability
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar and Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi held a phone call discussing regional stability and Islamabad's mediation efforts. Araghchi praised Pakistan's constructive role, while Dar affirmed that diplomacy remains the only viable path toward peace.

stories.title: US launches Project Freedom in Strait of Hormuz with 15,000 troops and over 100 aircraft
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command launched Project Freedom, an operation to restore navigation through the Strait of Hormuz involving approximately 15,000 troops and over 100 aircraft. The operation aims to secure the strategic waterway amid ongoing tensions with Iran.

stories.title: Search underway for two missing US troops in Morocco
stories.summary: Two US service members went missing near Tan Tan in southern Morocco during the African Lion joint military exercises. US Africa Command and Moroccan Royal Armed Forces launched coordinated search-and-rescue operations near the Cap Draa training site.

stories.title: Russia’s new jet-powered Geran-4 just met Ukraine’s STING interceptor: Who won?
stories.summary: Ukraine's STING interceptor engaged Russia's new jet-powered Geran-4 drone, which uses a turbojet engine rather than a standard propeller. The encounter tested both nations' evolving drone and counter-drone capabilities.

stories.title: Pak-China expand ties across sectors
stories.summary: President Asif Zardari's week-long visit to China focused on recalibrating Pakistan's bilateral partnership around investment, industrial cooperation, and technology transfer. The visit signals a new phase with Pakistani provinces playing a greater role in trade and investment ties.

stories.title: Former NYC Mayor Giuliani hospitalised in ‘critical condition’
stories.summary: Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani has been hospitalized and is reported to be in critical but stable condition. President Trump praised Giuliani as a "true warrior" following news of his hospitalization.

stories.title: A look at the US military presence in Europe as Trump seeks to withdraw troops from Germany
stories.summary: President Trump's decision to withdraw thousands of U.S. troops from Germany has drawn attention to the broader American military presence in Europe. The forces serve as a deterrent to Russia and enable U.S. power projection globally. Analysts are assessing the implications of the planned drawdown.

stories.title: ICE operation in Brooklyn sparks skirmishes and complaints
stories.summary: An immigration enforcement operation by ICE in Brooklyn, New York, sparked skirmishes with demonstrators. One protester smashed the rear window of an ICE vehicle, and officers sustained minor injuries during the confrontation.

stories.title: Nigeria: Terrorists Burn Down Military Camp, Vehicles in Zamfara
stories.summary: Terrorists attacked and burned down a military camp and vehicles in Nigeria's Zamfara state. The assault reportedly aimed to seize the town during active trading at a popular weekly market.

stories.title: Why Kim Jong Un Won’t Pick Up the Phone and What to Do About It
stories.summary: An analysis argues the Trump administration should adopt a new strategy toward nuclear-armed North Korea, sharpening incentives and raising stakes rather than relying on legacy approaches. The piece contends that the traditional U.S. policy has created rather than reduced risk.

stories.title: Jemima ‘plans  to remarry’
stories.summary: British social activist Jemima Goldsmith, the ex-wife of Imran Khan, is reportedly engaged to Irish-Australian financier Cameron O'Reilly after a relationship of just over a year.

stories.title: Nigeria: PDP Convenes Emergency National Executive Committee Meeting Monday
stories.summary: Nigeria's Peoples Democratic Party Board of Trustees, led by Senator Adolphus Wabara, convened an emergency National Executive Committee meeting for Monday.

stories.title: Jewish continuity needs you. Donate to Jewish higher education - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored advertisement promoted donations to Jewish higher education institutions, framing support as a means of ensuring Jewish continuity and funding future community leaders.

stories.title: Kenya: Four Arrested After Failed Attempt to Steal Jet Fuel At Wilson Airport
stories.summary: Detectives from Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations arrested four suspects after foiling an attempted jet fuel theft at Wilson Airport in Nairobi.

stories.title: Two US soldiers missing after military exercises in Morocco
stories.summary: Two U.S. soldiers went missing during African Lion, the U.S. military's largest annual joint exercise in Africa, conducted in Morocco. The exercise involves more than 10,000 personnel from over 20 countries, including NATO allies.

stories.title: Russia plans to turn internet into state-controlled infrastructure – intelligence
stories.summary: Russia's Ministry of Digital Development is reportedly working on measures to convert the Russian internet segment into a fully state-controlled infrastructure. Ukrainian intelligence disclosed the plans, which aim to increase government oversight of online communications.

stories.title: Africa: Suspected Hantavirus Outbreak on Cruise Ship Kills 3 - WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reported that three people died in a suspected hantavirus outbreak linked to a cruise ship. The virus typically spreads through contact with urine or feces of infected rodents and can cause severe, sometimes fatal, lung infections.

stories.title: Sesame Street post honoring US Jews draws intense wave of antisemitic hate
stories.summary: A Sesame Street social media post honoring Jewish American Heritage Month drew a wave of antisemitic responses online. Influencer Dan Bilzerian called the video "Jewish supremacy," while other accounts compared it to propaganda.

stories.title: Jewish continuity needs you. Donate to Jewish higher education - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored appeal called for donations to Jewish higher education institutions, framing tax-deductible contributions as essential for training future leaders and preserving Jewish heritage.

stories.title: Japan PM says Iran war oil crisis having ‘enormous impact’ in Asia Pacific
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the oil crisis stemming from the Iran war is having an "enormous impact" on the Asia Pacific region. She made the remarks during a visit to Australia, where she signed energy supply agreements.

stories.title: Heeding Herzog, AG okays unconditional talks for plea deal in Netanyahu’s graft trial
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General approved unconditional talks for a possible plea deal in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial, following an offer by President Herzog to host negotiations. Netanyahu's lawyers had not yet responded to the president's proposal.

stories.title: Air raids, shelling reported across southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Lebanon's National News Agency reported Israeli forces bombed the towns of Khiam and Qantara in southern Lebanon overnight. Israeli drones flew over the area while forces dropped flares over Braachit and shelled areas near Yater, Majdel Selm, and other towns in the region.

stories.title: Ukraine remembers every journalist held in Russian captivity – Foreign Ministry
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry stated that the country continues to remember every journalist held in Russian captivity. Officials emphasized that democratic institutions remain a foundation of Ukraine's resilience even during the full-scale war.

stories.title: Malawi: Aid Cuts Hit Malawi Hard - IMF Warns of Rising Debt Pressure and Urgent Need for Reforms
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that global aid cuts are placing serious financial pressure on Malawi, exposing long-standing economic management weaknesses and raising concerns about rising debt.

stories.title: Rwanda: Tanzania, Rwanda Advance Ties
stories.summary: Tanzania and Rwanda advanced bilateral ties with discussions centering on trade, investment, logistics, security, and energy cooperation.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Support Mnangagwa's Constitutional Amendment Bill or Resign - Attorney General Tells Chiwenga
stories.summary: Zimbabwe's Attorney General Virginia Mabiza warned Cabinet members, reportedly directed at Vice President Constantino Chiwenga, against publicly opposing decisions made at the Cabinet level regarding President Mnangagwa's constitutional amendment bill.

stories.title: AJK PM grants land ownership to 1,000 families displaced by LoC shelling
stories.summary: Azad Jammu and Kashmir Prime Minister Raja Faisal Mumtaz Rathore announced ownership rights for more than 1,000 families displaced by Line of Control shelling in 1998 who had been living on state land near Mirpur since 2006.

stories.title: Hong Kong extends tax waiver for residents displaced by deadly Tai Po fire
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government extended a tax waiver for residents displaced by the deadly Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court, exempting them from the final tax for the 2025-26 assessment year following a similar waiver granted in December.

stories.title: Paralysed dancer Mo Li testifies in court for first time over Mirror concert accident
stories.summary: Hong Kong dancer Mo Li Kai-yin, paralysed after being struck by a giant screen at a Mirror concert at Hong Kong Coliseum in July 2022, testified in District Court for the first time during a damages assessment against Studiodanz.

stories.title: Dutch startup Intelic sets up drone marketplace for European militaries
stories.summary: Dutch startup Intelic has launched a drone marketplace called BASE aimed at European military customers. The platform allows defense ministries to explore drone systems ready for coalition use, with guaranteed interoperability between allied forces.

stories.title: North Korean women’s club to play rare football match in the South
stories.summary: North Korean women's football club Naegohyang FC will play South Korea's Suwon FC on May 20 in the semifinal of the Women's Asian Champions League. The match represents a rare sporting encounter between teams from the two Koreas.

stories.title: Rights group accuses Israel of torturing detained flotilla activists
stories.summary: Palestinian human rights organization Adalah accused Israeli forces of torturing two activists detained after the interception of the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla. Lawyer Lubna Tuma said activists Thiago Avila and Seif Abu Keshek were beaten, blindfolded, and forced to lie face down during detention.

stories.title: All-round hero Hardie helps Babar Azam’s Peshawar Zalmi win PSL 2026
stories.summary: Tom Hardie delivered an all-round performance of four wickets and 56 runs to lead Peshawar Zalmi to their second Pakistan Super League title in PSL 2026. Peshawar defeated Hyderabad Kingsmen by five wickets in the final.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: tanker hit by ‘projectiles’ in strait of Hormuz after Trump says US will help ‘guide’ stranded ships
stories.summary: A tanker was struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz after U.S. President Donald Trump announced the U.S. Navy would help guide stranded ships through the waterway. Iran's armed forces warned the U.S. Navy against entering the strait. Trump said any interference with the operation would be dealt with forcefully.

stories.title: How to escape Russia’s army: Soldiers serving in Ukraine seek a way out
stories.summary: Russia's military is facing a growing desertion crisis as soldiers serving in Ukraine seek ways to leave the army. The issue has intensified as Russian forces continue using large numbers of troops in wave attacks against Ukrainian defensive positions.

stories.title: Spanish prime minister’s plane makes emergency landing in Turkey
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's plane made an emergency landing in Turkey while he was en route to Armenia for a meeting of the European Political Community.

stories.title: US transfers crew of seized Iranian ship to Pakistan
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command said 22 crew members of the seized Iranian-linked vessel M/V Touska were transferred to Pakistan for repatriation to Iran. The ship had been intercepted after allegedly attempting to violate the U.S. naval blockade against Iran.

stories.title: Two dead after respiratory illness outbreak on cruise ship in atlantic
stories.summary: Two people have died following a respiratory illness outbreak on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean. South Africa's health ministry confirmed that one hospitalized patient in Johannesburg tested positive for hantavirus, a rare disease typically transmitted through contact with infected rodents.

stories.title: Why African leaders value seamless transcontinental links over US-China rivalry
stories.summary: African leaders are prioritizing seamless transcontinental transport links over US-China rivalry. While Washington frames the Lobito Corridor as countering Chinese influence, African governments seek to integrate it with Beijing-backed routes like the Tanzania-Zambia railway.

stories.title: China son calls mum to say he ‘might not return’ while saving driver from burning truck
stories.summary: A 24-year-old man named Zhang Jian from Shandong province, China, rescued a driver from a burning truck in the Baotashan Tunnel. During the rescue, he called his mother to say he "might not return," and the story has garnered widespread attention online.

stories.title: Three passengers dead, one case of hantavirus confirmed from Atlantic cruise ship, WHO says
stories.summary: The World Health Organization confirmed that three passengers have died and one case of hantavirus has been verified among passengers on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean. Six passengers in total fell ill.

stories.title: Iran executes three men accused of collaborating with Israeli Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed three men — Mehdi Rasouli, Mohammadreza Miri, and Ebrahim Dolatabadi — accused of collaborating with Israel's Mossad and inciting unrest during January protests in Mashhad. The charges included involvement in the killing of a security force member and actions against national security.

stories.title: Nigeria: 13 Inmates Set for Release At Keffi Correctional Centre
stories.summary: Thirteen inmates at the New Keffi Medium Security Custodial Centre in Nigeria are set to be released following an intervention by the Sunday and Omoikhere Orianran Foundation (SOOF).

stories.title: Nigeria: Xenophobia - Nigeria Warns Citizens Ahead of Monday Anti-Foreigner Protests in South Africa
stories.summary: The Nigerian Consulate General in Johannesburg issued a security advisory to Nigerian nationals in South Africa ahead of planned nationwide anti-foreigner protests scheduled for May 4, 2026.

stories.title: South Africa: 130 Nigerians Apply for Evacuation As Xenophobic Tensions Rise in South Africa
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government confirmed that 130 Nigerians in South Africa have applied for voluntary evacuation amid rising tensions linked to renewed anti-foreigner protests in parts of the country.

stories.title: Nigeria: Let Us End Internal Conflicts, Unnecessary Court Cases - Peter Obi
stories.summary: Peter Obi, the 2023 Labour Party presidential candidate in Nigeria, called on political actors to end internal party conflicts and unnecessary litigation, warning that such disputes are hindering national progress.

stories.title: Nigeria: U.S. Makes U-Turn, Lifts Visa Ban for Nigerian, Other Foreign Doctors
stories.summary: The Trump administration reversed a policy that had blocked many Nigerian and other foreign physicians from obtaining or renewing visas to practice in the United States. The change lifts a processing freeze linked to a prior travel ban.

stories.title: Nigeria: Atiku Warns Tinubu Against Squandering Oil Windfall, External Reserves
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Vice President Atiku Abubakar criticized President Bola Tinubu's economic management, warning against what he described as reckless depletion of external reserves to artificially support the naira.

stories.title: Britain set to enter talks to join the European Union’s $135 billion Ukraine loan
stories.summary: Britain is set to begin talks to join the European Union's approximately $135 billion loan to Ukraine. The arrangement could open opportunities for British businesses, particularly in the defense sector, to support Ukraine's needs.

stories.title: Nigeria: Xenophobia - Nigeria to Repatriate Citizens From South Africa
stories.summary: Nigeria's government announced plans to repatriate citizens from South Africa amid xenophobic tensions. Authorities confirmed that 130 Nigerians had already expressed willingness to return home.

stories.title: Rwanda: MPs Urge Recruitment Reforms As Less Than 1% of Applicants Get Jobs
stories.summary: More than 1.1 million Rwandans applied for government jobs in the 2024/2025 fiscal year, but only about 3,100 were hired. Members of Parliament called for reforms to improve the efficiency of public service recruitment.

stories.title: Nigeria: Presidency Mocks Peter Obi for Leaving ADC
stories.summary: Peter Obi announced his departure from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Nigeria but did not disclose which party he plans to join. The presidency responded by mocking his decision.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Urges Stronger Trade Systems Between Rwanda-Tanzania
stories.summary: President Paul Kagame called for stronger and more efficient trade systems between Rwanda and Tanzania as bilateral business activity continues to expand.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Condemns Killing of Mali's Defence Minister
stories.summary: Nigeria condemned the killing of Mali's Defence Minister, who died after sustaining injuries in a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) attack.

stories.title: Nigeria: Peter Obi Dumps ADC, Gives Reasons
stories.summary: Nigerian politician Peter Obi announced his departure from the African Democratic Congress party. Obi stated that his exit was not driven by personal grievances with party figures including former Senate President David Mark or former Vice President Atiku Abubakar.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Summons South African Ambassador Over Xenophobic Attacks
stories.summary: Nigeria summoned South Africa's ambassador over xenophobic attacks targeting African migrants, including Nigerians, in parts of South Africa. The diplomatic action followed reports of violent protests against foreign nationals in several South African locations.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Pirates Hijack Oil Tanker in Gulf of Aden, Second Strike in Weeks
stories.summary: Somali pirates hijacked an oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden, marking the second such attack in recent weeks. The incident signals a resurgence of piracy in one of the world's most critical shipping lanes near the coast of Yemen.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Army Defends Arrest of Activist Amid Allegations of Abuse
stories.summary: The Nigerian Army defended its arrest of an activist amid allegations of abuse during detention. Human rights activists and citizens have questioned whether the military's actions complied with legal standards for arresting and detaining civilians.

stories.title: South Korean team behind promising stroke research, treatment cites Chinese interest
stories.summary: South Korean scientists have identified a new treatment pathway for ischemic stroke involving oxidative stress-induced astrocytic collagen biosynthesis. The team reports that Chinese doctors have expressed interest in partnering to further develop the experimental drug. The research addresses one of the most difficult challenges in modern stroke medicine.

stories.title: Baby found dead at Wagga beach homeless encampment as mother and another infant taken to hospital
stories.summary: A baby was found dead in a tent at a homeless encampment near Wagga beach on the Murrumbidgee River in regional New South Wales, Australia, on Saturday. Police said there were no suspicious circumstances. A 37-year-old woman and a second infant were transported to hospital, and local officials called for action on the regional housing crisis.

stories.title: Japan sees largest protest in support of pacifist constitution as PM Takaichi pushes revisions
stories.summary: Japan saw its largest demonstrations in support of the pacifist constitution as Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called for discussions on revising the post-World War II document. Speaking during a visit to Vietnam, Takaichi said the constitution should be updated to reflect current demands. Nationwide protests were held opposing any changes.

stories.title: Medicine prices surge in Iran after war, shortages reported
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders reported that medicine prices in Iran have risen sharply due to war-related supply chain disruptions. The healthcare system, previously able to meet needs with locally manufactured supplies, is now under increased pressure from shortages and rising costs.

stories.title: Iran warns of ceasefire violation as US plans to escort Hormuz ships
stories.summary: Iran warned of a potential ceasefire violation as the United States announced plans to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz. A U.S. official described the escort effort as a humanitarian gesture intended to assist countries not directly involved in the war.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran talks ‘very positive,’ US to ‘guide’ ships through Hormuz from May 4
stories.summary: President Trump described US-led efforts to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz beginning May 4 as a 'humanitarian gesture' aimed at assisting neutral countries not involved in the Iran war. He called ongoing discussions with Iran 'very positive.'

stories.title: Kenya: Death Toll From Floods Climbs to 18, With Eastern Region Worst Hit
stories.summary: The death toll from ongoing floods across Kenya has risen to 18, with most fatalities caused by drowning. The eastern region has been the worst affected as heavy rains continue to impact multiple parts of the country, according to the Ministry of Interior.

stories.title: Two us soldiers missing in morocco, feared to have fallen into ocean during training exercise
stories.summary: Two U.S. soldiers went missing in Morocco and are feared to have fallen into the ocean during a training exercise. They were participating in African Lion, the U.S. military's largest annual joint exercise in Africa involving over 10,000 personnel from more than 20 countries.

stories.title: Panic in Philippines as Mayon volcano ashfall blankets towns in total darkness
stories.summary: Over 300 families were evacuated after Mayon volcano in the Philippines produced massive ashfall over the weekend, blanketing nearby towns in darkness. Philippine officials said no explosive eruption occurred, but lava deposits on the southwestern slope collapsed, triggering a pyroclastic flow of hot rocks, ash, and gas. Mayon has been erupting mildly on and off since January.

stories.title: Uganda: 28 Arrested in Kisoro Illegal Mining Crackdown, 25 Rwandan Nationals Among Suspects
stories.summary: Police in Kisoro District, Uganda, arrested 28 people during an operation targeting illegal mining at Kirwa Wolfram Mines. Twenty-five of those detained were identified as Rwandan nationals who allegedly crossed into Uganda through unofficial border points.

stories.title: Nigeria: EU, Unicef Launch €1m Drive to Return 20,000 Conflict-Hit Sokoto Children to School
stories.summary: The European Union and UNICEF have launched a €1 million initiative in Sokoto State, Nigeria, aimed at returning more than 20,000 conflict-affected children to school over the next two years.

stories.title: Rwanda: Govt Launches Centre to Boost Financing for Women-Led MSMEs
stories.summary: The Rwandan government, through the National Bank of Rwanda, has established a national centre to support women-owned and women-led micro, small, and medium enterprises by improving financial advisory services and expanding access to funding.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Hails 'Brotherly' Ties With Tanzania, Pledges Deeper Cooperation
stories.summary: President Paul Kagame described Rwanda-Tanzania relations as "brotherly" and reaffirmed his commitment to deepening cooperation in trade, investment, and infrastructure between the two countries.

stories.title: Rwanda: Restricting Social Media Use for Minors Is a Timely Move
stories.summary: Rwanda is considering legislation to restrict social media access for children under 16, citing the need for policy to catch up with rapidly evolving digital realities affecting minors.

stories.title: Tanzania: Kagame's Tanzania Visit Underscores Strategic Weight of Bilateral Ties
stories.summary: President Paul Kagame made a one-day working visit to Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, on May 3, underscoring the growing strategic importance of Rwanda-Tanzania ties in regional trade, logistics, and economic integration in East Africa.

stories.title: Could Iran’s escalating economic crisis weaken negotiating position with US?
stories.summary: Iran faces a deepening economic crisis as war damages, inflation, currency devaluation, unemployment, and reduced oil revenues compound existing pressures. One estimate circulating in Iranian media puts the economic damage from U.S.-Israeli attacks at nine times the national budget. The crisis may weaken Tehran's negotiating leverage with the United States.

stories.title: IMO says 20,000 seafarers stranded in Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: The International Maritime Organization reported that approximately 20,000 seafarers are stranded on about 2,000 vessels in the Strait of Hormuz since the war on Iran began. At least 19 attacks have killed 10 seafarers and injured eight others, with affected ships including oil tankers, cargo vessels, and cruise liners.

stories.title: Detained Gaza aid flotilla activists arrive in Netherlands
