stories.summary: Two activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla, a Gaza-bound aid mission, arrived in the Netherlands after being released from Israeli custody. The activists had been detained following Israel's interception of the flotilla.

stories.title: Cheaper durians for China, Hong Kong helpers camp in tents: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post compiled a weekend roundup covering several Asia-related stories, including cheaper durian imports to China via a new Southeast Asia rail link, new Middle East freight routes bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, Hong Kong domestic helpers camping in tents on days off, and Beijing's efforts regarding its operatives in Taiwan.

stories.title: Jim Chalmers rules out fuel excise extension and downplays hopes for tax relief in ‘most responsible’ budget yet
stories.summary: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers ruled out extending the 26-cent fuel excise cut and tempered expectations for additional tax relief in the upcoming May federal budget. Chalmers described it as the "most responsible" budget yet, warning there is limited room for further cost-of-living support while pledging it would help fight inflation.

stories.title: Iranian oil tankers reach Indonesian waters despite blockade
stories.summary: TankerTrackers.com reported that an Iranian-linked Very Large Crude Carrier named DERYA entered Indonesia's Lombok Strait heading toward the Riau Archipelago. The vessel reportedly evaded the U.S. Navy after a failed attempt to deliver approximately 1.88 million barrels of crude oil to India.

stories.title: US refuses to deploy Tomahawk missiles in Germany
stories.summary: The United States will not deploy a battalion equipped with long-range Tomahawk cruise missiles in Germany. The decision was confirmed by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who cited insufficient American stockpiles as the reason.

stories.title: Security or justice? Syria faces post-Assad reckoning after string of arrests
stories.summary: Syria's new post-Assad government arrested Amjad Youssef, a Syrian intelligence officer implicated in the 2013 Tadamon massacres of civilians. However, critics have accused the new authorities of "performative justice" and making deals with other suspects. Celebrations erupted in affected communities upon news of the arrest.

stories.title: Trump announces ‘Project Freedom’ to help stranded ships leave Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump announced "Project Freedom," a US operation to help stranded ships leave the Strait of Hormuz, set to begin Monday, May 4, 2026. Trump said US representatives are in discussions with Iran that could lead to a positive outcome for all parties.

stories.title: Iranian diplomat says ‘satisfactory’ deal must include compensation
stories.summary: Former Iranian ambassador to Lebanon Mojtaba Amani said Tehran will only accept a deal that includes compensation for war losses and reflects battlefield developments. He described Iran's 14-point proposal as its framework for ending the conflict and called demands for compensation from the U.S. and Israel logical.

stories.title: Poland has not received signals suggesting delays in Patriot deliveries, says defence minister
stories.summary: Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Warsaw has received no indications that potential delays in American weapons deliveries to Poland would affect planned Patriot missile system transfers.

stories.title: North Korea women's soccer club to make rare South Korea visit
stories.summary: A North Korean women's soccer club will travel to South Korea for a rare inter-Korean sports event this month. It marks the first time in eight years that a North Korean sports team will compete on South Korean soil.

stories.title: EU forging closer ties with Armenia as it sends experts to help counter Russian interference
stories.summary: The European Union is sending experts specialised in countering Russian propaganda and interference to Armenia, ahead of the bloc's first-ever summit with the country on Tuesday in Yerevan. The summit follows a pan-European gathering of approximately 45 leaders at the European Political Community meeting.

stories.title: Thousands of cancer patients in England to benefit from new immunotherapy jab
stories.summary: England's NHS announced that thousands of cancer patients annually will benefit from an injectable form of pembrolizumab, an immunotherapy treatment effective against several cancer types. The injection can be administered in under two minutes and works by blocking the PD-1 protein, enabling the immune system to attack cancer cells.

stories.title: Labour MPs say ‘endless drama’ of leadership speculation must stop
stories.summary: Labour MPs in the United Kingdom are calling for an end to leadership speculation surrounding Prime Minister Keir Starmer, as Downing Street pushes back against predictions of an imminent challenge. Some backbenchers warned that repeated briefings about potential leadership changes were alienating voters.

stories.title: AI helped Shenzhen judges handle cases 50% faster. Is this the future for China?
stories.summary: Shenzhen's Intermediate People's Court reported that AI-assisted tools helped judges process 50 percent more cases in 2025 than in 2024, with each judge handling an average of 744 cases. The court announced the pilot system will now be rolled out to courts in dozens of additional Chinese cities.

stories.title: Bondi beach was where her parents met – and where her father died defending his people
stories.summary: A royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion in Australia heard testimony from Sheina Gutnick, daughter of Reuven Morrison, who was killed while defending others during an alleged terrorist attack at Bondi Beach. Gutnick was the first witness at the commission's opening day of public hearings.

stories.title: Australian Jews recount harrowing stories in 1st public hearing in inquiry into Bondi massacre
stories.summary: Australia's Royal Commission into the Bondi massacre held its first public hearing, with members of the Jewish community recounting experiences of the attack. Witnesses described a surge in antisemitic incidents since the Hamas attack that triggered the Gaza war.

stories.title: Oil prices flat as Trump’s plan for Strait of Hormuz fails to calm market
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices remained largely flat after President Trump announced a maritime operation dubbed Project Freedom aimed at securing the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement failed to significantly move energy markets.

stories.title: Russians coordinate disinformation campaign against Defense Minister Fedorov
stories.summary: Ukraine's SPRAVDI Center for Strategic Communications and Information Security exposed a coordinated Russian disinformation campaign targeting Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. The center said Russia orchestrated the effort to undermine the minister.

stories.title: US Senator Graham rejects Iran offer, backs diplomacy with pressure
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham called Iran's latest peace proposal "utterly ridiculous" and accused Tehran of stalling negotiations. Graham endorsed President Trump's Operation Freedom maritime initiative aimed at restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: In Malaysia, Anwar’s former ally Rafizi Ramli grilled over US$278 million Arm chip deal
stories.summary: Malaysia's Anti-Corruption Commission questioned former economy minister Rafizi Ramli on Monday over a US$278 million semiconductor deal with British chip designer Arm Holdings. Rafizi, a former senior figure in Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's People's Justice Party, is among multiple ministers and officials swept up in the politically sensitive inquiry.

stories.title: White House posts Trump's photo with ‘I have all the cards’ message
stories.summary: The White House posted an image of President Trump holding Uno cards captioned "I have all the cards" amid tensions with Iran. Trump separately announced on Truth Social that the U.S. Navy would escort ships trapped in the Strait of Hormuz under a humanitarian effort called Project Freedom.

stories.title: Rudy Giuliani hospitalized in ‘critical but stable condition’, his spokesman says
stories.summary: Former New York City mayor Rudy Giuliani, 81, was hospitalized in critical but stable condition. He had told his talk show audience on Friday that his voice was affected by illness.

stories.title: Tanker hit by projectiles off UAE coast, maritime agency says
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a tanker was struck by unknown projectiles off Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates, though all crew were reported safe. Separately, a bulk carrier was attacked by multiple small craft approximately 11 nautical miles west of Sirik off Iran's coast.

stories.title: Iran says 37,000 buildings repaired after war damage
stories.summary: Iran's Housing Foundation reported it has repaired approximately 37,000 homes and commercial buildings damaged during the war. The Iranian Red Crescent Society said more than 125,000 civilian structures were destroyed or severely damaged, and 339 medical facilities were hit.

stories.title: Merz says no US Tomahawk deployment in Germany
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that the United States will not deploy Tomahawk cruise missiles in Germany for now, citing insufficient U.S. stockpiles. The deployment had been pledged under former President Biden in 2024. Merz also described a planned withdrawal of over 5,000 U.S. troops as expected.

stories.title: Ultra-low-priced tours exploiting mainland Chinese visitors survive despite crackdown
stories.summary: Ultra-low-priced tour packages targeting mainland Chinese visitors to Hong Kong persist despite tighter government regulations, according to an investigation by the South China Morning Post. Hong Kong's Travel Industry Authority recently revoked the licences of a travel agency and tour guide over suspected coerced-shopping cases between January and March.

stories.title: Iran reviewing US response to 14-point plan; Trump says Washington having 'very positive' discussions with Tehran
stories.summary: Iran said it is reviewing a US response to its 14-point proposal, relayed via Pakistan, while President Trump described ongoing discussions with Tehran as 'very positive.' Trump also announced plans to guide stranded vessels out of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Police brace for unrest at Meron after drastic cutbacks to Lag B’Omer revelry
stories.summary: Israeli police blocked roads and prepared for potential unrest at Meron ahead of Lag B'Omer celebrations following significant cutbacks to the annual event. Some ultra-Orthodox leaders called on attendees to carry pepper spray and tasers, while an alternate bonfire lighting was planned in East Jerusalem.

stories.title: Iran says it has received US response to its latest offer for talks
stories.summary: Iran confirmed it received the US response to its latest diplomatic offer, delivered through Pakistani intermediaries. US President Trump indicated he would likely reject the Iranian proposal, saying Tehran has "not paid a big enough price."

stories.title: Energy infrastructure facility hit in Mariupol; part of city left without power, says Andriushchenko
stories.summary: An energy infrastructure facility in occupied Mariupol, Ukraine, was hit during a nighttime attack, leaving part of the city without power. Petro Andriushchenko, an adviser to the city's exiled mayor, reported the strike and resulting outage.

stories.title: IDF captures Palestinian man who murdered son, burned his body, infiltrated Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli military captured a Palestinian man accused of murdering his 12-year-old son and burning the body. The suspect reportedly stabbed the boy near an agricultural area in the village of Beit Ur, near Ramallah in the West Bank, before infiltrating Israel.

stories.title: New drama ‘The Eichmann Trial’ at Jerusalem’s Beit Ha’am takes same stage as actual trial
stories.summary: A new theatrical production called "The Eichmann Trial" is being performed through May 4 at Jerusalem's Beit Ha'am, the same venue where Adolf Eichmann's actual 1961 trial took place. The drama explores the historic hearing and early German-Israeli relations.

stories.title: United Airlines Boeing 767 jet hits light pole, truck while landing at Newark
stories.summary: A United Airlines Boeing 767 carrying 231 passengers and crew from Venice, Italy, clipped a light post and truck on a highway while on final approach to Newark Liberty International Airport on Sunday. The aircraft landed safely. The Federal Aviation Administration said it would investigate the incident.

stories.title: German chancellor downplays row with Trump after troop drawdown announced
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz downplayed a disagreement with US President Donald Trump following Washington's announcement of a troop drawdown. Merz stressed there was no connection between their policy differences and the planned reduction, emphasizing the importance of continued cooperation within NATO.

stories.title: Hong Kong Exchange Fund records smallest gain in 5 quarters amid Middle East crisis
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Exchange Fund posted its smallest quarterly investment gain in five quarters, earning HK$34.5 billion (US$4.4 billion) in Q1—56 percent lower than the same period a year earlier. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority attributed the decline partly to the Middle East crisis weighing on stock market performance. It was still the fund's fifth consecutive quarterly gain.

stories.title: Mainland Chinese students turn to Hong Kong universities amid gaokao, US visa worries
stories.summary: Hong Kong universities are attracting growing numbers of mainland Chinese students seeking alternatives to the highly competitive gaokao exam and amid uncertainties caused by US-China tensions. A recent report attributes the trend to geographic proximity, cultural familiarity, and career planning considerations.

stories.title: Europe, Canada leaders meet in Armenia amid uncertainty over US policy
stories.summary: European leaders and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney convened in Yerevan, Armenia, on Monday for a European Political Community summit. The talks focused on security challenges including the Iran conflict, the war in Ukraine, and shifting transatlantic relations amid growing uncertainty about U.S. policy under President Donald Trump.

stories.title: How South Korea is transforming way it bids farewell to migrants killed at workplace
stories.summary: South Korea is changing how it honors migrant workers killed in workplace accidents, as highlighted by a memorial at Incheon International Airport for Nguyen Van Tuan, a 23-year-old Vietnamese worker who died in a conveyor belt accident in Icheon, Gyeonggi province. K-Comwel President Park Jong-kil led the ceremony.

stories.title: Israeli strikes intensify in southern Lebanon, casualties reported
stories.summary: Israeli forces intensified air strikes on several towns in southern Lebanon, killing one person and injuring eight others, including four paramedics, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. Hezbollah said it launched drone and missile attacks on Israeli forces in towns including Al-Bayada, Al-Naqoura, Houla, and Al-Qantara. The Israeli military reported intercepting missiles fired toward the Upper Galilee.

stories.title: News live: Bell says royal commission will look at ‘ugly displays of hostility’ towards Jewish Australians as hearings begin
stories.summary: Australia's royal commission into antisemitism has begun hearings, with references to "ugly displays of hostility" toward Jewish Australians. Separately, Treasurer Jim Chalmers said next week's federal budget would not extend the fuel tax cut beyond June but includes contingencies for economic fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: US officials say China sent dual-use materials to Iran
stories.summary: The New York Times, citing US officials, reported that Chinese companies shipped dual-use materials to Iran with potential military applications. Washington expressed concern over the shipments. Officials noted that China has avoided taking a firm position on the Iran conflict due to competing strategic interests.

stories.title: Three dead in hantavirus outbreak aboard polar cruise ship from Ushuaia bound for Cape Verde
stories.summary: The World Health Organization confirmed three deaths from a hantavirus outbreak aboard the polar cruise ship MV Hondius, operated by Dutch company Oceanwide Expeditions. The vessel departed Ushuaia, Argentina, on March 20 and was bound for Praia, Cape Verde.

stories.title: Orsi follows Milei and Kast aboard USS Nimitz as opposition alleges unconstitutionality
stories.summary: Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi visited the US aircraft carrier USS Nimitz in international waters off Uruguay's coast, following similar visits by Argentine President Milei and Chilean President Kast. The visit was part of the US Navy's Southern Seas 2026 regional deployment.

stories.title: Former New York mayor Rudy Giuliani in critical condition in hospital
stories.summary: Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani, 81, has been hospitalized in critical but stable condition, according to spokesperson Ted Goodman. No details on the cause were disclosed. Giuliani gained prominence after the September 11, 2001 attacks and later served as an attorney for Donald Trump during challenges to the 2020 election results.

stories.title: Hamas, Board of Peace clash over disarmament agreement, enter impasse in negotiations - report
stories.summary: Hamas and the Board of Peace have reached an impasse in negotiations over a disarmament agreement. Hamas stated it would only relinquish weapons after the full implementation of phase one of the deal, which requires Israel to withdraw from Gaza.

stories.title: Partisans destroy enemy KamAZ truck supplying ammunition to frontline
stories.summary: Agents of the ATESH partisan movement sabotaged a KamAZ truck belonging to Russia's 2nd Separate Guards Motor Rifle Brigade in the temporarily occupied Luhansk region of Ukraine. The vehicle had been used to deliver ammunition, food, and equipment to Russian frontline positions.

stories.title: Health Ministry panel seeks to halt use of medical cannabis in smokable form
stories.summary: An Israeli Health Ministry panel recommended halting the use of medical cannabis in smokable form. The committee cited potentially harmful effects and a rising number of users as reasons for proposing stricter guidelines and more limited use of the drug.

stories.title: Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez’s plane makes emergency landing in Turkey
stories.summary: A plane carrying Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez made an emergency landing in Ankara, Turkey, on Sunday evening due to a technical issue. Sánchez had been traveling to Yerevan, Armenia, for a European Political Community summit. The Spanish delegation was expected to continue to Armenia on Monday.

stories.title: Venezuelans rally in more than 120 cities worldwide demanding release of political prisoners
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader and 2025 Nobel Peace laureate María Corina Machado organized a global day of mobilization on Sunday, with rallies held in dozens of Venezuelan cities and over 120 locations worldwide. Demonstrators demanded the release of political prisoners and sought international attention for Venezuela's human rights situation.

stories.title: Peshawar Zalmi beat Hyderabad Kingsmen by 5 wickets, lift PSL trophy a second time
stories.summary: Peshawar Zalmi won their second Pakistan Super League title, defeating debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen by five wickets in the final at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium. Aaron Hardie's all-round performance led the victory.

stories.title: Former police spokesman John Tse set for top government media role
stories.summary: Former Hong Kong police spokesman John Tse Chun-chung is expected to be promoted to lead the government's Information Services Department on a three-year contract. Tse, who became widely known during the 2019 protests, has served as the government's information coordinator since 2024.

stories.title: China bride’s botched cold treatment causes 3-month coma, wakes 2 days before wedding
stories.summary: A 24-year-old bride named Wang Ranran from Taian, Shandong province, China, fell into a three-month coma after a botched cold treatment in January. She regained consciousness just two days before her scheduled wedding to fiancé Zhang Xirui.

stories.title: US ‘suffocating’ Iran with blockade: Treasury chief
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declared that Washington is "suffocating" Iran's leadership through an economic blockade, describing the campaign as a strategy to pressure Tehran's government.

stories.title: Centcom mobilises aircraft, troops for Hormuz maritime mission
stories.summary: US Central Command announced it will begin supporting "Project Freedom" starting Monday to restore freedom of navigation for commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. The operation involves aircraft and troops and is coordinated through a new "Maritime Freedom Structure" initiative involving the Departments of State and War.

stories.title: Germany calls US key Nato partner amid tensions
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz described the United States as Germany's most important NATO partner amid rising tensions. His remarks followed Washington's announcement of a roughly 5,000-troop reduction from Germany, ordered by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reportedly in response to disagreements over the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Illegal ‘free party’ at French military site draws up to 40,000 ravers
stories.summary: Up to 40,000 people attended an illegal "free party" rave at a military firing range near Bourges, France. Authorities are responding to the unauthorized gathering at the active military site.

stories.title: Censorship in Russia’s cultural sphere intensifies – media
stories.summary: Russian authorities are intensifying censorship of the country's publishing industry and cultural sector. Reports indicate that books are being confiscated, and even classic works by Russian authors are being subjected to state censorship.

stories.title: UN rapporteur warns of ‘Israelisation of Europe’
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese warned of a broader "Israelisation of Europe" during a speech in Athens. She said Israel is leveraging its relationship with Greece to advance regional aims, accusing it of exploiting European insecurities to further its strategic interests.

stories.title: Netanyahu's trial: A-G agrees to meet PM's defense for possible plea bargain
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General agreed to meet with Prime Minister Netanyahu's defense team to explore a possible plea bargain in his long-running criminal trial. The meeting follows an invitation from President Herzog aimed at initiating preliminary discussions on resolving the divisive case.

stories.title: Glimmer of hope in Hormuz Strait as fragile ceasefire holds: what happened overnight
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire has held into its third week, with signs of a potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump announced "Project Freedom" to help free stranded ships, set to begin Monday morning Middle East time.

stories.title: 2 men, including social activist, killed in separate attacks in KP's Bajaur
stories.summary: Two people, including social activist Malik Ziaur Rehman, were killed in separate armed attacks in Bajaur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Unidentified assailants shot Rehman near his residence in the Kohi area of Salarzai tehsil.

stories.title: In pictures: Glimpses of the star-studded HBL PSL 11 closing ceremony in Lahore
stories.summary: The 11th HBL Pakistan Super League closing ceremony took place at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium, featuring fireworks and performances by singers Aima Baig, Arif Lohar, and Atif Aslam before the final between Peshawar Zalmi and Hyderabad Kingsmen.

stories.title: Man found dead after driving car with improvised explosives into Portland athletics club
stories.summary: A man was found dead after driving a car loaded with improvised explosives into the Multnomah Athletic Club in Portland. Employees reported the incident shortly before 3 a.m. after the vehicle caught fire upon impact.

stories.title: Israel court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists amid abuse claims
stories.summary: An Israeli court ordered a two-day extension of detention for two foreign activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla intercepted by Israeli forces in international waters. The activists deny accusations against them, and their lawyers argue they were on a humanitarian mission. Allegations of abuse in custody have intensified the legal dispute.

stories.title: Ahead of Misri’s expected Nepal visit, Kathmandu expresses concern to India, China on Kailash yatra over Lipulekh
stories.summary: Nepal reiterated its territorial claim to Lipulekh Pass and raised concerns with India and China over the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra route ahead of an expected visit by Indian Foreign Secretary Misri to Kathmandu.

stories.title: Live: US to escort ships through Hormuz as Iran warns of ceasefire breach
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the United States will begin escorting stranded third-country vessels through the Strait of Hormuz starting Monday under a "Project Freedom" initiative. Iran responded by warning that any American interference would be considered a breach of the ceasefire between the two nations.

stories.title: Singapore software engineers with AI skills earn 25% more: ‘no longer nice-to-have’
stories.summary: Software engineers in Singapore with AI skills earn 13 to 25 percent more than their peers, according to a salary report by tech platform NodeFlair based on over 230,000 data points. The premium marks a shift from 2024, reflecting AI expertise becoming essential rather than optional.

stories.title: ‘Increasingly unsafe’: Australia’s in-home childcare program under threat from rising costs, advocate warns
stories.summary: Australia's publicly funded in-home childcare program, used by approximately 800 families, faces growing pressure from rising costs. Advocates warn the scheme is becoming increasingly unsafe, particularly for families in remote areas or those with children who cannot access mainstream care.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran warns Trump’s Hormuz mission will violate ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran protested after President Trump announced "Project Freedom," a US plan to escort stranded commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran warned that the mission would violate the existing ceasefire between the US and Iran.

stories.title: Sweden detains sanctioned tanker suspected of links to Russia’s shadow fleet
stories.summary: Swedish authorities detained a tanker in the Baltic Sea suspected of sailing under a false flag and belonging to Russia's sanctions-evading shadow fleet. The vessel is also listed under European Union sanctions.

stories.title: Iran warns US over Hormuz escort plan, says interference breaks ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian lawmaker Ebrahim Azizi warned that US involvement in managing traffic through the Strait of Hormuz would violate the ceasefire. He rejected what he called US attempts to shift blame and said the strait would not be managed under President Trump's plans.

stories.title: Former New York mayor Giuliani hospitalised in critical condition
stories.summary: Former New York City mayor and Trump adviser Rudy Giuliani, 81, has been hospitalized in critical but stable condition. His spokesman Ted Goodman did not disclose the cause of hospitalization or its duration.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines says it has nearly finished refunding customers after shuttering
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines announced it has nearly completed issuing refunds to customers whose flights were abruptly canceled when the budget carrier ceased operations on Saturday. The shutdown left thousands of passengers and staff stranded. The airline had been struggling financially for years, with rising jet fuel costs further undermining its viability.

stories.title: War update: 122 combat clashes, two frontline sectors see fiercest fighting
stories.summary: On May 3, Ukrainian defense forces recorded 122 combat engagements with Russian forces along the frontline. The heaviest fighting occurred in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors.

stories.title: Rudy Giuliani hospitalised in ‘critical but stable’ condition
stories.summary: Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani has been hospitalized and is in critical but stable condition, according to his spokesperson Ted Goodman. No details about the cause of hospitalization were provided. Goodman described Giuliani as "a fighter" and asked the public to pray for him.

stories.title: Elderly scam victims lose HK$850,000 on average, but ones who know finance lose more
stories.summary: Investment scams targeting elderly residents in Hong Kong rose 17 percent in the first quarter of 2026 compared to a year earlier, with average losses of HK$850,000 per victim. Police warned that better-educated retirees with investment experience were particularly vulnerable to fraudsters.

stories.title: Nobel laureate Mohammadi remains in critical condition in Iran, foundation says
stories.summary: Jailed Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi remained in critical condition in a cardiac care unit in northwestern Iran on Sunday. She had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days earlier, according to a foundation run by her family.

stories.title: Some Iranians fear the regime is now more entrenched - and ready for revenge
stories.summary: Iranians have expressed concern about potential increased repression by authorities once the current war ends. Citizens fear the regime may be more entrenched and prepared to retaliate against internal dissent in the post-conflict period.

stories.title: European leaders converge on Armenia as Russia looks on
stories.summary: European leaders gathered for two summits held in Armenia, a country traditionally considered Russia's closest regional ally. The convergence of European diplomatic activity in Yerevan signals shifting geopolitical dynamics as Moscow monitors developments.

stories.title: Noa Koler’s ‘Happy Place’ wins big in Israeli TV awards, rescheduled after Iran war
stories.summary: The Israeli public broadcaster Kan won 27 prizes at the belated 2025 Israeli Television Awards, which had been rescheduled due to the Iran war. Noa Koler's series "Happy Place" was among the top winners. Investigative journalist Ilana Dayan said the government was working to erase the memory of October 7 failures.

stories.title: Israeli raid in West Bank leaves 1 Palestinian dead, 4 wounded
stories.summary: A Palestinian man, Nayef Firas Ziad Samaro, 26, was killed and four others were seriously wounded during an Israeli military raid in Nablus in the occupied West Bank. The Palestinian Red Crescent reported that five people were hit by gunfire during the operation.

stories.title: Kenya death toll from floods, landslides rises to 18 people, police say
stories.summary: Kenya's national police service reported on Sunday that the death toll from flooding and landslides caused by heavy rains has risen to 18 people across the country.

stories.title: Bulk carrier attacked near Iran coast
stories.summary: Several small vessels attacked a bulk carrier near the coast of Iran. No further details on casualties or the identity of the attackers were immediately available.

stories.title: Trump says US in ‘very positive discussions’ with Iran over war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that his representatives are having 'very positive discussions' with Iran that could lead to an end to the war destabilizing the Middle East. The remarks followed earlier diplomatic signals from Iran's foreign ministry.

stories.title: Amsterdam bans public adverts for meat and fossil fuels
stories.summary: Amsterdam's local government has banned public advertisements for meat and fossil fuels, citing alignment with the Dutch capital's environmental targets.

stories.title: Thousands in India’s Manipur mark three years since ethnic clashes began
stories.summary: Thousands of people gathered in India's Manipur state to mark three years since ethnic violence broke out in the region. The protests highlighted ongoing tensions between communities in the northeastern state.

stories.title: ‘They know they’re safe’: beagles saved from US research facility after protests
stories.summary: Big Dog Ranch Rescue has arranged to purchase 1,500 beagles from Ridglan Farms, a dog breeding and research facility in Wisconsin that was the site of recent protests. The rescue organization's founder, Lauree Simmons, said the first dogs removed from the facility quickly warmed to their new caretakers.

stories.title: Hardie's 4-wicket haul puts Peshawar Zalmi in strong position, Hyderabad Kingsmen out for 129 runs
stories.summary: Bowling all-rounder Aaron Hardie took four wickets as Peshawar Zalmi bowled out Hyderabad Kingsmen for 129 runs in the HBL Pakistan Super League final at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium. Saim Ayub top-scored for Kingsmen with 54. Zalmi need 130 runs to win the PSL trophy.

stories.title: France backs Ukraine’s EU alignment but rules out ‘fast track’ to membership – Minister
stories.summary: France expressed support for Ukraine's gradual alignment with the European Union but ruled out any fast-track process for full EU membership, according to a French minister.

stories.title: Iran reviewing US response to 14-point proposal: state media
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry said it received the US response to its 14-point proposal via Pakistan and is reviewing it. A spokesperson said nuclear negotiations are not part of the current discussions. Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned that Washington faces a choice between a military operation or a negotiated deal.

stories.title: German Foreign Minister Wadephul, in call with Iranian counterpart, demands Hormuz reopening
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul spoke with his Iranian counterpart and demanded the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Germany expressed concern over the economic consequences of the strait's closure.

stories.title: Swedish coast guard seizes suspected false flag tanker in Baltic Sea
stories.summary: The Swedish Coast Guard seized a tanker in the Baltic Sea on Sunday suspected of belonging to Russia's so-called shadow fleet. The seizure near Stockholm is the latest in a series of similar enforcement actions by Swedish authorities in recent months.

stories.title: Paramilitary forces drone strike kills at least five near Sudan capital: rights group
stories.summary: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces carried out a drone strike near the Sudanese capital that killed at least five people, according to a rights group. The RSF, which has been fighting the Sudanese Army for over three years, did not immediately claim responsibility for the attack.

stories.title: Trump says ships blocked in Hormuz to be freed on Monday
stories.summary: President Trump announced that vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz would be allowed to depart starting Monday morning. He said he instructed US officials to prioritize the safe passage of ships and crews, while noting ongoing talks with Iran.

stories.title: After Maryland teacher’s death, 200-piece Judaica collection finds new life in Jewish museum
stories.summary: A 200-piece Judaica collection amassed over 35 years by Maryland teacher Deborah Brodie has been donated to the Capital Jewish Museum in Washington, DC, following her death. Brodie had used the collection as a hands-on educational tool for students with special needs.

stories.title: Nigerian, Beninese militias kill scores of herders
stories.summary: Security forces in Nigeria and Benin conducted operations targeting Fulani herding settlements, killing scores of herders. Personnel went door-to-door arresting young men suspected of being informants for al-Qaeda-linked group Ansaru, reportedly shooting those who resisted.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses bilateral ties, EU path with Czech PM Babiš
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš in Yerevan to discuss bilateral relations and Ukraine's path toward European Union integration.

stories.title: Israel court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of two activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla intercepted in international waters.

stories.title: 2 US Army soldiers missing after ‘African Lion’ military exercises in Morocco
stories.summary: Two US Army soldiers went missing in southwestern Morocco after going on a hike following the conclusion of the annual multinational 'African Lion' military exercises. US Africa Command confirmed the disappearances.

stories.title: Bai Chongen on China’s new economic paradigm and closing the US tech gap
stories.summary: Bai Chongen, dean of Tsinghua University's School of Economics and Management and a former Chinese central bank monetary policy committee member, discussed China's strategy to avoid economic stagnation, close the technology gap with the US, and foster innovation.

stories.title: Three dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise ship
stories.summary: Three passengers have died and one remains in intensive care after a suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard an Atlantic cruise ship. The World Health Organization reported that six passengers fell ill from the rodent-transmitted virus.

stories.title: IAEA to inspect lab near Zaporizhzhia NPP after reported attack
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency announced plans to inspect the External Radiation Control Laboratory near Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant after Russian forces controlling the site reported a drone strike on the facility.

stories.title: Palestinian man killed by Israel as his wife was giving birth
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed 26-year-old Naif Firas Ziad Samaro during a raid on Nablus in the occupied West Bank, according to Palestinian officials. The Palestinian Ministry of Health said he was struck in the head. His wife was in labour giving birth to their child at the time of his death.

stories.title: Heeding Herzog’s invitation, AG says she’s willing to discuss plea deal in Netanyahu trial
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara agreed to discuss a possible plea deal in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's criminal trial, responding to an invitation from President Isaac Herzog. She stipulated that talks must have no preconditions and must not affect ongoing court proceedings.

stories.title: Israel court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists; lawyers say pair subjected to 'severe physical abuse'
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of two foreign activists from a Gaza-bound flotilla for two days. The flotilla of over 50 vessels was intercepted by Israeli forces in international waters off Greece. Lawyers for the detained Spanish and other nationals alleged the pair were subjected to severe physical abuse.

stories.title: Student killed in missile strike on dormitory in Dnipro
stories.summary: A missile struck a dormitory at Dnipro National University in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro, killing a student.

stories.title: China’s Manus block a show of strength ahead of Xi-Trump summit
stories.summary: Beijing blocked Meta's $2 billion acquisition of Chinese-founded AI startup Manus and barred the company's two founders from leaving China. The move is seen as a demonstration of leverage ahead of a Xi Jinping–Trump summit amid shifting China-US business dynamics.

stories.title: Iran says US faces choice between 'impossible' military operation, 'bad deal'; Trump mulls peace proposal
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the United States must choose between an "impossible" military operation or a "bad deal" with Tehran. Negotiations have stalled since a Pakistan-brokered ceasefire took effect on April 8, with only one round of direct talks held in Islamabad. Tehran reportedly submitted a 14-point proposal to mediator Pakistan, which President Trump publicly dismissed.

stories.title: The longer the Iran war goes on, the greater the impact on inflation, the US central bank warns
stories.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari warned that a prolonged war involving Iran could increase inflation and constrain the US economy, particularly as disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz threaten global oil and gas flows.

stories.title: Ukraine ready for next round of trilateral talks, Zelensky says at meeting with Starmer
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, meeting with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer in Yerevan, stated that Ukraine is prepared for the next round of trilateral negotiations.

stories.title: Why Trump’s threat to pull even more US troops out of Germany is causing unease in Europe
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to withdraw additional American troops from Germany beyond the roughly 5,000 service personnel already ordered removed by the Pentagon. The move has generated unease among European allies concerned about the continent's security posture.

stories.title: ‘They see naked women’: Haredi leaders urge boycott of Tiberias mall over bikini ads
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) leaders in Tiberias, Israel, have called for a boycott of a local mall over bikini advertisements they deemed immodest. The city's deputy mayor pushed back against the proposed boycott, highlighting ongoing tensions between Haredi and secular communities.

stories.title: Why Israel’s uneasy Iran ceasefire may be better than it looks - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis examines whether US and Israeli capital markets may be adjusting to the prolonged standoff between the United States and Iran, suggesting the uneasy ceasefire could be more stable than it appears.

stories.title: Russian attack damages 35 houses in suburbs of Chornomorsk
stories.summary: A Russian strike on May 3 damaged 35 residential houses in the suburbs of Chornomorsk in Ukraine's Odesa region.

stories.title: Iran lawmaker says Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre‑war state
stories.summary: An Iranian lawmaker declared that the Strait of Hormuz will not revert to its pre-war status quo following the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. The statement signals Tehran's intent to maintain altered conditions in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Trump says US will ‘help free up’ ships stuck in Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that operations to free commercial ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz will begin on Monday. Trump warned that any interference with the effort would be met with a forceful response.

stories.title: German Chancellor downplays row with Trump after troop drawdown announced
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz downplayed a dispute with US President Trump over the Iran war and denied any link between their disagreement and Washington's announcement to reduce its military presence in Germany by 5,000 soldiers.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian drone attack in Zaporizhzhia rises to nine
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian drone attack on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia rose to nine, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Peshawar Zalmi win toss, opt to field first against debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen in PSL final
stories.summary: Peshawar Zalmi won the toss and chose to field first against debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen in the HBL Pakistan Super League season 11 final in Lahore on Sunday. Captain Babar cited the grassy pitch and said his team would aim to exploit the first six overs.

stories.title: Canada declares Khalistan extremists as ‘national security threat’
stories.summary: Canada's 2025 Public Report from the Canadian Security Intelligence Service has designated Khalistan extremist groups as a national security threat. The report was issued a year after the 40th anniversary of the Air India Flight 182 bombing, whose suspects had ties to such groups.

stories.title: Two US troops missing during African Lion exercise in Morocco, AFRICOM says
stories.summary: Two U.S. service members participating in the multinational African Lion 2026 exercise went missing near the Cap Draa Training Area close to Tan Tan in south-western Morocco. U.S. Africa Command reported the disappearance on Sunday and launched a search and rescue operation.

stories.title: Gov’t approves Smotrich ally Israel Malachi as Finance Ministry director-general
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved Israel Malachi, a close associate of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, as director-general of the Finance Ministry. Malachi previously served as treasurer of a council overseeing more than 40 West Bank settlements, drawing criticism over the appointment.

stories.title: Is Mali’s military government losing control?
stories.summary: A coalition of armed groups and rebels in Mali is challenging the authority of the country's military government. The situation raises questions about whether the junta is losing territorial control.

stories.title: Jerusalem Christians not surprised by attack on nun as abuse becomes routine
stories.summary: Christian clergy in Jerusalem report that incidents of ultra-Orthodox individuals spitting near them have escalated from isolated occurrences to daily events. Sixty-one physical attacks against Christians were recorded in Jerusalem in 2025.

stories.title: Merz ‘not giving up on working with Trump’ despite Iran war spat
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he will continue working with US President Trump despite their disagreement over the Iran war. In a televised interview on ARD, Merz downplayed US military drawdowns from Germany and Trump's public criticisms.

stories.title: Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages on Monday
stories.summary: Ukraine's national energy company Ukrenergo announced that no electricity consumption restrictions are planned for Monday, May 4.

stories.title: Israel court extends detention of Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: An Israeli court in Ashkelon extended by two days the detention of two activists arrested aboard a Gaza-bound flotilla. The vessel had been intercepted by Israeli forces in international waters near Greece.

stories.title: 2 men, including social activist, killed in separate attacked in KP's Bajaur
stories.summary: Two people, including social activist Malik Ziaur Rehman, were killed in separate armed attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Bajaur district on Sunday. Rehman was shot by unidentified assailants near his home in the Kohi area of Salarzai tehsil and later succumbed to his injuries.

stories.title: Trump rejects Iran proposal, urges pardon for Netanyahu from corruption charges
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, calling it unacceptable. He also urged Israeli President Isaac Herzog to grant a pardon to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on corruption charges.

stories.title: World Press Freedom Day marked in Gaza as journalist death toll rises
stories.summary: Palestinian journalists in Gaza observed World Press Freedom Day by commemorating colleagues killed and targeted by Israeli forces during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Three dead in suspected virus outbreak on cruise ship bound for Cape Verde
stories.summary: The World Health Organization confirmed one case of hantavirus and five suspected cases aboard a cruise ship traveling from Argentina toward Cape Verde. Three passengers have died from the suspected outbreak.

stories.title: 3 dead on Atlantic cruise ship from suspected hantavirus outbreak: WHO
stories.summary: Three people died aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius during a suspected hantavirus outbreak while the vessel traveled from Ushuaia, Argentina, to Cabo Verde. The WHO confirmed one hantavirus case and five additional suspected infections.

stories.title: Air defense forces neutralized 175 Russian drones, five missiles since morning
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces shot down or neutralized 175 Russian drones and five missiles during attacks on May 3, between 08:30 and 18:30.

stories.title: Is Israel expanding into Gaza despite ceasefire?
stories.summary: Forensic Architecture researcher Ray Adams Row Farr discussed evidence of Israeli territorial expansion into Gaza following the ceasefire in an interview with journalist Redi Tlhabi.

stories.title: Israel extends detention of 'tortured' Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended by two days the detention of activists Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila, arrested aboard the Global Sumud flotilla intercepted by Israeli forces in international waters en route to Gaza. Over 100 other activists were also detained.

stories.title: Three passengers dead after suspected hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship
stories.summary: Three passengers died aboard a cruise ship in the Atlantic from a suspected hantavirus outbreak. The WHO confirmed one case and identified five additional suspected infections, including a 69-year-old British national reported to be in intensive care in South Africa.

stories.title: Australia to hold first antisemitism commission hearing after Bondi Beach interim report
stories.summary: Australia will hold its first antisemitism commission hearing following the release of an interim report related to incidents at Bondi Beach. The commission will initially focus on defining antisemitism, with hearings scheduled to continue through the following Friday.

stories.title: Iran says US military operation ‘impossible’ as Trump mulls peace proposal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said on May 3 that he would review Iran's latest peace proposal. Iranian officials indicated the proposal had been submitted, though Trump expressed doubt about its acceptability.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz downplays rift with Washington despite US troop drawdown
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz sought to minimize tensions with Washington, stating that his criticism of President Donald Trump's Iran strategy was unrelated to the announced drawdown of US troops from Germany.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses strengthening air defense with Finnish PM
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks with Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo focused on strengthening Ukraine's air defense capabilities as a key defense priority.

stories.title: Hyderabad Kingsmen, Peshawar Zalmi set for PSL final face-off in Lahore today
stories.summary: Hyderabad Kingsmen and Peshawar Zalmi faced off in the PSL Season 11 final at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. Peshawar Zalmi reached the final after defeating Islamabad United by 70 runs in the first playoff.

stories.title: Israel’s strategy of ‘permanent war’: A race against time?
stories.summary: Political analyst Daniel Levy argued that US policy has become so deeply aligned with Israeli narratives that the two positions are effectively indistinguishable, describing Israel's approach as one of 'permanent war.'

stories.title: Two, including a social activist, killed in separate attacked in KP's Bajaur
stories.summary: Two people, including social activist Malik Ziaur Rehman, were killed in separate armed attacks in Bajaur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Unidentified assailants shot Rehman near his residence in the Kohi area of Salarzai tehsil.

stories.title: California, Arizona and Nevada propose water-saving plan for Colorado River
stories.summary: California, Arizona, and Nevada proposed voluntary water-saving measures for three years to address historically low levels at Lake Mead and Lake Powell, the two major reservoirs fed by the Colorado River, which supplies water to roughly 40 million people.

stories.title: Teens storm Scientology church in New York in latest ‘speed running’ incident
stories.summary: A group of teenagers forced entry into a Church of Scientology on West 36th Street in Manhattan, damaging property and injuring a staff member in what the church described as a 'speed running' incident, part of a trend going viral on social media.

stories.title: 'War relic' explodes under Austrian campfire, injuring five children
stories.summary: Five children aged 10 to 14 were injured in northern Austria on Saturday evening when a World War-era munition buried beneath their campfire exploded. Austrian police reported the incident on Sunday.

stories.title: Pope marks World Press Freedom Day, laments violations and honours slain reporters
stories.summary: Pope Leo marked World Press Freedom Day on Sunday by condemning persistent violations of media freedom worldwide. He also paid tribute to journalists killed while reporting from conflict zones.

stories.title: Zelensky meets PM of Norway in Yerevan to discuss Drone Deal, strengthening air defense
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre in Yerevan, Armenia, to discuss a drone procurement deal and measures to strengthen Ukraine's air defense capabilities.

stories.title: Iran drug prices rise as war hits industry, official says
stories.summary: Iran's medicines regulator Mahdi Pirsalehi stated that the ongoing war has increased drug prices and strained pharmaceutical supply chains. Rising costs in Iran's petrochemical and steel sectors have driven up production expenses, prompting officials to adjust drug prices and revise insurance budgets.

stories.title: High Court freezes TV regulatory body’s activities over controversial appointments
stories.summary: Israel's High Court of Justice froze the activities of the Second Authority, the country's television regulatory body, over controversial appointments, despite the government's repeated requests for extensions to continue operations.

stories.title: Protests erupt in Lebanon after displaced Shia community refuses to leave private school grounds
stories.summary: Protests erupted in Lebanon after displaced Shia individuals reportedly refused to vacate a private school. Parents at the school alleged the displaced group forced their way onto the premises, with some suggesting Hezbollah facilitated the takeover.

stories.title: Trump said to nix Iran plan that aimed to end war in month, defer nuclear issue
stories.summary: President Trump rejected an Iranian proposal that sought to end the war within a month by reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the US blockade, ending fighting in Iran and Lebanon, and proposing a 15-year uranium enrichment ban.

stories.title: Iran says U.S. military operation ‘impossible’ as Trump mulls peace proposal
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards intelligence organization told U.S. President Trump he must choose between "an impossible operation or a bad deal" with Iran, as Trump considered a peace proposal from Tehran.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza 'condom' flotilla, detaining nearly 200 activists, sparking backlash
stories.summary: Israel intercepted the Global Sumud Flotilla heading to Gaza and detained nearly 200 activists aboard. Israeli officials described the operation as an effort to neutralize both the flotilla and its potential impact on international narratives.

stories.title: Israel buying more F-35s, F-15IAs fighter jets, Netanyahu announces
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to purchase 25 Lockheed Martin F-35 fighter jets and 25 Boeing F-15IA jets, the Israeli variant of the F-15EX, with further details pending.

stories.title: Trump to review Iran peace proposal, signals strong doubts
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he would review a peace proposal submitted by Iran but expressed strong skepticism, stating on Truth Social that Tehran has "not yet paid a big enough price." The remarks came after Iranian media reported Tehran had transmitted the proposal to Washington.

stories.title: French Film Festival returns to Israel with Huppert, Bardot tributes
stories.summary: The French Film Festival is returning to Israel with screenings at venues in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Haifa, Herzliya, Sderot, Holon, and Jaffa. The festival includes tributes to actresses Isabelle Huppert and Brigitte Bardot.

stories.title: Two people die after explosion in southern England, police say
stories.summary: Two people died following an explosion at a house in Bristol, southern England. Avon and Somerset police declared a major incident and said they are treating the cause as suspicious.

stories.title: Russian drone strike in Kherson leaves one woman injured
stories.summary: A 46-year-old woman was injured in a Russian drone strike in the city of Kherson on the afternoon of May 3.

stories.title: Christina Lamb's quest for a new body to investigate crimes against journalists
stories.summary: On World Press Freedom Day, Reporters Without Borders reported the worst press freedom conditions in its 25-year index history, with Gaza among the deadliest places for journalists. Journalist Christina Lamb called for a new body to investigate crimes against reporters.

stories.title: Hezbollah pays steep price in battle to reverse its fortunes
stories.summary: Hezbollah is facing mounting military losses, mass displacement of its supporters, and growing political backlash in Lebanon. The militant group is struggling to reverse its fortunes amid sustained conflict.

stories.title: Iran oil shipments continue despite US seizures and diversions
stories.summary: Maritime monitoring site TankerTrackers.com reported that 25 tankers carrying crude oil departed Iran in April. Of those, seven were redirected back to Iran by the US from the Arabian Sea, two were seized in the Indian Ocean, and one reached the Far East.

stories.title: São Paulo creates Brazil-Israel Parliamentary Front, forming strategic alliance
stories.summary: The São Paulo city legislature established a Brazil-Israel Parliamentary Front. São Paulo became the second Brazilian city to adopt the IHRA definition of antisemitism, following Rio de Janeiro's adoption in March 2024.

stories.title: Tehran on the brink: Iran’s healthcare system nears collapse amid war
stories.summary: Iran's healthcare system is reportedly nearing collapse amid ongoing conflict, with hospitals in Tehran operating without anesthesia or antibiotics. The humanitarian situation across major Iranian cities is described as deeply alarming.

stories.title: Slovakia's PM Fico to attend Victory Day parade in Moscow, Russian TV says
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico plans to attend Russia's Victory Day parade in Moscow, according to Russian state television. Fico is among only a small number of global leaders expected at the scaled-back event this month.

stories.title: Ukraine to see variable cloudiness with no precipitation on Monday
stories.summary: A weather forecast for Ukraine on May 4 predicts variable cloudiness with no precipitation across most of the country, except for showers expected during the day in southeastern regions.

stories.title: Israel approves plan to buy F-35 and F-15IA fighter jets from Lockheed, Boeing
stories.summary: Israel's Ministerial Committee on Procurement gave final approval to purchase two new combat squadrons of F-35 and F-15IA jets from Lockheed Martin and Boeing. The deal is part of a 350 billion shekel ($119 billion) plan to bolster Israel's military readiness.

stories.title: Iran reviewing US response to 14-point plan, says spokesperson
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei confirmed that Tehran received Washington's response to its 14-point proposal, delivered via Pakistan. Officials in Tehran are now assessing the US position. Baqaei said the proposal focuses on ending the war and does not address nuclear negotiations.

stories.title: Hezbollah lawmaker says group can ‘thwart’ goals of Lebanon-Israel talks
stories.summary: A Hezbollah lawmaker stated that the group can thwart the goals of ongoing Lebanon-Israel negotiations. Israeli military operations in Lebanon have killed more than 2,600 people and displaced over a million.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Zaporizhzhia, injuries reported
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Zaporizhzhia, with explosions reported and strikes hitting garages. Multiple people were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Rubio to visit Rome, meet Pope Leo after Trump row in attempt to ‘thaw’ relations
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to Rome this week to meet Pope Leo XIV, following a public clash between President Trump and the pontiff over the Pope's anti-war rhetoric. The meeting, expected Thursday, aims to ease tensions between Washington and the Vatican.

stories.title: Strike on Dnipro: One killed, injury toll rises to 11
stories.summary: A Russian military strike on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on Sunday killed one person and injured 11 others.

stories.title: Two women die in Channel crossing attempt from France to Britain
stories.summary: Two women died after a boat carrying approximately 80 migrants capsized near Calais during an attempted Channel crossing from France to Britain. French authorities confirmed the incident on May 3.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian man in raid on Nablus in occupied West Ban
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted a raid in Nablus in the occupied West Bank, killing a 26-year-old Palestinian man during the operation.

stories.title: Russia is using Belarus as a launch pad for signal-relay balloons that help its drones reach Ukrainian cities
stories.summary: A Ukrainian border service spokesperson confirmed that a signal-relay balloon launched from Belarus crossed into Ukrainian territory on May 2. Russia is reportedly using Belarus as a launch site for such balloons to assist drone operations targeting Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz calls on Nawaz, discusses political situation in country, steps taken for peace in Middle East
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met PML-N leader Nawaz Sharif at their Jati Umra residence in Lahore to discuss the domestic political situation and Pakistan's peace efforts regarding the Middle East conflict. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also attended the meeting.

stories.title: Foreign soccer coach in top division questioned over alleged sexual harassment of taxi driver
stories.summary: A foreign soccer coach in his 50s working in Israel's top division was questioned at the Lev Tel Aviv police station over alleged sexual harassment of a taxi driver. He was released under restrictive conditions.

stories.title: Meteorologist shares weather forecast for Ukraine next week
stories.summary: Ukrainian meteorologists forecast dry and warm weather beginning Monday, with temperatures reaching up to 27°C in some areas. Rain and thunderstorms are expected in western regions during the second half of the week.

stories.title: Campaigners slam UK government threat to ban Palestine protests
stories.summary: Campaigners in the United Kingdom criticized government threats to ban pro-Palestinian protests, calling the move an attack on democratic rights. They also warned against conflating British Jewish communities with the state of Israel.

stories.title: Iran presents 14-point peace proposal, calls for end to war in 30 days
stories.summary: Iran presented a 14-point peace proposal with three main stages, aiming to transform the current ceasefire into a complete end to the war within 30 days. The plan was framed as a counter-proposal to the US's nine-point peace plan.

stories.title: Bank Hapoalim to open 54 Israeli museums, heritage sites with free admission over May weekends
stories.summary: Bank Hapoalim announced its "Poalim Israeli" initiative will provide free admission to 54 Israeli museums and heritage sites over three Friday-Saturday weekends in May, with advance registration required.

stories.title: Iran outlines three-stage plan to end war: Report
stories.summary: Iran has delivered a three-phase peace proposal to the United States through Pakistani intermediaries, aiming to convert the current ceasefire into a full end to the war within 30 days. The plan centers on a regional non-aggression commitment involving Israel.

stories.title: War update: 45 attacks since morning
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 45 attacks on Ukrainian defense positions since the start of the day, concentrating their main efforts on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka directions.

stories.title: Air force expansion propels Israel to a major military power - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis highlights Israel's expanding air force capabilities, noting that additional F-35 fighter jet purchases position Israel as a global leader in operating the advanced aircraft, despite lacking aircraft carriers or global power-projection ability.

stories.title: 'Prince of Arab Song' Hany Shaker dies at 74 after long illness
stories.summary: Egyptian singer Hany Shaker, widely known as the "Prince of Arab Song" and one of the Middle East's most celebrated music icons, died at age 74 on Sunday after a prolonged illness.

stories.title: Opec+ agrees third oil output quota hike since Hormuz closure
stories.summary: OPEC+ agreed on a modest oil output increase of 188,000 barrels per day for June, the third consecutive monthly hike. The increase excludes the United Arab Emirates, which left the group on May 1. The output boost remains largely symbolic due to ongoing disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz from the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: IAA reveals new study focused on ancient Jerusalem bullae in honor of Israel Excellence Week
stories.summary: The Israel Antiquities Authority released a new study examining ancient clay seal impressions, or bullae, from Jerusalem. The research spans administrative systems from the First Temple period through the end of the Second Temple period.

stories.title: Biggest supermarket chain pulls some dairy products from shelves in spat over Tnuva price hikes
stories.summary: Israel's largest supermarket chain removed certain dairy products from shelves in a dispute with dairy giant Tnuva over price increases on butter and soft cheeses ahead of the Jewish holiday of Shavuot. Other major food manufacturers are also expected to raise prices after the holiday.

stories.title: Germany urges Iran to reopen Hormuz, says nothing about US blockade
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul urged Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and dismantle its nuclear program following talks with his Iranian counterpart. Wadephul affirmed Berlin's alignment with Washington on Iran policy. Iran maintains it has the right to nuclear enrichment and denies pursuing weapons.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF finds cache of over 100 Hezbollah weapons in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces discovered a cache of over 100 Hezbollah weapons in southern Lebanon, including rockets, Kalashnikov rifles, and sniper rifles, during recent operations in the area.

stories.title: Cargo ship near Strait of Hormuz reports being attacked as Iran makes new peace proposal
stories.summary: A cargo ship near the Strait of Hormuz reported being attacked by multiple small craft, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre. All crew were safe after the incident off Sirik, Iran. The attack marks at least two dozen such incidents in the area since the Iran war began.

stories.title: Trump’s disapproval rating hits record high, new poll shows
stories.summary: A new Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll shows U.S. President Donald Trump's disapproval rating has reached 62%, the highest of his two terms. The decline is driven largely by negative assessments of his handling of economic issues, including rising gas prices and cost-of-living concerns linked to the ongoing U.S. war against Iran.

stories.title: USF strikes 38 Russian air defense systems in April
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces reported successfully striking 38 Russian air defense assets throughout April using drone operations.

stories.title: Man United beat Liverpool 3-2 to secure Champions League qualification
stories.summary: Manchester United defeated Liverpool 3-2 in a Premier League match, with Kobbie Mainoo scoring a late winner after Liverpool had recovered from a two-goal deficit. The result secures Champions League qualification for United.

stories.title: Four Palestinians charged for planning ISIS-inspired attacks across Israel
stories.summary: Israeli authorities charged four Palestinians with planning ISIS-inspired attacks at multiple locations across Israel, including Jerusalem's Damascus Gate and the West Bank settlement of Kiryat Arba. The suspects allegedly watched Islamic State videos and learned to fire weapons and construct explosives.

stories.title: Man, 36, to be charged for assaulting French nun in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli police requested a court extend the custody of Yona Schreiber, a 36-year-old man suspected of assaulting a French nun in Jerusalem last week. Authorities seek to hold him until the end of legal proceedings, and formal charges are expected.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll from Israeli attacks rises to 2,679
stories.summary: Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health reported that Israeli attacks have killed 2,679 people and wounded 8,229 others across the country between 2 March and 3 May.

stories.title: Israel extends detention of 'tortured' Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: Israel extended the detention of two Global Sumud Flotilla activists, Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila, who reportedly faced mistreatment in Israeli custody. Avila appeared at a Magistrate's Court hearing in Ashkelon on 3 May regarding his detention extension.

stories.title: Bulk carrier attacked by multiple small craft off Iran, UKMTO says
stories.summary: A bulk carrier was attacked by multiple small craft approximately 11 nautical miles west of Sirik, Iran, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre. All crew members were reported safe, and no environmental damage was recorded.

stories.title: Iran reviews US response to peace proposal, warns against further military action
stories.summary: Iran responded to President Trump's rejection of its peace proposal by warning Washington it must choose between an 'impossible' military operation or a 'bad deal.' Negotiations between the US and Iran have been stalled since a ceasefire took effect on April 8.

stories.title: Three dead on Atlantic cruise ship in suspected Hantavirus outbreak, says WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reported that three people have died aboard a cruise ship crossing the Atlantic following an outbreak that includes a confirmed case of hantavirus. The rare infection, which can be severe, has raised public health concerns about containment at sea.

stories.title: Is the future non-denominational? with Rabbi Avi Killip - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Rabbi Avi Killip discussed whether traditional Jewish denominational labels such as Reform, Conservative, and Orthodox still hold relevance today, and what alternatives may emerge in their place.

stories.title: Two US troops missing during African Lion exercise in Morocco
stories.summary: Two U.S. service members went missing during the African Lion military exercise near Tan Tan, Morocco. U.S. and Moroccan forces launched air, sea, and ground search operations to locate them.

stories.title: Jewish life in an illiberal age – with Jeffery Goldberg - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Journalist Jeffrey Goldberg discussed the state of Jewish life in the United States as the country approaches its 250th anniversary, examining what the current political climate means for the future of the American-Jewish experience.

stories.title: Israel approves plan to buy F-35 and F-15IA fighter jets from Lockheed, Boeing
stories.summary: Israel's defence ministry gave final approval to purchase two new combat squadrons of F-35 and F-15IA advanced fighter jets from Lockheed Martin and Boeing. The deal is valued at tens of billions of dollars.

stories.title: Russians strike residential area in Dnipro, damaging dormitory
stories.summary: A Russian strike on May 3 hit a residential area in Dnipro, damaging a dormitory building in the Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Bennett 2026 - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A discussion piece examines whether former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett is positioned as a right-wing ideologue or a potential unifying national figure ahead of a possible 2026 political bid.

stories.title: Gaza cannot be rebuilt until Palestinians control their own political future
stories.summary: Author Alaa Tartir argues that Gaza's reconstruction requires Palestinian-led political renewal rather than externally imposed frameworks, as Israel links rebuilding efforts to new conditions. Palestinians were seen near electoral candidate lists in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza.

stories.title: Is Israel going to restart the war on Gaza?
stories.summary: Israeli officials are pushing to resume military operations in Gaza despite an existing ceasefire. Critics argue the prior campaign failed to defeat Hamas and resulted in mass displacement of civilians.

stories.title: Lightning may have sparked fire destroying top US marine science lab, officials say
stories.summary: Officials are investigating whether a lightning strike caused a large fire that destroyed the Marine Science Laboratory at the University of South Florida on Saturday. Approximately 200 firefighters responded to the blaze, but the building was completely destroyed despite the massive emergency response.

stories.title: Three killed, four injured in car accident in northern Israel, fourth fatal accident in single day
stories.summary: Three people were killed and four injured in a car accident in northern Israel, marking the fourth fatal road accident in the country on a single day. Nine people were injured across the four incidents.

stories.title: Two foreign activists from Gaza flotilla appear in Israeli court
stories.summary: Two foreign activists detained from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla appeared before an Israeli court. Israel's foreign ministry stated the activists are affiliated with an organization sanctioned by the US Treasury.

stories.title: Catholic charity condemns Israel for Lebanon convent attack
stories.summary: French Catholic charity L'Oeuvre d'Orient condemned Israel after its forces demolished a convent belonging to the Salvatorian Sisters, a Greek Catholic order, in the southern Lebanese village of Yaroun. The organization called it a deliberate attack on a place of worship.

stories.title: Two US service members missing after joint military exercises in Morocco
stories.summary: Two US service members participating in the African Lion joint military exercises went missing near the city of Tan Tan in southern Morocco, US Africa Command reported Sunday. A US defense official said the soldiers disappeared while on a hike after the day's exercises had concluded.

stories.title: Jordan is enforcing a red line in Syria via airstrikes - analysis
stories.summary: Jordan carried out airstrikes in Syria near Sweida targeting drug smuggling networks, enforcing what analysts describe as a red line against cross-border narcotics trafficking.

stories.title: Live with Scott Galloway: Why the Jewish People Need Better Storytellers - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Noam Shuster-Eliassi spoke with Scott Galloway about Jewish identity and narrative challenges facing Israel in a conversation hosted by The Times of Israel.

stories.title: Zelensky arrives in Yerevan
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Yerevan, Armenia, to participate in the European Political Community summit.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of two Gaza flotilla activists until Tuesday
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila and Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek until Tuesday after the state requested a four-day extension for further questioning of the Gaza flotilla activists.

stories.title: 2 US troops reported missing amid African Lion exercise
stories.summary: The Moroccan army reported that two US service members went missing near a cliff during the African Lion military exercise near Tan Tan in southern Morocco. The incident remains under investigation and search operations are ongoing.

stories.title: Pluralizing the Jewish conversation with Amy Albertson - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Amy Albertson discussed her experience navigating Jewish identity after growing up in an interfaith family and living in Israel, in an interview exploring diverse perspectives within Jewish communities.

stories.title: Can Israel and Lebanon move from war to diplomacy? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Lebanese lawmaker Fouad Makhzoumi, Israeli analyst Sarit Zehavi, and Middle East expert Robert Satloff discussed prospects for transitioning Israel-Lebanon relations from conflict to diplomacy in a panel discussion.

stories.title: Artificial night light disrupts body clocks, may increase mortality, researchers say - study
stories.summary: Researchers at Tel Aviv University found that exposure to artificial light at night may disrupt biological rhythms and potentially increase mortality risk.

stories.title: Serbia’s FM Djuric to ‘Post’: Strategic partnership with Israel ‘historic step forward’ - interview
stories.summary: Serbian Foreign Minister Marko Djuric described his country's strategic partnership with Israel as a historic step forward. Djuric is a cousin of Alon Ohel, a Nova festival survivor and former Hamas hostage.

stories.title: Russia's Primorsk port hit as Ukraine launches wave of drone strikes
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Baltic Sea port of Primorsk on Sunday, temporarily setting it on fire, according to Leningrad Oblast governor Alexander Drozdenko. The attack was part of a broader wave of Ukrainian drone strikes across Russian territory.

stories.title: Rubio to visit Vatican, Rome after Trump row with Pope Leo
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit the Vatican and Italy this week for diplomatic meetings. The trip follows President Donald Trump's public criticism of Pope Leo XIV on social media over the pontiff's anti-war statements.

stories.title: US Secretary of State to travel to Vatican and Italy, newspapers report
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to the Vatican and Italy this week for meetings, according to Italian newspaper reports. The visit comes weeks after President Trump publicly attacked Pope Leo, drawing criticism from Christians across the political spectrum.

stories.title: The US vs Latin America: Varsha Gandikota and Susana Muhamad
