stories.summary: Varsha Gandikota interviews Colombian Environment Minister Susana Muhamad about the impact of the military-industrial complex on Global South sovereignty, focusing on US relations with Latin America.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Nikopol region leave five people injured
stories.summary: Five people were injured in Russian strikes on the Nikopol region of Ukraine, and law enforcement officers are investigating at the scenes of the attacks.

stories.title: Israel approves deal to buy fighter jets from U.S.
stories.summary: Israel approved the purchase of a squadron of F-35 stealth fighters from Lockheed Martin and a squadron of F-15IA warplanes from Boeing. The Defence Ministry confirmed the deal with the United States.

stories.title: Two killed and 16 injured in attempted channel crossing from France to U.K.
stories.summary: Two women died and 16 others were injured during an attempted English Channel crossing from France to the United Kingdom. A French maritime gendarmerie vessel rescued 17 people and brought them to Boulogne-sur-Mer, while 65 others remained on the grounded boat.

stories.title: Pantsir and Tor anti-air systems, two radars: what Ukraine’s drone forces destroyed in the first 48 hours of May
stories.summary: Ukraine's drone forces destroyed Pantsir and Tor anti-air defense systems along with two radars in the first 48 hours of May. This follows the destruction of 38 Russian air defense and radar units by the same forces during April.

stories.title: OPEC+ hikes oil production quotas, doesn't mention UAE pull-out
stories.summary: OPEC+ members including Saudi Arabia and Russia agreed to increase June oil production quotas by 188,000 barrels per day. The decision came amid the UAE's departure from the group and the ongoing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Footage shows rescuers clearing destroyed homes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Rescue teams cleared rubble from destroyed homes in the southern Lebanese town of Habboush following Israeli airstrikes. The Israeli military reportedly struck the area approximately one hour after ordering residents to evacuate, citing Hezbollah targets.

stories.title: Norwegian university professor: October 7 attacks 'most beautiful thing to happen in our century'
stories.summary: Bassam Hussein, a Norwegian university professor, called the October 7 attacks "the most beautiful thing to happen in our century" and claimed Israel seeks to "take over the Western empire."

stories.title: Russian Shahed drone hits residential building in Kryvyi Rih, leaving five injured
stories.summary: A Russian Shahed drone struck a multi-story residential building in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine, injuring five people who were hospitalized.

stories.title: Israel threatens Gaza war resumption to force disarmament as ‘truce’ frays
stories.summary: Palestinian factions have rejected US-backed proposals that would link humanitarian aid to Gaza to weapons surrender, insisting instead on a clear political pathway to resolve the conflict with Israel.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill one, injure four in latest West Bank raid
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed one person and injured four others during a raid in the West Bank. The victim, 26-year-old Nayef Firas Ziad Samaro, was brought to a hospital in Nablus where his wife was simultaneously giving birth.

stories.title: Rare mystical prayer book unveiled at ANU museum in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: A 16th-century handwritten prayer book based on Rabbi Isaac Luria's kabbalistic teachings has been unveiled at the ANU Museum in Tel Aviv. The rare siddur will go on public display beginning on Lag B'Omer.

stories.title: US conditions over armed groups complicates Iraqi govt formation
stories.summary: U.S. pressure on the Iraqi prime minister-designate regarding armed groups is expected to complicate efforts to form a new government amid deep political divisions in Iraq.

stories.title: Kuwait says it is increasing oil production
stories.summary: Kuwait announced its oil production is expected to reach 2.628 million barrels per day in June. Seven OPEC+ countries agreed to raise output targets by 188,000 barrels per day, though production has been curtailed due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war.

stories.title: Italian media reports US top diplomat Rubio to meet Pope Leo
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is reportedly traveling to Rome this week to meet Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Pope Leo XIV. The visit is aimed at easing strained relations after President Donald Trump publicly criticized the pontiff's anti-war remarks. The trip coincides with the first anniversary of Pope Leo XIV's papacy.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP vows terror group will ‘thwart’ Lebanon-Israel talks as clashes persist
stories.summary: A Hezbollah member of parliament vowed the group would work to derail Lebanon-Israel negotiations. Meanwhile, Hezbollah fired rockets and drones at troops without causing injuries, and the IDF destroyed an 80-meter tunnel in southern Lebanon and seized weapons.

stories.title: Southern Lebanon: Israeli strikes kill one, wounds rescuers
stories.summary: Israel carried out fresh air strikes in southern Lebanon, killing at least one person and wounding four others, including rescuers. The Israeli Defense Forces issued evacuation warnings for residents of more than ten villages and towns, including the city of Nabatieh. The strikes occurred despite a ceasefire agreement signed last month between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: French interior minister vows crackdown on illegal raves after thousands gather at military site
stories.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez vowed to crack down on illegal raves after thousands gathered at a military base near Bourges in central France, despite warnings about unexploded ordnance. Organizers said they chose the location to protest a proposed bill that would increase penalties for unregistered raves.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill three
stories.summary: Russia launched 268 drones and one ballistic missile at Ukraine overnight, killing at least three people. Strikes hit residential buildings and port infrastructure in Odesa and targeted the Kherson Oblast region. Ukrainian drones struck oil export terminals in Russia's Leningrad Oblast and targeted vessels in Russia's shadow fleet.

stories.title: French FM: Russia makes freedom of information its target
stories.summary: On World Press Freedom Day, France's foreign minister accused Russia of deliberately targeting freedom of information. France honored a French photojournalist killed in Ukraine by a Russian drone strike.

stories.title: Spirit pilot gets ‘overwhelming’ send-off from Southwest after his final flight is cancelled
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines pilot Jon Jackson received an emotional retirement send-off from Southwest Airlines staff at Baltimore-Washington International Airport on Saturday. His final scheduled Spirit flight was canceled after the airline ceased operations, having run out of cash following failed rescue talks with the Trump administration.

stories.title: 21 arrested for trying to sacrifice a baby goat on the Temple Mount
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested 21 individuals who attempted to sacrifice a baby goat on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem. The group is the latest to unsuccessfully try to revive animal sacrifice at the site of the ancient Jewish temples.

stories.title: UK tests new Skyhammer interceptor missiles in Jordan
stories.summary: The United Kingdom tested its new Skyhammer interceptor missiles during exercises in Jordan. The system is designed to counter Shahed-type drones and low-speed missiles.

stories.title: Iran plans to turn university site hit in US-Israeli strikes into museum
stories.summary: Iran announced plans to convert a university site damaged in US-Israeli airstrikes into a museum. Initial assessments estimated the damage to the university's buildings and facilities at approximately $14 million.

stories.title: Zelenskyy has no cards to play against Russia or the West
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy faces difficulty securing concessions from either Russia or Western allies that could offset the costs of a potential peace agreement for Ukraine's population.

stories.title: Pennsylvania's Swarthmore College sees 'hundreds of acts' of anti Israel vandalism
stories.summary: Swarthmore College in Pennsylvania reported "hundreds of acts" of anti-Israel vandalism on campus. Graffiti was spray-painted on buildings, trees, fences, and walkways, and college staff worked to remove the damage.

stories.title: Ceasefire just to hold parade in Moscow on May 9 ridiculous, says Tusk
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk dismissed Russia's proposed one-day ceasefire on May 9—Victory Day in Moscow—as "absurd." Poland stated it does not support the proposal.

stories.title: Lebanese media deletes animated Angry Birds caricature of Hezbollah leader after judicial order
stories.summary: Lebanese broadcaster LBCI removed an animated video depicting Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem as an Angry Birds character after a judicial order. Lebanese authorities warned against content that could deepen sectarian divisions.

stories.title: Two Sudanese women die in overcrowded migrant boat crossing from northern France
stories.summary: Two young Sudanese women suffocated and died on Sunday while attempting to cross the English Channel from northern France to Britain. They were on a small boat carrying more than 80 people, including pregnant women and children.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike Russian Kalibr carrier, the ship Karakurt, in Primorsk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service reported the successful strike on a Russian Kalibr cruise missile carrier, the Karakurt-class ship, in the port of Primorsk. Acting SBU head Major General Yevhenii Khmara briefed President Zelensky on the operation.

stories.title: Concern for jailed Iranian Nobel laureate as brother fears she is dying
stories.summary: Her family said the 54-year-old had been taken from prison to a local hospital after a sharp deterioration in her health.

stories.title: Trump: Iran has 'not yet paid a big enough price'
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Truth Social that Iran has "not yet paid a big enough price," while reviewing a 14-point peace proposal submitted by Tehran. Trump warned that U.S. and Israeli strikes could resume if Iran "misbehaves."

stories.title: Sudan strike kills nine relatives of army-backed militia chief
stories.summary: A drone strike on the family home of Sudan Shield commander killed nine of his relatives. Rival paramilitary forces have been escalating attacks across war-torn Sudan.

stories.title: A note to our readers regarding The Times of Israel’s guidelines on AI
stories.summary: The Times of Israel published an editorial note stating its newsroom does not use artificial intelligence to write or edit articles and follows strict editorial guidelines limiting the technology's use.

stories.title: Sleepless in Tehran as crowds rally behind the flag
stories.summary: Crowds gathered on the streets of Tehran in a show of public support amid tensions, with slogans addressed to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps urging soldiers to focus on the battlefield while civilians maintain control of the home front.

stories.title: Kurdish troops join Syria's army as unity efforts gather pace
stories.summary: Four Kurdish brigades have been merged with the Syrian armed forces as Damascus accelerates efforts to reunify the autonomous Kurdish region with state institutions.

stories.title: Exclusive: US and Israel reject joint Palestinian proposal for Gaza after meetings
stories.summary: The United States and Israel rejected a joint proposal from Palestinian factions that linked disarmament to statehood and security guarantees. The rejection came as ceasefire negotiations over Gaza stalled amid worsening food shortages in the Strip.

stories.title: OPEC+ lifts June output quota amid UAE departure
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia, Russia, and five other OPEC+ members agreed on Sunday to increase their oil production quota for June. The move followed the unexpected withdrawal of the United Arab Emirates from the cartel and was intended to signal organizational continuity.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's Primorsk oil port
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Primorsk oil port and several vessels in the Baltic Sea on Sunday as part of broader attacks on Russian energy infrastructure. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the strikes limit Russia's war potential, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov warned that continued attacks could push global oil prices higher.

stories.title: Canada to be first non-European nation at EPC summit as Carney seeks allies
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will attend the European Political Community summit in Yerevan, Armenia, making Canada the first non-European nation to participate in the 48-plus member grouping. The move reflects Ottawa's effort to build new trade and diplomatic alliances following the disruption of US markets under President Trump, while also signaling Western support for Armenia's distancing from Russia.

stories.title: Eight Kalibrs that won’t reach Ukraine: Ukrainian Special Operations Forces struck Russian missile corvette at Primorsk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces struck a Russian Karakurt-class missile corvette at Primorsk overnight on May 3, along with a patrol boat, a shadow fleet tanker, and the Primorsk oil terminal. President Zelensky confirmed the operation.

stories.title: More UNWRA ties to Hamas, Global Sumud Flotilla details emerge
stories.summary: A news roundup highlighted new reported ties between UNRWA staff and Hamas, as well as emerging details about the Global Sumud flotilla bound for Gaza.

stories.title: Russians attack Kryvyi Rih; high-rise building hit
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, striking a high-rise residential building and causing a fire.

stories.title: Two US service members reported missing in Morocco, officials say
stories.summary: U.S. Africa Command confirmed a search and rescue operation is underway for two U.S. service members reported missing in Morocco.

stories.title: US airlines step up as Spirit winds down
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines cancelled all flights and began winding down operations on Saturday, citing soaring fuel costs after a White House rescue package failed to materialise. American Airlines, Delta, United, and JetBlue are offering special fares to stranded Spirit passengers and considering hiring displaced Spirit staff.

stories.title: Court extends detention of 2 Gaza flotilla activists accused of Hamas links
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the detention of Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila, two Gaza flotilla activists accused of assisting the enemy during wartime and membership in a terror group. Spain has called for its citizen's release.

stories.title: On World Press Freedom Day, Pope honours journalists killed in war zones
stories.summary: On World Press Freedom Day, Pope Leo XIV called on the faithful to remember journalists who have lost their lives while reporting in war zones.

stories.title: Heat by design: Can cities be cooled without air conditioning?
stories.summary: The article explores the urban heat island effect, where cities can be up to 5.6 degrees Celsius warmer than surrounding areas due to roads, concrete, and dense construction. It examines design-based cooling strategies as alternatives to air conditioning in urban planning.

stories.title: Policeman gunned down near his home in KP's Lakki Marwat
stories.summary: A police constable named Irfanullah was shot and killed by suspected terrorists near his home in the Kaichi Kamar area of Lakki Marwat district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The officer, stationed in Peshawar, was on leave visiting his native village when he was targeted.

stories.title: Why a 5-year defence pact between North Korea and Russia could make China uneasy
stories.summary: Russian Defence Minister Andrey Belousov met North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in Pyongyang on April 26 to discuss a rare five-year defence cooperation plan. Analysts say the agreement could accelerate North Korea's military modernisation and may unsettle China, which views deepening Russia–North Korea ties as a potential challenge to its regional influence.

stories.title: Who are the two Gaza flotilla activists abducted by Israel?
stories.summary: Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila were among 175 Gaza-bound flotilla activists detained by Israeli forces.

stories.title: Heathrow in talks with airlines to end row that could delay third runway
stories.summary: Heathrow Airport's new chair Philip Jansen has opened negotiations with airlines including British Airways' parent company and Virgin, as well as local landowner Surinder Arora, to resolve disputes over costs and service. The disagreements threaten to further delay the £49 billion plan to build a third runway at Europe's busiest airport. Arora has been promoting his own rival £25 billion expansion scheme.

stories.title: Israel’s survival depends on leaders who put nation before self - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel's long-term survival depends on leaders who prioritize national unity over self-interest. It draws on historical examples of nations weakened by internal divisions rather than external enemies.

stories.title: High Court cites ‘rampant’ crime in face of Levin’s refusal to appoint judges
stories.summary: Israel's High Court highlighted "rampant" crime resulting from a shortage of judges, as Justice Minister Yariv Levin's lawyer refused to provide a timetable for new judicial appointments despite the court's urging.

stories.title: Congress concerned that Trump’s decision to reduce troop levels in Germany may send wrong signal to Putin
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Roger Wicker and Representative Mike Rogers, chairs of the Senate and House Armed Services Committees respectively, warned that President Trump's decision to reduce troop levels in Germany could send the wrong signal to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Masked men abduct prominent Malian lawyer in Bamako
stories.summary: A prominent Malian lawyer and politician critical of the ruling military junta was abducted by masked men overnight in the capital Bamako, according to family members.

stories.title: US Secretary of State Rubio to visit Vatican, Rome after Trump's row with Pope
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit Rome and the Vatican this week, where he is expected to meet Vatican Secretary of State Pietro Parolin and Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani. The visit follows a public clash between President Donald Trump and Pope Leo XIV over anti-war rhetoric.

stories.title: Republicans ‘concerned’ after Trump threatens to withdraw more US troops from Germany
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened on Saturday to withdraw significantly more US troops from Germany beyond the 5,000 already announced, leaving roughly 30,000 personnel in the country. The initial withdrawal followed remarks by the German chancellor suggesting the US was being humiliated by Iran. Senior Republicans have expressed concern over the troop reductions.

stories.title: US to cut troops in Germany as Iran war spat deepens
stories.summary: U.S.-German relations are deteriorating as President Trump and Chancellor Merz clash over policy regarding the war on Iran, with Washington announcing plans to reduce its troop presence in Germany.

stories.title: Israel issues new evacuation warnings in south Lebanon beyond occupied area
stories.summary: Israel issued new evacuation warnings covering more than 10 villages and towns in southern Lebanon, including several in the Nabatieh district north of the Litani River. Israeli troops remain stationed south of the Litani River in an occupied zone.

stories.title: Celebrating death: Ben-Gvir's birthday cake features noose
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir marked his birthday with a cake featuring a noose, referencing the death penalty law he and his party have championed. The gesture drew criticism as another controversial act by the far-right minister.

stories.title: In Mykolaiv, injury toll after morning ballistic missile attack climbs to five; houses damaged
stories.summary: A Russian ballistic missile struck the Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv on the morning of May 3, injuring at least five people. Private homes in the area sustained damage from the attack.

stories.title: A world of cultures comes alive at embassy fair in Washington
stories.summary: The annual Passport DC "Around the World Embassy Tour" transformed Washington's International Drive into a cultural fair, with embassies including Pakistan's hosting visitors with music, food, and cultural displays. The Pakistan Embassy featured traditional dhol drumming.

stories.title: It does not make sense to invest more Arab resources in a US alliance
stories.summary: The article argues that Arab states should not invest further in a U.S. alliance, contending that Washington will always prioritize Israel and that Arab unity is the path to regional security.

stories.title: Israel Hofsheet petitions High Court over state benefits it says favor haredi sector
stories.summary: The Israeli organization Israel Hofsheet petitioned the High Court challenging state benefits it argues disproportionately favor the ultra-Orthodox (haredi) sector. The petition claims benefits are structured around characteristics more common among haredi families, such as early marriage and large family size.

stories.title: Netanyahu boasts of Israel’s billion-dollar military investments
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a plan to invest approximately $119 billion in developing domestic military weapons systems to strengthen Israel's defense capabilities.

stories.title: Netanyahu says project to counter drone threat underway, but ‘will take time’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said a project to counter drone threats is underway but will take time. Hezbollah's first-person-view drones recently killed a soldier in south Lebanon and have caused dozens of injuries.

stories.title: Man suspected of plotting attack on Dutch princesses to appear in court
stories.summary: A man suspected of plotting an attack on Dutch princesses Amalia and Alexia is set to appear in court in the Netherlands. He was allegedly found with two axes inscribed with the names "Alexia" and "Mossad" along with "Sieg Heil," and a handwritten note referencing "Bloodbath."

stories.title: 2 dead and 16 injured in channel crossing from France to UK
stories.summary: A migrant boat attempting to cross the English Channel ran aground off the French coast, killing two Sudanese women and injuring 16 others. The incident is the latest deadly crossing as a new UK-France border deal is being tested.

stories.title: Trump says US withdrawing 'a lot' more troops from Germany than 5000 announced yesterday
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the U.S. will withdraw significantly more troops from Germany than the 5,000 initially disclosed. The drawdown follows a rift with Berlin after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz criticized U.S.-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Office of President outlines grounds for sanctions against Kiryukhin, Pozdnyakov, and Mamiashvili
stories.summary: Ukraine's Office of the President announced sanctions against Alan Kiryukhin for using cryptocurrency tools to circumvent restrictions, and against sports officials Stanislav Pozdnyakov and Mykhail Mamiashvili for supporting Russia's war effort. Ukraine is calling on the EU to align with these sanctions in its next package.

stories.title: Iran executes man convicted over killing of security officer in 2022 unrest
stories.summary: Iran executed a man convicted of killing a security officer during the 2022 nationwide protests. The defendant had reportedly confessed to assaulting the officer during the unrest.

stories.title: Vigilantes in Nigeria kill herders amid jihadist tensions, kidnapping gangs
stories.summary: A state-backed Nigerian militia and military forces killed scores of ethnic Fulani herders in raids near Kabe in Borgu district, Niger State. The operation also involved vigilantes from neighboring Benin. The herders were accused of serving as informants for the jihadist group Ansaru.

stories.title: Iran executes man convicted of killing security officer during 2022 protests - report
stories.summary: Iran executed Mehrab Abdollahzadeh, convicted of killing a security officer during the 2022 protests. The state news agency said he confessed, but the human rights group HRANA reported he was subjected to torture to extract forced confessions.

stories.title: Israeli military urges residents in southern Lebanon towns to evacuate amid strikes against Hezbollah
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings to residents of towns in southern Lebanon as it conducted strikes against Hezbollah positions. The military cautioned that anyone near Hezbollah fighters or facilities could be at risk during the operations.

stories.title: Was the Iran war the final blow in the collapse of Spirit Airlines?
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines, the U.S. budget carrier, ceased operations after 34 years amid disruptions linked to the Iran war, leaving roughly 17,000 employees without jobs.

stories.title: Police block roads around Meron ahead of Lag B’Omer as pilgrimage canceled
stories.summary: Israeli police blocked roads around the holy site of Meron ahead of Lag B'Omer after the annual pilgrimage was canceled due to wartime restrictions. Officers warned of "zero tolerance" for violent resistance to the guidelines.

stories.title: Sajid Sadpara summits world’s 5th highest mountain Makalu without supplemental oxygen
stories.summary: Pakistani mountaineer Sajid Ali Sadpara summited Mount Makalu (8,485m) in Nepal without supplementary oxygen on May 2. This marks his 10th summit in a quest to climb all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters without supplemental oxygen.

stories.title: The US sanctioned Chinese oil refineries. Now China is really pushing back
stories.summary: China issued an order directing domestic companies not to comply with US sanctions targeting five Chinese oil refineries accused of processing Iranian fuel. Analysts describe the directive as the first use of Beijing's mechanism to block foreign sanctions it considers improper, potentially complicating US enforcement of its Iran-related restrictions.

stories.title: Washington must not fall for Iran’s ceasefire and nuclear delay tactics - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Iran's diplomatic tactics in nuclear talks are designed to delay meaningful negotiations while extracting early concessions from the United States.

stories.title: Twenty-one detained as police thwart attempt to bring Passover sacrifice to Temple Mount
stories.summary: Israeli police detained 21 people after thwarting an attempt to bring a Passover sacrifice to the Temple Mount in Jerusalem. Last month, 14 Jewish men and boys were arrested on suspicion of trying to smuggle sacrificial goats onto the holy site.

stories.title: Green Party leader Zack Polanski condemns 'vile antisemitic caricature' in The Times
stories.summary: UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski condemned a cartoon published in The Times as a "vile antisemitic caricature," which appeared to depict him with a hooked nose. A party spokesperson accused media and politicians of mounting further attacks on Polanski following a violent incident targeting his community.

stories.title: Five people, including four paramedics, wounded in Israeli attack on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli strike near a medical center in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon wounded five people, including four paramedics, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The ministry condemned the attack and cited the Geneva Convention's protections for medical facilities.

stories.title: US DoD, tech giants bid to make armed forces 'AI-first'
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense and major technology companies are working to make American armed forces "AI-first." The effort follows an AI Acceleration Strategy outlined in a January memo by Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.

stories.title: The week in pictures: May Day marches, King Charles in Bermuda and Mali's rebel push
stories.summary: Key events of the week included May Day marches worldwide against rising living costs, King Charles III becoming the first reigning British king to visit Bermuda, and a joint jihadist-separatist offensive in Mali that resulted in the killing of defence minister Sadio Camara.

stories.title: INTERVIEW: Qualifying for LA2028 Olympics Pakistan’s main focus, says Manzoor Sr
stories.summary: Former Pakistan hockey Olympian Manzoor Senior said qualifying for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics is the national team's primary focus. Pakistan recently qualified for the 2026 Hockey World Cup and will compete in the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, later in 2026.

stories.title: Iran's IRGC: US must choose between 'impossible military operation' and 'bad deal'
stories.summary: The intelligence unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned that Washington must choose between a "bad deal" and an "impossible military operation." The IRGC said Tehran has set a deadline for the U.S. to lift its blockade on Iranian ports and cited shifting international attitudes toward Washington.

stories.title: Iran hangs man accused of killing security forces volunteer during 2022 protests
stories.summary: Iran executed Mehrab Abdollahzadeh, convicted of killing a security forces volunteer during the 2022 nationwide protests. The judiciary said he confessed and was executed on the charge of "corruption on earth."

stories.title: Ukraine just added a new line to its Russian-losses ledger: ground robots. The count starts at 1,306
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff added a new category to its daily Russian-losses report: ground robots. The count began on May 3 at 1,306 destroyed units, with 12 added in the most recent 24-hour period.

stories.title: Israel approves purchase of fighter jets from the US
stories.summary: Israel's Ministerial Committee on Procurement approved the purchase of two new combat squadrons of F-35 and F-15IA fighter jets from Lockheed Martin and Boeing in a deal worth tens of billions of dollars.

stories.title: Israel approves deal to buy fighter jets from US
stories.summary: Israel approved a deal to purchase new F-35 and F-15IA fighter jet squadrons from the United States as part of a $118 billion military buildup plan. Prime Minister Netanyahu highlighted the aircraft's capacity for long-range strikes, including against Iran.

stories.title: Explosion near gas station in Dnipropetrovsk region: Children from damaged bus evacuated to Zatyshne community
stories.summary: Approximately 40 children traveling on a bus in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region were evacuated to the Zatyshne community after the vehicle was damaged by a Russian airstrike on May 3. An explosion near a gas station in the area accompanied the strike.

stories.title: Sudanese woman and 16-year-old girl reportedly die trying to cross Channel
stories.summary: Two Sudanese female asylum seekers — reportedly a 16-year-old girl and a woman in her 20s — died while attempting to cross the English Channel early Sunday. Their boat, carrying approximately 82 people, ran aground on the beach at Neufchâtel-Hardelot near Boulogne, and several others were injured.

stories.title: From footwear to AI services: China moves up the value chain in exports
stories.summary: China is undergoing a structural shift in its export profile, moving from low-cost manufactured goods to higher-value technology and services. In 2025, exports of telecoms, computer, and information services reached 808 billion yuan, a 13 percent year-on-year increase.

stories.title: World may find itself ‘in a very Chinese time’ of data governance
stories.summary: China inaugurated the World Data Organisation in Beijing at the end of March, aiming to bridge the global data divide and promote digital economy development. The initiative reflects Beijing's broader strategy to shape international data governance norms and drive AI development.

stories.title: Between a fatwa and war: how Iran makes sense of its nuclear capability
stories.summary: Iran has stated it will protect its nuclear stockpile against threats from US President Donald Trump. The country's nuclear posture is shaped by both strategic calculations and a fatwa by former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei disapproving of nuclear weapons on religious grounds.

stories.title: Two US service members missing after military exercises in Morocco
stories.summary: Two U.S. service members went missing in south-western Morocco near the city of Tan Tan during the annual multinational African Lion military exercise. U.S. Africa Command and partner nations launched a search and rescue operation.

stories.title: US military says two service members taking part in Morocco drills missing
stories.summary: U.S. Africa Command reported that two American service members went missing during the African Lion military exercise in southwestern Morocco. Search and rescue operations are under way in the area.

stories.title: Taiwan President defiant as begins Eswatini trip; China calls him a 'rat'
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te began an official visit to Eswatini, one of Taiwan's few remaining diplomatic allies. China's Taiwan Affairs Office condemned the trip, calling Lai's actions comparable to "a rat scurrying across the street."

stories.title: World Press Freedom Day 2026: RSF report says press freedom at its lowest in 25 years
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders released its annual report on World Press Freedom Day, May 3, finding that global press freedom has fallen to its lowest level in 25 years. The report notes that over the past three years, journalists in conflict zones have increasingly become direct targets rather than witnesses.

stories.title: Taiwan’s leader visits Eswatini despite pressure from China to block trip
stories.summary: Taiwan President William Lai Ching-te is conducting a state visit to Eswatini, the sole African nation that maintains formal diplomatic recognition of Taiwan. The trip proceeds despite pressure from China to block it.

stories.title: Illegal party at French military site draws nearly 40.000
stories.summary: Up to 40,000 people gathered for an illegal rave at a former military site in France. Local authorities had to deploy bomb disposal experts after a shell was discovered near a road running through the party area.

stories.title: President, PM renew resolve to protect journalistic freedom, stress credible reporting
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif issued messages on World Press Freedom Day reaffirming the government's commitment to protecting press freedom. President Zardari referenced the event's theme, "Shaping a Future at Peace," linking truth to peace.

stories.title: Blue and White MK Chili Tropper quits party, raising speculation about his future… and Gantz’s
stories.summary: Israeli Knesset member Chili Tropper announced his departure from Benny Gantz's Blue and White party. Reports suggest he may join a party led by Gadi Eisenkot, fueling speculation about the future of Gantz's faction.

stories.title: US President Trump says not likely to accept Iranian proposal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would review a 14-point peace proposal submitted by Iran through mediator Pakistan but expressed doubt it would be acceptable, stating Tehran had "not yet paid a big enough price." The proposal was reported by Iranian news agencies Tasnim and Fars.

stories.title: OPEC+ raises oil output quotas for 'stability' after shock UAE pull-out
stories.summary: Seven OPEC+ members, including Russia and Saudi Arabia, raised their oil production quotas on Sunday. Analysts say the move aims to project stability following the United Arab Emirates' abrupt departure from the bloc, which took effect on Friday.

stories.title: OPEC+ hikes oil production quotas but stays mum on UAE pull-out
stories.summary: OPEC+ members including Saudi Arabia and Russia raised their collective oil production quota on Sunday, the third consecutive increase. The move came after the United Arab Emirates withdrew from the group, though the cartel did not formally address the UAE's departure.

stories.title: USAID finds evidence four more UNRWA employees participated in Oct. 7, have Hamas affiliation
stories.summary: A USAID investigation found evidence that four additional UNRWA employees participated in the October 7 attacks or had affiliations with Hamas. To date, 21 individuals have been suspended or disbarred as a result of the agency's investigations.

stories.title: Military and construction waste in Ukraine could become additional source of energy, says Turkish expert
stories.summary: A Turkish expert has proposed converting millions of tons of military and construction waste accumulated in Ukraine due to the war into an energy source. The waste could potentially be used to generate electricity and heat for the Ukrainian population.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill 10 as Zelensky says Ukraine hits oil tankers and terminal
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes across Ukraine killed at least three people, while a Ukrainian attack killed one person near Moscow. Ukraine also claimed strikes on Russian "shadow fleet" oil tankers, according to President Zelensky.

stories.title: How can China best profit from Trump’s latest rift with traditional US allies?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Beijing could benefit from Donald Trump's escalating disputes with European allies, including orders to withdraw US troops from Germany and threats to do the same in Italy and Spain. Some argue China should avoid drawing attention to itself while Washington's actions strain traditional transatlantic alliances.

stories.title: German fertiliser makers and farmers struggle with Iran war fallout
stories.summary: German fertiliser manufacturers and farmers are facing supply disruptions linked to the Israel-Iran war, as roughly one-third of global fertiliser supplies normally transit through the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict has raised concerns about sustained impacts on agricultural supply chains in Germany.

stories.title: 40 children narrowly escape Russian drone strike on bus near Dnipro: six wounded include a child and a pregnant woman
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a bus carrying approximately 40 children near Dnipro, Ukraine, wounding six people including a child and a pregnant woman. Across Ukraine, Russian attacks killed at least eight civilians and injured 90 in a single day, with 26 injured in Kherson Oblast alone.

stories.title: TNS student senate cuts Hillel ties over Israel trips, university says decision lacks 'authority'
stories.summary: The student senate at The New School (TNS) voted to cut ties with Hillel over the organization's Israel trip programs. The university stated the student senate's decision lacks institutional authority. Hillel TNS could regain good standing by renouncing its Hillel chapter status and ending participation in several Israel student trips.

stories.title: Enemy shell hits near gas station in Dnipropetrovsk region, six people wounded, including child and pregnant woman
stories.summary: Russian forces struck near a gas station in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, wounding six people including a child and a pregnant woman.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists appear in Israeli court after abduction
stories.summary: Activists seized from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla appeared before an Israeli court, which extended their detention by two days for further interrogation. A rights group reported the development to Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Russian strike kills one as Ukraine launches hundreds of drones
stories.summary: Russia reported that its air defence units intercepted and destroyed 334 Ukrainian drones overnight across more than a dozen regions near its western border. A Russian strike reportedly killed one person. Ukraine launched the large-scale drone operation targeting multiple Russian regions.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 3 – Scared and angry London Jews feel UK isn’t fighting antisemitism
stories.summary: A daily briefing covered the aftermath of a stabbing in London's Golders Green neighborhood and rising concerns among British Jews about antisemitism. The report also examined the economic situation in Israel's north and Haredi real estate developments in the south.

stories.title: Nepal’s Army in spotlight as new government takes assertive turn
stories.summary: Concerns have emerged about shrinking civic space and weakened democratic norms in Nepal since a new government took office a month ago. Attention has focused on the Nepal Army's growing prominence as Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli's administration prioritizes rapid delivery and an assertive governing approach.

stories.title: 2 dead after boat runs aground in France in failed crossing to UK
stories.summary: A migrant boat carrying 82 people ran aground on Hardelot beach near Boulogne-sur-Mer in northern France after its engine failed during an attempted English Channel crossing. Two people died and 16 were injured, including three with serious burns.

stories.title: Polanski says he would discourage ‘globalise the intifada’ chant but warns against march bans
stories.summary: UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski said he would discourage protesters from using the chant "globalise the intifada" but warned against legally banning the phrase or prohibiting a planned pro-Palestine march in London. Prime Minister Keir Starmer had called for tougher action against the chant following an attack on Jewish people in Golders Green.

stories.title: Japan contains one of its biggest wildfires in decades after 11-day battle
stories.summary: Wildfires in Japan's mountainous Iwate region were brought under control after an 11-day firefighting effort involving hundreds of firefighters and over 1,000 military personnel. The blazes burned approximately 1,600 hectares, damaged at least eight buildings, and caused two minor injuries.

stories.title: Two people dead after explosion at house in Bristol
stories.summary: Two people died after an explosion at a house in Bristol, England, early Sunday morning. Avon and Somerset police declared a major incident and are treating the cause as suspicious.

stories.title: In Kherson region, village of Inzhenerne attacked by drones for two days; casualties and damage reported
stories.summary: Russian troops conducted massive drone attacks on the village of Inzhenerne in the Kherson region's Naddniprianske subdistrict over two consecutive days, causing casualties and property damage.

stories.title: What’s Iran’s 14-point proposal to end the war? And will Trump accept it?
stories.summary: The United States is reviewing a 14-point proposal from Iran aimed at ending the ongoing conflict between the two sides. Deep mutual mistrust remains a significant obstacle to any agreement.

stories.title: Police arrest 12-year-old for bringing weapons to school, alleged intent to harm others
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a 12-year-old student for allegedly bringing weapons to school with intent to harm others. The school's principal said the suspect was released the same day but will not be allowed to return to the school.

stories.title: Top civil servants ‘liable if they don’t flag systemic loopholes’ under proposal
stories.summary: Hong Kong Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung announced a proposed accountability framework that would hold government department heads personally liable for failing to report systemic loopholes to superiors. Public perception may also factor into decisions on civil service pay adjustments.

stories.title: In village battered by settler violence, Palestinian still in coma nearly month after attack
stories.summary: Palestinian resident Zahran Shanabla of the West Bank village of Qusra remains in a coma nearly a month after being found unconscious following a settler assault in early April. The village's former mayor warned that ongoing settler harassment may provoke local residents to fight back.

stories.title: Taiwan President Lai Ching-te tours Eswatini amid diplomatic support
stories.summary: Taiwan President Lai Ching-te arrived in Eswatini for a state visit aimed at strengthening ties with one of Taipei's few remaining diplomatic allies. The visit proceeds despite international pressure from China to isolate Taiwan diplomatically.

stories.title: Most Jewish Mamdani voters support 2-state solution, fear rising antisemitism: poll
stories.summary: A poll of Jewish voters who supported New York politician Mamdani found that over 90% back a two-state solution and fear rising antisemitism. Most respondents linked rejection of Israel's existence with antisemitism.

stories.title: Lucy Powell says Labour has ‘no magic bullet’ as MPs brace for heavy losses in local elections
stories.summary: UK Labour deputy leader Lucy Powell warned there is "no magic bullet" for the party's problems as MPs prepare for expected heavy losses in local elections. She acknowledged widespread anger among Labour MPs following the Peter Mandelson vetting scandal.

stories.title: US ‘drowning in misinformation’ under RFK Jr, autism advocates say
stories.summary: A report accuses top health officials in the Trump administration, including HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., of fueling a "crisis of public trust" through misinformation about vaccines and autism. Autism advocates are calling on Congress to conduct oversight hearings and consider impeachment proceedings.

stories.title: How 2 Iranian brothers in China use ancient music as a bridge through wartime
stories.summary: Iranian twin brothers Majid and Massoud Shamaeezadah performed a concert of traditional Persian music in Beijing using ancient instruments. The musicians, based in China, said their performances carry deep emotional connections to their home country of Iran amid the ongoing war.

stories.title: Attack on civilian transport in Kherson: Injury toll climbs to five, one dead
stories.summary: A Russian attack on civilian transport in the Dniprovskyi district of Kherson killed one person and injured a total of five. An ambulance was also damaged in the attack.

stories.title: Paramilitary forces drone strike kills 5 near Sudan capital
stories.summary: A drone strike by Sudan's Rapid Support Forces killed five people near the capital on Saturday. The attack struck a vehicle traveling to Omdurman and is the latest incident targeting civilians on public roads in the area.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Israeli military urges southern Lebanon residents to evacuate amid operations against Hezbollah
stories.summary: The Israeli military urged residents of towns in southern Lebanon to evacuate amid ongoing operations against Hezbollah, warning that anyone near Hezbollah fighters or facilities could be at risk. Separately, US President Donald Trump said he was "not satisfied" with Iran's latest peace proposal, rejecting it almost immediately after it was delivered.

stories.title: Pilot, co-pilot arrested in deadly Bolivian military plane crash
stories.summary: The pilot and co-pilot of a Bolivian military plane involved in a deadly crash have been arrested and placed in pre-trial detention. They face charges of involuntary manslaughter related to the incident.

stories.title: Africa: DRC's Rise to Africa's Top Five - A Moment Built on Minerals and Momentum
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is projected to become sub-Saharan Africa's fifth-largest economy by 2026. The anticipated rise is driven by the country's vast mineral wealth and growing economic momentum, marking a significant shift in Africa's economic order.

stories.title: Israel issues evacuation warnings for 11 south Lebanon villages
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings for 11 villages in southern Lebanon. Despite an existing ceasefire, Israeli forces have continued conducting strikes and demolishing villages in the region.

stories.title: Post Oct. 7 world: Israel to purchase 50 F-35s, 25 new F-15s, doubling fleet sizes
stories.summary: Israel approved a roughly NIS 350 billion deal to purchase 50 F-35 and 25 new F-15 fighter jets, effectively doubling the size of both fleets. The agreement resolves an internal debate over which aircraft platform to prioritize.

stories.title: Invaders launch ballistic missile strike on Mykolaiv, leaving two people injured
stories.summary: Two people were injured in the Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv on May 3 following a Russian ballistic missile strike.

stories.title: AG said soon to file indictment against PM’s ex-chief of staff, who has been named ambassador to UK
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General is reportedly preparing to indict Tzachi Braverman, Prime Minister Netanyahu's former chief of staff who has been named ambassador to the UK. Braverman is suspected of interfering with an investigation into a classified document leak.

stories.title: Israel–Iran energy infrastructure war signals a dangerous new escalation - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israeli and Iranian strikes on refineries and gas facilities represent a dangerous new phase in the Israel-Iran conflict, with systemic risks extending beyond the immediate battlefield.

stories.title: 4 Killed, Oil Tankers Hit in Russian and Ukrainian Drone Strikes
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes on Ukraine killed three people, while Ukrainian drone attacks killed one person near Moscow. Ukraine also claimed to have struck Russian oil tankers in separate operations.

stories.title: Ukraine Hits Russian Oil Sites as 8 Killed in Both Countries
stories.summary: Ukraine reported striking several Russian ships on Sunday as both sides exchanged hundreds of drones. Eight people were killed across both countries in the latest round of attacks.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz blockade and other major naval sieges in modern times
stories.summary: An analysis examines the strategic use of naval blockades in modern warfare, including the Strait of Hormuz. Such blockades use sea control to cut supply lines and compel an adversary's surrender.

stories.title: Hospitals in Lebanon overwhelmed with patients injured by Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Hospitals across Lebanon are reportedly overwhelmed with patients wounded by Israeli military strikes. Medical facilities are struggling to cope with the influx of casualties.

stories.title: After Maduro
stories.summary: Following the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, supporters of his Bolivarian revolution are mobilizing to restore him to power. Reporters followed those fighting to keep the movement alive.

stories.title: ‘Nowhere to go’: domestic helpers spending days off in tents amid lack of options
stories.summary: Foreign domestic helpers in Hong Kong have been setting up tents beneath bus terminuses on their days off, citing a lack of alternative spaces. The tents, spotted in areas from Tai Po to Central, drew online attention during mainland China's Labour Day holiday, with some initially mistaking them for tourist camps.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes police car in Sumy region; injuries reported
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a police car in Bilopillia, Sumy region, seriously injuring two law enforcement officers.

stories.title: Bahria Town residents in Rawalpindi protest against absence of ‘basic amenities’
stories.summary: Residents of Bahria Town Phases 1–8 in Rawalpindi staged a protest at Allama Iqbal Junction Phase 8 on Saturday, demanding basic civic amenities from Bahria Town Private Limited and its founder Malik Riaz. Traders, property owners, families, and Jamaat-i-Islami representatives joined the demonstration, citing hefty fees paid without adequate services in return.

stories.title: Rubio to visit Vatican, Rome after Trump row
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit the Vatican and Rome following a dispute between the Trump administration and Pope Leo over his anti-war rhetoric. The row also involved criticism of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni for defending the pontiff.

stories.title: Polanski says he would ‘discourage’ the use of ‘globalise the intifada’ chant on marches – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Green Party leader Polanski apologized for retweeting a post about police force during an arrest in Golders Green and said he would discourage use of the chant "globalise the intifada" at marches. Prime Minister Starmer indicated support for banning some pro-Palestine demonstrations in certain instances, prompting organizers to warn of threats to free assembly.

stories.title: Nigeria summons South African envoy over attacks on its nationals
stories.summary: Nigeria summoned the South African ambassador in response to a wave of anti-migrant protests in South Africa, some of which turned violent and targeted Nigerian nationals.

stories.title: Takaichi bound for Australia to strengthen economic, security ties
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is visiting Australia for a three-day trip focused on defense, critical minerals, and economic security. The visit to Canberra follows an updated regional strategy she outlined in Vietnam, as both countries share growing concerns about the changing security environment in the Indo-Pacific.

stories.title: Anti-Christian aggressions on the rise in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Religious groups have documented a rise in harassment and violence against Christians in Israeli-occupied East Jerusalem. The Old City, home to holy sites for Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, has become a primary flashpoint for anti-Christian aggressions.

stories.title: The Strait of Hormuz: How the world endorsed Iran's blackmail - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion article contends that energy infrastructure has become a key battleground in the Iran conflict, with Iran's actions at the Strait of Hormuz threatening regional stability and global supply chains.

stories.title: Cuba's economy collapses, prices soar
stories.summary: Cuba is facing its worst economic crisis in decades, with many residents saying conditions surpass those of the 1990s Special Period following the collapse of Soviet support. The island imports approximately 80% of its food, and essential goods are becoming increasingly scarce amid a deepening energy emergency.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike two vessels of Russian shadow fleet at Novorossiysk Port entrance
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces struck two vessels belonging to Russia's shadow oil fleet at the entrance to the port of Novorossiysk.

stories.title: Trump: Iran should pay 'big price' before US agrees to deal
stories.summary: President Trump stated that Iran should pay a "big price" before the U.S. agrees to any deal. The two countries remain locked in a standoff over Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. blockade on Iranian ports.

stories.title: ‘Apartheid in the US’: Arizona’s secretary of state fights Trump’s plot to amass a ‘master list’ of voters
stories.summary: Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes has warned that the Trump administration is attempting to forcibly extract voter files from 30 states to build a centralized database of all Americans. Fontes cautioned that such a database could be used to regulate political opponents, including restricting access to bank accounts and healthcare.

stories.title: Are US Air Force C-17s flying cars into Beijing for Trump’s China trip?
stories.summary: Two U.S. Air Force C-17 heavy-lift cargo aircraft were spotted landing at Beijing Capital International Airport, signaling preparations for President Donald Trump's expected visit to China this month. Aviation enthusiasts in China posted images of the planes on social media.

stories.title: Ukraine drone attack hits Russian Baltic port, governor says
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck a Russian Baltic port with drones, according to the regional governor. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also reported Ukrainian strikes on two shadow fleet tankers near the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk.

stories.title: Two arrested for allegedly shooting at anti-government protesters with airsoft gun
stories.summary: Two suspects were arrested in Beersheba, Israel, for allegedly firing an airsoft gun at anti-government protesters from a moving car. Participants were hit but no injuries were reported. Separately, demonstrators in Tel Aviv called for a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 events.

stories.title: In Gaza, handmade dolls offer comfort to children after years of war
stories.summary: In Gaza, a mother of five has begun making handmade dolls to comfort children who lost their toys during years of war and restrictions. The initiative aims to provide emotional support to young people affected by the devastation.

stories.title: Japan contains one of its biggest wildfires in decades after 11-day battle
stories.summary: Japanese authorities contained one of the country's largest wildfires in decades after an 11-day firefighting effort. The blaze burned an area nearly five times the size of New York City's Central Park.

stories.title: One person killed and 18 others injured in Sumy region due to Russian shelling
stories.summary: One person was killed and 18 others were injured in Ukraine's Sumy region over the past 24 hours as a result of Russian attacks.

stories.title: Donald Trump says U.S. not likely to accept new Iran peace proposal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump indicated the United States is unlikely to accept a new Iranian peace proposal. Iran's Tasnim and Fars news agencies reported that Tehran had submitted a 14-point proposal to Pakistan, which is serving as a mediator in the negotiations.

stories.title: Are Somali pirates on a comeback in 2026?
stories.summary: Somali piracy, which peaked in 2010 and largely disappeared by 2013, has reportedly resurged in 2026. The development raises renewed concerns about maritime security in the waters off the Horn of Africa.

stories.title: ISW: Russia lost ground in Ukraine in April 2026 — first net loss since the Kursk incursion of August 2024
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War assessed that Russian forces lost control of 116 square kilometers in Ukraine during April 2026, marking Russia's first net territorial loss since the Kursk incursion of August 2024. The rate of Russian advance has been steadily declining since November 2025.

stories.title: Two Gaza flotilla activists to appear before Israeli court
stories.summary: Two foreign activists from a Gaza-bound flotilla are set to appear before an Israeli court. The detained activists have alleged brutal treatment, and the hearing was delayed amid a dispute over alleged links to the U.S.-sanctioned PCPA.

stories.title: Israel approves plan to buy F-35 and F-15I aircraft from US
stories.summary: Israel's defense ministry gave final approval to purchase two new combat squadrons of F-35 and F-15Ia aircraft from Lockheed Martin and Boeing in a deal worth tens of billions of shekels.

stories.title: Two Palestinians killed by Israeli fire since dawn
stories.summary: Two Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire in southern Gaza since dawn, according to Wafa news agency. One victim was shot east of Khan Younis, and a 15-year-old was killed in an Israeli drone strike. The post-ceasefire death toll in Gaza has reached 831.

stories.title: Israel weighs Gaza war restart after killing 3 Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel is considering resuming military operations in Gaza after killing three Palestinians, as ceasefire violations continue. Mediation efforts are ongoing amid the escalation.

stories.title: Soldier seriously wounded during hazing ritual, 4 comrades indicted
stories.summary: Four Israel Defense Forces soldiers have been indicted after a hazing ritual left a fellow combat soldier hospitalized with a punctured lung. The IDF condemned the abuse as unacceptable. The incident is the latest in a series of extreme hazing cases within the military.

stories.title: UK Jews turning to veterans from elite British units to guard community sites – report
stories.summary: Jewish community organizations in the United Kingdom, including the CST security group, are reportedly hiring veterans from elite British military units such as the Royal Marines and Parachute Regiment to guard community sites. Institutions are drawing on their own funds to help cover the costs.

stories.title: Two dead and five injured in Odesa region following attack on port infrastructure
stories.summary: Two people were killed and five others injured in Ukraine's Odesa region following a Russian attack targeting port infrastructure.

stories.title: Israel cancels Lag Ba’omer Meron pilgrimage after Home Front Command warnings
stories.summary: Israeli authorities cancelled the annual Lag Ba'omer pilgrimage to Mount Meron following Home Front Command warnings. Officials had initially considered a reduced symbolic event allowing gatherings of up to 1,500 people per compound before ultimately cancelling.

stories.title: King Charles grasped ‘opportunity’ on US trip, palace says
stories.summary: King Charles visited the United States and delivered a speech emphasizing the importance of NATO. Buckingham Palace said the trip was a diplomatic opportunity, and the speech received praise from both supporters and opponents of President Trump.

stories.title: Recruitment day for several ultra-Orthodox military tracks opens across Israel
stories.summary: Israel held recruitment days for several ultra-Orthodox military tracks, including the Hetz Company, Netzah Yehuda Battalion, and Hasmonaim Brigade. All three units have operated across multiple fronts during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Iran to turn university hit in US-Israeli strikes into museum
stories.summary: Iran announced plans to convert Isfahan University of Technology into a museum after the facility was damaged in a U.S.-Israeli strike in March. The university is considered one of the largest in Iran.

stories.title: UK airlines given green light to cancel or consolidate flights to conserve jet fuel
stories.summary: UK airlines have been authorized to cancel or consolidate flights this summer to conserve jet fuel amid ongoing Middle East conflict disrupting supply chains. Carriers are reviewing timetables to identify flights that can be cut with minimal disruption to avoid widespread summer travel chaos.

stories.title: JUI-F threatens protests over seminary raids in Balochistan
stories.summary: The Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) in Balochistan announced a protest movement against raids on religious seminaries across the province. Provincial chief Senator Maulana Abdul Wasey said a shutter-down strike would take place on May 6, followed by a march of seminary students and party workers toward Quetta on May 10.

stories.title: US to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany, Trump promises to cut 'a lot further'
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany, its largest European base, with President Trump promising further cuts. The drawdown comes amid tensions with Europe over the Iran war and tariff disputes.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists from Spain and Brazil appear in Israeli court
stories.summary: Two activists from a Gaza-bound flotilla—one from Spain and one from Brazil—appeared before an Israeli court after being detained. They were among 175 people intercepted in the Mediterranean as a flotilla of over 50 vessels attempted to break Israel's blockade of Gaza and deliver supplies.

stories.title: War update: 141 combat clashes over past day, fiercest fighting in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 141 combat clashes with Russian troops on May 2, with the fiercest fighting occurring in the Pokrovsk sector. Increased Russian pressure was also recorded in the Huliaipole and Kostiantynivka sectors.

stories.title: Persisting security challenge
stories.summary: An analysis highlights that Pakistan's focus on facilitating US-Iran talks has overshadowed pressing internal security challenges, a deteriorating relationship with Afghanistan, and the approaching first anniversary of the Pakistan-India standoff. The commentary argues that media and public discourse have inadequately addressed these domestic and regional concerns.

stories.title: Spotlight on the continued decline of press freedom globally
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that global press freedom has fallen to its lowest level in 25 years, releasing its annual index ahead of World Press Freedom Day. Partner organization Cartooning for Peace published animated films by cartoonists from Russia, Canada, and Turkey to mark the occasion.

stories.title: Ukrainian elderly woman rescued using robotic vehicle
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces attacked two tankers from Russia's shadow fleet near the Port of Novorossiysk on the Black Sea, as announced by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Separately, in Donetsk Oblast, an elderly woman was rescued using an unmanned ground vehicle.

stories.title: Germany troop cuts send wrong signal to Russia, say two top US Republicans
stories.summary: The chairs of the U.S. House and Senate Armed Services Committees criticized the planned withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany, warning it sends the wrong signal to Russia and risks undermining deterrence in Europe.

stories.title: Inflation surging past 50% in Iran
stories.summary: Inflation in Iran has surged past 50 percent as a US naval blockade of Iranian ports has sharply reduced the country's oil exports. Despite a fragile ceasefire pausing military hostilities, Iranians face rising prices for everyday goods and growing job losses.

stories.title: Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi hospitalised
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was urgently transferred from prison to a hospital after reportedly fainting twice on Friday. Her foundation described a severe deterioration in her health, following a suspected heart attack in late March.

stories.title: Air defenses down 249 out of 268 drones launched by Russia in overnight attack on Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 249 of 268 drones launched by Russia in an overnight attack beginning on May 2, according to Ukrainian military officials.

stories.title: New Iranian proposal to end the war under examination
stories.summary: A senior Iranian military officer said fresh fighting with the United States is "likely" after President Trump dismissed Tehran's latest negotiating proposal. The statement underscores rising tensions as Trump issued fresh threats to attack Iran.

stories.title: Attempted White House dinner assassin seeks to downgrade from prison suicide precautions
stories.summary: The individual who attempted an assassination at a White House dinner is seeking to be moved from suicide-prevention precautions. The suspect, identified as Allen, was placed in a padded safe cell with 24-hour lockdown procedures.

stories.title: Two foreign activists seized from Gaza aid flotilla appear before Israeli court
stories.summary: Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian citizen Thiago Avila appeared before an Israeli court on Sunday after being seized from a humanitarian aid flotilla bound for Gaza. Avila told his lawyers he was beaten so severely in Israeli custody that he lost consciousness twice.

stories.title: Israel issues new forced displacement orders in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel issued forced displacement orders covering more than ten villages and towns in southern Lebanon, including several in the Nabatieh district located north of the Litani River.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists detained by Israel face ‘extreme brutality’
stories.summary: Two foreign activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla of over 50 vessels appeared before an Israeli court after being detained. The flotilla, which departed from France, Spain, and Italy to break the Israeli blockade of Gaza, was intercepted by Israeli forces in international waters off Greece.

stories.title: Your backyard is the new front line - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses how electromagnetic threats have expanded from military battlefields to civilian areas, arguing that existing regulations have not kept pace with the evolving risks.

stories.title: “Kinetic sanctions” in action: Two more Russian shadow fleet tankers hit at Novorossiysk — the second naval drone strike in five days
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck two Russian shadow fleet oil tankers near the port of Novorossiysk, marking the second naval drone attack in five days. President Zelenskyy posted thermal footage showing a naval drone striking one of the vessels.

stories.title: Trump to review Iranian truce proposal as Israel strikes Lebanon
stories.summary: President Trump said he would review Iran's latest truce proposal but expressed doubt about agreeing to a deal. The announcement came as Israel continued conducting strikes in Lebanon.

stories.title: Why Hong Kong subsidies should go towards food, not fuel
stories.summary: The article argues Hong Kong should not renew its HK$3 per litre diesel subsidy when it expires at the end of June. It proposes redirecting the funds toward accelerating electrification of public transport, particularly the minibus fleet, amid rising fuel prices linked to the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: On press freedoms
stories.summary: On World Press Freedom Day, a commentary examines the state of media independence in Pakistan. It references a recent Pakistan Press Foundation report documenting escalating restrictions, repression, and other methods used to curtail press freedom over the past year, warning that such curbs jeopardize individual liberties.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,080 over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military estimated that Russia's total combat losses since the February 2022 full-scale invasion reached approximately 1,334,030 personnel by May 3, 2026, including 1,080 casualties in the preceding 24 hours.

stories.title: China calls Taiwan's president a 'rat' as he meets Eswatini king in surprise visit
stories.summary: China condemned Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te's surprise visit to Eswatini, calling him a "rat." During the meeting with King Mswati III, Lai declared Taiwan a sovereign nation.

stories.title: Foreign investors exit T-bills
stories.summary: Foreign investors have largely exited Pakistan's Treasury bills amid the regional conflict, according to State Bank of Pakistan data. The central bank recently raised T-bill yields by up to 83 basis points to nearly 12% in an effort to attract investment.

stories.title: Oil spike threatens Pakistan’s economic growth
stories.summary: Analysts warn that surging oil prices driven by the Middle East conflict could push Pakistan's inflation above 11%, widen the current account deficit beyond $8 billion, and slow GDP growth to 2.5–3.0% in fiscal year 2027.

stories.title: ‘It’s like a cat and mouse game’: on the frontline of Belgium’s fight against drug smugglers
stories.summary: Customs officers at the port of Antwerp, Belgium, are intensifying scanning operations to combat drug smuggling through one of Europe's main commercial gateways. Authorities have warned that Belgium risks becoming a narco-state as smugglers use increasingly sophisticated methods.

stories.title: Crowd disarms knife-wielding woman at Malaysia water festival
stories.summary: A woman armed with a knife was tackled by bystanders and security personnel during the Rain Rave Water Music Festival in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on Saturday night. The 28-year-old was arrested by police at the scene for possession of a weapon.

stories.title: Fuelling a continent: how China’s engineering prowess built Africa’s biggest oil refinery
stories.summary: The Dangote oil refinery in Lagos, Nigeria, built by Chinese engineering firms at a cost of about $20 billion, has supplied fuel to multiple African countries during energy disruptions caused by Middle East tensions. The refinery operates at a capacity of 650,000 barrels per day.

stories.title: Quirky China: robot plays dead for pesticide warnings; bot hugs girl, in-car toilet approved
stories.summary: A patrol robot in a high-visibility vest warning visitors about pesticide spraying at a park in Jilin province, northeastern China, went viral online. The robot used a loud hailer to humorously announce that worms exposed to the pesticide would "lie down and pretend to be dead."

stories.title: Russian drones hit energy infrastructure in Mykolaiv region, partial outages reported
stories.summary: Russian forces launched an overnight drone attack targeting energy infrastructure in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, causing partial power outages in the area.

stories.title: Germany takes US troop drawdown in stride but deterrence gaps remain
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced a withdrawal of approximately 5,000 US troops from Germany. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said the drawdown should spur Europeans to strengthen their own defences. Two senior Republican US lawmakers expressed concern over the decision, while NATO said it was working to understand the details of the plan.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A morning briefing summarized diplomatic developments around Iran's 14-point truce proposal, continued Israeli military activity in Lebanon, and disruptions to global energy flows. President Trump warned attacks could resume if Iran "misbehaves" while indirect engagement reportedly continues.

stories.title: Bin Laden nearly slipped out of Abbottabad: CIA report
stories.summary: A newly released CIA account reveals that Osama bin Laden had agreed in writing to relocate from his Abbottabad compound by September 2011, months before the May 2011 US raid. The CIA claims it was unaware of the relocation plan and says a delayed operation would have missed him.

stories.title: Israel approves purchase of 2 more squadrons of F-35I and F-15IA fighter jets from US
stories.summary: Israel's defense ministry approved the purchase of two additional squadrons of F-35I and F-15IA fighter jets from the United States. Defense officials said the procurement follows lessons learned from the recent Iran war. Shipments carrying 6,500 tons of military equipment also arrived in Israel.

stories.title: Man shot dead in Shfaram in 100th violent killing of 2026 in Arab community
stories.summary: A 28-year-old man named Hadi Su'ad was shot dead in Shfaram, marking the 100th violent killing of 2026 within Israel's Arab community. Reports indicate his father and brother were also killed in the past year in an apparent gangland feud that has claimed 35 lives.

stories.title: One in three HR leaders face opposition to inclusion schemes, study finds
stories.summary: A YouGov poll of 565 UK HR decision-makers, commissioned by employment charity Working Chance, found that more than a third faced pushback against equity, diversity, and inclusion initiatives over the past year. The charity warned this resistance could affect hiring prospects for people with criminal convictions.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war highlights: Trump casts doubt on new peace proposal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he would review a new peace proposal submitted by Iran but cast doubt on its acceptability. Tehran sent the plan, and Trump expressed skepticism about its prospects amid the ongoing Israel-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Iran juggles oil cuts and storage strain to resist US blockade
stories.summary: Iran is proactively reducing crude oil output to manage limited storage capacity as it faces a U.S. blockade. The strategy aims to avoid tanks reaching full capacity rather than waiting for a forced shutdown.

stories.title: Jordanian Armed Forces target drugs, weapons smuggling sites in Syria
stories.summary: The Jordanian Armed Forces carried out a precision operation targeting drug and weapons smuggling sites inside Syria. The military said the strikes aimed to prevent trafficked narcotics and arms from reaching Jordanian territory.

stories.title: Trump says US could restart Iran strikes ‘if they misbehave’
stories.summary: President Trump warned that the U.S. could resume strikes on Iran "if they misbehave." He said he had been told about the concept of a proposed deal with Iran but was waiting to receive the exact wording.

stories.title: Ukrainian National Guard destroys Russian Zhitel EW system in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Ukrainian National Guard drone operators from Lasar's Group destroyed a Russian R-330Zh Zhitel electronic warfare system in the Kharkiv region of Ukraine.

stories.title: South Korea holds pro-Palestine protest in solidarity with Gaza
stories.summary: Protesters gathered in Seoul, South Korea, to demonstrate in solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza amid ongoing Israeli military operations in the territory.

stories.title: CNN: Hezbollah fibre-optic drones pose major challenge
stories.summary: CNN reported that Hezbollah is deploying fibre-optic quadcopter drones that transmit no wireless signal, making them extremely difficult to jam or trace. Israeli military experts described the systems as highly effective due to their undetectable control method.

stories.title: ‘Not FIFA’s job’: Norway soccer chief calls to scrap FIFA Peace Prize after Trump award
stories.summary: Norwegian Football Federation president criticized FIFA's decision to award US President Donald Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize in December 2025, arguing that administering peace prizes is not FIFA's role.

stories.title: Iran says ball in US court on war or diplomacy
stories.summary: Iran's military warned that renewed hostilities with the United States are likely, while stating the diplomatic ball is in Washington's court. A protester in Washington, D.C., climbed the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge calling for an end to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Iran submits 14-point response to U.S. proposal to end war – CNN
stories.summary: Iran submitted a 14-point response to a US proposal aimed at ending the ongoing conflict, according to CNN. The document outlines Iran's conditions for a diplomatic resolution.

stories.title: Trump says US will cut its number of troops in Germany ‘way down’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated the United States would significantly reduce its troop presence in Germany. The Pentagon's announcement followed a public dispute between Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over defence spending and transatlantic relations.
