stories.title: 'An unforgettable show': Fans flock to free Shakira concert on Rio's Copacabana beach
stories.summary: Colombian superstar Shakira performed a free mega-concert on Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana beach, drawing large crowds of fans to the event.

stories.title: Iraq oil exports could resume within a week, minister says
stories.summary: Iraq's Deputy Oil Minister Basim Mohammed stated that Iraq could restore oil output and exports to normal levels within seven days once the Strait of Hormuz crisis ends. Current production stands at about 1.5 million barrels per day, with roughly 200,000 barrels exported via Ceyhan, Turkey.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. could restart Iran strikes ‘if they misbehave’
stories.summary: President Trump said the U.S. could restart military strikes on Iran "if they misbehave." He confirmed he had been briefed on the concept of an Iranian deal proposal and was awaiting the exact wording.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 65 as Trump reviews new plan to end war?
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new 14-point proposal to the United States aimed at ending the ongoing Iran war, now on its 65th day. President Trump said he is reviewing the plan.

stories.title: North Korea calls US cyber threat claims a fabrication, warns of countermeasures
stories.summary: North Korea's foreign ministry rejected U.S. allegations that Pyongyang poses a cyber threat, calling the claims fabricated to justify Washington's hostile policy. The statement, carried by state media KCNA, warned of possible countermeasures.

stories.title: Kenya battles to stop the 'goons and guns' as fears of political violence grow
stories.summary: Kenya is grappling with more than 100 gangs operating nationwide, as the growing use of political thugs raises concerns about potential violence ahead of upcoming elections.

stories.title: China blocks US sanctions against five ‘teapot’ refineries
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce blocked U.S. sanctions targeting five independent Chinese refineries accused of importing Iranian oil, calling the measures a violation of international law.

stories.title: 'We cannot give up': Hong Kong journalists navigate fear, surveillance and shrinking space
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government rejected criticism from foreign media and press freedom organizations as "slander" after jailed media tycoon Jimmy Lai received a free speech prize in Germany. Press freedom in the city has sharply declined since the 2020 National Security Law, with journalists facing surveillance, visa denials, and legal threats.

stories.title: Embassy of Ukraine in U.S. opens doors to visitors as part of Passport DC
stories.summary: The Embassy of Ukraine in Washington, D.C., opened its doors to the public as part of the annual Passport DC cultural festival, which features open houses at foreign embassies.

stories.title: Hong Kong faces hail threat as amber rainstorm warning issued
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory issued an amber rainstorm warning on Sunday afternoon and warned that hail could affect the city in the short term. The signal indicated heavy rainfall exceeding 30 millimeters per hour had fallen or was expected to persist.

stories.title: Finance chief says Hong Kong on track for strongest quarterly growth in 5 years
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said the city is on track for its strongest quarterly economic growth in nearly five years. He cited a 17 percent rise in visitor numbers and a 5.2 percent increase in retail and catering spending, boosted by mainland China's Labour Day holiday.

stories.title: Taiwan leader visits Eswatini despite China’s attempts to block trip
stories.summary: Taiwanese President William Lai Ching-te visited Eswatini despite Chinese efforts to block the trip, meeting King Mswati III and signing trade agreements between the two countries.

stories.title: Israeli military orders evacuations in 11 south Lebanon towns
stories.summary: The Israeli military ordered residents of 11 towns and villages in southern Lebanon—including Al-Duwayr, Arab Salim, Jebchit, and others near Nabatiyya—to evacuate immediately. The military accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire agreement and warned of forceful action.

stories.title: Casualties reported as Russia launches missile strike on Sumy region
stories.summary: Russian troops carried out a missile strike on civilian infrastructure in the Krolevets community of Ukraine's Sumy region on Saturday evening, injuring six people.

stories.title: Primorsk takes the torch from Tuapse: NASA satellites confirm fresh fires at Russia’s largest Baltic oil export terminal
stories.summary: NASA satellite imagery confirmed new fires at Russia's Primorsk oil export terminal on the Baltic Sea after reported Ukrainian drone activity over Leningrad Oblast on May 2-3. Pulkovo Airport in St. Petersburg was temporarily shut down, and local authorities claimed 59 drones were intercepted.

stories.title: Trump says US to withdraw significantly more than 5,000 troops from Germany
stories.summary: President Trump announced plans to withdraw significantly more than 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany, saying he intends to "cut way down." The drawdown comes amid a rift with NATO over the Iran war and faces bipartisan resistance in Congress.

stories.title: In Yemen, Starlink internet brings opportunities – for some
stories.summary: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service is expanding in Yemen, enabling growth in the country's digital workforce despite resistance from Houthi authorities and affordability barriers for many users.

stories.title: Israeli army demolishes monastery and school in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli army demolished a monastery and a school operated by the Sisters of the Holy Savior in the southern Lebanese border town of Yaroun. The school had served thousands of students from surrounding villages and was considered one of the region's most prominent educational institutions.

stories.title: Iran sets timeline, demands guarantees in peace proposal
stories.summary: Iran submitted a 14-point peace proposal responding to a US plan, calling for all issues to be resolved within 30 days. The framework demands guarantees against future attacks, withdrawal of US forces from around Iran, release of frozen assets, lifting of sanctions, and war reparations.

stories.title: The Oscars are drawing a new line on artificial intelligence
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences introduced new rules addressing the use of artificial intelligence in films eligible for the 2027 Academy Awards, marking the first such regulations.

stories.title: US to supply Israel with precision weapon kits, report says
stories.summary: According to the Israeli newspaper Haaretz, the United States plans to supply Israel with approximately 10,000 advanced precision weapon kits worth nearly $1 billion. The systems convert air-to-ground missiles into precision-guided munitions capable of targeting aerial threats, including some drones.

stories.title: Dynamic pay on platforms such as Uber should be banned, says TUC
stories.summary: The UK's Trades Union Congress called for a ban on dynamic pricing used by gig economy platforms such as Uber to set worker pay. A TUC report found that algorithmic pay-setting decouples earnings from time, skill, and effort, leaving workers describing their income as akin to gambling due to unpredictable wage fluctuations.

stories.title: Bangkok’s beloved street food culture at risk as vendor crackdown widens
stories.summary: Bangkok's street food vendors face growing pressure as Thai authorities widen crackdowns on roadside stalls and carts. The tighter controls threaten the livelihoods of sellers and the open-air food culture that defines the capital, which is popular among both locals and tourists.

stories.title: Inside the unflinching friendship shared between Israel and Serbia - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial highlighted the close relationship between Israel and Serbia, describing Serbia as a country that has consistently supported Israel through actions rather than ambiguous statements.

stories.title: PMD warns of Glof risk as rains, landslides batter GB
stories.summary: Intermittent rain across Gilgit-Baltistan on Saturday triggered landslides that temporarily blocked the Karakoram Highway and the Astore valley road. The Pakistan Meteorological Department issued a fresh alert warning of glacial lake outburst floods due to an approaching westerly weather system. Heavy rain and thunderstorms were also expected in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: In Philippines, youth suicide crisis exposes struggle for mental health support
stories.summary: Rising youth suicide rates in the Philippines, particularly in Manila, have exposed a severe shortage of mental health support. Emotional distress and digital triggers are cited as contributing factors. Advocates, including survivors turned mental health campaigners, are pushing the predominantly Catholic country to more openly address mental health services for young Filipinos.

stories.title: Tusk warns NATO disintegration is greatest threat to transatlantic unity
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that the greatest threat to transatlantic unity is not external adversaries but the ongoing disintegration of NATO.

stories.title: Iran tanker evades US blockade, reaches Asia Pacific, report says
stories.summary: A Very Large Crude Carrier linked to Iran's National Iranian Tanker Company evaded the US naval blockade and reached the Asia Pacific carrying over 1.9 million barrels of crude oil, according to TankerTrackers.com. The vessel was last tracked transiting the Lombok Strait toward the Riau Archipelago.

stories.title: Trump to review Iran's 14-point plan, warns strikes could resume
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated there is a possibility that strikes against Iran could resume if tensions escalate, while also saying he would review Iran's 14-point peace plan. Speaking in Florida, he claimed Tehran is 'decimated' and wants to make a deal.

stories.title: Trump’s US troop removal from Germany rebuked by Republicans, Nato
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced a drawdown of roughly 5,000 US troops from Germany over the next year, prompting criticism from NATO allies and Republican members of Congress. NATO said it is seeking details on the plan, while emphasizing the need for Europe to invest more in its own defence capabilities.

stories.title: Thai police raid illegal school run by Iranian couple, find 89 Israeli kids enrolled
stories.summary: Thai security forces raided an unlicensed school in Thailand run by an Iranian couple, finding 89 Israeli children enrolled. Two Iranian nationals and one Thai national were arrested and charged after complaints about foreigners operating businesses that could threaten national security.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says he 'can't imagine' Iran's latest peace plan is acceptable
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he "can't imagine" Iran's latest 14-point peace proposal is acceptable, casting doubt on its prospects. Iran's Tasnim and Fars news agencies reported that Tehran submitted the proposal through mediator Pakistan. Trump said Iran had "not yet paid a big enough price."

stories.title: Greta Thunberg says activists are being tortured in Israel
stories.summary: Activist Greta Thunberg condemned Israel's interception of more than 20 civilian vessels from the Global Flotilla in international waters, stating that around 200 participants were detained. She said many were released in Crete with injuries, and alleged that at least two activists were tortured.

stories.title: Polanski takes combative approach as Greens enter media spotlight
stories.summary: The UK Green Party faces intensified media scrutiny as it rises in the polls ahead of elections. Party co-leader Adrian Ramsay and others have navigated coverage ranging from legitimate policy questions to sensationalized stories, drawing comparisons to the media treatment of Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg during the 2010 election cycle.

stories.title: 'Aparthied Israel': UN rapporteur calls for release of Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese condemned Israel's interception of the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters and called for the release of two detained activists. She described the operation as hostage-taking and criticized Israel for being allowed to patrol European waters.

stories.title: Greece concerned over Ukraine's conditions for use of jointly produced naval drones – media
stories.summary: Greece has expressed concern over Ukraine's conditions for the use of jointly produced naval drones, particularly Ukraine's desire to have a say in how the weapons would be deployed in the event of military engagement.

stories.title: Millions of jobs lost as Iranians battle ‘Operation Economic Fury’
stories.summary: A ceasefire has paused the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, but the economic fallout—dubbed 'Operation Economic Fury'—continues to devastate daily life in Tehran, with millions of jobs lost across the country.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine give conflicting accounts of village in Sumy region
stories.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed on May 2 that its forces had captured the village of Myropillia in Ukraine's Sumy region. Ukraine's military denied the claim, stating the village had not changed hands. The conflicting accounts highlight the ongoing information battle alongside ground combat.

stories.title: Property management sector cites 25% guard shortage amid imported labour backlash
stories.summary: Hong Kong's property management industry reports a security guard shortfall of up to 25 percent. The sector defended the recruitment of mainland Chinese guards through a government labour importation scheme after the Richland Gardens estate in Kowloon Bay drew backlash for hiring 31 cross-border guards.

stories.title: US approves $8.6bn in arms sales to Middle East allies
stories.summary: The US State Department approved approximately $8.6 billion in arms sales to Middle East allies, invoking emergency circumstances to bypass the usual congressional review process.

stories.title: Nato meetings with TV and film-makers prompt claims it is seeking ‘propaganda’
stories.summary: NATO has held closed-door meetings with film and television writers, directors, and producers in Los Angeles, Brussels, and Paris, with a London session planned for June. The Guardian's reporting prompted accusations that the alliance is attempting to use the entertainment industry to generate propaganda supporting the bloc.

stories.title: Why does China portray India as an elephant? Decoding the politics of animal analogy
stories.summary: An analysis examines China's longstanding use of animal metaphors—the dragon for China and the elephant for India—in diplomatic discourse. The framing, popularized by former Premier Wen Jiabao during a 2010 India visit, has persisted through cycles of border tensions and diplomatic resets over the past 15 years.

stories.title: From phones to humanoid robots: China’s supply chain eyes next growth curve
stories.summary: Chinese smartphone and electronics component suppliers are pivoting toward the fast-growing humanoid robotics industry as the mobile market slows. The crossover gained visibility after Honor's humanoid robot D1, developed by the smartphone maker, won a robot half-marathon in Beijing, outperforming established Chinese robotics firms such as Unitree.

stories.title: How Thailand as transit hub feeds India’s exotic pet craze: ‘it’s organised crime’
stories.summary: Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi airport has emerged as a key transit hub for wild animal smuggling fueling India's exotic pet market. Authorities intercepted a 19-year-old passenger attempting to smuggle wildlife to Taipei. Investigators describe the trade, promoted through social media platforms, as organized crime.

stories.title: Trump says Iran has not yet ‘paid a big enough price’ as he reviews new peace proposal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he would review a new 14-point peace proposal from Iran but expressed doubt about its prospects, stating Tehran had "not yet paid a big enough price." Iran's Tasnim and Fars news agencies reported the proposal was submitted via mediator Pakistan. Tehran said the "ball is in the United States' court."

stories.title: Trump says US not likely to accept new Iran peace proposal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he is reviewing a new Iranian peace proposal but stated he 'can't imagine' accepting it, amid concerns that fighting between the US and Iran could resume.

stories.title: Part of Sumy region left without power due to shelling
stories.summary: Shelling in Ukraine's Sumy region caused power outages affecting part of the area. No further details on casualties or the extent of damage were immediately available.

stories.title: UAE lifts all air traffic restrictions introduced since Iran war
stories.summary: The UAE's aviation authority lifted all air traffic restrictions that had been imposed during the Iran war, signaling a broader recovery in the Middle East travel sector.

stories.title: Qatar rejects report that it backed ICC chief against Netanyahu
stories.summary: Qatar denied reports that it offered to support ICC prosecutor Karim Khan, rejecting the claims and pointing to Israel's history of spreading misinformation on such matters.

stories.title: Trump threatens to take Cuba 'almost immediately' after tightening sanctions on the regime
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said at a private event in West Palm Beach, Florida, that the US would take Cuba "almost immediately." The remarks came hours after Trump signed an executive order substantially expanding economic sanctions against the Cuban government led by Miguel Díaz-Canel, significantly escalating bilateral tensions.

stories.title: Live like a Montefiore at Tel Aviv’s Fiori 41
stories.summary: The Fiori 41 Hotel is located in Tel Aviv's historic Montefiore neighborhood, parallel to Rothschild Boulevard, within the UNESCO-designated White City area.

stories.title: Dubai, Israel, and the impact of the Iran war on hospitality
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran has significantly disrupted Dubai's tourism and hospitality sector, particularly affecting travel from Israel. The impact on the industry was described as almost immediate following the escalation of regional hostilities.

stories.title: Riding the rails through a fractured land, young people reflect on real life, today
stories.summary: A report from a train journey between Nahariya near the Lebanese border and the southern city of Beersheba features six young Israelis discussing 30 months of war, societal divisions, Israeli media, and their hopes for the future.

stories.title: How China’s industrial tourism boom is creating a new generation of tech-savvy children
stories.summary: China is experiencing a boom in industrial tourism, with urban middle-class families visiting high-tech facilities to expose children to real-world technology. Activities include watching electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft at aviation companies, fostering enthusiasm for Chinese technology among a new generation.

stories.title: IDF, Border Police raid illegal weapons production site in Nablus
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Forces and Border Police raided an illegal weapons production site in Nablus in the occupied West Bank. Forces discovered a lathe used for manufacturing weapons along with illegal firearms, including an M16 rifle, a pistol, and a shotgun.

stories.title: Trump expresses doubt that Iran’s peace proposal is ‘acceptable’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he is reviewing Iran's 14-point peace proposal but expressed doubt that it is acceptable, warning that military strikes could resume if Tehran 'misbehaves.'

stories.title: Russia organizes protests near Ukrainian embassies under guise of “honoring memory of victims in Odesa”
stories.summary: Russian authorities organized protests outside Ukrainian embassies worldwide, ostensibly to commemorate victims of a May 2, 2014 incident in Odesa. Ukrainian officials characterized the demonstrations as a Russian propaganda operation.

stories.title: Middle East states eye transport resilience with new logistics corridor to bypass Hormuz
stories.summary: Middle Eastern governments are reviving proposals for overland oil and gas pipelines and planning new rail-sea transport corridors to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping lanes. The push follows wartime disruption of these key maritime routes during the conflict between the US-Israel alliance and the Iran-led Axis of Resistance.

stories.title: Illegal Thai school found to be caring for 89 Israeli children - report
stories.summary: Thai authorities raided an unlicensed school called Arki Kid in Thailand and found 89 Israeli children, aged 2 to 12, being cared for at the facility. The school was only licensed to look after up to 18 children between the ages of 2 and 5.

stories.title: Trump reviewing deal with Iran, says they 'have not yet paid a big enough price'
stories.summary: President Trump confirmed on Truth Social that he is reviewing a plan sent by Iran but stated he "can't imagine that it would be acceptable." He added that Iran has "not yet paid a big enough price."

stories.title: Singapore’s safe-haven status draws more Chinese capital into property sector
stories.summary: Singapore continues to attract significant Chinese capital into its property sector, with China becoming one of the largest sources of real estate investment in the city-state. Analysts attribute the trend to Singapore's safe-haven status amid global uncertainty.

stories.title: Manasseh’s children come home to Zion - and fulfill a 2,700-year promise - opinion
stories.summary: Hundreds of members of the Bnei Menashe community from northeastern India made aliyah to Israel, fulfilling what supporters describe as a 2,700-year-old promise linked to the lost tribe of Manasseh.

stories.title: Iran offers Strait deal; Trump dissatisfied but prefers non-military path
stories.summary: Iran has proposed a deal regarding the Strait of Hormuz, but US President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with the offer. Despite domestic pressure to break Iran's control over the strategic waterway, Trump reportedly prefers a non-military approach to resolving the standoff.

stories.title: Can relocating Pablo Escobar’s hippos to Anant Ambani’s Vantara solve Colombia’s problem?
stories.summary: Colombia has considered relocating some of the invasive hippos descended from Pablo Escobar's private collection to Anant Ambani's Vantara animal sanctuary in India. Questions remain about whether the facility can house around 80 hippos and whether relocating wild animals across continents is feasible.

stories.title: Australia news live: Joyce says plane Rinehart’s company gave One Nation ‘won’t really worry’ voters; three dead and man arrested in Sydney
stories.summary: In Sydney's southwest suburb of Rosemeadow, three people were found dead and a 32-year-old man was arrested early Sunday morning following an incident at a home. Separately, in Australian politics, debate continued over Coalition preferences for One Nation in the Farrer byelection.

stories.title: Airlines rush to help stranded Spirit passengers after budget carrier collapses
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines ceased operations, stranding passengers across the United States. Competing airlines moved to accommodate affected travelers, even as they face rising fuel costs linked to the U.S.-Israel war with Iran.

stories.title: Why did the UAE quit OPEC and OPEC+?
stories.summary: The UAE's decision to withdraw from OPEC and OPEC+ reflects years of simmering competition with Saudi Arabia over production quotas and market influence. The departure raises questions about the impact on global oil prices and the future cohesion of the oil-producing cartel.

stories.title: Russian cyberattacks against Ukraine may be classified as war crimes — CCD
stories.summary: International investigators are increasingly considering Russian cyberattacks against Ukraine as potential war crimes, according to the Cyber Centre for Digital research. The classification could set a precedent in international humanitarian law.

stories.title: Security cabinet to discuss renewed Gaza fighting after Hamas responds to BoP plan - report
stories.summary: Israel's security cabinet is set to discuss renewed military operations in Gaza following Hamas's response to a proposed plan. Israel is seeking concrete steps toward Hamas disarmament and the installation of a new technocratic government in the territory.

stories.title: NYC’s New School rejects student senate’s vote to defund and cut ties with Hillel
stories.summary: The New School in New York City rejected a vote by its student senate to defund and sever ties with Hillel, the prominent Jewish campus organization. University officials stated the student senate lacked the authority to make such a decision.

stories.title: Trump: There’s a possibility we could renew strikes on Iran ‘if they misbehave’
stories.summary: President Trump said he is reviewing a new Iranian proposal to end the war but said he cannot imagine it will be acceptable. He warned of possible renewed strikes on Iran. Separately, Jordan carried out strikes on drug and weapons storage sites in southern Syria.

stories.title: How unlicensed mainland Chinese tour groups cash in on Hong Kong campsites
stories.summary: Unlicensed mainland Chinese tour groups have been operating hiking trips into Hong Kong's countryside during China's Labour Day holiday. The Ham Tin Wan campsite in Sai Kung was packed with an estimated 500 tents, causing sanitation problems.

stories.title: Why Japan-China ties can benefit from promoting people-to-people exchanges
stories.summary: Analysts argue that Japan-China relations, at their lowest point since normalization in 1972, could benefit from expanded people-to-people exchanges to bridge a widening perception and information gap between the two nations.

stories.title: Chinese man makes history as first educator from mainland university to lead top US institute
stories.summary: S. Jack Hu, originally from rural China, was appointed chancellor of UC Riverside, becoming the first person with a bachelor's degree from a mainland Chinese university to lead a top U.S. institution. The 62-year-old's story gained widespread attention on social media.

stories.title: At least six dead, thousands displaced as heavy rains hit northeastern Brazil
stories.summary: Heavy rains in northeastern Brazil killed at least six people and displaced thousands in the states of Pernambuco and Paraiba over a 48-hour period. The Brazilian federal government confirmed the casualties and displacement on May 2.

stories.title: Police neutralize Russian missile with two 400-kilogram warheads in Kirovohrad region
stories.summary: Police explosive experts in Ukraine's Kirovohrad region successfully defused two warheads, each weighing 400 kilograms, from a Russian missile. The operation neutralized the ordnance without casualties.

stories.title: Illegal rave draws 20,000 to 'dangerous' military site in France
stories.summary: An illegal rave drew approximately 20,000 people to a military site in France. Emergency services treated 12 people for minor injuries on the morning of May 2.

stories.title: BGU student initiates website that connects protected space owners with unprotected neighbors
stories.summary: Ben-Gurion University student Tamir Cohen has created a website connecting Israelis who own protected spaces with neighbors who lack access to missile shelters. More than a third of Israelis reportedly live without a standard protected space against ballistic missiles from Iran.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says reviewing 14-point plan; Israel pounds Lebanon
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated he is reviewing a 14-point plan submitted by Iran but expressed doubt that a deal could be reached. Separately, Israel continued airstrikes on Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump says US could restart strikes on Iran
stories.summary: Speaking to reporters in West Palm Beach, Florida, President Donald Trump said the United States could resume military strikes on Iran, highlighting the fragility of the current pause in hostilities between the two countries.

stories.title: Jefferson Lewis charged with murder over death of Kumanjayi Little Baby near Alice Springs
stories.summary: Northern Territory police in Australia charged Jefferson Lewis with the murder of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, a Warlpiri girl who went missing from a town camp near Alice Springs on April 25 and was found dead five days later.

stories.title: Top Republicans express concern over Trump plan to withdraw troops from Germany
stories.summary: Two senior Republican lawmakers expressed concern over the Pentagon's plan to withdraw 5,000 US troops from Germany, a NATO ally. The move is part of broader troop redeployment decisions under the Trump administration.

stories.title: 71-year-old Palestinian woman said injured in settler attack near Hebron
stories.summary: A 71-year-old Palestinian woman and three others were reportedly injured during a settler attack in the village of Jabel Jales near Hebron in the occupied West Bank. The incident reportedly began after settlers entered the village, sparking confrontations with residents.

stories.title: Airlines scramble to help stranded Spirit passengers after budget carrier collapses
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines ceased operations, leaving passengers stranded across the country. Other airlines scrambled to accommodate affected travelers, with the budget carrier's collapse linked in part to economic consequences of the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: War update: 116 clashes on front lines, heaviest fighting in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces and Russian troops engaged in 116 combat clashes since the start of the day, with the heaviest fighting concentrated on the Pokrovsk axis. The intensity of engagements underscores continued Russian pressure along multiple front-line sectors in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran presents 14-point plan to US to end war, Washington yet to respond
stories.summary: Iran submitted a 14-point proposal to the United States aimed at ending the ongoing war, transmitted via Pakistan, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim News Agency. The plan responds to a reported nine-point U.S. proposal that included a ceasefire with a two-month timeline. Tehran is pushing for key issues to be resolved within 30 days.

stories.title: Jordan strikes drug, weapons storage sites in Syria's Suweida
stories.summary: Jordan announced it carried out strikes on drug and weapons smuggling sites in Syria's Suweida province. The targeted area is under the control of anti-government Druze militias. Jordan said the operation aimed to disrupt cross-border narcotics and arms trafficking networks.

stories.title: The Iran war has strengthened Ukraine in surprising ways. Could a ceasefire with Russia be closer?
stories.summary: An analysis suggests the Iran war has indirectly strengthened Ukraine's position, as President Zelensky visited Gulf states to showcase his country's military capabilities. The developments have raised speculation about whether a ceasefire with Russia could be approaching.

stories.title: The clandestine network smuggling Starlink tech into Iran to beat internet blackout
stories.summary: Sahand tells the BBC World Service he sends satellite internet terminals into Iran to help show "the real picture".

stories.title: Philippines volcano erupts, blanketing ash across the sky
stories.summary: The Mayon Volcano in the Bicol region of the Philippines erupted, sending a large cloud of ash and debris into the sky and blanketing surrounding areas.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three in south Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike killed three people in the town of al-Sama'iya in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The attack occurred despite a ceasefire that took effect on April 17, 2026, and was later extended. Israeli forces have continued air strikes and artillery fire across Lebanon throughout the truce period.

stories.title: Kyiv under drone attack as air defense systems engage targets
stories.summary: Russian strike drones attacked Kyiv, prompting air defense systems to engage targets over the Ukrainian capital. The attack is part of Russia's ongoing aerial campaign against Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Iran says US comments confirm ‘piracy’ in maritime actions
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei accused the United States of openly admitting to piracy after remarks by the US president regarding the seizure of Iranian vessels. Baghaei posted on X that Washington had effectively acknowledged unlawful maritime actions. He said the US president had described the ship seizures as piracy and boasted about acting like pirates.

stories.title: Trump says he’s reviewing new Iran proposal to end war
stories.summary: President Trump confirmed he is reviewing a 14-point Iranian proposal to end the war, transmitted via Pakistan. Semi-official Iranian outlets Tasnim and Fars reported the plan was sent in response to a nine-point U.S. proposal. Pakistan has hosted previous rounds of negotiations between the parties.

stories.title: Fibre-optic drones | The phantom that flies
stories.summary: Fibre-optic-guided first-person-view attack drones have emerged as a disruptive force on the battlefield in the Russia-Ukraine war and in parts of the West Asia conflict. The small unmanned machines represent a significant evolution in drone warfare technology.

stories.title: Ukrenergo not predicting power outages for Sunday
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that no electricity consumption restrictions are expected on Sunday, May 3. The forecast suggests a stable power supply across the country for that day.

stories.title: ‘Angry Birds’-style video caricaturing Hezbollah draws rebuke
stories.summary: An animated video parodying the game 'Angry Birds' depicted Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem and his fighters as birds and Israelis as green pigs. The video drew a rebuke from critics.

stories.title: OPEC | Cracks in the oil crown
stories.summary: OPEC faces a significant challenge following the UAE's departure from the cartel. The organization was already contending with shifts in the global energy landscape, geopolitical tensions, and declining market influence.

stories.title: Three people dead and man arrested after incident in southwest Sydney
stories.summary: Three people died at a home in Rosemeadow, in Sydney's southwest, after police responded to reports of a disturbance at approximately 1:30 a.m. on Sunday. A 32-year-old man was taken into custody at the scene.

stories.title: Person found dead in car after it plows into health club in Portland, Oregon
stories.summary: A person was found dead inside a vehicle that crashed into the Multnomah Athletic Club in downtown Portland, Oregon, shortly before 3 a.m. Saturday. The car caught fire upon impact, and investigators later discovered explosives inside the vehicle.

stories.title: Two children injured in Russian drone attack in Sumy region
stories.summary: Two boys aged 10 and 11 were injured during a Russian drone attack in Ukraine's northeastern Sumy region on Saturday. The strike is part of continued Russian aerial attacks on communities near the border.

stories.title: Toronto anti-Israel activists who stormed IDF veterans lecture face new charges
stories.summary: Anti-Israel activists in Toronto who stormed a lecture by IDF veterans are facing new criminal charges. The charges include public incitement of hatred, unlawful assembly while masked, participation in a riot while masked, and mischief involving interference with the lawful enjoyment of property.

stories.title: Chronic patients neglected in Lebanon as war strains healthcare, MSF doctor says
stories.summary: A Médecins Sans Frontières doctor, Thienminh Dinh, warned that patients with chronic illnesses in southern Lebanon are going untreated as hospitals redirect resources to handle mass displacement. More than 1.6 million people have been displaced by Israeli attacks. Outpatient departments have closed to prioritize emergency care.

stories.title: Russian forces attack eight gas stations in Kharkiv over past several days
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked eight gas stations in the city of Kharkiv over the course of several days. Local officials described the strikes as an apparent attempt to spread panic among the city's residents.

stories.title: Man charged over bomb hoax after Peter Kay show evacuated
stories.summary: A 19-year-old man was charged with a bomb hoax after the Utilita Arena in Birmingham was evacuated during a live Peter Kay comedy show. West Midlands police said the evacuation was triggered by a report of a suspicious bag found near the venue, and the comedian was pulled from the stage mid-performance.

stories.title: UAE strengthens 'security cohesion' in Gulf with Bahrain - analysis
stories.summary: The UAE is strengthening security cooperation with Bahrain as part of broader Gulf security coordination efforts. The partnership comes amid new US arms sales to the region, reports of deepening Israel-UAE ties, and ongoing tensions with Iran.

stories.title: Lost in translation, found in love: Ariana Phillips’s path to marriage in Israel
stories.summary: Ariana Phillips, a graduate of Washington University in St. Louis, deepened her engagement with Judaism through campus organizations including Chabad and Hillel. Her journey ultimately led to marriage and life in Israel.

stories.title: Faith, hope and ancestry: William Lai’s clan village in Beijing’s push for cross-strait ties
stories.summary: The village of Xintian in China's Fujian province, the ancestral home of Taiwan's President William Lai Ching-te, has become a focal point for Beijing's efforts to promote cross-strait ties based on kinship and shared heritage. Fujian, the closest mainland province to Taiwan, serves as a key site for China's messaging toward the island.

stories.title: Don’t leave off the love: Devorah Ahavah Gerzoff’s journey to Jewish faith and Israel
stories.summary: Devorah Ahavah Gerzoff's gradual rediscovery of Judaism led her from suburban America to building a life connected to Israel. Her personal journey traces an evolving relationship with Jewish faith and Israeli society.

stories.title: Interior minister briefs PM Shehbaz on security situation in country
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi briefed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Lahore on the country's security situation. Naqvi also provided details on security arrangements for the upcoming Pakistan Super League final scheduled in Lahore.

stories.title: Ukrainian journalist explores resistance against Russia in essay-guide for French readers
stories.summary: A Ukrainian journalist has published an essay-guide for French readers exploring Ukraine's long history of resistance against Russian domination. The work argues that Ukrainian resilience was shaped over centuries by the country's culture, geography, and political traditions.

stories.title: Kuwait halts crude exports in April as Strait of Hormuz blockade bites
stories.summary: Kuwait recorded zero crude oil exports in April for the first time since the Gulf War, according to shipping monitor TankerTrackers.com. The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted tanker traffic, forcing Kuwait to divert its output to domestic storage and refining instead of overseas shipments.

stories.title: Israel accused of destroying Christian convent in Lebanon in latest attack on Christians
stories.summary: Cardinal Bechara al-Rai, Maronite Patriarch of Antioch, and other church leaders have accused Israel of destroying a Christian convent in Lebanon. They warned of a growing pattern of Israeli attacks targeting Christian communities in Lebanon, Israel, and the occupied Palestinian territories.

stories.title: ‘Naftali has no friends’: Ben Gvir, Bennett spar as top cops attend minister’s birthday party
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir clashed publicly after senior police officials attended Ben Gvir's birthday party alongside far-right activists. Bennett reiterated his pledge to dismiss officials who politicize their roles if he wins the next election. The incident raised concerns about improper conduct within the police leadership.

stories.title: How the ‘Soul of a Nation’ documentary helps defend Israel
stories.summary: The documentary "Soul of a Nation" presents a portrait of Israel aimed at countering anti-Israel narratives. The film focuses on depicting Israel's democratic institutions, diversity, and societal complexity.

stories.title: Mexican governor steps aside days after US accuses him of cartel ties
stories.summary: Sinaloa state governor Rubén Rocha announced on Friday that he would step down after U.S. authorities charged him and other Mexican ruling-party officials with alleged ties to the Sinaloa Cartel. The indictment marked a significant escalation of U.S. pressure on Mexico regarding cartel-related corruption.

stories.title: Beyond subsidies: what’s really driving China’s industrial climb
stories.summary: China's latest wave of industrial advancement, dubbed "China shock 2.0," centers on high-tech manufacturing sectors including electric vehicles, rather than the low-tech goods that defined its earlier export surge after WTO accession in 2001. Analysts argue that intensifying competition in advanced manufacturing goes beyond government subsidies.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Dnipropetrovsk region over 50 times, three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled communities in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region more than 50 times in a single day, injuring three people. The attacks targeted multiple locations across the region.

stories.title: Why are maritime laws failing to secure the seas?
stories.summary: Wars and territorial disputes are increasingly undermining international maritime laws designed to secure global shipping routes. The breakdown of established rules is disrupting trade and raising security concerns across key waterways worldwide.

stories.title: Israel strikes several parts of south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel launched new airstrikes on several targets in southern Lebanon, claiming to have struck Hezbollah positions. The attacks occurred despite a ceasefire that has theoretically been in effect since April 16.

stories.title: Russian drone strike hits supermarket in Kherson, four injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a supermarket in the Dniprovskyi district of Kherson, Ukraine, injuring four people according to preliminary reports.

stories.title: Ministers set to discuss renewing Gaza war as Hamas refuses to disarm — report
stories.summary: Israeli ministers are reportedly set to discuss renewing military operations in Gaza after Hamas refused to disarm. Arab diplomats say Hamas is willing to discuss disarmament only as part of establishing a Palestinian state. The IDF reported killing at least three militants in Gaza.

stories.title: Fighting reaches outskirts of Ukraine's stronghold Kostiantynivka
stories.summary: Fighting has reached the outskirts of Kostiantynivka, a key Ukrainian stronghold in the country's east. The city is part of a fortified belt of defensive positions established by the Ukrainian military in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Israel’s Eurovision delegation arrives in Vienna in high spirits, despite security threats
stories.summary: Israel's delegation for the 70th Eurovision Song Contest has arrived in Vienna ahead of the competition. Israel is set to participate in the first semifinal on May 12, with the final scheduled for May 16, amid heightened security concerns.

stories.title: Ukrainian military debunks Russian claim of capturing Myropillia in Sumy region
stories.summary: Ukraine's military denied Russian claims of capturing the village of Myropillia in the Sumy region, stating it remains under Ukrainian Armed Forces control. Officials said reports of Russian seizure of the village were false.

stories.title: CM Murad urges public to take precautionary measures amid heatwave alert for Sindh's central, upper regions
stories.summary: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah urged residents to take precautions as Pakistan's meteorological department warned that heatwave conditions would persist across central and upper Sindh. Daytime temperatures were expected to exceed normal levels by 3–5 degrees Celsius.

stories.title: Israel army says troops damaged 'religious building' in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli army admitted its troops damaged a "religious building" in southern Lebanon. The acknowledgment drew condemnation from L'Oeuvre d'Orient, a Catholic charity organization.

stories.title: US bypasses congressional review for military sales of $8.6 billion to Middle East allies
stories.summary: The US State Department bypassed congressional review to approve $8.6 billion in military sales to Middle East allies. Secretary of State Marco Rubio determined that an emergency existed requiring the immediate sales and waived the standard congressional review requirements.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines collapses amid rising fuel costs from war on Iran
stories.summary: US budget carrier Spirit Airlines has ceased operations after failing to secure a government bailout. The airline's collapse is attributed to rising fuel costs linked to the ongoing conflict involving Iran, which has disrupted global energy markets.

stories.title: Air defenses neutralize 220 of 227 drones launched by Russia in daytime attack on Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 220 of 227 drones launched by Russian forces during a daytime attack on May 2. The large-scale assault involved over 200 unmanned aerial vehicles targeting Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Karachi court grants bail to SSP's son arrested following heated exchange with police in DHA
stories.summary: A Karachi court granted bail to the son of SSP Nasim Ara Panhwar, who was arrested in Defence Housing Authority after a confrontation with police over an unauthorized police number plate on a private vehicle. A viral video of the altercation circulated on social media.

stories.title: Yemen says oil tanker hijacked off Shabwa coast, heads towards Somali waters
stories.summary: Yemen's coast guard reported that an oil tanker was hijacked off the coast of Shabwa governorate and was heading toward Somali waters. Authorities said efforts were under way to track the vessel and ensure the crew's safety.

stories.title: At least six dead in heavy rains in northeast Brazil, thousands displaced
stories.summary: Heavy rains in northeastern Brazil's Pernambuco and Paraíba states have killed at least six people and displaced thousands. Studies indicate that extreme rainfall events have become increasingly frequent across the country.

stories.title: Khartoum drone strike kills five Sudan NGO reports
stories.summary: A drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan, killed five people, according to local NGO reports. The attack was the second in one week, following a period of relative calm after government forces regained control of the city.

stories.title: Flotilla activists 'on hunger strike' amid Spain-Israel tension
stories.summary: Two flotilla activists detained by Israel, including one Spanish national, have reportedly begun a hunger strike. Spain has called for their immediate release amid rising diplomatic tensions between Madrid and Jerusalem.

stories.title: UK Muslim groups slam government for ‘scapegoating’ Gaza anti-genocide protests as antisemitism
stories.summary: Several UK Muslim organizations have criticized the British government for characterizing pro-Palestinian and anti-genocide protests as antisemitic. The groups rejected efforts to link Palestine solidarity demonstrations to violence and highlighted instances where Muslim victims have been overlooked.

stories.title: Ukraine eyes Belarus border activities as Russian strikes persist
stories.summary: Ukraine is closely monitoring military activity along its border with Belarus as Russian strikes on Ukrainian territory continue. Kyiv has imposed sanctions on Belarus for its role in supporting Russia's war effort and has stated it is prepared to respond to any threats.

stories.title: Political blame game begins and passengers left adrift after Spirit ceases operations
stories.summary: US discount carrier Spirit Airlines abruptly ceased all operations, stranding passengers and leaving employees without work. Republicans blamed the Biden administration for blocking a JetBlue acquisition deal, while Democrats pointed to surging fuel prices linked to tensions with Iran.

stories.title: China rejects U.S. sanctions on refineries over Iran oil links
stories.summary: China's Commerce Ministry rejected US sanctions on Chinese refineries over Iranian oil purchases, calling them a violation of international law. The ministry stated that the sanctions improperly restrict Chinese enterprises from conducting normal trade with third countries.

stories.title: Shooting at dinner attended by Trump spotlights US hotel industry's nagging and costly security problem
stories.summary: A suspect identified as Cole Allen, 31, stormed a security checkpoint and fired a shotgun near the White House Correspondents' Association dinner at the Washington Hilton while President Trump was in attendance. The incident has intensified scrutiny of hotel security practices across the US.

stories.title: Syria becomes alternative energy corridor for oil as Hormuz effectively blo
stories.summary: Syria has emerged as an alternative energy corridor, receiving hundreds of Iraqi oil trucks hauling crude overland for export to Europe. The shift comes as the Strait of Hormuz is effectively blocked, disrupting traditional maritime oil routes.

stories.title: Why Russia's Northern Sea Route is a risk for global trade
stories.summary: Russia is promoting its Northern Sea Route as a major global trade corridor between Europe and Asia through the Arctic. However, the route faces significant political and environmental challenges that could limit its viability.

stories.title: Why Russia's Northern Sea Route, the shortest maritime route between Asia and Europe, is a risk for global trade — and the environment
stories.summary: Russia is promoting its Northern Sea Route as the shortest maritime passage between Asia and Europe for global trade. However, the Arctic corridor faces significant political tensions and environmental risks that limit its viability.

stories.title: Why Russia's Northern Sea Route is a risky bet for global trade
stories.summary: Russia is promoting its Northern Sea Route as a major global trade artery connecting Europe and Asia through the Arctic. However, the route faces significant political and environmental challenges that make it a risky alternative to established shipping lanes.

stories.title: Why Russia’s Northern Sea Route remains a risky bet for global shipping
stories.summary: Russia is promoting its Northern Sea Route as a major global trade artery connecting Europe and Asia through the Arctic. However, the route faces significant political and environmental obstacles that make it a risky alternative for international shipping.

stories.title: Two Gaza aid flotilla activists brought to Israel for questioning, says ministry
stories.summary: Israel's foreign ministry confirmed that two Gaza-bound aid flotilla activists were brought to Israel for questioning after their vessels were intercepted. The ministry said both individuals are affiliated with a US-sanctioned organisation.

stories.title: Washington Hilton attack spotlights US hotel industry's nagging and costly security problem
stories.summary: A suspect identified as Cole Allen, 31, stormed a security checkpoint and fired a shotgun near the White House Correspondents' Association dinner at the Washington Hilton. In a manifesto, Allen mocked the hotel's security measures, spotlighting longstanding security vulnerabilities in the US hotel industry.

stories.title: Zelensky imposes sanctions on five individuals over national security threats
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky enacted a National Security and Defense Council decision imposing sanctions on five individuals deemed threats to Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. Specific identities of those sanctioned were not detailed in the announcement.

stories.title: Ukraine battlefield: Advanced Ukrainian drones raise concerns among Russian forces
stories.summary: Advanced Ukrainian drones are raising concerns among Russian forces as drone warfare continues to redefine front lines and create so-called "killing zones" on the battlefield. Reports describe sophisticated "Martian drones" being deployed alongside unmanned systems used for civilian rescue operations, including the evacuation of a 77-year-old woman in the Odesa region.

stories.title: Israel’s expanding ‘orange line’ tightens deadly no-go zones in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel has expanded what it designates as an "orange line" across Gaza, tightening movement restrictions and enlarging no-go zones. The expanding restricted areas are raising deadly risks for Palestinian civilians trying to navigate the territory.

stories.title: Washington Hilton attack spotlights hotel industry's nagging and costly security problem
stories.summary: A suspect was charged after breaching a security checkpoint and firing a shotgun near the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday. The incident occurred in close proximity to President Donald Trump. The suspect reportedly mocked the hotel's security measures that allowed him to approach the event.

stories.title: Zelensky announces upcoming government reshuffle, decisions expected next week
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced an upcoming government reshuffle in Ukraine, with some personnel changes to be approved at the Cabinet of Ministers level and others requiring parliamentary discussion. Decisions are expected the following week.

stories.title: IDF admits damaging Catholic convent in southern Lebanon, denies site demolished
stories.summary: The Israeli military acknowledged that its forces damaged a Catholic convent in southern Lebanon but denied the site was demolished. The IDF claimed Hezbollah had fired rockets from the compound multiple times during the war. The Catholic Church in Lebanon denied the compound was used by Hezbollah.

stories.title: Making it official: Inside the Nativ program training IDF soldiers to 'join the tribe'
stories.summary: The Nativ program, adopted by the Israeli military in 2000, trains IDF soldiers for religious conversion. Over 58,000 soldiers have enrolled since its inception, and nearly 20,000 have completed the conversion process.

stories.title: Drone strike kills five in Sudanese capital Khartoum
stories.summary: A drone strike carried out by the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group killed five people in Omdurman, near the Sudanese capital Khartoum.

stories.title: Jirga convened by KP CM decides on holding talks with Centre, other stakeholders over drone attacks
stories.summary: A grand jirga convened by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi in Peshawar decided to form a delegation to hold talks with Pakistan's federal government and other stakeholders over drone attacks in the province. Afridi has previously condemned persistent drone strikes in KP and hinted at legislation to criminalize collateral damage.

stories.title: Mali in crisis: Jihadist fighters and Tuareg separatists threaten Bamako
stories.summary: Mali faces an escalating security crisis as the jihadist group JNIM, linked to Al-Qaeda, and Tuareg separatist rebels have reportedly seized two northern cities and killed the defence minister. Several Malian soldiers have been arrested for allegedly collaborating with the militants. JNIM is attempting to impose a blockade on the capital, Bamako, while Russian mercenaries support the government.

stories.title: Nobel laureate Mohammadi in Iran hospital after 'cardiac crisis', foundation says
stories.summary: Imprisoned Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was hospitalized in Iran after reportedly suffering a cardiac crisis, according to her foundation. Further details about her condition were not immediately available.

stories.title: Three people injured in Russia's attacks on Sumy region
stories.summary: Three people were injured in the Sumy region of Ukraine as a result of Russian attacks over the course of a single day.

stories.title: Months into the US-Israel 'ceasefire', Gaza remains a scene of chaos and terror
stories.summary: Months after a US-brokered ceasefire, conditions in Gaza remain dire, with continued Israeli military operations causing civilian casualties. Reports describe blocked border crossings and collapsing hospitals, with a child reportedly killed by Israeli artillery near Gaza City while en route to a wedding.

stories.title: Fighting reaches outskirts of Ukraine's stronghold Kostiantynivka
stories.summary: Russian forces are advancing toward the city of Kostiantynivka in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, attempting to establish positions near a heavily defended area. Ukraine's top army official reported on Saturday that fighting has reached the outskirts of the city.

stories.title: Hamas completes Gaza voting for general political bureau head, winner to be announced - report
stories.summary: Hamas has completed voting within Gaza for a new head of its general political bureau. Branches in the West Bank and abroad are expected to finish their votes and announce a winner next week, according to Qatari outlet Al-Araby.

stories.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill seven amid fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit several locations in southern Lebanon, killing at least seven people amid a fragile ceasefire. Lebanon's National News Agency reported strikes on a car in Kfar Dajal killing two and a home in Lwaizeh killing three.

stories.title: Israel is making Palestinians disappear in more ways than one
stories.summary: Reports from Gaza describe a pattern of missing children, unrecovered bodies beneath rubble, and entire families killed in Israeli strikes. Civil defense teams have been searching for remains of families, including the Salem family, whose home was destroyed by Israeli forces.

stories.title: Peace agreement in war with Russia impossible without Ukraine's consent – Fico
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico stated that any peace agreement to end the war with Russia is impossible without Ukraine's consent. Fico said both he and Ukrainian President Zelensky are committed to maintaining friendly relations between Slovakia and Ukraine despite disagreements on some issues.

stories.title: Spain demands Israel release arrested Gaza flotilla crew member
stories.summary: Spain has demanded that Israel release Saif Abukeshek, a crew member from the Global Sumid Flotilla, who was detained after Israeli forces raided the vessel off the coast of Greece and transported him to Israel.

stories.title: Kurdistan Region hopes for stability with new Iraq Prime Minister
stories.summary: Iraq's Kurdistan Region expressed hope for stability under a new Iraqi prime minister. Iraq's premiership is traditionally chosen by Shi'ite political parties, reflecting their demographic majority, while the Kurdish bloc holds the presidency.

stories.title: Devastation of Southern Lebanon continues under ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israeli forces launched approximately 50 airstrikes on southern Lebanon within a 24-hour period despite a ceasefire being in place, killing at least 41 people. The strikes targeted areas in southern Lebanon, continuing a pattern of military operations in the region.

stories.title: Iraq says oil output can return to normal within days of Strait of Hormuz reopening
stories.summary: Iraq's deputy oil minister Basim Mohammed stated that the country could restore oil production and exports to normal levels within seven days of the Strait of Hormuz crisis subsiding. Current production stands at roughly 1.5 million barrels per day, with about 200,000 barrels exported daily through the Ceyhan terminal in Turkey.

stories.title: Nato seeks details as US says it will pull about 5,000 troops from Germany
stories.summary: NATO said it was working with the US to understand Washington's decision to withdraw approximately 5,000 troops from Germany amid a deepening transatlantic rift over the Middle East war. The move followed a public dispute between President Trump and German Chancellor Merz over Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Russians attack Naftogaz facilities in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk regions
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Naftogaz energy facilities in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions on May 2, injuring a company employee. Naftogaz is Ukraine's state-owned oil and gas company.

stories.title: Oil tanker hijacked off coast of Yemen and taken towards Somalia
stories.summary: An oil tanker was hijacked off the coast of Yemen and directed toward Somalia. It is the second such hijacking in the area within ten days.

stories.title: Nato seeks to ‘understand the details’ of US decision to withdraw troops from Germany
stories.summary: NATO said it is seeking to understand the details of a US decision to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany, ordered by President Trump amid a dispute with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The German government described the redeployment as anticipated and emphasized Europe's need to strengthen its own defense capabilities.

stories.title: Starmer urges tougher action against Gaza protests in U.K. following antisemitic attacks
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer called for tougher action against pro-Palestinian protests, suggesting that repeated marches have had a 'cumulative effect' contributing to a rise in antisemitic incidents across Britain.

stories.title: Mali investigates soldiers over role in coordinated insurgent attacks
stories.summary: Malian authorities are investigating soldiers suspected of involvement in coordinated attacks on army bases carried out last week by militants linked to al-Qaeda and separatist Tuareg rebels. A judicial official in Bamako confirmed the probe on May 2.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia reverses decision setting minimum age for Haj pilgrims at 15 years
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reversed a newly announced policy that would have set the minimum age for Haj pilgrims at 15 years. Pakistan's Ministry of Religious Affairs confirmed that Saudi authorities assured full refunds for any affected pilgrims.

stories.title: Global Sumud Flotilla claim detained activist never meant to go to Gaza, was on 'observer boat'
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla stated that a detained activist identified as Keshek was aboard an observer vessel that was never intended to enter Gaza. The organization said he was beaten and isolated from other participants during his detention by Israeli forces.

stories.title: Iranian proposal rejected by Trump would open strait before nuclear talks: Iran official
stories.summary: Iran proposed a deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz before nuclear negotiations begin, according to an Iranian official. The proposal also included ending hostilities and commitments that Israel and the United States would not launch further attacks. President Donald Trump rejected the offer.

stories.title: Russians strike Zaporizhzhia region with glide bombs, leaving one killed, two injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the village of Novooleksandrivka in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region with glide bombs, killing a 55-year-old man and injuring two others, including a 7-year-old girl.

stories.title: 'Drunk' Israeli reservist shoots at Palestinian homes in WB
stories.summary: An Israeli reservist was arrested after reportedly firing at Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank. The individual, described as an Israeli settler drafted into military service, was detained following the shooting incident.

stories.title: Hezbollah slams Lebanese TV for ‘Angry Birds’ clip mocking leader
stories.summary: Hezbollah condemned Lebanese broadcaster LBCI for airing a clip that depicted leader Naim Qassem and his operatives as characters from the video game Angry Birds fighting Israeli forces portrayed as green pigs. The group objected to the satirical portrayal of its leadership.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists: Israel treated us 'worse than animals'
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted and boarded a Gaza-bound flotilla in international waters, detaining activists on board. Multiple activists alleged they were subjected to abuse and physical mistreatment during the operation.

stories.title: 2 Gaza aid flotilla activists brought to Israel for questioning, its foreign ministry says
stories.summary: Two Gaza-bound aid flotilla activists — Spanish citizen Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Ávila — were brought to Israel for questioning after their vessels were intercepted. Israel's foreign ministry said both are affiliated with an organisation sanctioned by the US Treasury.

stories.title: Lebanese, US generals meet in Beirut to discuss security and ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanese army chief General Rudolf Haykal met US General Joseph Clearfield in Beirut to discuss Lebanon's security situation and regional developments. Clearfield heads a committee overseeing a US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: War update: 51 combat engagements on front line since morning, Pokrovsk direction remains hottest
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 51 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line since the morning, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk direction.

stories.title: Turkish authorities reportedly seize gold Hebrew manuscript inscribed on python skin
stories.summary: Turkish gendarmerie forces seized a gold Hebrew manuscript reportedly inscribed on python skin. A foreign national, identified only as A.E., was detained on suspicion of attempting to sell the artifact on the black market.

stories.title: Yemen reports hijacked oil tanker headed for Somalia
stories.summary: Yemeni authorities reported that a hijacked oil tanker was heading toward Somalia. The incident is at least the fourth vessel hijacking near the Somali coast in recent weeks, reflecting ongoing maritime insecurity in the region.

stories.title: Spain’s Sanchez demands Netanyahu free Spaniard seized on aid flotilla
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez demanded that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu release a Spanish national seized from an aid flotilla. Spain characterized the detention as an abduction and called for the individual's immediate return.

stories.title: Kenya flood death toll hits 10 as dam overflow risk raises alarm
stories.summary: At least 10 people have died across Kenya after heavy rains caused flooding and landslides in multiple regions. Authorities warned that rising river levels could threaten communities downstream from a major hydropower dam system.

stories.title: Taiwan president visits Eswatini days after blaming China for cancelled trip
stories.summary: Taiwan's President William Lai visited Eswatini, one of Taiwan's few remaining diplomatic allies, days after blaming China for the cancellation of a previous trip. China's government described the visit as a "stowaway-style escape farce," and details of how Lai reached Eswatini remain unclear.

stories.title: Senior Iranian officer warns war with US ‘likely’ after Trump rebuffs latest proposal
stories.summary: A senior Iranian military officer warned that war with the United States is likely after President Trump rejected Tehran's latest diplomatic proposal. The Pentagon reportedly estimates that a US naval blockade of Iranian ports has cost Tehran $4.8 billion in oil revenues.

stories.title: Syrian ministry condemns killing of Shia imam near Damascus
stories.summary: Syrian authorities condemned the killing of a Shia imam in a bomb blast in a suburb near Damascus. The incident is the latest in a series of security episodes in the area.

stories.title: Prices surge, jobs disappear as war strains Iran’s economy
stories.summary: Iran's economy is experiencing surging prices and rising unemployment amid ongoing conflict. New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has called on the country to prevail against its adversaries in what he described as an economic and cultural struggle.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian strike on minibus in Kherson rises to ten
stories.summary: The number of people injured by a Russian drone strike on a minibus in the city of Kherson has risen to ten.

stories.title: Israeli AI startup cracks code of who is at fault when system fails: What do they do? - interview
stories.summary: Israeli AI startup Dynamic Infrastructure, led by CEO Saar Dickman, has developed a platform focused on assigning liability when AI systems fail. Dickman discussed how the company manages fault determination in AI-related incidents.

stories.title: Pakistan slams 'one-sided' remarks by British diplomat on Pak-Afghan border situation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office rejected remarks by British Special Representative for Afghanistan Richard Lindsay regarding the Pak-Afghan border situation, calling them 'one-sided' and lacking understanding. Lindsay had shared a UN report documenting civilian casualties from strikes in eastern Afghanistan.

stories.title: Humpback whale 'Timmy' released in North Sea after weeks stranded off Germany
stories.summary: A humpback whale nicknamed 'Timmy,' stranded for weeks off the German coast in the North Sea, was successfully released. A GPS transmitter was attached to track the whale's movements after release.

stories.title: US carrier Spirit Airlines shuts down, industry’s first Iran war casualty
stories.summary: US discount carrier Spirit Airlines ceased operations after failing to secure creditor support for a government bailout. The airline's collapse is linked to a doubling of jet fuel prices during the two-month-old Iran war, costing thousands of jobs despite a proposed $500 million rescue plan from President Trump.

stories.title: Gaza death toll rises to 72,608
stories.summary: The Gaza Health Ministry reported that Israeli attacks killed at least four people and wounded 26 others in the latest 24-hour period. The cumulative death toll in Gaza since October 2023 has reached at least 72,608, with 172,445 wounded. Of those, 828 deaths have occurred since the ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: Mexican governor indicted by US steps down
stories.summary: Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha Moya stepped down after being indicted by the United States on charges of protecting the Sinaloa cartel. US authorities allege he helped the cartel smuggle drugs into the country and received millions of dollars in bribes.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike tactical Iskander missile group in Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck a tactical group of Russian Iskander missile systems in Crimea overnight on 2 May, also hitting Podlyot and MIS-M1 radar stations, ammunition depots, and drone command centers.

stories.title: Germany says US troop withdrawal 'foreseeable' as Nato seeks clarification
stories.summary: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius described the US decision to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany as foreseeable. NATO said it is seeking further clarification on the details of the redeployment.

stories.title: OPEC+ agrees in principle on small oil output quota hike without UAE, sources say
stories.summary: OPEC+ members agreed in principle on a modest oil output quota increase, though without the UAE's participation. The production hikes are largely symbolic given that most shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains halted by the US-Israeli war against Iran.

stories.title: Iran military official says renewed war with US ‘likely’
stories.summary: An Iranian military official declared that renewed war with the United States is "likely" after President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Tehran's latest negotiating proposal. The statement underscores rising tensions between the two countries amid the ongoing standoff.

stories.title: US to close Gaza monitoring centre as Trump plan stalls
stories.summary: The United States plans to close its military-run monitoring centre for the Gaza ceasefire. The facility had been unable to prevent Israeli violations of the truce or fully restore humanitarian aid flows into Gaza.

stories.title: China rejects US sanctions on refineries over Iran oil links
stories.summary: China rejected newly imposed US sanctions targeting five Chinese firms accused of purchasing Iranian oil. Beijing stated it would not comply with the measures.

stories.title: Humpback whale ‘Timmy’ released in North Sea after weeks stranded off Germany
stories.summary: A humpback whale nicknamed 'Timmy,' which had been stranded in shallow waters near Wismar, Germany, since early March, was released into the North Sea from a barge by a rescue team on Saturday.

stories.title: Building scaffolding gives burglars easy access, police say after 2 arrested
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested two burglary suspects after one allegedly used maintenance scaffolding on a residential building to enter homes through window grilles, stealing HK$6,000 in cash. Police warned that scaffolding-assisted break-ins are becoming a growing trend.

stories.title: Ukraine records specific activity on Belarussian border - Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported in a video address that unusual activity had been recorded on the Ukraine-Belarus border from the Belarusian side, and that Ukraine is monitoring the situation.

stories.title: Germany urges stronger European defence after US reduces troops
stories.summary: The United States announced it is withdrawing approximately 5,000 military personnel from Germany. German officials urged stronger European defense capabilities in response to the reduction of the American troop presence.

stories.title: US troop drawback underlines European defence responsibility, German minister says
stories.summary: Germany's defense minister emphasized that the withdrawal of approximately 5,000 US military personnel from Germany underlines Europe's need to take greater responsibility for its own defense. The US drawback signals a shifting security dynamic within the transatlantic alliance.

stories.title: FCC rejects Balochistan govt plea for lifetime facilities to retired chief secretaries, widows
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court rejected a Balochistan government plea to grant lifetime facilities to retired chief secretaries and their widows. The court ruled that the provincial notification lacked legal backing under the Rules of Business.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia’s only official liquor store runs short of supplies because of Iran war bottleneck
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's sole official liquor store is experiencing supply shortages due to disruptions caused by the Iran war. The Strait of Hormuz blockade has created a bottleneck, leaving shelves mostly bare with only expensive or lesser-known brands available.

stories.title: Why Ukraine and Israel are arguing over grain
stories.summary: Cargo ships carrying grain believed to originate from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine have docked at Israel's Haifa port. Ukraine considers the grain stolen, while Israel says there is insufficient evidence to confirm its origin.

stories.title: Zelensky, Fico discuss possibility of meeting soon
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Slovak Prime Minister Fico discussed the possibility of an in-person meeting in the near future during a phone call.

stories.title: Organisers challenge Starmer’s threat to ban some pro-Palestine marches
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer indicated he would support banning some pro-Palestine marches opposing Israel's actions in the Middle East. Protest organizers pushed back, arguing that such bans would undermine free assembly and free speech in Britain.

stories.title: Raqqa heritage sites face neglect after years of Syria civil war
stories.summary: Archaeological sites in Raqqa, Syria, are suffering widespread damage and neglect following years of civil war. Activists have warned that the heritage loss may become irreversible without urgent intervention.

stories.title: Mexico’s Sinaloa state governor resigns amid US drug trafficking charges
stories.summary: Sinaloa state governor Rubén Rocha Moya has stepped down from his post, taking what he described as a temporary leave to defend himself against US drug trafficking charges. He again denied allegations that he shielded cartel operations.

stories.title: Iran executes two men convicted of spying for Israel: Judiciary
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of espionage for Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. The men were accused of transmitting sensitive information and images to the Israeli spy service.

stories.title: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel laureate Mohammadi rushed to hospital following cardiac 'crisis'
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was transferred to a hospital on Friday after suffering a heart attack and two episodes of complete unconsciousness. A foundation run by her family described the deterioration of her health as catastrophic.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia sets minimum age for Haj pilgrims at 15 years
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has set the minimum age for Haj pilgrims at 15 years, effective May 3, 2026. Pakistan's religious affairs ministry relayed the Saudi directive that no departing flight may carry pilgrims under this age threshold.

stories.title: German, Japanese, Swiss, American, Taiwanese, British — all 2025-made parts found in Russian drones, Vlasiuk says
stories.summary: Ukraine's presidential commissioner for sanctions policy reported that Russian drones striking Ukraine contained components manufactured in 2025 from Germany, Japan, Switzerland, the United States, Taiwan, and the United Kingdom. A new activation unit labeled 'Transit Brd' was also identified among the parts.

stories.title: Yemen says oil tanker hijacked off Shabwa coast, heads towards Somali waters
stories.summary: Yemen's coast guard reported that the oil tanker M/T Eureka was hijacked off the coast of Shabwa province and directed toward Somali waters. Authorities said the tanker's location had been identified and recovery efforts were underway to ensure crew safety.

stories.title: Russian army attacks Kharkiv with drones, hits residential building, gas stations in several districts
