stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Kharkiv using drones, striking a residential building and gas stations across several districts of the Ukrainian city.

stories.title: China issues injunction to block US sanctions on companies buying Iranian oil
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce issued an injunction blocking US sanctions imposed on five Chinese oil refineries—Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian), Shandong Jincheng Petrochemical Group, Hebei Xinhai Chemical Group, Shouguang Luqing Petrochemical, and Shandong Shengxing Chemical—accused of purchasing Iranian oil.

stories.title: Israel detains two Gaza flotilla activists alleging Hamas links
stories.summary: Israel detained two activists from the Gaza-bound flotilla, with its foreign ministry alleging ties to Hamas. No evidence was presented to support the claims.

stories.title: Trump jokes U.S. Navy will take on Cuba on the way home from Iran
stories.summary: The Trump administration is conducting a prolonged pressure campaign aimed at pushing the Cuban government to undertake significant reforms. President Trump joked at an event that the U.S. Navy could take on Cuba on its way back from Iran.

stories.title: Latvian artists launched a protest campaign against Russia’s participation in the Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Latvian artists launched a protest campaign called 'Death in Venice' against Russia's participation in the 61st Venice Biennale. The campaign runs through Latvia's national pavilion until November 22.

stories.title: UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski is an ‘extremist,’ says Israel’s deputy FM
stories.summary: Israel's Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel labeled UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski an 'extremist,' accusing him of legitimizing violence against Jews. The remarks followed Polanski's criticism of police handling of the arrest of a terror attack suspect. Polanski is himself Jewish.

stories.title: 'Be our voice': Brutalized Iranians speak of loved ones taken by the Islamic regime
stories.summary: Families of Iranians who were executed or forcibly disappeared spoke about the Islamic regime's oppression, urging the international community to amplify their stories.

stories.title: Iranian strikes damage 16 US military sites across Middle East
stories.summary: Reports indicate that Iranian drone and missile strikes have damaged 16 US military sites across the Middle East during the ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.title: New tariff hike could cost Germany $18BN
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that tariffs on cars and trucks imported from the European Union will rise to 25 percent next week, a 10-percentage-point increase over the rate agreed in a trade deal last July. The hike could cost Germany an estimated $18 billion, given the automotive sector's central role in its economy.

stories.title: War in Sudan worsens measles outbreak, causes disease to spread
stories.summary: Sudan's ongoing war, now entering its fourth year, has largely halted vaccination programmes across the country. The disruption has worsened a measles outbreak and hampered efforts to control other disease outbreaks.

stories.title: Russian attacks in Kharkiv leave four injured
stories.summary: Four people were injured in Kharkiv as a result of Russian drone attacks targeting the city.

stories.title: Taiwan’s Lai makes Eswatini visit despite travel disruption
stories.summary: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te arrived in Eswatini, Taipei's sole remaining diplomatic ally in Africa. The visit followed an earlier cancellation after several countries revoked overflight permits, disrupting his travel plans.

stories.title: Pentagon announces withdrawal of 5.000 soldiers from Germany
stories.summary: The United States announced it will withdraw approximately 5,000 troops from Germany over the next year. The decision followed remarks by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz criticizing Washington's approach to Tehran. NATO said Saturday it is coordinating with the U.S. to understand the details of the drawdown.

stories.title: Lebanese health officials: 2,659 killed in Israeli attacks since 2 March
stories.summary: Lebanon's Public Health Emergency Operations Center reported that Israeli attacks have killed at least 2,659 people and wounded 8,183 others since Israel launched a fresh offensive on 2 March.

stories.title: Israel detains two Gaza activists after intercepting aid flotilla in international waters
stories.summary: Israel said Saturday it had detained two activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla for questioning after intercepting the vessel in international waters on Thursday. Spain condemned the detention of one of its nationals as illegal.

stories.title: Two killed in Russian attack on bus in Kherson
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on a bus in the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson killed two people and injured seven others on May 2. Ukrainian officials reported the strike occurred early Saturday morning.

stories.title: NATO says ‘working’ with U.S. to ‘understand' decision to cut troops in Germany
stories.summary: NATO said it is working with Washington to understand the U.S. decision to reduce its troop presence in Germany. The move followed President Donald Trump's renewed criticism of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who had accused Iran of humiliating Washington in negotiations over the conflict in West Asia.

stories.title: Power outages reported in Mykolaiv following Russian airstrike
stories.summary: Russian forces struck energy infrastructure in the Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv using Shahed drones, causing power outages across the city.

stories.title: IED attack targets police official’s residence in Lakki Marwat, causes significant damage
stories.summary: Unknown militants linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan planted an improvised explosive device at the home of Constable Tehsil Khan in the Shadikhel area of Lakki Marwat district. The blast caused significant structural damage to the residence but no casualties were reported.

stories.title: Germany urges stronger European defense after US announces troop drawdown
stories.summary: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius responded to the US announcement of a troop drawdown from Germany by urging stronger European defense capabilities. Pistorius said Germany is expanding its armed forces and is on the right track.

stories.title: Congolese cyclist begins 14,000km peace ride through 17 countries
stories.summary: A cyclist from the Democratic Republic of the Congo has begun a 14,000-kilometer journey through 17 African countries to promote peace. The ride comes as armed conflict continues in the DRC's eastern regions.

stories.title: Nobel laureate Mohammadi in Iran hospital after ‘cardiac crisis’, foundation says
stories.summary: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was hospitalized in Iran following what her foundation described as a "cardiac crisis." Mohammadi won the Nobel Prize for her campaign to advance women's rights and abolish the death penalty in Iran.

stories.title: What exactly is white phosphorus and why is it controversial?
stories.summary: Israel has been accused of extensively using white phosphorus munitions in Lebanon and Gaza, drawing condemnation from human rights monitors. The incendiary substance is controversial due to its severe burn effects on civilians.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires rockets at troops in Lebanon, no injuries; IDF strikes terror sites
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired rockets at troops in southern Lebanon without causing injuries. The Israeli military responded with strikes on approximately 50 Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanese villages, reportedly killing seven people after issuing evacuation warnings.

stories.title: Nato seeking to understand US decision to withdraw troops from Germany
stories.summary: NATO said it was working with Washington to understand the US decision to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany. The move followed a public dispute between President Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over the war on Iran.

stories.title: Japan Buys Russian Oil for the First Time Since Hormuz Closure
stories.summary: Japanese refiner Taiyo Oil is set to purchase Russian oil through the Sakhalin-2 project in Russia's Far East, marking Japan's first such purchase since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted global shipping routes.

stories.title: Pentagon partners with seven AI firms
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced agreements with eight AI companies—Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, Oracle, OpenAI, SpaceX, and startup Reflection—to deploy their technology in classified defense settings. Anthropic was notably absent from the list following a public dispute and legal battle with the Trump administration over AI ethics.

stories.title: Berlin urges stronger European defence
stories.summary: NATO said it is working with Washington to understand the decision to withdraw 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany, announced by President Trump following a dispute with Chancellor Friedrich Merz over the Iran conflict. Germany's defense minister called on European countries to use the reduction as motivation to strengthen their own defense capabilities.

stories.title: Dar discusses Middle East situation, its economic implications with Kuwaiti FM: FO
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar discussed the Middle East situation and its economic implications with Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah. Dar emphasized Pakistan's efforts to promote diplomacy and regional stability, and the Kuwaiti minister commended those efforts.

stories.title: Seven victims of Russian attack remain in hospitals in Ternopil
stories.summary: Seven people injured in a Russian attack on Ternopil, Ukraine, on 1 May remain hospitalised in stable condition.

stories.title: Mali probes soldiers working with rebels
stories.summary: Malian authorities are investigating military officers suspected of collaborating with jihadist and separatist fighters who launched coordinated attacks across the country. The prosecutor's office confirmed initial arrests have been made. Separately, the Azawad Liberation Front claimed it captured a military camp in Tessalit after Malian forces and Russian allies withdrew.

stories.title: Nato in talks with US over troops cuts
stories.summary: NATO said it is in discussions with Washington over President Trump's announcement to withdraw 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany. The decision followed a diplomatic dispute between Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over the Iran conflict. Germany's defence minister said the reduction should prompt European nations to bolster their own military capabilities.

stories.title: Pro-Palestine coalition condemns Starmer for suggesting ban on marches
stories.summary: A coalition of UK pro-Palestine campaign groups, including the Palestine Solidarity Campaign and Stop the War Coalition, condemned Prime Minister Keir Starmer for suggesting a ban on protest marches. The groups confirmed a planned Nakba Day demonstration in London on 16 May will proceed.

stories.title: Israel’s ‘two-tier’ policing and the crime epidemic in Palestinian towns
stories.summary: Murder rates in Palestinian communities inside Israel have surged, prompting accusations of systemic neglect and complicity by Israeli authorities. Critics describe a 'two-tier' policing system that under-resources law enforcement in Palestinian towns.

stories.title: Zelenskyy reported “unusual activity” along the border with Belarus
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported unusual activity along the Ukraine-Belarus border on 1 May, stating that Ukraine is monitoring the situation and is prepared to respond if necessary.

stories.title: China blocks US sanctions against refineries accused of buying Iranian oil
stories.summary: China's commerce ministry issued an injunction blocking US sanctions on five Chinese refineries accused of buying Iranian oil, including Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) and four smaller 'teapot' refineries. The US Treasury had imposed the sanctions in April.

stories.title: Badenoch apologises after Bloody Sunday footage used in post defending UK veterans
stories.summary: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch apologised after footage from the 1972 Bloody Sunday massacre in Derry was used in a party social media post criticising Labour's Northern Ireland Troubles legacy proposals. Badenoch said she did not approve the video and attributed its release to junior staff members.

stories.title: In Zaporizhzhia region, enemy strikes Tavriiske with guided aerial bombs; woman killed
stories.summary: In Zaporizhzhia region, Russian forces struck the settlement of Tavriiske with guided aerial bombs, killing a 62-year-old woman.

stories.title: France’s double standards on Israel is a betrayal of moral values - opinion
stories.summary: French President Macron faced criticism over perceived double standards in France's diplomatic approach toward Israel, Iran, and Hezbollah. Critics accused Paris of inconsistency in balancing its relationships with these actors amid ongoing regional conflicts.

stories.title: A resting place for a rebel prince in Abbottabad
stories.summary: A historical feature explores Shahzada House on Circular Road in Abbottabad, Pakistan. The building, hidden behind a weathered gate, is linked to a rebel prince and carries roots stretching across borders and centuries. Locals speak of it with an old-world reverence.

stories.title: Oil tanker hijacked off coast of Yemen, says coast guard
stories.summary: The Yemeni Coast Guard reported that the oil tanker M/T Eureka was hijacked off the coast of Shabwa province by unidentified armed men who steered it toward the Gulf of Aden in the direction of Somali waters. Efforts are underway to recover the vessel and ensure crew safety.

stories.title: Deputy commander-in-chief of AFU: Integration of modern military command and control systems and AI agents urgent
stories.summary: Ukraine's deputy commander-in-chief stated that integrating modern military command-and-control systems with artificial intelligence agents is an urgent priority, noting that work in this area is already underway.

stories.title: Russian drones strike Kharkiv for second consecutive day, damaging four gas stations and an apartment block
stories.summary: Russian drones struck the city of Kharkiv for the second consecutive day on 2 May, damaging four gas stations and an apartment block. Six people were injured in the attacks.

stories.title: UAE says air traffic back to normal as measures lifted
stories.summary: The UAE's General Civil Aviation Authority announced that air traffic has returned to normal after lifting precautionary measures imposed on 28 February at the start of the war on Iran, following a security and operational assessment.

stories.title: She answered an advert for a part-time helper. Then she lost HK$2.25 million
stories.summary: A 25-year-old woman in Hong Kong lost more than HK$2.25 million (US$287,190) after responding to an online job advertisement for a part-time helper role. The case has prompted calls for tighter regulations requiring online employment platforms to verify employers.

stories.title: Iran military official says renewed war with U.S. ‘likely’
stories.summary: An Iranian military official stated that renewed war with the United States is "likely" after President Trump rejected a new Iranian negotiating proposal. Iran had delivered the draft proposal to mediator Pakistan on Thursday evening.

stories.title: Pentagon tells UK, Poland, Baltics: weapons deliveries delayed — how it affects Ukraine’s arsenal
stories.summary: The Pentagon has warned the UK, Poland, and Baltic states of significant delays in deliveries of HIMARS and NASAMS weapons systems, as US stockpiles have been depleted by the war with Iran. Ukraine is already feeling the impact on its arsenal.

stories.title: Korean Air bans roosters on US-Philippine routes amid cockfighting outcry
stories.summary: Korean Air banned the transport of roosters on flights from the United States to the Philippines following pressure from animal rights advocates. The Philippines has a massive cockfighting industry, and the US is a significant source of fighting roosters for the trade.

stories.title: What we know about Iran’s peace proposal rejected by Trump
stories.summary: Iran proposed a phased peace plan that included ending hostilities, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and deferring nuclear negotiations. President Trump rejected the proposal, leaving diplomatic efforts stalled and regional tensions elevated.

stories.title: Deputy commander-in-chief of AFU stresses need to reevaluate protection of military equipment now
stories.summary: Brigadier General Andrii Lebedenko, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, called for a reevaluation of how military equipment is protected on the battlefield. He stressed the urgency of updating current protection measures.

stories.title: Zelenskyy and Fico hold phone call, exchange visit invitations to Kyiv and Bratislava
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico held a phone call in which Fico expressed support for Ukraine's EU membership. The two leaders exchanged invitations to visit Kyiv and Bratislava.

stories.title: Pro-Palestine coalition condemns Starmer for suggesting ban on marches
stories.summary: A coalition of pro-Palestine campaign groups in the UK condemned Prime Minister Keir Starmer for suggesting a ban on marches, accusing him of belittling antisemitism. The Palestine Solidarity Campaign confirmed that a planned Nakba Day march in London will proceed.

stories.title: NATO seeks clarity as US to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany amid rift with Europe
stories.summary: NATO is seeking clarity after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany amid a transatlantic rift over the war on Iran. President Trump has also indicated he may pull US troops from Italy and Spain due to those countries' opposition to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: U.S. warns shipping firms they could face sanctions over paying Iranian tolls in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States warned international shipping firms they could face sanctions for paying Iranian tolls in the Strait of Hormuz. Approximately one-fifth of the world's trade in oil and natural gas normally transits the strait at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Tanzania shuts camp housing thousands of Burundi refugees
stories.summary: Tanzania closed the Nduta refugee camp in its northwest, returning almost all remaining Burundian refugees to Burundi, according to activists and the United Nations.

stories.title: The dark side of Gaza’s new fancy cafes and restaurants
stories.summary: New cafes and restaurants are opening across the devastated Gaza Strip, highlighting the stark contrasts within the territory's ongoing humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Taiwan’s William Lai lands in eSwatini on trip Beijing calls a political ‘stunt’
stories.summary: Taiwanese President William Lai Ching-te made a surprise visit to eSwatini, Taiwan's sole diplomatic ally in Africa. Beijing condemned the trip as a political stunt, while Lai confirmed his arrival in a social media post.

stories.title: Iran stand-off could leave Trump worse off than before he went to war
stories.summary: The ongoing standoff between the United States and Iran risks leaving President Trump in a worse strategic position than before the war began. With both sides far apart in negotiations and no clear resolution in sight, the implications for the U.S. and the Republican Party remain grim.

stories.title: Iran standoff could leave Trump worse off than before he went to war
stories.summary: More than two months into the U.S.-Iran conflict, President Trump faces the prospect of an indefinite standoff that has yielded neither a decisive military nor diplomatic victory. Analysts warn the prolonged confrontation could leave the situation worse than before hostilities began.

stories.title: Nobel peace laureate Narges Mohammadi in Iran hospital after ‘cardiac crisis’
stories.summary: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was hospitalized in Iran after experiencing a cardiac crisis while imprisoned. She received the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize for her campaign to advance women's rights and abolish the death penalty in Iran.

stories.title: Mali probes soldiers suspected of involvement in military base attacks
stories.summary: Malian authorities are investigating five army personnel, including three active-duty soldiers, suspected of involvement in coordinated attacks on a military base last week.

stories.title: ‘They don’t belong in our environment’: US vineyards battle spotted lanternflies as invasive insects spread
stories.summary: Spotted lanternflies, an invasive insect species, are spreading across vineyards from Virginia to New York, draining grapevines and reducing yields. Growers, including those at Zephaniah Farm Vineyard in Leesburg, Virginia, have resorted to manually squashing the insects, which were first noticed on the property about three years ago.

stories.title: Iran will not accept ‘imposed’ peace, Trump not satisfied with negotiations
stories.summary: A senior Iranian military officer warned on Saturday that renewed fighting with the United States was likely, after President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest negotiating proposal. Iran had delivered a new draft to mediator Pakistan on Thursday. The U.S.-Israeli military campaign, launched in late February, has been paused since April 8.

stories.title: Deputy commander-in-chief of AFU: Battlefield future depends on full system integration and decision automation
stories.summary: Ukraine's Deputy Commander-in-Chief Brigadier General Andrii Lebedenko stated that the future of the battlefield depends on complete system integration and automated decision-making. His remarks emphasize the Armed Forces of Ukraine's focus on technological modernization.

stories.title: IDF's AI unit transformed air force effectiveness in Iran war, commander tells 'Post'
stories.summary: Colonel Rotem Beshi, commander of an IDF artificial intelligence integration unit, discussed how AI transformed Israeli air force effectiveness during the war on Iran. The unit is responsible for integrating and relaying AI capabilities across the Israeli military.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes kill 10 people in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli drones and warplanes struck several towns in southern Lebanon, killing at least 10 people, despite a ceasefire that has been in place since 17 April. Hezbollah has pledged to continue its attacks.

stories.title: Iranian proposal rejected by Trump would open strait before nuclear talks, Iran official says
stories.summary: Iran proposed opening the Strait of Hormuz before nuclear negotiations, but President Trump rejected the offer. Trump said he was "not satisfied" with Iran's latest proposal without specifying his objections, and the White House declined to comment on the status of talks.

stories.title: Iran executes two for spying for Israel
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of spying for Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. One, identified as Karimpour, allegedly passed sensitive information to a Mossad officer, while Bakarzadeh was accused of collecting details on government figures and key sites, including near Natanz.

stories.title: Flotilla activists return to Istanbul after Israel detains them at sea
stories.summary: Activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla returned to Istanbul after Israel intercepted their Gaza-bound aid convoy at sea and detained the participants.

stories.title: US’s Spirit Airlines goes bankrupt amid Iran war price fuel surge
stories.summary: US low-cost carrier Spirit Airlines ceased operations and filed for bankruptcy, citing surging fuel prices linked to the war on Iran. The airline told passengers not to go to the airport after failing to secure a bailout.

stories.title: Enemy strikes minibus in Kherson again; driver injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a minibus in the city of Kherson, injuring the driver. It was the latest in a series of Russian attacks targeting civilian vehicles in the area.

stories.title: PMD issues Glof alert due to westerly wave, rainfall across GB and KP
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department issued an alert for glacial lake outburst floods in Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa due to an incoming westerly wave. Over 7.1 million people in these regions are vulnerable to such floods, which can cause sudden releases of water and debris.

stories.title: US bypasses congressional review for military sales of $8.6 billion to Middle East allies
stories.summary: The Trump administration bypassed congressional review to approve over $8.6 billion in military sales to Israel, Qatar, Kuwait, and the UAE. Secretary of State Marco Rubio cited an emergency justification for the immediate sales, which came nine weeks into the US-Israel war against Iran.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines shuts down, industry’s first Iran war casualty
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines ceased operations immediately after its board failed to reach an agreement on a rescue deal, making it the first airline industry casualty linked to the economic disruptions of the Iran war.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines prepares to shut down operations overnight, sources say
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines is preparing to shut down operations overnight after a board meeting ended without an agreement on a rescue plan. The budget carrier has been struggling financially amid rising fuel costs linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Israeli strike on southern Lebanese village kills three
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the village of Louaizeh in southern Lebanon killed at least three people, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strike brought the total number of people killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon that Saturday to at least seven.

stories.title: London police refuse to investigate British nationals accused of war crimes in Gaza
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police declined to investigate British nationals accused of committing war crimes while fighting for Israel in Gaza. Human rights groups condemned the decision not to pursue the allegations against UK citizens.

stories.title: London police refuse to investigate British nationals accused of war crimes in Gaza
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police declined to investigate ten British nationals accused of war crimes and crimes against humanity while serving with the Israeli military in Gaza. The Palestinian Centre for Human Rights and the Public Interest Law Centre had filed a 240-page dossier with the Met's War Crimes Team in April of last year.

stories.title: Sudan's medicine crisis worsens
stories.summary: Sudan's ongoing medical crisis is being worsened by disruptions to key shipping routes caused by the Iran-related conflict in the Middle East. Aid organizations report severe difficulties delivering food and medicine to millions of Sudanese already affected by the country's own internal conflict.

stories.title: U.S. military reaches deals with 7 tech companies to use their AI on classified systems; Anthropic not on the list
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense reached agreements with seven technology companies to deploy their artificial intelligence tools on classified military computer networks. Anthropic, a major AI firm, was notably absent from the list of selected companies.

stories.title: US-Germany spat over Iran intensifies as Hegseth orders troop removal
stories.summary: The dispute between the US and Germany over the war on Iran escalated after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius responded that Europeans must take greater responsibility for their own security.

stories.title: Ukraine hits oil facilities in Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck oil facilities deep inside Russian territory, targeting a key revenue source that funds Moscow's invasion of Ukraine. The broader economic impact of the strikes remains unclear. Separately, Kyiv is offering higher pay and phased demobilization to address difficulties in recruiting young people after four years of war.

stories.title: Senior Iranian officer says renewed war with US ‘likely’
stories.summary: A senior Iranian military officer stated on Saturday that renewed armed conflict with the United States is "likely." The remarks came after President Trump rejected Tehran's latest negotiating proposal and issued fresh threats to attack Iran, reflecting heightened tensions between the two countries.

stories.title: Trump 'not satisfied' with Tehran offer
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he was not satisfied with Iran's latest proposal for peace talks. A senior Iranian official warned that renewed fighting between the U.S. and Iran was "likely" after Washington rejected the offer. A fragile ceasefire between the two countries, now three weeks old, continues to hold.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Kharkiv with drones; three people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Kharkiv with drones, injuring three people. The strike adds to the ongoing pattern of Russian aerial assaults on Ukrainian urban centers.

stories.title: Mali: Rebels take key Tessalit military camp
stories.summary: Armed rebels seized the key Tessalit military camp in northern Mali on Friday, dealing a major blow to Mali's army and its Russian mercenary allies. Tuareg separatists and jihadist groups appear to be coordinating efforts against the ruling military junta. Al Qaeda-linked insurgents have also called on Malians to rise up and support a transition to Sharia law.

stories.title: US to withdraw 5.000 troops from Germany
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense announced late Friday that approximately 5,000 American troops—about 14 percent of U.S. forces in Germany—will be withdrawn over the next year. The move follows German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's comments that Iran was "humiliating" the United States, which drew a sharp response from President Trump. NATO said it is working with Washington to understand the decision.

stories.title: Two more minors arrested for killing of Yemanu Binyamin Zalka, 14 suspects in total
stories.summary: Two additional minors have been arrested in connection with the killing of Yemanu Binyamin Zalka, bringing the total number of suspects to fourteen. The newly arrested suspects are aged 15 and 17, and police said they had previously identified them as participants in the attack.

stories.title: UKMTO reports 'suspicious approach' off Yemen, urges caution
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a 'suspicious approach' incident approximately 156 kilometres southwest of al-Mukalla, Yemen. UKMTO advised vessels transiting the area to exercise caution and report any suspicious activity.

stories.title: Iran standoff could leave Trump worse off than before he went to war
stories.summary: More than two months into the U.S.-Iran conflict, President Trump faces the risk of an indefinite standoff with no clear off-ramp. Iran submitted a fresh negotiation proposal, which Trump quickly rejected. Analysts warn the impasse could leave the U.S. in a worse strategic position than before the war began.

stories.title: The ageing dilemma: why robots can’t save us but China-US cooperation might
stories.summary: US medical anthropologist Arthur Kleinman of Harvard University argued that the United States and China must cooperate on 'social technology' to address the global ageing crisis. He proposed that each country learn from the other's elder-care models despite geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Russians attempt to dislodge Ukrainian Defense Forces from northern outskirts of Pokrovsk
stories.summary: Russian troops are attempting to push Ukrainian Defense Forces from the northern outskirts of Pokrovsk in order to advance toward the town of Shevchenko. Russian forces are reportedly amassing armored vehicles and tanks in the southern part of Pokrovsk.

stories.title: ‘Trump is an idiot’: Californians fume over soaring petrol prices
stories.summary: Californians are expressing frustration over surging petrol prices driven by Middle East hostilities that have constrained global crude oil supply. Residents directed anger at President Trump as fuel costs continued to climb.

stories.title: Russia’s inching advance in Ukraine approaches eastern fortress belt
stories.summary: Russian troops are advancing toward Kostiantynivka in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, attempting to establish positions near a heavily fortified defensive belt. Ukraine's top army official said forces are repelling persistent Russian infiltration attempts on the city's outskirts.

stories.title: More killed, displaced as Israel strikes south Lebanon villages
stories.summary: Israel continued to issue evacuation orders and conduct airstrikes on villages in southern Lebanon despite a US-brokered truce. The ongoing operations have displaced and killed scores of civilians in the region.

stories.title: Apple says India antitrust body overstepping judicial authority as spat intensifies
stories.summary: Apple accused India's Competition Commission of overstepping its judicial authority as a dispute between the company and the antitrust body intensified. The commission has sought Apple's financial information since 2024 following an investigation that found the company abused its dominant market position.

stories.title: King Charles gets warm welcome in Bermuda after whirlwind US visit
stories.summary: King Charles made the first visit by a reigning British monarch to Bermuda in the territory's roughly 400-year history. The trip followed a broader visit to the United States.

stories.title: Bus hit in Kherson: Injury toll climbs to nine
stories.summary: A Russian attack on a bus in the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson wounded at least nine people, including a medical worker. The injury toll climbed from initial reports over the course of the morning.

stories.title: Guilty by Association Agreement
stories.summary: The European Union's response to Israel's recently announced new illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank is under scrutiny. The analysis examines the EU's Association Agreement with Israel in the context of documented human rights abuses.

stories.title: Settlers fire at Israeli paraglider, Palestinian homes, in separate incidents
stories.summary: Two Israeli settlers belonging to West Bank area defence force units fired weapons in separate incidents — one shooting at a paraglider mistaken for a terrorist infiltration and another firing at Palestinian homes. The second settler had his weapon confiscated by authorities.

stories.title: Rescuers release humpback whale that was stranded off German coast
stories.summary: Rescuers transported a stranded young humpback whale from the German coast to the North Sea off Denmark using a water-filled barge. The calf, nicknamed Timmy or Hope, was released despite marine experts deeming the operation inadvisable due to the animal's low chances of survival.

stories.title: NATO assessing details of US troop withdrawal from Germany
stories.summary: NATO is reviewing the details of a planned withdrawal of approximately 5,000 US troops from Germany over the next six to twelve months, amid growing tensions between Washington and its European allies.

stories.title: Trump says US Navy acting ‘like pirates’ to enforce Iran blockade
stories.summary: President Trump described the US Navy's enforcement of a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz as akin to piracy, calling the operation 'a very profitable business' as part of ongoing pressure on Iran.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest man suspected of attacking nun near Jerusalem’s Old City
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a 36-year-old man suspected of carrying out a racially motivated attack on a nun near Jerusalem's Old City. The suspect remained in custody following the arrest.

stories.title: USA: Soaring petrol prices in California
stories.summary: Rising petrol prices in California reflect a broader global energy crisis triggered by the ongoing war involving Iran. With U.S. midterm elections approaching in November, fuel costs are becoming a significant political issue. Americans are facing growing frustration as gasoline prices climb despite the country being more insulated than parts of Asia and Europe.

stories.title: Ukraine is hitting oil facilities deep inside Russia; soaring fuel prices could blunt the impact
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones have been striking oil facilities deep inside Russian territory, targeting fuel infrastructure. However, analysts note that rising fuel prices resulting from the attacks could blunt their strategic impact on Russia's war effort.

stories.title: UAE bars citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has prohibited its citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq. Authorities instructed UAE nationals already present in those countries to contact the foreign ministry's emergency line for assistance.

stories.title: Two detained Gaza flotilla leaders brought to Israel for questioning
stories.summary: Israel brought two detained Gaza flotilla leaders — Palestinian-Spanish citizen Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Ávila — to Israel for questioning. Israeli authorities accused both of belonging to a US-sanctioned Hamas-affiliated organisation and said consular visits would be provided.

stories.title: Power substation and energy company catch fire in Chuvashia
stories.summary: In Russia's Chuvash Republic, fires broke out overnight Friday at a building belonging to an energy supplier in Alatyr and at a power substation in Kanash. The causes of the fires were not immediately detailed in initial reports.

stories.title: Hezbollah’s fibre-optic drones pose new challenge for Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah has deployed fibre-optic guided drones against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, presenting a new tactical challenge. Unlike conventional GPS- or radio-guided drones, fibre-optic models cannot be electronically jammed, making them significantly harder to counter.

stories.title: Hezbollah's fibre-optic drones pose new challenge for Israel's military
stories.summary: Hezbollah's fibre-optic guided drones are posing new challenges for Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, killing two soldiers and one civilian contractor in under a week. The small, inexpensive devices cannot be electronically jammed and are forcing the Israeli military to adapt its tactics despite an April ceasefire.

stories.title: War 'likely' to resume, says Iran's military headquarters
stories.summary: Iran's military headquarters issued a statement saying the resumption of war between the United States and Iran is "likely," citing evidence that Washington is not committed to agreements. Tehran stated it had shown flexibility during talks in Islamabad and during the ceasefire but believes the US has not reciprocated.

stories.title: US says Aoun-Netanyahu meeting could help restore Lebanese control in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The US Embassy in Beirut expressed support for a potential meeting between Lebanese President Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. The embassy said Lebanon is "at a crossroads" and that direct engagement with Israel could help restore Lebanese sovereignty in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Saudi liquor store runs short because of Iran war bottleneck
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's only official alcohol retail outlet has experienced supply shortages due to shipping disruptions caused by the war on Iran. The conflict has delayed shipments to the kingdom.

stories.title: Hong Kong set for thunderstorms on Sunday as cold front approaches city
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Observatory forecast thunderstorms for Sunday as a cold front moved across the Guangdong coast, with temperatures expected to drop to around 21 degrees Celsius the following day.

stories.title: Turkey releases arrested 1 May protesters
stories.summary: Turkish security forces arrested more than 500 protesters during May Day demonstrations in Istanbul on Friday. The detained individuals have since been released by authorities.

stories.title: UN to assess Iranian attacks on Middle East telecoms
stories.summary: The United Nations telecommunications agency condemned Iranian attacks on telecommunications infrastructure across the Gulf region. The UN body plans to assess the damage caused by the strikes on Middle Eastern telecoms networks.

stories.title: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi hospitalised in Iran
stories.summary: Imprisoned Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been hospitalized in Iran. Her supporters reported a "catastrophic deterioration" in her health following a suspected heart attack.

stories.title: Mali probes alleged military links to jihadis after major attacks
stories.summary: Malian authorities announced an investigation into alleged links between military officers and jihadi and separatist groups following the largest round of attacks in the country in over a decade.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia launches approximately 1,600 drones, nearly 1,100 guided bombs, and three missiles at Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Russia launched approximately 1,600 attack drones, nearly 1,100 guided bombs, and three missiles against Ukraine over the past week. The figures underscore the intensity of ongoing Russian aerial assaults on Ukrainian targets.

stories.title: Zambia cancels world’s largest human rights and tech summit days before start
stories.summary: The Zambian government cancelled the RightsCon 2026 summit on human rights and technology just days before it was scheduled to open in Lusaka on May 5–8. Permanent Secretary Thabo Kawana of the Ministry of Information and Media said the conference did not align with "national values." The event is considered the world's largest gathering on digital-age human rights.

stories.title: Germany-US spat over Iran war intensifies
stories.summary: Tensions between the United States and Germany escalated after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the withdrawal of 5,000 American troops from German soil. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius responded by saying Europeans must take greater responsibility for their own security.

stories.title: China Eastern says sorry for boarding bridge collision at Shanghai airport
stories.summary: China Eastern Airlines apologised after one of its aircraft struck a boarding bridge while taxiing at Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport. The airline attributed the incident to a mechanical malfunction on a flight arriving from Chengdu and confirmed all passengers were safe.

stories.title: US to withdraw about 5,000 troops from Germany
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the withdrawal of about 5,000 troops from Germany within the next year. The decision coincided with Trump announcing increased tariffs on EU cars and trucks and renewed criticism of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over his comments on Iran negotiations.

stories.title: US-Germany spat over Iran intensifies as Hegseth orders troop removal
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the removal of 5,000 American troops from Germany, the largest US military base in Europe. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said the move had been anticipated and urged Europe to strengthen its own defence capabilities.

stories.title: U.S. sanctions are ‘collective punishment’, says Cuba during May 1 marches
stories.summary: During May Day marches in Cuba, officials described U.S. sanctions as "collective punishment" against the island nation. President Trump has publicly mused about taking over Cuba, which has been under a near-continuous U.S. trade embargo since 1959.

stories.title: Up to 30,000 expected at French military site for illegal rave despite unexploded mortar risk
stories.summary: Authorities in central France warned that up to 30,000 people were expected at an illegal rave party held at a military site over the weekend. Officials described the location as extremely dangerous due to the possible presence of unexploded mortars on the grounds.

stories.title: Illegal rave draws 20,000 to 'dangerous' military site in France
stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 people gathered at a military site in France on Saturday for an illegal rave. Authorities had warned attendees about the dangers of unexploded ordnance and possible blasts at the location.

stories.title: Three people wounded in Sumy region due to Russian attacks
stories.summary: Three people were wounded in the Sumy region of northeastern Ukraine over a 24-hour period due to Russian shelling. Civilian infrastructure in the region was also damaged in the attacks.

stories.title: 300 verbal warnings issued to Sharp Island visitors on Labour Day
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department issued approximately 300 verbal warnings to visitors at Sharp Island on May 1, the start of mainland China's Labour Day holiday. Around 3,000 people visited the UNESCO Global Geopark site, exceeding expectations and prompting the deployment of additional staff.

stories.title: Court restricts abortion access across U.S. by blocking mailing of mifepristone
stories.summary: A U.S. court ruling has restricted abortion access nationally by blocking the mailing of mifepristone, a medication used in medical abortions. The decision cited Louisiana's ban on medical abortions and its policy recognizing unborn children as legal persons from conception.

stories.title: US threatens shipping firms with sanctions over Iran Hormuz toll
stories.summary: The United States warned international shipping firms they could face sanctions for making toll payments to Iran at the Strait of Hormuz. The threat comes amid an Iranian blockade, stalled diplomatic talks, and growing fears that renewed conflict between the US and Iran is likely.

stories.title: Trump expands US sanctions on Cuban government and affiliates
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order expanding U.S. sanctions against the Cuban government, targeting individuals and entities supporting Havana's security apparatus or complicit in corruption and human rights violations. The move follows the ouster of Venezuela's leader as part of broader regional pressure.

stories.title: New Mexico trial citing ‘public nuisance’ laws against Meta, social platforms
stories.summary: A trial beginning Monday in Santa Fe, New Mexico, accuses Meta Platforms of designing Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp to addict young users and failing to protect children from sexual exploitation. Filed by state Attorney General Raúl Torrez under public nuisance laws, the case could force sweeping operational changes or Meta's withdrawal from the state.

stories.title: Rescuers search for man who went missing while hiking after row with girlfriend
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities are searching for a 28-year-old man who lost contact with his family after arguing with his girlfriend and going hiking. Police received a report on Saturday, and rescuers have deployed a helicopter to locate him along a trail section.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF kills Hezbollah terrorists in southern Lebanon, targets terror infrastructure
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces reported killing Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon and striking what it described as terror infrastructure. In a separate incident, Hezbollah launched several rockets toward IDF soldiers operating in the area, which landed in open areas without causing casualties.

stories.title: 60-day clock ticking over US: All you need to know about the War Powers Act deadlines and extensions
stories.summary: Scrutiny is intensifying over the U.S. War Powers Act as a 60-day deadline approaches amid the ongoing Iran conflict. With indirect negotiations stalled and tensions high, questions are mounting about the legality of continued military engagement and the constitutional limits of presidential war powers.

stories.title: Police raid Arab-majority party offices and confiscate Palestinian flag
stories.summary: Israeli police raided the offices of an Arab-majority political party and confiscated a Palestinian flag. Knesset member Ofer Cassif condemned the raid, saying it has a chilling effect on freedom of expression and association. It remains unclear whether officers had a search warrant.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Trump says U.S. Navy acting 'like pirates' to carry out naval blockade
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump described the Navy's enforcement of a naval blockade on Iranian ports as acting "like pirates" in remarks made on May 1, 2026. Trump said U.S. forces had seized a ship along with its cargo and oil, calling the operation "a very profitable business."

stories.title: Drone attack: Fire at industrial facility in Ternopil extinguished
stories.summary: Emergency responders in the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil extinguished a fire at an industrial facility caused by a Russian drone attack on May 1. The strike targeted civilian infrastructure in a region far from the front lines.

stories.title: Islamabad United blink in last over as Hyderabad Kingsmen win cliffhanger to make PSL decider
stories.summary: Hyderabad Kingsmen defeated Islamabad United in a dramatic Eliminator-2 at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium to reach the PSL final. The debutants won by two runs after Islamabad faltered in the last over, with Marnus Labuschagne celebrating on the field.

stories.title: Hamas says Israel ‘prolonging’ war through daily violations
stories.summary: Hamas accused Israel of prolonging the war in Gaza through daily killings and demolitions, describing them as violations. The militant group said Israel's continued military operations are obstructing prospects for ending the conflict.

stories.title: Trump says US Navy acting ‘like pirates’ to carry out naval blockade of Iranian ports
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that the U.S. Navy was acting "like pirates" in enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports. He described the seizure of ships, some carrying oil, as "a very profitable" business.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines closes as fuel prices double due to Iran war
stories.summary: Florida-based budget carrier Spirit Airlines ceased operations on Saturday after jet fuel prices doubled due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. The closure, occurring two months into the conflict, will cost thousands of jobs. President Trump had proposed $500 million to save the airline but faced opposition from Republicans and advisers.

stories.title: ‘Eyes and ears of the Jewish community’: NYC’s Shomrim watch groups take up counter-terrorism
stories.summary: New York City's Shomrim volunteer patrol groups, traditionally focused on preventing street crime, are now receiving counter-terrorism training. The program teaches members to identify terror tactics and spot threats, integrating the local patrols into the broader Jewish community security network.

stories.title: China trip will go ahead as planned – and it will be amazing, Trump insists
stories.summary: President Donald Trump confirmed his planned trip to China will proceed as scheduled around May 14, despite the stalled negotiations with Iran. Trump said the visit with Chinese President Xi Jinping would be "amazing," after having previously postponed it from late March.

stories.title: ‘Deplorable’: ICE hires firm accused of ‘torture’ to track down undocumented children
stories.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement awarded a contract to a private security firm, which has faced allegations of torture and enforced disappearance, to help locate unaccompanied undocumented minors in the United States. The contractor denied the allegations and will assist ICE in putting personnel on the ground.

stories.title: Family of six held by ICE arrives back in Colorado as lawyer attacks ‘kidnapping’
stories.summary: The El Gamal family, an Egyptian mother and her children previously detained by U.S. immigration authorities, returned to their home in Colorado after being released and then re-arrested. Their attorney, Eric Lee, accused the government of kidnapping, alleging officials attempted to violate a federal judge's order.

stories.title: Iran executes two men convicted of spying for Israel: judiciary
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of spying for Israel, the judiciary announced on Saturday. The hangings are the latest in a series of espionage-related executions carried out by Iranian authorities in recent weeks.

stories.title: Presidential jet gifted to Trump by Qatar completes testing
stories.summary: A Boeing 747 gifted to US President Donald Trump by Qatar has completed testing. The aircraft is expected to begin service as the new Air Force One presidential plane during the summer.

stories.title: US to withdraw about 5,000 troops from Germany
stories.summary: The United States is withdrawing approximately 5,000 troops from Germany. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said the withdrawal had been anticipated and emphasized that Europe needs to take greater responsibility for its own security.

stories.title: Iran’s meme war against Trump ushers in a future of ‘slopaganda’
stories.summary: An analysis describes how official Iranian social media accounts dramatically increased their reach during the war with the US, with views rising thirtyfold in 150 days. The campaign relied heavily on memes and has been characterized as a new form of online propaganda.

stories.title: Warehouse damaged due to nighttime attack on port infrastructure in Odesa region
stories.summary: A warehouse in Ukraine's Odesa region was damaged during a nighttime Russian attack targeting port infrastructure. No casualty details were immediately provided.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines appears closer to shutdown as time dwindles for government bailout
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines appears to be moving closer to a shutdown as prospects for a government bailout diminish. The airline entered bankruptcy proceedings for the second time in under two years, with soaring jet fuel prices linked to the Iran war contributing to its financial difficulties. President Trump had floated a bailout idea the previous week.

stories.title: Upscale Shouson Hill house burgled, HK$1.1 million in watches, foreign currency stolen
stories.summary: A residence on Shouson Hill Road in Hong Kong's Deep Water Bay was burglarized, with luxury watches and foreign currency worth over HK$1.1 million stolen. Police are investigating whether the intruders entered by scaling the wall of a neighboring vacant property. A domestic helper discovered signs of forced entry on Saturday morning.

stories.title: Power of the powerless
stories.summary: The article discusses Václav Havel, the Czech dissident, playwright, and last president of Czechoslovakia, and his 1978 essay on power, resistance, and moral responsibility. Havel became a leading opponent of communist rule after the 1968 Warsaw Pact invasion suppressed the Prague Spring, enduring persecution and imprisonment for his activism.

stories.title: War update: 138 combats on front lines; most attacks occur in Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces recorded 138 combat engagements with Russian forces along front lines on May 1, 2026. The highest concentration of attacks occurred in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: Thirteen killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, health ministry says
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed thirteen people, including four women and a child, according to the Lebanese health ministry. The strikes occurred amid ongoing fighting between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah, despite a ceasefire being in place.

stories.title: Trump says US Navy acting like ‘pirates’ during Iran blockade
stories.summary: At a rally in Florida, President Donald Trump described U.S. Navy operations seizing a ship during the American blockade of Iranian ports, saying the Navy acted "like pirates." Trump told the crowd the military took over the vessel and its cargo, calling it a profitable operation.

stories.title: Global order shift
stories.summary: At a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that terrorism has no nationality or theology. The remark, made alongside counterparts from China, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, and Central Asian states, drew criticism from domestic audiences in India.

stories.title: U.S. criticizes Zambia over delayed $1bn health aid deal
stories.summary: The United States sharply criticized Zambia after a deadline passed without the signing of a health aid agreement worth more than one billion dollars. Washington expressed dissatisfaction with the delay in finalizing the deal.

stories.title: Lebanon says 13 killed in Israeli strikes in south
stories.summary: Lebanon reported that 13 people were killed in Israeli strikes in the country's south. The attacks continued despite a ceasefire that took effect on April 17.

stories.title: U.S. to close its flagship Gaza mission as Donald Trump plan stalls
stories.summary: The United States plans to close its Civil-Military Coordination Centre in Israel, which served as its flagship mission for Gaza operations. The closure represents another setback for President Donald Trump's stalled plan for Gaza.

stories.title: Some pro-Palestinian protests could be banned amid attacks on British Jews
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer warned that some pro-Palestinian demonstrations could be banned, citing concerns about the cumulative effect of marches and language used at protests. Metropolitan Police leadership said the threat to British Jewish communities is at its highest level following a series of recent attacks.

stories.title: Top UK cop: British Jews facing greatest ever threat amid ‘epidemic’ of antisemitism
stories.summary: London Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley said British Jews face their greatest-ever threat amid what he described as an epidemic of antisemitism. Rowley has requested funding for 300 armed officers to protect London's Jewish community, while Prime Minister Keir Starmer is considering banning some anti-Israel protests.

stories.title: Four killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon killed four people and wounded others, according to the Wafa news agency. The strikes targeted the towns of Kfar Dajjal, Shoukin, Froun, Adshit, Majdal Zoun, and several other locations. The Israeli military had issued expulsion orders to nine villages prior to the attacks.

stories.title: In Kherson, enemy attacks minibus, two dead, seven injured
stories.summary: A Russian attack struck a minibus in Kherson, Ukraine, killing two people—including a municipal utility worker and an unidentified woman—and injuring seven others. Authorities are working to determine the identity of the second victim.

stories.title: UK Green Party candidate posts about killing Zionists from Anne Frank parody account
stories.summary: UK Green Party candidate Tina Ion posted content about killing Zionists from a parody account based on Anne Frank, also referring to "Jewish Nazis" as "money grubbing thieves." The party has faced multiple antisemitism allegations, and two candidates were detained on suspicion of stirring up racial hatred online.

stories.title: Gulf countries’ plans to bypass Strait of Hormuz still far off, experts warn
stories.summary: Experts warn that Gulf states' plans to build oil export infrastructure bypassing the Strait of Hormuz face significant obstacles. Economic constraints, political considerations, and regional diplomatic rivalries are expected to delay such projects.

stories.title: Trump-EU rift spurs Germany to boost military, add 75,000 soldiers
stories.summary: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called on Europeans to strengthen their own defenses after the Pentagon announced the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. soldiers from Germany. Germany plans to add 75,000 troops to its military. The drawdown follows tensions between Washington and its transatlantic allies over the Iran conflict and tariff disputes.

stories.title: US LNG exports to Asia surged in April as Middle East conflict curtailed supply
stories.summary: US liquefied natural gas exports to Asia increased by more than 175 percent in April, driven by supply disruptions linked to the ongoing conflict between Iran and other parties in the Middle East.

stories.title: Japan’s Takaichi pledges deeper energy cooperation with Vietnam
stories.summary: Japanese Foreign Minister Sanae Takaichi visited Hanoi and signed six agreements with Vietnam covering energy cooperation, technology, agriculture, and space. The visit aimed to deepen bilateral ties between the two countries.

stories.title: US ‘still not satisfied’ after Tehran conveys another offer
stories.summary: After Pakistan transmitted Iran's latest proposal to the United States, President Trump said he was still not satisfied with Iran's offer to end the Middle East conflict. Trump acknowledged Pakistan's role in mediating, appreciating PM Shehbaz Sharif and FM Munir's efforts.

stories.title: Iran stalemate
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Iran remain deadlocked despite a ceasefire extended largely through Pakistan's mediation efforts. Mutual blockades around the Strait of Hormuz continue to disrupt global energy markets and fuel inflation. Reports indicate Iran sent a new set of proposals to Washington via Pakistani intermediaries.

stories.title: OneFamily brings 1,000 bereaved Israelis together for Remembrance Day
stories.summary: The Israeli organization OneFamily held a Remembrance Day ceremony bringing together approximately 1,000 bereaved family members of fallen soldiers and terror victims. The event honored those lost to conflict and terrorism.

stories.title: Asylum seeker sent back to France in ‘one in, one out’ scheme to be returned to Syria
stories.summary: A 26-year-old Kurdish Syrian asylum seeker, sent from the UK to France under a bilateral "one in, one out" agreement between Prime Minister Keir Starmer and President Emmanuel Macron, now faces deportation to Syria after French authorities deemed it safe. He says he fled forced conscription by the YPG militia.

stories.title: UAE’s Opec exit signals aim to accelerate foreign policy diversification
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates officially exited the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), framing the move as a step toward greater economic autonomy. The departure coincided with a downgrading of Emirati diplomatic participation in Gulf regional forums, signaling Abu Dhabi's broader effort to diversify its foreign policy and expand its global influence.

stories.title: China’s live music boom spreads to smaller cities as consumption drive expands
stories.summary: High-profile live music events are expanding beyond China's major cities into smaller counties and towns. Dianjiang, a county in Chongqing, hosted a large concert in April featuring Mandopop star Jeff Chang. The trend reflects Beijing's push to boost domestic consumption and tap into previously overlooked markets.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 142 out of 163 Russian drones overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 142 of 163 Russian drones launched beginning the evening of May 1. The drones were destroyed or electronically suppressed overnight.

stories.title: Crisis in Sindh health department as 75pc of top-level technical posts lying vacant
stories.summary: More than 75 percent of top-level technical posts in Sindh's health department are vacant, with 53 of 70 Grade-20 positions unfilled primarily due to retirements without replacements. The shortages come as the Pakistani province faces multiple outbreaks of infectious diseases.

stories.title: ‘Golden week’ begins with bang in Hong Kong, but restaurants’ gains ‘limited’
stories.summary: Hong Kong recorded a 13% year-on-year increase in mainland Chinese visitors on the first day of China's Labour Day 'golden week' holiday. However, a restaurant trade lawmaker noted that more cautious tourist spending resulted in limited gains for the sector.

stories.title: Iran official says war 'likely' as Israel strikes Lebanon
stories.summary: An Iranian official said war with Israel is "likely" as Israeli forces struck targets in Lebanon. Tensions continued over the Strait of Hormuz after President Trump said he was not satisfied with a new Iranian negotiation proposal.

stories.title: Iran official says war 'likely' as Trump snubs peace proposal
stories.summary: An Iranian official declared that war with the United States is "likely" after President Trump said he was "not satisfied" with a new Iranian proposal for negotiations. The standoff over the Strait of Hormuz continued on Saturday amid the diplomatic impasse.

stories.title: Capital Deve­lopment Authority halts land retrieval drive amid PM’s skyscraper relief
stories.summary: Pakistan's Capital Development Authority halted operations against informal settlements to retrieve state land in Islamabad after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif intervened to stop enforcement action against the "One Constitution" skyscraper on Constitution Avenue. The decision sparked widespread criticism on social media.

stories.title: Germany says it expected Trump’s withdrawal of US troops as row over Iran comments grows – live
stories.summary: Germany's defence minister responded to U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement that 5,000 American troops will be withdrawn from bases in Germany. Separately, a senior Iranian military officer told Fars news agency that renewed fighting between the U.S. and Iran was "likely," after Trump reportedly rejected a new Iranian peace proposal delivered via Pakistan.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,240 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces lost approximately 1,240 troops in a single day of fighting in Ukraine, bringing total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, to roughly 1,332,950 personnel as of May 2, 2026.

stories.title: Who owns Novitex: Iran's largest crypto exchange used by IRGC to move millions - explainer
stories.summary: An investigation revealed that Nobitex, described as Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has been used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to move funds. Founded by two brothers using an alternative family name, the platform has processed tens to hundreds of millions of dollars in transactions linked to sanctioned groups.

stories.title: Mini-crises sparked by the Iran war may add up to a big collapse
stories.summary: Analysts warn that the Iran war could trigger a cascading series of economic mini-crises rather than a single major crash. Some suggest the closure of the Strait of Hormuz may increase European and Asian dependence on US oil and gas, potentially benefiting the Trump administration.

stories.title: Hezbollah’s fibre-optic drones pose new challenge for Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah is deploying drones guided by fibre-optic cables rather than conventional GPS or radio signals, making them resistant to electronic jamming by Israel. The thin cables can extend for dozens of kilometres from the launch site, presenting a new tactical challenge for Israeli defenses.

stories.title: On May Day people across US rally for workers, peace, democracy
stories.summary: Across the United States, people marked May Day on Friday by participating in a general strike and rallies. Demonstrators called for increased funding for healthcare and education, as well as peace and democracy.

stories.title: Oscars bans AI actors and writers
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced new rules barring AI-generated actors and writers from Oscar eligibility. The policy marks the Academy's first formal stance on artificial intelligence in filmmaking, an issue that was central to the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes high-rise building in Kharkiv, injuring two people
stories.summary: Two people were injured in Kharkiv, Ukraine, after a Russian drone struck a residential high-rise building during the night of May 2. The attack targeted a civilian area of the city.

stories.title: Iran: Jailed Nobel winner Narges Mohammadi hospitalized
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was hospitalized after suffering a cardiac crisis in detention. Mohammadi, who won the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize for her advocacy of women's rights and freedom, remains in Iranian custody.

stories.title: Rebuilding Gaza Strip: Labour Day is the last thing on Palestinians minds
stories.summary: In Khan Younis in the Gaza Strip, workers continue clearing rubble around the clock seven months after a ceasefire ended two years of war. The laborers earn only a few euros per day, barely enough to support their families, as reconstruction efforts remain in early stages.

stories.title: Trump told Congress that hostilities "have terminated"
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told Congress that hostilities with Iran "have terminated" as the 60-day War Powers Resolution deadline for securing congressional authorization expired on Friday. Trump argued the law was unconstitutional and cited a ceasefire reached in early April as evidence the conflict had already ended.

stories.title: US to withdraw 5.000 troops from Germany
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense announced late Friday that approximately 5,000 American troops—about 14 percent of U.S. service members in Germany—will be withdrawn over the next year. The move follows President Trump's plans to reduce the U.S. military presence in the NATO ally amid a diplomatic dispute over Germany's comments on Iran.

stories.title: ‘Notices, cases, red lines and violence’ put media in a bind
stories.summary: A Pakistan Press Foundation report documented at least 233 incidents of journalists being targeted in Pakistan between January 2025 and April 2026, including 67 assaults, 67 criminal complaints, 11 arrests, and three abductions. The Pakistan Electronic Crimes Act was cited as a major tool of legal pressure against media.

stories.title: Mali: Rebels take key Tessalit military camp
stories.summary: Armed rebels seized the key Tessalit military camp in northern Mali on Friday, defeating Malian army forces and their Russian mercenary allies. Tuareg separatists and jihadist groups appear to be coordinating operations against the ruling military junta. Al Qaeda-linked insurgents have also called on Malians to support a transition to Sharia law.

stories.title: Tuareg separatists and jihadists wage attacks across Mali
stories.summary: In Mali, Tuareg separatists and jihadist groups launched coordinated attacks, capturing a key northern military stronghold from the Malian army and its Russian mercenary allies on Friday. Al Qaeda-linked insurgents called on Malians to rise against the military-led government and support the imposition of Sharia law.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines begins ‘wind-down’, cancels all flights over fuel crisis
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines has ceased operations and canceled all flights, initiating a wind-down of the US-based budget carrier. The shutdown, triggered by a doubling in jet fuel prices, is expected to result in thousands of job losses.

stories.title: Explosion of bombs left over from strikes kills 14 Iranian Revolutionary Guard members, reports say
stories.summary: An explosion of unexploded ordnance left over from earlier strikes killed 14 members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps near the northern city of Zanjan, northwest of Tehran. The report was published by Nournews, a website believed to have close ties to Iran's security establishment.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. Navy acting ‘like pirates’ to carry out naval blockade of Iranian ports
stories.summary: President Donald Trump described the U.S. Navy as acting "like pirates" while enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports. He made the comments while discussing the recent seizure of a ship by American forces.

stories.title: Death of China celebrity cat leads to hospital compensation, benefits 1,100 stray felines
stories.summary: A celebrity cat in Shenzhen, China, died due to a medical error at a veterinary hospital, prompting the facility to offer compensation to the owner. The hospital also committed to providing free sterilization for 1,100 stray cats as part of the settlement.

stories.title: Russians strike Zaporizhzhia region 857 times over past day, leaving three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 857 strikes on 45 settlements across Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over the past day. Three people were wounded in attacks on the Zaporizhzhia district.

stories.title: How the Iran war is hurting travelers, airline industry
stories.summary: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran conflict is disrupting global air travel by triggering a jet fuel shortage. European travelers may face higher ticket prices and altered summer travel plans as airlines contend with rising fuel costs.

stories.title: How Trump is inadvertently bringing Japan, South Korea together
stories.summary: Japan and South Korea are strengthening diplomatic ties through high-level meetings amid growing regional volatility. Analysts say the rapprochement reflects shared concerns over China, North Korea, and uncertainty about US commitments under President Trump.

stories.title: Naqvi pledges ‘merit over politics’ in FIA hiring
stories.summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited FIA headquarters in Islamabad and pledged that over 1,300 new appointments at the Federal Investigation Agency would be based on merit and transparency, free from political influence. His remarks came shortly before the application deadline for the agency's largest recruitment drive in years.

stories.title: President Zardari wraps up China visit with new agreements
stories.summary: President Asif Ali Zardari returned to Pakistan after a five-day visit to China focused on strengthening bilateral economic cooperation. He departed from the Chinese city of Sanya, where he was seen off by senior Communist Party of China officials.

stories.title: Pakistan Medical Association warns of ‘man-made epidemic’ over syringe reuse
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical Association warned of a potential "man-made epidemic" caused by the widespread manufacture and use of reusable syringes despite a national ban. The PMA called for audits of syringe-manufacturing units and blamed drug regulatory authorities for a "catastrophic failure."

stories.title: UK PM Starmer says some pro-Palestinian marches could be banned, cites intifada chants
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said some pro-Palestinian marches could be banned, particularly those featuring calls for intifada. The remarks followed a rise in antisemitic incidents, including a stabbing attack in the north London suburb of Golders Green.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A Middle East Eye briefing highlighted intensifying pressure on Iran, continued violence in Lebanon, and rising geopolitical strain. Air defense activity in Israel, new U.S. sanctions on Iranian-linked networks, and maritime disruptions were noted. Diplomatic signals between Washington and Tehran remained mixed amid ongoing military activity.

stories.title: Twenty-four companies join private air defense initiative
stories.summary: Twenty-four Ukrainian companies from regions including Kharkiv, Odesa, Kyiv, Poltava, and Zakarpattia have joined a private air defense initiative aimed at bolstering Ukraine's defensive capabilities.

stories.title: China’s UN Envoy: Hormuz closure will dominate Trump-Xi talks
stories.summary: China's UN Ambassador Fu Cong stated that maintaining the ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz are urgent priorities. He indicated that the Hormuz closure is expected to dominate upcoming talks between President Trump and President Xi.

stories.title: 2026 already this century’s worst year for the press: RSF Press Freedom Index
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders' 2026 Press Freedom Index declared this year the worst for press freedom since the index began 25 years ago. For the first time, over half of the world's countries fall into "difficult" or "very serious" categories for press freedom.

stories.title: 'Very profitable business': Trump says US Navy seizing Iranian oil ‘like pirates’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump described the U.S. Navy's seizure of Iranian ships and cargo near the Strait of Hormuz as acting "like pirates" and called it "a very profitable business." The U.S. is conducting a naval blockade of Iranian ports, while Iran has blocked most non-Iranian shipping through the strait.

stories.title: US to ‘close its flagship Gaza mission’
stories.summary: The Trump administration is preparing to shut down the Civil-Military Coordination Centre near Gaza, a US military-run body tasked with monitoring the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and boosting aid flows. The closure marks another setback for Trump's Gaza peace plan amid repeated Israeli attacks since the October truce.

stories.title: US awards F-16 upgrade contract for Pakistan, other states
stories.summary: The US Air Force awarded a $488 million contract to Northrop Grumman for long-term engineering support of APG-66 and APG-68 radar systems used on F-16 fighter aircraft. Pakistan is among the countries covered by the deal, with work to continue through March 2036.

stories.title: Record-breaking May warmth soon to blow away as cold front moves towards eastern Australia
stories.summary: A high-pressure system pushed temperatures 10 to 14°C above average across four Australian states in early May, setting records in multiple regions. A cold front is forecast to move toward eastern Australia, bringing rain, thunderstorms, and significantly cooler conditions.

stories.title: Russian forces attack infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked an infrastructure facility in the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, with residents reporting explosions in the area.

stories.title: ‘Roommates’ and ‘How to Make Challah’: Different slices of Jewish American pie
stories.summary: The Times of Israel reviewed two films exploring Jewish American life: the Netflix comedy "Roommates" starring Sadie Sandler, currently the number-one film in Israel, and the 13-minute intergenerational indie short "How to Make Challah."

stories.title: U.S. withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, U.S. officials say
stories.summary: The United States will withdraw approximately 5,000 troops from Germany over the next six to 12 months, the Pentagon confirmed. The move follows clashes between President Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who criticized Washington's strategy in the US war with Iran.
