stories.summary: President Donald Trump traveled to The Villages, Florida, for his first public event since a foiled assassination attempt. The trip comes amid heightened security scrutiny and increasing political pressure on the administration.

stories.title: Trump's attacks on Europe's leaders worsen transatlantic frost
stories.summary: Relations between the United States and European allies have further deteriorated in recent weeks under President Donald Trump's leadership. Tensions with European leaders have deepened the existing transatlantic rift.

stories.title: US Navy turns to AI firm Domino for options to counter Iranian mines
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy awarded a contract to AI firm Domino to develop capabilities for detecting and countering Iranian mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The strait is one of the world's most critical shipping lanes for global energy supplies.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists taken to Crete after Israeli interception
stories.summary: More than 100 pro-Palestinian activists aboard aid ships heading to Gaza were taken to the Greek island of Crete after Israeli forces intercepted and seized their vessels in international waters near Greece. Flotilla organizers confirmed the activists' transfer to the town of Atherinolakkos.

stories.title: ‘Peace has become a dirty word’: Israel’s peace camp gathers
stories.summary: Israeli peace activists gathered in Tel Aviv to advocate for a resolution to the conflict amid diminishing prospects for peace negotiations.

stories.title: PM Svyrydenko: Russian drones targeted power facilities, critical infrastructure, and homes for 12 hours
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Svyrydenko reported that Russia launched more than 400 drones over a 12-hour period targeting Ukrainian power facilities, critical infrastructure, and residential buildings. The sustained aerial assault struck energy systems across the country.

stories.title: Russians strike Zhytomyr region with drones, damaging sports and educational infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone attack on Ukraine's Zhytomyr region, including the regional capital. The strikes damaged sports and educational infrastructure in the area.

stories.title: 'Iran's most potent weapon': Telegraph's Adrian Blomfield offers rare frontline glimpse of Hormuz
stories.summary: The Telegraph's Adrian Blomfield reported from the Strait of Hormuz, describing the waterway's complex maritime environment. He noted approximately 300 small speedboats operating at high speeds, creating an ambiguous ecosystem where smugglers, civilians, and military actors are difficult to distinguish.

stories.title: Oscar goes missing after director forced to check it on flight: ‘could be used as weapon’
stories.summary: Director Pavel Talankin's Academy Award went missing after a TSA agent at New York's JFK Airport required him to check the statuette on a transatlantic flight to Frankfurt, citing it as a potential weapon. The airline located the Oscar two days later. Talankin co-directed the best documentary winner Mr Nobody Against Putin.

stories.title: IDF official says Iran war will be ‘one big failure’ if enriched uranium not removed
stories.summary: A senior IDF official warned that the war with Iran will be "one big failure" unless Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile is removed through negotiations. The officer also said the IDF's ability to counter Hezbollah drone threats remains constrained by the terms of the existing truce.

stories.title: UAE says Iran cannot be trusted over Hormuz, peace efforts at an impasse
stories.summary: A senior UAE official stated that Iran cannot be trusted regarding any unilateral arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz, reflecting deep regional mistrust. Diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war remain at an impasse, with Washington and Dubai both expressing frustration.

stories.title: Zayn Malik’s family urge fans to donate to Palestine
stories.summary: The family of British-Pakistani singer Zayn Malik, currently recovering in hospital, has urged fans to donate to Palestinian charities rather than send flowers. The former One Direction member's relatives directed supporters toward humanitarian aid for Palestinians.

stories.title: Poll finds 61 percent of Americans believe attacking Iran was a mistake
stories.summary: A recent poll indicates that 61 percent of Americans consider the attack on Iran a mistake. Respondents expressed concern about the war's impact on the cost of living and voiced skepticism about the campaign's success so far.

stories.title: Small plane crash in Texas Hill Country leaves five dead
stories.summary: A Cessna 421C crashed among trees at night in Wimberley, Texas, approximately 40 miles southwest of Austin, killing all five people onboard. Hays County Judge Ruben Becerra confirmed the crash occurred late Thursday night.

stories.title: Pakistan sees decline in militant violence for 2nd straight month: PICSS
stories.summary: The Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies reported that militant attacks in Pakistan fell 42 percent in April 2026, dropping from 146 in March to 85. Fatalities from militant attacks also declined from 106 to 60, marking a second consecutive month of improved security.

stories.title: Oscar statuette for award-winning Mr Nobody Against Putin documentary goes missing on flight
stories.summary: The Oscar statuette awarded for the documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin" went missing after the 3.8-kilogram award was checked into hold luggage on a flight. Director Pavel Talankin was unable to carry the statuette in the cabin.

stories.title: Gazans face years of untreated fractures amid health collapse
stories.summary: Thousands of residents in Gaza are living with untreated bone fractures due to severe medical shortages and a collapsed healthcare system. Supply shortages, restricted movement, and lack of surgical capacity have delayed necessary operations and long-term orthopedic care.

stories.title: Israel delivers Tamir interceptors to US Marine Corps for MRIC program
stories.summary: Israel delivered Tamir interceptor missiles to the U.S. Marine Corps for the Medium Range Intercept Capability program. The MRIC system uses a truck-mounted Iron Dome launcher paired with Tamir interceptors.

stories.title: Netanyahu posts AI video of political rivals turning into Arabs
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted an AI-generated video on X depicting political rivals transforming into Arabs, drawing widespread accusations of anti-Arab racism. The post also received a community note on the platform that was itself criticized as racist.

stories.title: Elbit subsidiary Fuse, Mistral to provide US Army THOR  drones
stories.summary: Elbit Systems subsidiary Fuse and partner Mistral will supply the US Army with THOR Group 2 drones. The backpack-portable, fully autonomous multirotor aircraft will provide American units with organic aerial reconnaissance and operational capabilities.

stories.title: London stabbing suspect left hospital, 'attacked Muslim friend'
stories.summary: London police identified Essa Suleiman as the suspect in a Golders Green stabbing. He allegedly attacked an acquaintance, Ishmail Hussein, described as a Muslim friend, on the same day two Jewish men were also stabbed in the area. Suleiman had reportedly left a hospital before the attacks.

stories.title: War update: 55 combat engagements since morning, Pokrovsk direction remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces engaged in 55 combat clashes with Russian troops since the morning, with the Pokrovsk direction in eastern Ukraine remaining the most active sector. Russia continues to concentrate its main offensive efforts in that area.

stories.title: Trump ‘not satisfied’ with Iran’s latest peace proposal as talks stall
stories.summary: President Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest peace proposal, saying he was not satisfied with what Tehran offered. Iranian state media reported that Tehran submitted a new plan aimed at ending the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28. Negotiations remain stalled despite a weeks-long ceasefire.

stories.title: Al-Qaeda-linked insurgents establish check points around Bamako
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked insurgents have established checkpoints around Mali's capital, Bamako, and seized a northern town. The Islamist fighters called on Malians to rise up against the military-led government and transition to Sharia law.

stories.title: Russian forces have attacked Naftogaz facilities 96 times since start of year
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Naftogaz Group facilities 96 times between January and April, targeting energy production, gas transportation infrastructure, thermal power plants, and gas stations across Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine hits both Russia’s military and the infrastructure funding it – from a refinery in Perm to air defenses in occupied Donetsk
stories.summary: Ukraine conducted coordinated overnight strikes hitting a refinery in Russia's Perm region, air defense systems, and multiple ammunition and drone storage sites across Russian-occupied territories. The operation targeted both military assets and infrastructure funding Russia's war effort.

stories.title: Mass grave containing 55 bodies found in Syria’s Aleppo province
stories.summary: A mass grave containing the bodies of 55 men and women has been discovered in the village of Mazra'et Al-Raheb, southeast of Aleppo in Syria's Aleppo province. The circumstances surrounding the deaths have not yet been fully detailed.

stories.title: Ukraine plans army pay hikes, phased discharge — Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced planned reforms including military pay increases and a phased discharge system for soldiers. The measures aim to boost morale and address complaints about exhaustion and uneven workloads on the frontline.

stories.title: King Charles wins praise for deft handling of Trump on US state visit
stories.summary: King Charles received praise for his diplomatic handling of a state visit to the United States, during which President Trump lifted some tariffs on Scotch whisky. Charles balanced praise for his host with subtle criticism, though the visit's long-term impact on US-UK relations remains uncertain amid divisions over issues including the Iran war.

stories.title: US warns shippers against paying Strait of Hormuz tolls, ‘donations’
stories.summary: The United States issued a warning to international shipping companies not to pay tolls or donations demanded in the Strait of Hormuz. The advisory came as Iranian state media reported that Tehran had submitted a new peace proposal to Washington.

stories.title: Residential building on fire in Rivne following Russian drone attack
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack struck a residential building in the city of Rivne, Ukraine, causing damage and igniting a fire that spread across approximately 100 square meters of the roof.

stories.title: ‘It’s the little things’: Israeli mother juggles war, parenthood as her husband serves
stories.summary: An ongoing photojournalism series by Chen G. Schimmel documents the lives of Israeli soldiers' wives managing family responsibilities during wartime. The second installment profiles a mother navigating parenthood while her husband serves in the military.

stories.title: Israel’s death penalty law perpetuates racial discrimination: UN watchdog
stories.summary: A United Nations committee has criticized Israel's death penalty law, calling it a grave erosion of human rights that perpetuates racial discrimination.

stories.title: Sacked Russian Deputy Minister Flees to U.S. Amid Fraud Probe, Sources Say
stories.summary: Former Russian Deputy Minister Denis Butsayev reportedly fled to the United States amid a fraud investigation. He was dismissed from the Natural Resources and Environment Ministry shortly after leaving Russia.

stories.title: Israeli general says 'Jewish terrorism' risks West Bank uprising
stories.summary: A senior Israeli general warned that violent settler attacks in the occupied West Bank risk triggering a Palestinian uprising. The general described the phenomenon as "Jewish terrorism" and said tensions in the territory are rising.

stories.title: RAF chief calls Falklands defence 'non-negotiable' as Rubio plays down Pentagon memo
stories.summary: RAF Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth declared the defense of the Falkland Islands "non-negotiable," stating the UK remains on high alert following the leak of a Pentagon memo that considered reviewing US support for British sovereignty over the archipelago. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio played down the significance of the memo.

stories.title: Once the left wing of US Jewry, is J Street now the new center?
stories.summary: J Street, long considered the left wing of the American Jewish political lobby, is increasingly viewed as occupying a centrist position. The shift reflects declining Democratic support for Israel, with J Street's pushback against anti-Zionism placing it closer to the mainstream.

stories.title: Iraq starts work on Basra-Haditha oil pipeline: state media
stories.summary: Iraq has begun construction on an oil pipeline connecting the southern city of Basra to the western city of Haditha, according to state media. The pipeline is planned to have a capacity of 2.5 million barrels per day.

stories.title: Workers in land-trades sector call for total boycott of Israel
stories.summary: Members of the UK-based Solidarity Across Land Trades (SALT) union called on agricultural workers to boycott organizations linked with Israel. The appeal targets workers across the land-trades sector to take collective action.

stories.title: Warm, wild weather puts Europe on storm and drought watch in May
stories.summary: European weather forecasters warn that May will bring a mix of storms and unseasonably warm, dry conditions across the continent, raising concerns about both severe weather events and drought.

stories.title: Army plans fast follow-up to AI cyber wargame with industry: Officials
stories.summary: The U.S. Army plans to rapidly follow up on an AI-focused cyber wargame conducted with cybersecurity executives from 14 technology firms, exploring a Pacific-war scenario. Officials said the Army aims to fast-track new AI tools and develop policies allowing greater autonomy for AI agents in cyber operations.

stories.title: Average price of gas in California edges past $6 a gallon, highest level in four years
stories.summary: The average gasoline price in California reached $6.06 per gallon, the highest level in four years, while the national average hit $4.39 according to the American Automobile Association. Analysts attributed rising fuel costs partly to the impact of the US war on Iran, noting Americans have paid $21.7 billion more at the pump since the conflict began.

stories.title: IDF: Iron Beam laser saw limited use in Iran war due to lack of batteries, 14 needed
stories.summary: The IDF revealed that Israel's Iron Beam laser defense system saw limited deployment during the Iran conflict due to a shortage of batteries, with 14 units needed. Officials noted Iron Beam's per-shot cost is negligible compared to Arrow and Iron Dome interceptors, which cost millions and tens of thousands of shekels respectively.

stories.title: No magic way to stop Hezbollah's FPV drones from striking, IDF admits
stories.summary: The IDF acknowledged it has no reliable method to fully counter Hezbollah's first-person-view drones striking Israeli positions. However, military officials suggested that removing US-imposed restrictions on IDF operations in northern Lebanon could reduce the drone threat by approximately 80 percent.

stories.title: IDF shifts focus to Iranian nuclear threat as ballistic missiles, regime change fall by the wayside
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces are shifting strategic focus toward Iran's nuclear program, moving away from prioritizing ballistic missile threats or regime change. IDF officers clarified the military never promised regime change in Iran, only the possibility of creating conditions for such an outcome.

stories.title: Trump to put 25% tariffs on EU cars, says bloc not complying with trade deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced he would raise tariffs on European Union cars and trucks to 25 percent, accusing the bloc of not complying with a trade deal reached last July with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The previous agreement had set tariffs at 15 percent on most goods.

stories.title: Israeli Air Force says it dropped 135,000 bombs in recent wars, warns of Syrian military rebuild
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force disclosed it dropped 135,000 bombs during recent conflicts, including 23,860 munitions requested directly by ground forces for close support in Gaza and Lebanon. The IAF also warned about ongoing Syrian military rebuilding efforts.

stories.title: Andy Burnham has plan to return to Westminster ‘within weeks’, allies say
stories.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham reportedly has a plan to return to the UK Parliament within weeks through a byelection, with allies saying several Labour MPs are prepared to step aside. Burnham was previously blocked by Labour's ruling body from running in February's Gorton and Denton byelection.

stories.title: Air defense forces shot down 388 of 409 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 388 of 409 Russian attack drones launched on the morning of May 1. The drones included Shahed, Gerbera, Italmas, and other types used by the Russian military.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest man suspected of attacking nun near Jerusalem’s Old City
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a man captured on video attacking a nun near Jerusalem's Old City. The incident is part of a pattern of recent attacks targeting Christians in the area.

stories.title: White House declines to comment on Iran’s negotiation proposals
stories.summary: White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly declined to comment on the latest Iranian negotiation proposals submitted through Pakistan, stating the administration does not detail private diplomatic conversations. She reiterated President Trump's position that Iran must never possess a nuclear weapon and that negotiations continue.

stories.title: Pakistan's successful US-Iran mediation reflects South Asia rise
stories.summary: Pakistan's mediation between the United States and Iran reflects a growing South Asian role in Middle Eastern diplomacy. Analysts say the effort highlights shifting regional power balances amid ongoing Iran-US tensions and broader geopolitical realignment.

stories.title: Sabastian Sawe receives hero’s welcome in Kenya after sub-two hour marathon feat
stories.summary: Kenyan marathon runner Sabastian Sawe received a hero's welcome in his home region of western Kenya after becoming the first person to run an official marathon in under two hours, clocking 1 hour 59 minutes 30 seconds at the London Marathon. He was flown to Eldoret on a Kenyan military plane.

stories.title: Zayn Malik cancels all US dates of upcoming tour following illness
stories.summary: Former One Direction member Zayn Malik cancelled all US dates for his upcoming tour following hospitalization for an unspecified illness. Malik said in an Instagram post that he is recovering at home and thanked fans for their support.

stories.title: Woman charged over death of two eight-year-old girls after Wimbledon car crash
stories.summary: Claire Freemantle has been charged with two counts of causing death by dangerous driving and seven counts of causing serious injury after her car crashed into The Study Prep school in Wimbledon, south London, in July 2023. Two eight-year-old girls were killed in the incident.

stories.title: DRC's ex-president Joseph Kabila dismisses US sanctions as "politically motivated"
stories.summary: Former Democratic Republic of Congo president Joseph Kabila rejected newly imposed U.S. sanctions against him, calling them "unjustified and politically motivated." The sanctions were recently levied by Washington against the former Congolese leader.

stories.title: Russia may be able to sustain intensity of its offensive for another one to two years – Pivnenko
stories.summary: Ukrainian military intelligence chief Oleksandr Pivnenko assessed that Russia can sustain its current offensive intensity for one to two more years. However, he noted Russia lacks the capacity to form significant reserves for large-scale operations, particularly in northern Ukraine.

stories.title: Video of attack on French nun in Jerusalem causes widespread condemnation
stories.summary: A video showing an attack on a French Catholic nun and archaeological researcher on a Jerusalem street drew widespread condemnation. Israel's foreign ministry denounced the assault as a "shameful act" after footage showed a man pushing the woman to the ground and kicking her.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister: Israel’s war has cost US $100bn
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed on X that the US-Israeli war on Iran has cost the United States $100 billion, four times what the Pentagon has publicly stated. Araghchi accused the Pentagon of lying about the war's costs and criticized the financial burden on American taxpayers.

stories.title: Foreign Office cuts will weaken oversight of international law, MPs warn
stories.summary: A cross-party group of British MPs warned that the closure of the Foreign Office's international humanitarian law unit will weaken the UK's ability to monitor and respond to violations of international law. The issue was raised with Prime Minister Keir Starmer during parliamentary questions.

stories.title: How Iranian monarchists have targeted anti-war activists
stories.summary: Iranian-British engineer Arjang Alidai, based in the UK, has received hundreds of threatening messages from Iranian monarchists after voting in the 2024 Iranian presidential election. Anti-government Iranians who boycotted the vote have targeted voters and those opposing military action against Iran.

stories.title: Cubans mark May Day amid rising humanitarian crisis
stories.summary: May Day demonstrations took place worldwide, with notable events in several cities. In Istanbul, police used tear gas and arrested around 400 people. In Havana, a large march gathered amid Cuba's ongoing humanitarian crisis, while protests also began in Paris at Place de la République.

stories.title: ‘What’s our red line?’ British Jews question their safety
stories.summary: Jewish communities in Britain are increasingly discussing whether rising antisemitic incidents have reached a tipping point that might prompt them to leave the country. Some are considering Israel or other destinations as potential refuges.

stories.title: Zelensky announces launch of military reforms with higher pay and updated contracts
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky announced military reforms set to begin in June, including higher pay and updated contracts for soldiers, non-commissioned officers, and commanders. Initial results, particularly regarding financial support for service members, are expected this month.

stories.title: Activists on Gaza aid flotilla detained by Israel disembark in Crete
stories.summary: Activists detained by Israel after attempting to deliver aid to Gaza by flotilla have disembarked in Crete, Greece. Several European governments with nationals among those arrested have called on Israel to release them.

stories.title: Russian State Prosecutors Seek Forfeiture of Jailed Billionaire’s Assets
stories.summary: Russian state prosecutors are seeking to seize the assets of jailed billionaire Vadim Moshkovich. He is the first Forbes-listed billionaire to be arrested in Russia since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began.

stories.title: Power minister declares end to month-long loadshedding following arrival of LNG shipment
stories.summary: Pakistan's Power Minister Awais Leghari announced the end of a month-long period of electricity loadshedding following the arrival of a liquefied natural gas shipment. He attributed the outages to a gas shortage linked to the US-Iran war rather than system failures.

stories.title: Tribal chiefs lack legal authority to attest documents, Federal Constitutional Court rules
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court ruled that tribal chiefs nominated by their communities do not have legal authority to attest documents such as domicile certificates or national identity card applications. The ruling came while rejecting a petition by a self-proclaimed sardar of the Kharoti tribe seeking official recognition.

stories.title: Attack on Ternopil: About 20 Shahed drones explode over city, 10 people reported injured
stories.summary: Approximately 20 Russian Shahed drones exploded over the city of Ternopil in western Ukraine, injuring at least 10 people. More than 50 Shahed drones were detected approaching the city during the attack.

stories.title: Iranian official calls Strait of Hormuz Iran’s “natural right”
stories.summary: Iranian Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad declared that the Strait of Hormuz is Iran's "natural right" rather than an international waterway, according to comments reported by Tasnim news agency. The statement follows President Masoud Pezeshkian's characterization of the American naval blockade on the strait as "intolerable."

stories.title: Hezbollah drones wound 4 troops; IDF urges civilians to leave south Lebanon town
stories.summary: Hezbollah drone attacks wounded four Israeli soldiers near the Lebanese border, prompting the IDF Home Front Command to tighten security guidelines in border communities. Lebanese state media reported four people, including a woman, were killed in IDF strikes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: How Iranian monarchists have targeted anti-war activists
stories.summary: Supporters of Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran's last shah, have reportedly targeted anti-war activists through intimidation and violent attacks. The monarchist campaign has sought to silence critics opposed to their political agenda.

stories.title: Two injured, car destroyed by Hezbollah drone attack against northern Israel border town
stories.summary: A Hezbollah drone crossed into northern Israel and struck a border town, injuring two people and destroying a car. The IDF confirmed the incident and called it a violation of ceasefire understandings by Hezbollah.

stories.title: Russian drones hit food processing plant in Bohodukhiv, injuring four workers
stories.summary: Russian drones struck a food processing plant in Bohodukhiv in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, injuring four workers. The attack targeted a manufacturing facility in the city.

stories.title: Iranian-linked drones target opposition camp in Iraqi Kurdistan
stories.summary: Drones linked to Iran struck an opposition camp in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. The attack is part of a broader escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which has been increasingly drawn into regional tensions connected to the US-led war against Iran.

stories.title: EU trade deal with South America’s Mercosur bloc takes provisional effect
stories.summary: The EU-Mercosur free trade agreement has provisionally taken effect, creating one of the world's largest free trade zones encompassing approximately 720 million potential consumers across Europe and South America.

stories.title: WHO recorded 149 attacks on health care in Lebanon
stories.summary: The World Health Organization recorded 149 attacks by the Israeli military on healthcare facilities and workers in Lebanon since February 28. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also reported 26 attacks on healthcare in Iran and 6 in Israel during the same period.

stories.title: Trump says he will raise tariffs on EU autos to 25% for 'not complying' with trade deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced he will raise tariffs on European Union vehicles to 25 percent the following week, accusing the bloc of not complying with the 2025 trade agreement.

stories.title: Army reform in Ukraine to boost combat pay and reshape how troops are recruited and retained
stories.summary: Ukraine announced military reforms to restructure combat pay and troop recruitment and retention policies. The changes will link pay more closely to combat exposure and frontline responsibility, with infantry roles receiving the largest increases.

stories.title: Iran war hampering aid to refugees as costs soar, UN warns
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that the Iran war has more than doubled the cost of delivering humanitarian aid to war-torn Sudan by disrupting shipping routes. Rising transport costs and delivery delays are hampering relief efforts for Sudanese refugees.

stories.title: Commander of National Guard does not believe in potential offensive from Belarus
stories.summary: The commander of Ukraine's National Guard stated he does not believe Belarus will launch an offensive against Ukraine. He noted that strong Ukrainian defense units with significant drone capabilities are now deployed along the Belarusian border, making a rapid breakthrough like the 2022 invasion unlikely.

stories.title: Pro-Trump commentator snaps and drops F-bomb on CNN when asked to justify Iran war
stories.summary: CNN commentator Scott Jennings swore on live television after being repeatedly pressed by progressive commentator Adam Mockler to name a concrete political concession the U.S. had gained from its war with Iran. Jennings was unable to provide an answer during the exchange on NewsNight With Abby Phillip.

stories.title: Fifa Congress: Infantino tried to stage an Israel-Palestine handshake. He failed
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino attempted to arrange a handshake between Israeli and Palestinian representatives at the FIFA Congress but failed. Palestinian Football Association chief Jibril Rajoub reportedly refused, saying he could not shake hands with someone brought to "whitewash" Israeli actions.

stories.title: Pentagon announces deal with seven AI companies for classified systems
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced agreements with seven artificial intelligence companies to develop classified military systems. The deal comes amid a reported standoff with AI firm Anthropic and growing debate over AI use in the context of the Iran war.

stories.title: Israel’s Slow War on the West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli leaders appear increasingly comfortable with the potential collapse of the Palestinian Authority as Israel continues gradual military and political pressure in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: US Hormuz coalition ‘not in competition’ with France-Britain mission, says French minister
stories.summary: France's defense minister stated that the US-led naval coalition in the Strait of Hormuz is not competing with the separate Franco-British maritime mission in the area, describing the two efforts as complementary.

stories.title: Lebanese Health Ministry: Israel has killed 2618 since March
stories.summary: The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health reported that 2,618 people have been killed and 8,094 wounded by Israeli attacks between March 2 and May 1. The toll includes casualties from ongoing Israeli strikes in Lebanon following a ceasefire agreement reached on April 17.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest man after nun attacked in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a man in Jerusalem after a French nun was pushed and kicked near the Old City in an apparently unprovoked assault. The incident comes amid increasing harassment of Christians in Jerusalem by Jewish extremists.

stories.title: Israeli forces assault Palestinian child with Down syndrome
stories.summary: Armed Israeli forces chased and briefly detained a Palestinian child with Down syndrome in occupied East Jerusalem, according to footage that went viral online. The incident drew widespread attention and condemnation.

stories.title: General Staff confirms destruction of Su-57 and Su-34 aircraft in strikes on Shagol airfield
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed the destruction of Russian Su-57 and Su-34 aircraft at the Shagol airfield in Chelyabinsk Oblast on April 25. The strikes targeted one of Russia's advanced fighter jet bases deep inside Russian territory.

stories.title: Power minister declares end of month-long loadshedding following arrival of LNG shipment
stories.summary: Pakistan's Power Minister Awais Leghari announced the end of a month-long period of electricity loadshedding following the arrival of a liquefied natural gas shipment. Leghari attributed the outages to a gas shortage linked to the US-Iran conflict rather than systemic failures.

stories.title: Artist from war-torn north relocates to Tel Aviv, discovers success with works of kibbutz views
stories.summary: Israeli artist Doron Adorian, evacuated from northern Israel after October 7, 2023, relocated to Tel Aviv where she found success in the art community. Her paintings of kibbutz landscapes now hang in prominent collections, including that of former US Ambassador to Israel Jack Lew.

stories.title: Azerbaijan summons EU envoy in row over treatment of Karabakh Armenians
stories.summary: Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry summoned the EU envoy over a resolution concerning the treatment of Karabakh Armenians. Baku dismissed the resolution as "unfounded and biased," maintaining that Karabakh Armenians left the region voluntarily.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines prepares to cease operations amid financial struggles and high oil prices
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines is preparing to cease operations after running out of cash, with a rescue attempt by the Trump administration apparently stalling. The airline had struggled with post-pandemic demand before the war in Iran drove up jet fuel costs.

stories.title: General Staff confirms new strikes on oil refineries in Tuapse and Perm
stories.summary: On the night of May 1, Ukraine's defense forces struck oil refineries in Tuapse and Perm, Russia. The operation also targeted a Buk-M3 air defense system in occupied Donetsk region and Russian military warehouses.

stories.title: Israeli forces conduct raids and seize land in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces raided Burqa village near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, firing rubber-coated bullets, live ammunition, and gas canisters at Palestinians leaving Friday prayers, wounding a young man. Several young men and children were detained. Forces also seized land near the village of Kharsa close to Hebron.

stories.title: US sends 30 planeloads of military equipment to Middle East
stories.summary: The United States sent 30 planeloads of military equipment to the Middle East and delivered 6,500 tons of materiel to Israel. The shipments come amid concerns that the conflict with Iran could resume.

stories.title: Microbes coordinate activity to reduce competition, Israeli researchers discover
stories.summary: Israeli researchers led by Dr. Sarah Moraïs discovered that microbes coordinate their activity to reduce competition with neighboring organisms. The findings show microbes respond not only to environmental conditions but also to the presence and identity of other microbes nearby.

stories.title: US Navy turns to AI firm for options to counter Iranian mines
stories.summary: The US Navy awarded a contract to an artificial intelligence firm to develop capabilities for detecting and countering Iranian naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The effort is part of a broader push to enhance AI-driven mine countermeasures in the region.

stories.title: $7 billion lost from Russia’s war economy this year through Ukraine’s “long-range sanctions” on oil sector – Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian oil processing and export facilities have cost Russia $7 billion in lost revenue this year. The damage has reduced Russia's capacity to export oil at full volume.

stories.title: Rebel alliance seizes key Tessalit military camp in northern Mali
stories.summary: A rebel alliance of Tuareg separatists and jihadist fighters seized the key military camp at Tessalit in northern Mali. The groups have been waging a joint campaign against Mali's ruling military junta.

stories.title: Pentagon inks deals with AI giants, but not Anthropic
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense signed agreements with OpenAI, Google, and SpaceX, among others, to deploy advanced AI models on the military's classified networks. Anthropic was notably excluded from the deals.

stories.title: Youssou N'Dour and Fatoumata Diawara headline FEMUA 2026
stories.summary: The 2026 edition of FEMUA, the major music festival in Ivory Coast, features headliners Youssou N'Dour and Fatoumata Diawara. Founded by Magic System's A'Salfo, the festival takes place in Anoumabo and Dimbokro, with Gabon as this year's special guest country.

stories.title: Russian drone crash in Vinnytsia region leaves one injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone crashed in Ukraine's Vinnytsia region, injuring a woman who was hospitalized. The incident was part of ongoing Russian aerial attacks on Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: War criminal Mladic close to death, say lawyers asking judge for jail release
stories.summary: Lawyers for Ratko Mladic, the 84-year-old former Bosnian Serb military commander, have requested his release from prison, stating he is close to death. Mladic was sentenced to life imprisonment for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity during the 1992–95 Bosnian war.

stories.title: Synthesized Command & Control: A new way human choices can guide AI warfighting
stories.summary: Two AI experts proposed a concept called "Synthesized Command & Control," a framework designed to allow human decision-makers to guide and oversee AI systems used in military combat operations.

stories.title: Germany needs no tips from Donald Trump, says Merz's deputy
stories.summary: German Vice Chancellor Lars Klingbeil criticized U.S. President Donald Trump, saying Trump bears responsibility for the fallout from the Iran war and rising fuel prices. Klingbeil stated Germany does not need advice from Trump on policy matters.

stories.title: Wall Street rises towards more records as oil prices slip
stories.summary: U.S. stock markets rose on Friday, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.6 percent and building on its previous all-time high. Strong earnings from Apple and Estée Lauder, along with modest declines in oil prices, supported the rally.

stories.title: Oscar statuette for ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ goes missing on flight
stories.summary: Russian director Pavel Talankin's Oscar statuette for the documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin" went missing after he was required to check it into hold luggage on a flight from New York to Germany.

stories.title: UAE says Iran cannot be trusted over Hormuz, peace efforts at an impasse
stories.summary: A senior UAE official stated that Iran cannot be trusted regarding any unilateral arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz, which remains closed by Iranian forces. Peace efforts between the two sides are reportedly at an impasse.

stories.title: UAE's Opec exit seeks to hit Saudi Arabia where it hurts
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is exiting OPEC in a move seen as a direct challenge to Saudi Arabia's dominance of the oil bloc. Diverging positions on Israel and the war on Iran are deepening the rift between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh over regional influence and oil policy.

stories.title: Pakistan reports two polio cases, tally for current year reaches three
stories.summary: Pakistan confirmed two new wild poliovirus cases in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa districts of Bannu and North Waziristan, bringing the country's 2025 total to three. Officials cited ongoing access constraints in the affected areas as a major barrier to vaccination efforts.

stories.title: Beijing backs Cuba, Brazil slams BYD slave labour conditions: Latin America relations reads
stories.summary: Chile uncovered a smuggling ring that shipped an estimated $917 million in stolen copper to Chinese buyers over five years. Separately, Brazil criticized labor conditions at BYD facilities, and Beijing expressed support for Cuba.

stories.title: Sudanese schoolchildren race to make up for years lost to war
stories.summary: In Sudan, millions of children displaced by the ongoing war are now racing to return to school and recover years of lost education as conditions in some areas begin to stabilize.

stories.title: Russian airstrike hits agricultural enterprise in Zaporizhzhia region, one man injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out an airstrike on an agricultural enterprise in the Zaporizhzhia district of Ukraine. The attack damaged farming machinery and injured one man.

stories.title: Iran demands reparations from Arab states for enabling US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Iran's UN representative Amir-Saeid Iravani demanded reparations from Qatar, Bahrain, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Jordan for allegedly enabling US and Israeli military operations against Iran. The demand was made during remarks at the United Nations and reported by Iranian state media Press TV.

stories.title: What does $350 billion in Ukraine aid look like? Nothing—it’s not a real number
stories.summary: An analysis questions the widely cited $350 billion figure for Ukraine aid, arguing the number does not accurately represent actual expenditures. The piece examines how the figure has been characterized in political discourse.

stories.title: Bolivia's agro-environmental court judge shot dead amid wave of drug-related violence
stories.summary: Víctor Hugo Claure, dean of Bolivia's Agro-Environmental Court, was shot dead by hitmen in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. Authorities linked the killing to growing drug trafficking influence in the city. The assassination drew condemnation from the judiciary and opposition politicians.

stories.title: Cuban immigrant dies in Georgia detention center, ICE tells Congress
stories.summary: Denny Adán González, a 33-year-old Cuban immigrant, died inside the privately run Stewart detention center in Georgia in what is being investigated as a suicide. He is the 18th person to die in ICE custody this year.

stories.title: Aung San Suu Kyi moved to house arrest
stories.summary: Myanmar's ruling junta leader, acting as president, ordered Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi moved from an undisclosed detention location to house arrest to serve the remainder of her sentence.

stories.title: 60-day deadline for Congress' Iran war extension approval
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers face a 60-day deadline under the War Powers Resolution to approve or withdraw continued military action in the Iran conflict. Congress remains deadlocked with no agreement in sight as the deadline approaches.

stories.title: Clashes break out in Miranshah following killing of tribal elder
stories.summary: Armed clashes erupted in Miranshah, the headquarters of North Waziristan, after unidentified gunmen killed tribal elder Malik Saifullah Khan Dawar outside his residence. Members of the Darpa Khel tribe exchanged automatic weapons fire with militants for several hours following the killing.

stories.title: Russian drone attack leaves part of Ternopil without power, casualties reported
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on Ternopil, Ukraine, left parts of the city without power and caused casualties. Details on the extent of injuries and damage are still emerging.

stories.title: British police charge man with stabbing attack on two Jewish Londoners
stories.summary: British police charged 45-year-old Essa Suleiman with two counts of attempted murder and possession of a bladed article following a stabbing attack on two Jewish men in the Golders Green area of north London.

stories.title: In Odesa, Russian drone strikes roof of shopping center
stories.summary: On the afternoon of May 1, a Russian drone struck the roof of a shopping center in Odesa, Ukraine, causing damage to the commercial building.

stories.title: Charles tamed Trump while rebuking Trumpism in ego-flattering masterstroke
stories.summary: During a state visit, King Charles III hosted U.S. President Donald Trump at a White House state dinner and presented a brass bell from HMS Trump, a Royal Navy submarine launched in 1944. The gesture was widely seen as a diplomatic move to appeal to both Republicans and Democrats.

stories.title: Do 10-year-old girls really need skincare routines?
stories.summary: In France, experts are raising concerns about a growing trend of children and pre-teens adopting elaborate skincare routines. Specialists warn that many of these products are unsuitable for young skin and may increase the risk of allergic reactions.

stories.title: Japanese man arrested after wife incinerated at zoo
stories.summary: Japanese police arrested Tatsuya Suzuki in Hokkaido on suspicion of transporting and incinerating the body of his 33-year-old wife, Yui Suzuki, at a tourist facility zoo where he worked. Authorities have not disclosed how the victim died.

stories.title: Migrants risk hunger and drowning on route from Horn of Africa to Yemen
stories.summary: The Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa to Yemen remains one of the world's deadliest migration paths, with over 900 deaths or disappearances recorded in 2025. Migrants continue making the dangerous journey despite the known risks of hunger and drowning.

stories.title: Trump’s assumptions are running his Iran policy aground—again
stories.summary: An analysis argues that President Trump's policy assumptions regarding Iran are proving counterproductive, highlighting the need for a more robust interagency decision-making process in Washington.

stories.title: Hezbollah announces operations against Israeli military in Southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced military operations against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, citing Israeli ceasefire violations including home demolitions and airstrikes. The group said it launched attacks targeting Israeli soldiers in al-Bayyada, Bint Jbeil, and Houla, according to Al Mayadeen.

stories.title: Ukrainian Air Assault Forces strike concentration of 'Pskov paratroopers' in Hryshyne
stories.summary: Ukrainian Air Assault Forces conducted a precision airstrike on a concentration of Russian troops, reportedly from the Pskov paratroopers unit, in the central part of Hryshyne.

stories.title: What next for Lebanon if ceasefire with Israel expires on 17 May
stories.summary: The ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon is set to expire on May 17, raising questions about the country's next steps. Journalists from The New Arab discussed the competing pressures shaping Lebanon's political and security decisions.

stories.title: 'Let the IDF win': Bennett criticizes gov't restrictions on soldiers operating in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Naftali Bennett criticized the Israeli government for imposing restrictions on IDF operations in southern Lebanon. He argued that the limitations allow Hezbollah fighters to remain in areas the military has been forbidden to strike.

stories.title: Fragments from UAV damage kindergarten in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: In the Zolotonosha district of Ukraine's Cherkasy region, debris from a Russian drone and its blast wave damaged a kindergarten on May 1 during an air raid alert.

stories.title: Could key climate talks mark ground zero in global push to ditch fossil fuels?
stories.summary: Colombia hosted representatives from nearly 60 countries in Santa Marta for climate negotiations focused on transitioning away from fossil fuels. The Colombian government used the gathering to push for shifting its own economy and the broader global economy toward clean energy.

stories.title: The industrial crisis is challenging both the EU and France's distinct social and economic models
stories.summary: On International Workers' Day, economist Rémi Bourgeot discussed the structural challenges facing France and the EU's economic models, arguing that isolated reforms like labor market liberalization cannot address what he describes as systemic deindustrialization across Europe.

stories.title: Israeli continues strikes near Tyre and Nabatieh
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes struck near Tyre and Nabatieh in southern Lebanon, killing a woman and injuring four others in one attack on a home near Tyre. Additional strikes near Nabatieh and Tyre killed three more people. Over 20 people were killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon in a single day, according to Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Dubai chefs shrink menus as Iran war makes tomatillos, scallops harder to source
stories.summary: Chefs in Dubai are shrinking menus as the Iran war disrupts supply chains for ingredients like tomatillos and scallops. UAE food service operators reported an average 27 percent drop in demand compared to the previous year.

stories.title: Dr Abu Safiya’s son fears for his father's safety in detention
stories.summary: The son of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya expressed fears for his father's safety while in Israeli detention. He reported that Dr. Abu Safiya has suffered abuse and medical neglect during his imprisonment.

stories.title: Ukraine could sign EU accession treaty by 2027, ratification to take several years – Kachka
stories.summary: Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister Taras Kachka stated that the country could complete EU accession negotiations within 12–18 months after an intergovernmental conference expected in July. An accession treaty could potentially be signed by 2027, though ratification would take additional years.

stories.title: Pentagon clears 7 tech firms to deploy their AI on its classified networks
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense announced agreements with seven technology firms—Amazon Web Services, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, OpenAI, SpaceX, and Reflection—to deploy their AI capabilities on the Pentagon's classified networks.

stories.title: US Army tests fresh drones, 3D printers at ‘Balikatan’ drill in the Philippines
stories.summary: The U.S. Army tested new drone systems, 3D printers, and a containerized solar-panel micro grid during the Balikatan military exercises in the Philippines. The solar power system is being evaluated as a quieter alternative to diesel generators for field operations.

stories.title: Oscar? I Hardly Know Her. Lufthansa Loses ‘Mr. Nobody’ Filmmaker’s Oscar Statuette.
stories.summary: TSA agents at a US airport reportedly required filmmaker Pavel Talankin to check his Oscar statuette into cargo, claiming it could be used as a weapon. Lufthansa subsequently lost the gold-plated award during transit.

stories.title: Russian attack hit port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack overnight damaged port infrastructure in Ukraine's southern Odesa region and wounded two people in the city of Odesa, according to regional governor Oleh Kiper on Friday.

stories.title: Russia kept its “fifth-generation” Su-57 stealth fighter near the Urals — Ukrainian drones found it anyway
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russian Su-57 stealth fighters and an Su-34 fighter-bomber at Shagol airbase in Chelyabinsk Oblast near the Ural Mountains. Satellite imagery confirmed damage to the aircraft, despite Russia positioning its advanced jets far from the front lines.

stories.title: Man convicted of attempting terror attack at Israeli embassy in London
stories.summary: Abdullah Albadri, a Kuwaiti national, was convicted in the UK of attempting a terror attack at the Israeli embassy in London. He tried to breach the embassy's perimeter armed with two knives in April 2025 after his asylum claim was rejected.

stories.title: Will Japan’s new arms export rules spark a high-end defence boom?
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced amendments to Japan's Three Principles on Transfer of Defence Equipment and Technology. Analysts say the overhaul of arms export regulations could enable Japan to export high-end weapons, including sixth-generation fighter jets.

stories.title: Lebanese President met with US Ambassador to discuss ceasefire developments
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with US Ambassador Michel Issa on Friday to discuss the ceasefire agreement with Israel. The meeting was held in preparation for further talks in Washington. Israel has continued strikes in Lebanon despite the ceasefire.

stories.title: IAEA to inspect 14 power substations that Russia tries to destroy this winter, says Shmyhal
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency is planning to inspect 14 power substations in Ukraine that Russia has targeted for destruction. Ukrainian Prime Minister Shmyhal announced the IAEA mission, noting the substations are critical to nuclear safety.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Proposed Medical Aid Reforms Spark Fears of Healthcare Crisis in Zimbabwe
stories.summary: Zimbabwe's government has proposed an overhaul of medical aid regulations, prompting warnings from industry stakeholders that the changes could increase healthcare costs, reduce access, and potentially collapse private medical coverage for thousands of citizens.

stories.title: Kenya: Police Nab Nine in Intelligence-Led Operation in Trans Nzoia West
stories.summary: Police in Trans Nzoia West Sub-County, Kenya, arrested nine suspected members of a criminal gang in an intelligence-led security operation. The arrests targeted a group described by authorities as a notorious criminal network.

stories.title: Ghana: Let's Raise Awareness About Mental Health This May - Betty Elikem Azornu
stories.summary: Mental health advocate Betty Elikem Azornu called for increased awareness about mental health in Ghana during May, noting that public conversation on the issue has long been suppressed by stigma.

stories.title: Ghana: Health Ministry Warns Public Against Fake Recruitment Links
stories.summary: Ghana's Ministry of Health issued a public warning against fake recruitment websites circulating on social media, which falsely claim to be linked to the ministry's ongoing recruitment exercise.

stories.title: US congressmen introduce resolution condemning Hasan Piker for alleged antisemitism
stories.summary: US Representatives Josh Gottheimer and Mike Lawler introduced a House resolution condemning online commentator Hasan Piker and Candace Owens for alleged antisemitism. Piker rejected the resolution, stating he has spent his career combating all forms of bigotry, including antisemitism.

stories.title: Ukraine intelligence operation inflicts heaviest losses on Kadyrov's 'Akhmat' unit – HUR
stories.summary: Between February and April 2026, Ukraine's military intelligence unit "Shamanbat," composed of fighters from free Ichkeria, conducted operations alongside the 104th Territorial Defense Brigade to eliminate mercenaries from Kadyrov's "Akhmat" unit in the Sumy direction. HUR described it as inflicting the heaviest losses on the Chechen force.

stories.title: The Deeper Pattern Behind China’s Military Purges
stories.summary: An analysis examines recent military leadership purges under Chinese President Xi Jinping, suggesting that newly appointed commanders are officials previously blocked by predecessors. The reshuffling reflects deeper patterns of consolidating control within China's armed forces.

stories.title: Sudan's Tuti Island is recovering from nearly two years of paramilitary siege
stories.summary: Residents are returning to Tuti Island in Sudan's capital Khartoum after nearly two years of paramilitary siege. Fishing boats are again moving along the Nile, though damaged homes remain visible alongside fields and old neighborhoods following prolonged conflict and displacement.

stories.title: Starmer accused of 'weaponising' antisemitic attack to target pro-Palestine protests
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has been accused of exploiting a recent antisemitic stabbing attack in London to justify a crackdown on pro-Palestine protests. Starmer called for the prosecution of people who chant 'globalise the intifada.'

stories.title: El Niño conditions likely to develop during 2026 monsoon season in South Asia, PMD says
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department warned that El Niño conditions are likely to develop during the 2026 monsoon season in South Asia, accompanied by above-normal minimum and maximum temperatures across most of the region.

stories.title: US criticises allies over failure to stop Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: The US State Department criticized allied nations for failing to prevent a Gaza-bound aid flotilla that was subsequently seized by Israeli naval forces. Spokesperson Tommy Pigott called the flotilla a 'baseless, counterproductive stunt' and urged allies to deny port access and refueling to involved vessels.

stories.title: Middle Israel: Will Bennett and Lapid's fourth Israeli alliance last? - opinion
stories.summary: Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid unveiled a new political alliance this week, the fourth such Israeli centrist partnership. Analysts note the alliance is untested and could fail like predecessors, though early assessments identify some favorable factors.

stories.title: Drop the cynicism: Bennett, Lapid's merger represents Israel's search for unity - opinion
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid have announced a political merger. Commentators describe the alliance as reflecting Israel's emphasis on political maneuvering over substantive policy.

stories.title: Ukraine sees path to Japanese arms after Tokyo eases export rules
stories.summary: Ukraine's ambassador to Japan, Yurii Lutovinov, said Tokyo's relaxation of weapons-export rules opens a path for discussions that could eventually lead to Japan supplying military equipment to Ukraine. The move represents Japan's latest shift away from its post-war pacifist stance on arms transfers.

stories.title: Iran submits negotiations proposal to Pakistani mediators
stories.summary: Iranian officials submitted a new negotiation proposal to Pakistani mediators amid stalled US-Iran talks. The move comes as a US blockade on the Strait of Hormuz continues.

stories.title: The lobbying to bring back Russian gas is back. Faster electrification is the answer
stories.summary: The conflict with Iran is boosting Russia's energy revenues and reviving lobbying efforts in Europe to resume Russian gas imports. Analysts argue that faster electrification, rather than renewed gas dependence, should be Europe's response.

stories.title: Explosions heard in Ternopil
stories.summary: Explosions were reported in the Ukrainian city of Ternopil during an air raid alert. No further details on casualties or damage were immediately available.

stories.title: Howe says Saudi owners’ desire for success at Newcastle remains unchanged
stories.summary: Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe stated that the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund's ambitions for the club remain unchanged. Separately, PIF announced on Thursday it would end its funding of LIV Golf after the 2026 season.

stories.title: Why Trump Might Come to Regret the Iran War
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the U.S. war with Iran, which President Trump had hoped would be transformational, risks becoming another protracted round in the broader regional conflict rather than achieving decisive results.

stories.title: Woman killed, children injured as Israel attacks Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck targets in Lebanon, killing a woman and injuring children, according to reports. The ongoing assault has displaced large numbers of people in Lebanon and continues despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Trump’s threat: Why cutting US troops in Europe won’t be easy
stories.summary: Amid rising transatlantic tensions linked to the Iran conflict, former President Trump threatened to reduce the US military presence in Germany. Analysts note that withdrawing US troops from Europe would face significant logistical and strategic obstacles.

stories.title: 8 Trapped After Permafrost Thaw Triggers Coal Mine Collapse in Russia’s Far East
stories.summary: Eight workers were trapped after a coal mine collapsed in Russia's Far East due to permafrost thawing. The mining company's CEO attributed the accident to the thawing of an underground pocket of ice or unstable rock known as a "lens."

stories.title: ‘Hotter than Hawaii’: London and East Anglia expected to reach 27C on Friday
stories.summary: The UK Met Office forecast temperatures of up to 27°C in London and East Anglia on Friday, marking the warmest day of the year so far. The temperatures would exceed forecasts for Sydney, Buenos Aires, and Tunis.

stories.title: Iran official reveals how Mojtaba Khamenei escaped US strike
stories.summary: Senior Iranian official Mohsen Qomi revealed that Mojtaba Khamenei narrowly survived US-Israeli strikes that killed his father, Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, along with his wife and son. Khamenei reportedly escaped the attack by only minutes.

stories.title: 'Backbone of our society': President, premier pay tribute to workers of Pakistan on International Labour Day
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif issued separate statements on International Labour Day, praising the country's domestic and overseas workers as the backbone of society and a pillar of national strength.

stories.title: Expert says Gulf war has become 'trap of easy solutions' for Trump
stories.summary: An expert assessed that the war in the Persian Gulf has become a "trap of easy solutions" for President Trump, who had expected a quick victory. The conflict has dragged on, disrupted markets, and is approaching the 60-day threshold requiring congressional authorization.

stories.title: ‘Turbulent and dangerous’: How shipping is the new global battleground
stories.summary: Geopolitical tensions are disrupting global shipping lanes from the Strait of Hormuz and the Panama Canal to the South China Sea and Black Sea. These pressures are rewriting the rules of maritime trade and raising costs across multiple critical waterways.

stories.title: Liberia: Liberia, France Launch Ambitious Sports and Youth Cooperation Agenda
stories.summary: Liberia and France launched a Youth and Sports Exchange Initiative following high-level bilateral talks in Paris. The program aims to strengthen youth empowerment and sports development cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: IDF Home Front restores security guidelines for northern border towns with Lebanon
stories.summary: The IDF Home Front Command raised the security level to "Yellow" for northern Israeli border towns adjacent to Lebanon. The decision followed Hezbollah attacks that wounded civilians and ongoing drone strikes in the area.

stories.title: Nigeria: Manufacturing Sector's Tax Contribution Rises to N1.17trn, Spurs Demand for Fiscal Support
stories.summary: Nigeria's manufacturing sector contributed N1.17 trillion in Value Added Tax revenue in 2025, representing a 45.61 percent increase over the N803.53 billion collected in 2024. Industry groups are calling for additional fiscal support measures from the government.

stories.title: NH lawmaker faces little pushback after Holocaust deniers testify to education commission
stories.summary: New Hampshire state Representative Matt Sabourin dit Choinière reportedly facilitated Holocaust deniers' testimony before the state's education commission in January. The effort aimed to insert Holocaust denial into New Hampshire's public education guidelines and drew little pushback from other lawmakers.

stories.title: New Hampshire lawmaker reprimanded for ‘final solution’ joke at Jewish colleague
stories.summary: New Hampshire Republican state legislator Travis Corcoran was reprimanded for making a "final solution" joke directed at Democratic Representative Jessica Grill, who is Jewish. Corcoran claimed he was unaware of Grill's Jewish heritage and called the disciplinary proceedings a "kangaroo court."

stories.title: Trump assassination attempt at press gala: Mainstream media and conspiracy theories
stories.summary: Following an attempted attack on U.S. President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, social media was flooded with conspiracy theories claiming the incident was staged. FRANCE 24 examined how mainstream media coverage may be amplifying or combatting such disinformation.

stories.title: Ukraine launches push to sync sanctions with allies — Russia’s shadow grain fleet first on the list
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky announced a new initiative to coordinate sanctions with allied nations, beginning with efforts to target Russia's shadow grain fleet. The system is modeled on Ukraine's earlier work against Russia's shadow oil tanker network, with enhanced coordination expected in May.

stories.title: President Macron attends Orion 26 excerices
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron attended the final phase of the Orion 26 military exercises, a large-scale combat simulation involving thousands of troops from France and several European nations. The drills, which began in February, reflect Europe's growing focus on military readiness amid Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Six wounded after stabbing attack at high school in Washington state
stories.summary: A high school student in Tacoma, Washington, was charged with multiple counts of first-degree assault after a mass stabbing at a campus on Thursday. Four students were left in critical condition, and a security guard was also injured in the attack.

stories.title: Woman denied permanent birth control on NHS wins case with ombudsman
stories.summary: Leah Spasova, a psychologist from Oxfordshire, England, won her case with the UK health ombudsman after spending 10 years fighting to obtain a tubal ligation on the NHS. She had been denied the permanent contraceptive procedure over concerns she might regret it, while men could access vasectomies.

stories.title: Errors, bad weather caused deadly Bolivian military plane crash: Probe
stories.summary: An investigation found that pilot errors and bad weather caused a fatal Bolivian military plane crash in February. The aircraft veered off the runway at El Alto International Airport near La Paz.

stories.title: Well-known businessman exposed for embezzling over ₴100 million from one of country’s largest banks
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service, working with the Prosecutor General's Office, documented new criminal activity by the former beneficial owner of one of Ukraine's largest banks. The well-known businessman is accused of embezzling over 100 million hryvnias from the institution.

stories.title: More Hongkongers can drive to Macau under expanded travel scheme
stories.summary: Hong Kong and Macau are expanding a cross-boundary driving scheme to allow more Hong Kong permanent residents to drive to Macau via the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge. The Transport Department announced 400 new multiple-entry quota places for non-commercial private car drivers.

stories.title: Ukrainian paratroopers thwart Russian attempt to reach frontline positions via gas pipeline
stories.summary: Ukrainian paratroopers repelled a Russian attempt to use a gas pipeline as a concealed route to approach Ukrainian frontline positions. Russian troops had previously used similar infrastructure-based tactics to advance.

stories.title: 4 killed in second Indonesia train crash in days
stories.summary: A train struck a car at a level crossing in Central Java, Indonesia, killing four people including two children. Police said thick fog prevented the driver from seeing the oncoming train. The incident occurred days after another deadly train crash near Jakarta.

stories.title: War-battered Syria now sells itself as a safe corridor amid regional conflict
stories.summary: Syria, after enduring 14 years of civil war, is now positioning itself as a safe transit corridor amid broader regional conflict.

stories.title: US criticises allies over failure to stop Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: The US State Department criticized allied nations for failing to prevent the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla from departing, highlighting inaction amid rising tensions between Washington and European capitals. Protests took place outside Greece's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Athens over the detention of flotilla members.

stories.title: Tokyo man who attacked teens with hammer arrested after manhunt
stories.summary: Tokyo police arrested Teruyuki Takabayashi, 44, in Narashino, Chiba Prefecture, on suspicion of attempted murder after he allegedly struck a 17-year-old high school student in the face with a hammer in Fussa, western Tokyo. A manhunt followed the Wednesday morning attack.

stories.title: Security footage shows suspect Cole Allen shooting Secret Service officer before White House dinner
stories.summary: US Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro released security footage showing suspect Cole Allen shooting a Secret Service officer before a White House dinner. The video shows Allen preparing for what appeared to be an attack on the president.

stories.title: Trump administration rejects need for Iran war Congressional approval despite deadline – US politics live
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth argued that a ceasefire agreement with Iran paused the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock, rejecting the need for Congressional approval to continue military operations. Separately, Iran sent its latest peace proposal to the US via Pakistani mediators.

stories.title: How Turkey's new 'kamikaze' drones may outclass Iran's Shahed
stories.summary: Turkey is developing new AI-powered kamikaze drone platforms that may surpass Iran's Shahed drones in capability. The systems, produced by Turkish aviation company Baykar, enable coordinated swarms, precision strikes, and resistance to electronic warfare.

stories.title: India's cows offer biogas alternative to Mideast energy crunch
stories.summary: In rural Uttar Pradesh, India, residents like villager Gauri Devi in Nekpur are using biogas produced from cow dung as an alternative cooking fuel. The shift helps ease pressure on LPG supplies disrupted by the Iran war.

stories.title: 'We should be able to open up negotiations' with Ukraine, Sweden's EU minister says
stories.summary: Sweden's EU Affairs Minister Jessica Rosencrantz discussed opening negotiations with Ukraine during a visit to France. She also addressed Europe's energy crunch and its implications for the continent's competitiveness.

stories.title: Women reveal battle with little-known chronic leg fat condition called lipoedema
stories.summary: Research suggests lipoedema, a chronic condition involving disproportionate leg fat, may affect up to one in ten women globally. Patients have spoken publicly about the challenges of living with the little-known disorder.

stories.title: Kenya temporarily waives fuel standards to combat Iran war shortages
stories.summary: Kenya announced a temporary waiver of fuel quality standards to address shortages caused by disruptions from the war involving Iran in the Middle East. The measure aims to ease supply constraints affecting the country.

stories.title: UN says Iran war doubles Sudan aid costs and delays deliveries
stories.summary: UNHCR reports that the Iran war has approximately doubled the cost of delivering humanitarian aid to Sudan. Disruption along Gulf shipping corridors, including the Strait of Hormuz, has forced longer routing from Europe, causing delays and rising fuel and insurance costs.

stories.title: Destruction and casualties: Aftermath of Russian attacks on Kherson and its suburbs
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Kherson and its suburbs with drones, causing significant destruction. The strikes killed one person and injured several others.

stories.title: 'A common enemy, but not a common project': A fragile jihadist-separatist alliance in Mali
stories.summary: Mali faces a serious security challenge as Al-Qaeda-linked jihadist fighters and Tuareg separatists have launched coordinated attacks and tightened a blockade around the capital, Bamako. The escalation puts pressure on Mali's military rulers but raises questions about the durability of the jihadist-separatist alliance.

stories.title: Oil prices rise amid US-Iran impasse
stories.summary: Global oil prices eased slightly on Friday after surging above $126 per barrel amid fears that the prolonged US-Iran war could worsen supply shortages. In a related development, the United Arab Emirates announced plans to formally exit OPEC.

stories.title: Russia just got its Crimea looter back — and he’s not even pretending to lay low
stories.summary: Russian national Butyagin, freed in a five-for-five prisoner exchange between Poland and Belarus, told Russian state media he plans to resume illegal archaeological excavations in Crimea. Ukraine had previously charged him for looting cultural artifacts from the peninsula.

stories.title: Egypt conducts live-fire military exercises near Israeli border
stories.summary: Egypt carried out the 'Badr 2026' live-fire tactical exercises in the Sinai Peninsula near the Israeli border. The drills involved army units, special forces, fighter jets, and tanks.

stories.title: Pentagon plans to make US military ‘AI-first fighting force’ by pairing with companies
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced agreements with seven AI companies—SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, Reflection, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services—to transform the US military into an "AI-first fighting force." The partnerships have raised concerns about public spending, cybersecurity, and domestic surveillance.

stories.title: US administration says war "terminated", no approval needed
stories.summary: US lawmakers remain deadlocked over the War Powers Resolution as the 60-day deadline for Congressional approval of military action approaches. The Trump administration has argued the war with Iran has been "terminated," asserting no Congressional authorization is needed.

stories.title: US Navy turns to AI firm Domino for options to counter Iranian mines
stories.summary: The US Navy is working with AI firm Domino to develop options for countering Iranian naval mines. The partnership centers on the speed of Domino's AI-driven approach to mine countermeasures.

stories.title: Giorgia Meloni’s moral retreat on Gaza
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's stance on Israel's military campaign in Gaza has drawn criticism for being driven by political calculation rather than moral principle.

stories.title: Switzerland allocates additional CHF 50M for Ukraine reconstruction projects
stories.summary: Switzerland announced an additional CHF 50 million in grant funding for Ukraine reconstruction projects. The funding is part of a third call for investment projects developed in cooperation with the Swiss private sector.

stories.title: Woman jailed for life for murdering sister and stealing her Rolex
stories.summary: Nancy Pexton, 70, was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 22 years for murdering her sister Jennifer Abbott in a London flat in Camden. She stabbed Abbott 10 times and stole her Rolex watch, leaving the body for three days.

stories.title: Why US may regret pushing allies towards greater defence autonomy
stories.summary: The article discusses the potential long-term consequences for the United States of encouraging allies to develop greater defence autonomy. It notes that calls for European and East Asian allies to increase their own defence spending predate the Trump administration.

stories.title: What is Hezbollah's 'suicide combat' strategy in south Lebanon?
stories.summary: Hezbollah is deploying close-range 'suicide combat' units and drone ambush tactics in southern Lebanon, marking a significant shift in the group's military strategy against Israeli forces.

stories.title: Greek Orthodox Church sounds alarm over attacks on Christians in Jerusalem
stories.summary: The Greek Orthodox Church has raised concerns about escalating attacks on Christians in Jerusalem. The warning followed the arrest of a Jewish man in connection with a violent assault on a nun in the city this week.

stories.title: The Route Back Home: How Gaza's children use art to express the nightmares of genocide
stories.summary: An exhibition at the Old Palestine House in Brighton displays artwork and written testimonies by children from Gaza depicting their experiences since October 2023. The show includes a blank canvas belonging to eight-year-old Ghazi Ramadan, who wanted to draw a shopping mall but was unable to complete it.

stories.title: Korchakivka in Sumy region remains under control of Armed Forces of Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian military officials confirmed that the village of Korchakivka in the Sumy region remains under the control of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, denying reports that Russian forces had captured it.

stories.title: Australian Indigenous protesters and police clash over arrest of suspected killer of 5-year-old girl
stories.summary: Police in Alice Springs, Australia, fired tear gas at hundreds of Indigenous protesters who gathered outside a hospital following the arrest of a man accused of killing a five-year-old girl. Members of the crowd demanded the suspect face customary law and attacked police, emergency workers, and set vehicles on fire.

stories.title: Israel’s Rafah crossing clampdown freezes Gaza’s academic hopes
stories.summary: Israel's closure of the Rafah crossing over approximately two years of war has left students in Gaza unable to travel abroad to take up scholarships. The border restrictions have effectively frozen academic opportunities for Gaza's student population.

stories.title: Israel's death penalty law perpetuates racial discrimination: UN watchdog
stories.summary: A UN anti-racism committee has called on Israel to immediately repeal its recently enacted death penalty law targeting Palestinian prisoners. The committee said the legislation perpetuates racial discrimination.

stories.title: Pentagon seals artificial intelligence agreements with seven tech giants
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense signed AI integration agreements with seven technology companies, including SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services. The contracts aim to deploy AI tools in classified operational environments to strengthen U.S. military technological capabilities.

stories.title: The West’s bubble of illusion about Israel - and about itself – is finally being burst
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the conflict in Gaza and military operations in Lebanon have eroded Western moral legitimacy, while the Iran conflict is challenging Western military primacy.

stories.title: From life in North Korea to pink hair dye: K-pop band 1VERSE spills all
stories.summary: K-pop band 1VERSE, whose members hail from North Korea, Japan, and the United States, discussed their diverse backgrounds during a stop in Paris on their world tour. The group spoke with France 24's Yuka Royer.

stories.title: UN says Israel death penalty law targets Palestinians, erodes rights
