stories.summary: Research ahead of UK elections on May 1 reveals nearly twice as many men as women are standing as candidates across local, mayoral, and devolved elections. Democracy campaigners warned that women remain "massively underrepresented" on ballot papers across all political parties.

stories.title: Uganda: Amnesty Urges Probe Into Alleged Security Force Abuses During January 15 Polls
stories.summary: Amnesty International has called for investigations into alleged human rights abuses by Ugandan security forces during the January 15 presidential and parliamentary elections. The allegations include unlawful killings, arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, and torture.

stories.title: Mali: Russia Vows to Keep Forces in Mali Despite Warning From Separatists to Withdraw
stories.summary: Russia declared that its forces would remain in Mali to continue supporting the country's military rulers, rejecting withdrawal demands from Tuareg separatists. The statement followed surprise attacks by separatists that forced Russian troops out of a key northern town.

stories.title: UN Chief warns consequences of Middle East crisis 'grow dramatically worse'
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that the Middle East crisis is worsening with each passing hour and called for a pathway to peace. He noted that restrictions on movement in the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted global energy supplies, transport, manufacturing, and food markets.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudanese Refugees Injured in Sixth Armed Attack On Camp in Ethiopia
stories.summary: Sudanese refugees were injured in an armed attack on Aftit camp in Ethiopia's Amhara province on Tuesday evening. It was the sixth such armed incident at the camp, raising concerns about deteriorating security conditions for refugees in the settlement.

stories.title: Sudan: 17 Sudanese Refugees Drown Off Tobruk, Libya
stories.summary: The UNHCR confirmed that at least 17 Sudanese refugees drowned after a shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Tobruk, Libya. Of the 33 people believed to have been on board, only seven survived, and nine remain missing.

stories.title: Brent touches $126 amid US military plan for 'short and powerful' strikes on Iran
stories.summary: Brent crude surged to $126.41 a barrel on Thursday after reports that US Central Command was preparing "short and powerful" strikes on Iranian infrastructure. Prices later settled near $114. The European benchmark has risen more than 60% since the US-Iran war began on February 28.

stories.title: Report: Cost of war on Iran closer to $50 billion
stories.summary: A CBS News report citing US officials estimated the total cost of the Iran war at approximately $50 billion, double the $25 billion figure previously announced by Pentagon official Jules Hurst for 'Operation Epic Fury.' The discrepancy reportedly stems from the initial estimate not accounting for damaged or destroyed military equipment.

stories.title: Sheryl Sandberg endows scholarship at Camp Ramah in California in honor of late husband
stories.summary: Sheryl Sandberg, the author of "Lean In" and a prominent philanthropist, endowed a scholarship at Camp Ramah in California in honor of her late husband. Sandberg has been a longstanding donor to Jewish and Israeli causes.

stories.title: Trump says ‘probably’ when asked if he might pull US troops out of Italy, Spain
stories.summary: President Trump indicated he would "probably" consider withdrawing US troops from Italy and Spain when asked about the possibility. The remarks follow earlier US statements about potentially reducing military personnel stationed in Germany.

stories.title: Trump says 'probably' when asked if he might pull US troops out of Italy, Spain
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said "probably" when asked whether he might withdraw U.S. troops from Italy and Spain. The comment followed his announcement that Washington was considering reducing military personnel stationed in Germany.

stories.title: Panama president says port caught in US-China dispute
stories.summary: Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino said his country maintains a positive relationship with China despite being caught in a US-China dispute. He defended Panama's takeover of port contracts previously held by Hong Kong's CK Hutchison.

stories.title: ‘Even 1 case is too many’: experts warn of lasting harm after alleged dog cage child abuse
stories.summary: Psychologists in Hong Kong warned of lasting mental harm to children after two toddlers were allegedly confined in a dog cage, sparking public outrage. More than 100 reports have been filed since a mandatory child abuse reporting requirement took effect in January.

stories.title: NBU downgrades 2026 GDP growth forecast
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Bank downgraded its GDP growth forecast for 2026, projecting more restrained economic expansion than previously anticipated.

stories.title: Trump says Secret Service agent at dinner was not hit by friendly fire
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that the Secret Service agent injured during an attack at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner was not struck by friendly fire.

stories.title: GOP lawmaker pushed to add a Holocaust denier to New Hampshire’s Holocaust panel
stories.summary: A Republican lawmaker in New Hampshire attempted to place a Holocaust denier on the state's Holocaust education commission. The effort drew condemnation from Jewish leaders and other lawmakers.

stories.title: Myanmar ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi moved to house arrest, military says
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government announced that former leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been moved from prison to house arrest. The Nobel Peace Prize laureate has been in detention since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.

stories.title: Aung San Suu Kyi: The Myanmar democracy icon detained for years
stories.summary: Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been largely out of public view since she was ousted in the 2021 military coup. Little information has emerged about her condition during her years of detention.

stories.title: Iran war may cause food shortages in Africa, world’s largest fertiliser firm says
stories.summary: Yara International CEO Svein Tore Holsether warned that the Iran war could cause food shortages and price rises in Africa's most vulnerable communities. The world's largest fertiliser company cautioned that soaring fertiliser prices could trigger a global bidding war, leaving the poorest countries unable to secure essential supplies.

stories.title: Danish treatment of Greenlandic mother may be ‘ethnic discrimination’, says UN
stories.summary: The United Nations warned Denmark that the removal of a Greenlandic Inuit mother's newborn child may constitute "ethnic discrimination." Keira Alexandra Kronvold's daughter was taken into foster care in November 2024, two hours after birth, based on parenting competency tests that have since been banned.

stories.title: Many Asian-Americans feel excluded from ‘true’ US identity, survey finds
stories.summary: A survey found that many Asian-Americans feel excluded from being seen as "truly" American by mainstream U.S. society. The findings highlight ongoing identity struggles among Asian-Americans despite being born and raised in the United States.

stories.title: King Charles’ gift amuses Chinese, anti-spy agency makes allegation: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: A weekly roundup from the South China Morning Post highlights stories including projections that the U.S.-China economic gap will widen to $11 trillion by decade's end. Other topics covered include the Iran conflict's potential to bring the two powers closer and a gift from King Charles that amused Chinese audiences.

stories.title: Hegseth decries spread of 'falsehoods' regarding security of Kuwaiti base during Iran war
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was questioned by Representative Patrick Ryan of New York about the security of a US base in Kuwait. Ryan pressed Hegseth on an Iranian drone attack in early March that killed six US Army Reserve soldiers.

stories.title: Scared and angry UK Jews demand government do more to address antisemitic violence
stories.summary: Following an antisemitic stabbing attack in the Golders Green area of north London, British Jewish community members demanded the government take stronger action against antisemitic violence. Residents expressed fear and skepticism about whether authorities would adequately respond to the rising threat.

stories.title: Ukraine returns 2,126 children abducted by Russia — Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that 2,126 children abducted by Russia have been returned to Ukraine through the Bring Kids Back UA initiative.

stories.title: Police say they will charge people with unrest in Alice Springs after arrest over death of Kumanjayi Little Baby
stories.summary: Northern Territory police in Australia said one person faces charges and more are expected over unrest in Alice Springs following the arrest of a man connected to the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby. The child's body was found 5km from the Old Timers town camp. Her grandfather, a senior Warlpiri elder, appealed for calm.

stories.title: US determines hostilities against Iran have ended, says official
stories.summary: A senior US official told NBC News that US hostilities against Iran, which began on February 28, have been 'terminated.' The two sides agreed to a two-week ceasefire on April 7 that has since been extended, with negotiations restarting alongside the halt in fighting.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Iran briefly activates Tehran air defences against ‘reconnaissance drones’
stories.summary: Tehran briefly activated air defences for approximately 20 minutes late Thursday to counter what Iranian state news agencies Tasnim and Fars described as small aircraft and reconnaissance drones. Separately, the Trump administration signaled it would not be constrained by a congressional authorization deadline for the US-Israeli war against Iran.

stories.title: Oscar goes missing after Academy Award winner is blocked from taking it on flight
stories.summary: An Academy Award winner was prevented from carrying their Oscar statuette onto a flight, after which the award went missing. The airline issued an apology and launched an urgent internal search for the trophy.

stories.title: HK$1 minimum wage rise unlikely to significantly lift low-paid incomes, experts say
stories.summary: Hong Kong's minimum wage rose by HK$1 (13 US cents) effective May 1, but experts warned the increase is unlikely to significantly boost low-paid workers' incomes. Analysts said the rise broadly aligns with recent pay trends and should help preserve purchasing power under a new formula.

stories.title: Separate cities or shared space? Ministries divided over Negev housing plan for Haredim
stories.summary: Israeli government ministries are divided over plans to build three new cities in the Negev desert for the growing ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) population. The debate centers on whether to create separate Haredi communities or integrated shared spaces, reflecting broader tensions over economics and the future of Haredi life in Israel.

stories.title: Hong Kong slams attempts to sugarcoat Jimmy Lai’s criminal acts in press freedom index
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government condemned the use of a global press freedom index to criticize the jailing of former media owner Jimmy Lai Chee-ying. Authorities accused anti-China forces and foreign media of attempting to sugarcoat Lai's criminal acts and smear the city's press freedom record.

stories.title: New Banksy statue of man blinded by flag draws crowds in London
stories.summary: Street artist Banksy confirmed a new work in central London: a statue of a suited man blindly stepping off a plinth while holding a flag that blocks his view. The piece appeared on Wednesday near Pall Mall and has drawn large crowds.

stories.title: US prosecutors release new footage of Trump shooting suspect
stories.summary: The US Justice Department released previously unseen footage of the Trump shooting incident. Prosecutors presented the footage to demonstrate that the Secret Service agent injured during the attack was not struck by friendly fire.

stories.title: Kurdish militant says Turkey stalled peace talks over reforms
stories.summary: Kurdish militant leader Murat Karayilan accused Turkey of stalling peace negotiations despite steps taken toward a ceasefire. Karayilan said Turkey has failed to advance reforms necessary for the peace process.

stories.title: London assailant charged with attempted murder over terror stabbing of 2 Jews
stories.summary: A man in London has been charged with attempted murder in connection with the antisemitic stabbing of two Jewish individuals in Golders Green. Following the attack, Britain raised its national terrorism threat level from 'substantial' to 'severe.'

stories.title: ISW explains why Putin called Trump
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin used an April 29 phone call with US President Trump to reaffirm his original military objectives in Ukraine. Putin sought to portray Russia's victory as inevitable.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on former Congo President Joseph Kabila
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila. The action was announced on April 30.

stories.title: Israeli group asks high court to order release of Gaza doctors
stories.summary: Israeli rights groups petitioned the high court to order the release of Gaza doctors, alleging Israel is detaining healthcare workers without charge. Hundreds of health workers reportedly remain in Israeli custody.

stories.title: Trump congratulates Zaidi on his nomination to be next Iraqi prime minister
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump congratulated Ali al-Zaidi on his nomination to become Iraq's next prime minister. Trump said he looked forward to a productive new relationship with the incoming Iraqi leader.

stories.title: Condemnation and protests against Israel’s raid of Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Israel intercepted Gaza-bound aid boats in international waters, drawing widespread international condemnation and sparking protests. The raid on the humanitarian flotilla has intensified diplomatic criticism of Israel's actions regarding the blockade of Gaza.

stories.title: US urges meeting between Lebanese president, Israeli PM
stories.summary: The US Embassy in Lebanon urged a meeting between the Lebanese president and Israeli Prime Minister amid ongoing hostilities. Israeli strikes killed 17 people in Lebanon despite a ceasefire being in effect.

stories.title: Israel said bracing for Iran fighting to resume soon, as Trump briefed on military options
stories.summary: Israel is reportedly preparing for a possible resumption of fighting with Iran, with Defense Minister signaling conflict could resume soon. US Central Command has reportedly requested a hypersonic missile be sent to the Middle East. Iran's president condemned the US naval blockade as 'intolerable,' while President Trump was briefed on military options.

stories.title: Trump, Fox News praise UAE decision to leave Opec
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump praised the United Arab Emirates' decision to leave OPEC amid the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. Trump expressed approval of UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed's move, suggesting it could help lower oil prices.

stories.title: Italy condemns 'unlawful' Israeli interception of Gaza flotilla
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned Israel's interception of an aid flotilla bound for the Gaza Strip as "unlawful." Meloni called for the release of Italian nationals who were aboard the vessels.

stories.title: UN climate body presses on after US quits, while China leads with renewables
stories.summary: The UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is continuing its work despite the US government's withdrawal, with IPCC chair Jim Skea noting the US is just one of 195 member countries. China is meanwhile leading in renewable energy development.

stories.title: Some US troops cite benefits of Germany presence as Trump threatens pullback
stories.summary: Germany hosts approximately 35,000 active-duty U.S. military personnel, making it the largest American military footprint in Europe. Some U.S. troops stationed there have highlighted the strategic benefits of the German presence amid President Trump's threats to reduce the deployment.

stories.title: Russian city faces toxic aftermath of refinery attack
stories.summary: Residents of a Russian city were warned to limit outdoor activity and keep windows shut after elevated benzene levels were detected in the air following an attack on a local oil refinery.

stories.title: Georg Baselitz, the German painter who turned postwar art upside down, dies at 88
stories.summary: German painter Georg Baselitz, known for his provocative upside-down compositions that challenged postwar art conventions, has died at the age of 88.

stories.title: US suffered 'disgraceful defeat', Iran’s Supreme Leader says
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei declared that the United States suffered a "disgraceful defeat" in the region, according to a written message broadcast on Iranian state television.

stories.title: Pakistan, 10 other nations condemn Israeli assault on Gaza aid flotilla, 'unlawful detention' of activists
stories.summary: Pakistan, Türkiye, Brazil, Jordan, Spain, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Colombia, Maldives, South Africa, and Libya jointly condemned Israel's assault on the Global Sumud Flotilla. Their foreign ministers called the interception and detention of humanitarian activists in international waters a flagrant violation of international law.

stories.title: Scientology ‘speed running’ trend has LA abuzz and church unhappy
stories.summary: A viral trend of young people rushing Church of Scientology buildings in Los Angeles has drawn large crowds to Hollywood Boulevard. The Church of Scientology said it is "reviewing all available remedies" in response to the so-called speed-running raids.

stories.title: Why governments beyond Hong Kong are wary of prediction markets
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government paused a plan to allow the Hong Kong Jockey Club to offer basketball betting after the rise of prediction markets prompted officials to reassess the regulatory landscape. Governments globally are examining the challenges posed by these online platforms.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Air Force reports efficiency problems: 170 crews report no shootdowns in year
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Force disclosed significant efficiency problems among drone-interceptor crews. Of more than 300 crews, 170 failed to shoot down a single enemy UAV over the past year.

stories.title: Palestinian FA chief blasts Israeli VP at FIFA Congress
stories.summary: Palestinian Football Association chief Jibril Rajoub confronted Israel FA Vice-President Basim Sheikh Suliman at the FIFA Congress. The clash centred on the ongoing war in Gaza.

stories.title: German lawmaker says 'trust in this White House' not the same
stories.summary: German European Parliament member Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann said trust in the current US administration to protect Berlin has diminished. She acknowledged that US troop presence in Germany remains mutually beneficial but expressed concern over President Trump's unpredictability.

stories.title: Lebanon's internal splits over talks with Israel trip up Saudi mediation efforts
stories.summary: Internal divisions among top Lebanese officials are disrupting Saudi Arabia's mediation efforts to help Lebanon present a unified position in historic negotiations with Israel. Lebanese sources and foreign officials told Reuters that the growing rift has complicated diplomatic progress in Beirut.

stories.title: Fema employees who criticized Trump cuts reinstated after months on leave
stories.summary: Fourteen FEMA employees were reinstated after spending eight months on administrative leave for signing a public letter criticizing Trump administration funding cuts. The "Katrina declaration" warned that the cuts left the US dangerously unprepared for natural disasters.

stories.title: ‘Love relay’: lonely China cancer patient orders ‘company’ via food delivery platform
stories.summary: A 24-year-old cancer patient named Little Li in Foshan, Guangdong province, China, ordered "companionship" through a food delivery platform while hospitalized. The story went viral, sparking a widespread outpouring of support online.

stories.title: UAE refers Sudan general and others to court over ammunition shipment for Sudanese army
stories.summary: The UAE referred the chief of staff of Sudan's army along with 12 other defendants and six companies to its State Security Court. The charges relate to an alleged attempt to move ammunition through UAE territory destined for the Sudanese army.

stories.title: US urges Lebanese president to meet Netanyahu, suggests sit-down could lead to IDF pullout
stories.summary: The US Embassy in Lebanon urged Lebanese President to meet Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, suggesting direct engagement could lead to an Israeli military withdrawal. Political leaders in Beirut remain divided over the proposed talks with Jerusalem.

stories.title: Iran ‘dying to make a deal’, US war costs soar: here’s what happened overnight
stories.summary: The US-Israeli war on Iran entered its third month with diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran remaining stalled. President Trump claimed Iran is "dying to make a deal" but acknowledged uncertainty about the Iranian leadership and the status of negotiations.

stories.title: One of Khmelnytskyi NPP power units resumes operation after repairs
stories.summary: A power unit at the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine resumed operation after completing scheduled maintenance that began on April 28.

stories.title: Uganda court sentences man to death for killing four young children at nursery school
stories.summary: A Ugandan court sentenced a man to death on Thursday for killing four young children at a nursery school earlier in April. The attack in the East African country sparked widespread public outrage and heightened concerns about the safety of pupils in schools.

stories.title: Pivotal US-Iran war deadline approaches with no end in sight for conflict
stories.summary: A key U.S. deadline related to the conflict with Iran is approaching, with no resolution in sight. Prospects for ending the war remain highly unlikely.

stories.title: US combatant chiefs want more amphibious ready groups, Marine commandant says
stories.summary: U.S. combatant command leaders have all requested amphibious ready groups and Marine Expeditionary Units, according to the Marine Corps commandant. The demand underscores the continued importance of amphibious capabilities across multiple geographic commands.

stories.title: FIFA head announces no changes to Iran's World Cup schedule as protestors demand team ban
stories.summary: Protesters gathered outside the FIFA Congress in Vancouver demanding Iran's national team be banned from the upcoming World Cup over alleged ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced no changes would be made to Iran's schedule.

stories.title: UK PM Starmer says Jews are scared, promises action after London stabbings
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged action to protect Britain's Jewish community, acknowledging widespread fear following the stabbing of two men in the Golders Green area of north London. The attack followed a series of antisemitic incidents in the capital.

stories.title: Russia bans imports of foreign satellite terminals, including Starlink
stories.summary: Russia has banned the import of foreign satellite communication terminals, including SpaceX's Starlink devices.

stories.title: Key deadline looms in US-Iran war as conflict drags on
stories.summary: A key deadline is approaching in the US-Iran conflict as the war continues. Democrats in Congress are pushing for a war powers vote, while Republican lawmakers continue to support President Trump's approach to the conflict.

stories.title: China scraps tariffs for all but one African nation
stories.summary: China announced the removal of tariffs on imports from all African nations with which it has diplomatic relations, except one. The zero-tariff regime boosts China's soft power on the continent, though analysts warn it may lead to uneven economic gains among African countries.

stories.title: It's not just oil: Iran war also threatens Asia's food security
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran conflict is threatening Asia's food security by disrupting fertilizer supply chains. Chinese restrictions have compounded the problem as planting season begins across the region.

stories.title: Japan survey finds sexual abuse at 15% of hospitals. Is the true scale higher?
stories.summary: A Japanese government survey found that more than 15% of hospitals and long-term care facilities have recorded cases of sexual assault or abuse of patients. The first-of-its-kind survey received responses from 1,113 of 5,000 invited institutions, with many incidents involving psychiatric care staff.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran says US ports siege ‘intolerable’; Trump mulls action
stories.summary: Israeli military strikes on Lebanon have killed at least 2,586 people and wounded more than 8,000 since March 2, according to local media reports.

stories.title: Evening update
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed at least 32 people on Thursday as Israeli ground operations expanded. Air defence systems were activated over Tehran against small drones and surveillance aircraft. The UAE banned travel to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, urging its citizens to leave those countries immediately.

stories.title: Jihadists urge united front against Mali junta as Bamako blockade begins
stories.summary: Jihadist groups in Mali have called for a unified uprising against the ruling military junta, coinciding with a blockade of key roads leading into the capital, Bamako. The escalation follows coordinated attacks on junta positions and raises fears of deepening instability in the conflict-affected country.

stories.title: Russia conducts psychological operation in Kharkiv border region – CCD
stories.summary: Russia's forces are conducting a psychological operation in border areas of Ukraine's Kharkiv region, dropping leaflets from drones that encourage local residents to collaborate, according to Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation.

stories.title: Georg Baselitz, the German painter who turned postwar art upside down, dies at 88
stories.summary: German painter Georg Baselitz, known for his provocative postwar art including his signature upside-down paintings, has died at the age of 88. Baselitz was a major figure in contemporary European art who often challenged conventions of artistic expression.

stories.title: Venice Biennale jury resigns days before start of top art exhibition
stories.summary: The jury for the Venice Biennale resigned days before the opening of the prestigious art exhibition. The resignations followed tensions over Russia's return to the event for the first time since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Man accused in Trump assassination attempt agrees to remain in custody
stories.summary: The man accused of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump at a press gala in Washington agreed on Thursday to remain in custody while his case proceeds. The incident occurred at a black-tie event in the U.S. capital.

stories.title: War update: 109 combat clashes on frontline
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces reported 109 combat clashes with Russian troops along the frontline since the start of the day.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll from Thursday reaches 32, Israeli troops hit
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the town of Harouf in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh district killed one woman and injured three, including a child, bringing Lebanon's 24-hour death toll to 32. Hezbollah said its fighters attacked Israeli forces operating up to 10 kilometers inside Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Top general in West Bank warns ‘Jewish terrorism’ could spark Palestinian uprising — report
stories.summary: Israeli Central Command chief Avi Bluth reportedly warned that settler violence in the West Bank amounts to "Jewish terrorism" and could trigger a Palestinian uprising. Bluth cautioned that Palestinians "won't remain indifferent forever" and said the violence is causing significant damage to Israel.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Mykolaiv again, damage reported in private sector
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the southern Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv again using drones, causing damage to the private residential sector.

stories.title: Trump says Secret Service agent not shot by friendly fire, as attack video is released
stories.summary: President Trump and the Secret Service stated that a federal agent injured during an attack at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner was not hit by friendly fire. Authorities released video footage showing the suspect shooting the officer while rushing through security.

stories.title: 214 robots take the field at US national competition for Jewish schools
stories.summary: The Center for Initiatives in Jewish Education hosted its annual national robotics competition in New York, featuring 214 robots from Jewish schools across the United States. The event highlighted the growing role of STEM programs in Jewish education.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill 9 people, including 2 children
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities reported that Israeli strikes killed nine people, including two children. President Joseph Aoun condemned what he called continuing Israeli violations in southern Lebanon during a meeting with a delegation from the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

stories.title: Amnesty urges Nigeria to investigate deaths in army-run camp, military says report baseless
stories.summary: Amnesty International called on Nigeria to investigate reports that at least 150 people, mostly children, died in an army-run camp in Kwara state. The Nigerian military dismissed the reports as baseless.

stories.title: 13 terrorists killed as bids to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in KP foiled: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) reported that security forces killed 13 Fitna al Khawarij (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) militants during two foiled infiltration attempts along the Pak-Afghan border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Mohmand district. ISPR described the militants as Indian-sponsored terrorists.

stories.title: Dutch authorities evacuate Kempen Airport as wildfires break out near military training areas
stories.summary: Dutch authorities evacuated Kempen Airport in southern Netherlands on Thursday after a large wildfire broke out near a military training area. The blaze is the latest in a series of fires amid exceptionally dry conditions in the country.

stories.title: Graham Platner becomes presumptive Dem. nominee as opponent Janet Mills drops out of race
stories.summary: Graham Platner became the presumptive Democratic nominee for US Senate in Maine after opponent Janet Mills dropped out of the race. His anti-Israel rhetoric and past Nazi tattoo have drawn concern from Jewish organizations.

stories.title: Tony Blair’s thinktank urges Labour to scrap ‘unaffordable’ pension triple lock
stories.summary: The Tony Blair Institute urged the UK Labour government to scrap the state pension triple lock, calling it "unaffordable" amid mounting fiscal pressure partly driven by the Iran war. The thinktank recommended a broader overhaul of the pension system.

stories.title: Under-fire British PM Starmer heckled after Jewish-targeted stabbings
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer was heckled during a visit following a series of knife attacks targeting Jewish communities in the UK. Crowds shouted hostile slogans at the prime minister, reflecting public anger over the government's response.

stories.title: Hong Kong public hospitals to extend time for daily visits from 5 to 9 hours by July 31
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Hospital Authority announced that all rehabilitation and palliative wards in public hospitals will extend daily visiting hours from five to nine hours by July 31. Paediatric wards will also allow round-the-clock visits by the same deadline.

stories.title: Russian archaeologist Butyagin plans to resume illegal excavations in Crimea
stories.summary: Russian archaeologist Alexander Butyagin announced plans to resume the Myrmekion archaeological expedition near Kerch in Russian-occupied Crimea, which Ukraine and international observers consider illegal excavation on occupied territory.

stories.title: U.K. calls antisemitism an emergency as police investigate stabbing attack on 2 Jewish men
stories.summary: British police arrested a 45-year-old man on suspicion of attempted murder after a stabbing attack on two Jewish men in the United Kingdom. Authorities classified the incident as an act of terrorism and are investigating possible motives, including any potential link to Iranian proxies.

stories.title: KP CM Afridi hints at legislation against collateral damage in drone strikes
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi indicated plans to introduce provincial legislation criminalizing collateral damage from drone strikes. The move follows public anger from his constituency and a meeting of district lawmakers who pledged a united effort to protect civilians.

stories.title: US embassy in Beirut says Lebanon is at ‘crossroads’, calls for meeting with Netanyahu
stories.summary: The US embassy in Beirut called for a direct meeting between Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying Lebanon stands at a "crossroads." The embassy stated that US-facilitated engagement between the two countries could begin a "national revival" for Lebanon.

stories.title: Former Spandau Ballet singer jailed for 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual assaults
stories.summary: Former Spandau Ballet singer Ross Davidson, 38, was sentenced to 14 years in prison after being convicted of multiple rapes and sexual assaults. The offences were committed against six women between August 2013 and December 2019 across two separate trials.

stories.title: Ceasefire ‘stops’ War Powers clock on Iran, Hegseth claims
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claimed that a ceasefire pauses the 60-day clock under the War Powers Resolution of 1973, which governs unauthorized military deployments. However, the relevant provisions of the law make no mention of a ceasefire halting the timeline.

stories.title: Medical bus destroyed in Russian attack near Dnipro
stories.summary: A vaccination bus operated by Ukraine's Ministry of Health was destroyed in a Russian strike in the suburbs of Dnipro, belonging to the regional Center for Disease Control and Prevention.

stories.title: Syrian pilot confessions reveal centralized bombing orders during war
stories.summary: Confessions from Syrian pilots revealed that bombing orders during the Syrian war were centralized. Some officers received special trust from the leadership and were assigned intensive bombing missions.

stories.title: Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf look to fire FM Araghchi over allegiance to IRGC commander - report
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf are reportedly seeking to dismiss Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, alleging he has been acting primarily on behalf of IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi rather than the civilian government.

stories.title: Russia conducts first Soyuz-5 rocket launch, Roscosmos says
stories.summary: Russia's space agency Roscosmos announced the first launch of the Soyuz-5 expendable rocket on April 30 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.

stories.title: Iranian media: Iran’s air defence engaging drones over Tehran
stories.summary: Iran's air defense systems engaged small drones and surveillance UAVs over Tehran, according to the Tasnim news agency. Air defense sirens were heard across western, central, and southeastern areas of the Iranian capital.

stories.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum says proof needed after US charges Sinaloa governor for cartel ties
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum responded to U.S. charges against Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha alleging cartel ties, demanding "clear evidence" from Washington. Sheinbaum suggested the charges announced on Wednesday could be politically motivated if proof is not provided.

stories.title: Ukraine builds system to counter Russia's shadow grain fleet – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is developing a system to counter Russia's shadow grain fleet, which is used to circumvent sanctions and export stolen Ukrainian grain.

stories.title: Ukraine builds system to counter Russia's shadow grain fleet – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is developing a system to counter Russia's shadow grain fleet, which has been used to circumvent sanctions on Russian grain exports.

stories.title: US condemns ‘counterproductive’ Gaza aid flotilla seized by Israel
stories.summary: The US State Department condemned the Gaza-bound humanitarian aid flotilla seized by Israeli forces in international waters, calling it a "counterproductive" and "pro-Hamas" stunt. Spokesman Tommy Pigott said the flotilla undermined President Trump's peace plan for Gaza.

stories.title: Anti-Israel oysterman in Maine poised to become Democratic nominee for US Senate
stories.summary: Graham Platner, a Maine oysterman with anti-Israel views and a past Nazi tattoo, is poised to become the Democratic nominee for US Senate after the state's governor ended her campaign. His candidacy has raised concern among Jewish groups.

stories.title: JTS ‘breaks mold,’ names campus innovator Rabbi Mike Uram as next chancellor
stories.summary: The Jewish Theological Seminary named Rabbi Mike Uram as its next chancellor. Uram, who previously served at the Jewish Federations of North America and Penn Hillel, does not hold a doctorate, which is unusual for the Conservative Judaism institution's leadership.

stories.title: Trump in fresh attack on Germany's Merz over Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over his stance on Iran, urging him to stop interfering with efforts to eliminate Iran's nuclear threat. Trump said the campaign would make the world, including Germany, safer.

stories.title: The View From Europe
stories.summary: Belgian Defense Minister Theo Francken discussed topics including U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the Strait of Hormuz, and NATO in a Europe-focused segment.

stories.title: Russia is losing ground first time in 27 months. Ukraine’s drones might be why.
stories.summary: Ukraine appears to be reclaiming territory from Russia for the first time in 27 months. Analysts attribute the shift partly to Ukraine's effective use of mid- and long-range drone strikes against Russian combat units.

stories.title: Attack on Jewish man outside Los Angeles synagogue investigated as hate crime
stories.summary: A Jewish man was attacked outside a Los Angeles synagogue after being followed by a suspect in a car. Authorities are investigating the assault as a hate crime.

stories.title: From apps to autos: China’s data reach sparks US espionage and sabotage concerns
stories.summary: A US congressional advisory committee heard testimony that China has built a state-driven campaign to harvest American data for strategic purposes, including potential use in a conflict over Taiwan. Experts told the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission that Washington is falling short in countering Beijing's data-collection efforts.

stories.title: See you in Beijing: the big shift in Xi’s travel plans and what it means for China
stories.summary: China has significantly reduced overseas state visits by President Xi Jinping, instead hosting a steady stream of foreign leaders in Beijing. Data compiled by the South China Morning Post shows Beijing is prioritizing neighborhood diplomacy and engagement with European middle powers.

stories.title: Defense Ministry purchases 8,000 Octopus interceptor drones for AFU
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense announced the purchase of 8,000 Octopus interceptor drones for the Armed Forces of Ukraine. The drones are intended to strengthen air defense capabilities and increase interception of enemy aerial targets.

stories.title: Defense Ministry purchases 8,000 Octopus interceptor drones for AFU
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense is purchasing 8,000 Octopus interceptor drones to bolster the Armed Forces of Ukraine's air defense capabilities and increase interception rates of enemy aerial targets.

stories.title: Russia rejects Mali rebels' call to withdraw
stories.summary: Russia rejected a call from Malian rebels to withdraw its forces from the country. Moscow's Africa Corps paramilitary unit recently pulled out of a key northern town following rebel attacks that also targeted the capital and killed Mali's defence minister.

stories.title: Palestine FA chief hits out at Israel federation VP at FIFA Congress
stories.summary: At the FIFA Congress in Canada, the Palestine Football Association president confronted the Israel federation vice president. The two delegations had been seated in close proximity at the event.

stories.title: China's FM talks to Rubio, says Taiwan 'biggest risk' in ties
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister spoke with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio ahead of a planned May summit, identifying Taiwan as the "biggest risk" in bilateral relations. Ties between Beijing and Washington have remained relatively stable despite complications from the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Rachel Goldberg-Polin’s memoir about her son's murder tops NYT bestseller list
stories.summary: Rachel Goldberg-Polin's memoir about her son Hersh, who was kidnapped from the Nova Music Festival on October 7, 2023, and later killed in Gaza, reached the top of the New York Times bestseller list.

stories.title: LA police investigating attack on Jewish teacher outside synagogue as hate crime
stories.summary: Los Angeles police are investigating an attack on a 32-year-old Jewish teacher outside the Adas Israel synagogue as a hate crime. No arrests have been made. The synagogue was previously the site of violence during an anti-Israel protest in 2024.

stories.title: Watch: Supreme Court to Centre: Amend law on pregnancy termination | Above the Fold | 30.04.2026
stories.summary: India's Supreme Court directed the central government to amend laws on pregnancy termination. Other major stories included concerns in Kargil over Ladakh's new districts, flooding in Bengaluru from heavy rains, and global tensions surrounding the Iran war.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill four in Gaza, medics say, amid new ceasefire push
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least four Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Thursday, according to health officials. Meanwhile, Hamas leaders met mediators in Cairo to discuss reinvigorating a fragile six-month-old U.S.-brokered truce.

stories.title: U.S. acknowledges Russia is helping Iran in war
stories.summary: General Dan Caine, Head of the US Joint Chiefs of Staff, stated that Russia is providing some degree of assistance to Iran in its war against the United States. The acknowledgment marks a public US recognition of Russian involvement in supporting Tehran during the conflict.

stories.title: U.S. acknowledges Russia is helping Iran in war
stories.summary: U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman General Dan Caine stated that Russia is providing some degree of assistance to Iran in its war with the United States, marking an official U.S. acknowledgment of Russian involvement.

stories.title: EU says troop deployments in Europe 'in U.S. interest'
stories.summary: The European Union argued that U.S. troop deployments in Europe serve American interests, responding to the latest tensions with President Trump. Trump has been critical of European NATO allies over their response to his military action against Iran.

stories.title: UK Green Party candidates arrested following antisemitic posts, posts supporting terror - Telegraph
stories.summary: Several UK Green Party candidates were arrested following antisemitic social media posts and content supporting terrorism, including imagery featuring a Hamas operative with the slogan "resistance is freedom."

stories.title: Only 22% of Israeli 9th graders met English requirements in latest tests, sparking alarm
stories.summary: Recent testing found only 22% of Israeli ninth graders met English proficiency requirements. Results were particularly low at Arabic-speaking schools, where just 9% met standards compared to 27% in Hebrew-speaking schools. A teacher shortage was cited as a contributing factor.

stories.title: Vedomosti reports Russia’s former deputy natural resources minister left for US after resigning
stories.summary: Russian business daily Vedomosti reported that Denis Butsayev, Russia's former deputy minister of natural resources and ecology, left Russia for the United States after resigning from his position a week earlier.

stories.title: US gas reaches $4.30 per gallon; Trump says prices will drop after Iran war
stories.summary: US gasoline prices rose nearly 30 cents in one week to reach $4.30 per gallon, driven by a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and a diplomatic deadlock with Iran. President Trump stated prices would fall after the Iran war concludes.

stories.title: Israeli rights group asks high court to order release of Gaza doctors
stories.summary: An Israeli rights group petitioned the country's high court to order the release of approximately 14 Palestinian doctors from Gaza who have been held without charge for more than a year.

stories.title: 'Clock on diplomacy has not stopped': FO says Pakistan remains actively engaged with Iran, US to resolve conflict
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi stated that Pakistan remains actively engaged with both Iran and the United States to achieve a diplomatic resolution to their conflict. He emphasized that the "clock on diplomacy has not stopped" and expressed hope for a negotiated settlement.

stories.title: UAE bans travel to Iran, Lebanon and Iraq, urges its citizens to leave region
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates banned its citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, citing regional security developments. The UAE foreign ministry also urged citizens already in those countries to leave immediately.

stories.title: Palestinians mourn football loving teenager killed by Israeli army
stories.summary: Mourners in Hebron buried 16-year-old Ibrahim al-Khayatt, a Palestinian teenager who was shot in the chest by Israeli soldiers. The teenager was described as a football enthusiast.

stories.title: Zelensky says Iran war leaves Kyiv hanging for peace talks
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the U.S.-Iran war has left Kyiv waiting for peace talks with Russia. Negotiations between Russia and Ukraine stalled in mid-February.

stories.title: Iran 'will not capitulate', conflict resolution expert says
stories.summary: Iran's supreme leader rejected U.S. President Donald Trump's warning of a prolonged naval blockade, claiming the United States had suffered a defeat. Conflict resolution expert Oliver McTernan told FRANCE 24 that Iran "will not capitulate" and characterized the U.S. actions as a miscalculation.

stories.title: Unrest in Alice Springs after Jefferson Lewis arrested over death of Kumanjayi Little Baby
stories.summary: Unrest erupted in Alice Springs, Australia, after police arrested 47-year-old Jefferson Lewis in connection with the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, who disappeared five days earlier. An angry crowd clashed with police outside the hospital where Lewis was being treated.

stories.title: Russian archaeologist freed in prisoner exchange says he’s grateful his country came to his aid
stories.summary: A Russian archaeologist freed in a prisoner exchange described his detention in Poland, saying he was held with little activity before being transferred. He expressed gratitude for his country's efforts to secure his release but said the European scientific community's response was insufficient.

stories.title: Media reports of explosion near military enlistment office in Bila Tserkva
stories.summary: In Bila Tserkva, Ukraine, a local resident threw a grenade near a Territorial Center for Recruitment and Social Support building, causing an explosion. Media reported the incident near the military enlistment office; further details on casualties were not immediately available.

stories.title: Media reports of explosion near military enlistment office in Bila Tserkva
stories.summary: In Bila Tserkva, Ukraine, a local resident threw a grenade near a Territorial Center for Recruitment and Social Support building, causing an explosion. Media reported the incident near the military enlistment office.

stories.title: Wife of Spain PM Sanchez files assault complaint against far-right influencer
stories.summary: Begoña Gómez, the wife of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, filed an assault complaint against a far-right influencer. Details of the alleged incident were not immediately elaborated upon.

stories.title: Air defence sirens heard in Tehran, Iranian news reports
stories.summary: Iran's Mehr news agency reported that air defense sirens were heard in parts of Tehran. The agency did not specify the cause of the sirens.

stories.title: Israel has higher cost of living than wealthier European nations, study shows
stories.summary: A study by the Aaron Institute for Economic Policy found that Israel's cost of living exceeds that of wealthier European nations. Sharp increases in food and housing prices over the past two decades were identified as the primary drivers.

stories.title: Palestinian journalist released from Israeli prison unrecognisable
stories.summary: Palestinian journalist Ali al-Samoudi was released from Israeli prison showing severe weight loss and signs of torture, appearing unrecognizable to those who knew him.

stories.title: Iran accuses Israel of 'piracy' for seizure of Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry condemned Israel's interception and boarding of the Global Sumud Flotilla, a humanitarian aid convoy headed for Gaza, calling the seizure in international waters an act of piracy. Tehran urged the international community to press for the release of detained activists.

stories.title: Hegseth testifies on Iran war before Senate committee: Key takeaways
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified before a Senate committee alongside a top general for a second consecutive day regarding the war with Iran. The hearings marked the first public Congressional sessions since the conflict began.

stories.title: Migrant boat disaster off Libya kills 17 Sudanese, UN says
stories.summary: The UN refugee agency reported that 17 Sudanese migrants died when their boat capsized near Tobruk, Libya, with nine others still missing.

stories.title: Flotilla activist: Israel’s ‘brutal attack’ will not deter us
stories.summary: Activist Omer Aslan said Israel's interception of 22 boats belonging to the Global Sumud Flotilla late Wednesday would not deter future efforts. Aslan described the Israeli action as a "brutal attack."

stories.title: Oscar belonging to co-director of Putin film missing after TSA makes him ship it
stories.summary: The Oscar statuette belonging to Pavel Talankin, co-director of the documentary "Mr Nobody Against Putin," went missing after TSA agents at New York's JFK airport confiscated it, claiming it could be used as a weapon. Talankin was forced to ship the award rather than carry it onto his flight.

stories.title: Former Welfare Ministry official joins Yashar!, Eisenkot vows post-war trauma rehabilitation plan
stories.summary: Former Israeli Welfare Ministry official Yehezkeli joined the Yashar! organization, while former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot announced a post-war rehabilitation plan addressing trauma among veterans and affected populations.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says he’s seeking details of Putin’s May 9 ceasefire proposal
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated he is seeking more details about a short-term ceasefire proposal made by Russia to U.S. President Donald Trump. The proposal was linked to the May 9 date, a significant holiday in Russia.

stories.title: US Congress passes short-term renewal of Fisa warrantless spying powers
stories.summary: The US Congress passed a 45-day extension of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which grants intelligence agencies warrantless spying powers. Republican infighting over reform provisions has repeatedly blocked longer-term renewal efforts.

stories.title: Starmer’s sister-in-law feared what might have happened in arson attack, court hears
stories.summary: Three men with links to Ukraine are on trial for alleged arson attacks on properties connected to UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. His sister-in-law Judith Alexander testified about an attack on a house in Kentish Town, saying she feared what could have happened had she not woken up. The defendants deny all charges.

stories.title: Belgium joins Special Tribunal for Russia’s crime of aggression against Ukraine
stories.summary: Belgium announced it will join the Special Tribunal established to prosecute the crime of aggression committed by Russia against Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump: US ‘might’ restart war with Iran, ‘probably’ will withdraw troops from Italy and Spain
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said from the Oval Office that Iran "wants to make a deal" but that he did not know whether the U.S. would resume hostilities following the ceasefire. He also suggested the U.S. would "probably" withdraw troops from Italy and Spain.

stories.title: Gianni Infantino confirms Iran World Cup participation
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed that Iran will participate in the upcoming World Cup, emphasizing football's role in promoting unity among nations.

stories.title: Report: Russian police arrest 16 men over queer dating group on Russian social network VK, charging them with ‘extremism’
stories.summary: Police in Russia's Karachay-Cherkessia republic arrested at least 16 men connected to a queer dating group on the social network VK. They face criminal charges of organizing the activities of an extremist organization, according to the human rights group SK SOS.

stories.title: Mali pays tribute to Defence Minister Sadio Camara
stories.summary: Mali held a tribute for Defence Minister Sadio Camara, who was killed the previous weekend. Details surrounding his death were not elaborated in the broadcast, which also covered other international stories.

stories.title: How is Israel replicating its Gaza tactics in Lebanon?
stories.summary: Israeli forces have carried out widespread attacks on civilian targets in Lebanon, employing tactics observers say mirror those previously used in Gaza.

stories.title: Trump says Iran can play at World Cup in US after FIFA confirmation
stories.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed that Iran will play its scheduled World Cup matches. US President Trump subsequently agreed, stating Iran can participate in the tournament being hosted in the United States.

stories.title: Navy, Marine Corps weighing force generation model revamp for amphibs
stories.summary: U.S. Navy and Marine Corps leaders are considering overhauling the 36-month Optimized Fleet Response Plan for amphibious ships. The proposed change would implement a longer cycle accommodating two deployments per vessel.

stories.title: Trump says ‘probably’ when asked if he might pull US troops out of Italy, Spain
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said "probably" when asked about potentially withdrawing U.S. troops from Italy and Spain. The remark followed his announcement the previous day that Washington was considering reducing American military personnel in Germany.

stories.title: Lebanon’s internal splits over talks with Israel trip up Saudi mediation efforts
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's envoy visited Beirut to mediate between Lebanese factions on negotiations with Israel, but internal divisions between Lebanon's president and Hezbollah-allied parliament speaker Nabih Berri hampered the effort.

stories.title: Deadline approaches for Trump to secure Congressional approval for Iran war
stories.summary: The Trump administration faces a May 1 deadline to obtain congressional authorization for continuing military operations in Iran under the War Powers Act's 60-day limit. The White House may argue that a recent truce reset the legal clock.

stories.title: Brazil MPs slash Bolsonaro prison term in blow to Lula
stories.summary: Brazil's conservative-majority Congress overrode President Lula da Silva's veto of legislation that significantly reduces former President Jair Bolsonaro's 27-year prison sentence for coup plotting. The vote marked Lula's second major legislative defeat in two days.

stories.title: Senate vote leaves Cuba’s uncertain future at dangerous crossroads
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate voted 51–47 to block a Democratic-led war powers resolution on Cuba, leaving President Trump's authority over Cuba policy largely unchecked. The vote reflects Congress's continued difficulty in asserting war powers oversight regarding the island.

stories.title: US senator raises ‘serious constitutional concerns’ about war in Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Tim Kaine raised constitutional concerns that the Trump administration may exceed the 60-day limit for military action in Iran without congressional approval under the 1973 War Powers Act. The deadline was set to expire on Friday.

stories.title: The InSight Take: Rubén Rocha Moya’s Alleged Sinaloa Cartel Ties Highlight Criminal Governance in Mexico
stories.summary: U.S. prosecutors have indicted Sinaloa state Governor Rubén Rocha Moya for alleged ties to the Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel. The indictment outlines what prosecutors describe as a system of criminal governance in the Mexican state.

stories.title: Iraqi PM-designate says Trump invited him to US once govt formed
stories.summary: Iraqi prime minister-designate Ali al-Zaidi said U.S. President Donald Trump invited him to visit Washington once a new Iraqi government is formed, signaling a potential strengthening of U.S.-Iraq relations.

stories.title: Leader of Iran's Jewish community pledges allegiance to Mojtaba Khamenei
stories.summary: The leader of Iran's Jewish community publicly pledged allegiance to Mojtaba Khamenei. Iran's Jewish population, though a fraction of its pre-1979 size, remains the largest Jewish community in the Middle East outside Israel.

stories.title: Iran’s supreme leader tells US its only place in Persian Gulf is at ‘bottom of its waters’
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei declared the United States defeated in its war against Iran and said America's only place in the Persian Gulf was "at the bottom of its waters." The statement was released to mark Iran's annual Persian Gulf Day.

stories.title: Ukrainian General Staff confirms strikes on Russia’s Orsknefteorgsintez plant and two helicopters
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on April 29–30 targeting Russia's Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery and other key military and infrastructure targets, as well as the destruction of two Russian helicopters.

stories.title: Pacific Marines will be first to test-drive new pilot-optional helicopter
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps' Pacific forces will be the first to test the Aerial Logistics Connector, a new pilot-optional helicopter. The service is targeting an operational demonstration in 2027.

stories.title: Zack Polanski’s criticism of Golders Green attack arrest will have ‘chilling effect’, says Met chief
stories.summary: Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley criticized Green Party leader Zack Polanski for sharing a post about the arrest of a terror suspect in Golders Green, north-west London. A 45-year-old man was arrested after two Jewish people were stabbed; officers used a stun gun to subdue him.

stories.title: RSF condemns ‘kidnapping’ of three journalists on board Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders condemned the detention of journalists aboard the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla, including Al Jazeera correspondent Hafed Mribah and cameraman Mahmut Yavuz, describing the incident as a kidnapping.

stories.title: Spain PM condemns Israel ‘assaulting a civilian flotilla’ bound for Gaza
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez accused Israel of violating international law by detaining civilians aboard an aid flotilla headed for Gaza in international waters. Sanchez called on the EU to immediately suspend its association agreement with Israel. Germany and Italy also condemned the Israeli action.

stories.title: Cost of Iran war equals aid for more than 87m people: UN chief
stories.summary: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher stated that spending on the Iran war is equivalent to the cost of providing aid to more than 87 million people, warning that millions face hunger without urgent humanitarian funding.

stories.title: Scared and angry British Jews demand more from government after knife attack
stories.summary: British Jews in the north London suburb of Golders Green expressed fear and anger at the government following a knife attack in which two men were stabbed in the street. Some community members questioned whether they should leave the country.

stories.title: Arif Habib-led consortium notifies Privatisation Commission of its intent to acquire remaining 25pc PIA stake
stories.summary: The Arif Habib Corporation-led consortium has notified Pakistan's Privatisation Commission of its intent to acquire the remaining 25 percent stake in Pakistan International Airlines. The total private-sector investment is expected to reach approximately Rs180 billion, including Rs55 billion in divestment proceeds to the government and Rs125 billion in fresh equity.

stories.title: “The voice of her generation” — Marina Er Gorbach takes SEEfest 2026 Legacy Award
stories.summary: Ukrainian director Marina Er Gorbach received the South East European Film Festival's 2026 Legacy Award in Los Angeles, recognized as a leading voice of her generation.

stories.title: Deadly Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon killed at least nine people, including two children, according to Lebanon's health ministry, despite an existing ceasefire between the two sides.

stories.title: Iran may run out of oil storage within weeks under US blockade pressure
stories.summary: Iran faces the prospect of running out of oil storage capacity within weeks due to the U.S. naval blockade of its ports. Tehran has been forced to store extracted oil using onshore facilities and floating storage aboard vessels.

stories.title: US Congress passes bill to resume funding for DHS and end partial shutdown
stories.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives passed a funding bill to reopen the Department of Homeland Security and end a partial government shutdown that had left many federal workers without pay. The measure excluded funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

stories.title: Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil assets hit four-month high – Bloomberg
stories.summary: According to Bloomberg, Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil infrastructure reached a four-month high, marking the most intense monthly level of strikes since December of the previous year.

stories.title: European Parliament backs establishment of a special tribunal for Russia
stories.summary: The European Parliament voted to support the establishment of a special tribunal to prosecute Russian officials for crimes related to the war in Ukraine, naming the State Duma and Constitutional Court among bodies that should face prosecution.

stories.title: Wife of Spain’s PM Sanchez files assault complaint against far-right influencer
stories.summary: The wife of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, Begoña Gómez, filed an assault complaint against a far-right influencer who had approached her to question her about a corruption case.

stories.title: UAE refers Sudan arms shipment suspects to State Security Court
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates referred 13 suspects and six companies to its State Security Court over allegations of unauthorized ammunition transfers to Sudan's army, according to the UAE state news agency WAM.

stories.title: Senate Republicans again block effort to halt Trump’s war in Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate voted 47–50 to block a Democratic war powers resolution aimed at limiting President Trump's military operations in Iran. Republican Senators Susan Collins and Rand Paul broke with their party to support the measure, while Democrat John Fetterman opposed it.

stories.title: Iranian economic collapse may come too late for Trump
stories.summary: An analysis suggests that Iran's economic collapse under U.S. pressure may not produce swift concessions, and that President Trump may face a prolonged standoff if he expects Tehran to capitulate first.

stories.title: Partial US government shutdown ends after Congress votes to fund DHS
stories.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives passed a bipartisan measure to fund much of the Department of Homeland Security, excluding immigration enforcement, ending a 75-day partial government shutdown. The deal covers agencies including the Secret Service and TSA.

stories.title: Donald Trump backs proposal to rename ICE as ‘NICE’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump expressed support for renaming Immigration and Customs Enforcement from ICE to "NICE." The proposal originated as a social media joke but gained traction amid ongoing scrutiny of ICE's operations and a record-high number of detainee deaths in custody.

stories.title: Freshly transferred Justices Sattar, Kayani to hear cases at PHC, LHC from coming week
stories.summary: Pakistan's Justices Babar Sattar and Mohsin Akhtar Kayani will begin hearing cases at the Peshawar High Court and Lahore High Court, respectively, following their transfers from the Islamabad High Court. The transfers, approved by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan on April 28, drew criticism from lawyers' bodies.

stories.title: Belgium plans to nationalise nuclear power plants
stories.summary: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever announced plans to nationalize the country's nuclear power plants, citing the need to reduce dependence on fossil fuel imports and increase control over domestic energy supply.

stories.title: On the way to Israel, stop at City of Dreams Mediterranean
stories.summary: Cyprus, located about 40 minutes by air from Tel Aviv, is being promoted as a travel stopover for visitors heading to Israel. The island is positioned as offering proximity to the region without its intensity.

stories.title: Germany says 'prepared' for any US troop reduction
stories.summary: Germany said it is prepared for a potential reduction of U.S. troops after President Trump suggested redeploying some of the tens of thousands of American military personnel stationed there. The threat came amid a dispute between Trump and Chancellor Friedrich Merz over the war in Iran.

stories.title: Jury of Italy's Venice Biennale resigns over Russia row
stories.summary: The international jury of the Venice Biennale resigned days before the contemporary art fair's opening. While no official reason was given, the resignations followed the Italian government's opposition to Russia's participation in the event.

stories.title: Italy condemns 'unlawful' Israeli interception of Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Italy condemned Israel's seizure of aid ships bound for Gaza as unlawful, with Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's office demanding the immediate release of all detained Italian nationals.

stories.title: Trump, Fox News praise UAE decision to leave Opec
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump praised the United Arab Emirates' decision to leave OPEC, calling it a positive move. Trump expressed approval of UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed's decision amid tensions linked to the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Israel says detained Gaza flotilla activists to be taken to Greece
stories.summary: Israel announced that dozens of activists intercepted from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla in international waters near Crete would be transported to Greece for disembarkation.

stories.title: Trump, Fox News praise UAE decision to leave Opec
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Fox News praised the UAE's decision to leave OPEC. Analysts suggested the move would reduce Saudi Arabia's influence over UAE oil policy.

stories.title: Zaporizhzhia NPP loses external power — again. Fifteenth blackout since the full-scale invasion
stories.summary: The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine lost external power for the fifteenth time since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion. A drone strike on Monday killed one person in a workshop near the facility, prompting IAEA chief Grossi to warn of dangers from military activity near nuclear sites.

stories.title: Iran War Nears 60-Day War Powers Deadline
stories.summary: The U.S. conflict with Iran is approaching the 60-day deadline under the War Powers Resolution. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has argued that the current ceasefire has paused the statutory clock, a claim disputed by some lawmakers.

stories.title: Mexico’s Sheinbaum questions US claims of drug ties to Sinaloa governor
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum questioned U.S. allegations against Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha after U.S. prosecutors unsealed an indictment charging Rocha and nine others with ties to the Sinaloa cartel.

stories.title: Economic Fury and Claims of Victory
stories.summary: The United States and Iran have shifted from open hostilities to unsuccessful negotiations and economic pressure since a ceasefire took effect three weeks ago. The Trump administration is pursuing a dual strategy of a naval blockade on Iran's maritime trade and expanded sanctions targeting its oil and banking sectors.

stories.title: UN chief: Cost of Iran war could have funded aid for 87 million people
stories.summary: UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher told AFP that the estimated $25 billion the U.S. has spent on the war in Iran could have funded the UN's entire 2026 humanitarian plan, providing life-saving aid to 87 million people. The UN has so far received only 28 percent of its proposed $23 billion funding for this year.

stories.title: Jury of Italy’s Venice Biennale resigns after demanding Israel, Russia be excluded
stories.summary: The five-member jury of the Venice Biennale international art exhibition resigned after the organization rejected their demand to exclude works from Israel and Russia, whose leaders face International Criminal Court arrest warrants.

stories.title: Detained Gaza-bound flotilla members will be transferred to Greece, Sa’ar says
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced that detained members of the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla would be transferred to Greece. Israel said the IDF intercepted the flotilla near Crete after it allegedly tried to block an Israeli merchant vessel. Several European nations condemned the pre-dawn seizure.

stories.title: British white supremacist found guilty of plotting gun attack
stories.summary: A British white supremacist who idolized Adolf Hitler was convicted in London of preparing terrorist acts after attempting to purchase a gun and ammunition from undercover officers.

stories.title: US troop withdrawal from Germany would be 'foolish', expert says
stories.summary: Security expert Dafydd Townley of the University of Portsmouth called President Trump's renewed threat to withdraw U.S. troops from Germany "foolish," citing Germany's critical role as a logistical and refueling hub for American air force operations within NATO.

stories.title: ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’: Israel rolls out red carpet as Tel Aviv hosts early premiere
stories.summary: Tel Aviv hosted an early premiere of "The Devil Wears Prada 2" ahead of the film's U.S. release, drawing celebrities and creatives in the weeks following the war.

stories.title: Air Force seeks to scrap its E-11 BACN fleet
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force plans to retire its fleet of seven E-11 BACN airborne communications relay aircraft. The service intends to replace their capability with the emerging Department of the Air Force Battle Network system.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Kherson region leave one person killed, six injured
stories.summary: Russian shelling attacks across the Kherson region of Ukraine killed one person and injured six others throughout the day. The strikes targeted multiple locations in the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Finance ministry flags risk to Pakistan's external sector amid global uncertainty
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ministry of Finance warned that the country's external sector faces risks from global uncertainties and the ongoing Middle East conflict, despite a healthy domestic primary balance of 3.3 percent of GDP. The warning appeared in the ministry's Monthly Economic Update and Outlook for April 2026.

stories.title: Israeli commander says troops are 10km into Lebanon and 'do not intend to pull back'
stories.summary: Israeli Northern Command chief Raf Milo announced that Israeli forces have advanced 10 kilometers into southern Lebanon and do not intend to withdraw. He said troops are clearing an area encompassing 60 Lebanese villages and described the operation as ongoing.

stories.title: ‘A new chapter’: first commercial fight from US since 2019 lands in Venezuela
stories.summary: The first direct commercial flight between the United States and Venezuela since 2019 landed in Caracas. The resumption follows the U.S. special forces capture of President Nicolás Maduro roughly four months earlier, with officials on both sides hailing improved diplomatic ties.

stories.title: Iran confirmed to play at World Cup according to FIFA chief Infantino
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed that Iran will participate in the 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by the United States. Iran's inclusion had been uncertain amid the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Lebanon’s divisions over Israel talks hinder Saudi mediation
stories.summary: Internal political divisions within Lebanon have complicated Saudi Arabia's efforts to mediate a unified Lebanese position for negotiations with Israel.

stories.title: Lebanon political rifts derail Saudi-Israel mediation push
stories.summary: Internal political divisions in Lebanon have reportedly stalled a Saudi-led mediation effort with Israel. Saudi Arabia has warned against rushing into any agreements amid the ongoing diplomatic impasse.

stories.title: Venice Biennale jury walks out in full — Russia and Israel return to award contention
stories.summary: The entire international jury of the Venice Biennale resigned on April 30, 2026, over a dispute about including works from Russia and Israel, whose leaders face ICC arrest warrants. Ticket-holders will now take over voting on awards.

stories.title: Fifa chief says Iran will play in World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed at the FIFA Congress in Vancouver that Iran will participate in the 2026 World Cup and play matches in the United States despite the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Kosovo to hold snap elections in June
stories.summary: Kosovo will hold snap parliamentary elections in June, its third vote in roughly eighteen months. Prime Minister Albin Kurti formed a government in February, but a political deadlock over the presidential election triggered the new vote.

stories.title: Ukraine’s USFs strike facilities of key Russian drone developer
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, specifically the Raid regiment, struck facilities belonging to the Russian Special Purpose Center Bars-Sarmat. The targeted complex is located in temporarily occupied areas of the Zaporizhzhia region along the Sea of Azov coast.

stories.title: Piracy rises off Somalia as US-Israeli war on Iran diverts naval forces
stories.summary: Piracy incidents have increased off the coast of Somalia as naval forces have been diverted to the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. More than a dozen sailors, mostly Pakistani nationals, are currently being held by Somali pirates.

stories.title: Amazon says damaged UAE cloud region recovery to take several months
stories.summary: Amazon reported that restoring its cloud computing operations in the United Arab Emirates will take several months after Iranian retaliatory drone strikes damaged data centres in early March. The disruption affected Amazon Web Services, the world's largest cloud provider.

stories.title: Italy condemns ‘unlawful’ Israeli raid of Gaza-bound aid ships
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's office condemned Israel's interception of aid ships bound for Gaza as unlawful and demanded the release of detained Italian citizens. Germany and Italy issued a joint statement urging respect for international law. Israel confirmed arresting approximately 175 activists from at least 20 ships in international waters.

stories.title: Russia’s windfall from the Iran war is temporary. Ukraine’s isn’t.
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Russia's economic and strategic gains from the Iran conflict are temporary, while Ukraine has secured more lasting advantages. Author Artur Kalandarov contends that Kyiv, unlike Moscow, has leveraged the war to obtain durable strategic benefits.

stories.title: Syria government confirms detention of missing German journalist
stories.summary: Syria's government confirmed the detention of German journalist Eva Maria Michelmann, who had been missing since January in the city of Raqqa. Press freedom organizations have called for her immediate release.

stories.title: Camp Mystic halts summer reopening after Texas flood deaths
stories.summary: Camp Mystic in Texas suspended plans to reopen for the summer following the deaths of 27 young campers in a July 4 flood. The decision came amid intensifying pressure from Texas lawmakers and victims' families as investigations into the camp's disaster response continue.

stories.title: What Is Behind Russia’s Pared-Back WWII Victory Day Parade?
