stories.summary: Two deadly stabbing incidents in Jewish cities in Israel prompted a swift government response, drawing criticism from Arab citizens who say authorities have long neglected a crime wave affecting their communities.

stories.title: US intervention forces end to decade of statistical opacity at Venezuela's Central Bank
stories.summary: Venezuela's Central Bank has begun publishing economic indicators withheld for at least a decade, following the U.S. military intervention that led to the capture of former president Nicolás Maduro on January 3. Newly released data showed monthly inflation reached 32 per cent in January before declining to 13.1 per cent in March.

stories.title: Russia’s role in Mali questioned as rebels push for exit
stories.summary: Rebel groups in Mali have called for the withdrawal of Russian forces, with a pullback from the northern city of Kidal highlighting growing pressure on Moscow's Sahel presence. Analysts note this reflects a broader questioning of Russia's military role across the region despite Moscow's claims of success.

stories.title: White House quiet as China ramps up trade leverage before Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: The White House has remained unusually quiet as China increases its trade leverage ahead of a planned summit between President Trump and President Xi. Observers noted the Trump administration's response has been uncharacteristically muted.

stories.title: Deadly migration route leaves Horn of Africa migrants stranded
stories.summary: Migrants from the Horn of Africa, primarily Ethiopia, are returning to Djibouti after failed attempts to cross the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait to reach Gulf countries. More than 900 deaths were recorded on this route in 2025, making it the deadliest year on record.

stories.title: Viral pro-Iran AI memes blur lines between propaganda and entertainment
stories.summary: Iranian-American creator Mahdi Hemmat is generating millions of views with AI-generated, Lego-style rap videos that promote pro-Iran narratives and criticize President Trump amid the U.S.-Iran-Israel conflict. The content illustrates how digital creators are using entertainment formats to shape political opinion among younger Western audiences.

stories.title: Tai Po fire: tendering system can’t stop firms manipulating market, inquiry hears
stories.summary: A public inquiry into Hong Kong's deadly Tai Po fire heard that the official tendering system cannot prevent engineering firms from colluding to manipulate the building maintenance market. Three Urban Renewal Authority officials testified that the statutory body lacked the capacity to combat bid-rigging.

stories.title: Why are Western feminists silent on the war on Iranian women?
stories.summary: Western feminist organizations that previously supported Iranian women protesting compulsory hijab laws have been largely silent as Iranian women are reportedly being killed amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: China’s Tiangong space station to double in size as Nasa phases out ISS
stories.summary: China confirmed plans to expand its Tiangong space station, potentially more than doubling its size to accommodate growing scientific demand and international cooperation. The expansion comes as NASA prepares to retire the International Space Station in early 2031.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit unlikely to revive Chinese investment in US, report warns
stories.summary: A Rhodium Group report warns that Chinese foreign direct investment in the United States is unlikely to recover significantly even if Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump reach a deal at their planned Beijing summit. Chinese FDI in the U.S. has remained at low levels since collapsing from its 2016 peak.

stories.title: Telegraph and Politico owner says journalists must support Israel or resign
stories.summary: Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner told staff at Politico and the Telegraph that supporting Israel is a core value of employment at the outlets and that journalists unwilling to comply should resign. The remarks prompted concerns about editorial independence.

stories.title: DR Congo creates paramilitary mining guard
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo announced the creation of a paramilitary mining guard backed by U.S. and UAE funding. The force is expected to grow to over 20,000 personnel by 2028 to secure mining operations and strengthen state control over critical mineral resources.

stories.title: Spectator owner’s son calls for mine-laden ‘floating wall’ to stop Channel crossings
stories.summary: Winston Marshall, son of Spectator owner Paul Marshall and a former member of Mumford & Sons, proposed constructing a mine-laden "floating wall" in the English Channel to stop small boat crossings. He described those crossing as economic migrants rather than refugees.

stories.title: Russians shell Donetsk region over 1,400 times in one day, leaving one killed, several injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out over 1,400 shelling attacks in Ukraine's Donetsk region in a single day, damaging 21 civilian structures. One person was killed and three were injured.

stories.title: $25bn or $1 trillion: How much has Iran war really cost the US?
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers clashed on Capitol Hill over the true cost of the war with Iran, with estimates ranging from $25 billion to $1 trillion, highlighting concerns about a lack of transparency in military spending.

stories.title: Israel says intercepted 175 Gaza flotilla activists on 20 boats
stories.summary: Israel's Foreign Ministry confirmed it intercepted approximately 175 activists from more than 20 boats attempting to deliver aid to Gaza. The activists were taken aboard an Israeli navy vessel and transported to Israel.

stories.title: World’s top media outlets urge Israel to allow independent access to Gaza
stories.summary: Major international media organizations have called on Israel to grant independent journalists access to the Gaza Strip. Israel continues to block foreign reporters from entering the territory despite a ceasefire being in place.

stories.title: Army requests funds to speed development, production of EW systems
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's fiscal year 2027 budget request includes funding to accelerate the development and production of electronic warfare and signals intelligence systems, enabling faster fielding and continued experimentation.

stories.title: UK police arrest 'mahdi' claimant's followers over rape claims
stories.summary: British police deployed hundreds of officers in raids on properties in Crewe, Cheshire, linked to the Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light. The operation targeted followers of a self-proclaimed mahdi over rape allegations.

stories.title: Rwanda: Who Is Eligible for Rwanda's $100m SME Fund?
stories.summary: Rwanda announced a $100 million fund for small and medium enterprises, offering eligible SMEs a grace period of up to 24 months to stabilize and expand their operations.

stories.title: Israel kills nine people in southern Lebanon despite ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed nine people in southern Lebanon despite an active ceasefire agreement. The Lebanese government condemned the attacks as violations of the ceasefire terms.

stories.title: US weighs training Lebanese army unit to disarm Hezbollah
stories.summary: The United States is considering a plan to arm and train Lebanese army units to disarm Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. The initiative comes as Israeli military strikes in the region continue to escalate.

stories.title: South Africa: March and March Anti-Immigrant Protest Ends in Chaos
stories.summary: An anti-immigrant protest march in South Africa descended into chaos after demonstrators deviated from the agreed route and attacked immigrants.

stories.title: Shahed drones begin maneuvering when interceptor drones approach — 'Flash'
stories.summary: Russian Shahed-type drones have begun performing evasive maneuvers when approached by Ukrainian interceptor drones. The behavioral change is attributed to the likely installation of cameras on the Shahed drones, enabling real-time threat detection.

stories.title: Russia has given Iran something more important than weapons
stories.summary: Russia has provided Iran with significant political backing and diplomatic support opposing escalation, which analysts say has been more consequential in shaping the conflict than weapons transfers.

stories.title: South Africa: Mthatha Residents Block N2 Over Water Crisis
stories.summary: Residents of Mthatha, South Africa, blocked the N2 highway to protest a prolonged water crisis. Locals reported going months without access to running water.

stories.title: Iran's leader accuses US of driving Middle East insecurity, defends Iran’s military capabilities
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei accused the United States of driving instability across the Middle East, citing the presence of US military bases in the Persian Gulf region. He also defended Iran's military capabilities amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: African oil producers defend need to drill at fossil fuel exit talks
stories.summary: Oil-producing African nations at fossil fuel phaseout talks in Colombia stated they would continue drilling to support economic growth, underscoring tensions between climate commitments and the fiscal needs of developing producers.

stories.title: Hong Kong homebuyers flock to new launches as flats sell out swiftly
stories.summary: Hong Kong homebuyers purchased most newly released residential units on Thursday, with all 120 flats at One Victoria Cove I in Hung Hom selling out. Developers are ramping up new construction launches amid sustained housing demand.

stories.title: Mali: Mali Junta Leader to Attend Funeral of Defence Minister Killed in Rebel Attacks
stories.summary: Mali's junta leader Assimi Goïta is expected to attend the funeral of Defence Minister Sadio Camara, who was killed in a rebel assault on his home. The attacks have destabilised the military government's hold on power.

stories.title: 'Next Iran'?: Turkey accelerates 60,000-tonne aircraft carrier amid Israel tensions
stories.summary: Turkey is accelerating construction of a 60,000-tonne aircraft carrier amid rising tensions with Israel. As Israel compares Turkey to Iran and strengthens ties with Greece and Cyprus, Ankara is investing in naval power to reassert its regional position.

stories.title: 'Next Iran'?: Turkey accelerates 60,000 tonnes aircraft carrier amid Israel tensions
stories.summary: Turkey is accelerating construction of a 60,000-tonne aircraft carrier as tensions with Israel escalate. The move comes as Israel strengthens ties with Greece and Cyprus, and Ankara seeks to reassert its naval power in the region.

stories.title: A world adrift looks to China for institutional anchors. Enter Hong Kong
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Hong Kong could serve as an institutional anchor amid growing strain on the international order, as unilateralism and protectionism erode confidence in rules-based global frameworks.

stories.title: South Africa: Ramaphosa Picks 4 November for Local Government Elections
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa announced 4 November as the date for local government elections during a meeting with mayors and premiers at the Birchwood Hotel in Ekurhuleni. Voters will elect representatives to councils across the country.

stories.title: Pakistan’s IMF-backed recovery under pressure as US-Iran mediation stalls
stories.summary: Pakistan's efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran have placed Islamabad near the centre of Middle East diplomacy, but the ongoing conflict is straining its fragile economy. Soaring oil prices and disrupted Strait of Hormuz flows are hitting Pakistan especially hard given its thin foreign exchange reserves.

stories.title: US seeks new coalition to get ships moving again in Strait of Hormuz, internal cable says
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department and Pentagon are jointly seeking to build a new international coalition to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to an internal diplomatic cable. The initiative aims to address disruptions caused by the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'My Enemies Want Me Out Using Insecurity' - Tinubu
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu characterised the country's rising insecurity as a politically motivated tool wielded by his opponents. He framed the violence as being weaponised against his administration rather than solely a national security challenge.

stories.title: Two months on, Qatar gas disruption jolts global supply
stories.summary: Two months after disruptions to Qatar's gas exports, the crisis is raising questions about global energy supply stability. Doha's financial reserves have helped it absorb the economic shock so far.

stories.title: Russia’s close ally now has enough nuclear warheads and delivery systems to breach US missile defense
stories.summary: North Korea, a close Russian ally, is reported to possess enough nuclear warheads and delivery systems to potentially breach U.S. missile defense capabilities.

stories.title: 'How are we going to get back home?' Islamist group tightens blockade on Mali capital
stories.summary: An Islamist group has tightened its blockade around Mali's capital, disrupting movement and supplies. The escalation follows the recent assassination of Mali's defense minister in a series of nationwide attacks.

stories.title: Russians attack Dnipropetrovsk region, leaving one killed, four injured
stories.summary: A Russian attack on the Dnipro district in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region killed one person and wounded four others.

stories.title: Tariffs on digital displays could help avoid US military dependence on China, policy group says
stories.summary: A US policy group argued that tariffs on digital displays could reduce American military dependence on Chinese technology. President Trump previously signed legislation requiring the Pentagon to plan for ending reliance on adversary-sourced technology by 2027.

stories.title: An Ayatollah for the Aggrieved
stories.summary: An analysis examines why Iran's Supreme Leader continues to draw support from Sunni admirers despite sectarian divisions, arguing that Iran's stance of resistance against Western powers remains the primary appeal.

stories.title: Israel intercepts and detains crews of Gaza aid flotilla near Crete
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted at least 22 boats from the Global Sumud Flotilla near the Greek island of Crete and detained their crews. The flotilla of approximately 58 vessels carrying people from 70 countries had departed from Italy to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza in an attempt to break Israel's maritime blockade.

stories.title: Nations urged to 'go further' as fossil fuel exit talks wrap up in Colombia
stories.summary: Fossil fuel exit negotiations concluded in Colombia, with participants urging nations to accelerate their transition away from fossil fuels. The push gained momentum as the war on Iran triggered a global energy crisis.

stories.title: Israeli maps outline expanded zone of military control in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel has quietly published new maps showing an expanded restricted military zone in Gaza, effectively placing at least 64 percent of the territory under Israeli military control.

stories.title: Iran says ‘new chapter’ in Strait of Hormuz after US ‘shameful failure’
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei declared a 'new chapter' in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming a shift in the strategic balance following what he called America's 'shameful failure' in its military campaign in the region.

stories.title: Ship Ukraine says carries stolen grain will not offload in Israel after diplomatic row
stories.summary: A ship that Ukraine alleges was carrying grain stolen from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory will not offload its cargo in Israel following a diplomatic dispute. An Israeli official said the decision was made by the importer, not the government.

stories.title: Israel just quintupled its PR budget to $730 million; experts say it won’t work
stories.summary: Israel increased its public relations budget fivefold to $730 million. Experts expressed skepticism that the spending would significantly improve the country's international image given ongoing government policies.

stories.title: Soaring fuel prices in Pakistan threaten economic and political crises
stories.summary: Pakistan's monthly fuel import bill surged from $300 million to $800 million, placing severe strain on the country's economy and raising concerns about potential political instability.

stories.title: Uncovering Roots podcast: Israel's Paraguay scheme exposed
stories.summary: A podcast investigation examines a scheme linked to Israel involving Paraguay, exploring its impact on victims and the lasting trauma they have carried for decades.

stories.title: Report: United Russia sets turnout targets for party primaries, mobilizes public-sector workers to meet them
stories.summary: Russia's ruling United Russia party and the Kremlin's political bloc have set turnout targets exceeding 10% of voters for upcoming party primaries. Regional administrations are reportedly mobilizing public-sector and state-company workers to meet these targets ahead of the State Duma campaign. Russians have complained on social media about being coerced into participating.

stories.title: Russians attempting to break through to Kupiansk from two directions – military
stories.summary: Russian forces are attempting to advance toward the city of Kupiansk in Ukraine's Kharkiv region from both banks of the Oskil River. Ukrainian military officials reported the dual-axis offensive aimed at breaking through to the strategically important town.

stories.title: Africa: Amine Laghidi, the First Moroccan and African to be Awarded a Prize at the Trieste Summit
stories.summary: Professor Amine Laghidi of Morocco received a Special Award at the Trieste Summit, becoming the first Moroccan and African to be honoured at the event. Laghidi heads several global organisations.

stories.title: China’s US experts are falling short in the ‘great power game’, top scholar argues
stories.summary: A prominent Chinese academic argued that China's U.S. experts must better study America's internal crises, including political culture shifts, racial tensions, and fiscal unsustainability, to help Beijing navigate the rivalry with Washington.

stories.title: 'The world deserves food sovereignty and more secured food access for everybody'
stories.summary: At a high-level summit in Colombia, Delphine Lévi Alvarès of the Center for International Environmental Law argued that Middle East instability underscores the urgent need to decouple global food and energy systems from fossil fuels. She called for greater food sovereignty and secured food access worldwide.

stories.title: Press freedom at lowest level in 25 years: RSF
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that global press freedom has reached its lowest level in 25 years. The organization noted that the average score for all countries and territories worldwide has never been so low.

stories.title: Galilee man who swore loyalty to ISIS, planned attack on soldiers, indicted on terror charges
stories.summary: Israeli authorities indicted a man from the Galilee region on terror charges after he allegedly swore loyalty to ISIS and planned an attack on soldiers. Authorities noted a pattern of Arab citizens of Israel pledging allegiance to ISIS in recent years.

stories.title: Tracking the shadow fleet: How Iran evaded the US naval blockade in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has employed a shadow fleet of vessels using fake flags and transponder-darkening techniques to evade the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: What does the UAE walking out of OPEC mean for Russia’s war on Ukraine?
stories.summary: The UAE's departure from OPEC is expected to reduce oil revenue flowing to Moscow, weakening but not collapsing Russia's financial capacity to sustain its war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Media orgs call on Israel to allow foreign reporters into Gaza
stories.summary: Editors from more than two dozen media organizations called on Israel to permit foreign journalists to enter Gaza, challenging the rationale behind the ban on independent press access to the territory.

stories.title: Iran war tests India’s Brics leadership as ‘political relevance’ questions mount
stories.summary: India's leadership of Brics is being tested by the bloc's failure to agree on a common position regarding the Middle East conflict. A meeting of Brics officials in New Delhi last week exposed divergent interests among the group's ten members.

stories.title: Starmer calls for ‘swift and visible’ response to attacks on Jews
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer called for a 'swift and visible' response to antisemitic attacks during a Downing Street meeting following an assault in north London that wounded two people.

stories.title: When the US and Israel bombed Tehran, I did not flee. Here’s why
stories.summary: A first-person account describes the decision of an Iranian resident to remain in Tehran during US and Israeli bombing, reflecting on Iranians' deep connection to their homeland despite the strikes.

stories.title: Russians unable to create buffer zone on border – SBGS spox
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Border Guard Service reported that Russian forces have been unable to significantly expand their zone of control along the northern border area, failing to establish a meaningful buffer zone.

stories.title: Manchester United’s Kobbie Mainoo signs new five-year deal
stories.summary: Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo signed a new five-year contract with the club. The England international had been linked with a departure after losing his starting place under manager Ruben Amorim.

stories.title: Chemical Emergency Alert Issued in Perm After Ukraine Strikes Industrial Sites
stories.summary: Authorities in Russia's Perm region issued a chemical emergency alert following Ukrainian strikes on industrial sites. Regional officials later claimed the warning was a test, despite residents reporting large smoke clouds and a chemical odor in the area.

stories.title: 'Piracy': Israel raids Gaza-bound aid flotilla off Greek coast
stories.summary: Israeli naval forces intercepted a Gaza-bound aid flotilla in international waters off the Greek coast, raiding at least 15 boats. Israel's foreign ministry said approximately 175 activists from over 20 vessels were taken into Israeli custody.

stories.title: Former Bnei Brak principal wanted in Israel for sex crimes against children arrested by ICE
stories.summary: A former principal from Bnei Brak wanted in Israel on charges of sex crimes against children was arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Farkas appeared before a federal courthouse in Trenton, New Jersey, and was ordered to remain in custody.

stories.title: Cambridge A-level paper leak brings distress to bright students
stories.summary: Pakistan's Inter-Board of Coordination Commission is seeking a report from Cambridge after an alleged leak of the A-level Mathematics (9709) exam paper. Students and parents raised concerns about the transparency of the examination system, with reports of the paper circulating before the test.

stories.title: Zelensky orders talks with U.S. to verify details of Russia’s temporary truce proposal
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky ordered Ukrainian representatives to consult with the US president's team to clarify details of Russia's proposal for a short-term ceasefire. The directive signals Ukraine's willingness to examine the terms before responding formally.

stories.title: U.S. charges governor of Mexican state of Sinaloa with drug trafficking
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department charged Sinaloa state Governor Ruben Rocha with drug trafficking, alleging links to the Sinaloa Cartel. Rocha denied the charges on April 29, calling them politically motivated.

stories.title: PSX plunges over 4,700 points as bears maintain control
stories.summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange experienced a sharp selloff, with the KSE-100 index plunging over 4,700 points—a drop of roughly 2.89 percent—during Thursday's intraday trading. The decline marked a third consecutive session of losses, driven by investor concerns over the economic outlook, disappointing corporate earnings, and rising global oil prices amid geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Gaza genocide death toll rises to 72,601
stories.summary: Medical officials in Gaza reported that the death toll from Israel's war on the enclave has reached 72,601, with 172,419 wounded since October 7, 2023. Since a ceasefire in October of the previous year, at least 824 additional people have been killed.

stories.title: Keir Starmer demands ‘swift, agile and visible’ response to London attack
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer convened a Downing Street meeting following a suspected terrorist stabbing attack in Golders Green, north-west London, a neighborhood with a large Jewish community. Starmer called the incident an attack on Britain's Jewish community and demanded a swift response from the government and criminal justice system.

stories.title: US military commanders to brief Trump on new options against Iran, Axios reports
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command has prepared a plan for 'short and powerful' military strikes against Iran and is set to brief President Trump on the new options, according to Axios. The development comes amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Will the Iran war reshape the global energy order?
stories.summary: Amid the Iran conflict, global energy dynamics are shifting as OPEC faces weakening influence, US oil exports increase, and China accelerates its transition toward renewable energy sources.

stories.title: Wang Fuk Court resident finds charred HK$100,000 inheritance after opening safe
stories.summary: Residents returning to the fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court estate in Tai Po, Hong Kong, discovered charred banknotes worth approximately HK$100,000 each inside safes retrieved from the wreckage. Several local storage companies offered free services to affected residents as a gesture of support.

stories.title: Mali crisis deepens as separatists and jihadists step up attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military launched strikes on the city of Kidal after separatist Azawad Liberation Front fighters claimed control. Jihadist group JNIM has intensified coordinated attacks and announced a blockade of roads leading to the capital Bamako, deepening the country's security crisis.

stories.title: Xi Jinping urges ‘disruptive innovation’ to boost China amid high-stakes US tech race
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for "disruptive innovation" and stronger basic research capabilities at a symposium in Shanghai. He emphasized expanding China's talent pool and fostering tolerance for failure amid an intensifying global technology competition with the United States.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 30 – Siege warfare? Who’ll blink first in tense Iran blockade
stories.summary: A briefing covers multiple Middle East developments including a new aid flotilla heading to Gaza, Israel's posture in Lebanon, and the tense standoff around the Iran blockade, alongside the appointment of a special envoy to the Christian world.

stories.title: Former CSRC chairman Yi Huiman to face trial for taking bribes, abusing power
stories.summary: Former China Securities Regulatory Commission chairman Yi Huiman will face trial on charges of accepting large bribes and abusing power. Prosecutors allege he used his position to provide benefits in job promotions, company listing approvals, and loan acquisitions.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz blockade: 'Who will blink first' ?
stories.summary: The US has discussed extending its blockade of Iranian ports through the Strait of Hormuz for months, pushing Brent crude to its highest level since March 2022. Both Washington and Tehran appear locked in a standoff, with neither side willing to make concessions.

stories.title: Bank of England warns ‘higher inflation is unavoidable’ after leaving interest rates on hold
stories.summary: The Bank of England held interest rates at 3.75% in an 8-1 vote but warned that higher inflation is unavoidable due to the Middle East conflict. The bank signaled that rate hikes could come later in the year.

stories.title: China sparks backlash with plan to send jobless graduates to vocational school
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security announced plans to expand vocational training for young jobseekers, aiming to upskill one million youth for emerging industries like robotics and AI. The policy, which encourages university graduates to attend technical schools, has drawn criticism amid China's ongoing youth unemployment crisis.

stories.title: Middle East ceasefires: A fragile peace on the brink | The Deep Dive
stories.summary: An analysis examines fragile ceasefires across the Middle East, from Tehran to Gaza and Lebanon, assessing the risk that unstable truces could trigger a new regional crisis.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: Satellite firm’s ‘secret sauce’ | 3D-print factory in a box | Ship-lobby ad
stories.summary: The article covers defense industry developments including a satellite firm's technology, a 3D-printing factory system, and a ship-lobby advertisement. No specific conflict-related details were provided.

stories.title: Bodycam footage shows police detaining London stabbing suspect
stories.summary: Metropolitan Police bodycam footage shows officers detaining a suspect following a knife attack near a synagogue in Golders Green, London. Two men were stabbed in the incident, which occurred amid a series of recent arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in the area.

stories.title: Hungary has fired Netanyahu's pal Orbán but is Magyar different?
stories.summary: Peter Magyar won Hungary's elections after 16 years of Viktor Orbán's rule, promising reforms on rule of law and anti-corruption. However, analysts note Magyar's stance on Israel is not expected to differ significantly from Orbán's.

stories.title: ‘They’re as lost and inauthentic as us’: the Oscar winner who made a Farage satire – and released it on WeTransfer
stories.summary: Oscar-winning filmmaker Aneil Karia has released a satirical short film called "Vote Gavin Lyle," starring Jack Lowden as a Reform-style parliamentary candidate. The film was distributed via WeTransfer.

stories.title: SBU drones hit Lukoil’s Perm refinery — 1,500 km from Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's SBU security service conducted a drone strike on the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Russia's Perm region, located more than 1,500 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. The facility processes nearly 13 million tons of crude oil annually.

stories.title: Press freedom at lowest level in 25 years: RSF
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that global press freedom has reached its lowest level in 25 years, with the average score across all countries and territories hitting a record low.

stories.title: Russian tanker hit in Black Sea left adrift after Ukrainian strike – Navy spox
stories.summary: A Russian tanker struck by the Ukrainian Navy in the Black Sea on April 29 reportedly lost propulsion and was left adrift. Ukrainian officials indicated the vessel likely did not sink after the attack.

stories.title: Mamdani says he would encourage King Charles to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he would encourage King Charles to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond to the Indian subcontinent during the monarch's state visit. India has indicated it will continue to pursue the return of the diamond from the United Kingdom.

stories.title: War fears mount as Trump mulls Iran strikes, blockade continues
stories.summary: Oil prices surged as President Trump reportedly moved away from negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz in favor of economic pressure and military threats against Iran. The escalation has heightened fears of a broader conflict.

stories.title: Telegraph and Politico owner says journalists must support Israel or resign
stories.summary: Mathias Döpfner, CEO of Axel Springer and owner of the Telegraph and Politico, reportedly told journalists they must support Israel or resign. Journalists at the outlets have accused Döpfner of editorial interference through his pro-Israel directives.

stories.title: Up seven in a year, up 50 since 2022. Ukraine climbs RSF press freedom rankings as global score hits 25-year low
stories.summary: Ukraine rose seven places in Reporters Without Borders' annual press freedom rankings, climbing 50 spots since 2022. Meanwhile, the United States dropped to 64th place as the global press freedom score hit a 25-year low.

stories.title: In 1946, Hong Kong’s governor Sir Mark Young returns after WWII – SCMP archive
stories.summary: A 1946 archival report describes the return of Hong Kong Governor Sir Mark Young to the colony on April 30, 1946, after being held as a prisoner of war by the Japanese during World War II. He paid tribute to those who fell defending Hong Kong.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least nine in south Lebanon, in breach of ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least nine people across multiple locations in southern Lebanon, including Jebchit, Toul, and Harouf. Residential buildings were destroyed in the attacks, which Lebanon says breach the existing ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza aid ships in international waters, organisers say
stories.summary: Israel intercepted humanitarian aid ships bound for Gaza in international waters, according to organizers from the Global Sumud Flotilla. The vessels were reportedly seized hundreds of miles from the Gaza coast.

stories.title: UK pledges extra £25mn for Jewish security after London stabbings
stories.summary: The UK government announced an additional £25 million in security funding for Jewish communities following a series of stabbing attacks in London. The allocation is part of broader efforts to protect the community.

stories.title: 'Sickening': British papers react to anti-Semitic attack in London
stories.summary: British newspapers led with coverage of the Golders Green stabbing attack targeting London's Jewish community. Other front-page stories included King Charles's speech to the US Congress and tensions between the US president and the German chancellor.

stories.title: Eurozone inflation soars to 3% as Iran war drives up energy prices
stories.summary: Eurozone inflation rose to 3% in April, up from 2.6% in March and 1.9% in February, driven largely by energy price increases linked to the Iran conflict. The European Central Bank faces pressure as growth stumbles and a key interest rate decision approaches.

stories.title: Mexico’s cartel crackdown hits top ranks – but will it fuel Jalisco violence?
stories.summary: Mexican special forces arrested Audias Flores, alias "El Jardinero," a potential successor to late Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader "El Mencho," after finding him hiding in a drainage pipe at a ranch in Nayarit state. The arrest raises concerns about possible cartel infighting and escalating violence in Jalisco.

stories.title: Russia strikes Odesa with drones, injuring 20 people and damaging homes, kindergarten, hotel
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Odesa with a series of drones overnight, injuring at least 16 people including a 17-year-old. Residential homes, a kindergarten, and a hotel were damaged in the attack, according to Odesa military administration head Serhiy Lysak.

stories.title: Belarusian defectors tell Euromaidan Press: US sanctions relief unlocks the bank funding shells Russia fires at Ukraine
stories.summary: Belarusian defectors told Euromaidan Press that U.S. sanctions relief on Belarus has enabled bank funding that supports ammunition production ultimately used by Russia against Ukraine. Former security officers described it as a direct investment in weaponry fired across the border.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi signs order on mandatory rotation of frontline troops
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi signed an order mandating rotation for frontline servicemen. The order establishes clear time limits for deployment at forward positions and sets requirements for rest and support.

stories.title: Under Ukraine pressure, Israel blocks suspect Russian grain ship
stories.summary: Under pressure from Ukraine, Israel blocked a Russian grain ship from unloading its cargo at an Israeli port. Israel's Grain Importers Association said the Russian supplier would need to find an alternative destination.

stories.title: Why is China banning drone sales in Beijing?
stories.summary: Chinese authorities in Beijing have tightened regulations on drone sales, citing public safety concerns. The BBC reports on the reasons behind the new restrictions on drone purchases and operations in the capital.

stories.title: US house to consider resolution condemning Hasan Piker, Candace Owens for antisemitism
stories.summary: US Representatives Mike Lawler and Josh Gottheimer are advancing a bipartisan resolution in the House to condemn commentators Hasan Piker and Candace Owens for what lawmakers describe as antisemitic rhetoric. Piker has criticized the resolution.

stories.title: Burkina Faso ups security after Mali attacks
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's ruling junta tightened security in the capital Ouagadougou following coordinated attacks in neighboring Mali, according to security sources.

stories.title: KIIS poll: Ukrainian trust in US security guarantees falls from 39% to 27% in three months
stories.summary: A poll by Ukraine's Kyiv International Institute of Sociology found that trust in US security guarantees among Ukrainians fell from 39 percent to 27 percent over three months, with 57 percent doubting Washington would help repel a new Russian attack.

stories.title: Somalia shapes its own destiny in global security forums
stories.summary: Somalia has taken on new roles within the United Nations and the African Union, transitioning from being a subject of international security decisions to actively participating in shaping them.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russian oil pipeline station for 2nd straight day, forcing school closures
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the city of Perm for a second consecutive day, targeting a Transneft linear production and dispatch station. Smoke was seen rising over the city, and local schools were closed as a precaution.

stories.title: Mamdani calls on King Charles to return Koh-i-Noor diamond
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called on King Charles to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond, which the British Empire took from the Indian subcontinent in the 1800s. Mamdani made the remarks during the third day of the monarch's state visit, before greeting Charles and Queen Camilla at a 9/11 memorial event.

stories.title: Attacks on hospitals, medics rising, driven by Middle East war
stories.summary: Attacks on hospitals and healthcare workers are increasing globally, driven significantly by the conflict in the Middle East. In Gaza, only one hospital remains functional, while 26 healthcare sites in Iran have reportedly been targeted.

stories.title: Eurozone inflation jumps to 3.0 percent as Israeli-US war drives up energy prices
stories.summary: Eurozone inflation rose sharply to 3.0 percent in April, up from 2.6 percent the prior month, according to Eurostat data. The acceleration was driven largely by surging energy costs linked to the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: ‘Cartographic Inaccuracies’: Nepal Airlines apologises for showing J&K as part of Pakistan in ‘network map’
stories.summary: Nepal Airlines apologized for publishing a network map on social media that depicted Jammu and Kashmir as part of Pakistan. The airline called the depiction a 'significant cartographic inaccuracy' that did not reflect the official stance of Nepal or Nepal Airlines.

stories.title: Kenya: Kitui Senator Seeks Answers As Killings Spark Security Outcry
stories.summary: Kitui Senator Enoch Wambua called for urgent government action after a series of bandit attacks in Kenya's Kitui County killed at least eight people, sparking a security outcry.

stories.title: ‘Historic breakthrough’: Colombia climate talks end with hopes raised for fossil fuel phaseout
stories.summary: Nearly 60 countries at a climate conference in Colombia backed voluntary national roadmaps to phase out fossil fuel production and use. The initiative emerged from two days of intensive talks driven by frustration with the pace of UN climate summits.

stories.title: Women sexually assaulted during Nigerian fertility festival
stories.summary: Several women were sexually assaulted during the Alue-do fertility festival in Nigeria's Delta state in March 2026. Community leaders of the Oramudu community said the event was "hijacked by hoodlums" from outside who attacked women in the streets.

stories.title: Russia rejects Tuareg rebels' call to withdraw from Mali
stories.summary: Russia rejected Tuareg rebel demands to withdraw its forces from Mali, reaffirming its military presence in the country. The statement came after separatists and jihadists launched attacks against Mali's military junta, which Russian paramilitary forces support.

stories.title: US: Hegseth under fire in Congress over Iran war as diplomacy stalls
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faced Congressional criticism over the launch of the Iran conflict without proper authorization. Democrats challenged the war's justification and its estimated $25 billion cost, while President Trump rejected Iran's proposal regarding the Strait of Hormuz, leaving diplomacy stalled.

stories.title: Explosions rock Russia’s Dzerzhinsk
stories.summary: Explosions were reported in Dzerzhinsk in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, with smoke rising near an explosives plant. Residents in the city of Perm also reported repeated explosions.

stories.title: Global oil price hits 4-year high on concerns Iran war could worsen
stories.summary: Global oil prices surged past $122 per barrel, reaching a four-year high amid fears that the US-Iran conflict could escalate and disrupt Middle East oil supplies. Reports indicated that President Trump was being briefed on plans for military strikes against Iran.

stories.title: Investigation: Russian shadow airlines use Algeria as base for secretive missions
stories.summary: An investigation reveals that Algeria has become a hub for Russian shadow airlines conducting secretive missions. Algeria is also a key buyer of Russian arms at a time when Moscow's military exports have declined following its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: By failing to sanction Israel, the EU has confirmed once again its global irrelevance
stories.summary: The European Union has not imposed sanctions on Israel despite calls to do so. Critics argue the EU's inaction undermines its founding principles and facilitates impunity for alleged acts of aggression.

stories.title: US allocates $100 million to repair Chornobyl confinement damaged in Russian drone strike – Zelenskyy
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy announced that the United States will allocate $100 million toward repairing the Chornobyl nuclear confinement structure, which was damaged by a Russian Shahed-style drone strike in February 2025. Full restoration is estimated to cost over €500 million.

stories.title: US Supreme Court weighs ending protected status of Haitians, Syrians
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court heard arguments on whether to end Temporary Protected Status for Haitian and Syrian nationals. Lawyers representing the TPS holders argued that conditions in Haiti and Syria remain too dangerous for safe return.

stories.title: Oil surge triggers ‘biggest energy crisis’, IEA chief warns
stories.summary: IEA Director Fatih Birol warned that the world faces its worst energy crisis in history due to surging oil prices driven by Middle East conflict. Speaking in Paris, Birol said the price spike is straining economies and increasing government costs globally.

stories.title: Minerals over ideology? US embraces pragmatic diplomacy to break China’s rare earths grip
stories.summary: The Trump administration is pursuing pragmatic diplomacy to reduce US dependence on China's dominance in rare earth minerals. Efforts include partnerships on resource projects such as the Phalaborwa Rare Earths Project in South Africa, even where broader political relations are strained.

stories.title: China vegetarian woman, 107, captivates internet with robust health and sharp memory
stories.summary: A 107-year-old woman named Ding Guijuan from Cixi, Zhejiang province, China, has gone viral on social media for her sharp memory and robust health. Local media reported on her longevity tips, drawing widespread online attention.

stories.title: US-Iran negotiations: A Trumpe-l'œil
stories.summary: Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj published a cartoon in The New Arab commenting on US-Iran negotiations, with the title playing on the French phrase "trompe-l'œil" to suggest the talks are illusory.

stories.title: Why the UAE is leaving OPEC
stories.summary: The UAE announced its departure from OPEC, reportedly frustrated by production quotas capping output at 3.2–3.4 million barrels per day despite capacity nearing five million. The timing coincides with the UAE facing Iranian attacks, including over 2,800 drones and missiles.

stories.title: Germany approves 2027 budget with $13.5 billion for Ukraine
stories.summary: Germany's parliament approved the 2027 federal budget, allocating €11.6 billion in aid to Ukraine and €144.9 billion for defense. Total government borrowing is set at €196.5 billion, with Ukraine aid scheduled to decrease to €8.5 billion annually starting in 2028.

stories.title: UK pledges wider legislation to tackle state-sponsored threats after Golders Green stabbing
stories.summary: The UK government pledged an additional £25 million for Jewish community protection following a stabbing in Golders Green, London, bringing total security funding this year to £58 million. Officials also announced plans for broader legislation to address state-sponsored threats.

stories.title: A short video helps science reporting, but not India’s newsroom realities
stories.summary: A study found that a brief seven-minute video intervention improved journalists' ability to write accurate science headlines. However, the piece notes that India's newsroom conditions present broader challenges to implementing such improvements in science reporting.

stories.title: Ukrainian Navy strikes two Russian boats guarding Kerch Bridge
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Naval Forces struck two Russian boats assigned to guard the Kerch Bridge, which connects Russia to occupied Crimea. No further details on damage or casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: Civilians or Hezbollah: Who did Israel hit on Lebanon’s ‘Black Wednesday’?
stories.summary: Israel stated it targeted Hezbollah positions during strikes on Lebanon on what has been called 'Black Wednesday,' but analysts and experts contend the evidence indicates civilians were hit.

stories.title: Trump threatens Germany with US troop reduction after Merz’s Iran war criticism – Europe live
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to reduce American troop levels in Germany after Chancellor Friedrich Merz criticized the US approach to the Iran war, saying Washington was being "humiliated" in the conflict. The exchange highlights growing transatlantic tensions over Middle East policy.

stories.title: Hegseth faces further grilling over Iran war strategy and costs – US politics live
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faced questioning from the Senate Armed Services Committee over Iran war strategy and costs. The hearing followed a contentious nearly six-hour session in the House, where Democrats and some Republicans challenged Hegseth on the war's management.

stories.title: Local election campaigning enters final week as forecaster warns Labour could lose 1,850 English seats –UK politics live
stories.summary: Campaigning for local elections in England has entered its final week, with forecaster Robert Hayward predicting Labour could lose approximately 1,850 seats. The Reform party is expected to gain significantly at the expense of both Labour and the Conservatives.

stories.title: Israeli forces storm Gaza flotilla off Greece, abduct 175
stories.summary: Israeli forces boarded and seized more than 20 humanitarian aid boats in international waters off Greece, detaining 175 people. The flotilla was the latest attempt to break the Israeli naval blockade of Gaza.

stories.title: UK to tackle antisemitism ‘emergency’ as police probe double stabbing
stories.summary: The UK government declared antisemitism an "emergency" and announced £25 million for increased police patrols and security around Jewish sites including synagogues and schools. The announcement followed a double stabbing of two Jewish men in London's Golders Green and a series of arson attacks.

stories.title: Rise in caesarean section births in Gaza brings danger and infection risks
stories.summary: During Caesarean Awareness Month in April, health workers in Gaza report rising rates of caesarean section births amid deteriorating medical conditions, increasing the risks of infection and complications for mothers.

stories.title: South Sudan: 'There Is No Food' - Multiple Crises Push South Sudan Deeper Into Hunger
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that millions of people across South Sudan face emergency hunger levels as conflict, flooding, displacement, and economic shocks converge. WFP is working to deliver food and nutrition aid in hard-to-reach areas, but access and funding constraints threaten response efforts.

stories.title: Russia hits Odesa in two overnight waves — kindergarten, high-rises, hotel damaged; 20 injured
stories.summary: Russia launched two waves of overnight strikes on Odesa on April 30, damaging a kindergarten, residential high-rises, a hotel, and a shopping mall. At least 20 people were injured, two of them critically.

stories.title: Vietnam moment?
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Pakistan's investment outlook has improved significantly, citing macroeconomic stabilization under a 37-month IMF Extended Fund Facility, a narrowed fiscal deficit, nearly doubled reserves to $14.5 billion, and successive sovereign credit upgrades by Fitch, S&P, and Moody's.

stories.title: Environmental disaster fears grip Russia as Ukraine targets oil refineries
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck a major Russian oil refinery in Tuapse, one of Russia's largest, causing significant oil spills and reports of black rain in the surrounding area. The attack has raised environmental disaster concerns in the region.

stories.title: War update: 177 combat clashes over past day, 41 attacks repelled in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 177 combat engagements with Russian troops along the frontline on April 29. The Pokrovsk sector saw the heaviest activity, with 41 Russian attacks repelled by Ukrainian defenders.

stories.title: AI bots told scientists how to make biological weapons
stories.summary: An AI chatbot provided scientists with a detailed plan for creating biological weapons, including steps to maximize the likelihood of a successful attack.

stories.title: UAE’s Opec exit
stories.summary: The UAE announced its exit from OPEC, driven by dissatisfaction with production quotas that capped its output well below capacity. Analysts noted the decision also reflects broader geopolitical shifts and intra-Gulf rivalries, particularly with Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Ministers under pressure to tackle antisemitism after Golders Green attack – live updates
stories.summary: The UK government announced £25 million to bolster security for Jewish communities following a stabbing attack in London's Golders Green neighborhood. A 45-year-old British national born in Somalia was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and remains in police custody.

stories.title: Paris neighbourhoods: Exploring the massive 17th arrondissement
stories.summary: A feature explores Paris's 17th arrondissement, highlighting its diverse architecture from Haussmannian apartment blocks to modern glass towers. The segment includes a behind-the-scenes look at the Arc de Triomphe and the legacy of urban planner Baron Haussmann.

stories.title: Crude oil prices hit four-year high as Iran war threatens to drag on
stories.summary: Brent crude prices reached their highest level since the start of the Ukraine war after President Trump signaled the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz could last months. The oil supply disruption has triggered economic concerns, with calls for a windfall tax on companies like TotalEnergies amid soaring profits.

stories.title: US: Supreme Court weakens voting rigths act
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court struck down a majority-Black congressional district in Louisiana in a 6-3 decision, ruling it relied too heavily on race. The ruling weakens protections under the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and is expected to make it harder for minority communities to challenge discriminatory redistricting.

stories.title: Australian police find body in search for missing indigenous girl, 5
stories.summary: Australian police found a body believed to be that of a missing five-year-old Indigenous girl in a remote community in central Australia. The child, referred to by her family as Kumanjayi Little Baby per Indigenous custom, was reported missing from her home on Saturday. Police are searching for the alleged perpetrator.

stories.title: New Zealand’s Christchurch mosque killer loses bid to overturn convictions
stories.summary: Brenton Tarrant, the white supremacist who killed 51 people at two Christchurch mosques in 2019, lost his appeal to overturn his conviction and life sentence. The 35-year-old had argued that detention conditions during his trial rendered him incapable of rational decision-making when he pleaded guilty.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly passes film city, environment, wildlife bills amid uproar
stories.summary: The Punjab Assembly passed the Punjab Film City Authority Bill 2026, introduced by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb, amid heated debate between ruling and opposition lawmakers. Supporters argued the legislation would revive Pakistan's film industry and boost tourism, while critics questioned the government's priorities.

stories.title: Shelling from across Afghan border injures 5 in KP's South Waziristan: security sources
stories.summary: Mortar shells fired from across the Afghan border struck homes in Angoor Adda village in South Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, injuring five people including four children and a woman. Security sources attributed the shelling to Afghan Taliban and affiliated elements, saying such cross-border attacks on civilians have occurred repeatedly.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran-US standoff drags on
stories.summary: The standoff between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz continues, with President Trump indicating the naval blockade could last months. The crisis has disrupted oil flows and driven prices to multi-year highs.

stories.title: Gaza: expanding Israeli military zone fuels fears of long-term control
stories.summary: Israel has expanded its military zone in Gaza to cover nearly two-thirds of the territory since an October ceasefire. While Israel says the restrictions support aid delivery, Palestinians fear long-term displacement and permanent Israeli military presence.

stories.title: CENTCOM chief to brief Trump on new plans for military action against Iran — report
stories.summary: CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper is reportedly preparing to brief President Trump on new military options against Iran. According to Axios, the plans include short intensive strikes, seizing parts of the Strait of Hormuz, and special forces operations to capture enriched uranium.

stories.title: Oil price tops $126 a barrel after Trump warns Iran blockade could last ‘months’
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged above $126 per barrel, the highest since 2022, after President Trump warned the US naval blockade of Iranian ports could last months. The spike followed a 13% rise in 24 hours as peace talks remained stalled and Iran kept the Strait of Hormuz largely closed.

stories.title: Middle East: Rising tensions on Israel’s border as Iran negotiations falter
stories.summary: Tensions between Hezbollah and Israel are rising after a reported breach of a ceasefire boundary known as the "yellow line," with Israel threatening further strikes. US-Iran negotiations remain stalled, complicating regional de-escalation efforts. Israel also faces a scandal over alleged grain imports from Russia.

stories.title: Air defenses down 172 out of 206 drones launched by Russia in overnight attack on Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 172 out of 206 drones launched by Russia in an overnight attack beginning the evening of April 29. The strikes were part of a large-scale aerial assault on Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Air France-KLM cuts capacity growth forecast amid expected $2.4bn fuel bill rise
stories.summary: Air France-KLM reduced its 2025 capacity growth forecast to 2–4%, down from 3–5%, citing a projected $2.4 billion increase in fuel costs driven by the Iran war. The surge in Brent crude prices since the Middle East conflict began is straining airline industry finances.

stories.title: Republic of Congo president holds talks with Russia's Vladimir Putin
stories.summary: Republic of Congo President Denis Sassou Nguesso held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin in Moscow on Wednesday.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza flotilla near Crete and detains 175 activists
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted a flotilla of at least 22 pro-Palestinian aid boats in international waters near the Greek island of Crete, detaining approximately 175 activists. The flotilla was attempting to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza.

stories.title: Press freedom worldwide falls to its lowest level in 25 years
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that global press freedom has declined to its lowest level in 25 years. The organization warned that journalism is being increasingly criminalized worldwide.

stories.title: 'Assault on city's fundamental values': Attack on nun in Jerusalem sparks widespread condemnation
stories.summary: A 36-year-old man was arrested by Israeli police in connection with an assault on a nun in Jerusalem. The attack drew widespread condemnation, with officials calling it an assault on the city's fundamental values.

stories.title: The Eulogy That Explains Israel’s Current Tragedy
stories.summary: An article reflects on an iconic Israeli funeral oration delivered 70 years ago, arguing that its wisdom about restraint and peace has been forgotten in the context of Israel's current trajectory.

stories.title: China forges new aviation alliances to fast-track C929 certification
stories.summary: China's Civil Aviation Administration signed partnership deals with Hong Kong and Macau aviation authorities to accelerate type certification for the C929 widebody airliner. The C929 is being developed to compete with Boeing and Airbus models, building on cooperation frameworks established during the C919 narrowbody program.

stories.title: Oil surge on Trump blockade warning tests stocks’ resilience
stories.summary: Crude oil prices surged to a four-year high after US President Donald Trump suggested a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz could last months. Brent crude jumped as much as 7.3%, surpassing $126 per barrel, following reports of Trump meeting oil executives to discuss extending the blockade.

stories.title: No new contract awarded to build Karachi's Red Line corridor, Sindh High Court told
stories.summary: The Sindh High Court was told that the provincial government had not awarded a new contract for the Mosamiyat-to-Numaish corridor (Lot 2) of Karachi's delayed Bus Rapid Transit Red Line. The Sindh advocate general said a new contract would be awarded after completion of a notice period, while the petitioner's counsel alleged the work had been handed to the Frontier Works Organisation.

stories.title: Russian attacks hit energy and transport infrastructure in Mykolaiv region, five injured
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes hit energy and transport infrastructure in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, injuring five people.

stories.title: Shock in India after man takes remains of his sister to bank to prove her death
stories.summary: A man in India's Odisha state carried his deceased sister's remains to a bank in Keonjhar after officials refused to release funds without proof of her death. The incident involving Jitu Munda sparked widespread outrage over bureaucratic insensitivity.

stories.title: Independent press being stifled in Pakistan, says Hameed Haroon
stories.summary: DawnMedia Chief Executive Hameed Haroon said independent press in Pakistan is being stifled, describing the current environment as 'the law of the jungle.' Speaking alongside journalist Mazhar Abbas in Karachi, Haroon argued that government pressure on free media has intensified compared to previous eras, including periods of martial law.

stories.title: At least six Australian activists detained by Israel navy after Gaza flotilla boats intercepted
stories.summary: At least six Australian activists were detained by the Israeli navy after their boats, part of the Global Sumud flotilla bound for Gaza, were intercepted in international waters. CCTV footage showed Israeli personnel boarding the vessels, and family members have called on the Australian government to intervene.

stories.title: US reaffirms support for Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara
stories.summary: US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau reaffirmed Washington's support for Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara during a visit to Rabat. Landau urged a swift resolution to the territorial conflict, which has persisted since 1975.

stories.title: Last Beefeater and Brewers Fayre restaurants to close, with loss of 3,800 jobs, Premier Inn owner says
stories.summary: Whitbread, the owner of Premier Inn, announced the closure of all remaining Beefeater and Brewers Fayre restaurants across the UK and Ireland, resulting in approximately 3,800 job losses. The company cited rising costs and tax increases as reasons for the strategic reset.

stories.title: Pakistan opens up road trade routes into Iran amid Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Pakistan activated overland trade corridors into Iran after shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted by US-Iran tensions. The move is intended to transport stranded cargo that can no longer reach Iran by sea.

stories.title: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai honored by DW
stories.summary: Imprisoned Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai, founder of the city's largest pro-democracy newspaper, was honored by Deutsche Welle. Lai is serving a 20-year prison sentence. His son said the award shows that those fighting for freedom "are never alone."

stories.title: Iran supreme leader says US suffered 'disgraceful defeat'
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader declared that the United States suffered a "disgraceful defeat," while President Trump urged Iran to capitulate. Iran's parliament speaker had previously dismissed Washington's economic pressure campaign.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza flotilla, Trump urges Iran to ‘give up'
stories.summary: Israel intercepted a Gaza-bound aid flotilla while President Trump publicly urged Iran to surrender, saying the country should "just give up." Iran's parliament speaker rejected the US economic pressure campaign.

stories.title: Pentagon just unlocked $400 million in Ukraine aid that had been “collecting dust” after McConnell’s WP column
stories.summary: The Pentagon released $400 million in previously authorized military aid for Ukraine that had gone unspent for months. The funds, part of the 2026 defense authorization, were reportedly unlocked following a Washington Post column by Senator Mitch McConnell.

stories.title: Samsung, SK Hynix flag record supply squeeze in memory market as AI demand soars
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix warned of a prolonged global memory chip supply crunch driven by surging artificial intelligence demand. Samsung reported its order fulfillment rate had fallen to a record low, with customers pre-booking memory capacity for 2027. Both companies have increased investments in their China wafer fabrication facilities.

stories.title: Russian military loses another 1,470 troops and two helicopters in war against Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost approximately 1,470 troops and two helicopters in the past 24 hours. Total estimated Russian combat losses since February 2022 have reached approximately 1,330,290 personnel.

stories.title: Why King Charles’ ‘Trump bell’ gift amuses Chinese internet users
stories.summary: Chinese social media users reacted with amusement after Britain's King Charles presented US President Donald Trump with a World War II-era submarine bell during a state visit. In Chinese culture, gifting a bell carries inauspicious connotations, adding unintended humor to the diplomatic gesture.

stories.title: Myanmar’s blanket prison term reduction trims Aung San Suu Kyi’s sentence
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government issued a blanket prison term reduction that applies to deposed leader Aung San Suu Kyi, marking her second amnesty this month. However, the exact remaining length of her sentence remains unclear.

stories.title: 'Haitian solutions for Haitian problems: Every international intervention in Haiti has failed'
stories.summary: As the Kenyan-led peace force prepares to leave Haiti, experts argue that every international intervention in the country has failed. Professor Rosa Freedman called the Kenyan mission a failure and urged locally-driven solutions to Haiti's crisis, noting that gang violence is intertwined with systemic corruption.

stories.title: Africa: Africa's Integration Moment - From Rhetoric to Reality
stories.summary: The African Continental Free Trade Area, a flagship African Union initiative, aims to create a single continental market for goods and services. While Africa's integration agenda is advancing, implementation has been slower than envisioned. Full realization could boost intra-African trade and industrialization.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza aid flotilla in international waters off Greece, detaining dozens
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters near the Greek island of Crete, detaining crews from dozens of boats attempting to break Israel's maritime blockade of Gaza. The flotilla had departed from Barcelona earlier in the month with over 70 boats and around 1,000 participants from multiple countries.

stories.title: Healthcare Devices Association of Pakistan alarmed by illegal syringes spreading HIV and hepatitis
stories.summary: The Healthcare Devices Association of Pakistan raised alarm over the continued illegal manufacture and sale of banned reusable syringes, including devices fraudulently labeled as 'auto-disable.' HDAP warned the practice contributes to the spread of HIV and hepatitis and urged authorities to crack down on the entire supply chain.

stories.title: ‘Domestic pressures in US, Iran may stall peace deal’
stories.summary: Speakers at a panel discussion in Lahore warned that domestic political pressures in both the United States and Iran could stall a final peace deal, potentially pushing global crude oil prices beyond $120 per barrel. An Iranian proposal regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz was said to be gaining traction.

stories.title: Police arrest man suspected of attacking French nun at Jerusalem biblical site
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a 36-year-old man suspected of attacking a French nun at a biblical site on Mount Zion in Jerusalem. The sister sustained facial bruises in the alleged assault, and police said they treat attacks on clergy with utmost severity.

stories.title: Lebanon’s ex-president Amin Gemayel says time is right for direct talks with Israel
stories.summary: Former Lebanese president Amin Gemayel stated that conditions are favorable for direct negotiations between Lebanon and Israel. Gemayel, who led Lebanon during its civil war, said the Lebanese people desire peace and stability.

stories.title: ‘We’re coming for you’: NT police search for suspect after body of missing five-year-old found
stories.summary: Police in Australia's Northern Territory are searching for a murder suspect after discovering a body believed to be that of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, who went missing near Alice Springs. The body was found after a five-day search in the area.

stories.title: U.S. ambassador: Discussion on Ukraine’s reconstruction must begin now for success
stories.summary: Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Roman Popadiuk urged that discussions on Ukraine's post-war reconstruction should begin immediately, arguing that planning must happen in advance despite the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Jimmy Lai wins free speech award in Germany
stories.summary: Jailed Hong Kong media entrepreneur Jimmy Lai was awarded Deutsche Welle's freedom of speech award for his role in the pro-democracy movement. Lai, who is serving a 20-year sentence under Hong Kong's national security law, will be honored in absentia at the DW Global Media Forum in Bonn on June 23.

stories.title: Pentagon chief spars with lawmakers over Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth clashed with Democratic lawmakers during his first congressional testimony since the start of the war with Iran. Appearing before the House Armed Services Committee, Hegseth dismissed criticism as 'defeatist,' while Representative Adam Smith challenged the conflict's regional fallout and toll on U.S. troops.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes, shelling pummel southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes and artillery struck multiple towns in southern Lebanon, including Beit Yahoun, Jmaijmeh, and Bint Jbeil. Lebanon's National News Agency reported damage to residential buildings and infrastructure across the targeted areas.

stories.title: Find your place at Israel’s top university – Join us May 8 - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Hebrew University of Jerusalem is hosting a Campus Open Day on May 8, showcasing international degree programs, scholarships, and career opportunities for prospective students.

stories.title: Drap lab in Karachi achieves WHO prequalification, ministry says
stories.summary: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority announced that the Central Drugs Laboratory in Karachi achieved World Health Organisation prequalification. The certification confirms the facility meets rigorous international standards for testing the safety, efficacy, and quality of pharmaceutical products.

stories.title: Netanyahu urges Trump to cap Lebanon talks at two-three weeks amid IDF restraint - report
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged President Trump to limit Lebanon ceasefire negotiations to two to three weeks, according to reports. Israeli officials argue that continued Hezbollah attacks are undermining Israel's deterrence.

stories.title: US to refuse visa to applicants who fear returning home
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department instructed all embassies and consulates to deny visas to non-immigrant applicants who express fear of returning to their home country. Consular officers are now required to ask additional screening questions about whether applicants have experienced harm or mistreatment in their country of nationality.

stories.title: UN nuclear chief: Iran’s highly enriched uranium likely still buried at Isfahan site
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said Iran's stockpile of approximately 440 pounds of 60-percent enriched uranium is likely still stored at a buried facility in Isfahan. Grossi noted that inspectors need access to the site and that current US-Iran negotiations differ significantly from the 2015 talks due to Iran's nuclear advances.

stories.title: Male pageant contestant’s viral swimsuit walk sparks body image debate in Philippines
stories.summary: A contestant named RJ Perkins, 21, sparked debate about male beauty standards in the Philippines after his appearance in the swimsuit round of the Mister Pampanga pageant went viral. The discussion centered on whether pageantry should accommodate participants who do not fit traditional body ideals.

stories.title: Funeral services for Mali's slain defence minister to be held on Thursday
stories.summary: Funeral services for Mali's defense minister, who was killed in an assault on his home, are scheduled for Thursday. The attack was part of a wave of violence that has destabilized the country's ruling military junta.

stories.title: Israel says 175 activists seized from Gaza-bound flotilla and taken to Israel
stories.summary: Israel's foreign ministry confirmed that approximately 175 activists were seized from around 20 Gaza-bound boats and transported to Israel. The Gaza Sumud Flotilla said at least 22 boats were stormed by Israeli forces beginning around 04:30 GMT.

stories.title: Emirati telecom giant ‘mulling exit’
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi-based telecom giant Etisalat is reportedly reviewing its stake in Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) as part of a broader portfolio optimization exercise that could lead to an exit. PTCL stated it was unaware of any change in shareholders' plans, while sources indicated the review was not country-specific.

stories.title: Could a ‘reckless’ Trump’s ‘destroy-and-deal’ tactics target North Korea?
stories.summary: Amid a rift among US Republicans over strikes on Iran, Korean American Grassroots Conference head Kim Dong-seok urged Seoul to recognize the influence of hawkish "new neocons" on President Trump's foreign policy. Conservative commentator Tucker Carlson publicly criticized Trump as a "slave" to interventionists willing to use military force.

stories.title: US seeks new int'l coalition to get ships moving again in Hormuz, internal cable says
stories.summary: The United States is seeking to build a new international coalition to restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to an internal diplomatic cable. U.S. embassies were instructed to deliver the request to partner nations by May 1, excluding Russia, China, and other adversaries.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran blockade could last months, sending oil soaring
stories.summary: President Trump warned that the US naval blockade on Iran could last months, causing Brent crude oil futures to surge 7.6% to $119.69 per barrel.

stories.title: Massive attack on Odesa damages high-rise buildings, injures 16 people
stories.summary: A massive Russian attack on Odesa damaged high-rise residential buildings and civilian facilities across multiple districts, injuring at least 16 people. The Primorskyi district sustained the most damage.

stories.title: 90% of Russian passenger traffic still flies on Boeing and Airbus, while Russia promotes its MS-21 as “Boeing killer”
stories.summary: Despite Russia promoting its domestically produced MC-21 aircraft as a competitor to Boeing, approximately 90 percent of Russian passenger air traffic still relies on Boeing and Airbus planes. The MC-21 originally depended on American engines and imported composite materials before sanctions disrupted its supply chain.

stories.title: US turns down Iranian proposal to end war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to end the ongoing conflict, insisting that the naval blockade of Iran would continue until Tehran agrees to a nuclear deal. Iran warned of 'unprecedented military action' in response to shipping restrictions, while the USS Gerald R. Ford was set to return after a ten-month Middle East deployment.

stories.title: At least 6 political prisoners died in Russian custody in the first 4 months of 2026
stories.summary: At least six political prisoners have died in Russian custody in the first four months of 2026, according to the human rights organization Memorial. The group estimates more than 5,000 people in Russia are victims of political repression, with at least 68 dying in custody over the past 15 years.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 62 as Trump asks Iran to ‘give up’?
stories.summary: On day 62 of the US-Iran conflict, President Donald Trump stated that the US naval blockade of Iranian ports is succeeding and urged Tehran to capitulate. Iran's parliament speaker dismissed the economic pressure campaign.

stories.title: Correcting Course in the Indo‑Pacific
stories.summary: An analysis examines US Indo-Pacific strategy following President Trump's meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. While the visit produced commercial deals and demonstrated warm bilateral ties, the piece argues broader regional strategic challenges remain unaddressed.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Tensions between Iran and the United States remain elevated, with President Trump reportedly rejecting Iran's peace proposal and signaling the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports will continue until Tehran agrees to a nuclear deal. Iran's oil minister said the blockade has not affected domestic fuel distribution.

stories.title: Trump administration urges countries to help citizens stuck in Syria as Australia maintains hardline stance
stories.summary: The Trump administration is urging countries to repatriate citizens stranded in Syria following the fall of Islamic State. Australia's Albanese government maintains its refusal to bring home a group of Australian women and children who recently left the al-Roj detention camp in northeastern Syria.

stories.title: Industrial costs up 50% in Hong Kong since start of Middle East war: oil executive
stories.summary: An oil industry representative in Hong Kong reported that industrial and commercial operating costs have risen 50% since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran. Taxi unions called on the government to extend diesel and LPG subsidies as energy prices continue climbing due to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Could the US-Iran war become a protracted ‘frozen’ conflict?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest the US-Iran war is evolving into a protracted conflict of attrition in the absence of a permanent diplomatic agreement. Both sides continue to bear significant economic and military costs with no resolution in sight.

stories.title: Former U.S. ambassador: Ukraine’s combat-ready army will be pillar of regional security
