stories.summary: An analysis found that at least 98 Russian vessels subject to UK sanctions transited through British waters in the past month. The movements occurred despite threats by Prime Minister Keir Starmer to crack down on Russia's so-called shadow fleet.

stories.title: Russians launch drone attack on rescue workers in Marhanets, damaging depot
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone attack targeting rescue workers in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region of Ukraine. The strike damaged a depot and emergency equipment in what was described as a deliberate attack on first responders.

stories.title: Trump reportedly tells aides to prepare for extended blockade of Iran
stories.summary: President Trump reportedly instructed aides to prepare for an extended naval blockade of Iran. While hosting King Charles, Trump said the British monarch agreed that Iran must not obtain nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Iran talks stall amid Hormuz tensions and ceasefire violations in Lebanon
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts to address the broader Middle East conflict have stalled as the US evaluates Iran's latest proposal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Tensions in Lebanon continue to rise despite a fragile ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: A faraway conflict threatens livelihoods in India's glass hub
stories.summary: Supply chain disruptions caused by Middle East tensions have driven up costs in India's glass manufacturing hub, threatening the livelihoods of workers dependent on the industry.

stories.title: Hezbollah carries out wave of attacks on Israeli forces in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced multiple attacks on Israeli forces operating in southern Lebanon. The group claimed it shot down a Hermes 900 drone over al-Qantara, struck a Merkava tank with an explosive drone, and targeted Israeli troops with drone swarms in al-Taybeh and Bint Jbeil.

stories.title: SpaceX ties Elon Musk's compensation to Mars colonisation goal
stories.summary: SpaceX's board approved a compensation plan for CEO Elon Musk tied to goals including Mars colonization and operating data centers in space. The details were disclosed in a confidential registration statement filed with the SEC as SpaceX prepares for a public offering.

stories.title: Israeli contractor killed, his son wounded by Hezbollah drone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli contractor Amer Hujirat was killed and his son wounded by a Hezbollah explosive drone while operating an excavator in southern Lebanon. The Israeli prime minister said a special project is underway to counter the growing drone threat.

stories.title: Iraqi president nominates Ali al-Zaidi as PM-designate
stories.summary: Iraqi President Abdul Latif Rashid nominated Ali al-Zaidi as prime minister-designate. The nomination comes after U.S. President Trump earlier threatened to cut support for Iraq if former premier Nouri al-Maliki, who has close ties to Iran, returned to power.

stories.title: The tragedy of recurring Rohingya refugee deaths
stories.summary: A fishing trawler carrying Rohingya refugees capsized, drawing renewed attention to the deadly risks faced by displaced Rohingya and the human cost of their protracted displacement from Myanmar.

stories.title: Explosions rock Kyiv, six killed in Russia, Ukraine
stories.summary: Explosions struck Kyiv as both Russia and Ukraine intensified aerial attacks, with six people killed across both countries. Both sides have primarily targeted energy infrastructure in recent months as the conflict continues.

stories.title: UK faces £35bn hit and risk of recession this year over impact of Iran war, thinktank warns
stories.summary: The UK's National Institute of Economic and Social Research warned that Britain faces a £35 billion economic hit and possible recession this year due to fallout from the Iran war. Even under a best-case scenario, NIESR projected slower economic growth through 2026 and 2027.

stories.title: Pair of Hong Kong luxury homes sells for US$41m as market sizzle increases
stories.summary: Mainland Chinese property tycoon Zhao Zhijun sold two adjoining units at 8-12 Peak Road in Hong Kong for a combined HK$320 million (US$40.8 million), realizing an 86 percent gain over 16 years. The sale reflects renewed demand from mainland buyers restoring liquidity to Hong Kong's luxury property market.

stories.title: UN sanctions brother of Sudan's RSF leader, Colombian mercenaries
stories.summary: The United Nations imposed sanctions on Algoney Dagalo, the younger brother of Rapid Support Forces leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, as well as Colombian mercenaries linked to Sudan's conflict. The sanctions target individuals involved in the ongoing civil war in Sudan.

stories.title: Mali military leader Goita meets Russian ambassador after attacks, office says
stories.summary: Malian military leader Assimi Goita met with the Russian ambassador on Tuesday in Bamako, according to his office. It was Goita's first public appearance since insurgents carried out simultaneous attacks across Mali on Saturday.

stories.title: Zelensky: We have information on which areas will be main targets for Russian forces this spring and summer
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine has intelligence on which areas Russian forces plan to target this spring and summer. He stated that Ukraine would share this information with its partners, including details about potential Russian operations in NATO countries.

stories.title: UN court orders medical review of jailed Bosnian Serb general Mladic amid release bid
stories.summary: The UN war crimes court in The Hague ordered an independent medical assessment of Ratko Mladic, the 84-year-old Bosnian Serb general serving a lifetime sentence. The order follows Mladic's request for early release on health grounds, according to court documents published Tuesday.

stories.title: Israel using water access as 'weapon' in Gaza: MSF
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières accused Israel of using water access as a weapon in Gaza. The medical charity documented multiple incidents in which its clearly marked water trucks and boreholes were shot at or destroyed.

stories.title: 'Empowered': UAE's exit from Opec appeases Trump, delivers blow to Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has withdrawn from OPEC amid the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The move is seen as a gesture toward the Trump administration and a strategic challenge to Saudi Arabia's leadership of the oil-producing bloc.

stories.title: Amer Hujirat, Defense Ministry civilian contractor, killed in Hezbollah drone attack in Lebanon
stories.summary: Amer Hujirat, a civilian contractor with Israel's Defense Ministry, was killed in a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon. The incident highlights evolving threats from Hezbollah, which has been deploying fiber optic-guided drones against Israeli forces.

stories.title: Israeli soldier shows Gaza’s Beit Hanoon completely flattened
stories.summary: A video recorded by an Israeli soldier revealed widespread destruction in the town of Beit Hanoon in northern Gaza, showing the area has been almost completely flattened during military operations.

stories.title: Trump’s Ukraine envoy stepping down amid stalled peace talks with Russia
stories.summary: Acting US Ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis is stepping down and retiring amid stalled US-brokered ceasefire talks to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Reports indicate Davis had grown frustrated with President Trump's policies and his diminishing support for Kyiv.

stories.title: Pro-Kurdish party criticises Turkey's 'hesitant' steps toward PKK peace
stories.summary: Turkey's pro-Kurdish DEM Party issued one of its strongest criticisms of the government's handling of the peace process with the PKK on Tuesday. The party highlighted a growing stand-off between Ankara and Kurdish militants over next steps to end the decades-long conflict.

stories.title: Trump approval rating falls to lowest level amid Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's approval rating has dropped to 34 percent, the lowest of his current term, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll. The decline has accelerated since the US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28, with rising fuel prices compounding public dissatisfaction.

stories.title: Democrats urge Trump to keep ban on Chinese cars in US as Xi meeting looms
stories.summary: More than 70 House Democrats, led by Representative Debbie Dingell, sent a letter urging President Trump to maintain restrictions on Chinese automakers entering the U.S. market. The appeal comes weeks before Trump's planned trip to Beijing for a meeting with President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: US not funding Congo's $100 million mine guard, embassy says
stories.summary: The United States said on Tuesday it is not funding any security units tasked with policing or guarding mines in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The statement from the US embassy in Kinshasa came after Congo announced plans to launch a $100 million paramilitary force to secure mining sites.

stories.title: ‘Alpha’ troops and more ships: Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao outlines vision for service
stories.summary: Acting U.S. Navy Secretary Hung Cao outlined his vision for the service in one of his first public addresses, calling for "alpha" troops and an expanded fleet. He emphasized a shift in priorities and made controversial remarks about personnel standards.

stories.title: Trump hails British as ‘friends’ as King Charles III visits amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump hosted King Charles III at the White House, praising the British as friends. The state visit aimed to demonstrate allied unity despite reported divisions between the U.S. and UK over the Iran conflict.

stories.title: President on winter preparations: Ukraine must build reserves to ensure people have what they need
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy emphasized the need to build energy reserves ahead of the next heating season. He said every community in Ukraine must have sufficient reserves to ensure electricity and heating regardless of circumstances.

stories.title: Iran’s Guards seize wartime power, blunting Supreme Leader’s role
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has seized wartime executive powers amid the country's ongoing conflict, diminishing the role traditionally held by Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Reports indicate that with Khamenei absent, no other actor within the Iranian system has the capacity to resist the Guards' expanded authority.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox draft protesters storm Israel military police chief's home
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox anti-conscription protesters in Israel stormed the home of the military police chief. The incident was in response to government moves to enforce penalties against those who refuse military service.

stories.title: Beyond the headlines: Finding an anchor in the shelter - opinion
stories.summary: The article offers a personal reflection on life in Israel beyond the headlines of conflict, providing a weekly glimpse into everyday experiences including moments in shelters.

stories.title: Trump hits back at German chancellor over Iran war remarks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz after Merz said Iran was humiliating the US in war-related negotiations. Trump accused Merz of supporting Iran's nuclear ambitions, though Merz has publicly stated Iran must not acquire nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Report: Qatar offered to ‘look after’ ICC prosecutor who issued warrants for Israeli leaders
stories.summary: A Wall Street Journal editorial cited a recording in which the manager of a private intelligence operation alleged that Qatar offered to support ICC prosecutor Karim Khan. The operation reportedly sought to discredit a woman who accused Khan of sexual abuse. Khan had issued arrest warrants for Israeli leaders.

stories.title: Bangladesh starts fuelling its first nuclear power station
stories.summary: Bangladesh began fuelling its first nuclear power station as the country faces annual electricity shortages during summer heat waves. The Rooppur plant is expected to help alleviate strain on Bangladesh's overstretched power grid.

stories.title: EU says it has approached Israel over Russian grain boat that docked in Haifa
stories.summary: The European Union has contacted Israel regarding a Russian vessel that docked at the port of Haifa carrying what Ukraine described as stolen Ukrainian grain. An EU foreign affairs spokesperson confirmed the approach on Tuesday.

stories.title: Mali junta leader vows crackdown after insurgent attacks shake Bamako and north
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita made his first public appearance following coordinated insurgent attacks in Bamako and northern regions over the weekend. He pledged to "neutralise" those responsible as jihadist and separatist groups escalated violence across the country.

stories.title: King Charles III Delivers Pointed Message in Address to U.S. Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the US Congress during his Washington visit, delivering remarks that praised multilateral institutions, warned about climate change, and championed diversity.

stories.title: Gold miners set to stay in Mali despite attacks, industry sources say
stories.summary: International mining companies are expected to continue investing in Mali despite Saturday's insurgent attacks that killed the country's defence minister. Industry executives and analysts said the attacks have raised concerns about supply routes but are unlikely to drive firms out of one of Africa's most resource-rich countries.

stories.title: Suspected members of Nigeria-linked Black Axe crime gang arrested in Switzerland
stories.summary: Suspected members of the Nigeria-linked Black Axe crime gang were arrested in Switzerland on accusations of involvement in romance scams and cyberfraud. Europol announced the arrests on Tuesday.

stories.title: Flying cars and 5-minute charges: China's EV industry sees opportunity in Iran crisis
stories.summary: China's electric vehicle industry sees a commercial opportunity arising from the U.S.-Iran conflict, as the global scramble for fuel accelerates interest in alternatives. Companies are promoting advanced EV technologies including rapid-charging systems.

stories.title: US spy agencies examining how Iran would react to Trump declaring victory
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are analyzing how Iran might respond if President Trump declares victory in the ongoing conflict. The assessment aims to understand implications of a potential US pullback, amid concerns the war could hurt Republican prospects in midterm elections.

stories.title: As US-Iran talks remain ‘stalled’, experts warn of ‘long-term disruptions’
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations remain stalled, with no breakthrough reported. The standoff between Washington and Tehran has contributed to rising global oil prices, raising concerns among experts about long-term disruptions to energy markets.

stories.title: Hungary's outgoing PM Orban offers to quit as Fidesz party chief, local media say
stories.summary: Hungary's outgoing Prime Minister Viktor Orban offered his resignation as leader of his right-wing Fidesz party on Tuesday. A Fidesz party congress scheduled for June will decide whether to accept his resignation, according to a party lawmaker.

stories.title: Drone diplomacy wins Ukraine valuable allies, but now it must deliver
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has leveraged Ukraine's drone warfare expertise into diplomatic agreements during visits to the Middle East and Europe. Kyiv is using its military technology capabilities to strengthen its diplomatic position and secure new partnerships.

stories.title: Mexico's military captures top cartel leader in another blow to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel
stories.summary: Mexico's military captured a top leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, dealing another blow to the organization. The cartel was designated a foreign terrorist organization by U.S. President Trump along with five other Mexican cartels.

stories.title: How China’s reported ban on sulphuric acid exports could have overseas buyers reeling
stories.summary: China has reportedly moved to ban exports of sulphuric acid, a key ingredient in fertilizer production and metal processing. The squeeze on the commodity was initially triggered by the U.S.-Israel conflict in Iran and the effective blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, which disrupted shipments from a region accounting for a quarter of global production.

stories.title: US lawmakers move to mandate first comprehensive review of China’s AI capabilities
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers introduced a draft bill that would require the State Department to produce the first comprehensive assessment of China's artificial intelligence capabilities. The proposed legislation calls for identifying specific AI leaders in China and evaluating Beijing's progress using independent benchmarks.

stories.title: Watch: Elderly woman rescued by robot from Ukraine's frontline
stories.summary: The Ukrainian army used a drone to locate an elderly woman stranded near the frontline and dispatched a ground robot to rescue her. She was attempting to leave her war-torn village when the military intervened.

stories.title: New-generation Ukrainian FPV drones tested at proving ground
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense and the Brave1 defense-tech cluster tested new-generation strike FPV drones from eight domestic manufacturers at a proving ground.

stories.title: New-generation Ukrainian FPV drones tested at proving ground
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense, working with the Brave1 defense innovation cluster, tested new-generation strike first-person-view drones from eight Ukrainian manufacturers at a proving ground. The tests evaluated next-generation FPV drone capabilities for battlefield use.

stories.title: US spy agencies examine how Iran would react to Trump declaring victory
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are examining how Iran might respond if President Trump declared a unilateral victory in the two-month-old war. The assessment aims to gauge Tehran's potential reactions to such a move.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills five in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the southern Lebanese town of Majdal Zoun killed at least five people, including three paramedics trapped under rubble from an earlier attack, according to Lebanon's health ministry. At least two Lebanese soldiers accompanying a rescue team were also wounded.

stories.title: UAE OPEC departure 'a manifestation of dissatisfaction vis à vis Saudi Arabia', expert says
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC and OPEC+, effective May 1, citing national interests. An expert described the move as a "manifestation of dissatisfaction" with Saudi Arabia, OPEC's de facto leader, amid longstanding tensions over production quotas.

stories.title: Trump says Iran in ‘state of collapse’, wants US to open Hormuz Strait as soon as possible
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated on social media that Iran is in a "state of collapse" and wants the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as soon as possible. It was unclear how Iran had allegedly communicated that message.

stories.title: Iran and US allowed Russian superyacht to cross Strait of Hormuz, source says
stories.summary: A superyacht owned by Russian billionaire Alexey Mordashov was permitted to transit the blockaded Strait of Hormuz after maintenance in Dubai because neither Iran nor the United States objected. A source close to Mordashov confirmed the passage on Tuesday.

stories.title: Watch: UAE shocks world with dramatic OPEC exit | Above the Fold | 28.04.2026
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced a dramatic exit from OPEC, shocking global energy markets. The development was among several major international stories including an Indian heatwave, an SCO summit, and a Jakarta train crash.

stories.title: At UN, China denounces Japan and EU over South China Sea remarks
stories.summary: At the United Nations, China's deputy UN ambassador Sun Lei condemned remarks by Japan and the European Union regarding the South China Sea. Sun called Japan's statements unwarranted and accused them of distorting the facts.

stories.title: The biggest military spenders
stories.summary: Global military spending has increased for the 11th consecutive year, according to the latest report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI). The data highlights a sustained upward trend in defense budgets worldwide.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1525: Tuapse burns again, Crimea’s Iskander bunkers cracked open, and Washington loses another envoy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy unveiled a "Drone Deals" export framework as Ukrainian strikes hit Russian missile bunkers in Crimea and reignited a fire at the Tuapse refinery on day 1,525 of the war. The same day, the Financial Times reported that the US ambassador in Kyiv is resigning.

stories.title: US-Israel talks to discuss shifting military aid funding to joint defense partnership
stories.summary: The United States and Israel are set to begin talks in May on restructuring their military relationship, potentially shifting from traditional aid funding to a joint defense partnership model.

stories.title: Finance minister says no plans of seeking more bilateral financing after recent inflows from Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said the government has no plans to seek additional bilateral financing after receiving $3 billion from Saudi Arabia. He made the remarks at the first EU-Pakistan Business Forum in Islamabad, stating Pakistan's external position had stabilized.

stories.title: Netanyahu trial: President’s legal team invites prosecution, defense to preliminary plea-deal talks
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog's legal team invited both the prosecution and Netanyahu's defense lawyers to preliminary talks on a possible plea deal. The discussions are meant to test whether an agreement can be reached before Herzog considers a formal pardon request from Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Turkey offering to broker agreement between US, Lebanon on Hezbollah, sources tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Turkey has offered to broker an agreement between the United States and Lebanon regarding Hezbollah, according to sources cited by the Jerusalem Post. The Lebanese government has reportedly been hesitant about the initiative due to concerns over expanding Turkish influence in the country.

stories.title: FIFA introduces new World Cup red-card rules to combat racism
stories.summary: FIFA announced new red-card rules for the upcoming World Cup aimed at combating racism. Players who cover their mouths during confrontations or walk off the pitch in protest of refereeing decisions may be sent off under the new measures.

stories.title: Canadian PM invited to attend European Political Community summit in May
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has been invited to attend the European Political Community summit in Armenia next month. European Council President Antonio Costa said this marks the first time a non-European country has been invited to participate in the EPC gathering.

stories.title: Trump administration blocks US wind energy projects in switch to oil and gas
stories.summary: The Trump administration canceled two previously permitted U.S. wind energy projects and agreed to pay millions in refunds to the developers, on the condition the funds be reinvested in oil and gas. Representatives Jared Huffman and Jamie Raskin had called the agreements unlawful.

stories.title: Cao says industry needs to ‘move forward’ in first speech as acting SecNav
stories.summary: Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao delivered his first public remarks since assuming the role, urging the defense industry to accelerate progress. He outlined priorities for the service going forward.

stories.title: Trump's threats to steal Iran's oil continue a long history of US pillage
stories.summary: US President Trump has threatened to seize Iran's oil resources amid the ongoing military conflict. The rhetoric has drawn comparisons to a broader history of US economic coercion in countries such as Zimbabwe and Venezuela.

stories.title: Israel says has ‘no territorial ambitions’ in Lebanon, despite evacuations
stories.summary: Israel stated it has no territorial ambitions in Lebanon despite issuing evacuation warnings to residents of over a dozen villages and towns located outside or along the so-called "Yellow Line" in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: EU climate chief says energy crisis boosts case to ditch fossil fuels
stories.summary: European Commissioner for Climate Action Wopke Hoekstra said the energy crisis caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran strengthens the case for phasing out fossil fuels. He cited the closure of the Strait of Hormuz as a major driver of global energy price increases and Europe's vulnerability to import dependence.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire can’t paper over fires in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Despite ongoing U.S.-Iran peace negotiations in Islamabad, hostilities continue in the Strait of Hormuz, where ships have been attacked. Israel continues striking Lebanon, and disagreements over Iran's nuclear program remain unresolved, undermining ceasefire efforts.

stories.title: Zelensky: AFU will have priority access to sufficient weapons despite exports
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the Ukrainian Armed Forces will retain priority access to sufficient weapons, even as Ukraine moves to export domestically produced arms. Any surplus beyond military needs will be made available for international sale.

stories.title: Continuing hostilities in Lebanon as 1.2 million displaced sink into despair
stories.summary: Despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire, Israel has continued military strikes in Lebanon and occupies a strip of the south, while Hezbollah has maintained attacks against Israeli forces. The ongoing hostilities have displaced approximately 1.2 million people, creating a severe humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: China Pulls the Plug on Meta’s AI Acquisition
stories.summary: China blocked Meta's planned artificial intelligence acquisition, reflecting Beijing's shifting national security concerns. The decision represents a reversal that could affect Meta's AI development strategy.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill five, including 9-year-old boy, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on the Gaza Strip on Tuesday killed five Palestinians, including a 9-year-old boy, according to health officials in Gaza. The strikes were reported by medics in the territory.

stories.title: US intel agencies examining how Iran would react if Trump declares victory in war
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are analyzing how Iran might respond if President Trump were to declare victory in the ongoing conflict. Early assessments concluded Tehran would likely interpret such a declaration as a win for Iran. The White House says negotiations are continuing.

stories.title: 'Victory to the resistance': CAIR allegedly cosponsored event writing letters to terrorists
stories.summary: The Council on American-Islamic Relations' Washington chapter allegedly co-sponsored an event that involved writing letters to imprisoned individuals described by critics as terrorists. The event drew scrutiny as CAIR's executive director is running for state office.

stories.title: Mali leader says situation under control
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita addressed the nation in a video statement following coordinated attacks across the country. Separately, the Islamic State claimed responsibility for an attack in Nigeria's Adamawa State that killed at least 29 people.

stories.title: King Charles calls for NATO unity, Ukraine support in US Congress speech
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the US Congress during a four-day visit to the United States, calling for NATO unity and continued support for Ukraine. The British monarch praised the US-UK relationship while delivering pointed messages to lawmakers.

stories.title: UAE leaves OPEC in a blow to oil cartel
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, stating the decision serves its national interests. The UAE had long expressed frustration with production quotas, and its relationship with Saudi Arabia, OPEC's de facto leader, had grown increasingly strained.

stories.title: Drone strike in southern Sudan kills 11: medical source
stories.summary: A drone strike on the city of Rabak in southern Sudan killed 11 people, according to medical sources. A second drone strike was also reported further north in Khartoum state.

stories.title: FO says Cambodia has agreed on early repatriation of 54 Pakistanis arrested following scam centre raid
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office announced that Cambodian authorities agreed to the early repatriation of 54 Pakistani nationals arrested during a raid on a scam center. Reports indicated that over 200 Pakistanis were held in overcrowded Cambodian facilities with inadequate conditions.

stories.title: Oil tycoons deny paying bribes to former Nigerian minister
stories.summary: Several oil tycoons denied paying bribes to former Nigerian Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke. She is accused of receiving luxury accommodations and lavish spending sprees in the United Kingdom, charges she also denies.

stories.title: Mountaineer climbs Everest for Palestinian children
stories.summary: Mountaineer Mostafa Salameh is attempting to summit Mount Everest while carrying letters written by children in Gaza. The climb is intended to draw attention to the plight of Palestinian children in the territory.

stories.title: Armed group announces siege on Mali capital
stories.summary: The armed group JNIM has declared the start of a "total siege" on Mali's capital, Bamako. The announcement signals a significant escalation by the al-Qaeda-linked group against the Malian government.

stories.title: US ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis to resign amid “frustration” with Trump – FT
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis plans to resign in the coming weeks, the Financial Times reported. Her departure adds to significant turnover among senior US diplomats in Kyiv during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Britain challenges court decision that Palestine Action ban was unlawful
stories.summary: The British government on Tuesday challenged a court ruling that its ban on pro-Palestinian group Palestine Action was unlawful. Britain had designated Palestine Action a terrorist organisation, but a court found the move unlawfully interfered with freedom of expression.

stories.title: ICC orders $8.5 million in compensation for victims of Timbuktu Islamist who imposed sharia law
stories.summary: International Criminal Court judges in The Hague ordered 7.25 million euros ($8.5 million) in compensation for more than 65,000 victims of a Malian Islamist who helped impose sharia law on Timbuktu in 2012. The defendant was a key figure in the police force that ordered public floggings and other punishments.

stories.title: Melnyk suggests IAEA Chief Grossi could be next UN Secretary-General
stories.summary: Ukraine's Permanent Representative to the UN, Andrii Melnyk, suggested that IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi could be a candidate for the next UN Secretary-General. The proposal highlights Grossi's international profile amid ongoing nuclear safety concerns.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of Gaza hospital director without charge
stories.summary: An Israeli court approved the continued detention of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in Gaza, without filing charges. The Beersheba District Court upheld his detention under the "Unlawful Combatants Law." Physicians for Human Rights said he is held in harsh conditions and denied medical care.

stories.title: US and Nato faced with frustrating ‘marriage crisis’, Belgian defence minister says
stories.summary: Belgian Defence Minister Theo Francken described the U.S.-NATO relationship as a "marriage crisis" during a think tank event in Washington. He cited growing frustrations on both sides of the Atlantic and urged the United States to stand with its allies.

stories.title: Beverley Martyn, spirited British folk singer, dies aged 79
stories.summary: British folk singer-songwriter Beverley Martyn has died at age 79. She was known for collaborations with her former husband John Martyn, as well as solo work spanning from 1960s singles to a 2014 comeback album. Her family said she died peacefully at home.

stories.title: New pirate group behind latest Somali hijacking: officials
stories.summary: Security officials said a recent pirate attack off the coast of Somalia was carried out by a newly identified group of "opportunistic criminals." The hijacking has renewed attention on piracy in the region.

stories.title: US conditions for paying UN dues include China curbs, report says
stories.summary: The United States has conditioned the release of billions of dollars in unpaid UN dues on specific reforms, including cost-cutting and measures to counter China's influence within the organization. Diplomatic notes circulated by the US outlined nine "quick-hit" reforms required before further funding is released.

stories.title: News live: King Charles praises ‘ambitious’ Aukus and expresses pride in Australia in speech to US Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the U.S. Congress and praised the Aukus nuclear submarine partnership, emphasizing defense ties between the UK, the U.S., and Australia. Separately, the Australian federal government announced A$45 million in funding to fast-track environmental approvals for mining, energy, and housing projects.

stories.title: JNF halts most funding for at-risk youth in West Bank over settler violence links
stories.summary: The Jewish National Fund has halted most of its funding for at-risk youth programs in the West Bank over links to settler violence. JNF's chairman said the money had been supporting activities that led to the expulsion of Palestinians and vowed not to fund extremist outposts.

stories.title: King Charles praises Nato and urges defence of Ukraine in key speech during Trump visit
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the U.S. Congress, emphasizing the importance of NATO, the defense of Ukraine, and the transatlantic "special relationship" between Britain and the United States. The speech, marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, was widely interpreted as an implicit appeal to President Trump to uphold traditional European alliances.

stories.title: Anti-Israel protesters shout “child killers” at Oslo Independence Day celebration
stories.summary: Anti-Israel protesters disrupted an Israeli Independence Day celebration in Oslo, Norway, shouting chants including "child killers" and "Death to the IDF." The incident prompted calls for police action against the demonstrators.

stories.title: Zelensky: Export of Ukrainian weapons will become reality, all details agreed
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that all details regarding the export of Ukrainian weapons have been agreed upon and approved at the state institutional level. Ukraine plans to make arms exports a reality while ensuring its own military needs are met first.

stories.title: Gantz warns Bennett-Lapid alliance could harm chances of replacing government
stories.summary: Israeli opposition figure Benny Gantz warned that a political alliance between Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid could undermine efforts to replace the current government. Gantz released a campaign video calling for a broad bloc representing all of Israel, accusing Bennett and Lapid of prioritizing internal leadership rivalries.

stories.title: A-G moves to press criminal charges against Israel Prison Service commissioner
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney-General moved to press criminal charges against Israel Prison Service Commissioner Yaakobi. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir denounced the attorney-general, calling her actions anti-democratic and accusing her of attempting to frame the commissioner.

stories.title: UAE leaves Opec in huge blow to global oil producers' group
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its withdrawal from OPEC, dealing a significant blow to the oil producers' group amid an energy crisis linked to the Iran war. UAE Energy Minister Suhail Mohamed al-Mazrouei said the decision followed a strategic review of the country's energy policies.

stories.title: Russia's FSB says archaeologist Butyagin released by Poland in prisoner swap, TASS reports
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service confirmed that archaeologist Alexander Butyagin was released by Poland as part of a prisoner swap, according to state news agency TASS. The exchange was announced on Tuesday.

stories.title: Iraq air defences fire at drone over Baghdad's Green zone
stories.summary: Iraq's air defense systems fired at a drone flying over Baghdad's fortified Green Zone, which houses the US embassy. The incident occurred on Tuesday, though further details about the drone's origin were not immediately confirmed.

stories.title: Blaze at Moscow construction site kills at least seven
stories.summary: At least seven people were killed and 13 others injured in a fire at a building under construction in northern Moscow on Tuesday. Firefighters brought the blaze under control, according to Russian authorities cited by TASS.

stories.title: Marine requirement for lightweight counter-drone tech to be released in coming months
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps plans to release a formal requirement for lightweight counter-drone technology in the coming months. Although no official program of record exists yet, such systems have already been deployed to Marines in the field under an urgent operational need designation.

stories.title: Lebanon to enter direct talks with Israel, seeking permanent ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi announced that Lebanon will enter direct negotiations with Israel aimed at securing a permanent ceasefire and full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory. Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah resumed on March 2 amid the broader US-Israeli war on Iran. A US-brokered truce was extended on April 23, though Hezbollah is not party to it.

stories.title: Northern Ireland makes arrest linked to suspected New IRA car bombing
stories.summary: Police in Northern Ireland arrested a suspect linked to a suspected car bombing attributed to the New IRA. The dissident nationalist group has been escalating threats nearly 30 years after the Good Friday Agreement largely ended sectarian violence in the region.

stories.title: SSU detains IT specialist who recruited spotters for Russian intelligence
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained an IT specialist accused of helping Russian intelligence recruit Ukrainian citizens as spotters. The suspect allegedly assisted in building a network to gather information for Russian services inside Ukraine.

stories.title: War deepens generational rift inside Iranian-American households
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran is deepening generational divides within Iranian-American households. Younger Iranian Americans are pushing back against anti-war stereotypes and challenging older family members' political assumptions, complicating the community's often-simplified public image.

stories.title: UAE pulls out of OPEC oil cartels citing 'national interests'
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will withdraw from both OPEC and OPEC+ on Friday, citing national interests. The UAE, a major global oil producer, had previously clashed with the cartel over production quotas. The decision sent shockwaves through energy markets already unsettled by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Herzog’s office invites Netanyahu’s lawyer, AG to discuss potential plea deal
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog's office invited Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's lawyer and the Attorney General to discuss a potential plea deal. The move aims to explore whether an arrangement can end Netanyahu's corruption trial, which resumed after a pause due to the Iran war.

stories.title: Crime rampant in Negev due to police lacking manpower, comptroller report says
stories.summary: An Israeli state comptroller report found that police in the Negev region are short 205 officers, contributing to rampant crime including extortion and declining road safety. The findings contrast with National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir's promises to restore governance in the area.

stories.title: Children at 'breaking point' in Darfur as they face extreme hunger and violence, UN says
stories.summary: The United Nations children's agency issued an emergency warning on Tuesday about five million children facing extreme deprivation across Sudan's Darfur region. The warning comes as the country's civil war enters its fourth year, with children experiencing severe hunger and violence.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russian missile hub in occupied Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces struck a storage base for Russian Iskander operational-tactical missile systems in occupied Crimea on the night of April 28. The attack was carried out by drones operated by middle-strike units targeting the missile hub.

stories.title: Lebanese soldiers wounded in Israeli strike during rescue mission
stories.summary: Two Lebanese soldiers were wounded when Israeli forces struck their patrol during a civilian rescue operation in the border town of Majdal Zoun in the Tyre district. The unit was operating alongside civil defence teams and civilian bulldozers at the time of the strike.

stories.title: Nearly eight million people in South Sudan at risk of acute hunger: NGOs
stories.summary: Aid agencies warned that nearly eight million people in South Sudan face acute hunger and that time is running out to prevent an irreversible humanitarian catastrophe. NGOs called for urgent international action to address the crisis.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF dismantles largest Hezbollah tunnel network in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces said it dismantled the largest Hezbollah tunnel network discovered in southern Lebanon. The tunnel system reportedly ran two kilometers in length and ten kilometers in width, with the capacity to hold thousands of fighters.

stories.title: Trump scolds Germany’s Merz for criticism of Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz for his comments on the US-led war in Iran, saying Merz "doesn't know what he's talking about." Merz had argued that Tehran was "humiliating" Washington. Trump defended the military campaign as necessary.

stories.title: Belarus frees Polish journalist, Warsaw frees Russian archaeologist in prisoner swap
stories.summary: Belarus released Polish-Belarusian journalist and activist Andrzej Poczobut as part of a prisoner exchange at the Polish-Belarusian border. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed the swap on Tuesday, which also involved Poland releasing a Russian archaeologist.

stories.title: IDF stood by while Israelis burnt West Bank home, beat elderly Palestinian man - Army Radio
stories.summary: According to Israeli Army Radio, IDF soldiers arrived at the West Bank village of Jalud after Israeli rioters had already entered. The soldiers reportedly remained by their vehicles for approximately five minutes without intervening as rioters burned a Palestinian home and beat an elderly Palestinian man.

stories.title: 'Only yes means yes' rape definition backed by EU lawmakers
stories.summary: The European Parliament voted to adopt a consent-based definition of rape, backing the principle that "only yes means yes." However, criminal law definitions of rape still vary significantly among EU member states.

stories.title: Trump’s FCC orders review of ABC licences after Kimmel’s ‘expectant widow’ joke
stories.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission ordered an early licence review of ABC's television stations after late-night host Jimmy Kimmel made an "expectant widow" joke that drew White House criticism. The standoff marks the first major crisis for Walt Disney's new CEO Josh D'Amaro.

stories.title: “Drone Deals”: Ukraine to export surplus weapons as Zelenskyy unveils new defense trade framework
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced a new defense trade framework allowing Ukraine to export surplus weapons production. He noted that some weapons categories now have up to 50 percent excess manufacturing capacity beyond domestic needs.

stories.title: For Russia’s Ailing Coal Sector, Not Even the Middle East Crisis Can Bring Relief
stories.summary: Analysts say Russia's struggling coal sector is unlikely to benefit from the Middle East crisis. Both Russian and Western experts suggest the turmoil may instead accelerate Asia's transition toward alternative energy sources, further weakening demand for Russian coal.

stories.title: How a rising star of France’s far right weaponised a routine inquiry against public broadcasters
stories.summary: A routine French parliamentary fact-finding inquiry has become a polarising political spectacle, providing France's far right with a platform to campaign against public broadcasters. A rising figure in the far-right movement has used the proceedings to advance a culture-war agenda in Paris.

stories.title: Nearly 50 strikes hit Dnipropetrovsk region, leaving two killed, 11 injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched nearly 50 drone strikes and artillery attacks across three districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region in a single day. The strikes killed two people and injured 11 others.

stories.title: After 60 days of war in Iran, does US Congress want a say?
stories.summary: Sixty days into the US war in Iran, legal experts say President Trump requires Congressional approval under US law to continue military operations. However, members of Congress may avoid forcing a vote on the issue altogether.

stories.title: Five wounded in two shootings in Athens, gunman at large
stories.summary: Greek authorities identified the suspect in two Athens shootings on Tuesday as an 89-year-old garbage collector from the Athens area. Five people were wounded in the attacks at a social security office and a courthouse.

stories.title: AG set to indict Israel Prisons chief in probe linked to Ben Gvir
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General is set to indict the head of the Israel Prisons Service in a probe linked to National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir. The chief allegedly informed a colleague suspected of covering up Jewish nationalist violence about a covert investigation into the matter.

stories.title: Rescuers trapped during operation in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Members of a rescue team became trapped while conducting an operation in the southern Lebanese town of Majdal Zoun, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The Lebanese army has been working to extract the trapped rescuers.

stories.title: Massive explosion from Israeli operation seen in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military carried out strikes on what it described as a Hezbollah tunnel in southern Lebanon, producing massive explosions captured on video. The operation is part of ongoing Israeli military activity in the region.

stories.title: Brazil's Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro are neck and neck in presidential runoff, poll finds
stories.summary: A poll by AtlasIntel and Bloomberg showed Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro tied in a simulated presidential runoff ahead of this year's election. The survey was released on Tuesday in São Paulo.

stories.title: Can the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty prevent a disaster?
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General warned that the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty's influence is waning. The statement raises concerns about the global agreement's ability to prevent a nuclear disaster amid rising international tensions.

stories.title: CPJ calls for release of missing German journalist in Syria
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists called for the release of a German journalist who went missing in Syria more than three months ago. Her lawyer said she is likely being held in a prison in Damascus.

stories.title: How a controversial gas pipeline deal could further stall Bosnia's EU accession
stories.summary: A US-backed gas pipeline project could help Bosnia reduce its reliance on Russian energy, but the European Union has warned that a deal with a company linked to Trump allies could jeopardize Bosnia's EU accession prospects.

stories.title: Ex-President Lacalle Pou: 'I will not die without seeing Paraguay have a sea outlet in Uruguay'
stories.summary: Former Uruguayan President Luis Lacalle Pou publicly advocated for building a port in Uruguay to give landlocked Paraguay maritime access. He made the remarks at an event in Santa Rita, in Paraguay's Alto Paraná department, marking the tenth anniversary of a partnership between Paraguayan and Uruguayan agricultural firms.

stories.title: How London police are battling rampant phone theft
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police have deployed interceptor teams to combat a surge in mobile phone thefts carried out by teenagers on e-bikes. Officers highlighted the vulnerability of commuters and tourists distracted by their devices on city streets.

stories.title: Russia expanding mobilization, planning further offensive operations – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Russia's political leadership is planning further offensive operations and preparing to expand mobilization to involve more military personnel. He warned of increased Russian efforts to bring additional forces into the ongoing war.

stories.title: United Arab Emirates leaves OPEC amid energy crisis fueled by Iran war
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its withdrawal from OPEC and the OPEC+ alliance, effective May 1, marking one of the most significant departures in the cartel's six-decade history. The decision comes amid a major energy crisis triggered by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the U.S.-Iran war that began on February 28.

stories.title: Haredi anti-draft rioters break into Military Police chief’s home with family inside
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox anti-draft protesters in Israel broke into the home of the Military Police chief while his family was inside. Prime Minister Netanyahu, the defense minister, and the IDF chief of staff all condemned the incident, with the latter calling it a "dangerous red line."

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox draft protesters break into military police chief's yard, block highway
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox draft protesters broke into the yard of Israel's military police chief and blocked Highway 4 in both directions. Israeli media reported several altercations between the demonstrators and police officers during the protest.

stories.title: Irsa asks provinces to ensure untreated wastewater does not make its way to rivers and natural streams
stories.summary: Pakistan's Indus River System Authority urged provincial governments to prevent untreated wastewater from being discharged into rivers and natural streams. IRSA Chairman Amjad Saeed cited alarming deterioration of water quality in the Indus Basin Irrigation System due to pollution and salinity.

stories.title: Families forced into displacement by famine in Sudan
stories.summary: Millions of people in Sudan face severe hunger and displacement as the country's ongoing war disrupts food supplies. Families are dependent on limited and inconsistent humanitarian aid to survive.

stories.title: Russian Yacht, Cruise Ships Ferry Seafarers Out of Gulf – Philippines
stories.summary: The Philippines reported that Russian and other vessels, including cruise ships, have been ferrying seafarers out of the Gulf region. Among them was the 142-meter yacht Nord, flagged to Russia and reportedly linked to Russian billionaire Alexei Mordashov, which passed through the strait.

stories.title: Noam Bettan strolls through Israel's musical history in Eurovision trailer
stories.summary: Israeli Eurovision 2026 representative Noam Bettan appeared in a promotional trailer dancing to excerpts from Israel's four previous Eurovision-winning songs. The clip concluded with Bettan performing a portion of his upbeat entry for the 2026 contest.

stories.title: FCC orders review of ABC licenses after Jimmy Kimmel’s Melania Trump joke
stories.summary: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission announced an accelerated review of eight local broadcasting licenses held by ABC. The move followed White House criticism of late-night host Jimmy Kimmel over a joke about Melania Trump, prompting critics to characterize the review as politically motivated regulatory retaliation.

stories.title: Austrian pleads guilty to ISIL-planned attack on Taylor Swift concert
stories.summary: A man identified as Beran A. pleaded guilty in Austria to planning an ISIL-directed attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. He also admitted to conspiring in additional attack plots abroad.

stories.title: Acting SecNav: ‘I’m not going to have my son go to war the way I did'
stories.summary: Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao stated that defense industry cooperation could help the Pentagon avoid mistakes made during the Global War on Terror era. He made the remarks while filling in for his recently ousted predecessor.

stories.title: US boards, releases vessel suspected of heading to Iran
stories.summary: US Central Command said Marines boarded the Comoros-flagged commercial vessel Blue Star III in the Arabian Sea on suspicion it was heading to Iran, but released it after determining it would not dock at an Iranian port. CENTCOM stated it has now redirected 39 vessels since the start of its blockade on Iranian ports.

stories.title: Trump approval dips to record low amid Iran war, inflation woes: Poll
stories.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll found President Trump's approval rating has dropped to a record low amid the ongoing war in Iran and rising inflation. Only 22 percent of US voters approved of his handling of the cost of living.

stories.title: Ukraine to seek accountability for archaeologist Butyagin despite his return to Russia – MFA
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it will pursue legal accountability for Russian archaeologist Alexander Butyagin, who is suspected of conducting illegal excavations in occupied Crimea. Butyagin was returned to Russia from Poland as part of a prisoner exchange.

stories.title: Pentagon formally requests name change to War Department, setting up fight with Dems
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense has formally submitted a legislative proposal to Congress requesting a name change back to the War Department. The Pentagon estimates spending approximately $50 million in fiscal year 2026 to begin implementing the change, a move expected to face opposition from Democrats.

stories.title: 'When media freedom goes, the rest is not far behind', campaigner says
stories.summary: The Liberties Media Freedom Report 2026 found that media freedom and pluralism in the EU continued to face significant challenges in 2025. The Civil Liberties Union for Europe warned that political interference in public broadcasting remains widespread across the bloc.

stories.title: How the UAE’s decision to leave Opec could recast the Middle East
stories.summary: The UAE's departure from OPEC is seen as both a political and business decision that could reignite tensions between the UAE and Saudi Arabia. The move gives the UAE freedom to respond independently to constrained oil supplies and maximize profits amid the disruption caused by the U.S.-Iran war.

stories.title: The IDF soldier who destroyed Jesus' statue is not one bad apple
stories.summary: An IDF soldier destroyed a statue of Jesus in Lebanon, prompting Israel to characterize the incident as an isolated act. Critics argue the desecration reflects broader institutional attitudes rather than the actions of a single individual.

stories.title: European parliament urges EU to draw up standardised consent-based definition of rape
stories.summary: The European Parliament voted on April 28 with 447 of 720 MEPs in favor of a report urging the EU to develop a standardized consent-based definition of rape. Eight EU member states currently include force or violence rather than consent in their national criminal definitions of rape.

stories.title: America's special relationship 'probably Israel', says UK ambassador to US
stories.summary: UK Ambassador to the US reportedly remarked in February that America's special relationship is "probably Israel" rather than the UK. The comments, first reported by the Financial Times, surfaced during the King's state visit to Washington.

stories.title: Gulf leaders meet in Saudi Arabia to discuss response to Iranian strikes
stories.summary: Gulf state leaders convened in Saudi Arabia to discuss their collective response to Iranian strikes. The summit marked their first in-person meeting since their nations became directly involved in the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Fast-food ‘chicken war’ sparks political cockfight in Paris suburb
stories.summary: A mayor in the Paris suburb of Saint-Ouen attempted to block a popular fast-food outlet from selling what he called "junk food," sparking a political dispute. The controversy has become another point of contention among France's divided left-wing parties.

stories.title: Russia wants up to 20,000 foreign recruits in 2026, using coercion and deportation threats to bring people to the frontlines – Ukrainian intelligence
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence reports that Russia aims to recruit up to 20,000 foreign nationals for military service in 2026, using coercion and deportation threats. Moscow has throughout the war deployed migrants and vulnerable groups to high-risk frontline positions with limited training.

stories.title: Netanyahu’s first cross-examination in over two months cut short hours early
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu underwent his first cross-examination in over two months in his corruption trial, but the session was cut short. Netanyahu claimed authorities had intimidated witness Shlomo Filber into testifying against him and denied that Bezeq tycoon Shaul Elovitch had complained to him about telecom matters.

stories.title: Mali military leader Goita emerges as Russia declares it halted coup
stories.summary: Malian military leader Assimi Goita was seen publicly for the first time since recent rebel attacks, as Russia announced it had helped halt an attempted coup against Mali's military government. Moscow sought to counter speculation about the stability of its allied regime in Bamako.

stories.title: Austrian man pleads guilty to foiled attack on Taylor Swift’s Vienna concert
stories.summary: A man pleaded guilty in an Austrian court on Tuesday to plotting a foiled attack on Taylor Swift's Vienna concert. He was also accused of planning attacks in the Middle East that were never carried out.

stories.title: No 10 dismisses Reeves’s reported plan for freeze on private rents
stories.summary: The UK government dismissed a reported plan by Chancellor Rachel Reeves to freeze private sector rents as a measure to address rising housing costs linked to the Iran war. A Downing Street spokesperson said on April 28 that a rent freeze was not the approach the government would take.

stories.title: Judicial Commission of Pakistan approves transfer of 3 IHC judges
stories.summary: Pakistan's Judicial Commission, chaired by Chief Justice Yahya Afridi, approved the transfer of three Islamabad High Court judges to other high courts. The meeting was convened by the JCP secretary after the chairman declined to call it on a member requisition.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF, Border Police investigate dozens of east Jerusalem terror suspects, confiscate weapons
stories.summary: The IDF and Israeli Border Police conducted a counterterrorism operation in east Jerusalem, arresting six suspects and confiscating over 2,000 rounds of ammunition along with weapons and explosives.

stories.title: 89-year-old man arrested over Athens double shooting
stories.summary: An 89-year-old man was arrested in the Greek port city of Patras on suspicion of shooting and wounding several people in attacks on a social security office and an appeals court in Athens. He was reportedly attempting to flee to Italy when detained following a nationwide manhunt.

stories.title: UK summons Iranian ambassador over embassy's 'unacceptable' comments on social media
stories.summary: The United Kingdom summoned Iran's ambassador after the Iranian embassy posted social media content that British officials deemed unacceptable. Middle East Minister Hamish Falconer told the embassy it must stop communications that could be interpreted as encouraging violence in the UK.

stories.title: Sa’ar scolds Ukraine for doing Twitter diplomacy — but he does just the same, as does everyone else
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar criticized Ukraine for conducting diplomacy via social media platform X, despite regularly using the platform himself to praise or criticize foreign counterparts. The exchange highlights how public social media diplomacy has become a standard practice among global leaders.

stories.title: Iranian regime targets diaspora with propaganda, financial appeals, analyst says - interview
stories.summary: Geopolitical analyst Ashkan Rostami discussed how the Iranian regime is targeting its diaspora with propaganda and financial appeals to bolster support during the ongoing conflict. The campaign reportedly aims to mobilize overseas Iranians in favor of the government.

stories.title: CCD says reports of new Russian offensive on Kyiv manipulation
stories.summary: Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation said claims of a new Russian offensive on Kyiv are manipulative. The center clarified that recent military statements about fortification construction in northern Ukraine are unrelated to any alleged planned Russian attack on the capital.

stories.title: Ryanair CEO warns airlines could fail as fuel prices surge
stories.summary: Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary warned that some European airlines could collapse if jet fuel prices remain elevated through summer due to disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. He said Ryanair is relatively protected by fuel hedging but that competitors without similar coverage face serious financial difficulties.

stories.title: US soldier accused of betting on Maduro's removal pleads not guilty to fraud charges
stories.summary: A U.S. Army officer accused of using classified information to win approximately $400,000 on an online prediction market by betting on Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro's removal has pleaded not guilty to fraud charges.

stories.title: Chitral's Kalash Valleys added to Unesco's World Heritage Tentative List
stories.summary: The Kalash valleys in Chitral district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, have been added to UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List. Inclusion on the list is a prerequisite for a site to be considered for full World Heritage inscription.

stories.title: Trump hails ‘special relationship’ during ceremonial welcome for King Charles’s state visit
stories.summary: President Donald Trump praised the U.S.-UK "special relationship" during a ceremonial military welcome for King Charles III and Queen Camilla at the White House. The remarks came amid recent tensions between London and Washington.

stories.title: Ukraine says it shot down 33,000 Russian drones in March, monthly record
stories.summary: Ukraine's defence minister reported that the country shot down more than 33,000 Russian drones of various types in March, setting a monthly record since Russia's full-scale invasion began. Ukraine's drone interception technology has drawn military interest from around the world.

stories.title: Russia calls for rapid restoration of peace in Mali after sustaining casualties
stories.summary: Russia called on Tuesday for the rapid restoration of peace and stability in Mali, where Russian forces have suffered casualties while helping the military-led government fight insurgents. The statement followed a series of weekend attacks by insurgents near the capital Bamako and across the country.

stories.title: Northern Irish police arrest man over suspected New IRA car bombing
stories.summary: Northern Irish police arrested a man on Tuesday in connection with a car bomb attack on a Belfast police station claimed by the militant group New IRA. Police stepped up patrols after the group warned it would target officers at their homes.

stories.title: SpaceX ties Musk compensation to Mars colonisation goal
stories.summary: SpaceX has structured compensation for CEO Elon Musk that ties significant rewards to the company's Mars colonisation objectives. The arrangement reflects the challenge of maintaining Musk's focus amid his numerous business and governmental commitments.

stories.title: Finland and Estonia say US defence deliveries delayed over Middle East war
stories.summary: The presidents of Finland and Estonia said on Tuesday that some US defence equipment deliveries to Europe are being delayed because of the war in the Middle East. The announcement was made in Helsinki during a joint appearance.

stories.title: Ukraine says Israeli buying of ‘stolen’ grain from Russia not ‘legitimate’
stories.summary: Ukraine stated that Israel's purchase of grain from Russia that Ukraine considers stolen from its territory is not legitimate. Traders have noted it is impossible to trace the origin of wheat once it has been mixed with other supplies.

stories.title: US soldier accused of gambling on Maduro removal due in court
stories.summary: A US Army soldier who allegedly used insider information to win $400,000 by betting on the removal of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro appeared in a New York court on Tuesday. He was expected to enter a plea to fraud charges.

stories.title: COGAT says MSF 'lost moral direction' after NGO's claim that Israel is 'using water as a weapon'
stories.summary: Israel's Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) accused Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) of losing its "professional and moral direction" after the NGO alleged that Israel is using water as a weapon.

stories.title: Israeli chef closes Berlin restaurant amid constant threats
stories.summary: Israeli chef Eyal Shani closed his Berlin restaurant Gila & Nancy after months of sustained pro-Palestinian protests and threats directed at the establishment. The closure reflects ongoing tensions in European cities linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Starmer sees off major Labour rebellion over call for Mandelson inquiry
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer defeated a Labour rebellion in Parliament that sought to force a privileges committee inquiry into his appointment of Peter Mandelson. Downing Street mobilized significant pressure to block the referral, but Labour MPs warned Starmer was depleting his political capital and leaving the party vulnerable to accusations of a cover-up.

stories.title: Czech Republic to join Special Tribunal Agreement
stories.summary: The Czech Republic announced its intention to join the Enlarged Partial Agreement to establish a Special Tribunal focused on prosecuting the crime of aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan treated for eye ailment then sent back to prison
stories.summary: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan received treatment for an eye ailment before being returned to prison. His supporters and family have expressed concerns about his medical care and demanded the presence of loved ones during procedures.

stories.title: UAE leaves OPEC and OPEC+ in huge blow to global oil producers' group
stories.summary: The UAE announced its withdrawal from both OPEC and OPEC+, criticizing fellow Arab states for insufficient support against Iranian attacks during the regional war. The move represents a significant blow to the oil cartel's unity.

stories.title: US Supreme Court hears claims Cisco aided Chinese human rights abuses
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court heard arguments on Tuesday in a lawsuit brought by members of the Falun Gong spiritual movement accusing Cisco Systems of facilitating religious persecution in China. The case carries broad implications for human rights litigation in American courts.

stories.title: UK PM Starmer avoids parliament probe over Epstein associate Peter Mandelson
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer survived a parliamentary vote that sought to refer him to a committee investigating whether he misled parliament. The controversy centers on his appointment of Peter Mandelson, a former associate of Jeffrey Epstein, as envoy to the United States.

stories.title: Charles on a mission: Can king's state visit salvage US-UK ties?
stories.summary: King Charles III is delivering a speech to the U.S. Congress emphasizing British-American unity and democratic values during a four-day state visit. The address comes at a time of significant divisions between the UK and the U.S. over the war in Iran, tariffs, and other issues.

stories.title: Insurgents reshaping Mali: Tuaregs seek autonomy, jihadists pursue caliphate across Sahel
stories.summary: Analysts describe the insurgency in Mali as a reconfiguration of authority across the Sahel, with Tuareg rebels seeking autonomy and jihadist groups like JNIM pursuing a broader caliphate. Nina Wilen of the Egmont Institute noted that recent coordinated attacks show insurgents can strike at the heart of the Malian state.

stories.title: As war nears two months, displaced Lebanese family sinks into despair
stories.summary: A displaced Lebanese family is enduring deteriorating conditions in makeshift tents as the war in the region approaches its two-month mark. The family's situation highlights the growing humanitarian toll of the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: US soldier pleads not guilty to charges of betting on Nicolás Maduro’s ouster
stories.summary: U.S. Army soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke, 38, pleaded not guilty in a Manhattan federal court to fraud charges alleging he used insider information to win $400,000 by betting on the removal of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro on the prediction platform Polymarket.

stories.title: Which other countries have left OPEC as the UAE announces exit?
stories.summary: The UAE announced its departure from OPEC following decades of membership. Several other countries have previously left the oil cartel at various points in its history.

stories.title: Which other counties have left OPEC as the UAE announces exit?
stories.summary: The UAE announced its departure from OPEC on Tuesday after decades of membership, joining a list of countries that have previously left the oil cartel. The decision raises questions about the future cohesion of the organization amid ongoing energy market disruptions.

stories.title: General Syrotenko: Engineering troops favor remote mining
stories.summary: General Syrotenko of Ukraine's engineering troops stated that forces are prioritizing remote mining operations using unmanned aerial vehicles and ground-based robotic systems to strengthen battlefield defenses.

stories.title: IDF blows up 2 vast Hezbollah attack tunnels built with ‘direct guidance’ from Iran
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces demolished two large Hezbollah attack tunnels in Qantara, southern Lebanon, using 450 tons of explosives. The underground systems spanned two kilometers and reached depths of 25 meters, and were reportedly built with direct guidance from Iran.

stories.title: UN official warns Gaza faces 'ongoing' deadly Israeli strikes
stories.summary: UN Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Khiari told the Security Council that Gaza continues to endure deadly Israeli strikes alongside severe humanitarian conditions, with approximately 1.8 million people displaced and dependent on aid. He also warned that Israeli violence and settlement expansion in the West Bank are undermining prospects for a political solution.

stories.title: From exile to judge: Symbolism in Syria’s trial of Assad, former officials
stories.summary: In Syria, Judge al-Aryan—who was once sentenced to death under the Assad government—is now presiding over the trial of former President Assad and other officials. The case carries deep symbolism for Syria's transitional justice process, though observers note that broader accountability efforts remain far from complete.

stories.title: Leaked footage 'shows last days' of Syria's Sednaya Prison
stories.summary: Footage purportedly showing the interior of Syria's notorious Sednaya Prison during its final days under the Assad regime has surfaced online. The leaked material has raised questions about the fate of large quantities of missing evidence from the facility.

stories.title: Who are the Iraqi faction leaders wanted by the US?
stories.summary: The United States issued bounties for two Iran-aligned faction leaders in Iraq, accusing their groups of carrying out attacks on American interests in Iraq and Syria. The move targets senior figures within militias closely tied to Tehran.

stories.title: Kremlin Calls for Stability in Mali as Rebels Seize Kidal and Target Capital
stories.summary: The Kremlin called for stability in Mali as rebel forces seized the city of Kidal and advanced toward the capital. Moscow acknowledged it did not know the current status or whereabouts of Mali's military junta leader Assimi Goïta.

stories.title: US seeks to accelerate deportations of migrant children in custody, CNN reports
stories.summary: April 28 - The U.S. administration is bringing forward immigration hearings for deportations of migrant children in custody by weeks or even months in a bid to accelerate the process, CNN reported on

stories.title: King Charles prepares speech on 'reconciliation and renewal' to US Congress after White House welcome
stories.summary: King Charles III is set to address a joint session of the U.S. Congress on April 28, focusing on themes of reconciliation and renewal in the U.S.-UK relationship, 250 years after American independence. The speech follows a formal military welcome at the White House hosted by President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Ukraine tracking multiple ships carrying Russian-stolen grain as Israel dispute expands to Egypt and Algeria
stories.summary: Ukraine says it is tracking multiple ships carrying grain it alleges was stolen by Russia, as the dispute has expanded to involve Israel, Egypt, and Algeria. Kyiv is compiling information on the vessels and associated entities while continuing diplomatic protests over previous deliveries.

stories.title: Why Iran Isn’t Blinking Yet
stories.summary: Iran continues to withstand pressure from President Trump's blockade strategy, which aims to force shutdowns at Iranian oil fields. Analysts note that Tehran has experience enduring economic pressure campaigns from previous rounds of sanctions.

stories.title: Iran bans steel exports after war damage to industry and strikes
stories.summary: Iran has banned steel exports following significant war damage to its industrial infrastructure, including airstrikes that hit production facilities. The ban comes as the country faces deepening economic pressure from sanctions and rising inflation.

stories.title: The Hormuz digital chokepoint: How does the Iran war threaten subsea cables? - explainer
stories.summary: An explainer examined how the Iran conflict threatens subsea cables near the Strait of Hormuz. These fiber-optic and electrical cables on the sea floor carry approximately 99% of global internet traffic.

stories.title: Foreign Ministry: Israel has received multiple shipments of stolen Ukrainian grain
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry stated that Israel has received more than two shipments of agricultural products illegally exported by Russia from temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories.

stories.title: Ghana rejects proposed US health aid deal, citing data concerns, source says
stories.summary: DAKAR, April 28 - Ghana has rejected a bilateral health deal with the U.S., a source familiar with the negotiations told Reuters, the latest stumbling block to the Trump administration's effort to ove

stories.title: Police open investigation into Golders Green memorial wall arson
stories.summary: London police opened an investigation into an arson attack on a memorial wall in Golders Green. Counter Terrorism Policing London is leading the probe, though the incident is not currently being treated as terrorism. No arrests have been made.

stories.title: IRGC shores up wartime power in Iran, blunting supreme leader’s role
stories.summary: Analysts assess that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has consolidated wartime decision-making power, diminishing the role of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Experts describe the IRGC-dominated deliberations as painfully slow, yielding an uncompromising stance in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita reappears in Bamako after weekend attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita reappeared publicly in Bamako on Tuesday after being absent since large-scale jihadist-separatist attacks over the weekend. His office said he met with the Russian ambassador to Mali during the appearance.

stories.title: Virginia Giuffre’s brother criticizes King Charles III for not meeting survivors of Epstein abuse
stories.summary: Sky Roberts, brother of the late Virginia Giuffre, criticized King Charles III for not meeting with survivors of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse during the king's U.S. state visit. Roberts said survivors were meeting with members of Congress and still fighting for accountability, while powerful figures connected to the abuse remained out of reach.

stories.title: UK probe attack on London memorial to Iranians
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are investigating a suspected arson attack on a memorial wall in Golders Green dedicated to Iranians. The incident occurred amid rising tensions and related episodes across the British capital.

stories.title: Iran uses improvised oil storage to avoid damage to oil facilities amid blockade - report
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly using improvised oil storage solutions to cope with a blockade threatening its oil infrastructure. The country's extraction and refining systems cannot be easily shut down, with Kharg Island facilities at risk of failure if oil flow is interrupted.

stories.title: UAE says Opec exit aligns with long-term energy strategy
