stories.summary: Gaza's post-ceasefire death toll has reached 818 after a boy was killed by Israeli forces in Khan Younis. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers set fire to a Palestinian home as settler violence continued.

stories.title: Plane crash in South Sudan kills 14
stories.summary: A plane crash near Juba, South Sudan, killed 14 people. Bad weather is reported to have been a contributing factor, underscoring ongoing aviation safety and infrastructure challenges in the country.

stories.title: BYD, China’s EV king, posts a 55% slump in first-quarter profit
stories.summary: BYD, China's largest electric vehicle maker, reported a 55 per cent year-on-year decline in first-quarter net profit to approximately 4.09 billion yuan (US$590 million). Revenue fell 11.8 per cent to 150.2 billion yuan, as weakness in the domestic Chinese market offset rising exports.

stories.title: Europe makes mistake regarding war in Ukraine back in 2022, says Estonian president
stories.summary: Estonian President Alar Karis said Europe missed an opportunity to begin peace talks with Moscow at the start of the full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022, calling it a strategic mistake.

stories.title: Lapid to be allocated 10 out of top 24 mandates in Together Party's Knesset list, sources tell KAN
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid have agreed that Lapid's Yesh Atid party will receive 10 of the top 24 spots on their joint Together Party Knesset list, with provisions enabling the factions to split after the election.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russian oil refinery causes major fire, officials say
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike caused a large-scale fire at the Rosneft-owned Tuapse oil refinery on Russia's Black Sea coast on Tuesday, prompting evacuations of nearby buildings. The refinery had already halted operations since April 16 following a previous drone attack. Kyiv has intensified strikes on Russian infrastructure since March.

stories.title: Google breaks ground on AI megahub in India
stories.summary:
Tech giant Google on Tuesday marked the ceremonial start of work on its largest artificial intelligence hub outside of the United States with a groundbreaking ceremony in India.
The firm promised in O

stories.title: How a surgeon kept a Sudan hospital functioning on the war’s front line
stories.summary: Dr. Jamal Eltaeb led Al Nao hospital in Omdurman, near Khartoum, keeping it operational as control of the area shifted between the Sudanese army and paramilitary Rapid Support Forces fighters on the war's front line.

stories.title: Russia is killing journalists and jailing them as “terrorists,” Ukraine tells UN
stories.summary: Ukraine's delegation to the United Nations reported that at least 26 Ukrainian media workers are being held in Russian captivity and 147 have been killed since the full-scale invasion began. Ukraine accused Russia of killing journalists and jailing them on terrorism charges.

stories.title: White House to review presidential security; spotlight on line of succession
stories.summary: The White House announced a review of presidential security following a foiled attack at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents Association Dinner, an event attended by several cabinet secretaries, raising questions about the presidential line of succession.

stories.title: Authorities Order Evacuations Following Third Ukrainian Strike on Tuapse Refinery
stories.summary: Authorities ordered evacuations following a third Ukrainian strike on the Tuapse refinery. Separately, at least three people were killed in overnight attacks on Russia's Belgorod region.

stories.title: Displaced women in Lebanon face period poverty amid Israel's war
stories.summary: Women displaced by Israeli military operations across Lebanon are struggling to access menstrual hygiene supplies. The situation highlights a hidden crisis of poverty, stigma, and neglect among displaced populations.

stories.title: Amnesty calls for US strike on Yemen to be investigated as war crime
stories.summary: Amnesty International called for an investigation into a U.S. airstrike on a migrant detention facility in Yemen, which killed at least 68 people, arguing it may constitute a war crime.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Budget airlines first to cut flights as jet fuel prices soar
stories.summary: Budget airlines began cutting flights as jet fuel prices surged amid the Israel-Iran war, while US and Iranian officials clashed over Tehran's nuclear program at a UN review of the atomic treaty. Iran's foreign minister praised Russia's diplomatic support.

stories.title: U.S. Trade Representative's Office to hear investigations on Trump’s new import taxes
stories.summary: The U.S. Trade Representative's Office scheduled hearings on new temporary import taxes that President Trump imposed after the Supreme Court struck down his preferred tariffs in February.

stories.title: BP reports huge profit rise in first quarter amid Iran war
stories.summary: BP reported a significant rise in first-quarter profits driven by higher oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict. Strong trading performance and market volatility also contributed to the surge.

stories.title: Russians attack infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih again; one person injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine, for the second time in one morning, injuring one person in the attack.

stories.title: How the US-Israeli war is collapsing the sanctions regime on Iran
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran is undermining international sanctions enforcement on Tehran. Analysts note that circumvention mechanisms already exist and the conflict is encouraging more entities to exploit them.

stories.title: Mapping the destruction: How Israel ‘wiped out’ Lebanon’s Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: An Al Jazeera visual investigation mapped systematic demolition of the Lebanese border town of Bint Jbeil by Israeli forces, drawing comparisons to the devastation seen in Gaza.

stories.title: When will Strait of Hormuz be ‘safe’ for commercial shipping again?
stories.summary: Analysts warn that even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens to commercial shipping, insurance costs could rise to 20 times pre-war levels, posing lasting economic consequences for global trade.

stories.title: ‘Back to what he used to be’: Babar Azam’s unlearning journey
stories.summary: Pakistan cricket captain Babar Azam trained at the Hanif Mohammad High-Performance Centre in Karachi ahead of Peshawar Zalmi's HBL Pakistan Super League qualifier against Islamabad United, with observers noting a return to his earlier batting form.

stories.title: Mossad chief says agency’s operations penetrated ‘core’ of Iran, Lebanon secrets
stories.summary: Mossad Director David Barnea stated that the agency's operations penetrated the "core" of Iranian and Lebanese intelligence secrets. He commended ten operations for outstanding achievements in 2025 and highlighted enhanced cooperation with the Israeli military.

stories.title: Sydney concert to benefit Bondi terror victims canceled after choir opposes singing with Jewish group
stories.summary: A planned benefit concert in Sydney for Bondi terror victims was canceled after more than half of the Australian Hellenic Choir voted against performing alongside the Sydney Jewish Choral Society, prompting accusations of antisemitism.

stories.title: Mexican cartel leader found hiding in a ditch
stories.summary: Mexican authorities captured Audias Flores Silva, a key leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, who was found hiding in a ditch. His arrest comes approximately two months after the cartel's top leader was killed.

stories.title: 'Firmly committed' to Iran-US peace, Pakistan tells UN Security Council
stories.summary: Pakistan's UN representative Asim Iftikhar Ahmad told the Security Council that Islamabad remains committed to a peaceful resolution of the US-Iran conflict, warning that the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz could trigger severe global economic and security consequences.

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi says US requested new round of talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stated that the United States has requested a new round of talks with Tehran. Reports indicate Trump is dissatisfied with Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while postponing nuclear discussions.

stories.title: Shelling causes new power outages in three regions, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Russian shelling caused power outages across three Ukrainian regions as of the morning of April 27. The Sumy region was the hardest hit, with additional outages reported in the Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv regions, according to Ukrenergo.

stories.title: Why Moody’s has raised China’s credit outlook amid Iran war shocks
stories.summary: Moody's Ratings upgraded China's sovereign credit outlook from "negative" to "stable," signalling increased confidence in the world's second-largest economy. The move came amid energy shocks from the US-Israel war in Iran and broader concerns about the global economic trajectory. Moody's had previously downgraded China's sovereign rating from Aa3 to A1 in 2017.

stories.title: Energy security comes first for Indonesia as it defies EU over Russian oil
stories.summary: Indonesia is proceeding with plans to import 150 million barrels of Russian oil despite new EU sanctions targeting the Karimun Oil Terminal in Indonesia for alleged connections to Russia's shadow fleet and circumvention of the oil price cap. The European Commission announced the sanctions as part of its 20th package of measures against Russia.

stories.title: China upgrades maritime rescue range and depth as ambitions on high seas expand
stories.summary: China's maritime rescue authorities have expanded their deep-sea search and rescue capabilities beyond 4,000 metres, according to state media outlet People's Daily. The Nanhai Rescue Bureau, responsible for operations in China's southern waters, credited the development of high-tech equipment for enabling practical operations at such depths.

stories.title: Middle East crisis could cost world $1tn while oil firms make ‘obscene’ profit, analysis finds
stories.summary: An analysis cited by climate campaigners estimates the Middle East oil and gas crisis could impose up to $1 trillion in additional costs on the global economy. Petroleum companies are reportedly earning substantial profits from elevated fuel prices. Campaigners called for urgent windfall taxes at a conference in Colombia.

stories.title: African cotton: Governments step back in as markets falter
stories.summary: The cotton sector across the CFA franc zone is undergoing major restructuring. Mali faces a sharply weaker season, Benin has recorded a record year, and Burkina Faso has moved toward nationalisation, as governments intervene amid falling global cotton prices.

stories.title: Hong Kong urged to shift focus from tourist numbers to increasing spending
stories.summary: Researchers from Hong Kong Polytechnic University and consultancy Think China urged Hong Kong to prioritise increasing tourist spending over boosting visitor numbers. Their preliminary findings show mainland Chinese visitor arrivals have recovered to about 88 per cent of pre-pandemic 2018 levels, but high-income travellers are spending less and adopting more selective consumption habits.

stories.title: Is capitalism fuelling today’s wars? Varsha Gandikota & Jason Hickel
stories.summary: Political economist Jason Hickel and Varsha Gandikota-Nellutla discussed whether capitalism drives modern conflicts and whether Global South nations can reclaim sovereignty in the current global order.

stories.title: Mossad head Barnea highlights operational capabilities, strategic success against Iran, Hezbollah
stories.summary: Mossad Director David Barnea praised the agency's operational capabilities during a citation ceremony, highlighting what he described as strategic successes in operations against Iran and Hezbollah carried out in target countries.

stories.title: Mikhail Piotrovsky runs Russia’s Hermitage Museum. EU just sanctioned him for legitimizing Russia’s occupation of Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Union sanctioned Mikhail Piotrovsky, director of Russia's Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg, for his role in legitimizing Russia's occupation of Ukraine.

stories.title: Austria Islamic State man admits plot on Taylor Swift concert in Vienna
stories.summary: A man accused of pledging allegiance to Islamic State and plotting an attack on Taylor Swift's Vienna concerts in August 2024 pleaded guilty as his trial began on Tuesday in Austria. Austrian authorities had cancelled Swift's three scheduled Eras Tour performances after the plot was thwarted.

stories.title: Mali reeling after coordinated attacks expose security cracks
stories.summary: Mali faced widespread instability after coordinated attacks by jihadist fighters and rebel groups resulted in the seizure of multiple towns and military bases over the weekend, exposing significant security vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Turkish Airlines: Rising fuel costs and regional conflict force African retreat
stories.summary: Turkish Airlines is suspending routes to 10 African destinations after a decade of expansion on the continent. Rising fuel costs and regional geopolitical conflicts are cited as the primary factors driving the retreat.

stories.title: US startups explore genome editing in human embryos, raising ethical concerns
stories.summary: A press review covered multiple global stories, including US startups exploring genome editing in human embryos, raising ethical concerns. Other topics included photos of starving soldiers in Ukraine, the controversial Alloncle report on French public broadcasting, and President Trump's renewed call to fire talk show host Jimmy Kimmel.

stories.title: Military base in Crimea, where Russia stores Iskander missiles, catches fire following a nighttime attack
stories.summary: A military base in Russian-occupied Crimea used to store Iskander operational-tactical missile systems caught fire following a nighttime attack on April 27–28.

stories.title: Mali: Rebels Now in Control of Key Mali Town After Attacks
stories.summary: Jihadist and Tuareg separatist forces seized control of the key northern Malian town of Kidal following coordinated attacks on military junta positions across the country, according to local sources and an ally of the local governor.

stories.title: King Charles to promote British-US unity in speech to Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III is scheduled to address the US Congress with a speech emphasizing British-American unity, shared values, and global security cooperation, amid ongoing tensions related to the Iran conflict and transatlantic defense ties.

stories.title: Israel orders Lebanese to flee over a dozen towns and villages
stories.summary: Israel's military ordered residents in more than a dozen towns and villages in southern Lebanon to evacuate northward immediately, citing Hezbollah's violation of a ceasefire agreement. Israeli artillery and air strikes on southern Lebanon have continued despite a ceasefire signed on April 16.

stories.title: Trump not happy with latest Iran proposal to end the war, U.S. official says
stories.summary: A US official said President Trump was dissatisfied with Iran's latest proposal to end the war, as oil prices continued to climb in early Asia trading on April 28, 2026, reflecting the distance between the two sides in negotiations.

stories.title: The cost for Ukraine of Trump’s deal with Lukeshenka
stories.summary: Three rounds of US sanctions relief over six months freed more than 400 prisoners and partially reopened Belarus's financial system as part of a Trump-Lukashenko deal. However, the Belarusian regime continues to support Russia's war effort in Ukraine, raising questions about the cost to Kyiv.

stories.title: The evolving China-Pakistan space cooperation
stories.summary: The article examines the evolving space cooperation between China and Pakistan, framing it as an extension of their longstanding "all-weather" strategic partnership.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 28 – Untangling the Iran-Russia-Hezbollah web
stories.summary: Mideast expert Ksenia Svetlova analyzed the Tehran-Moscow-Hezbollah relationship and assessed that Gulf states face a critical juncture as they plan for the possibility of a nuclear-armed Iran.

stories.title: What does a $1 billion default look like? In Ukraine, it looks like six new sleeper cars.
stories.summary: Ukraine's state rail operator, which has defaulted on its debt, introduced six new sleeper cars despite ongoing destruction of its rolling stock. Russia is reportedly destroying rail carriages at a rate approximately forty times faster than Ukraine can build replacements.

stories.title: Iran Is More Unified Than Ever
stories.summary: Analysts argue that the war with the US and Israel has deepened unity among Iranian officials and strengthened connections between the government and the public. The conflict has reportedly consolidated internal cohesion across Iran's political and security establishment.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Patriot systems are on a “starvation ration,” Air Force spox says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson stated that Ukraine's Patriot air defense systems are operating on a "starvation ration" of interceptors. Russia fired more than 700 missiles at Ukraine over the past winter, a significant portion of which were ballistic missiles.

stories.title: Sudan: Darfur - Two Decades On, a New Generation of Children Faces 'Horrific Violence'
stories.summary: A UN report warned that children in Sudan's Darfur region face a renewed cycle of violence, hunger, and displacement two decades after the conflict first drew international attention. The agency said the current crisis is receiving insufficient global notice.

stories.title: Russians strike infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, one person killed, five wounded
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck an infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk region, killing one man and wounding five others.

stories.title: Security fears mount for Ghana’s border economy after convoy attack
stories.summary: Three civilians were killed in an attack on a military-escorted convoy along the Bawku-Bolgatanga corridor in northern Ghana. The corridor is a key commercial route linking Accra with Burkina Faso and Togo, and the incident has heightened security concerns for the border economy.

stories.title: Israel's policy of endless war is fuelled by the crisis of Zionism
stories.summary: An opinion piece by Andrew Hammond argues that Israel's pursuit of continuous military campaigns is driven by internal insecurity and a crisis within Zionism, contending the approach has failed to achieve regional stability or hegemony.

stories.title: Hafiz Saeed's close aide and key LeT figure Sheikh Yousaf Afridi shot dead in Pakistan
stories.summary: Sheikh Yousaf Afridi, a close aide to Hafiz Saeed and key figure in the Lashkar-e-Taiba militant group, was shot dead in Pakistan. Afridi reportedly played a role in recruitment and coordination of the group's activities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: Tel Aviv’s ‘Open Houses’ offers fresh peek at private and public spaces
stories.summary: Tel Aviv's annual 'Batim Mibifnim' (Homes from the Inside) event, which opens private and public spaces to visitors, begins registration on May 1.

stories.title: Iraq names little-known banker Ali al-Zaidi as PM after five-month deadlock
stories.summary: Iraq named Ali al-Zaidi, a little-known banker, as prime minister-designate following a five-month political deadlock. Reports suggest al-Zaidi was a largely unknown figure whom Iraq's political factions settled on as a compromise candidate.

stories.title: Attack against Ghana military convoy kills three civilians
stories.summary: A military-escorted civilian convoy in northern Ghana was attacked on Monday, killing three civilians and injuring one, according to the Ghana Armed Forces.

stories.title: French researcher cracks 4,000-year-old Elamite script from Iran
stories.summary: French archaeologist François Desset has made significant progress in deciphering Linear Elamite, a 4,000-year-old script from what is now Iran that has long eluded researchers. His work has drawn comparisons to Jean-François Champollion, who deciphered ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics in the 19th century.

stories.title: Who is Iyad Ag Ghali, Mali’s most wanted man?
stories.summary: Iyad Ag Ghali, leader of the al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM (Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin), is Mali's most wanted man. His organization, allied with Tuareg separatists, carried out the largest coordinated attack in Mali in over a decade. French forces, Malian authorities, and Russian mercenaries have all failed to capture him.

stories.title: Starmer says 'people might change their habits' because of Iran war
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer warned that the ongoing war on Iran could affect everyday life in the UK, suggesting people might need to alter their supermarket purchases and holiday plans depending on the conflict's duration and economic impact.

stories.title: Ukraine doubled all of 2025’s interceptor drones in just four months, minister says
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said Ukraine doubled its entire 2025 output of interceptor drones in just four months. The Defense Procurement Agency scaled deliveries through three parallel channels, including a weapons marketplace.

stories.title: Araghchi visit highlights Iran-Russia coordination during US-Iran conflict tensions - analysis
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met with Russian President Putin in Moscow, underscoring Tehran's efforts to secure Russian support amid stalled negotiations with the United States and ongoing uncertainty over the Iran-Israel conflict.

stories.title: Budget airlines first to cut flights as jet fuel prices soar
stories.summary: Ryanair, Transavia, Volotea and other low-cost airlines are feeling the financial pain from high jet fuel prices as a result of the Middle East war and are cutting flights. Transavia, the lowcost airl

stories.title: India, New Zealand boost trade diversification with ‘forward-looking’ pact
stories.summary:
A free-trade agreement signed between India and New Zealand has marked yet another regional push towards diversification and away from overdependence on major powers.
The deal, which comes after 15 ye

stories.title: Need for speed: China’s EV, battery makers race to cut charging times to under 10 minutes
stories.summary: Battery makers and electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers have seized on the Beijing Auto Show to showcase technologies promising shorter charging times in a race triggered by BYD and Contemporary Ampere

stories.title: Chinese man supports 6 siblings while parents want more kids, say it boosts chance of success
stories.summary:
A 21-year-old man from central China, whose greatest wish is for his parents to stop having more children, sells pork to support his six younger siblings.
In April, Sun Pan, from Shaoyang in Hunan pro

stories.title: Drones attack oil refinery in Tuapse again
stories.summary: Drones attacked the oil refinery in Tuapse, in Russia's Krasnodar region, on Monday night, igniting a fire at the facility's tank farm in yet another strike on the site.

stories.title: Germany's Merz 'disillusioned' with US and Israel over Iran
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed disillusionment with the United States and Israel over the war on Iran, noting that early promises of a swift resolution had not materialized. Merz called for independent European ideas on resolving the conflict.

stories.title: Fact check: Cloud seeding didn't make it rain in Iran
stories.summary: Social media claims that the destruction of a climate research center in the UAE caused heavy rainfall in Iran have been debunked. Fact-checkers found the claims linking cloud seeding to the precipitation were misleading.

stories.title: 600 Google staff urge CEO to reject classified US military AI contract
stories.summary: Approximately 600 Google employees signed a letter urging CEO Sundar Pichai to reject a classified US military artificial intelligence contract. The employees argued that safeguards proposed by Google are unenforceable under Pentagon policy.

stories.title: Ex-Foreign Office chief says Mandelson’s appointment raised more red flags than any other he oversaw - UK politics live
stories.summary: Philip Barton tells committee he thought Mandelson’s Epstein links were ‘potentially difficult’ but he was not consulted in decisionQ: Was there pressure on you to approve Mandelson’s vetting?This is

stories.title: Gaza's injured women forced to rebuild lives amid genocide
stories.summary: Women in Gaza who lost limbs during Israeli military strikes are struggling to rebuild their lives and care for their families. They face severe poverty and a lack of adequate medical support amid the ongoing crisis.

stories.title: Pity the poor man’s Rambo
stories.summary: The article is a cultural commentary drawing parallels between the Hollywood Rambo franchise and American military interventions, referencing the Indian film Dhurandhar.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF destroys over 1,000 Hezbollah terror sites in southern Lebanon, seizing weapons
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces announced it dismantled more than 1,000 Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon, seizing a wide range of weapons the group had allegedly planned to use against Israeli soldiers.

stories.title: First LNG shipment since Iran war began appears to exit Hormuz
stories.summary: The first liquefied natural gas shipment since the start of the Iran conflict has apparently transited the Strait of Hormuz. The tanker Mubaraz was tracked passing the southern tip of India, according to ship-tracking data.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 95 of 123 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 95 of 123 Russian drones launched against Ukraine since the evening of April 27.

stories.title: Google signs Pentagon deal to provide AI models for classified government work
stories.summary: Google signed a contract with the U.S. Pentagon to supply artificial intelligence models for classified government work. The Defense Department is seeking to maintain flexibility in how AI is applied to defense, despite concerns from tech developers about using unreliable AI in weapons systems.

stories.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz if US lifts its blockade and the war ends
stories.summary: Iran offered to end its chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz if the US lifts its blockade on the country and ends the war in a proposal that would postpone discussions on the Islamic Republic's nuclear p

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran says it needs guarantees against attacks before Gulf can be stable
stories.summary: Tehran’s UN envoy says ‘full respect’ of Iran’s rights also key for lasting regional stabilityUS is being ‘humiliated’ by Iran’s leadership, says Friedrich MerzThe White House said on Monday it was ex

stories.title: The other life of US soldier accused of betting on Maduro's removal
stories.summary: A US Army officer charged with using classified information to win $400,000 by betting on Venezuelan President Maduro's removal also operates as a real estate investor. He reportedly maintained Airbnb properties with highly positive guest reviews.

stories.title: UN expresses 'deep concern' over Mali attacks, calls for international assistance
stories.summary: The United Nations Secretary-General expressed "deep concern" over weekend attacks in Mali and called for international assistance to address the escalating violence.

stories.title: Lebanon health ministry says Israeli strikes kill 4 in south despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry said Israeli strikes on the country's south on Monday killed four people including a woman and wounded 51 others, three of them children, despite a ceasefire between Israel a

stories.title: Congressmen call for National Guard to address drone threat at World Cup
stories.summary: Several US congressmen have called for the deployment of the National Guard and immediate interagency coordination to secure airspace over the 11 American host cities for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, citing concerns about potential drone threats.

The report found that Israeli military operations damaged 5,000 hectares of forest cover and reshaped southern Lebanon's physical and ecological landscape.

stories.title: Calls for ‘student premium’ to support disadvantaged young people after GCSEs
stories.summary: A coalition of 14 social mobility organisations in the UK is urging the government to create a "student premium" to support disadvantaged young people after age 16. They warn that a post-16 funding gap risks young people falling out of education, employment, and training.

stories.title: The next Knesset should belong to those who choose to serve - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argued that the next Knesset should prioritize representatives from communities that serve Israel, framing mandatory service as a nonpartisan Zionist principle.

stories.title: Iran oil shipments plunge as Hormuz blockade tightens, data shows
stories.summary: Iranian oil shipments have fallen sharply as the Strait of Hormuz blockade tightens, according to Kpler data cited by the Wall Street Journal. Analysts warn Iran's crude production could drop to around 1.2–1.3 million barrels per day by mid-May if restrictions persist.

stories.title: Philippines’ Sara Duterte hits back against wealth allegations as impeachment looms
stories.summary: Philippine Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio and her spouse are pushing back against allegations of ill-gotten wealth as the House of Representatives prepares to submit Articles of Impeachment to the Senate, potentially by early May.

stories.title: Doctor arrested on suspicion of threatening Channel 12 journalist Mohammad Magadli
stories.summary: A 40-year-old doctor from northern Israel was arrested on suspicion of repeatedly threatening Channel 12 journalist Mohammad Magadli by phone from an unknown number.

stories.title: Hong Kong adds spared Wang Fuk Court block to resettlement plan as most opt to sell
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government will include Wang Chi House — the only block undamaged in the November 26 Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po that killed 168 people — in its resettlement plan after three-quarters of homeowners indicated they preferred to sell their flats to authorities. The block had originally been excluded from long-term resettlement proposals.

stories.title: Video: Iran’s UN envoy says Tehran ‘not bound’ by UN Law of the Sea
stories.summary: Iran's UN envoy Amir Saeid Iravani declared that Tehran is 'not bound' by the UN Law of the Sea and defended Iran's maritime actions in the Strait of Hormuz. He accused some nations of 'double standards' regarding the US-imposed maritime blockade.

stories.title: U.S., Iran clash over Tehran's nuclear programme as review of atomic treaty begins at UN
stories.summary: The United States and Iran clashed over Tehran's nuclear programme as a review of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty opened at the United Nations. Russia's Ambassador-at-Large Andrey Belousov objected to singling out Iran, calling the criticism politicisation and expressing hope it would not derail the conference.

stories.title: Top Jalisco cartel leader 'El Jardinero' arrested in Mexico, minister says
stories.summary: Mexican special forces arrested Audias Flores, known as "El Jardinero," a top commander of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, in the western state of Nayarit. Security Minister Omar García Harfuch announced the operation on Monday.

stories.title: China’s Politburo steps up policy response as Iran war shakes global economy
stories.summary: China's Politburo pledged a holistic policy response to external shocks from the US-Israel war on Iran, emphasizing energy security, technological self-reliance, and control over industrial supply chains. The meeting, led by President Xi Jinping, addressed the conflict's widening impact on the global economy.

stories.title: Trump fires independent board overseeing National Science Foundation
stories.summary: The Trump administration fired members of the National Science Board, which independently oversees the National Science Foundation. Board members received an email from the Presidential Personnel Office stating their positions were terminated effective immediately, a move critics called a dangerous attack on US innovation.

stories.title: Around 20,000 seafarers stranded in Persian Gulf as Hormuz stays shut despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 seafarers, mostly from India, remain stranded in the Persian Gulf as the Strait of Hormuz stays shut despite a ceasefire. The mariners have endured missile blasts and food shortages since the Iran war began two months ago.

stories.title: Asean’s natural leader, Bali on edge over Japanese earthquake: 7 Asia highlights
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post highlighted seven Asia stories from the past week, including Indonesia ceding its role as ASEAN's natural leader to Singapore, concerns in Bali over a potential magnitude-9 megathrust earthquake following a Japanese quake, and a deadly Japanese Type 10 tank explosion that killed three.

stories.title: Oil prices rise despite Iran’s proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Brent crude prices rose more than 1 percent even as Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for deferring nuclear negotiations.

stories.title: Mexico captures top cartel leader ‘El Jardinero’ hiding in roadside ditch
stories.summary: Mexican military forces captured Audias Flores Silva, known as "El Jardinero," a top regional commander of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), in northwestern Mexico. He was considered a possible successor to the cartel's recently killed leader. The United States had offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest.

stories.title: Supply shock from Iran war drives electronics component prices up globally
stories.summary: Supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran have sharply increased global prices of printed circuit boards, Reuters reported. An Iranian strike on the Jubail petrochemical complex halted production of high-purity polyphenylene ether resin, which accounts for about 70 percent of global supply.

stories.title: US challenges Iran’s role in UN nuclear talks, Tehran rejects accusations
stories.summary: The US and Iran clashed at a UN conference reviewing the Non-Proliferation Treaty after Tehran was selected as a vice president of the meeting. Washington called the move an 'insult,' accusing Iran of failing its nuclear obligations. Iran rejected the accusations.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump not happy with Iran's latest peace proposal, US official says
stories.summary: A US official said President Trump is unhappy with Iran's latest peace proposal, which would set aside Iran's nuclear programme until the war ends and shipping disputes through the Strait of Hormuz are resolved. Washington and Tehran remain in a standoff over the critical waterway through which a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas normally passes.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Marian Marinica Resigns As Warriors Head Coach
stories.summary: Zimbabwe's senior men's national football team head coach Marian Marinica has resigned from his position, as confirmed by the Zimbabwe Football Association (ZIFA).

stories.title: Gambia: Gender Gaps Deepen Climate Crisis As New Report Calls for Urgent Action in Gambia
stories.summary: A study conducted under a Food and Agriculture Organization project found that climate and disaster risks in The Gambia disproportionately affect women due to structural inequalities in access to resources, decision-making, and livelihoods.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Blames Cartels for Attempts to Derail Social Health Authority Rollout
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto accused cartels of attempting to derail the rollout of the Social Health Authority, while asserting that the country is pursuing universal health coverage through legislation designed to outlast political cycles.

stories.title: Mali's PM urges public to remain calm during visit to victims of coordinated attacks
stories.summary: Mali's transitional Prime Minister General Abdoulaye Maiga visited victims of coordinated attacks by jihadi and rebel forces that took place on Saturday and killed the country's defence chief. He urged the public to remain calm.

stories.title: Media freedom ‘under sustained attack’ across EU as public trust drops, report finds
stories.summary: The Civil Liberties Union for Europe reported that media freedom across the EU is under sustained attack, with journalists facing rising harassment, threats, and violence. The report also found increasing concentration of media ownership and declining public trust in news outlets across the bloc.

stories.title: Black gold, dead cattle: The displaced search for answers in Uganda’s oil zone
stories.summary: In Uganda's oil-producing region, the Balaalo herding community lost grazing lands during a 2010 military operation and have been classified as squatters. They remain excluded from the economic benefits of the multi-billion-dollar oil industry that has developed on their former lands.

stories.title: Iran revises Minab school bombing death toll to 155
stories.summary: Iranian state media revised the death toll from a strike on a primary school in Minab to 155 people, including 73 boys and 47 girls. The attack occurred on 28 February, the first day of the war. Teachers, parents, and other staff were also among the dead.

stories.title: Sudan: At Least 7 Dead, UNHCR Aid Vehicle Destroyed in Kordofan and North Darfur Drone Strikes
stories.summary: A UNHCR aid vehicle carrying emergency shelter kits was destroyed by a drone strike near Tawila in North Darfur on April 24, leaving over 1,300 families without shelter. Separately, Rapid Support Forces drone strikes on El Obeid in North Kordofan killed at least seven people and wounded 22 others.

stories.title: Iran oil tankers turned back by US blockade, Hormuz traffic sparse
stories.summary: A US naval blockade has drastically reduced maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, turning back Iranian oil tankers. Daily ship crossings have plummeted from a pre-war average of 125–140 to just seven in the past day.

stories.title: Gunmen kill at least 29 in Nigeria’s northeast Adamawa State
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked Guyaku village in Adamawa State, northeastern Nigeria, killing at least 29 people in an hours-long assault. The regional ISIL affiliate claimed responsibility for the attack.

stories.title: Hong Kong home prices rise higher in March as rents peak for a fifth month straight
stories.summary: Hong Kong's lived-in home prices rose 1.4 percent in March 2026, bringing the first-quarter increase to 4.4 percent, according to official data. Rental prices also continued climbing for a fifth consecutive month. The market showed resilience despite uncertainties linked to the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Bahrain strips more than 60 people of their citizenship over activities linked to Iran
stories.summary: Bahrain revoked the citizenship of 69 individuals after they were convicted of communicating with foreign organizations and glorifying Iranian attacks during a recent conflict.

stories.title: Russian superyacht sails through Strait of Hormuz despite blockade
stories.summary: A 141-meter Russian superyacht linked to a close ally of President Vladimir Putin sailed through the Strait of Hormuz despite the ongoing blockade of the waterway.

stories.title: Compensation to be given to employers of reserve soldiers, Knesset plenum decides
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset plenum approved compensation for employers of reserve soldiers called up for duty. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said a solid economic rear is needed to support the conflict's frontlines.

stories.title: 600 Google staff urge CEO to reject classified military AI contract
stories.summary: Over 600 Google employees signed a letter to CEO Sundar Pichai urging the company to reject a classified military AI contract with the US Department of Defence. The signatories came from divisions including Google DeepMind and Cloud, as the company negotiates deploying its Gemini AI model in classified settings.

stories.title: What Congress Could Do to Stop the War
stories.summary: Congressional Republicans are declining to use their power of the purse to challenge or constrain the ongoing war effort. The article examines what legislative tools Congress could employ to intervene.

stories.title: The Iran War Is Tearing Trump’s Coalition Apart
stories.summary: The US-Israel war on Iran is creating divisions within President Trump's political coalition. The article explores tensions between the broader MAGA movement and the America First foreign policy stance regarding the conflict.

stories.title: Victorian Society publishes list of most endangered buildings in England and Wales
stories.summary: The Victorian Society published its annual list of the 10 most endangered buildings in England and Wales. Sites include the Tees Transporter Bridge in Teesside, a disinfecting station in Hackney, and a former working men's club in Barrow-in-Furness, all at risk of decay or neglect.

stories.title: Israel’s direction poses ‘existential threat’ to Judaism, UK’s leading progressive rabbis warn
stories.summary: Senior UK progressive rabbis Charley Baginsky and Josh Levy warned that Israel's current political direction risks becoming incompatible with Jewish values and poses an existential threat to Judaism. They argued that criticizing the Israeli government is a Jewish obligation, not disloyalty.

stories.title: Rachel Reeves’s fiscal rules buffer should be ‘significantly larger’, say peers
stories.summary: A House of Lords committee recommended that UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves maintain a significantly larger buffer against her fiscal rules, warning that public debt is on an unsustainable trajectory. Some of the current £22 billion headroom established at last year's budget is expected to be eroded by the Iran war's economic impact.

stories.title: Sudan paramilitary leaders acquired £17.7m property portfolio in Dubai, investigation reveals
stories.summary: An investigation found that family members and associates linked to RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti) acquired over 20 luxury properties worth £17.7 million in Dubai. The RSF leadership, accused of genocide in Sudan, reportedly used the UAE as a safe haven for family members and wealth.

stories.title: Nobel laureate biochemist Hartmut Michel joins Jilin University in China
stories.summary: German Nobel laureate Hartmut Michel, 77, who shared the 1988 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on photosynthesis, has joined Jilin University in Changchun, northeastern China, as a full-time professor. He will be based at the university's First Hospital as part of its talent recruitment strategy.

stories.title: Trump unhappy Iranian proposal does not address nuclear program, US official says
stories.summary: A US official said President Trump is unhappy that Iran's proposal does not address its nuclear program. Iranian sources had indicated the proposal would set aside nuclear discussions until the war ends and Gulf shipping disputes are resolved.

stories.title: Mexican military captures cartel commander Audias Flores
stories.summary: The Mexican military captured cartel commander Audias Flores and released footage of the operation that led to his apprehension.

stories.title: Araghchi says region in ‘major flux’ after talks in Russia
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X that he was pleased to engage with Russia 'at the highest level' amid regional instability. He described the strategic partnership between Tehran and Moscow as deepening through recent events.

stories.title: Kremlin says Putin received message from Iran’s new supreme leader
stories.summary: The Kremlin said Russian President Vladimir Putin received a message from Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Putin conveyed his appreciation during a meeting in St. Petersburg with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and praised Iran's defense of its sovereignty.

stories.title: Mexico’s Jalisco drug cartel commander ‘El Jardinero’ found hiding in ditch
stories.summary: Mexican Navy special forces apprehended Jalisco New Generation Cartel commander known as 'El Jardinero,' who was found hiding in a ditch. Authorities said no shots were fired during the operation.

stories.title: 'Looming' risk of nuclear arms race, UN meeting hears
stories.summary: A UN meeting on nuclear non-proliferation heard warnings of a 'looming' risk of a nuclear arms race. Amid heightened global geopolitical tensions, expectations for concrete outcomes from the gathering at UN headquarters remained uncertain.

stories.title: Brent rises above $108 amid ongoing tensions
stories.summary: Brent crude rose to approximately $108.68 per barrel, marking a seventh consecutive session of gains. US West Texas Intermediate also climbed to around $96.96. Ongoing supply concerns around the Strait of Hormuz and stalled US-Iran diplomacy drove the increases.

stories.title: Iraq’s Shi’ite alliance names Ali al-Zaidi as PM nominee
stories.summary: Iraq's Coordination Framework, an alliance of Shi'ite political blocs, nominated Ali al-Zaidi as its candidate for prime minister. The announcement was made in a coalition statement on Monday.

stories.title: Malay parties unite in Malaysia’s Negeri Sembilan in test of Anwar’s fragile alliance
stories.summary: Barisan Nasional (BN), a key coalition ally of Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, declared it had secured a simple majority to form a new state government in Negeri Sembilan with opposition parties. The move deepens a state-level crisis and poses the sharpest test yet of Anwar's fragile ruling alliance ahead of national elections.

stories.title: Executions in North Korea ramped up significantly during pandemic - report
stories.summary: A report indicates that North Korea significantly increased executions during the pandemic period, with some of those executed having been charged with cultural offenses including consumption of South Korean dramas and K-pop music.

stories.title: Afghan officials say Pakistani strikes killed 7, wounded 85 in first attacks since peace talks
stories.summary: Afghan officials reported that Pakistani strikes killed seven people and wounded 85 in the first attacks since bilateral peace talks began, including a reported strike near a university. Pakistan's Ministry of Information dismissed the reports as fabricated.

stories.title: IS claims responsibility for Nigeria attack that killed 29 people
stories.summary: The Islamic State claimed responsibility for an attack in Nigeria in which militants stormed a football pitch and opened fire, killing 29 people.

stories.title: Biden’s deputy secretary of state: Netanyahu helped ‘create a genocide in Gaza’
stories.summary: Former US Deputy Secretary of State Wendy Sherman said Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu helped 'create a genocide in Gaza' and acknowledged US responsibility. She later clarified she could not make a legal determination on whether genocide literally occurred.

stories.title: Russian court bans prominent gay rights group
stories.summary: A Russian court designated a leading gay rights organization as extremist on Monday and banned it from operating in the country. The ruling is part of a broader pattern of legal measures targeting LGBT+ activists in Russia.

stories.title: Britain’s King Charles arrives in US for trip overshadowed by Iran quarrel and shooting
stories.summary: King Charles is visiting the United States in what is described as the most high-profile trip of his reign. The visit will include an address to Congress and a state dinner at the White House.

stories.title: Indonesia: Many killed in train collision near Jakarta
stories.summary: A long-distance train collided with the rear car of a stationary commuter train outside Jakarta, Indonesia, killing at least 14 people.

stories.title: Trump not happy with latest Iran proposal to end the war
stories.summary: Iran's latest proposal to end the war would set aside discussions on its nuclear program until hostilities cease and Gulf shipping disputes are resolved. US President Trump reportedly opposes the proposal.

stories.title: Gunmen kill 29 in attack in Nigeria's Adamawa state, governor says
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a community in Adamawa state in northeastern Nigeria, killing at least 29 people. The state governor, based in the capital Yola, confirmed the death toll on Monday.

stories.title: Australia targets tech giants with levy unless they pay local news outlets
stories.summary: Australia introduced draft legislation that would require Meta, Google, and TikTok to pay local news publishers for content or face a levy of 2.25 percent of their Australian revenue. The measure aims to support struggling media outlets and reduce the dominance of global tech platforms.

stories.title: France says Iran must make ‘major concessions’ for peace
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot told the UN Security Council that Iran must make major concessions in negotiations with the United States. He called on Tehran to fundamentally change its position and pursue peaceful coexistence in the region.

stories.title: Britain says Iran must not ‘hold world economy hostage’
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper said the UK is increasing pressure on Iran to prevent it from disrupting global trade through its control of the Strait of Hormuz. She stressed the economic risks posed by interference with the vital shipping route.

stories.title: Southeast Asia’s office workers reel from energy-saving drive, heatwave
stories.summary: A heatwave across Southeast Asia is compounding discomfort in offices already affected by government-imposed energy-saving temperature controls linked to the war in Iran. The prolonged shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz has drained energy reserves, and abnormally hot conditions are expected to persist across the region.

stories.title: Popular protests may be inevitable, warns Iran's Supreme National Security Council - Iran Intl
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council warned that popular protests may become inevitable as the economy cannot withstand more than six to eight weeks of the US naval blockade, according to Iran International. The blockade has been in place for two weeks.

stories.title: Trump unlikely to accept Iran proposal, CNN reports
stories.summary: CNN reported that US President Donald Trump is unlikely to accept a proposal from Iran, citing officials familiar with internal discussions. US officials said reopening the Strait of Hormuz without addressing uranium enrichment could weaken Washington's negotiating leverage.

stories.title: SSU detains student coordinating Russian attacks on energy sector in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a student in the Cherkasy region accused of being an FSB agent who coordinated Russian missile and drone strikes on regional energy infrastructure.

stories.title: SSU detains student coordinating Russian attacks on energy sector in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a student in the Cherkasy region who was coordinating Russian missile and drone attacks on local energy infrastructure. The suspect was identified as an agent of Russia's FSB intelligence service.

stories.title: Trump reportedly unhappy with Iranian proposal to reopen Hormuz, shelve nuclear issue
stories.summary: US President Trump is reportedly unhappy with Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while shelving the nuclear issue. The report also noted an IDF soldier was severely wounded in a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Malta calls early election, with PM pledging stability amid Iran war
stories.summary: Maltese Prime Minister Robert Abela announced a snap parliamentary election for May 30, calling the vote a year before his term expires. Abela pledged stability amid the broader regional crisis related to the Iran war.

stories.title: Iran among dozens selected for vice presidency post at UN non-proliferation confab
stories.summary: Iran was among dozens of countries selected for a vice presidency post at a UN Non-Proliferation Treaty review conference. The US envoy called Tehran's selection an 'affront' to the treaty, citing Iran's record on non-proliferation commitments.

stories.title: Fallen soldier Sgt. Idan Fooks laid to rest in Petah Tikva cemetery
stories.summary: Sergeant Idan Fooks of the Israeli military was laid to rest in Petah Tikva. Fooks was killed in southern Lebanon on Sunday when a Hezbollah drone exploded near his unit's position.

stories.title: US stops Iranian-flagged tanker under port blockade
stories.summary: The US Central Command said the guided-missile destroyer USS Rafael Peralta stopped the Iranian-flagged tanker M/T Stream as part of the US blockade of Iran's ports. The vessel had last been tracked in the Malacca Strait. Iran has previously accused Washington of piracy over similar interceptions.

stories.title: Al Jazeera: Iran considering US request to restart talks
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported that Iran is reviewing a US request to resume negotiations but has not yet responded. Officials cited the nuclear issue and a trust deficit following previous US strikes during talks as key obstacles. Iran is reportedly proposing a phased approach prioritizing an end to hostilities.

stories.title: 14 killed in South Sudan plane crash near capital Juba
stories.summary: A passenger plane crashed southwest of Juba, South Sudan's capital, killing all 14 people on board.

stories.title: US Treasury chief says Iran’s oil industry is 'starting to shut'
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would intensify economic pressure on Iran, warning that the country's oil sector is under strain due to the US blockade. He claimed Iran's oil production is beginning to shut down and predicted gasoline shortages would follow.

stories.title: US reviews latest Iranian proposal to end war stalemate
stories.summary: President Trump met with senior national security advisers to review a new proposal from Iran aimed at resolving the ongoing war stalemate. Details of the Iranian proposal were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Culture of violence: On the Washington press dinner shooting
stories.summary: A shooting at the Washington press dinner prompted discussion about the culture of gun violence in the United States. Commentary noted that the proliferation of firearms has given a lethal dimension to political disagreements in the country.

stories.title: Ukraine summons Israeli envoy after month’s 2nd incident involving ‘stolen’ grain ship
stories.summary: Ukraine summoned Israel's envoy over a second incident in a month involving a ship allegedly carrying grain from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory. Kyiv said it reserves the right to pursue diplomatic and international legal responses if Israel does not reject the cargo.

stories.title: Why aircraft carriers are the best (and worst) place for laser weapons
stories.summary: Analysis suggests aircraft carriers are both ideal and challenging platforms for high-energy laser weapons. Their large size and abundant power generation make them suitable hosts, but operational limitations remain.

stories.title: Train collision in Indonesia kills seven as rescuers work to reach survivors
stories.summary: Two trains collided outside Jakarta, Indonesia, killing at least seven people and injuring 81. Rescuers worked to free two passengers still trapped in the wreckage after a long-distance train struck a commuter train overnight.

stories.title: Iran must make ‘major concessions’ to end crisis: France; Tehran calls for guarantees against attack
stories.summary: France called on Iran to make "major concessions" to resolve the ongoing crisis, while Tehran demanded guarantees against military attack. The exchanges took place during a UN session in which multiple countries pressured Iran over its control of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: French FM says Iran must make ‘major concessions’ to end crisis
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister told the UN Security Council that Iran must make "major concessions" to end the ongoing crisis. France's top diplomat stated that Tehran needs to demonstrate a path toward peaceful coexistence within its region.

stories.title: What’s driving the coordinated attacks across Mali?
stories.summary: Armed groups in Mali appear to be coordinating attacks across the country, according to Al Jazeera, which reported that multiple factions are joining forces in a series of escalating operations.

stories.title: As Hong Kong recalibrates, the blue economy offers an anchor
stories.summary: Hong Kong completed its first green methanol bunkering operation, advancing efforts to support decarbonisation of global shipping. The development is part of the city's push to position itself within the growing blue economy, which focuses on sustainable use of ocean resources.

stories.title: Film about life in Ukrainian shelters wins at The Webby Awards
stories.summary: The Ukrainian VR documentary "Shelter," which depicts life in wartime shelters, won at the 2026 Webby Awards in the Apps, Software & Immersive – Science & Education category.

stories.title: What we know about the US military’s new joint laser weapon system
stories.summary: The US Army and Navy are jointly developing a containerized 150-kilowatt high-energy laser weapon system. The effort aims to produce a deployable capability to counter incoming cruise missiles.

stories.title: Five killed in train crash near Indonesia’s Jakarta; rescue efforts ongoing
stories.summary: A train crash near Jakarta, Indonesia, killed at least five people. Indonesia's national rescue agency said efforts were ongoing to free passengers still trapped in the wreckage.

stories.title: US threatens sanctions for companies providing services to Iranian airlines
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that companies providing services to Iranian airlines could face sanctions under a campaign he called "Economic Fury." He urged foreign governments to ensure companies in their jurisdictions do not supply jet fuel, catering, or maintenance to Iranian aircraft.

stories.title: UN warns Hormuz disruption could trigger food emergency
stories.summary: Dozens of countries issued a joint statement led by Bahrain calling for the urgent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned the Security Council of severe global consequences, including fuel shortages and food insecurity, from the ongoing disruption.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson gives evidence in high-profile defamation case against star of directorial debut
stories.summary: Hollywood star Rebel Wilson gave evidence in a high-profile defamation case brought by Charlotte MacInnes, the Australian lead actor of Wilson's directorial debut film The Deb. The case involves claims about interactions on set of the musical comedy.

stories.title: Pentagon mulls plan to outsource warship design and building to South Korea, Japan
stories.summary: The Pentagon is considering a proposed US$1.85 billion feasibility study into outsourcing warship design and construction to South Korea and Japan. Included in the 2027 budget, the study would examine co-producing advanced frigates such as Japan's Mogami-class and South Korea's Daegu-class to supplement overstretched US Navy shipyards.

stories.title: Psychological warfare: Israelis receive threatening WhatsApp messages, likely from Iranian hackers
stories.summary: Israeli citizens received threatening WhatsApp messages believed to be from Iranian hackers. The attack pattern matches that of the Iranian hacker group Handala, which is known for combining cyberattacks with psychological warfare targeting civilians.

stories.title: China pandas rise from unknown status to become palace pets, then national symbols, treasures
stories.summary: Once overlooked in ancient Chinese folklore and literature, the giant panda has risen to become a national symbol and cultural treasure. Palaeontologists have discovered panda fossils across China dating back eight to nine million years.

stories.title: ‘Shortcomings and failures’ could sink Aukus nuclear submarines plan, UK inquiry warns
stories.summary: A UK parliamentary inquiry warned that funding shortcomings and failures could undermine the Aukus nuclear submarine plan. The House of Commons defence committee found that UK shipbuilding has been under-funded for decades and submarine availability is critically low, posing a threat to Australia's security.

stories.title: US senator criticises plan to vet visa applicants over Israel views
stories.summary: US Senator Chris Van Hollen criticized a reported plan to vet Green Card applicants based on their views on Israel, calling it outrageous. He argued the proposal would deny legal residency based on political speech.

stories.title: Tehran says Gulf stability depends on ‘permanent cessation of aggression’
stories.summary: Iran's UN Ambassador Amir Saeid Iravani told the Security Council that lasting Persian Gulf stability requires credible guarantees against further attacks on Iran. He called for a permanent cessation of aggression and full respect for Iran's sovereign rights.

stories.title: Fifteen students rescued after raid on Nigerian orphanage school: state government says
stories.summary: Nigerian security forces rescued 15 pupils after gunmen abducted 23 children and a school proprietor's wife during an attack on an unregistered orphanage and school in Kogi state. The state government confirmed the rescue operation following the Saturday night raid.

stories.title: Pizza Hut to pay family of Petah Tikva stabbing victim indefinitely, company announces
stories.summary: Pizza Hut announced it will pay the family of 21-year-old Yemanu Binyamin Zalka indefinitely after he was killed following his shift at the chain's Petah Tikva location. The company also committed to establishing a dedicated aid fund for his family.

stories.title: Russian superyacht crosses blockaded Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A Russian superyacht named Nord crossed the blockaded Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. The vessel departed Dubai Marina on Friday and arrived in Muscat, Oman, early on Sunday after transiting the strait on Saturday morning.

stories.title: Mali at risk of splintering after jihadi and separatist attacks
stories.summary: An alliance of al-Qaeda-linked militants and separatist rebels launched simultaneous attacks across Mali on Saturday. The assaults killed Defence Minister Sadio Camara, struck the capital's airport, and drove Russian soldiers from the northern desert town of Kidal.

stories.title: Freedom of navigation not negotiable: IMO addresses UN Security Council on maritime safety in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The International Maritime Organization addressed the UN Security Council on freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. IMO Secretary-General warned that any deviation from established maritime transit principles would set a negative precedent and undermine global shipping operations.

stories.title: King Charles arrives in US for state visit amid differences over Iran war
stories.summary: King Charles arrived in the United States for a state visit, the most consequential of his reign, marking the 250th anniversary of the US Declaration of Independence. The visit takes place amid diplomatic differences between the UK and US over the war with Iran.

stories.title: Bruised by Trump, NATO alliance considers end to annual summits
stories.summary: NATO members are discussing whether to end the alliance's tradition of annual summits. While President Trump's stance toward the alliance is a factor, some member states also want to reduce the frequency of high-level meetings.

stories.title: Nathan Chasing Horse sentenced to life in prison for sexual assault
stories.summary: Actor Nathan Chasing Horse, known for his role in Dances With Wolves, was sentenced to life in prison by a Nevada judge. A jury convicted him on 13 charges, mostly related to sexual assault of Indigenous women and girls, including one victim who was 14 when the assaults began.

stories.title: Will Asean’s scramble for Russian oil fuel shift in regional alliances?
stories.summary: Southeast Asian governments are seeking Russian oil and gas to offset fuel shortages caused by disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts say the scramble raises questions about whether Moscow could leverage its role as an emergency energy supplier to build longer-term influence in the ASEAN region.

stories.title: China faces a France-sized demographic loss that threatens coastal growth: analysts
stories.summary: China's population is projected to decline by roughly 60 million over the next decade, according to research firm Rhodium Group. Analysts warn the loss—equivalent to France's population—could weaken economic activity in wealthy coastal provinces and strain the public pension system.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump reviews peace plan; UN calls for Hormuz to reopen
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that the US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz risks triggering a global food emergency. President Trump is reviewing a peace plan as tensions in the waterway continue.

stories.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians and set house on fire
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians and set fire to a home in the occupied West Bank village of Jalud. The incident is part of a pattern of settler violence against Palestinian communities.

stories.title: Afghanistan says Pakistani strikes kill seven and wound 85 in first attack since peace talks
stories.summary: Afghan officials said Pakistani mortars and missiles struck a university and civilian homes in Kunar province in northeastern Afghanistan, killing seven and wounding at least 85. Pakistan denied the accusations, calling reports of targeting the university a "blatant lie." The strikes were the first reported since recent peace talks.

stories.title: Lithuania charges 13 people with two attempted murders linked to Russia's GRU, police say
stories.summary: Lithuania has charged 13 individuals from multiple countries with two attempted murders in Vilnius linked to Russia's GRU military intelligence agency. The country's chief of criminal police announced the charges on Monday.

stories.title: Washington Hilton says it was using Secret Service protocols on night of attack
stories.summary: The Washington Hilton hotel stated it was operating under "stringent" Secret Service protocols when a man breached security and fired shotgun rounds during a dinner attended by President Donald Trump on Saturday. The hotel issued the statement on Monday.

stories.title: Hezbollah launches 3 attacks on Israeli forces in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah said its fighters carried out three attacks against Israeli forces inside Lebanese territory on Monday. The group said it targeted a military bulldozer in Bint Jbeil, a Merkava tank in al-Qantara, and two gatherings of Israeli troops in Naqoura.

stories.title: Survivors of deadly Indonesia train crash pulled from wreckage
stories.summary: Two trains collided in Bekasi, near Jakarta, Indonesia, late Monday, killing at least four people and injuring dozens. Rescue teams pulled survivors from the wreckage following the crash.

stories.title: Targeting of synagogue, Judaica shop window ratchet up Toronto Jews’ concerns
stories.summary: A synagogue and a Judaica shop window were targeted in Toronto in two incidents that took place in broad daylight. The attacks have heightened concerns among the city's Jewish community, following other recent nighttime incidents against Jewish sites and businesses.

stories.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum warns US involvement in anti-drug operation not to be repeated
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that her government sent a diplomatic note to the United States regarding the unauthorized presence of U.S. officials at an anti-narcotics operation in the northern state of Chihuahua. She warned that such involvement should not be repeated.

stories.title: Suspect in Washington dinner shooting charged with attempting to assassinate Trump
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, was charged in Washington federal court with attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump after allegedly shooting a U.S. Secret Service agent while trying to breach security at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner.

stories.title: Ukraine at UN: All military operations near nuclear facilities must cease immediately
stories.summary: Ukraine called at the United Nations for an immediate halt to all military operations near nuclear facilities, citing the risk of a nuclear disaster. The statement came amid ongoing Russian military activity near Ukrainian nuclear sites during the war.

stories.title: Trump’s Golden Dome aimed at combating China’s ‘hypersonic weapons, cruise missiles’
stories.summary: A senior Pentagon official told Congress the United States currently lacks defences against hypersonic weapons and cruise missiles. President Trump's proposed US$185 billion Golden Dome missile shield aims to counter such threats, though it continues to face scepticism from lawmakers.

stories.title: Russia’s UN ambassador says Iran can restrict Hormuz traffic
stories.summary: Russia's UN Ambassador Vassily Nebenzia told the UN Security Council that Iran has the legal right to restrict navigation in the Strait of Hormuz during wartime for security purposes. He accused Western nations of hypocrisy for blaming Tehran for maritime disruptions in the waterway.

stories.title: Man charged with attempted assassination of Trump for correspondents’ dinner shooting
stories.summary: Cole Thomas Allen was charged with the attempted assassination of President Trump in connection with a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. Authorities said the 31-year-old had reserved a hotel room weeks in advance and faces up to life in prison.

stories.title: Reporters covered correspondents’ dinner shooting in real time. Conspiracies still spread
stories.summary: Despite extensive real-time coverage of the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, conspiracy theories spread rapidly from both ends of the political spectrum. Among the most prominent unfounded claims was that the shooting had been staged.

stories.title: China vows countermeasures if EU enacts 'Made in Europe' plan
stories.summary: China threatened countermeasures in response to the European Union's "Made in Europe" initiative, unveiled in March. The EU rules require companies seeking public funds in strategic sectors such as automobiles, green technology, and steel to meet minimum thresholds for EU-manufactured components.

stories.title: Ukraine to take measures against Israel if grain ship docks, source says
stories.summary: Ukraine warned that Israel could face diplomatic and legal consequences if it allows a vessel carrying grain from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory to dock at the port of Haifa. A Ukrainian diplomatic source disclosed the threat to Reuters on Monday.

stories.title: Legal limits on U.S. war involvement
stories.summary: The U.S. War Powers Act requires presidential authorization from Congress for military force abroad beyond 60 days. Questions are being raised about the Trump administration's legal obligations regarding ongoing U.S. military engagement in West Asia.

stories.title: Terror trial to begin for man accused of plotting attack on Taylor Swift concert
stories.summary: A terror trial is set to begin for 21-year-old Beran A., accused of plotting an attack on a Taylor Swift concert. Prosecutors say he received explosives training from Islamic State members.

stories.title: Five stand trial in Germany over attack on Israeli defence company office
stories.summary: Five defendants appeared in court in Stuttgart, Germany, on Monday facing charges of causing approximately one million euros in damage at the German offices of an Israeli defense company. No further details about the suspects' identities or affiliations were immediately provided.

stories.title: Bahrain revokes citizenship of 69 people for 'glorifying or sympathising with' Iranian attacks
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior ministry announced it has revoked the citizenship of 69 individuals, accusing them of sympathizing with Iranian attacks and collaborating with foreign entities.

stories.title: First teenage suicide linked to domestic abuse recorded in England and Wales
stories.summary: The first teenage suicide linked to domestic abuse has been recorded in England and Wales, involving a girl driven to take her own life after domestic violence. Police chiefs blamed violent pornography and toxic online influencers for rising teen abuse. Suicides after domestic abuse have outstripped homicides for the third consecutive year.

stories.title: UK has wealthy Europe’s ‘third-highest’ rate of young adults not in work or study
stories.summary: A Resolution Foundation report found the UK has the third-highest rate of young adults not in work or education among wealthy European countries. Nearly one million 16- to 24-year-olds are classified as NEETs, the highest level in over a decade, driven by rising ill-health and failures in benefits and job support systems.

stories.title: Half of England’s schools unfit due to leaks, mould and faulty toilets, poll finds
stories.summary: A survey by the National Association of Head Teachers found that half of headteachers in England say parts of their schools are out of use or unfit for purpose. Problems include leaks, mould, asbestos, faulty toilets, and malfunctioning fire doors, with closures affecting playgrounds, classrooms, and SEND facilities.

stories.title: Hong Kong to block off parts of Sharp Island shoreline to protect corals for ‘golden week’
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities plan to cordon off parts of Sharp Island's shoreline in Sai Kung to protect corals during the Labour Day golden week holiday. The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department will deploy 11 patrol officers daily and five marine staff to monitor visitor behaviour around the site.

stories.title: Iran condemns US seizure of oil tankers as 'piracy'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei condemned the US seizure of two Iran-linked oil tankers, the Majestic X and the Tifani, calling the action piracy and armed robbery on the high seas. The incident occurred amid ongoing US-Iranian tensions over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: The TV series, 'Unconditional,' has its Israeli premiere - review
stories.summary: The Israeli television series "Unconditional" premiered in Israel, co-created by Adam Bizanski and Dana Idisis. Bizanski, known for "Magpie," wrote the series, while Idisis is recognized for her work on "On the Spectrum."

stories.title: Russian shelling damages over 50% of high-rise buildings in Sloviansk community
stories.summary: Russian shelling has damaged more than 50% of high-rise residential buildings in the Sloviansk community of Ukraine's Donetsk region. Since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, 81 people have been killed and 402 wounded in the community.

stories.title: Assault outside synagogue, rock thrown through Judaica shop window raise Toronto Jews’ concerns
stories.summary: A man was assaulted outside a synagogue and a rock was thrown through the window of a Judaica shop in Toronto, both in broad daylight. No suspects have been identified in either incident, raising security concerns among the city's Jewish community.

stories.title: Al Qaeda group says Mali army quits northern town as insurgency spreads
stories.summary: Al Qaeda's West Africa affiliate, JNIM, claimed that Mali's army withdrew from the northern town of Tessit. The insurgent offensive included weekend attacks near the capital Bamako and across the country.

stories.title: Bahrain strips dozens of citizenship over Iran support
stories.summary: Bahrain's government revoked the citizenship of dozens of individuals, including dependents, accusing them of supporting hostile Iranian activities. The Ministry stated those affected were found to have colluded with foreign entities linked to Iran.

stories.title: Man pleads guilty to role in 2002 murder of Run-DMC’s Jam Master Jay
stories.summary: Jay Bryant pleaded guilty to a federal murder charge for his role in the 2002 killing of Run-DMC's Jam Master Jay, born Jason Mizell. Bryant admitted to helping others gain access to a recording studio where the rapper was ambushed. The case had gone unsolved for more than two decades.

stories.title: Gunmen kill at least 29 at football pitch in north-east Nigeria, governor says
stories.summary: Gunmen killed at least 29 people in Adamawa state in northeastern Nigeria, targeting young people gathered at a football pitch. The attack continues a wave of violence across the country, including a separate armed raid on an orphanage in Kogi state. Adamawa borders Cameroon and is a hotspot for jihadist and criminal gang activity.

stories.title: Remains from Israel’s North show Neanderthal children grew faster than modern humans - study
stories.summary: A study of remains found in northern Israel revealed that Neanderthal children grew faster than modern humans. The specimen, known as Amud 7, dates to approximately 51,000–56,000 years ago and represents the most complete Neanderthal infant skeleton ever discovered.

stories.title: The real reason Iran and the US cannot end the war: Money
stories.summary: Diplomats and analysts say the US-Iran war remains unresolved largely because of economic factors tied to Washington's sanctions-based strategy. President Trump's reluctance to abandon economic pressure on Iran is seen as a key obstacle to reaching a negotiated deal.

stories.title: Pakistan UN envoy warns Hormuz disruption threatens global stability
stories.summary: Pakistan's UN Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad warned the UN Security Council that disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz pose a serious threat to global stability. He emphasized that secure maritime routes are essential for international trade, development, and security.

stories.title: German Chancellor Merz says Iran is humiliating U.S. as talks stall
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused Iran of humiliating the United States as nuclear talks stalled. He remarked that Iranian negotiators effectively avoided substantive discussions, leaving American officials to travel to Islamabad and depart without results.
