stories.summary: In Mali, separatist group FLA and jihadist organization Jnim have formed an unprecedented alliance against the ruling military junta. Strategic towns have fallen and Defence Minister Sadio Camara's residence was destroyed, signaling a dangerous escalation for President Goïta.

stories.title: Syria begins long-awaited first trial of Assad-era officials
stories.summary: The first public trial of an Assad-era official opened in Damascus on Sunday. Atef Najib, a former brigadier general who headed the Political Security Branch in Daraa province and is a cousin of Bashar al-Assad, appeared in court facing charges related to crimes against the Syrian people.

stories.title: China warns EU to remove firms and citizens from Russian sanctions list
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce demanded the European Union remove Chinese companies and individuals from its latest Russia-related sanctions list. Beijing warned it would take necessary measures to protect the rights and interests of its citizens and firms, urging dialogue to resolve the dispute.

stories.title: Israeli embassy worker in Washington describes 'shouting, panic' at White House dinner shooting
stories.summary: Israeli Embassy spokesperson Tal Naim described hearing shouting and widespread panic at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in Washington after shots were fired. Naim said she was seated approximately 200 meters from the stage when the incident occurred.

stories.title: Cabinet approves ex-UK envoy Hotovely to lead National Public Diplomacy Directorate
stories.summary: Israel's cabinet unanimously approved former UK ambassador Tzipi Hotovely to head the National Public Diplomacy Directorate within the Prime Minister's Office, a position vacant for two years. Ministers also approved Doron Cohen as civil service commissioner.

stories.title: Pakistan PM dials Iranian President, discusses evolving regional situation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister held a 50-minute phone call with Iran's President to discuss the evolving regional situation. The two leaders exchanged views on ongoing efforts to promote peace and stability in the region, according to Pakistan's Prime Minister's office.

stories.title: How the shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner unfolded
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday evening. Secret Service agents evacuated President Donald Trump and his cabinet from the ballroom. The suspect was subsequently taken into custody at the scene.

stories.title: Kenya’s Sawe is world’s first man to run a sub-two-hour marathon in London
stories.summary: Kenyan runner Sebastian Sawe became the first person to complete a marathon in under two hours, breaking Kelvin Kiptum's previous world record of 2:00:35 at the London Marathon. Ethiopia's Tigst Assefa retained her women's title at the same event.

stories.title: Zelensky on Chernobyl anniversary: Russia again putting world at risk of man-made disaster
stories.summary: On the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called on the international community to prevent what he termed nuclear terrorism by Russia. Zelensky drew parallels between the 1986 catastrophe and current Russian threats to nuclear safety in Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack on Sevastopol Kills 1 – Moscow-Installed Governor
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck the port city of Sevastopol in Russian-annexed Crimea, killing one person, according to the Moscow-installed governor. The attack damaged several homes and a dance school across multiple neighborhoods.

stories.title: UAE to establish $272m national fund for industrial resilience
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced a one-billion-dirham ($272 million) national fund to strengthen industrial resilience. Prime Minister Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum said the fund will support localization of vital industries, supply chain resilience, and AI adoption in production and planning.

stories.title: China’s Li Auto targets BMW and Mercedes with premium SUVs in Middle East, Asia-Pacific
stories.summary: Beijing-based electric vehicle maker Li Auto is expanding into the Middle East and Asia-Pacific markets with premium SUVs designed to compete with BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Audi. Company president Ma Donghui said overseas deliveries are expected to account for 30 percent of total sales by 2030.

stories.title: Taliban govt says Afghans in Qatar can return 'with confidence'
stories.summary: The Taliban government urged Afghan nationals in Qatar to return home, stating they could do so "with confidence." However, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned of ongoing arbitrary arrests and torture of former government officials in Afghanistan.

stories.title: Trump says shooting at press dinner 'won't deter him' from Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump was evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner at the Washington Hilton after shots were fired outside the venue. Trump later told reporters the incident would not deter him from pursuing the war on Iran, adding the shooting was likely unrelated to the conflict.

stories.title: Fatah says it claimed ‘sweeping victory’ in local elections, despite democratic shortcomings
stories.summary: The Palestinian faction Fatah claimed a sweeping victory in local council elections, including in Jenin, where the Palestinian Authority had previously been accused of losing control to Hamas-linked Palestinian Islamic Jihad. The elections faced criticism over democratic shortcomings.

stories.title: Russian forces shell 18 settlements in Kharkiv region over past 24 hours, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled 18 settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region over a 24-hour period, resulting in civilian casualties. No further details on the scale of damage or specific locations were immediately provided by Ukrainian authorities.

stories.title: Lebanon won’t disarm Hezbollah, but will attack a 'generator owner'
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam criticized security forces for what he called unacceptable harsh actions following the arrest of a generator owner. The incident drew attention to a perceived double standard, as the Lebanese state has not moved to disarm Hezbollah.

stories.title: Mali’s Defence Minister Sadio Camara killed amid coordinated attacks
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed during coordinated attacks by armed groups. His death is considered a significant blow to Mali's ruling military government, which continues to fight insurgent forces across the country.

stories.title: Suspect at White House correspondents’ dinner shooting had multiple weapons, bulletproof vest: Trump
stories.summary: The suspect in the shooting at the White House correspondents' dinner has been identified as Cole Tomas Allen from California. President Trump described Allen as a "would-be assassin" who was carrying multiple weapons and a bulletproof vest.

stories.title: Ukrainians gather to remember Chernobyl disaster despite Russia’s war
stories.summary: Residents of Slavutych, Ukraine, gathered in the early hours of Sunday to commemorate the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster, placing candles on a radiation hazard symbol in the central square. The annual vigil took place despite wartime curfews and warnings against large gatherings during Russia's ongoing war.

stories.title: Trump says shooting at press dinner 'won't deter him' from Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that a shooting incident at the White House Correspondents' Dinner on 25 April 2026 would not deter him from pursuing the war with Iran. A suspect armed with a shotgun, handgun, and multiple knives was detained. Trump said the incident was unlikely linked to the conflict.

stories.title: China backs Myanmar’s push to ease diplomatic isolation, stamp out telecoms scams
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi pledged support for Myanmar's new government to engage with multilateral platforms and combat telecoms scam operations. During a meeting with junta leader Min Aung Hlaing, Wang reaffirmed China's backing for Myanmar's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

stories.title: Rescuers show aftermath of shelling in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Firefighters in Ukraine's Chernihiv region extinguished fires in Chernihiv city and the Borzna and Horodnia communities following Russian attacks on April 25 and the early morning of April 26. Rescuers documented the aftermath of the shelling.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 26 – As both sides keep striking, is there still a Lebanon ceasefire?
stories.summary: Times of Israel military correspondent Emanuel Fabian discussed the IDF's readiness regarding Iran, the fragile state of the Lebanon ceasefire amid continued strikes by both sides, and the case of two Israeli Air Force technicians accused of spying for Iran.

stories.title: Death of Mali defence minister Sadio Camara deals a heavy blow to junta
stories.summary: Mali's defence minister Sadio Camara, a key ally of Russia in the Sahel, was killed in a car bomb attack at his residence in the garrison town of Kati. His death is a significant blow to the ruling military junta.

stories.title: Israel threatens residents in south Lebanon in leaflets dropped over Sour
stories.summary: The Israeli army dropped leaflets over Mansouri village in the Sour district of southern Lebanon, warning civilians against entering nearly two dozen villages in the area. Army spokesperson Avichay Adraee also renewed warnings against accessing areas around the Litani River and villages within an Israeli-established zone roughly 10 kilometers inside southern Lebanon.

stories.title: US intercepts sanctioned merchant vessel in Arabian Sea, Central Command says
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command announced it intercepted a sanctioned merchant vessel in the Arabian Sea on Saturday, April 25. The ship was reportedly attempting to breach the U.S. blockade on Iran.

stories.title: Netanyahu, Herzog among world leaders ‘shocked’ by shooting at gala attended by Trump
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, President Herzog, and other world leaders expressed shock at the shooting outside the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner attended by President Trump. Multiple leaders condemned political violence and sent well-wishes to U.S. officials and attendees.

stories.title: At least four people killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza despite ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israeli forces continued advancing into western Gaza, expanding their area of control in the east. At least four people were reported killed in Israeli attacks despite an ostensible ceasefire being in place.

stories.title: Salah to miss rest of Liverpool season, says Egypt team director
stories.summary: Egypt national team director Hassan announced that Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah will miss the remainder of the club's season due to injury. Hassan added that Salah is expected to be fit for the 2026 World Cup, where Egypt is drawn in Group G alongside Belgium, New Zealand, and Iran.

stories.title: Israel destroys solar panels in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces destroyed solar panels in southern Lebanon. No further details on the specific location or scale of the destruction were immediately available.

stories.title: ‘Coolcation’ trend heats up as travellers flee rising temperatures
stories.summary: A growing travel trend dubbed "coolcation" is seeing tourists choose cooler-climate destinations to escape rising temperatures. The shift is driven by intensifying global warming affecting traditional warm-weather vacation spots.

stories.title: Donald Trump says shooting won’t ‘deter’ him from Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared that a shooting incident would not deter him from pursuing the war with Iran. Trump had previously cancelled his envoys' trip to Pakistan, where peace talks with Iran were being arranged.

stories.title: Deadly Israeli strikes hit Lebanon despite ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out strikes in at least four locations in southern Lebanon late Saturday, reportedly killing six people despite a recently extended ceasefire. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the attacks on Hezbollah positions, citing alleged ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill 2,490 people in Lebanon since 2 March
stories.summary: The Lebanese health ministry reported that Israeli attacks on Lebanon since 2 March have killed 2,496 people and wounded at least 7,725. Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed four people on Saturday despite a ceasefire that had been extended by three weeks.

stories.title: Donald Trump says suspect was armed with multiple weapons at White House correspondents’ dinner
stories.summary: A suspect armed with multiple weapons opened fire near the White House correspondents' dinner in Washington, D.C. One law-enforcement officer was struck but survived thanks to a bulletproof vest. President Donald Trump reported the suspect carried several firearms.

stories.title: Loud bangs and a Trump evacuation: chaos at correspondents' dinner
stories.summary: The Secret Service evacuated President Trump from the White House correspondents' dinner at the Washington Hilton after loud gunshots erupted. Hundreds of guests ducked under tables as authorities swarmed the banquet hall to secure the venue.

stories.title: China unveils world’s first coal fuel cell that can produce electricity with zero emission
stories.summary: Chinese scientists have developed a direct coal fuel cell that generates electricity from coal without combustion, reportedly achieving higher energy efficiency than conventional coal-fired power while producing zero carbon dioxide emissions.

stories.title: Teen arrested in Louisiana shooting got ride from scene from grandmother
stories.summary: Markel Lee, 17, was arrested in connection with a mass shooting at a Louisiana mall that killed a high school senior and wounded five others. Investigators used surveillance video and license plate readers to track a car driven by Lee's grandmother, who had unknowingly given him a ride from the scene.

stories.title: China Gen Z snipers nicknamed ‘Sweetheart’, ‘Gun Queen’ challenge gender stereotypes
stories.summary: Two female Gen Z snipers in China's People's Armed Police have gained attention for their marksmanship. Liu Jiangtao, 26, from Chongqing, broke the women's record in a sniper selection test by firing three rounds through a single hole on a coin-sized target at hundreds of metres.

stories.title: Shelling in Donetsk region over past 24 hours kills two, wounds five
stories.summary: Two people were killed and five wounded by Russian shelling in the Donetsk region over the past 24 hours. The attacks struck the areas of Druzhkivka and Oleksievo-Druzhkivka.

stories.title: Above-normal temperature forecast in Punjab
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast hot and dry weather across Punjab on Sunday, with temperatures expected to remain above normal in the central and southern plains. A weakening westerly wave has reduced the chance of rain, leaving dry and humid conditions across the province.

stories.title: Preserving Israel’s military edge: Strategic steps for the MOD - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that shifting regional alliances, major arms deals, and rising threats are placing unprecedented pressure on Israel's qualitative military edge. The analysis calls for a new strategy by Israel's Ministry of Defense to preserve its technological and military advantages.

stories.title: Punjab to export livestock
stories.summary: Punjab province in Pakistan signed memorandums of understanding with seven institutions, including China's Global Meat Company, to export livestock and meat. Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz presided over the meeting, which outlined plans to export one million livestock and install a boiler unit in collaboration with the Punjab Agriculture and Meat Company.

stories.title: Bus blast in Colombia kills 13 amid rising violence
stories.summary: An explosive device detonated on a bus in southwestern Colombia on Saturday, killing 13 people and injuring at least 38. Colombia's army chief described the attack as a terrorist act, amid escalating violence linked to drug trafficking in the region.

stories.title: Measles claims lives of 71 children across country in four months
stories.summary: Seventy-one children have died of measles across Pakistan in the first four months of the year, including 40 in Sindh province. The deaths were reported as the country observed World Immunisation Week, with experts calling for local vaccine manufacturing to reduce dependence on imports.

stories.title: US cancels envoy travel, shifts from talks to pressure as Iran’s divisions deepen - analysis
stories.summary: The United States canceled planned envoy travel related to Iran diplomacy, signaling a shift from negotiations to a pressure-based strategy. The White House indicated willingness to sustain a long-term posture in its conflict with Iran, while Tehran also showed no urgency to resume talks.

stories.title: Yemen’s landmine crisis endures despite truce and de-mining efforts
stories.summary: Landmines across Yemen continue to cause civilian deaths and injuries despite an ongoing truce and active de-mining operations. The crisis persists as a legacy of the country's prolonged conflict.

stories.title: Iran FM heads to Russia for talks, as US cancels Islamabad visit
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi headed to Russia for diplomatic talks after the US canceled a planned visit to Islamabad. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran would not negotiate under threats and blockade.

stories.title: Iran FM returns to Islamabad, as US envoys cancel visit
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Islamabad after US envoys canceled their planned visit to Pakistan. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran would not negotiate under threats or blockade conditions.

stories.title: Iran refuses 'imposed' talks with US as envoys cancel visit
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran would not engage in negotiations under threats and blockade, rejecting what Tehran characterized as imposed talks with the United States. U.S. envoys reportedly canceled a planned visit amid the impasse.

stories.title: Raghu Rai, legendary Indian photographer, dies at 83
stories.summary: Raghu Rai, the acclaimed Indian photographer and Magnum Photos member, has died at the age of 83. His decades-long career documented pivotal moments in India's modern history.

stories.title: 2 US citizens killed in raid on Philippines communist stronghold
stories.summary: Two U.S. citizens were among 19 people killed in a military raid on an alleged communist stronghold in the Toboso municipality of Negros Island, Philippines, on April 19. Over 300 residents fled their homes during the operation, and the Philippines Commission on Human Rights has launched a probe.

stories.title: First section of Fanling Bypass to open soon. So how will Hongkongers benefit?
stories.summary: The eastern section of Hong Kong's Fanling Bypass is set to open on May 3, marking the first major transport infrastructure project completed under the Northern Metropolis development plan. The 4-kilometer roadway is expected to reduce travel times by 10 minutes and serve the Fanling North New Development Area.

stories.title: Tel Aviv Museum of Art reimagines exhibitions amid wartime conditions
stories.summary: The Tel Aviv Museum of Art is adapting its programming amid wartime conditions in Israel, bringing art experiences into safe rooms and bomb shelters. The changes come as museums face closures and ongoing air-raid sirens disrupt normal operations.

stories.title: War, memory, and metal: Yaacov Dorchin’s latest Tel Aviv exhibition
stories.summary: Israeli sculptor Yaacov Dorchin, aged 80, has opened a new exhibition of iron sculptures in Tel Aviv. The works incorporate themes of angels, fish, memory, and wartime reflection.

stories.title: Finding meaning in dark times: A Viktor Frankl exhibition in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: A new exhibition in Tel Aviv explores the ideas of Viktor Frankl, the Holocaust survivor and psychiatrist known for his work on finding meaning in suffering. The show examines how his philosophy applies during times of crisis.

stories.title: Russians strike civilian and port infrastructure in Odesa region, one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck civilian and port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, injuring one person. The attack targeted key facilities in the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Kenyan appeal court overturns ruling that affirmed the right to abortion
stories.summary: A Kenyan appeals court overturned a previous landmark ruling that had affirmed access to abortion as a fundamental right. Critics warn the decision could push more women and girls toward unsafe procedures, though some have supported the court's reasoning.

stories.title: Israel, world leaders voice support for Trump after White House dinner shooting
stories.summary: Israel and several world leaders expressed support for President Trump and condemned the shooting attack at a Washington, DC hotel during the White House Correspondents' Association dinner. Officials voiced relief that no US officials were harmed in the incident.

stories.title: Information warfare is shaping the Israel, US war with Iran in real time - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argued that information warfare is playing a central role in shaping the conflict involving Israel, the United States, and Iran. The author contended that modern warfare increasingly revolves around controlling public narratives rather than solely territory or firepower.

stories.title: Recalibrating positions
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has publicly criticized US war-mongering and urged the United States and Iran to continue dialogue, warning of the conflict's toll on civilians in Iran and Lebanon. The editorial examines the tension between the Pope's calls for restraint and President Trump's multiple simultaneous confrontations.

stories.title: Oink-Off in Estonia: Pig contest highlights farming struggles
stories.summary: An agricultural fair in Tartu, Estonia, featured a pig imitation contest designed to draw attention to struggles in the country's pig farming sector. Local participant Andrus Maileht won the top prize for his performance.

stories.title: Iran executes man linked to militant group, says report
stories.summary: Iran executed a man identified as Amer Ramesh, convicted of membership in the Sunni militant group Jaish al-Adl, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. Authorities said he was arrested in southeastern Iran and charged with armed rebellion, including bombings and ambushes targeting Iranian security forces.

stories.title: Armed groups claim attacks across Mali
stories.summary: An Al-Qaeda-linked jihadist group announced its fighters joined forces with Tuareg rebels to launch coordinated attacks against Mali's military across the country. Helicopters flew over Bamako and fighting was reported near a military base close to the international airport in one of the most complex attacks in years.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in doubt after Trump scraps Pakistan visit
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran mediation efforts were thrown into uncertainty after President Trump canceled his envoys' planned trip to Pakistan for talks, dismissing Tehran's negotiating position. Trump later said Iran had revised its proposal within minutes of his cancellation decision.

stories.title: Oman's sultan meets Iran's foreign minister Aragchi in Muscat
stories.summary: Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said of Oman met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in Muscat. According to Oman's state news agency, the two discussed the regional situation and mediation efforts aimed at ending the war involving Iran.

stories.title: 🔴 Live: France's Macron says shooter attack at Trump media dinner 'unacceptable'
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in Washington as unacceptable.

stories.title: Ukraine marks 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear plant disaster
stories.summary: Ukraine marked the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear power plant explosion on Sunday. The commemoration comes amid the ongoing Russian invasion, which has placed the plant under renewed threat and raised concerns about potential radioactive risks.

stories.title: Pakistan taps UN committee to reshape national food policy
stories.summary: Pakistan has initiated dialogue with the UN Committee on World Food Security, seeking policy guidance to address national food security challenges amid climate and economic pressures. Federal officials discussed strategies to ensure food access during a meeting with the CFS panel.

stories.title: LA teacher suspect for White House press dinner shooting
stories.summary: Police identified the suspect in the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, a teacher from Torrance, California. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said charges related to the Saturday night attack would be filed shortly. A motive has not yet been determined.

stories.title: Immunity gap
stories.summary: A commentary highlights Pakistan's Expanded Programme on Immunisation, which since 1978 has helped avert 2.6 million child deaths and contributed to a 99.8% reduction in paralytic polio since 1994. The WHO estimates routine immunisation prevents up to 17% of childhood mortality in Pakistan.

stories.title: War update: 149 combat clashes over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces recorded 149 combat engagements with Russian troops over the past day on April 26. The clashes occurred across multiple sectors of the front line.

stories.title: Chornobyl’s surviving ‘liquidators’ return 40 years after nuclear disaster
stories.summary: Surviving cleanup workers, known as "liquidators," returned to the Chornobyl nuclear plant site to mark the 40th anniversary of the 1986 disaster. Approximately 600,000 soldiers, firefighters, engineers, miners, and medics participated in the original cleanup effort.

stories.title: Iran executes man over membership in jihadist group, armed rebellion
stories.summary: Iran executed a man identified as Amer Ramesh for alleged membership in the Sunni jihadist group Jaish al-Adl and for armed rebellion against security forces. The execution comes as Tehran has stepped up executions amid its ongoing conflict with the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Ukraine kill at least five, damage ship in port
stories.summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine killed at least five people and damaged a ship in a Ukrainian port. Separately, Ukrainian strikes on Russia injured at least six people in the Vologda region and annexed Crimea.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 124 Russian drones since yesterday evening
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces neutralized 124 out of 144 Russian drones launched since the evening of April 25. The interceptions were carried out by Ukraine's Air Defense Forces across multiple areas.

stories.title: Accused correspondents’ dinner attacker is California tutor and computer programmer
stories.summary: The suspect accused of carrying out the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner has been identified as Cole Tomas Allen, a California-based tutor and computer programmer. Allen holds a mechanical engineering degree from Caltech and spent the past six years working for a college test-preparation firm.

stories.title: For the US dollar, a subtler shift than a ‘petroyuan’ order is underfoot
stories.summary: Recent developments suggest a subtle shift in the global financial order around the U.S. dollar, involving converging events including Abu Dhabi's crown prince visiting Beijing, China outlining positions on the Iran war, Pakistan's role in U.S.-Iran diplomacy, and reports of increased yuan usage in international transactions.

stories.title: Southwestern China’s busiest airport disrupted by biggest hailstorm in a decade
stories.summary: Kunming Changshui International Airport in Yunnan province, southwestern China's busiest airport, was severely disrupted by the region's largest hailstorm in a decade. Fist-sized hailstones grounded flights, damaged over 110 aircraft, and stranded passengers when the storm struck on Saturday.

stories.title: Is Reform Judaism about modernity or tradition? with Rabbi Rick Jacobs - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Rabbi Rick Jacobs discusses the future direction of Reform Judaism, exploring tensions between modernity and tradition, personal choice and obligation, and the movement's focus on the Jewish community versus broader society.

stories.title: What Hasan Piker got wrong about Einstein and Zionism - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The article examines streamer Hasan Piker's statements about Albert Einstein's relationship with Zionism. Author Noam traces Einstein's full history with the movement, arguing Piker presented an incomplete portrait that does not hold up against the historical record.

stories.title: New auto assemblers dodge localisation details
stories.summary: New auto assemblers operating in Pakistan are avoiding disclosure of localisation details in their vehicle assembly operations. Local parts vendors complain of negligible use of domestically produced components, while CKD imports surged to $1.47 billion in the first nine months of fiscal year 2026.

stories.title: Trump unharmed as gunman fires shots toward White House correspondents’ dinner
stories.summary: President Donald Trump was unharmed after a gunman fired shots outside the White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Washington Hilton. Trump and senior officials were evacuated, a suspect was taken into custody, and no serious injuries were reported.

stories.title: Russian attacks in the Dnipropetrovsk region leave one killed, four injured
stories.summary: Russian attacks struck four districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, killing one person and injuring four others. The strikes targeted multiple areas across the region.

stories.title: Security operation in Belfast after police station car bomb
stories.summary: A car bomb detonated at a police station in Belfast around midnight, prompting a security operation in the area. Videos circulating on social media showed a vehicle on fire at the station.

stories.title: Iran war jitters to influence policy rate decision
stories.summary: Financial markets in Pakistan anticipate an interest rate increase in the upcoming monetary policy decision, driven largely by regional instability from the Gulf war rather than domestic inflation. Experts warn that the conflict's economic consequences for Pakistan and similar countries remain highly uncertain.

stories.title: Secret Stasi files reveal extent of Soviet misinformation over Chernobyl nuclear disaster
stories.summary: Newly revealed East German Stasi files show that Soviet and East German officials were aware of the full devastation of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster. Documents indicate the Stasi attempted to send potentially contaminated produce to West Germany, while Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev recommended misleading the public.

stories.title: Under Trump, green card seekers face new scrutiny for views on Israel
stories.summary: The Trump administration has introduced new scrutiny of green card applicants' views on Israel as part of the permanent residency process. The administration is also approving far fewer applications for permanent legal residency overall.

stories.title: Small plane crash near Minneapolis kills North Dakota state legislator and pilot
stories.summary: North Dakota state Representative Liz Conmy of Fargo was killed when a small plane crashed near Minneapolis. The crash also killed the pilot. State Senator Tim Mathern confirmed his colleague's death.

stories.title: What Hasan Piker got wrong about Einstein and Zionism - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A piece by Noam, published as sponsored content, examined streamer Hasan Piker's claims about Albert Einstein's relationship with Zionism. The article argued Piker presented an incomplete historical portrait of Einstein's views.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister expected back in Pakistan despite US cancellation
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister was expected to return to Pakistan for diplomatic discussions despite the cancellation of a planned visit by U.S. envoys. President Trump had scrapped his envoys' trip, stating there was no point in continuing the talks.

stories.title: US-Iran peace hopes fade as Trump scraps talks
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran have stalled after President Trump withdrew from negotiations. The talks were aimed at ending a two-month U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, but both Washington and Tehran have shown little willingness to compromise on their terms.

stories.title: Can diplomacy survive Trump’s shifting messaging?
stories.summary: US President Trump abruptly cancelled a planned visit by his envoys to Islamabad, where Pakistan had been mediating potential direct engagement between Washington and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The cancellation raises questions about the durability of diplomatic efforts amid shifting presidential messaging.

stories.title: Chinese travellers flock to Central Asia as flight bookings soar 120% on pre-Covid levels
stories.summary: Chinese tourist bookings to Central Asia have surged 120% above pre-Covid levels, driven by expanding air links and economic ties under the Belt and Road Initiative. China's Civil Aviation Administration data showed passenger traffic to Central Asia grew 59.3% in 2025 year-over-year.

stories.title: US reportedly denying green cards over anti-Israel social media posts
stories.summary: According to a New York Times report, U.S. immigration agents have been instructed to review applicants' social media for support of antisemitic terrorism or participation in anti-Israel campus protests. The policy has reportedly led to green card denials based on such online activity.

stories.title: Russia loses 960 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia's total combat losses since the February 2022 invasion have reached approximately 1,325,650 personnel as of April 26, 2026, including 960 troops lost in the past day.

stories.title: Lock in 5.50% eMazel Tov Bonds today - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Israel Bonds has launched eMazel Tov Bonds at a 5.50% rate on a newly redesigned website, marketed as a portfolio diversification option that also supports Israel's economy.

stories.title: US press dinner shooting casts fresh spotlight on Trump’s security
stories.summary: A shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in Washington, D.C., wounded a Secret Service agent and raised security concerns about presidential protection. A suspect armed with a shotgun and other weapons gained access to a floor above the event venue despite the presence of hundreds of law enforcement agents.

stories.title: How American taxpayers fund Trump’s wars
stories.summary: In 2025, American taxpayers collectively worked roughly 50 days to fund military spending. Defense contractors received approximately twice as much federal tax revenue as U.S. military service members, raising questions about the allocation of defense-related expenditures.

stories.title: World reacts to shooting at White House correspondents’ dinner
stories.summary: A shooting occurred at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in Washington, D.C. U.S. politicians from both parties and world leaders condemned the attack and expressed relief that President Donald Trump was unharmed.

stories.title: Ukraine marks 40th anniversary of Chernobyl disaster under cloud of war
stories.summary: Ukraine marked the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster amid its ongoing war with Russia. Kyiv has accused Moscow of repeatedly routing missiles and drones along flight paths near the Chernobyl plant.

stories.title: New fighting erupts in northern Mali's Kidal as army clashes with Tuareg rebels
stories.summary: Clashes between the Malian army and Tuareg rebels erupted in the northern city of Kidal on Sunday. The fighting followed coordinated attacks launched on Saturday by rebels and jihadist groups targeting major cities and government leaders across Mali.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: US Central Command intercepted a commercial vessel in the Arabian Sea linked to Iran's oil trade, ordering it back under escort. Tensions persist from Washington to the Strait of Hormuz, with stalled diplomacy, ongoing military operations, and deepening global economic risks.

stories.title: ‘What ceasefire?’, Lebanese ask as violence simmers in the south
stories.summary: Residents in southern Lebanon are questioning the effectiveness of the existing ceasefire as violence continues in the region. Analysts say the agreement falls short of a genuine ceasefire and remains at risk of collapsing entirely.

stories.title: Anthony Edwards injures knee in Timberwolves’ Game 4 win against Nuggets
stories.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards sustained a knee injury during a Game 4 playoff victory over the Denver Nuggets. Teammate Donte DiVincenzo was also hurt in the game. Minnesota won to take a 3-1 series lead.

stories.title: Russia reduces credit support for businesses – intelligence
stories.summary: Russian intelligence reports indicate that state-backed credit support for businesses is being scaled back in Russia. The reduction in financial support comes amid ongoing economic pressures related to the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Israel’s wars are changing sleep, diet, and exercise in alarming ways - study
stories.summary: An Israeli study found that ongoing wars are significantly affecting the sleep, diet, exercise, and screen-time habits of both adults and children in Israel. Researchers attributed the negative health behavior changes to elevated stress levels caused by the conflict.

stories.title: Hormuz stays flashpoint amid reopening move
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint as Iran demands the US lift its blockade while France, Turkey, and Germany push for de-mining and reopening the vital waterway. After US-Israeli strikes on Iran beginning February 28, Tehran shut the strait and later announced charges for vessels using the route.

stories.title: US intercepts vessel in Arabian Sea over Iran embargo
stories.summary: US Central Command intercepted the commercial vessel "Sevan" in the Arabian Sea for attempting to breach the Iran embargo. A US Navy helicopter from the guided-missile destroyer USS Pinckney carried out the interception. The ship, described as part of a network transporting Iranian oil and gas products, is being escorted back toward Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine marks 40 years since Chernobyl disaster amid war fears
stories.summary: Ukraine marked the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster amid ongoing war concerns. Kyiv has accused Russia of repeatedly sending missiles and drones on flight paths near the Chernobyl plant, including an attack last year that damaged a critical protective shield.

stories.title: Iran submits evidence of civilian attacks to ICC, Red Cross
stories.summary: Iran submitted documentation of attacks on civilians to the International Criminal Court and the International Committee of the Red Cross, according to Iranian Red Crescent Society head Pir-Hossein Kolivand. He said the ICC prosecutor accepted the documents as official evidence and that cases are being examined under international humanitarian law.

stories.title: Hong Kong plans new trial of infecting male mosquitoes to halt offspring growth
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities announced plans to trial a mosquito-control strategy in which male mosquitoes are infected with bacteria to prevent their offspring from reaching maturity. The initiative follows the city's first local dengue fever case in over a year, amid a rising mosquito population.

stories.title: Colombia explosives attack kills 13, police source says
stories.summary: At least 13 people were killed and 17 wounded in an explosives attack in western Colombia on Saturday, according to a police source. Colombian authorities have attributed the violence to dissident factions of the former FARC guerrilla group.

stories.title: Israel-Iran live: U.S. Navy intercepts Iran-linked vessel in Arabian Sea
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy intercepted an Iran-linked vessel in the Arabian Sea amid the broader Iran conflict. Separately, President Trump cancelled a Pakistan talks trip and announced the Iran war was on hold.

stories.title: IDF probes soldiers seen damaging solar panels in south Lebanon Christian village
stories.summary: The Israeli military launched an investigation after soldiers were seen damaging solar panels in the Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon. Lebanese media reported that IDF troops also damaged water infrastructure in the same village where a soldier previously destroyed a Jesus statue. The IDF said the actions do not align with its values.

stories.title: About 21 km of roads need to be covered with anti-drone nets in Sumy– City Military Administration
stories.summary: Sumy's City Military Administration announced that approximately 21 kilometers of roads and 8,000 square meters of open areas in the city need to be covered with anti-drone nets. The measure aims to protect residents and infrastructure from Russian drone attacks.

stories.title: Families of Iranian children killed in school air strike pen letter to Pope Leo
stories.summary: Families of Iranian children killed in a school air strike have written a letter to Pope Leo, thanking the pontiff for advocating on behalf of their children. The letter described him as "the voice for our voiceless children."

stories.title: We can make sure another Chornobyl disaster does not happen, here is how
stories.summary: The article argues that decentralized renewable energy systems offer a safer and more resilient alternative to centralized nuclear power, both in wartime and peacetime, as a way to prevent disasters similar to the 1986 Chornobyl nuclear accident.

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi to return to Pakistan before Moscow visit
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is scheduled to return to Pakistan following a visit to Oman before traveling to Moscow, according to IRNA. Araghchi previously met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir in Islamabad, with discussions focused on regional developments and bilateral ties amid ongoing ceasefire diplomacy.

stories.title: Patient allegedly attacks several nurses, police and member of the public at Sydney hospital
stories.summary: A 51-year-old patient was arrested after allegedly assaulting several nurses, police officers, and a member of the public at Prince of Wales hospital in Sydney on Saturday night. One nurse was seriously injured in the incident, prompting renewed calls for improved security measures in hospital emergency departments.

stories.title: Trump uninjured after after security incident at White House Correspondents’ Dinner
stories.summary: President Donald Trump was uninjured after a security incident at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington. Secret Service and other authorities responded as hundreds of guests ducked under tables during the disruption.

stories.title: Iran says controlled detonations to clear leftover munitions
stories.summary: Authorities in Iran's Zanjan Province warned residents of planned controlled detonations to dispose of unexploded ordnance left from recent attacks. The Ansar al-Mahdi Corps said the operations aim to neutralize inoperative munitions and ensure public safety in the area.

stories.title: Dozens of MPs oppose Streeting’s new power to say what NHS pays for drugs
stories.summary: Thirty-one UK Members of Parliament signed a House of Commons motion opposing Health Secretary Wes Streeting's plan to grant himself power to override the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence on NHS drug pricing. Critics described the move as a power grab and raised concerns it may be illegal and could benefit large pharmaceutical companies.

stories.title: Russian drones attack Chernihiv, fires break out in city
stories.summary: Russian drones attacked the city of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine, causing fires in private homes. The strike involved enemy unmanned aerial vehicles targeting residential areas.

stories.title: Coordinated attacks rock Mali, injure 16 across multiple Cities
stories.summary: Armed groups launched one of the largest coordinated attacks in Mali in recent years, striking targets across the capital Bamako and several other cities. Government officials confirmed at least 16 people were injured in assaults on both civilian and military sites.

stories.title: Shots fired as gunman charges at White House correspondents’ dinner; Trump unharmed
stories.summary: A gunman charged toward the stage at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in Washington, prompting Secret Service agents to rush President Trump and Vice President Vance to safety. The suspect was detained. Trump said he doubts the incident is linked to the Iran war and stated it will not change his position.

stories.title: Police say motive unknown in White House dinner attack
stories.summary: Investigators said the motive behind the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner remains unclear. Interim police chief Jeffery Carroll said it is too early to determine the suspect's intended target. US Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced preliminary charges including firearm-related offenses and assault on an officer.

stories.title: U.S. Navy intercepts Iran-linked vessel in Arabian Sea
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy intercepted an Iran-linked vessel in the Arabian Sea. The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned the M/V Sevan and 18 other "shadow fleet" vessels for transporting billions of dollars in Iranian energy products to foreign markets.

stories.title: U.S. sanctions waiver on Chabahar port ends on April 26, could signal end of 23-year-old connectivity project
stories.summary: A U.S. sanctions waiver on India's use of Iran's Chabahar port is set to expire on April 26, potentially ending a 23-year-old connectivity project. Officials are reportedly discussing a possible transfer of an IPGL subsidiary's stake to a local Iranian company to avoid sanctions.

stories.title: Russian drones attack Sumy region, leaving two killed
stories.summary: Two residents of the Bilopillia community in Ukraine's Sumy region were killed in a Russian drone attack. The strikes targeted the community located near the Russian border.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 58 as Tehran-Washington talks stall?
stories.summary: On day 58 of the Iran–US war, President Trump cancelled a planned trip by his envoys to Pakistan, marking the latest setback in stalled diplomatic efforts to negotiate an end to the conflict between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Explosive device kills 13, injures 38 on bus in southwestern Colombia as violence persists
stories.summary: An explosive device detonated on a bus in southwestern Colombia, killing 13 people and injuring 38. The attack is part of a series of explosions targeting public infrastructure in the country.

stories.title: Pregnant woman collapses and dies, doctors unable to save her or her twins
stories.summary: Reut Cohen, a pregnant woman in her 30th week, collapsed and was rushed to a hospital in Israel, where she underwent an emergency cesarean section. Both the mother and her unborn twin girls died. The family has raised questions about whether doctors previously missed a serious medical condition.

stories.title: Russian drones strike Dnipro: Fire breaks out at infrastructure facility
stories.summary: Russian strike drones attacked the city of Dnipro in central-eastern Ukraine, causing a fire at an infrastructure facility. The attack was the latest in a series of drone strikes on the city.

stories.title: Ukraine marks 40th anniversary of Chornobyl disaster under cloud of war
stories.summary: Ukraine commemorated the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chornobyl nuclear disaster on April 26 in Kyiv. The anniversary comes amid ongoing concerns that Russia's war against Ukraine could risk another nuclear catastrophe at or near the site of the world's worst nuclear accident.

stories.title: Hong Kong boosts e-cigarette ban awareness in mainland China before ‘golden week’
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities intensified publicity through mainland Chinese media ahead of a ban on possessing alternative smoking products, including e-cigarettes, in public places before the Labour Day holiday. Director of Health Ronald Lam said the Tobacco and Alcohol Control Office conducted over 11,000 inspections and issued about 2,200 fixed penalty notices this year.

stories.title: Several killed in Colombia highway bomb attack ahead of presidential election
stories.summary: At least 14 people were killed and 38 injured in a highway bomb attack in southwest Colombia. Authorities blamed dissidents of the former FARC guerrilla army for the attack, which occurred amid a wave of violence ahead of next month's presidential election.

stories.title: Republican Party weighs strategy as Iran war impacts voters
stories.summary: The Republican Party is recalibrating its strategy ahead of November midterm elections as rising fuel prices and President Trump's declining approval ratings — now in the mid-30s — create political challenges. Economic strain linked to the war with Iran has become a central voter concern, prompting party strategists to focus on economic messaging.

stories.title: Who is Cole Tomas Allen, the suspect linked to Trump’s press dinner shooting?
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen of Torrance, California, was identified as the suspect arrested in connection with the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday. Social media profiles matching Allen describe him as a highly educated tutor and amateur video game developer.

stories.title: Frenzy for Hong Kong luxury homes set to continue after 156% sales rise in first quarter
stories.summary: Sales of luxury homes in Hong Kong rose 156% in the first quarter of the year compared to the same period last year. Analysts attributed the surge to a buoyant stock market and attractively priced assets drawing wealthy investors, including mainland Chinese buyers, and predicted continued growth in the second quarter.

stories.title: The tortoise and the hare: will China beat the US in the race back to the moon?
stories.summary: The United States and China are both accelerating preparations for crewed lunar landings, with plans to build inhabited bases on the moon. NASA recently sent four astronauts around the moon, but China may reach the surface first. Both nations aim to search for resources and test technology for future Mars missions.

stories.title: From syringes to stents: Iran war exposes NHS dependency on petrochemicals
stories.summary: NHS officials raised concerns about potential shortages and rising costs for medicines and medical products due to a shipping standstill in the Gulf caused by the war in Iran. Many healthcare essentials—including syringes, intravenous bags, gloves, and active pharmaceutical ingredients—depend on petrochemicals transported through the region.

stories.title: Ghost MOTs: drivers warned over fake certificates that lead to huge repair bills
stories.summary: UK drivers were warned about fraudulent MOT certificates being issued for vehicles that have not been properly inspected. Secondhand car buyers are urged to carefully check vehicles, as fake tests can conceal serious safety defects such as low tyre tread and steering problems, leading to significant repair costs.

stories.title: Through the excitement of Israel-Lebanon talks, Hezbollah must not be forgotten - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that for the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire and peace talks to succeed, the main focus must be on defanging and marginalizing Hezbollah. The piece emphasizes the group's continued role as a threat to stability in the region.

stories.title: Grenade explosion in Zaporizhzhia apartment kills woman, injures two men
stories.summary: A grenade exploded inside an apartment in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, killing one woman and injuring two men with shrapnel wounds. The incident occurred in a residential apartment building.

stories.title: At Malaysia’s arms bazaar, drone dealers chase Southeast Asian market share
stories.summary: The Defence Services Asia exhibition in Kuala Lumpur showcased growing demand for unmanned aerial vehicles among Southeast Asian defense ministries. Drone vendors from multiple countries, including firms from Abu Dhabi to Pretoria, competed for contracts in the region's expanding UAV market.

stories.title: Iran markets hold steady despite sanctions, prices rise
stories.summary: Nearly two weeks after a US naval blockade, markets across Iran remain stocked with basic goods, though prices are rising and consumers worry about future shortages. President Masoud Pezeshkian accused the United States of using economic pressure to fuel public dissatisfaction, while Tehran pursues alternative land and maritime trade routes.

stories.title: Aliyah in wartime Israel: Building a new home, opening an English bookstore
stories.summary: Michal Goldschmidt, a former London curator, made aliyah to Israel during wartime and opened Bookhaus, an English-language bookstore in Tel Aviv. The store has become a community space for English-speaking readers.

stories.title: Colombia highway bomb attack kills 14
stories.summary: Suspected guerrillas detonated explosives on the Pan-American Highway in southwest Colombia, killing 14 people. The region has experienced a surge in violence in recent days.

stories.title: Clowning, caring, and claiming her voice: How Jerusalemite Channah Appel is making a difference
stories.summary: Jerusalemite Channah Appel is making a difference in her community through compassion, community initiatives, and personal determination. Her work spans clowning and caring activities across Israel.

stories.title: Six charged in UK after report van drove into drone maker’s gate
stories.summary: Six individuals have been charged in the United Kingdom after a van reportedly drove into the gate of UAV Tactical Systems, a company specializing in military drone manufacturing. The incident is being investigated as a deliberate act targeting the defense-related facility.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Iran's FM to return to Pakistan for talks as US envoys cancel visit
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to return to Islamabad on Sunday for further peace negotiations after departing Pakistan the previous day. US envoys canceled their planned visit to Islamabad after Iran refused to participate in direct negotiations with the United States.

stories.title: Blast targets minister’s home
stories.summary: A bomb exploded near the residence of Balochistan Irrigation Minister Mir Sadiq Umrani in Dera Murad Jamali, Pakistan, damaging parts of the house and destroying a nearby Wapda transformer. Umrani was not present at the time, and no casualties were reported among servants inside.

stories.title: Cybersecurity policy gaps expose firms to risks: survey
stories.summary: A Kaspersky survey on cybersecurity in Pakistani workplaces found that 39% of professionals consider their company's cybersecurity rules excessive or inappropriate, while 8% say their organizations lack such rules entirely. The findings highlight risks linked to shadow IT and unmanaged device usage.

stories.title: Latest Colombia bomb attack leaves 7 dead, more than 20 hurt
stories.summary: A bomb attack in Colombia killed at least seven people and injured more than 20 others. The incident is part of a wave of violence striking the South American country in the lead-up to a presidential election scheduled for May.

stories.title: Trump says DC shooting not linked to Iran as probe widens
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated he does not believe a shooting incident in Washington, DC, is linked to Iran. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said charges would be filed soon, while FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed investigators are examining recovered weapons and interviewing witnesses.

stories.title: 'I’m the only person who can do it': Why 102-year-old Dachau survivor Jean Lafaurie tells his story
stories.summary: Jean Lafaurie, a 102-year-old French Resistance member and Dachau concentration camp survivor, continues to share his wartime experiences with students. Ahead of France's National Day of Remembrance for Victims and Heroes of the Deportation, he spoke about solidarity among prisoners and warned about the resurgence of the far right in Europe.

stories.title: British farmers deliver 38 more off-road vehicles to Ukrainian troops
stories.summary: British farmers delivered 38 additional off-road vehicles to Ukrainian military forces through the Pickups for Peace initiative. The donation continues an ongoing civilian effort in the UK to support Ukraine's defense capabilities.

stories.title: Israel backs diplomacy with Lebanon but warns on Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israeli UN Ambassador Danny Danon expressed support for diplomatic efforts and direct negotiations with Lebanon. However, he warned that Israel would continue to respond to threats from Hezbollah, citing ongoing rocket fire and regional destabilization by the group.

stories.title: Could Russian missiles help India counter its arch-rival’s Chinese weapons?
stories.summary: India has reportedly signed a roughly $1.2 billion deal with Russia to acquire around 300 R-37M ultra-long-range air-to-air missiles, with deliveries expected within 12 to 18 months. The purchase comes as Pakistan and China deepen integration of their aerial weapons capabilities. India is also developing its own Astra Mk 2 and Mk 3 missiles domestically.

stories.title: Ukrainian action thriller billed as Saving Private Ryan for the drone age
stories.summary: A Ukrainian action thriller titled "Killhouse" has been released, based on the real-life rescue of a civilian couple from a battlefield by Ukrainian drone operators. The film features a cameo by former Ukrainian military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and is set in 2024.

stories.title: Tibetans-in-exile vote for new government as future without Dalai Lama looms
stories.summary: Tibetans living in exile voted on Sunday for leadership of the India-based Central Tibetan Administration, their government-in-exile. The election is seen as increasingly significant as the community prepares for a future without the aging Dalai Lama as its spiritual leader.

stories.title: India advises nationals in Mali to stay indoors, exercise caution due to security developments
stories.summary: The Indian embassy in Mali advised Indian nationals to stay indoors and exercise caution due to security developments in the country. The embassy said it was closely monitoring the situation in coordination with Malian authorities.

stories.title: Islamic militants, separatists claim simultaneous attacks across Mali
stories.summary: Islamic militants and separatist groups launched simultaneous attacks across Mali, with reports of explosions and gunfire near the town of Kati and Bamako's international airport. The U.S. Embassy in Bamako issued a security alert urging American citizens to shelter in place.

stories.title: Suspect in custody after Trump evacuated in shooting incident at White House correspondents’ dinner
stories.summary: President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump were evacuated unharmed from the White House correspondents' dinner at the Washington Hilton after gunshots interrupted the event. The FBI confirmed a suspect is in custody and faces two counts of felony firearms and assault charges.

stories.title: Israel PM orders attacks on Hezbollah after army alleges truce violations
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered military strikes on Hezbollah after the army alleged ceasefire violations. Hours before the order, the Israeli military said it had killed more than 15 fighters in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Video: Colombia blames dissident FARC rebel for deadly bus bomb
stories.summary: A bomb-laden bus exploded on the Pan-American Highway in Colombia, killing at least 14 people. Colombian authorities have blamed a dissident FARC rebel faction for the attack on the route leading toward Venezuela.

stories.title: Second attack in Dnipro injures three children
stories.summary: Three children were injured in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro during a second attack targeting a residential neighborhood. No further details on the origin of the attack were immediately provided.

stories.title: Iran president cites ‘contradiction’ in US pressure and diplomacy
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif that a growing contradiction exists between US diplomatic overtures and continued pressure measures, including a blockade. Pezeshkian said the contradiction has deepened mistrust among Iranian officials and citizens toward Washington. He noted that negotiations held in Islamabad had stalled.

stories.title: Israeli military launches raids after government directive
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes carried out airstrikes across southern Lebanon following a directive from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to target Hezbollah positions. Lebanon's National News Agency reported raids hitting several towns, including Haddatha, Zibqin, Khirbet Selm, and Sultaniyeh.

stories.title: US to allow denial of green card applicants over anti-Israel political opinions  - NYT
stories.summary: According to the New York Times, the United States plans to allow denial of green card applications based on applicants' anti-Israel political opinions. Related job postings reportedly now refer to immigration officers as "homeland defenders."

stories.title: From child laborer to union leader: Too-relevant story of 20th-century immigrant Pauline Newman
stories.summary: A new book by Cathryn J. Prince, titled 'For the Love of Labor,' chronicles the life of Lithuanian-born Pauline Newman, who immigrated to the United States as a child laborer and became a prominent union leader and activist fighting sexism and classism.

stories.title: At least 13 killed, 17 injured in Colombia explosives attack, police source says
stories.summary: At least 13 people were killed and 17 injured in an explosives attack on the Pan-American Highway in the El Tunel area of Cajibio municipality in Colombia's Cauca province. The site is approximately 35 kilometers from the provincial capital, Popayan.

stories.title: Araghchi holds calls with Egypt and Turkey on diplomacy
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held separate phone calls with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan to discuss diplomacy, ceasefire efforts, and regional developments. Fidan's conversation with Araghchi focused on Iran-U.S. negotiations. Fidan also spoke with Pakistan's Ishaq Dar on the same issue.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine will continue educational programs for Azerbaijani students
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine will continue its educational programs for students from Azerbaijan. The commitment maintains ongoing academic cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: Shooter arrested after gunfire at Trump event in Washington
stories.summary: A suspect was arrested after shots were fired during the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in Washington, D.C. President Donald Trump confirmed the shooter's apprehension on Truth Social. The U.S. Secret Service took the suspect into custody as witnesses reported multiple shots and guests took cover.

stories.title: US to add firing squad, electrocutions, gas asphyxiation to federal execution methods
stories.summary: The US Justice Department plans to add firing squads, electrocution, and gas asphyxiation as federal execution methods. The move follows difficulties obtaining drugs for lethal injections after President Trump rescinded a moratorium on federal executions last year.

stories.title: Israel says military killed three Hamas fighters
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it killed three Hamas fighters, including a commander it said had infiltrated Israel during the October 7, 2023 attacks. The other two were identified as a platoon commander and a military intelligence operative. The military did not specify where or when the killings took place.

stories.title: Hundreds of Israelis rally as US-Iran peace talks stall
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters rallied in Tel Aviv on Sunday amid concerns that US-Iran peace talks have stalled. Demonstrators expressed fears that the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran could resume.

stories.title: What’s fuelling the surge in South Koreans travelling to China?
stories.summary: A growing number of South Korean content creators are traveling to Chinese cities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen to produce travel vlogs. The surge follows China's extension of its unilateral visa-free policy for South Korean passport holders, originally introduced in 2024, allowing stays of up to 30 days.

stories.title: UAE and India discuss Middle East stability, energy security
stories.summary: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan met India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval in Abu Dhabi. The two discussed developments in the Middle East and their implications for regional and international security, stability, and global energy markets.

stories.title: Iran submits ‘framework’ for talks, stresses trust gap with US
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi submitted a negotiating framework to mediators in Islamabad, Pakistan. During talks with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Pezeshkian identified trust as the central issue, citing the blockade around the Strait of Hormuz and military activity in the Sea of Oman as major obstacles.

stories.title: Six killed in Israeli strikes on south Lebanon: Health Ministry
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed six people, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The Israeli military said it identified two projectiles launched from Lebanon and intercepted a suspicious aerial target, calling the launches a violation of ceasefire understandings by Hezbollah.

stories.title: UN says Hormuz disruption risks global food crisis
stories.summary: Jorge Moreira da Silva of the United Nations Office for Project Services warned that continued disruption from the Iran conflict could push approximately 45 million more people into hunger globally. He identified the blockage of fertiliser shipments through the Strait of Hormuz as a key driver of the risk.

stories.title: Gaza Civil Defence says Israeli strikes kill 13
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed 13 people, according to the territory's Civil Defence. Gaza's Interior Ministry said two of the dead were police officers.

stories.title: Russia pounds Ukraine’s Dnipro for 20 hours straight, killing eight people
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Ukrainian city of Dnipro over a continuous 20-hour period, killing at least eight people. The attacks came in successive waves, targeting residential buildings, commercial properties, and energy infrastructure.

stories.title: US scraps Islamabad visit as Trump cites new Iran proposal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump cancelled a planned visit by envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to Islamabad, where they were to meet Iranian officials, citing frustration over stalled negotiations. Shortly after the cancellation, Trump said the U.S. received a new proposal from Iran that he described as "much better."

stories.title: Sexual abuse in Iranian prisons sharply rises as population repression increases during ceasefire
stories.summary: Reports indicate a sharp rise in sexual abuse in Iranian prisons amid increased population repression during a ceasefire period. One young woman told The Media Line she was sexually assaulted during interrogation by officers using batons.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces destroy Russian shelter on Kupiansk front
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces destroyed a Russian military shelter in the Kupiansk sector of the front line. The Kupiansk area in northeastern Ukraine remains an active zone of combat operations.

stories.title: Police blocked members of anti-immigration group from Perth dawn service after Anzac Day booing in eastern states
stories.summary: Western Australian police preemptively blocked 15 members of anti-immigration groups from attending Anzac Day dawn service commemorations in Perth. The action followed disruptions at eastern Australian ceremonies, including a man arrested at Sydney's Martin Place dawn service where booing occurred during the Indigenous acknowledgment.

stories.title: Can Chongqing leverage its online viral fame to become an international tourism hub?
stories.summary: Chongqing, a mountainous city in southwestern China, has gained international attention through viral social media videos highlighting its unusual multi-level urban landscape. Content creators and tourism experts are exploring whether the city can translate its online popularity into sustained growth as an international tourism destination.

stories.title: Some Hong Kong trees are behaving strangely and botanists want to know why
stories.summary: Botanists in Hong Kong have called for a citywide study into how global warming is altering plant behavior across the territory. Species such as the red kapok tree and flame tree have shown incomplete winter leaf-shedding and early flowering in recent years, raising concerns about broader ecosystem impacts.

stories.title: Muddy yet clear-cut: How Chinese investors are turning jungle into Indonesia’s new capital
stories.summary: Chinese investors are playing a significant role in developing Nusantara (IKN), Indonesia's new capital being built in the jungles of Borneo. The city is intended to replace Jakarta, which faces severe congestion, pollution, and land subsidence, with the transition scheduled to begin in 2028.

stories.title: Rumours of China Forbidden City using 600,000 tonnes of pig blood to ‘dispel evil’ debunked
stories.summary: A recently published book by Zhou Qian, a 20-year researcher at Beijing's Forbidden City, has debunked the widespread rumor that 600,000 tonnes of pig blood are used annually at the palace to dispel evil. The liquid is actually a traditional adhesive applied to the landmark's iconic red walls and pillars.

stories.title: Israel told US to pressure Lebanon into acting against Hezbollah or risk ceasefire collapse - KAN
stories.summary: Israel reportedly urged the United States to pressure Lebanon into taking action against Hezbollah, warning that the ceasefire could otherwise collapse. Hezbollah and its political ally Nabih Berri, Lebanon's parliament speaker and Amal Movement leader, were cited as the main obstacles to the truce.

stories.title: Trump uninjured after security incident at White House correspondents’ dinner
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and other officials were evacuated from the annual White House Correspondents' Dinner on Saturday night after an unspecified security threat and reports of loud bangs. Secret Service agents drew weapons and cleared the banquet hall. No injuries were reported.

stories.title: Promoting Diaspora aliyah will never succeed through anger - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion article argues that efforts to encourage Diaspora Jews to immigrate to Israel should focus on partnership rather than accusations. It contends that anger-based messaging undermines Israel-Diaspora ties.

stories.title: Trump evacuated from White House Correspondents’ Dinner after shots fired; suspect apprehended
stories.summary: President Donald Trump and Vice President were evacuated unharmed from the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington after shots were fired, and a suspect was apprehended by the Secret Service. Separately, six people were charged in the UK after allegedly driving a van into the entrance of an Elbit-owned drone factory.

stories.title: IDF probes video showing soldiers destroying solar panels in Christian-Lebanese village
stories.summary: The Israeli military opened a probe into a video showing soldiers destroying solar panels in the Christian Lebanese village of Debel. The same village drew international outcry after an IDF soldier was photographed smashing a statue of Jesus.

stories.title: Kremlin eyes citizens’ wallets as budget deficit deepens – intelligence
stories.summary: Russian authorities are exploring new revenue sources to address a deepening state budget deficit, according to intelligence reports. Measures under consideration include increasing the financial burden on citizens and businesses.

stories.title: Netanyahu orders army to 'vigorously attack' Hezbollah in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to launch intensified attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon, even as six people were killed by strikes there despite a ceasefire that had been extended by three weeks.

stories.title: President Zardari arrives in China for visit focused on 'economic cooperation, CPEC'
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari arrived in Changsha, China, for a visit focused on economic cooperation and the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC). He was received by Hu Xusheng, Vice Chairman of the Hunan Provincial People's Congress.

stories.title: 40 years after Chernobyl: Pripyat today
stories.summary: DW visited the abandoned city of Pripyat, Ukraine, 40 years after the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster, accompanied by a former resident. Approximately 50,000 people permanently evacuated the city following the catastrophic reactor accident.

stories.title: Four killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, state media says
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed four people on Saturday, according to Lebanon's state news agency. The Israeli military reported that Hezbollah had fired rockets into Israel. The violence poses fresh challenges to a recently extended ceasefire between the two sides.

stories.title: Hungary’s Orban will not sit in Parliament after election loss
stories.summary: Viktor Orbán's coalition lost Hungary's April 12 parliamentary election, ending his 16-year hold on power. Orbán will not take a seat in the new parliament.

stories.title: Explosive device kills 13 and injures 38 on bus in Colombia
stories.summary: An explosive device detonated on a bus traveling along the Pan-American Highway in Cajibío, Cauca, southwestern Colombia, killing 13 people and injuring at least 38, including five children. Governor Octavio Guzmán confirmed the attack, which Colombia's army chief called a terrorist act linked to escalating drug-trafficking violence in the region.

stories.title: Trump cancels Pakistan talks trip, says Iran war on hold
stories.summary: President Donald Trump cancelled his envoys' trip to Pakistan for peace talks with Iran but stated that the war would not immediately resume. The cancellation came amid stalled negotiations between the two sides.

stories.title: Will South Korea or Japan develop a nuclear deterrent of their own?
stories.summary: Debate over independent nuclear deterrents has intensified in South Korea and Japan following the U.S.-led conflict with Iran. The IAEA director general has raised alarm over the shift. Both nations, long defined by their non-nuclear postures, are now seeing mainstream discussion of developing their own arsenals.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran rejects talks under siege, Trump cancels envoys’ trip
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran did not present a satisfactory offer for negotiations. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Pakistan following the breakdown. Trump also cancelled a planned trip by U.S. envoys to Islamabad.

stories.title: Six charged in UK after van hits Israel-linked drone factory
stories.summary: Six people are scheduled to appear in a UK court on Monday facing charges after a van allegedly drove into the entrance gate of a drone company linked to Israel. The incident targeted a facility associated with Israeli defense firm Elbit Systems.

stories.title: Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian calls on people to save energy
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian urged citizens to conserve energy. He has previously launched public awareness campaigns aimed at reducing national energy consumption.

stories.title: In call with Iranian president, PM says Pakistan committed to serving as 'honest and sincere facilitator'
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke by phone with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday after an Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Araghchi departed Islamabad. Sharif reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to serving as an honest facilitator in resolving the regional conflict.

stories.title: Under Trump, green card seekers face new scrutiny for views on Israel
stories.summary: The Trump administration has introduced additional scrutiny of green card applicants' views on Israel. Officials have characterized criticism of Israel as an "overwhelmingly negative" factor in immigration evaluations.

stories.title: Trump cancels envoys’ trip to Islamabad, hopes fade for breakthrough in Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump canceled his envoys' planned trip to Islamabad for Iran negotiations. Iran's Foreign Minister departed the Pakistani capital after holding talks with Pakistan's prime minister, dimming prospects for an immediate diplomatic breakthrough.

stories.title: Trump says cancelled envoys' Pakistan trip, but Iran war not resuming
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Islamabad and arrived in Muscat on Saturday, April 25, for meetings with Omani officials, following consultations in Pakistan.

stories.title: US embassy issues security alert amid arsons against UK Jewish sites
stories.summary: The U.S. Embassy in the United Kingdom issued a security alert following arson attacks against Jewish sites in Britain. The embassy advised American citizens to remain vigilant when visiting Jewish places of worship, religious sites, and community centers.

stories.title: Evening recap
