stories.summary: Israeli forces injured six Palestinians during a raid on a polling station in Khirbet Khallat al-Miyya in the occupied West Bank on Saturday. Lebanese state media reported new Israeli strikes in at least four locations in southern Lebanon after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered intensified attacks on alleged Hezbollah positions.

stories.title: US-Iran talks unlikely to reach breakthrough, Republican Party lawmaker says
stories.summary: Republican Representative Michael McCaul of Texas said he does not expect a significant breakthrough in ongoing US-Iran negotiations in the near term.

stories.title: Germany blames Russia for Signal phishing attacks on lawmakers
stories.summary: Germany has accused Russia of conducting phishing attacks via the Signal messaging platform targeting German lawmakers. Civil servants, diplomats, and journalists were also among those targeted by the campaign.

stories.title: Air defence systems activated in Iran’s Kermanshah
stories.summary: Air defense systems were activated over Kermanshah, Iran, and its surrounding suburbs, according to the Mehr news agency. Local sources suggested the activity may have been a defense system test, but Iranian officials had not issued formal confirmation.

stories.title: What rules govern international waters?
stories.summary: The article examines the legal framework governing international waters in the context of the Iran-U.S. conflict, including Iran's right to restrict transit through the Strait of Hormuz and the legality of the U.S. blockade. It also addresses rules on maritime interceptions and the role of international organizations.

stories.title: Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf | Iran’s wartime apparatchik
stories.summary: Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's Parliament Speaker and former IRGC commander, has emerged as a leading figure in Iran's wartime governance after much of the country's top leadership was killed. His background includes service during the 1980–88 Iran-Iraq war.

stories.title: Government said to have refused to increase air defense funds after 2024 Iranian attacks
stories.summary: A report alleges that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition government refused to increase air defense funding after Iranian attacks in 2024, despite recommendations to boost interceptor missile production. Some coalition members reportedly pushed to invest only in offensive military capabilities.

stories.title: The detained anti-colonial activist grabbing attention in West Africa: Who is Kemi Seba?
stories.summary: Kemi Seba, an anti-colonial activist detained in West Africa, has drawn significant attention for condemning France's influence in the region. He has also been accused of serving as a mouthpiece for Russian interests.

stories.title: Europe prepares for a longer war in Ukraine, with no strategy to end it
stories.summary: European governments are preparing for a prolonged war in Ukraine but lack a clear strategy to bring the conflict to an end. Expectations for a negotiated settlement between Moscow and Kyiv have continued to diminish.

stories.title: A 17th Century 'supercomputer' once owned by Indian royalty heads for auction
stories.summary: A 17th-century astrolabe, described as possibly the largest in existence, once owned by Indian royalty, is heading to auction. The astronomical computing instrument has never been publicly exhibited before.

stories.title: BBC visits Chernobyl ghost city 40 years after world's worst nuclear accident
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Jessica Parker visited Pripyat, Ukraine, approximately 40 years after the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster. The city was abandoned after an explosion at the nearby Chernobyl nuclear power plant forced the evacuation of its residents.

stories.title: Rescuers complete emergency response at site of four-story building destroyed by Russian strike
stories.summary: Rescue workers completed emergency operations at the site of a four-story building partially destroyed by a Russian strike. Six people were killed and 23 others were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Islamabad administration allows public, goods transport; revises business timings
stories.summary: Islamabad's administration lifted restrictions on public and goods transport entering the city on Saturday night, reopening bus stands citywide except the Faizabad terminal. Authorities also reopened hiking trails and public parks, including Daman-i-Koh and Lake View.

stories.title: Iran says it’s committed to ‘strengthening mutual trust’ in the region
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Muscat, Oman, in an official diplomatic trip. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran remains committed to strengthening mutual trust and constructive cooperation with Persian Gulf states.

stories.title: Drone attack leaves teenager without arm; family with two children evacuated again from Lyman
stories.summary: Ukraine's "White Angel" police unit evacuated a family with two children from Lyman in the Donetsk region, including a 17-year-old boy who lost his arm in a drone attack. The area remains under persistent threat from drone strikes.

stories.title: Israeli forces injure six Palestinians in raid on West Bank polling station
stories.summary: Israeli forces injured six Palestinians during a raid on a polling station in the Khirbet Khallat al-Miyya area south of Hebron in the occupied West Bank. The Palestinian Red Crescent Society said the injuries were caused by beatings during an incursion into a center used for 2026 local elections.

stories.title: New Israeli strikes reported in Lebanon after Netanyahu orders attacks
stories.summary: Lebanese state media reported new Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon on Saturday night, following earlier attacks that killed six people despite a recently extended ceasefire. The strikes came after Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered the military to "forcefully attack Hezbollah targets" in response to alleged truce violations.

stories.title: Slovenian president tells lawmakers to nominate PM able to form coalition
stories.summary: Slovenian President Nataša Pirc Musar announced she would not nominate a prime minister-designate following last month's election, as no parliamentary group secured sufficient support to form a governing coalition. She called on lawmakers to identify a candidate capable of assembling a majority.

stories.title: How media misreporting in Turmus Aiya shaped a false wartime narrative - opinion
stories.summary: A commentary piece argues that misreporting around Route 60 near the Palestinian town of Turmus Aiya contributed to a false wartime narrative. It highlights how unverified claims can quickly shape perceptions during active conflict.

stories.title: Will China’s mathematicians join a global effort to boycott the United States?
stories.summary: Over 2,300 mathematicians from at least 76 countries have signed a petition opposing the 2026 International Congress of Mathematicians being held in Philadelphia. The petition calls for relocating the prestigious conference, which also hosts the Fields Medal ceremony, out of the United States.

stories.title: Czech analyst: Western experts warned of Russian aggression but not its full scale
stories.summary: Czech analysts noted that Western experts, particularly in the Czech Republic, warned of potential Russian aggression following the 2014 annexation of Crimea. However, their predictions significantly underestimated the scale of the military campaign Russia ultimately launched.

stories.title: Romania finds parts of second drone after overnight Russian attack on Ukraine
stories.summary: Romania discovered parts of a second drone on its territory following an overnight Russian attack on Ukraine. Romania's Foreign Ministry summoned the Russian ambassador to protest the incident.

stories.title: Spain’s stance on Israel raises concerns over growing European delegitimization - opinion
stories.summary: Spain has faced criticism over its stance on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, with accusations that its rhetoric toward Israel and relative silence on Hamas amount to hypocrisy. Commentators have raised concerns about a broader trend of European delegitimization of Israel.

stories.title: Hundreds protest police inaction after pizzeria murder: ‘This is a wake-up call’
stories.summary: Hundreds of people protested in Petah Tikva, Israel, over perceived police inaction following the stabbing murder of a Pizza Hut worker on Independence Day. A teenage suspect was caught on camera holding a bloodied knife shortly after the attack.

stories.title: Woman and child injured in fresh spate of settler attacks on Palestinian villages
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages in Duma and the Hebron area, injuring a woman and a child. Reports indicated the victims had previously been displaced by violence, and IDF soldiers arrived only after attacks ended or were seen standing by without intervening.

stories.title: Iranian delegation led by Araghchi leaves after meeting PM, CDF Munir; Trump cancels US envoys' visit
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Islamabad after meeting Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir. Simultaneously, President Trump cancelled the visit of U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who had been expected to travel to Pakistan for Iran talks.

stories.title: Lebanon state media reports new Israeli strikes in south after Netanyahu order
stories.summary: Lebanese state media reported new Israeli airstrikes in at least four locations across southern Lebanon, hitting towns in the Bint Jbeil, Tyre, and Nabatieh districts. The strikes came after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered his military to attack Hezbollah targets.

stories.title: Three Palestine Action activists sentenced to 20 months for attack on US defense factory
stories.summary: Three Palestine Action activists—Najam Shah, Julian Gao, and Daniel Jones—were sentenced to 20 months in prison for their role in an April attack on the Teledyne Defense and Space factory in Shipley, England. They had been convicted in February.

stories.title: Trump cancels US envoys' trip to Pakistan for talks on Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump canceled a diplomatic trip to Pakistan by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner that was intended for talks related to the Iran conflict. Iran had previously stated there were no plans for a direct meeting with the U.S. delegation.

stories.title: To be the world No 2 financial centre, Hong Kong must be a rule maker
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said the city could become the world's second-ranked financial center within 10 to 15 years. The article argues that achieving this goal requires Hong Kong to move beyond competitiveness and become a global rule-maker amid geopolitical shifts.

stories.title: Dnipro: 208 residents file police reports over property damage from enemy attacks
stories.summary: In the Ukrainian city of Dnipro, 208 residents filed police reports over property damage caused by enemy attacks on April 25.

stories.title: Iran's Araqchi expected to visit Pakistan again after Oman trip, Mehr reports
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to return to Pakistan after visiting Oman and before traveling to Russia, according to Iran's Mehr news agency. His earlier meetings in Islamabad with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and other officials ended without a reported breakthrough in peace talks.

stories.title: Operation to recover boy swept away while swimming in water line continues for 2nd day in Karachi
stories.summary: Rescue workers in Karachi continued a second day of operations to recover 11-year-old Zahid Mohammed Khan, who was swept away while swimming in a Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation line in Scheme 33 near Al-Azhar Garden. Lifeguards from Rescue 1122 and the Edhi Foundation have been conducting the search.

stories.title: Sanctions on Russia: Do they work? Why? Why not? Blame? Changes?
stories.summary: A conference in Kyiv examined the effectiveness of Western sanctions imposed on Russia over the past 50 months. Topics included sanctions enforcement, accountability, the role of civil society, war profiteering, and which measures have and have not achieved their goals.

stories.title: Mali junta battles ‘terrorist groups’ amid intense fighting
stories.summary: Mali's military junta reported ongoing battles against what it called terrorist groups following surprise attacks in and around the capital Bamako. The whereabouts of junta leader General Assimi Goïta were reported as unknown during the fighting.

stories.title: Taliban Government says Afghans in Qatar can return 'with full confidence'
stories.summary: The Taliban government in Afghanistan said Afghans residing in a camp in Qatar can return home "with full confidence." A U.S. State Department spokesperson said moving the Afghans to a third country was a positive resolution for their safety.

stories.title: Explosion in southwest Colombia kills at least seven, state governor says
stories.summary: An explosion on the Pan-American Highway in Colombia's Cauca region killed at least seven people. Authorities in Cauca called on the national government to take decisive action in response to the attack.

stories.title: Iran’s armed forces warns US against renewed ‘aggression’
stories.summary: Iran's military warned the United States against continuing attacks in the region and pledged to maintain control over the Strait of Hormuz. The Khatam al-Anbiya Headquarters statement, reported by Tasnim news agency, threatened a forceful response if the US pursues what it called siege and piracy operations.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Dnipro kill eight, wound 49
stories.summary: Russian attacks on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro over a 24-hour period killed eight people and wounded 49 others.

stories.title: Ben Perry: How one Israeli actor turned sirens into viral comedy - interview
stories.summary: Israeli actor Ben Perry gained viral popularity online by turning wartime sirens into comedic content involving laughter, song, and dance. His videos accumulated millions of views over nearly six weeks of siren-related episodes.

stories.title: How serious is the rift in NATO?
stories.summary: Tensions within NATO have escalated as President Trump expressed anger over European allies' refusal to participate in the war against Iran. The disagreement has raised questions about the depth of the rift within the alliance.

stories.title: US State Department orders global warning about alleged AI theft by DeepSeek, other Chinese firms
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department issued a global diplomatic cable instructing embassies to raise concerns about alleged intellectual property theft by Chinese companies, including AI startup DeepSeek, targeting U.S. artificial intelligence labs. A separate message was sent to Beijing.

stories.title: Germany to send minesweeper for possible Strait of Hormuz mission
stories.summary: Germany plans to send a minesweeper for a possible mission in the Strait of Hormuz. A government spokeswoman said the vessel would deploy only after a lasting end to hostilities in the area.

stories.title: Azerbaijan donates five passenger buses to Ukraine - FM Sybiha
stories.summary: During Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's visit to Azerbaijan, Baku donated five passenger buses to Ukraine as humanitarian aid. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha announced the donation.

stories.title: Militants and separatists launch coordinated attacks across Mali
stories.summary: The al-Qaida-linked militant group JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front launched coordinated attacks across Mali on Saturday, targeting Bamako's international airport and locations in four other cities in central and northern Mali. JNIM claimed responsibility on its website, Az-Zallaqa. It was one of the largest such coordinated assaults in Mali in recent years.

stories.title: Netanyahu orders Israeli army to vigorously attack Hezbollah positions
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to launch forceful attacks on Hezbollah positions in Lebanon, despite a recently extended ceasefire. The directive was confirmed by Netanyahu's office and reported by Israel's Channel 12.

stories.title: Mali: Bamako and Other Locations Target of Coordinated Attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military government confirmed coordinated attacks in Bamako and other locations, stating that the attackers were terrorists who "suffered immediate setback" and many were "neutralised." The incidents targeted multiple sites across the country.

stories.title: Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi leaves after meeting with PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi left Islamabad after meeting Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir. A source said Araghchi conveyed Tehran's negotiating demands and reservations about U.S. conditions to Pakistani officials.

stories.title: Turnout low as Palestinians in West Bank and Gaza vote in local elections
stories.summary: Palestinian voters in the West Bank and Gaza's Deir el-Balah area participated in local elections, with only 21.2% turnout reported in the Gaza location. The vote in Deir el-Balah was the first there since 2006 and was widely viewed as a test for potential future elections.

stories.title: IDF says Gaza strike killed Oct. 7 attacker; local officials report 13 dead in attacks
stories.summary: The Israeli military said a series of strikes in Gaza killed an alleged October 7 attacker and targeted imminent threats to troops. Palestinian officials reported 13 people dead, including a pregnant woman carrying twins and two children, in strikes on homes near a hospital.

stories.title: Russian forces shell Nikopol and Synelnykivskyi districts in Dnipro region, six wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the Nikopol and Synelnykivskyi districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region on April 25, wounding six people, including two children.

stories.title: Israel must break free from the dangerous status quo - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that what was perceived as stability in Israel has become dangerous inertia, carrying real costs for the country's security, society, and public trust.

stories.title: Iran’s authorities project hardened stance with more talks on horizon
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with senior Pakistani officials in Islamabad before departing for Oman, with plans to continue onward to Russia. The visits come amid ongoing diplomatic efforts related to the regional conflict.

stories.title: Syrskyi: Ukraine’s strikes have cost Russia $25.5 billion
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi stated that Ukraine's strikes have inflicted an estimated $25.5 billion in costs on Russia. He emphasized Ukraine's reliance on asymmetric warfare and drones to hold the front despite being outnumbered.

stories.title: Members of Israel's Right in talks to form new party as alternative to Likud
stories.summary: Members of Israel's political right are in discussions to form a new party as an alternative to Likud. The initiative, informally called "Likud B," is being driven by right-wing figures who have had strained relations with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

stories.title: Pakistan says committed to mediator role after US-Iran talks called off
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke by phone with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday after US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad were called off. Sharif reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to serving as a facilitator for regional peace efforts.

stories.title: One police officer dead after Chicago hospital shooting
stories.summary: A shooting at a Chicago hospital on Saturday left one police officer dead and another in critical condition. The suspect has been taken into custody, according to local officials.

stories.title: Protestor depicts Israeli minister Ben Gvir covered in blood in Stockholm
stories.summary: Activists held a protest in Stockholm, Sweden, on Saturday in solidarity with Palestine. A demonstrator displayed an image depicting Israeli Minister Itamar Ben Gvir covered in blood.

stories.title: Palestinians vote in first elections since war, amid ongoing Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and central Gaza voted Saturday in municipal elections, the first since Israel's war on Gaza began. Nearly 1.5 million voters were registered in the West Bank and 70,000 in Gaza's Deir el-Balah area, though turnout was low amid continuing Israeli military operations.

stories.title: Oil tanker hijacked off Somalia
stories.summary: An oil tanker was hijacked off the coast of Somalia and taken into Somali territorial waters, according to a British maritime security agency report on Saturday.

stories.title: Drought displaces tens of thousands in Somalia: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that drought has displaced nearly 62,000 people across five Somali districts in 2025, with potentially hundreds of thousands affected nationwide.

stories.title: Syria to begin trying Assad-era figures on Sunday
stories.summary: Syria announced it will begin trials of prominent figures from ousted President Bashar al-Assad's government on Sunday. A justice ministry official confirmed the proceedings on Saturday, marking a significant step in the country's transitional justice process.

stories.title: Australia refuses repatriation help for citizens in Syria camp
stories.summary: Australia has refused to assist in repatriating citizens linked to suspected Islamic State fighters who are held in camps in Syria. The decision came after reports emerged that some families connected to the jihadists were attempting to return home.

stories.title: Six killed in Israeli strikes on south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed six people in southern Lebanon on Saturday, according to the country's health ministry. The attacks occurred despite a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah that was brokered by the United States and extended earlier in the week.

stories.title: Pakistan successfully launches indigenous satellite from China
stories.summary: Pakistan's Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) successfully launched its indigenous electro-optical satellite, EO-3, from China's Taiyuan Satellite Launch Centre. Pakistan's Foreign Office called the launch a significant milestone in the nation's space capabilities.

stories.title: After destroying more than 120 homes, wildfires still a danger, Georgia officials say
stories.summary: Two wildfires in Brantley County in south-eastern Georgia have destroyed more than 120 homes and continue to threaten the area. Officials warned that strong winds could spread the flames further, and smoke from the blazes contributed to at least one death in Florida.

stories.title: Over 5.7M square meters of road repairs completed in Ukraine since year starts
stories.summary: Ukraine has completed repairs on more than 5.7 million square meters of damaged road surfaces on international highways and state roads since the beginning of the year.

stories.title: “The Urals, Karl!”: Drones struck Russia’s Yekaterinburg for first time at record distance of 1,800 kilometers
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Russian city of Yekaterinburg in the Urals for the first time, covering a record distance of approximately 1,800 kilometers. The "Trinity" residential complex in the city center was damaged and six people were injured, with no air-raid warning issued to residents.

stories.title: Journalist Fakharur Rehman sent to jail on judicial remand following arrest in Peca case
stories.summary: A court in Islamabad rejected the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency's request for physical remand of journalist Fakharur Rehman and sent him to jail on judicial remand. Rehman was arrested under Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), accused alongside eight others of spreading alleged misinformation against state institutions on social media.

stories.title: Trump cancels US delegation’s trip to Pakistan for Iran negotiations
stories.summary: President Trump cancelled a planned U.S. delegation trip to Pakistan intended for negotiations related to Iran. Shortly before the announcement, Pakistani government sources confirmed the Iranian delegation had already departed Islamabad.

stories.title: Efforts to achieve peace, stability in region to continue: Pakistan's Deputy PM
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister affirmed that efforts to achieve peace and stability in the region would continue. No official confirmation has been given on whether direct talks between Washington and Tehran will occur during the visit.

stories.title: Macron says EU’s mutual defence clause ‘not just words’
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said the EU's mutual defence clause is "not just words," citing joint military aid sent to Cyprus after a drone attack on a British airbase there on February 28. He made the remarks during a visit to Athens, advocating for Europe's capacity for self-defence.

stories.title: Death toll in Dnipro attack rises to six, 47 people injured
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro rose to six, with 47 people reported injured.

stories.title: “Grandma, get on”: Ukrainian robot carried 77-year-old from grey zone near Lyman (VIDEO)
stories.summary: A Ukrainian ground robot was used to evacuate a 77-year-old woman from the grey zone near Lyman in eastern Ukraine. The robotic evacuation was carried out because enemy drones made conventional ground extraction impossible.

stories.title: US to let Venezuela pay Maduro’s lawyer in drug trafficking case
stories.summary: The United States has agreed to modify its sanctions on Venezuela to allow the government of President Nicolás Maduro to pay his lawyer in an ongoing drug trafficking case.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three Palestinians, including a child, in Gaza City
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike near Al-Dahyan School in northern Gaza City killed three Palestinians, including a child, and injured others on Saturday evening. Al-Shifa Hospital confirmed receiving the victims' bodies. Separately, Israeli forces fatally shot Bahjat Abu Al-Eish in the head at Jabalia refugee camp.

stories.title: Ukraine’s air defenses intercept majority of missiles and drones in massive attack on Dnipro, Mayor says
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 80% of missiles and 94% of drones during what Dnipro's mayor described as one of the most massive Russian attacks on the city.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone hits apartment building in Russian city of Yekaterinburg, local official says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a multi-storey apartment building in Yekaterinburg, Russia's fourth-largest city, according to the regional governor. It was the first reported attack on Yekaterinburg since the beginning of the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill six in southern Lebanon, ministry says
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed six people on Saturday, according to Lebanon's health ministry. Four were killed in strikes on a truck and motorbike in Yohmor al-Shaqeef in Nabatieh district, and two more died in an airstrike on Safad al-Battikh in Bint Jbeil district, despite a recently extended ceasefire.

stories.title: Zelensky: War against Ukraine must not be overshadowed by war in Middle East
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged the international community not to let the war in the Middle East overshadow Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine in Europe.

stories.title: Trump cancels Witkoff and Kushner’s trip to Islamabad for ‘time-wasting’ Iran talks
stories.summary: President Trump cancelled the trip of envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Islamabad, calling the Iran negotiations time-wasting. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi had already departed Pakistan following meetings with local leaders. Trump said Tehran could resume talks by simply calling.

stories.title: Trump cancels US envoys’ trip after Iran’s Araghchi leaves Pakistan
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump cancelled the trip of American envoys to Pakistan after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed the country. Trump suggested future communication with Iran could take place by phone, stating Tehran could simply call if it wished to negotiate.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi orders inspection of frontline military logistics
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief, General Oleksandr Syrskyi, ordered an inspection of logistical support for frontline service members, with a deadline of May 20 for the review.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister says 'yet to see if the US is truly serious about diplomacy'
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said after completing a visit to Pakistan that it remained to be seen whether the United States was genuinely committed to diplomacy. He stated on X that he and Pakistani officials had discussed Iran's proposed framework for permanently ending the conflict.

stories.title: Republicans retool midterm strategy: Trump's policies, but less Trump
stories.summary: Republicans in the United States are adjusting their strategy for the upcoming midterm elections amid rising gas prices, declining approval ratings for President Donald Trump, and the ongoing Iran war. The recalibration involves promoting Trump's policies while reducing emphasis on Trump himself.

stories.title: UK pro-Palestine activists break into Israeli weapons factory
stories.summary: Pro-Palestine activists in the United Kingdom broke into an Israeli weapons factory by cutting through the roof and abseiling inside. Police responded to the scene and arrested six people.

stories.title: India to bid for 2038 Asian Games in Ahmedabad
stories.summary: India's Olympic Association has submitted an expression of interest to the Olympic Council of Asia to host the 2038 Asian Games in Ahmedabad. IOA President P. T. Usha confirmed the bid, adding to India's plans to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games and its bid for the 2036 Olympics in the same city.

stories.title: Afghans in Qatar can return 'with full confidence', says Taliban govt
stories.summary: The Taliban government stated that Afghans in Qatar who had collaborated with US forces may return to Afghanistan safely. Over 1,100 Afghans had been staying at a former US base in Qatar awaiting processing for relocation to the United States before a Trump administration deadline to close the camp.

stories.title: Strait talks: What's at stake in Hormuz
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for Middle Eastern oil shipments, has become a focal point in the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict due to its strategic importance for global energy supplies.

stories.title: Syrian President al-Sharaa positions country for regional role in Gulf, EU meetings
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa traveled to Gulf states as part of efforts to build regional and European support for Damascus. The diplomatic push comes amid rising tensions across the Middle East.

stories.title: Lessons from the safe room: Navigating fear, routine, and family togetherness
stories.summary: An Israeli family described their experience navigating daily life, fear, and togetherness inside their home safe room during cycles of alarms and ceasefires.

stories.title: Social media influencer dies six days after car hit her outside London nightclub
stories.summary: Social media influencer Klaudia Zakrzewska, 32, died on Saturday, six days after a car struck her and other pedestrians outside a nightclub on Argyll Street in London's Soho at approximately 4:30 a.m. on April 19. A 58-year-old man also sustained life-changing injuries in the incident.

stories.title: Czech analyst: European militaries should learn from Ukraine’s Armed Forces
stories.summary: A Czech analyst argued that European militaries should study and learn from Ukraine's Armed Forces, describing them as effectively Europe's frontline army given their extensive combat experience.

stories.title: The saline blueprint: Can saving the Dead Sea reshape Middle East diplomacy?
stories.summary: A project originating from a 2016 photojournalism effort has grown into a global mission to document and archive the changing landscapes around the Dead Sea before further environmental degradation.

stories.title: Israel detains 11 Palestinians who returned to Jenin camp
stories.summary: Israeli forces detained 11 Palestinians who attempted to return to the Jenin refugee camp in the occupied West Bank. Israel has kept the camp closed off since 2025.

stories.title: Syria to begin trying Assad-era figures Sunday, justice ministry official says
stories.summary: Syria's justice ministry announced that trials of prominent figures from the Assad era would begin on Sunday in Damascus. The defendants include former security officials and militia leaders accused of atrocities, marking the first major test of Syria's post-Assad transitional justice system.

stories.title: Palestinians vote in first municipal elections since outbreak of Gaza war - analysis
stories.summary: Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza voted in their first municipal elections since the outbreak of the Gaza war. Analysts said the results could influence future plans for governance changes in Gaza.

stories.title: Mexico says US agents killed in crash weren't permitted to operate there
stories.summary: Mexico's government stated that two Americans reportedly working for the CIA who died in a car crash were not authorized to operate in the country. The crash occurred after a Mexican-led operation to destroy a drug laboratory.

stories.title: Assad regime figures to be put on trial in Damascus
stories.summary: Former officials from Bashar al-Assad's government are set to face trial in Damascus as Syria launches public prosecutions under a long-delayed transitional justice process. The proceedings target figures from the ousted regime accused of crimes during Assad's rule.

stories.title: Iran hajj pilgrims arrive in Saudi Arabia: report
stories.summary: Iranian pilgrims have arrived in Saudi Arabia for the annual Hajj pilgrimage. The arrivals took place despite ongoing regional tensions stemming from the recent Middle East conflict and strained relations between Tehran and Riyadh.

stories.title: Trump says canceling envoys' trip does not mean restart of Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said that cancelling his envoys' trip to Islamabad for Iran talks did not automatically mean the war with Iran would resume. When asked by Axios whether the cancellation signaled a return to hostilities, Trump responded that the administration had not yet considered that option.

stories.title: Ukrainian-Polish Historians’ Congress seen as step toward historical reconciliation
stories.summary: A Ukrainian-Polish Congress of Historians is scheduled for May 6–8 in Baranów Sandomierski, Poland. The event is seen as a potential platform for dialogue and progress toward reconciliation on complex shared historical issues.

stories.title: Reported US CIA agents killed in crash not authorised to operate: Mexico
stories.summary: Mexico's government stated that reported U.S. CIA agents killed in a crash on Mexican territory were not authorized to operate there. Officials said they are seeking further details about the incident, which has raised questions about American intelligence activities inside Mexico.

stories.title: President Zardari departs for China for visit focused on 'economic cooperation, CPEC'
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari departed from Lahore for a visit to China, with stops planned in Changsha, Hunan province, and Sanya, Hainan province. The Foreign Office said engagements will focus on economic and trade cooperation and the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

stories.title: Joy and desire for change as Gaza’s Deir el-Balah holds elections
stories.summary: Residents of Deir el-Balah in central Gaza voted in local elections for the first time since 2006. The vote took place amid widespread destruction and displacement caused by the ongoing conflict in the territory.

stories.title: Telecos to begin 5G trials in Gilgit-Baltistan soon
stories.summary: The Gilgit-Baltistan Council, chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, has approved policy directives for 5G test trials in the region. Four telecom operators are expected to begin testing soon once the telecom regulator receives formal approval.

stories.title: Trump cancels envoys’ trip to Pakistan for peace talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump ordered envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff not to travel to Islamabad for negotiations aimed at ending the eight-week U.S.-Iran war. Trump demanded Tehran make concessions before further talks. Vice President J.D. Vance had led an earlier round of negotiations.

stories.title: A difficult balance to find: Pakistan wants to be a key actor in shaping US-Iran peace
stories.summary: Pakistan has sought to position itself as a mediator in the U.S.-Iran war by offering to host peace talks between the two countries since the conflict began.

stories.title: Trump cancels envoy visit to Pakistan, says Iran can ‘call us’ to negotiate
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump cancelled a planned trip by Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan for talks with Iran, saying the 18-hour journey was not worthwhile. Trump suggested Tehran could simply call Washington to negotiate a deal. The announcement followed Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's departure from Islamabad.

stories.title: Iran FM Abbas Araghchi and Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif meet in Pakistan
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad. The meeting was part of broader diplomatic efforts to revive direct negotiations between Iran and the United States.

stories.title: Ukrainian government to provide support to Dnipro after massive Russian attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers announced it would provide support to the city of Dnipro following a large-scale combined Russian attack on April 25 that killed five people and injured more than 40.

stories.title: Trump cancels his envoys’ Pakistan trip for Iran ceasefire negotiations
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner not to travel to Islamabad for ceasefire talks with Iran, shortly after Iran's top diplomat left the Pakistani capital on Saturday. Trump said Tehran could initiate contact whenever it wished.

stories.title: From canvas to country: Israeli artists turn landscape into ideology and memory
stories.summary: An article explores how Israeli artists have historically depicted the landscape of the Land of Israel, shaping it through ideology, memory, and national longing rather than neutral observation.

stories.title: Iran's FM Araghchi meets PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir amid hopes for renewed US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held separate meetings with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir in Islamabad. Discussions covered regional developments and bilateral ties amid hopes for renewed US-Iran diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: Ink and irony: A closer look at the cartoonist who chronicled Israel’s formative years
stories.summary: A feature examines the work of cartoonist Arieh Navon, whose satirical sketches chronicled Israel's early statehood years. The story traces a personal journey beginning with a discarded book found at the National Library.

stories.title: Syria ministry reveals details behind arrest of massacre suspect
stories.summary: Syria's Interior Minister Anas Khattab personally interrogated Amjad Youssef following his arrest on suspicion of involvement in the Tadamon massacre. The ministry disclosed details surrounding the detention of the suspect.

stories.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi meets Pakistan Army chief Munir
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Pakistani Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir during his visit to Islamabad. It remains unclear whether the visit will lead to direct talks between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Italy’s Meloni opposes inviting Putin to upcoming G20 summit
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stated her opposition to inviting Russian President Vladimir Putin to the upcoming G20 summit, scheduled for December in the United States.

stories.title: Hope in Gaza as 300 couples get married at one time
stories.summary: In Gaza, approximately 300 couples were married in a joint wedding celebration. The participating couples were selected by draw from nearly 2,000 applicants.

stories.title: Hezbollah violates ceasefire with Israel again, launches projectiles at north
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched projectiles at northern Israel, violating the ceasefire. The Israeli Defense Forces described the incident as a blatant breach of the ceasefire understandings.

stories.title: Four family members gunned down in Islamabad suburbs, police say
stories.summary: Four members of a single family, including a woman and a teenager, were fatally shot inside a house in the Jhangi Syedan area on the outskirts of Islamabad. Police responded after neighbors reported hearing gunshots and found the bodies on the first floor of the residence.

stories.title: Turkey dismisses deputy education minister over school shootings
stories.summary: Turkey dismissed its deputy education minister following two deadly school shootings that killed nine people. The incidents sparked widespread public outrage across the country.

stories.title: Trumps says he is no longer sending envoys to Pakistan for Iran talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced he would no longer send U.S. envoys to Pakistan for negotiations with Iran, effectively halting the planned diplomatic engagement in Islamabad.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill 6 Across Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian strikes killed six people across Ukraine, including four in a single attack on an apartment block in Dnipro that also wounded 27. A separate strike nearly killed a local official.

stories.title: Remains of four individuals found in ongoing Polish-Ukrainian excavations in Volyn
stories.summary: Joint Ukrainian-Polish excavation teams discovered the remains of four individuals near the former villages of Ostrivky and Volia Ostrovetska in Ukraine's Volyn region.

stories.title: Macron reaffirms efforts to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron reaffirmed France's efforts to restore free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. TotalEnergies warned that a war in the region could trigger a global energy crisis.

stories.title: Viking's Jørn Henriksen new IAATO executive committee chair
stories.summary: Jørn Henriksen, director of expedition operations at Viking, was elected chair of the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO) executive committee.

stories.title: 'Security reality has not changed enough': Two kites from Gaza land in Kibbutz Nahal Oz
stories.summary: Two kites from Gaza landed in Kibbutz Nahal Oz near the border. The kibbutz issued a statement saying the incident demonstrates that the security situation has not sufficiently improved.

stories.title: Iran executes man over ‘mission’ for Israel’s spy agency
stories.summary: Iranian authorities have executed nine men on charges connected to nationwide protests since March 19. The executions are part of a broader crackdown following widespread unrest in the country.

stories.title: Ukraine’s prominent drone expert “Flash”: Russia’s cheap Molniya drones fly too low for radar
stories.summary: A prominent Ukrainian drone expert known as "Flash" warned that Russia's low-cost Molniya drones fly at very low altitudes and use materials that reduce radar visibility, making them difficult for Ukraine's air defenses to detect.

stories.title: Turkey may consider role in Hormuz demining after Iran-US deal, minister says
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Turkey could consider participating in demining operations in the Strait of Hormuz if Iran and the United States reach a peace agreement. The statement signals Ankara's potential role in regional security arrangements tied to any future deal.

stories.title: Falklands MPA back in UK to bolster air operations in Iran conflict, Defense Eye
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has withdrawn its sole Royal Air Force air-to-air refueling tanker from the Falkland Islands to support British air operations related to the Iran conflict in the Middle East, according to defense-focused UK news agencies.

stories.title: Billionaire Elon Musk enters courtroom showdown with OpenAI
stories.summary: Jury selection is set to begin in a lawsuit filed by Elon Musk against OpenAI in a courtroom near San Francisco. Musk, who once backed the AI startup, accuses it of abandoning its non-profit mission. The case reflects a broader rivalry between Musk's xAI lab and OpenAI's ChatGPT.

stories.title: Security vetting stepped up after MP is given bodyguard with far-right links
stories.summary: UK security firm Mitie, which holds a £31 million contract to provide bodyguards for Members of Parliament, has tightened its vetting procedures after a close protection operative with far-right links was assigned to guard a politician threatened by extremists. New measures include regular and random social media checks on staff.

stories.title: Injury toll from Russian strikes on Dnipro rises to 46
stories.summary: The injury toll from Russian strikes on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro rose to 46, including five children, as rescue and recovery operations continued.

stories.title: In pictures: High security in Islamabad’s Red Zone during Iranian delegation’s visit
stories.summary: Islamabad's Red Zone was placed under tight security and closed to all traffic during a visit by an Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Araghchi arrived carrying Tehran's formal response to US proposals conveyed through Pakistan amid intensifying diplomacy over the US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Photo of labourer smoking on scaffolding triggers anger after Tai Po blaze
stories.summary: A photograph of a Hong Kong construction worker smoking on bamboo scaffolding at a residential building in Tai On Building sparked public anger online. Internet users drew comparisons to the suspected cause of a recent deadly fire in Tai Po.

stories.title: Tunisia's main rights group says operations suspended
stories.summary: Tunisian authorities ordered a one-month suspension of the Tunisian League for Human Rights, one of the oldest human rights organizations in Africa and the Arab world.

stories.title: 68-year-old man and woman on motorcycle were killed by Russian FPV drone in Kherson this morning
stories.summary: A 68-year-old man and a woman riding a motorcycle were killed by a Russian FPV drone strike in Kherson. When police responded to the scene, Russia carried out a second strike deliberately targeting the first responders' vehicle.

stories.title: Police said planning to probe attempt to storm High Court’s Oct. 7 inquiry hearing
stories.summary: Israeli police are reportedly planning to investigate an attempt by a pro-government mob to storm the High Court during a hearing on the government's refusal to establish a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 attacks. The incident forced proceedings to halt and justices to be evacuated.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike Russian depots, command posts, troop concentrations, General Staff reports
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces conducted strikes against Russian ammunition depots, command posts, and troop concentrations, according to the Ukrainian General Staff.

stories.title: Pakistan's Shehbaz Sharif confirms Iran's delegation has left Islamabad
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif confirmed that Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation departed Islamabad after bilateral talks. Sharif said both sides discussed strengthening Pakistan-Iran relations and other matters of mutual interest.

stories.title: Festive mood in West Bank as local elections underway
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority held local elections across the West Bank, with a festive atmosphere reported in Bethlehem. Most candidate lists are aligned with President Mahmoud Abbas's Fatah party or running as independents, with no Hamas-affiliated lists participating.

stories.title: Met investigates hundreds of officers after using Palantir AI tool
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police launched investigations into hundreds of officers after deploying an AI tool built by Palantir over the course of a week. The software analyzed existing force data and flagged rule-breaking ranging from work-from-home violations to suspected corruption and criminal allegations.

stories.title: Iranian delegation has left Islamabad: Al Jazeera
stories.summary: An Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Islamabad after high-level meetings with Pakistani officials. The delegation reportedly delivered Iran's list of demands for ending the US-Israeli war, which Pakistani leaders are expected to relay to Washington.

stories.title: IT Coalition co-led by Estonia just crossed €1.4 billion with Ukraine’s drone programs as focus
stories.summary: The IT Coalition co-led by Estonia announced it has surpassed €1.4 billion in contributions, with a focus on Ukraine's drone programs. Estonia reaffirmed its commitment to allocate at least 0.25% of GDP to supporting Ukraine.

stories.title: Prince Harry pays tribute to fallen Ukrainian soldiers during visit to Kyiv region
stories.summary: Prince Harry, the Duke of Sussex, visited Ukraine's National Military Memorial Cemetery in the Kyiv region. He paid tribute to Ukrainian servicemen and women who died in the conflict.

stories.title: Update: Mali's army claims situation under control following attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military claimed the security situation was under control after armed militants staged simultaneous and coordinated attacks at multiple locations across the country involving several groups.

stories.title: Palestinians head to the polls for first time since Gaza war
stories.summary: Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and in Gaza's Deir al-Balah voted in municipal elections, the first since the Gaza war. President Mahmoud Abbas cast his ballot in Ramallah. The majority of candidates were affiliated with the ruling Fatah party, with no Hamas candidates standing.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill several in Ukraine's Dnipro
stories.summary: Russian strikes across Ukraine on Saturday killed at least six people, with most casualties resulting from an attack on a residential building in the eastern city of Dnipro, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Loud blasts, gunfire heard near Mali's main military camp, Reuters witness says
stories.summary: Two loud explosions and sustained gunfire were heard early Saturday morning near Mali's main military base at Kati, outside the capital Bamako. Soldiers deployed to the area and blocked off roads. A Reuters witness reported the incident on April 25.

stories.title: Bangladesh issues nationwide security alert over possible militant attacks
stories.summary: Bangladesh's police headquarters issued a nationwide security alert based on intelligence reports warning of possible militant attacks. Officials described the alert as urgent and confidential.

stories.title: Is Karachi disposable by design?
stories.summary: A January 18 fire at Gul Plaza in Karachi killed 70 people, followed by three additional market fires in the city that same month. The incidents have fueled public anger over years of urban negligence, including unsafe buildings, open manholes, and inadequate fire safety infrastructure.

stories.title: Major Russian attack on Ukraine kills four, wounds dozens
stories.summary: Russia attacked Ukraine with 619 drones and 47 missiles, according to Ukraine's air force. The assault killed at least four people and wounded dozens across the country.

stories.title: Attacks on Bamako a 'dramatic setback' for Malian government
stories.summary: Coordinated attacks struck Mali's capital, Bamako, in what analyst Andrew Lebovich of the Clingendael Institute called a "dramatic setback" for the junta-led government. He noted the incidents underscore the fragile security situation, with Malian authorities and their Russian partners struggling to secure the capital.

stories.title: Conspiracy theory over UFOs and missing scientists spreads from web to White House
stories.summary: A conspiracy theory linking the disappearances or deaths of at least 11 US scientists—allegedly connected to space, defense, and nuclear research—has spread from online platforms into rightwing media, mainstream press, and prompted attention from US lawmakers and the White House.

stories.title: Czech military expert: Ukrainian forces trade small territorial gains for heavy Russian losses
stories.summary: A Czech military expert assessed that Ukrainian forces are trading small territorial gains for heavy Russian losses. The analysis praised Ukraine's professionalism, integration of diverse weapon systems, and capacity for battlefield innovation.

stories.title: Two killed in strike on alleged drug boat in Pacific Ocean, US military says
stories.summary: The U.S. military said it struck an alleged drug trafficking boat in the Pacific Ocean, killing two people. The strike is part of an ongoing series of U.S. operations targeting suspected narcotics-smuggling vessels at sea.

stories.title: Palestinians bury pregnant woman and 2 of her children killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza buried a pregnant woman carrying twins and two of her children, who were among at least 13 people killed in Israeli strikes. Eight of the victims, including four police officers, were killed when Israel targeted a police vehicle in Khan Younis.

stories.title: Low voter turnout in Gaza as West Bank holds local elections
stories.summary: Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and in Gaza's Deir el-Balah area voted Saturday in municipal elections, the first since the Gaza war began. Turnout was low; nearly 1.5 million were registered in the West Bank and about 70,000 in central Gaza.

stories.title: US negotiators to go to Islamabad, but Iran says no direct talks
stories.summary: US negotiators are set to travel to Islamabad for indirect talks regarding Iran. Tehran's Foreign Ministry stated there would be no direct negotiations with the United States, and that Iran's concerns would be conveyed through mediator Pakistan.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires rockets at north, Israel hits terror targets in Lebanon amid shaky truce
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired rockets at communities in northern Israel, causing no injuries, while the Israeli military struck targets in Lebanon and said it killed several gunmen who posed a threat to its troops. The exchanges occurred amid an ongoing but fragile truce between the two sides.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine ready for trilateral talks with Russia in Azerbaijan
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is prepared to participate in trilateral talks with Russia in Azerbaijan.

stories.title: Russia attacked Dnipro for more than 10 hours. Five people are dead, up to six may still be under rubble
stories.summary: Russia attacked the Ukrainian city of Dnipro for more than 10 hours, killing at least five people with up to six more potentially trapped under rubble. At least 40 people were injured, including children, with 23 requiring hospitalization.

stories.title: Turkey casts itself as 'adult in the room' amid global reordering, FM tells Oxford audience
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan delivered a speech at Oxford University's Rhodes House, positioning Ankara as a central diplomatic broker amid stalled Iran-US talks and global market turbulence caused by regional tensions.

stories.title: Deporting soldiers? Why immigrant veterans fear removal from the US
stories.summary: The Trump administration's mass deportation campaign has raised concerns among immigrant veterans of the U.S. military, who fear they could be removed from the country despite their service.

stories.title: Voices from the Arab press: Lebanon succeeds in separating its path from Iran
stories.summary: Arab media commentators discussed Lebanon's efforts to chart a political course separate from Iran's influence. The piece compiled a weekly selection of opinions and analyses from Arab press outlets around the world.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz closure pushes Pakistan into expensive $18.4 per mmBtu LNG deal
stories.summary: Pakistan's state-run Pakistan LNG Limited accepted a revised bid of $18.4 per mmBtu from TotalEnergies for a late-April delivery. The high cost is linked to disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has constrained global energy shipments.

stories.title: Israel kills 10 in Lebanon despite ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed 10 people in Lebanon despite an extension of the ceasefire. Civilians attempting to return to southern Lebanon faced continued destruction, displacement, and ground clashes.

stories.title: Taliban says Afghans stuck in Qatar who helped US in war can safely return home
stories.summary: Afghanistan's foreign ministry spokesman Abdul Qahar Balkhi said Afghans who assisted US forces and have been stranded in Qatar can safely return home. The statement followed reports that the Trump administration was considering sending approximately 1,100 Afghans to the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Araghchi meeting with Pakistan's Sharif ends in Islamabad: Al Jazeera
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi concluded a meeting with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, according to Al Jazeera, citing a Pakistani official. Further details of the discussions were not immediately available.

stories.title: How the war on Iran is rewriting regional trade routes
stories.summary: The conflict involving Iran is reshaping regional trade corridors. A freight route originally planned to link India to Europe through the UAE and Israel is being rerouted through Saudi Arabia and Qatar, with Saudi Arabia Railways activating a new international freight corridor.

stories.title: 3 killed in latest clashes in India's troubled Manipur state
stories.summary: Three men were killed in gun battles between rival ethnic groups in Mullam village, Ukhrul district, in India's northeastern Manipur state. The region has experienced nearly three years of periodic clashes between the Meitei majority and the Kuki community, with over 250 people killed.

stories.title: Zelenskyy’s first official visit to Azerbaijan: Six bilateral deals, with defense industry as key area
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made his first official visit to Azerbaijan, where six bilateral agreements were signed. Defense industry cooperation was identified as a key area, with Zelenskyy emphasizing the high level of mutual respect between the two countries.

stories.title: Iran rules out talks with US unless blockade of ports lifted
stories.summary: US envoys were expected in Islamabad to begin a new round of peace negotiations with Iran, but Iranian state media indicated Tehran's representatives had no immediate plans for face-to-face talks. Iran has stated that diplomacy cannot proceed unless the US blockade of Iranian ports is lifted.

stories.title: Will the future world order be determined by who controls low Earth orbit?
stories.summary: An analysis explores how control of low Earth orbit may shape the future global order, citing the example of Starlink restoring communications in Caracas after US special forces raided Venezuela and abducted President Nicolás Maduro, which caused widespread power and communications blackouts.

stories.title: Iran resumes commercial flights from Tehran’s international airport for first time since conflict
stories.summary: Iran resumed commercial flights from Tehran's international airport for the first time since the conflict with the United States and Israel began two months ago.

stories.title: Ukraine and Estonia DMs sign cooperation memorandum
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov and Estonian Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur signed a memorandum of cooperation. The agreement is intended to expand collaboration between the two countries' defense industries.

stories.title: What to know about the Palestinian municipal elections
stories.summary: Palestinians voted in municipal elections across the West Bank and parts of Gaza amid ongoing destruction, political divisions between factions, and the continued Israeli occupation.

stories.title: Mississippi school kids stop school bus on highway after driver passes out
stories.summary: Middle school students aged 12 to 15 in Kiln, Mississippi, steered their school bus to safety on a highway after driver Leah Taylor lost consciousness due to an asthma attack. The students called for help, and Taylor credited them with saving her life.

stories.title: Australia and New Zealand gather in Turkiye to commemorate WWI battle
stories.summary: Australians and New Zealanders gathered at Gallipoli in Turkey to commemorate the World War I battle of the Dardanelles. The ceremony included hymns, prayers, and wreath-laying by representatives from multiple countries.

stories.title: Loud blasts, gunfire heard near Mali's main military camp, witness says
stories.summary: Loud explosions and gunfire were heard near Mali's main military camp in Bamako. The cause of the blasts was unclear, and no militant group immediately claimed responsibility.

stories.title: Major Russian attack on Ukraine kills four, wounds dozens
stories.summary: Russia launched a large-scale overnight attack on Ukraine using over 660 drones and missiles, killing four people and wounding dozens. The strikes hit multiple targets, including buildings in the eastern city of Dnipro, where rescue teams searched for survivors trapped under rubble.

stories.title: Russians attack minibus in Zaporizhzhia region, one killed and others injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked a commuter minibus in the village of Yurkivka in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. One person was killed and four others were wounded in the strike.

stories.title: CDF Munir meets Iran FM Araghchi amid hopes for renewed US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir in Islamabad amid hopes for renewed US-Iran negotiations. The meeting, the first after Araghchi's arrival, also included Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and other officials.

stories.title: Palestinians vote in first elections since Israel's invasion of Gaza
stories.summary: Nearly 1.5 million Palestinians in the West Bank and 70,000 in Gaza's Deir el-Balah area began voting in municipal elections on Saturday, the first vote since Israel's invasion of Gaza. The elections were marked by a narrow political field and widespread disillusionment.

stories.title: War-damaged mosque offered shelter during fighting in the Sudanese capital
stories.summary: The Gharib Allah Sufi mosque in the Sudanese capital served as shelter during fighting despite sustaining heavy war damage. The mosque sat on the frontline of the conflict for nearly two years.

stories.title: Iran executes man over 'mission' for Israel's spy agency
stories.summary: Iran executed Erfan Kiani by hanging after the country's Supreme Court upheld his death sentence. Authorities accused him of carrying out a mission on behalf of Israel's intelligence agency, Mossad. The sentence was confirmed by the judiciary's Mizan Online website.

stories.title: Iran executed alleged Israeli agent over sabotage in nationwide protests, state media claims
stories.summary: Iran executed Erfan Kiani, whom state media described as a Mossad-hired agent, for alleged destruction, arson, and spreading terror during nationwide protests in the city of Isfahan. Authorities accused him of wielding a machete and targeting public and private property.

stories.title: Laughing through it: Israeli comedy films to celebrate Independence Day
stories.summary: A selection of Israeli comedy films was highlighted for Independence Day viewing. The collection spans well-known classics and newer releases that continue to attract audiences across generations.

stories.title: Independence is a dance  between freedom and responsibility, Renana Raz tells 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli multidisciplinary artist Renana Raz discussed the meaning of independence in an interview, describing it as a balance between creative freedom and the responsibility that comes with it.

stories.title: Four people killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on the village of Yohmor al-Shaqif in Lebanon's Nabatiyeh district killed four people on Saturday, targeting a pickup truck and a motorcycle. The strikes followed Friday's violence, which killed six people in what was the deadliest day during the recently extended ceasefire.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill four in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes targeted a truck and a motorcycle in the southern Lebanese town of Yohmor al-Shaqif, killing four people, according to Lebanese state media.

stories.title: Sudan: Human Rights Orgs Condemn 'Forced Deportation' of Sudanese Writer From Egypt
stories.summary: Thirteen Sudanese and Egyptian human rights organizations condemned the forced deportation of Sudanese writer Idris Babiker from Egypt. They called for an investigation into what they described as harsh and inhumane detention conditions during his detention.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Army Claims Precision Strikes 'Inflicted Heavy Losses On RSF'
stories.summary: The Sudanese Armed Forces claimed they carried out precision strikes over three days across Blue Nile, Kordofan, and Darfur, reporting significant losses among the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

stories.title: President: Air defenses downed over 90% of aerial targets in Russian night attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that air defenses destroyed more than 90% of aerial targets during a massive Russian nighttime attack. He noted that defense against ballistic missiles remains the most vulnerable area.

stories.title: Mali junta reports ‘terrorist’ attacks on several targets
stories.summary: Armed groups launched attacks on military barracks and other targets in Mali's capital Bamako and other locations across the country. The military junta described the assailants as unknown armed terrorists and said fighting was ongoing. Intense combat was also reported near areas where junta leader General Assimi Goïta resides.

stories.title: Russian airstrikes kill at least seven people in Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russian drone and missile strikes across Ukraine killed at least seven people overnight, including five in the city of Dnipro, with at least 34 injured. Odesa and Kharkiv were also targeted in what officials described as one of the largest onslaughts in several days. Rescue workers continued searching for survivors in destroyed buildings.

stories.title: Dozens of Palestinians breach IDF checkpoints to enter Jenin refugee camp
stories.summary: Dozens of Palestinians breached Israeli military checkpoints to enter the Jenin refugee camp in the occupied West Bank. At least 10 Palestinians were detained, and IDF forces deployed drones to monitor and locate additional suspects.

stories.title: Mali: Malian Army Confirms Clashes With Armed Fighters in Key Cities
stories.summary: Mali's army confirmed clashes with armed fighters who attacked army barracks in the capital Bamako and other locations across the country on Saturday.

stories.title: Backing public transit on Shabbat, Bennett steers campaign into jammed center lane
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett has campaigned in support of public transit on Shabbat, seeking broader appeal beyond his traditional right-wing base. The move risks drawing votes away from potential coalition partners in upcoming elections.

stories.title: ICE planning facility for children and families on Pfas-contaminated site
stories.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement is planning a detention facility for children and families at England Airpark, a former military site in Louisiana. The groundwater at the location has been found contaminated with PFAS chemicals at levels of at least 41 million parts per trillion.

stories.title: Billionaire behind ‘American Factory’ firm warns of US exit amid trade friction with China
stories.summary: Fuyao Glass founder Cao Dewang warned the company could shut down its US manufacturing plants if trade friction and tariffs between the United States and China cause severe financial losses. The Chinese billionaire's firm, featured in the Oscar-winning documentary "American Factory," is one of the world's largest automotive glass producers.

stories.title: Rubio’s absence from Iran talks highlights stay-at-home role
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was absent from Iran-related negotiations, underscoring his increasingly domestically focused role. Rubio has been occupied with his dual responsibilities as Secretary of State and National Security Adviser in recent months.

stories.title: Bomb disposal experts in Dnipro recover Russian drone warhead from apartment
stories.summary: Police bomb disposal experts in Dnipro recovered an undetonated warhead from a Russian drone found inside an apartment in a high-rise residential building.

stories.title: Romania says drone fragments damage property during overnight Russian attack on Ukraine
stories.summary: Romania's defense ministry reported that drone fragments from an overnight Russian attack on Ukraine landed in the southeastern city of Galati. The debris damaged an electricity pole and a household annex. Romanian authorities recovered the fragments and confirmed property damage.

stories.title: No direct US-Iran talks despite negotiators heading to Pakistan
stories.summary: U.S. and Iranian negotiators are both heading to Islamabad, but Iran has ruled out direct talks with the United States. Instead, proposals will be relayed through Pakistani mediators.

stories.title: FLA claims attacks on Malian capital
stories.summary: The Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), a separatist group active in northern Mali for over a decade, claimed responsibility for surprise attacks on Mali's capital Bamako and other locations. Mali's military junta described the attackers as terrorist groups and said it was engaged in ongoing combat.

stories.title: What levers can Turkey use against Israel if their war of words escalates?
stories.summary: Tensions between Turkey and Israel have escalated after Istanbul's Chief Public Prosecutor filed charges against 35 individuals, including Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, over last year's attack on the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters. The charges seek lengthy prison sentences.

stories.title: Elections in West Bank provide 'credibility to Palestinian sovereignty', expert says
stories.summary: Local elections were held in the West Bank and parts of Gaza to determine the makeup of councils overseeing infrastructure services including water, roads, and electricity. Former French ambassador Bertrand Besancenot said high voter turnout would lend credibility to Palestinian sovereignty.

stories.title: Trump to attend White House Correspondents Association gala after years of boycott
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump plans to attend the White House Correspondents Association gala after years of boycotting the event. Some journalists have urged organizers to use the occasion to protest what they describe as Trump's efforts to undermine press freedom.

stories.title: ‘Scale and coordination of Mali attacks appear unprecedented’
stories.summary: Clashes between the Malian army and rebel armed groups have been reported across multiple cities in Mali, with observers describing the scale and coordination of the attacks as unprecedented.

stories.title: Indonesian UN peacekeeper becomes sixth killed in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Indonesian soldier serving with the United Nations peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon was killed, becoming the sixth UN peacekeeper to die in recent hostilities in the area.

stories.title: Zelensky announces five bilateral agreements with Azerbaijan
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced during a visit to Azerbaijan that the two countries would work on concluding five bilateral state agreements.

stories.title: Why Spain’s ‘fruit bowl’ diplomacy with China comes up rather empty
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has made four visits to Beijing in four years, but the trips have yielded mainly agricultural market access rather than a strategic shift. The engagements have not significantly altered Europe's trade imbalance with China or weakened transatlantic alignment.

stories.title: Trump to attend his first White House Correspondents’ Dinner; things could get awkward
stories.summary: President Donald Trump plans to attend the White House Correspondents' Dinner for the first time during his presidency. The event carries notable history for Trump, who was publicly mocked by then-President Barack Obama at the 2011 dinner.

stories.title: Palestinians vote in first elections since Gaza war
stories.summary: Nearly 1.5 million Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and approximately 70,000 in Gaza's Deir el-Balah area are registered to vote in local elections, the first held since the Gaza war. The vote was organized by the Ramallah-based Central Elections Commission.

stories.title: Flights resume at Tehran airport as US-Iran ceasefire holds
stories.summary: International flights resumed at Tehran's Imam Khomeini International Airport after weeks of disruption caused by the ongoing war, as a ceasefire between the United States and Iran continued to hold.

stories.title: Palestinian local elections give some Gazans a chance to vote for the first time in years
stories.summary: The West Bank-based Palestinian Authority included the Gazan city of Deir al-Balah in local elections to reinforce its claim to authority over the territory. The PA was ousted from Gaza by Hamas in 2007 and views the symbolic inclusion as a step toward reasserting governance there.

stories.title: US seeks to revoke citizenship of Pakistani-born doctor convicted in child exploitation case
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice filed a civil case to revoke the citizenship of a Pakistani-born physician convicted of sexually exploiting a minor. The doctor allegedly coerced an 11-year-old girl online starting in 2007 and concealed the offenses during his naturalization process.

stories.title: 5 cops among 8 injured in attacks on police vehicle, ambulance in KP's Bajaur
stories.summary: Five police officers and three other people were injured in two separate attacks in Khar tehsil, Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Unidentified assailants opened fire on a police vehicle and a Rescue 1122 ambulance on Friday night before fleeing.

stories.title: Romania says drone fragments damage property during overnight Russian attack on Ukraine
stories.summary: Romania's Defence Ministry reported that drone fragments caused property damage on its territory during an overnight Russian aerial attack on Ukraine. Bucharest condemned Russia's actions, calling them a challenge to regional security and stability in the Black Sea area.

stories.title: Iran conveyed 'demands and reservations' about US positions to Pakistan
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi conveyed Tehran's negotiating demands and reservations about U.S. positions to Pakistani officials during a visit to Islamabad. Pakistan is serving as an intermediary, while U.S. President Trump indicated Iran planned to make an offer in response to American demands.

stories.title: Japan evacuates thousands as hundreds of firefighters battle wildfires
stories.summary: Wildfires burning in the mountainous Iwate region of northern Japan have consumed approximately 700 hectares over three days. Hundreds of firefighters are battling the blazes, and authorities have urged more than 3,200 residents to evacuate their homes.

stories.title: Trapped in the Gulf, ship crews run low on food, water – and mental health reserves
stories.summary: The International Maritime Organisation has raised concerns about seafarers trapped in the Persian Gulf due to the weeks-long closure of the Strait of Hormuz. At least 10 seafarers have been killed in 29 attacks on vessels in the Gulf since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran, and several ships have been seized.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill 13 Palestinians in Gaza in last 24 hours
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least 13 Palestinians in the Gaza Strip over the past 24 hours. The intensified attacks followed a truce reached between Israel and Iran.

stories.title: Iraq deadlock persists over next prime minister
stories.summary: Iraq's ruling Shiite alliance has failed to reach consensus on a new prime minister. U.S. pressure has undermined frontrunner Nouri al-Maliki's candidacy, prolonging the political deadlock.

stories.title: Palestinian local elections give some Gazans a chance to vote for the first time in years
stories.summary: Palestinians voted in local elections on Saturday, with Gaza included for the first time in roughly two decades. The vote, held across the West Bank and parts of Gaza, serves as a gauge of political sentiment amid Israel's ongoing efforts against Palestinian statehood.

stories.title: Police detain six minors for Independence Day stabbing of pizzeria worker in Petah Tikva
stories.summary: Israeli police detained six minors in connection with the fatal stabbing of recently discharged IDF soldier Yemanu Binyamin Zalka outside a pizzeria in Petah Tikva on Independence Day eve.

stories.title: President Zardari to embark on official visit to China today; talks to focus on economic cooperation, CPEC: FO
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari embarked on an official visit to China from April 25 to May 1, traveling to Changsha in Hunan province and Sanya in Hainan province. Discussions with provincial leaders focused on economic and trade cooperation and advancing the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

stories.title: Watch: Witkoff and Kushner headed to Pakistan for Iran talks: White House
